options_en: Have the AI draft a plan, then review, push back on, and revise it item by item before executing.
Execute the AI's plan exactly as given, without questioning or changing anything.
Refuse AI help entirely and hand-design everything yourself even though the interviewer already allowed it.
Skip the upfront plan and let the AI write a random first pass of code to see what happens.
why: 面试官已经接受 AI 参与设计，AI 辅助规划能加速；但强信号来自你审查和塑形计划，而不是盖章批准。
why_en: Since the interviewer is fine with AI-assisted design, let the AI draft fast, but the strong signal comes from you actively vetting and reshaping the plan.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官希望看你亲自设计，应先自己画出结构，再把 AI 用在实现体力活上。
tradeoff: AI 起草求快 vs 你亲自把关求可控
optionExplanations: 面试官已经放行 AI 参与设计，就让它先起草求快，但每一项都要你审、你改。
原样照做等于把设计判断交给 AI，即使这轮允许用 AI，你也没留下把关痕迹。
本题面试官已经开放 AI 参与，还坚持全手写等于白白放弃这轮明确允许的加速方式。
没有先成型的计划直接摸索，AI 第一版会隐性定型架构，你事后很难说清楚为什么这样设计。
optionExplanations_en: Since the interviewer already opened the door to AI-assisted design, let it draft fast — you still review and revise every piece.
Taking the draft as-is hands the design call to the AI, and there's no sign of your judgment even though review was allowed.
Refusing all AI help here throws away speed the interviewer explicitly said you could use.
Skipping a plan and letting the AI free-write first quietly locks in the architecture, and you'll struggle to explain it later.

scenario: 你不确定这轮面试是否允许 AI 帮你做计划，还是只希望 AI 写实现。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether this interview allows AI to help with planning, or only expects AI to write implementation code.
q: 最好的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this?
options: 直接假设可以用 AI 做所有设计
先问面试官对 AI 参与规划的期望
完全不用 AI，全程手写
先按自己的想法做，等面试官发现问题再解释
options_en: Just assume AI can be used for all the design work.
Ask the interviewer up front what they expect from AI in planning.
Avoid AI entirely and write everything by hand.
Do it your own way and explain only if the interviewer objects.
why: 不同公司甚至不同面试官的预期不同，提前对齐能避免把可接受的用法误判成负面信号。
why_en: Ask the interviewer directly, because expectations for AI in planning vary by company and by interviewer.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则已经在题面里写清楚，就按规则执行并简短复述你的理解即可，不必再问。
tradeoff: 先问清楚 vs 自行假设后再纠偏
optionExplanations: 凭自己猜测替面试官做了决定，一旦猜错就等于在不该用 AI 设计时用了。
边界不清时先开口确认，一句话就能把后续所有 AI 用法钉死在正确范围内。
全程手写可能白白放弃面试官本来允许的加速手段，规则还没确认就先自我设限。
先斩后奏、等被指出才补救，既被动又显得你事先没想清楚边界。
optionExplanations_en: Guessing on the interviewer's behalf means you might use AI for design exactly when you weren't supposed to.
When the boundary is unclear, one quick question locks down how you can use AI for the rest of the round.
Going fully hand-written can throw away speed the interviewer would have allowed, based on a rule you never confirmed.
Doing it your way and explaining only when caught is reactive, and signals you never thought about the boundary upfront.

q: 补全 AI 规划的分界线：
q_en: Fill in the boundary line for AI-assisted planning:
text: 理解后提出反驳和修改叫{{审阅计划}}；看不懂却点头照做叫{{橡皮图章}}。
why: 面试官看的是你是否还在控制方案：理解后提出反驳和修改是审阅计划；看不懂却点头照做是橡皮图章。
why_en: The line is vetting versus rubber-stamping: pushing back on a plan you understand is control, nodding along to one you couldn't have written is not.
tradeoff: 审阅计划（理解+修改，慢但可控）vs 橡皮图章（照单全收，快但空心）

termDefinitions.meaning: 看不懂却直接盖章通过的行为，这里指对 AI 计划不加判断就照做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rubber-stamping means approving something without understanding it, here nodding along to an AI plan you couldn't defend.

scenario: 45 分钟的题面写着：先修 parser bug，再加搜索功能，最后优化性能。
scenario_en: Your 45-minute problem statement says: fix the parser bug, then add search, then optimize performance.
q: 多数 AI 编码面试题为什么需要先拆分阶段？
q_en: Why do most AI coding interview problems need to be split into phases first?
options: 因为 AI 每次只能生成一行代码
因为提前拆好阶段，就能跳过每个阶段该写的测试
因为问题常含修 bug、加功能、优化等多阶段
因为这类题目从来没有现成代码库
options_en: Because the AI can only generate one line of code at a time.
Because splitting into phases lets you skip the tests each phase would otherwise need.
Because these problems usually bundle multiple phases like fixing a bug, adding a feature, then optimizing.
Because this kind of problem never starts with an existing codebase.
why: 多阶段题需要你判断顺序和依赖，否则 AI 容易一次性生成难以验证的大块代码。
why_en: Multi-phase problems need you to decide the order and dependencies, or the AI will produce one large, hard-to-verify block of code.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BigTask[Big task] --> Phase1[Baseline]
  BigTask --> Phase2[Core feature]
  BigTask --> Phase3[Edges]
  Phase1 --> Prompt1[Small prompt]
  Phase2 --> Prompt2[Small prompt]
optionExplanations: 这个说法不成立，AI 完全能一次输出大段代码，限制不在这里。
拆分和是否写测试无关，每个阶段该测的部分照样要测，一步都省不掉。
阶段之间彼此有顺序和依赖，你得先想清楚顺序再分步提示 AI。
很多这类面试其实带现成代码库，这不是要拆分的理由。
optionExplanations_en: That's not actually true — the AI can output a large block in one go, so that's not the real limit.
Splitting the work has nothing to do with skipping tests; each phase still needs its own checks, none of them optional.
The phases depend on each other in order, so you have to work out that order before prompting step by step.
Plenty of these interviews do start from an existing codebase, so that's not the real reason to decompose.

scenario: 类似 Shopify 的开放式题：空仓库加一份 README，60 分钟内要交出能跑的小应用。
scenario_en: A Shopify-style open-ended round: an empty repo and a README, with a working small app due in 60 minutes.
q: 开放式从零构建时，哪些顺序原则通常成立？（多选）
q_en: For open-ended greenfield builds, which ordering principles usually hold? (Select all)
options: 先建数据模型，再写依赖这些模型的逻辑
先做核心功能，再补边界情况
先修会影响后续功能的 bug，再加依赖它的新功能
先优化还不存在的代码
options_en: Model your data first, then write the logic that depends on it.
Build the core functionality before handling edge cases.
Fix bugs that block later features before adding features that depend on them.
Optimize code that doesn't exist yet.
why: 这三条顺序能减少返工；反过来先优化还没成形的代码，往往把复杂度引到错误的地方。
why_en: Model-first, core-before-edge, and fix-before-feature ordering reduce rework, while optimizing code that doesn't exist yet wastes effort.
optionExplanations: 先定好对象和关系，后续逻辑才有稳定边界可以依靠。
主路径先跑通，剩下的少数分支能逐个补，不拖累主线。
先解除卡住后续功能的坏基础，别在它上面继续叠新功能。
代码还没写出来，根本没有可测的东西能拿来调优。
optionExplanations_en: Nail down the objects and relations first, so later logic has a stable boundary to build on.
Get the main path working first, then the few edge branches can be patched in without derailing it.
Clear the blocking bug before stacking a new feature on top of a broken base.
There's no code yet to profile or tune — there's nothing to optimize.

scenario: 类似 Shopify 的开放式教程题：你从空仓库和 README 开始，要构建一个小应用。
scenario_en: In a Shopify-like open-ended tutorial task, you start from an empty repo and a README and need to build a small app.
q: 最先应该让计划解决什么？
q_en: What should your plan solve first?
options: 最终性能优化
UI 配色
让 AI 一次写完整应用
先定义核心实体和数据结构
options_en: Final performance optimization.
The UI color scheme.
Let the AI write the entire app in one shot.
Define the core entities and data structures first.
why: 数据结构先定下来，会迫使你先理解系统对象和关系，后续逻辑才有稳定边界。
why_en: Modeling entities first in greenfield work forces you to understand the system's objects and relationships before any logic is written.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目是已有代码里的单点 bug，先定位失败路径比重新建模更重要。
tradeoff: 先建数据模型求稳定边界 vs 先让 AI 快速出一版看效果
optionExplanations: 系统结构还没成形就调优，之后架构一变这些优化全部作废。
配色不影响核心逻辑对不对，不该抢在架构判断前面处理。
把整个应用交给 AI 一次写完，你之后很难解释每个类的职责为什么这样分。
空仓库起步先把对象和关系定下来，后面每一步逻辑才有依据。
optionExplanations_en: Tuning performance before the structure even exists means the work gets thrown away once the architecture shifts.
Color choices don't affect whether the core logic is correct, so they shouldn't jump ahead of the architecture call.
Letting the AI write the whole app in one shot leaves you unable to explain why each class has the responsibilities it does.
Starting from an empty repo, pin down the objects and their relations first so every later step has something to build on.

scenario: 你直接对 AI 说“build the whole task scheduler”，指望它一次产出全部实现。
scenario_en: You just tell the AI to build the whole task scheduler and expect the entire implementation in one shot.
q: 缺少拆分时，AI 最容易生成什么样的代码？
q_en: Without decomposition, what kind of code is the AI most likely to generate?
options: 清晰、可验证、每步可解释的小改动
职责太杂的大块代码，需求一变就难重构
完全不包含任何实现
只包含测试
options_en: Clean, verifiable, small changes you can explain step by step.
One large block of code that covers too many responsibilities and is hard to refactor once requirements shift.
No implementation at all.
Only test code.
why: 大而泛的提示会把多个决策埋进一个输出，直到很晚才暴露错误方向。
why_en: A broad, undecomposed prompt buries many decisions inside one output, so a wrong direction only surfaces very late.
optionExplanations: 这是拆分得当时才会出现的结果，不是本题问的缺少拆分的后果。
职责混在一起，需求一变就要大改，返工成本随之升高。
AI 通常会给出实现，完全不产出代码不是常见的规划风险。
只有测试没有实现，没法验证真实行为，也不是缺少拆分的典型后果。
optionExplanations_en: That's what good decomposition produces — not the outcome of skipping it, which is what's being asked here.
Responsibilities get tangled together, so any requirement change forces a big rewrite and heavier rework.
The AI usually does produce an implementation; producing nothing at all isn't the typical risk here.
Tests with no implementation can't verify real behavior, and that's not the typical fallout from skipping decomposition either.

scenario: 你在给一个任务调度器写提示，手上这两条候选提示要判断粒度是否合适。
scenario_en: You're sizing prompts for a task scheduler and have to judge whether these two candidates hit the right granularity.
q: “Build the scheduler”和“Write the Task constructor”分别错在哪里？
q_en: What is wrong with “Build the scheduler” versus “Write the Task constructor”?
options: 前者太宽，后者太窄
前者太窄，后者太宽
两者都是理想粒度
两者都不能给 AI
options_en: "Build the scheduler" is too broad, and "Write the Task constructor" is too narrow.
"Build the scheduler" is too narrow, and "Write the Task constructor" is too broad.
Both prompts are the ideal granularity.
Neither prompt should ever be given to the AI.
why: 前者把多个算法和设计决策混在一个提示里；后者只是你自己可以直接手写的一行级任务。
why_en: The broad prompt bundles several algorithm and design decisions into one shot, while the narrow one is just a single line you'd type yourself.
tradeoff: 提示太宽（AI 决策过多，难验证）vs 提示太窄（你在替 AI 打字，没有价值）
codeSample:
太宽: "Build the scheduler"
太窄: "Write the Task constructor"
右粒度: 建 Task/Dependency 类型 -> 建依赖图 -> 拓扑排序 -> 处理 cycle
optionExplanations: 校准提示粒度正好卡在两者之间：一个太宽把决策全扔给 AI，一个太窄等于替它打字。
方向说反了：Build the scheduler 才是那个过宽的提示，不是过窄。
两个例子分别踩了过宽和过窄两个极端，都不是理想粒度。
两个提示都能用，只是各自需要往中间粒度调整，不是完全不能给 AI。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the calibration point in the middle: one prompt hands over every decision, the other has you typing for the AI.
The direction is flipped — "Build the scheduler" is the broad one, not the narrow one.
Each example sits at an opposite extreme, so neither is the ideal granularity.
Both prompts are usable, they just need to shift toward the middle granularity — neither is off-limits to the AI.

q: 把 task scheduler with dependencies 的合理拆分排好：
q_en: Put the reasonable decomposition for a task scheduler with dependencies in order:
steps: 用拓扑排序计算合法执行顺序
处理 cycle 情况
建 Task 和 Dependency 类型
根据输入构建依赖图
why: 先建 Task/Dependency 模型，把输入转成依赖图，再用拓扑排序求执行顺序，最后单独处理无解的 cycle。
why_en: For dependency scheduling: model tasks first, build the graph, topologically sort it, then handle the cycle case separately.
tradeoff: 一次性大提示（AI 承担全部决策）vs 按拓扑顺序拆成 4 个小步骤（你逐步验证）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Model[Model tasks] --> Graph[Build dependency graph]
  Graph --> Ready[Find ready tasks]
  Ready --> Schedule[Assign workers]
  Schedule --> Verify[Verify order]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每个节点排在它依赖的节点之后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so each node comes after everything it depends on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖图里出现环状依赖，导致不存在合法执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cycle is a circular dependency in the graph, which means no valid execution order exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务之间的先后依赖关系，通常建模成图中的一条有向边。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dependency is a must-come-before relationship between tasks, usually modeled as a directed edge in the graph.

scenario: 面试时长 45-60 分钟，你要把整道题拆成几个主要阶段写进计划里。
scenario_en: In a 45 to 60 minute interview, you need to split the whole problem into a few main phases in your plan.
q: 这道题的计划粒度，拆成几个阶段最匹配这个时长？
q_en: For that interview length, how many phases is the right planning granularity?
options: 只给一个笼统步骤，让 AI 自己规划全部实现
拆成三到五个可独立验证的阶段
拆成十几个逐行级别的小步骤
步骤数量不设上限，越细越好
options_en: Give the AI one vague step and let it plan the entire implementation.
Break it into three to five independently verifiable phases.
Break it into a dozen-plus line-by-line micro-steps.
Don't cap the step count at all — finer is always better.
why: 45-60 分钟 ÷ 一步一次提示-验证周期 ≈ 3-5 步；这个数字决定你该把计划切多细，也是后面判断有没有过度拆分的参照。
why_en: Divide the 45 to 60 minute interview by one prompt-and-verify cycle per step and you land on three to five steps, which sets how finely to slice your plan.
optionExplanations: 一步到底等于把全部架构决策交给 AI，45-60 分钟根本来不及逐项验证。
把 45 到 60 分钟按单步提示加验证来分配，落点刚好是三到五步。
十几个逐行步骤远超这个时长能验证的次数，变成人工盯着 AI 打字。
步骤越细耗时越多，超出面试时长就没时间跑完整个实现。
optionExplanations_en: One catch-all step hands the AI every architecture call, and 45 to 60 minutes isn't enough to verify it piece by piece.
Pace it at one prompt-and-verify cycle per step across 45 to 60 minutes and you land on three to five steps.
A dozen-plus line-by-line steps blows past how many checks that time budget can fit, turning into micromanaging.
The finer you slice it the more time it eats, and you'll run out of interview time before finishing the build.

scenario: 你已经形成计划：先修 parser bug，再用 BFS 加搜索功能，最后若需要处理加权边再优化。
scenario_en: You have a plan: fix the parser bug first, add search with BFS, then optimize for weighted edges if needed.
q: 在提示 AI 前应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do before prompting the AI?
options: 只在心里记住，不说出来
把三步计划一次性丢给 AI，不逐步确认
把计划告诉面试官，给他们纠偏窗口
不按计划顺序，先做优化再回头修 bug
options_en: Keep it in your head and never say it out loud.
Dump all three steps on the AI in one prompt without confirming each one.
Say the plan out loud to the interviewer so they get a chance to redirect you.
Ignore your own plan order and optimize first, then go back and fix the bug.
why: 说出计划展示战略思考，也给面试官一个在你走偏前就能提醒你的窗口。
why_en: Stating your plan out loud shows strategic thinking and gives the interviewer a window to redirect you before you head the wrong way.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目极小，也至少用一句话说明当前顺序和理由，而不是完全跳过。
tradeoff: 说出计划（多花十秒，换纠偏机会）vs 直接开始写（更快，但走偏了没人拦）

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层扩展、常用于求无权图的最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, or Breadth-First Search, expands level by level and is commonly used to find shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把输入文本解析成结构化数据的组件，这里指代码里已有的解析模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parser is the component that turns raw input text into structured data.

optionExplanations: 计划只留在你脑子里，面试官没有共享上下文，后面每次提示都要重新解释背景。
三步一次性丢给 AI，三个决策被压进一次输出，容易生成难验证的大块代码。
已经形成计划时，先花几秒说给面试官听，能在你走偏前就被拦住。
parser 的 bug 还没修，后面靠它的搜索功能等于建在坏地基上。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the plan in your head only means the interviewer has no shared context, and you re-explain the background every prompt after.
Dumping all three steps on the AI at once buries three decisions in a single output that's hard to verify.
Once you have a plan, saying it out loud gives the interviewer a few seconds to redirect you before you drift.
The parser bug is still broken, so the search feature you build next sits on a bad foundation.

scenario: 面试官全程看着你的屏幕，你刚定好三阶段计划，还没敲第一个提示。
scenario_en: The interviewer is watching your screen; you've just settled on a three-phase plan and haven't typed the first prompt.
q: 把计划说给面试官听有哪些作用？（多选）
q_en: What does saying your plan out loud to the interviewer accomplish? (Select all)
options: 保证 AI 输出永远正确
展示你在战略性思考
给面试官机会及时纠偏
建立共享上下文，后续提示更容易被理解
options_en: It guarantees the AI's output is always correct.
It shows you're thinking strategically.
It gives the interviewer a chance to redirect you early.
It creates shared context so your later prompts are easier to follow.
why: 计划沟通能同步方向和评估点，但仍需要你在执行时验证 AI 的结果，它不会替你保证正确性。
why_en: Sharing the plan syncs direction and gives the interviewer something to evaluate, but you still have to verify the AI's output yourself.
optionExplanations: 说出计划不能替代验证这一步，AI 仍可能跑偏或出错。
十秒话就能让面试官判断你是不是有方向，而不只是在打字。
面试官能在你投入实现前先拦住走偏的方向，省下返工时间。
后面每个提示，面试官都能对上你当前在做哪一步，少一次重新解释。
optionExplanations_en: Saying the plan out loud doesn't replace verification — the AI can still drift or get it wrong.
Ten seconds of talking lets the interviewer tell you have direction, not just that you're typing.
The interviewer can stop a wrong turn before you sink time implementing it.
Every prompt after that, the interviewer can place which step you're on, so you skip re-explaining.

scenario: 你已经决定在现有 `Grid` 类上用 BFS 找迷宫最短路径。
scenario_en: You have decided to use BFS on the existing `Grid` class to find the shortest maze path.
q: 哪条提示最能体现“用计划指导 AI”？
q_en: Which prompt best shows that you are using your plan to guide the AI?
options: 跟 AI 说 solve the maze 就行，别的不用管
在 Grid 类里用 BFS，指定入口和返回坐标路径
随便写个高效算法，思路交给 AI 决定
先把 Grid 类整个重写一遍再说
options_en: "Just tell the AI to solve the maze, nothing else specified."
"Implement BFS in the Grid class, with a named entry point and a returned coordinate path."
"Write some efficient algorithm, leave the approach up to the AI."
"Rewrite the whole Grid class first."
why: 提示把算法选择、入口对象和返回值都交代清楚，AI 负责实现细节，而不是替你决定路线。
why_en: This prompt spells out the chosen algorithm, the entry object, and the return value, so the AI implements your plan instead of choosing its own route.
whenOtherWins: 如果边权不一致，BFS 不再适合最短路径，应改用 Dijkstra 或 A*，并在提示里说明原因。
codeSample:
Implement BFS in the existing Grid class.
Start from start, stop at end, and return the shortest path as a list of coordinates.
Use the existing Cell representation; do not introduce a parallel grid model.
tradeoff: 笼统提示（AI 决定算法，快但失控）vs 精确提示（你决定算法，AI 负责落地）
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw prompt] --> AI[AI chooses plan]
  AI --> Drift[Drift]

flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> AI[Focused implementation]
  AI --> Review[Review diff]

flowchart LR
  Vague[Vague ask] --> AI[AI guesses structure]
  AI --> Mismatch[Mismatch risk]

flowchart LR
  Rewrite[Rewrite all] --> Scope[Scope creep]
  Scope --> Risk[Risk]

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层扩展节点，能在无权图里找到最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权最短路径的经典算法，权重非负时保证最优解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths in weighted graphs and guarantees optimality when weights are non-negative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 Dijkstra 基础上加启发函数、更快收敛到目标的最短路径算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A-star adds a heuristic on top of Dijkstra's algorithm to reach the target faster.

optionExplanations: 只说 solve the maze，AI 会自己挑算法和结构，你的判断没有出现在提示里。
算法、入口对象、返回格式都写清楚了，AI 复用现有 Cell，产出能直接接进代码库。
只要求高效不指定算法，AI 可能选一个和现有 Grid/Cell 不兼容的实现。
没必要的重写会把范围扩大到 Grid 本身，偏离找最短路径这个目标。
optionExplanations_en: Just saying "solve the maze" lets the AI pick its own algorithm and structure — your judgment never makes it into the prompt.
Naming the algorithm, entry point, and return format means the AI reuses the existing Cell and the result drops straight into the codebase.
Asking only for efficiency without naming an algorithm risks the AI picking something incompatible with the existing Grid and Cell.
An unnecessary rewrite drags scope onto the Grid class itself, away from the actual goal of finding the shortest path.

scenario: 题面是一段英文需求，代码库已有既定接口风格，你想省时间整段粘给 AI。
scenario_en: The problem is an English spec, the codebase already has its own interface conventions, and you want to save time by pasting it straight into the AI.
q: 把原始题目直接粘给 AI，而不先转化成自己的计划，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of pasting the raw problem into AI instead of translating it into your own plan first?
options: AI 一定读不懂英文题面，会给出错误方案
跳过转化这一步，代码依然会自动通过全部测试
跳过转化这一步，你反而会省下验证时间
AI 给方案，但未必贴合代码库或预期
options_en: The AI definitely can't read an English problem statement and will produce a broken solution.
Skipping the translation step still means the code automatically passes all the tests.
Skipping the translation step actually saves you verification time.
The AI will produce a solution, but it might not fit the codebase or expectations.
why: 原题提示让模型自己决定关键路线，你也失去了展示问题拆解和选型判断的机会。
why_en: Pasting the raw problem lets the model pick the approach on its own, and you lose the chance to show your own decomposition and judgment.
optionExplanations: 现代模型理解英文题目基本没有障碍，这不是真实风险。
方案通不通过测试，跟有没有先转化成自己的计划没有必然关系。
跳过转化通常不会省验证时间，返工反而可能更多，说反了。
AI 会给出方案，但它自己选的路线可能忽略代码库结构或面试官的期待。
optionExplanations_en: Modern models have no real trouble reading an English prompt — that's not the actual risk.
Whether the code passes the tests has no direct link to whether you translated the problem into your own plan.
Skipping the translation step rarely saves verification time — it's the opposite, it usually means more rework.
The AI will produce something, but the route it picks on its own can ignore the codebase's structure or what's expected.

q: 补全好提示应包含的上下文：
q_en: Fill in the context a good prompt should include:
text: 好的实现提示应说明选择的{{算法}}、要复用的{{数据结构}}，以及如何和现有{{接口}}交互。
why: 这些信息让 AI 沿你的计划写代码，而不是发明并行架构；缺一项，AI 就多一分自由决定权。
why_en: A good implementation prompt names the algorithm, the data structures to reuse, and the existing interfaces so the AI follows your plan instead of inventing its own.

scenario: 你已经想清楚要用 BFS，却在提示里逐行写出变量名、循环结构和每句代码。
scenario_en: You've already settled on BFS, but your prompt spells out variable names, loop structure, and every single line.
q: 提示“太具体”会带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem does an overly specific prompt create?
options: 你变成逐行口述，AI 只是代打
AI 会掌握太多上下文信息
输出内容一定会变得更短
面试官会看不到你的想法
options_en: You end up dictating line by line, and the AI is just typing for you.
The AI ends up with too much context.
The output is guaranteed to be shorter.
The interviewer can no longer see your thinking.
why: 目标是指导 AI 实现你的方案，而不是把每个变量名和每行代码都口述给它。
why_en: The goal is to direct the AI to implement your approach, not to dictate every variable name and every line yourself.
tradeoff: 太具体（你在打字，AI 只是代打）vs 右粒度（你定方向，AI 处理实现体力活）
optionExplanations: 提示细到每个变量名，你花的时间跟自己打字差不多，AI 没帮你分担设计。
上下文多少不是问题所在，缺的是留给 AI 的判断空间。
输出长短不是核心问题，谁在做设计决策才是关键。
面试官反而能看到你在口述每一行，只是看到的是打字而不是判断。
optionExplanations_en: When the prompt spells out every variable name, you spend as much time as typing it yourself — the AI isn't carrying any design load.
The amount of context isn't the issue — what's missing is room for the AI to actually judge anything.
Output length isn't the core problem — who's making the design call is.
The interviewer actually sees you dictating every line, just typing instead of deciding.

scenario: 你的计划里定了用 BFS 找最短路径，AI 交回来的代码却换成了 Dijkstra。
scenario_en: Your plan called for BFS to find the shortest path, but the code the AI hands back uses Dijkstra instead.
q: AI 回来后偷偷把你选的算法换成另一个，应该怎么处理？
q_en: If the AI quietly swaps your chosen algorithm for another one, how should you respond?
options: 只要能编译通过就直接接受
不问理由，立即放弃原计划改用它
看理由站不站得住，站不住就纠偏
不管算法换没换，跳过测试直接提交
options_en: Accept it as long as it compiles.
Abandon your original plan immediately without asking why, and switch to it.
Check whether there's a good reason; if not, correct it and redirect the AI.
Skip the tests and submit as-is, regardless of whether the algorithm changed.
why: 模型可以提供替代思路，但方案改变必须经过你判断，否则你就不再是驱动者。
why_en: The model can propose alternatives, but any change of approach must pass through your judgment, or you stop being the one driving.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Output[AI output] --> Drift{Changed algorithm?}
  Drift -->|yes| Stop[Stop and name drift]
  Stop --> Repoint[Repoint prompt]
  Repoint --> Verify[Verify against plan]
optionExplanations: 编译通过只说明语法没问题，不代表换掉的算法真的适合这道题。
不问理由直接放弃计划，如果 AI 的替代方案其实更好，你就白白丢了一个合理 pivot。
先判断替代算法有没有站得住的理由，站得住就用，站不住就纠偏重定向。
跳过测试只会让偷换算法的副作用更晚才暴露出来。
optionExplanations_en: Compiling only means the syntax is fine — it says nothing about whether the swapped algorithm actually fits this problem.
Dropping the plan without asking why means you might be throwing away a genuinely better alternative.
Check whether the swap has a solid reason first — keep it if it does, correct and redirect the AI if it doesn't.
Skipping the tests just delays when the side effects of the swapped algorithm finally show up.

scenario: 面试过半，三阶段计划刚执行到第二阶段，你在判断要不要改计划。
scenario_en: You're halfway through the interview, on phase two of your three-phase plan, weighing whether to revise it.
q: 哪些情况是修改计划的合理理由？（多选）
q_en: Which situations are valid reasons to revise the plan? (Select all)
options: 发现新的性能约束
数据模型比取向时看到的更复杂
AI 随口建议重写一切但你说不出理由
面试官给出改变范围的提示
options_en: You discover a new performance constraint.
The data model turns out more complex than it looked during orientation.
The AI casually suggests rewriting everything and you can't say why that would help.
The interviewer drops a hint that changes the scope.
why: 计划应该随新事实变化，而不是随 AI 的每一个建议摇摆。
why_en: Revise the plan when new facts change the problem, not just because the AI suggests something different.
optionExplanations: 约束一变，原计划可能不再可行，这时候改是有依据的。
模型复杂度变了，原来的拆分粒度和接口边界可能不够用了。
没有收益说明的重写建议只是噪声，跟着走等于把方向让给了 AI。
范围一变，哪些组件还要不要做都会跟着变，计划自然要跟上。
optionExplanations_en: When a constraint changes, the original plan may no longer hold up, so revising it is grounded in fact.
If the model turns out more complex, your original phase sizing and interface boundaries may no longer be enough.
A rewrite suggestion with no stated payoff is just noise — following it hands the direction over to the AI.
A scope change shifts which components still need building, so the plan has to move with it.

scenario: AI 建议用另一种数据结构，你能清楚解释它如何更好满足新发现的约束。
scenario_en: The AI suggests another data structure, and you can clearly explain how it better satisfies a newly discovered constraint.
q: 这属于什么情况？
q_en: What situation is this?
options: 失去控制
合理 pivot
必须拒绝 AI
测试无关紧要
options_en: Losing control of the design.
A legitimate pivot.
Something you must reject outright.
Something where tests no longer matter.
why: 只要新方案的理由来自你对约束的理解，采纳 AI 的建议也算是你在掌控。
why_en: Adopting the AI's suggestion still counts as control as long as you can explain why it better fits the newly discovered constraint.
whenOtherWins: 如果你说不出收益，就先保留原计划，或要求 AI 给出可验证的理由再考虑。
tradeoff: 坚持原计划（一致但可能过时）vs 采纳有理由的建议（灵活但要你能讲清楚为什么）
optionExplanations: 只要理由站得住脚，采纳建议不等于失控，这个说法过于绝对。
你能讲清新数据结构为什么更贴合刚发现的约束，方向依然是你在决定。
一刀切拒绝会让你错过一个真正更合适的方案。
换了数据结构之后更需要测试验证行为没有变化，不是可以忽略。
optionExplanations_en: As long as the reason holds up, taking the suggestion isn't losing control — that call is too absolute.
You can explain exactly why the new structure fits the newly found constraint, so the direction is still yours.
Rejecting every suggestion outright means missing a genuinely better option.
Swapping data structures makes testing more necessary, not less — behavior still needs verifying.

scenario: 你在修一个 parser bug，AI 连续三轮建议换框架、重写类层级，都没说清和这个 bug 的关系。
scenario_en: You're fixing a parser bug, and for three turns straight the AI has pushed framework swaps and class rewrites without tying any of it to the bug.
q: AI 反复建议大重写、换框架、从头再来，却说不清楚道理，这种现象在 AI 编码面试里通常叫什么？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what is it called when the AI repeatedly suggests big rewrites, framework swaps, or starting over without a clear reason?
options: Scope creep
Rubber-stamping
Test-driven iteration
AI spiral
options_en: Scope creep
Rubber-stamping
Test-driven iteration
An AI spiral
why: 这叫 AI spiral——模型不知道答案时开始乱提大重写建议，需要你停下来重新评估，而不是跟着转。
why_en: This is called an AI spiral: the model flails by proposing rewrites when it doesn't know the answer, and you need to stop and reassess instead of following along.

termDefinitions.meaning: 范围蔓延：改动或需求不断超出原计划边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when changes or requirements keep expanding beyond the original plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不理解却直接照单全收的行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rubber-stamping means approving something without actually understanding it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型没有把握时开始乱提大重写、换框架等建议的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AI spiral is when the model flails by proposing large rewrites or framework changes because it doesn't actually know the answer.

optionExplanations: Scope creep 描述的是需求或范围不断膨胀，不是模型说不清理由的乱提议。
Rubber-stamping 说的是你照单全收的态度，不是模型本身反复乱建议的行为。
Test-driven iteration 是先写测试再实现的正向流程，跟无根据的大重写无关。
模型没把握时靠乱提大重写制造进展感，这种现象就叫 AI spiral。
optionExplanations_en: Scope creep describes requirements or scope steadily ballooning, not the model flailing with unexplained suggestions.
Rubber-stamping describes your own habit of nodding along, not the model's repeated behavior.
Test-driven iteration is the healthy write-tests-first flow, unrelated to baseless big rewrites.
When the model fakes progress by pitching big rewrites it can't justify, that's called an AI spiral.

scenario: AI 连续建议重构类层级、换框架、从头开始，但没有解释这些如何解决当前 bug。
scenario_en: The AI keeps suggesting class hierarchy refactors, framework swaps, and starting over, but does not explain how any of that fixes the current bug.
q: 最好的反应是什么？
q_en: What is the best response?
options: 停下来重新定位问题，给 AI 更小的任务
跟着 AI 一路重写下去，保持表面上的进展
把暴露问题的测试删掉，假装一切正常
觉得卡壳解决不了，直接结束这场面试
options_en: Stop, re-pin down the actual problem, and give the AI a smaller, more concrete task.
Go along with the AI's rewrite spiral to keep up the appearance of progress.
Delete the tests that expose the problem and pretend everything's fine.
Decide it's unsolvable and just end the interview outright.
why: AI spiral 要靠你主动打断，回到问题本身和可验证的小步骤，而不是跟着模型的大动作走。
why_en: You have to interrupt an AI spiral yourself by reassessing the actual problem and handing the AI a smaller, verifiable task.
whenOtherWins: 如果架构确实阻止了需求实现，也要先讲清证据和最小迁移方案，而不是盲目重写。
tradeoff: 跟着 AI 重写（看似有进展，实则失控）vs 停下重新定位（慢一拍，但保持可验证）
optionExplanations: 先缩小任务范围，你就能重新验证每一步，不被卷入无根据的重写。
重写没解释怎么解决当前 bug，那种进展只是表面的。
删测试只会掩盖问题，bug 本身仍然存在。
结束面试放弃了展示你能识别并处理 AI spiral 的机会。
optionExplanations_en: Shrinking the task first lets you verify each step again instead of getting swept into an unjustified rewrite.
The rewrite never explains how it fixes the current bug, so that progress is only surface-level.
Deleting the tests just hides the problem — the bug is still there.
Ending the interview throws away the chance to show you can spot and handle an AI spiral.

q: 补全高质量 pivot 叙述：
q_en: Complete a high-quality pivot statement:
text: “我发现 brute force 对 phase three 的大输入{{不扩展}}，所以我会切到{{heap-based}}方案。”
why: 这句话把问题、触发约束和新路线一次说清——听起来是适应而不是慌乱，这是高质量 pivot 叙述的模板。
why_en: A strong pivot statement names the scaling problem and the replacement approach in one breath, which reads as adaptation rather than confusion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 穷举所有可能情况的解法，实现简单但通常不能应对大规模输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Brute force means trying every possibility, which is simple to implement but usually does not scale to large inputs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于堆这种数据结构的方案，常用来在大数据量下快速拿到最小/最大元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heap-based approach uses a heap data structure to efficiently get the minimum or maximum element even at scale.

q: 把规划到执行的闭环排好：
q_en: Put the planning-to-execution loop in order:
steps: 用第一步计划写具体提示
向面试官说明整体计划
取向后拆成 3-5 个阶段
审阅 AI 输出是否符合该阶段目标
why: 先拆阶段、再向面试官同步计划、然后用当前阶段目标写提示、最后审阅输出是否达标，形成闭环。
why_en: The loop is decompose into phases, state the plan aloud, prompt for the current step, then review the output against that step's goal.
tradeoff: 把整段闭环压成一次性长提示（AI 全权决定）vs 拆成阶段循环，每步都审阅再继续（你逐步把关）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> State[State plan aloud]
  State --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Revise{Need revise?}
  Revise -->|yes| Plan
  Revise -->|no| Next[Next step]

scenario: 平台化的结构化题面已经列好阶段：先修 bug，再加功能，最后优化。
scenario_en: A platform-run structured problem already lists the phases for you: fix the bug, add the feature, then optimize.
q: 结构化面试中，为什么拆分通常比开放式题更明显？
q_en: In a structured interview, why is decomposition usually more obvious than in an open-ended problem?
options: 结构化题反而没有任何额外约束
结构化题不需要读懂现有代码
因为题面通常已经写明了各阶段顺序
AI 会自动帮你拆成最佳执行步骤
options_en: Structured problems actually come with no extra constraints at all.
Structured problems don't require understanding the existing code.
Because the problem statement usually already spells out the phase order.
The AI automatically splits the work into the best execution steps for you.
why: 即使阶段已经写明（比如 bug fix -> feature -> optimization），你仍要在每个阶段内判断哪些部分需要自己思考，哪些适合交给 AI 实现。
why_en: Even when phases like bug fix, feature, and optimization are already spelled out, you still decide within each phase how much needs your reasoning versus AI implementation.
optionExplanations: 结构化题通常约束反而更多，比如平台限定的阶段顺序，这个说法不成立。
读懂现有代码仍是每个阶段动手前的前提，不能跳过。
阶段边界题面已经画好，你只需要在每个阶段内继续细化。
AI 不会替你决定阶段内的粒度，拆分的判断始终是你的工作。
optionExplanations_en: Structured problems usually come with more constraints, like a platform-fixed phase order, so that claim doesn't hold.
Reading the existing code is still a prerequisite before touching each phase — you can't skip it.
The phase boundaries are already laid out in the prompt, so you only need to refine within each one.
The AI doesn't set the granularity within a phase for you — deciding how to split the work is still your job.

scenario: 你要在 50 分钟内交付一个含 5 个同构 endpoint 的服务，得决定哪些先自己想清楚。
scenario_en: You have 50 minutes to ship a service with five identical endpoints and must decide what to think through yourself first.
q: 哪些任务更需要你先思考清楚，再让 AI 实现？（多选）
q_en: Which tasks require you to think them through first, then let the AI implement? (Select all)
options: 选择算法
生成五个同构 endpoint 的样板
处理关键边界条件
设计核心数据结构
options_en: Choosing the algorithm.
Generating boilerplate for five identical endpoints.
Handling the critical edge cases.
Designing the core data structures.
why: 算法、边界和数据结构是判断密集区；重复样板才是 AI 可以更自由处理的体量工作。
why_en: Algorithm choice, edge cases, and core data structures are judgment-heavy, while repetitive boilerplate is volume work the AI can handle with more freedom.
tradeoff: 判断密集任务（你先想清楚）vs 体量重复任务（AI 自由发挥也没关系）
optionExplanations: 算法选错会直接改变正确性和复杂度，这类判断必须你先拿主意。
五个 endpoint 结构相同，AI 复制这种模式的风险很低，可以放手。
边界条件是最容易漏、最容易出 bug 的地方，得你先想到。
数据结构一旦定下就是后续所有逻辑的地基，得你先决定。
optionExplanations_en: Picking the wrong algorithm changes correctness and complexity directly, so that call has to be yours first.
Five identical endpoints are low-risk for the AI to copy the pattern — you can let it run free here.
Edge cases are where bugs slip through most easily, so you need to spot them yourself first.
Once the data structure is set it becomes the foundation for everything downstream, so decide it yourself first.

scenario: 你正在修一个具体 bug，AI 却建议顺手重构整个类层级，你说不出这对修 bug 有什么帮助。
scenario_en: You're fixing one specific bug and the AI suggests refactoring the entire class hierarchy, with no benefit you can articulate.
q: AI 建议重构整个类层级，但你解释不出收益，最主要风险是什么？
q_en: If the AI suggests refactoring the whole class hierarchy and you cannot explain the benefit, what is the main risk?
options: 重构完代码一定会变得更短
范围膨胀，时间耗在无关改动上
测试数量会随着重构自动变多
面试官看到大重构一定更满意
options_en: After the refactor, the code is guaranteed to be shorter.
Scope creep: time gets burned on changes unrelated to the goal.
The number of tests automatically goes up along with the refactor.
The interviewer is guaranteed to be more pleased seeing a big refactor.
why: 无理由的大重构会把你从计划带走，也会让后续每个生成结果更难解释和验证。
why_en: An unjustified rewrite pulls you away from the plan and makes every later output harder to explain and verify.

termDefinitions.meaning: 范围蔓延：改动不断超出原计划边界，消耗与目标无关的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep means changes keep expanding beyond the original plan and burn time on work unrelated to the goal.

optionExplanations: 代码长短跟有没有收益无关，重构后也可能反而更冗长。
时间被无根据的改动占用，题目本身要解决的目标反而完不成。
测试数量不会因为重构自动增加，得你额外补上。
面试官更可能追问收益在哪里，而不是自动就更满意。
optionExplanations_en: Code length has nothing to do with whether there's an actual payoff — a rewrite can come out longer.
Time gets burned on unjustified changes, and the actual problem you were supposed to solve stays unsolved.
Test count doesn't grow on its own from a rewrite — you'd have to add those yourself.
The interviewer is more likely to ask what the payoff is than to automatically be pleased.

scenario: 这是 Rippling 式一轮:面试官沿途一个接一个给你测试用例,你增量地把功能建出来,而不是照着预列好的 bug→feature→optimize 阶段走。
scenario_en: This is a Rippling-style round: the interviewer hands you test cases one at a time as you build features incrementally, rather than following a pre-listed bug to feature to optimize phase list.
q: 你的拆解应该怎么组织?
q_en: How should you organize your decomposition?
options: 把整份阶段计划提前锁死,先不理会陆续给的用例
按陆续给的用例推进,一次实现一个功能过掉当前用例
跳过拆分,反正测试用例会替你把一切都定义好
把手上所有用例一次性丢给 AI,让它一口气把功能全写完
options_en: Lock in the full phase plan up front and ignore the test cases as they arrive.
Build incrementally, one feature at a time, to pass the test case you just got.
Skip decomposition since the test cases will define everything for you.
Dump every test case you have into the AI at once and let it build all the features in one go.
why: Rippling 式面试的用例是沿途逐个给的,拆解要跟着用例节奏走:每来一个用例就实现一个功能过掉它;代价是你不能像 Meta 那样提前锁死全部阶段,得随新用例调整顺序。
why_en: At Rippling the interviewer feeds test cases one at a time, so you pace your decomposition to them, building one feature per incoming case rather than pre-locking every phase.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 Meta 式题面已经写死 bug→feature→optimize 三阶段,就该提前规划完整阶段顺序,而不是等用例。
tradeoff: 跟用例增量推进(随新用例调整顺序)vs 提前锁死阶段(结构清晰但不适配沿途给用例的格式)
optionExplanations: 提前锁死阶段是 Meta 式题面的做法;这轮用例是沿途给的,死守旧顺序会和新用例对不上。
面试官每给一个用例,你就实现一个功能过掉它,拆解节奏跟着用例走。
用例只说明要过什么,不替你决定实现顺序和数据结构,跳过拆分照样失控。
一次全丢给 AI,多个功能被压进一次输出,还没来得及用用例逐个验证就难追踪。
optionExplanations_en: Locking phases up front is the Meta-style move; here the cases arrive along the way, so a fixed order drifts out of sync with each new case.
Each case the interviewer gives, you implement one feature to pass it, pacing the decomposition to the cases.
A test case only says what to pass, not the order or data structures, so skipping decomposition still loses control.
Dumping them all at once buries several features in one output you can't verify case by case.

scenario: 面试中你让 AI 自己发明了一套和现有类平行的架构,没引用代码库里已有的类;面试官指着其中一个类问 what does this class do。
scenario_en: During the interview you let the AI invent its own architecture parallel to the existing classes instead of referencing them; the interviewer points at one class and asks what it does.
q: 这一问最容易暴露什么?
q_en: What does that question most easily expose?
options: 那个类一定藏着编译错误,只是测试还没跑到它
你讲不清这个类做什么,因为架构是 AI 发明的,没经你手
面试官只是随口一问,答不出也不影响这轮评估
答不上来也没关系,当场再让 AI 把这个类从头到尾重新解释一遍就行
options_en: That class must be hiding a compile error the tests just haven't reached yet.
You can't say what it does, because the AI invented the architecture, not you.
The interviewer is only making small talk, so failing to answer won't affect the round.
No problem, just have the AI explain this class from top to bottom again for you on the spot.
why: 引用已有的类是为了你能解释代码库每一处;放任 AI 发明平行架构的代价,是你和代码失联,一句 what does this class do 就当场戳穿。
why_en: You reference existing classes so you can explain the whole codebase; when the AI invents a parallel architecture, one 'what does this class do?' exposes that you can't.
optionExplanations: 编译错误跟你能不能解释职责是两回事;这一问戳的是理解,不是语法。
架构是 AI 自己发明的,关键决策没经你手,所以你说不清它到底做什么。
这不是闲聊,答不出正是面试官用来判断你有没有和代码脱节的信号。
让 AI 再解释一遍只证明你要靠它读自己的代码,反而坐实了脱节。
optionExplanations_en: A compile error is a different matter from whether you can explain the class; the question probes understanding, not syntax.
The AI invented the architecture and the key calls never passed through you, so you can't say what it does.
This isn't small talk; failing to answer is exactly the signal the interviewer uses to catch you drifting from the code.
Having the AI re-explain it only shows you rely on it to read your own code, which confirms the disconnect.

scenario: 从零构建的题,时间紧,你跳过给实体建模,直接冲去写最有意思的核心逻辑;进入后一阶段时需求变得更具体。
scenario_en: In a greenfield build under time pressure, you skip modeling the entities and jump straight to the interesting core logic; then a later phase makes the requirements more specific.
q: 这种跳步最典型的后果是什么?
q_en: What is the most typical consequence of skipping ahead like this?
options: 代码缠在没定型的模型上,后期需求一具体就难重构,被迫返工
代码早期跑得动,所以后面阶段也不会因为缺模型而翻车返工
先写有意思的逻辑其实更快,数据模型可以边写边定型,几乎不用回头
缺的数据模型 AI 会在后面阶段察觉并自动帮你补齐好
options_en: The code tangles onto an unsettled model, so when requirements get specific later, it won't refactor and you rewrite.
The code runs early on, so later phases won't break or force rework from the missing model either.
Writing the interesting logic first is actually faster, and the data model can settle as you go with almost no backtracking.
The AI will notice the missing data model in a later phase and fill it in for you automatically.
why: 先建模会逼你在写逻辑前理清对象和关系;跳过它省下眼前几分钟,代价是后一阶段需求变具体时,代码建在漂移的地基上,只能推倒返工。
why_en: Modeling first makes you understand the objects before the logic; skipping it saves minutes now but forces a rewrite when a later phase pins requirements onto a shifting foundation.
optionExplanations: 没有稳定的数据模型,AI 生成的逻辑缠在一起,需求一具体就得推倒重来。
早期能跑不代表撑得住;后一阶段需求变细,缺模型的代码正是最先崩的地方。
先写逻辑看似快,实际是把理解对象的成本推到后面,连本带利地还。
AI 不会替你决定核心模型,它只会在你没定的地基上继续叠代码。
optionExplanations_en: Without a stable data model, the AI's logic tangles together and has to be torn down once requirements get specific.
Running early doesn't mean holding up; when a later phase tightens requirements, the model-less code is the first to break.
Writing logic first looks fast but only defers the cost of understanding the objects, which you pay back with interest.
The AI won't decide the core model for you; it just keeps stacking code on the foundation you never set.

scenario: AI 编码面试里，你要在很短时间内确认 AI 生成的代码是否正确，而不是逐行通读。
q: AI 编码面试中，最强的验证工具是哪两类？
options: 测试和类型系统
更长的提示和更多注释
截图和颜色主题
只读 AI 生成的解释文字
options_en: Tests and the type system.
Longer prompts and more comments.
Screenshots and color themes.
Just reading the AI's own explanation.
why: 测试把正确性具体化，类型系统能在运行前抓住一大类错误，二者都让验证不只靠人工通读。
why_en: Tests and the type system are your strongest verification tools because they make correctness concrete and catch bugs before you read a line.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Verify[Verification] --> Tests[Tests]
  Verify --> Types[Type system]
  Tests --> Behavior[Behavior confidence]
  Types --> Contract[Interface confidence]

termDefinitions.meaning: 编程语言在编译或运行前检查变量类型是否匹配的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A type system is a language mechanism that checks whether variable types match before or during execution.

q_en: In an AI coding interview, which two tools are your strongest verification tools?
scenario_en: In an AI coding interview, you need to confirm AI-generated code is correct quickly, not by reading every line.
optionExplanations: 测试给出可运行的通过/失败信号，类型系统在编译期就能拦下一类错误，两者合起来是最快的客观验证手段。
提示词写得再长也只是生成前的准备，跑不出来就验证不了生成后的代码对不对。
截图只能看界面像不像，看不出后端逻辑或边界条件对不对。
AI 自己的文字解释可能和它实际写出的代码对不上，不能当验证证据。
optionExplanations_en: Tests give a runnable pass/fail signal, and compile-time type checks catch a whole class of bugs — together the fastest objective check you have.
Longer prompts only shape what gets generated; they produce nothing you can run to confirm the result is correct.
Screenshots only show whether the UI looks right, not whether the backend logic or edge cases are correct.
The AI's own explanation can diverge from the code it actually wrote, so it isn't independent evidence.

scenario: 你打算先写好一批测试，再让 AI 按测试去实现功能。
q: 测试为什么会让 AI 生成代码更可靠？（多选）
options: 给模型明确的目标输出
约束模型对需求的解释空间
让你能用运行结果快速验证
保证测试本身永远正确
options_en: It gives the model a concrete target output.
It narrows the model's room to misinterpret the requirement.
It lets you verify behavior quickly by running the suite.
It guarantees the tests themselves are always correct.
why: 测试能约束实现并加速验证，但 AI 生成的测试也可能有错，需要你审查。
why_en: Tests give the AI concrete targets and let you verify quickly, but AI-written tests can still be wrong, so you have to review them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证某个输入是否产生期望输出的一次具体检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A test case is a concrete check that a given input produces the expected output.

q_en: Why do tests make AI-generated code more reliable? (multi-select)
scenario_en: You plan to write a batch of tests first, then have the AI implement the feature against them.
optionExplanations: 先写测试等于先给出具体的输入输出目标，AI 不用再猜你想要什么。
测试把「正确」的定义收窄，AI 更难悄悄按自己的理解跑偏。
跑一遍测试就能拿到通过/失败信号，不用逐行读代码去判断对不对。
别以为测试代码天然不会错——AI 写的用例期望值也可能算错，照单全收会掩盖真正的 bug。
optionExplanations_en: Writing tests first hands the AI a concrete input/output target instead of leaving it to guess.
Tests narrow the definition of correct, so the AI has less room to quietly drift from what you meant.
Running the suite gives a pass/fail signal in seconds, so you don't have to read every line to judge correctness.
Don't assume the tests are automatically correct — a miscalculated expected value in an AI-generated case will hide a real bug.

scenario: 开放式面试中你从空项目开始，要实现一个明确接口。
q: 开始写实现前，你应该先做哪件事？
options: 先让 AI 直接写出完整实现，最后再随便跑一遍看结果
先针对预期接口写会失败的测试，再让实现去满足测试
先跳过测试直接写实现，想着时间不够再回头补
先只写注释和函数签名，不写可运行的代码骨架
options_en: Have the AI write the full implementation right away, then just run it once at the end to see what happens.
Write tests against the intended interface first, then make the implementation satisfy them.
Skip tests and dive into the implementation, planning to circle back and add tests later once there's time.
Only write comments and function signatures, without a runnable code skeleton.
whenOtherWins: 如果是已有代码里的小 bug，可能先运行现有失败测试定位问题，再补边界测试。
tradeoff: 测试先行的目标明确性 vs 立刻动手写代码的表面速度
why: TDD 让失败测试成为 AI 的目标，也让你和面试官先对齐什么叫正确。
why_en: Test-first development gives the AI a concrete failing target and aligns you with the interviewer on what correct means before any code exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写测试、再写实现，让实现以通过测试为目标的开发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TDD means writing a failing test before the implementation, so the code is written to make that test pass.

q_en: Before you start writing the implementation, what should you do first?
scenario_en: In an open-ended interview, you start from an empty project and need to implement a clearly defined interface.
optionExplanations: 只适合你对需求已经很有把握、愿意事后一次性核对的情况；这里接口尚未验证，随便跑一遍也测不出关键分支，等于赌一把。
先写失败测试等于把接口契约钉死，AI 照着测试实现，你也能立刻用运行结果验证对不对。
'回头补'是错觉——跳过测试等于没有验证信号，bug 会一直藏到很晚才暴露，返工代价比先写测试更高。
注释和函数签名描述不了可运行的验证信号，写完也证明不了实现是否正确，只能当补充说明。
optionExplanations_en: Only pays off when you already trust the requirements and are fine checking everything in one pass at the end; starting from an unverified interface, running it once at the end won't surface the key branches — it's a gamble.
Writing the failing test first locks the interface contract, so the AI builds toward it and you get an instant pass/fail signal.
Circling back later is the illusion — skipping tests means no verification signal at all, so bugs stay hidden until much later and the rework costs more than writing tests up front would have.
Comments and signatures can't be executed, so they never prove the implementation is actually correct — at best they're a supplementary note, not a substitute for a runnable skeleton.

q: 把开放式 TDD + AI 的循环排好：
steps: 让 AI 实现到这些测试通过
和面试官确认输入输出与核心用例
审阅并运行测试结果
先写会失败的测试
tradeoff: 测试先行的对齐清晰度 vs 直接开写代码的表面速度
why: 先定义正确性，再写失败测试，然后让 AI 实现，最后运行和审阅结果。
why_en: The TDD loop is agree on behavior, write failing tests, ask the AI to implement, then run and review the results.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Cases[Define cases] --> Tests[Write tests]
  Tests --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Run[Run tests]
  Run --> Fix[Fix failures]
  Fix --> Run

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写测试、再写实现，让实现以通过测试为目标的开发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TDD means writing a failing test before the implementation, so the code is written to make that test pass.

q_en: Put the open-ended TDD-plus-AI loop in the right order:

scenario: 你还没开始写代码，先把想测试的输入输出讲给面试官听。
q: 实现前先和面试官确认测试用例，最直接的收益是什么？
options: 能让你跳过手动补充边界测试这一步
能保证 AI 之后写代码不会再犯错
提前暴露需求误解，建立共享的完成标准
能自动帮你想清楚所有边界条件
options_en: It lets you skip adding your own edge-case tests later.
It guarantees the AI won't make mistakes afterward.
It surfaces requirement misunderstandings early and creates a shared definition of done.
It automatically thinks through every edge case for you.
why: 对齐输入和期望输出能在编码前发现歧义，也让后续「测试通过」更有共识。
why_en: Agreeing on test cases before coding surfaces requirement misunderstandings early and gives everyone the same definition of done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入处于极端或特殊情况时的测试场景，如空值、最大值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge case is a test scenario at an extreme or unusual input, such as an empty or maximum value.

q_en: What's the most direct benefit of confirming test cases with the interviewer before implementing?
scenario_en: You haven't started coding yet; you walk the interviewer through the inputs and outputs you plan to test.
optionExplanations: 把提前对齐当成边界测试的替代品是夸大了——对齐只覆盖聊过的用例，边界条件还得你自己另外补。
把对齐当成 AI 以后不会犯错的保证书也是夸大——AI 照样可能在对齐之外的地方写错。
编码前先讲清楚输入输出预期，能在下笔前就揪出理解偏差，双方对「测试通过」有同一个标准。
对齐不会自动帮你想全边界，它依赖你主动提出用例，没提到的角落照样会被漏掉。
optionExplanations_en: Treating pre-alignment as a substitute for edge-case tests overstates it — alignment only covers the cases you actually discussed.
Treating alignment as a guarantee the AI won't slip up afterward overstates it too — mistakes can still happen outside what you aligned on.
Walking through inputs and outputs before coding catches misunderstandings early and gives both sides the same bar for passing.
Alignment doesn't auto-discover edge cases for you — it only covers what you actively bring up, so unmentioned corners still slip through.

scenario: 你已经写好测试，期望 AI 实现函数而不是自由解释题目。
q: 哪条提示最能利用测试约束 AI？
options: 凭直觉写一个你觉得好的解法
顺手把项目重构得看起来更整齐
忽略已有测试，直接从头写代码
让这些测试通过，且不改动现有接口
options_en: Write whatever solution feels good to you.
Casually refactor the project to look tidier.
Ignore the existing tests and start from scratch.
Make these tests pass without changing the existing interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果测试本身还没确认，先和面试官或自己审查测试，不要让错误测试驱动实现。
tradeoff: 测试约束下的目标明确性 vs 开放式探索的解法自由度
codeSample:
Implement `scheduleTasks(tasks, dependencies)` so the tests below pass.
Keep the public function signature unchanged.
Do not special-case only the visible examples.
why: 把测试作为目标交给 AI，会减少它对需求的自由发挥，也让验证路径清晰。
why_en: Prompting the AI to satisfy specific tests while keeping the interface fixed constrains its interpretation and makes verification straightforward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 函数对外暴露的名称、参数和返回值约定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface is the externally visible name, parameters, and return-value contract of a function.

q_en: Which prompt best uses the tests to constrain the AI?
scenario_en: You've already written tests and want the AI to implement the function instead of freely interpreting the problem.
optionExplanations: 只有完全探索性、还没有测试约束的早期阶段才适合凭直觉发挥；这里测试已经写好，交给直觉等于浪费约束。
重构适合已有测试保护、明确要整理代码的阶段；这里目标是实现功能，顺手重构容易碰坏还没验证的接口。
跳过已写好的测试从头写，等于把现成的验证信号扔掉，风险还是要从零验证。
把失败测试和「接口不能变」一起交给 AI 当目标，它照着具体用例写，你也能直接用测试结果核对。
optionExplanations_en: Freeform intuition fits an early exploratory stage with no tests yet; here the tests already exist, so ignoring them wastes that constraint.
Refactoring fits a stage where tests already protect you and tidying is the explicit goal; here it risks touching an interface nothing verifies yet.
Starting over and ignoring the tests you already wrote throws away a ready-made verification signal — you'd have to prove correctness from scratch again.
Handing the AI the failing tests plus a fixed-interface constraint gives it a concrete target, and you can check the result against the same tests.

scenario: 你已经用测试驱动开发（TDD）写完一版实现，测试全部通过。
q: TDD 后，你的主要审查重心会从哪里转到哪里？
options: 从审查实现，转到审查测试完整性和期望值
从审查测试内容，转到完全不再审查
从运行代码验证，转到只读注释猜测
从理解业务需求，转到只看编译速度快慢
options_en: From reviewing implementation lines to reviewing test completeness and expected values.
From reviewing the tests at all to not reviewing anything, ever.
From actually running the code to only skimming comments instead.
From understanding business requirements to only watching compile speed.
tradeoff: 逐行审查实现的细致度 vs 审查测试完整性的效率

rows: 耗时长，难覆盖全部路径
测试本身可能遗漏边界

why: 测试通过只能说明实现符合测试，所以你必须确认测试确实表达了题目的正确性。
why_en: Once tests pass, your job shifts to verifying that the tests themselves correctly express the problem, since passing tests only prove code matches the tests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写测试、再写实现，让实现以通过测试为目标的开发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TDD means writing a failing test before the implementation, so the code is written to make that test pass.

q_en: After TDD, where does your main review focus shift from and to?
scenario_en: You've finished an implementation using test-driven development, and all the tests pass.
optionExplanations: 审查重心从「实现代码」换成「测试是否完整、期望值是否算对」，因为通过测试只能证明实现符合测试本身。
测试通过不等于可以完全撒手——测试本身也可能写得不完整或期望值算错，不审查会漏掉这些。
读注释代替不了跑代码，注释和运行结果是两件不同的事，不能划等号。
编译速度和代码对不对是两个维度，编译快不代表需求理解对了。
optionExplanations_en: The focus shifts from the implementation to whether the tests are complete and the expected values are right, since passing only proves the code matches the tests.
Passing tests doesn't mean you can stop reviewing entirely — the tests themselves can be incomplete or have wrong expected values.
Reading comments is not a substitute for running code; they answer different questions.
Compile speed and correctness are unrelated dimensions — a fast compile says nothing about whether requirements were understood.

scenario: 你正在给一个新写的函数补测试用例，想确认覆盖是否够全。
q: 哪些类别常出现在一套好的测试里？（多选）
options: 只测一个随机大例子
happy path
空输入或零值
边界值、重复值和非法输入
options_en: Only one large random example.
The happy path.
Empty input or zero values.
Boundary values, duplicates, and invalid input.
why: 标准路径、空/单元素、边界、重复和非法输入能覆盖大多数常见漏洞；单个随机大例子不够。
why_en: Good tests cover the happy path, empty or zero input, boundaries, duplicates, and invalid input — a single large random example does not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入和流程都符合预期、程序应该顺利跑通的标准场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the standard scenario where input and flow are as expected and the code should just work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刚好落在允许范围最边缘的输入，如最大值、最小值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A boundary value is an input that sits right at the edge of the allowed range, like a minimum or maximum.

q_en: Which categories commonly appear in a good test suite? (multi-select)
scenario_en: You're adding test cases for a newly written function and want to confirm the coverage is thorough enough.
optionExplanations: 单个随机大例子规模大不等于边界全，很难复现具体失败原因，挡不住真正的风险。
happy path 先确认最基本功能是通的，是整套测试的地基，少了它没法判断后续失败是新问题还是从没跑通过。
空输入/零值成本很低但很容易漏——很多实现在空数组或 0 上直接抛异常或死循环。
边界值、重复值、非法输入是面试追问最爱问的角落，补上它们能挡住绝大多数实现漏洞。
optionExplanations_en: One big random example doesn't guarantee edge coverage and makes failures hard to reproduce — it doesn't block much risk.
The happy path confirms the basic behavior works at all — it's the foundation the rest of the suite builds on.
Empty input or zero values are cheap to test and easy to miss — many implementations throw or loop forever on them.
Boundary values, duplicates, and invalid input are exactly what interviewers probe — covering them blocks most implementation gaps.

q: 补全常见测试类别：
text: 好测试常覆盖：{{happy path}}、空/零输入、单元素、{{边界值}}、重复值、非法输入，以及有性能要求时的{{规模}}测试。
why: 不必每题全覆盖，但用这张清单扫一遍能发现最容易漏掉的测试洞。
why_en: You don't need every category every time, but scanning this checklist reveals the test gaps you're most likely to miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入和流程都符合预期、程序应该顺利跑通的标准场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the standard scenario where input and flow are as expected and the code should just work.

q_en: Fill in the common test categories:

scenario: 你写完核心测试后，想补更多边界条件。
q: 怎样使用 AI 最合适？
options: 完全相信 AI 自动生成的测试内容
让 AI 补边界测试，但逐条核对期望值和有效性
只让 AI 编写实现代码，绝不让它碰触测试用例
直接删除已经写好的全部测试
options_en: Trust everything the AI auto-generates in its tests.
Let the AI add edge-case tests, but review each expected value and whether it's a valid check.
Only let the AI write implementation code, never let it touch the test suite.
Just delete every test that's already been written.
whenOtherWins: 如果时间只够做核心路径，至少覆盖题目最可能追问的边界，而不是生成大量低价值测试。
tradeoff: AI 生成边界用例的速度 vs 人工逐条审查期望值的可靠性
why: AI 很适合帮你想空输入、重复、溢出等边界，但测试也会继承模型盲点。
why_en: AI is good at brainstorming edge cases like empty input, duplicates, and overflow, but the tests it writes can inherit the model's own blind spots.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  AI[AI suggests tests] --> Review[You review cases]
  Review --> Edit[Edit gaps]
  Edit --> Run[Run suite]
  Run --> Trust[Earn trust]

termDefinitions.meaning: 数值或容量超出系统能表示或处理的上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overflow happens when a value or capacity exceeds the limit a system can represent or handle.

q_en: What's the best way to use AI here?
scenario_en: After writing your core tests, you want to add more edge cases.
optionExplanations: 完全相信 AI 生成的测试等于放弃把关——期望值算错，或用例根本没执行到关键逻辑，都不会被发现。
让 AI 帮你头脑风暴边界用例，但逐条核对期望值和有效性，既借了 AI 枚举边界的速度，又不继承它的盲点。
只有在你完全不信任 AI、时间又很充裕时才合理——大多数场景下放弃 AI 在边界枚举上的效率并不划算。
删掉已有测试等于把验证过的安全网直接扔掉，几乎没有场景该这么做。
optionExplanations_en: Trusting AI-generated tests completely means no one checks them — a wrong expected value or a case that never exercises the real logic slips through.
Let the AI brainstorm edge cases, then verify every expected value and whether the check is meaningful — you get its speed without inheriting its blind spots.
Only makes sense if you distrust the AI entirely and have plenty of spare time — in most cases it wastes the AI's speed at enumerating edge cases.
Deleting tests you've already validated throws away a working safety net — almost no situation calls for that.

scenario: 平台给你的题目自带了几个示例测试用例，你准备开始写代码。
q: 结构化面试自带测试时，应该如何看待它们？
options: 平台给的测试就是完整规范，不用再看边界
读一遍确认格式没问题就够，不用真的跑一次
它们通常是起点，不一定覆盖所有边界
只要平台给了测试，就不该再自己补充测试
options_en: The provided tests are the complete spec, so there's no need to look for more edge cases.
Just reading through them once to check the format is enough — no need to actually run them.
They are usually a starting point and don't necessarily cover every edge case.
Once the platform provides tests, you shouldn't add your own on top.
why: 平台测试多半覆盖 happy path 和少量基础边界，你仍应补自己看出的关键条件。
why_en: Provided tests are usually a starting point, not a complete validation suite, so you should still add your own edge cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个边界条件同时出现的特殊情况，比一般边界值更少见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A corner case is a rare situation where multiple boundary conditions occur at once, less common than a single edge case.

q_en: In a structured interview with provided tests, how should you treat them?
scenario_en: The platform's problem comes with a few sample test cases, and you're about to start coding.
optionExplanations: 把平台自带用例当成完整规范是错的——它们通常只给基础场景和零星边界，追问角落照样容易漏。
光读一遍确认格式，等于放弃了现成的运行验证信号，发现不了实现和用例之间的真实偏差。
自带测试通常只是起步覆盖，不是完整覆盖，你仍要主动补自己看出的边界和 corner case。
补充测试和自带测试完全可以共存，谁都不排斥谁——多写测试从不是坏事。
optionExplanations_en: Treating provided cases as a complete spec is wrong — they usually cover only the happy path plus a few basics, leaving follow-up corners exposed.
Reading test code only checks the format, not actual behavior — running them is what surfaces a mismatch between the implementation and the cases.
Provided tests are usually a starting point, not full coverage, so you still need to add your own edge cases and corner cases.
Your own tests and the provided ones coexist fine — adding more coverage never conflicts with what's already there.

scenario: 题目涉及网格路径，平台测试只有普通 3x3 示例。
q: 你最应该补哪个测试？
options: 完全相同的 3x3 示例
随机改变量名
只测 UI 颜色
1x1 网格或起点等于终点
options_en: The exact same 3x3 example again.
Randomly rename variables.
Only test the UI color.
A 1x1 grid, or a case where the start equals the end.
whenOtherWins: 如果已有测试覆盖 1x1，则优先补障碍物、不可达路径或边界坐标。
tradeoff: 极小规模边界的发现效率 vs 重复已覆盖用例的低回报
why: 网格题的极小规模和起终点重合是常见边界，能快速暴露路径初始化问题。
why_en: For grid problems, a 1x1 grid or a start-equals-end case quickly exposes path-initialization bugs that a normal-sized example won't.
q_en: Which test should you add first?
scenario_en: The problem involves grid paths, and the platform's tests only include a plain 3x3 example.
optionExplanations: 重复已经通过的用例不会发现新问题，任何阶段都不该只重复覆盖过的场景。
改变量名不改变程序行为，根本不构成一次真正的测试。
颜色和路径算法的正确性无关，只有题目本身涉及 UI 渲染时才有意义，这里不涉及。
网格题规模最小、起点等于终点是最容易踩初始化坑的场景，能快速暴露越界或路径判断错误。
optionExplanations_en: Rerunning a case that already passed won't surface anything new — repeating covered scenarios never helps.
Renaming variables doesn't change program behavior, so it isn't really a test at all.
Color has nothing to do with path-algorithm correctness — that check only matters when the problem itself involves UI rendering, which it doesn't here.
A minimal grid or a start-equals-end case is exactly where initialization bugs hide, and it quickly exposes out-of-bounds or path-logic errors.

scenario: 你准备把一个正确但慢的算法换成更快实现。
q: 优化前后最重要的验证动作是什么？
options: 先跑全量测试定基线，每次改动后再跑
直接开始重写，最后统一检查一次
把运行慢的测试直接删掉
只看 AI 给出的文字解释
options_en: Run the full suite first to set a baseline, then rerun it after every change.
Just start rewriting, and check everything once at the end.
Just delete the tests that run slowly.
Only read the AI's written explanation.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有测试，先补最关键的行为测试，再开始优化。
tradeoff: 频繁跑基线测试的时间成本 vs 优化引入回归却发现太晚的返工成本
why: 优化会改变内部算法，测试套件是防止正确性回退的安全网。
why_en: Because optimization changes the internal algorithm, running the test suite before and after each change is the safety net against correctness regressions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Before[Baseline tests pass] --> Optimize[Optimize]
  Optimize --> After[Run same tests]
  After --> Compare[Compare behavior]
  Compare --> Safe[Safe optimization]

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改动之前记录下来的、用来对比的正确行为状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A baseline is the known-correct behavior recorded before a change, used later for comparison.

q_en: What's the most important verification step before and after optimizing?
scenario_en: You're about to replace a correct but slow algorithm with a faster implementation.
optionExplanations: 先跑全量测试立好基线，每次改动后再跑，任何一次改动引入的回归都能被立刻抓住，定位成本最低。
只适合改动极小、你对风险有绝对把握的情况；把优化拆成多步却只在最后查一次，坏了很难判断是哪步造成的。
把「跑得慢」误当成「测试有问题」删掉，删掉的往往正是最容易被优化破坏的行为验证。
AI 的文字描述不能替代跑测试得到的客观结果，任何验证场景都不该只依赖它。
optionExplanations_en: Running the full suite first sets a baseline, then rerunning after every change catches any regression immediately, keeping the cost of finding it low.
Only fits when the change is tiny and you're fully confident about the risk; checking once at the end makes it hard to tell which step broke things.
Deleting a test just because it runs slowly mistakes 'slow' for 'broken,' and it's usually the exact test that would catch what optimization breaks.
The AI's written explanation can't substitute for the objective result of actually running the tests.

q: 补全回归风险：
text: 优化前先跑测试，是为了确认已有行为{{通过}}；优化后再跑，是为了及时发现{{回归}}。
why: 没有基线时，你无法判断失败是新算法造成的，还是原本就坏。
why_en: Without a baseline, you can't tell whether a failure comes from the new algorithm or was already broken before.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

q_en: Fill in the regression risk:

scenario: 你在用类型语言写代码，编译器会在运行前做类型检查。
q: 为什么类型系统也可以看作一种测试套件？
options: 它能证明这段实现在时间和空间上都是最优解
它能在运行前抓住类型不匹配和空值错误
它能完全替代人工编写的业务逻辑单元测试
它只是编辑器里的格式化建议，和运行时报错无关
options_en: It proves this implementation is optimal in both time and space complexity.
It catches type mismatches and null-related errors before the code ever runs.
It can completely replace hand-written business-logic unit tests.
It's just a formatting suggestion your editor shows you, unrelated to runtime errors.
why: 编译器和类型检查器能把一类错误变成明确、可操作的反馈，尤其适合交给 AI 精准修复。
why_en: A type system catches interface, nullability, and mismatch errors before runtime, turning them into concrete feedback you can hand straight to the AI.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类型系统对变量是否可能为空（null）做的静态检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nullability checking is a static check for whether a variable might be null.

q_en: Why can a type system also be treated as a kind of test suite?
scenario_en: You're coding in a typed language, and the compiler runs type checks before the code executes.
optionExplanations: 类型检查和算法最优性是两回事——类型对了不代表时间或空间复杂度是最优的。
编译器在运行前就能抓住类型不匹配和空值相关错误，把它们转成能直接照做的具体反馈。
类型检查覆盖不了业务逻辑是否正确，类型对了只说明接口契约对了，人工写的功能测试还是要跑。
把类型系统当成编辑器里的格式化建议是低估——它捕获的是真实的逻辑风险（类型不匹配、空值），跟运行时报错直接相关。
optionExplanations_en: Type checking and algorithmic optimality are unrelated — correct types say nothing about whether the time or space complexity is optimal.
The compiler flags type mismatches and null-handling errors before the code executes, so you get specific, fixable feedback instead of a runtime crash.
Type checking doesn't cover business-logic correctness — correct types only confirm the interface contract, so hand-written functional tests are still needed.

Type errors are a real logic risk, not just formatting — reducing the type system to an editor's formatting suggestion misses that it's directly tied to runtime failures like mismatches and null derefs.

scenario: 编译器报出 line 42 的具体类型错误。
q: 给 AI 的最好提示是哪类？
options: something is wrong
把整个模块推倒重写，不管错误具体出在哪一行
修复第 42 行这个类型错误，保持接口语义不变
直接把类型检查器关掉，让报错先消失再说
options_en: "Something is wrong."
Tear down and rewrite the whole module, regardless of exactly which line the error is on.
Fix the type error on line 42, and keep the interface semantics unchanged.
Just turn off the type checker so the error disappears for now.
whenOtherWins: 如果类型错误反映设计不匹配，应先说明设计问题，再决定是否调整接口。
tradeoff: 具体错误位置带来的定点修复效率 vs 模糊描述带来的自由发挥风险
why: 具体错误位置和约束能让 AI 定点修复，比泛泛说「有问题」更可靠。
why_en: A specific type error with a line number and a constraint produces a much more reliable AI fix than a vague complaint like "something is wrong."

termDefinitions.meaning: 函数或类型对外承诺的行为约定，不只是名字和参数类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interface semantics are the behavioral contract a function or type promises externally, not just its name and parameter types.

q_en: Which kind of prompt works best for the AI here?
scenario_en: The compiler reports a specific type error on line 42.
optionExplanations: 只给一句模糊抱怨，AI 只能靠猜，几乎任何调试场景都不该这么模糊。
用最大范围的改动去应对一个局部错误，只有错误其实反映整体设计问题时才可能合理，这里不是。
把具体错误位置和「接口语义不能变」这条约束一起交给 AI，它能定点修复，不会顺手改坏其他调用方。
关掉类型检查器等于放弃这类问题的运行前验证能力，错误消失了但类型不安全问题还在。
optionExplanations_en: A vague complaint like this gives the AI nothing to aim at — it can only guess, which almost never fits a debugging scenario.
Rewriting everything to fix one local error only makes sense if the error actually reflects a design mismatch, which isn't the case here.
Handing the AI the exact error location plus the don't-change-interface-semantics constraint lets it fix the one spot without breaking other callers.
Turning off the checker removes its before-runtime safety net — the error disappears but the underlying type-unsafe code is still there.

scenario: AI 遇到类型报错时，有时会选择让报错消失，而不是修正根因。
q: AI 为了消除类型错误可能会做哪些危险捷径？（多选）
options: 在 TypeScript 里加 any
修正真实数据模型
加不必要的强制转换
忽略 nullability
options_en: Add `any` in TypeScript.
Fix the actual data model.
Add unnecessary type casts.
Ignore nullability.
why: 这些捷径让类型错误消失但没有修正根因，面试官看到会追问正确性。
why_en: Shortcuts like any, unnecessary casts, and ignored nullability make type errors disappear without fixing the underlying issue, and interviewers will ask about them.

termDefinitions.meaning: TypeScript 里关闭类型检查的万能类型，用它等于放弃该值的类型安全。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In TypeScript, any is an escape-hatch type that turns off type checking for that value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 告诉编译器把一个值当成另一种类型处理，但不做真正的运行时验证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A type cast tells the compiler to treat a value as another type without actually verifying it at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类型系统对某个值是否可能是 null 的显式标注和检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nullability is the type system's explicit marking and checking of whether a value can be null.

q_en: Which risky shortcuts might AI take to silence type errors? (multi-select)
scenario_en: When AI hits a type error, it sometimes makes the error disappear instead of fixing the root cause.
optionExplanations: 给报错的值加 any 等于让编译器不再检查它，报错消失但类型不安全的风险原样保留，之后用到这个值的地方都失去保护。
真正调整接口或数据结构，让类型契约本身变准确，是修根因的正确做法，不属于捷径。
用强制转换让编译器闭嘴，不代表值真的匹配那个类型，转换错了会在运行时才抛异常。
假装值不可能为 null 跳过判空，线上遇到真实 null 时会直接崩溃，而不是在编译期被拦下。
optionExplanations_en: Slapping any on the offending value tells the compiler to stop checking it — the error disappears but the type-unsafe risk stays, and every later use of that value loses protection.
Actually adjusting the interface or data model to make the type contract accurate is the real fix, not a shortcut.
A forced cast just silences the compiler — it doesn't prove the value really matches that type, and a wrong cast throws at runtime instead.
Pretending a value can never be null skips the check, so a real null in production crashes the app instead of being caught at compile time.

scenario: 你可能用 Go、Java 或 Python 写这道题，想知道各语言怎么提前发现类型错误。
q: 哪组语言机制都能在运行前帮你抓住类型问题？
options: 只要用 JavaScript 这一种语言就够了
靠 CSS 的 selectors 选择器语法
靠 Markdown 里的 tables 语法
Go、Java、Python 的静态类型检查机制
options_en: Plain JavaScript alone, as the only language, is enough.
Relying on CSS selector syntax.
Relying on Markdown table syntax.
The static type-checking mechanisms in Go, Java, and Python.
why: 不同语言工具不同，但共同点都是在运行前暴露接口或类型假设错误。
why_en: Go interfaces, Java generics, and Python type annotations checked with mypy all share the same goal: surfacing interface or type assumptions before you ever run the code.

termDefinitions.meaning: Go 语言里定义方法集合的类型约定，编译器据此检查实现是否满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Go interfaces define a set of methods a type must implement, checked by the compiler.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 里用类型参数写出可复用、类型安全代码的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Java generics let you write reusable, type-safe code using type parameters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给 Python 的类型注解做静态检查的工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mypy is a static type checker for Python's type annotations.

q_en: Which set of language mechanisms all catch type problems before runtime?
scenario_en: You might solve this problem in Go, Java, or Python, and want to know how each language catches type errors early.
optionExplanations: 原生 JavaScript 没有静态类型检查，类型错误只能等运行时才暴露，不算「运行前」的工具。
CSS 选择器管的是样式，跟变量类型或接口契约完全无关。
Markdown 只是文档格式语法，不参与代码的类型检查。
Go 的 interface、Java 的 generics、Python 配 mypy 的注解，各自都能在运行代码前暴露类型或接口假设错误。
optionExplanations_en: Plain JavaScript has no static type checking — type errors only surface at runtime, so it isn't a before-runtime tool.
CSS selectors control styling and have nothing to do with variable types or interface contracts.
Markdown is just document formatting syntax — it plays no role in type checking code.
Go's interfaces, Java's generics, and Python's annotations checked with mypy each surface type or interface mistakes before the code ever runs.

q: 把每个阶段后的验证流程排好：
steps: 如果失败，先形成假设
完成一个有意义里程碑
运行测试、编译或类型检查
基于最近改动定位并修复
why: 阶段后立即验证能把失败范围限制在最近变更，并让调试有明确假设。
why_en: Verifying right after each milestone confines failures to the most recent change and supports hypothesis-driven debugging.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Change[One change] --> Build[Build or typecheck]
  Build --> Tests[Run focused tests]
  Tests --> Decide{Pass?}
  Decide -->|yes| Continue[Continue]
  Decide -->|no| Debug[Debug latest]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个阶段性完成、值得停下来验证的开发节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A milestone is a meaningful stopping point in development worth verifying before moving on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先提出一个具体的失败原因猜测，再去验证它，而不是盲目试错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hypothesis-driven debugging means forming a specific guess about the cause of failure before investigating, rather than trying things at random.

q_en: Put the post-milestone verification flow in the right order:

scenario: 你打算写完全部功能，最后统一跑一次测试。
q: 把所有测试都留到最后运行，最常见的代价是什么？
options: 最后堆积出现级联失败，已经没有足够时间定位
以为推迟测试反而会让结果更准确
以为 AI 会自动帮你补齐所有剩余缺陷
以为编译速度反而会因此变得更快
options_en: Cascading failures pile up at the very end, with no time left to isolate them.
Assuming that delaying tests makes the results more accurate.
Assuming the AI will automatically finish patching all remaining defects.
Assuming compilation somehow becomes faster because of it.
why: 越晚运行，越难知道是哪一步引入错误，修复成本也越高。
why_en: The later you run tests, the harder it is to tell which step introduced the bug, so the fix cost keeps climbing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个早期错误没被及时发现，导致后续多个阶段一起出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascading failure is when an early undetected bug causes multiple later stages to break together.

q_en: What's the most common cost of leaving all tests to run at the very end?
scenario_en: You plan to write all the features first, then run the tests once at the end.
optionExplanations: 多个阶段的错误堆到最后一起爆发，分不清是哪一步改动引入的，修复窗口所剩无几。
测试准不准取决于用例设计本身，跟什么时候运行完全没关系。
跑测试只是给出通过/失败信号，修复 bug 仍然要人来做，AI 不会因为测试跑了就自动补齐。
运行测试的时机和编译速度是两件独立的事，互不影响。
optionExplanations_en: Errors from multiple stages pile up and surface all at once at the end, so you can't tell which change introduced which bug, with little time left to fix them.
How accurate tests are depends on how the cases were designed, not on when you happen to run them.
Running tests only produces a pass/fail signal — fixing the bug is still on you, the AI doesn't auto-patch things just because the suite ran.
When you run tests and how fast the code compiles are unrelated to each other.

scenario: 一个测试失败，你怀疑循环没有处理空数组。
q: 向 AI 求助前，最好的表达是什么？
options: 这段代码就是跑不通，你直接帮我改到能跑
我怀疑空数组没处理，请检查这个假设
这个测试老是失败，干脆先把它删掉再说
换一个算法直接重写，不用解释具体原因
options_en: "This code just doesn't work, please fix it so it runs."
"I suspect the empty-array case isn't handled — please check this hypothesis."
"This test keeps failing, let's just delete it."
Switch straight to a different algorithm and rewrite it, no need to explain why.
whenOtherWins: 如果错误消息已经明确指出语法或类型位置，可以直接给具体错误和约束。
tradeoff: 带假设提问的诊断精度 vs 直接报现象的省事

rows: 怀疑空数组路径未处理，请验证
报错加具体假设一起给
先诊断根因再决定要不要换

why: 带假设的提示展示你在诊断问题，也能让 AI 围绕具体根因工作。
why_en: A hypothesis-driven prompt shows your reasoning and points the AI at a concrete suspected root cause instead of a vague complaint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先提出一个具体的失败原因猜测，再去验证它，而不是盲目试错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hypothesis-driven debugging means forming a specific guess about the cause of failure before investigating, rather than trying things at random.

q_en: What's the best way to phrase your ask before turning to the AI?
scenario_en: A test fails, and you suspect the loop doesn't handle an empty array.
optionExplanations: 只描述现象「坏了」不给诊断方向，AI 只能从零开始猜，几乎任何调试场景都不该这么模糊。
带着「怀疑空数组没处理」这个具体猜测去提问，AI 能围绕它验证或推翻，修复方向更准。
把不方便的失败信号直接删掉，只有测试本身被证明是错的时候才该删，这里问题根因还在。
跳过诊断直接换算法，换了也不一定能解决具体的空数组漏洞，只有确定是算法级问题时才合理。
optionExplanations_en: Describing only the symptom — it's broken — gives the AI no direction to guess from; almost no debugging scenario should stay this vague.
Naming the concrete suspicion — the empty-array case isn't handled — lets the AI verify or disprove it directly, aiming the fix at the real cause.
Deleting an inconvenient failing test only makes sense once the test itself is proven wrong; here the root cause is still sitting there.
Skipping diagnosis and switching algorithms doesn't necessarily fix a specific empty-array bug — that only makes sense once you know it's algorithm-level.

scenario: 你已经形成了失败假设，但想更快找到根因。
q: 形成假设后，最高效的下一步是什么？
options: 完全等 AI 回答完毕，才愿意自己动手
只靠自己一个人查，完全不允许 AI 参与
一边自己调查，一边把假设交给 AI 并行检查
直接跳过这条已经失败的测试不管
options_en: Wait entirely for the AI to finish answering before doing anything yourself.
Only investigate by yourself and don't allow the AI to participate at all.
Investigate yourself while also handing your hypothesis to the AI to check in parallel.
Just skip over this already-failing test and move on.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题很小且你能立刻定位，直接修复会比开第二条线更快。
tradeoff: 并行调查的定位速度 vs 单线调查的思路专注度
why: 你先形成判断，再让 AI 并行验证，不是外包思考，而是跑两条调查线。
why_en: Once you already have a hypothesis, investigating yourself while the AI checks the same theory in parallel usually finds the root cause faster than doing it serially.
q_en: Once you have a hypothesis, what's the most efficient next step?
scenario_en: You already have a hypothesis about the failure but want to find the root cause faster.
optionExplanations: 把调查完全串行化，人工排查要等 AI 先出结果，只有完全没头绪、必须先看 AI 反馈时才合理。
把 AI 排除在调试之外，放弃了它在快速枚举可能原因上的效率优势，只有明确不信任 AI 输出时才成立。
人工排查和 AI 验证同时跑起来，谁先找到根因就用谁的，两条线互不阻塞，通常比单线更快。
对失败测试视而不见，问题不会自己消失，只是被推迟到之后代价更高的时候暴露。
optionExplanations_en: Making the investigation fully serial — waiting for the AI before doing anything — only makes sense when you have zero leads and need its input first.
Cutting the AI out entirely gives up its speed at enumerating possible causes; that only holds when you distrust its output outright.
Running your own investigation and the AI's check on the same hypothesis in parallel means neither line blocks the other, usually finding root cause faster.
Ignoring a failing test doesn't make the problem disappear — it just resurfaces later, more expensive to fix.

scenario: 面试只剩不到三分之一时间，你在犹豫要不要跳过测试直接交付。
q: 为什么不要因为时间紧就跳过测试？
options: 以为写测试这件事本身会自动帮你生成实现代码
以为面试官只看最终代码能跑，压根不关心速度
以为测试只适合课后慢慢练习，面试现场用不上
跳过测试通常会在最后三分之一引发更昂贵的调试
options_en: Assuming that the act of writing tests will automatically generate the implementation code for you.
Assuming the interviewer only cares whether the final code runs, not about your process.
Assuming tests are only useful for slow practice after the interview, not something you'd use live.
Skipping tests usually causes more expensive debugging in the final third of the interview.
why: 测试是前期投入，能避免后面被隐藏 bug 和回归拖住。
why_en: Testing is an upfront investment that keeps hidden bugs and regressions from dragging down the final third of the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

q_en: Why shouldn't you skip tests just because time is short?
scenario_en: Less than a third of the interview remains, and you're tempted to skip tests and ship directly.
optionExplanations: 把测试的作用和实现代码生成搞反了，测试是验证工具，不会替你生成实现逻辑。
以为面试官只在乎代码最终能不能跑，低估了他们同样会看重你的过程和边界处理方式。
把测试的用途局限在课后练习，否认了它在面试现场同样能快速验证 AI 代码的价值。
跳过测试省下的时间，往往会在面试最后三分之一被更长的调试时间加倍还回去。
optionExplanations_en: This flips the roles — tests are a verification tool, they don't write the implementation logic for you.
Assuming the interviewer only cares whether the code runs at the end underestimates that they weigh your process and edge-case handling just as much.
Limiting tests to after-the-fact practice denies their value live in the interview, where they still verify AI-written code fast.
The time saved by skipping tests usually comes back doubled as debugging time in the final third of the interview.

q: 补全验证时机：
text: 不要等到最后；每完成一个{{阶段}}或有意义{{里程碑}}，就运行测试、编译或类型检查。
why: 这样每次失败都更可能来自最近改动，定位速度会快很多。
why_en: Running checks after each phase or meaningful milestone makes failures much easier to localize than waiting until the very end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个阶段性完成、值得停下来验证的开发节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A milestone is a meaningful stopping point in development worth verifying before moving on.

q_en: Fill in the verification timing:

scenario: 你在决定要不要为这道题额外写一个大规模输入的性能测试。
q: 什么时候应该加入规模或性能相关测试？（多选）
options: 题目有优化阶段
需求里提到大输入或不能超时
任何变量重命名都必须加百万数据测试
你准备替换底层算法
options_en: The problem includes an optimization phase.
The requirements mention large inputs or a time limit.
Every variable rename must come with a million-item scale test.
You're about to swap the underlying algorithm.
why: 规模测试用于确认算法级约束；无关的小改动不需要夸张性能测试。
why_en: Scale tests matter when there is a performance constraint, an optimization phase, or an algorithm swap — not for unrelated small changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用远大于日常示例的输入规模去验证程序是否仍在时限内正确运行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scale test runs the program against a much larger input than the usual example to confirm it still finishes correctly within the time limit.

q_en: When should you add scale or performance tests? (multi-select)
scenario_en: You're deciding whether to write an extra performance test with a large input for this problem.
optionExplanations: 题目设计了「先正确、再优化」阶段时，规模测试是验证优化到底有没有效的客观证据。
需求里写明大输入或时限，这个约束直接决定题目在大规模下还能不能按时跑完。
把和性能无关的小改动也套上规模测试，变量重命名不影响运行时间，加了纯属浪费时间。
换底层算法可能改变时间复杂度，复杂度的差别只有在大输入下才看得出来。
