scenario: 面试还剩 8 分钟，AI 交来 60 行图搜索代码，你只来得及做几处高杠杆检查。
scenario_en: Eight minutes left in the interview, the AI just dropped 60 lines of graph-search code, and you only have time for a few high-leverage checks.

q: BFS/DFS 在邻接表图上的典型时间复杂度是什么？
q_en: What's the typical time complexity of BFS/DFS on an adjacency-list graph?
options: O(V + E)
O(V * E * E)
O(2^V) 必然
options_en: O(V + E)
O(V * E * E)
O(2^V), always
why: V、E 是节点数与边数：邻接表上每个节点、边最多处理常数次，故 O(V+E) 线性增长。这是判断 AI 方案会不会在大图超时的依据，不是背诵点。
why_en: V and E are the vertex and edge counts; BFS and DFS touch each a constant number of times, giving linear O(V plus E) time, which flags whether a solution will time out.

termDefinitions.meaning: V 和 E 分别是图的节点数和边数，O(V+E) 表示耗时随两者之和线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: V and E are the number of vertices and edges in a graph; O(V+E) means running time grows linearly with their sum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

scenario: 图有 100 万节点、500 万条边，判题机 1 秒超时，你要先估 BFS/DFS 会不会超时。
scenario_en: The graph has a million nodes and five million edges with a one-second time limit, so you need to estimate whether BFS or DFS will time out.
optionExplanations: 错误。O(1) 意味着不看图的大小，但遍历至少要碰一遍每个可达节点。
正确。每个节点入队一次、每条邻接边扫一次，100 万点 + 500 万边约 600 万次基本操作，1 秒内跑得完。
错误。这种量级只会出现在对每条边再嵌套跑一遍全图的写法里，普通 BFS/DFS 有 visited 就不会退化到这里。
错误。O(2^V) 是枚举所有子集或所有路径的代价；只有不带 visited 的穷举才会爆到这个量级。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — O(1) would ignore graph size, but any traversal has to touch every reachable node at least once.
Correct — each node is enqueued once and each adjacency edge scanned once, so a million nodes plus five million edges is roughly six million basic steps, well inside one second.
Incorrect — that magnitude only shows up if you rerun a whole traversal per edge; a BFS or DFS with a visited set never degrades that far.
Incorrect — O(2^V) is the cost of enumerating every subset or every path, which only happens in brute-force search with no visited set.

q: 拓扑排序和普通图搜索的区别是什么？
q_en: What's the key difference between topological sort and generic graph search?
options: 拓扑排序只认边方向，无向图排不出顺序
普通图搜索遇有向边就报错，只认无向图
两者其实是同一种算法，只是换了个叫法而已
拓扑排序给DAG排顺序，图搜索问路径可达等
options_en: Topological sort only cares about edge direction, so undirected graphs can't be ordered
Generic graph search errors on directed edges, only handling undirected graphs
The two are really the same algorithm, just called by different names
Topological sort orders a DAG; graph search asks reachability, paths, and the like
why: 如果问题问“任务以什么顺序运行”，就是依赖线性化而不是泛化遍历。拓扑排序仍是图算法，但目标不同。
why_en: Topological sort answers dependency ordering in a DAG, while graph search usually answers reachability or paths.
tradeoff: 拓扑排序输出顺序 vs 图搜索回答路径/可达

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前置任务指向后续任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a DAG so every edge points from a prerequisite to a dependent task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有向无环图：边有方向且不存在环，常用于依赖排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DAG, Directed Acyclic Graph, has directed edges and no cycles, which is what topological sort operates on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

optionExplanations: 错误。拓扑排序恰恰依赖边的方向才能定义'谁在谁之前'，无向图上定义不出这种顺序——这点没错，但它不是本题问的'区别'本身。
错误。BFS/DFS 天然支持有向图，只是沿边的方向扩展，遇到有向边不会报错，也不受限于无向图。
错误。拓扑排序限定输入必须是 DAG 且答案是一个顺序，图搜索输入更一般、答案是路径或可达性，两者不是换个名字的同一个算法。
正确。拓扑排序回答'任务先后顺序'，图搜索回答'能不能到、最短路径、连通分量'，两者输入约束和答案形态都不同。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — topological sort does depend on edge direction to define 'what comes before what', which is true, but that's not the difference this question is asking about.
Incorrect — BFS/DFS naturally support directed graphs, they just expand along edge direction; directed edges don't cause errors and they aren't limited to undirected graphs.

Incorrect — topological sort requires a DAG input and its answer is an ordering, while graph search takes more general input and answers paths or reachability; they aren't the same algorithm under a different name.
Correct — topological sort answers 'what order can tasks run in', while graph search answers reachability, shortest path, or components; the input constraints and answer shapes differ.
scenario: 题面问“这些构建任务能按什么顺序跑”，你要决定是拓扑排序还是普通 BFS/DFS。
scenario_en: The problem asks what order these build tasks can run in, and you have to decide between topological sort and plain BFS/DFS.

scenario: 题目要求找出所有从起点到终点的合法路径，而不是一条最短路径。
scenario_en: The problem asks for all valid paths from start to target, not a single shortest path.
q: 这更接近哪种思路？
q_en: Which approach fits better here?
options: DFS / 回溯枚举路径
普通 BFS 到第一次到达就停止
Dijkstra 只返回最低成本
Union-Find 只判断同组
options_en: DFS / backtracking to enumerate paths
Plain BFS that stops at first arrival
Dijkstra that only returns lowest cost
Union-Find that only tells same-group
why: “所有路径”是枚举问题，DFS 的递归栈天然保存当前路径并能回溯。BFS 第一次到达只适合最短路径。
why_en: Finding all paths is an enumeration task that fits DFS and backtracking better than shortest-path search.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只需要最短或最少步数，就不要枚举所有路径，BFS/Dijkstra 更高效。
tradeoff: DFS/回溯枚举所有路径 vs BFS 只找第一条最短路径

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 尝试一个选择、递归探索、失败就撤销该选择的枚举方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking tries a choice, recurses, and undoes the choice on failure, used to enumerate all valid solutions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用最小堆每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点，求非负权图最短路径的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm always expands the node with the smallest known cost next, using a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并查集：维护元素分组、支持合并与查询同组的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Union-Find, or Disjoint Set Union, tracks groups of elements and supports merging groups and checking membership.

optionExplanations: 正确。递归调用栈就是当前路径的记录，遇到死胡同回溯换下一个分支，就能系统枚举出所有合法路径。
适合只要一条最短路径的场景；这里要求『所有路径』，BFS 第一次到达就停止，只能给出一条。
适合只要一条最低代价路径的场景；它只保留到每个节点的最优解，其余路径会被直接丢弃。
适合只需要判断两点是否同组的场景；它连单条路径都构造不出来，答不出『有哪些路径』。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the recursion stack naturally holds the path, and backtracking at a dead end tries the next branch, which systematically enumerates every valid path.
Fits when you only need one shortest path; here 'all paths' is required, and BFS stops at first arrival, giving just one.
Fits when you only need the single lowest-cost path; it keeps only the best solution to each node and discards the rest.
Fits when you only need to know whether two nodes are in the same group; it doesn't even construct a single path, so it can't answer 'what are the paths'.

q: 图搜索题中应主动提到哪些边界情况？
q_en: Which edge cases should you proactively mention in a graph-search problem?
options: 目标不可达或图不连通
自环
重复边
图其实是一棵树，没有环
options_en: The target is unreachable or the graph is disconnected
Self-loops
Duplicate edges
The graph is actually a tree with no cycles
why: 这些边界常不在样例里，但会影响 visited、返回值和距离逻辑。主动说出它们能展示完整性。
why_en: Disconnected graphs, self-loops, duplicate edges, and tree-shaped graphs are important graph edge cases.
optionExplanations: 正确。样例常常只覆盖可达情况，不可达要有明确返回值而不是崩溃。
正确。自环会让节点连向自己，visited 逻辑要能正确处理。
正确。重复边可能让邻接表膨胀，也可能重复松弛同一条边。
正确。树没有环，说明这一点能展示你考虑了输入的完整取值范围。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — sample data often only covers reachable cases; unreachability needs an explicit return value, not a crash.
Correct — a self-loop connects a node to itself, and visited logic must handle it correctly.
Correct — duplicate edges can bloat the adjacency list or relax the same edge more than once.
Correct — naming that a tree has no cycles shows you considered the full range of possible inputs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录已经访问过的节点，防止图中的环导致重复访问或死循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A visited set records nodes already processed, preventing cycles from causing repeated visits or infinite loops.

scenario: 白板上交付一版可达性 BFS，给的样例只有一个连通小图，你要主动补说边界。
scenario_en: You are delivering a reachability BFS on the whiteboard and the only sample is one small connected graph, so you should raise the edge cases yourself.

q: 最快判断 AI 写的图算法是否“名实相符”的方法是什么？
q_en: What's the fastest way to sanity-check whether AI-written graph code matches its name?
options: 只看函数名是否合理
只看注释里是否写了 shortest
对照算法名和核心数据结构是否一致
看变量是否按字母排序
options_en: Only check whether the function name sounds reasonable
Only check whether the comment says 'shortest'
Check whether the algorithm's name matches its core data structure
Check whether variables are sorted alphabetically
why: 算法名称对应的数据结构如果不对，通常在读循环前就已经错了。数据结构是最便宜的 sanity check。
why_en: The core data structure is a quick sanity check: queue for BFS, stack for DFS, and heap for Dijkstra or A*.
optionExplanations: 错误。函数名可以随便起，不代表内部实现真的对。
错误。注释可能是错的或过时的，不能替代代码逻辑检查。
正确。队列对应 BFS、栈对应 DFS、堆对应 Dijkstra/A*，对不上通常读循环前就能发现问题。
错误。变量顺序和算法正确性无关。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — a function can be named anything regardless of what it actually implements.
Incorrect — a comment can be wrong or stale and shouldn't replace checking the logic.
Correct — a queue maps to BFS, a stack to DFS, and a heap to Dijkstra or A*; a mismatch usually shows up before you even read the loop.
Incorrect — variable ordering has nothing to do with algorithm correctness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 Dijkstra 基础上加入到目标的启发式估计，按 f = g + h 排序扩展节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A* extends Dijkstra by adding a heuristic estimate of the remaining cost, expanding nodes in order of f equals g plus h.

scenario: AI 交来一个名叫 `dijkstra` 的函数，面试只剩 30 秒，你要判断它名实是否相符。
scenario_en: The AI hands you a function named `dijkstra` and you have 30 seconds left to judge whether it actually is one.

q: 把图搜索题的 AI 面试工作流按顺序排列。
q_en: Put the AI-interview workflow for a graph-search problem in the correct order.
steps: 提示 AI 生成实现，并明确输入表示和返回值。
用不可达、自环、重复边等边界测试验证。
说出节点、边、权重和目标。
根据无权/有权/启发式/只需遍历选择 BFS、Dijkstra、A* 或 DFS。
审查核心数据结构和高风险 bug。
why: 先建图再选算法，然后让 AI 写代码并按算法不变量审查。最后用边界输入验证比只跑 happy path 更有价值。
why_en: A good graph workflow models the graph, picks traversal, prompts implementation, reviews invariants, and tests edge cases.
tradeoff: 先建模选算法再验证 vs 直接让 AI 写代码就交卷

A[Clarify node and edge] --> B[Pick BFS DFS Dijkstra]

q: 填空：BFS 为什么能求无权最短路？
q_en: Fill in the blank: why BFS finds the unweighted shortest path.
text: BFS 按{{距离层级}}处理节点，所以第一次到达某个节点时，已经使用了{{最少边数}}。
text_en: BFS processes nodes in {{nondecreasing distance order}}, so the first time it reaches a node, it has used the {{fewest edges}}.
why: 队列保证深度 1 的节点都在深度 2 之前处理。这正是无权最短路的证明。
why_en: BFS reaches nodes in nondecreasing edge distance, so first discovery is the fewest-edge path.

q: 这段代码中，哪一点最能说明它按 BFS 的层序顺序扩展？
q_en: Which detail in this code best shows it expands in BFS level order?
scenario: 你让 AI 写“无权图中从 start 到 target 的最短路径”。它返回下面代码。你现在要快速判断这是不是 BFS，而不是 DFS 或 Dijkstra。
scenario_en: You asked the AI to write "shortest path from start to target in an unweighted graph." It returned the code below. You need to quickly tell whether this is BFS rather than DFS or Dijkstra.
options: 用递归后序遍历，走到底才处理节点
使用 FIFO 队列并从左侧弹出
维护入度数组，等前置任务清零
用最小堆按代价弹出当前最优节点
options_en: Use recursive postorder traversal, processing a node only after going all the way down
Use a FIFO queue and pop from the front
Maintain an indegree array and wait for prerequisites to hit zero
Use a min-heap that pops the current lowest-cost node
why: `deque.append` 把新发现的节点放到队尾，`popleft` 总是取最早入队的节点，这就是 FIFO。无权图里 FIFO 会先处理距离 start 为 1 的节点，再处理距离为 2 的节点，因此第一次到达目标就是最短步数。
why_en: The append plus popleft pattern creates FIFO order, which expands an unweighted graph layer by layer and gives shortest paths by number of edges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：最早放进去的元素最早被取出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First in, first out: the earliest inserted item is removed first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指向某节点的边的数量，用于统计它还有多少前置依赖没完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Indegree is the number of edges pointing into a node, used to count how many prerequisites it still has.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次弹出当前最小值的数据结构，Dijkstra/A* 用它按代价扩展节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap always pops the smallest value first, which Dijkstra and A* use to expand the cheapest known candidate.

optionExplanations: 错误。递归后序意味着先深入到底再回退处理，这是 DFS 的特征，这段代码里也没有递归，不是层序扩展。
正确。append 加入队尾、popleft 从队头弹出就是 FIFO，无权图下会先处理距离小的节点，天然形成层序。
错误。维护入度数组、等前置任务清零是拓扑排序（Kahn 算法）的做法，跟按层扩展没有关系，这段代码也没有入度统计。
错误。按代价弹出当前最优节点是 Dijkstra/A* 的特征，这段代码没有权重和堆结构。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — recursive postorder means going deep first and processing on the way back, a DFS trait, and this code has no recursion at all — it's not level order.
Correct — appending to the tail and popping from the head with popleft is FIFO, which naturally processes closer nodes before farther ones on an unweighted graph.
Incorrect — tracking indegree and waiting for it to hit zero is Kahn's algorithm for topological sort, unrelated to level-order expansion, and this code has no indegree counting.
Incorrect — popping the current lowest-cost node is a Dijkstra/A* trait, and this code has no weights or heap structure.

q: BFS 和 DFS 的实际内存差异常是什么？
q_en: What's the practical memory difference between BFS and DFS?
options: BFS存当前层，DFS只存一条路径
DFS 必须存所有节点的所有路径
BFS 内存占用和图的宽度无关
二者都不需要 visited
options_en: BFS keeps the whole current layer; DFS only keeps one path
DFS must store every path to every node
BFS's memory use has nothing to do with graph width
Neither needs a visited set
why: 宽图中 BFS 要保存当前整层节点，可能很大；DFS 只沿一条分支下探，内存和深度更相关。
why_en: On a wide graph BFS must hold the entire current layer, which can be large, while DFS only follows one branch down, so its memory tracks depth.
tradeoff: BFS 存整个 frontier vs DFS 只存当前路径

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录已经访问过的节点，防止图中的环导致重复访问或死循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A visited set records nodes already processed, preventing cycles from causing repeated visits or infinite loops.

optionExplanations: 正确。宽图会让 BFS 的当前层队列迅速变大，而 DFS 只顺着一条分支走，内存开销明显不同。
错误。DFS 通常只保留当前这一条路径，不会同时存下所有可能路径。
错误。BFS 的 frontier 会随图变宽而线性增长，宽图正是它最容易吃满内存的场景。
错误。没有 visited 记录，图中的环会导致重复访问甚至死循环。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a wide graph makes BFS's current-layer queue balloon quickly, while DFS only follows one branch at a time, so their memory footprints differ sharply.
Incorrect — DFS typically keeps only the current path, not every possible path at once.
Incorrect — BFS's frontier grows linearly with graph width, so a wide graph is exactly where it's most likely to exhaust memory.
Incorrect — without a visited record, cycles in the graph cause repeated visits or even an infinite loop.
scenario: 在 100 万节点、分支度很高的宽社交图上做全图遍历，进程内存上限 512MB。
scenario_en: You are traversing a wide social graph of a million high-degree nodes under a 512 MB process memory cap.

scenario: 问题问从一个公交站到另一个站最少换乘次数，每次换乘成本相同。
scenario_en: The problem asks for the fewest transfers from one bus stop to another, where every transfer costs the same.

q_en: How should you model this and pick an algorithm?
options: 用 Dijkstra，因为换乘之间权重必须不同
用正则解析站点名字就算建好图了
用 LRU 缓存最近访问过的站点
把站点或线路状态建成无权图，用 BFS 求最少层数

Just parse stop names with regex and call the graph built
Use LRU to cache the most recently visited stops
Model stops or route-states as an unweighted graph and use BFS for the fewest layers
why: “最少换乘”是最少步数问题，若每步成本相同就是无权最短路。节点具体定义要看输入，但 BFS 是核心选择。
why_en: Minimum transfers with equal step cost is an unweighted shortest-path problem for BFS.
whenOtherWins: 如果不同换乘或线路有不同代价，就应转成加权图并考虑 Dijkstra。
tradeoff: 无权换乘用 BFS vs 不同代价换乘需要 Dijkstra

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用最小堆每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点，求非负权图最短路径的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm always expands the node with the smallest known cost next, using a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种缓存淘汰策略：优先淘汰最久未被访问的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU, Least Recently Used, is a cache eviction policy that evicts the least recently accessed item first.

optionExplanations: 错误。每次换乘代价相同就意味着边权全部相等，此时无需 Dijkstra 的堆和权重开销。
错误。正则解析不出站点和线路之间谁连着谁，图根本没建出来，算法没法跑。
错误。LRU 是缓存淘汰策略，解决的是内存问题，答不出'最少换乘次数'。
正确。把站点或线路状态建成无权图，边权相等时 BFS 第一次到达终点的层数就是最少换乘次数。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — equal-cost transfers mean every edge has the same weight, so Dijkstra's heap and weight bookkeeping aren't needed.
Incorrect — regex parsing can't recover which stops or routes connect to which, so no graph actually gets built, and there's nothing for an algorithm to run on.
Incorrect — LRU is a cache-eviction policy for memory pressure, it can't answer 'what's the fewest transfers'.
Correct — modeling stops or route-states as an unweighted graph means BFS's layer count at first arrival is exactly the fewest transfers.

scenario: 网络路由题中，每条链路有不同延迟，目标是最低总延迟路径，延迟非负。
scenario_en: In a network routing problem, each link has a different non-negative latency, and the goal is the path with the lowest total latency.
q: 应向 AI 指定哪种算法和结构？
q_en: Which algorithm and structure should you tell the AI to use?
options: Dijkstra 用最小堆，按延迟扩展
普通 BFS 队列，只按跳数扩展，不看延迟
DFS 用栈递归，找到第一条路径就返回
拓扑排序用入度数组，按依赖顺序处理，不比代价
options_en: Dijkstra with a min-heap, expanding by lowest latency
A plain BFS queue, expanding purely by hop count, ignoring latency
DFS with a stack or recursion, returning on the first path found
Topological sort with an indegree array, ordering by dependency and never comparing cost
why: 不同延迟是加权最短路，BFS 只会最小化跳数。最小堆保证每次扩展当前最低代价候选。
why_en: Network latency routing with non-negative weights should use Dijkstra with a min-heap.
whenOtherWins: 如果网络拓扑是 DAG 且还有特殊顺序结构，可以考虑 DAG 最短路；一般非负加权图用 Dijkstra。
tradeoff: 非负权重延迟用 Dijkstra vs 无权跳数才用 BFS

termDefinitions.meaning: 用最小堆每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点，求非负权图最短路径的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm always expands the node with the smallest known cost next, using a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前置任务指向后续任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a DAG so every edge points from a prerequisite to a dependent task.

optionExplanations: 正确。它按已知的最低延迟优先处理候选，直接对应本题'非负延迟求最低总延迟路径'的目标。
适合每条边代价相同、只求最少跳数的场景；这里延迟不同，跳数少不代表总延迟低。
适合只要任意可达路径、不比较代价的场景；这里要求最低延迟，DFS 第一条路径质量完全不可控。
适合对有向无环图按依赖关系排出执行顺序；它不比较代价，回答不了'哪条路径延迟最低'。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it always advances toward whichever candidate currently has the lowest known latency, matching this problem's non-negative-latency, lowest-total-latency goal.
Fits when every edge costs the same and you just need fewest hops; here latencies differ, so fewer hops doesn't mean lower total latency.
Fits when any reachable path is enough and cost doesn't matter; here lowest latency is required, and DFS's first path quality is completely uncontrolled.
Fits ordering a DAG's tasks by dependency; it never compares cost, so it can't answer 'which path has the lowest latency'.

scenario: 迷宫题只要求找到任意一条可行路径并输出，不要求最短。
scenario_en: A maze problem only asks for any one feasible path to output, not the shortest one.
q: 可以优先考虑什么？
q_en: What should you reach for first?
options: A*，因为所有迷宫都必须启发式
DFS，因为任意路径即可
Dijkstra，因为边权不同
Union-Find，判断是否连通就够
options_en: A*, because every maze must use a heuristic
DFS, because any path is enough
Dijkstra, because edge weights differ
Union-Find, since knowing it's connected is enough
why: 任意路径不需要 BFS 的层序保证。DFS 实现简单，递归栈也自然保存当前路径。
why_en: If any path is enough, DFS is often simpler than BFS because shortestness is not required.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求改为最短路径或最少步数，BFS 是更正确的默认选择。
tradeoff: 任意路径用 DFS vs 最短路径才需要 BFS

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 Dijkstra 基础上加入到目标的启发式估计，按 f = g + h 排序扩展节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A* extends Dijkstra by adding a heuristic estimate of the remaining cost, expanding nodes in order of f equals g plus h.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用最小堆每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点，求非负权图最短路径的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm always expands the node with the smallest known cost next, using a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并查集：维护元素分组、支持合并与查询同组的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Union-Find, or Disjoint Set Union, tracks groups of elements and supports merging groups and checking membership.

optionExplanations: 适合有可靠距离估计、要更快找到目标的场景；这里没给到目标的距离信息，也不要求最短，用不上启发式。
正确。只要任意一条可行路径，DFS 用递归或栈探到目标就能直接返回，实现和验证都最简单。
适合边权不同、要求最低总代价路径的场景；题目没说权重不同，强行加权重是过度设计。
适合只需要判断是否连通的场景；它给不出路径长什么样，答不出题目要输出的具体路径。
optionExplanations_en: Fits when you have a reliable distance estimate and want to reach the goal faster; here there's no distance-to-target information and shortest isn't required, so a heuristic isn't useful.
Correct — since any feasible path is enough, DFS can return as soon as recursion or a stack reaches the target, which is the simplest to implement and verify.
Fits when edge weights differ and you need the lowest total-cost path; the problem never says weights differ, so forcing weights on is over-engineering.
Fits when you only need to know connectivity; it can't tell you what the path looks like, so it can't answer what the problem asks to output.

q: BFS 如果等到出队才标记 visited，为什么可能出问题？
q_en: If BFS only marks visited on dequeue, why can that go wrong?
options: 队列会变成后进先出的栈
算法反而能正确处理负权边
同节点重复入队，扰乱距离记录
节点会被误判成永远不可达
options_en: The queue turns into a last-in-first-out stack
The algorithm actually gains support for negative weights
The same node gets enqueued repeatedly, corrupting distance records
The node gets wrongly judged as permanently unreachable
why: 普通 BFS 应在发现节点时就声明它已经被安排访问。这样每个节点只会有一个最短发现层级。
why_en: Marking on dequeue lets duplicate discoveries accumulate and can corrupt BFS distance bookkeeping.
optionExplanations: 错误。数据结构本身没有变化，出队顺序依然是 FIFO，跟标记时机无关。
错误。标记时机和权重支持完全无关，BFS 本来就不处理带权图。
正确。发现节点时不立刻标记，后续别的父节点还会把它重新入队，导致同一节点多次进队。
错误。节点仍然会被正确访问到，只是可能被重复处理，不会被误判为不可达。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — the data structure itself doesn't change; dequeue order is still FIFO regardless of when you mark visited.
Incorrect — when you mark visited has nothing to do with weight support, and BFS never handles weighted graphs anyway.
Correct — if a discovered node isn't marked immediately, other parents keep re-enqueuing it, so the same node ends up in the queue multiple times.
Incorrect — the node still gets visited correctly, just potentially processed more than once; it won't be mistaken for unreachable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：最早放进去的元素最早被取出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First in, first out: the earliest inserted item is removed first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录已经访问过的节点，防止图中的环导致重复访问或死循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A visited set records nodes already processed, preventing cycles from causing repeated visits or infinite loops.

scenario: 百万节点社交图求最短跳数，AI 版 BFS 在节点出队时才执行 `visited.add(node)`。
scenario_en: On a million-node social graph you need the fewest hops, and the AI BFS only calls `visited.add(node)` when a node is dequeued.

q: 提示 AI 写图算法前，哪些建模信息应明确？
q_en: Before prompting the AI to write a graph algorithm, which modeling details should be clear?
options: 节点的身份和编码方式
边是有向还是无向
边是否有权重，权重是否非负
目标是最短、任意路径、所有路径还是连通性
options_en: The identity of nodes and how they're encoded
Whether edges are directed or undirected
Whether edges are weighted, and whether weights are non-negative
Whether the goal is shortest, any path, all paths, or connectivity
why: 这些信息决定输入解析、邻接结构、算法选择和返回值。图题的大错常从建模含糊开始。
why_en: Clear graph prompts specify node identity, edge direction, weight assumptions, and the exact query objective.
optionExplanations: 正确。节点身份不清楚，AI 很难正确解析输入。
正确。有向/无向决定了邻接表怎么建、算法怎么扩展。
正确。权重前提说错，Dijkstra 之类算法会静默给出错误答案。
正确。目标不同，BFS/DFS/Dijkstra/回溯的选择完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — without clear node identity, the AI struggles to parse the input correctly.
Correct — directed versus undirected determines how the adjacency structure is built and how the algorithm expands.
Correct — getting the weight assumption wrong lets algorithms like Dijkstra silently return a wrong answer.
Correct — a different goal means a completely different choice among BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, or backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用最小堆每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点，求非负权图最短路径的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm always expands the node with the smallest known cost next, using a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 尝试一个选择、递归探索、失败就撤销该选择的枚举方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking tries a choice, recurses, and undoes the choice on failure, used to enumerate all valid solutions.

scenario: 你要写一段提示，让 AI 一次写对“课程表能否修完”这类图题，不能靠来回追问补细节。
scenario_en: You need one prompt that gets the AI to solve a course-schedule style graph problem correctly the first time, without rounds of follow-up questions.

q: 图搜索题中，面试官最看重的能力是什么？
q_en: In graph-search problems, what do interviewers care about most?
options: 默默让 AI 自己挑算法，不追问理由
死记硬背每种算法的复杂度表格
刻意回避讨论不可达这类边界情况
识别隐藏图、解释算法选择、验证输出
options_en: Silently letting the AI pick the algorithm without asking why
Rote-memorizing the complexity table for every algorithm
Deliberately avoiding discussion of unreachable edge cases
Spotting the hidden graph, explaining the algorithm choice, and verifying the output
why: AI 能快速写 BFS/DFS/Dijkstra，但识别“最少公交换乘”这类隐藏图并选对算法是你的工作。验证则证明你没有盲信输出。
why_en: Interviewers care most that you spot the hidden graph, choose the traversal deliberately, and verify the AI's code.
optionExplanations: 错误。默默让 AI 挑、不追问理由，面试官看不到你的推理过程。
错误。复杂度表帮助判断超时，但死记硬背不是面试官最看重的能力。
错误。主动讨论不可达等边界，恰恰是展示完整性的机会，回避反而减分。
正确。AI 能快速写代码，但识别隐藏图、选对算法、验证输出是候选人的核心工作。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — silently letting the AI pick without asking why hides your reasoning from the interviewer.
Incorrect — a complexity table helps judge timeouts, but rote memorization isn't the top skill interviewers look for.
Incorrect — proactively discussing edge cases like unreachability is exactly the chance to show completeness; avoiding it costs points instead.
Correct — the AI can write code quickly, but spotting the hidden graph, choosing the right algorithm, and verifying the output is the candidate's core job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按到起点的距离一层层扩展节点的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level outward from the start node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径尽量深入，走到底再回溯的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用最小堆每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点，求非负权图最短路径的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm always expands the node with the smallest known cost next, using a min-heap.

scenario: AI 能秒出 BFS/DFS/Dijkstra 的面试里，面试官要靠什么区分候选人的真实水平。
scenario_en: In an interview where the AI can emit BFS, DFS, or Dijkstra instantly, the interviewer needs something else to tell candidates apart.

q: 填空：曼哈顿距离。
q_en: Fill in the blank: Manhattan distance.
text: 在四方向网格中，从 `(r1, c1)` 到 `(r2, c2)` 的曼哈顿距离是 {{abs(r1-r2) + abs(c1-c2)}}。
text_en: On a 4-direction grid, the Manhattan distance from `(r1, c1)` to `(r2, c2)` is {{abs(r1-r2) + abs(c1-c2)}}.
why: 四方向移动每步只能改变一个坐标，所以真实路径不可能比这个距离更短。它通常是 A* 的可采纳启发式。
why_en: Manhattan distance is admissible on a four-direction grid because no path can be shorter than the coordinate difference sum.

scenario: 你已看出这是无权最短路问题，现在要把它交给 AI 生成代码，而这题的边或状态转移有些特殊之处 AI 可能比你更懂。
scenario_en: You've recognized this is an unweighted shortest-path problem and are about to hand it to the AI to code, but the edges or state transitions have quirks the AI may understand better than you.
q: 该怎么给 AI 下这条提示？
q_en: How should you phrase the prompt to the AI?
options: 命令它“严格用 BFS 实现”，别的都不许
说“找出这些节点间的最短路径”，留出算法余地
只说“写个算法”，节点和边都不交代
让它把四种图算法都写一遍再挑
options_en: Order it to “implement strictly with BFS” and nothing else
Say “find the shortest path between these nodes” and leave the algorithm open
Just say “write an algorithm” without naming nodes or edges
Have it write all four graph algorithms and then pick one
why: 给 AI 报目标而非锁死算法，是留门 vs 过早收敛的取舍：锁死 BFS 会关掉 AI 提出更贴题算法的机会；代价是你仍要自己对面试官报出算法名以证明理解。
why_en: Tell the AI the goal rather than lock the algorithm, so it can suggest something better suited to the specifics.
whenOtherWins: 若题目已明确写死是无权最短路、没有任何特殊结构，直接点名 BFS 也无妨，省一轮来回。
tradeoff: 锁死算法 vs 报目标留余地

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按距离层级从起点向外一圈圈扩展，用队列实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands outward level by level from the start using a FIFO queue.

optionExplanations: 错误。锁死“只准 BFS”会关掉 AI 根据题目特殊结构提出更优算法的可能，把它降级成打字机。
正确。报出目标“找最短路径”既表达了需求，又留出余地让 AI 提议更贴题的选择。
错误。不交代节点和边，AI 只能猜建模，生成的代码大概率答非所问。
错误。让它全写一遍既浪费时间也没帮你做判断，选择仍落在你身上却没做。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — forcing “BFS only” shuts the door on the AI proposing a better fit for the problem's quirks.
Correct — stating the goal expresses the need while leaving room for the AI to suggest a better-suited algorithm.
Incorrect — without naming nodes and edges the AI must guess the model and will likely miss the mark.
Incorrect — writing all four wastes time and still leaves the decision to you, undone.

scenario: 同一道无权最短路题，你既要向面试官展示理解，又要驱动 AI 写代码，两个听众诉求不同。
scenario_en: On the same unweighted shortest-path problem you must both show the interviewer you understand it and drive the AI to write code — two audiences with different needs.
q: 对面试官和对 AI 分别该说什么？
q_en: What should you say to the interviewer versus to the AI?
options: 对两者都只报目标，都不提算法名
对面试官报算法名，对 AI 报目标
对面试官报目标，对 AI 锁死算法名
对两者都锁死“用 BFS”
options_en: Give both only the goal and name no algorithm
Name the algorithm to the interviewer, give the AI the goal
Give the interviewer the goal, lock the AI to the algorithm name
Lock both to “use BFS”
why: 两个听众的诉求相反：面试官要听到“无权最短路，所以 BFS”这句证明你能识别隐藏图；AI 要的是目标，锁死算法反而堵住它提更优解的路。
why_en: Tell the interviewer the algorithm to prove recognition, and tell the AI the goal so it can still suggest something better.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确让你少解说、只管产出结果，可以省掉对他报算法名这一步。
tradeoff: 对面试官报算法名 vs 对 AI 报目标

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按距离层级从起点向外一圈圈扩展，用队列实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands outward level by level from the start using a FIFO queue.

optionExplanations: 错误。对面试官也只报目标，就没展示出你能把“最少步数”识别成无权最短路这个关键信号。
正确。算法名是给面试官的理解证明，目标是给 AI 的需求，两者各取所需。
错误。对面试官只报目标少了识别信号，对 AI 锁死算法又堵住它的改进空间，正好两头都做反了。
错误。对面试官需要的是算法名而非命令句，对 AI 锁死又限制了它，两个诉求都没满足。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — giving the interviewer only the goal hides the key signal that you recognized “minimum steps” as an unweighted shortest path.
Correct — the algorithm name proves recognition to the interviewer while the goal gives the AI its requirement.
Incorrect — this inverts both: the interviewer loses the recognition signal and the AI loses room to improve.
Incorrect — the interviewer needs the algorithm name, not a command, and locking the AI limits it; neither need is met.

scenario: BFS/DFS 在邻接表上是 O(V+E)，而 Dijkstra 和 A* 的最坏复杂度是 O((V+E)·log V)，多出一个 log V 因子。
scenario_en: BFS/DFS run in O(V+E) on an adjacency list, while Dijkstra's and A* are O((V+E)·log V) in the worst case — an extra log V factor.
q: 这个多出来的 log V 来自哪里？
q_en: Where does that extra log V factor come from?
options: 来自 visited 集合的哈希查找
来自最小堆每次插入和弹出的开销
来自路径列表拼接的复制成本
来自递归调用栈的深度
options_en: From hash lookups on the visited set
From each push and pop on the min-heap
From copying when concatenating the path list
From the depth of the recursion call stack
why: BFS 用普通队列，入队出队是 O(1)；Dijkstra/A* 换成最小堆按代价取最小节点，每次堆操作约 O(log V)，乘到 V+E 次操作上就多一个 log V。这个数字用来预判大图上带堆的方案会不会超时。
why_en: BFS uses an O(1) queue, but Dijkstra and A* swap in a min-heap whose push and pop cost about log V each, adding that factor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按距离层级从起点向外一圈圈扩展，用队列实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands outward level by level from the start using a FIFO queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加权非负图上求最短路的算法，用最小堆每次取当前代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths on a non-negative weighted graph, always expanding the lowest-cost node via a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 加启发式：按 已花代价 + 到目标的估计代价 排序，空间寻路时更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A* is Dijkstra plus a heuristic: it orders the frontier by cost-so-far plus an estimate to the goal, which is faster for spatial pathfinding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最小堆(优先队列):每次弹出当前最小键值元素,插入与弹出约 O(log n)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap (priority queue) always pops the smallest-key element; push and pop each cost about O(log n).

termDefinitions.meaning: V 是图的节点数(vertices),E 是边数(edges),复杂度常用它们表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: V is the number of vertices (nodes) and E the number of edges; graph complexities are written in terms of them.

optionExplanations: 错误。visited 用哈希集合，查一次是均摊 O(1)，不引入 log 因子。
正确。最小堆按当前代价排序，每次 push/pop 约 O(log V)，是 Dijkstra/A* 比 BFS 多出的那一档。
错误。路径复制影响的是常数与空间，不是这里 log V 的来源。
错误。Dijkstra/A* 是堆驱动的迭代循环，不靠递归栈深度。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — the visited set is a hash set with amortized O(1) lookups, adding no log factor.
Correct — the min-heap orders nodes by current cost, and each push/pop costs about log V, the extra tier over BFS.
Incorrect — path copying affects constants and space, not the log V here.
Incorrect — Dijkstra and A* are heap-driven iterative loops, not recursion-depth bound.

scenario: 一道路径题你拿不准是无权最短路(BFS)还是加权最短路(Dijkstra)，而 Dijkstra 只在权重非负时才正确。
scenario_en: On a path problem you're unsure whether it's unweighted (BFS) or weighted shortest path (Dijkstra), and Dijkstra is only correct when weights are non-negative.
q: 该怎么处理这份不确定？
q_en: How should you handle the uncertainty?
options: 默默选一个算法，先写出来再说
说出假设并当场验证前提，再定算法
让 AI 自己决定用哪个算法
直接上最复杂的 A* 保底
options_en: Silently pick one algorithm and just code it
State your assumption, verify the precondition, then commit
Let the AI decide which algorithm to use
Default to the most complex option, A*, to be safe
why: 决定 Dijkstra 是否成立的前提是“权重非负”：说出“我认为是加权最短路，先确认权重非负”既当场堵住负权导致的静默错误，又向面试官展示了透明推理。代价是多花几句话，但比默默押错强。
why_en: Say your assumption out loud and verify the precondition, like confirming weights are non-negative before committing to Dijkstra.
whenOtherWins: 若前提本就一目了然(权重显然非负或题目写明无权)，就不必反复声明，直接选定即可。
tradeoff: 默默押一个算法 vs 说出假设并验证前提

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按距离层级从起点向外一圈圈扩展，用队列实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands outward level by level from the start using a FIFO queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加权非负图上求最短路的算法，用最小堆每次取当前代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths on a non-negative weighted graph, always expanding the lowest-cost node via a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 加启发式：按 已花代价 + 到目标的估计代价 排序，空间寻路时更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A* is Dijkstra plus a heuristic: it orders the frontier by cost-so-far plus an estimate to the goal, which is faster for spatial pathfinding.

optionExplanations: 错误。默默押注若前提(如权重非负)不成立，Dijkstra 会静默给出错误答案，你还看不出错在哪。
正确。声明假设+验证前提既避免负权等静默 bug，也让面试官看到你的推理链。
错误。把判断甩给 AI 恰恰放弃了面试官最想看的——你自己的算法识别与前提检查。
错误。无脑上 A* 需要可采纳启发式，抽象图上没有启发式它退化成 Dijkstra，还平添复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — a silent guess means that if the precondition (non-negative weights) fails, Dijkstra returns a wrong answer silently.
Correct — stating the assumption and verifying the precondition avoids silent bugs and shows your reasoning to the interviewer.
Incorrect — offloading the call to the AI drops exactly what the interviewer wants: your own recognition and precondition check.
Incorrect — defaulting to A* needs an admissible heuristic; on abstract graphs it degrades to Dijkstra and only adds complexity.

scenario: 一道遍历题你一时判断不清到底要不要“最短”，图既不算太深也没有权重，必须先选一个默认算法开工。
scenario_en: On a traversal problem you can't yet tell whether “shortest” is required; the graph is neither very deep nor weighted, and you must pick a default to start.
q: 拿不准时哪个是更安全的默认选择？
q_en: When in doubt, which is the safer default?
options: DFS，因为它只存当前路径、内存更省，深入也更快
BFS，因为它对最短和任意路径都不会错
A*，因为启发式总能加速
Dijkstra，因为它最通用
options_en: DFS, since it only stores the current path so it's lighter and dives faster
BFS, because it's safe for both shortest and any-path needs
A*, because a heuristic always speeds things up
Dijkstra, because it's the most general
why: 不确定时选 BFS 是低后悔的默认：若结果其实要最短路，BFS 天然给出；若只要任意路径，BFS 照样返回一条。DFS 反过来——若需要最短它却给不出，还可能先撞上一条很长的绕路。
why_en: When in doubt reach for BFS, because it still gives a shortest path if that turns out to matter, and any path otherwise.
whenOtherWins: 若已确认只要任意路径、或图极深极宽内存吃紧，DFS 只存当前路径反而更省。
tradeoff: 不确定时默认 BFS vs DFS

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按距离层级从起点向外一圈圈扩展，用队列实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands outward level by level from the start using a FIFO queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径走到底再回溯，用栈或递归实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, goes as deep as possible down one path before backtracking, using a stack or recursion.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 加启发式：按 已花代价 + 到目标的估计代价 排序，空间寻路时更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A* is Dijkstra plus a heuristic: it orders the frontier by cost-so-far plus an estimate to the goal, which is faster for spatial pathfinding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加权非负图上求最短路的算法，用最小堆每次取当前代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths on a non-negative weighted graph, always expanding the lowest-cost node via a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 启发式:对某状态到目标剩余代价的估计,A* 用它决定先扩展谁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state to the goal; A* uses it to decide which node to expand next.

optionExplanations: 错误。DFS 确实省内存、深入也可能先撞到一条路，但若这题其实要最短路，它给不出最短，反而可能是很长的绕路。
正确。BFS 按距离层扩展，需要最短时天然满足，只要任意路径时也照样返回一条，后悔最小。
错误。A* 只有在有可采纳启发式(如空间距离)时才快，抽象图上没启发式反而退化成 Dijkstra。
错误。Dijkstra 是为加权图设的，无权图上多带一个最小堆，白付 log V 的代价。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — DFS is lighter and may hit a path fast, but if shortest turns out to matter it can't give it and may return a long detour.
Correct — BFS expands by distance level, so it satisfies a shortest need naturally and still returns any path, the lowest-regret default.
Incorrect — A* is fast only with an admissible heuristic like spatial distance; on abstract graphs it degrades to Dijkstra.
Incorrect — Dijkstra is built for weighted graphs; on an unweighted one it just adds a needless log V from the heap.

scenario: 社交图里要“列出距离某用户 K 跳以内的所有节点”，边无权重，只按跳数分层。
scenario_en: In a social graph you must “list every node within K hops of a given user”; edges are unweighted and you only care about hop-count layers.
q: 哪种算法最贴这类分层枚举？
q_en: Which algorithm fits this layered enumeration?
options: DFS，一路深入更快
BFS，因为它天然按跳数逐层扩展
Dijkstra，用最小堆按跳数排序
A*，向某个目标做启发式搜索
options_en: DFS, going deep is faster
BFS, because it naturally expands hop by hop in layers
Dijkstra, sort by hop count with a min-heap
A*, heuristic search toward a target
why: K 跳枚举本质是层序遍历：BFS 一圈是一跳，处理完第 K 层就能干净地停下，无需额外的深度记账。DFS 先扎到底，要把“当前深度”额外维护好才不漏不重，反而绕。
why_en: BFS naturally processes the graph one hop-layer at a time, so you just stop after the K-th layer.
whenOtherWins: 若边带权、要按“总代价”而非跳数分层，就得换 Dijkstra；这里跳数无权，BFS 正合适。
tradeoff: 按跳数分层用 BFS vs 加权分层

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按距离层级从起点向外一圈圈扩展，用队列实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands outward level by level from the start using a FIFO queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：沿一条路径走到底再回溯，用栈或递归实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, goes as deep as possible down one path before backtracking, using a stack or recursion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加权非负图上求最短路的算法，用最小堆每次取当前代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths on a non-negative weighted graph, always expanding the lowest-cost node via a min-heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 加启发式：按 已花代价 + 到目标的估计代价 排序，空间寻路时更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A* is Dijkstra plus a heuristic: it orders the frontier by cost-so-far plus an estimate to the goal, which is faster for spatial pathfinding.

optionExplanations: 错误。DFS 先一路扎到底，要按“第几跳”分组反而得额外记账深度，容易漏或重。
正确。BFS 一层正好是一跳，扩展到第 K 层停下就得到全部 K 跳内节点，天然契合。
错误。边无权时跳数就是层数，用最小堆按跳数排序是白背 log V 的堆开销。
错误。A* 是朝单一目标做启发式搜索，这里要的是“所有”近邻节点，没有单一终点可估计。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — DFS dives deep first, so grouping by hop count needs extra depth bookkeeping and risks misses or repeats.
Correct — one BFS layer is exactly one hop, so stopping after layer K yields all nodes within K hops.
Incorrect — with unweighted edges hops equal layers, so a min-heap just adds needless log V overhead.
Incorrect — A* is heuristic search toward one target, but here you want all nearby nodes with no single endpoint to estimate.

scenario: 题目是资源分配或区间调度，优化目标明确，物品有一个很自然的排序键（比如结束时间、大小）。
scenario_en: The problem is resource allocation or interval scheduling, has a clear optimization goal, and has a natural sort key such as end time or size.
q: 面对这种天然带排序键的优化题，你该怎么对待贪心？
q_en: How should you treat greedy when an optimization problem has a natural sort key?
options: 先把贪心当候选方案，验证局部选择是否安全
不做验证，直接把任意排序结果当成最优解交上去
断定这类题目永远不能用贪心
改把它当字符串解析题来处理
options_en: Treat greedy as a candidate and verify the local choice is actually safe.
Submit any sorted-order result as if it were optimal, without verifying.
Decide this kind of problem can never use greedy.
Treat it as a string-parsing problem instead.
why: 贪心的机会很多，但正确性是有条件的；AI 很容易写出看起来合理的贪心代码。
why_en: Treat greedy as a candidate strategy that still needs justification, not an automatic answer.
whenOtherWins: 如果局部选择会锁死后续组合，或者问题其实是 NP-hard 装箱，贪心可能只是启发式，需要 DP 或回溯兜底。
tradeoff: 贪心跑得快、代码简单 vs 正确性需要先证明或反例验证
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Greedy idea] --> B{Can prove local choice?}
B -->|yes| C[Use greedy]
B -->|no| D[Look for DP or search]
C --> E[Test counterexamples]

termDefinitions.meaning: 每一步都做当前看起来最优的选择、且不回头调整的算法策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step and never reconsiders it.

optionExplanations: 候选而非结论：排序键给了贪心机会，但仍要靠交换论证或反例把它坐实。
跳过验证等于把'看起来对'当成'证明对'，反例往往几秒就能戳穿这类方案。
一刀切拒绝贪心会错过区间调度这类确实有精确贪心解的题目。
排序键指向的是资源分配/调度结构，跟字符串解析没有关系，判错了问题类型。
optionExplanations_en: Greedy earns a look here because of the sort key, but it still needs an exchange argument or counterexample before you trust it.
Skipping verification treats 'looks right' as 'proven right' -- a counterexample can break it in seconds.
Ruling out greedy outright would miss problems like interval scheduling that do have a provably exact greedy solution.
The sort key points to resource allocation or scheduling, not string parsing -- that's the wrong problem category.

scenario: 面试只剩 35 分钟，你要在动手写代码前先判断这道优化题该走贪心还是直接上 DP。
scenario_en: With only 35 minutes left, you need to decide up front whether this optimization problem is a greedy candidate or should go straight to DP.
q: 哪些信号说明一个优化题值得先考虑贪心？
q_en: Which signals make an optimization problem worth considering greedy first?
options: 优化目标带自然排序键，比如按结束时间、大小或时长排序
当前这步的选择不会严重限制下一步能选什么
题目属于资源分配、调度、区间管理或装箱
题目要求穷举列出所有合法解
options_en: The optimization goal has a natural sort key, like end time, size, or duration.
The choice at this step doesn't badly constrain what you can pick next.
The problem is resource allocation, scheduling, interval management, or bin packing.
The problem asks you to enumerate every valid solution.
why: 前三项说明局部选择可能有全局意义；穷举所有解通常是回溯问题，不是贪心信号。
why_en: Natural ordering, low future coupling, and allocation-or-scheduling domains are the classic greedy cues.
optionExplanations: 排序键让你能一次线性扫描做决策，省去回头比较所有组合的搜索空间。
选择互不牵连，挡住了'现在选的会不会锁死后面'这个最大的贪心风险。
这些领域历史上多有可证明的贪心解法，值得先起草一个基线再验证。
要求列出所有解指向的是回溯/DFS，硬套贪心会漏掉大部分合法解。
optionExplanations_en: A sort key means one linear pass instead of comparing every combination.
Choices that don't constrain the future rule out the biggest greedy risk -- an early pick locking out later options.
These domains have a track record of provable greedy solutions, worth a greedy baseline first.
Needing every valid solution points to backtracking or DFS; forcing greedy here would miss most solutions.

q: 填空：贪心正确的两个核心性质。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the two core properties that make greedy correct.
text: 贪心要正确，通常需要{{贪心选择性质}}和{{最优子结构}}同时成立。
why: 局部最优选择必须不会破坏全局最优，做完选择后剩下的问题还要像原问题的缩小版。缺一项，贪心就可能只是看起来合理。
why_en: Greedy correctness depends on the greedy-choice property and optimal substructure.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Choice[Greedy choice] --> Safe[Does not hurt optimum]
  Safe --> Sub[Remaining subproblem]
  Sub --> Repeat[Repeat same rule]
  Repeat --> Opt[Global result]

termDefinitions.meaning: 局部最优选择不会妨碍达到全局最优解的性质。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The greedy-choice property means a locally optimal choice never prevents reaching the global optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 做完一次选择后，剩下的子问题仍是同类型问题的一个更小实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimal substructure means the remaining subproblem is a smaller instance of the same type of problem.

scenario: AI 已经生成了一版贪心代码，面试官要求你先讲清为什么它对，再运行测试。
scenario_en: The AI has already produced a greedy solution, and the interviewer wants you to justify why it is correct before you run anything.
q: 提交贪心方案前，应该先问自己哪几个诊断问题？
q_en: What diagnostic questions should you ask before submitting a greedy solution?
options: 我能做出一个选择、并且永远不用撤销它吗？
做完一个选择后，剩下的问题还是同类型的小问题吗？
能不能构造一个小反例，让这个策略给出错误答案？
AI 生成代码的速度快，是不是就意味着它一定正确？
options_en: Can I make a choice and never need to undo it?
After one choice, does the remaining problem look like a smaller version of the same thing?
Can I construct a small counterexample where this strategy fails?
Does the AI generating code quickly mean the code must be correct?
why: 这些问题分别检查可提交性、最优子结构和反例。AI 生成速度不等于算法正确。
why_en: Before trusting greedy, ask whether choices can be committed, whether the remaining problem is similar, and whether a counterexample exists.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Before submitting] --> B[State local rule]
B --> C[Try exchange argument]
C --> D[Test small counterexample]
D --> E[Name exact or heuristic]
optionExplanations: 问这句挡住的是'选完又想反悔'的风险，贪心选择一旦不可逆就必须先确认它安全。
问这句是在确认最优子结构成立，不然规则用到一半就会失效。
主动找反例是最快的证伪方式，几秒钟就能戳穿一个看似合理的贪心。
生成速度快只说明 AI 打字快，跟局部选择是否安全无关，是要打破的错误直觉。
optionExplanations_en: This checks whether the choice is truly irreversible -- the biggest risk if you'd ever need to undo it.
This confirms optimal substructure holds, otherwise the rule breaks down partway through.
Hunting for a counterexample is the fastest way to disprove a greedy idea that only looks reasonable.
Fast generation only means the AI types quickly -- it says nothing about whether the choice is safe, and that's the assumption to break.

scenario: 同一道区间题，按结束时间贪心是精确最优，按时长贪心却有反例，两版都能过样例。
scenario_en: On the same interval problem, sorting by end time is provably optimal while sorting by duration has counterexamples, yet both versions pass the sample tests.
q: 为什么说贪心是最容易“看起来对但其实错”的模式？
q_en: Why is greedy so likely to look right while being wrong?
options: 贪心代码在语法上写不出来、通常连编译都过不了
有诱人的局部选择，但只有部分能保证全局最优
贪心算法只能处理字符串类型的输入
贪心方案的运行速度永远比动态规划慢
options_en: Greedy code can't even be written syntactically and usually won't compile.
There's a tempting local choice, but only some choices are actually globally optimal.
Greedy algorithms only work on string inputs.
Greedy is always slower than dynamic programming.
why: 自然排序会诱导你和 AI 过早提交策略。真正要证明的是这个局部选择不会牺牲未来最优。
why_en: Greedy is risky because many problems have tempting local choices but only some make those choices globally safe.
tradeoff: 看似合理的局部选择 vs 站得住脚的全局最优证明
optionExplanations: 贪心代码语法上通常完全合法、能编译能跑，这正是它危险的地方，不是编译问题。
危险来自看起来合理的局部选择，未必等于全局最优，这正是要每次单独证明的地方。
贪心广泛用在区间、装箱、图论等非字符串问题上，限定成字符串处理是判错了范围。
有些贪心（如区间调度）是精确解且比 DP 快得多，速度比较不能替代正确性判断。
optionExplanations_en: Greedy code is usually syntactically fine and compiles and runs -- that's exactly what makes it dangerous, not a compile error.
The risk is a locally tempting choice that isn't automatically globally optimal -- that's what needs proving each time.
Greedy is widely used for intervals, packing, and graphs, not just strings -- that's the wrong scope.
Some greedy solutions, like interval scheduling, are exact and faster than DP -- speed doesn't decide correctness.

scenario: 自动售货机找零，面额只有 1/3/4 元，题目要求用最少硬币凑出 6 元。
scenario_en: A vending machine makes change with only 1, 3, and 4 unit coins, and the problem asks for the fewest coins to reach 6.
q: 硬币找零中，面额 `[1, 3, 4]`、目标 6 为什么能反驳“每次取最大硬币”？
q_en: In coin change with denominations [1, 3, 4] and target 6, why does this disprove largest-coin-first?
options: 贪心选 6 枚，最优需要 7 枚
这个金额在 1/3/4 面额下根本无法凑出、本身就无解
得到 4+1+1 三枚，最优是 3+3 两枚
取最大硬币策略在任意面额下都最优
options_en: Greedy uses six coins while the optimum needs seven.
This amount can't be made at all under the 1/3/4 system, so it has no solution.
It takes 4+1+1, three coins, while the optimum is 3+3, two coins.
Largest-coin-first is always optimal for any denomination set.
why: 一次看似最好的 4 会把后续逼进两个 1。这个小反例证明贪心选择性质在任意面额下不成立。
why_en: The 1,3,4 coin system breaks largest-coin greedy because 4 plus 1 plus 1 is worse than 3 plus 3.
tradeoff: 贪心选最大面额（简单快）vs 动态规划找到真正最优组合
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Six[Amount 6] --> Four[Take 4]
  Four --> One[Take 1]
  One --> One2[Take 1]
  Six --> ThreeA[Take 3]
  ThreeA --> ThreeB[Take 3]
optionExplanations: 枚数对不上真实计算过程，贪心走的是 4+1+1 三枚，不是六枚。
面额里含 1 就一定有解，这个选项在起点就站不住。
贪心先拿 4 把自己逼进两个 1，比 3+3 多花一枚，这正是反例要证明的落差。
这句话就是被这个反例推翻的断言，反例存在本身已经否定它。
optionExplanations_en: The coin count is wrong -- greedy actually takes 4+1+1, three coins, not six.
A coin set with 1 in it always has a solution, so this option fails at the starting premise.
Greedy grabs 4 first and gets boxed into two 1s, one coin worse than 3+3 -- exactly the gap the counterexample shows.
This is the very claim the counterexample disproves; its existence already refutes the statement.

scenario: 给一组会议区间，目标是选择最多数量的互不重叠会议。
scenario_en: Given meeting intervals, the goal is to choose the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings.
q: 给定这些会议区间，标准的贪心策略应该怎么排序、怎么选？
q_en: For these meeting intervals, how should the standard greedy strategy sort and select?
options: 按开始时间从最晚到最早排序，然后再依次挑选会议
按会议名称的字母顺序排序后再选
不排序，直接优先选时长最长的会议
按结束时间排序，依次选最早结束且不冲突的会议
options_en: Sort by start time from latest to earliest, then pick in that order.
Sort meetings alphabetically by name.
Skip sorting and always pick the longest meeting first.
Sort by end time and repeatedly pick the earliest-ending compatible meeting.
why: 最早结束的会议给未来留下最多空间。这个问题的交换论证很经典，所以贪心是精确最优而不是启发式。
why_en: Maximum non-overlapping interval scheduling is solved by choosing the earliest-ending compatible interval.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题改成带权收益最大化，单纯最早结束不够，通常需要加 DP。
tradeoff: 按结束时间贪心（可证明精确最优）vs 按开始时间/名称/时长排序（无法保证最优）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Sort[Sort by end time] --> First[Pick earliest end]
  First --> Compatible[Skip conflicts]
  Compatible --> Next[Pick next compatible]
  Next --> Result[Max count]
optionExplanations: 开始时间晚不代表给后面留的空间少，排序方向本身就选错了维度。
名字顺序和会议的时间结构没有任何关系，纯属误用排序键。
只挑时长最长的会议容易占满本可以塞下多场短会的时间段，选出的场数反而更少。
最早结束的会议留给后续的空间最大，这是有交换论证撑腰的标准精确解。
optionExplanations_en: A later start time doesn't mean less room left for later meetings -- this sorts on the wrong dimension entirely.
Alphabetical order has no relationship to the timing structure of the meetings -- it's just the wrong key.
Picking the longest meeting first can hog a slot that could've fit several shorter ones, so the total count drops.
The earliest-ending meeting leaves the most room for what comes after -- the exact solution backed by an exchange argument.

q: 填空：区间调度为什么按结束时间贪心？
q_en: Fill in the blanks: why does interval scheduling greedily sort by end time?
text: 选择{{最早结束}}的可兼容区间，会给后续区间留下{{最多空间}}。
why: 如果某个最优解第一个选的不是最早结束区间，通常可以交换成最早结束区间而不减少可选数量。这就是直觉版交换论证。
why_en: Choosing the earliest finishing compatible interval leaves the most room for future intervals.

scenario: 你在给同事审查一段“最大不重叠区间”的贪心实现，想确认这一行条件到底在保证什么。
scenario_en: You are reviewing a greedy implementation for maximum non-overlapping intervals and want to confirm what this condition guarantees.
q: 这段最大不重叠区间代码中，`start >= last_end` 的含义是什么？
q_en: In this maximum non-overlapping interval code, what does `start >= last_end` mean?
options: 当前区间和上一个已选区间不重叠，可以安全加入
当前区间必须比上一个已选区间更短
当前区间是这批区间里权重或收益最大的那个区间
当前区间一定是排序后的最后一个
options_en: The current interval doesn't overlap the last selected one, so it's safe to add.
The current interval must be shorter than the last selected one.
The current interval has the largest weight or payoff among all intervals.
The current interval must be the last one after sorting.
why: 排序保证遍历顺序是结束时间递增；这个条件只负责兼容性。选中后更新 last_end，作为后续区间的边界。
why_en: The condition checks compatibility with the last selected interval after sorting by end time.
optionExplanations: start >= last_end 就是不重叠的判定式，满足才 append 并推进 last_end。
代码里根本没有比较区间长度，长度约束是凭空加上去的。
这段代码没有权重字段，也没按权重排序，权重这个概念在这里不存在。
排序只保证遍历顺序按结束时间递增，选中的不一定是数组里位置最后的那个。
optionExplanations_en: `start >= last_end` is literally the no-overlap test -- pass it and the code appends and advances `last_end`.
The code never compares interval lengths, so a length requirement is invented out of nowhere.
There's no weight field or weight-based sort in this snippet -- weight isn't a concept here at all.
Sorting only guarantees traversal order by end time, not that the selected interval sits last in the array.

scenario: 给一组会议区间，目标是需要的最少房间数，而不是最多能选多少会议。
scenario_en: Given meeting intervals, the goal is the minimum number of rooms needed, not the maximum number of meetings selected.
q: 面对“最少需要多少房间”这个目标，应该用哪种贪心结构？
q_en: For the goal of minimum rooms needed, which greedy structure should you use?
options: 按结束时间排序，贪心选最多不重叠的区间
按开始时间排序，用最小堆维护当前活跃会议的最早结束时间
忽略时间顺序，每次都优先安排时长最长的会议
用并查集（Union-Find）把重叠的会议合并成一组
options_en: Sort by end time and greedily pick the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.
Sort by start time and keep a min-heap of the earliest end time among active meetings.
Ignore time order and always schedule the longest meeting first.
Use union-find to merge overlapping meetings into groups.
why: 最少房间数等价于任意时刻最大重叠数。最小堆记录活跃会议的结束时间，能判断是否复用房间。
why_en: Minimum meeting rooms uses a min-heap of active end times after sorting by start time.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是最多选择多少不重叠会议，才使用按结束时间选择的区间调度策略。
tradeoff: 统计任意时刻最大重叠数（最小堆）vs 选出最多不重叠子集（按结束时间贪心）
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Meeting[Next meeting by start] --> Heap[Min heap of end times]
  Heap --> Reuse{Earliest end <= start?}
  Reuse -->|yes| Pop[Reuse room]
  Reuse -->|no| New[Need new room]
  Pop --> Push[Push current end]
  New --> Push

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种维护不相交集合、支持快速合并和查询的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Union-Find is a data structure that tracks disjoint sets and supports fast merge and lookup operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶总是当前最小元素的优先队列结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a priority queue whose top element is always the current smallest value.

rows: 维护活跃区间最早结束时间
背包式近似（非区间调度标准解）
合并重叠区间为连通分量
分组/连通性问题，不是计数问题

optionExplanations: 这是'选最多不重叠会议数'那题的正确贪心，但这里问的是房间数，目标换了策略也要换。
最小堆堆顶是当前活跃会议里最早结束的那个，能立刻判断有没有房间可复用。
时长排序看不出'此刻有几个会议同时占用房间'，跟房间需求峰值没有关系。
并查集擅长找连通分量，不维护'谁先结束'这种时间顺序，答不出房间数。
optionExplanations_en: This is the right greedy for maximizing non-overlapping meeting count, but the goal here is room count -- a different target needs a different strategy.
The heap top is the earliest-ending active meeting, so you can instantly tell whether a room can be reused.
Sorting by duration says nothing about how many meetings overlap at any instant, which is what room count tracks.
Union-find groups connected components; it doesn't track who finishes first, so it can't answer a room-count question.

scenario: 同一份会议区间数据，一个需求是排出最多互不冲突的会议，另一个是算峰值要几间会议室。
scenario_en: Same set of meeting intervals: one requirement is to schedule the most non-conflicting meetings, the other is to count how many rooms the peak needs.
q: 最大不重叠区间和最少会议室为什么不能用同一套贪心？
q_en: Why can't maximum non-overlapping intervals and minimum meeting rooms use the same greedy strategy?
options: 两题的输入区间格式完全不同，没法类比
最少会议室问题的区间不能先排序处理
最大不重叠区间问题必须依赖动态规划求解
前者选最大不重叠子集，后者统计最大重叠数
options_en: The two problems' input interval formats are completely different, so they can't be compared.
The minimum-rooms problem can't be sorted first.
Maximum non-overlapping intervals must rely on dynamic programming.
One selects the maximum non-overlapping subset; the other counts the maximum simultaneous overlap.
why: 两个题都长得像区间题，但目标不同。目标变化会改变贪心选择和数据结构。
why_en: Selecting a maximum compatible subset is different from counting active resources, so the greedy strategy changes.
tradeoff: 选子集最大化数量（排序扫描）vs 统计同时活跃资源数（最小堆）

rows: 最大不重叠区间（按结束时间贪心）
维护活跃区间最早结束时间

optionExplanations: 两题输入其实都是 (start, end) 区间，格式一样，问题不在输入。
两题都要先排序，只是一个按开始、一个按结束，排序本身不是障碍。
最大不重叠区间有 O(n log n) 的贪心精确解，不需要 DP。
一个在选子集、一个在数峰值，目标不同才是排序键和数据结构都要换的根因。
optionExplanations_en: Both problems take the same (start, end) interval format -- the input isn't where they diverge.
Both problems sort first, just on different keys (start vs. end) -- sorting itself isn't the obstacle.
Maximum non-overlapping intervals has an exact O(n log n) greedy solution; it never needed DP.
One selects a subset, the other counts a peak -- that goal difference is why the sort key and structure both change.

scenario: 你在审查一段“最少会议室”贪心实现，想确认堆顶条件到底在判断什么。
scenario_en: You are reviewing a greedy minimum-meeting-rooms implementation and want to confirm what the heap-top condition checks.
q: 这段最少会议室代码中，`heap[0] <= start` 表示什么？
q_en: In this minimum-meeting-rooms code, what does `heap[0] <= start` mean?
options: 当前这个会议必须被丢弃，不能安排
说明此刻所有房间都空闲着、没有会议在占用
最早结束的会议已经结束，可以复用这个房间
堆里保存的是每个会议的开始时间
options_en: The current meeting must be dropped and can't be scheduled.
It means every room is currently free with no meeting occupying any of them.
The heap top (earliest-ending active meeting) has already ended, so this room can be reused.
The heap stores each meeting's start time.
why: 堆顶是最早结束的活跃会议。如果它不晚于当前开始时间，当前会议可以接到同一房间后面。
why_en: The heap top is the earliest ending active meeting, so it can be reused if it ends before the new start.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶总是当前最小元素的优先队列结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a priority queue whose top element is always the current smallest value.

optionExplanations: 代码逻辑里没有丢弃分支，条件成立时走的是复用房间，不是丢弃会议。
堆里有元素恰恰说明至少有一个房间正在被占用，跟'都空闲'矛盾。
heap[0] 不晚于当前开始时间，说明这个房间已经腾出来了，可以 heapreplace 复用。
堆里存的是 end 而不是 start，heapreplace/heappush 操作的对象说明了这一点。
optionExplanations_en: There's no discard branch in this code -- when the condition holds, it reuses a room, it doesn't drop the meeting.
A non-empty heap means at least one room is currently occupied, which contradicts 'every room is free.'
`heap[0]` not later than the current start means that room has already freed up, so `heapreplace` can reuse it.
The heap stores end times, not start times -- that's what `heapreplace`/`heappush` are operating on.

scenario: 任务有不同内存需求，服务器容量固定，目标是用尽量少的服务器装下所有任务。
scenario_en: Tasks have different memory needs, server capacity is fixed, and the goal is to fit all tasks using as few servers as possible.
q: 这个“用最少服务器装下所有任务”的问题，更接近下面哪种经典问题？
q_en: This use-the-fewest-servers-to-fit-all-tasks problem is closest to which classic problem?
options: Edit distance：计算把一个字符串变成另一个的最少编辑步数
拓扑排序：给有依赖关系的任务排出一个合法顺序
无权图最短路：找从起点到终点边数最少的路径
Bin packing：把所有物品装进尽量少的固定容量箱子
options_en: Edit distance: compute the minimum edits to turn one string into another.
Topological sort: order dependent tasks into one valid sequence.
Unweighted shortest path: find the path with the fewest edges.
Bin packing: pack all items into as few fixed-capacity bins as possible.
why: 装箱的目标是把所有物品放入尽量少的固定容量箱子。精确最优是 NP-hard，面试里常接受清楚说明的贪心基线。
why_en: Minimizing servers for fixed-capacity tasks is a bin-packing problem where greedy heuristics are often the practical interview answer.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目要求精确最优且规模很小，可考虑回溯/搜索；如果是选子集最大价值，那是 knapsack 而非 bin packing。
tradeoff: 贪心装箱启发式（快、近似）vs 精确最优搜索（慢、NP-hard 才需要）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一批物品装进容量固定的箱子、目标是用最少箱子数的经典问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bin packing is the classic problem of fitting items into fixed-capacity bins using as few bins as possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需的最少插入/删除/替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, or substitutions to turn one string into another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前面指向后面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points from earlier to later.

optionExplanations: 编辑距离处理字符串变换步数，跟'装得下装不下'的容量约束毫无关系。
拓扑排序解决的是依赖顺序，这题没有任务之间谁先谁后的约束。
最短路关心的是路径长度，这题看的是空间够不够，没有'起点到终点'的概念。
任务=物品、服务器容量=箱子容量，目标是用最少箱子装下所有任务，结构完全对应。
optionExplanations_en: Edit distance counts string-transformation steps -- it has nothing to do with a 'does it fit' capacity constraint.
Topological sort solves ordering under dependencies; this problem has no task-must-come-before-task constraint.
Shortest path cares about path length; this problem is about whether things fit, with no start-to-end path concept.
Tasks map to items and server capacity maps to bin capacity -- using the fewest bins to fit everything is exactly bin packing.

scenario: 把大小不一的任务装到容量固定的服务器上，目标是把用到的机器数压到最少。
scenario_en: You are packing variable-sized tasks onto fixed-capacity servers, and the goal is to minimize how many machines you use.
q: 文章列出的装箱贪心策略有哪些？
q_en: Which bin-packing greedy strategies are listed here?
options: First-Fit：把物品放进第一个能容纳它的箱子
Best-Fit：把物品放进剩余空间最少但仍能容纳的箱子
First-Fit Decreasing：先按大小降序排序，再做 First-Fit
永远只把最小的物品放进箱子，直到所有箱子都满
options_en: First-Fit: place the item in the first bin that has room.
Best-Fit: place the item in the tightest bin that still fits.
First-Fit Decreasing: sort items largest-first, then apply First-Fit.
Always place only the smallest items into bins until every bin is full.
why: FFD 先处理大物品，减少后续无法放置的风险。小物品先放容易造成碎片化。
why_en: First-Fit, Best-Fit, and First-Fit Decreasing are the common bin-packing greedy strategies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扫描已有箱子，把物品放进第一个能装下它的箱子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit scans existing bins and places the item in the first one that has enough room.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把物品放进放入后剩余空间最小、但仍能装下它的箱子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Best-Fit places the item in the bin that leaves the least remaining space while still fitting it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

optionExplanations: 扫到第一个能装下就放，实现最简单，代价是容易留下零碎空间。
多扫一遍找最紧的箱子，打包更紧凑，但每次都要多比较。
先按大小降序排再 First-Fit，先处理大物品能显著降低后期无处安放的风险。
只放小物品会让箱子很快被填满、大件却没地方去，装箱数会远多于必要值。
optionExplanations_en: Place into the first bin that fits -- simplest to implement, at the cost of leaving fragmented space behind.
Scan for the tightest-fitting bin -- packs denser, but costs an extra comparison pass each time.
Sort largest-first, then First-Fit -- placing big items early sharply cuts the risk of nowhere to put them later.
Placing only small items fills bins quickly while large ones have nowhere to go, pushing bin count above what's needed.

q: 填空：First-Fit Decreasing 的步骤。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the steps of First-Fit Decreasing.

why: 先放大物品是一种实用启发式，因为小物品通常更容易塞进剩余空间。它不是保证最优的精确算法。
why_en: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest first and then applies First-Fit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

scenario: 用 FFD 把一批容器镜像装到固定容量节点上，面试官问这个启发式最坏能比最优差多少。
scenario_en: You use FFD to pack container images onto fixed-capacity nodes, and the interviewer asks how far off the optimum this heuristic can be in the worst case.
q: FFD 已知的最坏情况箱子数保证大致是什么样的公式？
q_en: What is the rough worst-case bin-count guarantee for FFD?
options: 结果恰好总是精确等于 OPT 个最优箱子数
无论输入什么，总是需要 2^n 个箱子
目前没有任何已知的近似保证结论
options_en: At most (11/9) times OPT plus 6/9 bins.
The result is always exactly equal to the optimal number of bins, OPT.
It always requires 2^n bins, regardless of the input.
There is currently no known approximation guarantee at all.
why: FFD 的近似保证公式是 (11/9)×OPT + 6/9，OPT 是这批输入下真正的最优箱子数；面试不需要背这个数字，但知道'存在近似界'能支撑你说清'这是启发式、有保证但非最优'。
why_en: FFD is bounded by about eleven-ninths of the optimal bin count plus six-ninths, which matters for stating it's a bounded heuristic, not an exact optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个问题在给定输入下真正的最优解数值，比如最优箱子数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OPT is the true optimal value for the given input, such as the optimal number of bins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

optionExplanations: 这就是 FFD 已知的近似界，说明它是有保证的启发式，不是精确最优算法。
FFD 是近似算法，不保证跟最优箱子数完全相等，这里把近似说成了精确。
2^n 是指数级，装箱问题的箱子数不会随物品数指数爆炸，这个说法夸张失实。
FFD 恰恰是研究得很透的问题，是有明确近似界的，不是没人研究过。
optionExplanations_en: This is FFD's known approximation bound -- it makes FFD a heuristic with a guarantee, not an exact optimum.
FFD is approximate, not guaranteed equal to the optimal bin count -- this mistakes 'bounded' for 'exact.'
Bin count doesn't blow up exponentially with item count the way 2^n implies -- this overstates it wildly.
FFD is actually a well-studied case with a known bound -- this claims no guarantee exists, which is false.

scenario: AI 写了最简单的 FFD：每个物品扫描所有已有箱子。
scenario_en: The AI wrote the simplest FFD implementation: each item scans all existing bins.
q: 这段实现的主要性能特征是什么？
q_en: What is the main performance characteristic of this implementation?
options: 这段代码的时间复杂度恒为 O(1)，与物品数量无关
朴素扫描最坏是 O(n^2)，可用有序结构优化
这段代码保证总能返回精确最优的装箱方案
这段代码完全无法处理任何容量限制条件
options_en: This code's time complexity is constant, O(1), independent of item count.
Naive scanning is O(n^2) in the worst case; an ordered structure can improve it.
This code is guaranteed to always return the exact optimal packing.
This code cannot handle any capacity constraint at all.
why: 每个物品可能扫描所有箱子，所以最坏二次方。除非题目明确要求更快，朴素版在面试中常可作为清晰基线。
why_en: Naive FFD can be quadratic because each item scans existing bins, though ordered capacity tracking can improve it.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入规模大或复杂度要求明确，应该让 AI 用平衡树等结构维护剩余容量。
tradeoff: 朴素双重循环（O(n^2)，实现简单）vs 平衡树/堆维护剩余容量（O(n log n)，实现更复杂）

termDefinitions.meaning: 常数时间复杂度，运行时间基本不随输入规模变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means constant time complexity that does not grow with input size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入规模翻倍时运行时间大约变成四倍的复杂度量级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(n squared) means the runtime roughly quadruples whenever the input size doubles.

optionExplanations: 外层遍历物品、内层遍历箱子，两层循环摆在那，不可能是常数时间。
每个物品最坏要扫一遍所有已开箱子，朴素版就是 O(n^2)，换有序结构能降下来。
装箱精确最优是 NP-hard，这几行朴素代码不可能顺带保证最优。
`load + item <= capacity` 这行本身就在做容量检查，跟'不处理容量'的说法矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: There are two nested loops right there in the code -- that can't be constant time.
Each item can scan every open bin in the worst case, so naive it's O(n^2), and an ordered structure can cut that down.
Exact bin packing is NP-hard; these few lines of naive code can't incidentally guarantee optimality.
The line `load + item <= capacity` is literally the capacity check -- that contradicts 'no capacity handling.'

scenario: 服务器同时有 CPU 和内存上限，任务也有两个资源需求。
scenario_en: Each server has both CPU and memory limits, and each task consumes both resources.
q: 服务器同时受 CPU 和内存上限约束时，面试中合理的贪心思路是什么？
q_en: When servers are constrained by both CPU and memory, what is a reasonable greedy interview approach?
options: 只根据任务的名称字符串本身来排序
直接忽略其中一个资源维度的约束
按更紧张的归一化资源需求排序，另一维只作可行性检查
声称一维版本的 FFD 在双资源约束下仍然精确最优
options_en: Sort tasks purely by their name string itself.
Simply ignore one of the two resource dimensions.
Sort by the tighter normalized resource demand and use the other dimension only as a feasibility check.
Claim the one-dimensional FFD is still exactly optimal even under two resource constraints.
why: 多维装箱更难，实用做法是用一个启发式排序近似处理，并明确说明放弃了精确最优保证。成熟回答会讲清 tradeoff。
why_en: For multi-resource packing, a practical interview heuristic sorts by the tightest normalized resource and checks all capacities.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目要求严格最优且规模很小，可以回溯搜索；如果只需可行分配，启发式更务实。
tradeoff: 归一化排序启发式（务实、放弃精确最优）vs 精确回溯/搜索（能保证最优、规模必须很小）
codeSample:
key = max(cpu / cpu_cap, mem / mem_cap)
items_sorted = sorted(items, key=key, reverse=True)
# 先放这个任务在哪个维度上最接近容量瓶颈

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同量纲的数值换算到同一个 0 到 1 的比例范围，方便比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization rescales values with different units onto a common 0-to-1 range so they can be compared.

optionExplanations: 名字跟 CPU/内存占用没有任何数值关系，排序结果等于没排序。
忽略一个维度会让被忽略的那个资源真的超出服务器上限。
用 max(cpu/cpu_cap, mem/mem_cap) 找出哪个维度更紧张，两个约束都纳入了考虑。
多维装箱比一维更难，一维的精确最优保证不能照搬过来。
optionExplanations_en: The name string has no numerical relationship to CPU or memory usage, so this sort accomplishes nothing.
Ignoring a dimension lets the ignored resource actually blow past the server's real limit.
`max(cpu/cpu_cap, mem/mem_cap)` finds which dimension is tighter, so both constraints get accounted for.
Multi-resource packing is harder than one-dimensional packing; the one-dimensional guarantee doesn't carry over.

q: 填空：二维装箱启发式中的排序键。
q_en: Fill in the blank: the sort key in a two-dimensional packing heuristic.
text: CPU + 内存装箱可按 `max(cpu/cpu_cap, mem/mem_cap)` 降序排序，也就是先放{{相对最紧张资源}}占比高的任务。
why: 这个键问的是该任务在哪个维度上最接近容量瓶颈。它是合理启发式，不是必须背的公式。
why_en: The max-normalized-resource key prioritizes items that are tight in at least one capacity dimension.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同量纲的数值换算到同一个 0 到 1 的比例范围，方便比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization rescales values with different units onto a common 0-to-1 range so they can be compared.

scenario: 一道题要求返回精确最少硬币数，另一道只要求箱子数尽量少，你在两处都写了贪心。
scenario_en: One problem demands the exact minimum coin count while the other only asks for as few bins as possible, and you used greedy in both.
q: “贪心近似”和“贪心错误”的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between approximate greedy and wrong greedy?
options: 二者其实完全一样，只是叫法不同，没有区别
近似策略在任何情况下都一定无法返回合法解
错误策略只是运行得慢一点而已，答案本身并没有别的问题
近似有保证但可能非最优；错误则不满足题意，必须换算法
options_en: The two are actually identical, just different names, no real difference.
An approximate strategy can never return any valid solution under any circumstance.
A wrong strategy is merely a bit slower, with nothing else wrong about the answer itself.
Approximate can be non-optimal but comes with a stated guarantee; wrong fails the requirement and needs a different algorithm.
why: Bin packing 的 FFD 常是可接受近似；非标准硬币找零的最大硬币策略则会返回非最优答案，不符合精确题意。
why_en: Approximate greedy can be acceptable with stated guarantees, while incorrect greedy fails the required objective.
tradeoff: 近似（非最优但有保证，可接受）vs 错误（不满足题意，必须替换算法）

rows: 假装存在多项式最优证明

optionExplanations: 这句话抹掉了两者最关键的区别：是否满足题目要求，二者并不能划等号。
近似解依然是合法解，只是数量或代价可能不是最优，不是'无解'。
错误策略的问题是答案本身不对，不是跑得慢，速度从来不是这里的争议点。
近似能带着已知保证说出口，错误必须承认并换算法，这是两者的真正分界。
optionExplanations_en: This erases the key distinction -- whether the requirement is actually met -- the two aren't interchangeable.
An approximate solution is still valid, just possibly non-optimal in count or cost, not 'no solution at all.'
A wrong strategy gives the wrong answer outright -- speed was never the issue here.
Approximate comes with a stated guarantee even if non-optimal; wrong fails the requirement and forces a swap.

scenario: 题目是 0/1 knapsack：从物品中选一个子集，在容量内最大化价值。
scenario_en: The problem is 0/1 knapsack: choose a subset of items to maximize value within capacity.
q: 为什么不能直接把它当 bin packing 用 FFD？
q_en: Why can't you directly treat this as bin packing and use FFD?
options: knapsack 选子集要 DP；装箱是尽量少用箱子
这两个问题的容量约束设定完全一样
knapsack 问题里其实没有容量限制
FFD 用在 knapsack 上也总返回最大价值
options_en: Knapsack needs DP to pick a subset; bin packing just uses as few bins as possible.
The two problems set up their capacity constraints identically.
The knapsack problem actually has no capacity limit.
FFD also always returns the maximum value when used on knapsack.
why: 目标函数不同：装箱关注箱子数量，knapsack 关注价值。按大小或比率贪心在 0/1 knapsack 上可能远离最优。
why_en: Bin packing packs all items into few bins, while zero-one knapsack selects a value-maximizing subset and usually needs DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 fractional knapsack，可以按价值密度贪心；0/1 版本不能随意拆分物品。
tradeoff: Bin Packing：装下全部、最少箱子数 vs 0/1 Knapsack：选子集、最大化价值

termDefinitions.meaning: 从若干不可拆分物品中选一个子集，在容量限制内让总价值最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The 0/1 knapsack problem selects an unsplittable subset of items to maximize total value within a capacity limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把物品按大小从大到小排序，再依次执行 First-Fit 装箱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items largest-first, then applies First-Fit bin packing.

optionExplanations: 一个在选子集最大化价值、一个在装下全部最少化箱子数，目标函数不同，算法自然不同。
两题算法和目标都不同，容量约束'设定一样'这个前提本身站不住。
容量限制正是 knapsack 存在取舍的原因，没有容量限制的话直接全选就行。
FFD 从头到尾只关心'装不装得下'，从不比较价值，用在 knapsack 上不会自动最大化价值。
optionExplanations_en: One selects a value-maximizing subset (needs DP), the other packs everything into as few bins as possible.
The algorithms and goals differ entirely, so the premise that the capacity setups match is already wrong.
The capacity limit is exactly why knapsack requires tradeoffs at all -- without it you'd just take everything.
FFD only ever asks 'does it fit,' never compares value, so running it on knapsack won't maximize value.

scenario: 图最短路问题存在负权边，AI 生成了 Dijkstra。
scenario_en: The shortest-path graph has negative-weight edges, and the AI generated Dijkstra.
q: AI 用 Dijkstra 处理带负权边的最短路，你应该如何纠正？
q_en: If the AI uses Dijkstra on shortest paths with negative edges, how should you correct it?
options: 只把优先队列换成普通的先进先出队列，其他核心逻辑完全不变
指出非负权重前提被打破，改用 Bellman-Ford
删掉所有带负权的边，直接回避掉这个问题
断言负权边完全不会影响最短路的最终结果
options_en: Just swap the priority queue for a plain FIFO queue and leave all the core logic unchanged.
Point out that the non-negative-weight assumption is broken; switch to Bellman-Ford.
Delete every negative-weight edge outright to sidestep the problem entirely.
Assert that negative edges have no effect on the final shortest-path result at all.
why: Dijkstra 是贪心式扩展最近节点，依赖非负权重。负权会让已确定距离后来变小。
why_en: Negative edges invalidate Dijkstra's greedy finalization assumption, so Bellman-Ford is the safer alternative.
whenOtherWins: 如果确认所有权重非负，Dijkstra 仍然是合适选择。
tradeoff: Dijkstra（贪心扩展、要求非负权重、更快）vs Bellman-Ford（允许负权、松弛 V-1 轮、更慢）

termDefinitions.meaning: 每一步贪心地扩展当前已知距离最短的未访问节点的最短路算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm greedily expands the unvisited node with the currently smallest known distance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对所有边反复做 V-1 轮松弛来求最短路、并支持负权边的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bellman-Ford computes shortest paths by relaxing every edge for V-1 rounds and supports negative-weight edges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能快速取出当前最小或最大元素的队列结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority queue quickly returns the current smallest or largest element.

optionExplanations: 换队列类型只影响效率，不解决'已确定距离被负权边后续压低'这个根本问题。
非负权重是 Dijkstra 贪心扩展成立的前提，前提被打破就该换成支持负权的 Bellman-Ford。
如果负权边是题目给定条件，删边等于改了题目而不是解决它。
已经确定的最短距离完全可能被后面出现的负权边继续压低，这句断言与算法行为矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping the queue type only affects speed -- it doesn't fix a finalized distance getting undercut by a negative edge later.
Non-negative weights are the precondition for Dijkstra's greedy finalization; once that breaks, Bellman-Ford handles it.
If negative edges are part of the given problem, deleting them changes the problem instead of solving it.
An already-finalized shortest distance can still shrink from a later negative edge -- that contradicts this claim.

scenario: 任务有依赖关系，某任务必须在另一个任务之后才能开始。
scenario_en: Tasks have dependencies, so some tasks can only start after other tasks finish.
q: 为什么“每次选最短任务”不足以处理带依赖的调度？
q_en: Why is choosing the shortest task each time not enough for scheduling with dependencies?
options: 任务之间的依赖关系总是可以被贪心直接忽略掉
所有任务其实都必须在同一时刻一起开始
会违反依赖关系，需要先用拓扑排序建立合法顺序，再谈优化
最短任务优先策略在任何带依赖的调度场景下都始终保持最优
options_en: Dependencies between tasks can always be safely ignored by greedy.
All tasks must actually start at the exact same moment.
It can violate dependencies; you need topological sort first to build a valid order, then optimize.
Shortest-task-first stays optimal in every dependency-laden scheduling scenario.
why: 依赖关系是硬约束，不能靠局部时长排序绕过。先保证合法顺序，再谈成本或时间优化。
why_en: Dependencies are hard constraints, so topological ordering must come before greedy duration choices.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有依赖、只有独立任务的排序或资源分配，贪心调度可能成立。
tradeoff: 先拓扑排序保证合法顺序（硬约束优先）vs 直接按时长贪心（可能违反依赖）

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前面指向后面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points from earlier to later.

optionExplanations: 忽略依赖会产出违反前置任务顺序的非法调度，依赖是硬约束不是可选项。
有依赖关系恰恰说明某些任务必须等前置任务完成，不是同时开始。
先用拓扑排序拿到不违反依赖的合法顺序，之后才轮到按时长这类软优化。
这个策略只在没有依赖的场景下成立，一旦引入依赖前提就被打破了。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring dependencies produces an illegal schedule that violates ordering -- dependencies are a hard constraint.
Having dependencies means some tasks must wait for others to finish, not that everything starts simultaneously.
Topological sort first gets a legal order that respects dependencies; only then does duration optimizing make sense.
This strategy only holds with no dependencies -- once dependencies exist, its premise breaks.

scenario: 题目明确要求返回精确最优解、不接受近似，你在判断贪心能不能直接交。
scenario_en: The problem explicitly requires the exact optimum and will not accept an approximation, so you are deciding whether greedy can be submitted as is.
q: 哪些情况说明贪心可能不是精确正确的答案？
q_en: Which situations suggest greedy may not be an exact correct answer?
options: 选择组合之间相互影响，早期选择会锁死后续
题目要求精确最大价值的 0/1 knapsack
硬币面额是任意集合而不是已知规范系统
区间调度要求最大数量且按结束时间选择
options_en: Choices interact with each other, so an early choice can lock out later possibilities.
The problem requires the exact maximum value for 0/1 knapsack.
The coin denominations are an arbitrary set, not a known canonical system.
Interval scheduling asks for the maximum count and picks greedily by end time.
why: 前三项都有反例风险或需要全局状态。标准最大不重叠区间是贪心可证明正确的例外。
why_en: Greedy is suspect when choices interact, exact knapsack is required, or arbitrary coin systems can create counterexamples.
tradeoff: 存在反例风险的场景（DP/回溯更安全）vs 可证明精确的标准贪心（区间调度）
optionExplanations: 早期选择锁死后续可能性，正是贪心选择性质被破坏的典型信号。
0/1 knapsack 通常需要 DP，按密度贪心可能拿到远低于最优的价值。
非规范面额下最大硬币贪心有已知反例，不能默认它总是对的。
这恰恰是贪心可证明精确正确的经典场景，不属于'贪心可能不精确'这一类。
optionExplanations_en: An early choice locking out later options is the textbook sign the greedy-choice property has broken down.
0/1 knapsack usually needs DP; greedy by value density can land far below the true optimum.
Arbitrary denominations have known counterexamples for largest-coin greedy -- it can't be assumed to always work.
This is exactly the case where greedy is provably exact, so it doesn't belong in the 'may not be exact' bucket.

scenario: AI 刚生成一个贪心方案，你还没证明它正确。
scenario_en: The AI has just generated a greedy solution, and you have not proven it correct yet.
q: AI 刚生成一个贪心方案、还没证明它正确时，最有价值的下一句提示是什么？
q_en: When the AI has generated a greedy solution but you have not proven it correct, what is the most useful next prompt?
options: 请把所有变量名改得更短一些
不用测试，直接把这个方案当最终答案提交上去
把代码里的注释全部删掉
请给我一个能让这个贪心策略失败的小输入
options_en: Shorten every variable name in the code.
