termDefinitions.meaning: 把候选生成和计数合并到同一趟遍历里完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fusion means combining candidate generation and counting into a single traversal pass.

optionExplanations: 候选遍历时的每一步路径就是一份共同好友证据，边走边加分，就不用等生成完候选再单独跑一遍交集计算了。
融合计数不改变候选生成方式，依然只沿共同好友路径走，不会多访问全网陌生人。
字母序 tie-break 是排序阶段单独做的，跟遍历时是否顺手计数没有关系，照样能做。
跳过本人和已有好友的过滤仍在写入分数之前完成，判断合法性的逻辑并没有变差。
optionExplanations_en: Every step of the walk is already evidence of a mutual friend, so scoring while you go skips having to run a separate intersection pass once candidates are done.
Fusing the count doesn't change how candidates are generated — it still only walks mutual-friend paths, so no extra strangers get visited.
Alphabetical tie-breaking happens separately at sort time, unrelated to whether counting happens during the walk — it still works the same.
The skip check for self and existing friends still runs before anything is written into the score map, so validity logic isn't any worse.

scenario: 同一个候选可能通过多个直接好友被访问到，你要正确累计分数。
scenario_en: The same candidate may be reached through multiple direct friends, so you need to accumulate the score correctly.
q: `scores[ff] = scores.get(ff, 0) + 1` 的语义是什么？
q_en: What does `scores[ff] = scores.get(ff, 0) + 1` mean?
options: 把已有好友重新加入推荐
候选每被一个不同共同好友路径访问一次，互友分数加一
候选名字每长一个字符加一
每个候选在整个过程里只允许出现一次且分数固定为 1
options_en: It re-adds existing friends back into the recommendations.
Each visit through a distinct mutual-friend path increments that candidate's mutual score by one.
It adds one for every extra character in the candidate's name.
Each candidate is allowed to appear only once in the whole process, with a fixed score of one.
codeSample:
# ff: a friend-of-friend reached during the walk
scores[ff] = scores.get(ff, 0) + 1
# repeated visits => higher mutual-friend score
why: map 聚合把多条二跳路径合并成一个候选分数。它正好等于 mutual friend count。
why_en: Incrementing on each two-hop visit aggregates mutual friend counts per candidate.
whenOtherWins: 如果排名只要求是否存在共同好友而不关心数量，可以用 set 代替计数 map。
tradeoff: 计数式 map（保留数量） vs 存在性 set（只判断有无）

termDefinitions.meaning: 取字典里 ff 当前的分数，不存在则默认为 0。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: scores.get(ff, 0) reads the current score for ff, defaulting to zero if it is not present yet.

optionExplanations: 已有好友在写入 score map 之前已经被跳过，这行代码不会把他们重新加回来。
`scores.get(ff, 0) + 1` 每次访问都在原有分数上加一，多条不同好友路径到达同一候选就会累加出真实的共同好友数。
分数只跟访问次数有关，跟候选名字字符串的长度完全无关。
get 加一的写法允许同一个 key 被多次访问、分数持续累加，不是只出现一次固定为 1。
optionExplanations_en: Existing friends are already skipped before anything reaches the score map, so this line doesn't re-add them.
`scores.get(ff, 0) + 1` adds one on top of the existing score each visit, so multiple distinct friend paths to the same candidate accumulate into the real mutual count.
The score only tracks visit count, nothing to do with the length of the candidate's name string.
The get-plus-one pattern lets the same key be hit repeatedly with the score kept climbing — it's not capped at appearing once with a fixed score of one.

q: 填空：huge benchmark 有 {{5000}} 个 users 和 {{25000}} 条 edges，平均度数 ≈ 2×edges/users = {{10}}，说明这是一张 {{稀疏}} 图——这正是二跳解法比全量扫描快的前提。
q_en: Fill in: The huge benchmark has {{5000}} users and {{25000}} edges, so average degree is about 2*edges/users = {{10}}; that makes it a {{sparse}} graph, which is why two-hop beats scan-all.
text: 填空：huge benchmark 有 {{5000}} 个 users 和 {{25000}} 条 edges，平均度数 ≈ 2×edges/users = {{10}}，说明这是一张 {{稀疏}} 图——这正是二跳解法比全量扫描快的前提。
why: 平均度数远小于用户总数，说明每个人的二跳邻域只是全网的一小片，这个稀疏性假设是二跳优化生效的根本原因。
why_en: Average degree stays far below the user count, so each user's two-hop neighborhood is a small slice of the network, which is exactly why the two-hop optimization works.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 2×边数/用户数估算的图平均连接密度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Average degree, computed as two times edges divided by users, estimates how densely connected the graph is.

termDefinitions.meaning: 边数远少于完全图、平均度数很低的图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse graph has far fewer edges than a complete graph and a low average degree.

scenario: 你刚把 Friend Recommender 从 scan-all 优化到二跳 walk，要把这次优化提炼成可迁移到其他题目的经验。
scenario_en: You just optimized Friend Recommender from scan-all to a two-hop walk and need to extract lessons that transfer to other problems.
q: 从 scan-all 到二跳 walk 的优化过程中，能提炼出哪些通用经验？
q_en: What general lessons can you extract from optimizing scan-all into a two-hop walk?
options: 候选资格由局部邻域决定时，优先遍历局部邻域
如果遍历路径本身就是分数证据，就在遍历中计数
返回 top 5 不代表可以不检查候选合法性
扫描全网总是比图遍历快
options_en: When eligibility is defined by a local neighborhood, traverse that neighborhood first.
If the traversal path is itself the scoring evidence, count while you walk.
Returning only the top five does not mean you can skip validity checks.
Scanning the whole network is always faster than graph traversal.
why: 核心是从规则推导候选空间，并把计数合进遍历。全量扫描只是正确性基线。
why_en: The lesson is to derive the candidate neighborhood from the rule and count evidence during traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由资格规则决定、值得遍历的局部图范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The local neighborhood is the limited part of the graph worth traversing, as defined by the eligibility rule.

optionExplanations: 先从规则推导出候选只可能出现在局部邻域，再针对那片区域遍历，能省掉检查大量注定无效的对象。
遍历路径本身能证明分数（如共同好友数）时，边走边计数能省掉一趟单独的计分遍历。
输出上限只决定最后截取几条，跟候选合不合法是两件事，截断前仍要做完整的资格检查。
本题的 benchmark 已经证明二跳 walk 比全量扫描快约 48 倍，这条说法跟实测结果相反。
optionExplanations_en: Once the rule tells you eligibility is local, walk that local neighborhood first — it skips checking a mass of objects that could never qualify.
When the traversal path is itself proof of a score (like a mutual count), counting while you walk skips a separate scoring pass.
The output cap only decides how much gets sliced at the end — it's separate from validity, which still has to be checked before truncating.
This contradicts the actual benchmark, where the two-hop walk ran roughly 48x faster than the full scan.

scenario: 社交网络会频繁新增和删除好友关系，你考虑缓存每个用户的推荐列表。
scenario_en: The social network frequently adds and removes friendship edges, and you are considering caching each user's recommendation list.
q: 最大工程风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest engineering risk?
options: 缓存机制本身只能保存最多 5 个字符
加了缓存之后二跳遍历反而会退化成全网的全局扫描
一条边变化可能影响多个用户的分数，失效范围难界定
使用缓存会让候选名字之间无法比较大小
options_en: The cache can only store up to five characters.
Adding a cache would degrade the two-hop walk back into a full network-wide scan.
A single edge change can affect many users' scores, making invalidation scope hard to bound.
Using a cache would make candidate names impossible to compare.
why: 一条边会改变两端及其邻居的二跳候选和分数。对这个规模而言，直接算更简单。
why_en: Friendship mutations can invalidate many local recommendation caches.
whenOtherWins: 如果网络很少变化且查询量巨大，预计算或增量维护可能值得。
tradeoff: 预计算换读延迟 vs 直接现算换失效简单

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次数据变化需要连带失效的缓存范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidation scope is how much cached data must be expired after a single underlying change.

optionExplanations: 缓存能存任意长度的数据，这个字符数限制的说法不成立。
加缓存不改变底层遍历算法，二跳 walk 该怎么走还怎么走，不会退化成全局扫描。
一条好友关系变化会同时影响两端用户及其邻居的候选和分数，很难精确界定要失效哪些缓存条目，这是真正的工程风险。
缓存后候选名字仍是普通字符串，字符串比较不受缓存影响。
optionExplanations_en: Caches can hold data of any length — this character-count limit isn't a real constraint.
Adding a cache doesn't change the underlying traversal; the two-hop walk still runs the same way, it doesn't degrade into a full scan.
One friendship edge changing affects both endpoints and their neighbors' candidates and scores, so it's genuinely hard to bound exactly which cache entries to invalidate — that's the real risk.
Cached or not, candidate names are still plain strings, and string comparison isn't affected by caching.

scenario: 网络只有几十个用户，推荐逻辑还在快速变化，你需要先交付正确版本。
scenario_en: The network has only a few dozen users, the recommendation logic is still changing quickly, and you need to ship a correct first version.
q: 哪种方案可能更务实？
q_en: Which approach may be more pragmatic?
options: 构建复杂缓存并维护增量失效逻辑
为区区几十个用户专门搭建一套分布式图计算集群
干脆随机挑几个人当作推荐结果
scan-all 基线：简单、小图成本可接受
options_en: Build a complex cache and maintain incremental invalidation logic.
Stand up a whole distributed graph-compute cluster just for a few dozen users.
Just recommend a few random people.
The scan-all baseline: simple, and cheap enough on a small graph.
why: 优化要服务约束。小图上全量扫描更易读，等性能测试暴露成本后再转二跳也合理。
why_en: For tiny graphs, the simple scan baseline may be the most pragmatic first implementation.
whenOtherWins: 在本文 huge benchmark 的 5000 用户、200 次查询下，二跳 walk 明显胜出。
tradeoff: 先交付简单基线 vs 提前为规模优化

termDefinitions.meaning: 用多台机器并行处理图计算的架构，通常在图规模很大时才需要。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distributed graph compute spreads graph processing across multiple machines, typically needed only at very large scale.

optionExplanations: 几十个用户的规模下增量失效逻辑带来的维护成本远超它能省下的计算量，是过度设计。
分布式图计算是为超大规模图准备的，用在几十个用户身上纯属杀鸡用牛刀。
随机挑人直接违反共同好友排序规则，牺牲了正确性，不是权衡取舍。
网络只有几十人，规则还在变，scan-all 足够快、代码也最容易读懂和改动，是这个阶段最务实的选择。
optionExplanations_en: At a few dozen users, the maintenance cost of incremental invalidation logic dwarfs whatever compute it would save — overkill here.
Distributed graph compute is built for huge graphs; running it for a few dozen users is a sledgehammer for a nail.
Picking people at random breaks the mutual-count ranking rule outright — that's sacrificing correctness, not making a tradeoff.
With only a few dozen users and rules still changing, scan-all is fast enough and the easiest code to read and modify — the pragmatic choice at this stage.

scenario: Friend Recommender 要过自动化测试：同一份图在 Python 和 Java 下必须给出一模一样的推荐顺序。
scenario_en: Friend Recommender has to pass automated tests: the same graph must yield exactly the same recommendation order in Python and in Java.
q: 如果不按名字做 tie-break，跨语言或跨运行可能出现什么问题？
q_en: If you do not tie-break by name, what cross-language or cross-run issue can appear?
options: 同分顺序跟 map 迭代顺序走，跨语言不稳定
共同好友的计数会莫名其妙变成负数
二跳遍历会因此漏掉图里一部分真实有效的候选
整体查询复杂度会退化成指数级
options_en: Tied order follows whatever the map happens to iterate in, unstable across languages.
The mutual friend count would inexplicably turn negative.
The two-hop walk would end up missing some genuinely valid candidates in the graph.
The overall query complexity would degrade to exponential.
why: 哈希容器迭代顺序不应进入可观察输出。显式二级排序消除这种偶然性。
why_en: Alphabetical tie-breaking prevents hash-iteration order from leaking into results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表/集合遍历时元素出现的顺序，语言和版本间可能不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Iteration order is the sequence elements come out in when walking a hash map or set, which can differ across languages and versions.

optionExplanations: 少了字母序这一级，同分候选只能按 map 内部的迭代顺序输出，而这个顺序在不同语言、不同版本间可能不一样，结果就不稳定。
计数逻辑跟排序无关，缺 tie-break 不会让共同好友数变负。
tie-break 只影响排序阶段的输出顺序，不会让遍历阶段少访问候选。
排序复杂度顶多是 O(n log n) 级别的差异，不会因为少一级排序键就退化成指数级。
optionExplanations_en: Without the alphabetical level, tied candidates fall back to whatever order the map happens to iterate in — and that order can differ across languages and versions, so output isn't stable.
Counting logic is unrelated to sorting; missing a tie-break wouldn't turn mutual counts negative.
Tie-breaking only affects output order at sort time — it doesn't make the traversal visit fewer candidates.
Sorting complexity differs by at most an O(n log n) factor, not by dropping to exponential just from missing one sort key.

scenario: 你在面试中要把这个题归到 Graph Search & Pathfinding 模式。
scenario_en: In an interview, you need to classify this problem under the Graph Search and Pathfinding pattern.
q: 最有说服力的解释是什么？
q_en: What is the most convincing explanation?
options: 因为规则规定最多只返回 5 个名字
推荐候选正是从源点走两条边到达的节点
因为结果里带着候选名字字符串
因为排序键用到了一个负数写法
options_en: Because the rule caps the result at five names.
The recommendation candidates are exactly the nodes reached by walking two edges from the source.
Because the results contain candidate name strings.
Because the sort key uses a negative-number trick.
why: 共同好友规则直接对应二跳图遍历。它是 BFS 思路在推荐问题里的特化。
why_en: The mutual-friend rule is a two-edge graph traversal from the source user.
whenOtherWins: 如果推荐由全局文本相似度或 embedding 相似度决定，就不一定是图搜索主导。
tradeoff: 图遍历视角（结构驱动） vs 表面特征视角（字符串/数字细节）

termDefinitions.meaning: 从起点逐层向外扩展访问邻居的图遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, or Breadth-First Search, explores a graph outward layer by layer from a starting node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图遍历开始的起点，这里是发起推荐请求的用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source node is where a traversal starts, here the user requesting recommendations.

optionExplanations: 返回上限 5 只是输出截断的实现细节，跟这道题属于哪种算法模式无关。
候选资格「至少一个共同好友」本身就定义了从源点走两条边能到达的节点集合，这正是图搜索模式的核心特征。
结果里带名字字符串只是展示细节，不是判断算法模式的依据。
排序键用负数只是 Python 里实现降序的写法技巧，跟这题属于图搜索模式没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: The five-item cap is just an output-truncation detail, unrelated to which algorithm pattern this problem belongs to.
The eligibility rule — at least one mutual friend — literally defines the set of nodes reachable by walking two edges from the source, which is the core signature of a graph-search pattern.
Having name strings in the result is just a display detail, not evidence for classifying the algorithm pattern.
Using a negative number in the sort key is just a Python trick for descending order, unrelated to why this is a graph-search pattern.

scenario: 你看着 huge benchmark 的结果，要向面试官总结这组数据说明了什么设计结论。
scenario_en: You are looking at the huge benchmark results and need to summarize the design conclusion for the interviewer.
q: 这组 benchmark 数据（huge: 5000 users, 25000 edges, scan-all 361.8ms, two-hop 7.6ms）说明了什么？
q_en: What design conclusion do these benchmark numbers show: huge has 5000 users, 25000 edges, scan-all takes 361.8ms, and two-hop takes 7.6ms?
options: 这个提速只对 huge 数据集成立，换数据集就会反转
361.8ms 已经说明 scan-all 存在 bug，需要重写而不是优化
二跳遍历把候选空间从全网收窄到局部邻域，带来约 48 倍的实测提速
两种算法的渐进复杂度完全相同，只是常数因子不同
options_en: This speedup only holds for the huge dataset and would reverse on a different one.
The 361.8 millisecond result proves scan-all has a bug that needs a rewrite, not an optimization.
The two-hop walk narrows the candidate space from the whole network to a local neighborhood, giving roughly a 48x measured speedup.
Both algorithms have identical asymptotic complexity, differing only by a constant factor.
why: benchmark 量化了候选空间收窄带来的真实收益：48 倍不是常数因子差异，而是从 O(V·d) 降到局部邻域的结构性变化。
why_en: The benchmark quantifies a real structural win: the 48x gap comes from narrowing the candidate space, not from a constant-factor tweak.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种方案耗时的比值，用于说明结构性优化的收益规模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Speedup is the ratio between two runtimes, showing how large a structural optimization's payoff really is.

optionExplanations: 稀疏图下二跳邻域远小于全网这个前提没变，换成规模相近的稀疏图，提速方向不会反转。
361.8ms 是 scan-all 算法本身的成本，不是实现里的 bug——它按规则老老实实扫了全网，这属于优化空间的问题。
把候选生成收紧到二跳邻域而非全网扫描，才是那 48 倍差距的来源，这是算法结构的胜利，而不是简单调参能达到的效果。
两者渐进复杂度并不相同：scan-all 是 O(V·d)，二跳约是度数平方级，规模越大差距越明显，不只是常数因子。
optionExplanations_en: Two-hop stays much smaller than the full network on any sparse graph of similar shape, so the direction of the speedup doesn't flip.
361.8ms is the algorithm's inherent cost, not an implementation bug — it dutifully scans the whole network as designed; that's an optimization opportunity, not a defect.

Restricting candidate generation to the two-hop neighborhood instead of scanning the whole network is what produces that roughly 48x gap — a win from algorithm structure, not something simple tuning could reach.
The two algorithms don't share asymptotic complexity: scan-all is O(V times d), two-hop is roughly degree-squared, and the gap widens with scale, not just a constant factor.

scenario: scan-all 扫全网 V 个用户，对通过校验的候选做一次比较排序收尾。V 是用户数，d 是平均好友集大小。
scenario_en: Scan-all walks all V users, then finishes with one comparison sort of the candidates that passed the filter. V is the user count, d the average friend-set size.
q: 为什么每查询成本记为 O(V·d)，排序项 O(V·log V) 不算主导？
q_en: Why is the per-query cost written as O(V·d), with the sort term O(V·log V) not counted as dominant?
options: 排序只作用于通过校验的候选，数量远少于 V，被 O(V·d) 的扫描加交集成本盖过
计数都是小整数，比较排序会退化成 O(V) 的计数排序，排序项因此消失
排序每查询只调一次，摊到这次查询的 V 次交集上，均摊成本降到常数
O(V·log V) 恒小于 O(V·d)，因为 log V 在任何规模下都小于平均度数 d
options_en: The sort runs only over candidates that passed the filter, far fewer than V, so the O(V·d) scan-plus-intersection cost swamps it.
The counts are small integers, so the comparison sort degrades into an O(V) counting sort and the sort term vanishes.
The sort runs once per query, amortized across that query's V intersections, so its amortized cost drops to a constant.
O(V·log V) is always smaller than O(V·d) because log V is below the average degree d at any scale.
why: 总成本 = O(V) 扫描 + 每有效候选 O(d) 交集 + O(V·log V) 排序;排序只作用于正分候选(远少于 V),被 O(V·d) 盖过。O(V·d) 才是判断要不要换二跳算法的基准。
why_en: It's O(V) to scan plus O(d) per valid candidate plus an O(V log V) sort, but the sort touches only positive-score candidates, far fewer than V, so O(V·d) dominates.

termDefinitions.meaning: V 是网络里的用户总数,scan-all 的外层循环要走一遍所有 V。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: V is the total number of users in the network; scan-all's outer loop walks all of them.

termDefinitions.meaning: d 是平均好友集大小,一次共同好友交集的期望成本约 O(d)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: d is the average friend-set size; one mutual-friend intersection costs about O(d) on average.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠两两比较元素决定顺序的排序(归并/快排),n 个元素约做 n·log n 次工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A comparison sort orders elements by pairwise comparisons like merge or quicksort, doing about n log n work for n items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠桶计数而非比较来排小范围整数,可达 O(n),但不是通用排序会自动用的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counting sort orders small-range integers by bucketing rather than comparing, reaching O(n), but a generic sort does not fall back to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把偶发的昂贵操作成本平摊到多次操作上得到的平均成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Amortization spreads the cost of an occasional expensive operation across many operations to get an average cost.

optionExplanations: 排序的输入只是正分候选(通常几十个),V·log V 是宽松上限;主导成本是对全网 V 个用户各做一次 O(d) 交集。
计数排序才是 O(V),但代码调的是通用比较排序 sort(),不会自动退化,排序仍是 V·log V 级。
均摊针对偶发的昂贵操作,而排序每次查询都实打实跑一遍,是固定的一次性成本,摊不掉。
log V 未必小于 d:本例 log₂5000≈12 反而略大于 d≈10;排序不主导靠的是候选数少,不是这个不等式。
optionExplanations_en: The sort's input is only the positive-score candidates, usually a few dozen, so V·log V is a loose upper bound; the dominant cost is one O(d) intersection for each of V users.
Counting sort would be O(V), but the code calls a generic comparison sort() that never falls back to it, so the sort stays at V·log V.
Amortization applies to occasional expensive operations, but the sort actually runs on every query as a fixed one-time cost that cannot be spread away.
log V is not necessarily below d: here log2 of 5000 is about 12, slightly above d of about 10; the sort stays non-dominant because there are few candidates, not because of this inequality.

scenario: Inventory Packer 给你一个 warehouse catalog，要求返回的结果能用 item name 直接查到它所在的 bin id。
scenario_en: In Inventory Packer you get a warehouse catalog and must return a result where an item name looks up the bin id it landed in.
q: Inventory Packer 的题目规则包括哪些？
q_en: Which rules define the Inventory Packer problem?
options: 每个 item 有 weight 和 size
每个 bin 同时有 weight cap 和 size cap
item 不能拆分到多个 bin
输出是 bin id 到 item 列表的唯一格式
options_en: Every item has both a weight and a size.
Every bin enforces a weight cap and a size cap at the same time.
An item cannot be split across multiple bins.
The output must be formatted as bin id mapped to a list of items.
why: 输出要求是 item name 到 bin id 的 assignment。核心约束是两个容量维度同时满足，且物品不可拆。
why_en: The packer assigns indivisible weighted and sized items into bins with two simultaneous capacity limits.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

optionExplanations: 每个 item 都带这两个属性，可行性检查要同时看这两项数值。
bin 有两条独立上限，装箱前必须先确认两条都还有余量。
整份 item 只能进一个 bin，不允许拆成几份分开装。
实际输出按 item 名字对应到它所在的一个 bin id，不是 bin 对应一串 item 列表。
optionExplanations_en: Every item carries both attributes, so the fit check always looks at both numbers.
Each bin enforces two independent limits, so both need headroom before an item goes in.
A whole item goes into exactly one bin; it never gets split across several.
The real output maps each item name to the one bin id holding it, not a bin mapped to a list of items.

scenario: Bin 0 已经放了 Monitor(8kg,6size) 和 Keyboard(2kg,3size)，两者 weight 加起来是 10，正好把这个 bin 的 weight cap 用满；size 只用了 9。
scenario_en: Bin 0 already holds Monitor (8 kg, size 6) and Keyboard (2 kg, size 3). Their total weight is 10, exactly filling the weight cap, while size used is only 9.
q: 为什么这时候 Mouse(1kg,1size) 不能放进同一个 bin？
q_en: Why can Mouse (1 kg, size 1) not go into the same bin now?
options: 它说明这次判断里 size cap 从头到尾都没被逼近过，先不用管它
它说明 Monitor 和 Keyboard 现在应该拆开，分别放进两个不同的 bin
它说明只要一个维度满了，另一维度就算还有空间，也不能再放入新 item
它说明从这一刻起，之后所有物品都必须各自新开一个 bin 才行
options_en: It shows the size cap never came close to its limit in this check, so it can be set aside.
It shows Monitor and Keyboard should now be split apart into two separate bins.
It shows that once either dimension, weight or size, is full, no new item can go in even if the other still has room.
It shows every item from this point on must open its own separate bin.
why: weight 和 size 都是硬约束，任一维度超限都非法。装箱判断必须同时检查两个维度。
why_en: A bin is feasible only when both weight and size limits remain satisfied.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

optionExplanations: size 不是可以忽略的软约束，它和 weight 一样是必须同时满足的硬上限。
两件已放入的商品不需要重新拆分，问题只出在新来的 Mouse 放不进而已。
Bin 0 的 weight 已经封顶，哪怕 size 还剩 1，也照样判定放不下。
只是这一个 bin 满了，其它还没填满的 bin 依然可以正常接收新 item。
optionExplanations_en: The size cap isn't a soft guideline, it is just as hard a limit as weight.
The two items already placed don't need to be split up, the problem is only that Mouse has nowhere to go.
Bin 0's weight is already maxed out, so even one spare size unit doesn't let Mouse in.
Only this one bin is full; other bins that still have room keep accepting new items normally.

q: 填空：找到绝对最少 bin 数的通用 bin packing 是 {{NP-hard}}，所以 Inventory Packer 采用快速 {{heuristic}}。
q_en: Fill in: Finding the absolute minimum bin count for general bin packing is {{NP-hard}}, so Inventory Packer uses a fast {{heuristic}}.
text: 找到绝对最少 bin 数的通用 bin packing 是 {{NP-hard}}，所以 Inventory Packer 采用快速 {{heuristic}}。
why: 题目要的是在测试输入上接近最优且足够快，而不是证明全局最优。贪心启发式是合理选择。
why_en: Because exact bin packing is NP-hard, the practical goal is a fast near-optimal heuristic.

termDefinitions.meaning: NP-hard：还没有已知的多项式时间算法能保证求出精确最优解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NP-hard means no known polynomial-time algorithm is guaranteed to find the exact optimal solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: heuristic（启发式）：为了速度放弃全局最优保证，用经验规则快速给出足够好的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heuristic is a practical rule of thumb that trades a guaranteed optimum for a fast, good-enough answer.

scenario: 你要先写一个简单、正确、速度足够的装箱基线。
scenario_en: You need a simple, correct, fast-enough packing baseline first.
q: First-Fit 的规则是什么？
q_en: What is the First-Fit rule?
options: 对每个 item 都尝试所有已开 bin 的组合，挑出全局最优的分配方案，代价很高
按顺序放进第一个两个容量都够的已开 bin；都放不下才新开一个 bin
把 item 和 bin 都随机打乱，反复重排直到侥幸凑出一个合法分配
不管当前 bin 是否还有空间，每个 item 都直接各自新开一个独立 bin
options_en: Try every combination across all opened bins for each item and pick the globally optimal assignment, at high cost.
Process items in order and place each in the first already-open bin that satisfies both capacity limits; open a new bin only if none fit.
Shuffle items and bins randomly and keep reshuffling, hoping to stumble onto a legal assignment.
Open a brand-new bin for every item regardless of whether an existing bin still has room.
why: First-Fit 是纯贪心：第一个合法位置就提交，不回头。它实现简单且保证约束有效。
why_en: First-Fit greedily places each item into the first existing bin that can hold it.
tradeoff: 先合法即提交的贪心速度 vs 穷举比较求全局最优
whenOtherWins: 如果输入顺序对抗性强，先排序的 First-Fit Decreasing 通常更稳。

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  Item[Next item] --> Scan[Scan bins in order]
  Scan --> Fit{First fit found?}
  Fit -->|yes| Place[Place and stop]
  Fit -->|no| New[Open new bin]
  New --> Place
optionExplanations: 穷举所有组合能保证全局最优，但当 bin 数变多时开销爆炸，不是这里定义的规则。
First-Fit 就是按输入顺序扫描已开 bin，第一个两项容量都够的就直接放进去。
反复随机重排属于试错式做法，不是这个规则里确定性的一次扫描。
每次都新开 bin 会让 bin 数线性爆炸，完全没有复用已有空间。
optionExplanations_en: Exhaustive search over every combination can guarantee a global optimum, but its cost explodes as bins grow, that isn't what this rule describes.
First-Fit scans already-open bins in input order and places the item in the first one whose weight and size both still fit.
Randomly reshuffling and retrying is trial and error, not this rule's single deterministic pass.
Opening a new bin every time makes bin count blow up linearly and never reuses existing space.

scenario: Bin cap 是 weight 15、size 10；当前 bin 已用 weight 12、size 4，这时来了一个 (w4,s2) 的 item。
scenario_en: Bin caps are weight 15 and size 10; the current bin has used weight 12 and size 4, and then a (weight 4, size 2) item arrives.
q: `b.can_fit(item)` 必须同时验证哪些条件？
q_en: Which conditions must `b.can_fit(item)` check at the same time?
options: item.weight 不超过 bin 剩余 weight
item.size 不超过 bin 剩余 size
item.name 字母序排在 bin id 前面
两个容量条件都通过才可放入
options_en: The item's weight must not exceed the bin's remaining weight capacity.
The item's size must not exceed the bin's remaining size capacity.
The item's name must sort alphabetically before the bin id.
Both capacity conditions must pass before the item can be placed.
why: 两个 cap 任一超限都不能放。正确性测试会抓住只检查一个维度的实现。
why_en: A fit check must require both remaining weight and remaining size to be sufficient.

termDefinitions.meaning: can_fit：判断某个 item 能否放进某个 bin 的可行性检查函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: can_fit is the feasibility check that decides whether an item can be placed into a given bin.

optionExplanations: weight 检查只挡住重量超限的组合，是两项必检里的一项。
size 检查只挡住体积超限的组合，跟 weight 检查是并列的另一项。
item 名字和 bin id 的字母顺序跟能不能放进去没有任何关系。
只写一个维度合格就放行，会漏掉另一维度早已超限的非法组合。
optionExplanations_en: The weight check alone only blocks weight overruns, it's one of two required checks.
The size check blocks size overruns, sitting alongside the weight check as the second requirement.
Alphabetical order between item name and bin id has nothing to do with whether it fits.
Passing only one dimension lets illegal placements through where the other dimension is already over.

scenario: 你在 First-Fit 中找到了第一个能放当前 item 的 bin。
scenario_en: In First-Fit, you have found the first bin that can hold the current item.
q: 为什么 `break` 很关键？
q_en: Why is `break` critical here?
options: 没有 break 的话，后面每个 bin 的 `can_fit` 检查都会被强制跳过，永远判定放不下
break 触发后会自动新开一个 bin，把当前 item 重新放进这个刚开的 bin 里去
break 会让后面所有 bin 的两个容量检查都被跳过，从而让整个放置流程变快
item 已经放置成功，继续扫描可能造成重复放置，或把 assignment 覆盖成错误 bin id
options_en: Without break, the can_fit check on every later bin would be forced to skip and always report infeasible.
Triggering break automatically opens a new bin and re-places the current item into that freshly opened bin.
Break would skip both capacity checks on every remaining bin, making the whole placement loop faster.
The item is already placed; scanning on could double-place it or overwrite the assignment with the wrong bin id.
why: First-Fit 的定义就是第一个能放就停。继续循环既浪费，也可能覆盖记录。
why_en: First-Fit commits to the first feasible bin, so the bin loop must stop after placement.
tradeoff: 第一个可行 bin 立即停止 vs 继续扫描以寻找更优 bin
whenOtherWins: Best-Fit 需要扫描所有可行 bin 后再选剩余空间最小者，那时不能在第一个可行 bin 处 break。

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: can_fit：判断某个 item 能否放进某个 bin 的可行性检查函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: can_fit is the feasibility check that decides whether an item can be placed into a given bin.

termDefinitions.meaning: assignment：从 item name 映射到 bin id 的输出结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The assignment is the output map from item name to the bin id that holds it.

termDefinitions.meaning: break：跳出当前循环的控制语句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: break is the loop-control statement that exits the current loop immediately.

optionExplanations: break 只是跳出循环，并不会让后面 bin 的 can_fit 一律失败，这个因果关系是反的。
break 只是退出当前循环，不会触发任何新开 bin 的动作。
break 省下的是继续扫描的时间，不是让容量检查本身被跳过而变快。
item 已经落袋，继续往后扫会把它错误地又放一次，或把 assignment 覆盖成别的 bin id。
optionExplanations_en: Break just exits the loop, it doesn't make every later bin's can_fit call fail, that causal claim is backwards.
Break only exits the current loop, it never triggers opening a new bin on its own.
What break saves is the time spent scanning further, not the checks becoming faster by being skipped.
The item is already placed, scanning on risks double-placing it or overwriting the assignment with a different bin id.

scenario: First-Fit 扫完所有已有 bin 都放不下，进入 warehouse.new_bin() 分支；测试会校验 assignment 覆盖全部 item。
scenario_en: First-Fit scans every existing bin without a fit and falls into the warehouse.new_bin() branch, while the tests check that the assignment covers every item.
q: First-Fit 的“新开 bin”分支最常见的 bug 是什么？
q_en: What is the most common bug in First-Fit's open-new-bin branch?
options: 新开 bin 时忘记生成新的 bin_id，两个 bin 被记成同一个 id
新 bin 一旦创建，就会自动把后面所有剩余物品统统装进去
创建了新 bin，但忘记把 item 放进去，或忘记记录进 assignment
新 bin 不需要遵守任何 weight 或 size 容量限制，随便装
options_en: Forgetting to generate a fresh bin_id, so two different bins end up sharing the same id.
Once created, the new bin automatically absorbs every remaining item that comes after it.
A new bin gets created, but the current item never gets added to it or logged in the assignment.
The new bin does not need to respect any weight or size capacity limit, so anything goes.
why: warehouse 只负责创建空 bin，不会替你放 item。add 和 assignment 两步都不能漏。
why_en: Creating a bin does not place the item; the solver must add it and record the bin id.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: assignment：从 item name 映射到 bin id 的输出结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The assignment is the output map from item name to the bin id that holds it.

optionExplanations: id 复用确实会让 assignment 记录冲突，但这不是新开 bin 分支最容易踩的坑。
新 bin 只是一个空容器，不会自动把后面所有物品都吞进去。
只创建了空 bin，却漏掉把当前 item 塞进去、或漏了在 assignment 里记一笔，最容易漏这两步。
新 bin 和已有 bin 一样，也要老老实实遵守 weight 和 size 两条上限。
optionExplanations_en: A reused bin_id would corrupt the assignment map, but that isn't the most common slip in the open-new-bin branch.
A new bin is just an empty container, it doesn't automatically swallow every item that comes after it.
It's easy to create the empty bin but forget to add the item, or forget to log it in the assignment map.
A new bin has to obey the same weight and size caps as any existing bin, no exception.

scenario: warehouse 的 catalog 可能扩到几千个 item，你要判断 First-Fit 的运行时会不会先成为瓶颈。
scenario_en: The warehouse catalog may grow to a few thousand items, and you need to judge whether First-Fit runtime becomes the first bottleneck.
q: First-Fit 装 n 个物品、已开 b 个 bin 时总体复杂度如何描述？
q_en: How should you describe First-Fit's total complexity for n items and b opened bins?
options: O(log n)，因为每次放置都要先做一次二分查找来确定位置
O(n · b)，最坏情况 b = n 时会退化为 O(n²)
O(2ⁿ)，因为要枚举所有可能的子集组合来逐一比较
O(1)，因为每个 item 只放一次，处理完就直接算结束
options_en: O(log n), because each placement first does a binary search to find the spot.
O(n times b), which degrades to O(n squared) in the worst case when b equals n.
O(2 to the n), because it enumerates every possible subset combination to compare.
O(1), because each item is placed exactly once and that counts as finished.
why: 每个 item 最多扫一遍已有 bin，n×b 是 O(n·b)；最坏每个物品都新开 bin 时 b=n，退化成 O(n²)。这说明千级 catalog 下 First-Fit 仍够快，不必换算法。
why_en: First-Fit scans existing bins for each item, so n items times b bins gives O(n·b), which only degrades to O(n squared) when every item opens its own bin.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

optionExplanations: First-Fit 里没有二分查找这一步，它是线性扫描已开的 bin，不是 O(log n)。
每个 item 最多把已开的 b 个 bin 扫一遍，n 个 item 乘 b 次扫描就是这个量级。
枚举子集是穷举搜索的复杂度，First-Fit 从不回头比较，不会跑到指数级。
放一次不代表零开销，扫描已开 bin 找位置本身就要花时间，不是常数。
optionExplanations_en: First-Fit never does a binary search, it linearly scans already-open bins, so it isn't O(log n).
Each item scans at most the b already-open bins once, so n items times b scans lands here.
Enumerating subsets is exhaustive-search complexity; First-Fit never backtracks to compare options.
Placing an item isn't free, scanning open bins to find a spot still costs time, so it isn't constant.

scenario: 评测套件有三组输入：basic catalog、四个相同 item、以及专门打乱顺序来打贪心的 adversarial large catalog。
scenario_en: The suite has three inputs: the basic catalog, four identical items, and an adversarial large catalog ordered specifically to attack a greedy pass.
q: First-Fit 在哪些测试上没问题？
q_en: Which tests does First-Fit handle correctly?
options: 只在空输入上能通过
只在 item 可以被拆分时才能通过
在所有测试上都没问题，包括 adversarial large catalog
在 basic test 和四个相同 item 的 test 上都没问题
options_en: It only passes on an empty input.
It only passes when items are allowed to be split.
It passes every test, including the adversarial large catalog.
It passes both the basic test and the four-identical-item test.
why: First-Fit 正确性没问题，普通输入也能装得可以。失败出现在输入顺序专门对它不利的大 catalog。
why_en: First-Fit is valid and passes simple cases, but it is vulnerable to adversarial item order.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

optionExplanations: 空输入当然能过，但这不是它唯一能过的场景，说得太窄了。
题目从头到尾都不允许拆分 item，这个前提在任何测试里都不成立。
对抗性大 catalog 恰恰是它翻车的地方，说全部测试都没问题不准确。
在普通输入和同质物品这两类测试里，First-Fit 给出的结果都合法且够用。
optionExplanations_en: It does pass on an empty input, but claiming that's the only case it handles is too narrow.
Splitting items is never allowed in this problem, so this premise never actually holds.
The adversarial large catalog is exactly where it stumbles, so claiming every test passes is inaccurate.
On ordinary input and on identical-item input, First-Fit's results stay legal and good enough.

scenario: 评测套件专门设计了一个大 catalog 来暴露 First-Fit 对输入顺序的敏感性。
scenario_en: The test suite includes a large catalog designed to expose First-Fit's sensitivity to input order.
q: 填空：large catalog 有 {{30}} 个 items，bin cap 为 weight {{15}}、size {{10}}。
q_en: Fill in: The large catalog has {{30}} items, with bin caps of weight {{15}} and size {{10}}.
text: large catalog 有 {{30}} 个 items，bin cap 为 weight {{15}}、size {{10}}。
why: 这组数字不是随便定的：前一半 item 先把很多 bin 填到接近满，后一半大 item 因此挤不进去。它是后续分析“为什么 First-Fit 会开 22 个 bin”的输入基线。
why_en: The large catalog is deliberately sized and ordered to expose First-Fit's sensitivity to input order.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

scenario: large catalog 是一个 30 个 item 的对抗性输入：前 15 个 item 的 size 是 4，后 15 个 size 是 6，bin cap 是 weight 15、size 10。
scenario_en: The large catalog is a 30-item adversarial input: the first 15 items have size 4, the last 15 have size 6, and each bin caps weight at 15 and size at 10.
q: large catalog 中 First-Fit 为什么会开很多孤立 size-6 item 的 bin？
q_en: Why does First-Fit open many isolated bins for size-6 items in the large catalog?
options: size-4 两两配对填到 size 8，size-6 一放进去就超过上限
weight cap 才是这里真正的限制，size cap 全程根本就没起作用
size-6 item 天生就不能和任何其它 item 共享同一个 bin，注定孤立
First-Fit 会刻意跳过还有空间的旧 bin，特地去开一个全新的空 bin
options_en: Size-four items pair up to fill bins to size eight, so a size-six item pushes past the cap.
The weight cap is actually the binding limit here, and the size cap never comes into play at all.
Size-six items are inherently unable to share a bin with any other item, doomed to be alone.
First-Fit deliberately skips bins that still have room and opens a brand-new empty bin instead.
why: size 8 + 6 = 14 超过 size cap，早期看似合理的配对留下了无用空隙。后面大物品只能单独开 bin。
why_en: First-Fit packs early size-four items into bins that later cannot accept size-six items.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  Small[Size 4 items first] --> Pair[Pairs fill size 8]
  Pair --> Gap[Only size 2 left]
  Big[Later size 6 item] --> NoFit[Cannot fit]
  NoFit --> Alone[New lonely bin]
optionExplanations: 前 15 个 size-4 两两凑成 size 8 后，剩下的 2 格空间塞不下任何 size-6 item。
weight cap 在这批数据里其实没被撑满，真正卡住的是 size 这一维。
size-6 item 不是天生排斥合租，只是恰好没有 bin 还留着够大的空隙。
First-Fit 不会主动跳过有空位的旧 bin，它就是老实检查每个旧 bin 装不装得下。
optionExplanations_en: Once the first fifteen size-four items pair up to fill bins to size eight, only two units of room remain, too little for a size-six item.
The weight cap never actually gets maxed out in this dataset, size is the dimension doing the blocking.
Size-six items aren't inherently unshareable, it's just that no bin happens to have enough leftover room.
First-Fit never deliberately skips a bin with room, it honestly checks whether each old bin still fits the item.

scenario: large catalog 是刻意设计的对抗性输入（30 个 item，bin cap weight 15、size 10），运营给的预算是 18 个 bin。
scenario_en: The large catalog is a deliberately adversarial input with 30 items, bin caps of weight 15 and size 10, and an operations budget of 18 bins.
q: 填空：large catalog 中 First-Fit 使用 {{22}} 个 bin，超过 {{18}} 个 bin 预算。
q_en: Fill in: On the large catalog, First-Fit uses {{22}} bins, exceeding the {{18}}-bin budget.
text: large catalog 中 First-Fit 使用 {{22}} 个 bin，超过 {{18}} 个 bin 预算。
why: 22 个 bin 是合法但不经济的结果；18 是运营定的 bin 数预算（给定目标，不是公式推出来的），超出意味着仓储成本没压下来。
why_en: Twenty-two bins is a valid packing, but it misses the operations team's eighteen-bin budget target.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

scenario: First-Fit 因为小物品先到而把很多 bin 填成不适合后续大物品的形状。
scenario_en: First-Fit lets early small items shape many bins in a way that later large items cannot use.
q: 最小改动的修复是什么？
q_en: What is the smallest useful fix?
options: 把所有 item 都随机打乱顺序，反复重复尝试直到凑巧成功
把每个 item 都改成新开一个独立 bin，从此不再复用旧 bin
先按 footprint 降序排序，再运行同一个 First-Fit 放置循环
只把 item 按名字字母顺序重新排序，再运行同一个 First-Fit 放置循环
options_en: Shuffle every item randomly and keep retrying until it happens to work.
Give every item its own new bin and stop reusing existing bins from then on.
Sort items by descending footprint first, then run the same First-Fit placement loop.
Reorder items purely by alphabetical item name, then run the same First-Fit placement loop.
why: First-Fit Decreasing 改变的是输入顺序，不是放置规则。先放难放的大物品，再让小物品填空。
why_en: First-Fit Decreasing fixes the order by placing larger-footprint items before smaller fillers.
tradeoff: 重排输入顺序（改动小） vs 重写放置规则本身（改动大）
whenOtherWins: 如果输入已经按合理的大到小顺序到达，原始 First-Fit 可能得到同样结果。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Footprint here is the weight-plus-size estimate of how hard an item is to place; a larger footprint means a harder fit.

optionExplanations: 随机打乱再赌运气不是可控修法，重跑多次也不保证稳定改善。
让每个物品都单开一个 bin 直接放弃了复用空间，bin 数只会更多不会更少。
只改到达顺序、不动放置规则，先让占位大的物品占好空 bin，小物品再去填缝。
按名字字母排序跟物品占多大空间毫无关系，就算接上同一个放置循环也解决不了顺序敏感问题。
optionExplanations_en: Shuffling randomly and hoping for the best isn't a controllable fix, repeated runs give no guaranteed improvement.
Giving every item its own bin abandons space reuse entirely, bin count only goes up, never down.
It only changes arrival order, not the placement rule, letting bulky items claim empty bins first so small ones fill gaps after.
Alphabetical name order has nothing to do with how much space an item needs, so even feeding it into the same placement loop still doesn't fix order sensitivity.

q: 为什么排序必须是 decreasing，而不是 ascending？
q_en: Why must the sort be decreasing rather than ascending?
options: ascending 排序之后，can_fit 的两个容量检查会被跳过，装箱直接变非法
descending 先放大物品占位，小物品后填空隙；ascending 会重现先失败的顺序

ascending 顺序会让 Python 的 sorted 函数直接对数字类型报错崩溃

Descending order places large items first so bins start full, small items fill leftover gaps; ascending recreates the failure order.
Either ascending or descending order can be mathematically proven to reach the globally optimal bin count.
Ascending order makes Python's sorted function crash with an error on numeric types.
why: 大物品需要更空的 bin，小物品更容易塞进剩余空间。先难后易是这个启发式的核心。
why_en: Descending order places hard-to-fit items while bins are still empty.
tradeoff: 先难后易（descending） vs 先易后难（ascending）
whenOtherWins: 如果业务目标是保持原始处理顺序而不是减少 bin 数，可能不能重排输入。

sorted 函数对数字排序没有方向限制，ascending 不会让它报错。
optionExplanations_en: Sort direction doesn't touch can_fit's logic, both capacity checks still run exactly the same way.
Placing large items first claims the bin's skeleton while it's still empty, then small items fill the gaps; ascending puts small items first and repeats the original failure order.
Neither direction has a proof of global optimality, descending is just empirically less likely to leave dead space.
sorted has no directional restriction on numeric sorting, ascending order won't make it error.

q: FFD 的总体复杂度是哪一项？

options: O(n log n + n · b)，最坏仍会退化到 O(n²)
O(n²)，因为排序本身就要两两比较所有 item
O(n³)，因为要为每个 item 重新排序一次所有 bin

options_en: O(n log n plus n times b), which still degrades to O(n squared) in the worst case.
O(n squared), because sorting itself compares every pair of items.
O(n cubed), because every item re-sorts the entire bin list.
O(b), because the sorting overhead can be ignored entirely.
why: 排序是 O(n log n)，放置循环仍是同一套 O(n·b)；最坏情况（每个 item 都新开 bin）两者相加仍退化成 O(n²)，说明排序这步不会成为新瓶颈。
why_en: Sorting adds O(n log n) on top of the same O(n times b) placement loop, so the worst case still collapses to O(n squared).

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

optionExplanations: 多出来的只是一次 O(n log n) 排序，加上原来那套 O(n·b) 放置循环，量级并没有质变。
排序确实要比较，但用的是 O(n log n) 的高效算法，不是两两全比较的平方级。
放置阶段并不会为每个 item 重新排一遍所有 bin，排序只在开头做一次。
排序本身要遍历并比较全部 n 个 item，开销不可能小到可以完全忽略。
optionExplanations_en: The only addition is one O(n log n) sort on top of the same O(n times b) placement loop, no qualitative jump.
Sorting does compare elements, but it uses an efficient O(n log n) algorithm, not an all-pairs quadratic comparison.
The placement phase never re-sorts all the bins for every item, sorting happens exactly once up front.
Sorting itself has to traverse and compare all n items, so its cost can't be dismissed as negligible.

scenario: 面试官追问 FFD 到底有没有理论上界，还是纯经验之谈。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether FFD has any theoretical bound or is just empirical.
q: 填空：经典一维 FFD 有约 {{(11/9) * OPT + 6/9}} 的最坏情况 bin 数上界。
q_en: Fill in: Classic one-dimensional FFD has a worst-case bin-count bound of about {{(11/9) * OPT + 6/9}}.
text: 经典一维 FFD 有约 {{(11/9) * OPT + 6/9}} 的最坏情况 bin 数上界。
why: 这个证明是标准一维 bin packing 的结果，给出了相对 OPT 的最坏倍数。本文两维 cap 和 summed key 不直接被该证明覆盖，但方向性结论一致：FFD 通常远好于 First-Fit。
why_en: The classic FFD approximation bound applies to one-dimensional bin packing, not directly to this two-cap variant.

scenario: 业务改成必须证明最少 bin 数，输入规模很小，可以接受更慢算法。
scenario_en: The requirement changes: you must prove the minimum bin count, the input is small, and a slower algorithm is acceptable.
q: 更合适的方向是什么？
q_en: What direction is more appropriate?
options: 继续只用 First-Fit，不对现有代码做任何改动或调整，照旧跑下去
只是把 item 的名字字段改成按字母降序，重新排一遍序而已，不动放置
改用 branch-and-bound 或 IP 去搜索证明精确最优解
直接在 can_fit 里把 size cap 这一维约束整个忽略掉不查，图省事
options_en: Keep using plain First-Fit and make no changes to the existing code at all, just keep running it.
Just re-sort items by their name field in descending alphabetical order, leaving placement untouched.
Switch to branch-and-bound or IP to search for and prove the exact optimum.
Simply drop the size cap dimension out of can_fit entirely to save the trouble.
why: 精确最优需要搜索或约束求解，通常只适合小输入。FFD 是近似启发式，不提供两维全局最优证明。
why_en: Exact optimality calls for search or integer programming rather than a greedy heuristic.
tradeoff: 精确最优但慢（搜索/IP） vs 近似启发式但快（FFD）
whenOtherWins: 在本文测试这种中等输入和近似目标下，FFD 更简单且足够快。

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: branch-and-bound：通过剪枝系统搜索所有候选分配，找到证明最优的解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound systematically searches candidate assignments while pruning bad branches to prove optimality.

termDefinitions.meaning: IP（整数规划）：把装箱问题写成整数约束的数学规划，交给求解器求精确解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Integer programming formulates the packing problem as integer-constrained equations and hands it to a solver for an exact answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

optionExplanations: 继续用 First-Fit 拿到的只是合法解，没法满足业务要证明最少 bin 数的新要求。
按字母重排跟物品占用的容量没关系，不会朝着找最优解的方向前进。
输入小、能接受更慢，正好是搜索式精确解法值得上场的场景，用它才能真正证明最优。
直接不检查 size cap 会让输出变成非法装箱，不是解决最优性问题的办法。
optionExplanations_en: Sticking with First-Fit only gives a legal packing, it can't satisfy a requirement to prove the minimum bin count.
Re-sorting by alphabet has nothing to do with how much capacity items use, it doesn't move toward an optimal solution.
A small input that can tolerate being slower is exactly when a search-based exact method earns its keep.
Simply skipping the size cap check turns the output into an illegal packing, that doesn't solve optimality.

scenario: FFD 已经通过全部测试，面试官追问还有没有同族启发式能把平均 bin 数再压一点。
scenario_en: FFD already passes every test, and the interviewer asks whether a sibling heuristic can shave the average bin count a bit further.
q: Best-Fit Decreasing 和 First-Fit Decreasing 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between Best-Fit Decreasing and First-Fit Decreasing?
options: BFD 完全不需要先排序这一步，只有 FFD 才需要先排序再放置，这点上两者不同
都先按 footprint 降序排序；BFD 挑剩余空间最少的可行 bin，FFD 挑第一个可行 bin
BFD 会直接忽略 weight 和 size 两个容量限制，只有 FFD 才检查容量，BFD 不查
两者在放置规则、排序方式和实现复杂度上完全等价，彼此毫无区别，是同一个算法
options_en: BFD skips the sorting step entirely; only FFD needs to sort before placing, that's the difference between them.
Both sort by descending footprint first; BFD picks the feasible bin with the least remaining room, FFD picks the first feasible bin.
BFD ignores both the weight and size capacity limits, while only FFD checks them, BFD skips capacity entirely.
The two are completely equivalent in placement rule, sort order, and implementation complexity, essentially one algorithm.
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Sort[Sort desc by footprint] --> FFD[FFD: first feasible bin]
  Sort --> BFD[BFD: feasible bin with least leftover]
why: BFD 的放置规则更细，通常平均略好，但实现也更复杂。本文 FFD 已通过所有测试。
why_en: Best-Fit Decreasing changes the placement rule after the same descending sort.
tradeoff: 更省 bin 数但扫描更多（BFD） vs 更简单但可能多用几个 bin（FFD）

optionExplanations: BFD 同样要先排序，跳过排序这一步的说法不成立。
两者都先按 footprint 降序排列；差别只在放进哪个 bin：FFD 抓第一个能装的，BFD 挑剩余空间最少的那个。
BFD 和 FFD 一样要检查两条容量限制，不会因为换了放置规则就不看容量。
两者放置规则明显不同，一个是第一可行、一个是最紧可行，实现复杂度也不一样。
optionExplanations_en: BFD also needs the sort step first, claiming it skips sorting doesn't hold up.
Both sort by descending footprint first; the difference is only which bin gets the item: FFD grabs the first that fits, BFD picks the one with least room left.
BFD checks both capacity limits exactly like FFD does, switching the placement rule doesn't drop the checks.
Their placement rules clearly differ, one takes the first feasible bin and the other the tightest, so complexity differs too.

scenario: FFD 已经通过测试，但你想在平均 bin 数上再挤一点提升。

把每个 item 都单独开一个新 bin，不再复用
直接删掉 assignment 这个返回值
Best-Fit Decreasing，把 item 放进剩余空间最少的可行 bin
options_en: First-Fit Ascending, processing items by ascending footprint.
Give every item its own new bin instead of reusing existing ones.
Just remove the assignment return value entirely.
Best-Fit Decreasing, placing each item into the feasible bin with the least remaining room.

tradeoff: 平均 bin 数更少但扫描更多（BFD） vs 实现更简单（FFD）
whenOtherWins: 如果面试目标是最短可通过实现，FFD 已经足够时不要过度工程化。

Placing each item into the tightest still-feasible bin can shave off a few more bins on average, at the cost of scanning more candidates.

q: 把 First-Fit 在 adversarial catalog 中失败的因果链排成正确顺序。

steps: 前 15 个 size-4 item 先到，许多 bin 被两两装到 size 8

剩余 size-6 item 大多只能各自新开 bin

why_en: First-Fit's failure comes from early placements creating gaps that later large items cannot use.

q: First-Fit 和 First-Fit Decreasing 在实现上的核心差异是什么？
q_en: What is the core implementation difference between First-Fit and First-Fit Decreasing?
options: FFD 在同一个放置循环之前，多加了一步按 footprint 降序排序
FFD 不需要调用 `can_fit` 做容量检查，因为排序已经保证每个 item 都能放进当前 bin
First-Fit 从来不会新开 bin，只会复用已有 bin
FFD 会在放置失败后回溯，撤销之前已经做出的选择
options_en: FFD adds one extra step before the same placement loop: sorting items by descending footprint.
FFD never calls can_fit to check capacity, because sorting already guarantees every item fits into the current bin.
First-Fit never opens a new bin and only reuses existing ones.
FFD backtracks and undoes earlier placements when a later item fails to fit.
why: 两者的放置规则完全一致：第一个可行 bin。不同只在 item 到达顺序。
why_en: FFD is First-Fit preceded by descending item ordering.
tradeoff: 多一步排序换更好的 bin 数（FFD） vs 零预处理但顺序敏感（First-Fit）

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD：先把 item 按 footprint 降序排序，再运行同一套 First-Fit 放置逻辑。

options: 会自动变成 Best-Fit 而不是 First-Fit
会保证得到全局最优的 bin 数
会更接近原始未排序时小物品先到的失败顺序，结果通常更差

why: ascending 把容易放的小 item 提前处理，可能再次堵住大 item 所需空间。它和修复目标相反。

options: 放入第一个可行 bin 后忘记 break
