termDefinitions.meaning: 给定 clue 和线长，枚举该线所有合法填法的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A line possibility generator enumerates every valid layout for a line given its clue and length.

scenario: 你要写传播版 solver，它必须在每轮之间保留足够状态才能继续收缩候选。
scenario_en: You're writing the propagation solver, and it has to carry enough state between rounds to keep shrinking the candidates.
q: 传播版 solver 需要同时维护哪些状态？（多选）
q_en: What state must a propagation-based solver maintain? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 当前 grid 的已知 UNKNOWN/FILLED/EMPTY
每一行剩余可能候选列表
每一列剩余可能候选列表
所有历史失败棋盘的完整列表
options_en: The grid's currently known UNKNOWN, FILLED, and EMPTY cells.
Each row's remaining candidate layout list.
Each column's remaining candidate layout list.
A full history list of every previously failed board.
why: 传播靠 grid 与行列候选互相收缩；历史失败棋盘不是核心状态，回溯栈自然保存分支。
why_en: The propagation solver maintains the grid plus remaining candidate layouts for every row and column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未被确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell has not been determined yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定被涂色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FILLED is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed colored in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定为空白。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EMPTY is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed blank.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

optionExplanations: grid 记录每格当前确定到什么程度，是传播判断「这格已知」还是「仍待推」的基础。
行候选列表随着传播不断收缩，收缩到只剩一种时就能推出这一行的强制格。
列候选和行候选同理，两边互相过滤才是传播能级联推导的关键。
失败棋盘不需要记录，回溯栈本身就负责撤销和尝试下一分支，留着历史只会浪费内存。
optionExplanations_en: The grid tracks how determined each cell currently is, which is the base state propagation reads and updates.
Row candidate lists keep shrinking as propagation runs, and once only one layout remains, that row's forced cells drop out.
Column candidates work the same way, and it's this mutual filtering across both axes that drives the cascade.
Failed boards don't need to be kept — the recursion stack already handles undoing and trying the next branch, so history just wastes memory.

q: 补全候选过滤规则：
q_en: Complete the candidate-filtering rule:
text: 过滤一条线的候选时，保留那些在每个已知格上都与 grid {{一致}} 的候选；UNKNOWN 格则 {{不限制}} 候选。
why: 已知格是已经被传播或猜测确认的约束，候选必须服从；UNKNOWN 还没有信息，不能提前排除。
why_en: Filtering keeps candidates that agree with known cells while unknown cells impose no constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未被确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell has not been determined yet.

scenario: 传播版扫描一条线的全部剩余候选，想在不做任何猜测的前提下确定某些格子。
scenario_en: The propagation solver scans all remaining candidates of one line, trying to fix cells without guessing at all.
q: 传播中的 overlap argument 指的是什么？
q_en: What does the overlap argument mean in propagation?
options: overlap 指两个 run 允许物理重叠占位
一条线剩余候选在某格值相同，该格就被强制为这个值
行 clue 与列 clue 在交叉格上可互相覆盖
候选数不为 1 时，传播就一定推不出格子
options_en: Overlap means two runs are allowed to physically overlap in placement.
If a line's remaining candidates agree on one cell, that cell is forced to that value.
Row and column clues can overwrite each other's value at the crossing cell.
As soon as more than one candidate remains, propagation can never force any cell in that line.
why: 某格在所有合法候选中都相同，说明无论最终选哪个候选，该格都必须是这个值。
why_en: The overlap argument marks a cell forced when every remaining layout for that line gives it the same value.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Poss[Remaining line candidates] --> Same{same value at cell}
  Same -->|yes| Force[write forced cell]
  Same -->|no| Unknown[keep unknown]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条线所有剩余候选在某格取值相同时，直接把该格定为这个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The overlap argument forces a cell value when every remaining candidate layout for that line agrees on it.

optionExplanations: overlap argument 讲的是候选之间在某格取值一致，不是两个 run 本身允许在图形上物理重叠。
只要一条线剩下的每种候选在某格都给出同一个值，无论最终选哪个候选那格都必须是这个值。
行 clue 和列 clue 各自独立推导同一个格子，取值必须一致才成立，不存在互相覆盖删除。
候选数大于 1 时仍可能在某些格子上完全一致，那些格子照样能被强制推出，不是数量大于 1 就完全推不动。
optionExplanations_en: The overlap argument is about candidates agreeing on one cell's value, not about two runs physically overlapping in placement.
As long as every remaining candidate for a line agrees on one cell, that cell must take that value no matter which candidate ends up chosen.
Row and column clues are derived independently for the same cell and must agree — one clue can't simply overwrite the other.
Even with more than one candidate left, some cells can still agree across all of them and get forced — it isn't true that more than one candidate blocks every deduction.

scenario: 一条长度 5 的线，clue 是 `[4]`；只有两种合法摆放：从第 0 格开始，或从第 1 格开始。
scenario_en: A length-5 line has clue [4], and the only two valid placements start at cell 0 or cell 1.
q: 这两种摆放会强制哪些格子？
q_en: Which cells are forced by these two placements?
options: 列 0、4 必定 FILLED
列 1、2、3 必定 FILLED
所有格子必定 EMPTY
没有任何格子能推出
options_en: Columns 0 and 4 must be FILLED.
Columns 1, 2, and 3 must be FILLED.
Every cell must be EMPTY.
No cell can be deduced at all.
why: 长度 4 的 run 只能从 0 或 1 开始，两种摆放都覆盖中间三格，因此这些格子是 forced filled。
why_en: A length-four run in a five-cell line must cover the three middle cells in every valid placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定被涂色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FILLED is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed colored in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定为空白。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EMPTY is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed blank.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

optionExplanations: 格 0 和格 4 恰好是两种摆放里各自会变化的那两端，不是共同的部分。
只有两种合法摆放，无论挑哪一种，格 1、2、3 在两边都会被涂上，所以它们必然是 FILLED。
clue `[4]` 明确要求有一个长度 4 的 filled run，不可能整条线都 empty。
两种摆放对中间三格给出同样的值，这正是 overlap argument 能直接推出格子的例子。
optionExplanations_en: Cell 0 and cell 4 are exactly the two endpoints that differ between the two placements, not the shared part.
Only two placements are legal, and whichever one you pick, cells 1, 2, and 3 end up filled either way, so they're forced FILLED.
The clue [4] requires one filled run of length 4, so the whole line being empty is impossible.
Both placements agree on the same value for the middle three cells — this is exactly what the overlap argument catches.

scenario: 你有一条 line 的当前已知格和该线当前剩余候选，需要过滤掉与已知格冲突的候选。
scenario_en: You have the current known cells for one line and its remaining candidates, and you need to filter out candidates that conflict with known cells.
q: 哪段代码表达了文章里的 `_filter_against`？
q_en: Which code snippet expresses the article's _filter_against logic?
options: [p for p in possibilities if all(line[i] == p[i] for i in range(0, len(line), 1))]
[p for p in possibilities if all(l == UNKNOWN or l == q for l, q in zip(line, p))]
[p for p in possibilities if p[0] == line[0] and p[-1] == line[-1]]
[p for p in possibilities if any(line[i] == p[i] for i in range(0, len(line), 1))]
options_en: Keep candidates that match the line at every position, UNKNOWN cells included.
Keep candidates that agree wherever the cell is known; UNKNOWN imposes nothing.
Keep candidates only when their first and last cell match, ignoring the middle.
Keep candidates that agree with the line in at least one position.
why: 候选只需要匹配已知格；UNKNOWN 位置不能要求候选等于 UNKNOWN。
why_en: Filtering keeps candidates that match every known cell and ignores unknown positions.
whenOtherWins: 如果 line 已经完整无 UNKNOWN，可以直接比较整条线的 run 是否等于 clue。
tradeoff: 逐位过滤已知格（准确但每轮要扫全候选）vs 只查首尾（快但漏检中间矛盾）
codeSample:
def _filter_against(possibilities, line):
    # UNKNOWN 位置不限制候选，已知格必须逐位相同
    return [p for p in possibilities
            if all(l == UNKNOWN or l == q
                   for l, q in zip(line, p))]
optionExplanations: UNKNOWN 不是一个具体状态，把它当成必须相等的固定值，会把每个候选都判成不匹配。
已知格必须逐位匹配，UNKNOWN 格不参与比较——正好对应候选过滤该有的语义。
只查首尾会漏掉中间任何位置的冲突，过滤形同虚设。
`any` 只要一处相同就放行，几乎所有候选都能活下来，候选表根本不会收缩。
optionExplanations_en: UNKNOWN isn't a concrete state; treating it as a fixed value to match wrongly rejects every candidate.
Known cells must match position by position while UNKNOWN cells impose no constraint — exactly what candidate filtering should do.
Checking only the endpoints misses any conflict in the middle, so the filter does nothing useful.
With any, a candidate survives by agreeing in just one position, so the list barely shrinks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未被确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell has not been determined yet.

scenario: 传播中某一行按已知格过滤后候选列表变成空，solver 要决定这条分支怎么办。
scenario_en: During propagation a row's candidate list goes empty after filtering against the known cells, and the solver must decide what that means.
q: 传播中过滤某行或某列后候选列表为空，意味着什么？
q_en: What does an empty candidate list mean after filtering a row or column in propagation?
options: 这条线其实已经 solved，只是忘了在 grid 上标记完成
当前已知格与该线 clue 互不兼容，分支应立即失败
可以先跳过这条线继续传播，回头再补上随便一种候选
这说明这条 clue 写错了，应当在候选生成阶段就修正它
options_en: This line is actually already solved; the grid just forgot to mark it complete.
The known cells are incompatible with that line's clue, so the branch should fail immediately.
You can skip this line for now, keep propagating, and later patch it with whichever candidate is convenient.
It means this clue itself was written wrong, so it should be fixed back at the candidate-generation step.
why: 零候选说明没有任何合法线布局能满足当前已知状态；在搜索中这就是猜错后的快速矛盾。
why_en: An empty candidate list is a contradiction because no valid line layout remains compatible with the known cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某条线过滤候选后列表变空，说明当前分支不可能成立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contradiction is an empty candidate list showing the current branch cannot be valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

optionExplanations: 候选为空说明没有任何合法排布存在，不是「已经 solved 但没打标记」——这两种状态完全不同。
候选列表空了，意味着没有任何合法布局能满足当前已知格，这个分支必须立即判失败。
跳过不检查会让矛盾状态被带进后续传播和搜索，之后更难定位问题，而且也没有「随便一种」合法候选可以补。
candidate 为空反映的是当前分支与已知格冲突，不是这条 clue 本身写错了，不该去改动生成阶段的 clue。
optionExplanations_en: An empty candidate list means no valid layout exists at all — it isn't the same as being 'solved but unmarked,' those are different states.
An empty candidate list means no valid layout can satisfy the known cells anymore, so this branch must fail right away.
Skipping the check just carries the contradiction into later propagation and search, making it harder to trace — and there's no legitimate 'any candidate' to patch in later.
An empty candidate list reflects a conflict between the branch and known cells, not a mistake in the clue itself — the clue shouldn't be edited back at generation time.

q: 把一次传播循环的核心步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the core steps of one propagation loop in the correct order:
steps: 过滤每条列候选，提交列中所有候选一致的格子
若某行或列候选为空，返回矛盾
过滤每条行候选，提交行中所有候选一致的格子
只要本轮填了新格，就继续下一轮
一整轮没有新格时停止传播
why: 行和列的顺序可以互换，关键是每轮过滤候选、发现 forced cell，并在没有变化时收敛。
why_en: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates, commits forced cells, detects contradictions, and stops when a full pass makes no changes.
tradeoff: 跑到没有新格再停（信息榨干但每轮要扫全表）vs 一有新格就立刻回溯尝试（分支更早但推理不彻底）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Start[Start pass] --> Filter[Filter candidates]
  Filter --> Empty{any list empty}
  Empty -->|yes| Fail[contradiction]
  Empty -->|no| Force[derive forced cells]
  Force --> Changed{changed}
  Changed -->|yes| Start
  Changed -->|no| Done[fixed point]

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某条线过滤候选后列表变空，说明当前分支不可能成立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contradiction is an empty candidate list showing the current branch cannot be valid.

scenario: 传播已经收敛，但 grid 里仍有 UNKNOWN，且没有任何线能再推出 forced cell。
scenario_en: Propagation has converged, but the grid still contains UNKNOWN cells and no line can produce another forced cell.
q: 下一步应该怎么做？
q_en: What should the solver do next?
options: 直接把当前半成品 grid 当作最终答案返回
挑一个 UNKNOWN 格猜状态，再重新传播
清空所有候选列表，从头重新生成一遍
从此以后完全忽略列 clue 只看行 clue
options_en: Return the current half-filled grid as the final answer.
Guess a state for one UNKNOWN cell, then propagate again.
Clear every candidate list and regenerate everything from scratch.
Ignore column clues from now on and rely on row clues only.
why: 传播不能解决局部歧义时，回溯负责试探；每个猜测后再传播能让错误分支快速产生矛盾。
why_en: When propagation stalls, the solver guesses an unknown cell and runs propagation again so wrong guesses fail quickly.
whenOtherWins: 如果传播已填满所有格子，只需要验证 solved，不必再猜。
tradeoff: 猜测后重新传播（错误分支快速矛盾）vs 直接暴力搜完剩余格子（不利用已推出的约束）
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Fixed[Propagation fixed point] --> Unknown{unknown cells left}
  Unknown -->|no| Solved[check solved]
  Unknown -->|yes| Guess[pick first unknown]
  Guess --> Filled[assume filled]
  Guess --> Empty[assume empty]
  Filled --> Prop1[propagate]
  Empty --> Prop2[propagate]
optionExplanations: grid 里还有 UNKNOWN，题目要求返回完整解或 None，半成品不满足要求。
传播推不动时说明只剩局部歧义，挑一个 UNKNOWN 格假设一个状态、猜完立刻重新传播，能快速验证对错。
候选内容并没有变化，重新生成只是白白重复一遍计算。
丢掉列 clue 会让能推出的格子少一半，传播能力直接大幅削弱。
optionExplanations_en: The grid still has UNKNOWN cells; the requirement is to return a full solution or null, not a half-finished grid.
When propagation stalls it's just local ambiguity — guessing one UNKNOWN cell's state and re-propagating right after quickly confirms whether that guess holds.
Nothing about the candidates has changed, so regenerating them just repeats the same computation for nothing.
Dropping column clues removes half the cells propagation could otherwise force, sharply weakening it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未被确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell has not been determined yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定被涂色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FILLED is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed colored in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定为空白。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EMPTY is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed blank.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播卡住后，对某个 UNKNOWN 格做假设并重新传播的兜底搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback search guesses a value for an unknown cell and reruns propagation when deduction stalls.

scenario: fallback search 要在一个 UNKNOWN 格上试 FILLED，失败后必须完整回到猜测前的状态。
scenario_en: The fallback search is about to try FILLED on an UNKNOWN cell, and on failure it must return to exactly the pre-guess state.
q: 在 fallback search 里做一次猜测前，为什么要 clone 哪些东西？（多选）
q_en: Before making a guess in fallback search, what must be cloned and why? (Choose all that apply.)
options: grid
row_poss 的每个候选列表
col_poss 的每个候选列表
只 clone grid，不 clone 候选列表就一定安全
options_en: The grid.
Every candidate list inside row_poss.
Every candidate list inside col_poss.
Cloning only the grid, and skipping the candidate lists, is always safe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。

scenario: 传播版 `_search` 返回后，调用方要靠返回值决定继续传播、猜测还是判定无解。
scenario_en: After the propagation solver's _search returns, the caller uses the return value to decide whether to keep propagating, guess, or declare no solution.
q: 传播版 `_search` 的主要返回情况有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the main return cases for the propagation _search method? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 传播发现矛盾，返回 None
没有 UNKNOWN 且 puzzle.is_solved() 为真，返回 puzzle
有 UNKNOWN 时尝试两个状态的子分支
传播一轮无变化时直接返回未完成 puzzle
options_en: Propagation finds a contradiction, so it returns None.
There are no UNKNOWN cells left and puzzle.is_solved() is true, so it returns the puzzle.
With UNKNOWN cells remaining, it tries both states as child branches.
When a propagation pass makes no changes, it immediately returns the unfinished puzzle.
why: 无变化只表示纯传播卡住，不表示 puzzle 已经完成；仍有 UNKNOWN 时需要 fallback search。
why_en: Search returns failure on contradiction, success on a fully solved grid, or recurses on guesses when unknown cells remain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未被确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell has not been determined yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某条线过滤候选后列表变空，说明当前分支不可能成立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contradiction is an empty candidate list showing the current branch cannot be valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播卡住后，对某个 UNKNOWN 格做假设并重新传播的兜底搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback search guesses a value for an unknown cell and reruns propagation when deduction stalls.

optionExplanations: 候选列表出现矛盾说明这条分支不可能成立，直接返回 None 让上层换下一个选择。
没有 UNKNOWN 且确实满足所有 clue，说明已经解出，直接返回这份 puzzle。
还剩 UNKNOWN 时传播已经卡住，只能对其中一格分别假设 FILLED 和 EMPTY 递归下去。
一轮没变化只说明纯推理暂时卡住，不代表已经解完，这时该进入猜测分支而不是直接返回。
optionExplanations_en: An empty candidate list means the branch is impossible, so it returns None immediately so the caller tries the next option.
No UNKNOWN cells left and every clue actually satisfied means the puzzle is solved, so it returns that grid.
When UNKNOWN cells remain, propagation alone is stuck, so it branches by trying FILLED and EMPTY for one cell in turn.
No change in one pass just means deduction stalled, not that solving is done — it should fall into the guessing branch, not return early.

scenario: line possibility generator 收到 clue `[0]` 和线长 `length`。
scenario_en: The line possibility generator receives clue [0] and a line length.
q: 应该返回什么？
q_en: What should it return?
options: return [tuple([UNKNOWN] * length)]
return [tuple([FILLED] * length)]
return [tuple([EMPTY] * length)]
return None
options_en: return [tuple([UNKNOWN] * length)]
return [tuple([FILLED] * length)]
return [tuple([EMPTY] * length)]
return None
why: `[0]` 有且只有一种合法线布局：整条线都是 EMPTY。
why_en: The [0] clue has exactly one valid layout, an all-empty line.
whenOtherWins: 如果普通 clue 的最小长度超过 line length，才应该返回空候选表示无解。
tradeoff: `[0]` 特判返回唯一 EMPTY 布局（简单直接）vs 走通用 run 放置逻辑（多余，因为没有 run 可放）
codeSample:
if clues == [0]:
    return [tuple([CellState.EMPTY] * length)]
# 唯一合法布局：整条线全空
# 其余 clue 才进入通用的 run 放置递归
optionExplanations: 候选必须是具体确定的状态，返回全 UNKNOWN 根本不算一个合法候选。
`[0]` 明确是没有 filled run，返回全 FILLED 正好和定义相反。
`[0]` 只有一种合法布局：整条线全 EMPTY，直接返回这唯一的候选即可。
`[0]` 是有解的合法 clue，返回 None 会让整个 solve 提前误判为无解。
optionExplanations_en: A candidate must be a concrete resolved state; returning all UNKNOWN isn't a valid candidate at all.
[0] specifically means zero filled runs, so returning an all-FILLED layout is the exact opposite of its definition.
[0] has exactly one valid layout — the whole line EMPTY — so returning just that single candidate is correct.
[0] is a solvable clue, so returning None would wrongly make the entire solve fail prematurely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定被涂色。

scenario: line generator 拿到一条线的 clue，发现最短占用长度已经超过这条线的长度。
scenario_en: The line generator finds that a clue's minimum required length already exceeds the length of the line.
q: 如果 `sum(clues) + len(clues) - 1 > length`，line generator 应该怎样处理？
q_en: If sum(clues) + len(clues) - 1 is greater than length, how should the line generator handle it?
options: 强行截断最后一个 run，把候选长度硬凑够
忽略所有 run 之间要求的强制 empty 间隔
悄悄把这条线的 clue 改写成 `[0]` 糊弄过去
返回空候选列表，因为这条 clue 放不进该线
options_en: Force-truncate the last run and pad the candidate length to fit.
Ignore the mandatory empty gap required between every pair of runs.
Silently rewrite this line's clue as [0] to paper over the problem.
Return an empty candidate list because the clue cannot fit in the line.
why: 最短占用都超过线长，说明没有合法布局；空候选会在传播或搜索中触发矛盾。
why_en: If the minimum required length exceeds the line length, no valid layout exists and the candidate list is empty.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一行/列里连续被 filled 的一段格子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A run is a contiguous block of filled cells on a line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某条线过滤候选后列表变空，说明当前分支不可能成立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contradiction is an empty candidate list showing the current branch cannot be valid.

optionExplanations: 截断 run 会生成一个候选长度对得上、但和原始 clue 要求的 run 长度不符的假候选，误导后续推理。
间隔是 clue 语义的一部分，忽略它会让候选允许相邻 run 直接贴在一起，等于悄悄放宽了这条 clue 的要求。
改写成 `[0]` 是在伪造一个完全不同的题面，跟原始约束毫无关系，只是把问题藏起来而不是处理它。
最短占用长度都超过线长时，这条 clue 在这条线上根本放不下，候选就该是空列表。
optionExplanations_en: Truncating the run produces a candidate whose length fits but whose run lengths no longer match the original clue, misleading later deduction.
The gap is part of what the clue means; skipping it lets a candidate place adjacent runs touching, quietly loosening the clue's actual requirement.
Rewriting it to [0] fabricates an entirely different puzzle with no relation to the original constraint — it hides the problem instead of handling it.
When the minimum required length exceeds the line length, this clue simply cannot fit on this line, so the candidate list should be empty.

scenario: 一个约束题同时给了每行和每列的独立 clue，修复某个格子会同时影响一行和一列。
scenario_en: A constraint problem gives independent clues for every row and every column, so fixing one cell affects both a row and a column.
q: 为什么它特别适合传播？
q_en: Why is this especially suitable for propagation?
options: 因为行 clue 和列 clue 彼此完全独立、互不影响
因为这类题目只能按单一行方向孤立求解
因为所有 Nonogram 谜题天生都没有任何歧义
一个轴推出的强制格会立刻收缩另一轴候选，形成级联
options_en: Because row clues and column clues are entirely independent of each other.
Because this kind of puzzle can only be solved along a single row direction.
Because every nonogram puzzle is inherently unambiguous.
A forced cell on one axis immediately shrinks the other axis's candidates, creating a cascade.
why: Nonogram 的强约束来自行列交叉；每个确定格子都会同时成为另一条线的已知约束。
why_en: Nonograms suit propagation because every fixed cell constrains both its row and its column, creating cascades.
whenOtherWins: 如果约束只存在于单个独立维度，传播收益会弱很多，简单枚举可能足够。
tradeoff: 多轴交叉约束（传播收益大）vs 单轴独立约束（传播收益弱，枚举可能就够）
optionExplanations: 如果行列真的互不影响，确定一格根本不该改变另一条线的候选，这和传播能级联的事实矛盾。
列方向同样可以独立求解并推导，传播正是同时用两个方向，不是只能按行。
文章明确提到仍需要 fallback search 处理歧义，可见并非天生无歧义。
行列在共享格子上交叉，一格被确定就同时收窄了它所在行和列的候选，形成级联推导。
optionExplanations_en: If rows and columns were truly unrelated, fixing one cell shouldn't change the other line's candidates — that contradicts propagation's cascading behavior.
Columns are equally solvable and deducible; propagation specifically works both directions at once, not rows alone.
The article explicitly says fallback search is still often needed for ambiguity, so puzzles aren't inherently unambiguous.
Rows and columns cross at shared cells, so fixing one cell narrows candidates on both its row and column at once, creating a cascade.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播卡住后，对某个 UNKNOWN 格做假设并重新传播的兜底搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback search guesses a value for an unknown cell and reruns propagation when deduction stalls.

q: 把 propagation + fallback search 的整体 solver 流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full propagation plus fallback search solver flow in the correct order:
steps: 为所有行和列生成初始候选列表
若传播失败，当前分支返回 None
clone grid 与候选列表，猜一个 UNKNOWN 为 FILLED 或 EMPTY
运行传播直到收敛
若无 UNKNOWN，则验证并返回 solved puzzle
why: 每个搜索节点都先传播；传播失败就剪枝，传播完成且无未知就验证，否则才进入猜测子分支。
why_en: The full solver generates candidates, propagates at each node, fails on contradiction, returns solved grids, and guesses only when unknowns remain.
tradeoff: 每个节点先传播再判断（推理优先，分支更浅）vs 每个节点直接猜测再验证（更简单但分支爆炸）
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Generate[Generate row and column candidates] --> Prop[Propagate constraints]
  Prop --> Fail{contradiction}
  Fail -->|yes| None[return None]
  Fail -->|no| Complete{complete}
  Complete -->|yes| Return[return puzzle]
  Complete -->|no| Branch[guess and recurse]

scenario: 你的 row-by-row solver 在一道有解的 10×10 上返回无解，怀疑部分列检查太严。
scenario_en: Your row-by-row solver reports no solution on a 10x10 that does have one, and you suspect the partial column check is too strict.
q: partial column check 中最常见的错误是什么？
q_en: What is the most common mistake in partial column checks?
options: 检查每个已经关闭的 run 是否匹配 clue 对应前缀
发现某个 run 长度超过对应 clue 值时立即返回 false
列填满后调用 extract_runs 做最终整体对比
把正在尾部增长的 run 当作已经关闭，要求它立刻等于 clue
options_en: Check that every already-closed run matches the clue's corresponding prefix.
Return false immediately once a run's length exceeds its corresponding clue value.
Once the column is full, call extract_runs for one final full comparison.
Treating an open trailing run as closed and requiring it to equal the clue immediately.
why: 开放 run 还可能继续增长，只能检查它没有超过目标长度；过早要求相等会剪掉合法分支。
why_en: The common bug is treating an open trailing run as completed and requiring it to equal the clue too early.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一行/列里连续被 filled 的一段格子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A run is a contiguous block of filled cells on a line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

optionExplanations: 这恰恰是部分列检查该做的事——已关闭 run 必须匹配 clue 前缀，不是常见错误。
run 一旦超过对应 clue 的长度就该判 false，这是正确逻辑，不是 bug。
列填满后做一次完整的 extract_runs 对比，是最终验证该有的一步，做法没问题。
最常踩的坑是把还在增长的尾部 run 当成已经封闭，提前要求它等于目标长度，误杀本该合法的分支。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what a partial column check should do — a closed run must match the clue prefix, this isn't the common mistake.
Returning false the moment a run exceeds its clue length is correct behavior, not a bug.
Running one full extract_runs comparison once the column is complete is the necessary final verification step, not a mistake.
The common trap is treating an open trailing run as already closed and requiring it to match the target length too early, wrongly killing valid branches.

scenario: 评测套件里有无解的 puzzle，solver 必须按约定返回，而不是抛异常或空转到超时。
scenario_en: The test suite includes unsolvable puzzles, and the solver must return in the agreed way instead of throwing or spinning until timeout.
q: 如果没有任何合法填法能同时满足所有行列 clue，solver 应返回什么？
q_en: If no valid fill satisfies all row and column clues, what should the solver return?
options: 最后一个尝试的半成品 grid
全 EMPTY grid
全 FILLED grid
null/None
options_en: The half-finished grid from the last attempted branch.
An all-EMPTY grid.
An all-FILLED grid.
null / None.
why: 题目要求无解时返回空结果；传播或搜索最终会让所有分支矛盾并返回 None。
why_en: If no grid satisfies all clues, every branch fails and the solver returns null.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定为空白。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EMPTY is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed blank.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定被涂色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FILLED is the cell state meaning the cell is confirmed colored in.

optionExplanations: 半成品 grid 不满足任何一条完整的 clue 组合，不能当作答案交出去。
全空 grid 只有在所有 clue 都是 `[0]` 时才合法，不是无解时的默认答案。
全涂色 grid 同样要满足每条 clue，无解时它一样违反约束。
确实无解时每个分支都会矛盾收场，solver 该老实返回 null 而不是硬凑一个假答案。
optionExplanations_en: A half-finished grid doesn't satisfy any complete combination of clues, so it can't be handed back as the answer.
An all-EMPTY grid is only valid if every clue is [0]; it isn't a default fallback for unsolvable puzzles.
An all-FILLED grid still has to satisfy every clue, so it violates the constraints just as much when unsolvable.
When truly unsolvable, every branch ends in contradiction, so the solver should honestly return null instead of faking an answer.

q: 补全从三版解法抽象出的路线：
q_en: Complete the general path abstracted from the three solver versions:
text: 先写 {{raw backtracking}}；再把工作单位从 cell 提升到 {{row/line candidates}}；最后先做 {{propagation}}，只在推不动时搜索。
why: 这条路线体现了约束满足题的常见升级：先正确，再更大粒度使用结构，最后把搜索推迟到必要时。
why_en: The progression is raw backtracking, larger structured choices, then propagation before search.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking tries a choice, recurses, and undoes it on failure to try another option.

scenario: 面试里遇到一道新的多轴约束题，你要在动手前决定直接搜索还是先写传播。
scenario_en: In an interview you hit a new multi-axis constraint problem and must decide, before coding, whether to search directly or propagate first.
q: 文章建议遇到类似约束题时先问哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: What questions does the article suggest asking for similar constraint problems? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 输入是否有来自多个轴的约束
是否能便宜地枚举每条线的合法选项
固定一条线是否会明显约束另一条线
是否可以忽略所有局部矛盾
options_en: Does the input carry constraints from more than one axis?
Can you enumerate each line's valid options cheaply?
Does fixing one line meaningfully constrain another?
Can you just ignore every local contradiction?
why: 如果多轴约束、候选可枚举、交叉影响强，传播通常比直接搜索更值得优先写。
why_en: Propagation is attractive when constraints come from multiple axes, line options are enumerable, and fixing one line constrains another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 约束满足问题：给一组变量赋值，同时满足多条约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CSP, a constraint satisfaction problem, assigns values to variables so every constraint holds at once.

optionExplanations: 只有单轴约束时传播收益有限，先确认是不是真的存在多个方向的约束再决定要不要上传播。
如果一条线的合法候选枚举起来很贵，传播的过滤成本也会跟着变贵，这一点值得先算一算。
固定一条线对另一条线几乎没有约束力时，级联推导就推不出多少格子，传播的价值会打折扣。
局部矛盾恰恰是分支该立即失败的信号，忽略它只会让错误分支继续往下算，浪费时间。
optionExplanations_en: Propagation helps less with only one axis of constraints, so it's worth confirming multiple directions actually constrain the puzzle first.
If enumerating a line's valid candidates is expensive, propagation's filtering cost gets expensive too — worth estimating up front.
If fixing one line barely constrains another, the cascade won't force many cells, which weakens propagation's payoff.
A local contradiction is exactly the signal a branch should fail immediately — ignoring it just lets a doomed branch keep computing.

scenario: Nonogram Solver 的评测套件按 5×5、10×10、15×15、25×25 四档递增出题，每档都有独立的 5000ms 时间预算。
scenario_en: The Nonogram Solver benchmark uses increasing puzzle sizes, 5x5, 10x10, 15x15, and 25x25, each with its own 5000 ms time budget.
q: 题解为什么要专门设计这四档递增规模，而不是只测一个大棋盘？
q_en: Why does the solution use four increasing puzzle sizes instead of testing only one large board?
options: 只是想确认程序在更大网格上不会因内存不足而崩溃
要求所有解法在四档上都必须使用完全相同的时间复杂度
规模越大意味着 clue 携带的约束信息越少，只是让题目更难猜
让每一档依次暴露不同解法各自在哪个量级开始超时
options_en: It's only to confirm the program does not crash from running out of memory on larger grids.
It requires every solution to have the exact same time complexity across all four tiers.
A larger grid means the clues carry less constraining information, just making it a harder guess.
So each tier exposes exactly where a given solution starts blowing its time budget.
why: 四档规模像一把标尺，逐步逼出每种解法各自在哪个量级失速：cell-by-cell 在 10×10、row-by-row 在 15×15，只有传播能撑到 25×25。
why_en: The four size tiers act like a ruler that exposes exactly where each solution stalls, from cell-by-cell at 10x10 up to propagation clearing 25x25.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按单个格子逐一猜 FILLED/EMPTY 的最朴素回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cell-by-cell backtracking guesses FILLED or EMPTY for one cell at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先枚举整行合法填法，再按整行回溯的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Row-by-row backtracking enumerates whole valid row layouts and backtracks one row at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

optionExplanations: 内存崩溃只是极端情况，四档的真正目的是暴露不同解法各自的时间失速点。
四档递增恰恰是为了看出不同解法复杂度不同，不是要求它们表现一致。
clue 携带的约束信息和棋盘规模没有必然关系，规模变大不代表约束变弱。
从 5×5 一路加到 25×25，就是要让每种解法各自在哪一档开始扛不住预算这件事无所遁形。
optionExplanations_en: A memory crash is an edge case; the real point of four tiers is to expose where each solution's timing starts to fail.
The increasing tiers exist precisely to reveal different solutions have different complexity, not to force them to behave the same.
How much constraint a clue carries has no necessary link to board size — bigger doesn't automatically mean weaker constraints.
5 by 5 up through 25 by 25 works like a ruler, and stepping through it shows exactly where cell-by-cell stalls at 10 by 10 and row-by-row at 15 by 15.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么不直接继续优化 row-by-row 的排序或剪枝。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you would not just keep optimizing row-by-row ordering or pruning.
q: 最好的回答是什么？
q_en: What is the best answer?
options: 因为只要把行按 clue 长度重新排序，就能把 NP-hard 问题变成 O(n)
因为 row-by-row 在所有 15×15 题目上跑出来都已经足够快，不用再动
因为列 clue 其实是多余信息，删掉也完全不影响正确性
列 clue 和行 clue 一样强，只当拒绝器浪费了一半信息，该让它主动传播
options_en: Just reordering rows by clue length can turn the NP-hard problem into O(n).
Row-by-row already runs fast enough on every 15x15 puzzle in practice, no need to change it.
Column clues are actually redundant information — dropping them doesn't hurt correctness at all.
Column clues carry just as much signal as row clues; using them only as a rejector wastes half the information — they should actively propagate.
why: row_bt 的问题不是单纯顺序不好，而是没有把列约束用来推导格子；传播把两轴信息都前置使用。
why_en: The key is that columns are not just validators; they should actively shrink possibilities and force cells.
whenOtherWins: 如果列约束非常弱或题目只要求小规模，row-by-row 加简单剪枝也可能足够。
tradeoff: 把列约束当主动推导源（传播，更快但要维护候选状态）vs 把列约束只当事后过滤器（row backtracking，简单但慢）
optionExplanations: 给行排序只是换尝试顺序，候选空间大小完全没变，不会把复杂度类别从指数降到线性。
benchmark 明明白白显示 row_bt 在 15×15 要约 68000ms，早就超出 5000ms 预算，谈不上「已经够快」。
删掉列约束会让候选过滤少一半信息来源，传播能力直接打对折，不是多余信息。
row-by-row 把列约束只当成事后拒绝器，等于浪费了一半推导信息；该让它加入传播，两轴一起收缩候选。
optionExplanations_en: Reordering rows only changes try order; the candidate space size is unchanged, so it can't drop the complexity class from exponential to linear.
The benchmark clearly shows row_bt takes about 68000ms at 15 by 15, already blowing the 5000ms budget — nowhere near 'already fast enough.'
Dropping column constraints removes half the information candidate filtering relies on, cutting propagation's power in half — they aren't redundant.
Row-by-row treats column clues as a mere after-the-fact filter, throwing away half the deductive power — folding them into propagation lets both axes shrink candidates together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先枚举整行合法填法，再按整行回溯的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Row-by-row backtracking enumerates whole valid row layouts and backtracks one row at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

scenario: 传播版跑一道 25×25，传播收敛后 grid 里仍然留着一批 UNKNOWN 格子。
scenario_en: On a 25x25 puzzle the propagation converges but the grid still has a batch of UNKNOWN cells left.
q: 为什么文章说 Nonogram 仍然可能需要 fallback search？
q_en: Why does the article say a Nonogram solver may still need fallback search?
options: 传播永远不会填任何格
所有 Nonogram 都能纯传播解出
fallback search 是为了打乱输出
传播只能推出逻辑强制格，遇到局部歧义时必须尝试假设
options_en: Propagation never fills in any cell at all.
Every nonogram can be solved by pure propagation alone.
Fallback search exists just to shuffle the output.
Propagation only derives logically forced cells, so local ambiguity still requires a guess.
why: 传播是局部推理，不保证消除所有歧义；搜索负责处理需要假设才能推进的分支。
why_en: Propagation handles forced deductions, but ambiguous puzzles can still require guesses and backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播卡住后，对某个 UNKNOWN 格做假设并重新传播的兜底搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback search guesses a value for an unknown cell and reruns propagation when deduction stalls.

optionExplanations: 传播恰恰能填出大量强制格，这是它比暴力搜索快的核心原因，这个说法完全相反。
如果所有题都能纯传播解出，benchmark 里就不需要区分 propagate_bt 和 fallback 分支了。
fallback search 是为了在传播卡住时继续推进，不是随便打乱结果。
传播只能确认「无论哪个候选都一样」的格子，遇到多个候选并存的歧义就推不动了，只能靠假设分支去试。
optionExplanations_en: Propagation is exactly what fills in large numbers of forced cells — that's why it beats brute search, so this claim is backwards.
If pure propagation solved every puzzle, there'd be no need to distinguish a fallback branch in the benchmark at all.
Fallback search exists to keep making progress when propagation stalls, not to scramble the result.
Propagation can only confirm cells where every remaining candidate agrees; once genuine ambiguity remains, it stalls and needs a guessed branch to move forward.

scenario: 你要把 cell_bt → row_bt → propagate_bt 三版解法的经验压成一句可迁移的结论。
scenario_en: You want to compress the lesson of the three solutions — cell_bt, row_bt, propagate_bt — into one transferable takeaway.
q: Nonogram Solver 这篇题解最核心的经验是什么？
q_en: What is the core lesson from the Nonogram Solver breakdown?
options: 所有约束满足问题都应该从逐格暴力搜索开始并到此为止
只要用递归实现回溯，就完全不需要维护候选列表
列 clue 完全可以留到整块棋盘填满后再一次性检查
约束题先找可传播结构，让推理主动缩小搜索树
options_en: Every constraint satisfaction problem should start with brute-force cell search and stop there.
As long as you implement backtracking with recursion, you never need to maintain candidate lists.
Column clues can wait entirely until the whole board fills up, checked all at once at the end.
Find propagable structure first so deduction shrinks the search tree.
why: 本题从逐格暴力到行候选再到行列传播，核心就是把 clue 转成主动约束，少靠盲目搜索。
why_en: The main lesson is to turn constraints into propagation so deduction shrinks the search before backtracking is used.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

optionExplanations: 文章正是从暴力搜索一路升级出去的，逐格搜索恰恰是被替代的起点，不是应该止步于此的终点。
递归和要不要维护候选列表是两回事，propagation 版本照样递归还要维护候选。
列信息可以边推边用来收缩候选，留到棋盘填满才检查会白白错过大量提前推导的机会。
题解走的是暴力→行粒度候选→行列传播这条升级路线，核心是先挖出能推理的结构，让约束主动帮你砍掉搜索空间。
optionExplanations_en: The article specifically upgrades away from brute-force cell search — that's the replaced starting point, not a recommended stopping point.
Recursion and maintaining candidate lists are separate concerns; the propagation version still recurses and still keeps candidates.
Column information can shrink candidates as you go; waiting until the board fills up throws away a lot of early deduction.
From per-cell brute force to row candidates to two-axis propagation, the core lesson is to find where deduction applies first so constraints shrink the search tree instead of just waiting on search.

scenario: `solve()` 第一行就 `puzzle = self.puzzle.clone()`，solver 全程在这个副本上试填、回溯、失败。
scenario_en: solve() starts with puzzle = self.puzzle.clone(), and the solver guesses, backtracks, and fails all on that copy.
q: solver 为什么一开始就把传入的 puzzle 克隆一份再工作？
q_en: Why does the solver clone the incoming puzzle before doing any work?
options: 让失败搜索只弄脏副本，不污染调用者原始 grid
克隆时顺便把 clue 编译成候选填法列表
副本对象比原对象读写都更快一些
防止多线程并发写同一个 grid 时发生数据竞争和撕裂
options_en: So a failed search only dirties the copy, never the caller's original grid.
Cloning also compiles the clues into candidate fills along the way.
The copy is somewhat faster to read and write than the original.
To stop concurrent threads racing and tearing the same grid.
optionExplanations: solver 反复试填再回退，直接改原 grid 会在失败路径上留下半成品；副本把这些脏状态隔离在调用者之外。
clone 只复制 grid 的格子状态，候选列表是另外单独 generate 出来的，两件事不相干。
读副本不会比原对象更快，性能从来不是这次 clone 的动机。
这份 solver 是单线程递归搜索，clone 防的是自我污染，而不是并发竞争。
optionExplanations_en: The solver guesses and backtracks repeatedly, so writing the original grid would leave half-filled state on failure; the copy isolates that from the caller.
Clone only copies cell state; the candidate lists are generated separately, so this is unrelated.
Reading the copy is not faster than the original; performance was never the reason to clone.
This solver is single-threaded recursion — clone guards against self-pollution, not concurrency.
why: solver 是破坏性的反复试填，clone 用一份可丢弃的副本换来调用者输入的不可变；代价是多一份 O(r·c) 的内存拷贝。
why_en: The solver mutates the grid as it guesses and backtracks, so it works on a throwaway clone to keep the caller's input intact — at the cost of one extra O(r·c) copy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制一份对象，之后的改动只作用在副本上，原对象不受影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clone makes a copy so later changes touch only the copy, leaving the original untouched.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存棋盘每个格子状态的 r×c 二维数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The grid is the r-by-c array holding each cell's state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

scenario: cell-by-cell 版只在填完某行最后一格时才比对该行 runs 与 clue，中途每填一格并不检查。
scenario_en: The cell-by-cell version compares a row's runs against its clue only when the row's last cell is set, not after each cell mid-row.
q: 为什么行内中途不比对 runs 是否等于 clue？
q_en: Why not compare a row's runs against its clue midway through the row?
options: 部分填的行 runs 本就不必等于 clue，中途比对没意义
中途检查会顺手修改格子状态，破坏之后回溯的 UNKNOWN 恢复
extract_runs 只能沿列方向提取，行方向算不出来
clue 会在填充过程中被动态改写，比不了
options_en: A partly filled row's runs need not equal the clue yet, so a mid-row check is pointless.
A mid-row check would mutate cell state and break the later UNKNOWN restore on backtrack.
extract_runs can only read along columns, not rows.
The clue is rewritten dynamically while filling, so it can't be compared.
optionExplanations: 行没填完时这一行的 runs 属于中间状态，可以暂时不匹配 clue；填满整行那一刻的比对才真正判定违规。
extract_runs 只是读当前行的值来算 runs，并不写格子；状态恢复由 unwind 的 set UNKNOWN 负责，与检查无关。
行和列的 runs 都能算，方向从来不是限制；问题出在检查的时机而非轴向。
clue 是题目给定的固定输入，全程不会变，动态改写的说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Before a row is full its runs are only a prefix and may legitimately differ from the clue; only at the last cell does a mismatch mean a real violation.
extract_runs just reads the row to compute runs; it never writes cells, and restoring UNKNOWN is unwind's job, not the check's.
extract_runs works on both rows and columns; the issue is timing, not axis.
The clue is a fixed given input that never changes, so it is never rewritten.
why: 行没填满前 runs 只是前缀、允许不等于 clue；把行检查放到行末，是在第一个能确定违规的时刻剪枝，省掉中途注定不匹配的无效比对。
why_en: A partial row's runs are only a prefix and may differ from the clue, so the row check runs at the last cell — the first moment a mismatch is real — and skips wasted mid-line comparisons.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一行/列里连续被 filled 的一段格子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A run is a contiguous block of filled cells on a line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述一行/列上从左到右（或从上到下）filled run 长度的整数列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clue is the ordered list of filled-run lengths required on one row or column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读一条线的当前格子、算出它的 filled run 长度序列的辅助函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: extract_runs is the helper that reads a line's current cells and returns its filled-run lengths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未确定是 filled 还是 empty。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell is not yet decided as filled or empty.

scenario: cell-by-cell 版把整个棋盘存在一个 r 行 c 列的 grid 里，并按格子顺序逐格递归下探。
scenario_en: The cell-by-cell version stores the whole board in one r-by-c grid and recurses cell by cell in order.
q: 补全 cell-by-cell 的空间复杂度：
q_en: Complete the space complexity of cell-by-cell backtracking:
text: grid 本身占 {{O(r·c)}}，递归栈深度等于已下探的格子数所以也是 {{O(r·c)}}，合计 {{O(r·c)}} 的多项式空间——远小于 2^(r·c) 的时间。
why: 空间 = grid 存储 O(r·c) + 递归调用栈 O(r·c)；r=行数、c=列数、栈深等于已探格子数 r·c。它是多项式空间，说明 cell-by-cell 的真正瓶颈只在指数时间，不在内存。
why_en: Space is O(r times c) for the grid plus O(r times c) for the recursion stack, so memory is only polynomial — the real bottleneck is the exponential time, not space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录尚未返回的递归调用的栈；深度等于当前下探的层数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The recursion stack holds the not-yet-returned recursive calls; its depth equals how deep the search has descended.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存棋盘每个格子状态的 r×c 二维数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The grid is the r-by-c array holding each cell's state.

scenario: row-by-row 回溯每行选一个候选 fill、共 r 行，搜索树最多 P^r 个叶子；到达一个叶子后还要验证全部列。
scenario_en: Row-by-row backtracking picks one candidate fill per row over r rows, up to P^r leaves; at each leaf it still verifies all columns.
q: 除了 P^r 个叶子，row-by-row 每个叶子还要额外付出多少代价？
q_en: Beyond P^r leaves, what extra cost does row-by-row pay per leaf?
options: O(r·c) 的整盘列扫描
O(1) 的常数级检查
O(P) 重新枚举该行候选
额外再乘上一个 2^c 的因子
options_en: An O(r·c) scan of the whole board's columns.
An O(1) constant-time check.
An O(P) re-enumeration of that row's candidates.
One more 2^c multiplicative factor.
optionExplanations: 每落一个叶子都要逐列重算 runs 检查一致性，扫过 r×c 个格子，所以真实上界是 P^r 个叶子乘以每叶 O(r·c)。
列一致性检查要遍历整盘格子，不是常数级；把它当 O(1) 会低估总代价。
候选是开局一次性 generate 好的，叶子处只做列扫描，不会再重新枚举行候选。
列扫描是线性 O(r·c) 而非再套一层 2^c；2^c 是 cell-by-cell 的量级，用错了方案。
optionExplanations_en: Each leaf rescans every column to recompute runs, walking r×c cells, so the real bound is P^r leaves times O(r·c) per leaf.
The column-consistency check walks the whole board, not a constant; calling it O(1) underestimates the cost.
Candidates are generated once up front; a leaf only scans columns, it never re-enumerates row candidates.
The column scan is linear O(r·c), not another 2^c factor; 2^c belongs to cell-by-cell, the wrong solver here.
why: 叶子数是 P^r（P=每行平均合法候选数、r=行数），但每到一个叶子都要 O(r·c) 地扫全部列验证一致性；总代价是 P^r × O(r·c)，别只数叶子忘了每叶的列扫描。
why_en: Leaves number P^r, but each leaf costs O(r·c) to scan every column for consistency, so the real total is P^r times O(r·c) — don't count leaves and forget the per-leaf column scan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一行/列里连续被 filled 的一段格子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A run is a contiguous block of filled cells on a line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条线满足其 clue 的一种合法填法；过滤会逐轮删掉不再匹配已知格的候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate is one valid fill of a line that satisfies its clue; filtering drops candidates that no longer match the known cells.

scenario: 传播反复扫全盘：每次 pass 过滤候选并提交所有被强制的格子，直到某次 pass 没有新格被固定才停。
scenario_en: Propagation repeatedly scans the whole grid: each pass filters candidates and commits every forced cell, stopping when a pass fixes no new cell.
q: 凭什么保证这个传播循环一定会终止？
q_en: What guarantees this propagation loop terminates?
options: 每次有效 pass 至少固定一格，格子有限，故最多 rows×cols 轮
因为每次 pass 一定恰好固定一格不多不少，跑满整盘格子数那么多轮之后必然停下
循环里有显式计数器，到上限就强制退出
候选列表只增不减，最终收敛到唯一解
options_en: Each effective pass fixes at least one cell, and cells are finite, so at most rows×cols passes.
Each pass fixes exactly one cell, so it stops after as many passes as there are cells on the board.
An explicit counter in the loop forces an exit at its limit.
Candidate lists only grow, converging to a unique solution.
optionExplanations: 只要一次 pass 还在提交新格，它至少推进一格；能提交新格的轮数被有限的格子数卡住，无新格时循环退出。
一次 pass 可能一口气固定多格，也可能一格都固定不了就触发退出；不是恰好一格。
代码没有硬编码计数器，靠的是 changed 标志：本轮没有新格被固定就停，不是数到某个上限。
候选列表是被 filter 越过滤越短，不是只增不减；把方向记反了。
optionExplanations_en: As long as a pass commits a new cell it advances by at least one; the number of such passes is capped by the finite cell count, and the loop exits when none change.
A single pass may fix several cells at once, or zero (which triggers the exit); it is not exactly one per pass.
There is no hard-coded counter; the changed flag stops the loop when a pass fixes no new cell, not at some limit.
Filtering makes candidate lists shrink, not grow; this reverses the direction.
why: 终止性靠单调进度：每次有效 pass 至少把一个 UNKNOWN 格固定成确定值，而格子总数 rows×cols 有限，所以固定新格的 pass 最多 rows×cols 次，之后必有一次 pass 无变化并退出。
why_en: Each effective pass fixes at least one UNKNOWN cell and cells are finite at rows×cols, so at most rows×cols passes make progress before one changes nothing and the loop stops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播的一轮：把全盘每条线都过滤一次并提交所有被强制的格子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pass is one propagation sweep that filters every line and commits any forced cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格尚未确定是 filled 还是 empty。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNKNOWN is the cell state meaning the cell is not yet decided as filled or empty.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条线满足其 clue 的一种合法填法；过滤会逐轮删掉不再匹配已知格的候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate is one valid fill of a line that satisfies its clue; filtering drops candidates that no longer match the known cells.

scenario: 传播每一轮（pass）对每条线做一次过滤：拿已知格去筛掉不再匹配的候选，随候选收缩，后面的 pass 越跑越便宜。
scenario_en: Each propagation pass filters every line once, dropping candidates that no longer match the known cells; as candidates shrink, later passes get cheaper.
q: 补全单次传播 pass 的成本量级：
q_en: Complete the cost of a single propagation pass:
text: 一次 pass 的成本 ≈ {{所有线剩余候选数之和}} 的线性量（每个候选按其线长各测一次），所以候选越少后面的 pass {{越便宜}}。
why: 单 pass 成本 ≈ Σ(每条线的剩余候选数)，每个候选沿其线长各扫一次；这是算术不是搜索。用途：它解释了为什么传播随候选收缩越跑越快，而 P^r 的搜索每层都指数膨胀。
why_en: A pass costs about the sum of remaining candidates across all lines, since each is tested once along its line; that's arithmetic, so passes get cheaper as candidates shrink.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播的一轮：把全盘每条线都过滤一次并提交所有被强制的格子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pass is one propagation sweep that filters every line and commits any forced cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条线满足其 clue 的一种合法填法；过滤会逐轮删掉不再匹配已知格的候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate is one valid fill of a line that satisfies its clue; filtering drops candidates that no longer match the known cells.

scenario: 传播+回退能在毫秒级解掉测试里的 25×25，但 Nonogram 判定本身是 NP-complete。
scenario_en: Propagation plus fallback solves the test suite's 25x25 in milliseconds, yet deciding a Nonogram is itself NP-complete.
q: 既然 Nonogram 是 NP-complete，传播到底改变了什么？
q_en: Given Nonogram is NP-complete, what does propagation actually change?
options: 只改善真实 puzzle 的实际表现，最坏复杂度仍是指数
把最坏复杂度从指数降到多项式，问题不再是 NP-complete
让 solver 对所有可能输入都保证毫秒返回
证明了 Nonogram 其实属于 P
options_en: It only improves real puzzles' practical runtime; the worst case stays exponential.
It lowers the worst case from exponential to polynomial, so it's no longer NP-complete.
It guarantees a millisecond return on every possible input.
It proves Nonogram actually lies in P.
optionExplanations: 传播把人类的 overlap 推理机械化，让设计良好的真实 puzzle 大多不靠搜索就解出；但对抗性最坏输入仍可能逼出指数级回退。
最坏复杂度是问题固有的属性，任何算法都改不了它；传播只挪动了实际耗时，不动复杂度类。
对刻意构造的最坏 puzzle，propagation 收敛后仍剩大量歧义，回退可能指数级展开，不存在全输入的毫秒保证。
除非 P=NP，否则没人能把 NP-complete 问题证进 P；一个快解法不构成这种证明。
optionExplanations_en: Propagation mechanizes the human overlap deduction so well-formed real puzzles mostly solve without search, but adversarial worst cases can still force exponential fallback.
NP-completeness is the problem's inherent hardness; no algorithm changes the worst-case bound — propagation shifts real runtime, not the complexity class.
On a crafted worst-case puzzle, ambiguity remains after propagation and fallback can expand exponentially; there is no all-inputs millisecond guarantee.
Short of P=NP, no one proves an NP-complete problem into P; a fast solver is not such a proof.
why: NP-complete 是问题的固有最坏难度，传播这类启发式改不了它；它改的是真实、良构 puzzle 的平均表现——多数格子靠演绎定下、搜索只收尾。代价：遇到对抗性输入仍会退化成指数搜索。
why_en: Propagation can't change the NP-complete worst case; it only speeds up real, well-formed puzzles where deduction fixes most cells, while adversarial inputs still fall back to exponential search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Nondeterministic Polynomial-time complete：一类最坏情况被认为无多项式算法的判定问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NP-complete (Nondeterministic Polynomial-time complete) is a class of decision problems with no known worst-case polynomial algorithm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 若一条线所有合法候选在某格取值一致，该格就被强制成那个值——人类解谜时的推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The overlap argument: if every valid candidate for a line agrees on a cell, that cell is forced to that value.

q: Route Planner 的主方法要最小化什么？
q_en: What does the main Route Planner method minimize?
options: 只数经过的总站点数，不看每条边花了多少时间
总旅行时间，包括换乘线时的 5 分钟罚时
线路名称按字典序排序，和耗时无关
路径中用到的不同线路数量，不看每段边花多久
why: 边有 travel_time，且切换 line 会额外加 5 分钟；目标是最小化累计时间。
why_en: The planner minimizes total travel time, including a five-minute penalty whenever the route switches lines.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Edge[Travel time] --> Total[Total route time]
  Transfer[Line change penalty] --> Total
  Total --> Min[Minimize total]
options_en: The total number of stations passed through, ignoring how long each edge takes.
Total travel time, including a five-minute penalty per transfer.
Alphabetical order of the line names, unrelated to how long the route takes.
The number of distinct lines used along the route, ignoring how long each segment takes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换线路时额外加的 5 分钟成本，只有到达线路和下一条边线路不同才触发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transfer penalty is the extra five minutes added whenever the route switches lines.

optionExplanations: 只数经过的总站点数，会丢掉每条边的旅行时间和换乘罚时，两条站数相同的路线可能耗时完全不同。
对，目标函数就是这个：把每条边的 travel_time 累加，再加上每次换乘的 5 分钟罚时。
线路名称的字典序和路线快慢毫无关系，只是排序习惯，不是优化目标。
路径中用到的线路数量会漏掉具体时间，线路数相同但换乘罚时和边权可以差很多。
optionExplanations_en: Counting the total stations passed through throws away each edge's travel time and the transfer penalty, so two routes with the same station count can take very different amounts of time.
Correct — the objective is exactly this: sum every edge’s travel_time and add five minutes for each transfer.
Alphabetical order of line names has nothing to do with how fast a route is; it's just a sort convention, not the optimization target.
The number of distinct lines used ignores actual time — two routes with the same number of lines can still differ a lot in edge weight and transfer cost.
scenario: 地铁 Route Planner：每条边是分钟数，换线额外 +5 分钟，用户要的是最早到达。
scenario_en: In a metro route planner each edge costs minutes and every line change adds five more, and the rider just wants to arrive earliest.

q: 补全换乘罚时规则：
q_en: Complete the transfer-penalty rule:
text: 第一条边没有上一条线路，因此 {{不算换乘}}；后续边如果 `current_line != next_line`，就加 {{5 分钟}} 并把 transfer count 加一。
why: 换乘成本取决于到达当前站时所在线路，这也是后续 state key 必须包含 line 的根本原因。
why_en: A transfer penalty applies only after the first edge when the next edge's line differs from the line used to arrive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换线路时额外加的 5 分钟成本，只有到达线路和下一条边线路不同才触发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transfer penalty is the extra five minutes added whenever the route switches lines.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 用来判断某个状态是否已经找到最优解的键；相同 key 的到达会被合并成一个状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The state key is what Dijkstra uses to decide whether two arrivals count as the same state and can be merged.

q: 为什么按 hop count 的 BFS 不适合这个主路由问题？
q_en: Why is hop-count BFS a poor fit for the main routing problem?
options: 边权不同时，跳数少不等于总时间少
BFS 无法处理带环的图，会陷入死循环
BFS 出队时不会把已走过的路径记下来
BFS 的 visited 集合会漏掉部分邻居站点
why: 测试图里 Blue 三跳共 7 分钟，比 Red 两跳 8 分钟更快；BFS 会优先返回两跳路径。
why_en: BFS minimizes number of edges, but this route planner must minimize weighted travel time.
options_en: Different edge weights mean fewer hops doesn't mean less time.
BFS cannot handle graphs with cycles and would loop forever.
BFS never records the path taken so far when it dequeues a node.
BFS's visited set can skip over some neighboring stations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按跳数一层层扩展的图搜索算法，不看边的权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS is Breadth-First Search, a graph search that expands nodes layer by layer in hop-count order, ignoring edge weight.

optionExplanations: 对，跳数只数边的个数；三跳的 Blue 只要 7 分钟，两跳的 Red 反而要 8 分钟，BFS 按跳数排的话就会挑错路线。
错，BFS 配合 visited 集合不会死循环，它照样能处理带环的图，只是按层展开、不看权重，环不是它的问题。
错，BFS 完全可以在每个队列条目里带上已走过的 path，问题出在它排序候选的标准，不是要不要存路径。
错，BFS 的 visited 集合会覆盖每个邻居，不会漏站，它错的是选择标准而不是搜索范围。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — hop count only counts edges, so a three-hop Blue route at seven minutes can still beat a two-hop Red route at eight, and BFS picks by hop count regardless.
Wrong — BFS paired with a visited set never loops forever; it still handles cyclic graphs fine, it just expands layer by layer and ignores weight, which has nothing to do with cycles.
Wrong — BFS can absolutely carry the path so far in each queue entry; the real issue is what it sorts candidates by, not whether it stores a path.
Wrong — BFS's visited set covers every neighbor, so it never skips a station; its flaw is the ranking criterion, not search coverage.
scenario: Central→Airport：Red 两跳共 8 分钟，Blue 三跳共 7 分钟，要求返回最快路线而不是最少站。
scenario_en: From Central to Airport, Red is two hops at eight minutes and Blue is three hops at seven, and we must return the fastest route rather than the fewest stops.

scenario: 站点图的每条边有非负旅行时间，还可能加非负换乘罚时，需要找最小总时间。
scenario_en: Each edge in the station graph has non-negative travel time, and transfers add a non-negative penalty; find the minimum total time.
q: 应该从哪类算法开始？
q_en: Which algorithm family should you start with?
options: Dijkstra
普通 BFS
拓扑排序
二分搜索
why: 非负加权最短路的标准工具是 Dijkstra；关键是定义正确的状态，而不只是换一个优先队列。
why_en: Dijkstra is the right family for non-negative weighted shortest paths, provided the state captures everything future costs depend on.
whenOtherWins: 如果每条边代价完全相同，BFS 更简单；如果有负权边，Dijkstra 不适用。
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Heap[min time heap] --> Pop[pop best state]
  Pop --> Relax[relax weighted edges]
  Relax --> Heap

flowchart LR
  Queue[FIFO queue] --> Hops[hop layers]
tradeoff: 非负权最短路正确性 vs 模板简单但假设更强（无权/无环）
options_en: Dijkstra's algorithm.
Plain breadth-first search.
Topological sort.
Binary search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理非负权最短路径的经典算法，每次从堆里弹出当前累计代价最小的候选状态来扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm repeatedly expands the lowest cumulative-cost candidate to find shortest paths on non-negative weighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按跳数一层层扩展的图搜索算法，不看边的权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS is Breadth-First Search, a graph search that expands nodes layer by layer in hop-count order, ignoring edge weight.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只对无环有向图（DAG）成立的排序方法，按依赖顺序排列节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort is an ordering that only works on a directed acyclic graph, arranging nodes by dependency order.

optionExplanations: 对，非负权最短路的标准工具，只要状态定义完整（覆盖到达线路等未来依赖），Dijkstra 就能保证正确。
边代价完全相等时 BFS 更简单直接，但本题边权不同，按跳数排序会选错路线。
拓扑排序只对无环 DAG 成立，交通线路图通常存在环，不满足它的前提。
二分搜索用于在有序数据里查找目标值，不是为图上找最短路径设计的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the standard tool for non-negative-weight shortest paths; as long as the state definition covers every future dependency like arrival line, Dijkstra gives the right answer.
BFS is simpler when every edge costs the same, but here edge weights differ, so ranking by hop count picks the wrong route.
Topological sort only works on an acyclic DAG, and transit line maps usually contain cycles, so its precondition doesn't hold.
Binary search finds a target in sorted data — it isn't built for finding shortest paths on a graph at all.

q: BFS baseline 虽然返回错路线，但它仍记录了哪些运行信息？（多选）
q_en: Even though the BFS baseline returns the wrong route, what runtime information does it still track? (Select all that apply.)
options: 当前 path
当前 line
累计 total_time
transfer count
why: BFS baseline 的问题不是不会累计时间，而是 queue 的出队顺序仍按 hop count，不按累计时间。
why_en: The BFS baseline can track time and transfers, but it still expands by hop count instead of accumulated cost.
options_en: The current path so far.
The current line.
The accumulated total_time.
The transfer count.
optionExplanations: 对，每个 queue entry 都会带着走到当前站的完整 path 列表一起入队。
对，entry 记录到达时所在的 line，后续才能判断下一跳要不要付换乘罚时。
对，total_time 在每次入队时都累加了 travel_time 和罚时，不是没算。
对，transfers 会在每次判定发生换乘时加一，跟 path、time 一起存进 entry。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — every queue entry carries along the full path list of stations visited so far.
Correct — each entry records the arrival line so later hops can tell whether a transfer penalty applies.
Correct — total_time is accumulated with every push, adding travel_time and any penalty; it isn't skipped.
Correct — transfers increments whenever a transfer is detected and is stored in the entry alongside path and time.
scenario: 你在 review 一个返回了错路线的 BFS baseline，决定换 Dijkstra 时哪些簿记可以直接留用。
scenario_en: You are reviewing a BFS baseline that returned the wrong route and deciding which of its bookkeeping fields you can keep when you switch to Dijkstra.

q: 这组耗时数据最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design conclusion does this timing example support most strongly?
options: 该按累计时间选路线，而不是按跳数选路线
跳数最少的 Red 一定是最优路线
边数越少，总时间就一定越短
换乘更多条线路的路线一定更慢
why: Blue 三跳共 7 分钟，比两跳的 Red（8 分钟）和 Green（10 分钟）都快；必须按累计权重排序而不是跳数，这正是后面要换成 Dijkstra 的原因。
why_en: Blue wins at seven minutes despite having the most hops, so routes must be ranked by accumulated time, not hop count.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  C[Central] -->|Green 5| P[Park]
  P -->|Green 5| A[Airport]
  C -->|Red 4| H[Harbor]
  H -->|Red 4| A
  C -->|Blue 2| M[Mall]
  M -->|Blue 2| S[Stadium]
  S -->|Blue 3| A
scenario: 同一起点 Central 到 Airport 有三条候选线路：Green 经 Park 两跳共 4+6=10 分钟，Red 经 Harbor 两跳共 5+3=8 分钟，Blue 经 Mall、Stadium 三跳共 2+3+2=7 分钟。
scenario_en: From Central to Airport, Green takes two hops for 10 minutes, Red takes two hops for 8 minutes, and Blue takes three hops for 7 minutes.
options_en: Rank routes by accumulated time, not by hop count.
The fewest-hop Red route must be optimal.
Fewer edges always means less total time.
A route touching more lines is always slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 路径经过的边数，不考虑每条边具体权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hop count is the number of edges on a path, regardless of each edge's weight.

optionExplanations: 对，三跳的 Blue 总共只花 7 分钟，两跳的 Red、Green 反而更慢，说明必须按累计时间排序，不能看跳数。
错，Red 两跳但要 8 分钟，比三跳的 Blue 慢，跳数最少不等于耗时最短。
错，Blue 边数最多却耗时最少，边数和总时间没有必然的单调关系。
错，这三条路线里没有一条发生换线，例子本身没有涉及换乘，推不出「换线越多越慢」这个结论。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the three-hop Blue route still only takes seven minutes, beating both two-hop Red and Green, so routes must be ranked by accumulated time.
Wrong — Red has fewer hops but takes eight minutes, slower than three-hop Blue, so fewest hops doesn't mean fastest.
Wrong — Blue has the most edges yet the least time, so edge count and total time aren't reliably related.
Wrong — none of these three routes switches lines at all, so this example says nothing about whether more line changes make a route slower.

scenario: 你已经决定用 Dijkstra，需要每次扩展当前累计时间最小的未完成路径。
scenario_en: You have chosen Dijkstra and need to expand the unfinished route with the lowest accumulated time each step.
q: 应该用什么 frontier 结构？
q_en: What frontier structure should you use?
options: FIFO 队列（按加入顺序出队）
按累计时间排序的 min-heap
栈（后进先出）
普通哈希 set
why: Dijkstra 的核心是始终弹出当前最便宜的候选状态；min-heap 正好支持这个操作。
why_en: Dijkstra needs a min-heap frontier so it always expands the lowest accumulated-time state next.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有边代价相同，FIFO queue 的 BFS 就已经按距离递增扩展。
tradeoff: 按代价排序的堆 vs 按加入顺序的队列
options_en: A FIFO queue that pops in insertion order.
A min-heap ordered by cumulative time.
A stack (last in, first out).
A plain hash set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种能以 O(log n) 时间取出当前最小元素的数据结构，这里按累计时间排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a data structure that returns the smallest element in O(log n) time, here ordered by cumulative travel time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出队列，BFS 按加入顺序处理站点，不看权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A FIFO queue processes stations in the order they were added, ignoring edge weight.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索中还未确定最终结果、等待被扩展的候选状态集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The frontier is the set of not-yet-settled candidate states waiting to be expanded.

optionExplanations: 边代价都相等时，FIFO 队列出队顺序天然就是按距离递增，等价于 Dijkstra；但本题边权不同，它会退化成 BFS。
对，min-heap 每次能以 O(log n) 弹出当前最小累计时间的候选，正是 Dijkstra 每步要做的操作。
栈后进先出，总是优先扩展最新加入的候选，和累计代价完全无关。
哈希 set 不保证任何弹出顺序，只能做去重/成员判断，撑不起需要有序扩展的 frontier。
optionExplanations_en: When every edge costs the same, a FIFO queue's pop order already matches increasing distance and is equivalent to Dijkstra — but here edge weights differ, so it degenerates into plain BFS.
Correct — a min-heap pops the lowest accumulated-time candidate in O(log n), exactly the operation Dijkstra needs at every step.
A stack is last-in-first-out, always expanding whatever was pushed most recently, with no relation to accumulated cost.
A plain hash set has no defined pop order — it's good for dedup/membership checks, not for an ordered frontier.

scenario: `line` 是到达当前站的线路，`conn.line` 是下一条边的线路，需要计算换乘。
scenario_en: `line` is the line used to arrive at the current station, and `conn.line` is the next edge's line.
q: 哪段逻辑正确处理第一跳和同线继续？
q_en: Which logic correctly handles the first hop and staying on the same line?
options: is_transfer = line is not None and line != conn.line
is_transfer = line != conn.line  # compares current line with next edge's line
is_transfer = True  # marks every relaxed edge as a transfer
is_transfer = conn.travel_time > 5  # compares edge duration to five minutes
why: 第一跳没有 prior line，不应罚时；之后只有线路变化才算换乘。
why_en: A transfer occurs only when there is a previous line and the next edge uses a different line.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务把上车也算一次换乘，第一跳规则要改；本文规则明确第一跳不罚。
codeSample:
is_transfer = line is not None and line != conn.line
new_time = time + conn.travel_time + (5 if is_transfer else 0)
new_transfers = transfers + (1 if is_transfer else 0)
# line is None only on the first hop, so it never counts as a transfer
# is_transfer flips to True only when the next edge uses a different line
tradeoff: 首跳不罚时 vs 之后按线路是否变化判断
options_en: Only count it as a transfer when there was a previous line and it differs from the next edge.
Count it as a transfer whenever the current line differs from the next edge.
Always treat every edge as a transfer.
Treat it as a transfer whenever the edge's travel time exceeds five minutes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换线路时额外加的 5 分钟成本，只有到达线路和下一条边线路不同才触发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transfer penalty is the extra five minutes added whenever the route switches lines.

optionExplanations: 对，line is None 时直接跳过判断，第一跳不罚时，之后靠线路是否变化决定要不要付 5 分钟。
错，line 初始值是 None，`None != conn.line` 恒为真，这段代码会把第一跳也误判成换乘。
错，把每条边都当换乘会让同线继续走的路线也被多算 5 分钟，明显算错。
错，换乘和这条边自己的耗时无关，5 分钟是罚时数值不是判断条件，这段逻辑把两者搞混了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it skips the check while line is None, so the first hop is free, and every later hop is judged purely by whether the line changed.
Wrong — line starts as None, and `None != conn.line` is always true, so this code wrongly penalizes even the very first hop.
Wrong — treating every edge as a transfer overcharges routes that stay on the same line, adding five minutes where none is owed.
Wrong — whether a transfer happened has nothing to do with that edge's own duration; five minutes is the penalty amount, not the trigger condition.

q: Dijkstra 只用 station 作为 visited key 会丢掉什么关键信息？
q_en: What key information is lost if Dijkstra uses only station as the visited key?
options: 到达该 station 时所在的 line
站点本身的名称字符串
这条边自身携带的 travel_time
整张图里全部站点间的连接关系
why: 未来离开当前站是否要付换乘罚时取决于上一条 line；只保存 station 会把不同 line 的到达状态错误合并。
why_en: A station-only key loses the arrival line, which determines the transfer cost of the next edge.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  X[Same station] --> L1[arrive on Red]
  X --> L2[arrive on Blue]
  L1 --> Cost1[next edge may transfer]
  L2 --> Cost2[next edge may stay]
  Cost1 --> Different[different future cost]
  Cost2 --> Different
options_en: The line the arrival was on when it reached that station.
The station's own name string.
The travel_time carried by this particular edge.
The connections between all stations across the entire graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 用来判断某个状态是否已经找到最优解的键；相同 key 的到达会被合并成一个状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The state key is what Dijkstra uses to decide whether two arrivals count as the same state and can be merged.

optionExplanations: 对，离开当前站要不要多付 5 分钟换乘费，得看上一条走的是哪条 line；只存站名会把不同线路抵达的状态错误合成一个。
错，站点本身的名称字符串一直就在 key 里，没有丢失任何信息。
错，travel_time 是这条边自身的属性，relax 时直接从边上读取，跟 visited key 存什么无关。
错，整张图的连接关系存在 network 对象里，和 visited key 记录哪个状态无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — future transfer cost depends on the line used to arrive, so keying on station alone wrongly merges arrivals on different lines into one state.
Wrong — the station's own name string is already part of the key, so nothing about it gets lost.

next_state = (conn.destination, conn.line)
if new_time < best.get(next_state, math.inf):

    heapq.heappush(heap, (new_time, counter, conn.destination, conn.line))
# best/parent only update on strict improvement, so parent always matches the recorded best time

q: 在 `(station, line)` Dijkstra 中，哪些 map/结构是核心？（多选）

`parent[state]` 存成功 relax 时的前驱状态
`transfers[state]` 存该状态已用换乘数

options_en: `best[(station, line)]` stores that state's minimum known time.
`parent[state]` stores the predecessor on a successful relax.
`transfers[state]` stores the transfer count used to reach that state.
`visited[station]` alone decides whether to discard all same-station states.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 用来判断某个状态是否已经找到最优解的键；相同 key 的到达会被合并成一个状态。

对，transfers 和 best、parent 一样按完整状态存，最后随 Route 一起返回给调用者。
错，只按 station 丢弃会把不同线路的到达错误合并，重现最早那个 station-only 的 bug。

Correct — parent updates only when a relax actually improves the state, so the reconstructed path always matches the recorded best time.
Correct — transfers is keyed the same way as best and parent, and gets returned together with the final Route.

q: 为什么 parent pointer 只应在 `new_time` 真正改善 `next_state` 时写入？

options: 否则更差路径可能覆盖最优状态的前驱，重建路径与时间不一致
因为 parent 这个字典变量在 Python 里一旦赋值就不能再修改
因为算法最终只需要返回总耗时的数字，不需要具体走过的路径
因为 heap 里的元组只能存数字，装不下站点这类字符串对象
why: parent 必须描述 best 时间对应的路径；无条件覆盖会让返回路线和累计时间脱节。
why_en: Parent pointers must be updated only on improvement so the reconstructed route matches the recorded best time.
options_en: Otherwise a worse path could overwrite the optimal state's predecessor, so the rebuilt path stops matching the recorded time.
Because a parent pointer can only be written once due to language limits.
Because Dijkstra doesn't need to return a path.
Because a heap cannot store strings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每个状态的前驱状态，只在终点弹出后一次性回溯出完整路径，而不是每次都复制整条 path。

optionExplanations: 对，只有真正更优时才更新，parent 链条才会和 best 记录的时间描述同一条路径。

q: 为什么 heap tuple 里常放一个单调递增的 counter？
q_en: Why is a monotonically increasing counter often included in the heap tuple?
options: 打破 time 相同时的比较顺序，避免比较到不可比较的元素
把 counter 加进旅行时间里，人为抬高总耗时来做惩罚
专门用来把每次换乘罚时的具体金额单独计算出来
专门在没有 parent pointer 记录前驱时，用它兜底重建路径
why: Python heap 会按 tuple 后续元素破平；counter 让相同 time 的条目也能稳定排序。
why_en: A monotonic counter breaks heap ties deterministically and prevents comparing arbitrary payload objects.
options_en: It breaks ties when two candidates share the same time, avoiding comparison of incomparable payloads.
It gets added into the travel time itself, artificially inflating total cost as a penalty.
It is used to compute the exact amount of each transfer penalty on its own.
It steps in as a fallback to rebuild the predecessor path when there's no parent pointer.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The counter is a monotonically increasing tie-breaker in the heap tuple that keeps entries with equal time comparable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种能以 O(log n) 时间取出当前最小元素的数据结构，这里按累计时间排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a data structure that returns the smallest element in O(log n) time, here ordered by cumulative travel time.

optionExplanations: 对，Python 比较 tuple 时前一项相同会比下一项，counter 保证永远不会比到 station 这类不可比较的对象上。
错，counter 只用来打破平局排序，从不会被加进 travel_time，也不会让真实总耗时变高。
错，换乘罚时固定是 5 分钟，由 is_transfer 逻辑单独算好，counter 只管排序，不参与这笔金额的计算。
错，parent pointer 才负责记录前驱、重建路径；counter 只是 heap 排序用的平局打破器，跟路径重建无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — when Python compares tuples with equal first elements it moves to the next one, and the counter guarantees that comparison never reaches an incomparable object like a station.
Wrong — the counter only breaks ties in ordering; it's never added into travel_time and never inflates the real total cost.
Wrong — the transfer penalty is a fixed five minutes computed separately by the is_transfer logic; the counter only handles ordering and plays no part in that amount.
Wrong — the parent pointer is what records predecessors to rebuild the path; the counter is just the heap's tie-breaker, unrelated to path reconstruction.
scenario: Python heapq 的条目形如 `(time, station, line, path)`，两条候选 time 相同时会继续比后面的元素。
