options: 把入度为 0 的任务放入 queue
pop 一个 ready task 加入 order

options_en: Put zero-in-degree tasks into the queue.
Pop a ready task and append it to the order.
Decrement the in-degree of its dependents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个任务还没完成的依赖数量。

q: 哪段代码正确构建 reverse adjacency？

options: in_degree = {t.name: 0 for t in tasks}

for t in tasks:

whenOtherWins: 如果输入本来就是 dep-to-dependent 的邻接表，就不用再反向构建一次。

Initialize in_degree to zero for every task and stop there.
For every task, append the task's own name onto its own dependents entry — a self-loop pointing at itself.
Point dependents directly at task.depends_on without inverting it.
tradeoff: 反转依赖方向建 dependents 表 vs 直接复用 depends_on 原始方向

这只是把入度表清零，完全没有建立依赖到后继任务的映射，查不到谁依赖谁。
把任务自己名字加进自己的列表里，方向反了还自环，没有反映真正的依赖关系。

q: Kahn topological sort 的时间复杂度是什么？
q_en: What is the time complexity of Kahn topological sort?
options: O(V + E)
O(log V)
why: 构建反向图访问每条依赖边一次，主循环每个任务出队一次、每条边再被更新一次，总量是线性的。
why_en: Building the reverse graph touches every edge once, and the main loop visits each task and each edge once more, so the total cost is linear.
scenario: 任务图有 V 个任务、E 条依赖边，你要确认 Kahn 排序在大图上是否还跑得动。
scenario_en: The task graph has V tasks and E dependency edges, and you need to know whether Kahn's sort still scales on a large graph.
options_en: O of V plus E, linear in tasks and edges.
O of V squared times E.
O of two to the V, exponential.
O of log V.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复取出入度为 0 的任务来生成拓扑序的算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kahn's algorithm generates a topological order by repeatedly removing zero-in-degree tasks.

optionExplanations: 每条边和每个任务都只被处理一次，加起来就是任务数加边数的线性量级。
这是给带二次方开销的算法准备的量级，这里每个任务和每条边都只碰一次，用不到这么多计算。
指数级通常出现在枚举子集或搜索所有组合，这里没有枚举动作，只是顺着入度扫一遍。
对数级通常来自不断折半的结构，比如平衡树查找，这里要看完每个节点和每条边，不可能这么快。
optionExplanations_en: Every edge and every task is touched exactly once, which adds up to linear in the number of tasks plus edges.
That shape belongs to algorithms with quadratic-ish overhead; this one only touches each task and edge once, so it never needs that much work.
Exponential blowups usually come from enumerating subsets or search paths, and there's no enumeration here — just a straight scan driven by in-degree.
Logarithmic time usually comes from repeatedly halving a structure, like a balanced-tree lookup; this has to visit every node and edge, so it can't be that fast.

q: 拓扑序和并行调度的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between a topological order and a parallel schedule?
options: 两者完全一样，只是叫法和写法习惯不同而已
并行调度过程完全不需要满足任何依赖关系约束
拓扑序只是合法线性序，并行调度还要决定任务何时在哪个 worker 上运行
拓扑序一旦算出来就自动最小化了整个 makespan，不需要再管 worker 怎么分配
why: 一个合法顺序不会告诉你如何利用多个 worker，也不会告诉你多个 ready task 该优先谁。
why_en: A valid order alone does not tell you how to use multiple workers or which ready task to prioritize when several compete.
scenario: Optimizer 的第一个方法给出拓扑序，第二个方法给出多 worker 的并行计划；面试官问两者到底差在哪。
scenario_en: Optimizer's first method returns a topological order, while the second returns a multi-worker parallel plan; the interviewer asks what really differs.
options_en: They are exactly the same thing, just different naming conventions.
A parallel schedule never needs to respect any dependency constraint.
A topological order is just a valid sequence, while a parallel schedule also decides when and on which worker each task runs.
A topological order automatically minimizes the whole makespan once it's computed., with no need to worry about how workers get assigned
tradeoff: 拓扑序（只保证依赖合法）vs 并行调度（还要分配 worker 和时间区间）

rows: 依赖顺序+worker 容量+时间区间

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到所有任务全部完成的总耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until every task has finished.

optionExplanations: 两者产出的信息量完全不同：一个只给顺序，一个还要给 worker 和时间区间，不是换个说法而已。
并行调度依然要保证依赖先完成才能开始后继任务，只是额外多管了 worker 分配。
拓扑序只保证先后关系合法，真正落到 worker 上跑，还需要决定谁用哪台机器、什么时间点。
顺序本身不含并行度和 worker 数信息，同一个合法顺序在不同分配策略下能跑出完全不同的完工时间。
optionExplanations_en: The two outputs carry very different information — one is just an order, the other also assigns workers and time intervals, not a rename of the same thing.
A parallel schedule still must let dependencies finish before their dependents start; it just adds worker assignment on top of that constraint.
A topological order only guarantees valid before/after; actually running it on workers still needs deciding which machine and when.
The order alone carries no information about parallelism or worker count, so the same valid order can produce very different finish times under different assignment strategies.

scenario: 你已有 Kahn 输出的 execution_order，想用一个直接贪心法分配到固定数量 worker。
scenario_en: You already have an execution_order from Kahn and want a simple greedy way to assign tasks to a fixed number of workers.
q: Solution 2 的基本做法是什么？
q_en: What is the basic idea of Solution 2?
options: 忽略依赖关系只按 duration 从长到短排序，完全打乱了正确的执行前提
按 execution_order 逐个任务，交给最早空闲的 worker
每隔一秒重新扫描一次所有任务状态
把每个任务随机分配给某个 worker
why: fixed-order list scheduling 消耗一个预先算好的顺序，每次用 worker heap 找最早空闲的 worker。
why_en: Fixed-order list scheduling consumes a precomputed order and repeatedly pulls the earliest-free worker off a heap.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务优先级必须随运行进展变化，预先固定顺序会错过新解锁的关键任务。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Order[Kahn order] --> Task[next task]
  Workers[min worker heap] --> Free[earliest free worker]
  Task --> Assign[assign interval]
  Free --> Assign
  Assign --> Workers
options_en: Ignore dependencies entirely and sort tasks from longest duration to shortest., which completely breaks the correct execution precondition
Walk the execution order one task at a time and hand each to the earliest-free worker.
Rescan every task's status once every simulated second.
Assign each task to a random worker.
tradeoff: 消耗预先算好的固定顺序 vs 每次事件重新决策（event-driven）

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶始终是最小值的数据结构，弹出操作是 O(log n)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a data structure whose top is always the smallest value, with O(log n) pop and push.

optionExplanations: 扔掉依赖关系会让还没 ready 的任务被提前派发，破坏正确性，不是一个可行的简化。
顺着已经算好的拓扑序走一遍，每次派活就摘队首任务给当前最早腾出手的 worker，逻辑简单又能保证依赖合法。
定时轮询要么浪费 CPU 空转等待，要么在两次扫描之间错过任务完成的时机，不是这题要的做法。
随机分配不看依赖也不看 worker 空闲状态，既可能违反顺序也浪费并行效率。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping dependencies lets a not-yet-ready task get dispatched early, breaking correctness — that's not a valid shortcut.
Walk the precomputed topological order and hand the next task to whichever worker frees up soonest — simple logic that still respects dependency order.
Polling on a fixed interval either burns CPU spinning or misses a completion between scans — neither matches what this solution does.
Random assignment ignores both dependencies and worker availability, risking an invalid order and wasted parallelism.

scenario: 并行调度中需要不断找到最早空闲的 worker，并在安排任务后更新它的下次空闲时间。
scenario_en: A parallel scheduler repeatedly needs the earliest-free worker and then updates that worker's next available time.
q: 应该用什么结构维护 worker？
q_en: Which data structure should maintain worker availability?
options: 把每个 worker 的状态拼成一个普通的长字符串，还得自己写解析和比较逻辑
min-heap of `(available_time, worker_id)`
用一个只能后进先出、不能随便取的栈，无法排序更没法比较可用时间
给每个 worker 分配一段字母表 bitmask 编码，也查不出谁的时间最早
why: min-heap 能以 O(log W) 弹出最早可用的 worker，并在任务结束时间更新后放回。
why_en: A min-heap pops the earliest-available worker in O(log W) time and pushes the updated availability back in.
whenOtherWins: worker 数极小时线性扫描也够用，但 heap 写法更通用、结果也更确定。
options_en: Concatenate every worker's state into one long plain string., and you'd still have to write your own parsing and comparison logic
A min-heap of (available_time, worker_id) pairs.
A stack that only pops in strict last-in-first-out order., which can't be ordered or compared by available time
Encode every worker into a segment of an alphabet bitmask., and still can't tell you who's free soonest
tradeoff: min-heap 维护 worker 可用时间 vs 每次线性扫描找最早空闲 worker

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶始终是最小值的数据结构，弹出和插入都是 O(log n)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a data structure whose top is always the smallest value, with O(log n) pop and push.

optionExplanations: 字符串没有排序语义，每次找最早空闲的 worker 还得自己解析比较，等于白拼。
堆顶始终是可用时间最小的那个 worker，弹出和更新都是对数时间，正好匹配反复取最早空闲这个操作。
栈只能拿到最后放进去的元素，找不到时间最早的那个 worker，跟这里要的查询完全对不上。
bitmask 编码适合表示集合成员关系，不携带可用时间这种连续数值，排不出谁最早空闲。
optionExplanations_en: A plain string has no ordering semantics, so you'd still have to parse and compare it yourself just to find the earliest-free worker.
The heap's top is always the worker with the smallest available time, and both pop and update run in log time — exactly the repeated 'find earliest free' operation this needs.
A stack only gives you the most recently pushed item, not the worker with the smallest available time, so it can't answer this query.
A bitmask is good for set membership, not a continuous value like available time, so it can't tell you who's free soonest.

q: 补全任务 start time 公式：
q_en: Fill in the task start-time formula:
text: 一个任务的开始时间应为 max({{所有依赖完成的最晚时间}}, {{worker 空闲时间}})，event-driven 版还会纳入当前模拟时间。
why: 任务必须等最后一个依赖完成，同时也必须等有 worker 可用。
why_en: A task starts at the maximum of dependency readiness and worker availability.

q: earliest-start helper 如果对依赖完成时间取 min 而不是 max，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the earliest-start helper takes min instead of max over dependency finish times?
options: 任务可能在某个依赖还没完成前就开始
所有任务都会等到最慢的那个依赖完成才开始
只有没有前置依赖的任务会被这处改动影响
只是把判断条件换了一下，不影响调度是否正确
why: 一个任务要等所有 prerequisite 完成，最早开始时间取决于最后完成的那个依赖。
why_en: A task must wait for its last prerequisite, so using the minimum dependency finish time can schedule it too early.
scenario: 某任务有两个 prerequisite，分别在 t=3 和 t=20 完成；earliest-start helper 决定它几点能开工。
scenario_en: A task has two prerequisites that finish at t=3 and t=20, and the earliest-start helper decides when it may begin.
options_en: The task might start before one of its dependencies has actually finished.
Every task would end up waiting for its slowest dependency before it can start.
Only tasks with no upstream dependencies would be affected by this change.
It just swaps which condition gets checked, without affecting whether the schedule is correct.
optionExplanations: 取最小值只看跑得最快完成的那个依赖，任务就可能在别的依赖还没做完时就抢跑开始。
这个 bug 只会让任务提前开始，不会让它反而等更久；说它会等最慢依赖完成，正好说反了方向。
没有依赖的任务本来就不用等谁，取最小还是最大对它们毫无影响，问题恰恰出在有依赖、且完成时间不同的任务上。
任务提前于依赖开始会读到还没算出来的数据或状态，这正是一个正确性 bug，不是换个判断条件那么无关紧要。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the min only looks at whichever dependency finishes fastest, so the task can jump the gun while another dependency is still unfinished.
This bug makes tasks start too early, not wait longer — claiming it waits for the slowest dependency has the direction backwards.
Tasks with zero dependencies never waited on anyone in the first place, so min vs max changes nothing for them; the damage lands on tasks that have multiple dependencies finishing at different times.
Starting before a dependency finishes means reading data or state that isn't ready yet — that's a real correctness bug, not a harmless swap of which condition gets checked.

scenario: fixed-order scheduler 正在处理一个任务，已知 `earliest` 和弹出的 `worker_free`。
scenario_en: The fixed-order scheduler is handling one task and already knows earliest and the popped worker_free time.
q: 哪段代码正确计算任务运行区间？
q_en: Which code correctly computes a task's run interval?
options: start = 0; end = earliest
start = min(earliest, worker_free); end = task.duration  # picks whichever condition is satisfied earlier
start = max(earliest, worker_free); end = start + task.duration
start = worker_free - task.duration; end = worker_free
why: 任务必须同时满足依赖完成和 worker 空闲两个条件，取较晚的那个作为开始时间，再加上 duration。
why_en: A task must satisfy both dependency completion and worker availability, so start is the later of the two, and end adds the duration.
whenOtherWins: 在 event-driven 版本里还要把 current_time 也纳入 max，防止任务被安排到模拟时间之前。
codeSample:
worker_free, worker_id = heapq.heappop(workers)
start = max(earliest, worker_free)
end = start + task.duration
timeline[name] = (start, end)
# max(), not min() -- a task waits for BOTH conditions
options_en: Set start to 0 and end to earliest.
Take the minimum of earliest and worker_free as start, and end equals just the duration — picks whichever condition is satisfied earlier.
Take the maximum of earliest and worker_free as start, then add the duration to get end.
Set start to worker_free minus the duration and end to worker_free.
tradeoff: 取 max(依赖完成时间, worker 空闲时间) vs 只看其中一个条件
optionExplanations: 开始时间写死成 0 完全不看依赖和 worker 状态，结束时间也没加上任务本身要跑多久。
取最小值会挑那个更早满足的条件，可能在依赖还没完成或 worker 还没空出来时就起跑；结束时间也漏加了起点。
两个条件都要满足，所以取较晚的那个当起点，再把 duration 加上去得到结束时间，这正是两个约束的正确合成方式。
倒着从 worker 空闲时间减 duration 算出的起点跟依赖完成时间毫无关系，是编造出来的时间点。
optionExplanations_en: Hard-coding start to 0 ignores both dependency and worker state entirely, and end skips adding how long the task actually runs.
Taking the min picks whichever condition is satisfied earlier, which can start the task before a dependency finishes or before a worker is even free; end also forgets to add start.
Both conditions must hold, so the start is the later of the two, and adding the duration gives the end — this is the correct way to combine both constraints.
Working backward from worker-free time minus duration has nothing to do with when the dependencies actually finish; it's an invented timestamp.

q: fixed-order worker assignment 的调度循环复杂度主要是什么？
q_en: What is the main loop complexity of fixed-order worker assignment?
options: O(2^V)，枚举所有可能的任务子集
O(W^V)，枚举 worker 的全部分配方式
O(V log W)，另有 O(V+E) 预处理
O(1)，与任务数量完全无关
why: 每个任务只做一次 heap pop 和 push，worker heap 大小为 W；拓扑排序预处理仍是线性的。
why_en: Each task does exactly one heap pop and push against a worker heap of size W, and the topological-sort setup stays linear.
scenario: 任务数 V 很大、worker 数 W 较小，你想确认 fixed-order 调度循环会不会先成为瓶颈。
scenario_en: V is large and W is small, so you want to check whether the fixed-order assignment loop becomes the bottleneck.
options_en: O of two to the V, enumerating every possible task subset.
O of W to the V, enumerating every way to assign workers.
O of V log W, plus O of V plus E setup.
O of 1, completely independent of the number of tasks.
optionExplanations: 这套算法没有枚举任务子集这个动作，每个任务只处理一次，用不到指数级开销。
枚举每种 worker 分配方式是暴力搜索的做法，这里每个任务只对 worker 堆做一次弹出和插入。
每个任务对 worker 堆做一次对数时间的弹出和插入，加上前面拓扑排序本身的线性预处理。
任务数变多，worker 堆的弹出插入次数也跟着变多，耗时不可能和任务数完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: There's no subset enumeration here — every task is handled exactly once, so it never pays exponential cost.
Enumerating every possible worker assignment is what brute-force search would do; here each task only does one pop and push against the worker heap.
Each task does one log-time pop and push against the worker heap, on top of the linear topological-sort preprocessing that came before it.
As the task count grows, the number of worker-heap pops and pushes grows with it, so the cost can't be independent of task count.

q: 这条链对并行调度设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this chain imply for parallel scheduling?
options: 只要 worker 数量够多，这条链也能被压缩到更短时间，只要调度足够聪明
把链拆给不同 worker 并行执行就能突破这个下界
无论并行度多高，makespan 都不可能低于这条链总时长，调度必须让它连续拿到 worker
这条链和独立任务同等重要，谁先跑不影响最终 makespan，可以随时被别的任务抢占 worker
why: 链上任务必须严格串行，1+8+8+8+1=26 秒是任何调度都无法突破的下界，所以关键链必须优先拿到 worker。
why_en: The chain must run strictly in sequence, so its 26-second total is a hard lower bound no schedule can beat, which is why it must get priority for workers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Setup[setup] --> B1[build 1]
  B1 --> B2[build 2]
  B2 --> B3[build 3]
  B3 --> Final[finalize]
  Final --> Bound[critical path lower bound 26]
scenario: critical-path graph 里 setup→build-1→build-2→build-3→finalize 的 duration 分别是 1/8/8/8/1 秒，这五个任务必须严格顺序执行。
scenario_en: In the critical-path graph, setup, build-1, build-2, build-3, and finalize take 1, 8, 8, 8, and 1 seconds and must run in strict order.
options_en: Adding enough workers can compress this chain to finish faster., as long as the scheduler is clever enough
Splitting the chain across workers in parallel can beat this lower bound.
No matter how many workers you have, the makespan can never beat this chain's total duration, so the scheduler must keep it running back to back.
This chain is no more important than the independent tasks, so run order doesn't matter., and can be preempted by other tasks for a worker at any time

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定整个调度下界的那条最长依赖链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the longest dependency chain, and it sets the lower bound on the whole schedule.

optionExplanations: 链上每一步都要等前一步做完才能开始，多加 worker 也没法让本该串行的步骤同时跑。
拆开也没用，因为链上后一个任务本来就依赖前一个任务的结果，物理上没法提前开始。
链上五个任务必须首尾相接地跑完，26 秒是任何 worker 数下都甩不掉的下限，调度只能想办法不让它中途被别的任务插队。
如果这条链被独立任务插队占用 worker，链会被推迟完成，makespan 也会跟着变长，先后顺序其实很关键。
optionExplanations_en: Every step in the chain must wait for the previous one to finish, so adding more workers can't make sequential steps run at the same time.
Splitting it up doesn't help, because each later task in the chain genuinely depends on the previous one's output and can't physically start early.
The five chained tasks must run back to back, so 26 seconds is a floor no worker count can beat; scheduling can only avoid letting other work cut in front of it.
If independent tasks grab the workers this chain needs, the chain finishes later and the makespan grows with it — run order clearly matters here.

q: fixed-order scheduler 在 critical-path graph 上为什么得到 38 秒？
q_en: Why does the fixed-order scheduler produce 38 seconds on the critical-path graph?
options: 调度器其实完全没有检查过任何一条依赖关系
调度器把可用 worker 的数量错误地写死成了一个
Kahn 顺序把 scan 排在 setup 前，worker 先被占满，链晚 12 秒启动
调度器把每个任务的 duration 数值错误地重复加了两遍，导致每个任务的运行时长都被错误地翻倍计算
why: 固定顺序在 t=0 就承诺了 scan 优先，导致真正决定 makespan 的 build chain 等 worker。
why_en: Fixed-order scheduling commits workers to scans first, delaying the critical chain and producing a 38-second makespan.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Ready[t0 ready tasks] --> Scans[workers take scans]
  Scans --> Delay[setup waits]
  Delay --> Late[build chain starts late]
  Late --> M38[makespan 38]
scenario: critical-path graph 里 26 秒的关键链和几个独立 scan 抢同一批 worker，Kahn 顺序把 scan 排在前面。
scenario_en: In the critical-path graph a 26-second dependency chain and several independent scans compete for the same worker pool, and Kahn's order lists the scans first.
options_en: The scheduler actually never checks any dependency at all.
The scheduler hard-codes the available worker count down to just one.
Kahn's order lists the scans before setup, so workers get taken by scans first and the chain starts 12 seconds late.
The scheduler mistakenly adds every task's duration value in twice.，so every task's run time gets mistakenly doubled
optionExplanations: 如果完全不检查依赖，调度结果会直接违反先后顺序，而不是单纯多花 12 秒。
如果 worker 只有一个，两个 worker 场景下的并行行为根本不会出现，问题不在 worker 数写死。
在最初那一刻 Kahn 顺序先把 worker 分给了 scan 任务，等它们跑完 setup 才能开始，链条整体被推迟了 12 秒。
duration 被重复计算会让单个任务本身变慢，而这里是任务被延迟启动，两者原因不一样。
optionExplanations_en: If dependencies were never checked, the result would violate ordering outright, not just cost an extra 12 seconds.
If only one worker existed, the two-worker parallel behavior seen elsewhere wouldn't show up at all — the worker count isn't hard-coded here.
At the very start Kahn's order hands the workers to the scan tasks first, so setup can't start until they finish, pushing the whole chain 12 seconds late.
Double-counting a duration would make one task itself run longer, whereas what actually happens is the task starting late — a different failure entirely.

q: critical-path graph 的失败结构包括哪些元素？（多选）
q_en: Which elements make up the failure shape of the critical-path graph? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 一条长依赖链决定下界
多个独立长 scan 一开始就 ready
scan 看起来可以填满 worker 但不推进关键链
所有任务都互相依赖成环
why: 独立 scan 与关键链竞争 worker，暴露了固定顺序不按剩余关键工作优先的问题。
why_en: The graph mixes a long critical chain with independent scans that distract a fixed-order scheduler.
scenario: 同一张图上 fixed-order 跑出 38 秒，而关键链本身的下界只有 26 秒，你要定位图里造成差距的结构。
scenario_en: On this graph the fixed-order scheduler takes 38 seconds while the chain alone bounds it at 26, and you need to name the structures causing the gap.
options_en: A single long dependency chain sets the lower bound.
Several independent long scans are ready from the very start.
The scans look like they fill up the workers but don't advance the critical chain.
Every task depends on every other task, forming a cycle.
optionExplanations: 这条链的总时长就是整张图无论怎么调度都甩不掉的最短完工时间。
这些扫描任务互相之间没有依赖，一开始就全部满足条件，会跟链条一起抢 worker。
扫描任务能让 worker 看起来很忙，但它们不解锁链条上的下一个任务，对缩短 makespan 没有帮助。
整图是一个有向无环图才能做拓扑排序；如果真的成环，算法根本跑不完，这不是这道题的失败模式。
optionExplanations_en: This chain's total duration is the shortest possible finish time for the whole graph no matter how you schedule it.
These scans have no dependencies on each other, so they're all ready from the start and compete with the chain for workers.
Scans keep workers looking busy, but they don't unlock the next task on the chain, so they do nothing to shorten the makespan.
The graph has to be acyclic for topological sort to even work; if it really formed a cycle, the algorithm couldn't finish at all — that's not what's failing here.

q: Kahn 输出顺序为什么不能直接当作最优并行调度优先级？
q_en: Why can't Kahn's output order be used directly as the optimal parallel-scheduling priority?
options: Kahn's algorithm 根本不能产生一个合法的顺序，这跟实际观察到的结果不符
多个任务同时 ready 时，Kahn 顺序只是插入或任意 tie-break，不知道关键路径
Kahn's algorithm 会直接忽略掉所有依赖关系，但它其实完全依赖入度这个依赖信号
Kahn's algorithm 一次只能处理单独一个任务，但实际上它可以处理任意多任务和边的整张图
why: 拓扑序只保证依赖合法，不保证把 worker 分配给最影响 makespan 的 ready task。
why_en: Kahn's tie-breaking creates a valid order but does not prioritize work that controls the makespan.
scenario: 某时刻 5 个任务同时 ready 但只剩 1 个空闲 worker，你想直接拿 Kahn 输出顺序当挑选优先级。
scenario_en: At one moment five tasks are ready but only one worker is free, and you're tempted to use Kahn's output order as the pick priority.
options_en: Kahn's algorithm cannot produce a valid order in the first place., which doesn't match what's actually observed
When several tasks are ready at once, Kahn's order is just insertion order or an arbitrary tie-break, with no idea which sits on the critical path.
Kahn's algorithm ignores every dependency relationship outright., when it's actually driven entirely by the in-degree signal
Kahn's algorithm can only ever process a single task at a time., when it can actually handle a whole graph with any number of tasks and edges

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定调度下界的最长依赖链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the longest dependency chain, which sets the lower bound on the schedule.

optionExplanations: Kahn 算法本来就是专门产生合法拓扑序的算法，产不出顺序不是它的问题。
多个任务同时满足条件时，谁先入队完全看插入顺序或随意的 tie-break，算法根本不知道谁在关键链上。
Kahn 算法恰恰是靠入度这个依赖信号驱动的，忽略依赖它连排序都做不出来。
算法每一步确实弹出一个任务，但这只是遍历顺序，并不代表它不能处理有很多任务的整张图。
optionExplanations_en: Kahn's algorithm exists specifically to produce a valid topological order, so producing no order at all isn't a real failure mode of it.
When several tasks are ready at once, whichever gets queued first is just insertion order or an arbitrary tie-break — the algorithm has no idea which one sits on the critical chain.
Kahn's algorithm is literally driven by in-degree, a dependency signal — ignoring dependencies would mean it couldn't even produce an order.
The algorithm does pop one task at a time, but that's just traversal order — it doesn't mean it can't handle a graph with many tasks.

scenario: 固定顺序在 critical-path graph 上把关键链饿住；你希望每次任务完成时重新看哪些任务 ready，并按剩余关键工作排序。
scenario_en: Fixed order starves the critical chain on the critical-path graph; you want to re-check ready tasks at each completion and sort by remaining critical work.
q: 应该升级成哪种调度方式？
q_en: Which scheduling approach should this be upgraded to?
options: 继续原封不动地沿用固定不变的、Kahn 早就排好的那份顺序，这份顺序已经被证明会让链条变慢
干脆让每一个 worker 都完全随机地去领取下一个任务
改用 event-driven，按 critical-path priority 排
把所有任务强行改成必须严格串行、一个接一个地运行
why: event-driven 每次跳到下一个完成事件再重新分配 worker，critical-path priority 则让长链任务优先。
why_en: Event-driven simulation re-evaluates ready tasks at completion events and prioritizes the longest remaining chain.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务非常少且 fixed-order 已满足 makespan 目标，简单方案可能足够。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Events[task completions] --> Ready[recompute ready tasks]
  Ready --> Priority[sort by critical length]
  Priority --> Workers[assign free workers]
  Workers --> Events
options_en: Keep reusing the fixed order that Kahn's algorithm already computed, unchanged., and that order has already been shown to slow the chain down
Just let every worker grab its next task completely at random.
Switch to event-driven scheduling, ordered by critical-path priority.
Force every task to run strictly one after another instead.
tradeoff: event-driven 每次完成事件重新决策 vs fixed-order 在 t=0 一次性决定

rows: 一次性 t=0 排好顺序
每次完成事件重新决策

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间跳到下一个任务完成事件才重新决策，而不是按固定顺序预先分配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Event-driven simulation jumps time forward to the next task-completion event and re-decides then, instead of pre-assigning a fixed order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定调度下界的最长依赖链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the longest dependency chain, which sets the lower bound on the schedule.

optionExplanations: 已经证明这份固定顺序会让 worker 先被扫描任务占满、链条延后，继续用它解决不了问题。
随机领取完全不看谁在拖长 makespan 的关键链上，效果和固定顺序一样碰运气。
每次有任务完成就重新看谁 ready，并优先把 worker 给剩余关键链最长的任务，这正好对症下药。
把独立的扫描任务也强行串行化只会白白浪费并行度，问题只出在关键链没被优先，不是并行本身有问题。
optionExplanations_en: That fixed order is already proven to let scans occupy the workers first and delay the chain — sticking with it doesn't fix anything.
Random pickup ignores which task sits on the makespan-driving chain, so it's just as much a gamble as the fixed order.
Re-checking what's ready at every completion and prioritizing the worker for whichever task has the longest remaining chain targets exactly this failure.
Forcing even the independent scans to run one at a time just wastes parallelism for no reason — the real problem is priority, not parallelism itself.

q: 补全 critical-path length 定义：
q_en: Fill in the definition of critical-path length:
text: 一个任务的 critical-path length 等于它自己的 {{duration}} 加上所有 dependent 链中最长的 {{后续工作长度}}。
why: 这个数估计如果现在不做该任务，会拖住多少剩余链式工作。
why_en: A task's critical-path length is its own duration plus the longest remaining dependent chain after it.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Task[task duration] --> CP[critical length]
  Child1[dependent chain A] --> Max[max child length]
  Child2[dependent chain B] --> Max
  Max --> CP

q: 没有 dependent 的叶子任务 critical-path length 是什么？
q_en: What is the critical-path length of a leaf task with no dependents?
options: 它自己的 duration
所有任务 duration 之和
worker 数
why: 叶子后面没有后续链，所以剩余关键工作就是它本身的运行时间。
why_en: A leaf task has no successors, so its critical length is just its own duration.
scenario: critical_length 定义为从该任务起算的最长剩余链总时长；某任务跑 5 秒且没有任何 dependent。
scenario_en: critical_length is defined as the longest remaining chain starting at a task; this one runs for 5 seconds and has no dependents at all.
options_en: Its own duration.
Zero.
The sum of every task's duration.
The number of workers.
optionExplanations: 没有后继任务时，公式里取最大值那部分是空的算作 0，剩下的就只是这个任务本身要跑多久。
0 意味着这个任务不占用任何剩余关键工作量，但它自己确实要花时间执行，不该被当作 0。
把所有任务加总算的是全图总工作量，跟这一个叶子任务后面还剩多少关键链完全是两个概念。
worker 数是资源容量，跟单个任务自身要跑多久、后面还有没有后续链没有任何关系。
optionExplanations_en: With no successors, the recursive max term is empty and defaults to zero, leaving just this task's own run time.
Zero would mean this task contributes no remaining critical work at all, but it still takes real time to run — it shouldn't be treated as zero.
Summing every task's duration gives the total work in the whole graph, a completely different number from how much critical chain is left after one leaf.
Worker count is a resource capacity number — it has nothing to do with how long one task runs or whether anything follows it.

scenario: 你已经有 dependents map，需要递归计算每个任务的 longest remaining chain，并做 memoization。
scenario_en: You already have a dependents map and need to recursively compute each task's longest remaining chain with memoization.
q: 哪段递归公式符合文章实现？
q_en: Which recursive formula matches the article's implementation?
options: sum(t.duration for t in all_tasks) for every task
min(longest_chain(s) for s in successors) if successors else 0  # keeps only the shortest branch below it
duration - len(successors) * average_child_duration
duration + (max(longest_chain(s) for s in successors) if successors else 0)
why: 关键路径只关心最长的那条后继链，而不是所有后继总和；当前任务本身的 duration 也必须计入。
why_en: Critical length only cares about the single longest successor chain, not the sum of all of them, and it must also add the task's own duration.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是按总工作量排序而不是 makespan 关键链，可以换成 subtree work 之类的不同优先级。
options_en: Sum every task's duration in the whole graph, for every task.
Take the minimum of longest_chain over its successors, or zero if there are none — keeps only the shortest branch below it.
Subtract the successor count times their average duration from this task's duration.
Add the duration to the maximum longest_chain among its successors, or zero if there are none.
tradeoff: 取后继链的 max（关键路径长度）vs 取 sum（总工作量）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把递归子问题的结果缓存起来，避免重复计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memoization caches the result of a recursive subproblem so it is never recomputed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个任务自己的 duration 加上它后面最长的剩余依赖链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Critical-path length is a task's own duration plus the longest remaining chain of work after it.

optionExplanations: 给每个任务都套用全图总时长，等于让所有任务的优先级变成同一个数字，完全分不出谁在关键链上。
取最小值会挑最短的那条后继链，恰好丢掉了真正拖慢完工时间的那条最长链。
减去平均子任务时长是编出来的公式，既不反映真实剩余工作量，数值上也可能变成负数。
自身时长加上后继里最长的那条链，没有后继就补 0，这正是这个概念的定义。
optionExplanations_en: Applying the whole graph's total duration to every task would give every task the same priority number, with no way to tell which one sits on the critical chain.
Taking the min picks the shortest successor chain, throwing away exactly the longest chain that actually drives the finish time.
Subtracting an average child duration is a made-up formula that doesn't reflect real remaining work and can even go negative.
A task's own duration plus the longest chain among its successors, or zero when there are none, is exactly the intended definition.

scenario: 在某个时刻有多个 ready tasks，但 free workers 不够，需要选择谁先跑。
scenario_en: At one moment several tasks are ready, but there are not enough free workers, so the scheduler must choose which tasks run first.
q: event-driven 版本用什么 priority？
q_en: What priority should the event-driven version use?
options: 永远按每个任务的 duration 从短到长升序排序，跟任务后面还有多长的链没关系
永远按输入列表里给定的原始先后顺序处理
每次分配前都先把 ready 列表打乱成随机顺序
critical_length 降序，任务名作为稳定 tie-break
why: 最长剩余链优先能防止关键链被独立 filler 任务阻塞；任务名 tie-break 让输出确定。
why_en: Prioritizing the longest remaining chain keeps the critical chain from being blocked by independent filler work, and the name tie-break keeps output deterministic.
whenOtherWins: 如果有真实业务优先级或截止期，priority key 需要把这些约束纳入。
options_en: Always sort by each task's duration, shortest first., regardless of how long a chain trails behind the task
Always process tasks in whatever order the input list originally gave.
Shuffle the ready list into a fresh random order before every assignment.
Descending critical_length, with the task name as a stable tie-break.
tradeoff: 按 critical_length 降序（保关键链）vs 按 duration 或输入顺序（保公平/简单）

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个任务自己的 duration 加上它后面最长的剩余依赖链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Critical-path length is a task's own duration plus the longest remaining chain of work after it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当两个候选的排序键相等时，用来决出确定顺序的额外规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tie-break is the extra rule that produces a deterministic order when two candidates have equal sort keys.

optionExplanations: 按时长短的先跑会让又短又不在关键链上的任务抢先拿 worker，把真正拖慢完工时间的长链晾在一边。
输入顺序只是任务被列出来的先后，和它对完工时间的影响力毫无关系。
每次都随机洗牌会让关键链任务时而优先时而不优先，结果不确定，也没有理由能保住它优先跑。
剩余关键链越长越先分配，保证它不被短小的任务插队；名字当 tie-break 让并列情况下结果每次一致。
optionExplanations_en: Running shortest-duration tasks first lets short, off-chain filler tasks grab workers ahead of the long chain that's actually driving the finish time.
Input order is just the order tasks happened to be listed in — it has nothing to do with how much they affect the finish time.
Reshuffling randomly before every assignment means the critical chain sometimes wins and sometimes doesn't, with no guarantee it stays prioritized.
Assigning by longest remaining chain first keeps the critical chain from being cut in line by short filler tasks, and the name tie-break keeps ties deterministic.

q: event-driven simulation 维护了哪些运行时结构？（多选）
q_en: Which runtime structures does event-driven simulation maintain? (Choose all that apply.)
options: worker heap：空闲 worker
events heap：正在运行任务的完成事件
completed set 和 completion_times
scheduled set
why: workers 管资源，events 推动时间前进，completed/completion_times 解锁依赖，scheduled 防止重复派发。
why_en: The simulation tracks free workers, in-flight completion events, completed tasks, finish times, and already scheduled tasks.

rows: 按时间找最早空闲 worker
按完成时间排进行中任务
已完成任务和完成时刻
已派发但未完成的任务

scenario: event-driven 版本要让模拟时间在完成事件上跳跃、复用 W 个 worker，且同一任务不能被派发两次。
scenario_en: The event-driven version must jump simulated time to completion events, recycle W workers, and never dispatch the same task twice.
options_en: A worker heap tracking free workers.
An events heap tracking completion times of in-flight tasks.
A completed set and completion_times map.
A scheduled set.
optionExplanations: 记录哪些 worker 现在空着、什么时候空出来的，是分配新任务时要查的资源池。
按完成时间排好正在跑的任务，模拟时间就靠弹出堆顶跳到下一个事件。
标记哪些任务真正做完了、几点做完的，用来判断后继任务是否 ready。
标记哪些任务已经派给 worker 但还没完成，防止同一个任务被再分配一次。
optionExplanations_en: It tracks which workers are currently idle and when, the resource pool checked before assigning new work.
It keeps in-flight tasks ordered by finish time, and the simulation clock advances by popping the earliest one off this heap.
It marks which tasks are actually done and exactly when, which is what decides whether their dependents are now ready.
It marks which tasks are already handed to a worker but not finished yet, so the same task can't get assigned twice.

q: `scheduled` set 在 event-driven 版本中的作用是什么？
q_en: What does the scheduled set do in the event-driven version?
options: 只是单纯记录所有已经完成的任务
防止 ready helper 在后续调用中把已经派发但尚未完成的任务再次分配
完全替代 completion_times 这个字典，但两者存的信息类型完全不一样，谁也换不了谁
用来计算每个任务的 critical_length
why: ready task 可能多次出现在 helper 输出里；任务一旦被 worker 抢走就要标记 scheduled，避免重复安排。
why_en: The scheduled set prevents a ready task that is already assigned but not completed from being assigned again.
scenario: ready-task helper 只看 completed 集合，所以已派发但还在跑的任务每轮都会被它再次列为 ready。
scenario_en: The ready-task helper only looks at the completed set, so a task already dispatched but still running keeps showing up as ready every round.
options_en: It simply records every task that has already completed.
It stops the ready-task helper from handing out a task that is already dispatched but not yet finished.
It completely replaces the completion_times dictionary., but the two store completely different kinds of information and can't substitute for each other
It is used to compute each task's critical_length.
optionExplanations: 记录已完成的是另一个集合的职责，这个集合关心的是占了 worker 但还没做完的中间状态。
每次重新扫描时可能又把同一个还没跑完的任务列进来，这个集合就是用来把它过滤掉的。
完成时间字典存的是完成时刻这个数值，这个集合只是个名字集合，两者记录的信息完全不同，谁也替代不了谁。
关键链长度是靠后继图递归算出来的，跟一个任务是否已经派给 worker 没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Recording finished tasks is the completed set's job; this set is about the in-between state of already occupying a worker but not done yet.
Every time the ready-task helper rescans, it can list the same still-running task again, and this set is what filters that duplicate out.
The completion-time dictionary stores an actual finish timestamp, while this is just a set of names — they hold different information and neither can replace the other.
Critical-chain length is computed recursively from the dependents graph, which has nothing to do with whether a task has already been handed to a worker.

scenario: assign_ready 每次调用 ready-task helper，但有些 ready task 可能已经被分配到 worker 还没完成。
scenario_en: assign_ready calls the ready-task helper each time, but some ready tasks may already be assigned to workers and not completed yet.
q: 哪段过滤逻辑能防止重复分配？
q_en: Which filtering logic prevents duplicate assignment?
options: scheduled.clear() 之后什么后续处理都不做
ready = get_ready_tasks(set())，直接忽略当前真实的完成状态
ready = [task for task in tasks if task.name in scheduled] 反过来过滤，这个方向反了，会把刚解锁但还没派发的任务全部漏掉
ready = [t for t in scheduler.get_ready_tasks(completed) if t.name not in scheduled]
why: scheduled 表示已经占用 worker 的任务，虽然未 completed，但不能再次派发。
why_en: Filtering out already scheduled tasks prevents duplicate assignments across repeated ready scans.
whenOtherWins: 如果维护的是 in-degree ready 堆并只在入堆时处理一次，也可以不用反复扫描 helper。
codeSample:
ready = [
    t for t in scheduler.get_ready_tasks(completed)
    if t.name not in scheduled
]
# already-dispatched tasks are filtered out so they aren't assigned twice
options_en: Clear the scheduled set and do nothing else afterward.
Call get_ready_tasks with an empty set, ignoring the real completed state entirely.
Filter the other way around: keep only tasks whose name is already in scheduled — the direction is backwards and drops every newly-unlocked task.
Keep ready tasks from get_ready_tasks(completed) whose name is NOT already in scheduled.
tradeoff: 每次重新扫描 ready helper 并过滤 scheduled vs 维护增量 in-degree 优先队列
optionExplanations: 清空这个集合会让已经在跑的任务重新被当成可以派发，反而制造了重复分配的漏洞。
传一个空的完成集合去查 ready，会把还没解锁依赖的任务也当成 ready，跟真实完成状态完全脱节。
只保留已经在集合里的任务，等于把新解锁但还没派发的任务全部漏掉了，方向反了。
先用真实的完成集合问谁 ready，再把已经派发的排除掉，这样才不会把还没跑完的任务再派一次。
optionExplanations_en: Clearing the set makes already-running tasks look assignable again, which is exactly the bug that causes duplicate dispatch.
Querying ready tasks with an empty completed set treats tasks with unmet dependencies as ready too, completely detached from real progress.
Keeping only tasks already marked dispatched drops every newly-unlocked, not-yet-dispatched task — the filter direction is backwards.
Ask for ready tasks using the real completed set, then drop anything already dispatched, so an in-flight task never gets dispatched twice.

q: 为什么 event loop 要一次性 drain 掉同一 end_time 的所有 completion events 后再 assign_ready？
q_en: Why should the event loop drain all completion events with the same end_time before assign_ready?
options: 因为 heap 这种数据结构不能存两个相同的时间戳，而不是任务处理逻辑本身决定的
因为依赖只能严格按顺序一个接一个地完成
否则同一时刻完成的多个 worker 只释放一部分，新任务被安排得过晚
否则所有任务都会被重复安排运行一次
why: 同一时刻完成的任务应同时释放 worker 和依赖；先分配会低估可用 worker 数。
why_en: All tasks completing at the same time should release their workers before assigning new work at that time.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Pop[first completion at t] --> Drain[drain all events at t]
  Drain --> Free[release all workers]
  Drain --> Done[mark all completed]
  Free --> Assign[assign newly ready tasks]
  Done --> Assign
scenario: 3 个任务同时在 t=8 完成，事件堆里躺着 3 条同一时刻的 completion event，之后才轮到分配。
scenario_en: Three tasks all finish at t=8, so the event heap holds three completion events at the same timestamp before any assignment happens.
options_en: Because a heap data structure cannot store two equal timestamps., not something decided by the task-processing logic itself
Because dependencies can only ever finish one strictly after another.
Otherwise only some of the workers finishing at that instant get released, so new work gets scheduled later than necessary.
Otherwise every task would end up getting scheduled to run twice.
optionExplanations: 堆完全可以存重复的时间戳，只是弹出顺序按值排，这不是要一次处理完的原因。
多个独立任务完全可以在同一时刻各自完成，先后顺序不是必须严格分开的。
如果只处理第一个完成事件就去分配，同一时刻其它刚释放的 worker 还没被记入可用池，新任务只能等到下一轮才被派发。
一次性处理完是为了把状态更新完整，跟任务会不会被重复安排是两件事。
optionExplanations_en: A heap can absolutely hold duplicate timestamps — pop order just follows value — so that's not why draining matters here.
Multiple independent tasks can genuinely finish at the exact same instant; nothing forces them into strict one-after-another order.
If assignment happens after only the first completion event, the other workers freeing up at that same instant aren't in the available pool yet, so new work waits an extra round to get dispatched.
Draining fully is about getting the state updated in one pass — it's unrelated to whether a task gets scheduled twice.

scenario: event loop 已弹出一个完成事件 `(end_time, name, worker_id)`，还需要处理同一时刻的其他完成事件。
scenario_en: The event loop has popped one completion event, (end_time, name, worker_id), and still needs to process other completions at the same time.
q: 哪段代码表达了文章里的 drain 逻辑？
q_en: Which code expresses the drain logic from the article?
options: return immediately，什么 drain 都不做
while workers: pop workers，把 worker 堆整个清空，既不检查完成时间戳也不释放对应的正在运行任务
if events: events.clear()，直接清空事件堆
while events and events[0][0] == end_time: pop and mark completed
why: inner loop 把同一时间完成的任务都加入 completed，并把它们的 worker 都放回 pool。
why_en: The loop drains every event with the same finish time so all simultaneous completions are visible before reassignment.
whenOtherWins: 如果事件系统天然就批量返回同一 timestamp 的事件，可以在更高层做同样的处理。
codeSample:
while events and events[0][0] == end_time:
    et, tn, wi = heapq.heappop(events)
    completed.add(tn)
    completion_times[tn] = et
    heapq.heappush(workers, (et, wi))
# all workers finishing at end_time are freed first
options_en: Return immediately and skip draining anything at all.
Pop every worker off the heap in a loop until it's completely empty — checks no timestamp and frees no specific in-flight task.
Clear the entire events heap outright whenever it's non-empty.
Keep popping and marking events complete while the next one shares the same end_time.
tradeoff: drain 同一时刻的所有 completion events 再分配 vs 逐个处理一有完成就立即分配
optionExplanations: 直接返回什么都不处理，连第一个完成事件本身都没标记完成，连基本状态更新都做不到。
把 worker 堆整个清空清的是空闲池本身，既没有处理任何完成事件，也没有把这一刻真正解锁的 worker 放回去。
把整个事件堆清空，会连未来其它时刻的完成事件也一起丢掉，破坏了后续时间线。
只要堆顶下一个事件的时间戳还等于当前完成时刻，就继续弹出标完成、释放 worker，直到时间戳变了为止，正好一次性处理完同一时刻的完成事件。
optionExplanations_en: Returning immediately doesn't even mark the first popped event complete — no state gets updated at all.
Draining the worker heap empties the free-worker pool itself — it never processes any completion event, nor does it put back the workers actually freed at this instant.
Clearing the whole events heap throws away every future completion event too, wrecking the rest of the timeline.
Keep popping and marking tasks complete as long as the heap's next timestamp still equals this completion time, until it changes — this drains exactly the completions sharing this instant.

q: event-driven 的 `start = max(earliest, worker_free, current_time)` 为什么要包含 `current_time`？
q_en: Why does event-driven start = max(earliest, worker_free, current_time) include current_time?
options: 防止在当前模拟时刻之前安排新任务
让所有任务都要等到最晚完成的依赖才能开始
把它当成 duration 的替代值来用
跳过依赖是否完成的检查，直接开始任务
why: assignment 发生在某个事件时刻；即使 worker_free 和 dependency time 较早，任务也不能回到过去开始。
why_en: Including current_time prevents assigning a task to start before the simulation time at which the decision is made.
scenario: 在 t=12 的事件时刻分配任务：它的依赖早在 t=4 就完成，worker 也从 t=6 起一直空闲。
scenario_en: You are assigning at the t=12 event: this task's dependency finished back at t=4 and the worker has been idle since t=6.
options_en: It prevents scheduling a new task to start before the current simulated moment.
It makes every task wait for its slowest dependency before it can start.
It treats current_time as a stand-in replacement for duration.
It skips checking whether dependencies are done and starts right away.
optionExplanations: 前面的空闲时间或依赖完成时间都可能早于当前处理到的那一刻，加上模拟时间保证任务不会被安排到过去。
它只是抬高起点的下限，跟等哪个依赖完成没关系；说要等最晚依赖才能开始，其实把 current_time 管的事和依赖完成时间管的事搞混了。
任务本身要跑多久是另一个变量，模拟时间只影响起点，两者管的是完全不同的量。
依赖检查还是通过其它那一项体现，这里只是额外加了一个不能早于此刻的条件。
optionExplanations_en: Worker-free time or the dependency finish time can both be earlier than the moment being processed, so adding the current simulated time stops a task from being assigned to a point in the past.
It only raises the floor on the start time and has nothing to do with which dependency finishes last — this option confuses what current_time controls with what dependency time controls.
How long the task itself runs is a separate variable; the current time only affects the start point — they govern completely different quantities.
Dependency checking still happens through the other term in the max; the current time just adds one more condition that the start can't be before 'now'.

q: 把 event-driven simulation 的主流程排成正确顺序：

在当前时间分配 ready 且未 scheduled 的任务给空闲 worker
弹出最早完成事件，批量处理同一时间完成的任务
把完成任务加入 completed 并释放 worker
再次调用 assign_ready，直到 events 为空

q: 文章中 event-driven 版本按 ready-task helper 反复扫描时的整体复杂度形状是什么？

O(2^V)，枚举所有任务子集
O(log V)，只做一次二分查找
O(V^2 + V·E)，每次事件都重新扫一遍
why: 每次完成事件后都可能调用一次 assign_ready，而它内部扫描一次 ready-task helper是 O(V+E)；最多 V 次扫描叠加成平方项。
why_en: Every completion event can trigger an assign_ready call that rescans the ready-task helper in O(V+E), and up to V such rescans compound into a squared term.
scenario: 任务图变大后，你担心 event-driven 版本反复调用 ready-task helper 带来的额外开销。
scenario_en: As the task graph grows, you are worried about the extra cost from repeatedly calling the ready-task helper in the event-driven version.
options_en: O of W factorial, enumerating every ordering of workers.
O of two to the V, enumerating every task subset.
O of log V, from a single binary search.
O of V squared plus V times E, from rescanning after every event.
optionExplanations: 阶乘级通常来自枚举全排列，这里没有给 worker 排列组合任务这种动作。
指数级一般来自枚举子集，这里每次只是扫描一遍 helper，不涉及枚举。
二分查找要求数据有序才能跳过大半；这里要重新判断的是未排序的 ready 状态，做不到这么快。
每次完成事件都可能重新扫一遍线性的 helper，最多重复整张图规模那么多次，叠加起来就变成了平方项。
optionExplanations_en: Factorial growth usually comes from enumerating full permutations, and nothing here assigns tasks to workers by permutation.
Exponential growth usually comes from subset enumeration, and here it's just one rescan of the helper each time, no enumeration involved.
Binary search only skips most of the data when it's sorted; the ready-task state being rescanned here isn't sorted, so it can't be that cheap.
Every completion event can trigger a fresh linear rescan of the helper, and that can repeat as many times as there are tasks, compounding into a squared term.

scenario: 如果任务图很大，反复调用 ready-task helper 的 O(V²+V·E) 扫描成本开始明显。
scenario_en: On a large task graph, the O(V^2 + V*E) cost from repeatedly scanning ready tasks has become visible.
q: 如何扩展优化 ready-task 扫描的开销？
q_en: How can you optimize the cost of repeatedly scanning ready tasks?
options: 每次调用都把整个依赖图从零开始完整地重新构建一遍
干脆把 ready-task helper 整个删掉，改成随机分配任务，虽然运行更快，但完全丢掉了依赖约束，调度结果可能非法

options_en: Rebuild the entire dependency graph completely from scratch on every single call.
Just drop the ready-task helper entirely and assign workers at random instead., which runs faster but throws away the dependency constraint entirely, so the schedule can become invalid
Rewrite every single task's duration value down to zero seconds.
Maintain in-degree counters like Kahn's algorithm, decrementing dependents on completion and pushing newly-ready tasks into a priority queue.
tradeoff: 维护增量 in-degree 优先队列（省重复扫描）vs 每次完成事件都重新扫描 ready-task helper（写法简单）

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个任务还没完成的依赖数量。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按优先级取出元素的数据结构，这里按 critical_length 排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority queue pops elements in priority order, here ordered by critical_length.

optionExplanations: 重建整张图不会减少扫描量，反而是每次都白白重复一遍原本就该只做一次的工作。
把 helper 删掉换成随机分配虽然快，但直接丢掉了依赖约束，调度结果不再合法。
把时长改成 0 只是让问题看起来消失了，实际任务还是要花时间跑，这是在造假数据不是在优化。
像最初那样维护未完成依赖数，每条边只在完成时被处理一次，新 ready 的任务按优先级直接入队，避免了反复整表扫描。

Dropping the helper for random assignment is fast, but it throws away the dependency constraint entirely, so the schedule stops being valid.
Zeroing out every duration just makes the problem look like it vanished; the tasks still take real time to run — that's faking the data, not optimizing.

Maintaining unmet-dependency counts the way the original ordering step did means each edge is only touched once at completion, and newly-ready tasks go straight into a priority queue instead of triggering a full rescan.

q: critical-path-length priority 是否保证任意 precedence scheduling 都最优？
q_en: Does critical-path-length priority guarantee optimal scheduling for every precedence graph?
options: 是的，它是一个数学上被严格证明过的最优算法
只要 worker 数大于 1，它就永远能保证达到最优，这跟排序策略本身无关
只有在完全没有任何依赖关系时才保证最优
不是；这类 precedence 调度问题在理论上普遍是 NP-hard
why: 最长剩余链是很好的启发式，能通过本文测试，但不能证明所有图都达到最优 makespan。

Only in the special case where there are no dependencies at all.
No — this class of precedence scheduling problem is generally NP-hard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 目前没有已知多项式时间算法能保证求出最优解的一类问题。

q: 文章提到 work-conserving greedy 的 Graham bound 是什么形状？

There is no theoretical upper bound at all — it could be arbitrarily many times the optimum.
The makespan is at most 2 minus 1 over W times the optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不让 worker 空闲的贪心调度算法的近似比上界。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只要还有 ready task，就绝不让 worker 空闲的调度策略。

这个倍数是个夸张到不合理的下限，这个策略的表现远比这好，不会差这么多。
这类不空闲策略恰恰是有经典理论上界的，说没有任何上界跟这个近似比结果矛盾。

That multiple of optimal is an unreasonably loose floor; this scheduling rule performs far better than that in practice.
This never-idle strategy actually has a well-known classic upper bound, so claiming there's no bound at all contradicts that result.

q: 为什么「只改成 event-driven，但不加 critical-path priority」仍可能得到 38 秒？

给它加上 priority 反而会破坏调度结果的 correctness
scan 这类任务其实完全不需要占用任何 worker

options_en: Event-driven simulation as a technique simply cannot handle dependencies., because by design it can't read the before/after relationship between tasks
Adding a priority rule on top would actually break the schedule's correctness.
Tasks like the scans don't actually need to occupy any worker at all.
The scans and the build chain are ready at the same moment, so if the ready helper returns a scan first, the critical chain still gets delayed.
optionExplanations: 重新决策一直都在按依赖关系判断谁 ready，只改成事件触发并不影响它对依赖的处理能力。
优先级只是决定同时 ready 的多个任务谁先拿 worker，不会破坏依赖顺序本身的合法性。
扫描任务是真实要执行的工作，跟其它任务一样要占用一个 worker 的时间。

Priority only decides which of several simultaneously-ready tasks gets a worker first; it doesn't touch the legality of the dependency order itself.
Scan tasks are real work that still has to run, occupying a worker's time just like any other task.
Going event-driven only fixes when to re-check readiness; with no rule for which of several simultaneously-ready tasks wins, a scan can still get dispatched first.

q: 为什么「给固定预建顺序加 priority」也不等价于 event-driven？

scenario: 你保留 t=0 一次排好的执行列表，只是改成按 critical_length 排序；但 build-1 在 t=0 时还没 ready。

options_en: A priority key cannot compare numbers.
Fixed-order scheduling has no concept of workers.
Event-driven simulation doesn't need dependencies.
A fixed precomputed order cannot re-admit a task that just became unlocked when something finishes.
optionExplanations: 给固定顺序加优先级排序，比较数字本身没有任何技术障碍，问题不出在这。
固定顺序一样有 worker 分配任务，只是决策时机是一次性的，并不是缺 worker 这个概念。
事件驱动同样要靠依赖和未完成依赖数判断谁 ready，只是重新评估的时机变多了，依赖检查一点没少。

optionExplanations_en: Sorting a fixed order by a priority number has no technical obstacle around comparing numbers — that's not the actual gap.
Fixed-order scheduling still uses a worker structure to assign tasks; the issue is that the decision only happens once, not that workers are missing.
Event-driven scheduling still relies on dependency and unmet-count information to decide readiness — it just re-evaluates more often, not less.
The order is locked in up front, so a critical task that only becomes unlocked mid-run can't be inserted into that precomputed list — it has to wait its turn in the fixed sequence.
