Wrong altitude — skips the top level and gives the deepest detail.
Wrong register — a design segue in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片：按某个键把数据切成多份分到不同节点，分摊读写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data by a key across multiple nodes so each holds a slice and the load is spread.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希：一种分片键映射方式，加减节点时只搬动少量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys to nodes so that adding or removing a node moves only a small fraction of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制因子：每份数据保存的副本数量，例如三副本抗单点故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The replication factor is how many copies of each piece of data are kept — e.g. three replicas to survive a node failure.

scenario: 系统设计轮时间过半，面试官说「We're low on time — pick the most interesting part and go deep.」你怕像之前那样越挑越乱、把思路挑丢。
scenario_en: Halfway through a design round the interviewer says, "We're low on time — pick the most interesting part and go deep." You're afraid of drifting and losing the thread like before.
q: 面试官让你挑一块深挖，怎么开口点题不跑偏？
q_en: When asked to pick one part to go deep, how do you open without drifting?
options: Um, so there's the cache, and the queue, and yeah, how about we go to the first idea, or maybe, let me think what I was...
The most interesting part is the write path — that's where the consistency tradeoff lives. Let me zoom in there.
So so the read pass is is the most, the most, in in the part that, that matters, so...
The component possessing the greatest technical significance shall now be examined in depth.
tradeoff: 主动点名最关键组件 vs 罗列一堆不下钻：点名让深挖有焦点，代价是放弃其它块；罗列显得全面，却把有限时间耗在挑不定上。
why: 时间紧时先一句点名「最有意思的是写路径，一致性取舍就在这」，立刻锁定焦点再深挖；把组件罗列一遍却挑不定，只会把宝贵时间耗光。
why_en: When time is short, name the target in one line — "the interesting part is the write path, that's where the consistency tradeoff lives" — then dive, instead of listing components and stalling.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官还没决定深挖哪块、明确让你「先列出候选再一起选」时，才先罗列组件而不马上锁定。
options_en: Um, so there's the cache, and the queue, and yeah, how about we go to the first idea, or maybe, let me think what I was...
The most interesting part is the write path — that's where the consistency tradeoff lives. Let me zoom in there.
So so the read pass is is the most, the most, in in the part that, that matters, so...
The component possessing the greatest technical significance shall now be examined in depth.
optionMeanings: 组件罗列一遍还挑不定，说「要不我们回第一个想法」丢了线。
一句点名写路径是焦点，理由是一致性取舍，再下钻。
结巴「so so、is is、in in」，句子挂在半空挑不出重点。
用「shall now be examined」的公文腔宣布要深挖。
optionMeanings_en: Lists components, can't decide, says "how about the first idea" — thread lost.
Names the write path as the focus, cites the consistency tradeoff, then dives.
Stutters "so so, is is, in in" — sentence dangles, no point emerges.
Announces the deep dive in a stiff "shall now be examined" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 时间被挑选耗掉，对方看你在原地绕。
焦点立刻锁定，剩下的时间全花在深度上。
对方只听到卡顿，等不到你选出哪一块。
过度正式，像宣读而不是选重点。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Time burns on choosing; they watch you circle in place.
Focus locks instantly and the rest of the time buys depth.
They hear only stalling, never which part you picked.
Over-formal — like an announcement, not picking a focus.
optionDirectness: 错在挑不定，罗列加丢线把时间耗空。
抓住「点名焦点+给理由+下钻」的深挖开场。
错在卡顿，句子停在原地没落到具体组件。
错在语域，选重点用公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — can't commit; listing plus a lost thread drains the clock.
Nails the deep-dive opener: name the focus, give the reason, drill in.
Wrong — stalls in place; never lands on a concrete component.
Wrong register — picking a focus in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径：一次写请求经过的组件链路，通常是一致性和持久化取舍的所在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the chain of components a write request travels through, usually where consistency and durability tradeoffs live.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性取舍：为了更快或更可用，允许读到稍旧的数据 vs 保证读到最新写入之间的权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The consistency tradeoff is the choice between always reading the latest write versus tolerating slightly stale reads for more speed or availability.

scenario: Gamma 后端面试，面试官问「What were the main tradeoffs?」上次你在这里说到「keeping simple and make the, make the system flexible」就卡进「sorry, let me think how to say」。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round the interviewer asks, "What were the main tradeoffs?" Last time you got to "keeping it simple and make the, make the system flexible" then stalled into "sorry, let me think how to say."
q: 面试官问主要取舍，怎么一句话架住框架？
q_en: When asked for the main tradeoffs, how do you frame it in one line?
options: One trade-off was between keeping it simple and make the, make the system flexible, so sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
There are so many tradeoffs honestly — consistency, latency, cost, complexity, flexibility — I could go through each for a while, where do you want me to start...
The principal tradeoff pertains to the dichotomy between simplicity and extensibility of the system.
The main tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility — I went simple now, and here's what it costs us later.
tradeoff: 点名取舍轴+代价 vs 卡在措辞：一句「X vs Y，我选了 X，代价是…」既清晰又显成熟；卡在「how to say」把思考过程暴露成空白。
why: 讲取舍用固定公式「X versus Y，我选了 X，代价是…」：先点名两端，再说选哪端、代价是什么。卡在措辞或罗列一堆取舍都接不住。
why_en: Use the formula "the main tradeoff is X versus Y — I chose X, and here's the cost": name both poles, say which you picked, and own the price — don't stall on wording.
whenOtherWins: 只有当确实有多个同等重要的取舍、面试官也想听全时，才先列出取舍清单再逐条展开。
options_en: One trade-off was between keeping it simple and make the, make the system flexible, so sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
There are so many tradeoffs honestly — consistency, latency, cost, complexity, flexibility — I could go through each for a while, where do you want me to start...
The principal tradeoff pertains to the dichotomy between simplicity and extensibility of the system.
The main tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility — I went simple now, and here's what it costs us later.
optionMeanings: 点到取舍就卡进「make the, make the」和「how to say」。
罗列一大串取舍却不选一个展开，反问对方从哪讲。
用「pertains to the dichotomy」的公文腔描述取舍。
一句点名「简单 vs 灵活」，说清选了哪端和代价。
optionMeanings_en: Reaches the tradeoff then stalls into "make the, make the" and "how to say."
Reels off many tradeoffs but commits to none, asking where to start.
Describes it in a stiff "pertains to the dichotomy" register.
Names "simple vs flexible," states which side and its cost.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听到的是你在找词，不是你的判断。
铺得太广，面试官等不到一个明确取舍。
过度正式，像术语堆砌而非工程判断。
对方立刻听到清晰、成熟的权衡判断。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you word-hunting, not your judgment.
Too broad — they never get one clear tradeoff.
Over-formal — jargon stack, not an engineering call.
They hear a clean, mature weighing of the tradeoff.
optionDirectness: 错在卡壳，取舍轴还没说完就断在措辞上。
错在铺太广，列了五个取舍却不落地一个。
错在语域，工程取舍用公文体显得空洞。
抓住「X vs Y + 选哪端 + 代价」的取舍公式。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — stalls; the tradeoff axis breaks off mid-wording.
Wrong — too broad; five tradeoffs listed, none committed to.
Wrong register — an engineering tradeoff in bureaucratese rings hollow.
Nails the formula: X vs Y, which side you chose, the cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 简单 vs 灵活：现在实现越简单越快上线，但未来扩展新场景就要改动更多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Simplicity versus flexibility: a simpler build ships faster now, but supporting new cases later takes more rework.

scenario: 系统设计轮，你在白板画好了框图，面试官说「Walk me through your diagram.」你怕像之前那样一个方框一个方框地念、越念越散。
scenario_en: In a design round you've drawn boxes on the whiteboard and the interviewer says, "Walk me through your diagram." You worry about naming box after box and drifting like before.
q: 怎么把画好的框图讲出声，让对方跟得上？
q_en: How do you narrate a finished diagram so the interviewer can follow?
options: Sure — a request hits the load balancer, goes to the API service, which reads cache and falls back to the DB. Let me trace one write.
So this is the, the API, and this box is is the, the database, and then the arrow, the arrow goes to, um...
Okay there are a lot of boxes here, this one connects to that one and also this one, arrows everywhere, let me see if I can remember what each of them does...
Observe the diagram: component one interfaces with component two, which subsequently transmits to component three.
tradeoff: 顺着请求流讲 vs 逐个念方框：跟着一次请求走让对方顺着数据流理解；逐个点名方框省事，却让人拼不出它们怎么串起来。
why: 讲框图别逐个念方框，跟着「一次请求怎么流过」走：负载均衡→API→缓存→回落数据库，再单独追一次写。数据流是面试官理解架构的主线。
why_en: Don't name boxes one by one — trace one request through: load balancer to API to cache, falling back to the DB, then follow a single write; the data flow is the thread they follow.
whenOtherWins: 只有当图里各组件相互独立、没有单一请求串起它们时，才逐个介绍组件而不走数据流。
options_en: Sure — a request hits the load balancer, goes to the API service, which reads cache and falls back to the DB. Let me trace one write.
So this is the, the API, and this box is is the, the database, and then the arrow, the arrow goes to, um...
Okay there are a lot of boxes here, this one connects to that one and also this one, arrows everywhere, let me see if I can remember what each of them does...
Observe the diagram: component one interfaces with component two, which subsequently transmits to component three.
optionMeanings: 跟着一次请求流讲：LB→API→缓存→回落 DB，再追一次写。
逐个指方框「this is the API, this box is is the DB」并卡在箭头。
感叹方框太多、箭头到处都是，还得回想每个干嘛。
用「component one interfaces with component two」的公文腔念图。
optionMeanings_en: Traces one request: LB to API to cache, falls back to DB, then a write.
Points at boxes — "this is the API, this box is is the DB" — stuck on an arrow.
Marvels at how many boxes and arrows, still recalling what each does.
Reads the diagram in a stiff "component one interfaces with two" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方顺着数据流走，一遍就看懂架构。
对方听到零散方框，拼不出整体怎么运转。
显得连自己的图都不熟，信心全无。
过度正式，像读框图说明书而非讲设计。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They ride the data flow and grasp the architecture in one pass.
They hear scattered boxes, can't assemble how it runs.
Looks like you don't know your own diagram — no confidence.
Over-formal — like reading a diagram manual, not explaining.
optionDirectness: 抓住「跟着一次请求走完数据流」的讲图主线。
错在逐个点方框，还卡在箭头上串不起来。
错在没主线，感叹方框多却不追任何一条流。
错在语域，讲图用公文体听着像说明书。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the narration thread: follow one request through the data flow.
Wrong — names boxes one by one and stalls on an arrow, nothing links.
Wrong — no thread; marvels at boxes without tracing any flow.
Wrong register — narrating a diagram in bureaucratese sounds like a manual.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器：把进来的请求分摊到多台服务器，避免单台过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer spreads incoming requests across multiple servers so no single one gets overloaded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存回落：先查缓存，命中就返回，未命中再去数据库取并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache fallback means checking the cache first and, on a miss, reading from the database and filling the cache.

scenario: Amazon 电面 coding，你拿到一道 trie（前缀树）题。上一次在 Alterion 你直接闷头写、边写边嘟囔「so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node」。
scenario_en: In an Amazon phone screen you get a trie (prefix-tree) problem. Last time at Alterion you dove straight in, muttering "so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node."
q: 动手敲代码前，第一句该怎么说清思路？
q_en: Before you start typing, what's your first line to lay out the approach?
options: So let me see, so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node, insert, okay, and then...
Okay, type in the parameter key, function, str, tree node, okay so it's a dict, and then we insert...
Let me talk through my approach first — I'll use a trie, insert char by char, then DFS from the prefix node.
Prior to implementation, I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy for the problem presently at hand.
tradeoff: 先讲思路再写 vs 闷头敲：先讲一句让面试官对齐方向、能早点纠偏；直接写省了开口，却把思路埋在键盘声里，错了也没人拦。
why: 写代码前先宣布「先讲思路再动手」，点名数据结构和步骤（trie、逐字符插入、从前缀 DFS），让面试官对齐；边写边嘟囔零碎词等于没讲。
why_en: Before coding, say "let me talk through my approach first" and name the data structure and steps — trie, insert char by char, DFS from the prefix node — so they can align, instead of muttering fragments as you type.
whenOtherWins: 题目极简单、或面试官说「直接写、边写边说」时，才跳过预讲直接开敲。
options_en: So let me see, so start with, then we return a list of str and prefix tree tree node, insert, okay, and then...
Okay, type in the parameter key, function, str, tree node, okay so it's a dict, and then we insert...
Let me talk through my approach first — I'll use a trie, insert char by char, then DFS from the prefix node.
Prior to implementation, I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy for the problem presently at hand.
optionMeanings: 闷头开写、嘟囔「prefix tree tree node」，没先讲思路。
边敲边念参数和类型当讲解，没给出算法结构。
先宣布要讲思路，再给出算法结构和步骤，然后才动手。
用「I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy」的公文腔开场。
optionMeanings_en: Dives in typing, mutters "prefix tree tree node" — no plan stated first.
Narrates params and types as "the plan" — "type in the parameter key, str."
Announces the plan first: trie, insert char by char, DFS from the prefix node.
Opens in a stiff "I shall articulate my algorithmic strategy" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官不知道你要写什么，错了也没法早拦。
对方听到的是键盘旁白，不是可评估的思路。
面试官提前对齐方向，能在写错前给你纠偏。
过度正式，像宣读方案而非结对编程。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They don't know what you're building; can't catch a wrong turn early.
They hear keyboard narration, not an evaluable plan.
They align on direction early and can steer you before a bug.
Over-formal — like reading a proposal, not pairing.
optionDirectness: 错在没预讲就开敲，思路埋在键盘声里。
错在把敲字过程当讲解，没给出算法结构。
抓住「先讲思路+点名数据结构和步骤」的编码开场。
错在语域，结对编码用公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — types before explaining; the plan is buried in keystrokes.
Wrong — narrating typing isn't a plan; no algorithm structure given.
Nails the coding opener: state the plan, name the data structure and steps.
Wrong register — pairing in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树：一种按字符逐层展开的树，用来高效存取有公共前缀的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a prefix tree that branches on each character, giving fast lookup and storage of strings that share prefixes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索：一条路走到底再回溯，常用来遍历树或图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, explores one branch as deep as possible before backtracking — a common way to traverse a tree or graph.

scenario: 系统设计轮，面试官问「How big is this — walk me through the scale.」上次你憋着心算，只挤出「the scale is is in in terms of the traffic, but it's not about the traffic...」。
scenario_en: In a design round the interviewer asks, "How big is this — walk me through the scale." Last time you computed silently and only forced out "the scale is is in in terms of the traffic, but it's not about the traffic..."
q: 怎么把容量估算「说」出来，让面试官跟着你的数字走？
q_en: How do you narrate a scale estimate out loud so the interviewer can follow the numbers?
options: So the scale is is, in in terms of the traffic, but it's not, it's not about the traffic, but about the...
Let me do a quick back-of-the-envelope: say 200M daily users, 10% active at peak, so ~20M concurrent — that drives our fan-out.
There are lots of numbers we could estimate — users, requests, storage, bandwidth — it depends, let me just pick some and see what comes out...
I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation of the anticipated load parameters of the system.
tradeoff: 出声估算+落到设计 vs 憋着算或含糊：出声报公式让对方跟得上、还看到数字怎么用；憋着心算省了开口，却让思考过程变成一段空白。
why: 估算要出声报公式（200M 日活×10% 峰值≈20M 并发）、带单位、说清驱动什么（fan-out）。憋着心算或「about the traffic」都藏起推导。
why_en: Narrate the estimate as a formula — 200M daily users times 10% peak equals ~20M concurrent — with units and what it drives (fan-out); don't compute silently or wave at "the traffic."
whenOtherWins: 面试官说「规模先不用估、假设很大就行」时，才略过数字直接进设计。
options_en: So the scale is is, in in terms of the traffic, but it's not, it's not about the traffic, but about the...
Let me do a quick back-of-the-envelope: say 200M daily users, 10% active at peak, so ~20M concurrent — that drives our fan-out.
There are lots of numbers we could estimate — users, requests, storage, bandwidth — it depends, let me just pick some and see what comes out...
I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation of the anticipated load parameters of the system.
optionMeanings: 憋着心算，只挤出「is is、in in」这类卡顿和含糊。
出声把公式和单位报出来，算出并发量，再点名它驱动 fan-out。
罗列能估的一堆量却不落公式，说「随便挑几个看看」。
用「I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation」的公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: Computes silently, forcing out only "is is, in in, about the traffic."
Says the formula aloud: 200M daily times 10% peak ~ 20M concurrent, drives fan-out.
Lists estimable quantities but no formula — "let me just pick some."
Frames it in a stiff "I shall now undertake a quantitative estimation" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方只看到你卡住，看不到任何数字或推导。
面试官跟着数字走，还看到它怎么约束设计。
铺一堆待估项却无结论，对方等不到落点。
过度正式，像宣读而不是白板估算。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see only a stall — no numbers, no reasoning.
They follow the numbers and see how it constrains the design.
Many quantities floated, no result — they get no landing.
Over-formal — like an announcement, not a whiteboard estimate.
optionDirectness: 错在憋着心算，出口只剩卡顿和含糊。
抓住估算叙述三拍：公式、单位、约束哪条设计。
错在只列待估项，不给公式也不给结论。
错在语域，白板估算用公文体显得僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — computing silently; only stalls and "about the traffic" come out.
Nails the estimate narration: formula aloud, units, and what it drives.
Wrong — lists quantities but gives no formula and no result.
Wrong register — a whiteboard estimate in bureaucratese feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 粗略估算：用几个近似数字快速算出量级，不求精确，只求数量级对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A back-of-the-envelope estimate is a quick rough calculation using round numbers to get the order of magnitude, not an exact figure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扇出：一次写入或事件需要推送/复制到很多下游（如关注者），量级直接决定负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is when one write or event must be pushed to many downstream consumers (like followers); its size directly sets the load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并发用户数：同一时刻在线活跃的用户数，是算服务器和连接数的基数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrent users is how many are active at the same moment — the base figure for sizing servers and connections.

scenario: TikTok 广告后端面试,被问「campaign 设置为什么用关系型库而不是 NoSQL」。她卡成「Relational data model and relational data, okay okay」,然后开始罗列字段,不给拍板理由。
scenario_en: In the TikTok ads backend interview she's asked why she chose a relational DB over NoSQL for campaign settings. She echoes "relational data model and relational data, okay okay" and lists fields without a deciding reason.
q: 「为什么选关系型而不是 NoSQL」怎么一句给出决定性理由?
q_en: How do you give the deciding reason for "relational over NoSQL" in one line?
options: We use the relational data model and relational data, so campaign type, ROI goal, budget — it's all relational, so it made sense to me.
So, NoSQL could also work, but relational is also fine, there are some tradeoffs, so, let me think, I'd say it just fit better somehow.
I went relational over NoSQL because the settings were highly relational and needed joins. That costs easy horizontal scaling — fine at our write volume.
When selecting a database one must weigh consistency, scalability, and the data model, since relational systems provide ACID guarantees and referential integrity throughout.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「X over Y because 约束 Z, 代价 W」拍板 vs 罗列字段+「it made sense」never justifies。
why: 把决定压成「X over Y because 约束 Z; 代价 W, 可接受因为…」。她的毛病是罗列字段加「it made sense」,不给决定性理由。
why_en: Say "relational over NoSQL because the data was relational and needed joins; the cost is scaling, which was fine" — don't just say it made sense.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只想确认你知道两种库的区别、还没到定型阶段,先并列讲差异、暂不拍板也可以。
options_en: We use the relational data model and relational data, so campaign type, ROI goal, budget — it's all relational, so it made sense to me.

We go the sync way, not the async way, because the user submit and then the read pass is faster, so it feel more real-time to them.
So, a queue could help with load, but sync is also okay, and, hmm, there are pros and cons, so I'd say we just went with what was simpler.
Synchronous and asynchronous communication each present distinct tradeoffs in coupling, latency, and throughput that architects must carefully evaluate before deciding on either one.

why_en: Say "sync because the advertiser needs instant success or error; async would cut coupling but costs that feedback" — don't drift into aligning the API.

Caching introduces a well-known tradeoff between data freshness and read latency that engineers should always weigh against the volatility of the underlying data source.

We do the migration step by step, not one time, because if it break, the roll back pass is easier, and, so so, it's more safe for us.

So, pessimistic is safer, but optimistic is lighter, there are tradeoffs, um, so we just picked the lighter one I think.
Optimistic and pessimistic concurrency control differ mainly in how they handle contention, and the right choice depends on the expected conflict rate within the workload.

q: 「为什么自建而不是用现成的」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "build in-house over adopting an existing component" in one line?
options: We build it self, not use the ready one, because our logic is special, the ready one can not fit, so so, we have to do our own.
Build-versus-buy decisions weigh engineering cost against control and fit, and teams should evaluate whether an off-the-shelf solution meets their specific requirements first.
So, buying is faster, but building gives control, both have tradeoffs, and, let me think, we kind of just built it ourselves.
I built it because our budget rules were too custom for any off-the-shelf tool to fit. That costs more maintenance, accepted since the logic was core.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「自建 because 太定制, 代价维护」拍板 vs「build it self」Chinglish 加绕分工。

why_en: Say "built it because the rules were too custom for any off-the-shelf tool; the cost is more maintenance, accepted since it was core" — don't drift to team structure.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求很通用、现成组件基本能覆盖,那直接用现成的、省下维护成本更明智。

scenario_en: She's asked why she chose to lock the API contract with other backend engineers up front instead of each side building first and reconciling later. She repeats "align the API constructs with other backend engineers" with no reason.
q: 「为什么一开始就定死 API 契约」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "lock the API contract up front" in one line?
options: So, we could also align later, but early is also fine, there are tradeoffs both ways, so we just agreed on it early I guess.
I locked the contract early because both sides were building in parallel, so a mismatch would block us. That costs some upfront design time, well worth it.
We align the API construct early, not later, because if not, the two side will not match, and then the integrate pass will break.
Defining an API contract early versus iterating later is a coordination tradeoff, and the decision depends on team parallelism and the cost of downstream integration rework.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「早定 because 并行会 block, 代价前期时间」vs「integrate pass」错词加重复原话。
why: 把决定压成「早定契约 because 双方并行、不对齐会互相 block; 代价是前期设计时间, 值得」。她的毛病是重复「align the API」不给理由。
why_en: Say "locked it early because both sides built in parallel and a mismatch would block us; the cost is upfront design time, well worth it" — don't just repeat aligning the API.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有你一个人开发、没有并行方,那先各写各的、后期再对齐反而更灵活。

q: 你会怎么组织这段「背景」回答？
q_en: How do you structure this "background" answer?

I've mostly done backend, but honestly nothing too advanced — just regular CRUD services and some maintenance, so I still have a lot to learn.

My background is primarily backend, secondarily frontend, at a 70-to-30 split, utilizing Java and PHP in a professional capacity.

q_en: For this opening "quick intro," what do you say?
options: I'm a software engineer who now work at TikTok, right now, and I, TikTok, I do the ads stuff...
Sure — I'm a backend engineer at TikTok on the ads platform. Before that, Meta. I'm looking to own a product end-to-end.

q: 有初步判断、需要一秒确认取舍，第一句怎么起手？
q_en: You have an instinct but need a beat to check the tradeoff — what's your first line?
options: My first instinct is simplicity over flexibility — let me walk through that tradeoff.
One tradeoff was, um, keeping it simple and make it flexible, so, sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
Oh there were so many tradeoffs on that project — speed, safety, complexity — so many angles I could take, let me figure out which to even talk about first...
There existed a notable tradeoff. I shall now elaborate upon the considerations therein.
tradeoff: 先定方向再想 vs 边复读边卡：给出初步判断买来组织空间，代价是要为方向负责；复读题目省事，却把空白暴露给对方。
why: 有初步判断时先用「My first instinct is X」给方向，再补一句检验取舍，把停顿变成有掌控的思考，而不是把犹豫念出声。
why_en: Lead with "my first instinct is X, then let me check the tradeoff" — it names a direction and turns the pause into visible thinking.
whenOtherWins: 只有当取舍你早想透、能一句说完时，才不用「first instinct」句式，直接给结论更利落。

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径：一个查询请求读数据时经过的组件链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The read path is the chain of components a request goes through when data is read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径：一次写入/提交经过的组件链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the chain of components a request goes through when data is written.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片：把一份大数据按 key 拆到多台机器上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits one large dataset across multiple machines by a key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制：把同一份数据在多个副本上保存以提高可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication keeps copies of the same data on multiple replicas for availability.

scenario: Convoke coding 轮，面试官让你「implement a dictionary without using a dictionary」。你有初步思路，别像上次「my initial idea is maybe」绕圈。
scenario_en: In a Convoke coding round you're asked to "implement a dictionary without using a dictionary." You have an idea — don't circle on "my initial idea is maybe" like last time.
q: 有初步思路、想边说边确认可行，怎么起手？
q_en: You have an approach in mind and want to check it aloud — how do you open?
options: My first instinct is an array plus a hash function — let me check that gives O(1) reads.
Oh, so first thing is that the dictionary can read a key one time, so how can I, if I want to read it, my initial idea is maybe...
There's a bunch of ways — hash sets, linked lists, arrays, trees — I could go so many directions, let me just think out loud for a while...

tradeoff: 亮方案再验证 vs 边绕边找：先给一个候选再检验，代价是可能要收回；反复「maybe」听着像还没方向。
why: coding 起手先用「My first instinct is X」亮一个候选方案，再当场验证复杂度，比反复「maybe」绕圈显得有掌控。
why_en: Open coding with "my first instinct is X, let me sanity-check it" — one clear candidate beats circling with "my initial idea is maybe."
whenOtherWins: 只有当题目一眼看不出方向、确实需要先枚举时，才先摆几种再选，而不是硬报一个。

scenario: IKEA 的 ML 面试，面试官问：「Tell me about a production issue you debugged.」你有例子但要一秒挑，别像上次「Okay, um, okay, so」堆语气词。
scenario_en: In IKEA's ML interview the interviewer asks, "Tell me about a production issue you debugged." You have examples but need a beat to pick — not another "Okay, um, okay, so."
q: 想用一秒挑好例子，开口第一句怎么说？
q_en: You need a second to pick the right example — what's your opening line?
options: Okay, um, okay, so, one production issue that I personally debugged was, um...
Oh there were quite a few — config drifts, deploys break, alerts fire — so many stories I could pick, let me think about which is best to tell you...
Let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one I actually owned.
Permit me a brief moment to recollect a suitable production incident to recount.
tradeoff: 一句缓冲 vs 语气词填空：一句缓冲显得从容并预告结构；堆语气词只是把停顿念出声。
why: 讲故事前用「Let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one」买一个从容缓冲，好过用一串语气词把空白念出声。
why_en: Before a story, say "let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one" — a clean buffer beats stacking "okay, um, okay, so."
whenOtherWins: 只有当例子脱口而出、不用挑时，才直接开讲，省掉「让我想一秒」更利落。

scenario: Alterion coding 轮拿到 Trie 题（前缀树，支持 insert 和 startsWith）。你不确定 startsWith 到底返回什么，别像上次「why do we want a list of string」自问自答。
scenario_en: In an Alterion coding round you get a Trie problem (prefix tree with insert and startsWith). You're unsure what startsWith returns — don't self-ask "why do we want a list of string" like last time.
q: 需求还没完全确认，动手前第一句该怎么说？
q_en: The ask is still fuzzy — what's your first line before coding?
options: Before I dive in, let me make sure I get the ask — startsWith returns all words with that prefix, right?
So start with... then we return a list of str, why do we want a list of string, let me, let me think...
Okay so there's insert, there's startsWith, return types, edge cases, empty prefix, no matches — so much to consider, let me talk through all of it...
Kindly permit me to confirm the precise specification of the startsWith operation prior to implementation.
tradeoff: 先确认需求 vs 边猜边写：先跟面试官对齐省得写错方向，代价是多花一次确认；自己猜可能整段返工。
why: 需求不清时先「Before I dive in, let me make sure I understand the requirement」把它确认成一句 yes/no，比自问自答「why do we want...」把困惑说给自己听强。
why_en: When the ask is fuzzy, say "before I dive in, let me make sure I get the requirement" and confirm it as a yes/no — don't mutter the confusion to yourself.
whenOtherWins: 只有当题目已经写得非常明确、没有歧义时，才不用再确认，直接开写更快。

scenario: Majestic 面试，面试官问：「Which data structure would you use to store that?」你想说哈希表，但上次开口成「So hash map, hash map, read read」原地打转。
scenario_en: In a Majestic interview the interviewer asks, "Which data structure would you use to store that?" You mean a hash map, but last time you looped "so hash map, hash map, read read."
q: 心里已有答案，怎么一句给出方向而不复读打转？
q_en: You already have the answer — how do you state a direction in one line without looping?
options: So hash map, hash map, read read, so if I want to store user info that I read and write a lot, then...
My first instinct is a hash map — let me say why that fits here.
Well it depends — could be a hash map, a tree, an array — each has pros and cons on reads, writes, memory, let me weigh those out loud...
I would elect to employ a hash map, the rationale for which I shall presently expound.
tradeoff: 一句定方向 vs 复读词卡住：先亮答案再解释显得果断；重复关键词只是把犹豫暴露出来。
why: 已有答案时用「My first instinct is X」一句给方向再解释，别把关键词复读成原地打转。
why_en: With an answer in mind, say "my first instinct is X, let me say why" — don't loop "hash map, hash map, read read" in place.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官明显想让你先对比几种结构时，才用「it depends」展开，而不是直接报一个。

用「I shall presently expound」的书面公文腔。

果断给方向，再补理由，显得有掌控。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash map uses a hash function to map keys to buckets for average O(1) reads and writes.

scenario: IKEA 面试，面试官问：「How did you prevent recurrence?」你上次一开口就复读「Recurrence, prevent recurrence, and so to prevent the same issue...」。
scenario_en: In an IKEA interview the interviewer asks, "How did you prevent recurrence?" Last time you opened by echoing "recurrence, prevent recurrence, and so to prevent the same issue..."
q: 想争取一秒思考又不复读问题，怎么起手？
q_en: You want a beat to think without echoing the question — how do you open?
options: Recurrence... prevent recurrence, yeah, so, to prevent the same issue from happening again, um...
Oh good question — prevention's such a big topic, testing, monitoring, reviews, alerts, guardrails, so many layers, let me think which to highlight...
Good question — let me take a sec. The main thing I added was stronger validation.
In order to preclude a recurrence of the aforementioned issue, I implemented several measures.
tradeoff: 一句缓冲进正题 vs 复读关键词：缓冲句买来思考又不显空；复读问题词只是原地回声。
why: 想买时间别复读问题里的词，用「Good question — let me take a sec」买缓冲，再直接给主干答案。
why_en: To buy time, don't echo the question's words — say "good question, let me take a sec," then give the core answer.
whenOtherWins: 只有当答案立刻就位、不需要缓冲时，才直接说主干，省掉「让我想一秒」。

用「preclude the aforementioned issue」的公文腔。

铺垫太长，对方等不到具体动作。

termDefinitions.meaning: 校验：在处理前检查输入/变更是否合法，不合法就拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Validation checks that input or a change is legal before it's processed, rejecting bad ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 护栏：预设的规则/限制，防止危险操作真正生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guardrails are preset rules that block dangerous operations before they take effect.

scenario: WOP 支付工程面，面试官抛开放设计题：「Design a system to store onboarding step status.」你想直接冲，但上次「where do we store it, let me think」乱起手。
scenario_en: In a WOP payments engineering round the interviewer opens with a design prompt: "Design a system to store onboarding step status." You want to charge in, but last time you fumbled "where do we store it, let me think."
q: 拿到开放设计题，动手前第一句怎么起手最稳？
q_en: Given an open design prompt, what's the steadiest first line before diving in?
options: Oh, there's an enum, um, where do we store it, let me think, where we store, I was starting an entity...
Before I dive in, let me confirm the requirements and rough scale — is this per-user and real-time?
Okay so a system — storage, the API, the data model, consistency, scale — so many pieces, let me start thinking through all of them one by one...
Prior to commencing the design, I shall solicit clarification regarding the functional requirements.
tradeoff: 先澄清需求与量级 vs 直接冲实现：先对齐范围避免设计跑偏，代价是花一两句；直接冲容易在细节里迷路。
why: 开放设计题先「Before I dive in, let me confirm the requirements and scale」定好范围和量级再动手，别一上来陷进存储细节。
why_en: For an open design prompt, lock the requirements and scale first — "let me confirm the requirements and rough scale" beats jumping to "where do we store it."
whenOtherWins: 只有当需求和量级面试官已经讲得很清楚时，才跳过澄清直接进设计。

scenario: Alterion 技术面，面试官让你设计一个数据存储。你想先问清是读多还是写多——上次你把它说成「separate the read pass and the write pass」就卡住了。
scenario_en: In an Alterion technical interview you're asked to design a datastore. You want to check whether it's read- or write-heavy first — last time you said "separate the read pass and the write pass" and stalled.
q: 想先反问读多还是写多，这句该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you ask whether it's read- or write-heavy before you design?
options: Quick question before I dive in — are we optimizing for reads or writes here?
So for the database I would separate the read pass and the write pass, so, so if we want consistency...
I mean it depends, right, like reads and writes, both matter, so so maybe I think about which one, the read or the write, or maybe both, let me...
Kindly clarify whether the anticipated workload is predominantly read-oriented or write-oriented.
tradeoff: 先反问定方向 vs 直接开设计：一句澄清换来对齐，多花几秒；不问就设计，可能整个方案压错读写侧。
why: 设计存储前先反问「读多还是写多」，一句话把方向钉住；术语是 read path / write path，不是「read pass」。
why_en: Pin the direction first — "reads or writes?" — the term is read path vs write path, not "read pass."
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官已经明说了读写比例时，才不用再问，直接按给定前提设计。

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径：一条数据被查询/读取时经过的处理链路。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the chain of steps a request goes through when data is written.

scenario: IKEA 的 ML 面试，面试官建议在每次读取时加一层远程缓存查询。你觉得这会多一次网络往返，但上次你只会说「we call it once, then call it another」绕不清楚。
scenario_en: In IKEA's ML interview the interviewer suggests a remote cache lookup on every read. You think it adds a network round trip, but last time you only managed "we call it once, then call it another" and couldn't land it.
q: 想礼貌地指出「这会多一次 round trip」，怎么说？
q_en: How do you politely flag that this adds a round trip?
options: So we call it once, then the user change a little, then we call it another, so it's like twice, so...
Hmm, maybe, I'm not sure, it might be fine, or it might be slower, it kind of depends, I guess a call could, or could not, add time...
I could be wrong, but wouldn't a remote lookup on every read add an extra round trip?
No, that's incorrect — an additional cache lookup never increases latency.
tradeoff: 礼貌反问点出成本 vs 含糊绕圈：一句「wouldn't that add a round trip?」既质疑又留台阶；绕圈或硬撑都传不出你的判断。
why: 质疑方案时用「I could be wrong, but wouldn't that…?」软化的反问点名代价（多一次 round trip），既表达判断又不显对抗。
why_en: Soften a challenge with "I could be wrong, but wouldn't that add a round trip?" — you flag the cost without sounding combative.
whenOtherWins: 只有当那次额外往返其实无关紧要、或已被批处理消掉时，才不必提出，直接接受方案即可。
options_en: So we call it once, then the user change a little, then we call it another, so it's like twice, so...
Hmm, maybe, I'm not sure, it might be fine, or it might be slower, it kind of depends, I guess a call could, or could not, add time...
I could be wrong, but wouldn't a remote lookup on every read add an extra round trip?
No, that's incorrect — an additional cache lookup never increases latency.
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：用「call it once… another」绕，说不清是多一次往返。
一堆「maybe / not sure」对冲，没给出任何判断。
用一句软化的反问提出质疑，指出会多一跳。
自信断言「加缓存绝不增延迟」，其实说反了。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: "call it once… another" — never says round trip clearly.
All "maybe / not sure" hedging, offers no judgment.
Softens the challenge into a question, names the extra hop.
Confidently claims caching never adds latency — backwards.
optionScenarioImpacts: 绕不清，对方没听懂你的顾虑。
全是对冲，显得你自己也没把握。
顾虑清楚传达，还给对方留了台阶。
自信却错，硬撑最伤可信度。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Too tangled — they don't catch your concern.
Pure hedging; you sound unsure yourself.
Concern lands clearly, with room for them to respond.
Confident but wrong — bluffing hurts credibility most.
optionDirectness: 错在表达，往返的意思被绕没了。
错在对冲，只有 maybe 没有判断。
抓住「软化反问 + 点名代价」的质疑法。
错在硬撑，把错的说得斩钉截铁。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong delivery — the round-trip point gets lost in the tangle.
Wrong — hedge only, no actual judgment offered.
Nails it: soft challenge plus naming the concrete cost.
Wrong — states a false claim with total certainty.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往返：一次请求发出到收到响应的完整网络来回，多一次往返就多一份延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A round trip is one full request-and-response cycle over the network; each extra one adds latency.

scenario: Convoke 实现题里，面试官问 hash map 内部怎么工作。你记不清确切步骤，上次你直接说「I forgot, I don't remember」就僵住了。
scenario_en: In a Convoke coding round the interviewer asks how a hash map works internally. You can't recall the exact steps — last time you just said "I forgot, I don't remember" and froze.
q: 记不清确切实现、但知道大概形状，怎么说不至于僵？
q_en: You can't recall the exact steps but know the shape — how do you say it without freezing?
options: Yeah, that's what I thought just now, but I forgot what a hash map is doing, I forgot that.
I'm not 100% on the exact steps, but the shape is: hash the key to an index, then store it in an array.
It maps the key to, hmm, to a value, or to an index, or a hash code, I think, something with the key, let me think, maybe...
A hash map keeps keys in a sorted tree, so every lookup is O(log n).
tradeoff: 认不确定但给形状 vs 直接认输：说「不确定细节，但形状是…」保住推进；只说「I forgot」把主动权交还给沉默。
why: 记不清 API/步骤时，用「I'm not 100% sure, but the shape would be…」承认不确定再补上结构，比干说「I forgot」强得多。
why_en: When the exact steps escape you, say "I'm not 100% sure, but the shape would be…" and give the structure — far better than "I forgot."
whenOtherWins: 只有当你其实清楚记得确切实现时，才不用加不确定前缀，直接自信讲出来更利落。
options_en: Yeah, that's what I thought just now, but I forgot what a hash map is doing, I forgot that.
I'm not 100% on the exact steps, but the shape is: hash the key to an index, then store it in an array.
It maps the key to, hmm, to a value, or to an index, or a hash code, I think, something with the key, let me think, maybe...
A hash map keeps keys in a sorted tree, so every lookup is O(log n).
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：直接认「I forgot」然后僵在原地。
先说不确定细节，再给出「hash key → index → 数组」的形状。
在 value / index / hash code 之间摇摆，说不出结构。
自信地把 hash map 说成排序树、O(log n)，其实错了。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: admits "I forgot" and freezes in place.
Flags uncertainty, then gives "hash key → index → array."
Wavers between value / index / hash code, no structure.
Confidently calls it a sorted tree, O(log n) — wrong.
optionScenarioImpacts: 沉默替你回答，对方判定你不懂。
推进没停，还展示了你其实懂原理。
摇摆显得心里没底，对方帮不上忙。
自信却错，比承认不确定更掉分。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Silence answers for you; they read it as not knowing.
Keeps moving and shows you do grasp the idea.
Wavering reads as no footing; they can't help.
Confident but wrong — worse than admitting doubt.
optionDirectness: 错在放弃，认输后没有任何补救。
抓住「认不确定 + 补形状」，把僵局变成推进。
错在没结构，选项间摇摆等于空转。
错在硬编，把记错的当定论说出口。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — gives up, nothing follows the surrender.
Nails "admit doubt, then give the shape" — turns a freeze into progress.
Wrong — no structure; wavering options just spin.
Wrong — states a misremembered fact as settled truth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表：用哈希函数把 key 映射成数组下标，实现平均 O(1) 的读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash map uses a hash function to turn a key into an array index, giving average O(1) lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对数时间复杂度：数据翻倍，操作步数只多一步，比 O(1) 慢但比线性快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(log n) means the work grows by one step each time the data doubles — slower than O(1), faster than linear.

scenario: Gamma 后端面试，你说这个项目难在流量，话说到一半意识到真正的难点是业务逻辑复杂度。上次你「it's not this, it's not about the traffic, but…」绕得很乱。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend interview you say the project was hard because of traffic, then mid-sentence realize the real difficulty was business-logic complexity. Last time you tangled it into "it's not this, it's not about the traffic, but…"
q: 中途发现自己说错了，怎么优雅地纠正？
q_en: You catch yourself mid-sentence — how do you correct it gracefully?
options: The hard part was the traffic, but the, it's not this, it's not about the traffic, but about the complexity...
Wait, so, the traffic, or, no, hmm, I mean it was traffic but also not really traffic, more like the logic, or both, let me...
Oh I'm so sorry, I misspoke, that was totally wrong of me, my apologies, please ignore what I just said, sorry again...
Actually, let me correct that — the hard part wasn't traffic, it was the business-logic complexity.
tradeoff: 一句干净纠正 vs 边说边绕/狂道歉：「Actually, let me correct that」一步换新说法；绕或狂道歉都把小口误放大成慌乱。
why: 说错时用一句「Actually, let me correct myself —」干净地覆盖旧说法，直接给对的版本；反复否定或连声道歉只会把小失误放大。
why_en: When you misspeak, one clean "actually, let me correct that —" overwrites the old line; looping or over-apologizing just amplifies a tiny slip.
whenOtherWins: 只有当口误无关紧要、完全不影响理解时，才不必正式纠正，接着往下说更自然。
options_en: The hard part was the traffic, but the, it's not this, it's not about the traffic, but about the complexity...
Wait, so, the traffic, or, no, hmm, I mean it was traffic but also not really traffic, more like the logic, or both, let me...
Oh I'm so sorry, I misspoke, that was totally wrong of me, my apologies, please ignore what I just said, sorry again...
Actually, let me correct that — the hard part wasn't traffic, it was the business-logic complexity.
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：反复「it's not this / not about the traffic」绕圈否定。
在 traffic 和 logic 之间来回改口，越说越乱。
为一个小口误连声道歉，把注意力全引到失误上。
一句干净的改口，覆盖错话直接给出对的版本。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: loops "it's not this / not about the traffic" in circles.
Flip-flops between traffic and logic, gets messier.
Over-apologizes for a small slip, spotlighting the error.
A clean pivot that swaps the slip for the right version.
optionScenarioImpacts: 绕圈否定，对方听不出你到底想说什么。
来回改口，显得思路没理顺。
小失误被道歉放大，反而显得慌。
一步接回，显得冷静、掌控得住。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Circular negation; they can't tell what you mean.
Flip-flopping reads as unformed thinking.
Apology magnifies a slip and makes you look rattled.
One clean pivot — reads as calm and in control.
optionDirectness: 错在打转，否定了半天没给新说法。
错在反复改口，方向一直不定。
错在过度道歉，把小事放大成大事。
抓住「一句覆盖 + 直接给对的」的自我纠正法。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — circles on negation, never lands the new line.
Wrong — keeps flip-flopping, direction never settles.
Wrong — over-apology inflates a slip into a big deal.
Nails self-correction: one overwrite, straight to the right line.

scenario: IKEA 系统设计轮，面试官让你设计一个匹配系统。你想先澄清范围（单区域还是全球），上次你笼统说「I would first clarify the constraints」却没问出具体问题。
scenario_en: In IKEA's system-design round you're asked to design a matching system. You want to clarify scope first — single-region or global — but last time you just said "I would first clarify the constraints" without asking anything concrete.
q: 开始设计前想澄清一个具体范围问题，怎么问？
q_en: How do you ask one concrete scoping question before you design?
options: Before I sketch anything — is this single-region, or do we need to handle global traffic?
So I would first clarify the business object and the constraints of the marketplace, at a high level...
There's a lot to clarify, like scope, users, regions, scale, consistency, so many things, where should I even start, maybe I list them all...
Prior to commencing the design, I request clarification regarding the geographic scope of the system.
tradeoff: 问一个具体范围问题 vs 空喊「澄清约束」：具体问题立刻缩小设计面；空喊澄清听着像套路，没换来任何信息。
why: 澄清要问出一个能改变设计的具体问题（单区域还是全球），而不是空说「I'll clarify the constraints」——后者不缩小任何设计面。
why_en: A good clarifier asks something that changes the design — "single-region or global?" — not a vague "I'll clarify the constraints."
whenOtherWins: 只有当范围已在题面明确给定时，才不必再问，直接按给定范围往下设计。
options_en: Before I sketch anything — is this single-region, or do we need to handle global traffic?
So I would first clarify the business object and the constraints of the marketplace, at a high level...
There's a lot to clarify, like scope, users, regions, scale, consistency, so many things, where should I even start, maybe I list them all...
Prior to commencing the design, I request clarification regarding the geographic scope of the system.
optionMeanings: 一个具体范围问题：一区还是全球，立刻收窄设计面。
她的老毛病：泛泛说要澄清约束，却没问出具体东西。
把要澄清的都堆出来，却不知从哪问起。
用「Prior to commencing」的公文腔问地理范围。
optionMeanings_en: One concrete scope question that narrows the whole design.
Her habit: vaguely promises to clarify, asks nothing.
Piles up everything to clarify, unsure where to start.
Asks geographic scope in stiff "prior to commencing" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 一问就砍掉一半设计面，显得有章法。
听着像套路开场，没换来任何信息。
堆一长串反而显得没抓手。
生硬像文书，暖不起对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: One question halves the design space — looks methodical.
Sounds like a canned opener, yields no information.
The long pile reads as having no handle on it.
Stiff like a memo, kills the conversational tone.
optionDirectness: 抓住「问一个改变设计的具体范围」这一步。
错在空泛，喊澄清却没有任何具体问题。
错在铺满，罗列一堆不落到一个问句。
错在语域，口语澄清用书面公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Nails it: one concrete scope question that changes the design.
Wrong — vague; says "clarify" but asks nothing specific.
Wrong — lists everything, never lands one question.
Wrong register — a spoken clarifier in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单区域：系统只部署在一个地理区域，不用跨区做复制和一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-region means the system runs in one geographic region, with no cross-region replication to handle.

scenario: Alterion 面试，面试官提议用最终一致的存储放用户刚提交的设置。你担心用户读到旧值，上次你把「has ACID」说成「half acid」还卡住了。
scenario_en: In an Alterion interview the interviewer proposes an eventually-consistent store for settings a user just saved. You worry the user reads a stale value — last time you said "half acid" for "has ACID" and stalled.
q: 想礼貌指出「最终一致会让用户读到旧数据」，怎么说？
q_en: How do you politely flag that eventual consistency could show stale data?
options: If we want consistency we use SQL like MySQL because it's half acid, it's the, so...
Maybe eventual consistency is fine, or maybe not, it kind of depends on the user, sometimes stale is okay, sometimes not, so hard to say...
One concern — if a user reads right after writing, eventual consistency could show them stale data, right?
I wish to raise an objection concerning the consistency guarantees of the proposed datastore.
tradeoff: 点名读己写场景 vs 说错术语/含糊：具体到「写完立刻读」让质疑有分量；说错 ACID 或含糊「看情况」都传不出顾虑。
why: 质疑一致性要落到具体场景「写完立刻读」（read-your-writes），说清最终一致会返回 stale 数据；关键词是 ACID，不是「half acid」。
why_en: Ground the challenge in "read right after write" (read-your-writes) — eventual consistency can return stale data; the term is ACID, not "half acid."
whenOtherWins: 只有当这份数据能容忍短暂陈旧（如展示类、非关键路径）时，才不必反对最终一致。
options_en: If we want consistency we use SQL like MySQL because it's half acid, it's the, so...
Maybe eventual consistency is fine, or maybe not, it kind of depends on the user, sometimes stale is okay, sometimes not, so hard to say...
One concern — if a user reads right after writing, eventual consistency could show them stale data, right?
I wish to raise an objection concerning the consistency guarantees of the proposed datastore.
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：把「has ACID」说成「half acid」并卡住。
在「行不行」之间反复对冲，没给出顾虑。
落到「写完立刻读」的场景，点名会读到旧值。
用「I wish to raise an objection」的公文腔提反对。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: says "half acid" for "has ACID" and stalls.
Hedges back and forth on "fine or not," states no concern.
Grounds it in read-after-write, names the stale value.
Objects in a stiff "I wish to raise an objection" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 术语说错还卡住，顾虑完全没传出去。
全是对冲，对方听不出你反对什么。
质疑有具体场景撑着，显得有分量。
生硬像法律函，破坏协作气氛。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Wrong term plus a stall — the concern never lands.
Pure hedging; they can't tell what you're objecting to.
A concrete scenario backs the challenge — it carries weight.
Stiff like a legal notice, sours the collaborative vibe.
optionDirectness: 错在词形，「half acid」是口误还卡住。
错在对冲，只有「看情况」没有立场。
抓住「落到读己写场景 + 点名旧值」的质疑法。
错在语域，口语质疑用公文体显生硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong term form — "half acid" slips, and then a stall.
Wrong — hedge only, "it depends," no position taken.
Nails it: ground in read-your-writes, name the stale read.
Wrong register — a spoken challenge in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最终一致性：写入后副本会在一段时间后趋于一致，期间读可能拿到旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas converge over time, so a read soon after a write may return an old value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性——关系型事务提供的四个保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the four guarantees a relational transaction gives: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读己所写：同一用户写入后立刻读，应当能读到自己刚写的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes means a user who just wrote a value should immediately see it on their next read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 陈旧数据：反映旧版本、还没同步到最新写入的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stale data reflects an older version that hasn't caught up with the latest write.

scenario: Alterion 面试，面试官问你有没有亲手配过 Kafka。你没配过但懂原理，上次你说「the Kafi configuration part is not managed by myself」有点乱。
scenario_en: In an Alterion interview you're asked if you've configured Kafka yourself. You haven't, but you get the model — last time you fumbled "the Kafi configuration part is not managed by myself."
q: 没亲手用过但懂原理，怎么答既诚实又显专业？
q_en: You haven't used it hands-on but grasp the model — how do you answer honestly yet sharply?
options: Have I built Kafka before, the Kafi, the configuration part is not managed by myself, but I understand...
I haven't configured Kafka myself, but conceptually it's an append-only log partitioned by key.
Yeah, I've set up Kafka end to end — it's basically a database you query with SQL.
No, I'm sorry, I've never touched it, I really should have, sorry, that's a gap, my apologies...
tradeoff: 认没做过但给原理 vs 硬吹/狂道歉：一句「没配过，但原理是…」既诚实又展示深度；硬吹会被追问穿帮，狂道歉放大短板。
why: 没亲手用过某工具时，先坦白「没配过」，紧接着一句原理（Kafka 是按 key 分区的 append-only log）证明你懂；硬吹很快被追问穿帮。
why_en: If you haven't used a tool, admit it, then prove understanding in one line — "Kafka is an append-only log partitioned by key"; bluffing collapses under the next question.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实亲手配过时，才直接讲实操细节，不用先声明「没做过」。
options_en: Have I built Kafka before, the Kafi, the configuration part is not managed by myself, but I understand...
I haven't configured Kafka myself, but conceptually it's an append-only log partitioned by key.
Yeah, I've set up Kafka end to end — it's basically a database you query with SQL.
No, I'm sorry, I've never touched it, I really should have, sorry, that's a gap, my apologies...
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：「the Kafi… not managed by myself」绕不清。
先坦白没配过，再用一句原理证明你懂。
硬吹「端到端配过」，还把 Kafka 说成 SQL 数据库。
为没用过连声道歉，把短板越描越大。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: "the Kafi… not managed by myself" — tangled.
Admits no hands-on, then proves the model in one line.
Bluffs "set it up end to end," calls Kafka a SQL database.
Over-apologizes for not using it, magnifying the gap.
optionScenarioImpacts: 绕不清，诚实和懂原理都没传出去。
既诚实又展示深度，对方愿意深聊。
一追问就穿帮，可信度全丢。
道歉放大短板，显得不自信。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Too tangled — neither honesty nor grasp comes through.
Honest and shows depth; they'll happily go deeper.
One follow-up exposes the bluff; credibility gone.
Apology inflates the gap and reads as insecure.
optionDirectness: 错在表达，绕得听不出你到底懂不懂。
抓住「坦白没做 + 一句原理」的诚实展示法。
错在硬吹，还把概念说反了。
错在过度道歉，把小空白说成大问题。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong delivery — too tangled to tell if you understand.
Nails it: admit no hands-on, then one line of the model.
Wrong — bluffs and gets the concept backwards.
Wrong — over-apology turns a small gap into a big one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息/流平台，把消息按 key 分区、以 append-only log 顺序存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming platform that stores messages in an append-only log, partitioned by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只追加日志：新记录只往末尾加、不改旧记录的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An append-only log is storage where new records are only added at the end and old ones are never changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 key 分区：用 key 把数据流拆成多个可并行处理的子流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioned by key means the stream is split by key into sub-streams that can be processed in parallel.

scenario: Alterion 编码轮，题目要你实现 trie 的 startsWith。你不确定它该返回所有匹配单词还是只返回布尔，上次你自问「why we want to return a list of string」绕了很久。
scenario_en: In an Alterion coding round you implement a trie's startsWith. You're unsure whether it returns all matching words or just a boolean — last time you muttered "why we want to return a list of string" and looped for a while.

scenario: TikTok 广告系统设计面试，面试官问系统大概每秒多少请求。她一紧张就想跳过估算，说「这个不好估」。

q: 这个 QPS 该怎么当场估给面试官听？
q_en: How do you estimate the QPS out loud for the interviewer?
options: That's really hard to estimate without production data, so I'd rather not put a number on it right now.
The QPS is probably around a million or so — that feels about right for a system this size.
Let's say 100 million users, ~1% active per second — that's roughly 1 million QPS. I'll design for that.
Um, I'm not totally sure, it could be, like, a lot, maybe a million, but honestly it really depends on so many things I can't say.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳：先设假设、当众算出约 1M QPS vs 躲开数字或只抛一个没来路的数。
why: 先亮假设（1 亿用户、每秒 1% 活跃），当众把乘法做完得出约 100 万 QPS，再用它拍板。她的毛病是一紧张就躲开数字。
why_en: State your assumptions out loud, do the multiplication to land on roughly a million QPS, then use that number to drive the design.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说先不管量级、只想听功能设计，那晚点再估、先讲功能也可以。

scenario: 面试官问事件日志系统每天大概要存多少数据。她想说清，却卡成「the data volume is very big, the storage pressure...」。

q: 每天的存储量该怎么估着说出口？
q_en: How do you estimate the daily storage out loud?
options: Say 1 billion events a day at ~1 KB each — that's roughly 1 TB a day, so I'd use cheap object storage.

To estimate storage, one multiplies the daily event count by the average event size to obtain the total daily volume that must be provisioned.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳：假设加乘法算出约 1TB/天 并拍板存储 vs 只说「数据很大、压力很大」的直译。

why_en: Assume 1 billion events times 1 KB, multiply out loud to roughly 1 TB a day, and let that pick cheap object storage.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只想听存什么字段、schema 怎么设计，那先讲数据模型、量级放后面也行。

The peak time the QPS will be very high, so we need more buffer, the average is not enough I think.

q_en: How do you estimate the fan-out write amplification out loud?
options: That depends on how many followers people have, which varies a lot, so it's hard to give a number here.
Say the average person has 500 followers — one post fans out to ~500 writes, so 1 million posts a day is roughly 500 million writes.

q: 面试官说得对时，怎么大方认错并给新方案?
q_en: When they're right, how do you concede gracefully and give a new plan?
options: So so the cache, I mean the budget it changes, but maybe it's fine, or maybe not, it kind of depends, let me think how to say this...
Good point — you're right, per-second budget data is too fresh to cache. I'd read straight from the store instead.
Oh yeah, you're right, okay, let me just remove the cache then.
The cache will out of date very fast, so the read pass get the old budget, that's not good.
tradeoff: 大方认错 vs 绕圈/干认：一句「你说得对 + 我改成…」换来对齐；只干认不给方案，或绕圈，都显得没想清。
why: 认同对方时用「Good point — you're right, …」先认，再立刻给出替代方案(直接读源)，认得干脆也收得住。
why_en: Concede with "Good point — you're right" then immediately give the alternative, so you own it and still land a plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轮询:定时反复查询数据源看有没有变化,即使没变也照查。

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片:把一张大表按某个键拆到多台机器上,分担存储和查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits one large table across machines by a key to spread storage and query load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片键:决定一行数据落在哪个分片上的那个字段,选它决定查询是否集中。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key is the field that decides which shard a row lands on; it determines whether a query stays local.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扇出:一次查询被迫打到很多个分片而不是一个,变慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan out is when one query has to hit many shards instead of one, making it slower.

options: Good catch, you're right, I'll make it not sync then.
Yes the sync call will block, the request must wait the price to come back, so the round trip is long time.
Good catch — a sync call there does block the request. I'd make it async and fall back to a cached price.

tradeoff: 认错并给完整替代 vs 空认/绕圈:一句「同步确实会阻塞 + 改异步并用缓存兜底」既认又给出完整方案;只说「改成不同步」漏了兜底。

termDefinitions.meaning: 同步调用:发出请求后原地等对方返回,期间当前请求被卡住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A synchronous call waits in place for the response, blocking the current request meanwhile.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往返:一次请求发出到收到响应的完整网络来回,多一次就多一份延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A round trip is one full request-and-response cycle over the network; each one adds latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 丢事件:系统在高峰扛不住时把一部分消息直接丢弃,不再处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dropping events is when a system under load discards some messages instead of processing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 计费事件:一条代表扣费/花费的记录,丢了就会算错钱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A billing event is a record of a charge or spend; losing one means the money is counted wrong.

options: Exactly-once, um, exactly-once semantics... okay, so, let me, let me think how Kafka...
I haven't used exactly-once directly, but from first principles I'd expect idempotent writes plus committing offsets in one transaction.
Oh yeah, exactly-once just means Kafka literally never sends any message twice, so it's fully guaranteed out of the box, nothing to configure.
Honestly I've never touched that part, so I really don't know — sorry, maybe we can just skip this one.

why: 没深用过就先认领边界「I haven't used X directly」，再用「from first principles」把已知原理推出来，比卡死或硬编都可信。
why_en: Name the boundary — "I haven't used X directly" — then reason from first principles, which reads far stronger than freezing or bluffing.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实深用过、能直接讲实现时，才跳过「没用过」的免责，直接给答案更有分量。

I haven't used exactly-once directly, but from first principles I'd expect idempotent writes plus committing offsets in one transaction.
Oh yeah, exactly-once just means Kafka literally never sends any message twice, so it's fully guaranteed out of the box, nothing to configure.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：一个分布式消息/事件流平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform.

termDefinitions.meaning: exactly-once：每条消息在处理结果上不重不漏、恰好生效一次的语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means each message takes effect once — never lost, never duplicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一操作执行一次或多次，结果相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means running the same operation once or many times yields the same result.

termDefinitions.meaning: offset：消费者在 Kafka 分区中读到的位置游标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the position cursor tracking how far a consumer has read in a Kafka partition.

scenario: Alterion coding 轮，你做出了暴力解但卡在优化，脑子一片空白，上次僵在「okay... okay...」半分钟没出声。

q: 彻底卡住、需要提示时，怎么开口既不慌又不放弃？
q_en: Truly stuck and needing a hint — how do you speak up without panicking or quitting?
options: I've got a working brute force but I'm stuck making it faster — can I get a hint on which direction to explore?
Okay... okay, so... um, faster, faster, how to make it faster, let me, let me think...
It's already optimal, this brute force is basically O(n), so I don't think we can really do better here.
Yeah I'm really stuck, I honestly don't think I can figure this one out — sorry, I guess this just isn't my strongest area.
tradeoff: 主动要定向提示 vs 硬撑或弃题：求助换来推进和协作感，代价是暴露卡点；硬撑或放弃只会让空白更久。
why: 彻底卡住时，主动「can I get a hint on...?」把求助变成缩小范围的推进，比僵在「okay...」或硬说已最优都体面。
why_en: When truly stuck, ask "can I get a hint on X?" — a scoped ask moves you forward, unlike freezing on "okay..." or bluffing "it's optimal."
whenOtherWins: 只有当你其实还有没试的思路时，先自己出声试一版，再决定要不要要提示。
options_en: I've got a working brute force but I'm stuck making it faster — can I get a hint on which direction to explore?

termDefinitions.meaning: O(n)（线性时间）：耗时随数据量成正比增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(n), linear time, means the cost grows in proportion to the data size.

scenario: Convoke 面，面试官问你刚写的函数时间复杂度。你不确定，上次脱口「O(n) 吧」被追问就崩了。
scenario_en: In a Convoke round the interviewer asks the time complexity of the function you just wrote. You're unsure — last time you blurted "O(n), I guess" and crumbled on the follow-up.
q: 复杂度没把握时，怎么开口既不乱猜也不装懂？
q_en: Unsure of the complexity — how do you speak without wild-guessing or faking it?
options: It's O(n), definitely — there's just one main loop, so it's linear, I'm pretty sure.
Complexity, um, the complexity is... okay, so, the loop, the loop runs, let me, let me think...
Honestly I'm not great at complexity analysis, so I'd rather not just guess and get it wrong — sorry about that.
Let me reason through it — a loop inside a loop, so it's n times n, which is O(n²).
tradeoff: 出声逐步推导 vs 直接抛一个数字：推导换来可验证的可信度，代价是慢一点；直接报数字快却可能自信地错。

why_en: If you truly don't know, say "I haven't worked with that, so I won't guess," then pivot to the closest thing you have done — cleaner than bluffing or repeated apologies.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你其实有部分线索能推时，才别急着认「不知道」，先出声推一版。

抓住「先问规模+读写侧」这一步。
错在打转，罗列要素不落一个问句。
错在语域，口语开场用公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong term form — "read-many" isn't read-heavy.
Nails it: ask scale and read/write side first.
Wrong — lists factors, lands no single question.
Wrong register — a spoken opener in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读多：读请求远多于写请求的负载，设计偏向读优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-heavy means reads far outnumber writes, so the design optimizes for reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写多：写请求占主导的负载，设计偏向写吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-heavy means writes dominate, so the design optimizes for write throughput.

scenario: IKEA 系统设计轮，面试官让你设计一个库存扣减服务。你想先问「更看重低延迟还是强一致」，上次你没问就默认了强一致，方向压错。
scenario_en: In IKEA's system-design round you're asked to design an inventory-decrement service. You want to ask what matters more — low latency or strong consistency — but last time you defaulted to strong consistency without asking and tuned the wrong side.
q: 开始设计前想问清延迟和一致性哪个优先，怎么说？
q_en: How do you ask whether latency or consistency comes first before you design?
options: One thing first — what matters more here, low latency or strong consistency?
So is it strong consistent, or the final consistent one, the strong one or the final one, so...
Consistency, latency, hmm, both matter, so maybe consistency, or latency, or both, let me think which...
Kindly indicate whether the system should prioritize latency minimization or consistency guarantees.
tradeoff: 先问优先级 vs 默认一种：一句「延迟还是一致性?」定方向；默认强一致可能整体压错侧，白费功夫。
why: 设计前先问「更看重低延迟还是强一致」，一句话定优化方向；术语是 eventually consistent，不是「final consistent」。
why_en: Ask what matters more first — low latency or strong consistency — one question sets the optimization; the term is eventually consistent, not "final consistent."
whenOtherWins: 只有当题目已言明延迟或一致性哪个优先时，才不用再问，直接按给定优先级设计。
options_en: One thing first — what matters more here, low latency or strong consistency?
So is it strong consistent, or the final consistent one, the strong one or the final one, so...
Consistency, latency, hmm, both matter, so maybe consistency, or latency, or both, let me think which...
Kindly indicate whether the system should prioritize latency minimization or consistency guarantees.
optionMeanings: 开设计前一句问清延迟和一致性哪个优先。
口误把「eventual」说成「final」，然后卡住。
在延迟和一致性间反复对冲，不落定。
用公文腔问优先级，僵硬。
optionMeanings_en: One question up front — latency or consistency?
Says "final consistent" for eventually consistent, stalls.
Hedges between latency and consistency, never lands.
Asks the priority in stiff memo register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 优先级先定，方案不会压错侧。
词形跑偏还卡，顾虑没传出去。
全是对冲，显得心里没底。
生硬像文书，破坏对话感。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Priority set first; you won't design the wrong side.
Wrong form plus a stall; the point never lands.
Pure hedging; you sound unsure yourself.
Stiff like a memo, breaks the conversational feel.
optionDirectness: 抓住「先问延迟还是一致性优先」这一步。
错在词形，把 eventual 念成 final。
错在对冲，只有摇摆没有问句。
错在语域，口语澄清用公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Nails it: ask latency-vs-consistency priority first.
Wrong term form — "final consistent" is a slip.
Wrong — hedging only, no actual question asked.
Wrong register — a spoken clarifier in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低延迟：请求到响应的耗时很短。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low latency means a request returns a response very quickly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强一致：任何读都能读到最新写入的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means every read returns the most recent write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最终一致：写入后副本逐渐同步，期间读可能拿到旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventually consistent means replicas converge over time, so a read may briefly return an old value.

scenario: Convoke 系统设计轮，面试官抛出「设计一个通知系统」。你想先把功能需求和非功能需求分开列，上次你一上来就混着讲，越讲越乱。
scenario_en: In a Convoke system-design round the interviewer says "design a notification system." You want to split functional from non-functional requirements first — last time you mixed them from the start and got more tangled.
q: 想先把功能和非功能需求分开，怎么开口？
q_en: How do you split functional from non-functional requirements before designing?
options: So there is the function requirement and the non-function requirement, the function one and the non-function one, so...
Okay so notifications — push, email, SMS, scale, latency, delivery, so many things, let me, where do I start...
Let me split this into functional and non-functional requirements first — does that work?
I shall commence by delineating the functional requirements followed by the non-functional requirements.
tradeoff: 先分两类需求 vs 混着开讲：分开列给讨论一个骨架；混着堆越讲越乱，抓不住重点。
why: 开局先把需求分成功能和非功能两类，给后面讨论一个骨架；术语是 functional，不是「function requirement」。
why_en: Open by splitting requirements into functional and non-functional — it gives the discussion a backbone; the term is functional, not "function requirement."
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官已经替你把需求分好类时，才不用再分，直接接着往下讨论。
options_en: So there is the function requirement and the non-function requirement, the function one and the non-function one, so...
Okay so notifications — push, email, SMS, scale, latency, delivery, so many things, let me, where do I start...
Let me split this into functional and non-functional requirements first — does that work?
I shall commence by delineating the functional requirements followed by the non-functional requirements.
optionMeanings: 口误把「functional」拆成「function」加名词，还在原地绕。
她的老毛病：把功能点全堆出来，不做分类。
先把功能和非功能需求分开，再往下设计。
用公文腔宣布要先列功能再列非功能。
optionMeanings_en: Says "function requirement" for functional, loops.
Her habit: dumps every feature, never categorizes.
Splits functional from non-functional, then designs.
Announces the split in stiff memo register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 词形跑偏还绕，分类没做成。
混着堆显得没条理，越讲越乱。
两类分开，后面讨论有清晰骨架。
生硬像文书，暖不起对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Wrong form and looping; the split never happens.
Dumping unsorted reads as messy, gets tangled.
Two buckets give the rest a clean backbone.
Stiff like a memo, kills the conversational tone.
optionDirectness: 错在词形，functional 被拆成 function 加名词。
错在堆砌，罗列功能点却不分类。
抓住「先分功能/非功能两类」这一步。
错在语域，口语开场用公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong term form — "function requirement" isn't functional.
Wrong — dumps features without categorizing them.
Nails it: split functional vs non-functional first.
Wrong register — a spoken opener in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 功能需求：系统要做什么，如发送通知、去重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Functional requirements are what the system must do, like sending or de-duplicating notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非功能需求：系统要多好，如延迟、可用性、规模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements are how well it must perform — latency, availability, scale.

scenario: Gamma 系统设计轮，题目很大：设计一个完整的电商平台。你想主动收窄到下单写路径、把鉴权划出范围，上次你想全都覆盖，时间根本不够。
scenario_en: In a Gamma system-design round the prompt is huge: design a full e-commerce platform. You want to narrow to the order write path and put auth out of scope — last time you tried to cover everything and ran out of time.
q: 想主动把范围收窄到写路径、鉴权先不管，怎么说？
q_en: How do you narrow the scope to the write path and mark auth out of scope?
options: So there's checkout, auth, catalog, payment, search, maybe I do all of them, or, hmm, which first, let me...
I will focus the write pass first and put the auth to outside the scope, the write pass and the auth...
For this exercise I shall delimit the scope to the write path and designate authentication as out of scope.
To stay focused, I'll design the order write path and treat auth as out of scope — okay?
tradeoff: 主动收窄一条路径 vs 想全覆盖：收窄换来把核心讲深；贪多则每块浅尝，时间根本不够。
why: 题太大时主动收窄到一条核心路径、明确把某块划出范围，换来把主线讲深；术语是 write path，不是「write pass」。
why_en: When the prompt is huge, narrow to one core path and name what's out of scope — it buys depth on the main line; the term is write path, not "write pass."
whenOtherWins: 只有当题面范围本就很小、能全覆盖时，才不用收窄，直接把各块都讲到。
options_en: So there's checkout, auth, catalog, payment, search, maybe I do all of them, or, hmm, which first, let me...
I will focus the write pass first and put the auth to outside the scope, the write pass and the auth...
For this exercise I shall delimit the scope to the write path and designate authentication as out of scope.
To stay focused, I'll design the order write path and treat auth as out of scope — okay?
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：想把所有模块全覆盖，不知从哪起。
把 write path 说成「write pass」，收窄没说利落。
用公文腔宣布把范围限定到写路径。
主动收窄到下单写路径，把鉴权划出范围。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: tries to cover every module, unsure where to start.
Says "write pass" for write path; the narrowing is clumsy.
Delimits scope to the write path in stiff memo register.
Narrows to the order write path, drops auth from scope.
optionScenarioImpacts: 全铺开时间不够，每块都浅尝辄止。
词形跑偏，收窄的意图打了折。
生硬像文书，破坏协作感。
范围一收，时间够把核心讲深。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Covering all runs out of time; everything stays shallow.
Wrong form dilutes the narrowing you meant to make.
Stiff like a memo, sours the collaborative feel.
Narrowing buys time to go deep on the core.
optionDirectness: 错在贪多，想全覆盖反而铺不开。
错在词形，「write pass」不是 write path。
错在语域，口语收窄用公文体。
抓住「主动收窄+明确 out of scope」这一步。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — over-reaches; covering all spreads too thin.
Wrong term form — "write pass" isn't write path.
Wrong register — spoken scoping in bureaucratese.
Nails it: narrow on purpose and name what's out of scope.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径：一条数据被写入/更新时经过的处理链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the chain of steps a request goes through when data is written.

termDefinitions.meaning: 范围外：这次设计明确不处理的部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Out of scope means a part you explicitly decide not to handle in this design.

scenario: Alterion 系统设计轮，设计一个打车匹配系统。你脑子里冒出十个问题，想先问最影响设计的那一个，上次你一口气把问题全倒出来，显得没重点。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round you're designing a ride-matching system. Ten questions come to mind and you want to ask the one that shapes the design most — last time you dumped all of them at once and looked unfocused.
q: 有一堆问题，想先问最关键那个而不是全倒出来，怎么说？
q_en: You have many questions — how do you ask the highest-impact one first instead of dumping them all?
options: So I have questions — scale, region, latency, radius, drivers, riders, pricing, surge, let me just ask them all...
Biggest question first — does matching happen in real time within seconds, or can it batch?
The most important one, the real-time match or the batch match, the real-time one or the batch one, so...
Among my clarifications, the most consequential concerns whether matching must occur in real time.
tradeoff: 先问最关键一个 vs 一次全倒：一个高影响问题立刻收窄设计；全倒显得没主次，还占时间。
why: 问题很多时，先挑最能改变设计的那个问（实时还是可批处理），而不是一次全倒出来显得没重点。
why_en: With many questions, lead with the one that most changes the design — real-time or batch — instead of dumping all of them and looking unfocused.
whenOtherWins: 只有当几个问题同等关键、且时间充裕时，才可以一次多问几个。
options_en: So I have questions — scale, region, latency, radius, drivers, riders, pricing, surge, let me just ask them all...
Biggest question first — does matching happen in real time within seconds, or can it batch?
The most important one, the real-time match or the batch match, the real-time one or the batch one, so...
Among my clarifications, the most consequential concerns whether matching must occur in real time.
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：把十个问题一口气全倒出来，没重点。
先问最影响设计的一个：实时匹配还是可批处理。
把 real-time/batch 绕来绕去，不落成一个问句。
用公文腔说最关键的是实时性问题。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: dumps all ten questions at once, no priority.
Asks the one that shapes the design: real-time or batch?
Circles real-time/batch, never lands one question.
States the key one is real-time, in stiff memo register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 一串问题显得没主次，抓不住重点。
一问就砍掉一半设计面，显得有章法。
绕半天没锁定，浪费时间。
生硬像文书，暖不起对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A question dump reads as no priorities, no focus.
One question halves the design space — looks methodical.
Circles without pinning it; wastes time.
Stiff like a memo, kills the conversational tone.
optionDirectness: 错在铺满，一次倒出所有问题没主次。
抓住「先问最关键那一个」这一步。
错在打转，real-time/batch 绕着不问。
错在语域，口语澄清用公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — dumps every question with no priority.
Nails it: ask the single highest-impact question first.
Wrong — circles real-time/batch without asking.
Wrong register — a spoken clarifier in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时匹配：请求进来后几秒内就要给出匹配结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Real-time matching produces a result within seconds of the request arriving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 批处理：把请求攒起来周期性一起处理，而非逐条即时处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batch processing collects requests and handles them periodically instead of one at a time.

scenario: IKEA 系统设计轮，面试官说「设计一个聊天应用」。你习惯先把题目复述一遍，上次你说「so we design a chat app that let user to chat」等于没说，还卡住。
scenario_en: In IKEA's system-design round the interviewer says "design a chat app." You tend to echo the prompt back — last time you said "so we design a chat app that let user to chat," which said nothing and then you stalled.
q: 不想复述题目，想把它转成一个范围问题，怎么开口？
q_en: Instead of echoing the prompt, how do you turn it into one scoping question?
options: So we design a chat app that let the user to chat with each other, the user chat, so...
A chat app, okay, so, messages, users, presence, so so, where do I even start, let me think about chat...
Quick scoping — is this 1:1 messaging, or do we need group chat and presence too?
The task being a chat application, I shall first ascertain whether group functionality falls within scope.
tradeoff: 把题目转成范围问句 vs 原样复述：一个问句收窄设计；复述等于没说，还浪费开场。
why: 别把题目原样复述，把它转成一个能收窄设计的范围问句（一对一还是群聊）；复述既没信息又易卡在词形上。
why_en: Don't echo the prompt back — turn it into one scoping question that narrows the design (1:1 or group chat); echoing adds nothing and invites a fumble.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官已经把范围说得很清楚时，才不用再问，直接进入设计。
options_en: So we design a chat app that let the user to chat with each other, the user chat, so...
A chat app, okay, so, messages, users, presence, so so, where do I even start, let me think about chat...
Quick scoping — is this 1:1 messaging, or do we need group chat and presence too?
The task being a chat application, I shall first ascertain whether group functionality falls within scope.
optionMeanings: 她的老毛病：把题目原样复述，还说成「let the user to chat」。
被大题目卡住，要素乱转，开不了口问。
把题目转成范围问题：一对一还是群聊加在线状态。
用公文腔说要先确认是否含群聊。
optionMeanings_en: Her habit: echoes the prompt, says "let the user to chat."
Frozen by the big prompt, factors spin, asks nothing.
Turns the prompt into a scope question: 1:1 or group + presence.
Says it'll confirm group scope, in stiff memo register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 复述等于没说，还卡在词形上。
空转显得没头绪，开不了局。
一问就把设计面收窄，显得有章法。
生硬像文书，破坏对话感。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Echoing says nothing and snags on the wrong form.
Spinning reads as no thread; you can't get going.
One question narrows the design and looks methodical.
Stiff like a memo, breaks the conversational feel.
optionDirectness: 错在复述，把题目原样念还说错词形。
错在空转，被题目卡住不落成问句。
抓住「把题目转成一个范围问题」这一步。
错在语域，口语范围问句用公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — echoes the prompt and mangles the form.
Wrong — spins on the prompt, lands no question.
Nails it: convert the prompt into one scope question.
Wrong register — a spoken scope question in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一对一消息：两个用户之间点对点收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 1:1 messaging is point-to-point message exchange between two users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 群聊：多个用户在同一会话里收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Group chat lets many users exchange messages in one shared conversation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线状态：显示用户当前在线/离线/正在输入等状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence shows whether a user is currently online, offline, or typing.

scenario: Gamma 系统设计轮，设计一个新闻 feed。你想先问清 DAU 好给系统定量级，上次你没问规模、直接假设了一个数，面试官追问你哪来的。
scenario_en: In a Gamma system-design round you're designing a news feed. You want to ask the DAU first to anchor the scale — last time you skipped it, assumed a number, and the interviewer asked where it came from.
q: 想先问清 DAU 好给系统估量级，怎么说？
q_en: How do you ask the DAU up front so you can size the system?
options: Before I size anything — roughly what DAU are we targeting, ballpark?
So the daily user, the active user per day, how much is the DAU, the daily active number, so...
Users, so, maybe a million, or ten million, hmm, I'm not sure, let me just assume some number, or...
In order to dimension the system appropriately, kindly disclose the projected daily active user count.
tradeoff: 先问 DAU 定量级 vs 自己假设：问清规模让估算站得住；瞎猜一被追问就露馅。
why: 估算前先问清 DAU，给系统定一个量级，后面的容量估算才有据；别不问就假设，一追问就站不住。
why_en: Ask the DAU before estimating so the whole design has a scale anchor; don't assume a number — it collapses the moment they ask where it came from.
whenOtherWins: 只有当题目已经给定 DAU 或规模时，才不用再问，直接用给定数字估算。
options_en: Before I size anything — roughly what DAU are we targeting, ballpark?
So the daily user, the active user per day, how much is the DAU, the daily active number, so...
Users, so, maybe a million, or ten million, hmm, I'm not sure, let me just assume some number, or...
In order to dimension the system appropriately, kindly disclose the projected daily active user count.
optionMeanings: 开设计前先问 DAU，好给系统定量级。
把 how many 说成「how much」，绕着问 DAU。
她的老毛病：不问规模，自己瞎猜一个数。
用公文腔索要每日活跃用户数。
optionMeanings_en: Asks DAU up front to size the system.
Says "how much" for how many, circles on DAU.
Her habit: skips asking, guesses a number herself.
Requests the DAU count in stiff memo register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 量级先定，后面估算有据可依。
词形跑偏，问得不利落。
瞎猜被追问哪来的，站不住脚。
生硬像文书，暖不起对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Scale set first; later estimates have a basis.
Wrong form makes the question clumsy.
A guess invites "where from?" and can't hold up.
Stiff like a memo, kills the conversational tone.
optionDirectness: 抓住「先问 DAU 定量级」这一步。
错在词形，「how much」问的是不可数量。
错在跳过，不问规模直接假设。
错在语域，口语提问用公文体。
optionDirectness_en: Nails it: ask DAU first to anchor the scale.
Wrong form — "how much" is for uncountable amounts.
Wrong — skips scale and assumes a number.
Wrong register — a spoken question in bureaucratese.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数：一天内使用产品的独立用户数，衡量规模的常用指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU, daily active users, is the number of unique users who use the product in a day — a common scale metric.

scenario: Convoke 系统设计轮，设计一个视频平台。功能太多，你想先确认该聚焦上传还是播放，上次你想同时铺开上传、转码、推荐、播放，全都浅尝辄止。
scenario_en: In a Convoke system-design round you're designing a video platform. There's a lot, and you want to confirm whether to focus on upload or playback — last time you spread across upload, transcode, recommend, and playback all at once and stayed shallow.
q: 想先确认聚焦哪个核心用例再展开，怎么说？
q_en: How do you confirm which core use case to anchor on before expanding?
options: So upload, transcode, recommend, playback, CDN, so many parts, maybe I touch each a little, or, let me...
Which use case we focus, the upload use case or the play use case, the upload one or the play one, so...
Given the breadth, I shall solicit confirmation as to which core use case merits primary focus.
Given the breadth, should I anchor on the upload-and-transcode path, or on playback first?
tradeoff: 先确认一个核心用例 vs 每块都铺：锁定一个能讲深；全铺开则处处浅，时间不够。
