q: 这个「简单 vs 灵活」的取舍，怎么一句说清并拍板？
q_en: How do you state this "simple vs flexible" tradeoff in one line and commit?
options: The tradeoff was, keeping the implementation simple and make the simple and, make the system flexible enough for future promotion models, so, let me think how to say this...
The tradeoff was simplicity versus flexibility. I leaned toward the simpler design, since we only had two promotion models — I'd revisit it when a third one shows up.

There were certain tradeoffs between simplicity and flexibility that I had to take into consideration in the design.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：一句「X versus Y」+ 拍板 vs 把 simple/flexible 绕成一团、never lands。
why: 把取舍压成一句「simplicity versus flexibility」，再用「I leaned toward… because…」拍板并给触发条件。她的毛病是绕着 simple/flexible 打转、never lands。
why_en: Name the axis in one line — simplicity versus flexibility — then commit with "I leaned toward the simpler one because..." instead of looping on the words.
whenOtherWins: 如果两边都还没数据支撑、面试官只想听你识别出取舍存在，那点出 axis、暂不拍板也可以接受。

scenario: IKEA/ML 面试讲后端 workflow refactor 的取舍。她说成「one trade off is that this refactor takes some time, but the first trade off was the speed of migration versus the production safety」，绕了两圈才点到。
scenario_en: In the IKEA/ML interview she describes a tradeoff in a backend workflow refactor: "one tradeoff is that this refactor takes some time, but the first tradeoff was the speed of migration versus the production safety" — two loops before she lands it.
q: 「迁移速度 vs 生产安全」，怎么用「buys us… but costs us…」说清？
q_en: How do you frame "migration speed vs production safety" with "buys us... but costs us..."?
options: One tradeoff is that this refactor takes some time, but the first tradeoff was, the speed of migration versus the production safety, so, technically we had to rewrite more aggressively...
We rewrote the workflow aggressively so the migration would go as fast as possible and we could ship the refactor sooner.
There was a tradeoff around migration speed and production safety that we needed to be careful about here.
A faster migration buys us an earlier ship date but costs us production safety. On a mature system I chose the slower, safer rollout.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：一句「buys us X but costs us Y」+ 拍板 vs 「the first trade off was… takes some time」绕两圈。
why: 用「A buys us X but costs us Y」把收益和代价一句话摆平，再拍板选安全。她的问题是绕「the first trade off / takes time」，代价说不利落。
why_en: Say "a faster migration buys us an earlier ship but costs us safety," then commit — don't loop on "the first tradeoff was... takes some time."
whenOtherWins: 如果这是一个抛弃型原型、坏了也没影响，那直接选「快」而少谈安全代价也说得过去。

scenario_en: In the Alterion technical interview she's asked how to split the database. She says "I would separate the read pass and the write pass... because it's half acid" — "read pass" for read path, "half acid" for ACID.
q: 「强一致 → 选 SQL」这个取舍，怎么一句说清并拍板？
q_en: How do you state the "strong consistency → SQL" tradeoff in one line and commit?
options: The tradeoff is strong consistency versus write scale. These campaign writes must stay consistent, so I'd lean toward a SQL store like Postgres.

tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「consistency versus write scale」+ 拍板 vs 「read pass / half acid」错词形。
why: 先点名「strong consistency versus write scale」，再因为写必须一致而拍板选 SQL。她的错词形是「read pass」（应为 read path）、「half acid」（应为 ACID）。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次「请求发出去、响应回来」的完整往返；少一个 round trip 就省一段网络延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A round trip is one full request-out, response-back cycle; cutting one saves that slice of network latency.

scenario: Alterion 面试问前后端用 GraphQL 还是 REST。她说「GraphQL make the front end lighter... if we use RESTful API we need to validate the passing parameters if the structure is cracked with back end」，措辞乱、没拍板。
scenario_en: In the Alterion interview she's asked GraphQL or REST for frontend-backend. She says "GraphQL make the front end lighter... if we use RESTful API we need to validate the passing parameters if the structure is cracked with backend" — muddled, no commitment.
q: 该怎么点名 GraphQL vs REST 的取舍并拍板？
q_en: How do you name the GraphQL vs REST tradeoff and commit?
options: The tradeoff is GraphQL versus REST: GraphQL lets the frontend fetch exactly what it needs, but costs more server complexity. For this UI I'd lean GraphQL.
I'd use GraphQL because it makes the frontend lighter and you can fetch everything you need in a single query.
GraphQL make the front end lighter, so, if we use RESTful API then we need to validate the passing parameters, if the structure is, cracked with the backend, and do some conversion.
I'd pick whichever of GraphQL or REST fits the frontend better, it kind of depends on the case.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「GraphQL versus REST」+ 拍板 vs 「the structure is cracked」措辞乱、不落地。
why: 先点名「GraphQL versus REST」，说清 GraphQL 精确取数的好处和服务端更复杂的代价，再拍板。她的问题是措辞乱、never lands。
why_en: Name it — GraphQL versus REST — give GraphQL's precise-fetching upside and its server-complexity cost, then commit.
whenOtherWins: 如果接口简单、只有几个固定资源，REST 更省心；这时 GraphQL 的服务端复杂度就不值得。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种查询语言，前端用一次请求精确取到需要的字段；代价是服务端要维护 schema、解析更复杂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets the frontend fetch exactly the fields it needs in one request, at the cost of more server-side complexity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按资源划分固定端点的接口风格；简单直接，但前端常要多次调用或拿到多余字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST exposes fixed per-resource endpoints — simple, but the frontend often makes several calls or gets extra fields it doesn't need.

scenario: Gamma 面试问 campaign settings（类型、ROI 目标、预算、日期、product 级信息）怎么存。她容易列一堆方案却不拍板，卡在「keeping it simple and flexible」那种打转里。
scenario_en: In the Gamma interview she's asked how to store campaign settings (type, ROI goal, budget, dates, product-level info). She tends to list options without committing, drifting into that "simple and flexible" loop.
q: 面对「关系型还是文档型存储」，怎么避免只罗列、直接拍板说出口？
q_en: For "relational vs document store," how do you avoid just listing and commit out loud?
options: We could use a relational model, or maybe a NoSQL one, honestly there are pros and cons on both sides, so it really depends on a lot of different factors here, I think...
I'd use a relational database because everything is structured and relational, so it just fits.
These settings are structured and queried together, so I'd lean toward a relational store. If the schema starts varying per campaign, I'd switch to a document store.
There are various storage options with different tradeoffs that would need to be evaluated for this use case.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳直译：「I'd lean toward X, if Z changes switch to Y」拍板 vs 列方案却 depends on factors 不选。
why: 先拍板选关系型（因为字段结构化、要一起查），再给翻转条件（schema 按 campaign 变就换文档型）。她的毛病是罗列 pros and cons、never lands。
why_en: Commit to relational because the fields are structured and queried together, then give the switch condition — go document store if the schema starts varying per campaign.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个 campaign 的字段差别很大、schema 频繁变动，那文档型更合适，关系型的固定表结构反而拖累。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把每条记录存成自带结构 JSON 文档的 NoSQL 数据库，schema 可逐条不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document store is a NoSQL database that keeps each record as a self-describing JSON document, so the schema can differ row to row.

scenario: Alterion 面试里，面试官顺着寒暄问：「So, how was working on TikTok?」你想借这句自然切进技术话题。
scenario_en: In the Alterion interview the interviewer segues, "So, how was working on TikTok?" You want to ride it smoothly into technical talk.
q: 怎么从这句寒暄自然过渡到讲你的技术工作？
q_en: How do you bridge from this into your technical work naturally?
options: Honestly it was a great run — mostly ads and campaign backend. Happy to dig into any of it.
How was working on TikTok... yeah, I feel that feels good, we do some production logic, how how to promote the campaign campaigns...

Oh it was really good, I mean there were ups and downs like any job, some great teammates, some tough sprints, I learned so much about myself and about scale and collaboration, honestly I could go on and on...
My tenure at TikTok was satisfactory. I performed backend responsibilities pertaining to advertising campaigns.
tradeoff: 定调后主动递话 vs 复读加卡壳：一句定调加邀请显得从容可控；复读问题再结巴，把跳板浪费成空转。

why_en: A casual "how was it?" is a springboard — give a one-line warm take ("great run, mostly ads and campaign backend"), then offer to go deeper on any of it.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官只想闲聊、还没进技术环节时，才用一句轻松感受带过，不急着切进技术细节。

q_en: How do you say "an API gateway at the edge does auth, routing, and rate-limiting"?

So there's this gateway, and it does the auth, and also the routing, and also the rate limiting, and so on...
We put an API gateway at the edge for auth, routing, and rate-limiting, so services don't each reimplement it.
A centralized API gateway is deployed at the network perimeter to enforce authentication, routing, and rate-limiting concerns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 架在所有服务前的统一入口层,集中做认证、路由、限流等横切工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway is a single entry layer in front of your services that centralizes auth, routing, and rate-limiting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统最外层、靠近客户端的入口位置,请求先到这里再进内部服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The edge is the outermost entry point near the client, where requests land before reaching internal services.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内某个客户端能发的请求数,防止过载或滥用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate-limiting caps how many requests a client can send per unit time, protecting services from overload.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么内部服务间用 gRPC 不用 REST。你想说「gRPC 是走 HTTP/2 的二进制 Protobuf 契约,强类型又快;REST 就是 HTTP 上的 JSON」,但容易说乱。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you use gRPC between internal services instead of REST. You want to say "gRPC is a binary Protobuf contract over HTTP/2, typed and fast, while REST is just JSON over HTTP," but it tends to come out muddled.
q: 「gRPC 是二进制契约、REST 是 JSON over HTTP」该怎么一句说清?
q_en: How do you say "gRPC is a binary contract, REST is JSON over HTTP" in one clean line?
options: gRPC sends a binary Protobuf contract over HTTP/2, so it's typed and fast, where REST is just JSON over HTTP.
gRPC is a binary REST that uses the proto buffer to pass the message faster than the JSON.
So gRPC, it's binary, and REST is JSON, and gRPC is faster, and it uses the proto, and REST uses HTTP, so...
gRPC employs binary serialization over a multiplexed HTTP/2 transport, whereas REST exchanges textual JSON payloads over HTTP.

gRPC is a binary REST that uses the proto buffer to pass the message faster than the JSON.

why: 对比落在契约(gRPC 二进制强类型 vs REST 文本)与传输(HTTP/2 vs 普通 HTTP)两层;别把 gRPC 归成 REST。
why_en: Contrast a binary Protobuf contract over HTTP/2 with plain JSON over HTTP — gRPC isn't a "binary REST."
whenOtherWins: 对外公开、要浏览器直接可调时,REST + JSON 更通用,不必上 gRPC。

termDefinitions.meaning: 谷歌的 RPC 框架,用二进制 Protobuf 定义强类型契约、走 HTTP/2,服务间调用快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's RPC framework using a binary Protobuf contract over HTTP/2 for fast, strongly-typed service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源 URL 操作、通常传 JSON 的接口风格,通用可读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that operates on resource URLs with HTTP verbs, typically carrying human-readable JSON.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种二进制序列化格式,用 .proto 文件定义字段,比 JSON 小且强类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Protobuf is a compact binary serialization format defined by .proto schemas, smaller and more typed than JSON.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 的升级版,单条连接可多路复用并发流,gRPC 就跑在它上面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the HTTP upgrade that multiplexes many streams over one connection; gRPC runs on top of it.

scenario: 面试聊 GraphQL 好处。你想说「客户端按需取字段、不 over-fetch,但天真的 resolver 会撞 N+1,得用 dataloader 批量」,但容易只说「GraphQL 让前端更轻」。
scenario_en: An interview touches on GraphQL's upside. You want to say "the client fetches exactly the fields it needs so no over-fetching, but a naive resolver hits N+1, so you batch with a dataloader," but it tends to shrink to "GraphQL makes the front end lighter."
q: 「按需取字段避免 over-fetch,但要防 N+1」该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say "fetch only what you need, but watch the N+1 problem"?
options: GraphQL lets the front end ask only the fields it needs, so no over-fetch, but it has the N add one problem.
So with GraphQL you ask for just the fields you want, so no over-fetching, but then there's this N plus one thing, right, so...
GraphQL permits field-level selection to eliminate over-fetching, though naive resolver implementations incur the N+1 query problem.
The client picks exactly the fields it needs, but a naive resolver hits N+1 — one query per row — so you batch with a dataloader.
options_en: GraphQL lets the front end ask only the fields it needs, so no over-fetch, but it has the N add one problem.
So with GraphQL you ask for just the fields you want, so no over-fetching, but then there's this N plus one thing, right, so...
GraphQL permits field-level selection to eliminate over-fetching, though naive resolver implementations incur the N+1 query problem.

why: 用「hits N+1 — one query per row — so you batch with a dataloader」点出成因加解法;「N add one problem」既读错又停在问题上。
why_en: Say a naive resolver hits N+1 — one query per row — so you batch with a dataloader; naming the fix proves you know the mechanism.
whenOtherWins: 字段固定、端点简单、团队不熟 GraphQL 时,一个裁剪好的 REST 端点更省事。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种查询语言,客户端声明要哪些字段,一次按需取回,避免 over-fetch。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language where the client declares exactly which fields it wants and gets them in one request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接口返回了比前端实际需要的多得多的字段,浪费带宽和解析。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-fetching is when an endpoint returns far more fields than the client actually needs, wasting bandwidth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为一批数据先查一次列表,再对每行各查一次,导致 1+N 次查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The N+1 problem is one query for a list plus one extra query per row, blowing up into 1+N database hits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一批字段请求攒起来合成一次批量查询,用来消掉 N+1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dataloader batches many per-row field requests into a single query, collapsing the N+1 problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: GraphQL 里负责取某个字段数据的函数;写得天真就会逐行查库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A resolver is the function that fetches data for a GraphQL field; written naively it queries the database row by row.

scenario: 面试问支付回调怎么拿到结果。你想说「不轮询,注册个 webhook,事件一发生对方服务器主动调我们」,但容易把方向说反成「我们去调他们」。
scenario_en: An interview asks how you get the result of a payment callback. You want to say "don't poll — register a webhook so their server calls us when the event fires," but the direction tends to flip into "we call them."
q: 「注册 webhook 让对方主动调我们,而不是轮询」该怎么说?
q_en: How do you say "register a webhook so their server calls us, instead of polling"?
options: We set a web hook so we can call their server to ask if the event happened, instead of polling.
Instead of polling, we register a webhook so their server calls us the moment the event fires.
So instead of polling them over and over, we set up a webhook, so they call us, and we don't keep asking, so...
Rather than periodic polling, a webhook callback is registered so the provider invokes our endpoint on each event occurrence.
options_en: We set a web hook so we can call their server to ask if the event happened, instead of polling.
Instead of polling, we register a webhook so their server calls us the moment the event fires.
So instead of polling them over and over, we set up a webhook, so they call us, and we don't keep asking, so...
Rather than periodic polling, a webhook callback is registered so the provider invokes our endpoint on each event occurrence.
tradeoff: 地道「webhook so their server calls us」vs 卡壳「web hook so we can call their server」:方向反了——webhook 是对方调你,不是你调对方。
why: 用「register a webhook so their server calls us」把方向说对——webhook 是服务端主动回调你,轮询才是你反复去问。
why_en: A webhook means their server calls us when the event fires; polling is us asking over and over — keep the direction right.
whenOtherWins: 若你无法暴露公网端点、或事件极少,定时轮询他们的状态接口反而更简单可靠。
optionMeanings: 「webhook 让我们去调他们」,方向说反了。

反复念「他们调我们、不用一直问」,绕不出。
书面「注册回调,提供方在每次事件调用端点」。

Nails direction: webhook = they call back, replacing polling.
Wrong because it loops; re-explains, no clean line.
Wrong register — callback/endpoint is stiff speech.

termDefinitions.meaning: 你预先注册一个 URL,事件发生时对方服务器主动 POST 调用它,不用你反复问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is a URL you register so the other server actively calls you when an event fires, no repeated asking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 你按固定间隔反复请求对方,问有没有新结果;webhook 反过来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling is you repeatedly asking the other side whether there's a new result; a webhook flips that around.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个可被调用的 URL 地址;webhook 就是让对方来调你暴露的这个地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An endpoint is a callable URL; a webhook has the provider call the endpoint you expose.

scenario: 面试问网络超时后客户端重试会不会出问题。你想说「把 PUT 设计成幂等的,发两次落到同一状态,所以重试安全」,但容易把 idempotent 说成 idempotence 词形错。
scenario_en: An interview asks whether a client retry after a network timeout causes problems. You want to say "make the PUT idempotent — send it twice, same state — so a retry is safe," but idempotent tends to slip into the wrong form "idempotence."
q: 「PUT 幂等,重试安全」这层保证该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say "the PUT is idempotent, so a retry is safe"?
options: We make the PUT idempotence, so if we retry it, it will not create a duplicate.
So the PUT, if you send it again, it's fine, because it's idempotent, so retrying it is totally safe, so...
We make the PUT idempotent — send it twice and you land in the same state — so a retry after a timeout is safe.
The PUT operation is designed to be idempotent, guaranteeing identical resource state across repeated client invocations.
options_en: We make the PUT idempotence, so if we retry it, it will not create a duplicate.
So the PUT, if you send it again, it's fine, because it's idempotent, so retrying it is totally safe, so...
We make the PUT idempotent — send it twice and you land in the same state — so a retry after a timeout is safe.
The PUT operation is designed to be idempotent, guaranteeing identical resource state across repeated client invocations.
tradeoff: 地道「idempotent — send it twice, same state」vs 卡壳「idempotence」:形容词 idempotent 才是这里的词形,且要点出「同一状态」这个机制。
why: 用形容词「idempotent」加「send it twice and you land in the same state」点出机制;idempotence 是名词形、用错了。
why_en: Use the adjective idempotent and say sending it twice lands you in the same state, so a timeout retry is safe.
whenOtherWins: 若是 POST 这类天生非幂等的创建操作,改用幂等键(idempotency key)去重更合适。
optionMeanings: 用了名词形「idempotence」,词形错了。
反复念「再发一次也没事」,绕不出机制。
点出 idempotent + 发两次落同一状态 + 重试安全。
书面「保证跨重复调用状态一致」,定义腔。
optionMeanings_en: Uses the noun "idempotence" — wrong word form.
Loops on "sending it again is fine," no mechanism.
Names idempotent + twice-same-state + safe retry.
Textbook "guaranteeing identical state across invocations."
optionScenarioImpacts: 词形一错,听着像术语没吃透。
一直在打包票,始终没说为什么安全。
机制清楚,面试官立刻放心。

错在打转,反复保证没给机制。
抓住 idempotent:两次落同一状态,重试才安全。
错在语域,状态一致的定义腔生硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong form — the adjective is idempotent, not idempotence.
Wrong because it loops; reassurance, no mechanism.
Nails idempotent: twice, same state, so the retry is safe.
Wrong register — identical-state definition is stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一请求发一次和发多次结果一样、落到同一状态,所以重试是安全的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means one request or many identical ones leave the same state, so retrying is safe.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 里用整份资源覆盖式写入的动词,天生适合做成幂等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PUT is the HTTP verb that overwrites a resource with a full representation, naturally suited to being idempotent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端为一次操作带的唯一键,服务端用它去重,让非幂等操作也可安全重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key is a unique token the client sends so the server dedupes retries of non-idempotent operations.

scenario: 面试问接口要改结构、但老客户端还在用怎么办。你想说「给接口做版本,/v2 和 /v1 并存,改动不打断老客户端」,但容易说成「make the API version」词形怪。
scenario_en: An interview asks how you change an API's shape while old clients still call it. You want to say "version the API — ship /v2 alongside /v1 — so changes don't break existing clients," but it tends to come out as the odd "make the API version."
q: 「给接口做版本、不打断老客户端」该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say "version the API so you don't break existing clients"?
options: We version the API — ship /v2 next to /v1 — so we can change it without breaking existing clients.
We make the API version, so the old client will not break, and we add the version number in the path.
So we add a version, like v1 and v2, and the old clients stay on v1, and the new ones move to v2, so nothing breaks...
The API is versioned via distinct URI prefixes to preserve backward compatibility for all existing consumers.
options_en: We version the API — ship /v2 next to /v1 — so we can change it without breaking existing clients.
We make the API version, so the old client will not break, and we add the version number in the path.
So we add a version, like v1 and v2, and the old clients stay on v1, and the new ones move to v2, so nothing breaks...
The API is versioned via distinct URI prefixes to preserve backward compatibility for all existing consumers.
tradeoff: 地道「version the API, ship /v2 next to /v1」vs 卡壳「make the API version」:动词用 version,并让新老版本并存;「make ... version」是错词形。
why: 把 version 当动词说,让新老版本并行,让老客户端留在旧版继续跑;别把它当名词硬拼成词组。
why_en: Use version as a verb — ship /v2 next to /v1 so existing clients keep working; "make the API version" is the wrong form.
whenOtherWins: 若改动是纯新增字段、向后兼容,直接加字段即可,不必开新版本号。
optionMeanings: 动词 version + /v2 与 /v1 并存,不打断老客户端。
「make the API version」词形怪,把 version 当名词硬拼。
反复念 v1 老的 v2 新的,绕着说没落到动词。
书面「用不同 URI 前缀做版本保后向兼容」,定义腔。
optionMeanings_en: Verb version + /v2 beside /v1, existing clients unbroken.
"Make the API version" — odd form, version bolted on as a noun.
Loops on "v1 old, v2 new," talks around the verb.
Textbook "versioned via distinct URI prefixes" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 动词加并存,面试官听出你做过灰度迁移。

错在词形——version 当动词用,别硬拼成名词。
错在打转,铺陈新老没落到动词。
错在语域,前缀/后向兼容书面腔生硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails version as a verb: /v2 beside /v1, clients unbroken.
Wrong form — use version as a verb, not a bolted-on noun.
Wrong because it loops; old vs new, never the verb.
Wrong register — prefix/compatibility is stiff speech.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给接口分版本(如 /v1、/v2)并存,改动放进新版本,让老客户端继续用旧版。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: API versioning runs versions like /v1 and /v2 side by side so changes land in the new one and old clients keep the old.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新版接口不破坏按旧契约写的老客户端,它们不改代码也能继续工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backward compatibility means a new API version doesn't break clients written against the old contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改了接口结构或语义,导致按旧约定写的客户端调用失败,需靠新版本隔离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A breaking change alters the API shape or semantics so old clients fail, which versioning isolates.

scenario: 面试问服务间怎么互信。你想说「两个服务做 mTLS,双方都出示证书、互相校验,不只是客户端信任服务端」,但容易说成「double TLS」或只说加密。
scenario_en: An interview asks how services trust each other. You want to say "the two services do mutual TLS — each presents a cert and verifies the other, not just the client trusting the server," but it tends to come out as "double TLS" or just "encrypt."
q: 「服务间做 mTLS、双向校验证书」该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say "the services do mTLS, both sides verify certs"?
options: We use a double TLS so both services encrypt and trust each other.
So both services have a certificate, and each one checks the other's cert, so it's like a two-way TLS thing, so...
Mutual TLS is employed whereby both peers present X.509 certificates and perform bidirectional authentication of identity.
They do mutual TLS, so each side presents a cert and verifies the other — not just the client trusting the server.
options_en: We use a double TLS so both services encrypt and trust each other.
So both services have a certificate, and each one checks the other's cert, so it's like a two-way TLS thing, so...
Mutual TLS is employed whereby both peers present X.509 certificates and perform bidirectional authentication of identity.
They do mutual TLS, so each side presents a cert and verifies the other — not just the client trusting the server.
tradeoff: 地道「mutual TLS, each side presents a cert and verifies the other」vs 卡壳「double TLS」:mutual/两向校验是关键;double TLS 是自造词,且没点出双向。
why: 用「mutual TLS」点出两边都出证书并校验对方;普通 TLS 只有客户端验服务端,double TLS 是自造词。
why_en: Say mutual TLS — each side presents a cert and verifies the other, unlike plain TLS where only the client checks the server.
whenOtherWins: 若已在受信内网、或用服务网格 sidecar 托管身份,应用层不必自己处理 mTLS 握手。
optionMeanings: 「double TLS」是自造词,且只说加密没点双向校验。
反复念双方有证书、互查,绕成「two-way TLS thing」。
书面「双方出示 X.509 证书做双向身份认证」,定义腔。
点名 mutual TLS:双方各出示证书并校验对方。

Loops on both having certs, drifts to "two-way TLS thing."

抓住 mutual TLS:双方各出证书、互相校验。

Wrong because it loops; describes, never names it.
Wrong register — X.509/bidirectional auth is stiff.
Nails mutual TLS: both present certs and verify each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双向 TLS:客户端和服务端都出示证书并校验对方,不只是客户端验服务端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mTLS is mutual TLS where both client and server present and verify certificates, not just the client checking the server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加密并认证网络连接的协议,普通模式下只有客户端校验服务端身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS encrypts and authenticates a connection; by default only the client verifies the server's identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由可信 CA 签发、证明一个服务身份的凭证;mTLS 里双方都要出示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A certificate is a CA-signed credential proving a service's identity; in mTLS both sides present one.

scenario: 面试问缓存 miss 时同一个热点键被同时打穿怎么办。你想说「把相同的在途请求合并,第二个调用者等第一个的结果,不再打后端」,但容易只说「去重」讲不清机制。
scenario_en: An interview asks what happens when a hot key misses cache and many requests hit it at once. You want to say "coalesce identical in-flight requests — the second caller waits on the first instead of hitting the backend," but it tends to shrink to a vague "we dedupe it."
q: 「合并相同的在途请求、第二个等第一个」该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say "coalesce identical in-flight requests so the rest wait on the first"?
options: We do a request merge, so the same request will not call twice, we just dedupe it.
We coalesce identical in-flight requests — a second caller waits on the first instead of re-hitting the backend.
So if the same request is already going, we don't send it again, we just wait on the first one, so it dedupes, so...
Concurrent identical requests are collapsed via a single-flight mechanism to prevent redundant backend invocations entirely.
options_en: We do a request merge, so the same request will not call twice, we just dedupe it.
We coalesce identical in-flight requests — a second caller waits on the first instead of re-hitting the backend.
So if the same request is already going, we don't send it again, we just wait on the first one, so it dedupes, so...
Concurrent identical requests are collapsed via a single-flight mechanism to prevent redundant backend invocations entirely.
tradeoff: 地道「coalesce in-flight requests, second caller waits on the first」vs 卡壳「request merge / dedupe」:coalesce 加「等第一个」点出机制;「merge/dedupe」太笼统。
why: 用 coalesce 点出把相同在途请求合成一次、其余等它的结果;笼统的「合并/去重」说不清谁等谁。
why_en: Say we coalesce identical in-flight requests so the second caller waits on the first — vague "merge/dedupe" misses the mechanism.
whenOtherWins: 若请求不贵、或结果因人而异不可共享,合并收益不大,各自查更简单。
optionMeanings: 「request merge / dedupe」笼统,没说谁等谁。
点名 coalesce 在途请求:第二个等第一个,不再打后端。
反复念「已经在跑就等第一个」,绕成 dedupe 收尾。
书面「用 single-flight 合并并发相同请求」,定义腔。

机制清楚,面试官立刻懂缓存击穿的解法。
一直在铺陈,始终没给专有说法。
像念论文,口语场合显生硬。

Mechanism is clear; the cache-stampede fix lands.
You keep setting it up; no precise term surfaces.
Reads like a paper — stiff out loud.
optionDirectness: 错在笼统——merge/dedupe 没说清谁等谁。
抓住 coalesce:相同在途请求里第二个等第一个。
错在打转,绕半天才收到 dedupe。
错在语域,single-flight 定义腔生硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong because vague — merge/dedupe skips who waits on whom.
Nails coalesce: among identical in-flight calls, second waits.
Wrong because it loops; drifts before reaching dedupe.
Wrong register — single-flight definition is stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一时刻对同一键的多个请求合成一个,只打一次后端,其余等这个结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request coalescing merges many concurrent requests for the same key into one backend call; the rest wait on its result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指请求已经发出、还没拿到响应的这段时间;此时来的相同请求可被合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-flight describes a request already sent but not yet answered; identical requests arriving then can be merged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种模式:同一键同一时刻只允许一个真正的调用在飞,其余复用它的结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-flight is a pattern that allows only one real call per key at a time and shares its result with the rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热点键一失效,大量请求同时打穿到后端,合并/single-flight 就是为防它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede is many requests hitting the backend at once when a hot key expires; coalescing prevents it.

scenario: IKEA ML 面试，你想说你把前端从两次 API 调用优化成一次、省了约一秒；上次你说成「I decoupled the API, one call rather than two」，绕且用词不准。
scenario_en: In an IKEA ML interview you want to say you cut the front end from two API calls down to one, saving about a second; last time it came out as "I decoupled the API, one call rather than two."
q: 「合并调用、省一次往返」这个优化，该怎么一句说清？
q_en: How do you say the "merge the calls, save a round trip" optimization in one clean line?
options: I decoupled the API, so on the front end we only need one call rather than the previous two, so it saves about one second.
We collapse the two calls into a single round trip, so the page loads with one request instead of two.
So we call the API twice — once when the page loads, then the user changes a bit, then we call it again...
The quantity of API invocations was reduced from two to one, thereby decreasing aggregate page latency.
options_en: I decoupled the API, so on the front end we only need one call rather than the previous two, so it saves about one second.
We collapse the two calls into a single round trip, so the page loads with one request instead of two.
So we call the API twice — once when the page loads, then the user changes a bit, then we call it again...
The quantity of API invocations was reduced from two to one, thereby decreasing aggregate page latency.
tradeoff: 地道「one round trip」vs 卡壳直译：round trip 一词点出省的是网络往返；「decouple / one call rather than two」绕半天没说到机制。
why: 用「collapse the two calls into one round trip」点名机制——省的是一次网络往返，不是「decouple API」；动词落到 round trip 或 request 上。
why_en: Say we collapse the two calls into one round trip — the win is cutting a network round trip, not decoupling the API.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官只想听结论、不深究机制，直接说「we cut it to one request」也够，不必展开 round trip。
optionMeanings: 「decoupled，一次不是两次」，绕着说省一秒。
「合并成一次 round trip」，点出省的是往返。

A content delivery network geographically distributes cached assets to edge nodes proximate to end users.

scenario: 系统设计问缓存写路径怎么保证不丢数据。你想讲清 write-through 同步写库、write-back 先写缓存异步刷库的区别,上轮却卡成 “write to cache first, then… later”。
scenario_en: A round asks how the cache write path avoids data loss. You want to contrast write-through (sync to DB) with write-back (cache first, async flush), but last time you stalled at "write to cache first, then... later."
q: 「write-through 同步写缓存和库、write-back 先写缓存再异步刷库」这组区别怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you contrast write-through (cache+DB together) with write-back (cache now, flush to DB later)?
options: Write-through writes cache and DB together; write-back writes the cache and flushes to the DB later — fast, but a crash loses buffered writes.
Write-pass saves to the cache and the database at the same time, and write-behind save to the cache, database after.
So write-through is is write to both, and write-back is is later, later to the DB, faster but you can lose...
Write-through propagates each write synchronously to both the cache and the durable backing store, whereas write-back defers persistence to the database asynchronously.
tradeoff: write-through/write-back 术语 + 崩溃丢写的机制 vs “write-pass” 错词或打转:前者点名同步 vs 异步的取舍,后者暴露不熟。
why: write-through 同步写缓存和库更安全;write-back 先写缓存异步刷库更快,但崩溃会丢没刷回的写。术语别说成 write-pass。
why_en: Say write-through (sync to cache and DB) vs write-back (cache now, async flush) — the tell is write-back can lose buffered writes on a crash.
whenOtherWins: 若写很少、丢一点也无所谓,直接 write-through 最省心;write-back 的异步刷库复杂度不值当。
options_en: Write-through writes cache and DB together; write-back writes the cache and flushes to the DB later — fast, but a crash loses buffered writes.
Write-pass saves to the cache and the database at the same time, and write-behind save to the cache, database after.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写穿透:写操作同步写入缓存和数据库,保证一致但写更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through writes to both the cache and the database synchronously — consistent but slower writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写回:先只写缓存,稍后异步批量刷回数据库,更快但崩溃可能丢未刷的写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-back (write-behind) writes only the cache first and flushes to the DB asynchronously later — faster, but a crash can lose un-flushed writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓冲写:已写进缓存但还没刷回数据库的那批写,崩溃时会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Buffered writes are writes sitting in the cache that haven't been flushed to the DB yet — lost if the process crashes.

scenario: 内存满了要淘汰缓存条目,面试官问你用什么策略。你想区分 LRU 按最久未用、LFU 按访问次数最少来淘汰,上轮却把 LRU 说成 “throw the last used one”。
scenario_en: Memory is full and the interviewer asks your eviction policy. You want to separate LRU (least-recently-used) from LFU (least-frequently-used), but last time you said LRU "throws the last used one."
q: 「LRU 淘汰最久没被访问的,LFU 淘汰访问次数最少的」这组区别怎么说清?
q_en: How do you distinguish LRU (evict least-recently-used) from LFU (evict least-frequently-used)?
options: LRU throws out the last-used one, and LFU throws out the less-frequent one, by the count.
LRU evicts whatever hasn't been touched in the longest time; LFU evicts whatever's been hit the fewest times.
So LRU is is by time, by recency, and LFU is by, by how many times, how many times it's...
LRU evicts the entry bearing the oldest access timestamp, whereas LFU evicts the entry exhibiting the lowest cumulative access frequency.
tradeoff: LRU/LFU + recency vs frequency 的机制 vs “last-used” 说反:前者点名按什么淘汰,后者把最近用的当成要踢的。
why: LRU 按 recency(最久未用)淘汰,LFU 按 frequency(访问次数最少)淘汰;把 LRU 说成 “last-used” 正好说反了。
why_en: LRU evicts by recency (least recently used), LFU by frequency (fewest hits) — "last-used" is exactly backwards.
whenOtherWins: 若访问模式突变、旧热点该快速让位,LRU 更灵敏;LFU 会被历史高频卡住,这时别用 LFU。

We put some cache in Redis, so like when we query it's faster, something like that.
So we we look in the cache, and if it's not there, not there, we go to the, to the database, and then we put it back...
Upon a cache miss the system retrieves the record from the database and subsequently repopulates the cache.
tradeoff: 用 hit / miss / populate 三个术语讲完 cache-aside vs “put some cache in Redis” 含糊带过：前者证明你懂回源与写回，后者只报了个存储名。
why: 关键是 cache hit / cache miss 加“回源查库再写回”：一句话把命中返回和 miss 回源都讲了，这才是 cache-aside。
why_en: Say cache hit and cache miss plus "fall back to the DB and populate the cache" — that one line is the whole cache-aside read path.
whenOtherWins: 对方已在聊命中率细节时，可直接跳到 "our hit rate is around 95%"，不必从头讲 cache-aside 流程。
options_en: We check the cache first; on a miss we fall back to the DB and populate the cache.

So we we look in the cache, and if it's not there, not there, we go to the, to the database, and then we put it back...
Upon a cache miss the system retrieves the record from the database and subsequently repopulates the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要的数据在缓存里叫命中(hit)，不在、得回源查库叫未命中(miss)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache hit is when the data is already in the cache; a cache miss is when it isn't and you go to the source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，miss 时自己回源查库再把结果写回缓存的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the app checks the cache, and on a miss it reads the DB and writes the result back into the cache itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把回源查到的数据写进缓存，下次好命中；也说 warm the cache。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To populate the cache is to write the fetched data into it so the next read hits; also called warming the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存命中率：命中次数占总请求的比例，衡量缓存效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is the share of requests served from cache — the main measure of how well the cache is working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库，缓存 miss 时回源查的权威数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DB is the database — the source of truth you fall back to on a cache miss.

scenario: Alterion 追问：缓存怎么保证不返回过期数据？你想说「给缓存设个过期时间，到点自动失效」，但一时想不起 TTL 这个词，差点绕着描述。
scenario_en: The Alterion interviewer asks how the cache avoids serving stale data. You want to say "set an expiry so entries drop on their own," but the word TTL slips and you nearly describe around it.
q: 「给缓存设 TTL，到期自动失效，避免返回脏数据」这一句怎么地道说？
q_en: How do you say "set a TTL so the entry expires and we don't serve stale data"?
options: We set a time, so the data will be out of date after a while, and then it gets deleted.
So we we give it a time, a time limit, and when the time, when the time is up, it's not valid...
A time-to-live parameter is configured such that the cached entry is invalidated upon expiration.
We set a short TTL so the entry expires on its own, so we don't serve stale data.
tradeoff: TTL / expire / stale 术语 vs “set a time... out of date” 绕着说：前者点名机制并说清它防的问题，后者听着像不熟缓存术语。
why: 术语是 TTL（time to live）+ 动词 expire + “serve stale data”——一句话既交代到期失效，又点出它防的是返回脏数据。
why_en: It's TTL plus "expires" plus "serve stale data" — one line gives both the expiry and the problem it prevents.
codeSample:
# Redis: cache the value with a 60-second TTL
SET user:42 "{...}" EX 60
# EX 60 = expire after 60s; the key drops itself, no stale read
TTL user:42   # -> seconds left before it expires
whenOtherWins: 若一致性要求很高、必须写时主动失效而不是等到期，就该说 "we invalidate the key on write"，靠 TTL 兜底不够。
options_en: We set a time, so the data will be out of date after a while, and then it gets deleted.
So we we give it a time, a time limit, and when the time, when the time is up, it's not valid...
A time-to-live parameter is configured such that the cached entry is invalidated upon expiration.
We set a short TTL so the entry expires on its own, so we don't serve stale data.

反复 “we we / when the time” 打转，句子散了。
用 “configured such that / upon” 的书面腔念定义。
TTL 到期自动 expire，避免返回 stale 数据。

错在打转，到期语义被口水句盖掉。
错在语域，口语里书面体听着僵。

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活时间：给缓存条目设的过期时长，到点自动失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL, Time To Live, is the lifespan you set on a cache entry — it expires automatically when the time is up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经过期、和源数据不一致的旧数据；返回它叫 serve stale data。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stale data is cached data that's out of date versus the source; returning it is called serving stale data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动把缓存条目标记失效（通常写时触发），区别于等 TTL 到期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To invalidate is to actively mark a cache entry dead — usually on a write — as opposed to waiting for TTL expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存满时按最久未用踢掉条目，叫 evict；和到期 expire 是两回事。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction drops entries when memory is full — LRU throws out the least recently used — which is different from TTL expiry.

scenario: 系统设计里聊到某个明星用户的 key 被疯狂读，压垮了一台节点。你想描述这个「热点 key」问题和「复制到多节点分摊」的解法，但没找到 hot key 这个词。
scenario_en: Mid system-design, one celebrity's key is getting hammered and it's overloading a single node. You want to name the hot-key problem and the replicate-across-nodes fix, but the term hot key won't come.
q: 「单个热点 key 打爆一台分片，得复制到多个节点分摊读」这一句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "one hot key overloads a single shard, so we replicate it across nodes to spread the read load"?
options: There is like a very popular key, and it's queried a lot, so one machine gets, gets very busy.
One hot key hammers a single shard, so we replicate it across a few nodes to spread the load.
So so this key, this one key, it's read so many, so many times, and the one node, it kind of can't handle...
A single frequently-accessed key induces excessive load upon one shard, necessitating replication.
tradeoff: hot key / shard / replicate 术语 vs “one machine gets busy” 白描：前者证明你懂分片被热点拖累的机制，后者听不出问题在哪。
why: 术语是 hot key + “hammers a single shard” + “replicate across nodes”——一句话点出热点打爆单分片，以及靠复制分摊读的解法。
why_en: It's hot key plus "hammers a single shard" plus "replicate across nodes" — that names the problem and the fix in one breath.
whenOtherWins: 若热点是写而不是读，复制副本救不了热点写；那时该说 "we shard the key itself" 或加本地缓存/合并写。
options_en: There is like a very popular key, and it's queried a lot, so one machine gets, gets very busy.
One hot key hammers a single shard, so we replicate it across a few nodes to spread the load.
So so this key, this one key, it's read so many, so many times, and the one node, it kind of can't handle...
A single frequently-accessed key induces excessive load upon one shard, necessitating replication.

hot key 打爆单分片，复制到多节点分摊读。

用 “induces / necessitating” 的书面腔念定义。

They see you know the hot key kills one shard and the fix.
They stall in the filler and never hear a solution.

抓住 hot key/shard/replicate 的机制落点。
错在打转，分摊解法被口水句盖掉。
错在语域，口语里书面体听着僵。

Nails hot key/shard/replicate as the mechanism and fix.
Wrong because looping buries the spread-the-load fix.
Wrong register — written style is stiff spoken.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被访问量远高于其他 key 的热点键，容易把它所在的单个节点/分片压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is one key getting far more traffic than the rest, enough to overload the single node or shard that holds it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据水平切分后的一个分片；每个 key 通常只落在一个分片上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is one horizontal partition of the data; a given key usually lives on just one shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一个热点 key 复制到多个节点，让读请求分摊到副本上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To replicate is to copy the same hot key onto several nodes so reads spread across the copies.

scenario: 系统设计面追问并发:两个后台任务各拿了一把锁,又都在等对方那把,整个流程卡死。面试官问怎么回事、怎么修。她想说这是死锁、靠统一加锁顺序解决,却卡在词上。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: two background tasks each hold one lock and wait on the other, so everything hangs. She wants to say it's a deadlock fixed by a consistent lock ordering, but stalls on the term.
q: 想说「这是死锁——两个线程各拿一把锁又互等,我们靠统一加锁顺序解决」,该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say 'it's a deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other, so we impose a lock ordering'?
options: It's a dead-lock, the two threads lock each other, so we give them a lock order to not lock.
It's a deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other. We fixed it by always acquiring the locks in the same order.
So so the two threads, they they each hold a lock and, and wait for the other one, and it just, it just hangs.
A deadlock manifests when threads acquire locks in incompatible orders; enforcing a canonical global acquisition order eliminates the cyclic wait.
tradeoff: 地道 deadlock + lock ordering vs 卡壳:前者一句点出环等和修法;'they lock each other' 听不出你懂机制。
why: 术语是 deadlock:各持一锁、互相等待成环;修法说 acquire the locks in the same order,点出统一顺序才算懂机制。
why_en: Name the deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other — then fix it by acquiring the locks in one consistent order.
whenOtherWins: 如果全程只有一把锁,就没有死锁问题,直接说 'a single lock, no ordering needed' 即可。
options_en: It's a dead-lock, the two threads lock each other, so we give them a lock order to not lock.
It's a deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other. We fixed it by always acquiring the locks in the same order.
So so the two threads, they they each hold a lock and, and wait for the other one, and it just, it just hangs.
A deadlock manifests when threads acquire locks in incompatible orders; enforcing a canonical global acquisition order eliminates the cyclic wait.

反复 they、wait,绕在描述里落不到词。
教科书腔:念 cyclic wait、canonical order。

termDefinitions.meaning: 死锁:两个或多个线程各自持有对方需要的锁,谁都不肯放手,于是永远互相等待、谁也走不下去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when two or more threads each hold a lock the other needs and neither releases, so both wait forever.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加锁顺序:规定所有线程都按同一个固定顺序去获取多把锁,从而打破环形等待、避免死锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock ordering means all threads acquire multiple locks in the same fixed order, which breaks the cycle and prevents deadlock.

scenario: 并发追问:一个计数器被多线程更新,面试官不想用锁,问怎么无锁地安全更新。她想说用 CAS——读旧值、只在没被改过时写入、否则重试,却说不利落。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: a counter is updated by many threads and the interviewer wants no lock — how do you update it safely? She wants to say CAS: read, swap in only if unchanged, else retry, but it comes out clumsy.
q: 想说「用 compare-and-swap 无锁更新——只在值没变时写入,变了就重试」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'a compare-and-swap for a lock-free update — write only if the value hasn't changed, retry if it has'?
options: We use a compare-swap, we compare the value and change it without lock.
So so instead of a lock we we read it and then, then write it back, and if if someone changed it we try again.
We use a compare-and-swap — read the value, swap the new one in only if it hasn't changed, and retry if it has.
The update employs an atomic compare-and-swap primitive that commits only when the observed value matches the expected value, retrying under contention.
tradeoff: 地道 CAS + 条件重试 vs 卡壳:前者点出无锁机制;'compare-swap, change without lock' 听不出你懂重试。
why: 术语是 CAS(compare-and-swap):只在值没被改过时写入、否则重试——点出这个条件重试才算懂无锁。
why_en: Say compare-and-swap — write only if the value is unchanged, and retry on failure; the retry loop is what proves it's lock-free.
whenOtherWins: 如果争用很高、重试太多,退回锁或原子指令更稳,可说 'under heavy contention we'd just lock'。
options_en: We use a compare-swap, we compare the value and change it without lock.
So so instead of a lock we we read it and then, then write it back, and if if someone changed it we try again.
We use a compare-and-swap — read the value, swap the new one in only if it hasn't changed, and retry if it has.
The update employs an atomic compare-and-swap primitive that commits only when the observed value matches the expected value, retrying under contention.

教科书腔:念 primitive、observed value。

对方等 CAS 那个词,你却一直绕。

太书面像背的,显不出你写过无锁。

They wait for 'CAS' while you circle the description.
One line names lock-free and the retry; they nod.

termDefinitions.meaning: 比较并交换(CAS):一条原子指令,先检查内存里的值是否等于预期值,相等才写入新值,不等就失败、由调用方重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-swap (CAS) atomically checks whether a value equals the expected one and writes the new value only if it does, else it fails and you retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无锁:多个线程不用互斥锁也能安全更新共享数据,通常靠 CAS 这类原子指令加失败重试来实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock-free means threads update shared data safely without a mutex, typically via atomic ops like CAS plus a retry on failure.

scenario: 并发追问:服务会瞬间开几百个线程去调下游,把下游打挂。面试官问怎么限制同时并发数。她想说用信号量把并发上限卡在 N,却卡词。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: the service spawns hundreds of threads hitting a downstream and overwhelms it. How do you cap concurrent access? She wants to say a semaphore caps it at N, but stalls.
q: 想说「用一个带 N 个许可的信号量,最多只放 N 个线程同时进」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'a semaphore with N permits, so at most N threads run concurrently'?
options: We put a semaphore with ten permits in front of it, so at most ten threads hit the downstream at once.
We use a semaphore counter to limit how many thread can go in at the same time.
So so we we want to hold them back, so not too many, not too many threads go in at, at once, you know.
A counting semaphore initialized to ten bounds the number of threads permitted to enter the critical section concurrently.
tradeoff: 地道 semaphore + N permits vs 卡壳:前者点出许可上限;'semaphore counter to limit' 听不出你懂机制。
why: 术语是 semaphore:点出「N 个 permits、最多 N 个同时进」——许可数量才证明你懂它怎么限并发。
why_en: Say a semaphore with N permits, so at most N threads enter at once; naming the permit count proves you know how it caps concurrency.
whenOtherWins: 如果要跨进程、跨机器限流,单机信号量不够,得用分布式限流,可说 'a distributed rate limiter instead'。
options_en: We put a semaphore with ten permits in front of it, so at most ten threads hit the downstream at once.
We use a semaphore counter to limit how many thread can go in at the same time.
So so we we want to hold them back, so not too many, not too many threads go in at, at once, you know.
A counting semaphore initialized to ten bounds the number of threads permitted to enter the critical section concurrently.
optionMeanings: 地道:信号量+10 个许可+最多 10 个同时进。
词形错:semaphore counter,漏了许可概念。
反复 not too many,绕着说没落到词。

Chinglish 'semaphore counter'; loses the permit idea.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a counter with a fixed number of permits; a thread takes one to enter and returns it on exit, and when permits run out, others wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 许可:信号量里可被占用的名额;有 N 个许可就意味着最多允许 N 个线程同时进入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A permit is a slot in the semaphore; N permits means at most N threads may be inside at the same time.

q_en: How do you say 'size the pool to the workload — too few starve, too many thrash on context switches'?
options: We set the thread pool size, if too small the thread is not enough, if too big the CPU is busy switching.
So so the number of threads, if it's, if it's too low then things wait, and too high then it, it gets slow somehow.
The thread pool must be sized to the workload; insufficient parallelism starves throughput whereas excessive parallelism induces context-switch overhead.
We size the pool to the workload — too few threads and requests starve, too many and they thrash on context switches.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thrashing is when there are so many threads that the CPU spends most of its time switching between them instead of doing real work.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A context switch is the CPU's cost of saving one thread's state and restoring another's; more threads means more frequent switches.

q_en: How do you say 'a read-write lock — many readers together, but a writer takes it exclusively'?
options: We use a read-write lock, many read can go together and the write must be alone.
We use a read-write lock — any number of readers can hold it together, but a writer takes it exclusively.
So so it's a lock but for for reads it's shared, and then for, for writes only one, only one can go.
A read-write lock permits concurrent shared acquisition by multiple readers while mandating exclusive acquisition for any writer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读写锁:允许多个读线程同时持有(共享锁),但写线程必须独占(排他锁),适合读远多于写的场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-write lock lets many readers hold it at once (shared mode) but requires a writer to hold it alone (exclusive mode), ideal for read-heavy loads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独占/排他:写线程拿锁时,其它任何读或写线程都必须等待,保证写的时候没人在读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exclusive means that while a writer holds the lock, every other reader and writer must wait, so nobody reads mid-write.

We drop the lock and use an atomic counter — the increment is a single atomic op, so threads can't interleave.
Rather than guarding the counter with a mutex, we utilize an atomic fetch-and-add instruction that guarantees indivisible increments.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic counter's increment or decrement is a single indivisible hardware op, so concurrent threads don't corrupt it and no lock is needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交错:两个线程的操作步骤穿插着执行;原子操作能保证中间不会被别的线程插进来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To interleave is for two threads' steps to run intermixed; an atomic op guarantees no other thread slips in partway through.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取值并加:一条原子指令,读出当前值的同时把它加上给定量,常用来实现无锁自增。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fetch-and-add is one atomic instruction that reads the current value and adds to it in the same step, often used for lock-free increments.

scenario: 并发追问:一堆共享状态被多线程改得很乱、锁也满天飞。面试官问有没有干脆不用锁的设计。她想说把状态限制在单线程、让一个 actor 独占它、全走消息,却卡词。

We use actor model, the actor keep the state itself, so other thread cannot touch it and no need lock.
So so only one, only one thread owns the state, and others just, just send messages, so we we don't lock.
State mutation is confined to a single thread of control; the owning actor serializes all access through message passing, thereby obviating locks entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程封闭:把某份状态限制在单个线程里访问,别的线程碰不到,因此天然没有并发冲突、不需要加锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thread confinement keeps a piece of state accessible from only one thread, so no other thread can touch it and no lock is required.

termDefinitions.meaning: actor:一个独占自己私有状态的并发单元,外界只能给它发消息、由它自己串行处理,从而避免共享可变状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An actor is a concurrency unit that owns its private state; others only send it messages, which it processes one at a time, so state is never shared.

termDefinitions.meaning: 邮箱:actor 的消息队列;所有发给它的请求先进邮箱排队,再被它逐条处理,保证一次只处理一条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mailbox is an actor's message queue; requests to it queue up there and it handles them one by one, so only one is processed at a time.

scenario: Alterion 技术面,面试官问一个计数器被很多线程同时更新,为什么会突然变慢。她想说「锁被抢得很凶,线程只能排队,吞吐就掉下来了」,却只憋出「too many people use it at the same time」。

q: 想说「锁竞争激烈,线程只能排队执行,吞吐量就掉下来了」,该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say 'the lock is contended, so threads serialize and throughput tanks'?
options: Too many people use it at the same time, so it get very slow because they wait wait for their turn.
So so the lock, the lock is like, a lot of threads want it, want it, and they they wait and wait and it's slow.
The lock is contended, so threads serialize and throughput tanks.
Elevated contention on the synchronization primitive compels threads to execute sequentially, thereby diminishing throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 锁竞争:多个线程同时想拿同一把锁,拿不到的只能排队等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock contention is when multiple threads want the same lock at once, and the losers have to wait in line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本来能并发的操作,因为都在等同一把锁,被迫变成一个接一个顺序执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To serialize is to force operations that could run concurrently into one-at-a-time execution because they're waiting on the same lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统单位时间内能处理完成的请求数量;锁竞争严重时会明显下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is how many requests the system completes per unit time; heavy contention drags it down.

scenario: 系统设计追问并发:两个请求同时给同一个余额加钱。她想指出这里有竞态,却只憋出「两个东西同时发生就乱了」,说不出那个词。
scenario_en: A system-design follow-up: two requests add to the same balance at once. She wants to flag a race condition but only gets out 'two things happen at once and it breaks,' missing the term.
q: 想说「检查和写入之间有竞态,两个请求都读到旧值再各自写」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'there's a race between the check and the write — both read the old value, then both write'?
options: There's a race between the check and the write — both requests read the old value, then both update.
Two things happen at the same time and it kind of messes up the data.
So when the, when two requests come in in parallel, they they sort of step on each other and the number gets, gets wrong somehow.
A concurrency anomaly arises due to simultaneous access to the shared counter.
tradeoff: 术语 race + check/write vs 泛泛描述:「a race between the check and the write」点名机制;「同时就乱了」听不出你懂在哪。
why: 说 race condition 并点到「check 和 write 之间」——两个请求都读到旧值再各自写。定位到冲突窗口,才证明你懂机制而非只知词。
why_en: Name the race condition and pin it to the check-then-write window where both read the old value.
whenOtherWins: 只有对非技术听众解释时,「two updates collide」这种大白话反而更好懂。
options_en: There's a race between the check and the write — both requests read the old value, then both update.
Two things happen at the same time and it kind of messes up the data.
So when the, when two requests come in in parallel, they they sort of step on each other and the number gets, gets wrong somehow.
A concurrency anomaly arises due to simultaneous access to the shared counter.

q_en: How do you say 'use optimistic locking — bump a version and reject the write if the version doesn't match'?
options: I would just add a lock so that two writes don't, don't happen together on the row.
So we we can maybe have some kind of, of versioning thing where if the version is, is not the same we don't let it write.
Employ an optimistic concurrency-control mechanism utilizing version-based conflict detection.
Use optimistic locking — bump a version number and reject the write if the version is stale.

So we we can maybe have some kind of, of versioning thing where if the version is, is not the same we don't let it write.
Employ an optimistic concurrency-control mechanism utilizing version-based conflict detection.
Use optimistic locking — bump a version number and reject the write if the version is stale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 悲观锁:先锁住行再改,阻塞其他写;吞吐低但冲突多时更简单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pessimistic locking takes a row lock before writing, blocking other writers — lower throughput but simpler when conflicts are frequent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 行上的一个计数器,每次写自增;写入时版本对不上说明有人先改了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version number is a counter on the row that increments each write; a mismatch at write time means someone updated it first.

options: We make it so that if the retry happens, it doesn't do the thing twice by accident.
Make the write idempotent with an idempotency key so a retry or double-submit is a no-op.
So so we want to make sure that when the same request comes, comes again, we don't charge them, charge them twice.
The endpoint shall guarantee idempotence such that duplicate invocations produce identical state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集群当前有哪些活着的节点这份名单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Membership is the current list of live nodes in the cluster.

q_en: How do you say "across services, skip 2PC and use a saga with compensation"?
options: we do a two phase submit, or we can do a saga, so it commits in two phase and then submit, the phases...
so instead of doing the big lock thing across all of them, we let each one do its own part, and if one fails we undo the earlier ones, undo them one by one, yeah...
Across services I'd use a saga over two-phase commit — each step commits locally, with a compensating action to undo on failure.
Rather than a two-phase commit, a saga executes local transactions with compensating transactions to preserve consistency.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A compensating action is a reverse operation that undoes a committed local step, e.g. a refund for a charge.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「网络分区时你保一致还是保可用」。你想说 CAP 里二选一，却说成 CAP theory、choose two of three，没落到 CP/AP。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked, during a partition, whether you keep consistency or availability. You mean the CAP choice but say "CAP theory" and "choose two of three," never landing on CP/AP.
q: 「分区时 CAP 逼你在一致和可用里二选一」怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "under a partition CAP forces a choice between consistency and availability"?
options: Under a partition CAP forces a choice — go CP and reject writes, or go AP and serve maybe-stale data.
by the CAP theory we choose two of the three, so we pick the C and the A, or the P, two of three...
so when the network splits, you can't have both, you have to give up one, either the consistent one or the up one, you pick one, yeah...
The CAP theorem stipulates that under a partition a system must forfeit either consistency or availability.
tradeoff: 地道落点 vs 口号复述：CP/AP 加各自代价点名取舍；choose two of three 是常见误读，没落到分区下的真选择。
why: CAP 只在 partition 下二选一，不是「三选二」；要落到 CP 拒写保一致、AP 可用但可能读到旧值。
why_en: Under a partition CAP forces a choice — go CP and reject writes, or go AP and serve maybe-stale data.
whenOtherWins: 只有科普 CAP 由来时才提三个字母；正式答要落到分区下 CP 还是 AP。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP says that during a network partition a distributed system can keep either strong consistency or high availability, not both.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区时选一致：宁可拒绝请求也不返回不一致的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CP means choosing consistency in a partition: reject requests rather than return inconsistent data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区时选可用：继续响应，但可能返回旧数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AP means choosing availability in a partition: keep responding, but the data may be stale.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「怎么知道一个节点还活着」。你想说靠心跳和租约，却说成 send heart beat、alive signal，还卡在 kick it out。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how you know a node is still alive. You mean heartbeats and a lease but say "send heart beat" and "alive signal," and stall on "kick it out."
q: 「节点靠心跳续租约，漏跳就被剔除」这句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "a node holds its lease via heartbeats; miss them and it's evicted"?
options: each node sends a heart beat, like an alive signal, and if no signal we kick it out, the beat shows it's alive...
so every node keeps sending a little ping, like i'm here, i'm here, and if it stops for a while then we take it out of the group, yeah...
Each node periodically emits a heartbeat to renew its lease; upon expiry the node is deemed failed and removed.
Each node sends a heartbeat to hold its lease — miss a few and the cluster marks it dead and evicts it.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 拆词口水：heartbeat 加 lease、evict 点名机制；heart beat 拆开了，alive signal、kick out 太口水。
why: 术语是 heartbeat，一个词，别拆成 heart beat，再加 lease；点明漏跳到租约过期到被 evict，才说清存活检测。
why_en: Each node sends a heartbeat to hold its lease — miss a few and the cluster marks it dead and evicts it.
whenOtherWins: 只有对非技术的人打比方才说 keeps pinging i'm here；正式面试要 heartbeat、lease、evict。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段有时限的存活授权，靠心跳续期，过期就被判失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lease is a time-bounded liveness grant renewed by heartbeats; when it expires the node is treated as failed.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: To evict is to remove an unresponsive node from the cluster's membership.

scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked what to do when one node runs hot. You mean rebalancing to move partitions off it but say "re-balance the load" and "move the data around."
q: 「节点热了就 rebalance，把部分分片挪走匀负载」怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "when a node runs hot, rebalance by moving some partitions off it"?
options: we re-balance the load, so we move the data around to make it even, the load gets balanced, move it around...
When a node runs hot we rebalance — move some of its partitions elsewhere to even out the load.
so this one machine has too much on it, so we take some of its stuff and put it on the others, spread it out a bit, yeah...
When a node becomes hot, partitions are redistributed across the cluster to equalize load and preserve data locality.

why_en: When a node runs hot we rebalance — move some partitions off it to even out the load without wrecking data locality.

scenario: Alterion 技术面，面试官问「读多的数据库怎么扩」。你想说读写分离，却说成 separate the read pass and the write pass，还卡在 we want to consistency。

q_en: How does an engineer actually say "read/write separation" out loud?
options: I would separate the read pass and the write pass, so, so if we want it to be consistent...
so we send the reads to one place and the writes to another place, the read one is kind of a copy...
I'd split the read path from the write path — reads hit a replica, writes go to the primary.
The system shall segregate read operations from write operations across separate database nodes.

why_en: It's the read path and the write path — reads hit a replica, writes go to the primary.
whenOtherWins: 只有给非技术的人解释时才用 one place 大白话，正式面试要 path、replica、primary。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary is the database that takes all writes; replicas sync from it.

if the main one is dead, we do a failover to make the copy the main one, the failover happen fast...
so if it dies, we, we switch to another one, so that other one becomes the, the main one, yeah...

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「异步复制的代价是什么」。你想说最终一致性，却卡成 we want to consistency，还把 ACID 念成 half acid。

scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how a write won't be lost. You mean a majority of replicas must confirm, but circle into "most of the nodes say okay" instead of naming quorum.
q: 「写要过半副本确认才算提交」这句话怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "a write commits only after a majority of replicas confirm"?
options: we need most of the nodes to say okay, the quorum, so the majority, most of them ack, then it's done...
so we wait for enough of the copies to confirm, like enough of them, and then we know it's safe, so...
A write isn't committed until a quorum of replicas acks it, so it survives a node dying.

why_en: A write isn't committed until a quorum of replicas acks it, so it survives a node dying.

scenario: Anytime AI 做法律 RAG，面试官问系统怎么让模型答案有据可查。你想说「先检索相关片段，再让模型基于这些片段生成」，上轮却卡成 “use the RAG to search”。
scenario_en: Anytime AI builds legal RAG. The interviewer asks how the system keeps the model's answers grounded. You want to say "retrieve the relevant chunks first, then generate from them," but last time you stalled at "use the RAG to search."
q: 「先检索相关片段，再让模型基于这些片段生成答案」这套 RAG 怎么地道说出口？
q_en: How do you say the RAG flow out loud — retrieve the relevant chunks, then generate grounded in them?
options: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves pertinent context which is subsequently incorporated into the generative model's output.
It's RAG — we retrieve the relevant chunks, then the model generates an answer grounded in them.
We use the RAG to search the documents and let the model to answer based on it.
So so we we find some related text, some related text, and then the model, the model uses it to answer...

why_en: It's RAG — retrieve the chunks, then generate grounded in them; the verbs prove you know the mechanism, not just the acronym.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试聊的是纯生成、没有外部知识库，就不该硬套 RAG，直接说 “the model answers from its own weights” 更准。

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档被切成的小片段，检索时按 chunk 命中并喂给模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is a small slice a document is split into; retrieval matches and returns chunks to feed the model.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounded means the answer is backed by the retrieved text rather than made up by the model, i.e. grounded in the sources.

q_en: How do you say 'semantic search — match on meaning, not keywords'?
options: We do semantic search — we embed the query and match on meaning, not exact keywords.
We use the semantic search to find the meaning words, not the keyword matching.
So we we look for the meaning, the meaning of it, not the exact words, you know, the meaning...
Semantic search leverages dense vector embeddings to retrieve results by semantic proximity rather than lexical overlap.

why_en: Say semantic search and 'match on meaning, not keywords' — that names the mechanism instead of the calque 'meaning words.'

termDefinitions.meaning: 按含义相近来检索，而不是逐字匹配关键词，能找到说法不同但意思一样的内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Semantic search retrieves by closeness in meaning rather than exact keyword match, so it finds content that says the same thing in different words.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本编码成一串数字向量，含义相近的文本向量也相近，是语义检索的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding turns text into a numeric vector; texts with similar meaning get nearby vectors, which is what makes semantic search work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一串数字坐标，代表文本的语义位置；比较两个向量的距离就能判断意思是否接近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector is a list of numbers representing where text sits in meaning-space; comparing two vectors' distance tells you how close their meanings are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字面词匹配的传统检索，词对不上就找不到；也叫 lexical search。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Keyword or lexical search matches on the literal words, so it misses results that use different wording for the same idea.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存向量、并能按距离快速找最近向量的数据库，如 Pinecone、Milvus。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector DB is a database built to store embeddings and quickly find the nearest vectors by distance, like Pinecone or Milvus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索：不逐个精确比对，用索引快速找到足够近的向量，换速度牺牲一点精度。

termDefinitions.meaning: 文本或图片编码成的一串数字坐标，向量库靠比较它们的距离来检索。

termDefinitions.meaning: 向量库常用的一种 ANN 索引结构，用分层图快速跳到近邻。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW is a common ANN index structure vector DBs use — a layered graph that hops quickly toward the nearest neighbors.

scenario: 一个 ML 岗面试，面试官问你怎么权衡误报和漏报。你想说「这是精确率和召回率的取舍，防欺诈我优先召回」，但没利落说出 precision vs recall。
scenario_en: In an ML round, the interviewer asks how you'd weigh false alarms against misses. You want to say "it's a precision-recall tradeoff, and for fraud I'd favor recall," but you don't land precision vs recall cleanly.
q: 「这是精确率对召回率的取舍，这里我优先召回」怎么利落说出口？
q_en: How do you say 'a precision-recall tradeoff, and here I'd favor recall'?
options: We need to balance the precision rate and the recall rate to make the accuracy higher.
So so precision, precision is like, and recall is like, and we want, we want both to be high, you know...
It's a precision-recall tradeoff — here I'd favor recall so we don't miss real fraud, even if precision drops.
Precision quantifies the fraction of true positives among predicted positives, whereas recall measures coverage of actual positives.
tradeoff: precision vs recall 加一句偏向理由 vs 只报“precision rate/recall rate”：前者证明你懂何时优化哪个，后者只报名词。
why: 核心是 precision vs recall 加一句偏向哪边的理由：说清防欺诈优先 recall，才证明你懂什么时候优化哪个。
why_en: Say precision vs recall plus which you'd favor and why — that shows you know when to optimize which, not just the definitions.
whenOtherWins: 若正负样本均衡、误报漏报代价差不多，直接说 “I'd look at overall accuracy” 也够，不必强分 precision 和 recall。

So so precision, precision is like, and recall is like, and we want, we want both to be high, you know...
It's a precision-recall tradeoff — here I'd favor recall so we don't miss real fraud, even if precision drops.
Precision quantifies the fraction of true positives among predicted positives, whereas recall measures coverage of actual positives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在你判为正的里面，真正是正的占比；precision 高意味着误报少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the share of your positive predictions that are actually positive; high precision means few false alarms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在所有真正是正的里面，你成功抓到的占比；recall 高意味着漏报少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the share of all true positives you actually catch; high recall means few misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误报是把正常当成异常；漏报是把异常放过去。防欺诈通常最怕漏报。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive flags something normal as bad; a false negative lets something bad through. Fraud detection usually fears the miss most.

scenario: IKEA ML 轮聊你做的广告推荐排序。面试官问整体架构，你想说「先候选生成从百万缩到几百，再用排序模型打分」，上轮却说成 “candidate generate”。
scenario_en: In the IKEA ML round on your ad recommender, the interviewer asks for the overall shape. You want to say "candidate generation narrows millions to a few hundred, then a ranking model scores them," but last time it came out as "candidate generate."
q: 「先候选生成缩小范围，再排序模型打分排序」这套两阶段怎么说？
q_en: How do you say 'candidate generation then ranking' in a recommender?
options: It's two stages — candidate generation narrows millions to a few hundred, then a ranking model orders them.
First we do the candidate generate, then we do the rank model to sort them out.
So we we pick some candidates, some candidates first, and then we rank them, we rank them, you know...
The recommender employs a candidate-generation phase followed by a ranking phase that scores and orders the retrieved items.
tradeoff: candidate generation → ranking 加“缩到几百再打分” vs 说成 candidate generate：前者显得懂两阶段，后者名词当动词。
why: 术语是候选生成再排序：配“先缩到几百再打分”，证明你懂两阶段各干嘛，而不是把名词硬当动词。
why_en: It's candidate generation then ranking — 'narrow to a few hundred, then score' shows you know what each stage does.
whenOtherWins: 若候选集本来就只有几百个，直接一把排序就好，说 “we just rank them all” 更省，不必分两阶段。
options_en: It's two stages — candidate generation narrows millions to a few hundred, then a ranking model orders them.
First we do the candidate generate, then we do the rank model to sort them out.
So we we pick some candidates, some candidates first, and then we rank them, we rank them, you know...
The recommender employs a candidate-generation phase followed by a ranking phase that scores and orders the retrieved items.

用 “employs / phase” 书面腔念定义。

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐第一阶段：用便宜的方法从海量物料里快速召回几百个候选，重点是别漏、要快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the first recommender stage: cheaply retrieve a few hundred candidates from millions, optimizing for speed and not missing good ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐第二阶段：用较重的模型给这几百个候选精细打分排序，决定最终展示顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ranking model is the second stage: a heavier model scores and orders the few hundred candidates to decide the final display order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给用户推物料/内容的系统，典型是候选生成加排序的两阶段架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recommender suggests items or content to users, typically built as a two-stage candidate-generation-plus-ranking pipeline.

scenario: 还是推荐系统那轮，面试官问模型怎么上线服务。你想说「在线推理走低延迟接口、批量推理离线打分」，上轮卡成 “online predict / batch predict”。
scenario_en: Same recommender round. The interviewer asks how the model is served. You want to say "online inference behind a low-latency endpoint, batch inference offline," but last time you stalled at "online predict / batch predict."
q: 「在线推理走低延迟接口、批量推理离线打分」这一句怎么说地道？
q_en: How do you say 'online inference for live requests vs batch inference offline'?
options: We have the online predict and the batch predict — online is real time and batch is not.
We serve it online behind a low-latency endpoint for live requests, and run batch inference offline for bulk scoring.
So so for live we we serve it online, serve it online, and the big ones, the big ones we do in batch...
Online inference services requests synchronously under strict latency requirements, while batch inference processes datasets asynchronously offline.
tradeoff: online inference vs batch inference 加 endpoint/offline vs 生造 “online predict”：前者点名两种服务方式，后者听着生。
why: 地道说法是 online inference 对 batch inference：配 low-latency endpoint 和 offline，才点出两种服务方式的区别。
why_en: Say online inference versus batch inference, with 'low-latency endpoint' and 'offline' — that names the two serving modes.
whenOtherWins: 若请求本来就不在意延迟、可以攒着一起算，直接说 “we batch it” 就够，不必强调 online 端点。
options_en: We have the online predict and the batch predict — online is real time and batch is not.
We serve it online behind a low-latency endpoint for live requests, and run batch inference offline for bulk scoring.
So so for live we we serve it online, serve it online, and the big ones, the big ones we do in batch...
Online inference services requests synchronously under strict latency requirements, while batch inference processes datasets asynchronously offline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对每个实时请求即时算预测，走低延迟接口，用户等着结果，要求毫秒级返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Online inference computes a prediction on the spot for each live request behind a low-latency endpoint, so it must return in milliseconds while the user waits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线一次性给大批数据算预测（如每晚跑一遍），不赶实时，追求吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batch inference scores a large dataset all at once offline, like a nightly job, optimizing for throughput rather than real-time latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型对外暴露的服务地址，在线推理时请求打到这个 endpoint 拿预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An endpoint is the served address the model exposes; online requests hit this endpoint to get a prediction back.

scenario: IKEA ML 轮追问特征怎么保证训练和线上一致。你想说「用特征库，同一套特征离线训练、在线服务」，上轮却说成 “feature storage”，没点出 skew。
scenario_en: The IKEA ML round asks how you keep features consistent between training and serving. You want to say "a feature store gives the same features offline and online," but last time it came out as "feature storage," with no mention of skew.
q: 「用特征库，离线训练和在线服务用同一套特征、不出 skew」怎么说？
q_en: How do you say 'a feature store keeps training and serving features consistent — no skew'?
options: We have the feature storage to keep the features for the training and the serving both.
So we we keep the features in one place, one place, for training and for serving, so they match...
A feature store centralizes feature computation to guarantee consistency between training and serving, thereby preventing skew.
We use a feature store, so the same features run once — offline for training, online for serving — no skew.
tradeoff: feature store + “no train/serve skew” vs 说成 feature storage：前者点出一致性目的，后者只像个存储层。
why: 术语是 feature store 加 “no train/serve skew”：一句话点出同一套特征离线训练、在线服务，而不是只说存储层。
why_en: It's a feature store plus 'no train/serve skew' — same features offline and online, not the calque 'feature storage.'
whenOtherWins: 若特征简单、训练和线上就用同一段代码算，直接说 “we compute it inline” 也行，不必抬出 feature store。
options_en: We have the feature storage to keep the features for the training and the serving both.
So we we keep the features in one place, one place, for training and for serving, so they match...
A feature store centralizes feature computation to guarantee consistency between training and serving, thereby preventing skew.
We use a feature store, so the same features run once — offline for training, online for serving — no skew.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中管理特征的系统：同一套特征定义既供离线训练、又供在线服务，保证两边一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally manages features so the same definitions feed both offline training and online serving, keeping the two sides consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时和线上服务时算出的特征不一致，导致线上效果比离线差；特征库就是为了消掉它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Train/serve skew is when features computed at training differ from those at serving, hurting live performance; a feature store exists to eliminate it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 喂给模型的一个输入信号，如用户近 7 天点击数；特征库统一它的计算口径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature is one input signal fed to the model, like a user's clicks in the last 7 days; the feature store standardizes how it's computed.

scenario: TikTok 广告排序改动上线前，面试官问你怎么验证效果。你想说「跑 A/B、主指标看 CTR、延迟设护栏指标」，但没说出 guardrail metric。
scenario_en: Before shipping a TikTok ad-ranking change, the interviewer asks how you'd validate it. You want to say "run an A/B test, CTR as the primary metric, latency as a guardrail," but the phrase guardrail metric doesn't come.
q: 「跑 A/B，主指标看 CTR，延迟设护栏指标」这一句怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say 'an A/B test with CTR as the primary metric and latency as a guardrail'?
options: We do the AB testing and look at the main metric and also a guard metric to protect it.
So we we split the traffic, split the traffic, and check if the metric goes up, goes up, and also...
We A/B test the change — CTR is the primary metric, and latency is a guardrail so a win can't ship a regression.
An A/B test partitions traffic between variants while a guardrail metric constrains the experiment against regressions in secondary indicators.
tradeoff: primary metric + guardrail metric vs 生造 “guard metric”：前者证明你懂 A/B 不只盯一个数，后者术语没抓准。
why: 核心是 primary metric 加 guardrail metric：说 CTR 主看、延迟设护栏，才证明你懂 A/B 不能只盯一个数。
why_en: Say primary metric and guardrail metric — CTR to win on, latency to guard — so a win can't ship a regression.
whenOtherWins: 若改动只是内部工具、没线上流量，直接说 “we validate offline” 更实在，不必跑 A/B。
options_en: We do the AB testing and look at the main metric and also a guard metric to protect it.
So we we split the traffic, split the traffic, and check if the metric goes up, goes up, and also...
We A/B test the change — CTR is the primary metric, and latency is a guardrail so a win can't ship a regression.
An A/B test partitions traffic between variants while a guardrail metric constrains the experiment against regressions in secondary indicators.

CTR 定输赢，延迟当护栏兜底。
用 “partitions / constrains” 书面腔。

Loops on 'split the traffic.'
