termDefinitions.meaning: 把流量随机切成对照组和实验组，比较改动对指标的影响，判断能否上线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test randomly splits traffic into control and treatment groups to compare a change's effect on metrics and decide whether to ship it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 护栏指标：即使主指标涨了，只要它变差就不许上线的底线指标，如延迟、崩溃率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a line-in-the-sand metric like latency or crash rate; even if the primary metric wins, a regression here blocks the launch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率，广告/推荐常用的主指标，衡量展示后被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR, click-through rate, is a common primary metric for ads and recommendations — the share of impressions that get clicked.

scenario: ML 岗面试，面试官问模型上线后怎么保持效果。你想说「数据变了模型会漂移，监控到漂移就触发重训」，但没说出 drift 这个词。
scenario_en: In an ML round, the interviewer asks how you keep a model healthy after launch. You want to say "the model drifts as data shifts, so drift monitoring triggers a retrain," but the word drift doesn't come out.
q: 「数据分布变了模型会漂移，监控到就触发重训」这一句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say 'model drift, and a retraining trigger when accuracy drops'?
options: The model drifts as the data shifts, so we monitor for drift and trigger a retrain when accuracy drops past a threshold.
The model becomes not accurate over time, so we re-train the model again when it drops.
So so over time the model, the model gets worse, gets worse, and then we train it again, train it again...
As the input distribution evolves, model drift degrades performance, necessitating a retraining pipeline triggered by predefined thresholds.
tradeoff: model drift + retraining trigger vs 白描“not accurate over time”：前者点名机制，后者听不出你懂怎么发现和处理。
why: 术语是 model drift 加 retraining trigger：配“accuracy 跌破阈值就重训”，证明你懂漂移是怎么被发现和处理的。
why_en: Say model drift and a retraining trigger — 'retrain when accuracy drops past a threshold' shows how drift gets caught and fixed.
whenOtherWins: 若数据分布很稳、几乎不变，直接说 “we retrain on a fixed schedule” 就够，不必强调 drift 触发。
options_en: The model drifts as the data shifts, so we monitor for drift and trigger a retrain when accuracy drops past a threshold.
The model becomes not accurate over time, so we re-train the model again when it drops.
So so over time the model, the model gets worse, gets worse, and then we train it again, train it again...
As the input distribution evolves, model drift degrades performance, necessitating a retraining pipeline triggered by predefined thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布随时间变化，模型效果慢慢下滑的现象，需要监控和重训来救。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model drift is when the live data distribution shifts over time and the model's performance slowly degrades, so you monitor for it and retrain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 触发重训的条件：可以是效果跌破阈值，也可以是定时或数据量到量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retraining trigger is the condition that kicks off a retrain — a metric dropping below a threshold, a fixed schedule, or enough new data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入特征本身的分布变了（如用户行为变化），是 model drift 的常见来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data drift is a shift in the input feature distribution itself, like changing user behavior, and is a common cause of model drift.

scenario: 推荐排序那轮，面试官问排序阶段还能怎么提升。你想说「对 top-K 用更重的模型重排，只在候选短名单上跑」，上轮卡成 “re-rank the top K again”。
scenario_en: In the ranking round, the interviewer asks how you'd push quality further. You want to say "rerank the top-K with a heavier model, only on the shortlist," but last time you stalled at "re-rank the top K again."
q: 「对 top-K 用更重的模型重排，只在短名单上跑」这一句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say 'rerank the top-K with a heavier model, only on the shortlist'?
options: We use a big model to re-rank the top K again for a better order.
After the first pass we rerank the top-K with a heavier model — it's costly, so we only run it on the shortlist.
So so we take the top ones, the top ones, and then a bigger model, a bigger model, it reorders them...
A computationally heavier model reranks the top-K candidates from the initial retrieval stage to refine the final ordering.
tradeoff: rerank the top-K + heavier model + “only on the shortlist” vs 零碎的 “re-rank the top K again”：前者点出为何放最后一步。
why: 术语是对 top-K 做 rerank，配更重的模型：补“只在短名单上跑”，点出重排为何放最后一步。
why_en: Say rerank the top-K with a heavier model, 'only on the shortlist' — that explains why the heavy pass comes last.
whenOtherWins: 若第一轮召回本身就很准、量也不大，直接用它的分数就行，说 “the first pass is enough”，不必再重排。
options_en: We use a big model to re-rank the top K again for a better order.
After the first pass we rerank the top-K with a heavier model — it's costly, so we only run it on the shortlist.
So so we take the top ones, the top ones, and then a bigger model, a bigger model, it reorders them...
A computationally heavier model reranks the top-K candidates from the initial retrieval stage to refine the final ordering.

对短名单用更重模型重排。

用 “computationally / refine” 书面腔。

A heavier model reranks just the shortlist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随时间聚合的数字，比如 QPS、错误率，用来发现有没有出问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metrics are numbers aggregated over time, like QPS or error rate, used to spot that something is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带时间戳的事件记录，用来解释某一步到底发生了什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Logs are timestamped event records that explain what actually happened at a step.

scenario: Majestic Labs 面，面试官问你怎么衡量接口延迟。你想说看 p99 而不是平均值，因为均值把慢尾巴藏了，但上次绕进 "the average, the average latency" 没点出百分位。
scenario_en: At Majestic Labs the interviewer asks how you measure API latency. You want to say look at p99, not the average, because the mean hides the tail — but last time you looped on "the average, the average latency."
q: 想说「看 p99 而不是平均值，均值藏了百分之一用户的慢尾巴」，该怎么开口？
q_en: How do you say "look at p99, not the average — the mean hides the slow tail one user in a hundred hits"?
options: I'd look at p99, not the average — the mean hides the slow tail one user in a hundred hits.
We check the ninety-nine percentage, like the average of the top slow requests, the mean latency.
so like the the p, the ninety-nine, the slowest, um, the average is is fine but the tail, the tail...
The 99th percentile latency denotes the threshold below which ninety-nine percent of all requests complete.
tradeoff: 地道术语 p99 + 点破均值缺陷 vs 说 "the average"：前者说明你懂尾延迟才是体验瓶颈，后者暴露你只会看平均。
why: 术语是 p99——第 99 百分位。关键是点破均值：它把百分之一用户的慢尾巴平均掉了，所以看尾部而非 average。
why_en: It's p99 — the 99th percentile — and the key move is calling out that the average smooths away the slow tail one user in a hundred hits.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只关心整体趋势、没追问尾部体验，说 "latency's around X on average" 就够，不必上 p99。
options_en: I'd look at p99, not the average — the mean hides the slow tail one user in a hundred hits.
We check the ninety-nine percentage, like the average of the top slow requests, the mean latency.
so like the the p, the ninety-nine, the slowest, um, the average is is fine but the tail, the tail...
The 99th percentile latency denotes the threshold below which ninety-nine percent of all requests complete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求延迟排序后第 99 百分位的值：只有 1% 的请求比它更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99, the 99th percentile, is the latency only one percent of requests exceed — the slow tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有请求延迟的算术平均，会被大量快请求拉低，掩盖少数慢请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The average, or mean latency, is pulled down by the many fast requests and hides the slow few.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟分布最慢的那一小撮请求，往往就是用户真正感到卡的部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The tail is the slowest slice of requests — the part users actually feel as lag.

scenario: Nimbus 系统设计面，问一个请求跨好几个服务、变慢了怎么查。你想说靠分布式链路：一个 trace ID、每个服务加一段 span，但上次卡在 "we trace the, the request kind of" 说不清机制。
scenario_en: In a Nimbus system-design round you're asked how you debug a request that slows down across several services. You want to say a distributed trace — one trace ID, a span per service — but stalled at "we trace the, the request kind of."

q_en: How do you say "one trace ID follows the request, each service adds a span, so you see where the time goes"?
options: We trace the distribute, every service make a small span piece, then we follow the request path.
so we we trace it, the request goes to, to a service and a service, and each one, each one kind of adds a thing...
A distributed trace aggregates causally-related spans emitted by each service to reconstruct the end-to-end path.
One request carries a trace ID, and each service adds a span, so I can see where the time goes.
tradeoff: 地道术语 trace ID + span + 说清 "time goes where" vs 模糊 "trace the request"：前者点出机制，后者听不出你懂链路怎么拼起来。
why: 术语是 distributed trace：一个 trace ID 贯穿请求、每服务加一段 span，拼起来就看出时间花在哪一环。
why_en: It's a distributed trace — one trace ID threads the request, each service adds a span, so you see which hop ate the time.
whenOtherWins: 如果请求只在单个服务内，直接说 "I'd check that service's logs" 就够。

termDefinitions.meaning: 追踪一个请求穿过多个服务的完整路径，用来看它在哪一环变慢或出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed trace follows one request across many services to see where it slows or fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 链路里的一段：某个服务处理这个请求所花的一小段时间和上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A span is one segment of a trace — the slice of time and context one service spent on the request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贯穿整条请求的唯一标识，各服务用它把自己的 span 归到同一个 trace。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trace ID is the unique tag threading the whole request so every service files its span under the same trace.

scenario: Cirrus 系统设计面，问你告警怎么设才不吵。你想说按 SLO 的错误预算烧得多快来 page，而不是盯 CPU 过某条线，但上次卡在 "we alert when it's, when it's bad" 说不出术语。
scenario_en: In a Cirrus system-design round you're asked how to page without noise. You want to say alert on SLO burn rate — how fast the error budget drains — not on a raw CPU line, but stalled at "we alert when it's, when it's bad."
q: 想说「按 SLO 错误预算烧得多快来 page，而不是盯 CPU 过线」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "we page on SLO burn rate — how fast the error budget drains — not on a raw CPU threshold"?
options: We alarm on the burn rate of SLO, the error budget burns too quick, so then we page someone.
We page on SLO burn rate — how fast we're eating the error budget — not on a raw CPU threshold.
so we we don't alert on a, a number, we alert when the, the budget, the error budget kind of goes fast...
Alerts ought to be predicated on error-budget consumption rate relative to the objective, not on static thresholds.
tradeoff: 地道术语 burn rate + error budget vs 说 "alarm on the burn rate of SLO"：前者词序自然又点出预算机制，后者词形拧巴听着别扭。
why: 术语是 SLO burn rate：按错误预算烧得多快来 page，而非盯 CPU 过线，烧得快才是真出事。
why_en: It's SLO burn rate — you page on how fast the error budget drains, not a raw threshold.
whenOtherWins: 如果这信号没定 SLO、也没错误预算，就先说 "we'd alert if error rate crosses X"。
options_en: We alarm on the burn rate of SLO, the error budget burns too quick, so then we page someone.
We page on SLO burn rate — how fast we're eating the error budget — not on a raw CPU threshold.
so we we don't alert on a, a number, we alert when the, the budget, the error budget kind of goes fast...

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO, or service-level objective, is a target like "99.9% of requests succeed" that alerting is measured against.

termDefinitions.meaning: 错误预算被消耗的速度：烧得越快，说明离违反 SLO 越近，越该立刻 page。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Burn rate is how fast the error budget drains — faster burn means you're closer to breaching the SLO, so page now.

termDefinitions.meaning: SLO 允许的失败额度，比如 0.1% 的请求可以失败；用完就该停止发布、专注止血。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The error budget is the failure the SLO allows, like 0.1% of requests; spend it and you stop shipping to recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定阈值告警，比如 CPU 超 80% 就报，容易在没真出事时误报。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A threshold alert fires on a fixed line like CPU over 80%, which often pages when nothing is actually broken.

scenario: Vertex 系统设计面，问你为什么不能把 user ID 当 metric 的 label。你想说会 cardinality 爆炸、每个取值多一条时间序列、内存扛不住，但上次卡在 "it's too many, too many" 没点出术语。
scenario_en: In a Vertex system-design round you're asked why you shouldn't use user ID as a metric label. You want to say cardinality explodes — each value is a new time series, memory blows up — but stalled at "it's too many, too many."
q: 想说「拿 user ID 当 label 会 cardinality 爆炸，每个取值多一条时间序列」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "tagging metrics with user ID makes cardinality explode — every value spins up a new time series"?
options: If we tag metrics with user ID, cardinality explodes — every unique value spins up a new time series.
The cardinal number blow up, too many label value, so the metric use very big memory then.
so if we we put like the id as a label, then it's, it's a lot of, um, series, and it kind of just blows up...
High-cardinality label dimensions such as user identifiers induce a combinatorial expansion of stored time series.
tradeoff: 地道术语 cardinality explosion + 点出「每个取值一条时间序列」vs 说 "too many"：前者说清爆炸机制，后者听不出你懂为什么炸。
why: 术语是 cardinality explosion：user ID 这种高基数 label，每个取值都新建一条时间序列，数量爆炸、内存扛不住。
why_en: It's a cardinality explosion — a high-cardinality label like user ID spins up a new time series per value, so memory blows up.
whenOtherWins: 如果 label 取值少且固定（如 region），"that label's low-cardinality" 就够。
options_en: If we tag metrics with user ID, cardinality explodes — every unique value spins up a new time series.
The cardinal number blow up, too many label value, so the metric use very big memory then.
so if we we put like the id as a label, then it's, it's a lot of, um, series, and it kind of just blows up...
High-cardinality label dimensions such as user identifiers induce a combinatorial expansion of stored time series.

"it's, it's a lot / kind of blows up" 打转。
"combinatorial expansion" 书面腔。

Wrong form "cardinal number blow up" — translated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 label 有多少种不同取值：user ID 有几百万种就是高基数（high-cardinality）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is how many distinct values a label has — user ID with millions of values is high-cardinality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高基数 label 让存储的时间序列数量暴涨，内存和查询成本失控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cardinality explosion is when a high-cardinality label makes the number of stored time series blow up, wrecking memory and query cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给指标打的键值标签（如 status=200、region=us），用来切分和过滤指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A label is a key-value tag on a metric, like status=200 or region=us, used to slice and filter it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个指标加一组固定 label 取值下、随时间记录的一串数据点；label 组合越多，series 越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time series is one stream of points for a metric at a fixed set of label values; more label combos means more series.

scenario: Solace 系统设计面，问你日志怎么记才好查。你想说记 structured 的 JSON 字段、能按字段查，而不是 grep 一坨自由文本，但上次卡在 "we log it and we search the text" 没点出术语。
scenario_en: In a Solace system-design round you're asked how to log so it's queryable. You want to say structured JSON fields you can query by, not grepping free text, but stalled at "we log it and we search the text."
q: 想说「记 structured JSON 字段、按 user_id 直接查，而不是 grep 自由文本」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "we log structured JSON fields and query by user_id, instead of grepping free text"?
options: We use the structure log, put the field into the text, so we can grep it a bit more easy.
so we we log it in a, in a structured way, with like fields, so you can, you can search it not just text...
Log entries ought to be emitted as structured key-value payloads to enable field-level querying over substrings.
We log structured JSON fields, so I can query by user_id or status instead of grepping free text.
tradeoff: 地道术语 structured logging + 点出「按字段查 vs grep 文本」vs 说 "search the text"：前者说清可查询机制，后者听不出好处在哪。
why: 术语是 structured logging：日志写成 JSON 字段，能按 user_id、status 直接查，而非 grep 自由文本。
why_en: It's structured logging — logs as JSON fields you query by user_id, not grepping free text.

q_en: How do you say "watch the four golden signals — latency, traffic, errors, saturation, how full it's running"?
options: We watch the golden four signal — the latency, the traffic, the error, and how the system full.
I'd watch the four golden signals — latency, traffic, errors, and saturation, how full it's running.
so there's like four, four signals, the golden ones, latency and traffic and, and errors, and, and the last...

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Traffic is how much demand the system takes, like requests per second — the load level.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Saturation is how full the system is against its limits — CPU, memory, queues — the signal closest to a bottleneck and easiest to forget.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「一个 topic 的量太大，单消费者读不过来，你怎么扩？」你想说「开一个 consumer group，分区分给多个消费者并行读」，但一时说不利索。
scenario_en: In a system design round the interviewer asks how you scale reads when one consumer can't keep up with a busy topic. You want to say "put the consumers in a consumer group and split the partitions across them" but blank.
q: 想说「放进一个消费者组，每个分区归一个消费者，并行分担」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "put them in one consumer group and each partition goes to one consumer" — which line lands?
options: We make a consumer group so the queue split the partitions to every consumer to be parallel and faster.
We put the consumers in one consumer group, and each partition goes to exactly one consumer, so they share the load.
So we, we have like a group of consumers, and the partitions get, you know, kind of spread out so more than one can read at the same time...
Consumers are organized into a consumer group whereby each partition is assigned to precisely one member for parallel consumption.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs Chinglish/打转：「each partition goes to exactly one consumer」一句点出分配机制；「the queue split the partitions」主谓错、像没真用过。
why: 消费者组的机制是「每个分区归组里恰好一个消费者」，一句带出并行分担。主谓错或打转都露怯。
why_en: Put the consumers in one consumer group and each partition goes to exactly one consumer — that names the mechanism, not just the word.
whenOtherWins: 若瓶颈在单分区自己太热，加消费者也没用，得先按 key 重新分区；此时谈 consumer group 是答错方向。

We put the consumers in one consumer group, and each partition goes to exactly one consumer, so they share the load.
So we, we have like a group of consumers, and the partitions get, you know, kind of spread out so more than one can read at the same time...
Consumers are organized into a consumer group whereby each partition is assigned to precisely one member for parallel consumption.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers reading the same topic together; the broker splits partitions among them so they read in parallel without overlap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 topic 被切成的并行子队列，每个分区内消息有序;分区数决定并行度上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is one of the parallel sub-queues a topic is split into; messages are ordered within a partition and the count caps parallelism.

scenario: Nyxa 后端面，面试官问「你的消费者怎么保证不重复处理？」你想说「实际拿到的是 at-least-once，所以让消费者幂等去重，凑出 effectively-once」，但术语卡住了。
scenario_en: In a Nyxa backend round the interviewer asks how your consumer avoids double-processing. You want to say "you actually get at-least-once, so make the consumer idempotent and dedupe for effectively-once" but blank on the terms.
q: 想说「实际是 at-least-once，靠幂等去重凑出 effectively-once」，哪句是工程师的说法？
q_en: You want to say "it's at-least-once, so idempotent dedupe gets you effectively-once" — which line is how an engineer says it?
options: We use exactly-one delivery so the message never come twice and no need to worry the duplicate.
So the delivery is like, it can maybe send twice, so we have to, to handle the same thing coming again somehow, you know...
The system guarantees at-least-once delivery semantics, therefore consumers must implement idempotent processing to tolerate duplicates.
In practice you get at-least-once, so we make the consumer idempotent and dedupe — that buys you effectively-once.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 造词/打转：「at-least-once + idempotent dedupe = effectively-once」一句点出机制；「exactly-one」是造错的词形，露怯。
why: 真实系统多是 at-least-once，靠幂等去重凑 effectively-once。词形写成 exactly-one 或打转都露怯。
why_en: In practice it's at-least-once, so an idempotent consumer that dedupes gets you effectively-once — that's the real chain.
whenOtherWins: 若平台原生支持事务性 exactly-once 且你确实开了，就直说 we rely on exactly-once semantics，不必再讲手动去重。

So the delivery is like, it can maybe send twice, so we have to, to handle the same thing coming again somehow, you know...
The system guarantees at-least-once delivery semantics, therefore consumers must implement idempotent processing to tolerate duplicates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投递语义：消息保证至少送到一次，但可能重复，所以消费者要能容忍重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once is a delivery guarantee where a message arrives at least once but may be duplicated, so the consumer must tolerate repeats.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投递语义:每条消息的效果恰好生效一次;端到端实现代价高,常靠幂等去重来近似。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means each message takes effect precisely once; true end-to-end it is costly, so people approximate it with idempotent dedupe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一条消息处理一次和处理多次结果相同,所以重放重复不会造成额外影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means processing the same message once or many times gives the same result, so a replayed duplicate has no extra effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 去重:靠消息唯一 id 或 key 记住处理过的,再来同一条就跳过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dedupe means dropping repeats by remembering a message's unique id or key and skipping it if seen again.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投递上是 at-least-once,但靠去重让业务效果看起来只发生一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Effectively-once is at-least-once delivery made to have a once-only business effect by deduplicating.

scenario: 面试官追问「有些消息一直处理失败、卡住后面，你怎么办？」你想说「重试几次后甩进死信队列，别堵住后面的」，但 dead-letter queue 一时说不出口。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what you do when some messages keep failing and block the rest. You want to say "after a few retries, route them to a dead-letter queue so they don't block the line" but blank on the term.
q: 想说「重试几次后甩进死信队列，一条坏消息别堵住后面」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "after a few retries, send it to a dead-letter queue so one bad message doesn't block the rest" — which line lands?
options: After a few retries we route it to a dead-letter queue, so one bad message doesn't block the rest.
We put the fail message to a dead letter box so it will not stop other message to be handle.
So if a message keeps, keeps failing, we kind of move it somewhere else so it, so it doesn't, you know, hold up everything behind it...
Messages that repeatedly fail processing are relegated to a dead-letter queue for subsequent manual inspection and remediation.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs Chinglish/念稿：「route it to a dead-letter queue after a few retries」一句点出机制;「dead letter box」是错词形,露怯。
why: 机制是「重试 N 次后 route 到 dead-letter queue」，一句带出不堵主线。词形写成 dead letter box 就露怯。
why_en: After a few retries we route it to a dead-letter queue so one bad message doesn't block the rest — that names the mechanism.
whenOtherWins: 若失败是全局暂时故障(下游全挂),别急着进死信,该整体退避重试;死信是给「个别一直失败」的消息。
options_en: After a few retries we route it to a dead-letter queue, so one bad message doesn't block the rest.
We put the fail message to a dead letter box so it will not stop other message to be handle.
So if a message keeps, keeps failing, we kind of move it somewhere else so it, so it doesn't, you know, hold up everything behind it...
Messages that repeatedly fail processing are relegated to a dead-letter queue for subsequent manual inspection and remediation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门收「重试多次仍失败」消息的旁路队列;把坏消息挪出主线,方便事后排查,不再阻塞后面的消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter queue is a side queue for messages that keep failing after retries; it moves bad messages off the main line for later inspection so they stop blocking others.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理失败后再试一次;通常配退避和上限,超过次数才转入死信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retry re-attempts a failed message, usually with backoff and a cap, after which it is routed to the dead-letter queue.

scenario: Corvid 系统设计面，面试官问「同一个用户的事件必须按顺序处理，你怎么保证？」你想说「用 user id 当 partition key，同一 key 落同一分区，天然有序」，但表达打了结。
scenario_en: In a Corvid design round the interviewer asks how you keep one user's events in order. You want to say "use the user id as the partition key, so the same key lands on the same partition and stays ordered" but tangle up.
q: 想说「用 user id 做 partition key，同一 key 落同一分区、天然有序」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "key by user id, so the same key lands on the same partition, in order" — which line lands?
options: So to keep the order we, we send the same kind of events to, to the same place so they don't get, get mixed up in the wrong order...
We set a partition key so the same key always go to same partition and keep the order right.
We key by user id, so all of one user's events hit the same partition and stay in order.
By designating the partition key, records sharing a key are routed to an identical partition, thereby preserving their relative ordering.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 打转/念稿：「key by user id → same partition → in order」一句点出因果;泛泛「the same place」没说清 key 决定路由。
why: 顺序保证的机制是「同一 partition key 路由到同一分区，分区内有序」。用 user id 当 key 一句带出。
why_en: Key by user id so all of one user's events hit the same partition and stay in order — that names why ordering holds.
whenOtherWins: 若要的是全局有序(跨所有用户),单靠 key 不够,得单分区或加序列号;此时谈 partition key 只保住了分区内有序。
options_en: So to keep the order we, we send the same kind of events to, to the same place so they don't get, get mixed up in the wrong order...

We key by user id, so all of one user's events hit the same partition and stay in order.
By designating the partition key, records sharing a key are routed to an identical partition, thereby preserving their relative ordering.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the field that decides which partition a message lands on; the same key always routes to the same partition, preserving order among those messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息处理的先后顺序;多数队列只保证「同一分区内」有序,跨分区不保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ordering is the sequence in which messages are processed; most queues guarantee it only within a single partition, not across partitions.

scenario: 实时数仓面试，面试官问「每分钟统计一次点击数，晚到的事件怎么处理？」你想说「开一分钟 tumbling window，用 watermark 决定何时关窗、丢太晚的」，但术语卡壳。
scenario_en: In a real-time analytics interview, they ask how you count clicks per minute and handle late events. You want to say "a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark decides when to close it and drop late events" but blank.
q: 想说「一分钟 tumbling window，watermark 决定何时关窗、丢太晚的事件」，哪句是工程师的说法？
q_en: You want to say "a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark decides when to close it and drop late events" — which line lands?
options: We use a rolling window and a water line to know when the late data is too late to count.
We run a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark tells us when to close it and drop late events.
So we kind of group the events into, into time chunks, and then we have a thing that decides when it's, when it's too late for the old ones...
A tumbling window aggregates events over fixed intervals, while a watermark demarcates the threshold beyond which late arrivals are discarded.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the cursor marking how far a consumer has read in a partition; move it back and you re-read from that point.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay/reprocess means rewinding the offset and consuming messages again from an earlier point to recompute history after a logic change or bug fix.

scenario: 面试官问「既然是 at-least-once，重复消息会不会把余额扣两次？」你想说「消费者是幂等的，按 message id 去重，重放重复是 no-op」，但术语一时说不顺。

An idempotent consumer deduplicates on a unique message identifier such that reprocessing a duplicate event yields no additional effect.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 错词形/打转：「idempotent，dedupe on the message id，a no-op」一句点出机制;「is idempotence」是词形错。

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动限制发送/处理速率；throttle down 就是降速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To throttle is to cap the rate; "throttle down" means slow the sending rate.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问：消费者进程崩了重启，怎么保证不丢不重乱？你想说「处理完再提交 offset，崩了从上次 offset 重放」，但 offset 这个词卡住了。
scenario_en: In a system design round the interviewer asks: if the consumer crashes and restarts, how do you avoid losing or garbling messages? You want to say "commit the offset after processing and replay from the last committed offset" but stall on the term.
q: 想说「处理完才提交 offset，崩溃后从上次 offset 重放」，哪句最工程师？
q_en: You want to say "commit the offset only after processing, and on a crash replay from the last committed offset" — which line is most engineer-like?
options: We save the position number after we're done, so if it crashes we start from the last position we saved.
so we, we remember where we are, the, the number, so when it restart, we go back to where we were...
The offset is committed post-processing to enable resumption of the consumer upon failure.
We commit the offset only after processing, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset.
tradeoff: 术语落地 vs 绕圈直译：「commit the offset after processing」一句闭环；「save the position number」绕开了 offset 和重放语义。
why: 读取位置叫 offset，搭 commit / resume from。处理后才提交＝at-least-once，崩了重放，业务要幂等。
why_en: Commit the offset only after processing, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset and replays — that's at-least-once.
whenOtherWins: 若消息可丢、追求最低延迟，可先提交再处理（at-most-once），说 commit first, then process；此时不谈重放。
options_en: We save the position number after we're done, so if it crashes we start from the last position we saved.
so we, we remember where we are, the, the number, so when it restart, we go back to where we were...
The offset is committed post-processing to enable resumption of the consumer upon failure.
We commit the offset only after processing, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset.

「so we we the the number」绕圈。
「is committed post-processing」被动书面腔。
提交 offset 与重放位置一句闭环。
optionMeanings_en: Uses "position number," dodging the term offset.
Loops on "so we we remember the the number."
A passive "is committed post-processing" written register.
Closes the loop: commit offset, resume from last committed.
optionScenarioImpacts: 懂你意思，但觉得没掌握标准词。
听不出你到底提不提交。
像念规范，缺实感。
确认你懂提交时机与重放。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They follow you but sense you lack the standard term.
They can't tell if you commit, or replay, at all.
Reads like a spec, missing the "here's what I'd do" feel.
The interviewer sees you know commit timing and replay.
optionDirectness: 错在直译绕词，语义都糊了。
错在绕圈，提交时机没说清。
错在语域，被动书面显僵。
抓住提交时机与崩溃后从原位重放。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: paraphrase dodges "offset" and blurs replay.
Wrong: circling, commit timing never gets stated.
Wrong register — passive written style feels stiff.
Nails offset commit timing, then replay from last offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者在分区里读到的位置编号；提交 offset 就是记录「我处理到这儿了」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the position a consumer has read to in a partition; committing it records how far you've processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把当前读取位置持久化；处理完再提交，崩溃后就从这个点重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To commit the offset is to persist your read position so a restart resumes from that point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理后才提交 → 崩溃会重放未提交的消息，可能重复，所以业务要幂等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Committing after processing means a crash replays uncommitted messages at least once, so handling must be idempotent.

scenario: Alterion 面试，你想说「发到 topic，每个订阅者各拿一份」，结果说成「we put it in the Kafka Q, everyone who listen can get it」，把 pub/sub 扇出说成了点对点队列。
scenario_en: In an Alterion interview you want to say "publish to a topic and each subscriber gets its own copy," but you said "we put it in the Kafka Q, everyone who listen can get it," collapsing pub/sub fan-out into a point-to-point queue.
q: 想说「发布到 topic，扇出给每个订阅者各一份」，哪句最准？
q_en: You want to say "publish to a topic and fan out a copy to each subscriber" — which line is most precise?
options: We put it in the Kafka Q, and then everyone who listen can get the message from there.
We publish to a topic and fan out to each subscriber — every one gets its own copy.
The message is published to a topic and fanned out to all subscribing consumers respectively.
so we, we send it to the, the topic thing, and then the ones who want it, they each, they get...
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 混淆模型：「publish to a topic, fan out, each gets a copy」区分了 pub/sub 与点对点；她的「Kafka Q」把两种模型糊在一起。
why: pub/sub 是 publish to a topic + fan out，每个订阅者各一份；点对点队列一条消息只被一个消费者取走。说成「Kafka Q」会让人以为你不分这两种。
why_en: We publish to a topic and fan out a copy to each subscriber — that's pub/sub, not a point-to-point queue where one consumer takes each message.
whenOtherWins: 若每条消息只该被一个 worker 处理一次（任务分发），那是点对点队列，说 each message goes to one worker，别用扇出。
options_en: We put it in the Kafka Q, and then everyone who listen can get the message from there.
We publish to a topic and fan out to each subscriber — every one gets its own copy.
The message is published to a topic and fanned out to all subscribing consumers respectively.
so we, we send it to the, the topic thing, and then the ones who want it, they each, they get...
optionMeanings: 她的原话：说成「Kafka Q」，混淆两种模型。
publish→topic→fan out→各一份，到位。
「fanned out ... respectively」公文腔。
「the topic thing ... they each」打转。
optionMeanings_en: Her line: says "Kafka Q," blurring fan-out with point-to-point.
"Publish to a topic, fan out, each gets a copy" — precise.
A stiff "fanned out ... respectively" written register.
Loops on "the topic thing ... they each they get."
optionScenarioImpacts: 以为你分不清 pub/sub 和队列。
确认你懂扇出：各拿独立一份。
像念文档，缺对话感。
听不出是扇出还是抢占。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer thinks you can't tell pub/sub from a queue.
They confirm you get fan-out: each subscriber its own copy.
Reads like a doc, missing conversational feel.
They can't tell if it's fan-out or competing consumers.
optionDirectness: 错在模型混淆，扇出说成点对点。
抓住 publish→topic→fan out→各一份。
错在语域，「respectively」显僵。
错在打转，扇出关键点没落地。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: conflates fan-out with a point-to-point queue.
Nails pub/sub: publish to topic, fan out, each a copy.
Wrong register — "respectively" feels stiff spoken.
Wrong: circling, the fan-out point never lands.

termDefinitions.meaning: pub/sub 里的消息类别通道；生产者发布到 topic，订阅者按 topic 收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A topic is a named channel in pub/sub; producers publish to it and subscribers receive from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条消息复制分发给多个接收方，每个订阅者各拿一份独立副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one message is copied out to many receivers, each subscriber getting its own copy.

termDefinitions.meaning: pub/sub 一条消息扇出给所有订阅者；点对点队列一条消息只被一个消费者取走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In pub/sub one message fans out to all subscribers; in a point-to-point queue one consumer takes each message.

scenario: Alterion 系统设计面，问你怎么给这个 API 限流。你想说用 token bucket、允许短突发到桶容量，但上次卡在 "we we limit the rate somehow"。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round you're asked how you'd rate-limit the API. You want to say a token bucket allows short bursts up to the bucket size, but last time you stalled on "we we limit the rate somehow."
q: 想说「用 token bucket，按固定速率补令牌、允许突发到桶容量」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "a token bucket refills at a fixed rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size" out loud?
options: We use a token bucket — it refills at a steady rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size.
We add a rate-limit machine, a token barrel, it drop the token when too many request come in.
So so we kind of limit the rate, we we count the requests, and if it's too many we we block some, some of them...
The system shall admit requests only when a token is available, with tokens replenished at a fixed constant rate.
tradeoff: 允许突发 vs 绝对匀速：token bucket 放行桶容量内的突发，leaky bucket 把输出削成固定速率。
why: 地道说法是 token bucket：按固定速率补令牌、允许突发到桶容量；leaky bucket 则匀速漏出、削平所有突发。
why_en: It's a token bucket — refills at a fixed rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size, whereas a leaky bucket drains at a constant rate.
whenOtherWins: 如果你要的是绝对平滑、不允许任何突发，就该说 leaky bucket 匀速漏出，而不是 token bucket。
options_en: We use a token bucket — it refills at a steady rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size.
We add a rate-limit machine, a token barrel, it drop the token when too many request come in.
So so we kind of limit the rate, we we count the requests, and if it's too many we we block some, some of them...
The system shall admit requests only when a token is available, with tokens replenished at a fixed constant rate.

token barrel 生造词，搭配全错。
so so / block some 打转，没术语。
shall admit ... replenished 书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Names token bucket, refill plus burst cap.
"Token barrel" is invented; collocation off.
Loops on "so so / block some," no term.
"Shall admit… replenished" reads like a spec.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你懂突发与匀速的区别。
术语走形，像没真配过限流。
对方还在等你说出机制。
太正式，像念算法定义。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you grasp burst-vs-steady-rate.

错在语域，书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails token bucket plus the burst cap.
Wrong: invented term, unnatural collocation.
Wrong: pure loop, says nothing.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 令牌桶：按固定速率往桶里放令牌，每个请求消耗一个令牌，桶里攒的令牌允许短时突发，直到桶被掏空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token bucket refills tokens at a fixed rate; each request spends one, so saved-up tokens allow short bursts up to the bucket size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏桶：请求排进桶里、以固定速率匀速漏出，把输出削成恒定速率，不放任何突发过去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaky bucket queues requests and drains them at a constant rate, smoothing output and allowing no bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器：控制单位时间内允许多少请求通过，超出就拒绝或排队，保护下游不被打垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limiter caps how many requests are allowed per unit time, rejecting or queuing the rest to protect downstream.

scenario: Gamma 后端面，问你怎么把请求按 URL 路径分到不同服务。你想说需要 L7 负载均衡、能读 HTTP，但上次把 L4 L7 说反了。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round you're asked how to route requests to different services by URL path. You want to say you need an L7 load balancer that reads HTTP, but last time you mixed up L4 and L7.
q: 想说「需要 L7 负载均衡，它读 HTTP 请求、能按路径或 host 路由」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we need an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request so it can route by path or host"?
options: We use the layer-four balancer to read the URL and send it to the right service by the path.
So so it depends, we we route the traffic, based on the, based on the path I think, so the higher one, the higher one...
We need an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path or host.
An application-layer load balancer shall inspect the HTTP payload to perform content-based routing across backend pools.
tradeoff: 看内容 vs 只看四层：L7 读 HTTP 能按路径/host 路由，L4 只按 IP+端口转发、更快更省。
why: 地道说法是 L7 load balancer：它读 HTTP 请求，所以能按 URL 路径或 host 路由；L4 只看 IP 和端口、不看内容。
why_en: It's an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path or host, whereas L4 only sees IP and port.
whenOtherWins: 如果只要按 IP+端口快速转发、不关心内容，L4 更快更省，就别上 L7。
options_en: We use the layer-four balancer to read the URL and send it to the right service by the path.
So so it depends, we we route the traffic, based on the, based on the path I think, so the higher one, the higher one...
We need an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path or host.
An application-layer load balancer shall inspect the HTTP payload to perform content-based routing across backend pools.

so so / higher one 打转，没点名。
点名 L7，读 HTTP 按路径路由。
shall inspect payload 书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Says L4 reads the URL — mechanism reversed.
Loops on "so so / higher one," no term.
Names L7, reads HTTP, routes by path.

对方还在等你说出是哪一层。

They're still waiting for which layer.

错在打转，迟迟不落地。
抓住 L7 加按 HTTP 路径路由。
错在语域，书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: reversed — L4 can't see the URL.
Wrong: loops, lands too late.

Wrong register — written style feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 七层负载均衡：工作在应用层，能读 HTTP 请求内容，所以可以按 URL 路径、host、header 把流量路由到不同服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L7 load balancer works at the application layer and reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path, host, or header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 四层负载均衡：工作在传输层，只看 IP 和端口、不看请求内容，转发更快更省但没法按 URL 路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L4 load balancer works at the transport layer, forwarding by IP and port without reading content — faster but can't route by URL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器：把进来的流量分发到后面多台服务实例，常缩写 LB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer spreads incoming traffic across a pool of backend instances.

scenario: Majestic Labs 系统设计面，问异步任务突增时 worker 池怎么定容量。你想说按 queue depth 自动伸缩，但上次只会说 "we add more machine"。
scenario_en: In a Majestic Labs system-design round you're asked how to size the worker pool when async jobs spike. You want to say you autoscale on queue depth, but last time you only had "we add more machine."
q: 想说「按 queue depth 自动伸缩，backlog 越阈值加 worker、排空后缩回」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we autoscale on queue depth — add workers when the backlog crosses the threshold, scale back in as it drains"?
options: We open the auto-scale, when the machine is busy it add more machine by itself automatically.
So so when there's a lot, a lot of jobs, we we add some, some more workers, and then less, we we remove them...
The autoscaler shall provision additional worker instances whenever the observed queue depth exceeds the configured threshold.
We autoscale on queue depth — it adds workers when the backlog crosses the threshold, then scales back in as it drains.
tradeoff: 按信号自动伸缩 vs 手动定容量：盯 queue depth 越阈值加 worker、排空缩回，比拍脑袋定容量更贴流量。
why: 地道说法是 autoscale on queue depth：backlog 越过阈值就加 worker，队列排空后再 scale back in。
why_en: You autoscale on queue depth — when the backlog crosses the threshold it adds workers, and scales back in once the queue drains.
whenOtherWins: 如果负载平稳、频繁伸缩反而抖动，固定容量或按 CPU 更稳，就别盯队列深度。
options_en: We open the auto-scale, when the machine is busy it add more machine by itself automatically.
So so when there's a lot, a lot of jobs, we we add some, some more workers, and then less, we we remove them...
The autoscaler shall provision additional worker instances whenever the observed queue depth exceeds the configured threshold.
We autoscale on queue depth — it adds workers when the backlog crosses the threshold, then scales back in as it drains.

so so / add workers 打转。
shall provision instances 书面腔。
点名 queue depth 越阈值加 worker。
optionMeanings_en: "Auto-scale / add machine" — term mangled.
Loops on "so so / add workers."
"Shall provision instances" — a spec sheet.

对方还在等你说触发信号。

对方懂你按 backlog 自动伸缩。

错在语域，书面体僵硬。

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动伸缩：根据某个信号（CPU、队列深度等）越过目标，自动增减实例数，让容量跟着负载走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoscaling automatically adds or removes instances when a signal like CPU or queue depth crosses a target, so capacity tracks load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列深度：消息队列里积压待处理的任务数，backlog 越深说明处理跟不上、该加 worker。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth is the number of pending jobs backed up in the queue; a growing backlog signals you need more workers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缩回/扩出：scale out 是加实例扛更多负载，scale in 是负载降下来后减实例省成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scale out adds instances to handle more load; scale in removes them once load drops to save cost.

scenario: Eclipse Performance 面，问你怎么平衡发新功能和保稳定。你想说用 SLO 加 error budget、烧超了就冻结发版，但上次绕成 "we slow down features somehow"。
scenario_en: In an Eclipse Performance round you're asked how you balance shipping features with reliability. You want to say you use an SLO and error budget and freeze releases when it's burned, but last time you circled on "we slow down features somehow."
q: 想说「设一个 SLO，error budget 是 1 减 SLO；烧太快就冻结发版」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we set an SLO, the error budget is one minus it, and if we burn it too fast we freeze releases"?
options: So so we have a reliability goal, and if we we miss it too much then we we slow down the, the new features...
We set a 99.9% SLO, and the error budget is what's left — burn it too fast and we freeze feature launches.
We have a service level object of three nine, and when the budget of error is used up we stop to release.
An error budget denotes the permissible quantum of unreliability derived as one minus the service-level objective.
tradeoff: 发功能 vs 保可靠：error budget 没烧完就放手发，烧超了就冻结发版、先修可靠性。
why: 地道说法是 SLO 加 error budget：SLO 是可靠性目标，error budget 是 1 减 SLO 那点余额，烧太快就冻结发版。
why_en: It's an SLO plus an error budget — the SLO is the reliability target, the budget is one minus it, and burning it too fast freezes releases.
whenOtherWins: 如果这是安全或合规的硬红线、根本不给出错预算，就别用 error budget 那套弹性说法。
options_en: So so we have a reliability goal, and if we we miss it too much then we we slow down the, the new features...
We set a 99.9% SLO, and the error budget is what's left — burn it too fast and we freeze feature launches.
We have a service level object of three nine, and when the budget of error is used up we stop to release.
An error budget denotes the permissible quantum of unreliability derived as one minus the service-level objective.
optionMeanings: so so / slow down 打转，没术语。
点名 SLO，烧完预算冻发版。
service level object 术语走形。
one minus SLO 书面腔念定义。
optionMeanings_en: Loops on "so so / slow down," no term.
Names SLO; burned budget freezes releases.
"Service level object" — term mangled.
"One minus SLO" recited like a definition.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方还在等你说出术语。
对方懂你用预算管发版节奏。
术语走形，像没真用过。
太正式，像念定义。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They're still waiting for the term.
They see you gate releases by the budget.
Mangled term; sounds unused.
Too formal — reciting a definition.
optionDirectness: 错在打转，零术语。
抓住 SLO 加烧预算冻发版。
错在术语走形，三九也含糊。
错在语域，书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: loops, no term at all.
Nails SLO plus freezing on a burned budget.
Wrong: mangled term, "three nine" too.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：给某个可靠性指标定的目标，比如 99.9% 的请求成功，是团队承诺守住的线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO is a target for a reliability metric, like 99.9% of requests succeeding — the line the team commits to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 错误预算：1 减 SLO 得到的允许出错额度，比如 SLO 99.9% 就有 0.1% 可以烧；烧完就该停发版、专注修可靠性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An error budget is the allowed unreliability, one minus the SLO; when it's spent you stop shipping features and focus on reliability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 烧预算：消耗错误预算，出错越多烧得越快；burn rate 太高就要冻结发版。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To burn the budget is to consume error budget; a high burn rate means too many errors and triggers a release freeze.

scenario: Convoke 面，问某个 pod 启动要预热缓存、怎么避免流量太早打进去。你想说 readiness 拦流量、liveness 管重启，但上次说成 "the alive check and the ready check"。
scenario_en: In a Convoke round you're asked how to keep traffic off a pod that warms caches at startup. You want to say readiness gates traffic and liveness restarts, but last time it came out as "the alive check and the ready check."
q: 想说「liveness 挂了就重启 pod，readiness 没就绪就从 LB 拉出来」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "liveness restarts a hung pod, readiness pulls it out of the LB pool until it can serve"?
options: Liveness restarts a hung pod; readiness tells the LB to stop sending traffic until it can actually serve.
We add a health check, the alive check and the ready check, when it not ready we not send the request.
So so we we check if it's okay, and if it's not we we take it out, take it out of the, the pool for a bit...
The liveness probe governs container restart while the readiness probe governs inclusion within the load-balancing rotation.
tradeoff: 重启 vs 拦流量：liveness 探针管重启卡死的 pod，readiness 探针管在就绪前不放流量进来。
why: 地道说法是 liveness 重启、readiness 拦流量：liveness probe 挂了就重启 pod，readiness probe 没就绪就把它从 LB 拉出来。
why_en: Liveness restarts a hung pod, readiness gates traffic — the readiness probe pulls the pod out of the LB pool until it can serve.
whenOtherWins: 如果 pod 启动就能立刻服务、没有预热阶段，只留 liveness 也行，不必强调 readiness。

So so we we check if it's okay, and if it's not we we take it out, take it out of the, the pool for a bit...
The liveness probe governs container restart while the readiness probe governs inclusion within the load-balancing rotation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活探针：探测容器是否卡死，探测失败就让编排器重启这个 pod。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A liveness probe checks whether a container is hung; if it fails, the orchestrator restarts the pod.

termDefinitions.meaning: 就绪探针：探测容器是否能开始服务，没就绪就把它从负载均衡池里拉出来、不发流量进去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A readiness probe checks whether a container can serve yet; until it passes, the pod is pulled from the LB pool and gets no traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Pod：Kubernetes 里最小的部署单元，通常裹着一个容器，是重启和调度的对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes, usually wrapping one container, and is the unit that gets restarted or scheduled.

scenario: Amazon 电话面，问一个慢下游在客户端已超时后还在干活怎么办。你想说在入口设 deadline 往下传、每一跳按剩余预算取消，但上次只会说 "each one has a timeout"。
scenario_en: In an Amazon phone screen you're asked what to do when a slow downstream keeps working after the client already timed out. You want to say you set a deadline at the edge and propagate it so each hop cancels on the remaining budget, but last time you only had "each one has a timeout."
q: 想说「入口设 deadline 往下传，每一跳按剩余预算取消」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "we set a deadline at the edge and propagate it, so each hop cancels on the remaining budget"?
options: So so we we set a timeout, and then the next one also, also has a timeout, so it it doesn't wait too long...
We pass the time-out down to the next service, so it knows how long time is remaining to do the work.
Each downstream invocation shall inherit the residual deadline such that no computation proceeds beyond the caller's temporal budget.
We set a deadline at the edge and propagate it down, so each hop cancels once the caller's budget is gone.
tradeoff: 传 deadline vs 各设各的超时：把入口 deadline 往下传，下游按剩余预算取消，不做调用方已放弃的活。
why: 地道说法是 propagate the deadline：在入口设一个 deadline 往下传，每一跳知道还剩多少时间，调用方放弃了就不再干活。
why_en: You propagate the deadline — set it at the edge and pass it down, so each hop knows the time left and cancels once the caller has given up.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单个调用、没有链路下游，普通 timeout 就够，不必上 deadline 传播那套。
options_en: So so we we set a timeout, and then the next one also, also has a timeout, so it it doesn't wait too long...
We pass the time-out down to the next service, so it knows how long time is remaining to do the work.
Each downstream invocation shall inherit the residual deadline such that no computation proceeds beyond the caller's temporal budget.
We set a deadline at the edge and propagate it down, so each hop cancels once the caller's budget is gone.

how long time remaining 中式表达。
inherit residual deadline 书面腔。
点名 propagate deadline，逐跳取消。

抓住传 deadline 加逐跳取消。

termDefinitions.meaning: 截止时间传播：在入口设一个绝对 deadline，沿调用链往下传，每个下游按剩余时间决定还做不做，超了就取消。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Deadline propagation sets an absolute deadline at the edge and passes it down the call chain, so each hop cancels when the time budget is gone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超时：一次调用等待响应的最长时间，超过就放弃；各设各的超时不如统一传 deadline 精准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A timeout is the max time a call waits before giving up; per-hop timeouts are less precise than one propagated deadline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一跳：调用链里的一次服务到服务的调用，链路越深跳数越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hop is one service-to-service call in the chain; deeper chains have more hops.

scenario: Pareto 面，问你怎么安全上线一个有风险的改动、还能快速回滚。你想说做 canary、先给 5% 流量再放量，但上次说成 "we open it to little user first"。
scenario_en: In a Pareto round you're asked how to ship a risky change safely with fast rollback. You want to say you run a canary, send 5% first and ramp up, but last time it came out as "we open it to little user first."
q: 想说「做 canary，先给新版本 5% 流量、盯 error rate、健康再放量」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic, watch error rates, then ramp up"?
options: We do a gray release, we open the new version to little user first and see if it is okay then open more.
We ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic to the new version, watch error rates, then ramp up.
So so we we put it out slowly, to some, some users first, and if it looks, looks fine then we we give it more...
A canary deployment shall route a limited fraction of traffic to the new revision prior to progressive promotion.
tradeoff: 灰度爬坡 vs 整体切换：canary 先放小流量再 ramp up，blue-green 一次切换、可秒级回滚。
why: 地道说法是 ship it as a canary：先给新版本 5% 流量、盯 error rate，健康了再 ramp up；blue-green 则是切流量、可秒回滚。
why_en: You ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic, watch the error rate, then ramp up; blue-green instead flips traffic for instant rollback.
whenOtherWins: 如果要的是一次切干净、能瞬间整体回滚，就说 blue-green flip，而不是慢慢 ramp 的 canary。
options_en: We do a gray release, we open the new version to little user first and see if it is okay then open more.
We ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic to the new version, watch error rates, then ramp up.
So so we we put it out slowly, to some, some users first, and if it looks, looks fine then we we give it more...
A canary deployment shall route a limited fraction of traffic to the new revision prior to progressive promotion.

so so / give it more 打转。
route traffic fraction 书面腔。

termDefinitions.meaning: 金丝雀发布：先把一小部分流量（如 5%）导到新版本，盯错误率和指标，健康了再逐步放量到全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canary deploy sends a small slice of traffic, like 5%, to the new version, watches the metrics, then ramps up if it's healthy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 蓝绿发布：同时维护旧（蓝）新（绿）两套环境，把负载均衡一次切到绿，出问题再切回蓝、秒级回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blue-green deploy keeps old (blue) and new (green) environments; you flip the load balancer to green and flip back for instant rollback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 放量：逐步把导向新版本的流量比例调高，从小流量一路加到全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To ramp up is to gradually raise the share of traffic going to the new version, from a small slice up to full.

scenario: WOP.com 面，问流量突增超过容量时你先丢什么。你想说 shed load、先丢 low-priority 请求保住核心，但上次绕成 "we drop some less important ones"。
scenario_en: In a WOP.com round you're asked what you drop first when traffic spikes past capacity. You want to say you shed load, dropping low-priority requests first to protect the core, but last time you circled on "we drop some less important ones."
q: 想说「过载时 shed load，先丢 low-priority 流量，保住 critical 请求」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "under overload we shed load — drop low-priority traffic first so the critical requests still get served"?
options: So so when it's too much, we we drop some, some of the traffic, the less important, less important ones first...
When overload we throw away the low level request first, keep the important request can still be served.
Under overload we shed load — drop the low-priority traffic first so the critical requests still get served.
Upon saturation the system shall preferentially reject requests of inferior priority to preserve critical-path throughput.
tradeoff: 按优先级丢 vs 一刀切拒绝：过载先丢 low-priority 请求、保住 critical path，而不是无差别拒掉所有人。
why: 地道说法是 shed load by priority：过载时先丢 low-priority 流量，比如后台或非付费请求，保住 critical 请求能被服务。
why_en: You shed load by priority — under overload you drop low-priority traffic first, like background or non-paying requests, so the critical ones still get served.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有请求同等重要、排不出优先级，就该均匀限流，而不是挑 low-priority 丢。
options_en: So so when it's too much, we we drop some, some of the traffic, the less important, less important ones first...
When overload we throw away the low level request first, keep the important request can still be served.
Under overload we shed load — drop the low-priority traffic first so the critical requests still get served.
Upon saturation the system shall preferentially reject requests of inferior priority to preserve critical-path throughput.

throw away / low level 术语走形。
点名 shed load，低优先级先被丢。
reject inferior priority 书面腔。

termDefinitions.meaning: 卸载/丢负载：过载时主动拒绝或丢弃一部分请求，别让系统被全量压垮；常按优先级先丢低优先级的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding deliberately drops or rejects some requests under overload so the system isn't crushed, usually shedding low-priority traffic first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低优先级流量：可以先牺牲的那批请求，比如后台任务、非付费或可稍后重试的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-priority traffic is the requests you can sacrifice first, like background jobs, non-paying, or retryable calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键路径：用户完成核心任务必须走通的请求，过载时要优先保住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the requests a user must complete for the core task; you protect these first under overload.

scenario: Alterion 系统设计面，问推荐服务突然变慢会不会拖垮下单。你想说非核心功能先降级、保住主流程能走，但上次说成 "we just turn off some some features I guess" 就卡住了。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round you're asked whether a slow recommendation service should drag down checkout. Last time you stalled at "we just turn off some some features I guess."
q: 想表达「非核心功能先降级、保住主流程可用」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "we degrade non-critical features first so the core flow stays up" out loud?
options: We degrade gracefully — turn off recommendations, but checkout keeps working.
We just turn off some some features I guess, so the important thing still work maybe.
So so if something's slow, we we kind of turn off, turn off some stuff, and the main thing, the main thing still runs...
Non-essential functional components shall be selectively disabled in order to preserve the availability of the primary transactional pathway.
tradeoff: 地道术语 graceful degradation + 具体例子 vs 大白话「turn off some features」：前者点名策略并给出真实取舍，后者听不出你有章法。
why: 术语是 graceful degradation：主动关掉非核心功能，保住核心流程可用。举一个具体例子（推荐 vs 下单）比抽象说 "turn off features" 更让人信服。
why_en: It's graceful degradation — turn off a non-critical piece like recommendations so the core flow, checkout, keeps working.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有功能都是核心、砍不掉任何一块，就该转向 "we'd rather shed load evenly" 而不是挑功能降级。
options_en: We degrade gracefully — turn off recommendations, but checkout keeps working.
We just turn off some some features I guess, so the important thing still work maybe.
So so if something's slow, we we kind of turn off, turn off some stuff, and the main thing, the main thing still runs...
Non-essential functional components shall be selectively disabled in order to preserve the availability of the primary transactional pathway.

大白话「some some features」，没有术语没有例子。
反复 “so so / turn off” 打转，半天没落地。
shall be selectively disabled 书面腔，像念规范。

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统压力大或依赖出问题时，主动关掉非核心功能，保住核心流程能继续用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation means deliberately turning off non-critical features under stress so the core flow keeps working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户完成关键任务（如下单、支付）必须走通的那条主流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The core flow (critical path) is the sequence a user must complete for the key task, like checkout or payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关掉也不影响核心任务完成的功能，比如推荐、个性化展示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-critical feature is one you can disable without blocking the core task, like recommendations or personalization.

scenario: Majestic Labs 系统设计面，问高负载下慢请求怎么办。你上次绕进 "the latency for the latency"、"we still have the latency" 的循环，没点出术语。
scenario_en: In a Majestic Labs system-design round you're asked about slow requests under load. Last time you looped on "the latency for the latency" and never named the term.
q: 想说「高负载下 p99 尾延迟飙升」，该怎么开口？
q_en: How do you say "p99 tail latency spikes under load" cleanly?
options: so the latency, the latency for the latency gets worse, the slow ones get slow when there's traffic...
Under the big load, the latency of the ninety-nine percent slowest requests becomes very high suddenly.
the slowest requests start to lag once traffic goes up, the tail end kind of gets bad over time.
Our p99 tail latency spikes under load, so I'd add a cache and shed load.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 复读打转："p99 tail latency spikes" 一句点名指标；"the latency for the latency" 是空转，暴露你没抓住尾延迟这个词。
why: 术语是 "p99 tail latency"——第 99 百分位的尾部延迟。带上负载触发和一个应对（cache / shed load），就把打转变成一句有指标的判断。
why_en: It's p99 tail latency — say "spikes under load" plus a fix like cache or shed load, and the loop becomes one metric-anchored line.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只关心平均体验、没追问尾部，直接说 "latency goes up under load" 就够，不必上 p99。
options_en: so the latency, the latency for the latency gets worse, the slow ones get slow when there's traffic...
Under the big load, the latency of the ninety-nine percent slowest requests becomes very high suddenly.
the slowest requests start to lag once traffic goes up, the tail end kind of gets bad over time.
Our p99 tail latency spikes under load, so I'd add a cache and shed load.
optionMeanings: 空转打转，反复说慢却没术语。
把 p99 硬翻成 ninety-nine percent，直译腔。
只说 tail end gets bad，没量化没应对。
点名指标 + 负载触发 + 一个具体应对。
optionMeanings_en: Spins in place, all slow, never a term.
Translates p99 as "ninety-nine percent" — calque.
Just "tail end gets bad," no number, no fix.
Names the metric, the trigger, and one fix.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你在原地绕，没锁定问题。
能懂，但一听就是逐字翻译。
对方不知你会怎么量、怎么救。

optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you circling, never pinning it.
Clear, but obviously word-for-word.
They don't know how you'd measure or fix it.
One line: metric, trigger, direction — seasoned.

错在直译，那不是英语说法。
错在含糊，没指标也没应对动作。
抓住尾延迟飙升加一个具体缓解。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: pure loop, says nothing.
Wrong: a calque, not how it's said.
Wrong: vague, no metric and no action.
Nails the tail-latency spike plus a mitigation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟：把请求延迟排序后第 99% 那个值，代表大多数用户里最慢的一批体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 is the 99th-percentile latency — the value below which 99% of requests fall, capturing the slow tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 尾延迟：延迟分布尾部（最慢那批请求）的延迟，常用 p99/p999 衡量，比平均更影响体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tail latency is the latency of the slowest requests in the distribution, usually measured at p99 or p999.

termDefinitions.meaning: 卸载/丢负载：过载时主动拒绝或降级一部分请求，保住其余请求的延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To shed load is to drop or reject some requests under overload so the rest stay fast.

scenario: Gamma 后端面，问你的系统怎么扩容。你上次反复说 "large scale system"、"the scaling scale of the system"，没落到具体机制。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round you're asked how your system scales. Last time you repeated "large scale system" and "the scaling scale of the system" without a mechanism.
q: 想说「加无状态节点、水平扩容抗流量」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "scale out with stateless nodes to handle traffic" out loud?
options: We scale out horizontally — add stateless nodes behind the load balancer as traffic grows.
We make the system bigger to handle more scale, so it can take the large scale of the traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 横向扩容：靠加更多机器/实例来提升容量，对应 scale up（纵向，换更强的单机）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To scale out is to add more machines to grow capacity, as opposed to scaling up a single stronger box.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无状态：节点自己不保存会话/数据，任何一台都能处理任意请求，所以可随意增删。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless node keeps no local session or data, so any node can serve any request and you can add or remove them freely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器：把进来的流量分发到后面多台节点，常缩写 LB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer spreads incoming traffic across the pool of backend nodes.

scenario: 系统设计面，问下游依赖挂了怎么避免雪崩。你想说熔断，但怕术语的搭配说错。
scenario_en: In a system-design round you're asked how to stop a dead dependency from cascading. You want to say "circuit breaker" but fear botching the collocation.
q: 想说「连续失败后熔断打开，停止打死掉的下游」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "the circuit breaker trips open after repeated failures and stops calling the dead dependency"?
options: when the other service is down, we just stop calling it for a while so it can recover somehow.
we open a circuit breaker to break the circuit when the calls are failing too much time.
The circuit breaker trips open after N failures, so we stop hammering a dead dependency.
so if it keeps failing, we sort of cut it off, we stop the calls, then later we try it again maybe.
tradeoff: 地道搭配 vs 生造搭配："trips open" 是熔断器的标准说法；"break the circuit ... too much time" 是硬凑，暴露你只听过词、没用过。
why: 标准搭配是 "the circuit breaker trips open"，不是 open/break a circuit。加一句停止打死掉的下游，就点出机制：连续失败后快速失败。
why_en: The collocation is "the circuit breaker trips open" — then "stop hammering a dead dependency" shows the mechanism: fail fast instead of pounding a dead service.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是偶发的一次失败、下游没挂，直接 retry 就行，不必上熔断这套。
options_en: when the other service is down, we just stop calling it for a while so it can recover somehow.
we open a circuit breaker to break the circuit when the calls are failing too much time.
The circuit breaker trips open after N failures, so we stop hammering a dead dependency.
so if it keeps failing, we sort of cut it off, we stop the calls, then later we try it again maybe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 熔断器：一种容错模式，某依赖连续失败超过阈值就「打开」，短路后续调用，直接快速失败，给下游喘息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker is a fault-tolerance pattern that stops calling a failing dependency once errors cross a threshold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 熔断跳开：熔断器从闭合（正常放行）切到打开（拦截调用）的动作，是它的标准动词搭配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: "Trips open" is the standard phrase for a circuit breaker switching from closed to open and blocking calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖：你的服务要调用的下游服务或组件，它挂了会拖累你。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dependency is a downstream service your code calls; if it fails, it can drag you down too.

scenario: WOP.com 支付方向面，问重试导致重复扣款怎么办。你想说幂等 + 退避重试，但怕说成口水话。
scenario_en: In a WOP.com payments round you're asked how to stop retries from double-charging. You want to say idempotent plus backoff without turning it into mush.
q: 想说「重试加指数退避，并做成幂等，双重提交变成无操作」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "retry with exponential backoff and make it idempotent so a double-submit is a no-op"?
options: we retry it again, and we make it so the retry doesn't do it twice by accident, like a double charge.
so we try again, and then again, and we wait a bit each time, and we make sure it doesn't, um, double.
The retry mechanism shall be rendered idempotent such that duplicate submissions produce no effect at all.
We retry with exponential backoff and make it idempotent, so a double-submit is a no-op.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 绕圈解释："idempotent ... a no-op" 一句到位；"doesn't do it twice by accident" 是在绕着解释幂等，暴露你没这个词。
why: 术语是 "idempotent" 和 "exponential backoff"，收尾用无操作证明你懂机制：重试安全、退避不打垮下游，而不是用大白话绕。
why_en: Say "idempotent" and "exponential backoff," close with "a double-submit is a no-op" — the term proves the mechanism instead of talking around it.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作本身就只读、无副作用，直接 retry 即可，不必强调幂等或退避。
options_en: we retry it again, and we make it so the retry doesn't do it twice by accident, like a double charge.
so we try again, and then again, and we wait a bit each time, and we make sure it doesn't, um, double.
The retry mechanism shall be rendered idempotent such that duplicate submissions produce no effect at all.
We retry with exponential backoff and make it idempotent, so a double-submit is a no-op.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一操作执行一次和执行多次结果一样，所以重试或重复提交不会造成二次副作用（如重复扣款）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation has the same effect whether it runs once or many times, so retries can't double-charge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指数退避：每次重试等待时间成倍增长（如 1s、2s、4s），避免失败时一拥而上把下游压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait between retries so a struggling dependency isn't hammered by a retry storm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 空操作：一次不产生任何效果的调用；幂等下的重复提交就变成 no-op。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A no-op is a call that has no effect; under idempotency a duplicate submit becomes a no-op.

scenario: Gamma 后端面，问一个分片挂了会不会拖垮整个集群。你想说「把它隔离开，爆炸半径只到一个分片，不会波及整个 fleet」，但 blast radius 这个词想不起来，说成 “it doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully”。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round you're asked whether one bad shard takes down the whole cluster. You want to say you isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet, but the term won't come and it comes out as "it doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully."
q: 想说「把故障隔离开，爆炸半径只限一个分片，不会波及整个 fleet」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet"?
options: It doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully, because we kind of keep it in its own place.
So so if one shard, one shard breaks, it it stays there, it doesn't go, doesn't go to the other ones, I think...
Fault isolation mechanisms are implemented such that the scope of impact is confined to a singular partition.
We isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet.
tradeoff: 地道术语 blast radius vs 含糊「hopefully it doesn't spread」：前者一句话点名隔离范围，后者听着像在祈祷而不是设计。
why: 术语是 blast radius：一次故障最多能波及的范围。配一句「只限一个分片、不波及整个 fleet」，就点出隔离的边界在哪。
why_en: The term is blast radius — the scope one failure can reach. Pairing it with "one shard, not the whole fleet" names the isolation boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果分片强耦合、隔离不了，就该说 "it could still ripple"，别硬套 blast radius。

termDefinitions.meaning: 爆炸半径：一次故障最多能波及到的范围，范围越小说明隔离做得越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blast radius is the scope a single failure can reach; a smaller radius means better isolation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把故障限制在一个组件或分片内，不让它蔓延到其他部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To isolate a failure is to contain it to one component or shard so it can't spread further.

termDefinitions.meaning: 舱壁模式：把资源（连接池、线程池）按组件分开，一个组件耗尽资源不会拖垮其他组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The bulkhead pattern partitions resources like connection or thread pools per component, so one exhausting its pool doesn't sink the rest.

scenario: Alterion 系统设计面，面试官问「你这块用什么隔离级别，为什么」。你想说读已提交够快但会有不可重复读、要强一致就上可串行化，但一紧张就卡在术语上。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round the interviewer asks what isolation level you'd use and why. You want to contrast read-committed with serializable but freeze on the terms.
q: 想表达「读已提交只看到已提交行但两次读可能不同，可串行化像事务一个个跑」，怎么说出口？
q_en: You want to say "read-committed only sees committed rows but reads can differ, serializable acts as if transactions ran one at a time." How do you say it?
options: So read commit level, it only reads the commit data, and serializable is the most strong isolate level, yeah.
At read-committed you only see committed rows, but two reads can differ; serializable makes it look like transactions ran one at a time.
So the isolation, the isolation level is like how much the transactions can see each other, so read committed is one level and serializable is a higher one, right.
Read-committed permits non-repeatable reads, whereas serializable precludes all concurrency anomalies by enforcing a strictly serial execution order.
tradeoff: 术语加机制 vs 卡壳：地道版一句点到「读已提交能变、可串行化像单线跑」；卡壳版要么术语说歪，要么打转，要么书面腔。
why: 术语是 read-committed 和 serializable：前者只看已提交行但两次读可不同，后者表现得像事务一个接一个跑，一句话就点透强弱。
why_en: The terms are read-committed and serializable — one sees only committed rows but reads can differ, the other behaves as if transactions ran one at a time.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是泛泛说「我们要强一致」、面试官没追隔离级别，直接说 "we need strong consistency here" 也够，不必展开级别名。

At read-committed you only see committed rows, but two reads can differ; serializable makes it look like transactions ran one at a time.
So the isolation, the isolation level is like how much the transactions can see each other, so read committed is one level and serializable is a higher one, right.
Read-committed permits non-repeatable reads, whereas serializable precludes all concurrency anomalies by enforcing a strictly serial execution order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 隔离级别之一：一个事务只能读到别的事务已提交的数据，但同一事务里两次读同一行可能拿到不同值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-committed is an isolation level where a transaction only sees data other transactions have committed, but two reads of the same row can differ.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强隔离级别：并发事务的最终结果等价于它们按某种顺序一个接一个执行，杜绝并发异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable is the strongest isolation level, where concurrent transactions produce the same result as if they ran one at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一事务里两次读同一行拿到不同结果，因为中间别人改并提交了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-repeatable read is when the same row read twice in one transaction returns different values because another transaction changed it in between.

scenario: Convoke 系统设计面，你说要给查询字段建索引。面试官问「不建索引会怎样」。你想说有 B-tree 索引就能按序定位、没有就得全表扫，但上次说成「scan all the table」卡了一下。
scenario_en: In a Convoke design round you add an index on a query column. The interviewer asks "what if there's no index?" You want to contrast a B-tree seek with a full table scan.
q: 想表达「有 B-tree 索引就 log 时间定位到行、没有就退化成全表扫每行都读」，怎么说？
q_en: You want to say "a B-tree index seeks to the rows in log time, without one it falls back to a full table scan reading every row." How do you say it?
options: With a B-tree index it seeks to the rows in log time; without one it falls back to a full table scan and reads every row.
Without index we have to scan all the table, but with the B tree it's a tree so it's faster to find, you know.
So the index, the index helps us find, so if we have it we don't read everything, and if we don't have it we we read more rows, so yeah it's slower.
In the absence of a B-tree index the engine must perform a sequential full table scan, whereas the index enables logarithmic-time traversal to the target rows.
tradeoff: 术语加机制 vs 卡壳：地道版点到「B-tree 按序 log 时间定位、否则全表扫」；卡壳版要么 Chinglish「scan all the table」，要么打转，要么书面腔。
why: 术语是 B-tree index 和 full table scan：有索引就 log 时间定位，没有就每行都读。
why_en: The terms are B-tree index and full table scan — with the index you seek in log time, without it you read every row.
whenOtherWins: 如果还没到索引层面，先说 "this lookup is slow, we should index it" 就够。

Without index we have to scan all the table, but with the B tree it's a tree so it's faster to find, you know.
So the index, the index helps us find, so if we have it we don't read everything, and if we don't have it we we read more rows, so yeah it's slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种平衡树结构的索引，把键按序组织，查找、范围扫描都能在对数时间内定位到目标行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index is a balanced-tree structure that keeps keys in sorted order so lookups and range scans reach the target rows in logarithmic time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有可用索引时，数据库只能从头到尾把整张表每一行都读一遍来找匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full table scan reads every row of a table from start to finish because no usable index exists to jump straight to the matches.

scenario: Meridian 系统设计面，你说给 email 字段建了个索引。面试官问「按它查和按主键查有什么不同」。你想说走二级索引要回主键再取整行、多一跳，但一时找不到「回表」的说法。

q: 想表达「走二级索引要回到主键再取整行，比直接按主键查多一跳」，怎么说出口？
q_en: You want to say "a secondary-index lookup hops back to the primary key to fetch the full row, one extra step versus keying on the primary key directly." How do you say it?
options: So the second index, we use the second key to find, and then, and then we go to find the row, so it's like two times, yeah.
A secondary-index lookup resolves the primary key and then performs a second access to retrieve the complete row, incurring an additional traversal.
The second key points to the primary, so we look twice, one for the index and one for the primary key to get the row.
A secondary-index lookup hops back to the primary key to fetch the full row, so it's one extra step versus keying on the primary key directly.

why: 术语是 secondary index 和 primary key：走二级索引先拿主键、再回去取整行，比按主键多一跳。
why_en: The terms are secondary index and primary key — a secondary lookup resolves the primary key first, then fetches the row, one extra hop.
whenOtherWins: 如果只想说「这字段也能查」，先说 "we can also look it up by email" 就够。

The second key points to the primary, so we look twice, one for the index and one for the primary key to get the row.
A secondary-index lookup hops back to the primary key to fetch the full row, so it's one extra step versus keying on the primary key directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建在非主键字段上的索引，条目里存的是主键；按它查通常要拿主键再回去取整行，也就是回表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A secondary index is built on a non-primary-key column and stores the primary key, so a lookup usually fetches the primary key then goes back for the full row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识一行的键；很多存储引擎按主键把行聚簇存放，按主键查能直接定位到整行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary key uniquely identifies a row, and many engines cluster rows by it so a primary-key lookup reaches the whole row directly.

scenario: Nexworth 系统设计面，你把用户名冗余存进了订单表。面试官问「为什么不做规范化」。你想说反规范化让读不用 join、代价是写要多处同步，但一时说不清这个取舍。
scenario_en: In a Nexworth design round you copied the username into the orders table. The interviewer asks why you didn't normalize. You want to name the read/write tradeoff of denormalizing.
q: 想表达「反规范化让读不用 join，代价是一次写要更新好几处同一字段」，怎么说出口？
q_en: You want to say "denormalizing lets reads skip the joins, but a write then has to update the same field in several places." How do you say it?
options: So we make the data not normal, so the read is faster, and the write is, the write we need to change more, more place, yeah.
Denormalization introduces redundancy that accelerates reads by eliminating joins, at the expense of write amplification across duplicated copies.
We denormalize so reads skip the joins, but then a write has to update the same field in several places.
So normalize or denormalize, it's a tradeoff, the read and the write, so if we denormalize the read is better but the write, the write has some cost, right.
tradeoff: 术语加机制 vs 卡壳：地道版点到「反规范化读免 join、写要多处同步」；卡壳版要么 Chinglish「not normal」，要么书面腔，要么原地打转。
why: 术语是 denormalize：故意冗余让读跳过 join，代价是一次写要更新好几处同一字段。
why_en: The term is denormalize — you duplicate on purpose so reads skip joins, and pay by updating the same field in several places on writes.
whenOtherWins: 如果只想说「读多写少所以优化读」，先说 "it's read-heavy so we optimize reads" 也够。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆成不重复的表、用外键关联，避免冗余；读取时往往要 join 多张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To normalize is to split data into non-duplicated tables linked by keys, avoiding redundancy but often requiring joins to read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 故意把同一份数据冗余存进多处，让读取不用 join，代价是写入要同步更新每一份副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To denormalize is to duplicate data across places so reads avoid joins, at the cost of updating every copy on writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询时按关联键把多张表的行拼到一起，表越多、数据越大越慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables on a matching key at query time, and gets slower as tables and data grow.

scenario: Playground 电面，面试官问「每个请求都新开数据库连接会怎样、你怎么改」。你想说维护一个连接池、每个请求借一条复用，而不是每次新建，但一时说不利索。
scenario_en: In a Playground phone screen the interviewer asks what happens if you open a new DB connection per request and how you'd fix it. You want to describe a connection pool.
q: 想表达「维护一个连接池、每请求借一条用完还回去，而不是每次新建连接」，怎么说出口？
q_en: You want to say "we keep a connection pool and borrow one per request instead of opening a new connection every time." How do you say it?
options: So we do the connect pool, we pool the connect, so we don't open the connect every time, we reuse it, yeah.
We keep a pool of open connections and borrow one per request, instead of opening a new one every time.
So opening a connection every time is slow, so we we keep some connections, and when a request come we we give it one, and then it give back.
A connection pool maintains a set of pre-established database connections that are leased to requests, thereby amortizing connection setup overhead.
tradeoff: 术语加机制 vs 卡壳：地道版点到「连接池借一条复用、不每次新建」；卡壳版要么 Chinglish「pool the connect」，要么打转，要么书面腔。
why: 术语是 connection pool：预先开一批连接放池里，每请求借一条用完还回去，省掉每次建连的开销。一句话点出复用机制。
why_en: The term is connection pool — keep a set of open connections and borrow one per request instead of opening a new one every time.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只想听「建连很贵所以要复用」这个方向，先说 "opening connections is expensive, so we reuse them" 也够。

We keep a pool of open connections and borrow one per request, instead of opening a new one every time.
So opening a connection every time is slow, so we we keep some connections, and when a request come we we give it one, and then it give back.
A connection pool maintains a set of pre-established database connections that are leased to requests, thereby amortizing connection setup overhead.
