termDefinitions.meaning: 在预训练模型上用领域数据继续训练，改变模型权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-tuning continues training a pretrained model on domain data, changing its weights.

scenario: grounding 上下文里拼了 20 段材料，关键那一段正好排在正中间。检索日志显示它确实被召回了，模型却答错了。
scenario_en: Twenty passages were packed into the grounding context and the key one sits right in the middle; retrieval logs confirm it was returned, yet the model still answered wrong.
q: 这最可能是什么现象，该怎么缓解？
q_en: What phenomenon is this most likely, and how do you mitigate it?
options: 是 embedding 模型不够好：关键段的向量表示不准，应该换一个更强的检索模型重新灌库
是 lost in the middle：模型对上下文首尾的信息用得最好，正中间那段最容易被忽略
是 tokenizer 把中间那段截断了：超出 context window 的部分被静默丢弃，模型根本没看到
是采样温度太高导致输出随机：把 temperature 调到 0，同样的上下文就能稳定答对了
options_en: The embedding model is too weak: the key passage's vector is off, so swap in a stronger retriever and reindex.
It's lost in the middle: models use information at the start and end of a context best and most easily overlook the middle.
The tokenizer truncated that passage: anything past the context window is silently dropped, so the model never saw it.
Sampling temperature is too high: set temperature to 0 and the same context will answer correctly every time.
why: 研究发现模型在长上下文上的准确率呈 U 形——信息在开头或结尾时最好、在中间时最差；缓解是重排后把最相关的放首尾，并压掉无关段。
why_en: Research shows accuracy over long contexts follows a U shape, best at the start and end and worst in the middle, so rerank the most relevant passage to an edge and drop the filler.
optionMeanings: 归因为检索质量问题。
归因为长上下文的位置效应。
归因为超窗被截断。
归因为解码随机性。
optionMeanings_en: Blames retrieval quality.
Blames the positional effect in long contexts.
Blames truncation past the window.
Blames decoding randomness.
optionDirectness: 当关键段根本没被召回时才是这个原因。
当日志显示已召回、位置又在中段时的典型解释。
当总 token 确实超过窗口上限时才成立。
当同一份输入多次运行结果不稳定时才是它。
optionDirectness_en: The right cause only when the key passage was never retrieved.
The typical explanation when logs show it was retrieved and it sits mid-context.
Holds only if total tokens really exceeded the window.
That's the cause only when repeated runs on the same input disagree.
optionScenarioImpacts: 重灌一次全库，位置效应原封不动，问题照旧。
改成重排加裁剪，关键段被顶到首尾，答案就稳了。
去查窗口用量会发现远没超，排查方向白走一趟。
温度归零只是让错误答案变得更稳定地错。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You reindex everything, the positional effect survives, and the bug remains.
Reranking and trimming push the key passage to an edge and the answer stabilizes.
Checking window usage shows you're nowhere near the limit — a wasted investigation.
Zero temperature just makes the wrong answer wrong more consistently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长上下文里位于中段的信息最容易被模型忽略，准确率随位置呈 U 形。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lost in the middle describes how models most easily overlook information placed mid-context, with accuracy forming a U shape by position.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本切成 token 的组件，决定同一段话占多少 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tokenizer splits text into tokens and decides how many tokens a passage costs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 采样温度，控制生成的随机性，0 表示每次都取最高概率的词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temperature controls sampling randomness, where zero always picks the highest-probability token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本压成稠密向量的表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is the dense vector representation of text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对检索回来的候选再打一次分，把最相关的顶到最前面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reranking rescores the retrieved candidates so the most relevant ones move to the top.

scenario: 我在 Meta 砍掉了 onboarding 里的低价值字段，AI agent 的回答质量没有下降。面试官问：「输入信息变少了，凭什么质量不掉？」
scenario_en: I removed low-value onboarding fields at Meta and the AI agent's answer quality held. The interviewer asked why quality didn't drop when the input shrank.
q: 该怎么解释这件事？
q_en: How should I explain that?
options: 因为我们同时换了更强的基础模型，模型能力的提升刚好抵消了输入信息量的减少
因为 A/B 测试的 treatment 组质量没有显著回归，既然指标没动，说明砍字段本来就无所谓
因为剩下的字段做了摘要压缩，总信息量其实没变，只是换成了一种更省 token 的表达方式
被砍的字段多半是空值或默认值；context 更短更干净，grounding 看的是质量不是字段数
options_en: We swapped in a stronger base model at the same time, and the capability gain offset the lost input.
The A/B treatment showed no significant regression, and since the metric didn't move, cutting fields never mattered.
The remaining fields were summarized, so total information is unchanged — just expressed in fewer tokens.
The removed fields were mostly empty or default; a shorter, cleaner context still grounds well because quality beats field count.
tradeoff: 减字段 vs 保全量：减字段换来更短更干净的上下文和更低的填写摩擦，代价是必须先拿实验证明质量没有回归。
why: 被砍的字段本来就没携带独有事实，去掉它们只是去掉噪声；grounding 靠的是信息质量，而不是塞进去多少个字段。
why_en: Those fields carried no unique facts, so removing them removed noise, and grounding depends on the quality of the information rather than the number of fields.
whenOtherWins: 如果被砍的字段里有真正独有的事实（比如退货政策原文），那减字段就是在挖掉 grounding，质量一定会掉。
optionMeanings: 把结果归因为换模型。
把实验结论当成解释本身。
声称信息量守恒、只是换了表达。
指出被砍字段本就没有独有信息。
optionMeanings_en: Attributes the result to a model swap.
Treats the experiment's conclusion as the explanation.
Claims information was conserved, only re-expressed.
Points out the removed fields carried no unique information.
optionDirectness: 只有当模型版本确实同期变更时才成立，也毁掉了归因。
指标没动是结果，回答不了「为什么」这个问题。
当确实做了摘要压缩、而不是直接删除时才对。
当被删字段以空值和默认值为主时的真实原因。
optionDirectness_en: Only true if the model version really changed at the same time, which also destroys attribution.
A flat metric is the outcome; it doesn't answer why.
Right only if fields were summarized rather than deleted outright.
The real reason when the deleted fields were mostly empty or default values.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同时动两个变量，实验结论直接不可信。
面试官会追问「所以机制是什么」，我又回到原点。
和事实不符：那些字段是删掉的，不是压缩的。
把产品动作和 grounding 机制连起来，追问也接得住。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Changing two variables at once makes the experiment's conclusion untrustworthy.
They'll ask what the mechanism was and I'm back where I started.
It contradicts the facts: those fields were deleted, not compressed.
It links the product move to the grounding mechanism and survives follow-ups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让回答建立在提供的上下文事实上，而不是模型凭空生成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounding means answers are built on the facts provided in context rather than invented.

termDefinitions.meaning: A/B 实验里接受新方案的那一组，对照组叫 control。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The treatment is the A/B group receiving the new version, contrasted with the control group.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求里喂给模型的全部文本：指令、检索材料和用户输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context is all the text handed to the model in one request: instructions, retrieved material, and user input.

scenario: 教练在复盘里特意教了这组词：面试里说得出「harness」这个词，对方立刻知道你在这一行里待过。
scenario_en: My coach taught this vocabulary on purpose: saying the word "harness" in an interview immediately signals you've actually worked in this space.
q: LLM、harness、agent 这三个词分别指什么？
q_en: What exactly do the words LLM, harness, and agent each refer to?
text: 模型本身只会生成{{下一个 token}}；围在它周围的那一圈上下文、工具描述和调用循环叫 {{harness}}（马具）——有了它才能驾着模型跑向你要的方向。今天的 agent 基本都是{{多轮}}对话循环：一轮解决不了就把新信息接到对话末尾再来一轮。
text_en: The model itself only generates the {{next token}}; the ring of context, tool descriptions, and the calling loop around it is the {{harness}}, which is what lets you steer the model where you want. Today's agents are essentially {{multi-turn}} loops: when one turn isn't enough, new information is appended and another turn runs.
why: 把 LLM 和它外面那一圈分开说，就能干净地回答「你们的 agent 是什么」——模型是引擎，harness 才是我作为工程师真正在设计的东西。
why_en: Separating the model from the ring around it lets me answer "what is your agent" cleanly: the model is the engine, and the harness is what I as an engineer actually design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，本质是根据已有文本预测下一个 token 的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM stands for large language model, a model that predicts the next token from the text so far.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包在模型外面的那层工程：上下文组装、工具描述、调用循环和终止条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The harness is the engineering layer around the model: context assembly, tool descriptions, the calling loop, and stopping conditions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型切分文本的最小单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit a model splits text into.

scenario: 系统设计轮里我说了句「这听起来像一个 agent flow」，面试官接着问：「那你怎么定义 agent？」我需要一句不靠画图的定义。
scenario_en: In the design round I said "this sounds like an agent flow" and the interviewer asked how I define an agent — I need a one-line definition that doesn't rely on a diagram.
q: 怎么用一句话把 agent 和一问一答的 chatbot 区分开？
q_en: In one sentence, how do you separate an agent from a one-shot chatbot?
options: agent 是参数量更大的模型，能力更强所以能处理更复杂的任务，chatbot 用的是小模型
agent 一定是多个模型协同工作的系统，单个模型无论怎么包装都只能算 chatbot
agent 在 harness 里多轮循环：模型可要求调工具，结果回填进对话再继续，直到出终答
agent 就是能联网的 chatbot，区别只在于有没有接上搜索引擎这一个具体的能力
options_en: An agent is a bigger model, so it handles harder tasks, while a chatbot runs on a small one.
An agent is always several models working together; a single model can only ever be a chatbot.
An agent loops in a harness: the model can request tools, results are appended, and it continues until a final answer.
An agent is just a chatbot with internet access; the only difference is whether a search engine is attached.
tradeoff: 多轮 agent 循环 vs 单轮问答：多轮能自己去补缺失的信息，代价是延迟、token 成本和失控风险都随轮数放大。
why: 区别不在模型大小也不在模型个数，而在控制流：agent 允许模型在一次任务里反复要工具、把结果接回对话，直到自己判断可以收尾。
why_en: The difference isn't model size or model count but control flow: an agent lets the model keep asking for tools and folding results back into the conversation until it decides it can finish.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务一轮就能答完（固定 FAQ 查询、格式转换），套上 agent 循环只是白白多花延迟和 token。
optionMeanings: 用模型规模区分。
用模型个数区分。
用控制流与工具循环区分。
用是否联网区分。
optionMeanings_en: Distinguishes by model size.
Distinguishes by number of models.
Distinguishes by control flow and the tool loop.
Distinguishes by internet access.
optionDirectness: 同一个模型既能当 chatbot 也能当 agent，规模不是判据。
单模型加工具循环已经是 agent，多模型只是一种实现。
抓住了「谁决定下一步」这个真正的分界线。
联网只是众多工具里的一个，不构成定义。
optionDirectness_en: The same model can be either, so size isn't the criterion.
One model plus a tool loop already is an agent; multiple models is just one implementation.
It captures the real dividing line: who decides the next step.
Web access is one tool among many, not a definition.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官再追一句「那我把模型换小就不是 agent 了？」就答不下去。
会被反问「单 agent 加工具算不算」，定义立刻破。
接得住下一问「循环什么时候停」，也自然接到工具设计。
把一个具体能力当成范畴定义，显得只用过表层。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: One follow-up — "so a smaller model stops being an agent?" — and the answer collapses.
They'll ask whether one model plus tools counts, and the definition breaks immediately.
It sets up the next question about when the loop stops and leads naturally into tool design.
Treating one capability as the category definition reads as surface-level exposure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包在模型外面的上下文组装、工具描述和调用循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The harness is the context assembly, tool descriptions, and calling loop wrapped around the model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能在多轮循环里自己决定调用工具、并根据结果继续推进的 LLM 应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is an LLM application that decides on its own to call tools across multiple turns and keeps going based on the results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一问一答、不主动调用外部工具的对话应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chatbot answers one question at a time without initiating external tool calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型切分文本的最小单位，直接对应成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest text unit a model processes and maps directly to cost.

scenario: PropTech agentic 岗（Daisy 那轮）面试官说「我们的 agentic 系统已经相当成熟」，点名问 LangChain、LangSmith、LangGraph。我当时完全接不上。
scenario_en: In the PropTech agentic screen the interviewer said "we're quite advanced with our agentic system" and named LangChain, LangSmith and LangGraph. I had nothing.
q: 这三个东西该怎么各用一句话区分开？
q_en: How do you tell these three apart in one line each?
options: LangChain 搭 agent、LangSmith 做 tracing 与评估、LangGraph 是有状态图运行时
LangChain 是一个向量数据库、LangSmith 是它的托管云服务、LangGraph 是可视化流程图编辑器
三者是同一个库的三个版本号，LangGraph 最新，用最新那个就行，功能都是向后兼容的
LangChain 是模型供应商的 SDK、LangSmith 是提示词交易市场、LangGraph 是模型微调工具链
options_en: LangChain builds the agent, LangSmith does tracing and evaluation, LangGraph is the stateful graph runtime.
LangChain is a vector database, LangSmith is its managed cloud service, and LangGraph is a visual flowchart editor.
They're three version numbers of one library; LangGraph is newest, so just use it since everything is backward compatible.
LangChain is a model vendor's SDK, LangSmith is a prompt marketplace, and LangGraph is a fine-tuning toolchain.
tradeoff: 用框架 vs 直接调模型 SDK：框架给现成的工具调用协议和追踪能力，代价是多一层抽象，出问题要穿透它去 debug。
why: 一句话版本：LangChain 是搭 agent 的上层接口，LangGraph 是它底下那台有状态的图运行时，LangSmith 负责把每一次调用记录下来做评估。
why_en: The one-liner is that LangChain is the high-level interface for building agents, LangGraph is the stateful graph runtime underneath it, and LangSmith records every call for evaluation.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方的栈上根本没有 LangChain（自研 harness 或直接调模型 SDK），硬扯这三个名字反而像只会背框架名。
optionMeanings: 按「搭建、观测、运行时」三层分工。
把它们说成存储与云服务。
把它们当成同一个库的版本演进。
把它们说成供应商 SDK 与训练工具。
optionMeanings_en: Splits them into build, observe, and runtime layers.
Describes them as storage and a cloud service.
Treats them as versions of one library.
Describes them as a vendor SDK and training tooling.
optionDirectness: 对方在这套栈上做产品、想确认你能聊起来时的正解。
向量库是另一类组件，和这三个都不重叠。
三者是并存的独立组件，不是版本关系。
微调和提示词市场都不是这三个做的事。
optionDirectness_en: The right answer when they build on this stack and want to know you can hold a conversation.
A vector database is a separate category and overlaps none of the three.
They coexist as separate components, not as versions.
Neither fine-tuning nor a prompt marketplace is what any of them does.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻知道我至少读过文档，接得住后面的架构讨论。
一句就露馅：把编排框架说成了存储层。
会被追问「那你用的是哪个版本」，当场收不了场。
答案和事实无关，等于确认了这块完全空白。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They immediately know I've at least read the docs and can follow the architecture talk.
One line gives it away: calling an orchestration framework a storage layer.
They'll ask which version I used and there's no way to recover.
The answer is unrelated to reality and confirms the gap outright.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建 LLM 应用与 agent 的上层框架，提供统一的工具调用与模型抽象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangChain is the high-level framework for building LLM applications and agents with a unified tool-calling and model abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: LangChain 的可观测与评估平台，记录每次调用的输入输出用于调试和打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangSmith is the observability and evaluation platform that records each call's inputs and outputs for debugging and scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有状态的图式运行时：节点是函数、边是状态转移，支持 checkpoint 与人工介入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangGraph is a stateful graph runtime where nodes are functions and edges are transitions, with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop support.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次调用链路上的每一步记录下来，用于排查和评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tracing records every step along one call path so it can be debugged and evaluated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 软件开发工具包，供应商提供的调用其服务的官方库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SDK stands for software development kit, a vendor's official library for calling their service.

scenario: action item：动手写一个至少带一次工具调用的最小 agent，目标是面试里能在 60 秒内说清 LangChain 是什么、我用它做了什么。
scenario_en: Action item: build a minimal agent with at least one tool call, so I can explain in 60 seconds what LangChain is and what I built with it.
q: LangChain 1.0 之后的最小心智模型是什么？
q_en: What is the minimal mental model of LangChain after 1.0?
text: 用 {{create_agent}} 把一个模型和一组 {{tool}} 组装成 agent；它跑在 {{LangGraph}} 运行时上——节点是函数、边是状态转移，checkpoint、流式输出和人工介入都建在这几个概念之上；想在循环中间插手就用 {{middleware}}（日志、护栏、重试）。
text_en: Use {{create_agent}} to assemble a model plus a set of {{tool}} objects into an agent; it runs on the {{LangGraph}} runtime where nodes are functions and edges are transitions, with checkpointing, streaming and human-in-the-loop built on those ideas; to intervene mid-loop you use {{middleware}} for logging, guardrails and retries.
why: 60 秒版本就是这一句：模型加工具组装成 agent，跑在一个图运行时上，需要插手的地方用中间件——不用背整个 API 列表。
why_en: The sixty-second version is exactly this: a model plus tools assembled into an agent, running on a graph runtime, with middleware where you need to intervene — no API list memorization required.

termDefinitions.meaning: LangChain 1.0 里把模型和工具组装成 agent 的入口函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: create_agent is the LangChain 1.0 entry point that assembles a model and tools into an agent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带类型 schema 的外部能力，模型可以选择调用它并读回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tool is an external capability with a typed schema that the model can choose to call and read results from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 插在 agent 循环各阶段的钩子，用来做日志、改提示、加护栏或重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Middleware are hooks inserted into stages of the agent loop for logging, prompt shaping, guardrails, or retries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把图运行时的状态存下来，使流程能暂停、恢复或回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint persists the graph runtime's state so a run can pause, resume, or roll back.

scenario: Daisy 那轮面试官把 Temporal 介绍成他们基础设施的核心，我当场把它误认成了「一个 markdown 文件」。
scenario_en: In the Daisy screen the interviewer introduced Temporal as core infrastructure, and I mistook it for "a markdown file" on the spot.
q: Temporal 一句话是什么东西？
q_en: In one sentence, what is Temporal?
options: 一个消息队列：生产者投递任务、消费者拉取执行，靠重试和死信队列保证任务最终不丢
一个定时任务调度器：按 cron 表达式在指定时刻触发作业，失败了按重试策略自动重跑
持久化执行引擎：每一步记进 event history，崩溃后重放历史恢复现场
一个容器编排平台：把长任务打包成 pod 调度到集群上，节点挂了就在别的节点重新拉起来
options_en: A message queue: producers enqueue tasks, consumers pull and execute, with retries and a dead-letter queue so nothing is lost.
A cron scheduler: it fires jobs at specified times by expression and reruns them by retry policy on failure.
A durable execution engine: each step is written to an event history and replayed after a crash to restore state.
A container orchestrator: it packages long jobs as pods onto a cluster and reschedules them elsewhere when a node dies.
tradeoff: Temporal vs 队列加重试：Temporal 保住的是「跑到一半的进度」，代价是工作流代码必须确定性可重放，还多一套服务要运维。
why: 队列保的是「这条消息还在」，Temporal 保的是「这个流程执行到第几步、拿到过哪些结果」——崩溃后不用从头再跑一遍。
why_en: A queue guarantees the message still exists, while Temporal guarantees the workflow's progress and past results survive, so a crash doesn't send you back to step one.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务只跑几秒、失败了整体重试也没有副作用，一个带重试的队列就够了，没必要引入一整套编排引擎。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["workflow 开始执行"] --> B["每步写入 event history"]
  B --> C["进程崩溃"]
  C --> D["worker 重放 history"]
  D --> E["恢复到崩溃前状态 继续执行"]
optionMeanings: 把它理解成消息中间件。
把它理解成定时触发器。
把它理解成可重放的执行引擎。
把它理解成集群调度层。
optionMeanings_en: Reads it as message middleware.
Reads it as a time-based trigger.
Reads it as a replayable execution engine.
Reads it as a cluster scheduling layer.
optionDirectness: 队列保消息不丢，但不保流程执行到哪一步。
cron 决定「什么时候开始」，管不了「中途崩了怎么办」。
抓住了 durable execution 这个核心概念。
编排的是进程和容器，不是业务流程的中间状态。
optionDirectness_en: A queue keeps the message but not the workflow's position.
Cron decides when to start, not what happens after a mid-run crash.
It captures the core idea of durable execution.
It schedules processes and containers, not a business workflow's intermediate state.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方会追问「那跑了一半的状态怎么办」，答不上来。
把长流程的容错说成了触发时机，答非所问。
接得住下一问「workflow 和 activity 有什么区别」。
pod 重启后业务流程照样从头开始，没解决问题。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They'll ask what happens to half-finished state and there's no answer.
It turns fault tolerance for long flows into a question of trigger timing.
It sets up the next question about workflows versus activities.
A restarted pod still runs the business flow from scratch, so nothing is solved.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个持久化执行引擎：把长流程的每一步写进历史，崩溃后重放历史恢复执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is a durable execution engine that records each step of a long workflow and replays that history to resume after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久化执行：保证一段流程即使经历崩溃和重启也能跑到完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durable execution guarantees a workflow runs to completion even across crashes and restarts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次工作流执行的完整事件日志，是恢复状态的唯一依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event history is the complete log of one workflow execution and the sole basis for restoring its state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间表达式定时触发任务的调度方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduling convention that triggers jobs on a time expression.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复处理失败的消息被移入的专用队列，等待人工介入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter queue holds messages that repeatedly failed processing, waiting for manual intervention.

scenario: 面试官继续追问：「那你会怎么用 Temporal 写一个多步骤的长流程？」我需要知道它的两层分工。
scenario_en: The follow-up: "So how would you write a multi-step long-running flow in Temporal?" I need to know its two-layer split.
q: Temporal 里 workflow 和 activity 各自负责什么？
q_en: What do workflows and activities each own in Temporal?
text: {{workflow}} 是确定性、可重放的编排代码，负责「下一步做什么」，本身不能直接产生副作用；{{activity}} 才是真正调外部 API、写数据库的那一步，失败按重试策略自动重跑。崩溃恢复靠重放 {{event history}}，把状态放回崩溃前那一刻再继续。
text_en: A {{workflow}} is deterministic, replayable orchestration code that decides what happens next and performs no side effects itself; an {{activity}} is the step that actually calls an external API or writes a database, retried automatically on failure. Recovery replays the {{event history}} to restore the state just before the crash and continue.
why: 分层的理由是可重放性：编排代码每次重放都必须走出同一条路径，所以所有不确定的副作用都要被赶进 activity 里。
why_en: The split exists for replayability: orchestration code must take the same path every replay, so every nondeterministic side effect is pushed into an activity.

termDefinitions.meaning: Temporal 里描述流程步骤顺序的确定性代码，可以被反复重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A workflow in Temporal is deterministic code describing the order of steps, and it can be replayed repeatedly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工作流里真正执行副作用的一步：调 API、写库、发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An activity is the step inside a workflow that performs real side effects such as API calls, database writes, or sending messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同样的输入每次都走出同样的执行路径，重放才能得到一致结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Determinism means the same input always takes the same execution path, which is what makes replay consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次工作流执行的完整事件日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event history is the complete log of one workflow execution.

scenario: Alterion 技术轮问「你 React Context 熟吗」，我答了「I think I'll be able to handle it」——一个用了两年的核心 API，这句话当场被判红旗。
scenario_en: In the Alterion technical round I answered "I think I'll be able to handle it" about React Context — a core API I've used for two years, and it was flagged as a red flag.
q: 这句话该换成什么？
q_en: What should that sentence be replaced with?
options: 「我平时主要用 Redux 做状态管理，Context 用得比较少，不过概念相通，上手应该很快」
「createContext 建 context、useContext 读它，跨树共享、免 prop drilling」
「Context 就是 React 里的全局变量，挂上去所有组件都能拿到，跟往 window 上挂一个对象是一个意思」
「我在项目里用过 Context，具体 API 记不太清了，真要写的时候查一下官方文档就行」
options_en: "I mostly use Redux for state, so I don't reach for Context often, but the concepts overlap and I'd pick it up fast."
"createContext creates a context, useContext reads it: shared state across the tree, no prop drilling."
"Context is React's global variable — put a value on it and every component can read it, same as hanging an object on window."
"I've used Context on projects, I don't remember the exact API, but I'd just check the docs when I actually need to write it."
tradeoff: Context vs 状态管理库：Context 零依赖、适合主题和登录态这类低频值，代价是 value 一变整棵消费子树都会重渲。
why: 对一个用了两年的核心 API，含糊等于自我否定；一句「createContext 加 useContext，跨树共享、免 prop drilling」就足够，还能顺势带出典型场景。
why_en: Hedging on an API I've used for two years reads as self-doubt, and one line — createContext plus useContext to share state across the tree without prop drilling — is enough to close it.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方问的是「你们为什么选 Context 而不是状态库」，那就该讲取舍：低频全局值适合 Context，高频更新会拖垮整棵子树。
optionMeanings: 改口说自己主要用别的方案。
直接给出 API 名与它解决的问题。
用「全局变量」做类比。
承认记不清并交给文档。
optionMeanings_en: Deflects by saying I mainly use something else.
States the API names and the problem they solve.
Uses a "global variable" analogy.
Admits not remembering and defers to the docs.
optionDirectness: 只有当我确实没用过 Context 时才诚实，但这里不成立。
对方要确认基础功底扎实时的标准回答。
类比抹掉了 Provider 作用域和重渲行为，会被追问戳破。
对核心 API 说记不清，等于坐实了那个红旗。
optionDirectness_en: Honest only if I truly hadn't used Context, which isn't the case here.
The standard answer when they're checking that fundamentals are solid.
The analogy erases provider scoping and re-render behavior and won't survive a follow-up.
Saying you forget a core API confirms exactly the red flag.
optionScenarioImpacts: 把两年的实际经验主动说没了。
十秒内证明基础扎实，话题可以往上层推进。
下一问「Provider 的作用范围呢」立刻接不住。
红旗从「犹豫」升级成「确实不会」。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It talks away two years of real experience.
Ten seconds proves the fundamentals and the conversation can move up a level.
The next question about provider scope lands with no answer.
The red flag upgrades from hesitation to a confirmed gap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了把数据送到深层组件，被迫一层层往下传 props 的麻烦。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prop drilling is the chore of passing props down through every intermediate component just to reach a deep one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 创建一个 context 对象，配合 Provider 向整棵子树提供一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: createContext creates a context object whose provider supplies one value to an entire subtree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在组件里读取并订阅最近的那个 Provider 提供的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useContext reads and subscribes to the value from the nearest provider above the component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个集中式状态管理库，用单一 store 和纯函数 reducer 更新状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redux is a centralized state library that updates a single store through pure reducer functions.

scenario: action item 要求：五个常用 hook，每个都要能在 10 秒内说清它是干什么的，不能犹豫。
scenario_en: The action item: for each of the five common hooks, be able to say what it does in ten seconds with no hedging.
q: useState / useEffect / useCallback / useMemo / useRef 各是干什么的？
q_en: What does each of useState, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo, and useRef do?
text: {{useState}} 给组件一块会触发重渲的状态；{{useEffect}} 把渲染之外的副作用（订阅、请求、手动 DOM 操作）挂到渲染之后执行；useCallback 缓存{{函数}}引用、useMemo 缓存{{计算结果}}，都是为了让下游依赖不白白失效；{{useRef}} 存一个改了也不触发重渲的可变盒子。
text_en: {{useState}} gives a component state that triggers re-renders; {{useEffect}} runs side effects such as subscriptions, requests and manual DOM work after render; useCallback caches a {{function}} reference and useMemo caches a {{computed value}} so downstream dependencies don't invalidate for nothing; {{useRef}} holds a mutable box whose changes never trigger a re-render.
why: 记忆抓手是「会不会触发重渲」：useState 会、useRef 不会；useMemo 和 useCallback 都不改渲染结果，只是让引用在依赖不变时保持稳定。
why_en: The hook to remember them by is whether they trigger a re-render: useState does, useRef doesn't, and useMemo and useCallback only keep references stable when dependencies haven't changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存一个跨渲染保留、修改时不触发重渲的可变引用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useRef stores a mutable reference that persists across renders and never triggers a re-render when changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 渲染纯计算之外的事：订阅、发请求、改 DOM、设定时器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A side effect is anything outside pure render computation: subscribing, fetching, touching the DOM, setting timers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 告诉 hook「这些值变了才重新执行或重新计算」的那个数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The dependency array tells a hook which values must change before it re-runs or recomputes.

scenario: 一个列表组件在父组件每次重渲时都整体重画：一个昂贵的过滤计算被重跑、一个传给子组件的回调每次都是新引用、还有一个定时器 id 需要跨渲染保存。
scenario_en: A list component fully repaints on every parent render: an expensive filter recomputes, a callback passed to a child is a new reference each time, and a timer id must survive across renders.
q: 这三件事分别该用哪个 hook？
q_en: Which hook handles each of these three?
options: 过滤用 useCallback、回调用 useMemo、定时器 id 用 useState 存起来
过滤用 useMemo、回调用 useCallback、定时器 id 用 useRef
三件事都用 useState 存起来，在 useEffect 里同步更新，引用自然就稳定了
三件事都用 useRef 存，ref 改了不会触发重渲，这是最省渲染次数的做法
options_en: useCallback for the filter, useMemo for the callback, useState for the timer id.
useMemo for the filter, useCallback for the callback, useRef for the timer id.
Put all three in useState and sync them in useEffect so the references stay stable.
Put all three in useRef since ref changes never re-render, which is the cheapest option.
tradeoff: 加缓存 hook vs 不加：缓存换掉重复计算和引用抖动，代价是多了依赖数组这个新的出错面。
why: 分工是按「缓存的是什么」定的：useMemo 缓存值、useCallback 缓存函数、useRef 存一个和渲染无关的可变盒子。
why_en: The split follows what's being cached: useMemo caches a value, useCallback caches a function, and useRef holds a mutable box that has nothing to do with rendering.
whenOtherWins: 如果子组件没有被 memo 包住、或者那个计算本来就很便宜，加 useCallback 和 useMemo 只是徒增依赖数组的维护成本。
optionMeanings: 把三个 hook 的职责两两互换。
按缓存对象把三件事各归其位。
全部塞进状态并靠 effect 同步。
全部塞进 ref 以避免重渲。
optionMeanings_en: Swaps the responsibilities of the hooks around.
Assigns each case by what is being cached.
Puts everything in state and syncs via effect.
Puts everything in refs to avoid re-renders.
optionDirectness: useCallback 缓存的是函数，用它包一个计算结果不对路。
值、函数、跨渲染可变量三类各有对应 hook。
把派生值变成状态，会多一次渲染且容易不同步。
ref 变化不触发重渲，过滤结果改了界面不会更新。
optionDirectness_en: useCallback caches functions, so wrapping a computed value with it is the wrong tool.
Values, functions, and cross-render mutables each have their own hook.
Turning derived values into state adds a render and invites desync.
Ref changes don't re-render, so an updated filter result never reaches the screen.
optionScenarioImpacts: 过滤照样每次重跑，回调引用照样每次都变。
昂贵计算只在依赖变时重算，子组件不再无谓重渲。
多绕一圈 effect，还可能渲染出上一帧的旧值。
界面不再跟随数据更新，等于把 bug 换了个形式。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The filter still recomputes and the callback reference still changes every render.
The expensive computation only reruns when dependencies change and the child stops re-rendering.
An extra effect hop, plus the risk of rendering last frame's stale value.
The UI stops following the data, which just relocates the bug.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在依赖不变时复用上一次的计算结果，避免重复的昂贵计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useMemo reuses the previous computed result while dependencies are unchanged, avoiding repeated expensive work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在依赖不变时复用同一个函数引用，避免子组件因引用变化而重渲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useCallback reuses the same function reference while dependencies are unchanged, so children don't re-render on identity changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包住组件，让 props 浅比较相同时跳过重渲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: memo wraps a component so it skips re-rendering when a shallow props comparison finds no change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以从现有状态算出来的值，不该单独再存一份状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A derived value can be computed from existing state and should not be stored as separate state.

scenario: Playground 技术轮是 30 分钟 React live coding 加 15 分钟问答，目标是 20 分钟内写出一个功能完整、干净的小 CRUD 应用。
scenario_en: The Playground technical round is 30 minutes of React live coding plus 15 minutes of Q&A, with the goal of a clean working CRUD app in about 20 minutes.
q: 哪些模式必须练到不用想就能写出来？
q_en: Which patterns must be automatic before that round?
options: useState 加受控表单：value 绑 state、onChange 回写，提交前能就地校验
useEffect 加 fetch：显式画出 loading 和 error 两个分支，不只写成功路径
条件渲染加 .map() 列表渲染，每项带稳定 key，避免增删时错位
状态提升：两个兄弟组件要共享的状态挪到最近的公共父组件里
先手写一遍 fiber 调和算法，向面试官证明自己理解 React 底层原理
开场先配好 Webpack 加 Babel 的完整构建链路，再开始写第一个组件
options_en: useState with a controlled form: value bound to state, onChange writing back, validated in place before submit.
useEffect with fetch: explicitly render the loading and error branches, not just the success path.
Conditional rendering plus .map() list rendering with a stable key on each item so edits don't shuffle rows.
Lifting state up: move state shared by two siblings into their nearest common parent.
Hand-write the fiber reconciliation algorithm to prove you understand React internals.
Set up a full Webpack and Babel build chain before writing the first component.
why: 这四个加上「把重复逻辑抽成自定义 hook」就是一个小 CRUD 应用的全部骨架；30 分钟里没有时间现想，只能靠肌肉记忆。
why_en: These four plus extracting repeated logic into a custom hook are the entire skeleton of a small CRUD app, and thirty minutes leaves no room to think them up on the spot.
optionMeanings: 表单输入由 state 单向驱动。
异步请求的三态渲染。
列表与分支渲染的基本功。
共享状态的归属决策。
手写框架内部调和逻辑。
先做构建工具链配置。
optionMeanings_en: Form inputs driven one-way by state.
Three-state rendering for an async request.
The basics of list and branch rendering.
Deciding where shared state belongs.
Hand-implementing framework internals.
Configuring the build toolchain first.
optionDirectness: 挡住「输入了但拿不到值」这类最常见的现场卡壳。
挡住「网络一慢界面就白屏」的扣分点。

optionDirectness_en: Prevents the classic freeze where typing produces no value.
Prevents losing points to a blank screen on a slow network.
Without a stable key, deleting a row shifts input values onto the wrong one.
Getting ownership wrong leaves two copies of state that drift apart.
The round tests writing usable components fast, not rebuilding the framework.

面试官看到我主动想到了失败路径。
增删改都不会出现视觉错位。
父子数据流清楚，追问「为什么放这里」也答得出。
20 分钟全用在这上面，CRUD 一行都没写出来。
十几分钟花在配置上，功能部分直接来不及。

The interviewer sees I reached for the failure path unprompted.
Adds, edits, and deletes never shuffle rows visually.
Data flow is clear and "why does state live here" has an answer.
Twenty minutes vanish here and not one line of CRUD gets written.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入框的值完全由 React 状态驱动，每次输入都回写 state。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A key is a stable identity for a list item that React uses to tell which item is which.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增删改查，最基础的一组数据操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRUD stands for create, read, update and delete, the four basic data operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: React 内部把渲染工作拆成可中断小单元的调和架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fiber is React's internal reconciliation architecture that splits rendering into interruptible units.

scenario: live coding 要求：进页面时从 API 拉一份任务列表并渲染出来。30 分钟计时，面试官会特别看你有没有写非成功路径。
scenario_en: Live coding task: fetch a task list from an API on mount and render it. Thirty minutes on the clock, and the interviewer specifically watches for the non-success paths.
q: 这段 useEffect 最容易被扣分的地方是什么？
q_en: Where does this useEffect most easily lose points?
options: 只写了成功分支：没有 loading、没有 error 兜底，也没在卸载时取消响应
没有把 fetch 逻辑抽成自定义 hook，组件文件越写越长、换个页面没法复用
没有用 useMemo 缓存返回的数组，每次重渲都生成新引用，被 memo 包住的子组件也跟着白白重画
没有把请求放进 useLayoutEffect，首屏会先闪一下空白再把内容补上来
options_en: Only the success branch exists: no loading state, no error fallback, and no cancellation of a stale response on unmount.
The fetch logic isn't extracted into a custom hook, so the file grows and nothing is reusable on another page.
The returned array isn't wrapped in useMemo, so a memo-wrapped child repaints on every render for nothing.
The request isn't in useLayoutEffect, so the first paint flashes blank before the content arrives.
tradeoff: 手写 useEffect 加 fetch vs 用数据请求库：手写能展示我懂生命周期和竞态，代价是取消、错误态、重试全要自己写。
why: 异步请求有三种状态，写全 loading、error、success 才是完整答案；卸载时不取消，慢响应回来会往已经消失的组件里写状态。
why_en: An async request has three states, so loading, error and success all need rendering, and without cancellation a slow response writes into a component that no longer exists.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试明说用 React Query 或 SWR 这类数据请求库，loading 和 error 由库给出，重点就转到缓存 key 和失效策略上。
optionMeanings: 缺失败态与清理。
缺逻辑复用抽象。
缺引用稳定性优化。
换一个 effect 时机。
optionMeanings_en: Missing failure states and cleanup.
Missing a reuse abstraction.
Missing a reference-stability optimization.
Choosing a different effect timing.
optionDirectness: 限时轮里最先被看的就是三态是否写全。
同一个请求在两个页面复用时才值得抽。
只有当子组件被 memo 包住时才有收益。
useLayoutEffect 是同步测量布局用的，不适合发请求。

Worth extracting once the same request is reused on a second page.
Only pays off when the child is wrapped in memo.
useLayoutEffect exists for synchronous layout measurement, not for requests.

属于性能优化，30 分钟里不是评分重点。
改成同步 effect 反而会阻塞首帧绘制。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A slow network shows a blank screen and an error shows nothing at all — points lost immediately.
Slightly long code but complete behavior, which rarely costs points.
That's a performance tweak and not what a thirty-minute round grades.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在浏览器绘制之前同步执行的 effect，用来测量或修正布局。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useLayoutEffect runs synchronously before the browser paints, used to measure or correct layout.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先发的请求后返回，把旧数据盖在新数据上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition here means an earlier request returns later and overwrites newer data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一段可复用的 hook 逻辑抽成以 use 开头的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A custom hook extracts reusable hook logic into a function whose name starts with use.

scenario: GenLogs recruiter 问：「你有 AWS 或 Azure 经验吗？」我在 Meta 和 TikTok 用的都是公司自研的内部云，没碰过公有云控制台。
scenario_en: The GenLogs recruiter asked whether I have AWS or Azure experience. At Meta and TikTok I used in-house private clouds and have never touched a public cloud console.
q: 怎么答既诚实又不掉分？
q_en: How do I answer honestly without losing ground?
options: 「我在 Meta 和 TikTok 有云经验」——先把有经验三个字说出去，等对方追问具体服务名再随机应变
「没直接用过 AWS；我用的是 Meta 和 TikTok 的内部私有云，核心概念是同一套」
「没用过，但我学得很快」——简短承认就打住，不展开，尽快把话题推回我熟悉的项目上去
「我有云经验」，紧接着补一句「虽然我没真正用过 AWS，不过我会很快学会的」——两句连着说
options_en: "I have cloud experience from Meta and TikTok" — lead with the claim and improvise once they ask for service names.
"I haven't used AWS directly; at Meta and TikTok I worked on internal private clouds, and autoscaling, container orchestration and monitoring are the same concepts."
"I haven't used it, but I learn fast" — a short admission, no elaboration, then steer back to familiar projects.
"I have cloud experience," immediately followed by "though I've never actually used AWS, I'll pick it up fast" — both in a row.
tradeoff: bridge 到内部私有云 vs 直接说没用过：bridge 保住了「我懂云的核心概念」，代价是后面每一句都不能再自相矛盾。
why: 顺序是先明确说没直接用过公有云，再桥到内部私有云的同构概念；顺序反了就是自相矛盾，那比不会更扣分。
why_en: The order matters: state clearly that I haven't used the public cloud, then bridge to the equivalent concepts in the internal cloud, because the reverse order sounds self-contradictory.
whenOtherWins: 如果 JD 硬性要求某个具体服务的实操经验（比如「必须做过 EKS 生产运维」），坦白差距加一个学习计划比 bridge 更可信。
optionMeanings: 先声称有经验，细节留到被追问时。
先划清边界，再桥到同构的内部经验。
承认没有并快速转移话题。
先声称有经验，再当场自己否定。
optionMeanings_en: Claim experience first and leave details until pressed.
Draw the boundary first, then bridge to equivalent internal experience.
Admit the gap and change the subject quickly.
Claim experience, then contradict it in the next breath.
optionDirectness: 只有当我确实有公有云实操经历时才成立。
有可类比的内部经验、且能说出具体概念时的做法。
当对方明显不在意这项、只是走流程时够用。
两句话方向相反，任何前提下都站不住。
optionDirectness_en: Only holds if I really do have hands-on public cloud experience.
The move when comparable internal experience exists and I can name the concepts.
Enough when the recruiter clearly doesn't care and is just checking a box.
The two sentences point opposite ways and hold under no premise.
optionScenarioImpacts: 一被问「你用过哪些服务」就得往回缩，信任度掉得更快。
对方听到的是「概念齐了，只差 API 名字」。
把一个可以转化的差距直接留成了空白。
对方记住的是「他刚才说的不实」，比没经验更糟。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: One question about which services and I have to walk it back, costing more trust.
They hear "the concepts are there, only the API names are missing."
It leaves a convertible gap as a plain blank.
What they remember is that I overstated, which is worse than the gap itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 公司自建自用的云平台，对外不开放，接口和公有云不同但概念相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A private cloud is a company's own internal cloud platform with different APIs but the same concepts as a public one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动调度、扩缩和重启容器的系统能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Container orchestration automatically schedules, scales, and restarts containers.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 Kubernetes 服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EKS stands for Elastic Kubernetes Service, the managed Kubernetes offering on AWS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 职位描述，列出岗位职责和硬性要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JD stands for job description, the document listing a role's duties and hard requirements.

scenario: 被问到一个我没用过的工具（Temporal、LangChain、C#、AWS 都出现过）。这个模板要练到脱口而出。
scenario_en: Asked about a tool I've never used — Temporal, LangChain, C#, and AWS have all come up. This template has to be automatic.
q: 把「不熟悉的工具」bridge 模板的四段排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four beats of the unfamiliar-tool bridge template in the right order.
steps: 说清我理解的这个工具核心是什么，用我自己的话，而不是背它主页上的介绍
先明确承认：我没有直接用过这个工具
接一句为什么想深入，扣到对方产品上的一个具体点
桥到我做过的类似的事：同一类问题、同一层抽象
why: 顺序是先划边界、再给证据、再证明理解、最后表达意愿；把承认放在最前面，后面每一句才不会被听成夸大。
why_en: Admit the boundary first, then give evidence, then show understanding, then show intent — leading with the admission is what keeps everything after it from sounding inflated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「我没用过 X」转成「我做过同类的事」的一段过渡话术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bridge is the transition that turns "I haven't used X" into "I've done the same class of work."

scenario: Pinpoint recruiter：「我们团队用 C#，你没写过吧？」我有 Java 的生产经验，但确实没写过 C#。
scenario_en: Pinpoint recruiter: "Our team writes C#, and you haven't, right?" I have production Java experience but genuinely no C#.
q: bridge 那一句该拿什么来支撑？
q_en: What should the bridge sentence rest on?
options: 「我朋友从 Java 转 C# 说两周就上手了，所以我估计我也差不多，学习曲线应该不算陡」
「C# 我没写过，但语言只是工具，真正重要的是解决问题的能力，语法这种东西几天就能查会」
「没写过 C#，但我有 Java 经验——同样强类型、基于类，生态成熟度接近，几周能高效产出」
「我最近在自学 C#，官方文档前几章看完了，正在跟着做一个练手项目，下周应该能跑起来」
options_en: "A friend moved from Java to C# and was productive in two weeks, so I'd expect the same — the curve isn't steep."
"I haven't written C#, but a language is just a tool; what matters is problem solving, and syntax takes a few days to look up."
"No C#, but I have Java experience — both strongly typed and class-based with comparably mature ecosystems, so a few weeks to be productive."
"I've started learning C#, I've read the first chapters of the docs, and I'm building a practice project that should run next week."
tradeoff: 第一性原理推导 vs 引用别人的经验：自己推出来的相似点经得住追问，代价是我必须真的说得出两者在哪一层相似。
why: bridge 的说服力来自我自己推出来的相似点——强类型、基于类、生态成熟度；转述来的判断一被追问「哪里像」就塌。
why_en: A bridge convinces because I derived the similarity myself — strong typing, class-based design, comparable ecosystem maturity — while borrowed judgment collapses on the first "similar how?"
whenOtherWins: 如果我真的完全没有可类比的经验（比如从没碰过任何强类型语言），硬编相似点会被一个追问戳破，不如直接给学习计划。
optionMeanings: 用别人的转型经历做依据。
把语言差异整体消解掉。
用自己的 Java 经验推导相似维度。
用当下的自学进度做依据。
optionMeanings_en: Rests on someone else's transition story.
Dissolves the language difference altogether.
Derives similarity dimensions from my own Java experience.
Rests on current self-study progress.
optionDirectness: 道听途说的判断，我自己答不了「哪里像」。
听起来轻慢，也没给对方任何可验证的依据。
有可类比的语言经验、且能说出相似层面时的做法。
当我确实已经动手学了一段时间时可以作为补充。
optionDirectness_en: Hearsay judgment that leaves me unable to answer "similar how?"
It sounds dismissive and gives them nothing verifiable.
The move when comparable language experience exists and I can name the shared layers.
A fine supplement once I really have been learning hands-on.
optionScenarioImpacts: 追问一句「你觉得哪里像」就露出这是转述。
对方听到的是「他不认为这有什么要学的」。
给出三个可验证的相似维度和一个时间预期。
只能作为补充，单独说撑不起「能不能干活」。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: One "similar how?" reveals it was secondhand.
What they hear is that I don't think there's anything to learn.
It gives three checkable similarity dimensions plus a time estimate.
Fine as a supplement, but alone it doesn't answer whether I can do the job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 变量类型在编译期确定并强制检查，类型错误在运行前就被拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong typing fixes and checks variable types at compile time so type errors are caught before running.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从自己确知的事实一步步推出结论，而不是引用别人的结论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reasoning from first principles derives a conclusion step by step from facts you know yourself instead of quoting someone else's conclusion.

scenario: Amazon Round 2 讲 P99 故事：我调用下游 catalog 校验团队的 API，他们发新版本把超时从 500ms 改成 2s，把我这边打挂了。我当场把上下游说反了。
scenario_en: Telling the P99 story in Amazon Round 2: I call the catalog validation team's API, they shipped a release moving the timeout from 500ms to 2s and broke my service — and I got upstream and downstream backwards on the spot.
q: 在这段依赖关系里，谁是谁的 upstream？
q_en: In this dependency, who is upstream of whom?
options: 我是他们的 downstream，他们是我的 upstream——我依赖谁谁就在上游
我是他们的 upstream，因为请求是从我这边发起的，数据流也是从我流向他们那边的
看数据流向：响应从他们流回我，所以我是下游；但因为我发起调用，我同时也是上游
两边互为上下游，因为这是双向调用关系，这个词在微服务里没有固定方向
options_en: I am their downstream and they are my upstream — whoever I depend on sits upstream of me.
I'm their upstream because the request starts on my side and data flows from me to them.
Follow the data: responses flow from them to me so I'm downstream, but since I initiate the call I'm also upstream.
Both are upstream of each other since calls go both ways; the word has no fixed direction in microservices.
why: 方向由依赖决定，不由谁先发包决定：我调用他们的 API，所以我在下游；反过来别人依赖我的服务，我就是他们的 upstream。
why_en: Direction is set by dependency, not by who sends the first packet: I call their API so I'm downstream, and whoever depends on my service has me as their upstream.
optionMeanings: 按依赖方向判定。
按请求发起方判定。
按数据流向判定并自我矛盾。
认为方向不确定。
optionMeanings_en: Decides by dependency direction.
Decides by who initiates the request.
Decides by data flow and contradicts itself.
Claims the direction is undefined.
optionDirectness: 这就是行业里说这两个词时的默认含义。
发起方向和上下游无关，这正是我上次说反的原因。
同一个服务不可能既在上游又在下游。
确实存在互相调用的情况，但每条依赖边的方向仍然是明确的。
optionDirectness_en: This is what the industry means by default when using these two words.
Who initiates has nothing to do with it, which is exactly why I got it backwards.
One service can't be both upstream and downstream on the same edge.
Mutual calls do exist, but each dependency edge still has a definite direction.
optionScenarioImpacts: 「他们发版影响到下游」这句话就说得准了。
故事里的责任方会被说反，听的人要停下来重建关系。
面试官会花时间澄清词义，故事节奏断掉。
等于承认自己没有稳定的依赖关系词汇。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The line "their release broke their downstream" finally comes out right.
The story names the wrong party and the listener has to stop and rebuild the map.
The interviewer spends time clarifying vocabulary and the story loses its rhythm.
It amounts to admitting I lack stable vocabulary for dependencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 我依赖的那一方：我调用它的接口，它的变更会传导到我这里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Upstream is the side I depend on: I call its interface, and its changes propagate to me.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖我的那一方：我发新版本会影响到它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Downstream is the side that depends on me: my releases affect it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99 分位延迟：100 次请求里最慢的那 1 次达到的耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 is the 99th-percentile latency, the level reached by the slowest one request in a hundred.

scenario: Apple 面试官直接问「Java 熟练度 1 到 10 打几分」，我自评 7；这个团队日常就用 Java，下一轮很可能要现场写。
scenario_en: The Apple interviewer asked me to rate my Java from one to ten and I said seven; the team codes in Java daily and the next round may well be live Java.
q: 两周时间里复习什么最止血？
q_en: With two weeks, what review actually stops the bleeding?
options: 把 JVM 垃圾回收算法、G1 与 ZGC 的分代策略从头到尾看一遍，在深度上直接压过面试官
刷 200 道 LeetCode 的 Java 版本，把语法在算法题里练熟，业务框架先放一边完全不管
写一个最小 Spring Boot 服务：REST 端点收请求、JPA 存取、@Transactional 划事务边界
背 Java 八股：HashMap 扩容机制、synchronized 锁升级、ThreadLocal 内存泄漏这些高频考点
options_en: Read through JVM garbage collection, G1 and ZGC generation strategies end to end and out-depth the interviewer.
Grind 200 LeetCode problems in Java to drill syntax through algorithms and ignore application frameworks entirely.
Build a minimal Spring Boot service: a REST endpoint for requests, JPA for persistence, @Transactional for the transaction boundary.
Memorize the classic Java trivia: HashMap resizing, synchronized lock escalation, ThreadLocal memory leaks.
tradeoff: 补框架实操 vs 补语言八股：写一个能跑的 Spring Boot 服务直接对应「这个团队每天用 Java 做什么」，代价是深层原理题会答得浅。
why: 风险不在语法，而在「团队日常怎么用 Java」；把 REST、持久化、事务边界这条主链路手写一遍，现场写代码时才不是冷的。
why_en: The risk isn't syntax but how this team uses Java day to day, so hand-writing the REST, persistence, and transaction path once is what keeps a live round from starting cold.
whenOtherWins: 如果那一轮明说是纯算法轮（LeetCode 风格），那语法手感和标准库 API 反而比 Spring 更该先补。
optionMeanings: 补运行时与垃圾回收原理。
用算法题练语法手感。
手写一遍业务主链路。
背高频原理面试题。
optionMeanings_en: Study runtime and garbage collection internals.
Drill syntax through algorithm problems.
Hand-write the core application path once.
Memorize common internals questions.
optionDirectness: 当岗位真的是 JVM 调优方向时才是首选。
当那一轮确实是纯算法轮时才够用。
当团队日常写业务服务、且可能现场写代码时的首选。
当面试风格偏原理问答时才有性价比。
optionDirectness_en: The first choice only when the role really is JVM tuning.
Enough only when that round truly is pure algorithms.
The first choice when the team writes application services and may ask for live code.
Worth the time only when the interview style leans toward internals Q&A.
optionScenarioImpacts: 两周全花在用不上的深度上，现场写业务代码照样卡。
语法顺了，但被问「你怎么定事务边界」还是空白。
REST、持久化、事务这条主链路一次跑通，追问也有落点。
答得出定义，写不出一个能跑的接口。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Two weeks spent on depth I won't use, and live application code still stalls.
Syntax gets smooth, but "how do you set transaction boundaries" is still blank.
The REST, persistence and transaction path runs once, so follow-ups have somewhere to land.
I can recite definitions but can't write one working endpoint.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 生态里约定优于配置的应用框架，几行注解就能起一个 HTTP 服务。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: JPA stands for Java Persistence API, the object-relational mapping standard that maps entity classes to database tables.

scenario: Apple 技术轮前的最小复习目标：能口述一个 Spring Boot REST 服务从收请求到落库的完整链路。
scenario_en: Minimum prep goal before the Apple technical round: narrate a Spring Boot REST service end to end, from receiving a request to writing the database.
q: Spring Boot 从收请求到落库的最小闭环是什么？
q_en: What is the minimal loop of a Spring Boot service from request to database?
text: {{@RestController}} 把一个类暴露成 HTTP 端点，@GetMapping/@PostMapping 绑定路径和方法；持久层写一个继承自 JPA 的 {{Repository}} 接口，Spring 在运行时按方法名生成实现；写操作用 {{@Transactional}} 划事务边界——方法正常返回就提交，抛出运行时异常就整体{{回滚}}。
text_en: {{@RestController}} exposes a class as HTTP endpoints with @GetMapping and @PostMapping binding paths and methods; persistence is a {{Repository}} interface extending JPA whose implementation Spring generates from method names at runtime; writes use {{@Transactional}} to mark the transaction boundary, committing on normal return and {{rolling back}} entirely on a runtime exception.
why: 这条链路是 Java 后端面试的默认起点：说得出注解在哪一层生效，追问「事务边界放哪里」「为什么这里会回滚」才接得住。
why_en: This path is the default starting point in a Java backend interview, and knowing which layer each annotation acts on is what lets me answer where transaction boundaries go and why a rollback happens.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: @Transactional declares a transaction that commits when the method returns normally and rolls back on a runtime exception.

scenario: Amazon onsite loop：Round 3 是 Selling Assistant 的 HM，Round 4 是 AWS 另一个组的资深工程师。教练判断 Round 4 很可能就是 bar raiser。
scenario_en: Amazon onsite loop: Round 3 was the Selling Assistant hiring manager and Round 4 a senior engineer from a different AWS org, which my coach read as the likely bar raiser.
q: bar raiser 在一个 loop 里是什么角色？
q_en: What role does a bar raiser play in a loop?
options: HR 派来的流程监督员，只负责记录时间、确认题目合规，不参与技术评价，也不参与最终投票
来自招聘团队之外、经过专门训练的志愿者，负责横向定级把关和一场公平的复盘
本组最资深的工程师，因为最懂业务，所以由他来定候选人进来之后具体做哪个方向
候选人未来的 skip-level 经理，组织架构上是 HM 的上级，负责给这个 offer 定薪资
options_en: An HR-appointed process monitor who only tracks timing and question compliance, joining neither the technical assessment nor the final vote.
A trained volunteer from outside the hiring team who guards the leveling bar and runs a fair debrief.
The most senior engineer on the hiring team, who decides what the candidate will work on after joining.
The candidate's future skip-level manager, organizationally above the hiring manager and responsible for setting the offer.
why: 公开资料一致的三点：来自招聘团队之外（避开本组 bias）、经过专门训练的志愿者、对「这次录用有没有拉高这条线」负责；多数公开说法还提到他对 HM 有否决权。
why_en: Public sources agree on three things: they come from outside the hiring team to avoid its bias, they are trained volunteers, and they own whether this hire raises the bar.
optionMeanings: 把角色理解成流程合规监督。
外组受训志愿者，负责定级与公平复盘。
把角色理解成本组的技术权威。
把角色理解成管理链上的审批人。
optionMeanings_en: Reads the role as process compliance oversight.
A trained outside volunteer who owns leveling and a fair debrief.
Reads the role as the team's technical authority.
Reads the role as an approver in the management chain.
optionDirectness: 复盘确实要主持，但他同时给出实质性的技术评价。
对上 Round 4 来自外组这个观察，也解释了他为什么问得更宽。
本组最资深的人通常正是要被制衡的那一方。
定薪走的是招聘流程，不是这个角色的职责。
optionDirectness_en: They do run the debrief, but they also give substantive technical assessment.
It matches the observation that Round 4 came from another org and explains the broader questions.
The team's most senior engineer is usually the party being balanced, not the balancer.
Compensation runs through the recruiting process, not this role.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会低估 Round 4，把它当成走过场。
知道 Round 4 在做横向比较，答案要拉到公司层面而非本组细节。
会误以为 Round 4 在挑我进哪个方向，答偏成兴趣匹配。
会误以为要在那轮谈薪资和层级。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: I'd underestimate Round 4 and treat it as a formality.
Knowing it's a cross-company comparison, I pitch answers at company level rather than team detail.
I'd mistake it for team matching and drift into interest fit.
I'd wrongly bring up compensation and level in that round.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon 招聘流程里来自招聘团队之外的受训面试官，负责把关录用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bar raiser is a trained Amazon interviewer from outside the hiring team who guards the hiring standard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘经理，这个岗位未来的直属上级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HM stands for hiring manager, the candidate's future direct manager.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次 onsite 里连续进行的多轮面试的总称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A loop is the full set of back-to-back interviews in one onsite.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上级的上级，即隔一层的经理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skip-level manager is your manager's manager, one level removed.

scenario: 同一个 loop 里，招聘团队已经缺人缺了半年、急着补；bar raiser 来自一个完全无关的组，此前和这个岗位没有任何关系。
scenario_en: In the same loop, the hiring team has been short-staffed for six months and is eager to fill the role, while the bar raiser comes from an unrelated org with no stake in it.
q: 把把关人放在招聘团队之外，是在防什么？
q_en: What does placing the gatekeeper outside the hiring team protect against?
options: 防的是候选人作弊：外组的人拿不到本组的题库，题目就不会提前泄漏出去
防的是排期冲突：外组的人日程更空，能保证 loop 的五轮都排得开、不用改期
防的是本组的招聘偏差：急着补人时容易放松标准，外组的人没有这份压力
防的是薪资越权：外组的人不了解本组预算，所以不会随口承诺薪资范围
options_en: Cheating: someone from another org can't access the team's question bank, so questions don't leak in advance.
Scheduling conflicts: an outsider has a lighter calendar, so all five rounds fit without rescheduling.
The hiring team's own bias: teams in a hurry to fill a seat relax the bar, and an outsider carries no such pressure.
Compensation overreach: an outsider doesn't know the team's budget, so they won't promise a salary range.
why: 本组对候选人天然有 bias——缺人越久越容易「先招进来再说」；把一个没有交付压力的外部人放进来，才守得住「和公司内部同级相当」这条横向标准。
why_en: The hiring team is naturally biased because a long-vacant seat pushes toward "hire now and figure it out," so an outsider with no delivery pressure is what holds the cross-company bar.
optionMeanings: 把动机理解成防题目泄漏。
把动机理解成排期便利。
把动机理解成抵消本组的招聘偏差。
把动机理解成薪资权限隔离。
optionMeanings_en: Reads the motive as leak prevention.
Reads the motive as scheduling convenience.
Reads the motive as offsetting the hiring team's bias.
Reads the motive as separating compensation authority.
optionDirectness: 题库保密靠流程管控，和面试官来自哪个组无关。
排期是执行细节，撑不起一个专门设立的角色。
解释了为什么这个角色必须独立于用人团队。
定薪本来就不在面试官手里，无需靠换组来隔离。
optionDirectness_en: Question confidentiality is handled by process, not by which org an interviewer belongs to.
Scheduling is an execution detail and can't justify a dedicated role.
It explains why the role must be independent of the hiring team.
Interviewers never set compensation, so no org separation is needed for it.
optionScenarioImpacts: 把一个定级机制误解成保密机制。
会低估这一轮的权重，准备强度就跟着降下来。
明白这一轮是在和公司内同级横向比，答案要给可迁移的判断。
会误以为这轮能谈薪，把时间浪费在错误的话题上。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It mistakes a leveling mechanism for a confidentiality one.
I'd underweight the round and prepare for it less seriously.
Knowing it's a cross-company comparison, I give transferable judgment rather than team trivia.
I'd wrongly think salary is on the table and waste time on the wrong topic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 来自招聘团队之外的受训面试官，负责把关录用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bar raiser is a trained interviewer from outside the hiring team who guards the hiring standard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统性的判断偏差，这里指用人团队因为急需补人而放松标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bias here is the systematic tendency of a short-staffed team to relax its standard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断候选人对应公司内部的哪一个职级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leveling decides which internal job level a candidate maps to.

scenario: 招聘人接通就说「介绍下你自己」。你上一段工作因公司级裁员结束，这个岗位是你在 LinkedIn 上刷到的。GenLogs 和 Pinpoint 两次你都用这两件事开的场。
scenario_en: The recruiter opens with "tell me about yourself." Your last role ended in a company-wide layoff and you found this posting on LinkedIn — and you opened with exactly those two facts in both GenLogs and Pinpoint.
q: self-intro 的前两句该说什么？
q_en: What belongs in the first two sentences of your self-intro?
options: 先交代来路和处境：「我上一段工作因为公司裁员结束了，最近在 LinkedIn 上刷到你们在招人，看着挺合适，就投了一份简历过来试试。」
先说现在 own 什么再接时间线：「我在 TikTok own 广告投放全链路；此前在 Meta 做 onboarding 平台。」
从第一份工作开始按年份往下讲，把简历每一段的起止时间、职位名称和主要职责依次复述一遍，最后才说到现在。
开场只讲动机：先说你为什么想去创业公司、未来三五年的职业规划，具体做过什么留到对方追问的时候再展开。
options_en: Explain how you got here: "My last role ended in a layoff, I saw your posting on LinkedIn recently, it looked like a fit, so I sent a resume over."
Lead with what you own now, then the timeline: "At TikTok I own the ad campaign flow; before that I built onboarding at Meta."
Walk the resume chronologically from your first job — dates, titles and duties for every stint — and only reach the present at the end.
Open with motivation only: why you want a startup and your three-to-five-year plan, saving what you actually built for follow-ups.
tradeoff: 先说 impact vs 先交代来路：交代来路显得坦诚，代价是最宝贵的前 30 秒被裁员和求职渠道占满。
why: 开场 30 秒决定对方怎么给我贴标签。先说我现在 own 什么系统，再补时间线做证据；裁员和「怎么找到你们」不进开场。
why_en: The first thirty seconds decide how they file me, so I open with the system I own today and use the timeline as evidence behind it.
whenOtherWins: 只有当招聘人第一句就问「你为什么在看新机会」时，才提前说离职情况，而且一句带过就拉回你 own 的东西。
optionMeanings: 用裁员和求职渠道开场。
先给当前 ownership，再补履历。
按年份从头复述整份简历。
开场只谈动机与规划。
optionMeanings_en: Open with the layoff and how you found them.
Lead with current ownership, then the timeline.
Recite the whole resume by year.
Talk only about motivation and plans.
optionDirectness: 内推来的、对方早知情时才无所谓。
对方还不认识你时，先给一个可归类的标签。
对方手上没有简历、要完整履历时才有用。
适合已聊过背景的第二次通话。
optionDirectness_en: Only harmless when a referral already told them the story.
Right when they don't know you yet and need a label fast.
Useful only if they have no resume and want the full record.
Fits a second call where the background is already covered.
optionScenarioImpacts: 开场被裁员定调，能力标签没建立起来。
对方立刻知道你的层级和领域。
信息平铺，重点被时间顺序稀释。
只有意愿没有证据，听着像应届生。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The layoff sets the tone and no capability label lands.
They immediately know your level and your domain.
Everything is flat; chronology dilutes the point.
Intent without evidence sounds like a new grad.

q: self-intro 里描述职责，「some features」要换成什么句式？
q_en: What sentence pattern replaces "some features" when you describe your scope?
text: 自我介绍里「some features」全部删掉，换成三段式：I {{own}} 一个具名系统 — 涵盖它的 {{范围}}，重要性在于 {{影响}}。
text_en: Cut "some features" everywhere and use the three-part line: I {{own}} a named system — it covers this {{scope}}, and it matters because of this {{impact}}.
why: 「some features」既听不出层级也听不出规模。点名系统 + 说清范围 + 给出影响，一句话就把 scope 交代完。
why_en: "Some features" hides both scope and seniority, so name the system, state what it covers, and say why it matters.

scenario: WOP 招聘人 2 分钟里给了五个关键词：数字支付、PSP 集成、税务处理、checkout、tap-to-pay。你只反射一个。你真正做过的是 Meta 的多步骤 onboarding 数据流和 TikTok 的投放校验。
scenario_en: The WOP recruiter gave five keywords in two minutes: digital payments, PSP integrations, tax handling, checkout, tap-to-pay. You will mirror exactly one. What you actually built is Meta’s multi-step onboarding data flow and TikTok campaign validation.
q: 该挑哪个关键词反射回去？
q_en: Which of those keywords should you mirror back?
options: 挑 checkout 的多步流程：我在 Meta 做过从商家输入到后端的多步状态流转，被追问也接得住。
挑听起来最资深的 tax engine，就算自己没真做过，也先把「能扛复杂业务」的印象立起来再说。
五个关键词逐个都呼应一遍，每个说一句，证明你把他讲的每一点都听进去了、也都能接上话。
挑 tap-to-pay：这是最新的技术方向，能表现出你对支付行业前沿趋势的关注度和学习意愿。
options_en: Mirror the multi-step checkout flow: at Meta I built the multi-step state flow from merchant input to backend, so I can take the follow-up.
Mirror the tax engine because it sounds the most senior — even without having built one, it establishes that you handle complex business logic.
Echo all five keywords, one sentence each, to prove you took in every point he made and can speak to all of them.
Mirror tap-to-pay: it is the newest direction and shows how closely you follow payment-industry trends and want to learn.
tradeoff: 挑能接住追问的 vs 挑听起来最资深的：挑资深的开场更响，代价是下一个追问就落在你没做过的东西上。
why: 反射的那个词会立刻变成下一个技术追问。挑我真做过、能往下走两层的，而不是听起来最资深的。
why_en: Whatever keyword I mirror becomes the very next technical follow-up, so I pick the one I actually built and can go two layers deep on.
whenOtherWins: 如果五个关键词你一个都没做过，就反射最接近的那个，并当场说清你做过的是其中哪一段。
optionMeanings: 挑自己真做过的那个词。
挑最显资深的那个词。
五个词全部各回应一句。
挑最新潮的那个词。
optionMeanings_en: Pick the keyword you actually built.
Pick the keyword that sounds most senior.
Answer all five keywords one by one.
Pick the trendiest keyword.
optionDirectness: 你在其中一个方向有真实经历时。
对方明显在担心你级别不够时才有理由。
对方要求你逐条确认理解时才用。
岗位本身就是围绕这项新技术建的时才用。
optionDirectness_en: When you have real experience in one of those areas.
Only justified when they visibly worry you are too junior.
Only when they ask you to confirm each point back.
Only when the role itself is built around that new technology.
optionScenarioImpacts: 追问落在我准备过的那段流程上。
开场很响，第一个追问就穿帮。
开场变成复述清单，一个都没讲深。
话题被引到我没做过的硬件支付上。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The follow-up lands on the flow I have rehearsed.
A loud opening that the first follow-up exposes.
The opening becomes a checklist recital with no depth anywhere.
It steers the conversation to hardware payments I have never built.

scenario: 对方描述完岗位后说「介绍下你自己吧」。你过去两次都从最早的实习按年份往下讲，讲到现在时时间已经用掉一半。
scenario_en: They finish describing the role and say "tell me about yourself." Your last two attempts started at your earliest internship and walked forward by year, burning half the time before reaching the present.
q: self-intro 的四拍该按什么顺序讲？
q_en: In what order should the four beats of the self-intro come?
steps: 点出你想在这个方向深入的地方，把话头交回给对方
先说你现在 own 的系统和它的影响（impact first）
反射对方刚描述的一个具体岗位信号，说明它和你做过的哪件事对上
补一句时间线：此前在哪家公司做了什么，作为证据
why: 不是按年份走，而是 impact 先行、时间线只做证据，然后是连接、最后给方向——对方听完知道我是谁、能证明什么、想去哪。
why_en: Not chronological: impact first, timeline only as evidence, then the connection to their role, and finally the direction I want.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["现在 own 什么 — impact 先行"] --> B["时间线做证据"]
  B --> C["反射一个岗位信号"]
  C --> D["给方向并交回话头"]

scenario: 你的 self-intro 已经说了现在 own 什么、此前在 Meta 做什么，也反射了对方岗位的一个信号。还剩最后一句。
scenario_en: Your self-intro has covered what you own now, what you built at Meta, and one signal mirrored back from their role. One sentence left.
q: self-intro 的最后一句该说什么？
q_en: What should the last sentence of the self-intro do?
options: 再补第三个项目的细节，把简历上还没提到的经历尽量在开场一次讲完，免得后面没有机会说。
说一句「大概就是这些」然后停下来，等对方决定下一步问什么，自己不给任何方向性的信息。
直接问薪资区间和面试还有几轮，趁开场先把最关心的现实问题确认掉，免得后面几轮白花时间。
给方向并交回话头：「我想把支付这条线做深，也想听听这个岗位现在最难的部分是什么。」
options_en: Add a third project in detail so every unmentioned experience gets covered up front, in case there's no chance later.
Say "that's about it" and stop, letting them decide what comes next without offering any direction of your own.
Ask about the salary band and how many rounds remain, settling the practical questions before investing more time.
Give a direction and hand off: "I want to go deep on payments — and I'd like to hear what's hardest in this role right now."
tradeoff: 以方向收口 vs 继续堆项目：多讲一个项目显得内容多，代价是没人接得住，对方还得自己想下一句问什么。
why: 最后一句是交接棒。给一个方向加一个想了解的点，对方顺着往下问的就是我已经准备好的题。
why_en: The closing line is a handoff — give one direction plus one thing you want to know, and their next question lands on ground you already prepared.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方明确说「我想先完整听你的履历」，就把时间花在讲完经历上，方向留到他问 what are you looking for 时再给。
optionMeanings: 再塞一个项目进开场。
自然收尾，不给方向。
开场先谈薪资和流程。
给方向并抛回一个问题。
optionMeanings_en: Squeeze one more project into the opening.
Trail off without giving a direction.
Open with compensation and process.
Give a direction and hand back a question.
optionDirectness: 只有对方明说想听完整履历时才合适。
对方话很密、需要你尽快让出时间时勉强可用。
薪资明显有结构性错配、需要尽早止损时才提前问。
希望对方顺着你的方向提下一个问题时用。
optionDirectness_en: Only when they explicitly asked for the full record.
Barely works when they talk a lot and you must yield time.
Ask early only if a structural pay mismatch needs cutting fast.
Use it when you want their next question on your ground.
optionScenarioImpacts: 开场变长，反射建立的连接被冲淡。
主动权交出去，方向由对方来猜。
还没证明价值就先谈条件，顺序反了。
对方接着问的是你准备过的那块。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The opening drags and the connection you built gets diluted.
You hand over control and let them guess your direction.
Talking terms before proving value inverts the order.
Their follow-up lands on the part you rehearsed.

scenario: 「你为什么离开 TikTok？」在 WOP、GenLogs、Pinpoint、Assembled、Alma、Singular 等场次已经连续 7 次没有结构——Assembled 那次你当场说了「sorry, let me think about that」。
scenario_en: "Why are you leaving TikTok?" has now come out unstructured seven interviews in a row — in the Assembled call you actually said "sorry, let me think about that."
q: 第 7 次之后，真正的修法是什么？
q_en: After the seventh time, what is the actual fix?
options: 写成恰好 3 句（得到了什么 / 还缺什么 / 现在找什么），每天出声练到冷启动零停顿。
临场根据面试官的表情和反应即兴组织语言，保持自然，避免听起来像在背事先写好的稿子。
把完整答案打在纸上放到屏幕旁边，被问到就逐句照着念下来，保证每次说出来的内容完全一致。
把这个问题的答案压成一句「想找一个更能自己做主的机会」，短到几乎不可能说砸，也不给追问的把手。
options_en: Write it as exactly three sentences — what I got, what I'm missing, what I want now — and drill it out loud until it starts cold.
Improvise each time based on the interviewer's reaction, staying natural and avoiding anything that sounds scripted.
Keep the full answer printed next to your screen and read it line by line so every telling is word-for-word identical.
Compress it into one line — "I want a place where I can call more of the shots" — so short it can't go wrong and invites no follow-up.
tradeoff: 写死 3 句练到冷启动 vs 临场即兴：即兴听着自然，代价是已经连着 7 次卡壳，包括当场说「让我想想」。
why: 第 7 次说明缺的不是准备时间，是固定骨架。写死三句、出声练到冷启动，才不会再出现「让我想想」。
why_en: Seven misses means the gap isn't prep time, it's a fixed skeleton — three sentences drilled out loud until they start cold.
whenOtherWins: 只有当对方追一个具体细节（比如「那个项目上线后怎么样」）时，才离开三句骨架临场展开。
optionMeanings: 固定三句骨架并出声练。
每次临场重新组织。
照着稿子逐句念。
压成一句口号式回答。
optionMeanings_en: Fix a three-sentence skeleton and drill it aloud.
Reorganize from scratch every time.
Read a printed script line by line.
Compress it into one slogan.
optionDirectness: 同一个问题反复出问题时的标准解法。
只有这道题本来就答得很稳时才够。
写邮件或书面回复时可以照抄。
只剩十几秒收尾时才用得上。
optionDirectness_en: The standard fix once a question keeps failing.
Only enough if this answer were already reliable.
Fine for a written reply, not a live call.
Only useful when ten seconds remain to close.
optionScenarioImpacts: 第 8 次终于能冷启动说完整。
第 8 次大概率还是同样的卡壳。
念稿的节奏一听就出来，且答非所问。
一句话打发，对方感觉不到你想清楚了。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The eighth time finally comes out whole from a cold start.
The eighth time most likely stalls the same way.
Reading aloud is audible and rarely matches the question.
A one-liner leaves them unsure you've thought it through.

q: 「为什么离开 TikTok」的三句骨架是哪三拍？
q_en: What are the three beats in the "why I'm leaving TikTok" skeleton?
text: 为什么离职 = 三句：① 我在 TikTok 和 Meta {{得到了什么}}（发布、监控、规模化运营的生产直觉）→ ② 我还{{缺什么}}（接近产品决策和客户）→ ③ 我现在{{在找什么}}（端到端 own 一个问题）。
text_en: Why I'm leaving = three sentences: what I {{got}} at TikTok and Meta, what I'm still {{missing}}, and what I'm {{looking for}} now.
why: 三拍是「得到 → 缺 → 找」。有骨架在，被打断也能从任意一拍接回去，不会又退回流水账。
why_en: The arc is got it, missing it, looking for it — with those beats I can be interrupted and still pick the answer back up.

scenario: 答案库里「为什么离职」有三个版本：A 投 <100 人 early-stage、B 投 applied AI 公司、C 投 50-200 人 growth-stage。今天这通电话，对方的产品以 LLM agent 为核心。
scenario_en: Your answer bank has three "why I'm leaving" versions: A for sub-100-person early stage, B for applied-AI companies, C for 50-200-person growth stage. Today's call is with a company whose product is built on LLM agents.
q: 该用哪个版本？
q_en: Which version should you use?
options: 用版本 A：强调想端到端 own 一个问题、从第一个客户信号一直到上线看到结果，这条对任何比大厂小的公司都成立，也最好说。
用版本 C：强调把大厂的可靠性和发布流程带进一个架构决策还在制定中的环境，并参与塑造这些决策。
三个版本各说一小段，把自己想要的东西一次说全，让对方从里面自己挑他们最在意的那一条。
用版本 B：从 Meta 给 AI agent 喂业务数据的那层切入，说想参与 AI 系统本身的设计与评估。
options_en: Use version A: end-to-end ownership of a problem from the first customer signal all the way to launch — true of any company smaller than big tech, and the easiest to deliver.
Use version C: bring big-company reliability and rollout process into an environment where architecture decisions are still open to shape.
Give a slice of all three so everything you want is on the table and they can pick whichever matters most to them.
Use version B: start from the Meta layer that fed business data to the AI agent, and say you want inside the design and evaluation of the AI system itself.
tradeoff: 按公司类型选版本 vs 一套通吃：通吃省准备，代价是对 applied AI 公司说不出你离 AI 最近的那段经历。
why: 版本要对上对方的产品核心。对做 LLM agent 的公司，Meta 那段 onboarding 是我离 AI 最近的经历，不用等于浪费。
why_en: Match the version to their product core — for an LLM-agent company, the Meta onboarding layer is the closest I've been to AI and leaving it out wastes it.
whenOtherWins: 如果这家做的是 AI 之外的业务（支付、物流、B2B 工作流），版本 B 反而跑题，该退回 A 或 C。
optionMeanings: 端到端 ownership 版本。
把大厂经验带进扩张期版本。
三个版本混着说一遍。
回到 AI 系统本身的版本。
optionMeanings_en: The end-to-end ownership version.
The bring-big-company-rigor-to-growth version.
A blend of all three versions.
The go-back-into-the-AI-system version.
optionDirectness: 面对 0-1 阶段的小团队时最贴。
面对已有客户、正在扩张的团队时最贴。
任何单场面试都不该这么用。
对方产品核心就是模型或 agent 时最贴。
optionDirectness_en: Best against a 0-to-1 team still finding the product.
Best against a team with customers and a scaling problem.
Never the right move inside a single interview.
Best when the model or agent is their product core.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对，但没用上你唯一的 AI 经历。
扩张期语言对上不了 agent 产品的痛点。
三段并列等于没有立场，听着像在挑工作。
把最相关的一段经历放到了答案正中间。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Not wrong, but it leaves your only AI experience unused.
Scaling language doesn't touch what an agent product hurts from.
Three answers at once reads as shopping rather than choosing.
It puts your most relevant experience at the center.

q: 「为什么离职」的 A/B/C 三个版本各对应什么类型的公司？
q_en: Which company type does each of the A/B/C "why I'm leaving" versions target?
text: 版本 A → {{early-stage}}（<100 人、产品还在 0-1）；版本 B → {{applied AI}}（产品以 LLM/agent 为核心）；版本 C → {{growth-stage}}（50-200 人、已有客户开始扩张）。
text_en: Version A → {{early-stage}} (under 100 people, still 0-to-1); version B → {{applied AI}} (LLM or agent is the product); version C → {{growth-stage}} (50-200 people, customers already onboard).
why: 会前十分钟先判断公司类型再挑版本，判断依据是人数和产品阶段，不是行业标签。
why_en: Ten minutes before the call I classify the company by headcount and product stage, not by industry label, and pick the matching version.

scenario: 面试官问「你为什么离开 TikTok？」你答到一半顺势接上「所以我很想加入你们，因为你们做的东西……」，两个问题揉成了一段。
scenario_en: Asked "why are you leaving TikTok?", you slid halfway through into "...which is why I'd love to join you, because what you're building..." — merging two questions into one answer.
q: 这两题为什么必须分开答？
q_en: Why do these two questions have to stay separate?
options: 揉在一起没问题，本来就是同一件事的两面，一次说完还能省时间、显得逻辑连贯、不啰嗦。
分开答：离职那题只讲我缺什么，「为什么来这家」留到对方问，那时才点名他们的产品做连接。
分开答是因为面试官按题打分，混答会让评分表上有一栏空着，最后被算成没有回答这道题。
应该反过来：先讲为什么来这家，再顺带解释离职，用对这家公司的热情把离职话题盖过去。
options_en: Merging is fine — they're two sides of one thing, and covering both at once saves time and sounds coherent.
Keep them apart: the leaving answer only says what I'm missing, and why-this-company waits until they ask, so I can name their product then.
Keep them apart because interviewers score per question, and a merged answer leaves a blank row that counts as unanswered.
Do the reverse: lead with why this company and fold the leaving reason in, letting enthusiasm cover the departure topic.
tradeoff: 分开答 vs 揉成一段：揉着说省一次开口，代价是三句骨架被冲散，两边的落点都讲不深。
why: 离职那题的落点是「我缺什么」，why this company 的落点是「你们有什么」。合在一起，两个落点互相稀释。
why_en: The leaving answer lands on what I'm missing and why-this-company lands on what they have, so merging them dilutes both landings.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方直接问「为什么离开现在的公司来我们这」，那就是一题两问，这时才用一句话把两边接起来。
optionMeanings: 合并成一段一次讲完。
两题各自独立、各有落点。
以评分表机制为由分开。
先讲来意再补离职原因。
optionMeanings_en: Merge them into one continuous answer.
Keep two answers with two distinct landings.
Separate them because of scoring mechanics.
Lead with the attraction and tuck the exit in after.
optionDirectness: 对方一句话把两题一起问出来时才成立。
两题分别被问出来时的默认做法。
机制猜测；换个面试官就不成立。
离职原因确实敏感、想快速带过时的权宜。
optionDirectness_en: Only holds when they literally ask both in one breath.
The default whenever the two questions arrive separately.
A guess about scoring; a different interviewer breaks it.
A stopgap when the exit reason is genuinely sensitive.
optionScenarioImpacts: 三句骨架讲到一半就被自己岔断。
离职讲完整，公司理由留在最有效的位置。
理由是编的机制，真被追问会露馅。
热情盖不住空缺，对方还会把离职题问回来。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You derail your own three-sentence arc halfway through.
The exit lands whole and the company reason keeps its best slot.
The reasoning is invented and collapses under a follow-up.
Enthusiasm doesn't cover the gap; they ask the exit question again.

q: 「Why now」和「为什么离职」怎么分工，该说哪三件事？
q_en: How does "why now" differ from "why are you leaving," and which three things does it cover?
text: Why now 单独准备，说三件：我在 TikTok 待了{{多久}}、交付了{{哪些具体项目}}（Promotion Day、GM Max）、以及为什么{{现在}}是带着这个基础去下一站的时机。
text_en: Prepare "why now" separately and cover three things: {{how long}} I've been at TikTok, {{which projects}} I shipped, and why {{now}} is the right moment to take that foundation somewhere else.
why: 离职题讲的是缺口，why now 讲的是时机——待了多久、交付了什么、所以现在收得住。两题分开背。
why_en: The leaving answer is about the gap and why-now is about timing — how long, what shipped, and why the chapter closes cleanly here.

scenario: GenLogs 那次「为什么离职」，你把「end to end」重复了 4 次，中间没有转折也没有递进，整段听下来是同一个词的四种说法。
scenario_en: In the GenLogs call your "why I'm leaving" repeated "end to end" four times with no turn and no build — four phrasings of one word.
q: 这段回答的问题出在哪、怎么改？
q_en: What's actually wrong with that answer, and how do you fix it?
options: 缺弧线：四次「end to end」全是「我想要什么」，没有「我得到了什么」和「我还缺什么」这两拍。
用词太单调，换成 autonomy、full-stack、独立负责这些近义词轮流说，内容听起来就丰富了。
整段太短了，应该再举两个项目例子把它撑到一分半，信息量上去之后自然就有说服力了。
关键词选错了，「end to end」太抽象，应该整段换成「更接近客户痛点」这个说法反复强调。
options_en: It has no arc: all four "end to end"s are what I want, with no beat for what I got and what I'm missing.
The wording is monotonous — rotate through autonomy, full-stack and owning it yourself and it will sound much richer.
It's too short — add two more project examples to stretch it to ninety seconds and the volume will carry it.
The keyword is wrong — "end to end" is too abstract, so repeat "closer to customer pain" throughout instead.
tradeoff: 补齐三拍 vs 换同义词：换词让句子不重复，代价是整段仍然只有「我想要」一种信息。
why: 重复一个词不等于有结构。一段合格的回答里要出现三种不同信息：得到了什么、缺什么、现在找什么。
why_en: Repeating one phrase is not structure — a working answer carries three different kinds of information, not one said four ways.
optionMeanings: 问题是缺三拍中的两拍。
问题是词汇重复。
问题是篇幅不够。
问题是关键词选错。
optionMeanings_en: The problem is two missing beats.
The problem is repeated vocabulary.
The problem is insufficient length.
The problem is the wrong keyword.
optionDirectness: 整段只表达了一种诉求时的诊断。
结构已经完整、只是措辞单调时才对。
回答确实短到只有一句时才对。
关键词与对方业务完全无关时才对。
optionDirectness_en: The right diagnosis when the whole answer expresses one wish.
Only right if the structure is already complete and dull.
Only right if the answer really is a single sentence.
Only right when the keyword misses their business entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts: 补上前两拍，这段立刻有了因果。
换四个词说同一件事，信息量没变。
拉长到九十秒，重复也跟着变长。
换个词继续重复，还是一拍到底。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Adding the first two beats gives the answer cause and effect.
Four synonyms for one idea carry the same information.
Stretching to ninety seconds just stretches the repetition.
A new keyword repeated is still a single beat.

scenario: 你已经在不同场次说过两个方向：Inventing VC 那次是「infra AI 平台与可靠性」，WOP、Assembled、Pinpoint 是「端到端 ownership、更接近客户」。现在要挑一条以后只说它。
scenario_en: You have already given two directions in different calls: infrastructure AI platform and reliability at Inventing VC, and end-to-end ownership closer to the customer at WOP, Assembled and Pinpoint. Now you have to keep exactly one.
q: 该按什么依据挑出留下的那一条？
q_en: On what basis do you choose which direction to keep?
options: 挑听起来更资深的那条：infra 和可靠性在大厂语境里更像高级工程师的活，定级时也许更占便宜。
挑简历上字面证据更多的那条：哪条方向在简历里能找到更多关键词就留哪条，改起来也最省事。
先不挑：两条都留着，等某一家公司明确表态更看重哪一条时，再顺着他们的偏好把方向定下来。
挑实际反馈更好、且对得上你正在投的岗位类型的那条——产品向的端到端 ownership 就是它。
options_en: Keep whichever sounds more senior: infra and reliability read as higher-level work in big-tech language and may help at level-setting.
Keep whichever has more literal evidence on the resume, since the direction with more matching keywords is the cheapest to support.
Do not choose yet: hold both and let the first company that states a preference decide the direction for you.
Keep the one that has drawn better real responses and matches the roles you are applying to — the product-side end-to-end ownership line.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["两个方向都说出去了"] --> B["依据一 — 哪条拿到的实际反馈更好"]
  A --> C["依据二 — 我正在投哪一类岗位"]
  B --> D["留下产品向端到端 ownership"]
  C --> D
  D --> E["简历与故事按这一条重排"]
tradeoff: 按实际反馈挑 vs 按听起来资深挑：挑资深的短期定级也许好看，代价是我拿不出对应的故障、容量和可靠性数字。
why: 依据是「哪条是真的、我投的又是哪类岗位」，不是哪条听着更高级。产品向那条拿到的回应更好，就留它。
why_en: Choose by which direction is actually true and matches the roles I am applying to, not by which sounds more senior — the product line has drawn the better responses.
whenOtherWins: 如果我把投递重心整体切到平台/基础设施岗位，那就该改留 infra 那条——但简历和故事要跟着一起重排。
optionMeanings: 按听起来的资深程度挑。
按简历关键词数量挑。
推迟决定，让对方来定。
按真实反馈和投递方向挑。
optionMeanings_en: Choose by which sounds more senior.
Choose by which has more resume keywords.
Defer the decision and let them choose.
Choose by real responses and where you are applying.
optionDirectness: 只有你确实打算补齐可靠性经历时才成立。
简历本来就写得很准时才勉强够用。
你自己确实还在两条路之间摇摆时才诚实。
你已经积累了几十场反馈、能看出规律时。
optionDirectness_en: Only valid if you genuinely intend to build the reliability record.
Barely enough when the resume was already written accurately.
Honest only if you truly are still torn between the two paths.
Right once you have dozens of calls worth of signal to read.
optionScenarioImpacts: 定级也许好看，深挖时讲不出故障案例。
关键词多不代表故事强，追问会露底。
每家给一个版本，漂移问题原封不动。
方向和证据对齐，以后每场都能重复。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It may read as senior until a deep dive asks for an incident story.
More keywords is not a stronger story, and probing exposes the gap.
Each company gets its own version and the drift problem stays.
Direction and evidence line up, so every future call repeats it.

scenario: 你要在「平台/基础设施工程」和「产品工程」之间选一条对外统一的叙事线。两条线在面试里被问的问题、要的证据都不一样。
scenario_en: You have to pick one public narrative line — platform/infrastructure engineering or product engineering. The two get asked different questions and demand different evidence.
q: 这两条叙事线的根本区别落在哪个维度？
q_en: On which dimension do these two narrative lines actually differ?
options: 落在公司规模上：平台线只存在于大厂、产品线只存在于创业公司，挑公司规模就等于替你选好了线。
落在技术栈上：平台线写 Go 和 Kubernetes、产品线写 React 和 TypeScript，语言选择决定你属于哪条线。
落在职级上：平台线更容易被评成资深、产品线偏初级，所以一律往平台线靠会拿到更高的定级。
落在你服务谁：平台线的客户是内部工程师、用可靠性衡量；产品线的客户是终端用户、用采纳衡量。
options_en: Company size: platform work only exists in big tech and product work only in startups, so picking a size picks your line.
Tech stack: platform means Go and Kubernetes, product means React and TypeScript, and the language decides which line you're on.
Level: platform work is read as more senior and product work as junior, so leaning platform gets you a higher offer level.
Who you serve: platform serves internal engineers and is measured by reliability; product serves end users and is measured by adoption.
tradeoff: 平台线 vs 产品线：平台线要的是可靠性数字，产品线要的是客户影响；同一段经历没法同时当两边最强的证据。
why: 区别在服务对象和衡量指标，不在公司大小或语言。选一条，再把 TikTok/Meta 的经历按那条线重排证据。
why_en: The split is who you serve and how you're measured, not company size or language, so pick one line and re-rank your evidence for it.
optionMeanings: 按公司规模划分两条线。
按编程语言划分两条线。
按职级高低划分两条线。
按服务对象与指标划分。
optionMeanings_en: Split the lines by company size.
Split the lines by programming language.
Split the lines by seniority level.
Split by who you serve and how you're measured.
optionDirectness: 只在你只考虑一种规模的公司时勉强成立。
描述现象可以，用来定叙事线会选错。
薪资谈判里的传闻，不是叙事线的分界。
决定面试官会问你要哪一类证据。
optionDirectness_en: Barely holds if you only ever target one company size.
