optionExplanations_en: A transition is not mere politeness; it has three concrete functions, and skipping loses the interviewer and the redirect window.
Correct — the three functions (redirect moment, show structure, set checkpoint) are exactly the turn-signal value.
A transition is not stalling; it actively syncs and sets checkpoints, so treating it as a pause excuse misreads it.
A transition is not repeating conclusions; it is one brief bridge, and repeating wastes budget.

scenario: 你把范围定到「Airbnb 搜索排序，200ms 延迟」，准备转入数据策略。
scenario_en: You scoped it to 'Airbnb search ranking under 200 ms' and are about to move into data strategy.
q: 填空：一句好的转场信号包含哪三块？
q_en: Fill in: what three pieces make a good transition line?
text: 「我已经把范围定到 {{Airbnb 搜索排序、200ms 延迟}}（回顾上一步结论），下面进入 {{数据策略}}（点名下一步）——{{sound good/可以吗}}？（征得同意）」
text_en: "I've scoped this to {{Airbnb search ranking under 200 ms}} (recap the prior step), moving to {{data strategy}} (name the next step) — {{sound good}}? (check in)"
why: 好转场＝回顾上一步结论＋点名下一步＋征得同意（sound good?）。这既设了检查点，又给面试官一个重定向的窗口。
why_en: A good transition recaps the prior step, names the next step, and checks in, setting a checkpoint and a redirect window.

scenario: 面试一开始你就在白板/共享文档顶部有块空间可以用。
scenario_en: At the interview's start you have blank space at the top of the whiteboard or shared doc.
q: 一个低成本的进度管理技巧是什么？
q_en: What is a low-cost progress-management trick?
why: 开场就把 6 步写在白板顶端，每完成一步就打勾——一个对双方都可见的进度条。它让你和面试官随时知道走到哪、还剩哪几步，天然防止时间漂移。
why_en: Write the six steps at the top of the whiteboard and check each off as you transition, a shared visual progress tracker that prevents time drift.
tradeoff: 白板进度条(占几秒但双方可见) vs 靠记忆(省时但易漂移)
whenOtherWins: 若是纯语音、没有共享白板的电话面，就用口头 recap 代替打勾，效果类似但要更勤地口头同步进度。
options: 把每一步的完整笔记都写满白板，越详细越好
开场把 6 步写在白板顶端，每完成一步就打勾
全程不写任何东西，靠记忆管理进度，显得从容
只在最后 5 分钟把走过的步骤补写上去，当作总结
options_en: Fill the whiteboard with complete notes for every step — the more detail the better.
Write the six steps at the top and tick each one off as you go.
Write nothing all session and manage progress from memory to look composed.
Only in the last 5 minutes, jot the steps you covered down as a summary.
optionExplanations: 写满详细笔记会占用宝贵时间还挡视线；进度条要的是简洁可扫读。
对；顶端列 6 步+打勾＝低成本进度条，双方随时看到走到哪、还剩几步。
纯靠记忆容易漂移，也让面试官看不到结构，反而不利。
最后补写起不到实时防漂移的作用，进度条的价值在过程中而非结尾。
optionExplanations_en: Filling in detailed notes eats precious time and blocks the view; a tracker should be terse and scannable.
Correct — six steps at the top plus checkmarks is a low-cost tracker so both sides always see position and remaining steps.
Memory-only invites drift and hides your structure from the interviewer, which hurts.
Writing it at the end gives no real-time drift protection; the tracker's value is during, not after.

scenario: 你需要在陷太深之前就察觉「我在这步待太久了」。
scenario_en: You need to notice 'I've been on this step too long' before you sink too deep.
q: 检测「过度投入某一步」有哪三个信号？
q_en: What are the three signals for detecting over-investment in a step?
why: 三个信号：10 分钟阈值（最可靠的客观信号）、细节层级漂移（开始争超参/层数而非设计级取舍）、面试官重定向提示（「我们继续吧」或问别的步骤）。任一出现就该收手。
why_en: Three signals: the 10-minute threshold (most reliable, objective), detail-level drift (debating hyperparameters instead of design tradeoffs), and interviewer redirect cues.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["在某步待太久?"] --> B["信号1: 超过10分钟(最可靠客观)"]
  A --> C["信号2: 细节漂移(争超参/层数)"]
  A --> D["信号3: 面试官重定向提示"]
  B --> E["进入恢复协议"]
  C --> E
  D --> E
options: 10 分钟阈值、细节层级漂移、面试官重定向提示
自己感觉累了、面试官打了个哈欠、白板写满了
已经讲了 3 个要点、喝了一口水、看了一眼时钟
面试官记笔记、你停顿了一次、麦克风有回声
options_en: The 10-minute threshold, detail-level drift, and interviewer redirect cues.
Feeling tired, the interviewer yawning, and the whiteboard being full.
Having covered 3 points, taking a sip of water, and glancing at the clock.
The interviewer taking notes, you pausing once, and mic echo.
optionExplanations: 对；10 分钟阈值（客观）＋细节漂移＋面试官重定向，是本课给的三个可操作信号。
累了/哈欠/白板满都是主观或无关线索，不构成可靠的超时判据。
讲了几点、喝水、看表都不是过度投入的判据，和时长信号无关。
记笔记、停顿、回声是噪声，不能用来判断你是否在某步陷太深。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the 10-minute threshold (objective) plus detail drift plus interviewer redirect are the three actionable signals given here.
Tiredness, yawns, and a full whiteboard are subjective or irrelevant and are not reliable overrun criteria.
Covering points, sipping water, and clock-glancing are not over-investment criteria and are unrelated to duration signals.
Note-taking, a pause, and echo are noise and cannot indicate whether you have sunk too deep into a step.

scenario: 模型设计时你发现自己开始和面试官争「用 4 个还是 8 个注意力头」。
scenario_en: In model design you catch yourself debating '4 or 8 attention heads' with the interviewer.
q: 「细节层级漂移」这个超时信号具体长什么样？
q_en: What does the 'detail-level drift' overrun signal actually look like?
why: 细节漂移＝从设计级取舍掉进具体超参/层数/代码（如「4 还是 8 个注意力头」）。这类争论对整体设计几乎无增量，是你在这步陷太深的信号，该拉回设计级。
why_en: Detail drift is dropping from design-level tradeoffs into specific hyperparameters, layer counts, or code, like arguing 4 vs 8 attention heads.
tradeoff: 设计级取舍(该停留处) vs 超参/层数细节(漂移信号)
options: 从超参细节升回到设计级取舍——这是好现象，不是漂移
从设计级取舍掉进具体超参/层数/代码细节
从模型设计切换到评估步骤——正常转场，不算漂移
面试官突然问了一个和当前步骤无关的问题
options_en: Rising from hyperparameter detail back up to design-level tradeoffs — a good sign, not drift.
Dropping from design-level tradeoffs down into hyperparameters, layers, or code.
Switching from model design to evaluation — a normal transition, not drift.
The interviewer suddenly asking something unrelated to the current step.
optionExplanations: 方向反了：升回设计级是好事；漂移是往细节下沉，不是往上升。
对；掉进超参/层数这种低层细节，正是「陷太深」的典型表现，该拉回设计级。
切到下一步是正常转场，不是细节漂移，两个概念不同。
面试官问别的步骤属于「重定向提示」，是另一个信号，不是细节漂移。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: rising to design level is good; drift is sinking into detail, not rising.
Correct — dropping into low-level detail like hyperparameters and layers is the classic 'too deep' symptom; pull back to design level.
Moving to the next step is a normal transition, not detail drift — different concepts.
The interviewer asking about another step is a 'redirect cue', a different signal, not detail drift.

scenario: 欺诈题上，你在特征工程已经花了 12 分钟，意识到超时了。
scenario_en: On a fraud prompt you have spent 12 minutes on feature engineering and realize you have overrun.
q: 把「过度投入后的 3 步恢复协议」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 3-part recovery protocol after over-investment:
steps: 简短承认花了不少时间（不反复道歉）
当场给出这一步的决定（如：三个关键信号是交易速度、商户风险、设备指纹相似度）
立刻转入下一步（Moving to model design now）
why: 恢复协议＝承认→做决定→立刻走。关键是承认要简短、决定要果断、转场要立刻，别反复道歉。优雅的自我纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 信号。
why_en: The recovery protocol is acknowledge, decide, move on immediately, keeping the acknowledgment brief and the transition instant.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1 简短承认
花了些时间"] --> B["2 当场给决定
top-3 信号"] B --> C["3 立刻转下一步
模型设计"]

scenario: 你意识到某步超时，很想连着说好几句「抱歉，我花太久了，真不好意思……」
scenario_en: Realizing you overran a step, you feel the urge to say several apologies in a row.
q: 超时后反复道歉会怎样？正确做法是什么？
q_en: What happens if you over-apologize after overrunning, and what is the right move?
why: 反复道歉浪费时间、还显得不够沉稳。正确做法是一句简短「我在这上面花得够多了」，然后果断给决定、立刻转场。压力下的优雅自我纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 评估信号。
why_en: Repeated apologies waste time and read as less composed, so give one brief acknowledgment then decide and transition, since graceful self-correction is itself a Staff+ signal.
options: 反复道歉显得谦逊有礼，面试官会因此给你加分
一句简短承认后果断转场，别反复道歉
干脆完全不承认超时，假装什么都没发生继续讲
先花一分钟解释为什么会超时，把原因说清楚再继续
options_en: Repeated apologies look humble and polite, so the interviewer gives you points.
One brief acknowledgment, then a decisive transition — no repeated apologies.
Just never acknowledge the overrun and carry on as if nothing happened.
Spend a minute explaining why you overran, make the cause clear, then continue.
optionExplanations: 反复道歉不是谦逊，它消耗预算又暴露慌乱，是减分不是加分。
对；一句简短承认＋果断转场既止损又显沉稳，优雅纠偏是 Staff+ 信号。
完全不承认会让面试官觉得你没意识到时间问题，缺乏自我监控。
花一分钟解释原因又是新的浪费，承认要简短，别把道歉换成长篇解释。
optionExplanations_en: Repeated apologies are not humility; they burn budget and signal fluster — a minus, not a plus.
Correct — one brief acknowledgment plus a decisive transition stops the loss and reads as composed; graceful self-correction is a Staff+ signal.
Never acknowledging makes the interviewer think you missed the time issue, showing weak self-monitoring.
A minute of explanation is fresh waste; keep the acknowledgment brief rather than swapping apology for a long explanation.

scenario: 题目是广告点击预测，1M QPS、sub-50ms。默认预算里模型设计 8-10 分钟、部署 7-8 分钟。
scenario_en: The prompt is ad-click prediction at 1M QPS, sub-50ms; default budget gives model design 8-10 min and serving 7-8 min.
q: 这种延迟关键的题，时间预算该怎么调？
q_en: For this latency-critical prompt, how should you reshuffle the budget?
why: 延迟关键题让 serving 主导：把部署提到 10-12 分钟、把模型设计压到 6-7 分钟。因为吞吐/延迟在你讨论前就淘汰了整类架构，serving 决策才是这题的重心。并显式说明这次重分配。
why_en: Latency-critical prompts let serving dominate, so give serving 10-12 minutes and compress model design to 6-7, because throughput eliminates architectures before you discuss them.
tradeoff: serving 深度(延迟先淘汰整类架构) vs 模型设计深度(取舍多但非瓶颈)
whenOtherWins: 若这题延迟宽松、瓶颈在建模质量，就保持默认预算，不必把部署拉长——重分配要由约束驱动。
options: 保持默认预算不变，延迟题也按标准 8-10 分钟讲模型
部署提到 10-12 分钟、模型设计压到 6-7 分钟
把评估拉到 12 分钟，因为延迟关键题最难定义指标
把监控拉长，延迟题上线后最容易出问题所以监控最重要
options_en: Keep the default budget unchanged; even a latency prompt gets the standard 8-10 min on models.
Give serving 10-12 min and compress model design to 6-7.
Stretch evaluation to 12 min because latency prompts are hardest to measure.
Stretch monitoring because latency prompts break most after launch, so monitoring matters most.
optionExplanations: 延迟题保持默认就浪费了主动重分配的判断力——约束已明显把重心推向 serving。
对；serving 主导＝把部署拉到 10-12、模型压到 6-7，因为延迟先砍掉一批架构。
延迟题难点在 serving 不在评估，把评估拉到 12 分钟是重心放错。
监控重要但不是这题的主导约束，延迟才是；拉长监控偏离了约束驱动的重分配。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the default on a latency prompt wastes the judgment of a deliberate reshuffle; the constraint clearly shifts weight to serving.
Correct — serving dominates, so give it 10-12 and compress models to 6-7, since latency cuts architectures first.
The hard part of a latency prompt is serving, not evaluation, so stretching evaluation to 12 min misplaces the focus.
Monitoring matters but is not this prompt's dominant constraint — latency is; stretching monitoring departs from constraint-driven reshuffle.

scenario: 题目是生成式 AI（RAG、摘要），没有单一 ground truth，「好」很难定义。
scenario_en: The prompt is generative AI (RAG, summarization) with no single ground truth and 'good' hard to define.
q: 生成式 AI 题的时间预算该往哪倾斜？
q_en: Where should the time budget tilt for a generative-AI prompt?
why: GenAI 评估最难（无单一 ground truth），把评估拉到 8-10 分钟讲 LLM-as-judge、人工评估、忠实度；同时把部署压 -2 分钟（批/近实时常够用）。评估是这类题的重心。
why_en: For generative AI, evaluation is hardest with no single ground truth, so give evaluation 8-10 minutes for LLM-as-judge, human evaluation, and faithfulness, compressing serving by about 2 minutes.
tradeoff: 评估深度(无 ground truth，最难判好坏) vs 部署深度(批/近实时常够用)
whenOtherWins: 若这道 GenAI 题延迟极敏感（如实时对话助手），那 serving 又会回到重心，不能一味压部署。
options: 把模型设计拉到 12 分钟，专门讨论选哪个基座大模型
把评估拉到 8-10 分钟，部署相应压 -2 分钟
把数据策略拉到 10 分钟，因为 GenAI 成败全靠语料
保持默认预算，GenAI 和普通题的时间分配没区别
options_en: Stretch model design to 12 min just to discuss which base model to use.
Give evaluation 8-10 min and compress serving by about 2 min.
Stretch data strategy to 10 min because generative AI lives or dies on its corpus.
Keep the default budget; generative AI and ordinary prompts allocate time the same.
optionExplanations: GenAI 难点不在选哪个大模型，而在怎么评「好」，把模型拉到 12 分钟放错重心。
对；评估无 ground truth 最难，拉到 8-10 分钟讲 judge/人工/忠实度，压部署换出时间。
GenAI 也吃数据但这题的独特难点是评估，拉长数据没抓住主要矛盾。
GenAI 恰恰要往评估倾斜，说和普通题没区别就丢了域适配这个判断信号。
optionExplanations_en: The hard part of generative AI is not which large model but how to judge 'good', so stretching models to 12 min misplaces focus.
Correct — evaluation with no ground truth is hardest, so give it 8-10 min for judge/human/faithfulness and compress serving to fund it.
Generative AI uses data too, but this prompt's unique difficulty is evaluation, so stretching data misses the main tension.
Generative AI should tilt toward evaluation; saying it is no different forfeits the domain-adaptation judgment signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个大模型给另一个模型的输出打分/评判，替代部分人工评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM-as-judge uses one large model to score another model's outputs, partly replacing human evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成内容是否忠于检索到的证据、不编造，是 RAG 的关键评估维度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithfulness is whether generated content stays true to the retrieved evidence without fabricating, a key RAG eval dimension.

scenario: 题目是欺诈或医学影像：标签质量差、类别极不平衡、数据是主要瓶颈。
scenario_en: The prompt is fraud or medical imaging: poor label quality, severe class imbalance, data is the bottleneck.
q: 数据稀缺/噪声标签的题，时间预算怎么调？
q_en: For a data-scarce, noisy-label prompt, how do you adjust the budget?
why: 数据是瓶颈时把数据策略拉到 8-10 分钟，深入讲标签质量、类别不平衡、新鲜度；相应把监控压 -2 分钟。数据决策决定了这类题成败。
why_en: When data is the bottleneck, give data strategy 8-10 minutes for label quality, class imbalance, and freshness, compressing monitoring by about 2 minutes.
tradeoff: 数据策略深度(标签/不平衡是瓶颈) vs 监控深度(可压 -2 分钟)
whenOtherWins: 若数据充足、瓶颈其实在延迟或评估，就别硬拉数据策略——重分配始终跟着真实瓶颈走。
options: 把模型设计拉到 12 分钟，用更复杂的模型硬扛数据不足
数据策略拉到 8-10 分钟，监控相应压 -2 分钟
把部署拉到 10 分钟，先想怎么上线再回头补数据
保持默认预算，数据问题在评估阶段一起处理就行
options_en: Stretch model design to 12 min and brute-force data scarcity with a more complex model.
Give data strategy 8-10 min and compress monitoring by about 2 min.
Stretch serving to 10 min; deploy first and circle back to data later.
Keep the default; handle data issues together in the evaluation step.
optionExplanations: 数据不足时上更复杂模型只会过拟合，问题在数据层，堆模型解决不了。
对；瓶颈在数据就把预算投到数据策略，深挖标签/不平衡/新鲜度，压监控换时间。
先想上线再补数据是把顺序和重心都放错，数据没解决上线也白搭。
数据问题不能拖到评估才处理，它从训练一开始就污染一切，要在数据策略解决。
optionExplanations_en: A more complex model on scarce data just overfits; the problem is at the data layer and cannot be piled-model away.
Correct — when data is the bottleneck, invest the budget in data strategy on labels, imbalance, and freshness, compressing monitoring to fund it.
Deploy-first-then-data misplaces both order and focus; unsolved data makes launch pointless.
Data issues cannot wait for evaluation; they pollute everything from training onward and must be solved in data strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 正负样本比例极端悬殊（如欺诈只占 0.1%），会让模型偏向多数类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Class imbalance is an extreme skew between positive and negative samples (e.g. fraud is 0.1%), biasing the model to the majority class.

scenario: 你正按计划推进，面试官接连追问「怎么扛流量尖峰？」「feature store 挂了怎么办？」
scenario_en: You are on plan when the interviewer repeatedly asks 'handle a traffic spike?' and 'what if the feature store is down?'
q: 面试官反复追问 serving，你该怎么调整时间？
q_en: The interviewer keeps probing serving — how do you adjust time?
why: 面试官反复问某一步＝在告诉你他想看这里的深度，就顺势在 serving 上多花时间、讲深。反过来「行了，我们继续吧」就是让你立刻压缩转场。跟着面试官的线索走。
why_en: Repeated serving questions signal the interviewer wants depth there, so go deeper on serving, while 'that's fine, let's move on' means compress and transition immediately.
tradeoff: 跟着面试官线索加深 serving vs 守住原定预算保后续覆盖
whenOtherWins: 若面试官只是顺口一问、并未反复深挖，就简短回答后按原计划继续，不必大改预算。
options: 无视追问，坚持自己的时间计划把 serving 快速带过
顺势在 serving 上多花时间、讲得更深
把追问都推到最后 Q&A 环节统一回答，先走完流程
反问面试官为什么老问 serving，先搞清他的意图
options_en: Ignore the probes and stick to your plan, breezing past serving quickly.
Go deeper on serving right there, following the interviewer's lead.
Defer all probes to the final Q&A and finish the flow first.
Ask the interviewer why they keep asking about serving to clarify intent first.
optionExplanations: 无视反复追问会错过面试官明确给的信号，坚持原计划反而显得不会读场。
对；反复追问是重定向信号，顺势深挖 serving 正是跟着面试官线索的域适配。
把追问推到最后会让面试官觉得你回避，实时的深挖才是他想要的。
反问动机会显得防御，面试官的意图已经很清楚——他想看 serving 深度。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring repeated probes misses the interviewer's explicit signal, and sticking to plan reads as failing to read the room.
Correct — repeated probing is a redirect signal, so deepening serving follows the interviewer's cue — domain adaptation in action.
Deferring probes to the end makes the interviewer feel dodged; real-time depth is what they want.
Questioning their motive reads as defensive; the intent is already clear — they want serving depth.

scenario: 你还想在评估上多说两句，面试官说了句「That's fine, let's move on」。
scenario_en: You want to add more on evaluation, but the interviewer says 'that's fine, let's move on.'
q: 听到「行了，我们继续吧」这类提示，正确反应是什么？
q_en: On hearing 'that's fine, let's move on', what is the right response?
why: 这是明确的重定向提示：立刻压缩当前步、马上转场，别再补充。硬要多说会显得没读懂信号、也在浪费双方时间。面试官的节奏优先于你的计划。
why_en: It is a clear redirect cue, so compress the current step and transition immediately rather than adding more.
whenOtherWins: 若你判断当前这点是整题成败的关键、漏了会答不完整，可以用一句话说明「我补一句关键取舍就转」，但要极简。
options: 坚持把想说的评估细节补完，专业性不能打折
立刻压缩当前步、马上转场，别再补充
反问面试官「您是觉得这块不重要吗」再决定
假装没听见，继续按自己原本的节奏讲完
options_en: Insist on finishing the evaluation details you planned; professionalism must not be compromised.
Compress the current step and transition right away, adding nothing more.
Ask back 'do you think this part is unimportant?' before deciding.
Pretend not to hear and keep going at your own original pace.
optionExplanations: 硬补细节是没读懂信号，专业性不体现在无视提示上，反而显得不会配合。
对；「let's move on」是重定向提示，立刻压缩转场才是读懂了场、尊重面试官节奏。
反问会显得防御和纠缠，面试官已经明确表态，无需追问动机。
假装没听见是最差反应，直接踩了「无视重定向」的雷。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing details ignores the signal; professionalism is not shown by ignoring a cue, and it reads as uncooperative.
Correct — 'let's move on' is a redirect cue, so compress and transition immediately, which shows you read the room and respect their pace.
Asking back reads as defensive and clingy; the interviewer has been explicit, so probing motive is needless.
Pretending not to hear is the worst response, stepping straight on the 'ignore the redirect' landmine.

scenario: Airbnb 排序题进行到第 18 分钟，你正深挖 re-ranking，面试官突然问「position bias（位置偏差）怎么处理」——它其实是数据/标签层面的问题。
scenario_en: At minute 18 on an Airbnb ranking prompt, deep in re-ranking, the interviewer asks about position bias — really a data/label-level concern.
q: 18 分钟深挖 re-ranking 时被问 position bias，最好的处理是什么？
q_en: At 18 min deep in re-ranking, asked about position bias — best move?
why: 简短承认它是与评估相关的数据/标签问题，简洁作答，并在 2 分钟内信号转场到评估。既回应了面试官，又不在 re-ranking 上继续超投、把话题拉回时间线。
why_en: Briefly acknowledge it as a data/label concern tied to evaluation, answer concisely, and signal a transition to evaluation within two minutes.
tradeoff: 就地深挖 position bias(答得透) vs 简洁作答 2 分钟内转场(保后续覆盖)
whenOtherWins: 若才刚进入这一步、时间还很充裕，可以就地把 position bias 讲得更展开些，不必急着 2 分钟内转场。
options: 停下 re-ranking，花 8 分钟专门深挖 position bias 的各种去偏方法
简短承认它是与评估相关的数据/标签问题，简洁作答，2 分钟内信号转场到评估
回一句「这个不重要」，继续讲 re-ranking
承认自己不懂 position bias，直接跳过这个问题
options_en: Stop re-ranking and spend 8 minutes deep-diving every position-bias debiasing method.
Briefly acknowledge it as a data/label concern tied to evaluation, answer concisely, and signal a transition to evaluation within 2 minutes.
Say 'that's not important' and keep talking about re-ranking.
Admit you do not know position bias and just skip the question.
optionExplanations: 已经 18 分钟还花 8 分钟深挖 position bias 会严重超时，挤掉后面步骤。
对；简短承认+简洁作答+2 分钟内转场，既回应又止损，把话题顺势带回评估。
把面试官的问题说成不重要既失礼又错判——position bias 确实影响标签质量。
直接说不懂并跳过丢掉了展示判断的机会，其实你能把它归到评估/标签去回应。
optionExplanations_en: At 18 minutes, an 8-minute deep dive on position bias badly overruns and crowds out later steps.
Correct — brief acknowledgment, concise answer, transition within 2 minutes both responds and stops the loss, steering back to evaluation.
Calling the interviewer's question unimportant is rude and wrong — position bias really does affect label quality.
Just admitting ignorance and skipping forfeits a chance to show judgment; you can tie it to evaluation/labels instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户更爱点靠前的结果，导致点击标签高估了排在前面的项，是数据/标签层的偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is that users click higher-ranked results more, so click labels overstate top items — a data/label-level bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序后再对 top 结果做二次调整（如多样性、去重、业务规则）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking adjusts the top results after initial ranking, e.g. for diversity, dedup, or business rules.

scenario: 6 步默认预算里，模型设计拿到的时间占比最高。
scenario_en: In the default budget, model design gets the highest share of time.
q: 模型设计的默认预算约 8-10 分钟（~20%）意味着什么？
q_en: What does model design's default 8-10 min (~20%) budget imply?
why: 8-10 分钟是给定的节奏目标（不是算出来的），~20% 占比最高，因为模型设计信息密度大、取舍最多。但它仍受 10 分钟硬上限约束，超了就要压缩转场。
why_en: The 8-10 minutes is a given pacing target and the highest share at about 20% because model design is the most information-dense step, still capped at 10 minutes.
options: 意味着模型设计可以随便超时、突破 10 分钟硬上限，因为它是六步中最重要的一步
占比最高(~20%)的给定节奏目标，但仍受 10 分钟硬上限约束
意味着其他 5 步必须各压缩到 3 分钟以内，把时间都让给模型设计
意味着这个数字是从 45 分钟总时长精确算出的最优值，换题也不会变
options_en: It means model design can freely overrun past the 10-minute hard cap, because it is the most important of the six steps.
It is a given pacing target with the largest ~20% share, still under the 10-minute cap.
It means the other five steps must each compress under 3 minutes to hand time over to model design.
It means the number is a precisely computed optimum from the 45-minute total, fixed across prompts.
optionExplanations: 占比最高不等于可以超时——10 分钟硬上限对每步都适用，模型设计也不例外。
对；8-10 分钟是给定目标、~20% 最高份额，但硬上限仍是 10 分钟，超了就压缩。
其他步不必压到 3 分钟以内，各有自己的默认预算，这是过度牺牲。
它是给定的节奏目标不是算出来的最优值，且会按题目域重分配。
optionExplanations_en: The highest share does not permit overrunning; the 10-minute cap applies to every step, model design included.
Correct — the 8-10 min is a given target and the highest ~20% share, but the hard cap stays at 10 minutes, so overrun means compress.
Other steps need not compress under 3 minutes; each has its own default budget, so this over-sacrifices.
It is a given pacing target, not a computed optimum, and it gets reallocated by prompt domain.

scenario: 你对模型架构最擅长，忍不住在模型设计上讲了 15 分钟，越讲越细。
scenario_en: Strongest at model architecture, you cannot resist spending 15 minutes on model design, getting finer and finer.
q: 钻进自己最强的组件出不来，会付出什么代价？
q_en: What is the cost of tunneling into your strongest component?
why: 在最强组件上超投＝后面的评估、部署、监控没时间讲，导致覆盖不全（首要失败模式）。而且这暴露了初级信号——不会跨关注点做预算。深度救不了缺失的广度。
why_en: Over-investing in your strongest component leaves no time for evaluation, serving, and monitoring, causing incomplete coverage and exposing a junior signal.
options: 没什么代价，把最强的一块讲透就能盖过其他步的缺失
后面几步没时间讲，导致覆盖不全，还暴露初级信号
只会让面试官觉得你谦虚，因为你没有炫耀其他技能
面试官会因为你在一处的深度而自动补满其他步的分
options_en: No cost; nailing your strongest part outweighs missing the other steps.
Later steps get no time, causing incomplete coverage and exposing a junior signal.
It just makes the interviewer think you are modest for not showing off other skills.
The interviewer auto-fills the other steps' scores because of your depth in one place.
optionExplanations: 单点深度盖不过整体缺失——广度优先下，覆盖不全就是失败，深度补不回。
对；钻深＝挤掉后面步骤＝覆盖不全，同时暴露不会做全局预算的初级信号。
超投一处不是谦虚，恰恰是失控的表现，和谦虚无关。
面试官不会替你补分——没讲到的步骤就是没有信号，深度不能转移。
optionExplanations_en: Single-point depth cannot outweigh overall gaps; under breadth-first, incomplete coverage is failure and depth cannot recover it.
Correct — tunneling crowds out later steps into incomplete coverage while exposing a junior signal of no global budgeting.
Over-investing in one place is not modesty; it is loss of control, unrelated to modesty.
The interviewer does not fill in scores for you; unspoken steps yield no signal and depth does not transfer.

scenario: 超时后你要用一个固定的 3 步套路把自己拉回正轨。
scenario_en: After overrunning you use a fixed 3-part routine to get back on track.
q: 填空：过度投入后的 3 步恢复协议。
q_en: Fill in: the 3-part recovery protocol after over-investment.
text: 恢复协议＝{{承认花的时间}}（简短、不反复道歉）→ {{给出决定}}（如 top-3 信号）→ {{立刻转场}}到下一步。
text_en: Recovery protocol = {{acknowledge time spent}} (briefly, no over-apologizing) → {{state the decision}} (e.g. top-3 signals) → {{move on}} immediately to the next step.
why: 承认→决定→转场，三步都要快。核心是承认简短、决定果断、转场立刻，让优雅的自我纠偏本身成为 Staff+ 信号，而不是慌乱的道歉循环。
why_en: Acknowledge, decide, move on, all quickly, so that graceful self-correction becomes a Staff+ signal rather than a fluster of apologies.

scenario: 时间不够时，很多人干脆把「部署上线」整步跳过不讲。
scenario_en: Short on time, many people just skip the entire serving/deployment step.
q: 把部署这步整个跳过，会造成什么后果？
q_en: What is the consequence of skipping the serving step entirely?
why: 整步跳过部署＝丢掉一整块系统思维信号（延迟、吞吐、扩展、feature store），这是覆盖不全最严重的一种。宁可每步压薄、也要 6 步都触及；系统思维正是部署这步在评的。
why_en: Skipping serving forfeits an entire block of systems-thinking signal (latency, throughput, scaling, feature store), the worst form of incomplete coverage.
options: 没关系，部署是运维的事，ML 面试不看这块
丢掉一整块系统思维信号，是最严重的覆盖不全
反而加分，说明你懂得取舍、敢于砍掉次要步骤
只影响 Staff+ 评级，对 Senior 及以下没有影响
options_en: It is fine; serving is ops work and ML interviews do not assess it.
It forfeits a whole block of systems-thinking signal — the worst incomplete coverage.
It actually adds points, showing you can prioritize and dare to cut minor steps.
It only affects Staff+ ratings and has no impact at Senior or below.
optionExplanations: 部署恰恰是 ML SD 在评的系统思维，不是纯运维，跳过就丢了这块分。
对；整步跳过＝丢一整块系统思维信号，比每步压薄严重得多，覆盖不全就是失败模式。
砍掉整步不是取舍是遗漏——取舍是压薄不是跳过，跳过整步是负信号。
系统思维在各级别都被评，跳过部署对 Senior 同样扣分，不只 Staff+。
optionExplanations_en: Serving is exactly the systems thinking ML SD assesses, not pure ops, so skipping forfeits that score.
Correct — skipping the whole step drops an entire systems-thinking block, far worse than thinning each step; incomplete coverage is the failure mode.
Cutting a whole step is omission, not prioritization; prioritizing means thinning, not skipping, and skipping is a negative signal.
Systems thinking is assessed at every level, so skipping serving penalizes Senior too, not just Staff+.

scenario: 面试官不只看你设计得对不对，也在看你怎么分配这 45 分钟。
scenario_en: The interviewer watches not only whether your design is right but how you allocate the 45 minutes.
q: 为什么说「怎么分配时间」本身就是被评估的内容？
q_en: Why is 'how you allocate time' itself something being assessed?
why: 时间分配本身是一个设计决策和资历信号：它反映你能否在有限预算下管理覆盖、识别重心、按约束重排。管不好时间＝管不好一个真实项目的范围。
why_en: Time allocation is itself a design decision and seniority signal, reflecting whether you can manage coverage and reprioritize under a fixed budget.
options: 因为面试官需要凑够评分项，时间只是用来凑数的
时间分配本身就是设计决策，反映你能否管理覆盖与重心
因为面试有硬性 KPI 要求必须用满 45 分钟
因为讲得越久越显得内容多，时间长短直接等于分数高低
options_en: Because the interviewer needs to pad the rubric, so time is just filler.
Time allocation is itself a design decision, showing whether you manage coverage.
Because interviews have a hard KPI to use the full 45 minutes.
Because talking longer looks like more content, so duration equals score.
optionExplanations: 时间不是凑数项，它直接映射到「能否管理一个真实项目范围」的判断。
对；分配时间＝管理覆盖与重心的能力，这正是资历信号，和管真实项目同构。
没有「用满 45 分钟」的 KPI，重点是合理覆盖而非填满时间。
讲得久≠内容多，冗长反而是负信号，时长不等于分数。
optionExplanations_en: Time is not filler; it maps directly to the judgment of whether you can manage a real project's scope.
Correct — allocating time is the ability to manage coverage and focus, exactly the seniority signal, isomorphic to running a real project.
There is no 'fill 45 minutes' KPI; the point is reasonable coverage, not maxing time.
Talking longer is not more content; verbosity is a negative signal, and duration does not equal score.

scenario: 面试压力下你意识到跑偏了，能不能干净利落地把自己拉回正轨，本身也在被观察。
scenario_en: Under pressure you realize you drifted, and how cleanly you pull yourself back is itself being observed.
q: 在压力下优雅地自我纠偏，对评分意味着什么？
q_en: What does gracefully self-correcting under pressure mean for scoring?
why: 压力下的优雅自我纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 评估信号——它证明你有自我监控、能果断止损、不慌乱。所以恢复协议不只是补救，执行得干净利落反而是加分点。
why_en: Graceful self-correction under pressure is itself a Staff+ signal, proving self-monitoring and decisive recovery without panic.
options: 是中性的，纠不纠偏、纠得好不好都不影响面试官对你资历的评分
优雅纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 信号，证明你有自我监控
是负信号，一旦纠偏就暴露你之前跑偏了，不如硬撑到底装作没事
只对时间管理这一项打分有用，和整体资历评级完全无关
options_en: It is neutral; whether and how well you self-correct does not affect the interviewer's seniority scoring.
Graceful self-correction is itself a Staff+ signal, proving you monitor yourself.
It is a negative signal — correcting exposes that you drifted, so better to push through and act like nothing happened.
It only helps the time-management score and is entirely unrelated to overall seniority rating.
optionExplanations: 纠偏质量不是中性——干净利落的自我纠正是被明确评估的能力。
对；优雅纠偏证明自我监控和沉稳，是本课点名的 Staff+ 加分信号。
纠偏不是暴露弱点，硬撑跑偏才是；果断止损远好于将错就错。
它直接关联资历评级（Staff+ 信号），不只是时间分。
optionExplanations_en: Correction quality is not neutral; clean self-correction is an explicitly assessed ability.
Correct — graceful correction proves self-monitoring and composure, a Staff+ plus this lesson names.
Correcting is not exposing weakness; pushing through the drift is; decisive recovery beats compounding the error.
It ties directly to seniority rating (a Staff+ signal), not just the time score.

scenario: 问题澄清阶段，你已经问了七八个澄清问题，还在继续追问更多细节。
scenario_en: In clarification you have already asked seven or eight questions and keep probing for more detail.
q: 问题澄清阶段的过度投入陷阱是什么，怎么避免？
q_en: What is the over-investment trap in clarification, and how do you avoid it?
why: 陷阱是问一堆澄清题却不收敛。避免法：3-5 分钟内锁定目标、规模、延迟这几个关键约束就收敛出一句精确问题陈述，然后转场。澄清是为了收敛，不是无限提问。
why_en: The trap is asking many clarifying questions without converging, so within 3-5 minutes lock the key constraints into a precise problem statement and move on.
tradeoff: 多问澄清题(信息更全) vs 3-5 分钟内收敛(保住后面 5 步预算)
whenOtherWins: 若题目极度模糊、关键约束确实还没交代清楚，可以多问一两个，但仍要在 5 分钟内收敛出问题陈述。
options: 陷阱是问得太少，应该尽可能多问、覆盖所有可能情况
陷阱是问而不收敛；3-5 分钟内锁定关键约束就转场
陷阱是不该问任何澄清题，直接开始设计最省时间
陷阱是把澄清题写在白板上，占用了后面画图的空间
options_en: The trap is asking too few; ask as many as possible to cover every possibility.
The trap is asking without converging; lock the key constraints within 3-5 min, then move on.
The trap is asking any clarifying questions at all; just start designing to save the most time.
The trap is writing clarifying questions on the whiteboard, using up later drawing space.
optionExplanations: 问得越多越好正是陷阱本身——不收敛的提问会吃掉预算、拖慢全局。
对；澄清的目的是收敛，3-5 分钟锁定目标/规模/延迟就出问题陈述，然后转场。
完全不问会漏掉关键约束、方向可能全错，走另一个极端也不对。
占用白板空间不是这里的陷阱，真正的陷阱是问而不收敛。
optionExplanations_en: More is better is the trap itself; non-converging questions eat the budget and slow everything.
Correct — clarification aims to converge; lock objective/scale/latency in 3-5 min into a problem statement, then transition.
Asking nothing misses key constraints and may go entirely wrong — the opposite extreme is also wrong.
Using whiteboard space is not the trap here; the real trap is asking without converging.

scenario: 口头描述 YouTube 的「召回→排序→重排」流程要花 2-3 分钟，面试官还容易跟丢。
scenario_en: Verbally describing YouTube's candidate-generation to ranking to re-ranking flow costs 2-3 minutes and the interviewer can lose the thread.
q: 在 ML SD 面试里画图的核心价值是什么？
q_en: What is the core value of diagramming in an ML SD interview?
why: 一张好图把口头讲要 2-3 分钟的流程瞬间说清，省下的分钟可以投到取舍推理上。图是把「解释」压缩成「指认」的杠杆，不是装饰。
why_en: A good diagram makes instantly legible what verbal explanation costs 2-3 minutes, buying those minutes back for tradeoff reasoning.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["澄清后
高层系统图"] --> D["数据策略
数据流图"] D --> M["模型设计
架构草图(非平凡才画)"]
options: 让白板看起来更专业整洁，给面试官留下认真准备的印象
把口头要 2-3 分钟的流程一眼说清，省时投到取舍
证明你会用画图软件，展示工具熟练度和规范
把设计画得越复杂越好，用细节量压住面试官
options_en: Make the whiteboard look polished and tidy, leaving an impression that you came prepared.
Make a 2-3 minute verbal flow legible at a glance, buying minutes for tradeoffs.
Prove you can use diagramming software and show tool proficiency.
Draw the design as complex as possible to overwhelm the interviewer with detail.
optionExplanations: 整洁印象不是目的；图的价值在省时间和防跟丢，不在准备感或美观。
对；图＝把解释压成指认的杠杆，省下的 2-3 分钟正好投到取舍深挖。
面试不评你的画图软件熟练度，评的是设计沟通效率。
越复杂越好正好相反——过度工程是本课点名的常见错误。
optionExplanations_en: A tidy impression is not the point; a diagram's value is saving time and preventing lost threads, not looking prepared.
Correct — a diagram is a lever compressing explanation into pointing, and the 2-3 min saved goes into deeper tradeoffs.
The interview does not score software proficiency; it scores design-communication efficiency.
As-complex-as-possible is the opposite; over-engineering is a common mistake this lesson names.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 整场面试你可能画三种不同用途的图，各自对应框架的不同阶段。
scenario_en: Across the interview you may draw three purpose-specific diagram types, each mapping to a different framework phase.
q: ML SD 面试的三种核心图是哪三种？
q_en: What are the three core diagram types in an ML SD interview?
why: 三种：高层系统图（组件+箭头，澄清后画）、数据流图（原始→训练→预测→反馈，数据策略时画）、模型架构草图（内部结构，模型设计且非平凡时画）。各对应框架的一个阶段。
why_en: The three are the high-level system diagram, the data-flow diagram, and the model-architecture sketch, each mapping to a framework phase.
options: 类图、时序图、状态机图（这是软件工程通用三件套，不是本课的三种）
高层系统图、数据流图、模型架构草图
折线图、柱状图、饼图（这是数据可视化图表，不是系统设计图）
甘特图、燃尽图、看板（这是项目管理图，不是 ML 设计图）
options_en: Class, sequence, and state diagrams (the generic software-engineering trio, not this lesson's three).
High-level system diagram, data-flow diagram, and model-architecture sketch.
Line, bar, and pie charts (data-visualization charts, not system-design diagrams).
Gantt, burndown, and kanban (project-management charts, not ML design diagrams).
optionExplanations: 类图/时序图是通用 SWE 图，不是 ML SD 面试专用的这三种。
对；高层系统图/数据流图/模型架构草图，分别服务澄清、数据、模型三个阶段。
折线/柱/饼是数据图表，用来展示数据分布，不是设计系统结构。
甘特/燃尽/看板是项目管理工具，和设计一个 ML 系统的结构无关。
optionExplanations_en: Class and sequence diagrams are generic SWE diagrams, not the three specific to ML SD interviews.
Correct — high-level system, data-flow, and model-architecture sketch serve the clarify, data, and model phases.
Line/bar/pie are data charts for showing distributions, not for designing system structure.
Gantt/burndown/kanban are project-management tools, unrelated to structuring an ML system.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 问题澄清刚做完（约第 5-8 分钟），你要给整场设计立一个共享的心智模型。
scenario_en: Clarification just finished (around min 5-8) and you want to anchor a shared mental model for the whole design.
q: 高层系统图该什么时候画，能不能跳过？
q_en: When should the high-level system diagram be drawn, and can it be skipped?
why: 高层系统图要在澄清之后尽早画（约 min 5-8），因为它给双方立一个共享心智模型，后面所有讨论都挂在它上面。它是唯一「永不跳过」的图。
why_en: Draw the high-level system diagram early right after clarification (about min 5-8), because it anchors a shared mental model, and it is the one diagram you never skip.
whenOtherWins: 没有反例——高层系统图始终要画；若系统极简（单模型无外围组件），可以画得很小，但仍要画。
options: 等讲完所有细节后，在最后 5 分钟补一张总览图收尾
澄清后尽早画（min 5-8），立起共享心智模型，永不跳过
只在面试官明确开口要求时才画，否则全程靠口头讲完就够了
在模型设计阶段画，因为那时才清楚有哪些组件要连
options_en: Wait until all details are covered, then add a summary diagram in the last 5 minutes.
Draw it early right after clarification (min 5-8); it anchors a shared mental model and is never skipped.
Only draw it if the interviewer explicitly asks; otherwise talk through the whole thing verbally.
Draw it during model design, since only then do you know which components connect.
optionExplanations: 最后补图时心智模型早已（错误地）成型，事后画没有价值——这是「画太晚」的错误。
对；澄清后尽早画立共享心智模型，是三种图里唯一永不跳过的。
等面试官开口才画就晚了，高层图是你主动立框架的工具，不是被动等指令才用的道具。
组件在澄清后就大致清楚了，等到模型设计才画会错过锚定讨论的最佳时机。
optionExplanations_en: A late diagram comes after the mental model already (mis)formed and adds no value — the 'too late' mistake.
Correct — drawing it early after clarification anchors a shared model and is the only never-skip diagram of the three.
Waiting to be asked is too late; the high-level diagram is your proactive framing tool, not a prop you wait to be told to use.
Components are roughly clear after clarification; waiting until model design misses the best moment to anchor the discussion.
tradeoff: 早画图占掉的 2-3 分钟 vs 全场讨论有共享心智模型的沟通效率
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 数据策略阶段（约 min 8-15），你在讲数据从原始日志一路到训练、预测、再回流重训。
scenario_en: During data strategy (about min 8-15) you are explaining data from raw logs through training, prediction, and back to retraining.
q: 数据流图该在哪一步画？什么情况可以跳过？
q_en: At which step is the data-flow diagram drawn, and when can it be skipped?
why: 数据流图在数据策略阶段画（约 min 8-15），追踪原始数据→训练数据→预测→反馈回流。若管线本身很平凡（单一静态数据集、无反馈），可以跳过——画了也没增量。
why_en: Draw the data-flow diagram during data strategy (about min 8-15) to trace raw to training to predictions to the feedback loop, and skip it when the pipeline is trivial.
whenOtherWins: 若数据管线是单一静态数据集、没有反馈回流，就跳过数据流图，把时间留给别处。
options: 问题澄清阶段一开始就该画，越早锚定越好，和数据无关
数据策略阶段画（min 8-15）；管线平凡时可跳过
监控阶段画，因为反馈回流本来就属于监控范畴
任何阶段都必须画，它和高层图一样永不跳过
options_en: Draw it right at the start of clarification — the earlier the anchor, the better, unrelated to the data discussion.
Draw it in the data-strategy phase (min 8-15); skip it when the pipeline is trivial.
Draw it during monitoring, since the feedback loop belongs to monitoring anyway.
Always draw it; like the high-level diagram it is never skipped.
optionExplanations: 澄清阶段还没进入数据讨论，抢在这时画数据流图，时机和内容都对不上。
对；数据流图配合数据策略讲管线，平凡管线（静态数据集无反馈）没必要画。
反馈回流是数据流图的一部分，但整张图在数据策略阶段就该画，不是等到监控。
数据流图是可跳过的（管线平凡时），只有高层系统图才永不跳过。
optionExplanations_en: Clarification has not entered the data discussion yet, so drawing the data-flow diagram there mismatches both timing and content.
Correct — the data-flow diagram accompanies the data-strategy pipeline talk, and a trivial pipeline (static dataset, no feedback) need not be drawn.
The feedback loop is part of the data-flow diagram, but the whole diagram belongs in data strategy, not monitoring.
The data-flow diagram is skippable when the pipeline is trivial; only the high-level system diagram is never skipped.
tradeoff: 画数据流图的分钟 vs 讲清 原始→训练→预测→回流 链路的清晰度
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 模型设计阶段（约 min 15-22），你要决定要不要画一张模型内部结构草图。
scenario_en: In model design (about min 15-22) you must decide whether to sketch the model's internal structure.
q: 模型架构草图什么时候该画、什么时候该跳过？
q_en: When should you draw the model-architecture sketch, and when skip it?
why: 只在架构非平凡时画（双塔检索、多任务），画输入特征、层类型、embedding 维度、输出头、损失。若模型一句话说得清（逻辑回归、XGBoost），画草图就是浪费时间，直接口头说。
why_en: Sketch it only when the architecture is non-trivial (two-tower, multi-task), and skip it when the model is one-sentence describable like logistic regression or XGBoost.
whenOtherWins: 架构非平凡（双塔、多任务、多输出头、特殊交互层）时才值得画草图，标清输入维度、层类型、损失函数。
options: 任何模型都画草图，越详细越能显示技术深度
只在架构非平凡时画（双塔、多任务），简单模型跳过
只画一句话能说清的简单模型，复杂模型口头带过
在澄清阶段就提前画好，免得后面没有时间画
options_en: Sketch every model — the more detailed, the more depth it shows.
Sketch only non-trivial architectures (two-tower, multi-task); skip simple models.
Only sketch simple one-sentence models; describe complex ones verbally.
Draw it back in clarification so you do not run out of time later.
optionExplanations: 任何模型都画会在简单模型上浪费时间——一句话能说清的模型画草图没增量。
对；草图只为「空间关系重要」的非平凡架构服务，简单模型口头说更省时。
说反了：该画的恰恰是复杂架构（空间关系重要），简单模型才跳过。
澄清阶段还没定模型，画草图时机不对，应在模型设计阶段画。
optionExplanations_en: Sketching every model wastes time on simple ones — a one-sentence model gains nothing from a sketch.
Correct — the sketch serves only non-trivial architectures where spatial relationships matter; describe simple models verbally.
Reversed: the ones worth sketching are complex architectures (spatial relationships matter); simple models are what you skip.
Clarification has not fixed the model yet, so a sketch there is mistimed; draw it in model design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络末端针对某个任务的输出层；多任务模型有多个头。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An output head is the task-specific output layer at the end of a network; multi-task models have several.

tradeoff: 画草图的分钟 vs 非平凡架构里空间关系的表达清晰度
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 你画了高层系统图，但箭头都没写字，面试官盯着一条箭头问「这条代表什么？」
scenario_en: You drew a high-level system diagram but left arrows unlabeled, and the interviewer asks 'what does this arrow represent?'
q: 最常见的画图错误是什么，代价多大？
q_en: What is the single most common diagramming mistake, and what does it cost?
why: 未标注的箭头是最常见的画图错误：每条都逼面试官打断问「这代表什么」，一次约 15-20 秒。修法是每条箭头都标清流的是什么（「搜索请求」「特征向量」「排序结果」）。
why_en: Unlabeled arrows are the most common mistake, each forcing a 15-20 second interrupt asking what it represents, fixed by labeling every arrow with what flows.
options: 颜色用得太少、线条太细，整张图看起来单调不专业
未标注的箭头：每条制造一次 15-20 秒的打断
框画得不够方正，边角歪斜影响版面美观
图画在白板左半边而不是摆在正中间
options_en: Using too few colors and thin lines, so the whole diagram looks dull and unpolished.
Unlabeled arrows: each one costs a 15-20 second interruption.
Boxes not squared off, with crooked corners hurting the layout.
Drawing on the left half of the whiteboard instead of dead center.
optionExplanations: 颜色和线条粗细不影响理解，不是评分或效率问题。
对；未标箭头是头号错误，每条制造一次 15-20 秒打断，标清流的是什么即可消除。
框正不正方不影响理解，不是本课点名的错误。
画在哪一侧无关紧要，不构成沟通障碍。
optionExplanations_en: Color choice and line weight do not impede understanding and are neither a scoring nor an efficiency issue.
Correct — unlabeled arrows are the number-one mistake, each causing a 15-20 sec interrupt, removed by labeling what flows.
Whether boxes are square does not impede understanding and is not a mistake this lesson names.
Which side you draw on is irrelevant and creates no communication barrier.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 画图时要有一套统一的标注纪律，让每张图自解释。
scenario_en: You need consistent labeling discipline so every diagram is self-explanatory.
q: 画图的标注纪律具体包含什么？
q_en: What does diagram labeling discipline specifically include?
why: 纪律：每个框都命名、每条箭头都标注流的是什么，并在关键处加量化注解——serving 箭头上标 QPS、ETL 上标批处理频率、草图里标 embedding 维度。量化注解证明你在想扩展、延迟、漂移。
why_en: Name every box, label every arrow with what flows, and add quantitative annotations where they matter, like QPS on serving, batch frequency in ETL, and embedding dims in the sketch.
options: 只给最重要的两三个框命名，其余留白保持简洁
每个框命名、每条箭头标流的是什么，关键处加量化注解
把所有超参数、层数、损失函数都写进图里，越全越显功底
只标箭头不标框，框的含义留给口头补充说明
options_en: Name only the two or three most important boxes and leave the rest blank.
Name every box, label what flows on every arrow, and add numbers where they matter.
Write every hyperparameter, layer count, and loss function into the diagram — the fuller it is, the more depth it shows.
Label arrows only, not boxes, and explain the boxes verbally instead.
optionExplanations: 只命名部分框会留下无名框，制造「这是什么」的打断，纪律要求每个框都命名。
对；框命名+箭头标注+关键处量化注解，让图自解释，还顺带秀出你在想扩展/延迟/漂移。
把超参、层数、损失函数全塞进图是过度细节，图要停在组件层，不是塞满参数证明功底。
只标箭头不标框会留无名框，靠口头补充等于放弃图的自解释性。
optionExplanations_en: Naming only some boxes leaves nameless ones that trigger 'what is this' interrupts; discipline requires naming every box.
Correct — name boxes, label arrows, and add quantitative annotations where they matter, making the diagram self-explanatory and signaling scaling/latency/drift awareness.
Cramming every hyperparameter, layer count, and loss function is over-detail; a diagram stays at the component level, not stuffed with parameters to prove depth.
Labeling arrows only leaves nameless boxes, and verbal patching abandons the diagram's self-explanatory value.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 画图有几类常见错误会拖累而非帮助沟通，要能一一识别。
scenario_en: Several classes of diagramming mistakes hurt rather than help communication and must be recognized.
q: 以下哪些是本课点名的常见画图错误？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are the common diagramming mistakes named in this lesson? (multiple)
why: 常见错误：过度工程（画 K8s pods、负载均衡、DB 分片这些 DevOps 细节）、画太晚（先口头 20 分钟才补图）、组件无标注、从不更新（设计演进了图却停在旧版，会主动误导）。
why_en: Common mistakes are over-engineering with DevOps detail, drawing too late, unlabeled components, and never updating a stale diagram.
options: 过度工程：画 K8s pods、负载均衡、DB 分片等 DevOps 细节
画太晚：先口头讲 20 分钟，最后才补一张事后诸葛的图
组件无标注 / 从不更新：设计演进了图却停在旧版，主动误导
用了箭头连接组件（这是正常画法，不是错误）
options_en: Over-engineering: drawing K8s pods, load balancers, DB sharding and other DevOps detail.
Drawing too late: 20 minutes of verbal first, then an afterthought diagram.
Unlabeled components / never updating: the design evolves but the diagram stays stale and misleads.
Using arrows to connect components (this is normal practice, not a mistake).
optionExplanations: 对；画 DevOps 细节是过度工程，面试评 ML 判断不是运维，除非被问否则停在组件层。
对；先口头 20 分钟再补图，心智模型早已成型，事后图没价值。
对；无标注制造打断，从不更新的旧图会主动误导，两者都是常见错误。
用箭头连组件是正常画法本身，不是错误——错误是箭头没标注。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — DevOps detail is over-engineering; the interview scores ML judgment not ops, so stay at component level unless asked.
Correct — 20 minutes of verbal then a late diagram comes after the mental model formed, so it adds no value.
Correct — unlabeled components cause interrupts and a never-updated stale diagram actively misleads; both are common mistakes.
Using arrows to connect components is normal practice, not a mistake — the mistake is leaving arrows unlabeled.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在图里塞入与 ML 判断无关的运维细节（K8s、负载均衡、分片）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-engineering is stuffing a diagram with ops detail (K8s, load balancers, sharding) irrelevant to ML judgment.

category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 面试评的是你的 ML 判断，你却在高层图里画满了 K8s pods、负载均衡器、数据库分片。
scenario_en: The interview assesses your ML judgment, yet you fill the high-level diagram with K8s pods, load balancers, and DB sharding.
q: 在图里画满 K8s、负载均衡、分片这些细节，会怎样？
q_en: What happens if you pack the diagram with K8s, load balancers, and sharding detail?
why: 这是过度工程：面试评的是 ML 判断不是 DevOps，画满基础设施细节既浪费时间又转移了焦点。除非面试官明确问，图应停在组件层（客户端、网关、feature store、模型服务、日志、监控）。
why_en: It is over-engineering: the interview scores ML judgment not DevOps, so stay at the component level unless asked.
options: 加分，展示你连 K8s 扩缩容这些基础设施细节都懂
过度工程：ML 面试不评 DevOps，细节转移焦点
无所谓，画多画少都不影响最终评分结果
让图更完整，面试官会因此更信任你的整体设计能力
options_en: It adds points by showing you also understand infra detail like K8s auto-scaling.
Over-engineering: an ML interview scores ML judgment, not DevOps; detail shifts focus.
It makes no difference; more or less detail does not change the score.
It makes the diagram more complete, so the interviewer trusts your design ability more.
optionExplanations: 堆 K8s 扩缩容这类基础设施细节不加分——它转移了对 ML 判断的注意力，正是过度工程。
对；ML 面试评的是 ML 判断，除非被问，图停在组件层，别陷进 DevOps 细节。
并非无所谓——过度细节会吃时间、稀释 ML 信号，是明确的负面。
更多基础设施细节不等于更可信，反而暴露你没抓住这场面试评的重点。
optionExplanations_en: Piling on K8s auto-scaling detail does not add points; it diverts attention from ML judgment — exactly over-engineering.
Correct — an ML interview scores ML judgment, so unless asked, keep the diagram at component level and avoid DevOps detail.
It is not harmless — over-detail eats time and dilutes the ML signal, a clear negative.
More infra detail is not more credible; it reveals you missed what this interview assesses.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 设计演进了：你加了反馈回路和 feature store，但白板上的图还停在最初版本。
scenario_en: The design evolved: you added a feedback loop and feature store, but the whiteboard diagram is still the initial version.
q: 一张不随设计更新的旧图会造成什么？
q_en: What does a diagram that never updates with the design cause?
why: 从不更新的旧图会主动误导——它和你正在讲的设计不一致，面试官对着旧图理解会跑偏。修法是随设计演进补图：加上反馈回路、feature store、监控箭头，让图和口头保持同步。
why_en: A stale diagram actively misleads because it no longer matches the design you are describing, fixed by updating it as the design evolves.
options: 没影响，面试官会自动脑补最新的版本
旧图会主动误导：和当前设计不一致，理解会跑偏
反而更好，保持图不改动最省事也最简洁
只在最后总结时才有问题，过程中不更新没关系
options_en: No effect; the interviewer mentally patches in the latest version.
A stale diagram actively misleads: it no longer matches the design, so understanding drifts.
It is actually better; leaving the diagram untouched is simplest.
It only matters at the final summary; not updating along the way is fine.
optionExplanations: 面试官不会脑补——他看到的是白板上的旧图，不一致就会误导。
对；旧图和当前设计脱节会主动误导，随演进加反馈回路/feature store 才保持同步。
保持不动省的是画图的力气，代价是图变成误导源，得不偿失。
过程中的不一致就已经在误导了，不是等到总结才出问题。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer does not mentally patch it; they see the stale board diagram, and the mismatch misleads.
Correct — a stale diagram diverges from the current design and misleads; update with feedback loop and feature store to stay in sync.
Keeping it static saves drawing effort but turns the diagram into a misleading source — a bad trade.
The mid-process mismatch already misleads; the problem is not deferred to the summary.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 面试后半段你已经画好带标注的高层图，现在要讲「feature store → serving → 网关 → 客户端」这条路径要在 50ms 内完成。
scenario_en: Later on, with a labeled high-level diagram drawn, you want to say the feature-store to serving to gateway to client path must finish within 50 ms.
q: 已经有标注好的图后，最有效的讲法是什么？
q_en: With a labeled diagram already drawn, what is the most efficient way to explain?
why: 指着图上的箭头说「这条路径要在 50ms 内完成」，而不是再口头复述整条路径。指认代替复述每次省 30-60 秒，累积能多换 1-2 分钟投到深度（影子部署、A/B 设计）。
why_en: Point at the arrows and say 'this path must complete under 50 ms' instead of re-narrating the whole path, saving 30-60 seconds each time.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官刚加入或明显没跟上，第一次仍要口头把路径讲一遍建立共识，之后再用指认代替复述。
options: 把整条路径从头到尾再口头复述一遍，确保讲清楚
指着图上箭头说「这条要 50ms 内完成」，指认代替复述
把图擦掉重新画一张更详细的版本，从头再讲一遍这条路径
在图旁边再写一大段文字，专门说明这条路径
options_en: Re-narrate the whole path end to end to be sure it lands.
Point at the arrows and say 'this path must finish under 50 ms' instead of narrating it.
Erase the diagram, redraw a more detailed version, then narrate this path again from scratch.
Write a long paragraph beside the diagram describing this path.
optionExplanations: 再口头复述一遍浪费了图的价值——图存在的意义就是让你不用复述。
对；指认代替复述，每次省 30-60 秒，累积起来多出 1-2 分钟投到深度。
擦掉重画一张更详细的版本既费时又打断节奏，图已经够用就该用它指认。
在旁边写大段文字又回到冗长口头模式，违背了图的省时初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Re-narrating wastes the diagram's value; the diagram exists precisely so you need not narrate.
Correct — pointing substitutes for narration, saving 30-60 sec each time and compounding into 1-2 extra minutes for depth.
Erasing and redrawing a more detailed version costs time and breaks flow; if the diagram suffices, use it to point.
A long paragraph beside it returns to verbose narration, defeating the diagram's time-saving purpose.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 数据策略阶段你画数据流图，要把数据的完整生命周期串起来。
scenario_en: In data strategy you draw the data-flow diagram, chaining the full data lifecycle.
q: 把数据流图的环节排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the stages of the data-flow diagram correctly:
steps: 原始数据（日志、画像、上下文）
训练数据（经 join、聚合、特征抽取）
预测（模型对线上请求打分）
反馈回流到重训练
why: 数据流：原始数据→（转换）训练数据→预测→反馈回流重训。画的时候标清来源、转换、存储、批 vs 流、反馈回路——反馈回路正是体现你懂 training-serving skew 和持续学习的地方。
why_en: The data flow goes raw data, then transformed training data, then predictions, then the feedback loop back to retraining, with the loop showing continuous-learning awareness.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["原始数据
日志/画像"] -->|join/聚合| B["训练数据"] B --> M["模型"] M --> P["预测"] P -. 反馈 .-> A
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 欺诈检测题进行到第 18 分钟，澄清和数据策略都只口头讲了、一张图没画，你正要开始模型设计。
scenario_en: At minute 18 on a fraud prompt, clarification and data strategy were verbal only with no diagrams, and you are about to start model design.
q: 此时最好的做法是什么？
q_en: What is the best move at this point?
why: 先暂停，补一张高层系统图把前面已讨论的组件锚定下来，再进入模型设计（架构非平凡的话配一张草图）。缺了高层图后面全靠口头会越来越乱；补图永远比继续裸讲强。
why_en: Pause and draw a high-level system diagram to anchor the components already discussed, then proceed to model design with a sketch if the architecture is non-trivial.
whenOtherWins: 若时间已所剩无几、马上要收尾，补一张详图可能来不及，此时用极简高层图或口头 recap 锚定即可。
options: 不管图了，直接开始模型设计，反正前面口头讲过
先暂停补一张高层系统图锚定已讨论组件，再进模型设计
把前 18 分钟的内容全部推倒重来，从头再画一遍
只画一张最详细的模型架构图，直接跳过高层图
options_en: Skip diagrams and go straight to model design; you already covered it verbally.
Pause to draw a high-level diagram anchoring what was discussed, then do model design.
Scrap the first 18 minutes and redraw everything from scratch.
Draw only the most detailed model-architecture diagram and skip the high-level one.
optionExplanations: 继续裸讲会让后面越来越乱，缺高层图这个共享锚点，讨论没有依托。
对；先补高层图把已讨论组件锚定，再进模型设计，必要时配草图，止损又不推倒重来。
推倒重来浪费已完成的 18 分钟，补一张图就够，不必从头再画。
跳过高层图直接画模型架构缺了共享锚点，高层图恰恰是永不跳过那张。
optionExplanations_en: Continuing verbally-only gets messier; without the high-level anchor the discussion has nothing to hang on.
Correct — draw the high-level diagram to anchor discussed components, then proceed to model design with a sketch if needed, stopping the loss without a restart.
Restarting wastes the 18 minutes done; one diagram suffices, no need to redraw from scratch.
Skipping the high-level diagram for a model-architecture one loses the shared anchor; the high-level is the never-skip one.
tradeoff: 补图花掉的 1 分钟 vs 后半场讨论有共享锚点的清晰度
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 三种图各自对应框架的一个阶段和一套标注。
scenario_en: Each of the three diagram types maps to a framework phase and a labeling set.
q: 填空：三种图各自的绘制时机。
q_en: Fill in: when each of the three diagram types is drawn.
text: 高层系统图在 {{澄清之后/min 5-8}} 画（永不跳过）；数据流图在 {{数据策略/min 8-15}} 画；模型架构草图在 {{模型设计/min 15-22}} 画，且仅当架构 {{非平凡}} 时。
text_en: The high-level system diagram is drawn {{after clarification, min 5-8}} (never skipped); the data-flow diagram during {{data strategy, min 8-15}}; the model-architecture sketch during {{model design, min 15-22}}, only when the architecture is {{non-trivial}}.
why: 三种图的时机映射到框架三个阶段：澄清后立高层图、数据策略画数据流、模型设计非平凡才画草图。记住时机才能在对的时刻用对的图。
why_en: The three diagrams map to three framework phases: high-level after clarification, data-flow in data strategy, and the sketch only for non-trivial architectures in model design.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 高层系统图和模型架构草图画的是完全不同粒度的东西。
scenario_en: The high-level system diagram and the model-architecture sketch depict entirely different granularities.
q: 高层系统图 vs 模型架构草图，在「粒度」上有什么区别？
q_en: High-level system diagram vs model-architecture sketch — how do they differ in granularity?
why: 高层系统图停在组件名+方向层级（客户端、网关、feature store、模型服务），画系统间关系；模型架构草图深入单个模型内部（输入特征、embedding 层、交互层、输出头）。一个是系统级，一个是模型内部级。
why_en: The high-level diagram stays at component-name-plus-direction level across the system, while the sketch goes inside one model's internal structure.
tradeoff: 高层系统图(组件间关系) vs 架构草图(单模型内部结构)
options: 两者粒度一样，只是画在白板的不同位置
高层图停在组件名+方向；草图深入单模型内部结构
高层图画模型内部，草图画系统组件，正好相反
高层图只用文字，草图只用图形，是形式区别
options_en: Same granularity, just drawn in different spots on the whiteboard.
The high-level diagram stops at component names and direction; the sketch goes inside one model.
The high-level diagram shows model internals and the sketch shows system components — reversed.
One uses only text and the other only shapes — a difference in form.
optionExplanations: 两者粒度根本不同：一个系统级、一个模型内部级，不是画的位置问题。
对；高层停在组件+方向、画系统关系，草图钻进单模型内部结构，粒度截然不同。
方向反了：高层画系统组件、草图画模型内部，选项把两者对调了。
区别在粒度不在表现形式，两者都用框和箭头，不是文字 vs 图形。
optionExplanations_en: The two differ fundamentally in granularity: one system-level, one model-internal — not a positioning issue.
Correct — high-level stays at components-plus-direction for cross-system relations, while the sketch goes inside one model's structure, a sharp granularity difference.
Reversed: high-level shows system components and the sketch shows model internals; this option swaps them.
The difference is granularity, not representation form; both use boxes and arrows, not text vs shapes.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 你在高层系统图的 serving 箭头旁边有空间可以加一个注解。
scenario_en: You have room beside the serving arrow in the high-level diagram to add an annotation.
q: 在高层图上加什么样的量化注解最能体现系统思维？
q_en: What quantitative annotation on the high-level diagram best shows systems thinking?
why: 在关键处加量化注解：serving 箭头标 QPS/延迟、ETL 标批处理频率、草图标 embedding 维度。这些数字证明你在想扩展、延迟、漂移，而不只是把框连起来。
why_en: Add quantitative annotations where they matter, like QPS or latency on the serving arrow, to show you think about scaling, latency, and drift.
whenOtherWins: 若某处数字并不影响设计判断（如日志格式版本号），就别硬标，量化注解只加在扩展/延迟/漂移这类真正重要处。
options: 标上你最喜欢的那套框线与箭头颜色代码，让图更好看
在 serving 箭头上标 QPS 与延迟数字
标上这个组件用的是哪一年发明的技术
把整段模型损失函数公式抄在箭头旁边
options_en: Annotate with your favorite color codes for boxes and arrows, to make the diagram look nicer.
Write QPS and latency numbers on the serving arrow.
Annotate which year the technology behind the component was invented.
Copy the entire model loss-function formula next to the arrow.
optionExplanations: 颜色代码不携带任何工程信息，让图更好看也不体现系统思维。
对；QPS/延迟这类量化注解直接证明你在想扩展和延迟，是系统思维的信号。
技术发明年份是无关的历史事实，不影响任何设计判断。
抄整段公式是过度细节，图要停在组件层，量化注解是几个关键数字不是公式。
optionExplanations_en: A color code carries no engineering information, and making it prettier does not signal systems thinking either.
Correct — QPS/latency annotations directly show scaling and latency awareness, the systems-thinking signal.
The invention year is an irrelevant historical fact that affects no design judgment.
Copying a full formula is over-detail; the diagram stays at component level, and annotations are a few key numbers, not formulas.
tradeoff: 注解占掉的图面空间 vs 展示扩展/延迟/漂移意识的信号强度
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 数据流图上，一条转换路径是每日批处理，另一条是亚秒级流处理。
scenario_en: In the data-flow diagram, one transform path is daily batch and another is sub-second streaming.
q: 在数据流图上标注「批 vs 流」的延迟，主要传达什么信号？
q_en: Annotating 'batch vs streaming' latency on the data-flow diagram mainly signals what?
why: 标「batch, daily」「streaming, sub-second」直接体现你意识到 training-serving skew——如果训练用日更特征、线上用实时特征，两边不一致会掉点。延迟注解＝在展示你懂这个风险。
why_en: Labeling 'batch, daily' vs 'streaming, sub-second' signals awareness of training-serving skew, since mismatched feature freshness between training and serving degrades performance.
whenOtherWins: 若整条管线都是同一种时效（全批或全流），就不必特意对比标注，一句说明即可，避免冗余。
options: 传达你会用两种不同颜色的箭头来区分不同路径
意识到 training-serving skew
传达这个系统结构足够复杂，值得面试官多给一些印象分
传达批处理在任何场景下都一定比流处理更好
options_en: That you can use two arrow colors to tell the paths apart.
That you are aware of training-serving skew.
That the system's structure is complex enough to earn the interviewer's extra goodwill.
That batch is always better than streaming, in every scenario.
optionExplanations: 颜色不携带工程含义，延迟注解传达的是对时效不一致的意识。
对；把日更与亚秒两种时效并排标出，等于主动点名线上/训练特征不一致的风险。
系统复杂度不是加分理由，注解传达的是具体的偏斜风险意识，不是印象分。
批不一定比流好，各有适用场景；注解不是在评优劣而是标时效。
optionExplanations_en: Colors carry no engineering meaning; the latency annotation conveys awareness of freshness mismatch.
Correct — putting daily and sub-second side by side names the freshness mismatch risk yourself.
System complexity is not a scoring reason; the annotation conveys concrete skew-risk awareness, not extra goodwill.
Batch is not always better than streaming; each fits cases, and the annotation marks freshness, not superiority.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏斜
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练和线上服务时特征时效或计算不一致，导致线上效果掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-serving skew is a mismatch in feature freshness or computation between training and serving, degrading online performance.

category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 你 5 分钟前已经口头讲清了某条流程，现在又想画一张图，但这张图只是把刚说的话重复一遍。
scenario_en: You verbally explained a flow 5 minutes ago and now want to draw a diagram that merely restates what you just said.
q: 如果一张图只是复述你 5 分钟前说过的话，该怎么办？
q_en: If a diagram just restates what you said 5 minutes ago, what should you do?
why: 这种图没有增量，画它是浪费时间。应该停下来，把这段时间重定向到面试官在意的某个取舍的深度上。图要么省时间、要么加清晰度，纯复述两者都不占。
why_en: A redundant diagram adds nothing, so stop and redirect that time to depth on a tradeoff the interviewer cares about.
options: 照画不误，多一张复述图也能加深面试官的印象
停下来，把时间重定向到面试官在意的取舍深度
把这张图画得更华丽，弥补它没有新信息
画完后再口头把内容第三次复述一遍加深
options_en: Draw it anyway; one more restating diagram can still deepen the interviewer's impression.
Stop, and redirect that time into depth on a tradeoff the interviewer cares about.
Make the diagram fancier to make up for having no new information.
After drawing it, restate the content verbally a third time to reinforce it.
optionExplanations: 多一张纯复述图加深不了印象——它不省时间也不加清晰度，纯浪费预算。
对；复述图没增量就该停，把时间投到面试官在意的取舍深度上更值。
华丽弥补不了没有新信息，画工不是内容，纯复述图本质没价值。
第三次复述只会更浪费时间，问题是内容重复不是次数不够。
optionExplanations_en: One more purely redundant diagram deepens nothing; it neither saves time nor adds clarity — pure budget waste.
Correct — a redundant diagram adds nothing, so stop and invest the time in tradeoff depth the interviewer cares about.
Fanciness cannot compensate for no new information; draftsmanship is not content, and a restating diagram has no value.
A third restatement wastes more time; the problem is repeated content, not too few repetitions.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 画图时如果迟疑、边画边纠结，会向面试官传递某种信号。
scenario_en: If you hesitate and second-guess while drawing, it sends the interviewer a certain signal.
q: 为什么要练到每种图都能在 90 秒内画完？
q_en: Why practice drawing each diagram type in under 90 seconds?
why: 画图时迟疑会传递「你对自己的设计没把握」的信号。练到三种图各能在 90 秒内画完，就能流畅落笔、不打断思路，也让面试官相信你对设计有信心。
why_en: Hesitation while drawing signals uncertainty about your own design, so practice each type to under 90 seconds for fluent, confident execution.
options: 为了比别的候选人画得更快，纯粹比拼速度
画图迟疑＝对设计没把握的信号；练到 90 秒内流畅落笔
为了在 90 秒内画完，好把剩下的时间省下来歇口气
因为白板只租 90 秒，超时要额外收费
options_en: To draw faster than other candidates — a pure speed contest.
Hesitation signals you are unsure of your design; 90-second fluency signals confidence.
To finish within 90 sec so you can save the rest of the time to catch your breath.
Because the whiteboard is rented for only 90 sec and overtime costs extra.
optionExplanations: 不是和别人比速度——是让自己流畅、不显迟疑，速度是手段不是目的。
对；迟疑＝没把握的信号，练熟到 90 秒内能流畅画完，既省时又传递信心。
省时间不是为了歇口气，是为了把分钟投到取舍深度上。
白板收费是玩笑选项，和面试无关。
optionExplanations_en: It is not a speed contest with others; it is about fluent, hesitation-free execution — speed is a means, not the goal.
Correct — hesitation signals uncertainty, so drilling to under 90 sec makes drawing fluent and conveys confidence while saving time.
Saving time is not for catching your breath but for investing minutes in tradeoff depth.
Whiteboard rental fees are a joke option unrelated to the interview.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 你已画好带监控组件的高层图，面试官后续问「drift detection（漂移检测）怎么融进来？」
scenario_en: With a high-level diagram including a monitoring component drawn, the interviewer follows up 'how does drift detection fit in?'
q: 已有图作为共享参照时，怎么回答这个 follow-up 最高效？
q_en: With the diagram as a shared reference, how do you most efficiently answer this follow-up?
why: 指着图上的监控组件说「漂移检测在这里」，再补一条从监控回到数据/重训的箭头。图给了双方一个共享参照，让 follow-up 变成「在图上加一笔」而不是重新口头搭一遍上下文，对反馈回路尤其有效。
why_en: Point to the monitoring component and add an arrow from monitoring back to retraining, using the diagram as a shared reference so the follow-up becomes one stroke rather than rebuilding context verbally.
whenOtherWins: 若这个 follow-up 涉及一个图上完全没有的新子系统，可能需要在旁边另起一小块草图，而不是硬塞进现有图。
options: 从头口头重新搭一遍整个系统上下文，再回答这个问题
指着监控组件说「漂移检测在这里」，补一条回重训箭头
说这个问题超纲了，图上没画到所以不回答
把整张图擦掉，专门为漂移检测重画一张新图
options_en: Rebuild the whole system context verbally from scratch, then answer this question.
Point at monitoring, say 'drift detection sits here', and add an arrow back to retraining.
Say the question is out of scope because it is not on the diagram.
Erase the whole diagram and redraw one dedicated to drift detection.
optionExplanations: 重新口头搭一遍整个系统上下文浪费了图作为共享参照的价值，图存在就是为了省这一步。
对；指认监控组件+补一条箭头，把 follow-up 变成图上加一笔，尤其适合反馈回路。
漂移检测正好挂在监控组件上，不超纲；拒答丢掉了轻松作答的机会。
擦掉重画既费时又丢了已建立的共享参照，补一条箭头就够。
optionExplanations_en: Rebuilding the whole system context verbally wastes the diagram's value as a shared reference — it exists to save exactly this step.
Correct — point to monitoring and add one arrow, turning the follow-up into a single stroke, especially apt for feedback loops.
Drift detection hangs right on the monitoring component, so it is in scope; refusing forfeits an easy answer.
Erasing and redrawing costs time and loses the established shared reference; one arrow suffices.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 画高层系统图时你在犹豫要画到多细：是画客户端/网关/feature store/模型服务这一层，还是继续往下画负载均衡、pod、分片。
scenario_en: Drawing the high-level diagram you weigh how deep to go: the client/gateway/feature-store/model-serving layer, or down into load balancers, pods, and shards.
q: 高层系统图默认该停在哪个粒度？
q_en: At what granularity should the high-level diagram stop by default?
why: 默认停在组件名+方向层级（客户端、API 网关、feature store、模型服务、日志、监控），除非面试官明确要求才往下画基础设施。因为面试评的是 ML 判断，往下画 pod/分片就是过度工程。
why_en: Stay at the component-name-plus-direction level (client, gateway, feature store, model serving, logging, monitoring) unless the interviewer asks to go deeper.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确追问基础设施细节（如「这个 serving 层怎么扩」），才往下画负载均衡/副本/分片，此时是被要求而非主动过度工程。
options: 画到最细，把负载均衡、pod、分片全画出来
停在组件名+方向层级，除非被要求才往下画
只画一个「系统」大框，内部什么都不画
画到芯片和网络协议级别，展示底层功底
options_en: Go to the finest detail — load balancers, pods, and shards all drawn out.
Stop at component names plus direction, and go deeper only when asked.
Draw a single big 'system' box with nothing inside it.
Go down to chip and network-protocol level to show low-level chops.
optionExplanations: 画满 pod/分片是过度工程，ML 面试评的不是 DevOps，除非被问不该往下画。
对；停在组件+方向层级，既表达清系统关系又不陷进无关的基础设施细节。
只画一个大框没有任何信息量，起不到锚定组件讨论的作用。
芯片/协议级别彻底跑偏，和 ML 系统设计的评估维度毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing pods/shards is over-engineering; an ML interview does not score DevOps, so do not go deeper unless asked.
Correct — stopping at component-plus-direction expresses system relations without sinking into irrelevant infra detail.
One big box carries no information and cannot anchor a component discussion.
Chip/protocol level is wholly off-track and unrelated to what ML system design assesses.
tradeoff: 停在组件层省下的时间 vs 基础设施细节带来的（与评分无关的）完整度
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 你打算全程只用口头描述 YouTube 的「召回→排序→重排」多阶段流程，不画图。
scenario_en: You plan to describe YouTube's candidate-generation to ranking to re-ranking flow entirely verbally, no diagram.
q: 纯口头描述这种多阶段流程会有什么代价？
q_en: What is the cost of describing this multi-stage flow purely verbally?
why: 口头讲这种多阶段流程要花 2-3 分钟，且面试官容易在中途跟丢；一张图能让它瞬间清晰。代价就是时间和理解风险双输，正是该用高层图的场景。
why_en: Describing this multi-stage flow verbally costs 2-3 minutes and risks the interviewer losing the thread, whereas one diagram makes it instantly legible.
options: 没有代价，口头讲和画图的效果完全一样
要花 2-3 分钟且面试官易跟丢，时间和理解双输
口头讲反而更好，能省下白板空间留给后面的模型草图
只有语速慢的人才有代价，语速快就没问题
options_en: No cost; talking and drawing are exactly equivalent here.
It costs 2-3 minutes and risks a lost thread — you lose both time and comprehension.
Talking is actually better; it saves whiteboard space for the model sketch later.
Only slow speakers pay a cost; fast talkers have no problem.
optionExplanations: 并非等效——多阶段流程口头讲又慢又易跟丢，图能瞬间说清。
对；2-3 分钟＋跟丢风险是双输，多阶段流程正是该画高层图的典型场景。
省白板空间换不来时间和清晰度，代价仍是双输，口头讲不是更好。
语速快也难避免多阶段口头描述的跟丢风险，问题在结构不在语速。
optionExplanations_en: Not equivalent — a multi-stage flow described verbally is slow and easy to lose, while a diagram is instantly clear.
Correct — 2-3 minutes plus the lost-thread risk is a double loss, and a multi-stage flow is exactly when to draw a high-level diagram.
Saving whiteboard space does not buy back time or clarity; the cost is still a double loss, so verbal is not better.
Even fast talkers cannot avoid the lost-thread risk of verbal multi-stage description; the issue is structure, not speed.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 带标注的图让你用「指认」代替「复述」，每次省一点时间，累积起来可观。
scenario_en: A labeled diagram lets you point instead of re-narrate, saving a little each time that adds up.
q: 「指认代替复述」每次省多少、累积能换来什么？
q_en: How much does 'point instead of narrate' save each time, and what does it add up to?
why: 每次指认代替复述约省 30-60 秒，一场面试多次累积就多出 1-2 分钟，这些分钟正好投到深度（影子部署、A/B 设计）。反过来未标注箭头每次要 15-20 秒打断，是纯损耗。
why_en: Pointing instead of narrating saves 30-60 seconds each time, compounding to 1-2 extra minutes for depth, while an unlabeled arrow costs a 15-20 second interrupt each.
options: 每次省 5 秒，累积也就多几秒，可以忽略不计
每次省 30-60 秒，累积多出 1-2 分钟投到深度
每次省半小时，一场 45 分钟的面试能省出整整一个阶段
省多少无所谓，画图纯粹是形式不影响时间
options_en: It saves 5 sec each time, a few seconds total — negligible.
It saves 30-60 sec each time, compounding into 1-2 extra minutes for depth.
It saves half an hour each time — enough to skip a whole phase of a 45-minute interview.
The amount does not matter; diagramming is a formality with no time effect.
optionExplanations: 不止省 5 秒——每次 30-60 秒，累积起来是能投到深度的 1-2 分钟。
对；指认每次省 30-60 秒累积 1-2 分钟，未标箭头每次 15-20 秒损耗，一正一反差距明显。
半小时是荒谬夸大，一场面试总共才 45 分钟，省不出整整一个阶段。
省时间恰恰是画图的核心价值，说不影响时间是否定了本课的立论。
optionExplanations_en: Not just 5 sec — 30-60 sec each time compounds into 1-2 minutes you can invest in depth.
Correct — pointing saves 30-60 sec each, compounding to 1-2 min, while unlabeled arrows cost 15-20 sec each; the gap is clear.
Half an hour is absurd exaggeration; the whole interview is only 45 minutes, nowhere near a full phase.
Saving time is the core value of diagramming; claiming no time effect denies this lesson's thesis.
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 题目刚给出、你还没澄清清楚范围，就想立刻上手画高层图。
scenario_en: The prompt just landed and, before clarifying scope, you want to start drawing the high-level diagram immediately.
q: 画高层图和问题澄清，谁先谁后？
q_en: Which comes first, drawing the high-level diagram or problem clarification?
why: 先澄清范围，再画图锚定实现讨论。范围没定清就画，容易画出一张针对错误问题的图，后面还得推倒。图是用来锚定「已经澄清的设计」，不是用来代替澄清。
why_en: Clarify scope first, then diagram to anchor the implementation discussion, because diagramming before scope is set risks anchoring the wrong problem.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官一上来就把范围、目标、约束都给死了，几乎无需澄清，那可以很快就进入画高层图的环节。
options: 先画图再澄清，让图引导你去问澄清问题
先澄清范围，再画高层图锚定实现讨论
两件事同时做，边画边澄清最省时间
画图和澄清无关，随便哪个先都可以
options_en: Draw first, then clarify, letting the diagram drive your clarifying questions.
Clarify the scope first, then draw the high-level diagram to anchor implementation.
Do both at once; drawing while clarifying saves the most time.
Diagramming and clarification are unrelated; either order works.
optionExplanations: 先画图会锚定一个还没定清的问题，画错了还得擦；澄清才是画图的前提。
对；澄清范围在前、画图锚定在后，避免为错误问题画图、后面推倒重来。
边画边澄清听起来高效，实则容易画到一半发现范围变了要重画。
两者有明确先后：澄清定问题、图锚定已澄清的设计，顺序不能随意。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing first anchors an unsettled problem and may need erasing; clarification is the prerequisite for diagramming.
Correct — clarify scope first then anchor with a diagram, avoiding diagramming the wrong problem and a later restart.
Drawing while clarifying sounds efficient but often means redrawing when scope shifts mid-way.
There is a clear order: clarification defines the problem and the diagram anchors the clarified design, so order is not arbitrary.
tradeoff: 早开画抢到的时间 vs 先澄清范围避免为错误问题画图的返工风险
category: Diagrams In The ML SD Interview

scenario: 同一道 ML SD 题，Senior(L5) 和 Staff+ 的评分点不一样。
scenario_en: On the same ML SD prompt, the scoring focus differs between Senior (L5) and Staff+.
q: 从 Senior(L5) 到 Staff+，评分维度多了哪两条轴？
q_en: From Senior (L5) to Staff+, which two axes get added to the scoring?
why: L5：干净的图+扎实的技术答案就够了。Staff+ 评的是图「周围」的推理，多两条轴：主动识别风险、跨职能意识（成本/合规/隐私/团队）。这两条把「强工程师」抬到「技术领导」。
why_en: At L5 a clean diagram plus solid answers suffice, while Staff+ scores the reasoning around the diagram on two extra axes: proactive risk identification and cross-functional awareness.
tradeoff: Senior(图+技术答案) vs Staff+(主动识别风险 + 跨职能意识)
diagram:
flowchart TD S["Senior L5
干净图 + 扎实技术答案"] --> P["Staff+ 额外两轴"] P --> A["主动识别风险"] P --> B["跨职能意识
成本/合规/隐私/团队"]
options: 更快的编码速度 和 更多的顶会论文引用数量
主动识别风险 和 跨职能意识（成本/合规/隐私）
更漂亮的架构图 和 更长更详尽的口头回答
更强的算法推导 和 更深的模型收敛性数学证明
options_en: Faster coding speed and a higher count of top-conference paper citations.
Proactive risk identification and cross-functional awareness (cost/compliance/privacy).
Prettier architecture diagrams and longer, more exhaustive verbal answers.
Stronger algorithm derivations and deeper proofs of model convergence.
optionExplanations: 编码速度和论文引用不是 Staff+ 的评分轴，ML SD 评的是系统判断不是刷题或发表。
对；主动识别风险+跨职能意识正是把 Staff+ 和 Senior 分开的两条轴。
图更漂亮、回答更长都不是 Staff+ 信号，甚至冗长是负信号。
数学证明是知识深度，Staff+ 要的是工程判断和跨职能视野，不是推导。
optionExplanations_en: Coding speed and citations are not Staff+ axes; ML SD scores systems judgment, not grinding or publishing.
Correct — proactive risk identification and cross-functional awareness are the two axes separating Staff+ from Senior.
Prettier diagrams and longer answers are not Staff+ signals; verbosity is even a negative.
Mathematical proofs are knowledge depth, but Staff+ wants engineering judgment and cross-functional scope, not derivations.
category: Driving The Interview At Staff Level

scenario: 面试官问「这个排序问题用什么模型」。你可以背事实，也可以在约束下做决策。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'what model for this ranking problem?' You can state facts or decide under constraints.
q: 知识回忆(knowledge recall) 和 工程判断(engineering judgment) 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between knowledge recall and engineering judgment?
why: 知识回忆＝陈述事实（「XGBoost 原生处理缺失值」「Transformer 用自注意力」），展示工具熟悉度。工程判断＝在约束下做决策（团队没有 GPU serving 所以从简单开始）。Staff+ 评的是后者。
why_en: Knowledge recall states facts to show tool familiarity, while engineering judgment makes decisions under constraints, and Staff+ scores the latter.
tradeoff: 知识回忆(陈述事实、显示熟悉度) vs 工程判断(约束下做决策)
options: 两者是一回事，会背事实就等于会在约束下做判断
回忆＝陈述事实显示工具熟悉度；判断＝在约束下做决策
回忆是初级技能、判断是高级技能，但 ML SD 面试只考回忆
判断＝背更多更冷门的事实，回忆＝背常见的教科书事实
options_en: They are the same thing — reciting facts equals judging under constraints.
Recall is stating facts to show tool familiarity; judgment is deciding under constraints.
Recall is a junior skill and judgment a senior one, but ML SD interviews only test recall.
Judgment is reciting more obscure facts; recall is reciting common textbook facts.
optionExplanations: 会背事实不等于会判断——很多人能背 XGBoost 特性却选不对模型。
对；回忆是陈述事实，判断是在真实约束（GPU、团队、成本）下做决策，Staff+ 评后者。
面试恰恰重点考判断而非回忆，说只考回忆理解反了。
判断不是背更冷门的事实，判断的核心是约束下的取舍，不是知识冷门度。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting facts is not judgment; many can recite XGBoost traits yet pick the wrong model.
Correct — recall states facts while judgment decides under real constraints (GPU, team, cost), and Staff+ scores the latter.
Interviews emphasize judgment over recall, so 'only tests recall' is backwards.
Judgment is not reciting more obscure facts; its core is tradeoffs under constraints, not fact obscurity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在真实约束（团队、算力、成本、时间）下做出的设计决策，而非陈述事实。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engineering judgment is design decisions made under real constraints (team, compute, cost, time), not fact recall.

category: Driving The Interview At Staff Level

scenario: 排序问题，团队已在生产跑树模型、serving 栈只有 CPU、没有 feature store 迁移预算。面试官问「用什么模型」。
scenario_en: A ranking problem: the team already runs tree models in prod, the serving stack is CPU-only, and there is no feature-store migration budget. Asked 'what model?'
q: Staff+ 水准的回答该怎么组织？
q_en: How should a Staff+-level answer be structured?
why: Staff+ 回答：先摆约束（团队已跑树模型、CPU-only），再给推荐（先上 LambdaMART），再讲可逆性（测 NDCG 对比神经排序，收益够大再迁移）。判断体现在结构：约束在先、推荐在中、可逆性收尾。
why_en: A Staff+ answer leads with constraints (team runs tree models, CPU-only), then the recommendation (launch LambdaMART), then reversibility (measure NDCG vs a neural baseline and migrate only if the gap justifies the infra cost).
whenOtherWins: 若团队已有成熟 GPU serving 和 ML 平台、且长尾质量是核心瓶颈，直接上神经排序器可能更值，此时可逆性讨论转向如何控其成本。
options: 直接说「用 LambdaMART，处理 list-wise 排序、GBT 对表格特征强」就结束
先摆约束(CPU-only)，再推荐(LambdaMART)，再给可逆性(测 NDCG 差距)
推荐最前沿的神经排序器，说它长尾质量最好，不提约束
把 LambdaMART、神经排序、双塔全列出来，让面试官自己选
options_en: Just say 'use LambdaMART — handles list-wise ranking, GBTs are strong on tabular features' and stop.
Lead with constraints (CPU-only), then the recommendation (LambdaMART), then reversibility (measure the NDCG gap).
Recommend the most cutting-edge neural ranker for best long-tail quality, with no mention of constraints.
List LambdaMART, neural rankers, and two-tower and let the interviewer pick.
optionExplanations: 只说模型名+特性是 Senior 水准的知识回忆，没有约束和可逆性，够不到 Staff+。
对；约束→推荐→可逆性的结构正是工程判断，把团队/算力约束和迁移路径都讲清。
不提约束直接上最前沿模型，忽略了 CPU-only 和无迁移预算，正是缺判断的表现。
列一堆让面试官选是回避决策，Staff+ 要在约束下给出并论证一个推荐。
optionExplanations_en: Just naming the model and its traits is Senior-level recall with no constraints or reversibility — short of Staff+.
Correct — constraints then recommendation then reversibility is the judgment structure, addressing team/compute limits and the migration path.
Jumping to a cutting-edge model with no constraints ignores CPU-only and no migration budget — exactly the lack of judgment.
Listing options for the interviewer to pick dodges the decision; Staff+ must recommend and justify one under the constraints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种基于梯度提升树的 list-wise 排序模型，直接优化排序指标(如 NDCG)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LambdaMART is a gradient-boosted-tree list-wise ranking model that directly optimizes ranking metrics like NDCG.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益：排序质量指标，越靠前的相关项贡献越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a ranking-quality metric rewarding relevant items ranked higher.

category: Driving The Interview At Staff Level

scenario: 工程判断体现在推理的结构上，而不是单个答案对不对。
scenario_en: Engineering judgment shows in the structure of reasoning, not the correctness of a single answer.
q: 把 Staff+ 推理的正确结构排序：
q_en: Order the correct structure of Staff+ reasoning:
steps: 先摆约束：团队能力、serving 栈、成本、时间
再给推荐：在这些约束下先做什么
最后讲可逆性：怎么设计接口让日后能迁移/回退
why: 判断体现在结构：约束在先、推荐在中、可逆性收尾。这个顺序证明你的选择是被约束推出来的、且留了迁移余地，而不是拍脑袋。MAANG 评分明确看影响范围和驾驭模糊的能力。
why_en: Judgment shows in structure: constraints first, recommendation second, reversibility last, proving the choice is constraint-driven and leaves a migration path.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1 约束
团队/算力/成本"] --> B["2 推荐
约束下先做什么"] B --> C["3 可逆性
迁移/回退接口"]
category: Driving The Interview At Staff Level

scenario: 面试到「定义评估指标」这一刻，Senior 和 Staff+ 的表现不同。
scenario_en: At the 'define evaluation metrics' moment, Senior and Staff+ behave differently.
q: 在「指标定义」这一刻，Staff+ 比 Senior 多做了什么？
q_en: At the metric-definition moment, what does Staff+ do beyond Senior?
why: Senior 提出线下指标就停了；Staff+ 把线下指标连到业务 KPI，还加上护栏指标(guardrail)防止优化主指标时把别的搞坏。多连一层「指标→业务」和「护栏」正是资历差。
why_en: Senior proposes offline metrics, while Staff+ connects them to business KPIs and adds guardrail metrics to prevent optimizing one metric at another's expense.
tradeoff: Senior(只提线下指标) vs Staff+(连到业务 KPI + 加护栏指标)
options: Staff+ 把能想到的线下指标全列出来，靠数量堆多取胜
Staff+ 把线下指标连到业务 KPI，并加护栏指标防跑偏
Staff+ 只用单一指标，越简单越不容易出错
Staff+ 拒绝提前定义指标，说等上线看数据再说
options_en: Staff+ lists out every offline metric they can think of, winning on sheer quantity.
Staff+ connects offline metrics to business KPIs and adds guardrail metrics.
Staff+ uses a single metric — the simpler it is, the less can go wrong.
Staff+ refuses to define metrics up front, saying to wait for post-launch data.
optionExplanations: 多提几个线下指标还是停在 Senior 层，关键差在有没有连到业务和护栏。
对；连业务 KPI+加护栏是 Staff+ 信号，防止优化主指标时把留存/取消率搞坏。
只用一个指标可能漏掉护栏维度，简单不是这里的目标。
拒绝定义指标是回避，Staff+ 恰恰要主动把指标和业务、护栏连起来。
optionExplanations_en: More offline metrics still sits at the Senior layer; the key difference is connecting to business and guardrails.
Correct — connecting to business KPIs plus guardrails is the Staff+ signal, preventing damage to retention or cancellation while optimizing the main metric.
One metric may miss the guardrail dimension; simplicity is not the goal here.
Refusing to define metrics dodges; Staff+ proactively ties metrics to business and guardrails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化主指标时必须不能变差的底线指标（如取消率、留存），防止顾此失彼。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a floor metric that must not worsen while optimizing the main one, preventing collateral damage.

category: Driving The Interview At Staff Level

scenario: 设计到扩展性时，Senior 和 Staff+ 的主动程度不同。
scenario_en: On scalability, Senior and Staff+ differ in how proactive they are.
q: 在「扩展性」这一刻，Senior 和 Staff+ 的关键区别是什么？
q_en: On scalability, what is the key difference between Senior and Staff+?
why: Senior 被问到才答扩展；Staff+ 主动为系统估容量、指出瓶颈在哪，不等提问。主动 sizing 和标出瓶颈是资深信号——它证明你有运营大规模系统的经验直觉。
why_en: Senior answers scaling when prompted, while Staff+ proactively sizes the system and flags bottlenecks unprompted.
tradeoff: Senior(被问才答扩展) vs Staff+(主动估容量、标瓶颈)
options: Staff+ 被追问 QPS 和延迟目标才谈扩展，答得更详细
Staff+ 主动为系统估容量、指出瓶颈在哪，不等提问
Staff+ 完全不谈扩展，说那是运维的事
Staff+ 把所有组件都无脑加机器，不分析瓶颈
options_en: Staff+ only discusses scaling once asked about QPS and latency targets, in more detail.
Staff+ proactively sizes the system and flags where the bottleneck is, without being asked.
Staff+ does not discuss scaling at all, saying it is an ops concern.
Staff+ blindly adds machines to every component without analyzing bottlenecks.
optionExplanations: 被问才答就是 Senior 的表现，Staff+ 的差别恰恰在「主动」，答得详细不等于主动。
对；主动 sizing+标瓶颈证明你有运营大规模系统的直觉，是 Staff+ 信号。
扩展是系统设计核心不是纯运维，不谈就丢了这块信号。
无脑加机器不是主动 sizing，Staff+ 要先定位瓶颈再针对性扩，不是均匀堆机器。
optionExplanations_en: Answering only when asked is the Senior behavior; the Staff+ difference is being proactive, and detail is not proactivity.
Correct — proactive sizing plus flagging bottlenecks proves scale-operating intuition, a Staff+ signal.
Scaling is core to system design, not pure ops, and not discussing it forfeits that signal.
Blindly adding machines is not proactive sizing; Staff+ locates the bottleneck first then scales targetedly.
category: Driving The Interview At Staff Level

scenario: 你想在面试官问之前，主动指出这个设计潜在的业务风险。
scenario_en: You want to flag a potential business risk of the design before the interviewer asks.
q: 主动识别业务风险的三步模式是什么？
q_en: What is the three-part pattern for proactively identifying business risks?
