q_en: Which are PEFT (parameter-efficient fine-tuning) methods? (multiple)
why: PEFT 都冻结大部分权重、只训少量新增参数:LoRA(低秩增量)、prefix tuning(输入前拼可学 token)、adapter layers(层间瓶颈模块)。全量微调更新所有权重,不属于 PEFT。
why_en: PEFT methods freeze most weights and train a small added set: LoRA, prefix tuning, and adapter layers; full fine-tuning is not PEFT.
options: LoRA(低秩权重增量,可零延迟合并)
prefix tuning(在输入前拼可学习的 token embedding)
adapter layers(在 transformer 层间插瓶颈模块)
全量微调(更新模型所有权重)
options_en: LoRA (low-rank weight delta, zero-latency merge).
Prefix tuning (prepend learnable token embeddings to the input).
Adapter layers (insert bottleneck modules between transformer layers).
Full fine-tuning (update all model weights).
optionExplanations: 对;LoRA 是最主流的 PEFT,低秩增量+零延迟合并。
对;prefix tuning 只学一段前缀 embedding,冻结主体,是 PEFT。
对;adapter layers 在层间插小瓶颈模块,只训它,是经典 PEFT。
错;全量微调更新所有权重,恰恰是 PEFT 要避免的重成本做法。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — LoRA is the dominant PEFT method, low-rank delta with zero-latency merge.
Correct — prefix tuning learns only a prefix embedding with the body frozen, a PEFT method.
Correct — adapter layers insert small bottleneck modules between layers and train only those, classic PEFT.
Wrong — full fine-tuning updates all weights, the heavy cost PEFT avoids.

termDefinitions.meaning: 冻结模型,只学习一段拼在输入前的可训练 token embedding。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefix tuning freezes the model and learns only a trainable token-embedding prefix prepended to the input.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 transformer 层之间插入的小瓶颈模块,微调时只训它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adapter layers are small bottleneck modules inserted between transformer layers, the only part fine-tuned.

category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 想把一个大 teacher 模型的能力搬到一个小 student 上,让 student 学得比只看硬标签更多。
scenario_en: You want to move a large teacher's ability into a small student that learns more than from hard labels alone.
q: 知识蒸馏里 student 从 teacher 学的关键是什么?
q_en: In knowledge distillation, what is the key thing the student learns from the teacher?
why: student 学 teacher 的软概率输出,而不只是 one-hot 硬标签。软概率编码了类间关系("dark knowledge",如"7"比起"0"更像"1"),给出比硬标签丰富得多的监督信号,让小模型学到大模型的判别结构。
why_en: The student learns the teacher's soft probability outputs, not just one-hot hard labels, which encode inter-class relationships (dark knowledge).
options: 只学 one-hot 硬标签,和普通监督训练完全一样
学 teacher 的软概率输出,里面编码了类间关系
直接把 teacher 的权重复制到 student 里面
让 student 随机初始化后就不再训练它
options_en: Only the one-hot hard labels, exactly like ordinary supervised training.
The teacher soft probability outputs, which encode inter-class relationships.
Copy the teacher weights straight into the student.
Randomly initialize the student and then never train it.
optionExplanations: 只学硬标签就没蒸馏了,软概率里的类间信息才是蒸馏的价值。
对;软概率的 dark knowledge 提供硬标签没有的类间相似度,让小模型学得更好。
student 结构比 teacher 小,权重维度不匹配,无法直接复制。
不训练学不到任何东西,蒸馏需要用 teacher 输出做监督。
optionExplanations_en: Only hard labels isn't distillation; the inter-class info in soft probabilities is distillation's value.
Correct — soft-probability dark knowledge provides inter-class similarity absent from hard labels, helping the small model learn better.
The student is smaller with mismatched weight dimensions, so weights can't be copied directly.
Without training it learns nothing; distillation needs the teacher's outputs as supervision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练小 student 模仿大 teacher 的软输出,把能力迁移到更小模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Knowledge distillation trains a small student to mimic a large teacher's soft outputs, transferring ability into a smaller model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 软概率里蕴含的类间相似关系(如"7"更像"1"而非"0")。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dark knowledge is the inter-class similarity in soft probabilities (a '7' looks more like a '1' than a '0').

category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: teacher 的 softmax 输出几乎是 one-hot(某类接近 1),非目标类的概率几乎为 0,student 学不到类间关系。
scenario_en: The teacher's softmax is nearly one-hot (one class near 1), non-target class probabilities near 0, so the student can't learn inter-class relations.
q: 温度缩放(T>1)在蒸馏里起什么作用?
q_en: What does temperature scaling (T>1) do in distillation?
why: 把 teacher 的 logits 除以温度 T>1 再过 softmax,分布被软化,非目标类的相对概率被放大、显现出来。这样 student 才能学到"哪些非目标类更接近"的暗知识,而不是几乎 one-hot 的贫瘠信号。
why_en: Dividing teacher logits by T>1 before softmax softens the distribution, revealing non-target class probabilities so the student can learn dark knowledge.
options: T>1 让分布更尖锐,更接近 one-hot
T>1 软化分布,放大非目标类概率
T 就是学习率,调得越大训练收敛越快
T>1 会删掉非目标类,只保留最高的那类
options_en: T>1 sharpens the distribution, pushing it closer to one-hot.
T>1 softens the distribution and amplifies non-target class probabilities.
T is just the learning rate; larger values converge faster.
T>1 deletes the non-target classes and keeps only the top one.
optionExplanations: T>1 是软化不是锐化,更尖锐反而抹掉了要学的类间信息。
对;除以 T>1 让软分布显现非目标类相对概率,student 才能吸收暗知识。
T 是温度不是学习率,它调分布软硬,与步长无关。
软化是放大非目标类而非删除它们,恰恰相反。
optionExplanations_en: T>1 softens, not sharpens; sharper would erase the inter-class info to be learned.
Correct — dividing by T>1 surfaces non-target relative probabilities so the student absorbs dark knowledge.
T is temperature, not learning rate; it tunes distribution softness, unrelated to step size.
Softening amplifies non-target classes rather than deleting them — the opposite.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 logits 除以温度 T 再 softmax,T>1 使分布更平滑、显现非目标类概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temperature scaling divides logits by T before softmax; T>1 smooths the distribution and reveals non-target class probabilities.

category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 回忆蒸馏的损失如何同时用硬标签和 teacher 软输出。
scenario_en: Recall how the distillation loss combines hard labels and the teacher's soft outputs.
q: 补全知识蒸馏的损失:
q_en: Fill in the knowledge-distillation loss:
text: L = (1−α)·{{L_CE}} + α·{{T²}}·L_KL:前项对硬标签的交叉熵,后项是 teacher/student 软输出的 {{KL}} 散度。
text_en: L = (1−α)·{{L_CE}} + α·{{T²}}·L_KL: the first term is cross-entropy on hard labels, the second is the {{KL}} divergence between teacher/student soft outputs.
why: 两项加权:硬标签交叉熵保底正确性,teacher/student 软输出的 KL 散度传暗知识;乘 T² 补偿软化后梯度被缩小的量级。α 平衡两者。
why_en: It weights hard-label cross-entropy against the teacher-student soft-output KL divergence, scaling the KL term by T-squared.
category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 实时排序想用更小更快的 BERT,DistilBERT 保留约 97% BERT 准确率、参数少约 40%。
scenario_en: For real-time ranking you want a smaller, faster BERT; DistilBERT keeps ~97% of BERT's accuracy with ~40% fewer parameters.
q: DistilBERT 这组数字说明蒸馏的什么价值?
q_en: What does DistilBERT's numbers show about distillation's value?
why: 约 97% 准确率、少约 40% 参数、推理更快——蒸馏用很小的准确率代价换来显著更小更快的模型,足以放进实时排序的延迟预算。前提是 student 容量够大能吸收 teacher,且要先跑 teacher 全量推理产软标签。
why_en: DistilBERT keeps ~97% accuracy with ~40% fewer params and faster inference, trading tiny accuracy for a much smaller, real-time-viable model.
options: 说明蒸馏一定无损,准确率完全不会下降
小准确率代价换显著更小更快,够进实时预算
说明 student 越小反而越准,应该继续往下压
说明蒸馏不需要 teacher,student 自己就能学好
options_en: It shows distillation is lossless, with no accuracy drop at all.
A tiny accuracy cost buys a much smaller, faster model that fits the real-time budget.
It shows a smaller student is more accurate, so keep compressing.
It shows distillation needs no teacher; the student learns fine alone.
optionExplanations: 97% 意味着掉了约 3 个点,不是无损,蒸馏是有代价的权衡。
对;小代价换大瘦身+提速,正是蒸馏让大模型能落进实时预算的价值。
越压越准不成立,student 太小容量不足反而掉更多,存在下限。
蒸馏必须有 teacher 提供软标签,student 单独学不到暗知识。
optionExplanations_en: 97% means about 3 points lost, not lossless; distillation is a costed trade-off.
Correct — a small cost for big shrink-and-speedup is exactly how distillation makes big models fit real-time budgets.
Smaller isn't more accurate; too small a student underfits and loses more, with a floor.
Distillation needs a teacher for soft labels; the student can't learn dark knowledge alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: BERT 的蒸馏版,约 97% 准确率、参数少约 40%、推理更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DistilBERT is a distilled BERT keeping ~97% accuracy with ~40% fewer parameters and faster inference.

category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 要给蒸馏预算算力,团队以为蒸馏很便宜。
scenario_en: Budgeting compute for distillation, the team assumes it's cheap.
q: 蒸馏有哪笔容易被忽视的成本,还有什么前提?
q_en: What overlooked cost and prerequisite does distillation have?
why: 得让 teacher 对整个训练集跑一遍推理来产软标签,这是一次性但可观的算力,必须提前预算。另一个前提:student 容量要足够大,才装得下 teacher 的知识,太小会欠拟合、掉点更多。
why_en: You must run teacher inference over the full training set to produce soft labels — a one-time but significant compute — and the student must be large enough to absorb the teacher.
options: 蒸馏几乎零成本,直接拿现成的软标签训练就行了
teacher 全训练集跑一遍推理产软标签,student 要够大
蒸馏根本不需要训练集,只要拿到 teacher 的模型权重文件即可
student 容量越小越好,大小根本不是要考虑的问题
options_en: Distillation is nearly free — just train on ready-made soft labels.
The teacher runs inference over the whole training set for soft labels, and the student must be big enough.
Distillation needs no training set at all, only the teacher's model weight files.
A smaller student is always better; its capacity is not a concern at all.
optionExplanations: 软标签要现产:teacher 得对全训练集推理一遍,不是零成本。
对;一次性 teacher 全量推理是真实算力开销,加上 student 容量下限,是蒸馏两个易忽视点。
产软标签正需要训练集输入,只有权重没有数据蒸不了。
student 太小容量不足会欠拟合掉更多点,容量是硬约束。
optionExplanations_en: Soft labels must be generated: the teacher runs over the full training set — not free.
Correct — one-time full teacher inference is real compute, plus a student capacity floor, distillation's two overlooked points.
Producing soft labels needs the training-set inputs; weights without data can't distill.
Too small a student underfits and loses more; capacity is a hard constraint.
category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 要剪枝一个模型让它在标准 GPU/CPU 上真的变快,而不只是权重矩阵里多了很多 0。
scenario_en: You want pruning that actually speeds the model on standard GPU/CPU, not just more zeros in the weight matrix.
q: 结构化剪枝和非结构化剪枝的关键区别是什么?
q_en: What's the key difference between structured and unstructured pruning?
why: 结构化剪枝整块移除组件(卷积滤波器、注意力头、整层),产出真正更小的稠密网络,在标准硬件上直接加速;非结构化剪枝把单个权重置零,得到稀疏矩阵,要专门的稀疏计算库才可能加速,普通硬件上未必快。
why_en: Structured pruning removes whole components for a genuinely smaller dense model that speeds up on standard hardware, while unstructured zeros individual weights needing sparse libraries.
options: 结构化是置零单个权重、非结构化是删整层,正好相反
结构化删整块组件→稠密变小;非结构化置零单权重→稀疏
两者其实完全一样,都能在标准硬件上直接加速
两者都只是把权重数值变小一点,不改变结构
options_en: Structured zeros individual weights and unstructured deletes whole layers — exactly reversed.
Structured removes whole components giving a smaller dense model; unstructured zeros single weights giving sparsity.
They are actually identical and both speed things up on standard hardware.
Both merely shrink weight values a little without changing structure.
optionExplanations: 粒度说反了:结构化删整块组件,非结构化才是置零单个权重。
对;结构化产稠密小网络在标准硬件直接快,非结构化稀疏要专用库,这是能否真加速的分水岭。
两者硬件加速表现不同:稠密标准硬件就快,稀疏不装库未必快。
结构化会真正改变架构(移除整块),不是只把权重变小。
optionExplanations_en: Granularity reversed: structured removes whole components; unstructured zeros individual weights.
Correct — structured yields a dense small net fast on standard hardware while unstructured is sparse needing special libraries, the divide on real speedup.
Their hardware speedup differs: dense is fast on standard hardware, sparse may not be without libraries.
Structured genuinely changes the architecture by removing whole blocks, not just shrinking weights.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整块移除滤波器/注意力头/层,产出更小的稠密网络,标准硬件即加速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structured pruning removes whole filters/heads/layers, yielding a smaller dense network that speeds up on standard hardware.

termDefinitions.term: unstructured pruning / 非结构化剪枝
termDefinitions.meaning: 把单个权重置零得到稀疏矩阵,需稀疏计算库才可能加速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Unstructured pruning zeros individual weights into a sparse matrix, needing sparse-computation libraries to speed up.

tradeoff: 标准硬件上的真实加速 vs 剪枝粒度的灵活性
category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 要对一个训好的模型做结构化剪枝,同时把准确率损失控制在 <2%。
scenario_en: You structured-prune a trained model while keeping accuracy loss under 2%.
q: 把结构化剪枝的工作流排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the structured-pruning workflow correctly:
steps: 先训练出一个完整的高准确率模型
微调剪枝后的网络,恢复被剪掉带来的准确率损失
按重要性打分(L1 范数/Taylor 展开)对组件排序
移除得分最低的组件(滤波器/头/层)
why: 先训好完整模型→按 L1 范数/Taylor 展开给组件打重要性分→移除最不重要的组件→再微调恢复精度。这套"训练→剪枝→微调"能砍 FLOPs 30–70% 而准确率损失 <2%。
why_en: Train a full model, score components by L1 norm/Taylor, remove the lowest, then fine-tune to recover accuracy — cutting FLOPs 30-70% with under 2% loss.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  T["训练完整模型"] --> S["打分排序"]
  S --> R["移除最低分组件"]
  R --> F["微调恢复"]

termDefinitions.term: L1 norm / Taylor expansion 打分
termDefinitions.meaning: 用权重 L1 范数或 Taylor 展开估计每个组件对损失的重要性,以决定剪谁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scoring by L1 norm or Taylor expansion estimates each component's importance to the loss, deciding what to prune.

category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 结构化剪枝配合剪后微调,常能砍掉 30–70% 的 FLOPs 而准确率损失 <2%。
scenario_en: Structured pruning with post-prune fine-tuning often cuts 30-70% of FLOPs at under 2% accuracy loss.
q: 这组数字对边缘部署意味着什么?
q_en: What do these numbers mean for edge deployment?
why: FLOPs 砍 30–70% 直接换来延迟/能耗大幅下降,而 <2% 准确率损失通常可接受——对 <50MB/<10ms 的边缘预算,结构化剪枝往往是性价比很高的一步。这是经验量级,依模型/任务而变,不是保证。
why_en: Cutting 30-70% FLOPs sharply lowers latency/energy at under 2% accuracy loss, making structured pruning a high-value step for tight edge budgets.
options: 说明剪枝一定完全无损,可以一路剪到接近 0 也完全不掉点
FLOPs 砍 30–70%,<2% 损失换低延迟低能耗
说明剪枝反而会让模型变得更大、推理更慢
30–70% 指的是剪枝带来的准确率提升幅度
options_en: It shows pruning is completely lossless, so you can prune down to near zero without any drop at all.
Cutting 30-70% of FLOPs trades under 2% accuracy for low latency and energy.
It shows pruning actually makes the model bigger and inference slower.
The 30-70% refers to the accuracy gain that pruning brings.
optionExplanations: 有 <2% 损失说明不是无损,剪过头会崩,不能剪到 0。
对;把 FLOPs 削减翻译成延迟/能耗下降+可接受的精度损失,是边缘部署该讲的设计含义。
剪枝是让模型更小更快,方向说反了。
30–70% 是 FLOPs 削减幅度,不是准确率提升;准确率是略降 <2%。
optionExplanations_en: The under-2% loss shows it isn't lossless; over-pruning collapses accuracy, so not to zero.
Correct — translating FLOP cuts into latency/energy drop at acceptable accuracy loss is the edge-deployment implication to state.
Pruning makes the model smaller and faster — the direction is reversed.
30-70% is the FLOP reduction, not accuracy gain; accuracy slightly drops under 2%.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次前向的浮点运算量,衡量计算成本,减少它直接降延迟/能耗。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FLOPs (Floating-Point Operations) count a forward pass's arithmetic, a compute-cost measure whose reduction lowers latency/energy.

category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 便宜的压缩手段(量化/剪枝/蒸馏)都试过仍不达预算,或要为某类硬件长期打造最优架构。
scenario_en: Cheaper compression (quantization/pruning/distillation) is exhausted or you must craft an optimal architecture for a hardware class long-term.
q: 什么时候才轮到 NAS,怎么定位它?
q_en: When is NAS warranted, and how do you position it?
why: NAS 是最后手段:能自动搜出最优高效架构(EfficientNet 就出自此),但历史上要上千 GPU 小时。one-shot/权重共享(DARTS、OFA)可把成本降几个数量级。
why_en: Position NAS as the last resort: best results but historically thousands of GPU-hours, used only after cheaper techniques are exhausted.
options: 一上来就用 NAS,反正它出来的效果最好
把 NAS 当最后手段:效果最好但也最贵
NAS 是最便宜的手段,应该第一个拿来试
NAS 和量化成本差不多,先后顺序无所谓
options_en: Reach for NAS right away, since it gives the best results anyway.
Treat NAS as the last resort: best results but also the priciest.
NAS is the cheapest technique and should be tried first.
NAS costs about the same as quantization, so order does not matter.
whenOtherWins: 当量化/剪枝/蒸馏这些便宜手段就能满足预算时,根本不该动 NAS,先用它们省时省钱。
optionExplanations: 一上来就 NAS 是烧钱,多数预算便宜手段就能满足,不必付最贵代价。
对;NAS 效果最好但最贵,定位为最后手段、便宜手段用尽再上,是成本理性的做法。
NAS 恰恰最贵,不是最便宜,顺序上应最后而非最先。
NAS 比量化贵几个数量级,成本顺序很重要,不能忽略。
optionExplanations_en: Leading with NAS burns money; most budgets are met by cheaper techniques, so don't pay the costliest first.
Correct — NAS gives the best results but is costliest, positioned as last resort after cheaper techniques, the cost-rational move.
NAS is the costliest, not cheapest, so it goes last not first.
NAS is orders of magnitude costlier than quantization, so cost order matters and can't be ignored.

termDefinitions.meaning: one-shot/权重共享的 NAS 方法,把搜索成本从上千 GPU 小时降几个数量级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DARTS and OFA (once-for-all) are one-shot/weight-sharing NAS methods cutting search cost by orders of magnitude.

tradeoff: 架构质量的上限 vs 搜索要烧的 GPU 小时
category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 300M ViT 要压进 <50MB/<10ms,团队问第一个该动的压缩手段是哪个。
scenario_en: The 300M ViT must fit <50MB/<10ms; the team asks which compression to try first.
q: 成本有序的压缩流水线里第一步该做什么?
q_en: What's the first step in the cost-ordered compression pipeline?
why: 先做量化——最便宜:把权重/激活从 FP32 降到 INT8 等低精度,直接减体积和加速,改动小、常常一步就大幅接近预算。达标就停,不够再依次上剪枝、蒸馏、NAS。
why_en: Do quantization first — the cheapest step: lower precision (e.g. FP32 to INT8) shrinks size and speeds inference with minimal change, escalating only if needed.
options: 先做最贵的 NAS,从头搜一个高效架构出来
先做量化:最便宜,降精度直接减体积并加速
先做蒸馏,专门训一个更小的 student 模型
先做非结构化剪枝,把一半权重直接置零
options_en: Start with the costliest NAS and search an efficient architecture from scratch.
Quantize first — cheapest: lower precision shrinks size and speeds it up.
Distill first and train a dedicated smaller student model.
Prune unstructured first, zeroing out half the weights.
whenOtherWins: 若量化后仍超预算,再按成本顺序叠加剪枝、蒸馏,最后才考虑 NAS。
optionExplanations: NAS 最贵,放第一步违背成本有序原则,多数情况用不着。
对;量化最便宜、改动最小,先试它、达标即停,是成本有序流水线的起点。
蒸馏比量化贵(要跑 teacher 全量推理),不该排在量化之前。
非结构化剪枝产稀疏矩阵,标准硬件未必加速,也不是最便宜的第一步。
optionExplanations_en: NAS is costliest; putting it first violates cost ordering and is usually unnecessary.
Correct — quantization is cheapest with minimal change, so try it first and stop if met, the pipeline's starting point.
Distillation is costlier than quantization (needs full teacher inference), so it shouldn't precede quantization.
Unstructured pruning yields a sparse matrix that may not speed up standard hardware, and isn't the cheapest first step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权重/激活从高精度(FP32)降到低精度(INT8)以减体积、加速,是最便宜的压缩手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers weights/activations from high precision (FP32) to low (INT8) to shrink size and speed up, the cheapest compression.

tradeoff: 压缩收益 vs 每一级手段的工程与算力成本
category: Transfer Learning Fine Tuning And Model Compression

scenario: 推荐/广告服务系统每次请求位置有限，默认策略是永远服务「当前估计 CTR 最高」的物品。
scenario_en: A recommender/ads serving system has limited slots per request and by default always serves the item with the highest estimated CTR.
q: 只做 exploitation（永远服务最高估计 CTR）会引发什么系统性问题？
q_en: What systemic problem does pure exploitation (always serving the highest estimated CTR) cause?
why: 热门物品拿到更多曝光→更多点击数据→估计更自信→更被推，形成反馈闭环；新的、可能更好的物品拿不到曝光就永远缺数据、被埋没。所以服务路径必须留一部分流量做 exploration。
why_en: Popular items get more exposure and data, making their estimate more confident and getting them served even more — a feedback loop that starves newer, possibly better items of data.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["只服务最高估计 CTR"] --> X["热门物品拿更多曝光"]
  X --> D["积累更多点击数据"]
  D --> C["估计更自信→更被推"]
  C --> E
  N["新/更好物品"] -. 拿不到曝光 .-> Z["缺数据被埋没"]
options: 形成反馈闭环：热门物品持续拿曝光和数据、估计越发自信，新物品缺数据被埋没
系统会自动做冷启动重置：CTR 估计按天清零，所有物品重新公平竞争曝光位置
探索代价随候选臂数量线性上升，因为每次曝光都要重算全部臂的后验并排序
只会造成模型过拟合到少数活跃用户的点击模式，但物品曝光分布仍保持均匀
options_en: A feedback loop: popular items keep taking exposure and data and grow more confident, while new items are starved and buried.
The system auto-resets for cold start: CTR estimates zero out daily, so all items fairly re-compete for exposure slots.
Exploration cost grows linearly with the number of candidate arms, because every impression recomputes and re-ranks all arms' posteriors.
It only overfits the model to a few active users' click patterns, but item-level exposure stays uniformly distributed.
optionExplanations: 对；这就是 exploitation-only 的反馈闭环，赢家通吃，更好的新物品没机会拿到数据证明自己。
没有任何机制会自动清零估计，恰恰相反，估计会越攒越偏向老赢家。
线性探索代价是 fixed-ε 的毛病，且此处根本没在探索；与「永远 exploit」无关。
问题出在物品侧曝光高度集中，不是用户过拟合；曝光分布会变得极不均匀。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this is the exploitation-only feedback loop; winners take all and better new items never get data to prove themselves.
No mechanism resets estimates; on the contrary, estimates skew ever more toward old winners.
Linear exploration cost is a fixed-epsilon flaw, and here nothing is exploring at all; unrelated to pure exploitation.
The problem is item-side exposure concentration, not user overfitting; the exposure distribution becomes extremely skewed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例，常用作推荐/广告的即时奖励信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions that get clicked, often used as the immediate reward signal in recs/ads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用已知最优 vs 试探不确定项以获取信息，二者要在服务路径上权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exploitation serves the currently-best item; exploration tries uncertain items to gather information; serving must trade them off.

scenario: 用「累积 regret」形式化探索目标：regret = 每步最优臂本可拿的奖励 − 实际所选臂拿到的奖励，再对所有步求和。
scenario_en: Exploration is formalized by cumulative regret: at each step, (best arm's reward − chosen arm's reward), summed over all steps.
q: 为什么目标是让累积 regret 保持 sublinear，而不是追求零 regret？
q_en: Why is the goal to keep cumulative regret sublinear rather than zero?
why: 不试就无法知道哪个臂最优，必须交一点探索税，所以零 regret 不可达。sublinear（如 O(√T)）意味着 regret/T→0，即平均每次决策的探索代价随时间趋近 0，系统越跑越接近最优。
why_en: You can't know the best arm without trying, so zero regret is impossible; sublinear regret means regret/T goes to zero, so the per-decision exploration cost shrinks over time.
options: 零 regret：好算法应从第一次决策起就永不选错臂
constant regret：总探索代价是个固定常数，与运行多久无关
sublinear（如 O(√T)）：平均探索代价随 T 趋于 0
linear（如 O(T)）：只要 regret 有上界就行，增长斜率大小无所谓
options_en: Zero regret: a good algorithm should never pick a wrong arm from the very first decision.
Constant regret: total exploration cost is a fixed constant, independent of how long you run.
Sublinear (e.g. O(sqrt T)): the average per-decision exploration cost goes to zero.
Linear (e.g. O(T)): as long as regret is upper-bounded, its growth slope doesn't matter.
optionExplanations: 有不确定性时不试就无从知道最优臂，零 regret 不可实现。
常数 regret 同样不可达；在线学习必须持续付一点探索代价，关键是让它占比缩小。
对；sublinear 让 regret/T→0，探索税随时间被摊薄，这才是 bandit 的正式目标。
linear regret（如 fixed-ε）意味着永远按固定比例亏，斜率恰恰决定你是否在收敛。
optionExplanations_en: With uncertainty you can't find the best arm without trying, so zero regret is unattainable.
Constant regret is also unattainable; online learning must keep paying a little exploration cost — the point is to shrink its share.
Correct — sublinear makes regret/T go to zero, amortizing the exploration tax over time; this is the formal bandit objective.
Linear regret (e.g. fixed-epsilon) means losing a fixed fraction forever; the slope is exactly what tells you whether you're converging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 遗憾：每步「最优臂奖励 − 实际所选臂奖励」的累加，衡量探索的代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regret is the running sum of (best arm's reward − chosen arm's reward) per step, measuring the cost of exploration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 累积 regret 增长比 T 慢（如 O(√T)），使 regret/T→0，平均探索代价随时间趋 0。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sublinear regret grows slower than T (e.g. O(sqrt T)), so regret/T goes to zero and average exploration cost vanishes over time.

scenario: 把「每次请求该展示哪个物品」抽象成一个在线决策问题。
scenario_en: Abstract 'which item to show per request' into an online decision problem.
q: 补全多臂老虎机(MAB)的标准设定：
q_en: Complete the standard multi-armed bandit (MAB) setup:
text: MAB 设定：{{K}} 个臂各有未知的奖励分布；每次请求选 {{一}} 个臂、只观察到被选臂的奖励（点击/转化），目标是最大化{{累积}}奖励。
text_en: MAB setup: {{K}} arms each with an unknown reward distribution; per request you pull {{one}} arm and observe only that arm's reward (click/conversion), aiming to maximize {{cumulative}} reward.
why: 关键是「bandit feedback」——每次只看到被选臂的反馈，看不到没选的臂会怎样，这正是必须探索的根源。目标不是单次最优而是长期累积奖励。
why_en: The key is bandit feedback — you only observe the pulled arm's outcome, never the counterfactual, which is exactly why you must explore.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多臂老虎机：K 个未知回报的臂，每次拉一个、观察回报，最大化累积回报的在线决策模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAB (Multi-Armed Bandit) is an online decision model with K arms of unknown payoff; you pull one per round to maximize cumulative reward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只观察到被选动作的结果，观察不到未选动作的反事实结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bandit feedback means you only observe the outcome of the chosen action, never the counterfactual of the unchosen ones.

scenario: 想用最省事的方式在服务里加一点探索，先做个原型基线。
scenario_en: You want the simplest way to add a bit of exploration for a prototype baseline.
q: epsilon-greedy 每次决策是怎么选臂的？
q_en: How does epsilon-greedy pick an arm on each decision?
why: 以概率 ε（常 0.05–0.1）随机选一个臂做探索，其余 1−ε 概率选当前观测均值最高的臂做 exploitation。实现极简、适合当原型基线，但探索是「均匀」的。
why_en: With probability epsilon (typically 0.05–0.1) it picks a random arm to explore, otherwise it exploits the arm with the highest observed mean.
options: 给每个臂加一个随拉动次数衰减的置信奖励，选「均值+奖励」总分最高的臂
为每个臂维护一个后验分布，各抽一个样本，选样本最大的臂
永远选当前均值最高的臂，等收敛后再一次性随机重启所有估计
以概率 ε 随机选一个臂探索，其余 1−ε 概率选当前观测均值最高的臂
options_en: Add a confidence bonus that decays with pull count to each arm, and pick the highest mean-plus-bonus.
Maintain a posterior per arm, draw one sample each, and pick the arm with the largest sample.
Always pick the highest observed mean, then randomly reset all estimates once after it converges.
With probability epsilon pick a random arm to explore, otherwise pick the highest observed mean.
optionExplanations: 这是 UCB 的确定性置信上界打分，靠 bonus 而非随机数驱动探索。
这是 Thompson Sampling：每臂后验采样，探索量正比不确定性。
「先纯 exploit 再随机重启」不是任何标准 bandit 算法，重启会抛弃已学到的信息。
对；固定概率随机探索 + 其余时间贪心利用，实现只要几行代码。
optionExplanations_en: That's UCB's deterministic upper-confidence-bound scoring, driven by a bonus rather than randomness.
That's Thompson Sampling: sample each arm's posterior, so exploration scales with uncertainty.
'Pure exploit then random restart' isn't any standard bandit; restarting throws away learned information.
Correct — a fixed random-exploration probability plus greedy exploitation otherwise; a few lines of code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以概率 ε 随机探索、以 1−ε 选当前最优臂的简单 bandit 策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon-greedy explores a random arm with probability epsilon and exploits the current-best arm otherwise.

scenario: 一个臂已被拉 10 万次、明显很差；另一个只被拉 10 次、还很不确定。系统用 fixed ε=0.1 的 epsilon-greedy。
scenario_en: One arm has been pulled 100k times and is clearly bad; another was pulled only 10 times and is still uncertain. The system uses fixed epsilon=0.1 epsilon-greedy.
q: epsilon-greedy 的核心弱点是什么？固定 ε 会带来什么样的 regret？
q_en: What is epsilon-greedy's core weakness, and what regret does a fixed epsilon give?
why: 探索是「均匀」的：它对拉了 10 万次的烂臂和只拉 10 次的新臂花同样的探索预算，把钱浪费在早已成定局的臂上。固定 ε → linear regret（永远 10% 流量乱撒）；让 ε 随时间衰减能到 sublinear，但要调参。
why_en: Its exploration is uniform — it spends the same budget on a 100k-pull bad arm as on a 10-pull uncertain one; a fixed epsilon gives linear regret, while decaying epsilon reaches sublinear but needs tuning.
tradeoff: 均匀探索(实现简单) vs 按不确定性探索(样本更省)；fixed ε(linear regret) vs decayed ε(sublinear 但要调)
options: 探索预算会自动集中到高不确定臂上，固定 ε 已足以保证 sublinear regret
均匀探索：对已确定很差的臂和高不确定新臂花同样预算；固定 ε → linear regret
它假设奖励平稳，遇趋势内容必须加时间窗口，与 ε 的大小无关
每步都要更新全部 K 个臂的后验分布，计算 O(K)，在大 K 下太慢
options_en: Exploration budget auto-concentrates on high-uncertainty arms, so a fixed epsilon already guarantees sublinear regret.
Uniform exploration: same budget on a settled-bad arm as on a high-uncertainty new one; fixed epsilon gives linear regret.
It assumes stationary rewards and needs a time window for trending content, independent of epsilon's size.
Every step updates all K arms' posteriors, costing O(K), which is too slow for large K.
optionExplanations: 说反了：epsilon-greedy 的探索恰恰不会自动集中，固定 ε 给的是 linear regret。
对；均匀探索是它的病根，固定 ε 让 10% 流量永远乱撒，累积成 linear regret。
平稳性假设是 UCB 的软肋，不是 epsilon-greedy 的核心弱点。
O(K) 后验更新是 Thompson Sampling 的成本，epsilon-greedy 是 O(1)。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: epsilon-greedy's exploration does not auto-concentrate, and a fixed epsilon gives linear regret.
Correct — uniform exploration is the root flaw; a fixed epsilon squanders 10% of traffic forever, accumulating linear regret.
The stationarity assumption is UCB's weak spot, not epsilon-greedy's core weakness.
O(K) posterior updates are Thompson Sampling's cost; epsilon-greedy is O(1).

termDefinitions.meaning: 不论臂的不确定性高低，都以相同概率随机探索，浪费在已确定的臂上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Uniform exploration explores every arm with equal probability regardless of uncertainty, wasting budget on already-settled arms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 累积 regret 与步数 T 成正比（斜率固定），意味着永远按固定比例亏、不收敛到最优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linear regret grows proportionally to T, meaning you keep losing a fixed fraction forever and never converge to optimal.

scenario: 想要一个确定性(无随机数)、可解释、便于调试的探索策略。
scenario_en: You want a deterministic (no RNG), interpretable, debuggable exploration strategy.
q: UCB 怎么决定拉哪个臂？置信奖励项 sqrt(2·ln t / N_a) 起什么作用？
q_en: How does UCB choose an arm, and what does the bonus sqrt(2·ln t / N_a) do?
why: 打分 = 估计均值 + 置信奖励 sqrt(2·ln t / N_a)；N_a 越小 bonus 越大，优先探索欠采样臂，拉多后 bonus 收缩转向 exploit。
why_en: Score = estimated reward + a bonus sqrt(2·ln t / N_a); fewer pulls means a bigger bonus so under-explored arms get tried, and the bonus shrinks as the arm is pulled.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["臂 a"] --> S["打分 = 估计均值 + 置信奖励"]
  N["N_a 拉动次数少"] --> B["bonus 大 → 优先探索"]
  M["N_a 拉动次数多"] --> C["bonus 收缩 → 转向 exploit"]
  B --> S
  C --> S
options: 为每个臂维护 Beta 后验，各抽一个样本，选样本最大的臂展示
打分 = 均值 + 奖励，且奖励随拉动次数增大，专挑被拉最多的臂
打分 = 均值 + 置信奖励，拉得越少 bonus 越大
以概率 ε 随机选一个臂，其余时间选估计均值最高的臂
options_en: Maintain a Beta posterior per arm, draw one sample each, and show the arm with the largest sample.
Score = mean plus a bonus that grows with pull count, always picking the most-pulled arm.
Score = estimated mean plus a confidence bonus; fewer pulls means a bigger bonus.
Pick a random arm with probability epsilon, otherwise pick the highest estimated mean.
optionExplanations: 这是 Thompson Sampling 的后验采样，不是 UCB 的确定性打分。
方向搞反了：bonus 随拉动次数「减小」而非增大，UCB 是去探索欠采样的臂。
对；置信上界=均值+不确定性奖励，欠采样臂 bonus 大而被探索，是「面对不确定时保持乐观」。
这是 epsilon-greedy 的随机探索，不是 UCB 的确定性置信奖励。
optionExplanations_en: That's Thompson Sampling's posterior sampling, not UCB's deterministic scoring.
Direction reversed: the bonus shrinks with pull count, and UCB explores under-sampled arms.
Correct — upper confidence bound = mean + uncertainty bonus; under-sampled arms get a big bonus, i.e. 'optimism under uncertainty'.
That's epsilon-greedy's random exploration, not UCB's deterministic bonus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 置信上界：给每个臂打「估计均值 + 置信奖励」，欠采样臂奖励大而被优先探索的确定性策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UCB (Upper Confidence Bound) scores each arm as estimated mean plus a confidence bonus, deterministically exploring under-sampled arms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 臂 a 到目前为止被拉动的次数；越小说明对该臂了解越少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: N_a is the number of times arm a has been pulled so far; smaller means less known about it.

scenario: 用 UCB 服务新闻/时令商品，物品真实 CTR 随热点和季节漂移（非平稳）。
scenario_en: You serve news/seasonal items with UCB, but items' true CTR drifts with trends and seasons (non-stationary).
q: UCB 的默认形式在这种非平稳场景会出什么问题？怎么修？
q_en: What breaks with default UCB under non-stationarity, and how do you fix it?
why: 标准 UCB 假设每个臂奖励平稳(stationary)——它把很久以前的旧数据也算进均值，热点变了反应很慢，会长期押注一个早已过气的臂。修法：加滑动窗口或对历史打折(discounting)，让近期数据主导估计。
why_en: Standard UCB assumes stationary rewards and folds stale old data into the mean, so it reacts slowly to trend shifts; fix it with a sliding window or discounting so recent data dominates.
options: 它会自适应非平稳，无需任何改动，因为 bonus 项已经能追踪漂移
它假设奖励平稳、旧数据拖慢反应；加滑动窗口或历史打折让近期数据主导
它会因随机采样噪声太大而抖动，唯一修法是把 ε 调到 0
它的 O(K) 后验更新太贵，非平稳下必须换成 epsilon-greedy 降成本
options_en: It adapts to non-stationarity with no changes, since the bonus term already tracks drift.
It assumes stationary rewards and stale data slows it down; add a sliding window or discounting so recent data dominates.
It jitters from too much sampling noise, and the only fix is to set epsilon to 0.
Its O(K) posterior updates are too costly, so non-stationarity forces a switch to epsilon-greedy.
optionExplanations: 错；标准 UCB 的均值对所有历史等权，漂移下反应迟钝，并不会自适应。
对；平稳性假设是软肋，窗口/打折把旧数据的权重压下去，才能跟上热点。
UCB 是确定性算法、没有随机采样；ε 是 epsilon-greedy 的参数，张冠李戴。
O(K) 后验更新是 Thompson Sampling 的成本；UCB 本身是 O(1)，与非平稳无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — standard UCB weights all history equally and reacts sluggishly to drift; it does not self-adapt.
Correct — the stationarity assumption is the weak spot; windowing/discounting down-weights old data to track trends.
UCB is deterministic with no sampling; epsilon belongs to epsilon-greedy — a mix-up.
O(K) posterior updates are Thompson Sampling's cost; UCB is O(1) and unrelated to non-stationarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个臂的真实回报分布不随时间变化；非平稳则相反，需用近期数据主导估计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stationary rewards mean each arm's true payoff distribution doesn't change over time; non-stationary is the opposite and needs recency-weighted estimates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对历史观测打折或只用滑动窗口内数据，让估计偏向近期、跟上漂移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Discounting/windowing down-weights or drops old observations so estimates favor recent data and track drift.

scenario: 想要探索量自动随不确定性缩放、且能优雅应对非平稳的生产级 bandit 算法。
scenario_en: You want a production bandit whose exploration auto-scales with uncertainty and handles non-stationarity gracefully.
q: Thompson Sampling 每次决策是怎么工作的？
q_en: How does Thompson Sampling work per decision?
why: 贝叶斯法：每个臂维护一个后验（二元奖励用 Beta），每次请求对每个臂各抽一个样本、选样本最大的臂。臂越不确定后验越宽、被选中探索的概率越高，学明白后探索自动消退。代价是每次决策 O(K) 次后验更新。
why_en: It keeps a posterior per arm (Beta for binary rewards), draws one sample per arm each request, and picks the highest sample, so exploration auto-scales with uncertainty and fades as it learns.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["每臂维护后验(Beta)"] --> S["每臂各抽一个样本"]
  S --> M["选样本最大的臂"]
  M --> O["观察奖励"]
  O --> U["更新该臂后验"]
  U --> P
options: 每个臂维护后验分布，每次各抽一个样本、选样本最大的臂，观察后更新后验
给每个臂算 均值+sqrt(2 ln t/N_a) 的确定性打分，选最高分的臂
以固定概率 ε 随机探索，其余时间选观测均值最高的臂
把所有臂的历史点击平均，永远选平均点击率最高的那个臂
options_en: Keep a posterior per arm, draw one sample each, pick the largest sample, then update that arm's posterior on the observed reward.
Compute a deterministic score mean + sqrt(2 ln t / N_a) per arm and pick the highest.
Explore randomly with a fixed probability epsilon, otherwise pick the highest observed mean.
Average each arm's historical clicks and always pick the highest average click rate.
optionExplanations: 对；后验采样让探索量正比于不确定性、随学习自动消退，Google Ads / Netflix 生产在用其变体。
这是 UCB 的确定性置信上界，不是 Thompson 的贝叶斯采样。
这是 epsilon-greedy 的均匀随机探索，不会随不确定性缩放。
这是纯 exploitation（贪心），完全没有探索。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — posterior sampling makes exploration proportional to uncertainty and fade as it learns; Google Ads/Netflix run variants in production.
That's UCB's deterministic upper confidence bound, not Thompson's Bayesian sampling.
That's epsilon-greedy's uniform random exploration, which doesn't scale with uncertainty.
That's pure exploitation (greedy) with no exploration at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贝叶斯 bandit：为每臂维护后验，抽样后选样本最大的臂，探索量自动正比于不确定性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson Sampling is a Bayesian bandit that keeps a posterior per arm and samples to pick, so exploration is auto-proportional to uncertainty.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在观测数据后对臂真实奖励率的概率信念；二元奖励常用 Beta 分布表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A posterior is the probabilistic belief about an arm's true reward rate after data; Beta is the usual choice for binary rewards.

scenario: 同样的探索预算，epsilon-greedy 和 Thompson Sampling 把它分配到各个臂的方式不同。
scenario_en: Given the same exploration budget, epsilon-greedy and Thompson Sampling allocate it across arms differently.
q: 在「探索预算怎么分配」这一维度上，Thompson Sampling 相对 epsilon-greedy 强在哪？
q_en: On the dimension of how exploration is allocated, how does Thompson Sampling beat epsilon-greedy?
why: epsilon-greedy 均匀撒探索：烂臂和新臂一样对待。Thompson Sampling 按后验不确定性分配：越不确定的臂被抽中探索的概率越高、越确定的臂越少被探索，样本利用率高得多，学明白后探索自动消退。
why_en: Epsilon-greedy explores uniformly, treating bad and new arms alike, while Thompson Sampling allocates exploration in proportion to each arm's posterior uncertainty and fades it as it learns.
tradeoff: 均匀探索(简单但样本浪费) vs 按不确定性探索(样本省、自动消退但每步 O(K))
options: TS 的探索量更大，因此总能比 epsilon-greedy 更快找到最优臂
TS 按后验不确定性分配探索：越不确定越常探索、越确定越少探索，样本更省
TS 完全不探索，只在后验收敛后才开始利用最优臂
TS 的每步成本更低（O(1)），所以在大 K 下比 epsilon-greedy 更快
options_en: TS explores more in total, so it always finds the best arm faster than epsilon-greedy.
TS allocates exploration by posterior uncertainty: more-uncertain arms explored more, certain arms less — far more sample-efficient.
TS never explores; it only starts exploiting the best arm after the posterior converges.
TS has lower per-step cost (O(1)), so it's faster than epsilon-greedy at large K.
optionExplanations: 不是「探索更多」而是「探索更聪明」——把预算投到最需要的臂，而非无脑加量。
对；不确定性驱动的分配让每一次探索都花在最能减少不确定性的地方。
说反了：TS 一直在探索，只是探索量随不确定性自动缩放，不是收敛后才开始。
TS 每步是 O(K) 后验更新，比 ε-greedy 的 O(1) 贵，这恰是它的代价。
optionExplanations_en: Not 'more exploration' but 'smarter exploration' — budget goes to the arms that need it, not brute-force volume.
Correct — uncertainty-driven allocation spends each exploration where it reduces uncertainty most.
Backwards: TS explores throughout, just auto-scaled by uncertainty, not only after convergence.
TS is O(K) posterior updates per step, costlier than epsilon-greedy's O(1) — that's precisely its price.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用更少的数据学到同样好的策略；按不确定性分配探索能提升它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sample efficiency is reaching the same policy quality with less data; uncertainty-aware exploration improves it.

scenario: 生产级广告/推荐服务，物品集合大、CTR 随热点漂移，希望探索能自动随把握度缩放、不必人工调探索率。
scenario_en: A production ads/recs service with a large item set, CTR drifting with trends, wanting exploration to auto-scale with confidence without manually tuning an exploration rate.
q: 这套约束下，三种 bandit 里默认该选哪个？
q_en: Under these constraints, which of the three bandits is the default pick?
why: 选 Thompson Sampling：探索量自动正比于不确定性、学明白后自动消退，且用后验能优雅应对非平稳，无需像 ε 那样手调衰减。这也是 Google Ads / Netflix 生产采用其变体的原因。
why_en: Pick Thompson Sampling — exploration auto-scales with uncertainty and fades as it learns, and posteriors handle non-stationarity gracefully without tuning a decay schedule.
tradeoff: Thompson(自适应、免调、O(K)) vs epsilon-greedy(简单、O(1)、要调 ε) vs UCB(确定性可解释、假设平稳)
whenOtherWins: 若要一个无随机、可解释、便于线上审计每步决策的策略，UCB 更合适；只想 30 分钟搭个原型基线，epsilon-greedy 最省事。
options: epsilon-greedy：实现最简单，固定 ε 就能兼顾探索与非平稳
UCB：确定性打分最稳，且天然适应 CTR 漂移无需改动
Thompson Sampling：探索随不确定性自动缩放、免调、优雅应对非平稳
纯 exploitation：物品多时直接服务最高估计 CTR，省掉探索开销
options_en: Epsilon-greedy: simplest to build, and a fixed epsilon balances exploration and non-stationarity.
UCB: deterministic scoring is most stable and natively adapts to CTR drift with no changes.
Thompson Sampling: exploration auto-scales with uncertainty, tuning-free, and handles non-stationarity gracefully.
Pure exploitation: with many items, just serve the highest estimated CTR and skip exploration cost.
optionExplanations: 固定 ε 是均匀探索且给 linear regret，也不会自动适应漂移，不满足「自适应免调」。
标准 UCB 假设平稳，漂移下反应慢，需额外加窗口才行，并非「无需改动」。
对；后验采样一次性满足自适应探索、免调、抗非平稳三个诉求。
纯 exploitation 会触发反馈闭环、埋没新物品，正是本课要避免的默认坏解。
optionExplanations_en: A fixed epsilon is uniform exploration with linear regret and doesn't adapt to drift — fails the 'adaptive, tuning-free' ask.
Standard UCB assumes stationarity and reacts slowly to drift, needing an added window — not 'no changes'.
Correct — posterior sampling satisfies adaptive exploration, tuning-free, and non-stationarity all at once.
Pure exploitation triggers the feedback loop and buries new items — the very default this lesson warns against.

termDefinitions.meaning: 臂的真实回报随时间变化（热点、季节），要求策略偏重近期数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-stationarity means arms' true payoffs change over time (trends, seasons), requiring recency-weighted policies.

q: 把 Thompson Sampling 单次决策的循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order one Thompson Sampling decision cycle correctly:
steps: 从每个臂的当前后验各抽一个样本
选样本值最大的臂并展示
观察该臂的奖励（点击/转化）
用观测到的奖励更新该臂的后验（如 Beta 参数）
why: 每次决策：抽样→选样本最大臂→观察奖励→更新后验。不确定的臂后验宽、抽出的样本波动大，因而更常被选中探索；随着数据积累后验收窄，探索自动消退。
why_en: Each decision samples from every arm's posterior, picks the largest sample, observes the reward, then updates that arm's posterior, so exploration auto-fades as posteriors narrow.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["抽样"] --> B["选最大样本臂"]
  B --> C["观察奖励"]
  C --> D["更新后验"]
  D --> A

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新观测（成功/失败次数）更新臂的信念分布，是 Thompson Sampling 的学习步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A posterior update revises an arm's belief distribution with new observations (successes/failures) — the learning step of Thompson Sampling.

scenario: 已上线 fixed ε=0.1 的 epsilon-greedy；经过 1000 万次曝光，某些臂已被证明明显很差，但系统仍把 10% 流量继续撒向它们。
scenario_en: A fixed epsilon=0.1 epsilon-greedy is live; after 10M impressions some arms are conclusively bad, yet 10% of traffic still goes to them.
q: 该怎么改，才能让已充分了解的差臂少拿探索流量？
q_en: What change makes conclusively-bad, well-understood arms stop getting exploration traffic?
why: 换成 Thompson Sampling：它按后验不确定性分配探索，那些已被 1000 万次曝光「盖章」很差的臂后验很窄、几乎不再被抽中，探索自然收敛到还不确定的臂。fixed ε 做不到这点，因为它是均匀探索。
why_en: Switch to Thompson Sampling — it allocates exploration by posterior uncertainty, so arms proven bad over 10M impressions have narrow posteriors and are almost never sampled, unlike uniform fixed-epsilon.
tradeoff: Thompson(探索按不确定性收敛) vs fixed ε(永远均匀撒 10%)
whenOtherWins: 若你必须保留一个固定、可预测的探索比例（例如合规要求每个臂都持续有最低曝光做审计），fixed ε 的可控性反而是优点。
options: 把 ε 从 0.1 提到 0.2，加大探索让系统更快看清差臂
换成 Thompson Sampling：探索随后验不确定性自动收敛
保持 fixed ε，但把差臂的奖励人工置零，强行不让它们被选
改成纯 exploitation，彻底关闭探索，只服务当前最高估计 CTR
options_en: Raise epsilon from 0.1 to 0.2 to explore harder and see the bad arms sooner.
Switch to Thompson Sampling: exploration auto-converges by posterior uncertainty.
Keep fixed epsilon but manually zero out bad arms' rewards to force them unpicked.
Go pure exploitation, turning off exploration entirely and serving only the top estimated CTR.
optionExplanations: 调大 ε 只会把更多流量往差臂上撒，方向完全相反。
对；这正是课后测验的答案——TS 天然减少已了解臂的探索，把预算让给不确定臂。
人工置零是硬编码补丁，脆弱且需持续维护，没解决均匀探索的根本问题。
关掉探索会重回反馈闭环、埋没潜在更好的新臂，属于矫枉过正。
optionExplanations_en: Raising epsilon just pours more traffic onto the bad arms — the opposite direction.
Correct — this is the quiz answer: TS naturally cuts exploration on well-understood arms and reallocates to uncertain ones.
Manually zeroing is a brittle hard-coded patch needing constant upkeep and doesn't fix uniform exploration.
Turning off exploration re-triggers the feedback loop and buries potentially better new arms — an overcorrection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次把某物品展示给用户的机会，是 bandit 里一次「拉臂」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one chance to show an item to a user — one 'arm pull' in bandit terms.

scenario: 同一个缩略图对学生和退休老人都展示同一个「最优」封面，其实两类人偏好差很多，奖励被浪费。
scenario_en: The same 'best' thumbnail is shown to a student and a retiree, but their preferences differ a lot, so reward is wasted.
q: 上下文 bandit(contextual bandit) 相比 context-free bandit 变了什么？
q_en: What does a contextual bandit change compared to a context-free bandit?
why: context-free bandit 给所有人同一个最优臂；contextual bandit 条件于上下文向量 x，学「上下文→臂」的策略(policy)，为不同人选不同臂。
why_en: A context-free bandit picks one best arm for everyone, while a contextual bandit conditions on a context vector x and learns a policy mapping contexts to arms, maximizing E[reward | x, a].
diagram:
flowchart LR
  X["上下文 x(画像/会话/设备/时间)"] --> P["策略 policy"]
  P --> A["选 argmax E[reward|x,a] 的臂"]
  A --> R["观察奖励，更新策略"]
  R --> P
options: 它给所有用户选同一个全局最优臂，只是把估计刷新得更频繁
以上下文向量 x 为条件，学「上下文→臂」的策略
它放弃奖励最大化，改为纯随机展示以收集无偏数据
它把 K 个臂合并成一个，用一个回归模型直接预测点击
options_en: It picks one global best arm for all users, just refreshing the estimate more often.
It conditions on a context vector x and learns a context-to-arm policy.
It abandons reward maximization and shows arms purely at random to collect unbiased data.
It merges the K arms into one and uses a single regression to predict clicks directly.
optionExplanations: 这仍是 context-free 的思路（一个最优臂），没有引入个性化。
对；核心是条件化于 x、学一个策略函数，Meta 用它选内容格式、Netflix 选每人封面。
纯随机只是收集无偏数据的极端手段，不是这套算法的定义。
合并臂+单回归丢掉了「每个臂在不同上下文下的收益」这一核心结构。
optionExplanations_en: That's still the context-free idea (one best arm) with no personalization.
Correct — the essence is conditioning on x and learning a policy; Meta uses it for content format, Netflix for per-user artwork.
Pure random is just an extreme data-collection tactic, not what defines this algorithm.
Merging arms plus one regression discards the core structure of each arm's payoff under different contexts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以上下文 x 为条件选臂、学习「上下文→臂」策略的 bandit，用于个性化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contextual bandit conditions on context x and learns a context-to-arm policy, used for personalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从上下文映射到动作(臂)的函数，contextual bandit 学的就是它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A policy is a function mapping contexts to actions (arms), which is exactly what a contextual bandit learns.

scenario: Netflix 想给每位用户挑最能打动他的剧集封面；同一部剧对不同人该展示不同封面艺术图。
scenario_en: Netflix wants to pick the most compelling artwork per user; the same title should show different art to different people.
q: 该用 context-free 还是 contextual bandit？为什么？
q_en: Should you use a context-free or contextual bandit, and why?
why: 用 contextual bandit：不同用户对封面的偏好差异大，条件于上下文 x 才能为每个人选不同封面、把奖励对齐到个体偏好。context-free 只会给所有人一个「平均最优」封面，浪费掉个性化收益。
why_en: Use a contextual bandit — preferences for artwork vary a lot across users, so conditioning on context x lets you pick per-user art instead of one 'average-best' cover for everyone.
tradeoff: contextual(个性化、需上下文特征与更多数据) vs context-free(简单、但一刀切浪费个体收益)
whenOtherWins: 若手上根本没有有区分度的上下文特征，或流量太小学不动 per-context 策略，退回 context-free 的单一最优臂反而更稳。
options: context-free bandit：给全站选一个点击率最高的封面，简单又省数据
contextual bandit：条件于用户上下文，为不同人选不同封面，对齐个体偏好
纯 exploitation：直接上线历史点击最高的封面，不再探索
A/B 测试：把两张封面各分一半流量，选整体胜出的那张固定给所有人
options_en: Context-free bandit: pick one highest-CTR cover site-wide — simple and data-thrifty.
Contextual bandit: condition on user context to pick different covers for different people, aligning to individual preference.
Pure exploitation: ship the historically top-CTR cover and stop exploring.
A/B test: split traffic 50/50 across two covers and fix the overall winner for everyone.
optionExplanations: 全站单封面正是要避免的一刀切，丢掉了不同人群的偏好差异。
对；封面偏好高度个性化，条件于 x 的策略能把对的封面送给对的人。
纯 exploitation 无探索，且仍是一刀切，双重不满足个性化诉求。
静态 A/B 只能选出一个全局赢家，无法做到 per-user 个性化封面。
optionExplanations_en: One site-wide cover is exactly the one-size-fits-all to avoid, discarding across-segment preference differences.
Correct — artwork preference is highly personal, and a policy conditioned on x sends the right cover to the right person.
Pure exploitation has no exploration and is still one-size-fits-all — doubly failing personalization.
A static A/B can only pick one global winner, not per-user personalized artwork.

termDefinitions.term: context vector x / 上下文向量
termDefinitions.meaning: 描述当前请求的特征（画像、会话历史、设备、时间），contextual bandit 据此选臂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context vector x holds features of the current request (profile, session, device, time) that the contextual bandit conditions on.

scenario: 你想用「旧策略在线上收集的历史日志」离线评估一个新 contextual bandit 策略，但日志里每条数据都是旧策略按自己的概率选出来的。
scenario_en: You want to offline-evaluate a new contextual-bandit policy using historical logs collected by the old policy, but each log entry was chosen by the old policy's own probabilities.
q: logging policy 与 target policy 不匹配会带来什么问题？怎么纠正？
q_en: What problem does the logging-vs-target policy mismatch cause, and how do you correct it?
why: 历史日志由 logging policy 按自己的概率采样，直接评 target policy 会有选择偏差。用逆倾向加权(IPS)按 1/旧策略选该动作的概率 重加权纠偏。
why_en: Logs are biased by the logging policy's own action probabilities, so evaluating a target policy on them is biased; inverse propensity scoring (IPS) reweights each sample by 1/(logging-policy probability) to correct it.
options: 没有问题：只要日志量足够大，历史数据就能无偏地评估任何新策略
会有选择偏差：新策略在旧策略偏好的动作上被高估；用 IPS 逆倾向加权纠偏
只会让评估方差变大，用更多 epoch 重复训练即可消除，与倾向无关
会让新策略无法计算梯度，必须先把 contextual bandit 退化成 context-free
options_en: No problem: with enough logs, historical data unbiasedly evaluates any new policy.
Selection bias: the target policy is over-credited on actions the old policy favored; correct it with IPS reweighting.
It only inflates evaluation variance, removable by more training epochs, unrelated to propensity.
It makes the new policy's gradient uncomputable, forcing a downgrade to context-free.
optionExplanations: 数据量再大也消不掉系统性的选择偏差，偏差不是方差、不会随样本自动归零。
对；off-policy 评估的核心风险是偏差，IPS 用 1/倾向重加权还原到 target policy 下的期望。
问题是偏差不是方差，多跑 epoch 无济于事；必须显式做倾向纠正。
梯度照样能算，退化成 context-free 反而丢掉个性化，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: More data can't remove systematic selection bias; bias isn't variance and won't vanish with samples.
Correct — off-policy evaluation's core risk is bias, and IPS reweights by 1/propensity to recover the target policy's expectation.
The issue is bias not variance; more epochs won't help — you must explicitly correct propensity.
Gradients are still computable; downgrading to context-free just discards personalization — beside the point.

termDefinitions.meaning: logging policy 是收集日志的旧策略；target policy 是待评估的新策略，二者动作分布不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The logging policy collected the logs; the target policy is the new one being evaluated — their action distributions differ.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逆倾向加权：按 1/(旧策略选该动作的概率) 给样本重加权，纠正 off-policy 评估的选择偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IPS (Inverse Propensity Scoring) reweights samples by 1/(logging-policy action probability) to debias off-policy evaluation.

scenario: 用旧策略的历史日志评估新策略前，先想清楚该纠正什么。
scenario_en: Before evaluating a new policy on the old policy's logs, be clear about what to correct.
q: 补全 off-policy 评估的纠偏要点：
q_en: Complete the key points of off-policy evaluation:
text: off-policy 评估里，收集数据的是 {{logging}} policy、待评估的是 {{target}} policy；二者不匹配会引入偏差，用 {{IPS}}（逆倾向加权）按 1/旧策略概率重加权来纠正。
text_en: In off-policy evaluation, data comes from the {{logging}} policy and you're assessing the {{target}} policy; the mismatch adds bias, corrected by {{IPS}} reweighting by 1/(old-policy probability).
why: 不做 IPS，策略在旧策略偏好的动作上看起来很好，一上线就露馅。IPS 把被旧策略压制的动作按概率倒数放大回来，还原新策略在真实分布下的期望表现。
why_en: Without IPS a policy looks good on the old policy's favored actions but fails live; IPS upweights suppressed actions to recover the target policy's true expected performance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个策略收集的数据去评估另一个策略的表现，需纠正两者的动作分布差异。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Off-policy evaluation assesses one policy using data collected by another, requiring correction for their differing action distributions.

termDefinitions.meaning: logging policy 在该上下文下选中被记录动作的概率，是 IPS 加权的分母。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propensity is the logging policy's probability of choosing the logged action in that context — the denominator in IPS.

scenario: 面试官问：什么时候用 bandit 就够、什么时候要上真正的强化学习(RL)？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: when is a bandit enough, and when do you need full reinforcement learning (RL)?
q: bandit 与 full RL 的本质区别是哪一条？
q_en: What is the essential distinction between a bandit and full RL?
why: bandit 是单步：这次的动作不改变下一次决策所处的环境状态。RL 是序贯：动作会改变状态、影响未来的决策与回报。判据就是「动作有没有实质改变下一步的状态」。
why_en: A bandit is single-step — the action doesn't change the state for the next decision — while RL is sequential, where actions change state and affect future decisions and rewards.
tradeoff: bandit(单步、无状态转移、简单) vs RL(序贯、有状态转移、能规划但复杂)
diagram:
flowchart TB
  subgraph Bandit["bandit：单步"]
    B1["状态"] --> B2["动作"] --> B3["奖励"]
  end
  subgraph RL["RL：序贯"]
    R1["状态 s"] --> R2["动作"] --> R3["奖励 + 新状态 s'"]
    R3 --> R1
  end
options: bandit 只能处理二元点击/不点击奖励，RL 才能处理连续数值奖励和累积回报
bandit 单步、动作不改变下一步状态；RL 序贯、动作改变状态并影响未来决策
bandit 一定要用贝叶斯后验方法求解，RL 一定要用策略梯度方法，二者数学工具完全互斥
bandit 训练需要人工标注的监督数据，RL 完全不需要环境给出的任何奖励反馈信号
options_en: Bandits can only handle binary click/no-click rewards; only RL handles continuous-valued rewards and cumulative return.
A bandit is single-step and the action doesn't change the next state; RL is sequential and actions change state, affecting future decisions.
Bandits must be solved with Bayesian posterior methods and RL must use policy gradients; their math toolkits are completely mutually exclusive.
Bandit training needs human-labeled supervised data; RL needs no reward feedback signal from the environment at all.
optionExplanations: 奖励是连续还是二元与 bandit/RL 之分无关，两者都能处理各种奖励类型。
对；单步 vs 序贯、有无状态转移，才是区分 bandit 与 RL 的关键。
工具不互斥：bandit 有非贝叶斯变体，RL 也有价值/贝叶斯方法，这条把手段当本质。
RL 恰恰要靠 reward 信号学习，说它「不需要反馈」完全错误。
optionExplanations_en: Continuous vs binary reward is unrelated to the bandit/RL split; both handle various reward types.
Correct — single-step vs sequential, i.e. whether actions cause state transitions, is what separates bandits from RL.
The toolkits aren't exclusive: bandits have non-Bayesian variants and RL has value/Bayesian methods — this confuses means with essence.
RL learns precisely from reward signals; saying it needs no feedback is flatly wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强化学习：序贯决策，动作改变状态、影响未来回报，目标是最大化长期累积回报。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RL (Reinforcement Learning) is sequential decision-making where actions change state and future rewards, maximizing long-term return.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动作导致环境从一个状态变到下一个状态；bandit 无此，RL 的核心就在此。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state transition is the action moving the environment from one state to the next; bandits lack it, RL centers on it.

scenario: 两个任务：A. 广告创意选择——展示一条广告不会改变下一场竞拍的状态；B. 对话代理——每句回复都改变对话状态、影响后续走向。
scenario_en: Two tasks: A. ad-creative selection — showing an ad doesn't change the next auction's state; B. a dialogue agent — each reply changes conversation state and its future.
q: 这两个任务分别该用 bandit 还是 RL？判据是什么？
q_en: For these two tasks, bandit or RL, and by what criterion?
why: 判据：动作是否实质改变下一步的状态。广告创意选择不改变下场竞拍状态→bandit 就够；对话每句回复都改变对话状态、影响后续→需要 RL。Google 也是这么分工的（芯片布局/数据中心冷却用 RL，广告创意选择用 bandit）。
why_en: Criterion: does the action meaningfully change the next state? Ad selection doesn't change the next auction → bandit; a dialogue reply changes conversation state → RL.
tradeoff: bandit(无状态转移任务、简单可靠) vs RL(真有状态转移时才值得的复杂度)
whenOtherWins: 若广告投放要考虑「频次控制/长期用户疲劳」这类跨请求的状态累积，广告选择也会带上序贯性，这时 RL 或带状态的方法才更合适。
options: A 用 RL、B 用 bandit：对话是短交互所以更简单，广告要长期优化所以更复杂
两个都用 bandit：只要奖励是点击类信号，就不需要状态概念
A 用 bandit、B 用 RL：广告不改变下场竞拍状态，对话每句改变会话状态
两个都用 RL：任何在线决策都应按序贯问题建模才最优
options_en: A with RL, B with bandit: dialogue is short so simpler, ads need long-term optimization so more complex.
Both bandits: as long as the reward is a click-type signal, no state concept is needed.
A with bandit, B with RL: ads don't change the next auction's state, while each dialogue turn changes conversation state.
Both RL: any online decision is optimal only when modeled as a sequential problem.
optionExplanations: 判据用反了：对话才有状态转移该用 RL，广告选择无状态转移用 bandit。
有没有状态转移才是判据，不是奖励类型；对话明显有状态、不能当 bandit。
对；紧扣「动作是否改变下一步状态」这条启发式，正是 Google 的实际分工。
无状态转移的任务上 RL 是过度工程，徒增复杂度而无收益。
optionExplanations_en: The criterion is inverted: dialogue has state transitions (RL), ad selection has none (bandit).
The criterion is state transitions, not reward type; dialogue clearly has state and can't be a bandit.
Correct — it hinges on 'does the action change the next state', exactly Google's real split.
RL on a no-state-transition task is over-engineering, adding complexity with no gain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单步决策各自独立、互不影响状态；序贯决策前一步的动作会改变后续状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-step decisions are independent and don't affect state; sequential decisions have earlier actions change later states.

scenario: 面试里为一个简单的广告/排序信号选择问题，直接祭出 MDP、策略梯度、Q-learning 这套完整 RL 方案。
scenario_en: In an interview you propose a full RL stack (MDP, policy gradients, Q-learning) for a simple ad/ranking selection signal.
q: 对这种无状态转移的选择问题上 full RL，主要风险是什么？该怎么办？
q_en: For a no-state-transition selection problem, what's the main risk of full RL, and what should you do?
why: 这是 over-engineering：动作不改变状态，序贯建模的复杂度、样本需求与训练不稳定都白付。正解是用 bandit，把 RL 留给真有状态转移的场景。
why_en: It's over-engineering — with no state transitions, RL's added complexity, sample hunger, and training instability buy nothing; use a bandit and reserve RL for genuine state transitions.
tradeoff: full RL(能建模状态但复杂、样本贵、难稳) vs bandit(单步问题上更简单可靠)
options: 没有风险，RL 是更通用的框架，用它建模简单问题只会更保险
唯一风险是算力略高，把 batch size 调小就能抵消，方案本身没问题
属于 over-engineering：无状态转移下 RL 是白付成本
风险是 RL 收敛太快导致欠探索，应把折扣因子 γ 设为 1 来补偿
options_en: No risk — RL is more general, so modeling a simple problem with it is only safer.
The only risk is slightly higher compute, offset by a smaller batch size; the approach is otherwise fine.
It's over-engineering: without state transitions, RL's cost buys nothing.
The risk is RL converging too fast into under-exploration, fixed by setting the discount factor gamma to 1.
optionExplanations: 「更通用」不等于「更合适」，用重武器打简单问题徒增失败面。
问题不是算力，而是序贯建模在无状态转移场景本就多余，调 batch 无关痛痒。
对；判据是有无状态转移，没有就别上 RL，bandit 更简单可靠。
把 γ 设为 1 是 RL 内部参数把戏，回避不了「这问题根本不需要 RL」的事实。
optionExplanations_en: 'More general' isn't 'more appropriate'; a heavy tool on a simple problem just enlarges the failure surface.
The issue isn't compute; sequential modeling is superfluous without state transitions, and batch size is irrelevant.
Correct — the criterion is state transitions; absent them, skip RL and use a simpler, more reliable bandit.
Setting gamma to 1 is an internal RL knob that dodges the fact that this problem needs no RL at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用远超问题需要的复杂方案，带来无谓的成本、脆弱性和维护负担。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-engineering applies a solution far more complex than the problem needs, adding cost, fragility, and maintenance burden.

termDefinitions.meaning: 马尔可夫决策过程：用状态、动作、转移、奖励刻画序贯决策，是 RL 的标准框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MDP (Markov Decision Process) frames sequential decisions with states, actions, transitions, and rewards — RL's standard formalism.

scenario: 工程师给 epsilon-greedy 设 ε=0.1，问这个 0.1 到底控制什么、通常取多少。
scenario_en: An engineer sets epsilon=0.1 for epsilon-greedy; what does 0.1 control and what's the usual range?
q: epsilon-greedy 里的 ε 控制什么？典型取值是多少？调它意味着什么？
q_en: What does epsilon control in epsilon-greedy, its typical value, and what does tuning it mean?
why: ε = 每次决策做随机探索的概率，典型 0.05–0.1（即 5%–10% 流量交探索税），是经验设定而非公式推导；固定 ε → linear regret，衰减 ε 才能 sublinear。
why_en: Epsilon is the per-decision probability of random exploration, typically 0.05–0.1 (5–10% of traffic), an empirical knob that trades exploration against short-term exploitation and, if fixed, yields linear regret.
options: ε 是优化器的学习率，控制每步梯度更新的步长，典型 0.001 左右，与探索无关
ε 是随机探索概率，典型 0.05–0.1；固定 ε → linear regret
ε 是置信区间宽度，随拉动次数自动收缩，越拉越窄，无需人工设定
ε 是折扣因子，控制未来奖励在回报里的权重，典型取 0.9–0.99
options_en: Epsilon is the optimizer's learning rate controlling gradient step size, typically about 0.001, unrelated to exploration.
Epsilon is the random-exploration probability, typically 0.05–0.1; a fixed epsilon gives linear regret.
Epsilon is a confidence-interval width that auto-shrinks with pull count, narrowing as you pull, needing no tuning.
Epsilon is the discount factor weighting future rewards in the return, typically 0.9–0.99.
optionExplanations: 学习率是优化器的参数，不是 epsilon-greedy 的探索概率，混淆了概念。
对；ε 就是那 5%–10% 拿去随机探索的流量占比，越大短期利用收益越低。
自动收缩的置信项是 UCB 的 bonus；ε 由人工设定，不会自己缩。
折扣因子 γ 是 RL 里权衡未来奖励的参数，与 ε 无关。
optionExplanations_en: The learning rate is an optimizer parameter, not epsilon-greedy's exploration probability — a concept mix-up.
Correct — epsilon is the 5–10% of traffic spent on random exploration; the larger it is, the lower your short-term payoff.
An auto-shrinking confidence term is UCB's bonus; epsilon is set by hand and never shrinks itself.
The discount factor gamma weighs future rewards in RL and is unrelated to epsilon.

termDefinitions.meaning: epsilon-greedy 中每次做随机探索的概率，典型 0.05–0.1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon is the per-decision probability of random exploration in epsilon-greedy, typically 0.05–0.1.

scenario: 把 context-free bandit 升级成 contextual bandit 上线做个性化，需要额外准备哪些东西。
scenario_en: Upgrading a context-free bandit to a contextual bandit for personalization — what must you additionally prepare?
q: 落地 contextual bandit 相比 context-free 需要额外考虑哪些？(多选)
q_en: What extra concerns does a contextual bandit add over context-free? (multiple)
why: contextual bandit 额外要两样：把上下文映射到各臂奖励的函数逼近器，以及 off-policy 评估时用 IPS 纠正 logging/target 不匹配的偏差。
why_en: A contextual bandit needs a function approximator mapping context to reward and IPS to debias off-policy evaluation, unlike hardware count or GPU price which are irrelevant.
options: 一个函数逼近器（线性模型或小神经网）把上下文映射到各臂的期望奖励
off-policy 评估要用 IPS 纠正 logging policy 与 target policy 的不匹配
有区分度的上下文特征（画像、会话、设备、时间）以及足够的数据学 per-context 策略
把服务器机箱数量翻倍，否则 contextual bandit 无法运行
options_en: A function approximator (linear model or small neural net) mapping context to each arm's expected reward.
IPS during off-policy evaluation to correct the logging-vs-target policy mismatch.
Discriminative context features (profile, session, device, time) and enough data to learn a per-context policy.
Doubling the number of server chassis, without which a contextual bandit cannot run.
optionExplanations: 对；从「单一最优臂」变成「上下文→臂」，必须有函数逼近器来学这个映射。
对；用历史日志评新策略必然遇到 off-policy 偏差，IPS 是标准纠偏手段。
对；没有区分度的特征或数据不足，per-context 策略学不动，退化成 context-free。
错；机箱数量是产能问题，与「是否个性化决策」这一算法诉求无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — moving from one best arm to a context-to-arm map requires a function approximator to learn it.
Correct — evaluating a new policy on old logs inevitably hits off-policy bias, and IPS is the standard fix.
Correct — without discriminative features or enough data, a per-context policy can't be learned and collapses to context-free.
Wrong — chassis count is a capacity matter, unrelated to the algorithmic need for personalized decisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用线性模型或小神经网从上下文预测各臂期望奖励，是 contextual bandit 的核心组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Function approximation uses a linear model or small neural net to predict each arm's expected reward from context — the core of a contextual bandit.

scenario: 团队现在用「静态 A/B 测试」决定上线哪个排序模型，但内容更新快、想在服务路径里持续自适应地做探索。
scenario_en: The team uses static A/B tests to pick a ranking model, but content churns fast and they want continuous adaptive exploration in the serving path.
q: 为什么大厂（Meta/Google/Netflix）把持续自适应探索烘进服务路径，而不只靠静态 A/B？
q_en: Why do big platforms bake continuous adaptive exploration into serving rather than rely on static A/B alone?
why: 静态 A/B 是「先固定分流跑几周、再选赢家」的离散、慢反馈机制，追不上快速变化的内容与偏好。把 bandit 类自适应探索放进服务路径，能边服务边学、把流量实时挪向更优选项，持续压低 regret。
why_en: Static A/B is a slow, discrete 'fix the split, wait weeks, pick a winner' loop that can't keep up with fast-changing content, while adaptive bandits learn while serving and shift traffic in real time.
tradeoff: 自适应探索(边服务边学、实时挪流量) vs 静态 A/B(干净因果、但慢且离散)
whenOtherWins: 当你要的是「对某一次改动的干净、可报告的因果效应量」（含 guardrail 与显著性），静态 A/B 的固定分流反而更合适——bandit 的动态分配会让 end-of-experiment p 值失效。
options: 因为静态 A/B 在数学上永远得不到显著结果，只有 bandit 能算 p 值
因为自适应探索能边服务边学、实时把流量挪向更优项，追得上快变内容
因为 bandit 完全不需要任何离线评估，能省掉整个实验体系
因为静态 A/B 会违反用户隐私，法务要求必须用 bandit 替代
options_en: Because static A/B can mathematically never reach significance, and only bandits can compute p-values.
Because adaptive exploration learns while serving and shifts traffic to better options in real time, keeping up with fast-changing content.
Because bandits need no offline evaluation at all, letting you drop the whole experimentation stack.
Because static A/B violates user privacy, and legal requires replacing it with bandits.
optionExplanations: 静态 A/B 恰恰是算显著性的经典工具，说它得不到显著结果完全错。
对；服务路径里的自适应探索能持续学习、实时调流量，正是大厂的做法。
bandit 也要评估与监控，且离线门槛仍不可少，不能一句省掉。
隐私不是这里的区分点，理由牵强附会。
optionExplanations_en: Static A/B is the classic tool for computing significance; saying it can't reach significance is plainly wrong.
Correct — adaptive exploration in serving keeps learning and reallocates traffic live, exactly what big platforms do.
Bandits also need evaluation and monitoring, and the offline gate remains essential — you can't just drop it.
Privacy isn't the distinguishing factor here; the reason is a stretch.

termDefinitions.term: static A/B test / 静态 A/B
termDefinitions.meaning: 固定分流比例跑固定时长再比较的实验，反馈慢、分配不随中途结果调整。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A static A/B test fixes the split and duration then compares — slow feedback, no mid-flight reallocation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在服务路径上边学边把流量挪向更优选项的探索机制，如 bandit。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adaptive exploration learns online in the serving path and shifts traffic toward better options, as bandits do.

scenario: 面试官让你把 epsilon-greedy、UCB、Thompson Sampling 三个 bandit 放在一张表里比较。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson Sampling side by side.
q: 三种 bandit 在「探索机制 / 每步成本 / 非平稳适应」上分别是什么样？
q_en: How do the three bandits compare on exploration mechanism, per-step cost, and non-stationarity?
why: epsilon-greedy 固定概率均匀随机、O(1)、非平稳差；UCB 确定性置信奖励、O(1)、需加窗口；Thompson 后验采样按不确定性分配、O(K)、优雅适应非平稳。
why_en: Epsilon-greedy uses uniform random O(1) exploration and is poor under drift; UCB uses a deterministic O(1) bonus but assumes stationarity; Thompson uses O(K) posterior sampling scaled by uncertainty and adapts gracefully.
tradeoff: 简单/低成本(epsilon、UCB, O(1)) vs 自适应/样本省(Thompson, O(K))
options: 三者探索机制完全相同，只是 regret 常数不同，实践中可随意互换替代
ε 均匀随机、UCB 确定性 bonus、Thompson 后验采样
epsilon 和 UCB 都是贝叶斯采样，只有 Thompson 是确定性打分
三者都要 O(K) 后验更新，每步成本完全一致，区别只在是否可解释
options_en: Their exploration mechanisms are completely identical, differing only in regret constants, so they are freely interchangeable.
Epsilon is uniform random, UCB a deterministic bonus, Thompson posterior sampling.
Epsilon and UCB are both Bayesian sampling; only Thompson uses deterministic scoring.
All three need O(K) posterior updates with exactly equal per-step cost, differing only in interpretability.
optionExplanations: 机制并不相同：均匀随机、确定性 bonus、后验采样是三种本质不同的探索方式。
对；这张表就是它们的核心分工，选型时按成本、可解释性、非平稳需求取舍。
说反了：epsilon 是随机、UCB 才是确定性；贝叶斯采样是 Thompson 的专属。
只有 Thompson 是 O(K) 后验更新，epsilon 与 UCB 都是 O(1)，成本并不一致。
optionExplanations_en: The mechanisms differ: uniform random, deterministic bonus, and posterior sampling are three fundamentally different exploration styles.
Correct — this table is their core division of labor; choose by cost, interpretability, and non-stationarity needs.
Backwards: epsilon is random and UCB is deterministic; Bayesian sampling is Thompson's alone.
Only Thompson is O(K) posterior updates; epsilon and UCB are O(1), so costs are not equal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贝叶斯 bandit，为每臂维护后验、抽样选臂，探索量正比于不确定性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson Sampling is a Bayesian bandit that samples from per-arm posteriors so exploration scales with uncertainty.

scenario: 比较三种 bandit 的累积 regret 增长阶（T = 决策次数/时间步）。
scenario_en: Compare the cumulative-regret growth order of the three bandits (T = number of decisions/timesteps).
q: UCB 与 Thompson Sampling 的 regret 阶是多少？固定 ε 的 epsilon-greedy 又是多少？意味着什么？
q_en: What is the regret order of UCB and Thompson Sampling versus fixed-epsilon epsilon-greedy, and what does it imply?
why: UCB 与 Thompson 都是 O(√(T log T))（sublinear），regret/T→0 越跑越接近最优；固定 ε 是 O(T) linear，按固定比例永远亏。
why_en: UCB and Thompson both reach O(sqrt(T log T)) — sublinear, so regret/T goes to zero — while fixed-epsilon is O(T), losing a fixed fraction forever without converging.
options: 三者都是 O(T) linear regret，差别只在常数因子大小
UCB/Thompson 是 O(log T)、固定 ε 是 O(√T)，都属 sublinear
UCB/Thompson 是 O(√(T log T))；固定 ε 是 O(T)
固定 ε 最优达 O(√T)，UCB/Thompson 反而是 O(T)，因为采样噪声大
options_en: All three are O(T) linear regret, differing only in the constant factor.
UCB/Thompson are O(log T) and fixed epsilon is O(sqrt T), both sublinear.
UCB/Thompson reach O(sqrt(T log T)); fixed epsilon stays at O(T).
Fixed epsilon is best at O(sqrt T), while UCB/Thompson are O(T) due to sampling noise.
optionExplanations: 固定 ε 才是 linear，UCB/Thompson 是 sublinear，三者并不同阶。
阶数写错：UCB/Thompson 不是 O(log T)，固定 ε 也不是 √T 而是 linear。
对；sublinear vs linear 的分野决定了长期性能，固定 ε 的均匀探索税不会摊薄。
完全颠倒：采样的 Thompson 反而 regret 更优，固定 ε 才是 linear。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed epsilon is the linear one; UCB/Thompson are sublinear, so the three are not the same order.
Wrong orders: UCB/Thompson are not O(log T), and fixed epsilon is not sqrt(T) but linear.
Correct — the sublinear-vs-linear split decides long-run performance; fixed epsilon's uniform tax never amortizes.
Fully inverted: sampled Thompson has better regret, and fixed epsilon is the linear one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 累积 regret 随 T 的增长速度（O(T)、O(√T) 等），sublinear 表示平均代价趋 0。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regret order is how cumulative regret grows with T (O(T), O(sqrt T), …); sublinear means the average cost tends to zero.

scenario: 面试里被问「怎么在排序服务里做探索」，你想先给个简单基线再稳稳升级到生产方案。
scenario_en: Asked in an interview how to add exploration to a ranking service, you want to give a simple baseline then upgrade to a production answer.
q: 把「探索算法」这道题的高分作答顺序排好：
q_en: Order the high-scoring way to answer the exploration-algorithm question:
steps: 先提 epsilon-greedy 当最简单的原型基线
主动点出它的均匀探索弱点：对已确定很差的臂和新臂花同样预算、固定 ε 给 linear regret
提出 Thompson Sampling 作为生产升级：探索按不确定性自动缩放、优雅适应非平稳
补一句选型判据：无状态转移用 bandit，真有状态转移才上 RL
why: 高分作答的顺序是「先摆 naive 方案 → 自曝其短 → 给生产升级 → 点边界」：epsilon-greedy 立基线，说透均匀探索/linear regret，再升级 Thompson Sampling。
why_en: Strong answers go baseline → name its flaw → production upgrade → boundary: start epsilon-greedy, flag uniform-exploration/linear regret, upgrade to Thompson Sampling, then bound bandit vs RL by state transitions.

termDefinitions.term: naive baseline first / 先摆后破
termDefinitions.meaning: 面试作答先给简单方案并主动指出其缺陷，再引出更优方案，体现权衡意识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State a simple baseline and its flaw first, then motivate a better option — signaling tradeoff awareness in interviews.

scenario: 面试官问：「你怎么知道这个模型可以上生产了？」
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: 'How would you know this model is ready for production?'
q: 「生产就绪」的标准评估框架是什么？只报一个 held-out 数字或只做 A/B 够吗？
q_en: What's the standard framework for 'production ready'? Is one held-out number or an A/B test alone enough?
why: 生产就绪 = 离线评估（先在历史标注数据上过第一道门）后接在线验证（真实流量上确认），并清楚每一相能测什么、不能测什么。只报一个 held-out 数字或只做 A/B 都不够——面试官期待你不用提示就说全两相。
why_en: Production readiness is offline evaluation followed by online validation, knowing what each phase can and cannot measure; naming only one signals a production-experience gap.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["候选模型"] --> O["离线评估\n历史标注数据"]
  O -->|过门的 2-3 个| A["在线验证\n真实流量 A/B"]
  A --> D["上生产决策"]
options: 只要 held-out 测试集上的单一指标（如 AUC）够高，就算生产就绪
离线评估过第一道门、再用在线验证确认，且清楚每一相的能力边界
只做一次 A/B 测试就够，离线指标是多余步骤可以跳过
先小流量灰度上线观察崩溃率，不崩就算就绪，无需离线也无需 A/B
options_en: As long as one metric (e.g. AUC) on the held-out set is high enough, it's production ready.
Offline evaluation passes the first gate, then online validation confirms it, knowing each phase's limits.
One A/B test is enough; offline metrics are a redundant step you can skip.
Just canary a small % and watch crash rate; if it doesn't crash it's ready, no offline or A/B needed.
optionExplanations: 单一 held-out 数字是 proxy，不能保证线上成功，面试官会认为你缺生产经验。
对；两相评估各司其职——离线快而便宜地过滤，在线昂贵但给 ground truth。
跳过离线意味着 200 个候选要做 200 个 A/B，成本和风险都不可接受。
只看崩溃率测的是稳定性不是质量，缺了两相评估的核心。
optionExplanations_en: A single held-out number is a proxy that can't guarantee live success; the interviewer reads it as a production-experience gap.
Correct — the two phases play distinct roles: offline filters fast and cheap, online gives ground truth at a cost.
Skipping offline means 200 candidates would need 200 A/B tests — an unacceptable cost and risk.
Crash rate measures stability not quality, missing the core of two-phase evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时不参与、专门用于离线评估的历史标注数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A held-out set is historical labeled data excluded from training, used for offline evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分成对照/实验两组比较指标的在线受控实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test is a controlled online experiment splitting users into control/treatment groups to compare metrics.

scenario: 上任何线上流量之前，先在历史标注数据上衡量模型质量——「拿上季度的剧本走一次带妆彩排」。
scenario_en: Before any live traffic, measure quality on historical labeled data — a 'dress rehearsal on last season's script'.
q: 离线评估作为第一道门，核心优势有哪三个？
q_en: As the first gate, what are offline evaluation's three core strengths?
why: 离线评估：(1) 迭代快——分钟到小时，一下午能比几十个候选；(2) 成本低——零用户暴露、无营收/UX 风险；(3) 可复现——数据集确定 → 结果确定。Airbnb/Uber 常隔夜排队跑实验、次日看看板决定投哪些候选。
why_en: Offline evaluation is fast (minutes to hours, dozens of candidates in an afternoon), cheap (zero user exposure), and reproducible (deterministic datasets give deterministic results).
options: 实时反映用户行为演化、能捕获反馈闭环、直接测出营收影响
迭代快（分钟-小时）、成本低（零用户暴露）、可复现（确定数据→确定结果）
能提供 ground truth、覆盖真实时段与会话上下文、天然免疫分布漂移
自动完成 A/B 分流、算好显著性、给出可直接上线的因果结论
options_en: Reflects evolving user behavior in real time, captures feedback loops, and directly measures revenue impact.
Fast (minutes-hours), cheap (zero user exposure), reproducible (deterministic dataset gives deterministic result).
Provides ground truth, covers real time-of-day and session context, and is naturally immune to distribution drift.
Auto-runs the A/B split, computes significance, and yields a ship-ready causal conclusion.
optionExplanations: 这些恰恰是离线评估做不到的——它测不了行为演化和反馈闭环，那是在线的活。
对；快、省、可复现正是它能一下午筛掉几十个坏候选的原因。
ground truth 是在线评估的属性，离线只是 proxy，且会受分布漂移影响。
分流与显著性是在线 A/B 的工作，离线不产生因果上线结论。
optionExplanations_en: Those are exactly what offline can't do — it can't measure behavior evolution or feedback loops; that's online's job.
Correct — fast, cheap, reproducible is why it can filter dozens of bad candidates in an afternoon.
Ground truth is an online property; offline is only a proxy and is affected by distribution drift.
Splitting and significance are online A/B work; offline yields no causal ship decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上线前在历史标注数据上衡量模型质量的第一道门，快而便宜但只是 proxy。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offline evaluation measures quality on historical labeled data before launch — a fast, cheap first gate, but only a proxy.

scenario: 一个模型离线 AUC/NDCG/RMSE 都很漂亮，团队想据此直接判定生产成功。
scenario_en: A model has beautiful offline AUC/NDCG/RMSE, and the team wants to declare production success from that alone.
q: 离线评估的根本局限是什么？这些指标能保证线上成功吗？
q_en: What's offline evaluation's fundamental limit, and do these metrics guarantee live success?
why: 静态快照捕捉不到演化中的用户行为、反馈闭环和特征新鲜度问题；AUC/NDCG/RMSE 是 proxy 不是保证——它们能过滤掉明显差的模型，但确认不了生产成功。这道门只负责「排除坏的」，不负责「确认好的」。
why_en: Static snapshots miss evolving behavior, feedback loops, and feature freshness; AUC/NDCG/RMSE are proxies that filter clearly-bad models but can't confirm production success.
options: 没有根本局限：只要离线 AUC 够高就等于线上成功，可以跳过在线验证直接全量
静态快照测不到行为演化与反馈闭环；指标只是 proxy，能排坏不能保成功
局限只在算得慢，换更大集群把离线跑快就能当 ground truth 用
局限是离线只能测分类不能测排序，补个 NDCG 就没有任何盲区了
options_en: No fundamental limit: if offline AUC is high enough it equals live success, so you can skip online validation and go full traffic.
Static snapshots miss behavior evolution and feedback loops; the metrics are proxies that filter bad but never confirm success.
The only limit is slow compute; a bigger cluster makes offline fast enough to serve as ground truth.
The limit is offline can only test classification not ranking; add NDCG and there's no blind spot left.
optionExplanations: 把 proxy 当保证正是本课要破的误区，离线高不等于线上成功。
对；proxy 只能过滤明显差的模型，确认成功要靠在线 ground truth。
算得快解决不了「静态数据反映不了动态行为」这个本质盲区。
补一个指标补不上「静态快照 vs 动态线上」的结构性差距。
optionExplanations_en: Treating a proxy as a guarantee is exactly the fallacy this lesson breaks; high offline isn't live success.
Correct — proxies only filter clearly-bad models; confirming success needs online ground truth.
Faster compute doesn't fix the intrinsic blind spot that static data can't reflect dynamic behavior.
Adding one metric can't close the structural gap between a static snapshot and dynamic live traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与真实业务目标相关但不等同的可离线计算指标（AUC/NDCG/RMSE），能排坏但不保成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy metric correlates with but isn't the true business goal (AUC/NDCG/RMSE); it filters bad models but can't guarantee success.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，衡量分类器在所有阈值上的区分能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures a classifier's ranking/discrimination across all thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带位置折扣的分级相关性排序指标，靠前的相关结果权重更高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a position-discounted graded-relevance ranking metric.

scenario: 离线评估用的训练特征是批量算好的、可能过时几小时到几天，而线上服务用的是实时特征。
scenario_en: Offline evaluation uses batch-computed training features (hours-days stale) while serving uses real-time features.
q: 补全离线评估捕捉不到的这个偏差的名字与成因：
q_en: Name and complete the gap offline evaluation cannot detect:
text: 批量算的训练特征比实时服务特征陈旧几小时到几天，这个训练与服务特征不一致的缺口叫 {{training-serving skew}}（训练-服务偏差），离线评估{{捕捉不到}}它。
text_en: Batch training features are hours-to-days staler than real-time serving features; this gap is called {{training-serving skew}}, which offline evaluation {{cannot detect}}.
why: 训练时用的是隔夜批量特征，服务时用的是实时特征，两者取值不同 → 模型线上表现偏离离线。因为离线评估只有那份静态训练特征，它看不到这个偏差，只有上线后才暴露。
why_en: Training uses stale batch features while serving uses fresh ones, so live behavior diverges from offline, and offline evaluation — having only the static features — can't see it.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏差
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练用的批量特征与线上服务用的实时特征取值不一致，导致线上表现偏离离线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-serving skew is a mismatch between batch training features and real-time serving features, making live behavior diverge from offline.

scenario: 离线过门后，要在真实流量上确认模型确实改善了业务结果。
scenario_en: After the offline gate, you must confirm on live traffic that the model truly improves business outcomes.
q: 在线评估用哪些手段？它能测到离线测不到的什么？
q_en: What methods does online evaluation use, and what does it capture that offline can't?
why: 在线评估通过受控实验——A/B 测试、interleaving、多臂 bandit——在真实流量上测。它能抓到真实上下文（时段、设备、会话意图、竞争内容、演化中的偏好）和反馈闭环，这是 ground truth。
why_en: Online evaluation runs controlled experiments — A/B tests, interleaving, multi-armed bandits — on live traffic, capturing real context and feedback loops as ground truth.
options: 靠 A/B、interleaving、bandit 在活流量上测，拿到 ground truth
靠在规模大得多、标注更细的历史数据集上重跑离线指标，用增大的样本量换取 ground truth 的可信度
靠单元测试和集成测试验证代码正确性，等价于在线验证
靠人工标注更多历史样本，把 AUC/NDCG 刷得更高来确认线上会成功
options_en: Runs A/B, interleaving, and bandits on live traffic to get ground truth.
Reruns offline metrics on a much larger, more finely labeled historical dataset, trading a bigger sample size for ground-truth credibility.
Uses unit and integration tests to verify code correctness, which is equivalent to online validation.
Labels many more historical samples and pushes AUC/NDCG higher to confirm it will succeed live.
optionExplanations: 对；时段、设备、会话意图这些只有活流量里才有，静态数据集里根本不存在。
再大的历史集也是静态 proxy，反映不了用户此刻的真实反应。
测试验证的是代码不是业务效果，不是在线评估。
刷高离线指标还是离线，产生不了任何线上真实反馈。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — time of day, device, and session intent exist only in live traffic, never in a static dataset.
However large, a historical set is still a static proxy and can't reflect how users react right now.
Tests verify code not business effect, so they aren't online evaluation.
Polishing offline numbers is still offline and yields no real live feedback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在真实流量上用受控实验（A/B、interleaving、bandit）测业务效果，是 ground truth。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Online evaluation uses controlled experiments on live traffic (A/B, interleaving, bandits) to measure business effect — the ground truth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个排序器的结果混成一张列表给同一用户，按点击归属判优的排序评估法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving merges two rankers' results into one list for the same user and attributes clicks to judge which ranker is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出影响用户行为、用户行为又变成后续训练数据的循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop is when model outputs shape user behavior, which then becomes future training data.

scenario: 一个欺诈检测模型离线 AUC 很高，上线后没几天检出率就下滑。
scenario_en: A fraud model has high offline AUC but detection drops within days of launch.
q: 为什么反馈闭环在欺诈/垃圾信息这类对抗性领域最危险？
q_en: Why are feedback loops most dangerous in adversarial domains like fraud/spam?
why: 对抗性领域里有个会主动适应的对手：欺诈者一看到新检测模式就换打法，模型学到的旧模式迅速失效。所以一个离线完美的模型上线后会快速退化——这正是离线评估的静态快照永远看不到的动态。
