why: 用 Precision@5：固定只展示 5 个，关键是这 5 个里有多少相关（精度），而不是「有没有把所有相关都捞进来」（那是 Recall@K，检索阶段的目标）。UI 槽位固定 → 分母固定 → Precision@K 最贴。
why_en: Use Precision@5 — with only 5 fixed slots, what matters is how many of those 5 are relevant (precision), not whether all relevants were captured (Recall@K, the retrieval goal).
tradeoff: Precision@K（固定窗口内的精度、展示阶段） vs Recall@K（整体覆盖率、检索阶段）
whenOtherWins: 若你在检索/候选生成阶段、关心「有没有漏掉相关物品」而非前几名精度，就该用 Recall@K 而非 Precision@K。
options: Recall@5：看是否把所有相关物品都捞进这 5 个
Precision@5：固定 5 个里的相关比例
MRR：只看第一个相关结果出现的位置
log loss：评这 5 个结果的概率校准
options_en: Recall@5: whether all relevant items were captured into these 5 slots.
Precision@5: the relevant fraction among the fixed 5 shown.
MRR: only where the first relevant result appears.
Log loss: score the probability calibration of these 5 results.
optionExplanations: 把所有相关都塞进 5 个既不现实也非目标，覆盖率是检索阶段的事。
对；固定槽位下 Precision@K 直接问「展示的这几个有多少相关」，最贴合。
MRR 只关心第一个，浪费了固定 5 槽的其余信息。
log loss 评概率质量，不衡量固定窗口内的推荐精度。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming all relevants into 5 is neither realistic nor the goal; coverage is retrieval's job.
Correct — with fixed slots, Precision@K directly asks how many shown items are relevant — the best fit.
MRR only cares about the first, wasting the other fixed slots' information.
Log loss assesses probability quality, not recommendation precision in a fixed window.

termDefinitions.meaning: Precision@K = top-K 中相关的比例（展示精度）；Recall@K = 全部相关中被 top-K 覆盖的比例（检索覆盖）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@K is the relevant fraction within top-K (display precision); Recall@K is the fraction of all relevants captured in top-K (retrieval coverage).

scenario: 一个新排序模型离线 NDCG 涨了 2%，团队想据此直接上线。
scenario_en: A new ranker's offline NDCG rose 2%, and the team wants to ship on that alone.
q: 为什么离线指标过关后还必须做 A/B 测试才能上线？
q_en: Why must an A/B test still gate a launch after offline metrics pass?
why: 离线指标只是 proxy：2% 的 NDCG 提升可能不改变用户行为甚至变差。A/B 用真实流量验证「离线增益是否真变成业务 KPI 提升」，是上线前最后一道门。
why_en: Offline metrics are proxies — a 2% NDCG gain may not move behavior or may even degrade it — so an A/B test is the final gate that verifies the offline gain becomes a real business-KPI lift on live traffic.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  O["离线指标(proxy)\nNDCG/AUC/log loss"] --> A["A/B 测试\n真实流量最终门"]
  A -->|KPI 真提升| S["上线"]
  A -->|无提升/退化| R["拒绝"]
options: 不必：离线 NDCG 涨了就代表业务一定提升，可跳过 A/B 直接全量
离线是 proxy，A/B 才用真实流量验证 KPI 真提升
A/B 只是走流程，实际上线决策仍以离线指标为准
A/B 能完全替代离线评估，有它就不必再算离线指标
options_en: No need: an offline NDCG rise means business will surely improve, so skip A/B and roll out fully.
Offline is only a proxy; A/B verifies real KPI lift on live traffic.
A/B is just a formality; launch decisions still go by offline metrics.
A/B fully replaces offline evaluation, so you never need offline metrics.
optionExplanations: 把离线 proxy 当业务保证正是本课要破的误区，2% NDCG 未必转化。
对；A/B 是最终门，验证离线增益是否变成真实 KPI 提升，避免上线翻车。
A/B 不是走过场，它给的是离线给不了的 ground truth。
两相互补而非替代：离线负责海选、A/B 负责终审。
optionExplanations_en: Treating an offline proxy as a business guarantee is the fallacy to break; 2% NDCG may not translate.
Correct — A/B is the final gate verifying the offline gain becomes a real KPI lift, preventing bad launches.
A/B isn't a formality; it provides ground truth offline can't.
They're complementary, not substitutes: offline screens, A/B does final judgment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分成对照/实验组、比较业务指标的在线受控实验，是上线前最终门。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test randomly splits users into control/treatment groups to compare business metrics — the final pre-launch gate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键绩效指标，衡量业务成功的核心数字（CTR、营收/会话、预订率）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is the core business-success number (CTR, revenue/session, booking rate).

scenario: 开始一个 A/B 前，要先写下一个可证伪的假设，而不是「看看新模型好不好」。
scenario_en: Before an A/B, write a falsifiable hypothesis, not 'let's see if the new model is good'.
q: 一个合格的 A/B 假设由哪三部分组成？
q_en: What three parts make a proper A/B hypothesis?
why: 可证伪的假设 = 具体改动 + 预期指标 + 阈值，例如「把 YouTube 推荐的 pointwise 排序器换成 listwise 排序器，会让每次会话平均观看时长提升 ≥1%」。三要素齐全才能事前判定成败、不是事后找说法。
why_en: A falsifiable hypothesis is a concrete change + an expected metric + a threshold, e.g. 'replacing the pointwise ranker with a listwise ranker will raise avg watch time/session by ≥1%'.
options: 改动 + 预期指标 + 阈值（如观看时长 ≥+1%）
一句「新模型应该更好」即可，指标和阈值等上线后再补
预算 + 团队人数 + 截止日期这三件套
模型架构 + 超参数 + 训练数据量的完整记录
options_en: A change + an expected metric + a threshold (e.g. watch time ≥ +1%).
Just "the new model should be better"; add metric and threshold after launch.
Budget + team size + deadline.
A full record of model architecture + hyperparameters + training-data size.
optionExplanations: 对；改动+指标+阈值让假设可证伪、可事前判定成败。
没有指标和阈值就无法证伪，等于事后随便解释，不合格。
预算/人数/日期是项目管理要素，不是实验假设。
架构/超参是实现细节，不构成可证伪的业务假设。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — change + metric + threshold makes the hypothesis falsifiable and decidable in advance.
Without a metric and threshold it can't be falsified — just post-hoc rationalization, unacceptable.
Budget/headcount/dates are project management, not an experiment hypothesis.
Architecture/hyperparameters are implementation details, not a falsifiable business hypothesis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事前写死「改动→预期指标→阈值」，使实验结果能明确判成败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A falsifiable hypothesis fixes change → expected metric → threshold in advance so the result can be clearly judged.

scenario: Airbnb 测一个提升预订的排序改动：主指标是预订率，同时要盯页面加载时间和房东取消率。
scenario_en: Airbnb tests a ranking change to lift bookings: primary metric is booking rate, while watching page-load time and host cancellation rate.
q: primary metric 与 guardrail metric 有什么区别？各起什么作用？
q_en: What's the difference between a primary metric and a guardrail metric, and what does each do?
why: primary metric 是你想推动的直接目标（预订率/CTR/营收per会话）；guardrail metric 是不能被牺牲的底线（延迟、崩溃率、房东取消率），恶化即否决上线。
why_en: The primary metric is the direct target you want to move (booking rate/CTR/revenue), while guardrails are safety constraints that must not degrade — even a primary win is rejected if a guardrail worsens.
tradeoff: primary（推动的目标） vs guardrail（不可牺牲的安全底线）
options: 两者是同一回事，只是不同团队的叫法不同
primary 是要推动的目标；guardrail 是恶化即否决的底线
primary 只能有一个数值、guardrail 必须是文本描述
guardrail 是主指标，primary 只是参考背景
options_en: They are the same thing, just named differently by different teams.
The primary is the target to move; guardrails are floors whose degradation vetoes the launch.
The primary must be a single number and guardrails must be text descriptions.
The guardrail is the main metric; the primary is just background reference.
optionExplanations: 两者角色不同：一个是目标、一个是底线，不能混为一谈。
对；护栏的意义在于「即使主指标赢了，破坏了底线也不上」。
两者都是可量化指标，与「数值 vs 文本」无关。
说反了：primary 才是目标，guardrail 是约束。
optionExplanations_en: They play different roles: one is the goal, one is the floor — not interchangeable.
Correct — a guardrail means 'even if the primary wins, don't ship if the floor is broken'.
Both are quantifiable metrics; this isn't about number vs text.
Backwards: the primary is the goal, the guardrail is the constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实验想直接推动的业务目标（预订率、CTR、营收/会话）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary metric is the business target the experiment aims to move (booking rate, CTR, revenue/session).

termDefinitions.meaning: 不能被牺牲的安全约束（延迟、崩溃率、取消率），恶化即否决上线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a safety constraint (latency, crash rate, cancellation) that must not degrade — degradation vetoes launch.

scenario: 一个新推荐模型把点击率提升了 3%，但把 p99 服务延迟从 200ms 拉到 420ms（翻倍）。
scenario_en: A new rec model lifts CTR by 3% but doubles p99 serving latency from 200ms to 420ms.
q: 主指标（CTR）赢了，这个模型该上线吗？体现了什么设计原则？
q_en: The primary metric (CTR) won — should this model ship, and what principle does it show?
why: 不该上：延迟护栏被破坏（翻倍的 p99 会拖慢体验、可能违反 SLA）。这体现「护栏优先」——即使主指标涨了，只要系统健康或 UX 护栏恶化就否决。护栏就是为了挡住这种「赢了指标输了体验」的改动。
why_en: Don't ship — the latency guardrail is broken (doubled p99 hurts UX and may breach SLA); even a primary win is vetoed when a system-health/UX guardrail degrades.
tradeoff: 上线（+3% CTR） vs 否决（p99 延迟翻倍破坏系统健康护栏）
whenOtherWins: 若这类模型部署在离线批处理、延迟根本不进用户关键路径（如隔夜生成推荐），延迟护栏不再是硬约束，就可能放行。
options: 该上线：主指标 CTR 涨了 3%，延迟不重要
不该上：延迟护栏被破坏，护栏优先——主指标赢也否决
该上线，但把延迟阈值临时改高以让它通过
无法判断，A/B 只看主指标，护栏不参与上线决策
options_en: Ship it: the primary CTR rose 3%, latency doesn't matter.
Don't ship: the latency guardrail is broken; guardrails take priority, so a primary win is vetoed.
Ship it, but temporarily raise the latency threshold to let it pass.
Can't tell — A/B only looks at the primary; guardrails don't affect the launch decision.
optionExplanations: 延迟翻倍会伤体验、可能破 SLA，「延迟不重要」是危险误判。
对；护栏就是为挡这种赢指标输体验的改动，破护栏即否决。
为通过而临时放宽护栏是自欺欺人，等于取消了安全约束。
护栏恰恰是上线决策的一部分，忽略它会放行有害改动。
optionExplanations_en: Doubled latency hurts UX and may breach SLA; 'latency doesn't matter' is a dangerous misjudgment.
Correct — guardrails exist to block metric-wins-UX-loses changes; a broken guardrail vetoes.
Loosening the guardrail to pass is self-deception, effectively removing the safety constraint.
Guardrails are precisely part of the launch decision; ignoring them ships harmful changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求快于此值，衡量尾部延迟；翻倍意味着最慢那批用户体验显著变差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value 99% of requests beat — a tail-latency measure; doubling it markedly worsens the slowest users' experience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议，对延迟/可用性等的承诺阈值，护栏常对齐它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed threshold for latency/availability that guardrails often align to.

scenario: 你要为一个推荐模型 A/B 设计一套护栏指标，体现生产成熟度。
scenario_en: You're designing a guardrail set for a rec-model A/B to signal production maturity.
q: 一套成熟的护栏指标应包含哪些？(多选)
q_en: What should a mature guardrail set include? (multiple)
why: 建议至少 2 个护栏：一个 UX（崩溃率、取消率），一个系统健康（p99 服务延迟），可选再加一个业务护栏（广告营收/会话、司机收入）。多维度护栏才能挡住「主指标赢但从别处偷成本」的改动。护栏数量不是越少越好。
why_en: Define at least two guardrails — one UX (crash/cancellation rate), one system health (p99 latency) — plus optionally a business guardrail (ad revenue/session, driver earnings), to block changes that win the primary by stealing cost elsewhere.
options: 至少一个 UX 护栏，如崩溃率或取消率
至少一个系统健康护栏，如 p99 服务延迟
可选一个业务护栏，如广告营收/会话或司机收入
只保留主指标一个，护栏越少实验越干净
options_en: At least one UX guardrail, e.g. crash rate or cancellation rate.
At least one system-health guardrail, e.g. p99 serving latency.
Optionally one business guardrail, e.g. ad revenue/session or driver earnings.
Keep only the primary metric; fewer guardrails make a cleaner experiment.
optionExplanations: 对；UX 护栏挡住「指标涨但用户体验崩」的改动。
对；系统健康护栏挡住「指标涨但延迟/稳定性恶化」的改动。
对；业务护栏挡住「一个业务线赢但另一个业务线亏」的改动。
错；去掉护栏不是更干净，而是失去对副作用的防护，容易上线有害改动。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a UX guardrail blocks 'metric up but experience collapses' changes.
Correct — a system-health guardrail blocks 'metric up but latency/stability worsens' changes.
Correct — a business guardrail blocks 'one line wins while another loses' changes.
Wrong — dropping guardrails isn't cleaner; it removes side-effect protection and ships harmful changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: UX 护栏盯用户体验（崩溃/取消），系统健康护栏盯基础设施（延迟/错误率）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UX guardrail watches user experience (crash/cancellation); a system-health guardrail watches infrastructure (latency/error rate).

scenario: 实验设计里把统计功效(statistical power)设为 0.80。
scenario_en: The experiment design sets statistical power to 0.80.
q: 统计功效 0.80 是什么意思？它对应哪类错误？
q_en: What does statistical power 0.80 mean, and which error does it govern?
why: power=0.80 表示：若真有效应存在，有 80% 概率检测到它、20% 概率漏掉（Type II 错误/假阴性）。power 是给定的容错目标（不是公式算出来的），越高越不容易漏真效应，但需要更大样本。它约束的是「漏检真效应」的风险。
why_en: Power 0.80 means that if a real effect exists you have an 80% chance to detect it and a 20% chance to miss it (Type II error / false negative); higher power misses fewer real effects but needs more samples.
options: 80% 的实验结果一定正确，与错误类型无关
真效应存在时有 80% 概率检出，20% 漏掉（Type II）
有 80% 概率不犯假阳性，即 Type I 错误率是 20%
样本量正好是总流量的 80%
options_en: 80% of experiment results are certainly correct, regardless of error type.
If a real effect exists, an 80% chance to detect it and 20% to miss it (Type II error).
An 80% chance of avoiding a false positive, i.e. a 20% Type I error rate.
The sample size is exactly 80% of total traffic.
optionExplanations: power 不是「结果一定正确」，它专指检出真效应的能力。
对；power 管假阴性/Type II，0.80 即 20% 漏检风险。
假阳性由显著性 α 管，不是 power；两者是不同错误。
power 是概率目标，不是样本占流量的比例。
optionExplanations_en: Power isn't 'results are certainly correct'; it specifically measures ability to detect a real effect.
Correct — power governs false negatives/Type II; 0.80 means a 20% miss risk.
False positives are governed by significance alpha, not power; different errors.
Power is a probability target, not a fraction of traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真效应存在时检测到它的概率，1−β；越高越不漏真效应，但要更大样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Statistical power is the probability of detecting a real effect when it exists (1−beta); higher misses fewer effects but needs more samples.

termDefinitions.term: Type II error / 第二类错误
termDefinitions.meaning: 真有效应却没检测出来（假阴性），概率为 β=1−power。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Type II error is failing to detect a real effect (false negative), with probability beta = 1 − power.

scenario: 实验里有两种可能出错：把没效应的改动误判成有效，或把真有效应的改动误判成无效。
scenario_en: Two ways an experiment errs: calling a no-effect change effective, or calling a real effect ineffective.
q: 显著性 α 和统计功效各控制哪一类错误？
q_en: Which error does significance alpha control versus statistical power?
why: α 控制 Type I 假阳性（α=0.05 即 5% 误报），power=1−β 控制 Type II 假阴性。降 α 更防误报但更易漏检，两者只能靠加样本一起改善。
why_en: Significance alpha controls Type I error (false positive — calling a no-effect change effective, e.g. 5% at alpha=0.05); power controls Type II error (false negative — missing a real effect).
tradeoff: α↓（少假阳性但多假阴性） vs power↑（少假阴性但需更大样本）
options: α 控制 Type II 假阴性，power 控制 Type I 假阳性
α 管 Type I 假阳性，power 管 Type II 假阴性
α 和 power 都是同一把假阳性阈值，只是取值更严或更松
α 和 power 都与错误类型无关，只是样本量公式里的两个参数
options_en: Alpha controls Type II false negatives, and power controls Type I false positives.
Alpha controls Type I false positives; power controls Type II false negatives.
Alpha and power are the same false-positive threshold, just set stricter or looser.
Alpha and power are unrelated to error types; they're just two parameters in the sample-size formula.
optionExplanations: 对调了：α 管的是假阳性(Type I)，power 管的才是假阴性(Type II)。
对；α→Type I 假阳性、power→Type II 假阴性，是实验设计的两根轴。
两者管的是不同错误，α 管假阳性、power 管假阴性，不是同一把阈值。
它们直接对应两类错误的容忍度，进而决定样本量，不是与错误无关。
optionExplanations_en: Swapped: alpha governs false positives (Type I); power governs false negatives (Type II).
Correct — alpha→Type I false positive, power→Type II false negative, the two axes of experiment design.
They govern different errors — alpha false positives, power false negatives — not the same threshold.
They map directly to the two error tolerances, which then set sample size — not unrelated to error type.

termDefinitions.term: Type I error / 第一类错误
termDefinitions.meaning: 无真效应却判为有效（假阳性），概率为显著性水平 α。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Type I error is declaring an effect when there is none (false positive), with probability equal to significance level alpha.

termDefinitions.term: significance level α / 显著性水平
termDefinitions.meaning: 允许的假阳性概率上限（常 0.05），越小越难判显著。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The significance level alpha is the allowed false-positive probability (often 0.05); smaller makes significance harder to reach.

scenario: 团队争论 MDE 设多少：有人说按统计公式算，有人说 0.1% 的 CTR 提升根本不值得部署。
scenario_en: The team debates the MDE: some say derive it statistically, others say a 0.1% CTR lift isn't worth deploying.
q: 最小可检测效应(MDE)本质上是统计决策还是业务决策？
q_en: Is the minimum detectable effect (MDE) fundamentally a statistical or a business decision?
why: MDE 是业务决策：它是「小到什么程度就不值得部署」的门槛，由改动的收益与部署/维护成本决定，而非统计公式。例如设 MDE=0.5%，因为 0.1% 的 CTR 提升不值得上线的复杂度。定了 MDE 才反过来算样本量。
why_en: MDE is a business decision — the smallest improvement worth deploying, set by benefit-versus-cost, not a statistical formula — e.g. MDE=0.5% because a 0.1% CTR lift isn't worth the deployment complexity.
tradeoff: MDE 小（能测出微小效应但样本量暴涨） vs MDE 大（省样本但漏掉小而真的提升）
options: 统计决策：由显著性公式唯一确定，与业务收益无关
业务决策：小到不值得部署的门槛，据此反算样本量
由日活用户数直接决定，用户越多 MDE 越小
等于观测到的效应量，实验跑完才知道
options_en: A statistical decision: uniquely fixed by the significance formula, unrelated to business value.
A business decision: the not-worth-deploying threshold, which then sets sample size.
Directly set by daily active users; more users means smaller MDE.
Equal to the observed effect size, known only after the experiment finishes.
optionExplanations: MDE 不由统计公式给出，它是你先定的业务门槛、再喂进公式。
对；MDE 是「值不值得部署」的业务判断，决定后才反算样本量。
日活影响样本量与运行时长，不决定 MDE 这个业务门槛。
MDE 是事前设定的目标，不是事后观测到的效应。
optionExplanations_en: MDE isn't given by a statistical formula; it's a business threshold you set first, then feed into the formula.
Correct — MDE is the 'worth deploying?' business call, set first, then sample size is derived.
DAU affects sample size and runtime, not the MDE business threshold.
MDE is a pre-set target, not the post-hoc observed effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最小可检测效应：值得部署的最小改进幅度，是业务门槛而非统计结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect) is the smallest improvement worth deploying — a business threshold, not a statistical output.

scenario: 用功效分析算 A/B 样本量：n ≈ (Z_α/2 + Z_β)² · 2σ² / MDE²。
scenario_en: Compute A/B sample size via power analysis: n ≈ (Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta)² · 2σ² / MDE².
q: 样本量随哪些量怎样变化？公式各项分别代表什么？
q_en: How does sample size scale, and what does each term mean?
why: 样本量 ∝ 1/MDE²：MDE 减半样本量翻四倍；方差 σ² 越大、期望功效越高也越吃样本。它直接决定实验要跑多久、占多少流量。
why_en: Sample size grows as MDE shrinks (n ∝ 1/MDE², so detecting smaller effects explodes samples), as variance σ² rises, and as desired power rises; Z terms come from alpha and power.
options: 样本量随 MDE 增大而增大、随方差减小而增大，方向都相反
随 MDE 缩小（∝1/MDE²）、方差升高、功效升高而增大
样本量只由日活决定，与 MDE 和方差无关
样本量随 MDE 缩小而线性下降，越精细越省样本
options_en: Sample size grows as MDE grows and as variance shrinks — both directions reversed.
It grows as MDE shrinks (∝ 1/MDE²), as variance rises, and as desired power rises.
Sample size is set only by DAU, unrelated to MDE and variance.
Sample size falls linearly as MDE shrinks; finer detection saves samples.
optionExplanations: 方向全错：MDE 越小样本越多、方差越大样本越多。
对；1/MDE² 的平方关系是关键——想测半个效应要四倍样本。
MDE 与方差恰恰是样本量的核心驱动，不能忽略。
反了：MDE 缩小让样本按平方暴涨，不是线性下降。
optionExplanations_en: All directions wrong: smaller MDE needs more samples, larger variance needs more.
Correct — the 1/MDE² square law is key: halving the detectable effect needs 4x samples.
MDE and variance are the core drivers of sample size, not ignorable.
Reversed: shrinking MDE explodes samples quadratically, not a linear drop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 α、power、方差、MDE 反算所需样本量的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Power analysis derives the required sample size from alpha, power, variance, and MDE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标的波动程度，数据越吵需要越大样本才能压过噪声看清效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Variance σ² is the metric's noisiness; noisier data needs larger samples to see the effect over noise.

scenario: 样本量算得每臂 25 万、共 50 万；日活 10 万，原始需要 5 天。
scenario_en: Sample size is 250K/arm (500K total); with 100K users/day the raw need is 5 days.
q: A/B 运行时长怎么算？为什么要向上取整到整周？
q_en: How do you compute A/B runtime, and why round up to full weeks?
why: 运行时长 = 样本量 / 日流量（这里 50 万 / 10 万 = 5 天），再向上取整到整周（跑 7 或 14 天）。取整到整周是因为工作日和周末用户行为不同，跑满整周才能覆盖完整的周内周期、避免只采到工作日样本带来的偏差。
why_en: Runtime = sample size / daily traffic (500K/100K = 5 days), rounded up to full weeks (7 or 14 days) because weekday and weekend behavior differ, so a full week avoids weekday-only sampling bias.
options: 运行时长 = 样本量 × 日流量，取整到整月即可
= 样本量 / 日流量，再向上取整到整周
固定跑 24 小时，流量足够就够了，无需考虑周期
运行到 p 值第一次 <0.05 就停，越快越好
options_en: Runtime = sample size × daily traffic, rounded to full months.
= sample size / daily traffic, rounded up to full weeks.
Fixed at 24 hours; enough traffic suffices, no need for cycles.
Stop the moment p first drops below 0.05 — faster is better.
optionExplanations: 是除以日流量不是乘，取整到整周而非整月。
对；除法得原始天数，整周取整消除工作日/周末的周期偏差。
固定 24 小时会漏掉周内行为周期，采样有偏。
见 p<0.05 就停是 peeking，会抬高假阳性，正是要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: It's divided by daily traffic not multiplied, and rounded to weeks not months.
Correct — division gives raw days, and full-week rounding removes weekday/weekend cyclic bias.
A fixed 24 hours misses the weekly behavior cycle and biases sampling.
Stopping at p<0.05 is peeking, inflating false positives — exactly what to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: A/B 需跑多久 = 所需样本量 ÷ 日流量，取整到整周以覆盖周内周期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Runtime is how long the A/B runs = required sample size ÷ daily traffic, rounded to full weeks for the weekly cycle.

scenario: Instagram Reels 上线首周互动 +5%，到第三周衰减到 +1%。
scenario_en: Instagram Reels shows +5% engagement in week 1, decaying to +1% by week 3.
q: 这是什么效应？会怎样误导 A/B 结论？该怎么缓解？
q_en: What effect is this, how does it mislead A/B conclusions, and how to mitigate?
why: 这是新奇效应：用户只因内容「新」而短暂多互动，早期指标虚高，若此时下结论会高估真实长期效应。缓解：把实验跑 2-4 周，分析时间窗口趋势而非单一聚合值，等新奇消退看稳态水平。
why_en: This is the novelty effect — users engage more just because it's new, inflating early metrics — so decide too early and you overstate the long-term effect; mitigate by running 2-4 weeks and analyzing time-windowed trends.
options: 网络干扰：处理组泄漏到对照组，缓解靠聚类随机化
新奇效应：因内容新而短暂多互动；跑 2-4 周看趋势
peeking：提前偷看结果，缓解靠预先锁定样本量
分布漂移：训练集代表不了线上，缓解靠重训模型
options_en: Network interference: treatment leaks into control; mitigate with cluster randomization.
Novelty effect: users engage more just because it is new; run 2-4 weeks and read the trend.
Peeking: sneaking early looks; mitigate by pre-committing the sample size.
Distribution shift: training set misrepresents live; mitigate by retraining.
optionExplanations: 泄漏是网络干扰，本例是「新鲜感消退」的时间性衰减，不是干扰。
对；新奇效应让早期虚高，跑够 2-4 周、看窗口趋势才见稳态。
peeking 是提前停实验的问题，本例是效应随时间自然衰减。
分布漂移是离线-在线问题，与「新鲜感消退」无关。
optionExplanations_en: Leakage is network interference; this is temporal decay of novelty, not interference.
Correct — novelty inflates early metrics; run 2-4 weeks and read windowed trends to see steady state.
Peeking is stopping early; here the effect naturally decays over time.
Distribution shift is an offline-online issue, unrelated to novelty fading.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户仅因内容新而短暂多互动，使早期在线指标虚高，随时间衰减。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users engaging more just because something is new, inflating early online metrics that then decay.

scenario: Uber 测新的动态定价：处理组触发涨价 → 司机往涨价区聚集 → 对照组骑手的可用车也变了。
scenario_en: Uber tests new surge pricing: treatment triggers surge → drivers reposition to surge areas → available cars for control riders also change.
q: 这里对照组和处理组为什么不独立？属于什么问题？怎么缓解？
q_en: Why aren't control and treatment independent here, what problem is it, and how to mitigate?
why: 这是网络干扰：用户/资源会互相影响，处理效应「泄漏」进对照组（涨价改变司机分布，波及对照骑手），使对照不再是干净基线、偏差方向不可预测。缓解：聚类随机化——按地理/社交簇整块分配，让同一簇内不跨臂互相影响。
why_en: This is network interference — users/resources interact, so the treatment leaks into control (surge reshuffles drivers, affecting control riders), biasing in unpredictable directions; mitigate with cluster-based randomization.
tradeoff: 用户级随机化（简单但共享资源时会泄漏） vs 聚类随机化（整簇同臂、防泄漏但独立单元更少）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  T["处理组涨价"] --> D["司机往涨价区聚集"]
  D --> C["对照组可用车变化"]
  C --> B["对照被污染\n偏差方向不可预测"]
options: 样本量不够导致方差过大看不清效应，缓解靠加大流量、跑更久
网络干扰：处理效应泄漏进对照组，对照不再干净；缓解靠聚类随机化
新奇效应：司机对涨价机制觉得新鲜，效应会随时间衰减，缓解靠跑够 2-4 周
peeking：团队反复偷看中途 p 值，缓解靠预先锁定样本量和分析时点
options_en: Insufficient sample size makes variance too high to see the effect; mitigate by raising traffic and running longer.
Network interference: the treatment leaks into control so control isn't clean; mitigate with cluster randomization.
Novelty effect: drivers find the surge mechanism new, so the effect decays over time; mitigate by running 2-4 weeks.
Peeking: the team repeatedly checks the p-value mid-run; mitigate by pre-committing sample size and analysis time.
optionExplanations: 加样本救不了「对照被处理污染」的结构问题，方差不是根因。
对；共享司机池让处理泄漏进对照，聚类随机化把互相影响关进同一簇。
这不是新鲜感衰减，是组间通过共享资源相互影响，跑久也治不了泄漏。
peeking 是时间维度偷看，本例是空间/资源上的相互干扰，锁样本量治不了。
optionExplanations_en: More samples can't fix the structural issue of control being contaminated by treatment; variance isn't the root cause.
Correct — a shared driver pool leaks treatment into control; cluster randomization confines interactions within a cluster.
This isn't novelty decay; groups interact through a shared resource, so running longer alone doesn't stop the leakage.
Peeking is a temporal early look; this is spatial/resource interference between groups, which pre-committing alone can't fix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户或资源相互影响，使处理效应泄漏进对照组，违反组间独立假设。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Network interference is users/resources interacting so treatment leaks into control, violating between-group independence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理/社交簇整块分配同一实验臂，把相互影响关在簇内以防泄漏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cluster-based randomization assigns whole geographic/social clusters to one arm, containing interactions to prevent leakage.

scenario: 计划跑 21 天，第 4 天看到欺诈下降 3% 且 p<0.05，团队想立刻停实验上线。
scenario_en: Planned for 21 days, on day 4 you see a 3% fraud drop with p<0.05 and want to stop and ship now.
q: 在到达计划样本量前反复偷看、见显著就停，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What's the main risk of peeking before the planned sample and stopping when significant?
why: 这是 peeking：每偷看一次 p 值就等于多做一次假设检验，反复看会把整体假阳性率抬到 5% 以上，见显著就停会「捡」到随机波动造成的假阳性。所以第 4 天的 3% 可能是虚的。这正是课后测验的答案。
why_en: This is peeking — each early look is another hypothesis test, so repeated peeking inflates the overall false-positive rate above 5%, and stopping at significance catches random-noise false positives.
tradeoff: 预锁样本量+分析时点（假阳性受控） vs 见 p<0.05 就停（假阳性被抬高）
whenOtherWins: 若确实需要中途早停，应改用序贯检验(sequential testing)并对显著性边界做校正，而不是拿固定 α 反复偷看。
options: 样本量不足只会让功效不够、容易漏检真效应，这属于 Type II 错误风险
peeking：反复偷看抬高假阳性率，见显著就停会捡到虚假显著
网络干扰：欺诈者之间互相学习模仿，导致处理组效应被系统性高估
没有风险：只要某一天 p<0.05，就说明效应真实存在，可以立刻停止实验上线
options_en: Insufficient sample size only lowers power and risks missing a real effect — a Type II risk.
Peeking: repeated early looks inflate the false-positive rate, and stopping at significance catches spurious significance.
Network interference: fraudsters copy each other's behavior, systematically overstating the treatment effect.
No risk: the moment p<0.05 on any day, the effect is real and the experiment can stop and ship immediately.
optionExplanations: 问题不是漏检而是「多次偷看」抬高了假阳性（Type I），跟样本量大小无关。
对；每次偷看=多一次检验，固定 α 下反复看会把假阳性率推过 5%，是测验答案。
这不是干扰问题，本例没有欺诈者互相影响的机制，是提前停止导致的统计假阳性。
p<0.05 在偷看语境下并不可信，早停恰恰放大假阳性，不是「没有风险」。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't missing an effect but repeated looks inflating false positives (Type I) — unrelated to sample size.
Correct — each peek is another test; under fixed alpha, repeated looks push the false-positive rate past 5% — the quiz answer.
This isn't interference; there's no fraudster-copying mechanism here, it's statistical false positives from early stopping.
p<0.05 isn't trustworthy under peeking; early stopping amplifies false positives, so it's not risk-free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在达到计划样本量前反复查看结果并在显著时提前停，抬高整体假阳性率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Peeking is repeatedly checking results before the planned sample and stopping at significance, inflating the overall false-positive rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许中途多次查看但对显著性边界做校正，控制累积假阳性的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential testing permits multiple interim looks while adjusting significance boundaries to control cumulative false positives.

scenario: 业务方确实希望在实验中途能提前叫停明显有效/有害的变体，但又不想抬高假阳性率。
scenario_en: The business genuinely wants the option to stop clearly-good/bad variants mid-experiment without inflating the false-positive rate.
q: 既要允许早停、又要控制假阳性，正确做法是什么？
q_en: To allow early stopping while controlling false positives, what's the right approach?
why: 用序贯检验：它预先设计好中途多次查看时的显著性边界（比固定 0.05 更严），使累积假阳性率仍受控。这样可以合法早停。反面是拿固定 α=0.05 反复偷看，那会把假阳性抬高。默认仍应预锁样本量与分析时点。
why_en: Use sequential testing — it pre-designs stricter significance boundaries for repeated interim looks so cumulative false positives stay controlled, enabling legitimate early stopping.
tradeoff: 序贯检验（合法早停、边界更严、稍损功效） vs 固定样本预锁（最简单但不能中途停）
whenOtherWins: 若不需要早停，最简单稳妥的仍是预先锁定样本量和分析时点、到点再看，无需序贯检验的复杂度。
options: 继续用固定 α=0.05，每天查看一次结果，只要见到显著就立刻停止实验
用序贯检验：预设更严的显著性边界，控制累积假阳性下合法早停
把显著性水平 α 直接调到 0.5，让实验更容易显著，这样就能放心早停
取消所有护栏指标只保留主指标，这样早停就不会带来额外副作用
options_en: Keep fixed alpha=0.05, check daily, and stop the moment it's significant.
Use sequential testing: pre-set stricter significance boundaries to allow legitimate early stopping with controlled cumulative false positives.
Set alpha directly to 0.5 so the experiment reaches significance more easily, then stop early with confidence.
Drop all guardrails and keep only the primary metric, so early stopping brings no extra side effects.
optionExplanations: 固定 α 反复看正是 peeking，会抬高假阳性，不是解法。
对；序贯检验用校正后的边界让早停合法、假阳性可控。
把 α 调大只会让假阳性更多，方向完全错误，不是合法早停。
护栏与早停的假阳性问题无关，去掉护栏只会让破坏体验的改动更容易漏检。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed alpha with repeated looks is peeking, inflating false positives — not a fix.
Correct — sequential testing's corrected boundaries make early stopping legitimate with controlled false positives.
Raising alpha just makes more false positives — completely wrong direction, not legitimate early stopping.
Guardrails are unrelated to early-stopping false positives; removing them just makes UX-harming changes easier to miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为中途多次查看设计校正过的显著性边界，使累积假阳性受控、可合法早停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential testing designs corrected significance boundaries for interim looks so cumulative false positives stay controlled, allowing valid early stopping.

q: 把 A/B 测试设计的 7 步框架排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 7-step A/B testing design framework:
steps: 陈述假设（改动 → 指标 → 阈值）
定义主指标 + ≥2 个护栏（UX + 系统健康）
从业务影响确定 MDE
用功效分析算样本量（α=0.05, power=0.80）
估算运行时长 = 样本量 / 日流量，取整到整周
预先锁定分析计划（不 peeking）、用时间窗口趋势应对新奇效应
检查网络干扰，若用户相互影响则改聚类随机化
why: 先立可证伪假设，再定主指标+护栏，从业务定 MDE，据 MDE 算样本量，除以日流量得时长，预锁分析计划防 peeking 与新奇，最后检查网络干扰决定是否聚类随机化。顺序体现「先目标后统计再执行」的全生命周期思路。
why_en: Hypothesis → primary+guardrails → MDE from business → sample size via power → runtime → pre-commit against peeking/novelty → check network interference; the order goes goal, statistics, then execution.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  H["1.假设"] --> M["2.主指标+护栏"]
  M --> D["3.MDE(业务)"]
  D --> N["4.样本量(功效分析)"]
  N --> R["5.运行时长"]
  R --> P["6.预锁分析计划"]
  P --> I["7.查网络干扰"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 实验开始前就固定样本量与分析时点，防止事后偷看与随意早停带来的假阳性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-committing fixes the sample size and analysis time before the experiment to prevent peeking and false positives.

scenario: 三个 A/B 常见陷阱：新奇效应、网络干扰、peeking，症状和缓解各不同。
scenario_en: Three common A/B pitfalls — novelty effect, network interference, peeking — with different symptoms and fixes.
q: 这三个 A/B 陷阱各自的机制与缓解手段是什么？
q_en: What is each of these three A/B pitfalls' mechanism and mitigation?
why: 三者分属时间、结构、统计三层：新奇是早期虚高（跑 2-4 周），网络干扰是组间泄漏（聚类随机化），peeking 是反复偷看抬高假阳性（预锁样本量）。
why_en: Novelty is temporal inflation (mitigate: 2-4 weeks, windowed trends); network interference is structural leakage between groups (mitigate: cluster randomization); peeking is statistical false-positive inflation (mitigate: pre-commit or sequential testing).

rows: 因新而虚高、随时间衰减
组间共享资源相互影响

options: 三者本质相同，都靠加大样本量解决
新奇=时间性虚高、干扰=结构性泄漏、peeking=统计性假阳性
新奇靠聚类随机化、网络干扰靠跑久、peeking 靠加样本，各自对应
三者都是 Type II 错误的不同表现
options_en: All three are essentially the same, solved by more samples.
Novelty = temporal inflation, interference = structural leakage, peeking = statistical false positives.
Novelty via cluster randomization, interference via running longer, peeking via more samples — respectively.
All three are different manifestations of Type II error.
optionExplanations: 加样本救不了泄漏和偷看，三者机制不同、缓解也不同。
对；时间性/结构性/统计性三类坑，缓解手段一一对应。
缓解全部错配：新奇不是聚类能救、peeking 不是加样本能救。
peeking 是抬高假阳性(Type I)，新奇/干扰也不是 Type II，归类错误。
optionExplanations_en: More samples can't fix leakage or peeking; the three differ in mechanism and fix.
Correct — temporal/structural/statistical pitfalls with matching mitigations.
All mitigations mismatched: novelty isn't fixed by clustering, peeking isn't fixed by more samples.
Peeking inflates false positives (Type I), and novelty/interference aren't Type II either — miscategorized.

termDefinitions.term: time-windowed analysis / 时间窗口分析
termDefinitions.meaning: 按周/时段拆看指标趋势而非单一聚合值，用于识别新奇效应的衰减。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-windowed analysis reads metric trends by week/segment instead of one aggregate, revealing novelty decay.

tradeoff: 延长实验消新奇效应（代价：结论更晚） vs 预锁样本量防 peeking（代价：不能中途早停）

scenario: 在社交网络/双边市场/共享出行里做 A/B，用户之间会互相影响（分享、抢单、抢司机）。
scenario_en: Running A/B in a social network / two-sided marketplace / ride-share where users interact (sharing, competing for jobs/drivers).
q: 这类用户会相互影响的产品，该最优先防哪个陷阱？用什么随机化？
q_en: For products where users interact, which pitfall to guard first, and what randomization?
why: 最优先防网络干扰：用户级随机化会让处理组的效应通过互动泄漏进对照组，破坏独立性、偏差方向不可预测。改用聚类随机化——按地理/社交簇整块分同一臂，让相互影响都发生在簇内、不跨臂，恢复组间可比性。
why_en: Guard network interference first — user-level randomization lets treatment leak into control via interactions, so switch to cluster-based randomization (assign whole geo/social clusters to one arm) to contain interactions.
tradeoff: 用户级随机化（多独立单元、但共享资源时泄漏） vs 聚类随机化（防泄漏、但独立单元变少、功效下降）
whenOtherWins: 若用户彼此独立、不共享资源也不互动（如互不相关的单机功能），用户级随机化更简单、独立单元更多、功效更高。
options: 先防新奇效应，用用户级随机化即可
先防网络干扰，改用聚类随机化把相互影响关在簇内
先防 peeking，用户之间的影响与随机化无关
先防分布漂移，重训模型即可解决相互影响
options_en: Guard novelty first; user-level randomization suffices.
Guard network interference first; switch to cluster randomization to contain interactions within clusters.
Guard peeking first; user interactions are unrelated to randomization.
Guard distribution shift first; retraining fixes the interactions.
optionExplanations: 用户互相影响时，用户级随机化正是泄漏的来源，防新奇解决不了。
对；聚类随机化把互相影响限制在簇内，恢复处理/对照的可比性。
用户互动恰恰通过随机化单元影响独立性，与 peeking 无关。
分布漂移是离线-在线问题，重训救不了组间干扰。
optionExplanations_en: When users interact, user-level randomization is the leakage source; guarding novelty won't help.
Correct — cluster randomization confines interactions within clusters, restoring treatment/control comparability.
User interaction affects independence via the randomization unit, unrelated to peeking.
Distribution shift is an offline-online issue; retraining can't fix between-group interference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 供需两方在同一平台匹配（骑手-司机、买家-卖家），一方的实验会波及另一方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-sided marketplace matches supply and demand (riders-drivers, buyers-sellers), where an experiment on one side affects the other.

scenario: 实验平台（如 Amazon SageMaker）支持在实验进行中动态调整对照/实验的流量比例，无需重启。
scenario_en: Platforms like Amazon SageMaker support adjusting control/treatment traffic split mid-experiment without restarting.
q: 「动态流量分配」提供了什么能力？和 peeking 早停是一回事吗？
q_en: What does dynamic traffic allocation provide, and is it the same as peeking/early stopping?
why: 动态流量分配让你中途调整每臂流量占比而无需重启实验，属流量运营能力；peeking 则是拿固定 α 反复偷看就下显著性结论，两者不是一回事。
why_en: Dynamic traffic allocation lets you shift each arm’s share mid-experiment without a restart — that’s traffic ops, not peeking, which is repeatedly checking a fixed alpha and calling significance.
options: 它等价于 peeking，允许见显著就停并直接下结论
中途可调各臂流量而不重启；不替代统计框架
它自动消除网络干扰，无需聚类随机化
它把样本量需求降为零，任何效应都能瞬间检出
options_en: It equals peeking, letting you stop at significance and conclude directly.
You can shift each arm’s traffic mid-run without restarting; it does not replace the statistical framework.
It automatically removes network interference, so no cluster randomization is needed.
It drops the sample-size requirement to zero, detecting any effect instantly.
optionExplanations: 动态分配不是 peeking，也不豁免「反复看会抬高假阳性」的统计问题。
对；它只管流量调度，要保推断有效仍需序贯/bandit 框架配合。
流量调度不解决组间相互影响，网络干扰仍要聚类随机化。
样本量由功效分析决定，动态分配不会把它降为零。
optionExplanations_en: Dynamic allocation isn't peeking and doesn't exempt the false-positive inflation of repeated looks.
Correct — it only schedules traffic; valid inference still needs a sequential/bandit framework.
Traffic scheduling doesn't fix between-group interaction; interference still needs cluster randomization.
Sample size comes from power analysis; dynamic allocation doesn't zero it out.

termDefinitions.term: dynamic traffic allocation / 动态流量分配
termDefinitions.meaning: 实验进行中调整各臂流量比例而不重启的能力，如 SageMaker 支持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic traffic allocation adjusts each arm's traffic share mid-experiment without restarting, as SageMaker supports.

scenario: 把 A/B 假设写成可证伪的一句话模板，方便面试里直接套用。
scenario_en: Write the A/B hypothesis as a falsifiable one-line template to reuse in interviews.
q: 补全可证伪 A/B 假设的三要素模板：
q_en: Complete the three-part falsifiable A/B hypothesis template:
text: 假设 = 一个具体{{改动}} + 一个预期的{{指标}}移动 + 一个{{阈值}}，例如「换成 listwise 排序器会让观看时长/会话提升 ≥1%」。
text_en: Hypothesis = a concrete {{change}} + an expected {{metric}} move + a {{threshold}}, e.g. 'switching to a listwise ranker raises watch time/session by ≥1%'.
why: 三要素齐全才让实验事前可判成败：改动指明测什么、指标指明看哪个数、阈值（结合 MDE）指明多大才算赢。缺任何一个都退化成「看看好不好」的不可证伪表述。
why_en: All three make the experiment decidable in advance: the change says what to test, the metric which number, the threshold how big counts as a win.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判定实验成功的最小指标移动量，通常与 MDE 一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The threshold is the minimum metric move that counts as success, usually aligned with the MDE.

scenario: 为省时间，工程师想只跑周二到周四三天（流量最大）就得出 A/B 结论。
scenario_en: To save time, an engineer wants to conclude the A/B from just Tue-Thu (highest traffic).
q: 只采工作日高峰三天的样本，会带来什么偏差？为什么要跑满整周？
q_en: What bias comes from sampling only three weekday-peak days, and why run full weeks?
why: 工作日和周末用户行为不同（购物、娱乐、通勤模式都变）。只采工作日会系统性偏向某一类行为，结论无法泛化到全周。跑满整周（7/14 天）覆盖完整周内周期，样本才代表真实流量结构。
why_en: Weekday and weekend behavior differ, so sampling only weekdays systematically biases toward one behavior pattern; run full weeks (7/14 days) to cover the complete weekly cycle.
options: 没有偏差，只要样本量够就行，哪几天都一样
工作日/周末行为不同，只采工作日有系统性偏差
偏差来自流量太大，应改采周末低峰几天
只影响运行时长计算，不影响结论的代表性
options_en: No bias — as long as the sample is large, any days are equivalent.
Weekday and weekend behavior differ, so weekday-only sampling is systematically biased.
The bias is from too much traffic; sample low-peak weekend days instead.
It only affects runtime computation, not the representativeness of the conclusion.
optionExplanations: 样本量大但结构偏，仍无法代表全周行为，天数不是无所谓。
对；周内周期性让整周采样成为必需，否则结论有系统性偏差。
问题不是流量大小，是行为随星期几变化的周期性。
它直接影响样本代表性，不只是时长的算术。
optionExplanations_en: A large but structurally biased sample still can't represent the whole week; the days do matter.
Correct — the weekly cycle makes full-week sampling necessary or the conclusion is systematically biased.
The issue isn't traffic volume but day-of-week behavioral periodicity.
It directly affects sample representativeness, not just runtime arithmetic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户行为随星期几系统变化，要求实验覆盖完整整周以避免采样偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weekly seasonality is user behavior varying systematically by day of week, requiring full-week coverage to avoid sampling bias.

scenario: Airbnb 测一个提升预订的搜索排序改动，要选主指标和护栏。
scenario_en: Airbnb tests a search-ranking change to lift bookings and must pick primary and guardrail metrics.
q: 这个 Airbnb 实验，主指标和护栏分别该选什么？为什么这样搭配？
q_en: For this Airbnb experiment, what primary and guardrails, and why this pairing?
why: 主指标选预订率（直接目标）；护栏选页面加载时间（系统健康——排序变复杂别拖慢页面）和房东取消率（UX/供给健康——别为冲预订推不靠谱房源导致取消飙升）。主指标推目标，两个护栏各守一条不能牺牲的底线。
why_en: Primary = booking rate (direct target); guardrails = page-load time (system health — don't slow the page) and host cancellation rate (UX/supply health — don't chase bookings by pushing unreliable listings).
tradeoff: 只盯预订率（可能偷偷拖慢页面/推高取消） vs 加护栏（守住加载时间与取消率底线）
whenOtherWins: 若这次改动完全不碰服务延迟、也不改变房源质量分布（如纯前端文案改动），相应护栏可以放宽或替换成更相关的。
options: 主指标=页面加载时间，护栏=预订率和房东取消率两项
主指标=预订率，护栏=页面加载时间 + 房东取消率
主指标=预订率，不需要任何护栏，护栏只会拖慢实验分析
主指标和护栏都设成预订率，用两份同样的数据互相印证提高可信度
options_en: Primary = page-load time, guardrails = booking rate and host cancellation rate.
Primary = booking rate, guardrails = page-load time + host cancellation rate.
Primary = booking rate, no guardrails needed — guardrails only slow down analysis.
Set both primary and guardrail to booking rate, using duplicate data to cross-confirm confidence.
optionExplanations: 搭反了：预订率是目标（主指标），加载时间和取消率是要守的底线（护栏）。
对；预订率推目标，加载时间守系统健康、取消率守供给/UX，正是成熟搭配。
没有护栏就挡不住「冲预订却拖慢页面或推高取消」的副作用，不是拖慢分析。
主指标与护栏设成同一个没有意义，重复同一数据也印证不了任何额外信息。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: booking rate is the target (primary); load time and cancellation are the floors to protect (guardrails).
Correct — booking rate drives the goal, load time guards system health, cancellation guards supply/UX — a mature pairing.
Without guardrails you can't block the side effect of chasing bookings while slowing the page or raising cancellations.
Setting primary and guardrail identical is pointless; duplicating the same data confirms no extra information.

termDefinitions.term: host cancellation rate / 房东取消率
termDefinitions.meaning: 房东取消已确认预订的比例，Airbnb 的 UX/供给护栏之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Host cancellation rate is the share of confirmed bookings hosts cancel — an Airbnb UX/supply guardrail.

scenario: 团队把 MDE 定成 0.5%，理由是 0.1% 的 CTR 提升不值得部署与维护的复杂度。
scenario_en: The team sets MDE=0.5% because a 0.1% CTR lift isn't worth the deployment and maintenance complexity.
q: 把 MDE 从 0.1% 提高到 0.5% 对实验成本有什么影响？为什么这么设？
q_en: What does raising MDE from 0.1% to 0.5% do to experiment cost, and why set it there?
why: 样本量 ∝ 1/MDE²，把 MDE 从 0.1% 提到 0.5%（放大 5 倍）能把所需样本量缩小约 25 倍，运行时长大幅缩短。这么设是业务判断：0.1% 的 CTR 提升带来的收益盖不住部署/维护成本，不值得为它耗巨量样本去检测。
why_en: Since sample size ∝ 1/MDE², raising MDE 5x (0.1%→0.5%) cuts required samples ~25x and shortens runtime; you set it there because a 0.1% CTR gain isn't worth the deployment cost to detect.
options: 样本量按比例只缩小 5 倍，因为样本量与 MDE 成反比
样本量约缩小 25 倍（∝1/MDE²），时长大减
对样本量没影响，MDE 只改结论解读不改样本
样本量反而增大，因为要更精确地检测 0.5%
options_en: Sample size shrinks only 5x, since it's inversely proportional to MDE.
Sample size shrinks about 25x (∝ 1/MDE²) and runtime drops sharply.
No effect on sample size; MDE only changes interpretation.
Sample size grows, because detecting 0.5% needs more precision.
optionExplanations: 是平方反比不是线性反比，5 倍 MDE 对应约 25 倍样本缩减。
对；1/MDE² 让放宽 MDE 大幅省样本，而门槛高低是业务价值判断。
MDE 是样本量公式的分母平方项，影响巨大，不是不改样本。
放宽 MDE（测更大效应）省样本，不是增大。
optionExplanations_en: It's an inverse-square not inverse-linear law; 5x MDE means ~25x fewer samples.
Correct — 1/MDE² makes a looser MDE save many samples, and the threshold is a business-value call.
MDE is the squared denominator in the sample-size formula — a huge effect, not zero.
Loosening MDE (detecting a bigger effect) saves samples, not increases them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 样本量与 MDE 平方成反比，想检测越小的效应，代价按平方暴涨。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sample size is inversely proportional to MDE squared, so detecting smaller effects costs quadratically more.

scenario: 一个新 UI 改版首周各项互动指标暴涨，产品经理想立刻宣布成功、全量上线。
scenario_en: A new UI redesign spikes all engagement metrics in week 1, and the PM wants to declare success and full-roll now.
q: 面对首周暴涨，该怎么判断这是真实提升还是新奇效应？
q_en: Facing a week-1 spike, how do you tell a real lift from a novelty effect?
why: 别看单一聚合值就下结论：把实验跑够 2-4 周，按时间窗口看趋势——若增益从首周高位持续衰减到接近 0，就是新奇效应；若衰减后稳定在一个正的平台期，才是真实长期提升。等新鲜感退潮再判。
why_en: Don't conclude from one aggregate — run 2-4 weeks and read time-windowed trends: if the gain decays toward zero it was novelty, if it stabilizes at a positive plateau it's a real lift.
tradeoff: 首周就下结论（可能被新奇虚高误导） vs 跑 2-4 周看衰减后平台（识别真实长期效应）
whenOtherWins: 若改动本质上就是短命内容（限时活动、突发新闻），本来只需要短期效果，那么首周表现反而是相关的评估对象。
options: 首周暴涨就代表成功，无需等待衰减，立刻全量上线才最稳妥
跑 2-4 周看趋势：衰减到 0 是新奇，稳在正平台才真
把实验缩短到 3 天，趁用户热度最高、指标最好看时锁定结论上线
只要哪一天 p<0.05 就上线，后续趋势是否衰减都无关紧要
options_en: A week-1 spike means success; no need to wait for decay, full-roll immediately is safest.
Run 2-4 weeks and read the trend: decay toward zero is novelty, a stable positive plateau is real.
Shorten the test to 3 days and lock the conclusion while user hype and metrics look best.
Ship the moment any day shows p<0.05; whether the trend later decays is irrelevant.
optionExplanations: 首周暴涨正是新奇效应的典型症状，不等衰减就全量最危险。
对；看衰减后的稳态平台才能区分真提升与新鲜感，是新奇效应的标准应对。
缩短实验会把新奇虚高固化成结论，恰恰放大误判，不是「锁定」而是「锁死错误」。
在新奇效应下 p<0.05 也可能是短暂虚高，趋势恰恰是判断真假的关键，不能忽略。
optionExplanations_en: A week-1 spike is the textbook novelty symptom; full-rolling without waiting for decay is most dangerous.
Correct — reading the post-decay plateau distinguishes real lift from hype — the standard novelty response.
Shortening freezes novelty inflation into the conclusion, amplifying the misjudgment rather than locking in a good one.
Under novelty, p<0.05 can be transient inflation; the trend is exactly what determines real vs fake, not irrelevant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新奇消退后指标稳定下来的水平，代表真实长期效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The plateau is the level the metric settles at after novelty fades, representing the real long-term effect.

scenario: 在共享司机池的市场里做用户级 A/B，处理效应通过司机重定位泄漏进对照，偏差方向事先无法预测。
scenario_en: A user-level A/B in a shared-driver marketplace where treatment leaks into control via driver repositioning, biasing in an unpredictable direction.
q: 网络干扰的偏差为什么「方向不可预测」？这比一个已知方向的偏差更麻烦在哪？
q_en: Why is network-interference bias 'unpredictable in direction', and why is that worse than a known-direction bias?
why: 泄漏可能高估也可能低估处理效应（司机被吸走→高估；处理组拥堵→低估），符号事前未知。已知方向的偏差还能事后校正，未知方向只能靠聚类随机化从设计上消除。
why_en: Leakage can over- or under-state the effect depending on how resources flow between groups, so the sign is unknown in advance; a known-direction bias could be corrected one way, but an unknown direction can only be removed by design (cluster randomization).
options: 方向其实可预测，总是高估处理效应，直接减去固定值即可
符号事前未知（可高估可低估），只能靠聚类随机化从设计消除
方向不可预测但幅度总是很小，可忽略不计
这不是偏差问题，只是方差变大，加样本即可
options_en: The direction is actually predictable — it always overstates the effect — so subtract a fixed offset.
The sign is unknown in advance (over- or under-statement); only cluster randomization removes it by design.
The direction is unpredictable but the magnitude is always tiny and negligible.
It's not bias but larger variance, fixable by adding samples.
optionExplanations: 泄漏并不总是高估，符号取决于资源流向，减固定值会修错方向。
对；符号未知让事后校正失效，必须用聚类随机化在设计层面切断泄漏。
幅度未必小，且方向不定本身就使结论不可信，不能忽略。
它是系统性偏差不是纯方差，加样本消不掉偏差。
optionExplanations_en: Leakage doesn't always overstate; the sign depends on resource flow, so a fixed offset corrects the wrong way.
Correct — unknown sign defeats post-correction, so cluster randomization must cut leakage by design.
The magnitude isn't necessarily small, and unknown direction alone makes conclusions untrustworthy.
It's systematic bias not mere variance; more samples can't remove bias.

termDefinitions.term: unpredictable bias direction / 偏差方向不可预测
termDefinitions.meaning: 干扰可能高估或低估效应、符号事前未知，无法靠事后减一个固定量校正。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unpredictable bias direction means interference may over- or under-state the effect with unknown sign, uncorrectable by a fixed post-hoc offset.

scenario: 面试官问：既然有标准 A/B 测试，为什么还要 interleaving、bandit、switchback、准实验这些方法？
scenario_en: Interviewer: if we have standard A/B testing, why do we still need interleaving, bandits, switchback, and quasi-experiments?
q: 为什么需要「超越标准 A/B」的实验方法？
q_en: Why do we need experimentation methods beyond standard A/B?
why: 标准 A/B 在四类生产场景会失效：微小排序差异要几百万用户、动态优化时 50/50 会白烧钱、双边市场共享司机导致干扰、平台级发布无法按用户随机。每一类都有专门方法接手，答对方法体现你懂完整部署生命周期。
why_en: Standard A/B breaks in four production settings — tiny ranking effects, dynamic optimization, marketplace interference, and platform-wide launches — and each has a specialized method.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  F1["微小排序差异"] --> M1["Interleaving"]
  F2["动态优化/短命内容"] --> M2["Multi-armed bandit"]
  F3["双边市场干扰"] --> M3["Switchback"]
  F4["平台级/国家级发布"] --> M4["准实验 DiD/合成控制"]
options: 标准 A/B 只是慢又贵，这些新方法说到底只是换皮的更快版本 A/B，底层机制完全相同、没有本质区别
标准 A/B 在四类场景失效（微小排序差、动态优化、市场干扰、平台级发布），每类有专门方法接手
这些方法已经完全取代了 A/B，以后任何实验都该弃用 A/B、全改用它们，A/B 已彻底过时不再需要
它们只是显著性检验的不同叫法，换个名字，实验设计上并无区别
options_en: Standard A/B is only slow and costly, and these new methods are essentially just repackaged, faster versions of A/B with identical underlying mechanics.
Standard A/B fails in four settings (tiny ranking gaps, dynamic optimization, market interference, platform-wide launches), each with a specialized method.
These methods have fully replaced A/B; every future experiment should abandon A/B entirely and switch to them, since A/B is now completely obsolete.
They are just different names for significance testing, differing only in label, not in experimental design.
optionExplanations: 不是更快的 A/B：interleaving 是被试内设计、bandit 是自适应分配、switchback 是按时间聚类随机，机制根本不同。
对；四种失效场景对应四种方法，选对方法正是「按约束选实验设计」的体现，不是一招通吃。
A/B 仍是测绝对业务指标、做干净因果推断的金标准，新方法各有硬约束，不能全盘取代它。
它们改变的是随机化单元和分配策略（用户 vs 时间窗 vs 自适应），不只是检验名称。
optionExplanations_en: Not faster A/B: interleaving is within-subject, bandits are adaptive allocation, switchback is time-clustered randomization — fundamentally different mechanics.
Correct — four failure settings map to four methods; picking the right one is constraint-driven design, not one-size-fits-all.
A/B is still the gold standard for absolute business metrics and clean causal inference; each new method has hard constraints and can't replace it wholesale.
They change the randomization unit and allocation strategy (user vs time window vs adaptive), not just the test's name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分成两组、各看一个版本，比较绝对指标差异的被试间实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into two arms, each seeing one version, and compares absolute metric differences (a between-subject experiment).

scenario: 你要比较两个排序模型谁更好，但两者质量差异极小，标准 A/B 得几百万用户跑数周才可能测出显著差异。
scenario_en: You must compare two rankers whose quality gap is tiny; standard A/B would need millions of users over weeks to reach significance.
q: 该用标准 A/B 还是 interleaving 来筛这两个排序器？
q_en: Standard A/B or interleaving to screen these two rankers?
why: 微小排序差异用 interleaving：它把两个排序器的结果合并成一个列表给同一个用户，每个用户当自己的对照，消掉巨大的用户间方差，样本效率约 100 倍。标准 A/B 是被试间设计，靠海量样本压方差，太慢太贵。
why_en: Use interleaving for tiny ranking gaps because each user is their own control, killing between-user variance and needing far fewer samples than between-subject A/B.
tradeoff: Interleaving（样本效率高，但只测相对偏好）vs 标准 A/B（可测绝对业务指标，但要海量样本）
whenOtherWins: 当你要的是绝对业务影响（营收、会话时长）而不只是「谁的排序更受欢迎」时，interleaving 测不出，必须回到完整 A/B。
options: 标准 A/B：只有它才能对排序质量给出真正可信的结论，哪怕要几百万用户、连跑上数周也得咬牙跑完，忍一忍就好
都不用，直接看离线 NDCG 谁的分数更高就上线，线上实验的成本和排队时间完全可以省掉
Interleaving：合并两个排序器结果、每用户自己当对照，消掉用户间方差，样本效率约 100 倍
各投一半流量分别做两个独立 A/B，实验结束后再横向比较两个实验各自算出的绝对指标数值
options_en: Standard A/B: only it gives a trustworthy verdict on ranking quality, so even if it takes millions of users over several weeks, just grit your teeth and run it to the end.
Neither — just launch whichever scores higher on offline NDCG and skip online experiments entirely, saving all the cost and queue time.
Interleaving: merge both rankers' results, each user is their own control, killing between-user variance for ~100x sample efficiency.
Run two fully separate A/B tests at half traffic each, then after both finish compare their absolute metric numbers side by side.
optionExplanations: 标准 A/B 能测但极慢：微小差异被巨大用户间方差淹没，得几百万用户数周，成本不划算。
离线 NDCG 与线上真实点击常不一致，跳过线上实验会把「离线好看、线上翻车」的模型放出去。
对；被试内设计让同一用户同时体验两个排序器，方差骤降，是快速初筛排序器的首选。
两个独立 A/B 仍是被试间、仍要海量样本，还多引入实验间不可比问题，没解决方差难题。
optionExplanations_en: A/B can measure it but very slowly: a tiny gap drowns in huge between-user variance, needing millions of users over weeks.
Offline NDCG and real online clicks often diverge; skipping online tests ships models that look good offline but fail live.
Correct — within-subject design lets one user experience both rankers at once, slashing variance, the go-to fast screen for rankers.
Two separate A/B tests are still between-subject and still need huge samples, plus cross-experiment incomparability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个排序器的结果混编进同一个列表给同一用户，按点击归因判哪个排序器更受偏好的被试内实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving merges two rankers' results into one list for the same user and attributes clicks to decide which ranker is preferred — a within-subject experiment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序质量的离线指标，越靠前的相关结果得分越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is an offline ranking-quality metric that rewards relevant results placed higher.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被试间：不同用户分到不同版本；被试内：同一用户同时体验多个版本、自己当对照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Between-subject assigns different users to different versions; within-subject exposes the same user to multiple versions as their own control.

scenario: 面试官让你讲清 interleaving 到底怎么运作、为什么样本效率高。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to explain exactly how interleaving works and why it is so sample-efficient.
q: Interleaving 的核心机制是什么？
q_en: What is interleaving's core mechanism?
why: 把排序器 A、B 的结果交错合并成一个列表展示给同一用户，用户点了哪个结果就把功劳记给贡献它的排序器；因为同一用户同时看到两者、当自己的对照，用户间的口味差异被抵消，方差骤降。
why_en: Interleave A's and B's results into one list for the same user and credit each click to its source ranker, so each user is their own control and between-user taste variance cancels out.
diagram:
flowchart TB A["排序器 A 结果"] --> M["交错合并成一个列表"] B["排序器 B 结果"] --> M M --> U["同一用户浏览+点击"] U --> C["点击归因给贡献的排序器
点击多者胜"]
options: 把 A、B 结果交错合并成一个列表给同一用户，点击归因给贡献的排序器，每用户自己当对照
把用户随机分成 A 组和 B 组各看一个排序器，跑满整个实验周期后再比两组的平均点击率
先用 A 服务一周、再用 B 服务下一周，事后前后对比这两周各自的点击率高低
让人工标注员离线给两个排序结果打分，取平均分高的排序器
options_en: Interleave A's and B's results into one list for the same user, attribute clicks to the source ranker, each user their own control.
Randomly split users into group A and group B, each sees one ranker, run the full experiment period, then compare the two groups' average click rate.
Serve A for one week, then B for the following week, and afterward compare the two weeks' click rates against each other.
Have human annotators score both ranked lists offline and pick the ranker with the higher average.
optionExplanations: 对；合并成一个列表 + 同一用户当对照，正是消掉用户间方差、拿到 ~100 倍样本效率的关键。
这是标准 A/B（被试间），不同用户看不同版本，方差高，恰恰是 interleaving 要改进的对象。
前后分时段对比会被时间趋势污染（周中 vs 周末），不是 interleaving，也不控制混淆。
离线人工打分不是 interleaving，也测不到真实用户在线点击行为。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one merged list plus same-user control is exactly what cancels between-user variance for ~100x efficiency.
That's standard A/B (between-subject); different users see different versions, high variance — what interleaving improves on.
Before/after time comparison is polluted by temporal trends (midweek vs weekend), not interleaving and uncontrolled for confounders.
Offline human scoring isn't interleaving and can't capture real online click behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在合并列表里，用户点击某结果时把功劳记给最初产出该结果的排序器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Click attribution credits a click on a result in the merged list to whichever ranker originally produced that result.

scenario: 有人引用「interleaving 比 A/B 少用约 100 倍样本」这个数，问你能不能当成通用常数直接照搬。
scenario_en: Someone cites 'interleaving needs ~100x fewer samples than A/B' and asks whether you can treat it as a universal constant.
q: 「约 100 倍样本效率」这个数该怎么理解？
q_en: How should you read the '~100x sample efficiency' number?
why: ~100× 是 Netflix、微软等报告的经验观察值、不是公式推导，来源是「被试内消掉用户间方差」这一机制，具体倍数取决于方差结构，会随任务变化。所以它是量级直觉（省一两个数量级），不能当固定常数照抄进容量估算。
why_en: The ~100x is an empirical Netflix/Microsoft observation, not a formula — it comes from within-subject variance cancellation and varies with the variance structure, so treat it as an order-of-magnitude intuition, not a constant.
options: 它是精确常数，任何 interleaving 实验都恰好省 100 倍样本，可直接写进样本量公式
它是理论上限，实际永远达不到，最多省 2-3 倍
它是经验观察值（来自 Netflix/微软），源于消掉用户间方差，倍数随方差结构变化，只是量级直觉
它指 interleaving 慢 100 倍，是它相对 A/B 的最大缺点
options_en: It's an exact constant; every interleaving experiment saves exactly 100x samples, safe to plug into a sample-size formula.
It's a theoretical ceiling never reached in practice; you get at most 2-3x in reality.
It's an empirical Netflix/Microsoft observation from variance cancellation; the factor varies with variance structure — an order-of-magnitude intuition.
It means interleaving is 100x slower, its biggest drawback versus A/B.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标里由用户间差异 vs 版本差异各占多少方差；interleaving 越能消掉的用户间方差占比越大，省样本越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Variance structure is how much of a metric's variance comes from between-user vs between-version differences; the more between-user variance interleaving cancels, the more samples it saves.

optionExplanations: 当成精确公式就错了：真实省几倍会随任务波动，没人能保证每次都刚好 100 倍。
把它当成够不到的理论上限也不对，因为 100 倍本身就是从真实产品里量出来的效应，不是空想的上限。
对，它就是一线大厂测出来的经验数字，只当经验参考、别当成放之四海皆准的常数。
跟变慢没关系——这个数说的是能少用多少样本，不是运行时间变长。
optionExplanations_en: Treating it as an exact formula is wrong — real savings swing by task, so no one can guarantee precisely 100x every time.
Calling it an unreachable ceiling misses the point too, since that 100x is itself a number measured from real products, not a fantasy limit.
Correct — it's a number teams like Netflix and Microsoft actually measured, useful as a rough guide but never a plug-in number.
Has nothing to do with slowness — this number is about how few samples you need, not how long anything runs.

scenario: 要实现 interleaving，需要一个公平地把两个排序器的结果交错、并判定胜者的算法。
scenario_en: To implement interleaving you need an algorithm that fairly interleaves two rankers' results and decides a winner.
q: Interleaving 里最常用的 Team Draft 算法怎么判胜负？
q_en: How does the common Team Draft interleaving algorithm decide a winner?
why: Team Draft 像选球队：两个排序器轮流从各自列表里「挑人」放进合并列表，记住每个位置来自谁；用户点击后，跨众多用户统计哪个排序器被归因的点击更多，谁多谁胜。它是最常用的交错方式，保证位置分配大体公平。
why_en: Team Draft alternately 'drafts' picks from each ranker into one list, tracks each slot's source, and the ranker credited with more clicks across users wins.
options: 只看合并列表里谁的第一条结果被点击，就直接判那个排序器赢，把其余所有位置上的点击信号全部忽略掉
两排序器轮流从各自列表挑结果进合并列表并记录来源，跨用户统计被归因点击多者胜
把两个列表拼接后整体随机打乱，看用户点在拼接后的前半段还是后半段
按两个排序器的离线 NDCG 谁高判谁赢，点击只作参考
options_en: Whoever's first result in the merged list gets clicked wins outright, throwing away the click signals from every other position entirely.
The two rankers alternately draft results into the merged list, recording each source; the ranker with more attributed clicks across users wins.
Concatenate both lists, shuffle the whole thing randomly, and see whether users click into the first half or the second half.
Decide by whichever ranker has higher offline NDCG; clicks are only a tiebreaker.
optionExplanations: 只看第一条丢掉了绝大多数信号，位置偏置也会主导结果，不是 Team Draft 的做法。
对；轮流挑选保证位置公平、来源可追溯，再靠跨用户的点击归因累计判胜，是最常用的 interleaving 算法。
随机打乱破坏了公平的位置分配，也无法把点击干净归因到某个排序器。
离线 NDCG 是离线指标；interleaving 的整个意义就是用真实在线点击来判，不靠离线分。
optionExplanations_en: Looking only at the first result throws away most signal and lets position bias dominate — not Team Draft.
Correct — alternating drafts keep positions fair and sources traceable, then attributed clicks accumulated across users decide — the most common interleaving algorithm.
Random shuffling breaks fair position assignment and prevents clean per-ranker attribution.
Offline NDCG is offline; interleaving's whole point is judging by real online clicks, not offline scores.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最常用的 interleaving 交错算法：两个排序器轮流从各自结果里挑一条放入合并列表，点击归因后点击多者胜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Team Draft is the most common interleaving algorithm: two rankers alternately draft one result each into the merged list, and the one credited with more clicks wins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户更倾向点靠前的结果，与内容相关性无关；公平的交错设计要抵消它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is users' tendency to click higher-ranked results regardless of relevance; fair interleaving must offset it.

scenario: 有人想把 interleaving 当唯一的上线判据，你要说清它的适用边界。
scenario_en: Someone wants interleaving as the sole launch criterion; you must lay out where it stops applying.
q: Interleaving 有哪些固有局限？(多选)
q_en: What are interleaving's inherent limitations? (multiple)
why: 三条局限：只测「相对偏好」给不出营收/会话时长等绝对业务指标；只适用排序/推荐这类可交错的界面；单会话设计抓不到长期行为变化（如新奇效应消退）。因此它是初筛器，最终仍要 A/B 收口。GPU 成本与它无关。
why_en: Interleaving only measures relative preference, only fits rankable surfaces, and single-session design misses long-term shifts, so it screens candidates but A/B still closes the decision.
options: 只能测相对偏好，给不出营收、会话时长等绝对业务指标
只适用排序/推荐这类结果可交错的界面
单会话设计，抓不到长期行为变化（如新奇效应消退、留存）
需要更多 GPU 才能运行，是它比 A/B 更贵的主要原因
options_en: Measures only relative preference, giving no absolute business metrics like revenue or session length.
Only fits rankable surfaces like ranking/recommendation where results can be interleaved.
Single-session design misses long-term behavioral shifts (novelty fading, retention).
It needs more GPUs to run, the main reason it costs more than A/B.
optionExplanations: 对；它只告诉你「哪个排序更受偏好」，测不出这偏好是否转化为营收或时长，绝对指标得靠 A/B。
对；交错要求两套结果能合并成一个列表，购物车、结账等非排序界面无法这样交错。
对；一次会话内的偏好抓不到几周后的行为变化，长期效应仍需 A/B 观察窗。
错；interleaving 反而更省样本、更便宜，GPU 成本不是它的局限。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it tells you which ranking is preferred but not whether that converts to revenue or time; absolute metrics need A/B.
Correct — interleaving requires two result sets mergeable into one list; non-ranking surfaces like carts or checkout can't interleave.
Correct — one session's preference can't capture behavioral change weeks later, so long-term effects still need an A/B window.
Wrong — interleaving is cheaper and more sample-efficient; GPU cost is not its limitation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对新功能一开始的短暂追捧，随时间消退；单会话实验容易被它误导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users' brief initial enthusiasm for a new feature that fades over time, which single-session experiments can mistake for real gains.

scenario: 你有 10 个候选排序器，想又快又稳地选出最终上线的那个。面试里怎么组合 interleaving 和 A/B？
scenario_en: You have 10 candidate rankers and want to pick the launch one quickly yet reliably; how do you combine interleaving and A/B?
q: 把「interleaving 初筛 → A/B 收口」的两阶段流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the two-stage 'interleaving screen then A/B confirm' funnel:
steps: 用 interleaving 快速初筛，凭相对偏好淘汰明显更差的排序器
把候选缩到 1-2 个 finalist
对 finalist 跑完整 A/B，测营收/留存等绝对业务影响
按绝对指标做最终上线决策
why: 先用便宜的 interleaving 从一堆候选里快速砍到 1-2 个，再对少数 finalist 花贵的完整 A/B 测绝对影响、做上线决策。这样既拿到 interleaving 的速度，又保住 A/B 的绝对可信度，是漏斗式取信号。
why_en: Use cheap interleaving to narrow many candidates to 1-2 finalists, then spend a full A/B on those to measure absolute impact and decide — a funnel combining interleaving's speed with A/B's trustworthiness.
diagram:
flowchart LR N["10 候选排序器"] --> I["interleaving 初筛
相对偏好"] I --> F["1-2 个 finalist"] F --> AB["完整 A/B
绝对影响"] AB --> D["上线决策"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 经初筛后进入最终评估的少数候选方案，只对它们花昂贵的完整实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finalist is one of the few candidates surviving screening, on which you spend the expensive full experiment.

scenario: 面试官问：多臂老虎机（MAB）跟固定 50/50 的 A/B 到底有什么本质区别？
scenario_en: Interviewer: how is a multi-armed bandit (MAB) fundamentally different from a fixed 50/50 A/B?
q: 多臂老虎机（MAB）相对固定 A/B 的核心差别是什么？
q_en: What is a MAB's core difference from a fixed A/B?
why: MAB 在实验进行中就把流量动态倾斜向表现更好的 arm，而不是全程固定 50/50。这样能边学边少烧钱在差 arm 上，代价是分配随时间变化（非平稳），让固定终点的统计推断变难。
why_en: A MAB shifts traffic toward the better arm mid-experiment instead of a fixed 50/50, spending less on losers but making fixed-horizon inference harder.
options: MAB 也全程固定 50/50，只是最后用不同公式算显著性
MAB 需要更多 arm，至少 8 个才能启动，2 个 arm 用不了
MAB 在实验中动态把流量倾向表现更好的 arm，而非固定 50/50
MAB 只能离线跑，不能在线分配真实流量
options_en: A MAB also stays a fixed 50/50 throughout and just uses a different formula for significance at the end.
A MAB needs more arms, at least 8 to start, and can't run with only 2 arms.
A MAB dynamically shifts traffic toward the better-performing arm mid-experiment rather than a fixed 50/50.
A MAB can only run offline and cannot allocate real online traffic.
optionExplanations: 固定 50/50 正是 A/B 的做法，MAB 的整个卖点就是打破它、自适应分配。
MAB 对 arm 数没有下限，2 个 arm 也能跑；多 arm 只是它相对 A/B 的一个优势场景。
对；动态倾斜流量让它「边服务边学习」、减少累计后悔值，代价是分配非平稳。
MAB 就是在线自适应分配真实流量的框架，不是离线方法。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed 50/50 is exactly what A/B does; a MAB's whole point is to break it with adaptive allocation.
A MAB has no minimum arm count; 2 arms work fine, and many arms is just one of its advantage cases.
Correct — dynamic traffic shifting lets it 'learn while serving' and cut cumulative regret, at the cost of non-stationary allocation.
A MAB is precisely an online framework that adaptively allocates real traffic, not an offline method.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多臂老虎机：在多个候选（arm）间自适应分配流量、边学边把流量导向更优 arm 的实验框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAB (Multi-Armed Bandit) is an experiment framework that adaptively allocates traffic across arms, learning and shifting traffic toward better arms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 老虎机里的一个候选选项（如一个版本/一条 headline），MAB 要决定给每个 arm 多少流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An arm is one candidate option (a version/headline); the MAB decides how much traffic each arm gets.

scenario: MAB 每一步都要决定：给已知最好的 arm 更多流量，还是给不确定的 arm 一些流量去多了解它？
scenario_en: At each step a MAB must decide: send more traffic to the known-best arm, or give uncertain arms traffic to learn about them?
q: MAB 里的 exploration vs exploitation 张力是什么，累计后悔值指什么？
q_en: What is the exploration-vs-exploitation tension in a MAB, and what is cumulative regret?
why: Exploitation 把流量给当前最好的 arm 拿即时收益，exploration 分流量给不确定 arm 以免错过最优；累计后悔值是没选到最优 arm 而损失的总奖励，MAB 要把它压到最小。
why_en: Exploitation sends traffic to the currently best arm for immediate reward, exploration samples uncertain arms to avoid missing the true best, and cumulative regret is the total reward lost by not always picking the optimal arm.
tradeoff: Exploitation（拿即时收益，但可能错过更好的 arm）vs exploration（多了解 arm，但短期烧掉一些奖励）
options: Exploitation 给当前最好 arm 拿即时收益，exploration 分流量给不确定 arm；后悔值=没选到最优 arm 损失的总奖励
Exploration 指往候选列表里不断多加新的 arm，exploitation 指把表现差的 arm 逐个删掉，后悔值就是整个实验里被删掉的 arm 的总数量
两者是同义词，都指把流量全给最好的 arm，后悔值指实验总时长
Exploitation 是随机分配，exploration 是固定 50/50，后悔值是 p 值大小
options_en: Exploitation sends traffic to the current best arm for immediate reward, exploration samples uncertain arms; regret = total reward lost by not picking the optimal arm.
Exploration means continually adding new arms to the candidate list, exploitation means deleting the weak arms one by one, and regret is the total count of arms deleted over the whole experiment.
They are synonyms, both meaning give all traffic to the best arm, and regret is the total experiment duration.
Exploitation is random allocation, exploration is a fixed 50/50, and regret is the size of the p-value.
optionExplanations: 对；这正是 MAB 的核心张力，最小化累计后悔值就是在「即时收益」和「信息获取」之间动态平衡。
exploration/exploitation 说的是流量分配策略，不是增删 arm；后悔值是损失的奖励不是 arm 数。
两者是对立而非同义：全给最好 arm 是纯 exploitation，会因估计错误吃亏。
把定义完全对调了，且后悔值与 p 值是两个不同概念。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this is the MAB's core tension; minimizing cumulative regret balances immediate reward against information gain.
Exploration/exploitation are traffic-allocation strategies, not adding/removing arms; regret is lost reward, not arm count.
They are opposites, not synonyms: giving all traffic to the best arm is pure exploitation and suffers from estimation error.
It swaps the definitions and confuses regret with the p-value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整个实验里因为没有始终选中真正最优 arm 而少拿到的奖励总和；MAB 的优化目标是最小化它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cumulative regret is the total reward lost over the experiment by not always choosing the truly optimal arm; the MAB minimizes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 探索：分流量给不确定 arm 以获取信息；利用：把流量给当前估计最好的 arm 拿即时收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exploration sends traffic to uncertain arms for information; exploitation sends it to the current best arm for immediate reward.

scenario: 选一个 bandit 分配策略，你在 epsilon-greedy、UCB、Thompson Sampling 之间权衡探索方式。
scenario_en: Choosing a bandit allocation strategy, you weigh how epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson Sampling explore.
q: epsilon-greedy、UCB、Thompson Sampling 的探索机制分别是什么？
q_en: How do epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson Sampling each explore?
why: epsilon-greedy 以 ε 概率随机探索；UCB 给估计奖励加随样本缩小的置信奖励、定向探不确定 arm；Thompson 按奖励后验分布采样选 arm，工业最常用。
why_en: Epsilon-greedy explores randomly with probability epsilon, UCB adds a shrinking confidence bonus to favor uncertain arms, and Thompson Sampling samples from a Bayesian posterior over each arm's reward rate.
tradeoff: epsilon-greedy（简单但盲目探索）vs UCB（定向探不确定 arm）vs Thompson（贝叶斯采样，探索自然衰减）

rows: 以 ε 概率随机探
加置信奖励，随样本缩小

options: 三者其实都是固定 50/50 分配流量到实验结束，只是最后算显著性时公式名字不同
epsilon-greedy 随机探索、UCB 用置信奖励定向探、Thompson 按后验采样选 arm
epsilon-greedy 其实是贝叶斯方法、UCB 完全不做任何探索、Thompson 全靠随机数瞎猜，三者互不相关也没有共同框架
三者都要求先跑完整 A/B 才能启动，属于 A/B 的后处理步骤
options_en: All three actually hold a fixed 50/50 allocation until the experiment ends, differing only in the name of the significance formula at the end.
Epsilon-greedy explores randomly, UCB uses a confidence bonus to target exploration, Thompson samples from the posterior.
Epsilon-greedy is actually the Bayesian method, UCB does no exploration whatsoever, and Thompson relies purely on random guessing — the three are unrelated with no shared framework.
All three require a full A/B to finish first, being post-processing steps of A/B.
optionExplanations: 固定 50/50 是 A/B，不是 bandit；三者的分配都是自适应的。
对；三者探索方式不同——盲目随机、置信上界定向、后验采样，越往后探索越「聪明」，Thompson 工业最常用。
说反了：贝叶斯是 Thompson，UCB 靠置信奖励主动探索，三者都在做探索/利用平衡。
bandit 是独立框架，不是 A/B 的后处理，也不需要先跑完 A/B。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed 50/50 is A/B, not a bandit; all three allocate adaptively.
Correct — the three explore differently: blind random, upper-confidence targeting, posterior sampling, getting smarter in that order, with Thompson most used industrially.
Backwards: Bayesian is Thompson, UCB actively explores via a confidence bonus, and all three balance explore/exploit.
Bandits are a standalone framework, not A/B post-processing, and don't require a finished A/B.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以 1−ε 概率选当前最好 arm、以 ε 概率随机探索其他 arm 的简单 bandit 策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon-greedy picks the current best arm with probability 1 minus epsilon and explores a random arm with probability epsilon.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个 arm 的估计奖励加一个随样本增多而缩小的置信奖励，优先探索不确定的 arm。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UCB (Upper Confidence Bound) adds a confidence bonus, shrinking as samples grow, to each arm's estimated reward, favoring uncertain arms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个 arm 的奖励率维护后验分布，每次从后验采样再选采样值最高的 arm 的贝叶斯策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson Sampling keeps a posterior over each arm's reward rate and samples from it to choose an arm — a Bayesian strategy.

scenario: 一条突发新闻只在 6 小时内相关，你有 8 个标题变体，目标是最大化这段时间的总点击率（CTR）。
scenario_en: A breaking story is relevant for only 6 hours; you have 8 headline variants and want to maximize total CTR over that window.
q: 这种「短命、多变体、要最大化总收益」的场景该用哪种实验？
q_en: Which experiment fits a short-lived, many-variant, maximize-total-reward scenario?
why: 用带 Thompson Sampling 的多臂老虎机：6 小时窗口太短，A/B 固定 50/50 会把曝光浪费在差标题上，8 个变体等分更吃不饱样本；bandit 边学边导流，直接最大化总 CTR。
why_en: Use a multi-armed bandit with Thompson Sampling because the 6-hour window is too short for a fixed 50/50 A/B, and adaptive allocation shifts traffic to the best of 8 headlines to maximize total CTR.
tradeoff: Bandit（边学边赚、少烧差 arm，但固定终点推断难）vs A/B（干净因果，但短窗+多变体下浪费曝光）
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是拿到一个能长期复用、可做严格因果推断的绝对结论（而非最大化这一次的总收益），标准 A/B 的干净 p 值更合适。
options: 标准 A/B，把 8 个变体各分 1/8 固定流量，等跑满 6 小时收集完全部数据后再统一比较谁的 CTR 最高
带 Thompson Sampling 的多臂老虎机，边学边把流量导向表现好的标题，最大化窗口内总 CTR
Interleaving，把 8 个标题两两交错进同一个列表，靠点击归因比出相对偏好谁更受欢迎
Switchback，按城市或时间段每 30 分钟在 8 个标题间整体切换一次，观察哪个窗口点击率更高
options_en: Standard A/B: give each of the 8 variants a fixed 1/8 of traffic, run the full 6 hours, collect all the data, and only then compare whose CTR is highest.
A multi-armed bandit with Thompson Sampling, learning and shifting traffic to the best headline to maximize total CTR in the window.
Interleaving: merge all 8 headlines pairwise into one shared list and use click attribution to rank relative preference among them.
Switchback: switch the whole city or time segment among the 8 headlines every 30 minutes and see which window gets a higher click rate.
optionExplanations: 8 等分 + 固定分配意味着到实验结束才收敛，6 小时里大半曝光烧在差标题上，总 CTR 被拖低。
对；6 小时窗口配 8 个标题正是 bandit 的主场——流量会自动倾向点击好的那条，总点击不会被差标题拖累。
interleaving 只测「哪个更受偏好」的相对信号，不最大化总收益，也不适合 8 个并列文本变体。
switchback 是给双边市场干扰设计的（按时间/地域切），这里没有司机共享池，用错了工具。
optionExplanations_en: An 8-way even split with fixed allocation only converges at the end, wasting most impressions on weak headlines over 6 hours.
Correct — a 6-hour window with 8 headlines is exactly a bandit's home turf: traffic drifts on its own toward whichever headline clicks best, so nothing gets wasted on the losers.
Interleaving measures relative preference, not total reward, and doesn't fit 8 parallel text variants.
Switchback is for marketplace interference (switching by time/region); with no shared driver pool, it's the wrong tool.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示中被点击的比例，这里是要在 6 小时内最大化的目标奖励。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions clicked, here the reward to maximize within 6 hours.

scenario: 你用 bandit 跑了一个实验，想在结束时像 A/B 一样报一个 p 值下结论。
scenario_en: You ran a bandit experiment and want to report an end-of-experiment p-value like an A/B.
why: bandit 的自适应分配是非平稳的（各 arm 流量随时间变），违背固定终点检验假设的等概率、独立同分布，直接算末尾 p 值不成立、会给出错误显著性。缓解方向是专门设计，如混合自适应设计（MAD）在自适应分配里保留可做有效推断的部分。
why_en: Bandit allocation is non-stationary, which invalidates fixed-horizon p-values, so use designs like mixture adaptive design (MAD) that preserve valid inference.
q: 为什么 bandit 让「实验结束算 p 值」这件事变得不可靠？怎么补救？
q_en: Why do bandits make end-of-experiment p-values unreliable, and how do you fix it?
options: 非平稳的自适应分配违背固定终点检验假设，末尾 p 值失效；用混合自适应设计（MAD）保留可推断部分
bandit 的 p 值天然更准，因为样本都集中在表现好的 arm 上、噪声更少，末尾直接算就行，无需任何额外补救
问题只是样本不够多，把实验时长翻倍、样本堆够，末尾 p 值就恢复有效
bandit 根本不产生任何指标，无所谓 p 值，直接看总奖励即可，不存在推断问题
options_en: Non-stationary adaptive allocation violates fixed-horizon test assumptions, invalidating end p-values; use mixture adaptive design (MAD) to preserve valid inference.
Bandit p-values are naturally more accurate because samples concentrate on the better-performing arms with less noise, so you can just compute one at the end with no extra fix needed.
It's only a sample-size issue; double the duration and pile on samples and the end p-value becomes valid again.
Bandits produce no metrics at all, so p-values are irrelevant — just read total reward; there is no inference problem.
optionExplanations: 对；非平稳分配破坏了固定终点检验对等概率、独立同分布的假设，MAD 这类设计专门在自适应中留出可做有效推断的结构。
样本集中在好 arm 恰恰让分布非平稳、推断更难，不是更准。
堆样本不解决非平稳这个结构问题；p 值失效是分配随时间变导致的，不是样本量不够。
bandit 当然有指标（奖励、CTR），只是固定终点推断需要特殊处理，不能说没有推断问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — non-stationary allocation breaks the equal-probability, i.i.d. assumptions of fixed-horizon tests; MAD preserves a structure for valid inference.
Concentrating samples on good arms is exactly what makes the distribution non-stationary and inference harder, not more accurate.
More samples don't fix the structural non-stationarity; p-values fail because allocation changes over time, not from too few samples.
Bandits do have metrics (reward, CTR); fixed-horizon inference just needs special handling, so the problem is real.

termDefinitions.term: fixed-horizon inference / 固定终点推断
termDefinitions.meaning: 在预先设定的样本量/时间点上做一次显著性检验（如 A/B 的末尾 p 值），要求分配平稳、独立同分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fixed-horizon inference runs one significance test at a preset sample size or time (like A/B's end p-value), assuming stationary, i.i.d. allocation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 混合自适应设计：在自适应分配里混入一部分可做有效统计推断的结构，缓解 bandit 破坏 p 值的问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAD (Mixture Adaptive Design) blends a share of statistically valid structure into adaptive allocation to restore inference under bandits.

scenario: 面试里要一句话点出 bandit 和 A/B 各自「为什么而生」。
scenario_en: In an interview, capture in one line what bandits vs A/B each optimize for.
q: 一句话对比：bandit 和 A/B 各自优化的是什么？
q_en: In one line, what do bandits vs A/B each optimize?
why: bandit 优化「边服务边学习」——在实验期就尽量多赚、少烧差 arm；A/B 优化「干净的因果测量」——牺牲实验期收益换一个可信、可推断的绝对结论。选哪个取决于你更在意实验期收益还是结论的因果纯度。
why_en: Bandits optimize learning-while-serving (earn during the experiment), while A/B optimizes clean causal measurement (a trustworthy absolute conclusion).
tradeoff: Bandit（实验期收益最大化，但因果推断难）vs A/B（干净因果结论，但实验期要付浪费成本）
options: 两者都只优化统计功效，唯一区别是 bandit 更快
bandit 优化实验期总收益，A/B 其实也在优化实验期总收益，只是分配比例不同，二者的根本目标完全一致
bandit 优化「边服务边学习」的实验期收益，A/B 优化「干净的因果测量」
A/B 优化实验期收益、bandit 优化因果纯度，正好相反
options_en: Both optimize only statistical power, differing only in that bandits are faster.
Bandits optimize in-experiment total reward, and A/B actually optimizes in-experiment total reward too, just with a different split ratio — their fundamental goal is identical.
Bandits optimize in-experiment reward (learning while serving); A/B optimizes clean causal measurement.
A/B optimizes in-experiment reward and bandits optimize causal purity — exactly reversed.
optionExplanations: 统计功效只是 A/B 关心的一面；bandit 关心的是实验期少烧钱，两者目标根本不同。
A/B 不优化实验期收益——它固定 50/50、甘愿在差 arm 上付浪费成本换干净结论。
对；这就是那句可带走的对比——bandit 边赚边学，A/B 用实验期成本买因果纯度。
方向说反了：bandit 才是优化实验期收益的那个，A/B 才是买因果纯度的那个。
optionExplanations_en: Statistical power is only one A/B concern; a bandit's goal is spending less mid-experiment — different objectives.
A/B doesn't optimize in-experiment reward — it holds 50/50 and pays the waste to buy a clean conclusion.
Correct — that's the takeaway line: bandits earn while learning, A/B pays in-experiment cost for causal purity.
Reversed: bandits optimize in-experiment reward, and A/B buys causal purity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把结果差异干净地归因到「版本」这一处理变量，而非人群或时间的混淆，A/B 的核心价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Causal measurement cleanly attributes an outcome difference to the treatment (the version) rather than population or time confounders — A/B's core value.

scenario: Uber/DoorDash 想测新定价。骑手和司机共享同一个司机池：给一半骑手涨价会改变另一半（对照组）能叫到的车，两组不再独立。
scenario_en: Uber/DoorDash want to test new pricing. Riders share one driver pool: pricing up for half the riders changes car availability for the other (control) half, so arms aren't independent.
q: 这种共享司机池的双边市场该用哪种实验设计？
q_en: Which design fits a shared-driver-pool marketplace?
why: 用 switchback：按用户随机会因共享司机池干扰、违背 SUTVA，估计有偏；改成按「城市 × 30-60 分钟时间窗」整体切换处理——随机化单位是区域-时间块，不是用户数，块内所有人同处理、消掉干扰。
why_en: Use switchback because user-level randomization causes interference via the shared driver pool, violating SUTVA; instead randomize time windows within a region so everyone in a city-time block gets the same arm.
tradeoff: Switchback（消掉市场干扰，但有跨窗残留效应）vs 用户级 A/B（干净随机，但共享供给下干扰致偏）
whenOtherWins: 如果处理不共享稀缺供给、一个用户的体验不影响另一个用户（如纯前端 UI 改动），普通用户级 A/B 就够，不必上 switchback。
options: 用户级 A/B：把骑手随机分成两组、各自只看一种定价方案，实现起来简单直接、上线也快
Switchback：在地理区域内按时间窗随机，城市每 30-60 分钟整体切换处理，块内所有人同处理
Interleaving：把两种定价方案交错展示给同一个骑手，让他在同一次下单流程里同时看到两种价格再择优
准实验 DiD：直接拿涨价的城市和没涨价的城市的完单率指标做事后对比，不做任何随机化
options_en: User-level A/B: randomly split riders into two groups, each seeing only one pricing scheme — simple, direct, and quick to ship.
Switchback: randomize time windows within a region; a city switches its arm every 30-60 minutes, everyone in a block gets the same arm.
Interleaving: interleave the two pricing schemes for the same rider so they see both prices at once within a single order flow and pick the better one.
Quasi-experiment DiD: just compare completion-rate metrics between a price-raised city and a non-raised city after the fact, no randomization at all.
optionExplanations: 用户级 A/B 正是问题所在：共享司机池让处理组抢走对照组的车，两组不独立，估计有偏。
对；按城市-时间块整体切换消掉块内干扰，是共享供给市场做因果实验的标准招。
定价不能像排序结果那样交错展示给同一人，interleaving 在这里没有意义。
DiD 是没法随机时的准实验兜底；这里能主动做随机（按时间/地域），switchback 比事后观察更可信。
optionExplanations_en: User-level A/B is the very problem: the shared pool lets treatment steal cars from control, so arms aren't independent and estimates are biased.
Correct — switching whole city-time blocks removes within-block interference, the standard causal design for shared-supply markets.
Prices can't be interleaved to one person like ranked results; interleaving is meaningless here.
DiD is the fallback when randomization is impossible; here you can randomize by time/region, so switchback beats after-the-fact observation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在地理区域内按时间窗随机的实验：一个区域每隔一段时间整体在 treatment/控制间切换，用来消掉共享供给下的干扰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A switchback experiment randomizes time windows within a region, switching the whole region between treatment and control periodically to remove shared-supply interference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 稳定单元处理值假设：一个单元的结果只取决于它自己受的处理，不受别人处理影响；共享司机池会破坏它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SUTVA (Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption) says a unit's outcome depends only on its own treatment, not others'; a shared driver pool breaks it.

scenario: 在共享司机池的市场里坚持按骑手随机分组，测新定价对完单率的影响。
