Async batch: compute citywide ETAs once a night and serve every daytime request from a lookup.
Hard-code ETA as a fixed distance-based value that never changes with live traffic.
optionExplanations: ETA 不需要亚 100ms 同步响应，硬上同步是过度设计、成本更高，还没必要。
对；秒级持续更新、贴近当前路况，正是流式的定位，填补同步与批处理之间的新鲜度空档。
每晚算一次太陈旧，跟不上实时变化的路况，批处理的新鲜度不够。
写死 ETA 完全丢掉了随路况更新的需求，等于没有预测。
optionExplanations_en: ETA doesn't need sub-100ms synchronous response; forcing sync over-engineers it at higher cost for no benefit.
Correct — seconds-level continuous updates close to current traffic is streaming's niche, filling the freshness gap between sync and batch.
Nightly is too stale for live-changing traffic; batch's freshness is insufficient.
Hard-coding ETA drops the update-with-traffic requirement, effectively no prediction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件经消息队列进流处理器，计算窗口特征并打分，秒到分钟级更新的服务范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming near-real-time routes events through a queue into a stream processor that computes windowed features and scores in seconds to minutes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计到达时间，需随路况持续更新，是流式服务的典型应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) must update continuously with traffic — a canonical streaming use case.

scenario: 要画一个流式服务的数据流：从事件到打分结果落地。
scenario_en: Sketch a streaming service's data flow from event to scored result.
q: 流式近实时服务的典型管线是什么？
q_en: What is the typical streaming near-real-time pipeline?
why: 事件 → 消息队列（Kafka）→ 流处理器（Flink 或 Spark 结构化流）算窗口特征并打分 → 写低延迟存储或触发下游动作。因为它在 HTTP 往返之外异步处理，可以用比同步更重的模型/集成。
why_en: Events to a message queue (Kafka) to a stream processor (Flink or Spark Structured Streaming) that computes windowed features and scores, then writes to a low-latency store or downstream actions.
diagram:
flowchart LR E["事件"] --> K["消息队列
Kafka"] --> F["流处理器
Flink/Spark Streaming"] F --> W["窗口特征+打分"] --> S["低延迟存储/下游动作"]
options: 请求→模型服务器→一次 HTTP 往返内同步返回结果
事件→Kafka→Flink 算窗口特征打分→写低延迟存储
每晚 Spark 跑一次全量打分写进 KV，白天所有请求查表
把模型下发到客户端，所有事件都在端上本地处理不回传
options_en: Request to model server, synchronous return in one HTTP round-trip.
Events to Kafka, Flink computes windowed features and scores, then writes to a low-latency store.
Nightly Spark scores everything into a KV store and all daytime requests are lookups.
Ship the model to clients so every event is processed locally on-device and never sent back.
optionExplanations: 一次 HTTP 往返同步返回是同步范式，不是事件驱动的流式管线。
对；队列+流处理器+窗口特征打分+写低延迟存储，正是流式近实时的标准管线。
每晚全量打分查表是异步批处理，不是持续处理事件的流式。
端上处理是另一类；流式是服务端消费事件流做窗口计算与打分。
optionExplanations_en: A synchronous one-round-trip return is the sync paradigm, not an event-driven streaming pipeline.
Correct — queue plus stream processor plus windowed-feature scoring into a low-latency store is the streaming standard.
Nightly full scoring with lookups is async batch, not continuous event streaming.
On-device is different; streaming consumes an event stream server-side for windowed computation and scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/事件流平台，作为流式管线的入口缓冲并解耦事件生产与消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue / event-streaming platform that buffers and decouples event producers from consumers at a streaming pipeline's entry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理引擎，对事件流做有状态的窗口聚合与打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink and Spark Structured Streaming are stream processors that do stateful windowed aggregation and scoring over event streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一段滑动/滚动时间窗内聚合事件算出的特征（如近 30 秒浏览数）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A windowed feature is aggregated over a sliding/tumbling time window (e.g. views in the last 30 seconds).

scenario: 同步服务因延迟预算只能跑压缩过的小模型，你想用更强的集成模型但又要一定新鲜度。
scenario_en: A sync service can only run a compressed small model due to latency budget, but you want a stronger ensemble with some freshness.
q: 为什么流式范式能跑比同步更重的模型？
q_en: Why can streaming run heavier models than synchronous?
why: 因为流式在 HTTP 往返之外异步处理事件，不受「用户在同步等待」的严格延迟预算约束，秒级完成即可。少了这道紧箍咒，就能跑更大的模型或集成来换质量，而同步必须靠量化/蒸馏压小以守住毫秒预算。
why_en: Because streaming processes events asynchronously off the HTTP round-trip, free of sync's strict user-waiting latency budget, so it can run bigger models or ensembles that sync must shrink via quantization/distillation.
options: 因为它在 HTTP 往返之外异步处理，不受同步的延迟预算约束
因为流式框架会自动把模型裁剪得比同步用的更小更快
因为流式其实不跑模型，只做规则匹配和阈值告警
因为流式跑在更贵的专用推理芯片上，算力几乎无上限
options_en: Because it runs asynchronously off the HTTP round-trip, free of sync’s latency budget.
Because streaming frameworks automatically prune models smaller and faster than sync’s.
Because streaming runs no model at all, only rule matching and threshold alerts.
Because streaming runs on pricier dedicated inference chips with nearly unlimited compute.
optionExplanations: 对；脱离同步的即时延迟预算，秒级窗口内可跑更重的模型或集成，这正是流式的一个优势。
流式的模型可以更大不是更小，正因为它有更宽的延迟余量。
流式当然要用模型打分，不是纯规则匹配。
跑什么芯片和范式无关；关键是流式的异步性放宽了延迟预算，不是算力无限。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — off sync's instant latency budget, a seconds-level window can run heavier models or ensembles, a streaming advantage.
Streaming's models can be larger, not smaller, precisely because it has more latency headroom.
Streaming does use a model to score, not pure rule matching.
The chip is unrelated to paradigm; streaming's async nature relaxes the latency budget, it isn't unlimited compute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组合多个模型的预测以提升质量的方案，计算更重、延迟更高，同步范式常负担不起。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble combines multiple models' predictions for quality at higher compute and latency, often unaffordable in the sync paradigm.

scenario: 有人主张「流式就是更快的批处理，直接换上就行」，你要点出它的真实运维难点。
scenario_en: Someone claims 'streaming is just faster batch, swap it in', and you must surface its real operational hard parts.
q: 流式近实时有哪些核心工程挑战？(多选)
q_en: What are streaming near-real-time's core engineering challenges? (multiple)
why: 三大挑战：精确一次处理语义（事件不重不漏地被处理一次）；窗口特征与训练口径一致（否则产生偏斜）；管线维护（检查点、背压等有状态运维）。流式不是「更快的批处理」，其运维成本常被低估。它不比批处理便宜，成本不是这里的挑战点。
why_en: The hard parts are exactly-once semantics, windowed-feature consistency with training (else skew), and pipeline maintenance (checkpointing, backpressure); streaming isn't just faster batch and its op cost is underestimated.
options: 精确一次处理语义：事件不重不漏地恰好处理一次
窗口特征与训练口径一致，否则产生训练-服务偏斜
有状态管线维护：检查点、背压等运维负担
它一定比批处理更便宜，成本从不是问题
options_en: Exactly-once processing semantics: each event processed exactly once, no duplicates or drops.
Windowed-feature consistency with training, else training-serving skew results.
Stateful pipeline maintenance: checkpointing, backpressure, and related operational burden.
It's always cheaper than batch, so cost is never an issue.
optionExplanations: 对；流处理最难的保证之一就是精确一次，重复或丢事件都会污染特征和结果。
对；线上窗口特征若和训练时算法不一致，就会引入偏斜，是流式特有的一致性难点。
对；有状态流处理要管检查点、背压，运维复杂度远高于无状态服务。
错；流式运维成本常被低估、不比批处理便宜，成本反而是要警惕的点，不是「从不是问题」。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — exactly-once is one of stream processing's hardest guarantees; duplicates or drops corrupt features and results.
Correct — if online windowed features differ from training's computation, skew appears, a streaming-specific consistency challenge.
Correct — stateful streaming must manage checkpointing and backpressure, far more operationally complex than stateless serving.
Wrong — streaming's op cost is underestimated and it isn't cheaper than batch; cost is a caution, not a non-issue.

termDefinitions.term: exactly-once semantics / 精确一次语义
termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理保证每个事件恰好被处理一次，既不丢也不重复，避免特征/计数被污染。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once semantics guarantee each event is processed once — no drops or duplicates — so features and counts aren't corrupted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游处理速度跟不上上游事件速率时的反向节流机制，防止系统被淹没。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is a reverse throttling mechanism when downstream can't keep up with the upstream event rate, preventing overload.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期保存流处理的状态快照，故障后可从检查点恢复，保证有状态计算不丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Checkpointing periodically snapshots stream-processing state so it can recover after failure without losing stateful computation.

scenario: 你同时维护批处理特征库和流式特征库，担心两边同一个特征算出来不一致，导致模型行为漂移。
scenario_en: You maintain both a batch and a streaming feature store and fear the same feature diverging across them, drifting model behavior.
q: 为什么流式常配 dual-write（双写）模式，它解决什么？
q_en: Why does streaming often use a dual-write pattern, and what does it solve?
why: 双写让同一份特征同时写进批处理特征库和流式特征库，保持两边一致，避免「批算的特征和流算的特征对不上」造成的偏斜与漂移。代价是写路径更复杂、要处理两边一致性和失败重试。
why_en: Dual-write writes the same feature into both batch and streaming feature stores to keep them consistent, avoiding skew/drift from divergent feature values, at the cost of a more complex write path.
options: 把同一特征同时写进批处理和流式特征库，保证两边一致
双写指把模型复制两份同时跑，纯粹为了冗余和灰度备份
双写指每条数据写两遍数据库副本，用来提高读吞吐
双写是把预测结果同时发给用户和日志，与特征一致性无关
options_en: It writes the same feature into both the batch and streaming stores so the two stay consistent.
Dual-write means running two copies of the model at once, purely for redundancy and canary backup.
Dual-write means writing each record to two database replicas to raise read throughput.
Dual-write means sending predictions to both the user and logs, unrelated to feature consistency.
optionExplanations: 对；把特征同步写进两个特征库保持口径一致，正是双写要解决的批/流特征不一致问题。
双写针对的是特征库一致性，不是模型副本冗余。
写两遍库提读性能是别的概念，双写解决的是批/流两套特征库对齐。
双写关乎特征一致性，不是把预测同时发用户和日志。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — synchronizing the feature into both stores to keep definitions aligned is exactly what dual-write solves.
Dual-write targets feature-store consistency, not model-copy redundancy.
Writing twice for read performance is a different concept; dual-write aligns the batch and streaming feature stores.
Dual-write concerns feature consistency, not sending predictions to both user and logs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一份特征同时写入批处理与流式两个特征库，使两边取值一致，抑制偏斜和漂移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dual-write writes the same feature into both the batch and streaming feature stores so values stay consistent, suppressing skew and drift.

scenario: 团队打算把一个批处理特征管线直接改成流式，理由是「流式就是更快的批处理」。
scenario_en: The team plans to convert a batch feature pipeline to streaming, reasoning 'streaming is just faster batch'.
q: 把「流式=更快的批处理」当决策依据有什么风险？
q_en: What's the risk of treating 'streaming = faster batch' as a decision basis?
why: 风险是低估了流式的运维成本：它需要精确一次语义、有状态检查点、背压处理、窗口一致性等，这些持续的运维负担在批处理里根本不存在。把它当「更快的批处理」会漏算这些成本，上线后被运维复杂度反噬。
why_en: The risk is underestimating streaming's operational cost — exactly-once, checkpointing, backpressure, window consistency — none of which batch has, so treating it as faster batch undercounts ongoing ops burden.
options: 没有风险，流式确实只是更快的批处理，直接换更好
低估运维成本：精确一次、检查点、背压这些批处理都没有
风险只是延迟略高一点，功能和结果上和批处理没有差别
风险是流式一定更便宜，会让预算花不完而被下一年砍掉
options_en: No risk — streaming really is just faster batch, so swapping in is strictly better.
It underestimates ops cost: exactly-once, checkpointing, and backpressure simply do not exist in batch.
The only risk is slightly higher latency; functionally the results match batch.
The risk is streaming being always cheaper, leaving budget unspent and cut next year.
optionExplanations: 流式不是「更快的批处理」，它引入了一整套批处理没有的有状态运维负担。
对；持续的精确一次/检查点/背压/窗口一致性成本常被低估，这是那句「不只是更快的批处理」的告诫。
差别远不止延迟：语义保证和有状态运维是本质不同，功能与可靠性都不一样。
流式通常比批处理更贵、运维更重，不会让预算花不完。
optionExplanations_en: Streaming isn't 'faster batch'; it introduces a whole stateful ops burden batch lacks.
Correct — ongoing exactly-once/checkpointing/backpressure/window-consistency costs are underestimated, the point of 'not just faster batch'.
The difference is far beyond latency: semantic guarantees and stateful ops are fundamentally different in function and reliability.
Streaming is usually costlier and more ops-heavy than batch, not budget-saving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统上线后持续运行、监控、故障恢复所需的人力与资源投入；流式的这部分成本常被低估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Operational cost is the ongoing human and resource effort to run, monitor, and recover a system in production; streaming's is commonly underestimated.

scenario: 面试官提醒：命名服务范式之前，应先讲清哪三个约束？
scenario_en: The interviewer hints: before naming a serving paradigm, which three constraints should you state?
q: 选服务范式前，应先明确哪三个约束、并按谁做第一决策轴？
q_en: Before choosing a paradigm, which three constraints do you state, and which is the first axis?
why: 先说清延迟 SLA、预估 QPS、新鲜度要求这三条约束，再命名范式，体现约束驱动的推理。第一决策轴是延迟预算：请求路径上要亚 100ms（广告/搜索/欺诈）→ 必须同步；可容忍小时级 → 批处理；要新鲜但毫秒不强求（会话/异常）→ 流式。
why_en: State latency SLA, estimated QPS, and freshness first, then name the paradigm; the first axis is the latency budget — sub-100ms on the request path forces sync, hours-tolerant means batch, fresh-but-not-ms means streaming.
tradeoff: 先声明延迟/QPS/新鲜度再选范式（约束驱动）vs 先拍范式（易与真实约束错配）
whenOtherWins: 如果延迟预算宽松（小时级可接受），第一决策轴就退给成本/吞吐，直接选最便宜的批处理，而不是被延迟主导。
options: 先按团队最熟的技术栈选范式，约束等设计评审时再补上
先定延迟 SLA/QPS/新鲜度三约束，以延迟预算为第一决策轴
先选最便宜的批处理，等延迟不够用了再改造成同步
只看模型大小决定范式，模型大就同步、小就批处理
options_en: Pick the paradigm from the team’s most familiar stack and backfill constraints at design review.
State latency SLA, QPS, and freshness first, then let the latency budget be the first decision axis.
Start with the cheapest batch and rebuild it into sync once latency proves insufficient.
Decide purely by model size: big model to sync, small model to batch.
optionExplanations: 按熟悉度而非约束选范式，容易和真实延迟/新鲜度需求错配，正是要避免的反模式。
对；先摆三约束、以延迟预算为第一轴，是约束驱动推理，能干净地把场景映射到范式。
无脑先选批处理会在有严格延迟需求时翻车；延迟预算应先于成本判断。
模型大小是实现细节，不是选范式的第一决策轴；延迟/新鲜度/吞吐才是。
optionExplanations_en: Choosing by familiarity rather than constraints easily mismatches real latency/freshness needs — the anti-pattern to avoid.
Correct — stating three constraints with latency budget as the first axis is constraint-driven reasoning that cleanly maps scenario to paradigm.
Blindly picking batch fails under strict latency needs; latency budget should precede the cost judgment.
Model size is an implementation detail, not the first axis; latency/freshness/throughput are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对响应时间的服务级承诺（如 p99 < 100ms），是选服务范式的第一决策轴。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency SLA is a service-level commitment on response time (e.g. p99 < 100ms), the first axis for choosing a serving paradigm.

scenario: 面试里要按约束一步步推出服务范式，而不是张口就报一个。请把决策指南排好。
scenario_en: In an interview, derive the serving paradigm step by step from constraints rather than blurting one out. Order the guide.
q: 把「选服务范式」的决策指南排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the decision guide for choosing a serving paradigm:
steps: 先看延迟预算：亚 100ms 在请求路径→同步；小时级可容忍→批；要新鲜但非毫秒→流式
再看吞吐：百万-十亿/次跑→批；高 QPS 每请求→同步+自动扩缩；持续中等→流式
用成本当平手裁决：批最便宜、同步最贵、流式居中
MAANG 常混用：批预算冷启动/兜底 + 实时给活跃用户打分，特征存储做统一层
why: 决策顺序：延迟预算是第一轴→吞吐是第二轴→成本当平手裁决→现实里混用（批做冷启动/兜底，实时给活跃用户，特征存储统一）。先延迟后吞吐再成本，最后落到 hybrid，是约束驱动的完整推理。
why_en: Latency budget first, then throughput, cost as tiebreaker, and in reality hybrid — batch for cold-start/fallback plus real-time for active users, unified by a feature store.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  L["1. 延迟预算"] --> T["2. 吞吐"]
  T --> C["3. 成本平手裁决"]
  C --> H["4. 现实多为 hybrid"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用多种服务范式：如批处理预算冷启动/兜底、实时给活跃用户打分，用特征存储统一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hybrid architecture combines paradigms — e.g. batch for cold-start/fallback plus real-time for active users — unified by a feature store.

scenario: 外卖 App 要在下单页对餐厅做重排序，依据是用户实时 GPS 和最近 30 秒的浏览行为，延迟预算 200ms，用户在等页面加载。
scenario_en: A food-delivery app re-ranks restaurants on the order page using live GPS and the last 30s of browsing, within a 200ms budget while the user waits for the page.
q: 这种实时特征 + 200ms 预算的重排序该用哪种范式？
q_en: Which paradigm fits real-time features with a 200ms budget re-rank?
why: 实时 GPS 和最近 30 秒浏览只有请求时才存在，200ms 又卡在用户等待的加载路径上，只有同步能在一次往返里取特征并打分。
why_en: Use synchronous real-time inference with a low-latency feature store because the re-rank is on the 200ms request path and depends on live GPS and last-30s browsing available only at request time.
tradeoff: 同步+低延迟特征存储（200ms 内用实时特征打分）vs 批处理（便宜但预算不到实时 GPS/浏览特征）
whenOtherWins: 如果重排序不依赖此刻的实时信号、可用预算好的结果（如首页默认榜单、新鲜度可放宽），就改用更省的批处理。
options: 异步批处理：提前把每家餐厅的排序算好存起来，下单页查表
同步实时推理 + 低延迟特征存储：200ms 内取实时特征打分
流式近实时：把浏览事件进 Kafka，几秒后再更新排序
纯规则按直线距离排序，不用模型也不取任何实时特征
options_en: Async batch: pre-compute each restaurant's ranking and look it up on the order page.
Synchronous real-time inference plus a low-latency feature store: fetch live features and score within 200ms.
Streaming near-real-time: push browsing events into Kafka and update the ranking a few seconds later.
Pure straight-line-distance rule sorting, using no model and no real-time features.
optionExplanations: 批处理提前算好的排序拿不到用户此刻的位置和刚看过的店，个性化就失效了。
对；请求时才有的信号必须在同一次往返里取到，低延迟特征存储把取特征压到个位数毫秒，才留得出模型前向的时间。
秒级的流式赶不上 200ms 预算，用户在同步等页面加载，太慢。
纯距离规则丢掉了实时浏览行为和模型个性化，达不到重排序的目标。
optionExplanations_en: A pre-computed batch ranking can't see where the user is standing now or what they just browsed, so personalization breaks.
Correct — request-time signals must be fetched inside the same round-trip, and a low-latency store keeps that fetch to single-digit ms so the forward pass still fits.
Streaming's seconds can't meet a 200ms budget while the user synchronously waits for the page — too slow.
Pure distance rules drop live browsing and model personalization, missing the re-rank goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在候选已初排的基础上，用请求时的实时特征对结果重新打分排序，追求即时个性化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking re-scores an already-ranked candidate set using request-time real-time features for immediate personalization.

scenario: 一个大规模推荐系统既要覆盖冷启动/兜底、又要给活跃用户即时个性化，单一范式顾此失彼。
scenario_en: A large-scale recommender must cover cold-start/fallback and give active users instant personalization; a single paradigm can't do both well.
q: MAANG 规模系统通常怎么组合服务范式？
q_en: How do MAANG-scale systems usually combine paradigms?
why: 用混合架构：批处理预算冷启动和兜底结果（便宜、覆盖长尾），实时推理给活跃用户做即时打分（新鲜、个性化），两者由特征存储做统一层保证特征一致。这样各取所长——批处理压成本、同步保新鲜，避免单一范式的短板。
why_en: Use a hybrid — batch pre-computes cold-start/fallback cheaply while real-time scores active users freshly, unified by a feature store — taking each paradigm's strength and avoiding its weakness.
tradeoff: 混合（批压成本+实时保新鲜，但要维护两套+统一层）vs 单一范式（简单，但顾此失彼）
whenOtherWins: 如果系统规模小、流量低、需求单一（只要便宜或只要新鲜），单一范式更简单，不必背上维护两套管线和特征统一层的复杂度。
options: 只用同步一种范式，所有预测都在线现算，简单统一
混合：批处理兜底冷启动 + 实时给活跃用户打分
只用批处理一种，牺牲所有活跃用户的新鲜度换成本
为每个用户单独搭一套独立推理管线，互不复用
options_en: Use only synchronous, computing every prediction online for simplicity and uniformity.
Hybrid: batch covers cold-start and fallback while real-time scores active users.
Use only batch, sacrificing all active users' freshness to cut cost.
Build a separate independent inference pipeline per user with no reuse across them.
optionExplanations: 全同步在冷启动和长尾上白烧算力，成本失控，也没必要对不活跃用户实时现算。
对；批做便宜的冷启动/兜底、实时给活跃用户保新鲜，特征存储统一口径，是 MAANG 的主流做法。
全批处理让活跃用户吃陈旧结果，损失即时个性化，顾此失彼。
为每个用户单独搭管线不可扩展、无法复用，工程上不成立。
optionExplanations_en: All-sync wastes compute on cold-start and the long tail, blowing up cost with no need to infer live for inactive users.
Correct — batch for cheap cold-start/fallback plus real-time freshness for active users, unified by a feature store, is the MAANG mainstream.
All-batch feeds active users stale results, losing instant personalization.
A per-user pipeline is unscalable and non-reusable, engineering-infeasible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对新用户/新物品缺乏交互历史时的预测问题，常用批处理预算的通用/兜底结果覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold-start is predicting for new users/items with little interaction history, often covered by batch-precomputed generic/fallback results.

scenario: 混合架构里批处理、同步、流式三条路各自算特征，你怕它们口径不一致造成偏斜。
scenario_en: In a hybrid, batch, sync, and streaming each compute features, and you fear inconsistent definitions cause skew.
q: 特征存储在混合架构里扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role does the feature store play in a hybrid architecture?
why: 特征存储是把三种范式黏合起来的统一层：让训练、批处理、同步、流式都读同一份特征定义和取值，保证跨范式一致，从根上抑制训练-服务偏斜。它既服务离线训练，又给在线服务提供低延迟取特征。
why_en: The feature store is the unifying layer that lets training, batch, sync, and streaming read the same feature definitions and values, keeping them consistent across paradigms and suppressing skew.
options: 它只是给同步服务加的一个缓存，与训练和批处理无关
统一层：训练/批/同步/流式读同一份特征定义与取值
它是训练用的数据集划分工具，只在离线阶段发挥作用
它是模型注册表，只存模型版本和指标，不存任何特征
options_en: It's just a cache bolted onto the sync service, unrelated to training and batch.
The unifying layer: training, batch, sync, and streaming all read one set of feature definitions and values.
It is a training-time dataset-splitting tool that only matters in the offline stage.
It is a model registry that stores model versions and metrics only, never features.
optionExplanations: 特征存储服务于训练、批、同步、流式所有路径，不只是同步的缓存。
对；统一特征定义与取值、跨范式一致，是特征存储在混合架构里黏合各路、抑制偏斜的核心作用。
它恰恰同时服务离线训练和在线服务，不是纯训练期工具。
特征存储存的是特征不是模型版本，那是模型注册表的职责。
optionExplanations_en: The feature store serves training, batch, sync, and streaming, not just a sync cache.
Correct — unifying feature definitions and values across paradigms is its core glue role in a hybrid, suppressing skew.
It serves both offline training and online serving, not a training-only tool.
It stores features, not model versions — that's the model registry's job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中管理特征定义、离线和在线取值的系统，作为混合架构的统一层保证跨范式一致、抑制偏斜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally manages feature definitions and offline/online values as a hybrid's unifying layer, keeping paradigms consistent and suppressing skew.

scenario: 同一个模型，上同步线要压到毫秒预算，走批处理则没有即时延迟约束。
scenario_en: The same model must fit a ms budget on sync but has no instant-latency constraint in batch.
q: 同步 vs 批处理在能跑的模型保真度上有什么区别？
q_en: How do sync vs batch differ in the model fidelity they can run?
why: 同步受毫秒延迟预算约束，常得靠量化/蒸馏把模型压小、牺牲一点精度换速度；批处理没有即时延迟约束，可以跑全保真度的大模型甚至集成。取舍轴是「延迟预算 vs 模型保真度」。
why_en: Sync is bound by a ms budget and often needs quantization/distillation to shrink the model, trading accuracy for speed, while batch has no instant-latency constraint and can run full-fidelity large models or ensembles.
tradeoff: 同步（压小模型保延迟，损一点精度）vs 批处理（全保真度大模型/集成，但结果陈旧）
options: 两者能跑的模型完全一样，延迟预算只影响机器数量不影响模型
同步能跑更大的模型，因为它有专用 GPU 而且跑得更快
同步常需量化/蒸馏压小模型，批处理可跑全保真度大模型
批处理只能跑小模型，同步才能跑大模型，正好相反
options_en: Both run identical models; the latency budget changes only machine count, not model choice.
Sync can run larger models because it owns dedicated GPUs and runs faster.
Sync often needs quantization or distillation to shrink models, while batch can run full-fidelity large ones.
Batch can only run small models and sync runs large ones — exactly reversed.
optionExplanations: 延迟预算恰恰决定了同步得压小模型、批处理能跑大模型，绝非无影响。
同步更快不等于能跑更大模型；正因延迟紧它反而得把模型压小。
对；这就是取舍轴——同步用保真度换延迟，批处理用陈旧换保真度。
说反了：批处理能跑全保真度大模型，同步才受限要压小。
optionExplanations_en: The latency budget is exactly what forces sync to shrink and lets batch run large models — far from irrelevant.
Sync being fast doesn't mean larger models; the tight budget forces it to shrink instead.
Correct — that's the axis: sync trades fidelity for latency, batch trades staleness for fidelity.
Reversed: batch runs full-fidelity large models, sync is the constrained one that shrinks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型未经压缩、保留完整容量与精度的程度；批处理可跑全保真度，同步常需牺牲保真度换延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model fidelity is how uncompressed and full-capacity a model is; batch can run full fidelity while sync often trades it for latency.

scenario: 面试官给出同步广告排序的延迟目标是 p99 亚 50-100ms，问你这个数怎么约束设计。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives a sync ad-ranking latency target of p99 sub-50-100ms and asks how it constrains design.
q: 同步服务的「p99 亚 50-100ms」这个数意味着什么设计约束？
q_en: What design constraint does a sync service's 'p99 sub-50-100ms' imply?
why: p99 亚 50-100ms 是给定的 SLO 目标、不是公式推导值。这点预算要覆盖取特征+模型前向+网络，逼着你量化压小模型并按尾延迟规划容量。
why_en: p99 sub-50-100ms is a given SLO target, not a formula — 99% of requests must beat it — and since the budget must cover feature fetch plus forward pass plus network, it forces model compression and tail-latency capacity planning.
options: 它是由 QPS 和用户数算出的精确公式结果，改参数就会变
它是给定的 SLO 目标：预算要覆盖取特征+前向+网络
它只是平均延迟，偶尔超一点无所谓，不影响设计
它指模型每 50-100ms 更新一次权重，与请求延迟无关
options_en: It's an exact formula result from QPS and user count; change the params and it changes.
It is a given SLO target, and the budget must cover feature fetch, forward pass, and network.
It's just the average latency; occasionally exceeding it is fine and doesn't affect design.
It means the model updates weights every 50-100ms, unrelated to request latency.
optionExplanations: 这个数是产品定的 SLO 目标，不是从 QPS 推导出的公式值，性质不同。
对；它是「99% 快于此」的目标，预算被取特征+前向+网络瓜分，留给模型的很少，逼你压小模型、按尾延迟扩容。
p99 恰恰盯的是最慢 1% 而非平均，偶尔超标就违反 SLO，直接影响容量与模型设计。
它约束的是请求响应延迟，不是模型权重更新频率。
optionExplanations_en: The number is a product-set SLO target, not a formula derived from QPS — a different nature.
Correct — it's a '99% faster than this' target, and with the budget split across feature fetch, forward pass, and network, it forces shrinking the model and sizing by the tail.
p99 targets the slowest 1%, not the average; occasionally exceeding it violates the SLO and directly drives capacity and model design.
It constrains request response latency, not the model's weight-update frequency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标，如「p99 < 100ms」，是产品设定的性能目标而非公式推导值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a performance target like 'p99 < 100ms', a product-set goal rather than a formula result.

scenario: 延迟和吞吐都能满足时，面试官让你用成本当平手裁决，给三种范式的成本排序。
scenario_en: When latency and throughput both fit, the interviewer asks you to break the tie by cost — rank the three paradigms.
q: 按成本，三种范式怎么排序，这在决策里起什么作用？
q_en: By cost, how do the three paradigms rank, and what role does that play?
why: 成本从低到高：批处理最便宜（用完即走、大 batch 高利用率、spot），流式居中（持续运行），同步最贵（按峰值常备算力）。成本是平手裁决——当延迟和吞吐约束都满足、多个范式都可行时，用成本排序选最省的那个。
why_en: Batch is cheapest, streaming in between, sync most expensive; cost is the tiebreaker used to pick the cheapest feasible paradigm once latency and throughput are both satisfied.
tradeoff: 成本作平手裁决：批最便宜 < 流式居中 < 同步最贵；先满足延迟/吞吐，再用成本选最省
options: 同步最便宜 < 流式 < 批处理最贵，成本是第一决策轴
三者成本基本相同，所以成本不参与范式决策
批处理最便宜 < 流式 < 同步最贵；成本是平手裁决
流式最便宜，因为它只在事件到来时才消耗算力
options_en: Sync cheapest < streaming < batch most expensive, and cost is the first axis.
All three cost about the same, so cost plays no part in choosing a paradigm.
Batch cheapest, streaming in the middle, sync priciest — cost is the tiebreaker.
Streaming is cheapest because it consumes compute only when events arrive.
optionExplanations: 顺序反了，且成本是平手裁决而非第一轴——第一轴是延迟预算。
三者成本差异明显（批用完即走 vs 同步常备），成本当然参与决策。
对；批 < 流式 < 同步，成本用来在延迟/吞吐都满足时选最省的那个，是平手裁决。
流式是持续运行、成本居中，不是最便宜；最便宜的是用完即走的批处理。
optionExplanations_en: The order is reversed, and cost is a tiebreaker, not the first axis — latency budget is first.
The three differ clearly (batch spins down vs sync always-on), so cost does factor in.
Correct — batch < streaming < sync, and cost picks the cheapest once latency/throughput are met, as a tiebreaker.
Streaming runs continuously at moderate cost, not cheapest; the cheapest is spin-down batch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当多个方案在主约束（延迟/吞吐）上都可行时，用来做最终取舍的次级标准，这里是成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tiebreaker is a secondary criterion used to decide when several options all satisfy the primary constraints (latency/throughput); here it's cost.

scenario: 一个批处理作业要在一次运行里给数百万到数十亿条 用户×候选 打分，问你这对范式选择意味着什么。
scenario_en: A batch job must score millions-to-billions of user x candidate rows per run; what does this imply for paradigm choice.
q: 「一次跑百万-十亿条」这个吞吐量把设计推向哪种范式？
q_en: Which paradigm does 'millions-to-billions per run' throughput push toward?
why: 百万-十亿/次的巨量、可预先枚举的预测集，把设计推向异步批处理：一次大 batch 把海量样本喂满 GPU、利用率最高、单条成本最低，再把结果存起来供查表。若换成每请求同步现算这么大的集合，成本和延迟都撑不住。
why_en: A pre-enumerable set of millions-to-billions per run pushes toward async batch, where one large batch maxes GPU utilization at lowest per-item cost, versus infeasible per-request synchronous scoring at that scale.
options: 推向同步实时，每请求现算，靠自动扩缩硬扛十亿量级
异步批处理：大 batch 喂满 GPU，单条成本最低
推向流式，把十亿条拆成十亿个事件逐条流式处理
吞吐量只影响机器数量，和范式选择没有关系
options_en: Toward synchronous real-time, scoring per request and brute-forcing billions via autoscaling.
Async batch: a large batch saturates the GPU at the lowest per-item cost.
Toward streaming, splitting a billion rows into a billion events processed one at a time.
Throughput only changes machine count and has nothing to do with paradigm choice.
optionExplanations: 对十亿量级、可预枚举的集合每请求现算，成本和延迟都爆炸，自动扩缩也扛不住。
对；巨量可预枚举集合正是批处理主场，大 batch 高利用率、低单条成本，存结果查表。
把预枚举的十亿条硬拆成事件流是自找运维复杂度，批处理一次跑完更合适。
吞吐量是选范式的第二决策轴，绝非无关。
optionExplanations_en: Scoring a pre-enumerable billion-scale set per request explodes cost and latency; autoscaling can't carry it.
Correct — a huge pre-enumerable set is batch's home turf, with large-batch high utilization and low per-item cost, storing results for lookup.
Forcing a pre-enumerable billion rows into an event stream invites needless ops complexity; batch runs it in one pass.
Throughput is the second decision axis, far from irrelevant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间能处理的预测/请求数量；巨量可预枚举的预测集适合批处理一次算完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is predictions/requests processed per unit time; a huge pre-enumerable prediction set suits batch computing it all at once.

scenario: IoT 设备流要做异常检测，要求秒级发出告警，但不需要卡在某个用户请求的亚 100ms 关键路径上。
scenario_en: An IoT device stream needs anomaly detection with alerts in seconds, but not on any user's sub-100ms request critical path.
q: IoT 秒级异常告警该用哪种服务范式？
q_en: Which paradigm fits IoT seconds-level anomaly alerting?
why: 用流式近实时：设备事件持续进 Kafka、由流处理器算窗口特征并检测异常，秒级发告警。它要的是新鲜度和持续处理而非亚 100ms 同步响应，也没法等批处理的小时级。这正是流式填补同步与批处理空档的典型场景。
why_en: Use streaming near-real-time — device events into Kafka, windowed anomaly detection, alerts in seconds — since it needs freshness and continuous processing, not sub-100ms sync nor hours-late batch.
tradeoff: 流式（秒级持续告警，运维复杂）vs 批处理（便宜，但小时级告警太迟）
whenOtherWins: 如果异常判定不急、可接受小时/天级回顾（如离线合规审计），批处理更省；若必须在某个同步请求内即时拦截，才上同步。
options: 同步实时：每个设备读数都发一次 HTTP 请求等模型同步返回
流式近实时：事件进 Kafka、流处理器算窗口特征检测异常，秒级告警
异步批处理：每天凌晨跑一次异常检测，白天看报告
把阈值写死在设备固件里，永不更新模型
options_en: Synchronous real-time: each device reading fires an HTTP request and waits for a synchronous model return.
Streaming near-real-time: events into Kafka, stream processor computes windowed features and detects anomalies, alerting in seconds.
Async batch: run anomaly detection once at dawn daily and read reports during the day.
Hard-code thresholds into the device firmware and never update the model.
optionExplanations: IoT 异常检测不需要亚 100ms 同步响应，为每条读数做同步往返是过度设计、成本高。
对；持续消费事件、窗口检测、秒级告警正是流式定位，填补同步与批处理之间的空档。
每天一次太迟，异常要秒级发现，批处理的小时/天级新鲜度不够。
写死固件阈值丢掉了模型和持续更新能力，达不到异常检测目标。
optionExplanations_en: IoT anomaly detection doesn't need sub-100ms sync; a synchronous round-trip per reading over-engineers it at high cost.
Correct — continuous event consumption, windowed detection, and seconds-level alerts is streaming's niche, filling the sync-to-batch gap.
Once daily is too late; anomalies need seconds-level detection, and batch's hourly/daily freshness is insufficient.
Hard-coded firmware thresholds drop the model and continuous updates, missing the anomaly-detection goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 物联网：大量联网设备持续产生事件流，常用流式做窗口聚合与异常检测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IoT (Internet of Things) is many networked devices producing continuous event streams, commonly processed by streaming for windowed aggregation and anomaly detection.

scenario: 同步服务要在个位数毫秒内取到用户/上下文特征来打分，你在选特征取用的存储。
scenario_en: A sync service must fetch user/context features in single-digit ms to score, and you're choosing the feature-serving store.
q: 为什么同步服务的请求时特征取用要放在 Redis/DynamoDB 这类存储？
q_en: Why put a sync service's request-time feature fetch in a store like Redis/DynamoDB?
why: 因为整个响应只有几十毫秒预算，取特征这一步必须个位数毫秒内完成：Redis 是内存 KV、DynamoDB 是托管低延迟 KV，按 key 点查稳定快。若把特征放进要扫描或做联表的关系库/数仓，延迟到几十上百毫秒，直接吃穿延迟预算。
why_en: Because the whole response has only tens of ms and the feature fetch must finish in single-digit ms, so an in-memory/managed KV (Redis, DynamoDB) does fast point lookups, unlike a scan/join in a warehouse that would blow the budget.
options: 因为它们能跑复杂 SQL 联表，特征算得更全
因为个位数毫秒点查是硬需求，数仓扫描会吃穿延迟预算
因为它们最便宜，选它纯粹是为了压低存储成本
因为它们能永久保存全部历史特征，容量上限最大
options_en: Because they can run complex SQL joins for richer features.
Because single-digit-millisecond point lookups are a hard requirement and warehouse scans blow the budget.
Because they are the cheapest, chosen purely to cut storage cost.
Because they keep all historical features forever and have the largest capacity ceiling.
optionExplanations: 选它们恰恰不是为了跑联表——KV 按 key 点查才快，复杂 SQL 反而慢。
对；同步延迟预算逼着取特征必须个位数毫秒，内存/托管 KV 的点查稳定命中这个预算，数仓扫描来不及。
选它们首要是低延迟点查，不是便宜；成本是次要考量。
选它们是为低延迟点查，不是为最大容量或永久存全量历史。
optionExplanations_en: They're chosen precisely not for joins — KV point lookups by key are fast, while complex SQL is slow.
Correct — the sync budget forces single-digit-ms fetches, and in-memory/managed KV point lookups hit that budget while warehouse scans can't.
They're chosen first for low-latency lookups, not cheapness; cost is secondary.
They're chosen for low-latency lookups, not maximum capacity or forever-history storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按主键直接取一条记录的查询，KV 存储的点查是稳定的个位数毫秒，适合请求时取特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point lookup fetches one record by primary key; KV stores do this in stable single-digit ms, ideal for request-time feature fetch.

scenario: 把三种服务范式的一句话定位背下来，面试里能按约束秒选。
scenario_en: Memorize each serving paradigm's one-line niche so you can pick by constraint instantly.
q: 补全三种服务范式的定位口诀。
q_en: Fill in the one-line niche of each serving paradigm.
text: 亚 100ms 卡在请求关键路径（广告/搜索/欺诈）→ {{同步}}；小时级可容忍、预测集有界 → {{批处理}}（异步）；要新鲜但毫秒不强求（会话/异常）→ {{流式}}。三者共有的首要风险是 {{训练-服务偏斜}}。
text_en: Sub-100ms on the request critical path (ads/search/fraud) → {{synchronous}}; hours-tolerant with a bounded set → {{batch}} (async); fresh-but-not-ms (session/anomaly) → {{streaming}}. The shared first-order risk is {{training-serving skew}}.
why: 这四空是本章骨架：延迟卡死用同步、可陈旧用批、要新鲜但不卡死用流式，而三者都要防训练-服务偏斜。记住「约束→范式」这一步，面试里就能先声明延迟/QPS/新鲜度再报范式。
why_en: Sync for hard latency, batch for staleness-tolerant, streaming for fresh-not-instant, and all three must guard training-serving skew.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏斜
termDefinitions.meaning: 服务时特征/逻辑与训练时不一致导致线上掉点，是三种范式共有的首要风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-serving skew is serving-time features/logic diverging from training, degrading production performance — the shared first-order risk.

scenario: 一个推荐场景新鲜度要求介于两者之间：既嫌批处理隔夜太陈旧，又不需要秒级即时，分钟级更新就满意。
scenario_en: A rec use case wants freshness in between: nightly batch is too stale, but it doesn't need seconds — minute-level updates suffice.
q: 新鲜度要求「比批处理高、比同步松」时更该倾向哪种范式？
q_en: When freshness is 'higher than batch, looser than sync', which paradigm to lean toward?
why: 倾向流式近实时：它正是填补批处理（隔夜陈旧）和同步（亚 100ms、贵）之间空档的范式，秒到分钟级持续更新恰好匹配这种中间新鲜度。代价是比批处理运维重（精确一次、检查点、背压），要评估是否值得。
why_en: Lean streaming near-real-time — it fills the gap between stale nightly batch and expensive sub-100ms sync, matching minute-level freshness, at the cost of heavier ops than batch.
tradeoff: 流式（分钟级新鲜、填补空档，但运维重）vs 批处理（更省，但隔夜太陈旧追不上）
whenOtherWins: 如果分钟级新鲜其实并非必要、隔夜也能接受，就退回更便宜、运维更轻的批处理，别为用不上的新鲜度背流式复杂度。
options: 同步实时，反正越新鲜越好，直接上最贵的方案
流式近实时：秒-分钟级更新，正好落在批与同步之间
异步批处理，隔夜跑一次就够，新鲜度还可以再放宽
端上推理，把模型塞进用户设备本地实时计算
options_en: Synchronous real-time — fresher is always better, so just buy the priciest option.
Streaming near-real-time: seconds-to-minutes updates land exactly between batch and sync.
Async batch — one overnight run is enough and freshness can be relaxed further.
On-device inference — put the model on the user’s device and compute locally in real time.
optionExplanations: 同步的亚 100ms 和高成本对分钟级新鲜是过度设计，用不着为不需要的即时性买单。
对；中间新鲜度正是流式的定位，秒-分钟级持续更新填补批与同步之间的空档。
隔夜批处理太陈旧，恰恰是这里要改进的痛点，说新鲜度无所谓与前提矛盾。
端上推理是另一类方案，不解决服务端中间新鲜度的范式选择问题。
optionExplanations_en: Sync's sub-100ms and high cost over-engineer minute-level freshness; no need to pay for unneeded immediacy.
Correct — middle freshness is streaming's niche, with seconds-to-minutes updates filling the batch-to-sync gap.
Nightly batch is too stale — the very pain point here — so 'freshness doesn't matter' contradicts the premise.
On-device is a different approach and doesn't address the server-side middle-freshness paradigm choice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测反映最新数据/行为的及时程度；批处理最陈旧、同步最新鲜、流式介于两者之间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Freshness is how up-to-date a prediction is with the latest data/behavior; batch is stalest, sync freshest, streaming in between.

scenario: 候选人一上来就说「我用同步实时推理」，还没提任何延迟、QPS 或新鲜度数字。
scenario_en: A candidate opens with 'I'll use synchronous real-time inference' before stating any latency, QPS, or freshness numbers.
q: 先报范式、后补约束这种做法在面试里为什么被扣分？
q_en: Why is naming the paradigm before stating constraints penalized in interviews?
why: 因为它是结论先行、没有约束驱动的推理：不先给延迟 SLA、预估 QPS、新鲜度要求，就无法判断同步是不是对的选择，很可能过度设计（明明可批处理却上最贵的同步）或欠设计。正确做法是先声明三约束、再由它们推出范式。
why_en: Because it's a conclusion without constraint-driven reasoning — without a latency SLA, estimated QPS, and freshness, you can't tell if sync is right, risking over- or under-engineering; state constraints first, then derive the paradigm.
options: 不扣分，直接报同步永远是最安全的默认选项
因为结论先行、缺约束驱动：没延迟/QPS 就判不了对错
扣分只因为同步太贵，先报批处理就没有问题
因为面试只看你能不能背出三种范式的名字
options_en: It is not penalized; opening with sync is always the safest default.
Because it leads with a conclusion and skips constraint-driven reasoning: without latency or QPS you cannot judge it.
It is penalized only because sync is expensive; opening with batch would be fine.
Because the interview only checks whether you can recite the three paradigm names.
optionExplanations: 同步不是安全默认——它最贵、偏斜风险最高，无约束就报它常是过度设计。
对；扣分点在缺少约束驱动推理，先摆延迟/QPS/新鲜度再推范式才体现工程判断。
问题不在同步贵，而在没先声明约束就下结论；先报批处理同样是结论先行。
面试考的是约束到范式的推理过程，不是背名字。
optionExplanations_en: Sync isn't a safe default — it's priciest with the highest skew risk, and naming it without constraints is often over-engineering.
Correct — the penalty is missing constraint-driven reasoning; stating latency/QPS/freshness before deriving the paradigm shows engineering judgment.
The issue isn't sync's cost but concluding before stating constraints; opening with batch is equally conclusion-first.
Interviews test the constraint-to-paradigm reasoning, not reciting names.

termDefinitions.term: constraint-driven reasoning / 约束驱动推理
termDefinitions.meaning: 先明确延迟、吞吐、新鲜度、成本等约束，再由约束推出架构选择，而非先拍方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraint-driven reasoning states latency, throughput, freshness, and cost constraints first, then derives the architecture from them rather than picking a solution upfront.

scenario: 为 10 亿用户从 5 亿候选视频里做推荐，p99 延迟预算只有 200ms。
scenario_en: Recommend for 1B users over 500M candidate videos with a p99 latency budget of only 200ms.
q: 检索+排序的「三级漏斗」按顺序是哪三层？
q_en: What are the three stages of the retrieval-and-ranking funnel, in order?
why: 漏斗每级都是「更强的模型、更少的候选」：候选生成十亿→千级(10-20ms)、粗排千级→百级(10-30ms)、精排百级→最终(20-50ms)。顺序必须由宽到深，重模型只在小集合上跑才付得起。
why_en: The funnel runs candidate generation (billions to thousands), then coarse ranking (thousands to hundreds), then fine re-ranking (hundreds), each stage spending a heavier model on fewer items.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["5亿候选"] --> B["候选生成
两塔ANN · 10-20ms"] B --> C["~1000
粗排 · 10-30ms"] C --> D["~100
精排 · 20-50ms"] D --> E["最终结果"]
options: 候选生成:两塔 ANN 十亿→千级 → 粗排:轻量模型千级→~100 → 精排:重模型排 ~100
粗排:轻量模型先给十亿全量逐条打分 → 候选生成:ANN 再把结果压到千级 → 精排:重模型出最终结果
精排：重模型直接对全部候选打分 → 候选生成：负责去重降载 → 粗排：最后套业务规则收尾
候选生成：ANN 粗筛 → 精排：重模型直接排序 → 粗排：轻量模型再做一次二次兜底
options_en: Candidate generation: two-tower ANN cuts billions to thousands → coarse ranking: a light model trims to ~100 → fine ranking: a heavy model ranks the ~100.
Coarse ranking: a light model scores all billions one by one → candidate generation: ANN then compresses the result to thousands → fine ranking: a heavy model produces the final list.
Fine re-ranking: heavy model scores all candidates directly → candidate generation: handles dedup and load shedding → coarse ranking: applies business rules at the end.
Candidate generation: ANN pre-filters → fine re-ranking: heavy model sorts directly → coarse ranking: light model does a second fallback pass.
optionExplanations: 对；由宽到深，候选生成先把量降到千级，粗排再降到百级，精排才用得起最贵的模型。
顺序颠倒：让轻量模型先给十亿全量打分正是三级漏斗要避免的算力灾难，候选生成必须在最前面。
重模型对 5 亿候选逐个打分算不完，正是没有候选生成会崩的那条路径。
精排放粗排前面就白白让重模型处理了更多候选，违背「越往后候选越少、模型越重」的原则。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — broad to deep: candidate generation drops volume to thousands, coarse ranking to hundreds, so fine re-ranking can afford the most expensive model.
Backwards: scoring all billions with any model first is the compute disaster the funnel exists to avoid; candidate generation must come first.
A heavy model cannot score 500M candidates in budget — this is exactly the path that breaks without candidate generation.
Putting fine re-ranking before coarse ranking wastes the heavy model on more items, violating fewer-items-heavier-model ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索：不保证精确，但能在十亿向量里毫秒级找出最相似的 top-k。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search finds the most similar top-k vectors among billions in milliseconds, trading exactness for speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏斗第一级：用两塔+ANN 把海量物料快速粗筛到几百到几千个候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the funnel's first stage, quickly narrowing a huge corpus to a few hundred to few thousand candidates via two-tower + ANN.

q: 把「为什么要分三级漏斗」的推理链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the reasoning for why the pipeline is split into three funnel stages:
steps: 候选集降到千级后，粗排用轻量模型进一步筛到百级
单个模型无法在延迟预算内给 5 亿物料逐个打分
百级小集合上才付得起精排的重模型(DCN/多任务/transformer)
所以先用两塔 ANN 把十亿快速粗筛到千级
why: 推理起点是「一个模型算不完全量」这个约束，于是逐级用更强模型换更少候选：ANN 先降到千级 → 粗排降到百级 → 精排在百级上跑重模型。每一步都是拿广度换深度。
why_en: It starts from the constraint that no single model can score all items in budget, so each stage trades breadth for depth: ANN to thousands, coarse ranking to hundreds, then a heavy model on the hundreds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精排常用模型：显式建模特征交叉，比 MLP 更能学到高阶交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep Cross Network) explicitly models feature crosses, capturing higher-order interactions better than a plain MLP.

scenario: 面试官问：既然精排模型最准，为什么不直接用它给全部 5 亿候选打分，省掉前两级？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: since the fine-ranking model is most accurate, why not just score all 500M candidates with it and skip the earlier stages?
q: 为什么要分级而不是用最强模型对全量打分？
q_en: Why stage the pipeline instead of running the strongest model over everything?
why: 精排模型每个候选要几毫秒，5 亿候选根本算不完，且大多数是明显无关项。分级把重模型省到最后的百级小集合上，用广度换深度。
why_en: The fine model costs milliseconds per item, so scoring 500M is impossible in budget and most items are obviously irrelevant; staging saves the heavy model for the final ~100.
tradeoff: 分级(省算力但可能漏召回) vs 全量精排(最准但算不完)
whenOtherWins: 如果候选池本身只有几百个(如小型商品目录),就不需要漏斗,直接用一个精排模型全量打分反而更简单准确。
options: 因为精排模型只支持一次处理几百条输入,是框架的硬性 batch 上限,所以必须先砍到百级
因为候选生成的两塔模型比精排更准,精排只是用来做最后的多样性去重
因为对 5 亿候选逐个跑精排在延迟预算内算不完,且大多数明显无关,重模型该省到最后小集合
因为精排必须在 CPU 上跑而候选生成在 GPU 上,硬件不同所以要拆成两级流水线
options_en: Because the fine model can only take a few hundred inputs at once — a hard framework batch cap — so you must cut to hundreds first.
Because the two-tower model in candidate generation is more accurate than the fine model, which just does final dedup and diversity.
Because running the fine model over 500M candidates cannot finish in budget and most are obviously irrelevant, so the heavy model is saved for the final small set.
Because the fine model must run on CPU while candidate generation runs on GPU, so the hardware split forces two stages.
optionExplanations: batch 上限是可调工程参数,不是分级的根因;真正的原因是全量精排的总算力/延迟付不起。
说反了:两塔为速度牺牲了精度,精排才是最准的一级,不是只做去重。
对;约束是延迟预算 × 候选数,重模型只在广度已被砍小后才跑得起,这就是漏斗的意义。
硬件不是根因,候选生成和精排都能上 GPU;分级是为了控制总算力与延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Batch size is a tunable engineering knob, not the root reason; the real driver is that full fine-scoring cannot afford the compute/latency.
Reversed: the two-tower trades accuracy for speed, and the fine model is the most accurate stage, not just a dedup step.
Correct — the constraint is latency budget × candidate count, so the heavy model only runs once breadth is already cut, which is the funnel's whole point.
Hardware is not the root cause; both stages can run on GPU, and staging exists to control total compute and latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏斗最后一级:用最贵最准的模型对~100个候选精细排序,并叠加业务规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine re-ranking is the last stage, applying the most expensive, most accurate model to ~100 candidates plus business overlays.

scenario: 一个相关物料在候选生成阶段没被 ANN 召回,后面粗排和精排都没机会再见到它。
scenario_en: A relevant item is not retrieved by ANN in candidate generation, so coarse and fine ranking never see it.
q: 候选生成的漏项会造成什么后果,为什么它是杠杆最高的一级?
q_en: What is the consequence of a miss in candidate generation, and why is it the highest-leverage stage?
why: 漏斗只会往下删、不会往上加,候选生成漏掉的物料下游永远找不回来,所以它的 recall@k 是天花板。粗排/精排再强也只能在已召回集合里排序。
why_en: The funnel only removes items downstream, so anything missed in candidate generation can never be recovered, making its recall@k the ceiling for the whole system.
options: 漏掉的物料会在精排阶段被重模型自动补回,所以候选生成的召回率影响不大
漏掉的物料下游永远找不回来,候选生成的 recall@k 是全链路天花板
漏项只影响延迟不影响质量,因为候选越少后面算得越快、体验反而更好
漏掉的物料会进入一个二级召回队列,下一次请求时补进来,单次请求的质量不受影响
options_en: A missed item is automatically recovered by the heavy model in fine re-ranking, so candidate-generation recall barely matters.
A missed item can never be recovered downstream, so candidate-generation recall@k caps the whole pipeline.
Misses only affect latency, not quality, since fewer candidates make later stages faster and the experience better.
Missed items land in a secondary retrieval queue and are added on the next request, so a single request loses no quality.
optionExplanations: 错;精排只能对「已召回」的集合排序,它看不见没被召回的物料,补不回来。
对;这就是为什么候选生成盯 recall@k、其余阶段盯精度,漏召回是不可逆损失。
漏项直接损失了本该展示的相关内容,是质量损失而非单纯的延迟优化。
没有这种自动二级队列;漏召回就是当次结果里少了这个相关项,不会自动回补。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — fine re-ranking only sorts the already-retrieved set; it cannot see items that were never retrieved.
Correct — this is why candidate generation optimizes recall@k while later stages optimize precision; a miss is an irreversible loss.
A miss directly loses relevant content that should have shown, which is a quality loss, not just a latency win.
There is no such automatic secondary queue; a miss simply means that relevant item is absent from this result, with no auto-backfill.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在返回的前 k 个结果里,覆盖了多少真正相关物料的比例;候选生成的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@k is the fraction of truly relevant items captured within the top-k returned, the key metric for candidate generation.

scenario: 候选生成要在 10-20ms 内从十亿物料里找出相关候选,不能对每对 user-item 现算一个大模型。
scenario_en: Candidate generation must find relevant items among billions in 10-20ms, without running a big model on each user-item pair.
q: 两塔(two-tower)模型的结构和「联合训练」为什么能支撑毫秒级检索?
q_en: How does the two-tower model's structure and joint training enable millisecond retrieval?
why: query 塔吃用户上下文、item 塔吃物料特征,输出同维 embedding,联合训练让相关 pair 的向量靠近(余弦相似)。因为两塔独立,item 向量可离线预算入 ANN 索引,线上只算 query 向量再查 ANN。
why_en: The query tower encodes user context and the item tower encodes item features into same-dim embeddings, trained jointly so relevant pairs sit close, letting item vectors be precomputed offline into an ANN index.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["用户上下文"] --> QT["query 塔"] I["物料特征"] --> IT["item 塔"] QT --> QE["query embedding"] IT --> IE["item embedding
(离线预算入ANN)"] QE -. 余弦相似 .- IE
options: 双塔联合训练成同维 embedding,item 侧离线入 ANN,线上只算 query
两塔共享同一套权重,对每个 user-item 对在线拼接特征后过一个深层网络算出精确分
query 塔离线预算所有用户向量,item 塔在线为每个候选实时编码,再逐对算点积排序
两塔分别训练、互不影响,靠一个额外的交叉注意力层在线融合 user 和 item 特征
options_en: The two towers are trained jointly into same-dimension embeddings; item vectors go offline into ANN and only the query is computed online.
Both towers share one set of weights and, per user-item pair, concatenate features online through a deep network for an exact score.
The query tower precomputes all user vectors offline while the item tower encodes each candidate online in real time, then dot-products every pair.
The towers are trained separately and independently, fused online by an extra cross-attention layer over user and item features.
optionExplanations: 对;两塔分离是关键——item 侧能离线算好入索引,线上只剩一次 query 编码+ANN 查询,毫秒完成。
在线对每对过深层网络正是两塔要避免的,那是精排的做法,十亿量级算不完。
反了;是 item 向量离线预算、query 在线算,而非相反,且不做逐对点积而是 ANN 近似检索。
两塔必须联合训练才能让 query 和 item 落到同一可比空间;在线交叉注意力破坏了可预算性。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — tower separation is the key: item vectors are precomputed into the index, leaving only one query encode plus an ANN lookup online, done in milliseconds.
Running a deep network per pair online is exactly what two-tower avoids; that is the fine-ranking approach and cannot scale to billions.
Reversed: item vectors are precomputed and the query is computed online, and it uses ANN, not exhaustive per-pair dot products.
The towers must be trained jointly so query and item land in one comparable space; online cross-attention breaks precomputability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个独立编码器分别把 user 和 item 映射成同维向量,用向量相似度做匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model uses two separate encoders to map user and item into same-dim vectors, matched by vector similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象压成一个稠密向量,语义相近的对象向量距离近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector representation where semantically similar objects have nearby vectors.

scenario: 候选生成阶段要在十亿级物料上给出可供后续排序的候选集。
scenario_en: The candidate-generation stage must return a workable candidate set from billions of items.
q: 候选生成大致把量级从多少降到多少、用多长时间?这个规模决定了什么?
q_en: Roughly what count and latency does candidate generation target, and what does that size decide?
why: 经验量级:十亿物料 → ~500-2000 候选,10-20ms 内完成。这个「千级」输出规模是粗排的输入基数,决定后面 feature store 要批量取多少行特征、粗排要给多少候选打分。
why_en: Rough anchor: billions to ~500-2000 candidates in 10-20ms, and this thousands-scale output sets the base load for coarse ranking's feature fetches and scoring.
options: 从十亿降到~10 个候选,耗时约 100-200ms,直接就是最终展示给用户的结果集
从十亿降到~500-2000 个候选,10-20ms 完成,这个千级规模是粗排的输入基数
从十亿降到~100 万候选,约 1s 完成,再交给精排逐个用重模型打分
从十亿降到固定 256 个候选,耗时约 50ms,数量固定是为了对齐 GPU batch
options_en: From billions to ~10 candidates in about 100-200ms, which is directly the final set shown to the user.
From billions to ~500-2000 candidates in 10-20ms, and this thousands-scale count is the input base for coarse ranking.
From billions to ~1M candidates in about 1s, then handed to fine re-ranking to score each with the heavy model.
From billions to a fixed 256 candidates in about 50ms, fixed to align with the GPU batch size.
optionExplanations: ~10 是最终结果的量级,不是候选生成的输出;还要经过粗排精排两级才轮到它变这么小。
对;千级候选 + 10-20ms 是标准锚点,它决定了粗排要处理多少候选、取多少特征。
百万候选精排根本算不完;候选生成的意义正是把量降到千级而非百万。
候选数不是为对齐 batch 固定死的,而是由 recall 需求和下游预算决定的动态量级。
optionExplanations_en: ~10 is the final result scale, not candidate generation's output; it only shrinks that far after coarse and fine ranking.
Correct — thousands of candidates in 10-20ms is the standard anchor, and it sets how many candidates coarse ranking scores and how many features it fetches.
Fine re-ranking cannot score a million candidates; candidate generation exists precisely to cut to thousands, not millions.
Candidate count is not fixed to match a batch; it is a dynamic scale set by recall needs and downstream budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索返回相似度最高的 k 个结果;这里 k 约为几百到几千。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-k returns the k most similar results; here k is roughly a few hundred to a few thousand.

scenario: 两塔上线时,item 有十亿个而 query(用户上下文)每次请求都不同。要在 10ms 内查到候选。
scenario_en: At serving time there are billions of items while the query (user context) differs each request, and candidates must return in 10ms.
q: 两塔的哪一侧该离线预算、哪一侧在线算?为什么这样切?
q_en: Which tower is precomputed offline vs computed online, and why split it this way?
why: item 向量离线批量算好、灌进 ANN 索引;线上只对当次 query 算一个向量,再查 ANN 取 top-k。因为 item 集合巨大但相对稳定,query 小但每次都变——把不变的大集合预算掉,只在线算多变的小部分。
why_en: Item vectors are precomputed into the ANN index while only the per-request query vector is computed online, because items are huge but stable and the query is small but always changing.
tradeoff: item 离线预算(省在线算力但索引会漂移) vs 全在线(永远最新但十亿量级算不动)
whenOtherWins: 如果 item 特征高频变化(如实时价格、库存),离线预算的 embedding 会很快过期,这时需要流式重算 item 向量或把易变特征挪到粗排阶段处理。
options: query 向量离线预算好所有用户,item 向量在线为每个候选实时编码后逐对比对
两侧都在线算:每次请求都同时编码 query 和全部 item 向量,保证向量绝对新鲜
item 向量离线批量算入 ANN 索引,线上只算当次 query 再查 top-k
两侧都离线预算:把所有 user×item 的相似度提前算成一张大表,线上直接查表
options_en: Query vectors are precomputed for all users offline, while item vectors are encoded online per candidate and compared pairwise.
Compute both online: every request re-encodes the query and all item vectors to keep vectors absolutely fresh.
Item vectors are precomputed offline into the ANN index; online you compute only the current query and look up top-k.
Precompute both offline: materialize the full user×item similarity table ahead of time and just read it online.
optionExplanations: 反了;用户上下文每次请求都变、无法预算全,能预算的是相对稳定的 item 侧。
在线编码十亿 item 每次请求都算不完,正是两塔要绕开的算力灾难。
对;把不变的大集合(item)离线灌进索引,只在线算多变的小部分(query),毫秒级完成。
user×item 全量相似度表是十亿×十亿量级,存不下也没法及时更新,不可行。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed — user context changes every request and cannot be fully precomputed; the stable item side is what gets precomputed.
Encoding a billion items online per request cannot finish; this is the compute disaster two-tower avoids.
Correct — precompute the large stable set (items) into the index and compute only the small changing part (query) online, done in milliseconds.
A full user×item similarity table is billions×billions in size — unstorable and impossible to keep fresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先组织好的向量索引结构,支持毫秒级查最相似的 top-k。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index is a pre-built vector structure that answers top-k nearest-neighbor queries in milliseconds.

scenario: 训练两塔时,只有「用户点过的正样本」,没有天然的负样本告诉模型哪些 item 不相关。
scenario_en: Training the two towers, you only have positive samples (items the user engaged) and no natural negatives telling the model which items are irrelevant.
q: 两塔训练怎么造负样本?in-batch negatives 和 hard-negative mining 各解决什么?
q_en: How does two-tower training source negatives, and what do in-batch negatives vs hard-negative mining each solve?
why: in-batch negatives 把同 batch 别人的正 item 当负例,几乎零成本造大量负例。但它们偏易,需再用 hard-negative mining 挑相似难负例练边界。
why_en: In-batch negatives reuse other queries' positive items in the batch as negatives almost for free, while hard-negative mining adds similar-but-irrelevant items to force sharper decision boundaries.
options: 两塔不需要构造负样本,只对正样本做回归,把相关 pair 的余弦相似度压到 1 即可
从整个物料库均匀随机采样出大量负例,采样量越大越好,完全不需要区分难例和易例两类
in-batch negatives 免费造易负例,hard-negative mining 补难例
只用人工标注的负样本:让标注者逐条判断十亿级物料库里哪些 item 与当前 query 完全不相关
options_en: Two towers need no negatives at all — just regress positives, pushing relevant pairs’ cosine similarity to 1.
Uniformly sample a large pile of negatives from the whole corpus — the more the better, with no need to separate hard from easy at all.
In-batch negatives make easy negatives for free; hard-negative mining then adds the hard ones.
Use only human-labeled negatives, having annotators judge item by item, across a billion-scale catalog, which ones are irrelevant to this particular query.
optionExplanations: 没有负例模型学不到「什么不相关」,只压正 pair 会让所有向量塌到一起。
纯随机负例大多太容易(明显不相关),模型学不到相似项之间的细分边界。
对;in-batch 近乎免费但偏易,hard negatives 专挑相似难例,两者互补。
逐条人工标负样本成本极高、无法覆盖十亿量级,工业界靠 in-batch + hard mining。
optionExplanations_en: Without negatives the model cannot learn what is irrelevant; pushing only positives collapses all vectors together.
Purely random negatives are mostly too easy (obviously irrelevant), so the model never learns fine boundaries between similar items.
Correct — in-batch negatives are nearly free but easy, and hard-negative mining targets similar hard cases; the two complement each other.
Hand-labeling negatives item by item is prohibitively costly and cannot cover billions; industry uses in-batch plus hard mining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时把同一 batch 里其他样本的正 item 当作当前 query 的负例,免额外采样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-batch negatives treat other samples' positive items within the same batch as negatives for the current query, avoiding extra sampling.

termDefinitions.term: hard-negative mining / 难负样本挖掘
termDefinitions.meaning: 刻意挑选与 query 相似但实际不相关的样本作负例,逼模型学细分边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard-negative mining deliberately picks items similar to the query but actually irrelevant, forcing the model to learn finer boundaries.

scenario: item embedding 已离线灌入 ANN 索引,但物料的属性/热度在变,索引却没有及时重建。
scenario_en: Item embeddings were loaded offline into the ANN index, but item attributes/popularity change while the index is not refreshed in time.
q: embedding drift(嵌入漂移)是什么、怎么发生、如何缓解?
q_en: What is embedding drift, how does it happen, and how do you mitigate it?
why: 正常:离线算好的 item 向量代表当前物料语义。异常:物料变了但索引没重建→旧向量与真实语义脱节→检索悄悄退化、recall 下降却无报错。缓解:周期性重建索引或流式增量更新。代价:重建耗资源、流式更新增加系统复杂度。
why_en: Embedding drift is when item attributes change but the index is not rebuilt, so stale vectors silently degrade retrieval and lower recall with no error; mitigate with periodic re-indexing or streaming updates.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["item 属性变化"] --> B["索引未重建"] B --> C["旧向量脱离真实语义"] C --> D["recall 悄悄下降
无报错"] D -->|缓解| E["周期重建 / 流式更新"] E --> B
options: embedding drift 指 GPU 显存里向量被随机翻转的硬件位错误,靠 ECC 内存纠正,与语义无关
旧 item 向量与物料真实语义脱节→检索悄悄退化 recall 下降;缓解靠周期重建索引或流式增量更新
指训练时 loss 不收敛导致 embedding 发散,靠调小学习率解决,与线上索引无关
指用户 query 分布随时间变化,只需重训 query 塔即可,item 索引无需动
options_en: Embedding drift is a hardware bit-flip of vectors in GPU memory, corrected by ECC RAM — unrelated to semantic changes.
Stale item vectors detach from items' true meaning → retrieval silently degrades and recall drops; mitigate with periodic re-indexing or streaming updates.
It means training loss diverges so embeddings blow up, fixed by lowering the learning rate, unrelated to the serving index.
It means the user query distribution shifts over time, needing only a query-tower retrain, with no change to the item index.
optionExplanations: 这是硬件位翻转,不是 embedding drift;drift 是语义层面的过期,不是内存错误。
对;危险在于「无报错的悄悄退化」——recall 掉了但系统不报错,得靠重建/流式更新止损。
训练发散是另一回事;drift 说的是线上索引里的向量随物料变化而过期。
query 分布漂移是另一种问题;此处 drift 特指 item 索引里的向量过期,需重建 item 索引。
optionExplanations_en: That is a hardware bit-flip, not embedding drift; drift is semantic staleness, not a memory error.
Correct — the danger is silent degradation with no error: recall falls quietly, so periodic re-indexing or streaming updates are needed to stem it.
Training divergence is a different issue; drift is about serving-index vectors going stale as items change.
Query-distribution shift is a separate problem; this drift is specifically stale item vectors in the index, needing an item-index rebuild.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引里的物料向量因物料变化而过期,与真实语义脱节,导致检索质量悄悄下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift is when indexed item vectors go stale as items change, detaching from true meaning and quietly degrading retrieval.

scenario: 要为十亿向量选 ANN 索引结构,理解 HNSW、IVF、PQ 各自的机制与代价。
scenario_en: Choosing an ANN index structure for a billion vectors, you compare the mechanisms and costs of HNSW, IVF, and PQ.
q: HNSW、IVF、PQ 三种 ANN 结构分别靠什么机制、各自的主要代价是什么?
q_en: What mechanism does each of HNSW, IVF, and PQ use, and what is each one's main cost?
why: HNSW=多层可导航图,recall 高但内存/构建贵;IVF=k-means 切 Voronoi 单元只搜 nprobe 个,调 recall/延迟;PQ=子向量量化压 10-50×,略损精度。
why_en: HNSW is a multi-layer navigable graph (high recall but memory/build-heavy), IVF partitions space into Voronoi cells searched by nprobe (higher nprobe trades latency for recall), and PQ quantizes sub-vectors to codebook centroids for 10-50x compression at some accuracy cost.
tradeoff: HNSW(高 recall,吃内存) vs IVF(nprobe 调 recall/延迟) vs PQ(省内存,损精度)
options: HNSW=多层可导航图(吃内存),IVF=只搜 nprobe 个 Voronoi 单元,PQ=子向量量化压 10-50×
三者都是精确检索而非近似检索,区别只在实现语言不同:HNSW 用 C++、IVF 用 Python、PQ 用 CUDA 实现
HNSW 靠磁盘顺序扫描、IVF 靠哈希分桶、PQ 靠 B+ 树索引,三者互斥不可组合
HNSW 压缩内存最狠、IVF 精度最高无损、PQ 是唯一多层图结构,常单独使用
options_en: HNSW = multi-layer navigable graph (memory-heavy), IVF = searches only nprobe Voronoi cells, PQ = sub-vector quantization compressing 10-50x.
All three are exact rather than approximate search, differing only in implementation language: HNSW in C++, IVF in Python, PQ implemented in CUDA.
HNSW scans disk sequentially, IVF hashes into buckets, PQ uses a B+ tree, and the three are mutually exclusive and cannot combine.
HNSW compresses memory the most, IVF is highest-precision and lossless, and PQ is the only multi-layer graph, usually used alone.
optionExplanations: 对;三者机制清晰:图导航(HNSW)、单元剪枝(IVF)、码本压缩(PQ),常 IVF+PQ 组合。
它们都是「近似」检索不是精确,区别在结构不在语言。
机制描述全错;且 IVF+PQ 恰恰是常见组合,并非互斥。
反了:PQ 才是压缩最狠的,HNSW 是多层图,IVF 有损;PQ 常与 IVF 组合而非单用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — clear mechanisms: graph navigation (HNSW), cell pruning (IVF), codebook compression (PQ), often combined as IVF+PQ.
All three are approximate, not exact, and differ by structure, not programming language.
The mechanisms are all wrong, and IVF+PQ is in fact a common combination, not mutually exclusive.
Reversed: PQ compresses the most, HNSW is the multi-layer graph, IVF is lossy, and PQ usually combines with IVF rather than standing alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层图索引:高层稀疏长程边快速定位,低层稠密边精细搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a multi-layer graph index: sparse long-range links up top for fast jumps, dense links below for fine search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 k-means 把向量空间切成 Voronoi 单元,查询只搜最近的 nprobe 个单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IVF (Inverted File) partitions the vector space into Voronoi cells via k-means and searches only the nearest nprobe cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把向量切成子段,每段量化到学到的码本质心,大幅压缩内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PQ (Product Quantization) splits a vector into sub-segments and quantizes each to a learned codebook centroid, heavily compressing memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以聚类中心划分的空间区域,每个点归属最近的中心。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Voronoi cell is a region of space around a cluster center, with each point assigned to its nearest center.

scenario: 十亿 FP32 向量若全量驻内存,成本高得离谱,需要压缩才能放进 ANN 索引。
scenario_en: A billion FP32 vectors held fully in memory is prohibitively costly, so compression is needed to fit them in the ANN index.
q: PQ(Product Quantization)大致能压缩多少倍内存?代价是什么、下游影响什么?
q_en: Roughly how much memory does PQ compress, at what cost, and what does it affect downstream?
why: PQ 把向量切段、每段用码本质心的 id 代替原始浮点,大致压缩 10-50×。代价是量化误差→recall 略降。它决定十亿向量能否放进内存索引,直接影响单机能存多少物料、要不要分片。
why_en: PQ replaces each sub-vector with a codebook-centroid id, compressing memory roughly 10-50x at the cost of some recall loss, deciding whether a billion vectors fit in an in-memory index.
options: 压缩约 2×,代价是查询延迟翻倍,决定要不要上 GPU 加速
压缩约 10-50×,代价是量化误差让 recall 略降,决定十亿向量能否驻内存
压缩约 1000× 且几乎无损,所以任意规模都能单机放下,永远不用分片
不压缩内存,只压缩磁盘 IO 占用,代价是构建时间变长,查询时 decode 才解压反而更慢
options_en: About 2x compression, at the cost of doubled query latency, deciding whether to move to GPU acceleration.
About 10-50x compression, at the cost of quantization error slightly lowering recall — it decides whether a billion vectors fit in memory.
About 1000x compression and essentially lossless, so any scale fits on one machine and sharding is never needed.
It compresses disk IO, not memory, at the cost of longer build time — decompression only happens at query-time decode, making it slower.
optionExplanations: 2× 远低于 PQ 的实际压缩比;PQ 靠码本量化能到 10-50×。
对;10-50× 是标准锚点,拿 recall 换内存,直接决定内存索引容量与是否分片。
1000× 且无损不现实;PQ 是有损量化,压缩比也在 10-50× 量级。
PQ 压的就是向量内存占用(码本 id 代替浮点),不是只压磁盘 IO。
optionExplanations_en: 2x is far below PQ's real ratio; codebook quantization reaches 10-50x.
Correct — 10-50x is the standard anchor, trading recall for memory, directly setting in-memory index capacity and whether to shard.
1000x and lossless is unrealistic; PQ is lossy quantization with a 10-50x-scale ratio.
PQ compresses vector memory footprint (codebook ids replacing floats), not just disk IO.

termDefinitions.meaning: PQ 为每个子段学到的一组质心;向量子段用最近质心的 id 表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A codebook is the set of centroids PQ learns per sub-segment; each sub-vector is stored as the id of its nearest centroid.

scenario: 用 IVF 索引,发现召回率偏低漏掉相关项,想调 nprobe 参数来救。
scenario_en: Using an IVF index, recall is low and misses relevant items, so you consider tuning nprobe.
q: 调大 IVF 的 nprobe 会怎样?这个取舍的代价在哪?
q_en: What happens when you raise IVF's nprobe, and where is the tradeoff?
why: nprobe = 查询时搜索多少个最近的 Voronoi 单元。调大→覆盖更多候选单元→recall 上升,但要扫的单元变多→延迟近似线性上升。所以 nprobe 是 IVF 上「召回 vs 延迟」的直接旋钮。
why_en: nprobe is how many nearest Voronoi cells a query searches; raising it covers more candidates and lifts recall but scans more cells, so latency rises roughly linearly.
tradeoff: nprobe 大(recall 高、延迟高) vs nprobe 小(延迟低、易漏召回)
options: nprobe 越大 recall 越高、延迟近似线性上升,是召回 vs 延迟的旋钮
nprobe 只影响索引构建时间,查询延迟完全不受影响,所以尽量设到最大总没错
nprobe 越大延迟越低、recall 越低,和直觉相反,是用精度换速度的开关
nprobe 控制 PQ 的压缩率,与召回无关,主要影响索引占用的内存大小
options_en: Higher nprobe raises recall with roughly linear latency growth — it is the recall-vs-latency knob.
nprobe only affects index build time and never query latency, so cranking it to the maximum is always safe.
Higher nprobe lowers latency and lowers recall — counterintuitively a precision-for-speed switch.
nprobe controls PQ's compression ratio, unrelated to recall, mainly affecting index memory footprint.
optionExplanations: 对;多搜单元多找回相关项(recall↑)但扫描量增加(延迟↑),典型召回-延迟权衡。
nprobe 直接决定查询要扫多少单元,是查询期开销,不是构建期;设满会顶破延迟预算。
方向说反了:nprobe 大是 recall 高、延迟高,不是延迟低。
nprobe 是 IVF 的搜索广度参数,与 PQ 压缩率是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — more cells find more relevant items (recall up) but scan more (latency up), the classic recall-latency tradeoff.
nprobe directly sets how many cells a query scans — a query-time cost, not build-time; maxing it blows the latency budget.
Direction is reversed: high nprobe means high recall and high latency, not low latency.
nprobe is IVF's search-breadth parameter, separate from PQ's compression ratio.

termDefinitions.meaning: IVF 查询时搜索的最近 Voronoi 单元数量,越大覆盖越广、越慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: nprobe is the number of nearest Voronoi cells an IVF query searches; larger means broader coverage and slower queries.

scenario: 自建 HNSW 索引,要调 ef_construction 和 M 两个关键参数来平衡质量与资源。
scenario_en: Self-hosting an HNSW index, you tune the two key parameters ef_construction and M to balance quality against resources.
q: HNSW 的 ef_construction 和 M 分别控制什么?调大有什么代价?
q_en: What do HNSW's ef_construction and M each control, and what is the cost of raising them?
why: M 是每个节点的连边数(图有多稠密),ef_construction 是建图时每步考察的候选数(图建得多仔细)。两者调大 recall 更高,代价是内存与构建时间。
why_en: M is the number of links per node (graph density) and ef_construction is the build-time candidate breadth; raising either improves recall at the cost of more memory (M) and longer build time (ef_construction).
options: ef_construction 是查询超时时间、M 是最大内存上限,两者都是运行时限流参数
M=每节点连边数、ef_construction=建图候选广度;调大 recall 升,代价是内存与构建时间
M 控制向量的原始维度、ef_construction 控制向量压缩比例,和 recall 高低无关,只影响存储空间大小
两者都只影响查询延迟不影响 recall,调大只是让查询变慢没有质量收益
options_en: ef_construction is the query timeout and M is the memory cap; both are runtime throttling parameters.
M = links per node, ef_construction = build-time candidate breadth; raising them lifts recall at the cost of memory and build time.
M controls the vector's raw dimension and ef_construction controls the compression ratio, unrelated to recall, affecting only how much storage it uses.
Both only affect query latency, not recall; raising them just slows queries with no quality gain.
optionExplanations: 两者是建图期参数不是运行时限流;把建图广度和查询期的 ef_search 混为一谈了。
对;图越稠密越吃内存、建图越仔细越慢,两笔资源都是拿来换 recall 的。
这两个参数都不碰向量维度或压缩比,它们决定的是图结构本身的质量。
它们确实影响 recall(建图质量决定检索质量),不是只影响延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Both are build-time parameters, not runtime throttles; this conflates build breadth with query-time ef_search.
Correct — a denser graph costs memory and a more thorough build costs time; both resources are spent to buy recall.
Neither parameter touches vector dimension or compression ratio; they decide the quality of the graph structure itself.
They do affect recall (build quality drives search quality), not just latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 建图时每一步考察的候选邻居数,越大图质量越好、构建越慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_construction is how many candidate neighbors HNSW evaluates per build step; larger gives better graph quality but slower builds.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 中每个节点保留的连接数,越大图越稠密、recall 越高、内存越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: M is the number of links kept per HNSW node; larger makes the graph denser with higher recall and more memory.

scenario: 十亿级 ANN 索引放不进单机内存,团队在「全内存分片」和「单机磁盘索引」之间选,系统有 p99<200ms 的硬约束。
scenario_en: A billion-scale ANN index won't fit one machine's RAM; the team weighs sharded in-memory vs single-node disk-based index, under a hard p99<200ms constraint.
q: 有严格 p99 约束时,in-memory 分片 vs 磁盘索引该怎么选?
q_en: With a strict p99 constraint, how do you choose in-memory sharding vs a disk-based index?
why: 磁盘索引更便宜但尾延迟高、容易顶破 p99;有严格 p99 时应把索引分片到多机内存并行查再合并,内存查询延迟低且稳定。代价是机器成本和分片/合并的运维复杂度。
why_en: Disk indexes are cheaper but have high tail latency that breaks p99, so under a strict p99 you shard the index across machines' RAM and query in parallel, paying with machine cost and shard-merge complexity.
tradeoff: 内存分片(低稳尾延迟,贵+运维复杂) vs 磁盘索引(便宜,尾延迟高易破 p99)
whenOtherWins: 如果没有严格实时 p99 要求(如离线批量检索或后台推荐预算),磁盘索引更省钱,尾延迟高一点可以接受。
options: 选磁盘索引:它尾延迟更低更稳定,内存索引反而 p99 波动大,成本还高
选内存分片:分片到多机内存并行查再合并,延迟低而稳,代价是机器成本+分片运维复杂度
两者随便选都行:p99 只由模型决定,索引存哪里不影响尾延迟
选单机全内存不分片:直接买一台超大内存机器,避免分片就没有合并开销和尾延迟,成本和单点风险不用管
options_en: Pick disk: it has lower, steadier tail latency, while in-memory has high p99 jitter and costs more.
Pick in-memory sharding: shard across machines' RAM, query in parallel and merge for low steady latency, paying with machine cost and shard-merge ops complexity.
Either is fine: p99 is set by the model alone, and where the index lives does not affect tail latency.
Pick single-node all-in-memory without sharding: just buy one giant-RAM machine to avoid sharding, so there is no merge overhead or tail latency — cost and single-point risk don't matter.
optionExplanations: 反了;磁盘索引尾延迟更高(冷读、寻道),恰恰是它容易破 p99,内存才低而稳。
对;严格 p99 下要低且稳定的延迟,内存分片并行查最合适,代价是钱和运维。
索引介质直接决定读取延迟,磁盘 vs 内存对尾延迟影响巨大,不能不管。
十亿索引装不进单机内存正是前提;硬扛超大内存机成本极高且有单点风险,分片才是常规解。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed — disk has higher tail latency (cold reads, seeks), which is exactly what breaks p99; RAM is the low, steady option.
Correct — a strict p99 needs low steady latency, so sharded in-memory parallel query fits best, paying with cost and ops.
The storage medium directly sets read latency; disk vs RAM hugely affects tail latency and cannot be ignored.
The premise is that a billion vectors do not fit one machine's RAM; forcing a giant-RAM box is very costly with single-point risk, so sharding is the norm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引切成多份放到不同机器,查询并行发到所有分片再合并结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits the index across machines, querying all shards in parallel and merging the results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟:99% 的请求快于这个值,衡量尾部体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 is the 99th-percentile latency: 99% of requests are faster than this value, measuring tail experience.

scenario: 要为十亿向量选托管/自建向量库,团队小、想快速上线、能接受一定成本,但要求亚 10ms 检索且少运维。
scenario_en: Choosing a vector DB for a billion vectors: a small team wants fast time-to-market, accepts some cost, needs sub-10ms retrieval and minimal ops.
q: 小团队要少运维、快速上线,FAISS / ScaNN / Pinecone 该选哪个?
q_en: For a small team wanting minimal ops and fast launch, which of FAISS / ScaNN / Pinecone fits?
why: Pinecone 是托管 HNSW,亚 10ms 且免运维,最契合「小团队少运维快上线」。FAISS 最灵活但要自建自维;ScaNN 延迟最低但强绑 Google 基建。约束是运维成本而非极致延迟,所以选托管。
why_en: Pinecone is managed HNSW with sub-10ms latency and no ops, fitting a small team wanting a fast launch, while FAISS needs self-hosting and ScaNN couples to Google infra.
tradeoff: Pinecone(免运维,规模成本高+可调有限) vs FAISS(灵活最强,自建自维) vs ScaNN(延迟最低,绑 Google)
whenOtherWins: 如果要极致低延迟且已在 Google 基建上,ScaNN 亚 2ms(CPU)更优;如果要深度定制索引且有专人维护,FAISS 的灵活性无可替代。
options: 选 FAISS:它是全托管服务不用自己运维,小团队直接调 API 最省心
选 ScaNN:对小团队最友好、开箱即用,而且不绑定任何特定云厂商
选 Pinecone:托管 HNSW、亚 10ms 免运维,代价是成本与可调性有限
选自建 HNSW+PQ:虽然要自己养索引、耗大量人力持续维护,但小团队更该手搓获得完全控制
options_en: Pick FAISS: a fully managed service with no ops, so a small team just calls the API.
Pick ScaNN: friendliest for a small team, works out of the box, and locks you into no particular cloud vendor.
Pick Pinecone: managed HNSW, sub-10ms, no ops — paying with cost and limited tunability.
Pick self-built HNSW+PQ: despite having to maintain the index and pour ongoing headcount into it, a small team should hand-roll it for full control.
optionExplanations: FAISS 是库不是托管服务,得自己部署运维,与「少运维」诉求相反。
ScaNN 延迟最低但强耦合 Google 基建,不是「不依赖特定云、开箱即用」。
对;托管+亚10ms+免运维正好命中小团队约束,代价是贵和调参空间小。
小团队最缺的就是维护索引的人力,从零手搓与「少运维快上线」正相反。
optionExplanations_en: FAISS is a library, not a managed service — you deploy and operate it yourself, contrary to the minimal-ops need.
ScaNN has the lowest latency but couples tightly to Google infra, so it is not cloud-agnostic or turnkey.
Correct — managed + sub-10ms + no ops hits the small-team constraint, paying with cost and limited tuning.
A small team most lacks the headcount to maintain an index, so hand-rolling contradicts minimal-ops fast-launch.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 开源的向量检索库,支持 IVF+PQ/HNSW,灵活但需自建自维。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is Meta's open-source vector library supporting IVF+PQ/HNSW, flexible but self-hosted.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的向量检索库,用各向异性向量量化,CPU 上亚 2ms,但绑 Google 基建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ScaNN (Scalable Nearest Neighbors) is Google's library using anisotropic quantization for sub-2ms CPU search, coupled to Google infra.

termDefinitions.meaning: 托管向量数据库,底层托管 HNSW,亚 10ms、免运维但规模成本较高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pinecone is a managed vector database running managed HNSW with sub-10ms latency and no ops, at higher cost at scale.

scenario: 检索要按语言/地区/政策等元数据过滤,团队在 post-filtering 和 pre-filtering 之间权衡。
scenario_en: Retrieval must filter by metadata (language/region/policy), and the team weighs post-filtering vs pre-filtering.
q: post-filtering 和 pre-filtering 在机制和风险上有什么区别?
q_en: How do post-filtering and pre-filtering differ in mechanism and risk?
why: post-filtering 先检索再丢不合规项,简单,但过滤太狠会让结果不足 top-k。pre-filtering 按元数据分区只搜相关区,保数量但分区数暴涨。
why_en: Post-filtering searches ANN first then drops items failing the filter (simple, but heavy filtering can shrink the set below top-k), while pre-filtering partitions the index by metadata and searches only the relevant partition (guarantees count but multiplies partitions).
tradeoff: post-filtering(简单,结果数可能不足 top-k) vs pre-filtering(保证数量,分区暴涨)
diagram:
flowchart TB
  subgraph Post[post-filtering]
    P1["ANN 检索 top-k"] --> P2["丢弃不合规项"] --> P3["可能少于 top-k"]
  end
  subgraph Pre[pre-filtering]
    R1["按元数据分区"] --> R2["只搜相关分区"] --> R3["保证结果数量"]
  end
options: post-filtering 先分区再搜、pre-filtering 先搜再丢,两者只是叫法不同结果一样
post-filtering 先搜再丢不合规项(可能不足 top-k);pre-filtering 只搜相关元数据分区
两者都保证结果数量,区别只是 post 更快、pre 更省内存,没有其他取舍
post-filtering 只能过滤数值字段、pre-filtering 只能过滤文本字段,按字段类型二选一,不能混用
options_en: Post-filtering partitions then searches, pre-filtering searches then drops — just different names for the same result.
Post-filtering searches then drops non-compliant items (may fall below top-k); pre-filtering searches only the relevant metadata partition.
Both guarantee result count, differing only in that post is faster and pre saves memory, with no other tradeoff.
Post-filtering can filter only numeric fields and pre-filtering only text fields, chosen by field type — the two can't be mixed.
optionExplanations: 定义弄反了:post 是先搜后丢、pre 是先分区后搜,结果风险也不同。
对;核心区别是「先搜后丢会数量不足」vs「先分区保数量但分区膨胀」。
post 不保证数量(过滤后可能少于 top-k),这正是它的主要风险。
两者与字段是数值还是文本无关,过滤逻辑一样,区别在过滤发生在检索前还是后。
optionExplanations_en: Definitions reversed: post searches then drops, pre partitions then searches, with different risks.
Correct — the core difference is search-then-drop can under-fill vs partition-first guarantees count but bloats partitions.
Post does not guarantee count (may fall below top-k after filtering), which is its main risk.
Neither depends on numeric vs text fields; the filter logic is the same, differing in whether it runs before or after retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先做 ANN 检索,再把不满足元数据条件的结果丢掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Post-filtering runs ANN retrieval first, then drops results that fail the metadata condition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先按元数据把索引分区,查询只在符合条件的分区里检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-filtering partitions the index by metadata first, so a query only searches the qualifying partition.

scenario: 线上用 post-filtering,某些强过滤(小语种+特定地区)下,ANN 返回 top-k 后被过滤到只剩几条,结果集不足以填满页面。
scenario_en: In production with post-filtering, some strong filters (rare language + specific region) shrink the ANN top-k to just a few items, not enough to fill the page.
q: post-filtering 返回结果少于 top-k,最该怎么修?
q_en: When post-filtering returns fewer than top-k, what is the best fix?
why: 根因是「先检索再丢」在强过滤下会把集合丢到不足 top-k。最直接的修法是改成 pre-filtering:按该元数据把索引分区、只在相关分区里检索,从源头保证够 top-k 个合规候选。
why_en: The root cause is search-then-drop shrinking the set under strong filters, so the direct fix is pre-filtering: partition the index by that metadata and search only the relevant partition to guarantee enough compliant candidates.
tradeoff: pre-filtering(保证数量,分区管理成本) vs 继续 post-filtering(简单,强过滤下数量不足)
whenOtherWins: 如果过滤只是偶发轻度(大多数请求过滤后仍够 top-k),简单加大 over-retrieval 倍数继续 post-filtering 就够,不必上分区。
options: 调大 ANN 的 nprobe/ef 一直加,直到过滤后凑够 top-k,不改过滤策略
改成 pre-filtering:按该元数据把索引分区、只搜相关分区,从源头保证够数
放宽过滤条件,把不合规项也一并展示给用户,先把结果数量凑够再说
把 top-k 直接设成 1,只要有一条结果就不算「少于 top-k」
options_en: Keep raising ANN's nprobe/ef until enough survive filtering, without changing the filter strategy.
Switch to pre-filtering: partition the index by that metadata and search only the relevant partition, guaranteeing enough at the source.
Relax the filter and surface non-compliant items too, prioritizing filling the result count.
Set top-k to 1, so any single surviving result no longer counts as 'fewer than top-k'.
optionExplanations: 一味加大检索广度成本高且不稳,强过滤下仍可能不够,治标不治本。
对;分区检索让返回的每一条都天然合规,从根上保证数量,是标准解。
展示不合规项违反过滤本意(语言/地区/政策),是拿合规换数量,不可取。
把 top-k 降到 1 是掩盖问题,不能满足页面需要的结果数量。
optionExplanations_en: Just widening retrieval is costly and unstable, and may still under-fill under strong filters — treating the symptom.
Correct — partitioned search makes every returned item compliant by construction, guaranteeing count at the source, the standard fix.
Showing non-compliant items defeats the filter's purpose (language/region/policy), trading compliance for count.
Dropping top-k to 1 hides the problem and fails to deliver the result count the page needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: post-filtering 时多取几倍 top-k 候选,预留被过滤掉的余量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An over-retrieval multiplier fetches several times top-k in post-filtering to leave headroom for items that get filtered out.

scenario: 既有高基数维度(国家/语言,几百上千个值)又有低基数维度(是否成人内容等),想兼顾结果数量保证和分区可控。
scenario_en: You have both high-cardinality dims (country/language, hundreds of values) and low-cardinality dims (e.g. is-adult), and want both count guarantees and manageable partitions.
q: 同时有高基数和低基数过滤维度时,混合过滤该怎么分工?
q_en: With both high- and low-cardinality filter dims, how should hybrid filtering divide the work?
why: 对高基数维度(国家/语言)做 pre-filtering 分区,保证结果数量且分区数可控;对低基数维度用 post-filtering + over-retrieval 倍数在检索后过滤。这样既不让分区随所有维度组合爆炸,又保住数量。
why_en: Partition (pre-filter) on high-cardinality dims like country/language to guarantee count with a manageable partition count, and post-filter low-cardinality dims with an over-retrieval multiplier, so partitions don't explode across all dimension combinations.
tradeoff: 高基数 pre + 低基数 post(分区可控且保数量) vs 全维度 pre(分区组合爆炸)
whenOtherWins: 如果所有过滤维度都是低基数且过滤很轻,直接全 post-filtering + 适当过取倍数最简单,不必分区。
options: 对所有维度都做 pre-filtering 分区,维度越多分区越细,数量最有保证
对所有维度都做 post-filtering,统一在检索后过滤,避免任何分区管理
高基数维度(国家/语言)pre 分区保数量,低基数维度 post 过滤+过取倍数
对低基数维度 pre 分区、高基数维度 post 过滤,因为低基数分区少最省事
options_en: Pre-filter (partition) on every dimension; the more dimensions the finer the partitions, best for count.
Post-filter every dimension, filtering uniformly after retrieval to avoid any partition management.
Pre-partition high-cardinality dims (country/language) to guarantee count, and post-filter low-cardinality dims with an over-retrieval multiplier.
Pre-partition low-cardinality dims and post-filter high-cardinality dims, since few low-cardinality partitions are simplest.
optionExplanations: 对所有维度分区会让分区数按维度组合指数爆炸,存储和管理不可控。
全 post 在强过滤维度上又会回到「数量不足 top-k」的老问题。
对;高基数维度分区数可控且保数量,低基数留给 post,兼顾两端,是混合过滤的标准分工。
反了:高基数才该分区(分区数由值域决定但仍可控且保数量),低基数分区收益小、更适合 post。
