optionExplanations_en: Partitioning every dimension explodes partitions combinatorially, making storage and management unmanageable.
All-post reintroduces the under-top-k problem on strongly filtering dimensions.
Correct — high-cardinality partitions stay manageable and guarantee count, low-cardinality goes to post, balancing both, the standard hybrid split.
Reversed: high-cardinality dims are the ones to partition (guaranteeing count), while low-cardinality dims gain little from partitioning and suit post-filtering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个维度可能取值的数量;国家/语言是高基数,布尔标记是低基数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is how many distinct values a dimension can take; country/language are high-cardinality, boolean flags are low.

scenario: 粗排要在 10-30ms 内给候选生成来的~1000 个候选打分,选出~100 个进精排。
scenario_en: Coarse ranking must score the ~1000 candidates from candidate generation in 10-30ms and pass ~100 to fine re-ranking.
q: 粗排(coarse ranking)用什么模型、吃什么特征、预算多少?
q_en: What models, features, and budget does coarse ranking use?
why: 粗排用轻量模型(逻辑回归/浅层 MLP/小 GBDT),吃 embedding 之外的特征(user-item 交互计数、时段、设备、简单交叉),预算 10-30ms,把~1000 筛到~100。它比候选生成用更多特征、但仍要快。
why_en: Coarse ranking uses light models (logistic regression, shallow MLP, small GBDT) with features beyond embeddings (interaction counts, time-of-day, device, simple crosses) in a 10-30ms budget, cutting ~1000 to ~100.
options: 用最重的 transformer 多任务模型,吃全部原始特征,预算放宽到 100ms 追求最高精度
只用两塔 embedding 的余弦相似度重排,不引入任何新特征,和候选生成完全一样
轻量模型(LR/浅层 MLP/小 GBDT)吃交互计数/时段/设备特征,10-30ms 把千级筛到百级
不打分,直接按 item 热度排序取前 100,粗排本质是个热度榜
options_en: Use the heaviest multi-task transformer over all raw features, relaxing the budget to 100ms for max accuracy.
Just re-rank by two-tower embedding cosine similarity with no new features, identical to candidate generation.
Light models (LR/shallow MLP/small GBDT) over interaction-count/time-of-day/device features cut thousands to hundreds in 10-30ms.
Do not score at all; sort by item popularity and take the top 100 — coarse ranking is essentially a popularity board.
optionExplanations: 重 transformer + 100ms 是精排的做法,粗排要在千级候选上保持轻快。
粗排的价值正是引入 embedding 之外的新特征,只用余弦相似度等于没做粗排。
对;轻模型 + 交互/上下文特征 + 10-30ms,是粗排的标准配置。
纯热度榜忽略了个性化交互特征,粗排要打个性化分而非全局热度。
optionExplanations_en: Heavy transformer + 100ms is fine-ranking; coarse ranking must stay light over thousands of candidates.
Coarse ranking's value is adding features beyond embeddings; cosine-only means no real coarse ranking.
Correct — light models + interaction/context features + 10-30ms is the standard coarse-ranking setup.
A pure popularity board ignores personalized interaction features; coarse ranking scores personalization, not global popularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树,轻量高效的表格特征打分模型,常用于粗排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT (Gradient Boosted Decision Trees) is a light, efficient tabular scoring model often used for coarse ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层感知机,基础的全连接前馈神经网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) is a basic fully-connected feedforward neural network.

scenario: 粗排 p99 超预算。工程师第一反应是换更快的模型,但 profiling 显示模型推理只占一小部分。
scenario_en: Coarse ranking's p99 is over budget. The instinct is a faster model, but profiling shows inference is only a small fraction.
q: 粗排延迟的主要瓶颈通常是什么?该往哪里优化?
q_en: What is coarse ranking's dominant latency bottleneck, and where should you optimize?
why: 粗排要给~1000 个候选各取几百个特征,主要时间花在 feature store 检索而非模型推理。优化点是特征取用的批量化/缓存(一次批量取、缓存热特征),而不是换更快的模型。
why_en: Coarse ranking fetches hundreds of features for each of ~1000 candidates, so feature-store retrieval — not model inference — dominates latency, and the fix is batching/caching feature lookups.
tradeoff: 优化特征取用(批量+缓存,治本) vs 换更快模型(推理本就不是瓶颈,收效甚微)
whenOtherWins: 如果 profiling 显示推理确实占大头(如误用了重模型做粗排),那才该先换轻模型或量化;瓶颈定位要以实测为准。
diagram:
flowchart LR C["~1000 候选"] --> F["feature store 批量取
数百特征×1000 (主瓶颈)"] F --> M["轻量模型推理
(占比小)"] M --> O["~100 候选"]
options: 瓶颈是模型推理本身,应换更小的模型或做量化,feature store 取用开销小到可忽略不计
瓶颈是 feature store 检索(数百特征×1000 候选),应批量取用+缓存热特征
瓶颈是网络带宽,应把粗排服务和候选生成部署到同一进程消除 RPC
瓶颈是 GPU 显存不足,应加显存把 batch 开大,与特征取用无关
options_en: The bottleneck is model inference itself; swap in a smaller or quantized model, since feature-store lookups are small enough to ignore.
The bottleneck is feature-store retrieval (hundreds of features x 1000 candidates); batch the lookups and cache hot features.
The bottleneck is network bandwidth; co-locate coarse ranking and candidate generation in one process to eliminate RPC.
The bottleneck is GPU memory; add VRAM to enlarge the batch, unrelated to feature lookups.
optionExplanations: profiling 明确显示推理只占一小部分,换模型救不了主要延迟。
对;数百特征×1000 候选的取用才是大头,批量化+缓存才治本。
带宽不是这里的主因;主要是特征取用的次数与延迟,批量取才是关键。
粗排轻模型显存压力小,瓶颈在取特征而非显存或 batch 大小。
optionExplanations_en: Profiling clearly shows inference is a small fraction, so swapping models won't fix the main latency.
Correct — hundreds of features × 1000 candidates dominates; batching plus caching is the real fix.
Bandwidth is not the main cause here; it's the count and latency of feature lookups, so batching them is key.
A light coarse model has little VRAM pressure; the bottleneck is feature fetching, not memory or batch size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线存取模型特征的低延迟服务,推理前批量取候选的特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store is a low-latency service for serving model features, batch-fetched for candidates before inference.

scenario: 精排只需处理~100 个候选,预算可放宽到 20-50ms,要用最有表达力的模型。
scenario_en: Fine re-ranking handles only ~100 candidates with a relaxed 20-50ms budget and uses the most expressive models.
q: 精排为什么用得起最重的模型?典型用哪些模型、叠加什么?
q_en: Why can fine re-ranking afford the heaviest models, and what models/overlays does it use?
why: 候选已被前两级砍到~100,小集合才摊得起重模型的高单价,预算放宽到 20-50ms;典型是 DCN/多任务/inter-item transformer,再叠业务规则。
why_en: With only ~100 candidates left, the small set justifies expensive models in a 20-50ms budget, using DCN, multi-task models (engagement+satisfaction), and inter-item transformers, then business overlays like diversity/freshness/policy.
options: 因为精排全在 CPU 上跑没有 GPU 成本,所以模型大小可以任意加大
候选只剩~100,小集合才养得起 DCN/多任务重模型(20-50ms)
因为精排结果会被缓存复用,单次算得多贵都能摊薄,所以模型上不封顶
因为精排阶段不需要再取特征,省下的时间全给模型,所以能上超大模型
options_en: Because fine ranking runs entirely on CPU with no GPU cost, the model size can grow arbitrarily.
Only ~100 candidates remain, and only such a small set can afford heavy DCN/multi-task models within 20-50ms.
Because fine-ranking results are cached and reused, any per-call cost is amortized, so the model is unbounded.
Because fine ranking no longer fetches features, all the saved time goes to the model, enabling a huge one.
optionExplanations: 精排多在 GPU 上跑重模型,不是靠 CPU 免成本;根因是候选少了单价可承受。
对;小集合摊得起高单价,才用 DCN/多任务/transformer 并叠业务规则。
精排结果高度个性化+时效,难长期缓存复用;能上重模型是因候选少。
精排照样要取特征;能上重模型的根因是候选数从千级降到百级。
optionExplanations_en: Fine ranking usually runs heavy models on GPU, not free CPU; the reason is fewer candidates make per-item cost affordable.
Correct — a small set affords high per-item cost, enabling DCN/multi-task/transformers plus business overlays.
Fine-ranking results are highly personalized and time-sensitive, hard to cache long-term; heavy models are afforded by few candidates.
Fine ranking still fetches features; the reason heavy models are affordable is candidates dropping from thousands to hundreds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个模型同时预测多个目标(如点击 engagement 与满意度 satisfaction),共享表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multi-task model jointly predicts several targets (e.g. engagement and satisfaction) with a shared representation.

termDefinitions.term: business-logic overlay / 业务规则叠加
termDefinitions.meaning: 在模型分之上叠加的硬规则:多样性、新鲜度提升、政策过滤等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Business-logic overlays are hard rules applied on top of model scores: diversity, freshness boosting, policy filters.

scenario: 精排纯按分数排,结果前 5 个视频全来自同一个创作者,用户体验单调。
scenario_en: Ranking purely by score, the top 5 videos all come from one creator, making the feed monotonous.
q: 为什么精排后要加多样性等业务规则?不加会怎样?
q_en: Why add diversity and other business rules after fine ranking, and what happens without them?
why: 纯分数最优会让高分来源(同一创作者/同一话题)扎堆,体验单调、长期伤留存。多样性约束(限制同源占比)、新鲜度提升、政策过滤是叠在模型分之上的硬规则,把「单次相关最优」修正成「整体体验最优」。代价是牺牲一点单点相关性。
why_en: Pure top-score ranking clusters items from one source, hurting experience and retention, so diversity/freshness/policy overlays trade a bit of per-item relevance for better overall experience.
tradeoff: 多样性规则(整体体验更好,牺牲单点相关) vs 纯分数(单点最优但扎堆单调)
options: 不用加;模型分已经是全局最优,任何业务规则都只会拉低整体质量
加规则只是为了合规审计留痕,与用户体验无关,不加也不影响观感
纯分数会让同源/同话题扎堆伤留存,多样性/新鲜度规则把单点最优修正成整体最优
加规则是为了降低精排延迟,规则能提前砍掉一批候选让模型少算一些,和多样性体验无关
options_en: No need — the model score is already globally optimal, and any business rule only lowers overall quality.
Rules exist only for compliance audit trails, unrelated to user experience, so skipping them changes nothing.
Pure scoring clusters same-source/same-topic items and hurts retention; diversity/freshness rules turn per-item-optimal into overall-optimal.
Rules exist to cut fine-ranking latency by pruning a batch of candidates so the model computes less — unrelated to diversity or experience.
optionExplanations: 模型分优化的是单点相关,不含整体多样性;不加规则会扎堆,并非任何规则都降质。
多样性/新鲜度直接改变用户看到的排列,是体验问题不是纯审计。
对;规则把「单条最相关」修正为「整页最好看」,代价是略降单点相关性。
业务规则是排序后叠加的重排,不是为降延迟砍候选。
optionExplanations_en: The model score optimizes per-item relevance, not overall diversity; without rules items cluster, and not every rule lowers quality.
Diversity/freshness directly change what the user sees — an experience issue, not mere auditing.
Correct — rules turn most-relevant-per-item into best-overall-page, at the cost of slightly lower per-item relevance.
Business rules are a post-ranking rerank, not candidate pruning to cut latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制结果里同一来源/话题的占比,避免扎堆,提升整体体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A diversity constraint caps how many results share one source/topic to avoid clustering and improve overall experience.

scenario: 精排想上更大的 transformer 提升相关性,但单次推理逼近 50ms 预算上限,不能简单换回小模型。
scenario_en: Fine ranking wants a bigger transformer for relevance but inference nears the 50ms budget cap, and reverting to a small model isn't acceptable.
q: 精排面临「相关性 vs 延迟」矛盾时,怎么在不明显掉精度下压延迟?
q_en: Facing the relevance-vs-latency conflict in fine ranking, how do you cut latency without visibly losing accuracy?
why: 用量化(降精度加速)+知识蒸馏(把大模型能力压进小学生模型)在几乎不掉精度的前提下降延迟。相比直接换回小模型丢相关性、或硬扛大模型超预算,这是保住相关性又满足延迟的中间路。
why_en: Use quantization (lower precision for speed) plus knowledge distillation (compress the big model into a smaller student) to cut latency with minimal accuracy loss, unlike simply reverting to a small model.
tradeoff: 量化+蒸馏(几乎不掉精度地降延迟,需额外工程) vs 换小模型(简单但丢相关性)
whenOtherWins: 如果相关性差一点无所谓、工程资源紧张,直接用现成小模型最省事;蒸馏/量化的额外训练与验证成本只有在相关性关键时才值得。
options: 直接把 transformer 换成逻辑回归,虽然掉相关性但一定不超时,简单可靠
用量化(降精度加速)+知识蒸馏(大模型能力压进小模型),几乎不掉精度地压延迟
把精排预算从 50ms 硬调到 200ms,不改模型,让它慢慢算完
对每个请求缓存精排结果,第二次直接返回,绕开延迟问题
options_en: Just replace the transformer with logistic regression: it loses relevance but never times out — simple and reliable.
Use quantization (lower precision for speed) plus knowledge distillation (compress the big model into a small student) to cut latency with almost no accuracy loss.
Hard-raise the fine-ranking budget from 50ms to 200ms without changing the model, letting it finish slowly.
Cache each request's fine-ranking result and return it on the second hit, sidestepping the latency problem.
optionExplanations: 换 LR 是拿相关性换延迟,与「不明显掉精度」的目标冲突。
对;量化+蒸馏在保住相关性的同时降延迟,是相关性关键时的标准解。
把 p99 预算从 50ms 抬到 200ms 违反 SLA,是放弃延迟目标不是解决矛盾。
精排结果高度个性化时效强,难缓存复用,治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping to LR trades relevance for latency, conflicting with the no-visible-accuracy-loss goal.
Correct — quantization plus distillation cut latency while preserving relevance, the standard fix when relevance matters.
Raising the p99 budget from 50ms to 200ms violates the SLA — abandoning the latency goal, not resolving the conflict.
Highly personalized, time-sensitive fine-ranking results are hard to cache, so this treats the symptom.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大模型(teacher)的输出训练小模型(student),把能力压进更快的小模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Knowledge distillation trains a small student model on a big teacher's outputs, compressing capability into a faster model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权重/激活从高精度(FP32)降到低精度(FP16/INT8),加速推理、省内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers weights/activations from high precision (FP32) to low (FP16/INT8), speeding inference and saving memory.

q: 填空:三级漏斗每级的候选量级与延迟预算。
q_en: Fill in each funnel stage's candidate scale and latency budget.
text_en: Candidate generation: billions → ~{{500-2000}} candidates, budget {{10-20}}ms; coarse ranking: ~1000 → ~{{100}}, budget {{10-30}}ms; fine re-ranking: ~100 → final, budget {{20-50}}ms.
why: 记住量级递减(十亿→千→百)与预算递增(候选越少、模型越重、越舍得给时间)的对应关系:总预算被三级瓜分,任何一级超支都会顶破 p99。
why_en: Remember the shrinking counts (billions→thousands→hundreds) paired with growing budgets, since the total p99 is split across the three stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分配给某一级的时间上限,各级之和不能超过端到端 p99 目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget is the time ceiling allotted to a stage; the stages must sum within the end-to-end p99 target.

q: 填空:三级漏斗每一级在做的核心权衡。
q_en: Fill in the core tradeoff each funnel stage makes.
text: 漏斗每一级都用「更{{少}}的候选」换「更{{强}}的模型」——即拿{{广度}}换{{深度}};候选生成盯 {{recall}}(漏了不可恢复),后两级盯精度。
text_en: Each funnel stage trades {{fewer}} candidates for a {{heavier}} model — i.e. {{breadth}} for {{depth}}; candidate generation optimizes {{recall}} (misses are unrecoverable), later stages optimize precision.
why: 一句话记住漏斗:广度换深度。第一级 recall 优先(漏项不可逆),越往后候选越少、模型越重、越追求精度。
why_en: One-liner for the funnel: trade breadth for depth, with recall first up front (misses are irreversible) and precision growing downstream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回结果中真正相关的比例;后两级排序追求把最相关的排到最前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of returned results that are truly relevant; later ranking stages push the most relevant to the top.

scenario: 要给候选生成阶段定一个主指标来指导迭代;有人提议用 precision@k,有人提议 recall@k。
scenario_en: You must pick a primary metric to guide candidate-generation iteration; some propose precision@k, others recall@k.
q: 候选生成该以 recall@k 还是 precision@k 为主指标?为什么?
q_en: Should candidate generation optimize recall@k or precision@k, and why?
why: 候选生成盯 recall@k:它的职责是「别漏掉相关项」,漏了下游永远补不回来;精度(把最相关排最前)是后两级排序的活。用 precision 当主指标会奖励「少而准」,反而放大漏召回风险。
why_en: Candidate generation optimizes recall@k because its job is to not miss relevant items (misses are unrecoverable downstream), while precision — putting the most relevant on top — is the later ranking stages' job.
tradeoff: recall@k(不漏相关项,可能带进噪声由下游筛) vs precision@k(准但易漏,漏了不可逆)
whenOtherWins: 如果下游排序能力很弱、无法从噪声候选里挑出好结果,那才需要候选生成本身更看重 precision;通常下游足够强,recall 优先。
options: 以 precision@k 为主:候选越准确噪声越少,下游排序越省事,漏一点相关项也无所谓
以 recall@k 为主:职责是不漏相关项(漏了下游补不回),精度交给后两级排序
两个都不用,直接用点击率 CTR 当候选生成的主指标最贴近业务
用延迟当唯一主指标:候选生成只要够快,召回精度都不重要
options_en: Optimize precision@k: more precise, lower-noise candidates ease downstream ranking, and missing a few relevant items is fine.
Optimize recall@k: the job is not to miss relevant items (misses are unrecoverable downstream), leaving precision to later ranking stages.
Use neither; use click-through rate (CTR) as the primary metric since it is closest to business.
Use latency as the sole primary metric: as long as candidate generation is fast, recall and precision don't matter.
optionExplanations: 漏召回不可逆,precision 优先会奖励「少而漏」,与候选生成的职责相悖。
对;候选生成的天条是别漏相关项,精度是下游排序的目标。
CTR 是端到端业务指标,受下游排序主导,无法单独指导候选生成的召回。
只看延迟会牺牲召回质量;快但漏一堆相关项没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Misses are irreversible; prioritizing precision rewards few-but-missing, contradicting candidate generation's job.
Correct — candidate generation's cardinal rule is not to miss relevant items, leaving precision to downstream ranking.
CTR is an end-to-end business metric dominated by downstream ranking and cannot alone guide candidate-generation recall.
Optimizing latency alone sacrifices recall; fast but missing many relevant items is pointless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回前 k 个里相关项的比例;衡量「准不准」,是排序阶段目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@k is the fraction of the top-k that are relevant, measuring accuracy — the ranking stages' goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率:展示中被点击的比例,端到端业务指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions that get clicked, an end-to-end business metric.

scenario: 十亿级 ANN 索引已分片到多机,单个分片机器偶发宕机会让该分片的候选全查不到,且流量峰值时单副本扛不住。
scenario_en: A billion-scale ANN index is sharded across machines; a shard node's occasional crash makes that shard's candidates unreachable, and one replica can't absorb peak traffic.
q: 十亿级索引除了分片,为什么还要副本(replication)?
q_en: Beyond sharding, why does a billion-scale index also need replication?
why: 分片管容量与并行,副本管容错与负载:每分片 R 份拷贝,存储 = 索引总量 × R,峰值 QPS 被 R 均摊;代价是同步成本随 R 线性涨。
why_en: Sharding covers capacity and parallelism while replication covers fault tolerance and load: with R copies per shard, storage = index size x R and peak QPS is split across R, so sync cost grows linearly with R.
options: 副本是为了提高召回率:多份索引投票取交集能提升 recall,与容错无关
副本给每个分片多份拷贝→容错+峰值负载均衡,代价是存储/同步翻倍
副本是为了压缩内存:每份副本存不同精度,合起来能省一半显存
有了分片就不需要副本,分片本身已经天然容错,再加副本纯属浪费
options_en: Replication boosts recall: multiple index copies vote and intersect to raise recall, unrelated to fault tolerance.
Replication keeps several copies per shard for fault tolerance and peak load balancing, at the cost of doubled storage/sync.
Replication compresses memory: each replica stores a different precision, together halving VRAM.
Once sharded you need no replicas — shards are inherently fault-tolerant, so replication is pure waste.
optionExplanations: 副本存的是同一份数据的拷贝,不是投票机制,和 recall 提升无关。
对;这是两个正交维度,容量不够加分片、可用性不够加副本,互相替代不了。
副本是相同数据的冗余拷贝,不是不同精度分层,压缩是 PQ 的活。
分片本身没有冗余,单分片宕机就丢该分片数据,必须靠副本容错。
optionExplanations_en: Replicas are copies of the same data, not a voting scheme, and don't raise recall.
Correct — two orthogonal axes: add shards when capacity runs out, add replicas when availability does; neither substitutes for the other.
Replicas are redundant copies of identical data, not mixed-precision tiers; compression is PQ's job.
Sharding alone has no redundancy — one shard's crash loses that shard's data, so replication is required for fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个分片保存多份相同拷贝,用于容错和分摊查询负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication keeps multiple identical copies of each shard for fault tolerance and to spread query load.

scenario: 检索既要向量语义相似,又要能按关键词命中和复杂元数据过滤(如同时匹配品牌词并限定地区),团队想少运维。
scenario_en: Retrieval needs vector semantic similarity plus keyword hits and complex metadata filters (e.g. match a brand term and restrict region), with minimal ops.
q: 需要「向量+关键词混合检索且带复杂元数据过滤」时,四个候选里 Weaviate 相对更合适在哪?
q_en: When you need hybrid vector+keyword retrieval with complex metadata filters, why is Weaviate relatively fitting among the four?
why: Weaviate 原生支持 HNSW + 关键词的混合检索和元数据过滤,契合「语义+关键词+复杂过滤」需求。代价是复杂过滤下延迟会上升;若只需纯向量亚 10ms,Pinecone/FAISS/ScaNN 更简单快。
why_en: Weaviate natively supports HNSW plus keyword hybrid search and metadata filtering, fitting semantic+keyword+complex-filter needs, at the cost of higher latency under complex filters.
tradeoff: Weaviate(混合检索+元数据过滤灵活,复杂过滤延迟高) vs 纯向量库(更快但过滤/关键词弱)
whenOtherWins: 如果只需纯向量相似度、不要关键词或复杂过滤且要极致低延迟,ScaNN/Pinecone 更快更简单,不需要 Weaviate 的混合能力。
options: Weaviate 延迟最低,任何复杂过滤下都比其他三个快,所以选它
Weaviate 原生支持 HNSW+关键词混合检索与元数据过滤,代价是延迟升高
Weaviate 是唯一支持 GPU 的向量库,靠 GPU 算力来做混合检索加速
Weaviate 压缩率最高,靠 PQ 把索引压到最小,所以适合复杂过滤
options_en: Weaviate has the lowest latency and beats the other three under any complex filter, so pick it.
Weaviate natively supports HNSW + keyword hybrid search with metadata filtering, at the cost of higher latency.
Weaviate is the only GPU-capable vector database and accelerates hybrid search with GPU compute.
Weaviate has the highest compression, using PQ to shrink the index, which suits complex filtering.
optionExplanations: Weaviate 在复杂过滤下延迟反而升高,并非最低延迟;它胜在混合检索能力。
对;它的差异化是混合检索+灵活元数据过滤,而不是极致延迟。
GPU 支持不是 Weaviate 的卖点(FAISS 也有 GPU);它的卖点是混合检索。
压缩率不是 Weaviate 的差异点;它靠原生混合检索+过滤取胜。
optionExplanations_en: Weaviate's latency actually rises under complex filters, so it is not the lowest; its edge is hybrid search.
Correct — its differentiator is hybrid retrieval plus flexible metadata filtering, not peak latency.
GPU support is not Weaviate's selling point (FAISS also has GPU); its selling point is hybrid search.
Compression is not Weaviate's differentiator; it wins on native hybrid search plus filtering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持 HNSW + 关键词混合检索与元数据过滤的向量数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weaviate is a vector database supporting HNSW plus keyword hybrid search and metadata filtering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用向量语义相似度和关键词/词法匹配打分,再融合排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid search scores by both vector semantic similarity and keyword/lexical match, then fuses the rankings.

scenario: 面试官追问:候选生成用 ANN,那 ANN 的 recall 和延迟能同时拉满吗?
scenario_en: The interviewer probes: with ANN in candidate generation, can you max out both recall and latency at once?
q: ANN 检索里 recall 和延迟是什么关系?这对参数调优意味着什么?
q_en: What is the relationship between recall and latency in ANN search, and what does it mean for tuning?
why: ANN 是近似检索:搜得越广(HNSW 的 ef_search、IVF 的 nprobe 越大)recall 越高但延迟越高,二者是此消彼长。调优就是在 p99 预算内把 recall 顶到最高,而非同时拉满——鱼与熊掌不可兼得。
why_en: ANN is approximate: searching wider (higher ef_search/nprobe) raises recall but also latency, so tuning maximizes recall within the p99 budget rather than maxing both.
tradeoff: 搜索更广(recall 高、延迟高) vs 搜索更窄(延迟低、recall 低)
options: recall 和延迟无关,可以同时拉满,只要机器够快
recall 越高延迟一定越低,二者正相关,调大搜索广度双赢
搜得越广 recall 越高但延迟也越高,调优是在 p99 预算内把 recall 顶到最高
延迟只由向量维度决定,与搜索广度无关,调 ef_search/nprobe 只改变 recall 不影响延迟
options_en: Recall and latency are unrelated and can both be maxed, given fast enough machines.
Higher recall always means lower latency — they are positively correlated, so widening the search is win-win.
Searching wider raises recall but also latency, so tuning means maximizing recall within the p99 budget.
Latency depends only on vector dimension, unrelated to search breadth, so tuning ef_search/nprobe only changes recall, not latency.
optionExplanations: 近似检索里 recall 与延迟由搜索广度耦合,加机器改变不了单查询的此消彼长。
方向反了:recall 高通常伴随延迟高,不是延迟低。
对;这就是 ANN 调优的本质——在延迟预算内尽量拉高 recall。
ef_search/nprobe 直接决定扫描量,是延迟主因,不能说与广度无关。
optionExplanations_en: In approximate search recall and latency are coupled by search breadth; adding machines doesn't remove the per-query tradeoff.
Direction reversed: high recall usually comes with high latency, not low.
Correct — this is the essence of ANN tuning: push recall as high as possible within the latency budget.
ef_search/nprobe directly set scan volume and are the main latency driver, so they're not unrelated to breadth.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 查询期考察的候选数,越大 recall 越高、延迟越高(与建图期 ef_construction 不同)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_search is HNSW's query-time candidate breadth; larger raises recall and latency (distinct from build-time ef_construction).

scenario: 有人提议砍掉粗排,让候选生成的~1000 候选直接进精排,以简化流水线。
scenario_en: Someone proposes dropping coarse ranking and feeding candidate generation's ~1000 candidates straight into fine re-ranking to simplify the pipeline.
q: 如果砍掉粗排,直接让~1000 候选进精排,会发生什么?
q_en: What happens if you skip coarse ranking and feed ~1000 candidates directly into fine re-ranking?
why: 精排是最贵的模型,只在~100 候选上跑才付得起。让~1000 直接进精排会让精排算力/延迟约 10× 膨胀,顶破 20-50ms 预算。粗排的作用正是用轻量模型把千级先削到百级,为精排减负。
why_en: Fine ranking is the most expensive model and only affordable on ~100 candidates, so feeding ~1000 inflates its compute/latency roughly 10x and blows the budget — coarse ranking exists to pre-cut thousands to hundreds.
options: 没影响:精排本来就能处理任意数量候选,砍掉粗排能简化系统还更准
精排延迟大降:候选虽多但精排会自动只挑前 100 个算,其余跳过
精排算力/延迟约 10× 膨胀顶破预算,粗排正是为它把千级削到百级
候选生成会自动补偿:检测到没有粗排后把候选压到 100,精排无需任何改动
options_en: No impact: fine ranking can handle any candidate count, so dropping coarse ranking simplifies and improves accuracy.
Fine-ranking latency drops sharply: despite more candidates, it auto-picks only the top 100 to score and skips the rest.
Fine-ranking compute/latency inflates ~10x and blows the budget; coarse ranking exists to cut thousands to hundreds for it.
Candidate generation auto-compensates: detecting no coarse stage, it compresses candidates to 100 with no fine-ranking change.
optionExplanations: 精排单价高,候选从 100 涨到 1000 直接约 10× 成本,不可能又快又准。
精排不会「自动只算前 100」——判断谁是前 100 正是粗排要先做的事。
对;粗排是精排的减负阀门,砍掉它精排就被千级候选压垮。
候选生成不感知下游是否有粗排,也不负责把候选压到百级,那是粗排的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Fine ranking is costly per item, so going from 100 to 1000 candidates ~10x's cost — it cannot stay fast and accurate.
Fine ranking cannot auto-score only the top 100 — deciding which 100 is exactly coarse ranking's job.
Correct — coarse ranking is the relief valve for fine ranking; drop it and fine ranking is crushed by thousands.
Candidate generation is unaware of downstream stages and doesn't compress to hundreds — that is coarse ranking's role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏斗第二级:轻量模型给千级候选打分,削到百级交给精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coarse ranking is the funnel's second stage: a light model scores thousands of candidates down to hundreds for fine re-ranking.

scenario: 一个在笔记本上 20ms 出结果的模型,上线到 100K QPS 后 p99 冲到 500ms。
scenario_en: A model that returns in 20ms on a laptop blows past 500ms p99 once serving 100K QPS.
q: 低延迟大规模服务的四大支柱(不含硬件优化)是哪些?
q_en: What are the four pillars of low-latency serving at scale (excluding hardware optimization)?
why: dev→prod 是个延迟工程问题,四支柱是:模型/结果缓存、预计算、尾延迟 SLA(按 p99 定)、水平扩展。量化/编译等硬件手段属于下一课,不在这四条里。
why_en: The dev-to-prod gap is a latency-engineering problem addressed by four pillars: caching, pre-computation, tail-latency SLAs (framed on p99), and horizontal scaling.
diagram:
flowchart TB A["低延迟服务"] --> B["缓存
结果/特征"] A --> C["预计算
离线出结果"] A --> D["尾延迟 SLA
按 p99"] A --> E["水平扩展
无状态+LB"]
options: 缓存、预计算、尾延迟 SLA(按 p99)、水平扩展
量化、剪枝、编译优化、边缘部署,这些是硬件层模型优化技巧
分库分表、读写分离、主从复制、消息队列
梯度累积、混合精度训练、学习率调度、早停
options_en: Caching, pre-computation, tail-latency SLAs (on p99), and horizontal scaling.
Quantization, pruning, compilation, and edge deployment — these are hardware-level model-optimization techniques.
Database sharding, read-write splitting, primary-replica replication, and message queues.
Gradient accumulation, mixed-precision training, learning-rate scheduling, and early stopping.
optionExplanations: 对;这四条是系统层的延迟工程,和模型准确率无关,是本课主线。
量化/剪枝/编译/边缘是硬件层模型优化,属于下一课,不是这四支柱。
分库分表是传统数据层扩展,不是 ML 推理服务的四支柱。
这些是训练侧技巧,与线上推理延迟无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — these four are system-level latency engineering, independent of model accuracy, the lesson's spine.
Quantization/pruning/compilation/edge are hardware-level model optimization from the next lesson, not these pillars.
Database sharding is classic data-tier scaling, not the four serving pillars.
These are training-side tricks, unrelated to online inference latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数,衡量服务承受的并发请求量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures how many requests per second a service handles.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟:99% 的请求快于此值,衡量尾部体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 is the 99th-percentile latency: 99% of requests are faster than this, measuring tail experience.

scenario: 推荐服务里大量用户在短时间内重复发起相同查询(相同输入特征),结果几分钟内不会变。
scenario_en: In a recommendation service many users repeat identical queries (same input features) within a short window, and the result won't change for minutes.
q: 对重复的相同查询,最该先上哪种缓存?TTL 怎么定?
q_en: For repeated identical queries, which cache first, and how do you set TTL?
why: 结果缓存(Redis/Memcached)按输入特征做 key、存模型输出,命中就亚毫秒返回,效果取决于命中率。TTL 平衡新鲜度与命中率:短=新但命中低,长=命中高但易旧;按信号变化速度定。
why_en: Result caching (Redis/Memcached) keys on input features and stores the output for sub-ms hits, with TTL balancing freshness against hit rate — set it by how fast the signal changes.
tradeoff: 长 TTL(命中率高但结果旧) vs 短 TTL(新鲜但命中率低)
whenOtherWins: 如果查询几乎不重复(每个用户上下文都独一无二),结果缓存命中率极低不划算,应转向缓存中间特征或直接扩容。
options: 特征缓存:只缓存中间特征,最终输出每次重算,靠特征复用摊掉推理成本
结果缓存:按输入特征做 key 存输出,命中亚毫秒;TTL 按信号变化速度定
把模型权重常驻 GPU 显存,省掉每次请求重新加载权重的开销,重复查询自然变快
缓存 GPU 编译好的内核,避免每次推理重新编译算子,首次之后的调用更快
options_en: Feature caching: cache only intermediate features and recompute the final output every time, amortizing inference cost through feature reuse.
Result caching: key on input features, store the output for sub-ms hits, and set TTL by how fast the signal changes.
Keep model weights resident in GPU memory so no request reloads weights, which naturally speeds up repeated queries.
Cache the GPU's compiled kernels so inference never recompiles the operators, making calls after the first one faster.
optionExplanations: 重复相同查询下,直接缓存最终结果收益最大;特征缓存是更深一层、当结果不可复用时才用。
对;相同输入重复出现正是结果缓存的甜点,TTL 由信号变化速度决定。
权重常驻显存是必备基操,但它不解决「重复查询免算」这个命中率问题。
缓存编译内核是编译框架的事,与重复查询的结果复用无关。
optionExplanations_en: For repeated identical queries, caching the final result pays most; feature caching is one layer deeper for when results aren't reusable.
Correct — repeated identical inputs are the sweet spot for result caching, with TTL set by signal change rate.
Weights resident in VRAM is table stakes but doesn't address the hit-rate problem of skipping repeated queries.
Caching compiled kernels is the compiler's job, unrelated to reusing results for repeated queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长,到期即失效,平衡新鲜度与命中率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is how long a cache entry stays valid before expiring, balancing freshness against hit rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按输入特征做 key,直接缓存模型输出,命中即免推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Result caching keys on input features and stores the model output, skipping inference on a hit.

scenario: 结果缓存的 TTL 被设得很长以拉高命中率,但用户切换了地理位置后仍看到旧城市的结果。
scenario_en: Result-cache TTL is set long for a high hit rate, but after a user changes location they still see stale results for the old city.
q: TTL 设太长会有什么后果?快速变化的上下文为什么让失效很难?
q_en: What's the consequence of too-long a TTL, and why does fast-changing context make invalidation hard?
why: TTL 太长→命中率高但结果旧;用户切位置这类上下文突变让缓存 key 背后的前提失效,却没到期,只能返回错的旧结果。难点在于失效要么靠 TTL 被动等,要么靠上下文变化主动清,后者要能检测到变化。
why_en: Too-long TTL raises hit rate but serves stale results, and fast context changes (user switches location) invalidate the assumption behind a key that hasn't expired, so invalidation must actively detect the change rather than wait out the TTL.
tradeoff: 长 TTL(命中率高,上下文突变时返回旧结果) vs 主动失效(新鲜,需检测变化的机制)
options: TTL 太长完全没坏处:命中率越高越好,旧结果用户根本察觉不到,不需要主动失效
TTL 太长会降低命中率让缓存形同虚设,所以应该尽量设短,新鲜度不受影响
TTL 太长→命中高但结果旧;上下文突变让前提失效却没到期,只能返回旧结果
TTL 与新鲜度无关,它只决定缓存占多少内存,过期只是为了回收空间
options_en: Too-long TTL has no downside: a higher hit rate is always better, users never notice stale results, and no active invalidation is needed.
Too-long TTL lowers the hit rate and makes the cache useless, so set it as short as possible; freshness is unaffected either way.
Too-long TTL raises hits but serves stale results; a context change invalidates the assumption before expiry, so you return old answers.
TTL has nothing to do with freshness — it only decides how much memory the cache holds, and expiry just reclaims space.
optionExplanations: 上下文突变时旧结果就是错的,用户能感知(看到旧城市),不是无坏处。
反了:TTL 长是命中率高,代价是旧;短才是命中低。
对;长 TTL 的代价是上下文突变下返回旧结果,主动失效要能检测到变化。
TTL 直接决定结果能存多久即新鲜度,不只是内存占用。
optionExplanations_en: On a context change the stale result is wrong and noticeable (old city), so it's not harmless.
Reversed: long TTL means high hit rate at the cost of staleness; short TTL is the low-hit case.
Correct — long TTL's cost is stale results under context change, and active invalidation must detect the change.
TTL directly sets how long a result lives (freshness), not just memory footprint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让过期或不再正确的缓存条目作废,可被动等 TTL 或主动清。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache invalidation removes entries that are expired or no longer correct, either passively via TTL or actively.

scenario: 推理必须在线跑(结果不可复用),但每次请求都要重算一批昂贵的地理特征(如 Uber ETA 的路网/区域特征)。
scenario_en: Inference must run online (results not reusable), but each request recomputes a batch of expensive geo features (like Uber ETA's road/zone features).
q: 推理无法复用但特征昂贵时,该缓存哪一层?
q_en: When inference can't be reused but features are expensive, which layer do you cache?
why: 缓存深一层:结果不能复用,但昂贵的中间特征(地理特征)可缓存复用,即使推理仍在线跑也能砍掉每请求的重复特征计算。Uber ETA 缓存地理特征就是这招。
why_en: Cache one layer deeper: results aren't reusable but expensive intermediate features (geo features) can be, cutting per-request recomputation even while inference runs online, as Uber ETA does.
tradeoff: 特征缓存(省重复特征计算,占内存) vs 不缓存(每请求重算昂贵特征)
whenOtherWins: 如果整个结果本身可复用(相同输入重复出现),直接上结果缓存收益更大,不必只缓存特征。
options: 缓存最终结果:虽然每次推理的输入都不同、结果不可复用,强行缓存也能提速
缓存中间特征:昂贵的地理特征可复用,推理仍在线跑但省掉重复特征计算
缓存整个模型的前向输出张量,下次请求就直接跳过整个网络的计算
不缓存任何东西,把特征计算全搬到 GPU 上并行算就已经够快了
options_en: Cache the final result: even though every inference gets different inputs and results aren't reusable, forcing a cache still speeds things up.
Cache intermediate features: the expensive geo features are reusable, so inference still runs online but skips recomputing them.
Cache the model's whole forward output tensor so the next request skips the entire network.
Cache nothing — just move all feature computation onto the GPU and it is already fast enough.
optionExplanations: 结果不可复用,缓存它命中率近乎为零,白占内存。
对;结果不可复用时就退一层,缓存那批开销大的中间特征,推理仍在线跑但省了重复计算。
整个前向输出等价于结果,同样不可复用,缓存无意义。
上 GPU 减单次耗时,但仍每请求重算,特征缓存才免去重复计算。
optionExplanations_en: Results aren't reusable, so caching them yields near-zero hits and wastes memory.
Correct — since the result itself can't be reused, drop one layer down and cache the pricier intermediate features instead, still paying for inference each time.
The full forward output equals the result, equally non-reusable, so caching it is pointless.
GPU cuts per-call time but still recomputes every request; feature caching removes the repeated computation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存昂贵的中间特征而非最终结果,推理在线时也能省重复计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature caching stores expensive intermediate features rather than final results, saving recomputation even with online inference.

scenario: user-item 对可预测且量大(如首页推荐槽位),可以在低峰离线算好、存起来供瞬时取用,能接受结果几小时的滞后。
scenario_en: The user-item pairs are predictable and numerous (e.g. homepage slots), computable offline off-peak and stored for instant retrieval, with a few hours of staleness acceptable.
q: 对可预测的大量组合、能容忍一定滞后,该用哪种手段?代价是什么?
q_en: For predictable, high-volume pairs that tolerate some staleness, which technique, and at what cost?
why: 全量预计算:把推理搬到离线,低峰算好整份 slate 存起来,线上零推理成本瞬时取。代价是新鲜度 vs 延迟——结果可能滞后,要定一个可接受的 staleness 窗口。YouTube 对活跃用户预计算、长尾用户实时算。
why_en: Full pre-computation moves inference offline: compute slates off-peak and store them for instant zero-inference retrieval, trading freshness for latency with a defined staleness window, as YouTube does for active users.
tradeoff: 全量预计算(线上零推理成本,结果滞后) vs 在线推理(最新,每请求付算力)
whenOtherWins: 如果组合不可预测或结果必须实时最新(如突发新闻流),预计算会大量算无用/过期结果,应改在线推理或混合回退。
options: 在线推理:每个请求都实时算,永不做离线预计算,保证结果绝对新鲜但峰值算力吃紧、成本高
全量预计算:离线低峰算好 slate 存起来,线上零推理取;代价是新鲜度滞后
只上结果缓存,靠命中率自然覆盖所有可预测组合,不必做离线预计算
把模型剪枝量化到极小,让在线推理快到根本不需要任何预计算
options_en: Online inference: compute every request in real time and never pre-compute offline — perfectly fresh, but peak compute gets tight and costly.
Full pre-computation: build slates offline off-peak and serve them with zero online inference; the cost is staleness.
Just use result caching and let hit rate cover all predictable combinations, with no offline pre-computation.
Prune and quantize the model so small that online inference is fast enough to need no pre-computation.
optionExplanations: 可预测大量组合正适合离线预算,坚持全在线浪费峰值算力。
对;预计算把成本挪到离线低峰,线上瞬时取,代价是滞后需定窗口。
结果缓存靠请求触发填充,冷启动/长尾覆盖不全;预计算主动全量算好。
剪枝降单次延迟,但可预测组合离线预算能直接省掉在线推理成本。
optionExplanations_en: Predictable high-volume pairs suit offline pre-computation; staying fully online wastes peak compute.
Correct — pre-computation shifts cost to off-peak offline and serves instantly online, trading staleness with a defined window.
Result caching fills on request, missing cold/long-tail coverage; pre-computation proactively computes the full set.
Pruning cuts per-call latency, but for predictable pairs offline pre-computation removes online inference cost entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把推理挪到离线低峰算好结果存起来,线上直接取,零在线推理成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-computation moves inference offline to compute and store results, so online serving just retrieves them at zero inference cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计算结果允许过期的最长时间,超过就要重算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A staleness window is the maximum age a pre-computed result may reach before it must be recomputed.

scenario: 系统想尽量给实时最新结果,但偶发实时推理会超延迟预算,又绝不能给用户返回超时错误。
scenario_en: The system wants fresh real-time results but occasional real-time inference exceeds the latency budget, and timeouts to users are unacceptable.
q: 既要尽量实时又不能超时,该怎么设计?
q_en: How do you design for real-time-when-possible with no timeouts?
why: 混合回退:先试实时推理,若超预算就回退到预计算结果——优雅降级,永不超时。它把「实时最新」和「有保底」结合,代价是要维护实时+预计算双路径的复杂度。欺诈系统常用。
why_en: Hybrid fallback tries real-time first and falls back to a pre-computed result if over budget — graceful degradation with no timeouts — at the cost of maintaining dual real-time and pre-computed paths.
tradeoff: 混合回退(有保底不超时,双路径复杂) vs 纯实时(最新但偶发超时)
whenOtherWins: 如果实时推理延迟非常稳定、几乎不会超预算,纯实时更简单,不必维护第二条预计算回退路径。
options: 永远只用预计算结果,牺牲实时性换绝不超时,路径单一简单可靠
先试实时推理,超预算就回退到预计算结果:优雅降级,永不超时
把延迟预算调大到实时推理永远够用,就不需要任何回退路径
超时就重试实时推理,一直重试到成功为止,不引入预计算
options_en: Always serve pre-computed results only, trading freshness for zero timeouts on a single simple path.
Try real-time inference first and fall back to a pre-computed result when over budget: graceful degradation, never a timeout.
Raise the latency budget until real-time inference always fits, so no fallback path is needed.
On timeout just retry real-time inference until it succeeds, without any pre-computation.
optionExplanations: 纯预计算放弃了「尽量实时」的诉求,只在完全不要新鲜度时才合适。
对;实时优先+预计算兜底既新鲜又不超时,代价是双路径维护。
调大预算等于放弃 SLA,偶发慢请求照样拖垮尾延迟。
重试会叠加延迟、放大尾延迟,还是可能超时,不如直接回退。
optionExplanations_en: Pure pre-computation abandons the real-time-when-possible goal, fitting only when freshness is irrelevant.
Correct — real-time-first with pre-computed fallback stays fresh yet timeout-free, paying dual-path maintenance.
Raising the budget abandons the SLA; occasional slow requests still wreck tail latency.
Retries stack latency and amplify the tail, still risking timeout — falling back is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先试实时推理,超预算就回退到预计算结果,实现优雅降级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid fallback tries real-time inference and falls back to a pre-computed result when over budget, for graceful degradation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在压力下退回到较差但可用的结果,而不是直接失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation means falling back to a worse-but-usable result under stress instead of failing outright.

scenario: 汇报模型服务性能时,只报了平均延迟 5ms,面试官追问尾部情况。
scenario_en: Reporting service performance, you cite only a 5ms average latency, and the interviewer probes the tail.
q: 为什么可靠性要用 p50/p95/p99 百分位而不是平均延迟?
q_en: Why frame reliability on p50/p95/p99 percentiles rather than average latency?
why: 平均会被极慢请求拉偏又掩盖尾部:p50 是中位数,p95/p99 才暴露尾延迟。5ms p50 配 500ms p99 仍不可靠,100K QPS 下 1% 尾部就是 1000 req/s 变慢。
why_en: Averages hide the tail, while p50/p95/p99 expose it: a 5ms p50 with 500ms p99 is unreliable, and at 100K QPS a 1% tail is 1000 req/s degraded — millions daily.
options: 平均延迟更准确,百分位只是花哨表述,两者信息量完全相同
百分位才暴露尾延迟:5ms p50 配 500ms p99 仍然不可靠
只需看 p50 中位数,p95/p99 属于过度工程,日常监控用不上
百分位只在离线评估时用,线上监控看平均延迟就已经足够了
options_en: Average latency is more accurate; percentiles are just fancy phrasing carrying identical information.
Percentiles expose the tail: a 5ms p50 with a 500ms p99 is still unreliable.
Only the p50 median matters; p95/p99 are over-engineering you never need in day-to-day monitoring.
Percentiles belong to offline evaluation; watching the average is enough for online monitoring.
optionExplanations: 平均会被极端值扭曲又掩盖尾部,信息量远不如百分位。
对;p99 才是可靠性的度量,尾部乘上高 QPS 就是海量差体验。
只看 p50 恰恰漏掉尾延迟,这正是被诟病没生产经验的表现。
线上更要盯 p99,尾部随时会顶破 SLA,平均看不出来。
optionExplanations_en: Averages are distorted by extremes and hide the tail, carrying far less information than percentiles.
Correct — p99 is the reliability measure, and the tail times high QPS is a huge volume of bad experiences.
Watching only p50 misses the tail, exactly the signal of lacking production experience.
Online you must watch p99; the tail can breach the SLA anytime and the average won't show it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 50/95/99 百分位延迟;p50 是中位数,p95/p99 反映尾部慢请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p50/p95/p99 are the 50th/95th/99th-percentile latencies; p50 is the median while p95/p99 capture the slow tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务质量承诺,如实时端点 p99 < 100ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed quality target, e.g. p99 < 100ms for real-time endpoints.

scenario: 一个请求要并行扇出调用 10 个下游服务,响应必须等最慢的那个;每个服务各有 1% 概率慢。
scenario_en: A request fans out to 10 downstream services in parallel and must wait for the slowest; each has a 1% chance of being slow.
q: 扇出到 10 个各 1% 慢的服务,整体命中慢调用的概率约多少?说明什么?
q_en: Fanning out to 10 services each 1% slow, roughly what fraction of requests hit a slow call, and what does it show?
why: 尾延迟放大:并行调用的响应=所有调用里最慢的。10 个各 1% 慢,至少一个慢的概率=1 − 0.99^10 ≈ 9.6%。这是为什么分布式服务比单体更难保尾延迟——扇出越宽,尾部被放大得越狠。
why_en: Tail-latency amplification: a parallel response equals the slowest call, so with 10 calls each 1% slow, P(≥1 slow)=1 − 0.99^10 ≈ 9.6%, which is why fan-out makes distributed serving harder than monolithic.
options: 各服务互相独立不叠加,整体命中慢调用的概率照旧停在 1%
并行调用能把慢概率摊薄稀释,整体反而降到约 0.1% 左右,越并行越安全
取最慢那一路,概率约 9.6%(1−0.99^10),扇出放大尾部
只要发生并行扇出就一定踩中慢请求,概率接近 100%
options_en: The services are independent and don't compound, so the overall odds of a slow call stay at 1%.
Parallel calls dilute the slow probability, so overall it actually drops to roughly 0.1% — the more parallel, the safer.
You wait on the slowest path, so the odds are about 9.6% (1−0.99^10) — fan-out amplifies the tail.
Any parallel fan-out is bound to hit a slow call, so the probability is close to 100%.
optionExplanations: 服务独立没错,但响应取的是「最慢的那个」,慢概率会累加,不会停在 1%。
并行是同时发起而非分摊,取最大值反而把慢概率推高,不是摊薄。
对,10 条链路各 1% 慢,取最慢的那个后命中率跳到约 9.6%。
不是每次都踩中,只是概率明显变高,并非笃定的 100%。
optionExplanations_en: Independence is fine, but the response takes the slowest call, so the odds stack up past a single 1%.
Parallel means simultaneous, not diluted; taking the max pushes the slow odds up, not down.
Correct — with ten calls each 1% slow, taking the slowest pushes the hit rate to about 9.6%.
It's not a sure hit, just a much higher chance — 100% overstates it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扇出并行调用时,响应等于最慢的一个,慢概率随调用数放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tail-latency amplification: with fan-out, the response equals the slowest call, so the slow probability grows with the number of calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求并行调用多个下游服务再汇总结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is one request calling many downstream services in parallel and aggregating the results.

scenario: 一个请求并行调用 8 个微服务,每个的 p99 都是 50ms,单看每个都达标。
scenario_en: A request calls 8 microservices in parallel, each with a p99 of 50ms, and each looks compliant alone.
q: 8 个 p99=50ms 的并行调用,整体延迟会怎样?
q_en: With 8 parallel calls each at p99=50ms, what happens to overall latency?
why: 尾延迟放大:整体响应等 8 个里最慢的,相当一大批请求会超过 50ms。每个 1% 慢,至少一个慢的概率=1 − 0.99^8 ≈ 7.7%,远高于单个的 1%,所以不能用单服务 p99 推整体 p99。
why_en: Tail-latency amplification means the overall response equals the slowest of 8, so a significant fraction exceeds 50ms — with each 1% slow, P(≥1 slow)=1 − 0.99^8 ≈ 7.7%, far above 1%.
options: 整体 p99 还是 50ms,并行调用互不影响,取平均即可
整体 p99 会更低,并行执行让每一路调用都跟着提速
相当一批请求会超 50ms:整体等最慢的一个,尾部放大到 7.7%
整体延迟 = 8×50ms = 400ms,因为要串行等每一个返回
options_en: Overall p99 stays at 50ms because parallel calls don't affect each other, so just average them.
Overall p99 goes lower, since running in parallel speeds up each individual call.
A sizable share exceeds 50ms: the whole waits on the slowest, amplifying the tail to about 7.7%.
Overall latency is 8×50ms = 400ms, because you wait for each call serially.
optionExplanations: 并行取最慢会让整体 p99 高于单个,不能简单等于 50ms。
并行不会让单个提速,取最大值只会让整体尾部更差。
对;这就是那道 quiz 的答案——尾延迟放大让一大批请求超 50ms。
并行不是串行相加,不是 400ms;是取最慢那个,尾部约 7.7% 超标。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the slowest raises overall p99 above a single service's, not simply 50ms.
Parallelism doesn't speed each up; taking the max worsens the overall tail.
Correct — this is the quiz answer: tail amplification pushes a significant fraction past 50ms.
Parallel isn't serial addition (not 400ms); it's the slowest, with ~7.7% over budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把功能拆成小而独立的服务,一个请求可能并行调用多个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A microservice is a small independent service; one request may call several in parallel.

scenario: 服务 p99 偶发飙高,要定位是哪些常见原因引起的延迟尖刺。
scenario_en: The service's p99 occasionally spikes, and you must identify which common causes drive the latency spikes.
q: 推理服务尾延迟尖刺的常见成因有哪些?
q_en: What are common causes of tail-latency spikes in inference serving?
why: 常见成因:JVM GC 停顿、队头阻塞(长推理挡住短的)、扩容后的冷启动、GPU 利用率低。缓解队头阻塞可用抢占式调度——打断长请求先让短请求走。这些都是尾部而非平均的问题。
why_en: Common causes are JVM GC pauses, head-of-line blocking (a long inference blocks short ones), cold starts after scaling, and poor GPU utilization; preemptive scheduling mitigates head-of-line blocking.
options: 只有网络抖动这一个原因,和 GC 停顿、调度、冷启动统统无关
JVM GC 停顿、队头阻塞、扩容冷启动、GPU 利用率低
只由模型精度决定,模型越准延迟尖刺出现得越频繁
只和磁盘 IO 有关,把数据全放内存尖刺就会消失
options_en: Only network jitter is the cause — nothing to do with GC pauses, scheduling, or cold starts.
JVM GC pauses, head-of-line blocking, cold starts after scaling out, and low GPU utilization.
Purely model accuracy — the more accurate the model, the more often latency spikes.
Only disk IO — put all the data in memory and the spikes disappear.
optionExplanations: 网络抖动只是其一,GC/队头阻塞/冷启动/GPU 利用率都是主因。
对;这四类是尾延迟尖刺的常客,队头阻塞靠抢占式调度让短请求插队。
延迟尖刺与模型准确率无直接因果,是系统与调度层现象。
磁盘 IO 只是可能之一,GC 停顿和冷启动与磁盘无关。
optionExplanations_en: Network jitter is just one; GC/head-of-line blocking/cold starts/GPU utilization are all major causes.
Correct — these four are frequent tail-spike causes, and head-of-line blocking is eased by preemptive scheduling letting short requests jump ahead.
Latency spikes have no direct causal link to model accuracy; they're system/scheduling phenomena.
Disk IO is only one possibility; GC pauses and cold starts are unrelated to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个长请求占住处理槽位,后面的短请求被迫排队等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Head-of-line blocking is when one long request holds the processing slot, forcing short requests to queue behind it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 打断正在跑的长请求,优先让短请求执行,降低队头阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Preemptive scheduling interrupts a running long request to prioritize short ones, reducing head-of-line blocking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行时自动回收内存,JVM 的 GC 停顿会造成延迟尖刺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GC (Garbage Collection) reclaims memory automatically; JVM GC pauses cause latency spikes.

scenario: 要让推理服务能水平扩展、任意机器故障都能无缝接管,不能让请求粘在某台机器上。
scenario_en: You want inference to scale horizontally and survive any node failure seamlessly, without requests sticking to one machine.
q: 为什么无状态(stateless)服务设计是水平扩展的前提?
q_en: Why is stateless server design a prerequisite for horizontal scaling?
why: 无状态=没有会话亲和,每台机启动即加载相同权重、请求间不保留任何状态。于是 LB 可以把任意请求发给任意机器,某机故障其余无缝接管。有状态会把请求绑死在某机,阻碍扩展与故障转移。
why_en: Stateless means no session affinity: each server loads identical weights at startup and keeps nothing between requests, so the LB can route any request to any server and failover is trivial.
tradeoff: 无状态(易扩展/易故障转移,状态需外置) vs 有状态(本地状态快,绑死机器难扩展)
whenOtherWins: 如果单请求依赖大量会话内累积状态且外置代价过高(如有状态流式会话),才考虑会话亲和,但要牺牲无缝故障转移。
diagram:
flowchart LR LB["负载均衡器"] --> S1["server1
相同权重·无状态"] LB --> S2["server2
相同权重·无状态"] LB --> S3["server3
相同权重·无状态"] X["任意请求→任意机
挂一台无缝接管"] -.- LB
options: 无状态本身更慢,为了扩展性只能牺牲速度,是不得已的妥协
无状态=无会话亲和,每机加载相同权重,LB 可任意路由、故障接管
无状态意味着完全不加载模型权重,改靠远程调用模型拿权重,所以才能扩展
无状态指不用数据库,所有数据都放本机内存,因此扩展很快
options_en: Stateless is inherently slower, so you sacrifice speed for scalability as a forced compromise.
Stateless means no session affinity: every box loads identical weights, so the LB routes anywhere and failover is seamless.
Stateless means never loading model weights at all, fetching them via a remote call instead, which is why it scales.
Stateless means using no database and keeping all data in local memory, which makes scaling fast.
optionExplanations: 无状态本身不慢,它是可扩展与易故障转移的结构前提,不是速度妥协。
对;无会话亲和让任意请求可落任意机,是水平扩展和无缝故障转移的基础。
无状态照样在本机加载权重,只是请求间不保留会话状态。
无状态说的是不保留请求间状态,不等于不用数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Stateless isn't inherently slow; it's the structural prerequisite for scaling and easy failover, not a speed compromise.
Correct — no session affinity lets any request land on any server, the basis for horizontal scaling and seamless failover.
Stateless still loads weights locally; it just keeps no session state between requests.
Stateless is about not keeping cross-request state, not about avoiding databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器请求间不保留任何会话状态,每台机等价可互换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stateless means the server keeps no session state between requests, so all machines are interchangeable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一用户的请求固定路由到同一台机器,阻碍无缝故障转移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session affinity pins a user's requests to one machine, hindering seamless failover.

scenario: ML 推理不同请求耗时差异大(输入复杂度不同),要给 GPU 集群选负载均衡策略。
scenario_en: ML inference has widely varying per-request times (input complexity differs), and you must pick a load-balancing strategy for a GPU cluster.
q: 处理时间因输入而异的 ML 推理,该选哪种 LB 策略?为什么不用轮询?
q_en: For ML inference with input-dependent processing times, which LB strategy fits, and why not round-robin?
why: 选 least-connections 或 latency-aware:它们按实时负载/近期响应分流,能适应耗时不均。轮询假设每台工作量相等,遇到长短请求混杂会把慢请求堆到某台,加剧尾延迟。
why_en: Pick least-connections or latency-aware routing, which adapt to uneven processing by real-time load/recent latency, whereas round-robin assumes equal work and piles slow requests onto one node.
tradeoff: least-connections/latency-aware(适应耗时不均,需追踪状态) vs round-robin(简单,假设等量工作)
whenOtherWins: 如果每个请求耗时几乎相同(同构固定输入),轮询最简单公平,不需要追踪各机的活跃请求数或延迟。
options: 轮询(round-robin):完全不看各机负载,请求一律轮着发,均等但假设各机工作量完全相同
least-connections/latency-aware:按当前负载与最近响应动态分流
随机路由:请求随机撒到各机,短期波动大,不保证不堆慢请求
会话亲和:同一用户固定发一台机,图缓存命中却牺牲了负载均衡
options_en: Round-robin: completely ignore per-node load and rotate requests evenly — fair, but assumes every machine's workload is exactly equal.
Least-connections or latency-aware: route dynamically by current load and recent response times.
Random routing: scatter requests randomly, with high short-term variance and no guard against stacking slow ones.
Session affinity: pin a user to one machine for cache hits, at the cost of load balance.
optionExplanations: 轮询假设各机工作量相等,遇到耗时不均的请求会把慢请求堆到同一台机器上。
对,这两种策略按实际负载/响应速度分流,天生能吃下耗时不均的推理请求。
随机长期趋于均衡,但短期方差大,照样可能把长请求都甩给同一台。
会话亲和保的是缓存命中,却把请求焊死在一台机,和分摊耗时不均无关。
optionExplanations_en: Round-robin fires requests in strict rotation with no regard for load, so a run of slow inputs still stacks up on whichever node is next in line.
Correct — both route by current load or recent response speed, naturally absorbing input-dependent processing times.
Random balances out long-term, but short-term variance still stacks long requests on one node.
Session affinity protects cache hits, not load — it pins requests to one machine and ignores uneven timing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求发给当前活跃请求最少的机器,适应处理时间不均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least-connections routes a new request to the server with the fewest active requests, adapting to uneven processing times.

termDefinitions.term: latency-aware routing / 延迟感知路由
termDefinitions.meaning: 按各机近期响应时间分流,优先发给最近最快的机器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Latency-aware routing sends requests to the server with the lowest recent response time.

scenario: 流量有明显的日周期高峰,团队在 reactive 和 predictive 自动扩缩容之间选。
scenario_en: Traffic has clear daily peaks, and the team chooses between reactive and predictive auto-scaling.
q: reactive 和 predictive 自动扩缩容有什么区别?各自的软肋是什么?
q_en: How do reactive and predictive auto-scaling differ, and what is each one's weakness?
why: reactive:按 CPU/GPU 利用率>80% 或队列深度触发扩容——简单但滞后,扩容期间有冷启动降容量。predictive:用历史流量在高峰前提前扩容——避开冷启动,但依赖预测准确,预测错就多花钱或不够用。
why_en: Reactive scales on CPU/GPU utilization >80% or queue depth (simple but lagging, with cold-start dips), while predictive pre-scales before peaks from historical traffic (avoids cold starts but depends on forecast accuracy).
tradeoff: reactive(简单,滞后+扩容期冷启动) vs predictive(提前扩容避冷启动,依赖预测准)
options: reactive 达阈值才扩(滞后有冷启动);predictive 靠历史流量提前扩(依赖预测准)
两者完全一样,只是叫法不同,都是达到阈值才触发扩容
reactive 提前扩容避开冷启动、predictive 事后被动扩容,predictive 反应更慢更保守
predictive 永远更好,没有任何软肋,应无脑用它替代 reactive
options_en: Reactive scales only at a threshold (laggy, with cold starts); predictive pre-scales from historical traffic (but depends on forecast accuracy).
They are identical and just named differently — both only scale once a threshold is crossed.
Reactive pre-scales to dodge cold starts while predictive scales reactively after the fact, so predictive reacts more slowly and conservatively.
Predictive is always better with no weakness, so blindly replace reactive with it.
optionExplanations: 对;reactive 达阈值才扩(滞后+冷启动),predictive 按历史提前扩(避冷启动但赌预测)。
两者机制不同:一个事后触发、一个事前预测,不是叫法差异。
说反了:predictive 才是提前扩容,reactive 是达阈值事后扩。
predictive 依赖预测准确,预测错会过度扩容或不足,并非无软肋。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — reactive scales at a threshold (lag + cold start), predictive pre-scales from history (avoids cold start but bets on the forecast).
The mechanisms differ: one triggers after the fact, one forecasts ahead — not a naming difference.
Reversed: predictive pre-scales, reactive scales after crossing a threshold.
Predictive depends on forecast accuracy; a wrong forecast over- or under-provisions, so it isn't weakness-free.

termDefinitions.term: reactive auto-scaling / 反应式扩缩容
termDefinitions.meaning: 按当前 CPU/GPU 利用率或队列深度超阈值来触发增减机器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reactive auto-scaling adds or removes machines when current CPU/GPU utilization or queue depth crosses a threshold.

termDefinitions.term: predictive auto-scaling / 预测式扩缩容
termDefinitions.meaning: 用历史流量模式在高峰到来前提前增容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Predictive auto-scaling uses historical traffic patterns to add capacity before a peak arrives.

scenario: 扩容拉起一台新 GPU 实例后,它并不能立刻满载服务,而是有一段容量受限期。
scenario_en: After scaling up a new GPU instance, it can't serve at full capacity immediately but has a reduced-capacity warm-up period.
q: GPU 推理的冷启动大概要多久?这个数字对扩容策略意味着什么?
q_en: Roughly how long is GPU inference cold start, and what does that number imply for scaling?
why: 把权重加载进 GPU 大约要 30-60s,期间容量受限。这个滞后意味着 reactive 扩容「达阈值才拉」会在这 30-60s 里顶不住,所以要用 warm pools(预加载好的实例)+ predictive 提前扩,避开临阵冷启动。
why_en: Loading weights into a GPU takes roughly 30-60s with reduced capacity, so reactive scaling can't cover that window — hence warm pools (pre-loaded instances) and predictive pre-scaling.
options: 约 30-60s 把权重加载进 GPU,期间容量受限,得靠 warm pool 顶住
接近 0(约 1ms 量级),冷启动完全可以忽略不计,达阈值再扩容也完全来得及,不必预热
耗时被高估成约 1 小时,以为永远不能扩容,只能一开始就买满机器
冷启动时长只取决于网络,与加载权重进显存无关,提前扩没用
options_en: About 30-60s to load weights into the GPU; capacity is reduced in that window, so warm pools have to cover it.
Near zero (about 1ms), so cold start is fully negligible and scaling at the threshold is always timely enough — no pre-warming needed.
Overstated at roughly an hour, implying you can never scale out and must buy full capacity upfront.
Cold-start time depends only on the network, not on loading weights into VRAM, so pre-scaling is pointless.
optionExplanations: 对,30-60s 的显存加载滞后逼着你提前预热/扩容,不能临阵拉新机。
1ms 严重低估,大模型权重灌入显存通常要秒级到数十秒。
1 小时既高估又误导,真实做法是拿 warm pool 抵消这段滞后,不是放弃扩容。
冷启动主体就是把权重搬进显存,不是纯网络延迟的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the 30-60s VRAM load lag forces pre-warming or pre-scaling; you can't spin up a fresh node right at the threshold.
1ms badly underestimates it; pumping large-model weights into VRAM usually takes seconds to tens of seconds.
1 hour both overstates it and misleads — the real fix is a warm pool to absorb that lag, not giving up on scaling.
Cold start is mostly moving weights into VRAM, not a pure network-latency issue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新实例把模型权重加载进 GPU 的启动期,约 30-60s,期间容量受限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cold start is the period a new instance loads weights into the GPU (~30-60s) with reduced capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先加载好模型、随时可服务的备用实例,用来消除临阵冷启动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A warm pool holds pre-loaded, ready-to-serve instances to eliminate on-demand cold starts.

scenario: 为提升 GPU 吞吐,把并发到达的请求攒成一批做一次前向,但有的请求会因等待凑批而多等一会儿。
scenario_en: To raise GPU throughput, you group concurrently arriving requests into one forward pass, but some requests wait a bit for the batch to fill.
q: 动态批处理(dynamic batching)带来什么收益、代价是什么?
q_en: What does dynamic batching gain, and at what cost?
why: 动态批处理把并发请求合成一次前向,GPU 一次算多个→吞吐大涨。代价是攒批要等一小段时间(batch-accumulation wait),对单请求加了点延迟。所以它是吞吐 vs 延迟的权衡,批越大吞吐越高但等待越久。
why_en: Dynamic batching merges concurrent requests into one forward pass for much higher throughput, at the cost of a small batch-accumulation wait added to per-request latency — a throughput-vs-latency tradeoff.
tradeoff: 动态批处理(吞吐高,增加凑批等待延迟) vs 逐个处理(延迟低,吞吐低)
options: 只有收益没有代价:批处理既提吞吐又降单请求延迟,应无脑开最大批
并发请求合成一次前向→吞吐大涨,代价是凑批等待增加单请求延迟
批处理会降低吞吐但能降低延迟,是拿吞吐去换延迟的做法
批处理只影响模型准确率,对延迟和吞吐都没有任何影响
options_en: Pure upside: batching raises throughput and lowers per-request latency, so just run the largest batch.
Merging concurrent requests into one forward pass raises throughput a lot, at the cost of batch-accumulation wait per request.
Batching lowers throughput but lowers latency — it trades throughput for latency.
Batching only affects model accuracy and has no effect on latency or throughput.
optionExplanations: 批越大凑批等待越久,单请求延迟升高,不是无代价,批大小要权衡。
对;吞吐涨来自一次算多个,代价是凑批等待,典型吞吐-延迟权衡。
方向反了:批处理提吞吐、增单请求延迟,不是降延迟。
批处理直接影响吞吐与延迟,与准确率无关。
optionExplanations_en: Bigger batches wait longer to fill, raising per-request latency — not free, so batch size is a tradeoff.
Correct — throughput rises from computing many at once, at the cost of accumulation wait, the classic throughput-latency tradeoff.
Direction reversed: batching raises throughput and adds per-request latency, not lowers it.
Batching directly affects throughput and latency, not accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把并发到达的请求实时凑成一批做一次前向,提升 GPU 吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic batching groups concurrently arriving requests into one forward pass at runtime to raise GPU throughput.

q: 把低延迟服务的面试作答四步(推荐顺序)排好:
q_en: Order the four-step interview structure for low-latency serving:
steps: 无状态设计 + 选合适的 LB 算法
先说延迟 SLA,用百分位定(p99 <100ms)
自动扩缩容 + 冷启动缓解(warm pool)
对可预测/重复查询上预计算 + 缓存
why: 先立目标(p99 SLA),再用预计算+缓存把能省的请求省掉,然后无状态+LB 把剩余流量摊开,最后自动扩缩容+冷启动缓解兜住峰值。顺序是「定目标→减负载→分摊→弹性」。
why_en: State the p99 SLA first, then cut load with pre-computation and caching, then spread remaining traffic with stateless design plus LB, and finally absorb peaks with auto-scaling and cold-start mitigation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台无状态服务器的组件,配合扩缩容实现水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes requests across stateless servers, enabling horizontal scaling with auto-scaling.

scenario: 一个 100K QPS 的推荐系统,少数活跃用户贡献大部分流量,GPU 集群异构,流量有可预测的日高峰。
scenario_en: A 100K QPS recommender where a few active users drive most traffic, on a heterogeneous GPU cluster with predictable daily peaks.
q: 这个 100K QPS 推荐系统,四支柱该怎么组合落地?
q_en: How should the four pillars combine for this 100K QPS recommender?
why: 对头部活跃用户预计算 slate;Redis 结果缓存吃 >70% 命中;GPU 集群用 least-connections 分流;高峰前 predictive 扩容+warm pool,四支柱合力压住 p99。
why_en: Pre-compute slates for the top ~10% active users, a Redis result cache above 70% hit, least-connections across the GPU cluster, and predictive scaling ~30 min before peak plus warm pools.
tradeoff: 预计算+缓存(压住可预测流量,滞后) vs 全在线(最新,峰值扛不住)
whenOtherWins: 如果流量不可预测、几乎无重复查询,预计算与结果缓存收益骤降,应把重心放到弹性扩容与更强的在线推理优化上。
options: 全部请求都实时在线推理,不预计算不缓存,靠无限堆 GPU 硬扛 100K QPS,接受成本失控
头部预计算 slate、结果缓存、least-connections、predictive 扩容
只上结果缓存一招,其余三支柱都不用,只要命中率够高就能扛住 100K QPS
把模型剪到极小让单机扛下 100K QPS,不需要 LB、预计算和自动扩容
options_en: Serve every request with live online inference, no pre-compute and no cache, brute-forcing 100K QPS with unlimited GPUs and runaway cost.
Pre-compute slates for the head, a result cache, least-connections routing, and predictive scaling.
Use result caching alone and skip the other three pillars — a high enough hit rate carries 100K QPS.
Prune the model tiny so one machine handles 100K QPS, needing no LB, no pre-compute and no autoscaling.
optionExplanations: 全在线堆 GPU 成本极高又扛不住可预测峰值,浪费了预计算/缓存能省的部分。
对;四支柱协同——预计算削头部、缓存吃重复、LB 摊余量、预测扩容兜峰值。
只缓存覆盖不了长尾和冷启动,单招无法独撑 100K QPS 的 p99。
单机扛 100K QPS 不现实,剪枝也不能替代水平扩展与 LB。
optionExplanations_en: All-online with piled GPUs is very costly and can't handle predictable peaks, wasting what pre-compute/cache could save.
Correct — the four pillars work together: pre-compute trims the head, cache absorbs repeats, LB spreads the rest, predictive scaling covers peaks.
Cache-only misses the long tail and cold starts; one trick can't hold 100K QPS p99 alone.
One machine can't handle 100K QPS, and pruning doesn't replace horizontal scaling and LB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次性预先算好的一整组推荐结果(如首页整屏),供瞬时取用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slate is a full set of recommendations pre-computed at once (e.g. a homepage screen) for instant retrieval.

termDefinitions.term: cache hit rate / 缓存命中率
termDefinitions.meaning: 命中缓存的请求占比,决定缓存能省掉多少推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache hit rate is the fraction of requests served from cache, deciding how much inference is skipped.

scenario: 用户分布长尾:头部少数用户高频访问、可预测,尾部海量用户偶尔访问、不可预测(如 YouTube)。
scenario_en: A long-tail user base: a few active users visit often and predictably, while a vast tail visits rarely and unpredictably (like YouTube).
q: 头部活跃 vs 长尾用户,预计算该怎么分而治之?
q_en: For active-head vs long-tail users, how do you split pre-computation?
why: 对头部活跃用户预计算(可预测、高频,预算命中率高);对长尾用户实时算(不可预测,预算了大概率用不上、白费)。按访问可预测性分而治之,把预计算算力花在刀刃上。YouTube 即此做法。
why_en: Pre-compute for the predictable, high-frequency active head (high payoff) and compute long-tail users on the fly (unpredictable, so pre-computing mostly wastes work), splitting by access predictability as YouTube does.
tradeoff: 头部预计算+长尾实时(算力花在刀刃,双路径) vs 全量预计算(长尾大量白算)
whenOtherWins: 如果用户群小且几乎人人高频访问(无长尾),直接全量预计算最简单,不必区分头尾。
options: 长尾用户预计算、头部活跃用户实时算,因为长尾人多更该提前备好
头部活跃用户预计算(可预测高频),长尾用户实时算(预算多半白费)
全部用户一律预计算,人人提前算好一份结果,最公平也最省事
全部用户一律实时算,预计算太复杂不值得,一视同仁最简单
options_en: Pre-compute for long-tail users and compute the active head live, since the tail is bigger and deserves readiness.
Pre-compute for the active head (predictable, high-frequency) and compute the long tail live (pre-computing it mostly goes to waste).
Pre-compute for every user uniformly — everyone gets a ready-made result, which is fairest and simplest.
Compute every user live; pre-computation is too complex to be worth it and treating all users alike is simplest.
optionExplanations: 反了:长尾不可预测,预算的多半没人用;头部高频才值得预计算。
对;按可预测性分而治之,预计算算力花在头部,长尾实时兜底。
全量预计算会为极少访问的长尾白算海量结果,浪费算力。
全实时放弃了头部可预测流量本可省的推理成本,峰值更吃力。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: the long tail is unpredictable, so most pre-computed results go unused; the high-frequency head is worth pre-computing.
Correct — split by predictability, spending pre-compute on the head and serving the tail live.
Pre-computing all wastes huge compute on rarely-visited tail users.
All-live forgoes the inference savings available for the predictable head, straining peaks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量低频、不可预测的用户或物料,单个访问少但总量大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The long tail is the many low-frequency, unpredictable users or items — each rare but numerous in aggregate.

q: 填空:尾延迟与扇出的关键数字。
q_en: Fill in the key numbers for tail latency and fan-out.
text: 实时端点 SLA 常定 p99 < {{100}}ms;10 个各 1% 慢的并行调用,至少一个慢的概率 = 1 − {{0.99}}^10 ≈ {{9.6}}%;GPU 冷启动约 {{30-60}}s。
text_en: Real-time endpoint SLAs often target p99 < {{100}}ms; for 10 parallel calls each 1% slow, P(≥1 slow) = 1 − {{0.99}}^10 ≈ {{9.6}}%; GPU cold start is about {{30-60}}s.
why: 记住这三组锚点:p99<100ms 是实时 SLA 目标,尾延迟放大公式 1−(1−p)^n,冷启动 30-60s 决定要不要 warm pool。它们分别约束 SLA 定义、扇出设计、扩容策略。
why_en: Anchor three numbers: p99<100ms SLA target, tail amplification 1−(1−p)^n, and 30-60s cold start deciding warm pools.

termDefinitions.meaning: n 个各 p 概率慢的并行调用,至少一个慢的概率=1−(1−p)^n。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: For n parallel calls each slow with probability p, P(at least one slow) = 1−(1−p)^n.

scenario: 实时推荐端点要扛 100K QPS,每个请求扇出到 10 个模型服务,还要在流量高峰前扩容 GPU。
scenario_en: A real-time recommendation endpoint must handle 100K QPS, fanning each request out to 10 model services, and scale GPUs up before traffic peaks.

scenario: GPU 集群异构:有的机器是新的 A100、有的是老的 T4,算力差一截,想让快机多分担。
scenario_en: A heterogeneous GPU cluster: some new A100s, some old T4s with much less compute, and you want faster machines to take more load.
q: 异构 GPU 集群里想让快机器多干活,该用哪种路由?
q_en: In a heterogeneous GPU cluster wanting faster machines to do more, which routing fits?
why: 用 weighted routing:给算力强的机器更高权重、分更多请求,匹配异构算力。轮询会给快慢机同样多请求,慢机被压垮、快机闲置。latency-aware 也能间接适应,但 weighted 是直接按已知算力配比。
why_en: Use weighted routing to give stronger machines higher weights and more requests, matching heterogeneous compute, whereas round-robin overloads slow nodes and idles fast ones.
tradeoff: weighted routing(按算力配比,需知道各机能力) vs round-robin(等量分配,压垮慢机)
whenOtherWins: 如果集群是同构的(所有 GPU 一样),weighted 没有意义,round-robin 或 least-connections 就够。
options: 轮询:给每台机器分配完全一样多的请求,最公平,异构集群下也照样适用不受影响
weighted routing:按算力给强机更高权重,分到更多请求
会话亲和:同一用户固定发同一台机,异构下也能自然均衡
随机路由:随机撒请求,长期下来会自动补偿机器算力差异
options_en: Round-robin: give every machine exactly the same number of requests — fairest, and completely unaffected even on heterogeneous fleets.
Weighted routing: weight stronger machines higher so they take more requests.
Session affinity: pin a user to one machine, which still balances naturally on heterogeneous fleets.
Random routing: scatter requests randomly and let it compensate for compute differences over time.
optionExplanations: 轮询等量分配在异构集群里正是问题:慢机被同样多请求压垮。
对;weighted 按已知算力给权重,快机多分、慢机少分,匹配异构。
会话亲和管的是状态绑定,不解决快慢机算力配比问题。
随机无视算力差异,慢机照样按均值分到过多请求。
optionExplanations_en: Round-robin's equal split is exactly the problem in a heterogeneous cluster: slow nodes get crushed by equal load.
Correct — weighted routing assigns weights by known compute, giving fast nodes more and slow nodes less.
Session affinity handles state pinning, not matching load to compute capacity.
Random ignores compute differences; slow nodes still get their average (too many) requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每台机器的算力/权重成比例分配请求,快机多分、慢机少分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weighted routing assigns requests proportional to each machine's capacity/weight, sending more to faster machines.

scenario: 同样是「免掉在线推理」,结果缓存和全量预计算的触发方式和覆盖不同,要选合适的。
scenario_en: Both 'skip online inference,' but result caching and full pre-computation differ in how they're triggered and what they cover.
q: 结果缓存和全量预计算都免推理,核心区别在哪?
q_en: Result caching and full pre-computation both skip inference — what's the core difference?
why: 结果缓存是「被动、按请求触发填充」:请求来了没命中才算并存,冷启动阶段命中低。全量预计算是「主动、离线全量算好」:不等请求,提前把可预测组合全算好存起来,线上一定命中但会为没人访问的组合白算。
why_en: Result caching is passive and request-triggered (fills on a miss, low hit during cold start), while full pre-computation is proactive and offline (computes all predictable pairs ahead of time, always hitting but wasting work on unvisited pairs).
tradeoff: 结果缓存(被动填充,冷启动命中低) vs 全量预计算(主动全算,可能为无访问组合白算)
options: 两者完全一样,只是缓存介质和存放位置不同而已
结果缓存被动按请求填充;全量预计算主动离线全算好
结果缓存主动提前全算,预计算被动等请求,和名字正相反
结果缓存永远比预计算好,预计算已被淘汰,不必再考虑
options_en: They are the same thing and differ only in storage medium and location.
Result caching fills passively on request; full pre-computation computes everything offline up front.
Result caching proactively computes everything and pre-computation passively waits for requests — the opposite of their names.
Result caching is always better; pre-computation is obsolete and no longer worth considering.
optionExplanations: 两者触发机制和覆盖不同,不是介质差异。
对;缓存被动填(冷启动低命中),预计算主动全算(必命中但可能白算)。
说反了:缓存是被动触发,预计算才是主动全量。
两者是互补手段,预计算对可预测组合更省,并未被淘汰。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in trigger and coverage, not storage medium.
Correct — cache fills passively (low cold-start hit), pre-computation computes proactively (always hits but may waste work).
Reversed: caching is passively triggered, pre-computation is the proactive full-compute.
They're complementary; pre-computation saves more on predictable pairs and isn't obsolete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存刚上线为空,命中率低,需一段时间被请求填满才见效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache cold start is when the cache is empty at first with a low hit rate until requests fill it.

q: 填空:四种负载均衡策略各自的适用场景。
q_en: Fill in when each of four load-balancing strategies fits.
text: {{round-robin}}只在各机工作量相等时公平;{{least-connections}}发给活跃请求最少的机,适应耗时不均;{{latency-aware}}按近期响应时间路由;{{weighted}}给更快的 GPU 分更多请求。ML 推理优先前两者中的 least-connections 或 latency-aware。
text_en: {{round-robin}} is fair only with equal work per node; {{least-connections}} routes to the fewest active requests, adapting to uneven times; {{latency-aware}} routes by recent response time; {{weighted}} sends more to faster GPUs. ML inference prefers least-connections or latency-aware.
why: 四选一看约束:同构等量→轮询;耗时不均→least-connections;要盯尾延迟→latency-aware;异构算力→weighted。ML 推理耗时随输入变,默认 least-connections/latency-aware。
why_en: Pick by constraint: homogeneous equal work → round-robin; uneven times → least-connections; tail-sensitive → latency-aware; heterogeneous → weighted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依次把请求轮流发给每台机器,假设各机工作量相等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-robin sends requests to each machine in turn, assuming equal work per node.

scenario: 面试里你说「我们的模型服务平均 5ms,很快」,没有提尾部或百分位。
scenario_en: In an interview you say 'our model serving averages 5ms, very fast,' without mentioning the tail or percentiles.
q: 只汇报中位数/平均延迟会给面试官什么信号?该怎么说?
q_en: What signal does reporting only median/average latency send, and how should you frame it?
why: 只报中位数/平均会显得缺乏生产经验——真实可靠性看尾部。应围绕 p99 谈 SLA,并主动点出尾延迟放大、冷启动、GC 停顿等尾部风险,展示你知道大规模下体验由尾部决定。
why_en: Reporting only median/average signals a lack of production experience, since real reliability lives in the tail — frame SLAs on p99 and call out tail risks like amplification, cold starts, and GC pauses.
options: 显得很专业:平均延迟低就说明系统好,面试官会很满意
显得缺乏生产经验:可靠性看尾部,应围绕 p99 谈 SLA
没有任何信号:平均和 p99 本质等价,怎么说都无所谓
显得过度工程:提百分位会让面试官觉得你在炫技,不如只说平均
options_en: It looks professional: a low average means a good system and the interviewer is satisfied.
It signals thin production experience: reliability lives in the tail, so frame the SLA on p99.
It signals nothing: average and p99 are essentially equivalent, so either is fine.
It looks like over-engineering: percentiles read as showing off, so just quote the average.
optionExplanations: 平均低但 p99 高照样不可靠,只报平均恰恰暴露没盯过生产尾部。
对;围绕 p99 谈并主动点尾部风险,才显得懂大规模服务。
平均会掩盖尾部,与 p99 远不等价,说法不能随便。
谈百分位是行业标准而非炫技,只说平均才是短板。
optionExplanations_en: A low average with a high p99 is still unreliable; average-only exposes never watching the production tail.
Correct — framing on p99 and proactively naming tail risks shows you understand serving at scale.
The average hides the tail and is far from equivalent to p99, so phrasing matters.
Discussing percentiles is industry standard, not showing off; average-only is the weakness.

termDefinitions.meaning: p50:一半请求快于此值,但完全看不见尾部慢请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Median latency (p50) is the value half of requests beat, but it hides the slow tail entirely.

scenario: 多个推理引擎/模型副本要统一做路由、资源分配和扩缩容决策,不想让每个引擎各自为政。
scenario_en: Multiple inference engines/model replicas need unified routing, resource allocation, and scaling decisions rather than each acting alone.
q: 跨多个推理引擎统一路由/资源/扩缩容,该引入什么?
q_en: To unify routing/resources/scaling across many inference engines, what do you introduce?
why: 引入一个集中的控制层(controller):把路由、资源分配、扩缩容决策集中到一处统管多个推理引擎(如 Snowflake 的做法),避免各引擎各自决策导致的资源冲突和局部最优。代价是控制层本身成为需要高可用的关键组件。
why_en: Introduce a centralized controller layer that unifies routing, resource allocation, and scaling across inference engines (as Snowflake does), avoiding conflicting local decisions, at the cost of a critical component needing high availability.
tradeoff: 集中控制层(全局最优统一决策,单点需高可用) vs 各引擎自治(简单,资源冲突/局部最优)
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单一引擎或副本极少、流量平稳,各自反应式扩缩容就够,引入集中控制层反而增加复杂度和单点风险。
options: 让每个推理引擎各自独立决策扩缩容,不需要任何统一层,最简单
引入集中控制层统管路由/资源/扩缩容,代价是它需高可用
把所有引擎合并成一个巨型单体进程,彻底消除跨引擎协调
只加一个共享缓存就能自动协调所有引擎的路由和扩缩容
options_en: Let each inference engine decide its own scaling with no unified layer — the simplest option.
Introduce a centralized controller for routing, resources and scaling, at the cost of it needing high availability.
Merge every engine into one giant monolithic process to eliminate cross-engine coordination.
Just add a shared cache and it will automatically coordinate routing and scaling across engines.
optionExplanations: 各自为政会资源冲突、只求局部最优,规模大时协调不了。
对;集中控制层做全局决策,统一路由/资源/扩缩容,代价是自身要高可用。
合并成单体牺牲了多引擎的隔离与弹性,不是协调之道。
共享缓存只解决数据复用,不能替代路由和扩缩容的集中决策。
optionExplanations_en: Independent decisions cause resource conflicts and local optima, uncoordinated at scale.
Correct — a centralized controller makes global decisions unifying routing/resources/scaling, at the cost of its own high availability.
Merging into a monolith sacrifices multi-engine isolation and elasticity, not a coordination solution.
A shared cache only handles data reuse, not centralized routing and scaling decisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中管理多个推理引擎的路由、资源分配与扩缩容的协调组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A controller layer centrally manages routing, resource allocation, and scaling across multiple inference engines.

scenario: GPU 推理服务器利用率长期偏低,单请求延迟却不低,吞吐上不去。
scenario_en: A GPU inference server runs at chronically low utilization yet per-request latency isn't low and throughput won't rise.
q: GPU 利用率低会怎样拖累服务?常见修法是什么?
q_en: How does low GPU utilization hurt serving, and what's the common fix?
why: GPU 利用率低=昂贵算力空转,吞吐上不去、单位成本高,还常伴随尾延迟。修法是用动态批处理把并发请求凑批喂满 GPU,一次算多个提升利用率与吞吐;代价是凑批增加一点单请求延迟。
why_en: Low GPU utilization means expensive hardware idling — low throughput and high cost per request — and the common fix is dynamic batching to fill the GPU with concurrent requests, at a small latency cost.
tradeoff: 动态批处理(利用率/吞吐升,增单请求延迟) vs 逐个喂(延迟低,GPU 空转)
options: GPU 利用率低是好事,说明还有余量,不用去管它
算力空转、吞吐低成本高;修法是动态批处理喂满 GPU
利用率低只影响电费,对吞吐和延迟都没有什么影响
利用率低就应该立刻加更多 GPU,机器越多总归越好
options_en: Low GPU utilization is good news — it means headroom, so leave it alone.
Compute sits idle, throughput is low and unit cost high; the fix is dynamic batching to fill the GPU.
Low utilization only shows up on the power bill and doesn't affect throughput or latency.
Low utilization means you should add more GPUs right away — more machines is always better.
optionExplanations: 长期低利用率是浪费昂贵算力、吞吐上不去,不是有益余量。
对;凑批喂满 GPU 提升利用率与吞吐,代价是一点凑批延迟。
利用率低直接压低吞吐、抬高单位成本,不止是电费。
先加 GPU 不解决单机空转,应先靠批处理把现有 GPU 喂满。
optionExplanations_en: Chronic low utilization wastes expensive compute and caps throughput — not helpful headroom.
Correct — batching fills the GPU to raise utilization and throughput, at a small accumulation latency.
Low utilization directly cuts throughput and raises cost per request, not just electricity.
Adding GPUs first doesn't fix per-node idling; batch to fill existing GPUs first.

termDefinitions.meaning: GPU 计算单元的忙碌占比,低利用率意味着昂贵算力空转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPU utilization is the fraction of time the GPU's compute units are busy; low utilization means expensive hardware idling.

scenario: 系统级手段(缓存、负载均衡、扩缩容)已就位后,还想进一步压单请求的成本/延迟,且不想重训模型。
scenario_en: With system-level levers (caching, load balancing, auto-scaling) in place, you want to further cut per-request cost/latency without retraining.
q: 在目标硬件上优化模型的四个轴是哪些?
q_en: What are the four axes for optimizing a model on target hardware?
why: 四轴:量化、剪枝、编译、边缘 vs 云部署。它们大多不需重训就能把推理成本/延迟降 2-4×,是系统层手段之外「让模型本身更快更省」的下一层杠杆。
why_en: The four axes are quantization, pruning, compilation, and edge-vs-cloud placement, most of which cut inference cost/latency 2-4x without retraining.
diagram:
flowchart TB M["训练好的模型"] --> Q["量化
降精度"] M --> P["剪枝
去权重/结构"] M --> C["编译
优化执行图"] M --> E["边缘vs云
部署位置"] Q --> R["2-4× 降本降延迟
多数免重训"]
options: 数据增强、超参搜索、集成学习、蒸馏
量化、剪枝、编译、边缘 vs 云部署
分片、副本、缓存、预计算
梯度裁剪、批归一化、dropout、权重衰减
options_en: Data augmentation, hyperparameter search, ensembling, and distillation.
Quantization, pruning, compilation, and edge-vs-cloud placement.
Sharding, replication, caching, and pre-computation.
Gradient clipping, batch normalization, dropout, and weight decay.
optionExplanations: 这些是训练/调参手段,不是在目标硬件上给成品模型提速的四轴。
对;量化/剪枝/编译/边缘四轴大多免重训就能降本降延迟。
分片/副本/缓存是上一课的系统层手段,不是模型本身的优化轴。
这些是训练时的正则化技巧,与线上推理提速无关。
optionExplanations_en: These are training/tuning methods, not the four axes for speeding a finished model on hardware.
Correct — quantization/pruning/compilation/edge cut cost/latency mostly without retraining.
Sharding/replication/caching are last lesson's system-level levers, not model-optimization axes.
These are training-time regularization tricks, unrelated to inference speedup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 降低权重/激活的数值精度(FP32→FP16/INT8)以省内存、提速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers the numerical precision of weights/activations (FP32→FP16/INT8) to save memory and speed inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从头或继续训练模型;四轴多数无需重训即可提速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retraining trains the model further or from scratch; most of the four axes speed up without it.

scenario: 要把训练好的 FP32 模型量化到 INT8,团队在 PTQ 和 QAT 之间选。
scenario_en: Quantizing a trained FP32 model to INT8, the team chooses between PTQ and QAT.
q: PTQ 和 QAT 有什么本质区别?各自的代价是什么?
q_en: What's the essential difference between PTQ and QAT, and each one's cost?
why: PTQ 训练后直接转低精度、跑一份校准集设每层缩放,无需重训——快,但激活范围宽的层精度会掉。QAT 在训练中模拟量化噪声让权重对低精度更鲁棒——精度更好,但要一整轮训练周期。核心权衡是「精度 vs 是否重训」。
why_en: PTQ converts after training using a calibration set with no retraining (fast but degrades on wide-activation layers), while QAT simulates quantization noise during training for better accuracy at the cost of a full training cycle.
tradeoff: PTQ(免重训、快,精度损失大) vs QAT(精度好,需完整训练周期)
options: PTQ 需要完整重训才能转 INT8,QAT 只跑一次校准集设缩放,所以 QAT 工程成本更低
两者都在训练循环里做,唯一区别是 PTQ 目标 FP16、QAT 目标 INT8
PTQ 训练后转、校准集定缩放,免重训易掉点;QAT 训练中模拟量化噪声,精度好但要重训
PTQ 和 QAT 的精度与成本完全一样,只是不同框架对同一套流程的不同叫法
options_en: PTQ needs a full retrain to reach INT8 while QAT only runs one calibration pass, so QAT costs less engineering.
Both run inside the training loop; the only difference is PTQ targets FP16 and QAT targets INT8.
PTQ converts after training with a calibration set for scaling — no retrain but accuracy drops; QAT simulates quantization noise in training — accurate but needs a retrain.
PTQ and QAT have identical accuracy and cost; different frameworks just name the same process differently.
optionExplanations: 反了:PTQ 免重训,QAT 才需要完整训练周期。
两者都能到 INT8,区别不在精度位宽,而在是否在训练中模拟量化。
对;PTQ 快但精度易掉,QAT 精度好但要重训,权衡是精度 vs 重训成本。
两者精度和成本明显不同:QAT 精度更高但更贵。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: PTQ needs no retraining; QAT needs a full training cycle.
Both can reach INT8; the difference isn't bit width but whether quantization is simulated during training.
Correct — PTQ is fast but accuracy-prone, QAT is accurate but needs retraining; the tradeoff is accuracy vs retraining cost.
Their accuracy and cost clearly differ: QAT is more accurate but more expensive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后把 FP32 直接转低精度,用校准集设缩放,不重训。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PTQ (Post-Training Quantization) converts a trained FP32 model to low precision using a calibration set, without retraining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在训练中模拟量化噪声,让权重对低精度鲁棒,精度更好但需重训。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QAT (Quantization-Aware Training) simulates quantization noise during training so weights tolerate low precision, giving better accuracy but requiring a retrain.

scenario: 延迟/成本吃紧,要尽快把模型量化上线,没有重训预算,但能接受 0.5-2% 的精度损失。
scenario_en: Latency/cost is tight, you must ship a quantized model fast with no retraining budget, and can tolerate a 0.5-2% accuracy drop.
q: 没有重训预算、要快速上线、可接受小幅精度损失,选 PTQ 还是 QAT?
q_en: With no retraining budget, needing a fast launch and tolerating a small accuracy drop, PTQ or QAT?
why: 选 PTQ:训练后直接转 INT8、跑校准集即可,几小时上线,契合「无重训预算+可接受 0.5-2% 掉点」。QAT 要一整轮训练,只有在精度极敏感、且有重训资源时才值得。
