termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed bound on latency/availability whose breach triggers a high-priority alert.

scenario: 一个高重要度特征的 PSI 突破 0.25、在线指标也跌过阈值,但服务没报错、输出还正常,用户暂时没受明显影响。
scenario_en: A high-importance feature's PSI crosses 0.25 and an online metric dips past threshold, but serving is fine and outputs normal, with no clear user impact yet.
q: 这该归到哪个告警层，为什么不是立即 page？
q_en: Which alert tier is this, and why not page immediately?
why: 显著数据漂移(高重要度特征 PSI>0.25)+在线指标退化,属「退化但仍可用」,归 Tier 2:小时级告警。它需要尽快处理但系统没崩,占用即时 page 反而制造告警疲劳。
why_en: Significant data drift (high-importance feature PSI>0.25) plus online-metric degradation is 'degrading but functional,' so it is Tier 2 within-hours — it needs prompt attention but the system is not down, and paging immediately would breed alert fatigue.
tradeoff: Tier 2 小时级(退化但可用) vs Tier 1 page(系统正在坏)
options: Tier 1 立即 page:任何特征越过 PSI 阈值都必须马上把值班人叫醒
Tier 2 小时级:显著漂移+指标退化属退化但仍可用,系统还没崩
Tier 3 日报:输出目前还正常,再显著的漂移也只能算信息性观察
不告警:PSI 只是个参考指标,等在线指标彻底崩了再处理也不迟
options_en: Tier 1 page immediately: any feature crossing its PSI threshold must wake on-call right away.
Tier 2 within hours: significant drift plus metric decay is degrading-but-usable, and the system has not gone down.
Tier 3 daily digest: output still looks fine, so even significant drift is only an informational observation.
No alert: PSI is only a reference number, and it is fine to wait until online metrics fully collapse.
whenOtherWins: 若这个漂移已导致输出塌缩或延迟 SLA 违约、用户正在受损,就升级到 Tier 1 立即 page。
whenOtherWins_en: If the drift has caused output collapse or a latency SLA breach with users being harmed, escalate to Tier 1 page immediately.
optionExplanations: 把所有漂移都设成立即 page 会制造告警疲劳,只有正在伤用户才配 Tier 1。
对;显著漂移+指标退化但系统仍可用,正是 Tier 2 小时级的定义。
显著数据漂移比日报级(轻微/陈旧)更急,放 Tier 3 会拖成大故障。
PSI>0.25 在高重要度特征上是明确行动信号,不能不告警。
optionExplanations_en: Making all drift page-immediately breeds alert fatigue; only active user harm warrants Tier 1.
Correct — significant drift plus metric degradation while the system stays usable is exactly the Tier 2 within-hours definition.
Significant data drift is more urgent than digest-level (minor/staleness); Tier 3 would let it fester into a big outage.
PSI>0.25 on a high-importance feature is a clear action signal that must be alerted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按影响把告警分级(Tier 1 立即 page / Tier 2 小时级 / Tier 3 日报),控制噪声。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Severity tiers grade alerts by impact (Tier 1 page / Tier 2 within-hours / Tier 3 digest) to control noise.

scenario: 团队要决定「PSI 到多少才该告警」,有人想直接照搬教科书的 0.25,有人想按自己历史事故来定。
scenario_en: The team must decide 'at what PSI to alert,' with some wanting to copy the textbook 0.25 and others wanting to base it on their own past incidents.
q: 告警阈值最该怎么定？
q_en: How should alert thresholds be set?
why: 阈值要经验校准:回溯历史事故,看到底多大的漂移幅度才真正对应到用户可感的退化,再据此设阈值。照搬通用数字容易在你的业务上要么太吵、要么漏报。
why_en: Calibrate thresholds empirically: do a retrospective on past incidents to find what drift magnitude actually correlated with user-facing degradation, and set thresholds from that, since copying generic numbers is too noisy or too blind on your workload.
tradeoff: 经验校准阈值(贴合本业务) vs 照搬通用值(简单但常错配)
options: 直接照搬教科书的 0.25,它对所有系统都通用,不必看自家历史数据
经验校准:回溯历史事故,找出真正对应用户可感退化的漂移幅度
把阈值设到最敏感,宁可全报也不漏,噪声让值班人手工筛掉就行
阈值先随便设一个,反正上线之后总会凭手感不断往上往下调
options_en: Just copy the textbook 0.25; it is universal across systems and you need not look at your own history.
Calibrate empirically: replay past incidents to find the drift magnitude that actually tracked user-visible degradation.
Set thresholds to maximum sensitivity, over-alert rather than miss, and let on-call filter the noise by hand.
Pick any threshold to start, since you will keep nudging it up and down by feel after launch anyway.
whenOtherWins: 冷启动、还没有历史事故数据时,可先用 0.25 等通用值当起点,积累事故后再用经验值替换。
whenOtherWins_en: On cold start with no incident history, start from a generic value like 0.25 and replace it with empirical thresholds once incidents accumulate.
optionExplanations: 通用 0.25 未必匹配你的特征与业务,照搬常导致要么太吵要么漏报。
对;用历史事故反推「多大漂移=真退化」,阈值才贴合本业务,既不吵也不漏。
最敏感阈值制造海量误报,正是告警疲劳的根源。
随机阈值没有依据,会长期在误报和漏报之间乱跳。
optionExplanations_en: A generic 0.25 may not match your features and business, so copying it tends to be too noisy or too blind.
Correct — inferring 'what drift equals real degradation' from past incidents fits your workload, neither noisy nor blind.
The most sensitive threshold creates a flood of false alarms — the very source of alert fatigue.
Random thresholds have no basis and will swing between false alarms and misses for a long time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用历史事故的实际数据反推阈值,而非照搬通用默认值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Empirical calibration derives thresholds from real historical-incident data rather than copying generic defaults.

q: 告警响了,把 on-call 处置手册的四步排成正确顺序:
q_en: An alert fires — order the four on-call playbook steps correctly:
steps: 核实告警不是误报:查管线健康、特征新鲜度、监控本身是否有 bug
评估爆炸半径:哪些分段、多少比例流量受影响
按严重度执行响应:紧急再训练 / 回滚到上个 champion / 启用兜底启发式
记录根因并更新阈值:每次事故回灌到监控配置
why: 顺序是先证真再评估影响、再动手、最后固化经验:①核实防止为误报瞎忙;②评估爆炸半径决定处置力度;③按严重度选再训练/回滚/降级;④把根因和新阈值写回配置,让下次更准。
why_en: The order is verify, assess impact, act, then institutionalize: confirm it is not a false positive, gauge blast radius to size the response, execute by severity (retrain/rollback/fallback), then document root cause and update thresholds so next time is sharper.
diagram:
flowchart TB V["1. 核实非误报"] --> B["2. 评估爆炸半径"] B --> E["3. 执行响应
再训练/回滚/降级"] E --> D["4. 记录根因+更新阈值"] D -.回灌.-> V

termDefinitions.term: on-call playbook / 值班处置手册
termDefinitions.meaning: 告警触发后逐步照做的标准流程:核实→评估→响应→复盘,减少现场判断失误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An on-call playbook is a step-by-step standard procedure after an alert: verify, assess, respond, review — reducing on-the-spot mistakes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次故障影响到的分段和流量比例,决定该多用力处置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blast radius is the segments and traffic fraction a fault affects, sizing how forcefully to respond.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型不可用时退回的简单规则(如按热度排序),保证服务不彻底崩。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fallback heuristic is a simple rule (e.g. popularity ranking) the system falls back to when the model is unusable, keeping service alive.

scenario: 告警确认为真、爆炸半径评估完毕,现在要选具体响应动作,严重度为「系统正在严重伤用户」。
scenario_en: The alert is confirmed real and blast radius assessed; now choose the response action, with severity 'the system is seriously harming users.'
q: on-call 手册第三步「执行响应」通常在哪几种动作里按严重度选？
q_en: The playbook's third step 'execute response' typically chooses among which actions by severity?
why: 第三步按严重度在三种动作里选:紧急再训练(有干净数据、时间允许)、回滚到上一个 champion(最快止血、恢复已知良好版本)、或启用兜底启发式(连回滚都不稳时保底可用)。严重伤用户时优先回滚/降级先止血。
why_en: Step three picks by severity among emergency retraining (clean data and time allow), rollback to the previous champion (fastest stop-loss to a known-good version), or activating a fallback heuristic (guarantee availability when even rollback is shaky); with serious user harm, roll back or degrade first to stop the bleeding.
tradeoff: 回滚/降级(最快止血) vs 紧急再训练(治本但慢,需干净数据)
options: 只有紧急再训练这一个动作:不管训练数据是否已被污染、也不考虑回滚,一律立刻重训
紧急再训练 / 回滚到上个 champion / 启用兜底启发式,按严重度选
只能等下一个调度周期再统一处理,不做任何即时的响应动作
直接关停整个服务,不提供降级或兜底,等彻底修好了再开回来
options_en: Only one action, emergency retraining: retrain immediately regardless of whether training data is polluted and without considering rollback.
Emergency retrain, rollback to the previous champion, or switch on a fallback heuristic, picked by severity.
Wait for the next scheduled cycle and handle it in batch, taking no immediate response action.
Shut the whole service down with no degraded mode or fallback, and bring it back only once fully fixed.
whenOtherWins: 若退化温和、且已有验证干净的新数据,可跳过回滚直接紧急再训练治本;止血优先只在严重伤用户时压倒治本。
whenOtherWins_en: If degradation is mild and clean new data is validated, skip rollback and retrain to fix the root cause; stop-loss-first only overrides root-cause fixing under serious user harm.
optionExplanations: 紧急再训练若在脏数据上做反而更糟,不能作为唯一动作,严重时更该先止血。
对;三选一按严重度定,严重伤用户时回滚/降级最快恢复已知良好状态。
严重事故等下个周期等于放任伤害,违背 on-call 即时响应的初衷。
关停服务比降级更伤用户,兜底启发式正是为避免彻底关停而设。
optionExplanations_en: Emergency retraining on dirty data makes it worse, so it cannot be the only action, and serious cases should stop-loss first.
Correct — pick one of three by severity, and with serious harm rollback/degrade fastest restores a known-good state.
Waiting for the next cycle during a serious incident lets harm continue, defeating on-call's immediate-response purpose.
Shutting down harms users more than degrading; a fallback heuristic exists precisely to avoid full shutdown.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务切回上一个已知良好的模型版本(上个 champion),最快止血。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rollback switches serving back to the last known-good model version (the previous champion), the fastest stop-loss.

scenario: 面试官问你监控设计里最核心的取舍;你想给一句能收住全场、并说清怎么落地的话。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks the core tradeoff in your monitoring design and wants one closing line plus how you would implement it.
q: ML 监控的核心取舍是什么，最优做法是怎样落地的？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff in ML monitoring, and how does the optimal approach implement it?
why: 核心取舍是监控粒度 vs 运维成本:对每个特征高频跑昂贵统计是浪费,信号太少又留盲区。最优落地:重点监控高重要度特征、用预测分布当快速跳闸线、用历史事故经验校准告警阈值,把成本花在最能预警用户可感退化的地方。
why_en: The core tradeoff is monitoring granularity vs operational cost: expensive stats on every feature at high frequency is wasteful while too few signals leave blind spots, so the optimum monitors high-importance features, uses the prediction distribution as a fast tripwire, and calibrates thresholds empirically.
tradeoff: 监控粒度(覆盖全但贵) vs 运维成本(省钱但留盲区)
options: 核心取舍是精度 vs 召回,把决策阈值调一调即可,与监控成本无关
监控越多越好,只要算力买得够,根本不存在任何成本上的取舍
监控粒度 vs 运维成本:重点监控高重要度特征+预测分布当快跳闸线
核心取舍是 GPU vs CPU,选对推理硬件,监控开销自然就降下来了
options_en: The core tradeoff is precision versus recall; just move the decision threshold, and monitoring cost is not involved.
More monitoring is always better; buy enough compute and there is no cost tradeoff at all.
Monitoring granularity versus operational cost: watch high-importance features and use the prediction distribution as a fast tripwire.
The core tradeoff is GPU versus CPU; pick the right inference hardware and monitoring overhead drops by itself.
whenOtherWins: 若是高风险合规场景(如医疗/风控),可接受更高监控成本换取近乎全覆盖的粒度,天平偏向粒度而非省钱。
whenOtherWins_en: In high-stakes compliance settings (medical/risk), accept higher monitoring cost for near-full coverage, tilting toward granularity over savings.
optionExplanations: 精度/召回是模型评估指标,不是监控系统的成本-覆盖取舍。
监控有实打实的算力和维护成本,盲目全量监控不可持续,存在明确取舍。
对;粒度 vs 成本是核心轴,三招(重点特征+预测跳闸+经验阈值)把成本花在刀刃上。
GPU/CPU 是硬件选型,答不到监控覆盖与成本的系统级取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Precision/recall is a model-evaluation metric, not the cost-coverage tradeoff of a monitoring system.
Monitoring has real compute and maintenance cost, so blanket monitoring is unsustainable and a real tradeoff exists.
Correct — granularity vs cost is the core axis, and the three moves (key features, prediction tripwire, empirical thresholds) spend cost where it counts.
GPU/CPU is hardware selection and misses the system-level tradeoff of monitoring coverage vs cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控覆盖多少特征、多高频率;越细越无盲区但成本越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Monitoring granularity is how many features and how often you monitor; finer means fewer blind spots but higher cost.

scenario: 复习 PSI 的三档阈值与各自动作。
scenario_en: Review PSI's three threshold bands and their actions.
q: 补全 PSI 的三档阈值与对应处置：
q_en: Fill in PSI's three threshold bands and their actions:
text: PSI 阈值:<{{0.1}} 视为无明显漂移;{{0.1–0.25}} 为中度漂移,需{{排查}};>{{0.25}} 为显著漂移,需{{采取行动}}(排查/再训练)。
text_en: PSI thresholds: <{{0.1}} means no meaningful shift; {{0.1-0.25}} is moderate drift needing {{investigation}}; >{{0.25}} is significant drift needing {{action}} (investigate/retrain).
why: PSI 三档是经验分级:<0.1 稳、0.1–0.25 中度先排查、>0.25 显著要行动。它把连续的漂移分数转成清晰的处置动作,也对应告警分级里 PSI>0.25 归 Tier 2。
why_en: PSI's three bands are an empirical grading: under 0.1 stable, 0.1 to 0.25 moderate-investigate, above 0.25 significant-act, mapping a continuous score to clear actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 总体稳定性指数,衡量分布漂移;三档阈值 0.1/0.25 对应无/中度/显著。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PSI (Population Stability Index) measures distribution drift, with 0.1/0.25 bands for none/moderate/significant.

scenario: 回归型贷款违约模型,某天预测的平均违约率从 12% 跳到 40%。
scenario_en: A regression loan-default model sees its predicted average default rate jump from 12% to 40% one day.
q: 预测监控对回归模型看什么，这个突变说明什么、下一步该做什么？
q_en: What does prediction monitoring track for regression, what does this jump mean, and what next?
why: 回归型预测监控看输出的均值/方差/分位数随时间的变化。12%→40% 是输出分布突变,是症状不是根因:可能数据漂移、概念漂移、管线 bug 或特征陈旧。下一步先按 on-call 手册核实非误报、查未监控特征管线,再定性。
why_en: For regression, prediction monitoring tracks the output mean/variance/percentiles over time, and a 12% to 40% jump is a symptom not a root cause (data drift, concept drift, pipeline bug, or stale features), so next verify it is not a false positive and check unmonitored feature pipelines before diagnosing.
options: 看输出均值/方差/分位数;这是症状不是根因,先核实再查未监控管线
看输入 PSI;这种突变必然是数据漂移,直接触发一次全量再训练即可
看 GPU 利用率;突变说明算力不足,把推理节点扩容上去就会回落
看模型文件体积;突变说明参数损坏,回滚换一个模型文件就好了
options_en: Track output mean, variance and percentiles; this is a symptom not a cause, so verify it then check unmonitored pipelines.
Track input PSI; a jump like this has to be data drift, so just kick off a full retrain.
Track GPU utilization; the jump means not enough compute, and scaling out inference nodes will bring it back.
Track model file size; the jump means corrupted parameters, so roll back to another model file.
optionExplanations: 对;回归看均值/方差/分位数,输出突变只是症状,须按手册先证真、查管线再定根因。
预测监控看的是输出不是输入 PSI,且突变未必是数据漂移,直接再训练会跳过定位。
GPU 利用率是资源指标,和预测违约率的分布突变无关。
模型体积不变也与违约率突变无关,属无关项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — regression tracks mean/variance/percentiles, an output jump is only a symptom, so verify and check pipelines before naming a root cause.
Prediction monitoring tracks outputs not input PSI, and the jump is not necessarily data drift, so retraining outright skips localization.
GPU utilization is a resource metric, unrelated to a distributional jump in predicted default rate.
Model size does not change and is unrelated to the default-rate jump, an irrelevant option.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测值的分布;分类看类概率/频率,回归看均值/方差/分位数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The output distribution is the spread of the model's predictions; classification tracks class probabilities/frequencies, regression tracks mean/variance/percentiles.

scenario: 面试题「设计一个像 YouTube 的视频推荐系统」,目录有数十亿视频,每次请求要在 sub-100ms 内返回。
scenario_en: The interview prompt 'design a YouTube-like video recommender' with billions of videos and a sub-100ms per-request budget.
q: 视频推荐的主流架构是什么，为什么要分两阶段？
q_en: What is the dominant video-recommendation architecture, and why two stages?
why: 主流是两阶段:候选生成(轻量方法)先把数十亿视频收窄到数百个,排序(重模型)再精细打分。一个重模型直接扫全部视频在延迟预算内跑不完,分层是为兼顾规模与精度。
why_en: The dominant design is two stages: light candidate generation narrows billions to hundreds first, then a heavy model ranks precisely — one heavy model scoring every video can't fit the latency budget, so splitting balances scale and precision.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["数十亿视频"] --> CG["候选生成
轻量, ANN"] CG --> H["数百候选"] H --> RK["排序
重模型精打分"] RK --> T["最终数十条"]
options: 单阶段:一个重模型对全部数十亿视频逐条打分
两阶段:候选生成轻量筛选,排序模型精细打分,兼顾规模与延迟
两阶段:先用重模型给全部视频打分排序,再从排序结果里随机采样出候选集
三阶段纯规则过滤视频,全程不使用任何模型
options_en: Single stage: one heavy model scores all billions of videos one by one.
Two stages: light candidate generation filters first, then a ranking model scores precisely, balancing scale and latency.
Two stages: first use the heavy model to score and rank all videos, then randomly sample candidates from the ranked result.
Three stages of pure rule filtering, using no model at all.
optionExplanations: 单模型逐条给数十亿视频打分,时间开销远超预算,单阶段行不通。
对;候选生成先轻量筛掉大部分、排序再精细打分,两阶段撑住了这个延迟预算。
顺序反了:排序该在候选缩小之后做,不可能先排全部再采样。
只靠规则过滤扛不住海量个性化需求,精度不够。
optionExplanations_en: One model scoring billions one by one blows the budget, so a single stage does not work.
Correct — candidate generation filters lightly first and ranking scores precisely after, which is what makes the latency budget hold.
Order backwards: ranking should happen after candidates shrink, not before sampling from a full ranking.
Rule-only filtering can't handle personalization at this scale, so precision suffers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段推荐的第一阶段,用轻量方法从海量目录快速筛出数百候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the first stage of a two-stage recommender, using a light method to narrow a huge catalog to a few hundred candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第二阶段,用较重的模型给候选集精细打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ranking is the second stage, scoring the candidate set finely with a heavier model.

scenario: 候选人一上来就画两塔、画排序模型框图,完全跳过了「这是给谁、优化什么、什么约束」的澄清。
scenario_en: A candidate immediately draws two-tower and ranking boxes, skipping any clarification of who it serves, what to optimize, and the constraints.
q: 为什么「先做问题框定再画框图」很重要，跳过它的后果是什么？
q_en: Why frame the problem before drawing boxes, and what happens if you skip it?
why: 问题框定决定了标签定义、指标、架构与约束——它是所有下游设计的地基。跳过它是这类题的头号失分点:你可能给错误的目标造了个漂亮系统,澄清问题才让每个设计决策有依据。
why_en: Problem framing fixes the label definition, metrics, architecture, and constraints — the foundation for every downstream choice — and skipping it is the number-one failure mode, since you may build an elegant system for the wrong objective.
options: 框定决定标签/指标/架构/约束,跳过=为错目标造漂亮系统
框定只是暖场寒暄,经验丰富的候选人可以省略,直接开讲架构照样拿高分
框定只影响算法选型,与指标定义和业务目标没有关系
跳过框定没有代价,架构图画得够漂亮一样能拿到通过
options_en: Framing fixes labels, metrics, architecture and constraints; skip it and you build an elegant system for the wrong objective.
Framing is just a warm-up formality; an experienced candidate can skip it and still score well by diving straight into the architecture.
Framing only affects algorithm selection and has nothing to do with metric definitions or business goals.
Skipping framing costs nothing; a polished enough architecture diagram still passes the interview.
optionExplanations: 对;框定钉住目标与约束,后面每个决策才有依据,跳过它正是最常见的失分。
越资深越会花时间框定,因为它决定全局方向,不是可跳的形式。
框定恰恰把商业目标映射成 ML 指标,与指标定义紧密相关。
漂亮架构若对着错误目标就是白费,跳过框定代价极大。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — framing pins the objective and constraints so every later decision has a basis, and skipping it is the most common way to lose points.
More senior candidates spend more time framing because it sets global direction; it is not a skippable formality.
Framing precisely maps business goals to ML metrics and is tightly tied to metric definition.
A pretty architecture aimed at the wrong objective is wasted, so skipping framing is very costly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 画架构前先澄清目标、用户、约束、指标,把业务问题翻译成 ML 问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem framing clarifies objective, users, constraints, and metrics before architecture, translating a business problem into an ML one.

scenario: 澄清产品形态:这个推荐是首页 feed(用户刚进来、没有明确上下文),还是「看完这个接着看」的侧边栏(有当前正在看的视频作锚)。
scenario_en: Clarify the surface: is this a homepage feed (user just arrived, no explicit context) or a watch-next sidebar (anchored to the currently playing video)?
q: 首页 feed vs watch-next 侧边栏这个区分，主要驱动哪个下游设计决策？
q_en: Homepage feed vs watch-next sidebar mainly drives which downstream design decision?
why: 它决定候选生成的策略:首页 feed 没有当前视频锚点,要做宽主题的候选生成(覆盖用户广泛兴趣);watch-next 有正在看的视频作锚,要做上下文锚定的候选生成(与当前视频强相关)。
why_en: It drives the candidate-generation strategy: a homepage feed has no anchor and needs broad-topic candidate generation, while a watch-next sidebar is anchored to the current video and needs contextually-anchored generation.
tradeoff: 宽主题候选生成(首页、覆盖广兴趣) vs 上下文锚定候选生成(watch-next、强相关当前视频)
options: 决定用哪种数据库存视频元数据和索引
决定候选生成策略:有无「当前视频」作锚点
决定前端用哪个框架渲染推荐列表和播放器
决定排序模型训练要用几张 GPU、跑多少轮
options_en: Which database stores video metadata and its indexes.
The candidate-generation strategy: whether there is a current-video anchor.
Which frontend framework renders the recommendation list and player.
How many GPUs and epochs the ranking model needs for training.
whenOtherWins: 若产品其实是纯搜索结果页(用户已输入明确 query),候选生成就该由 query 驱动,而非 feed 的兴趣覆盖或 watch-next 的视频锚定。
whenOtherWins_en: If the surface is actually a search results page with an explicit query, candidate generation should be query-driven, not feed interest coverage or watch-next anchoring.
optionExplanations: 选数据库是存储层细节,与「有没有当前视频锚点」这个产品语义无关。
对;有无锚点直接决定候选生成是宽主题还是上下文锚定,这是产品澄清的核心影响。
前端框架与推荐候选策略无关,答不到设计影响。
GPU 数量是训练资源,不由产品形态的锚点差异决定。
optionExplanations_en: Choosing a database is a storage detail, unrelated to the product semantics of whether there is a current-video anchor.
Correct — presence of an anchor directly decides broad-topic vs context-anchored candidate generation, the core impact of this product clarification.
The frontend framework is unrelated to candidate strategy and misses the design impact.
GPU count is a training resource, not decided by the anchor difference in product surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以当前正在播放的视频为上下文锚点,推荐紧接着看的视频。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Watch-next uses the currently playing video as a context anchor to recommend what to watch next.

scenario: 澄清用户:目标用户是已登录(有丰富观看历史)还是匿名(几乎没有个人历史)。
scenario_en: Clarify the user: are targets logged-in (rich watch history) or anonymous (almost no personal history)?
q: 登录 vs 匿名这个区分，主要驱动哪个设计决策？
q_en: Logged-in vs anonymous mainly drives which design decision?
why: 它决定用协同过滤还是内容信号,以及要不要处理冷启动:登录用户有历史,可用协同过滤(看过 X 的人也看 Y);匿名用户没历史,得靠内容特征/上下文,面对冷启动问题。
why_en: It decides collaborative filtering vs content-based signals and whether you handle cold start: logged-in users have history for collaborative filtering, while anonymous users lack history and need content/context signals under cold start.
tradeoff: 协同过滤(需历史、登录用户) vs 内容/上下文信号(无历史、匿名/冷启动)
options: 决定视频要用什么编码格式、码率阶梯和转码成本怎么摊销
决定 CDN 边缘节点部署在哪些地区
决定用协同过滤还是内容信号,以及冷启动怎么办
决定排序模型的学习率和优化器怎么调
options_en: Which codec, bitrate ladder, and how transcoding costs get amortized for video storage.
Which regions the CDN edge nodes are deployed to.
Collaborative filtering vs content signals, and how cold start is handled.
How the ranking model’s learning rate and optimizer are tuned.
whenOtherWins: 若即便登录用户也普遍缺历史(新平台早期),那所有人都近似冷启动,应主打内容信号而非协同过滤。
whenOtherWins_en: If even logged-in users mostly lack history (an early-stage platform), everyone is near cold start and you should lead with content signals over collaborative filtering.
optionExplanations: 编码格式是存储/播放细节,与用户有无历史的建模选择无关。
CDN 部署是分发层,不由「登录 vs 匿名」的信号可得性决定。
对;有无历史直接决定 CF vs 内容信号与冷启动处理,是用户澄清的核心影响。
学习率是训练超参,不由用户是否登录这个产品语义决定。
optionExplanations_en: Codec is a storage/playback detail, unrelated to the modeling choice of whether the user has history.
CDN deployment is a delivery-layer concern, not decided by logged-in vs anonymous signal availability.
Correct — history availability directly decides CF vs content signals and cold-start handling, the core impact of this user clarification.
Learning rate is a training hyperparameter, not decided by the product semantics of logged-in status.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据行为相似的用户群推荐:看过 X 的人也看 Y,需要用户历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends from behaviorally similar users (people who watched X also watched Y), needing user history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新物品缺历史时无法用协同过滤,需内容/上下文兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when a new user or item lacks history so collaborative filtering fails and content/context must fill in.

scenario: 澄清内容规模:目录到底是几千个视频,还是数十亿个视频。
scenario_en: Clarify catalog scale: is it a few thousand videos or billions?
q: 目录规模这个澄清，主要决定哪个架构选择？
q_en: The catalog-scale clarification mainly decides which architecture choice?
why: 它决定候选生成阶段要不要上 ANN 检索:目录小可以暴力打分或简单过滤;数十亿量级无法逐个打分,必须用近似最近邻(ANN)在预算内把 billions 收窄到 hundreds。
why_en: It decides whether candidate generation needs ANN retrieval: a small catalog can be brute-force scored, but billions cannot be scored one by one and require approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search to narrow within budget.
tradeoff: 小目录(暴力/简单过滤够用) vs 数十亿目录(必须 ANN 检索)
options: 决定日志系统和监控告警的选型
决定候选生成要不要上 ANN 近似检索
决定 A/B 实验分几组、跑多长时间
决定推荐卡片的界面配色和排版
options_en: Which logging and monitoring-alert stack to adopt.
Whether candidate generation needs ANN approximate retrieval.
How many arms the A/B experiment runs and for how long.
The color scheme and layout of the recommendation cards.
whenOtherWins: 若目录只有几千条,ANN 是过度工程,直接暴力打分或简单启发式过滤更省事、还没有近似召回损失。
whenOtherWins_en: If the catalog is only a few thousand, ANN is over-engineering — brute-force scoring or a simple heuristic filter is simpler with no approximation recall loss.
optionExplanations: 日志系统是可观测性细节,与候选检索是否需要 ANN 无关。
对;规模是否到数十亿直接决定能否暴力打分,还是必须 ANN,这是内容澄清的核心。
A/B 分组是实验设计,不由目录规模决定。
配色是前端,与检索架构无关。
optionExplanations_en: A logging system is an observability detail, unrelated to whether retrieval needs ANN.
Correct — whether scale reaches billions directly decides brute-force vs mandatory ANN, the core of this content clarification.
A/B grouping is experiment design, not decided by catalog scale.
Color scheme is frontend, unrelated to retrieval architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索:牺牲一点精确度换取在海量向量里毫秒级找到相近项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search trades a little exactness for millisecond retrieval of nearby items among massive vectors.

scenario: 澄清优化目标:主要优化「观看时长」这种即时参与,还是「长期满意度/留存」这种慢变量。
scenario_en: Clarify the objective: optimize immediate engagement like watch time, or a slow variable like long-term satisfaction/retention?
q: 优化目标的澄清，主要决定哪些下游 ML 设计？
q_en: The objective clarification mainly decides which downstream ML choices?
why: 它决定标签定义、损失函数和护栏指标:优化观看时长就以预测观看时长为标签/损失;要长期满意度则得引入 7 天回访等慢标签,并配护栏指标防止只追即时参与把体验带偏。
why_en: It decides label definition, loss function, and guardrail metric: optimizing watch time makes predicted watch time the label/loss, while long-term satisfaction needs slow labels like 7-day repeat visits plus a guardrail so chasing engagement does not wreck experience.
tradeoff: 观看时长(即时、易测但易诱导标题党) vs 长期满意度(慢标签但护住留存)
options: 决定标签定义、损失函数和护栏指标怎么选
决定该用哪家云厂商、什么实例规格和预留实例折扣方案
决定视频缩略图的尺寸和压缩比
决定推荐结果缓存的过期时间设多久
options_en: Label definition, loss function, and which guardrail metrics to pick.
Which cloud vendor, instance type, and reserved-instance discount plan to use.
The thumbnail dimensions and compression ratio.
How long recommendation cache entries stay valid.
whenOtherWins: 若产品明确只追短期变现(如广告位测试),可暂时只用观看时长做标签,但仍应挂个护栏指标监控长期体验。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product explicitly chases short-term monetization (an ad-slot test), you may temporarily use watch time alone as the label, but still attach a guardrail to watch long-term experience.
optionExplanations: 对;目标直接决定标签、损失和护栏,是把商业目标翻译成 ML 问题的关键澄清。
云厂商是基建选型,与优化目标的标签定义无关。
缩略图尺寸是产品细节,不由优化目标决定。
缓存过期是工程参数,与标签/损失/护栏无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the objective directly decides label, loss, and guardrail, the key clarification translating business goals into an ML problem.
Cloud vendor is infrastructure selection, unrelated to the objective's label definition.
Thumbnail size is a product detail, not decided by the objective.
Cache expiry is an engineering parameter, unrelated to label/loss/guardrail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与主目标并列监控的副指标,防止一味优化主目标损害长期体验(如多样性、留存)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a secondary metric watched alongside the primary objective to prevent over-optimizing it from harming long-term experience.

scenario: 澄清约束:端到端延迟预算是宽松(几百 ms 可接受)还是紧张(必须 sub-100ms)。
scenario_en: Clarify constraints: is the end-to-end latency budget loose (a few hundred ms) or tight (sub-100ms)?
q: 延迟预算这个约束，主要决定哪个架构取舍？
q_en: The latency-budget constraint mainly decides which architectural tradeoff?
why: 它决定实时排序 vs 预计算:预算宽松可以在请求时跑更重的实时模型;预算紧张(sub-100ms)则很多计算得预先算好(如视频侧嵌入离线预计算),把在线只留下最省的那部分。
why_en: It decides real-time ranking vs precomputation: a loose budget allows a heavier real-time model at request time, while a tight sub-100ms budget forces precomputing much of the work (e.g. offline video embeddings) so only the cheapest part runs online.
tradeoff: 实时计算(灵活、新鲜但吃延迟预算) vs 预计算(省在线延迟但牺牲新鲜度/灵活性)
options: 决定服务该用什么编程语言、框架和部署容器规格
决定实时排序还是预计算:紧预算逼你离线算好
决定团队要招几个工程师、怎么分工
决定日志和特征数据保留多少天
options_en: Which programming language, framework, and deployment container spec implement the service.
Real-time ranking vs precomputation: a tight budget forces the work offline.
How many engineers to hire and how to split the work.
How many days logs and feature data are retained.
whenOtherWins: 若延迟预算宽松(离线批量推荐邮件、无需秒回),可以在请求时跑更重的实时模型换取更高精度,不必大量预计算。
whenOtherWins_en: If the latency budget is loose (offline batch recommendation emails with no instant response), run a heavier real-time model at request time for accuracy instead of heavy precomputation.
optionExplanations: 编程语言是实现细节,不由端到端延迟预算这个架构约束决定。
对;预算松紧直接决定哪些算实时、哪些预计算,是约束澄清的核心影响。
招聘是团队问题,与延迟预算的架构取舍无关。
日志保留是运维策略,与实时 vs 预计算无关。
optionExplanations_en: Programming language is an implementation detail, not decided by the end-to-end latency constraint.
Correct — how tight the budget is directly decides what runs real-time vs precomputed, the core impact of this constraint clarification.
Hiring is a team question, unrelated to the latency budget's architectural tradeoff.
Log retention is an ops policy, unrelated to real-time vs precomputation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把耗时计算提前离线算好存起来,在线只做最轻的查询,以压低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precomputation does expensive work offline in advance and stores it, so online only does light lookups to cut latency.

scenario: 澄清是否采集负反馈:系统要不要记录 skip、dislike 这类「用户不喜欢」的信号。
scenario_en: Clarify negative-feedback capture: does the system log skips/dislikes — signals of what users don't want?
q: 是否采集负反馈这个澄清，主要决定训练数据的什么？
q_en: The negative-feedback clarification mainly decides what about the training data?
why: 它决定训练数据是否含负信号:采集 skip/dislike 就能同时用正负样本训练;不采集就只有正样本(仅点击),模型会把「没点击」当中性,误读意图、强化低质推荐。
why_en: It decides whether training data includes negative signals: capturing skips/dislikes lets you train on both positive and negative samples, while positive-only (clicks) makes the model treat no-click as neutral, misreading intent.
tradeoff: 含负反馈(正负样本、更准建模不喜欢) vs 仅正反馈(把无点击当中性、易误读意图)
options: 决定训练数据含不含负信号,无点击算不算负例
决定视频清晰度档位、转码码率和存储空间占用大小
决定一屏推荐几条、下拉翻页拉多少
决定服务器机房放在哪个地理区域
options_en: Whether training data carries negative signals — does a no-click count as negative.
Which resolution tiers, transcoding bitrates, and how much storage space they occupy.
How many items per screen and per pagination fetch.
Which geographic region hosts the servers.
whenOtherWins: 若平台确实几乎没有可靠的负反馈渠道(如纯浏览无交互按钮),只能先用正样本+采样负例近似,但要显式承认这个偏差。
whenOtherWins_en: If the platform truly lacks reliable negative channels (pure browsing with no interaction buttons), you may approximate with positives plus sampled negatives, but explicitly acknowledge the bias.
optionExplanations: 对;采不采负反馈直接决定训练能否用负样本,是最容易被忽略却很关键的澄清。
清晰度是播放质量,与训练标签正负无关。
推荐条数是产品参数,不由负反馈采集决定。
机房位置是基建,与训练数据的正负信号无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — whether you capture negative feedback directly decides whether training can use negative samples, an easily overlooked but crucial clarification.
Resolution is playback quality, unrelated to positive/negative training labels.
The number of recommendations is a product parameter, not decided by negative-feedback capture.
Datacenter location is infrastructure, unrelated to positive/negative training signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户不喜欢的信号(skip、dislike),让模型学到「不该推什么」,而非只学正样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Negative feedback is signals of dislike (skip, dislike) that teach the model what not to recommend, not just positives.

scenario: 一个推荐系统只从正向参与(点击、观看)学习,把「用户没点」一律当作中性、无信息。
scenario_en: A recommender learns only from positive engagement (clicks, watches) and treats every no-click as neutral and uninformative.
q: 「只学正反馈、把无点击当中性」会导致什么后果链？
q_en: What consequence chain follows from 'learn only from positives, treat no-click as neutral'?
why: 只学正样本→把「没点」误当中性而非负信号→误读用户意图(其实是不喜欢)→继续推类似低质内容→正反馈回路自我强化,质量悄悄下滑。修法是显式建模负反馈(skip/dislike)。
why_en: Positive-only training treats no-click as neutral rather than negative, misreads intent, keeps recommending similar low-quality content, and self-reinforces via the feedback loop, quietly degrading quality — fixed by explicitly modeling negatives.
options: 无点击当中性→误读意图→继续推低质→回路自我强化
毫无影响,只用正样本的点击数据就足以学到完整的用户偏好分布
只会让训练更快收敛,是省算力的优点
会导致 GPU 过热掉卡,是硬件层面的问题
options_en: No-click read as neutral misreads intent, keeps pushing low-quality items, and the loop self-reinforces.
No effect; click data from positive samples alone is enough to learn the complete user preference distribution.
It only makes training converge faster, which saves compute.
It overheats the GPUs and drops cards, a hardware-level problem.
optionExplanations: 对;把负信号当中性抹掉了「不喜欢」,回路会不断强化低质推荐,必须显式建模负反馈。
正样本缺了「不喜欢」的一半信息,学不到完整偏好,并非无影响。
收敛快但学错了目标,把误读意图当优点是本末倒置。
GPU 过热与训练信号正负毫无关系,是无关项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — treating negatives as neutral erases 'dislike', and the loop keeps reinforcing low-quality recs, so negatives must be modeled explicitly.
Positives lack the 'dislike' half, so full preferences cannot be learned — not a no-op.
Fast convergence toward the wrong objective is not a benefit; calling misread intent an advantage is backwards.
GPU overheating has nothing to do with positive/negative training signal, an irrelevant option.

termDefinitions.term: positive-only bias / 仅正样本偏差
termDefinitions.meaning: 只用正向参与训练,把无交互误当中性,导致意图误读与低质自我强化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Positive-only bias trains only on positive engagement and mistakes no-interaction for neutral, causing intent misreading and low-quality self-reinforcement.

scenario: 商业目标是最大化广告收入,而观看时长是最直接的广告收入驱动。
scenario_en: The business goal is maximizing ad revenue, and watch time is the most direct driver of ad revenue.
q: 该把这个商业目标映射成哪个 ML 排序信号？
q_en: Which ML ranking signal should this business goal map to?
why: 映射成预测观看时长(predicted watch time)作排序信号:观看时长最直接驱动广告收入,让模型学着把预计看得更久的视频排上去。但要配护栏,否则会滑向标题党。
why_en: Map it to predicted watch time as the ranking signal: watch time most directly drives ad revenue, so the model learns to rank videos users will watch longer — but pair it with a guardrail or it slides toward clickbait.
tradeoff: 预测观看时长(直连广告收入但易诱导标题党) vs 纯点击(易被缩略图党刷,更浅)
options: 映射成预测点击率,不管用户看了多久
映射成预测观看时长作排序信号,另配护栏
映射成视频文件大小,文件越大越优先
映射成上传时间,越新的视频排越前面
options_en: Map it to predicted click-through rate, ignoring how long people watch.
Map it to predicted watch time as the ranking signal, with a guardrail.
Map it to video file size, ranking larger files higher.
Map it to upload time, ranking newer videos first.
whenOtherWins: 若目标其实是「让用户尽快找到想要的」(如客服短视频),预测点击/首屏满足度比观看时长更贴合,时长长反而可能是没找到。
whenOtherWins_en: If the goal is 'help users find what they want fast' (support clips), predicted click/first-screen satisfaction fits better than watch time, where long watch may mean they didn't find it.
optionExplanations: 纯点击只看点没点、看不到看多久,和「观看时长驱动广告收入」的目标不匹配。
对;预测观看时长最直连广告收入,是这个商业目标的标准 ML 映射,记得配护栏。
文件大小与用户是否爱看无关,不能当排序目标。
上传新旧是一个特征,不是要优化的商业目标。
optionExplanations_en: Pure clicks capture whether they clicked, not how long they watched, mismatching the watch-time-drives-revenue goal.
Correct — predicted watch time most directly connects to ad revenue, the standard ML mapping for this business goal, with a guardrail.
File size is unrelated to whether users enjoy it and cannot be a ranking target.
Upload recency is a feature, not the business objective to optimize.

termDefinitions.term: predicted watch time / 预测观看时长
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预估用户会看某视频多久,作为直连广告收入的排序信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Predicted watch time is the model's estimate of how long a user will watch a video, a ranking signal directly tied to ad revenue.

scenario: 商业目标是提升用户长期满意度(用 7 天回访、问卷、正负交互比来代理),你关心「最让人满意的视频有没有排在靠前」。
scenario_en: The goal is long-term user satisfaction (proxied by 7-day repeat visits, surveys, positive/negative interaction ratio), and you care whether the most satisfying videos rank near the top.
q: 该用哪个 ML 指标来衡量排序质量？
q_en: Which ML metric measures this ranking quality?
why: 用 NDCG:它对排序位置加权(越靠前贡献越大),正好衡量「最让人满意的视频是否排在前面」。满意度是慢变量,用 7 天回访等代理喂给 NDCG 评估排序好坏。
why_en: Use NDCG: it weights by rank position (higher positions count more), directly measuring whether the most satisfying videos sit near the top, with satisfaction proxied by 7-day repeat visits.
tradeoff: NDCG(位置加权、重排序顺序) vs Recall@K(只看有没有召回、不看顺序)
options: 用 Recall@K:只看相关视频有没有进候选集,不看排位
用准确率 accuracy:是否分类正确
用 NDCG:位置加权,衡量最满意的视频是否排在靠前
用 QPS:每秒查询数
options_en: Use Recall@K: only whether relevant videos entered the candidate set, ignoring rank.
Use accuracy: whether classification is correct.
Use NDCG: position-weighted, measuring whether the most satisfying videos rank near the top.
Use QPS: queries per second.
whenOtherWins: 若评估的是候选生成阶段(只关心相关视频有没有被召回、还没排序),那 Recall@K 比 NDCG 更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If evaluating candidate generation (only whether relevant videos were retrieved, not yet ranked), Recall@K fits better than NDCG.
optionExplanations: Recall@K 只管有没有召回,不管排在第几,答不了「满意视频是否靠前」。
accuracy 是分类指标,不衡量排序顺序质量。
对;NDCG 位置加权,正好评估最满意内容是否排前,匹配满意度目标。
QPS 是吞吐量指标,与排序质量无关。
optionExplanations_en: Recall@K only cares whether it was retrieved, not at what rank, so it cannot answer whether satisfying videos are near the top.
Accuracy is a classification metric and does not measure ranking-order quality.
Correct — NDCG is position-weighted and evaluates whether the most satisfying content ranks high, matching the satisfaction goal.
QPS is a throughput metric, unrelated to ranking quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益:按排位加权的排序质量指标,越靠前的相关项贡献越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a rank-weighted ranking-quality metric where relevant items nearer the top contribute more.

scenario: 商业目标是保护内容多样性——护住创作者生态、避免用户被困在信息茧房(filter bubble)。
scenario_en: The goal is protecting content diversity — safeguarding the creator ecosystem and avoiding filter bubbles.
q: 该用哪些 ML 指标来衡量多样性？
q_en: Which ML metrics measure diversity?
why: 用覆盖率(coverage:被推荐过的目录占比)衡量整体多样性,配列表内多样性(intra-list diversity:单次推荐列表内部够不够多元)。二者共同护住创作者生态与防茧房,常作为观看时长目标的护栏。
why_en: Use coverage (fraction of the catalog ever recommended) for overall diversity plus intra-list diversity (how varied a single recommendation list is), together guarding the creator ecosystem and against filter bubbles, often as a guardrail on watch time.
tradeoff: 覆盖率+列表内多样性(护生态、防茧房) vs 纯观看时长(集中头部、窄化)
options: 覆盖率(目录被推过的占比)+ 列表内多样性
只看观看时长,时长高就说明推荐够多元
用 p99 延迟衡量,响应越快多样性越好
用模型参数量衡量,参数越多推荐越多样
options_en: Coverage (share of the catalog ever recommended) plus intra-list diversity.
Just watch time — high watch time means the mix is diverse enough.
Use p99 latency: the faster the response, the more diverse the results.
Use model parameter count: more parameters, more diverse recommendations.
whenOtherWins: 若产品阶段目标是极致精准的窄推荐(如专业教程连播),暂时可弱化多样性护栏,但要监控长期茧房与创作者流失风险。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product phase targets ultra-precise narrow recommendations (a specialized tutorial series), you may relax the diversity guardrail temporarily but monitor long-term filter-bubble and creator-churn risk.
optionExplanations: 对;覆盖率+列表内多样性正是衡量多样性的两个互补维度,护生态又防茧房。
观看时长高常常来自集中推头部,反而与多样性对立,不能代表多样。
延迟是性能指标,与内容多样性毫无关系。
参数量是模型规模,与推荐多样性无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — coverage plus intra-list diversity are two complementary diversity dimensions, guarding the ecosystem and against bubbles.
High watch time often comes from concentrating on head content, opposing diversity, so it cannot represent it.
Latency is a performance metric with nothing to do with content diversity.
Parameter count is model size, unrelated to recommendation diversity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 目录中曾被推荐过的视频占比,衡量整体推荐多样性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage is the fraction of the catalog ever recommended, measuring overall recommendation diversity.

termDefinitions.term: intra-list diversity / 列表内多样性
termDefinitions.meaning: 单个推荐列表内部内容彼此差异程度,越同质越低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Intra-list diversity is how different the items within a single recommendation list are from each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐只喂相似内容,把用户困在越来越窄的兴趣圈里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A filter bubble is when recommendations feed only similar content, trapping the user in an ever-narrowing interest circle.

scenario: 在一个数十亿视频的系统里,你要评估候选生成阶段做得好不好——它负责把 billions 收窄成 hundreds 交给排序。
scenario_en: In a billions-of-videos system, evaluate how well candidate generation does — it narrows billions to hundreds for ranking.
q: 评估候选生成阶段，最合适的指标是什么？
q_en: What is the best metric to evaluate the candidate generation stage?
why: 用 Recall@K(前 K 个候选里覆盖了多少真正相关视频):候选生成的职责是检索完整性——一个没进候选集的视频永远没机会被排序。所以这一阶段看召回而非排序顺序。
why_en: Use Recall@K (how many truly relevant videos appear in the top-K candidates): candidate generation's job is retrieval completeness, since a video not in the candidate set can never be ranked, so measure recall not order.
tradeoff: Recall@K(候选阶段、看召回完整性) vs NDCG(排序阶段、看位置质量)
options: 用 p99 延迟,越快说明候选质量越好
用 NDCG,因为要重点比较候选之间谁排在前谁排在后
用点击率 CTR,点得多说明召回得准
用 Recall@K:候选生成看的是检索完整性
options_en: Use p99 latency — faster retrieval means better candidates.
Use NDCG, because what matters is comparing which candidates rank ahead of which others.
Use click-through rate; more clicks means retrieval was accurate.
Use Recall@K: candidate generation is judged on retrieval completeness.
whenOtherWins: 到了排序阶段,相关视频已在候选集里,这时要看它们排得对不对,该换成位置加权的 NDCG 而非 Recall@K。
whenOtherWins_en: At the ranking stage the relevant videos are already in the set, so you care whether they are ordered well and switch to position-weighted NDCG instead of Recall@K.
optionExplanations: 延迟是性能约束,不衡量候选集有没有把相关视频捞全。
NDCG 衡量排序顺序,但候选生成阶段还没排序,重点是召回而非顺序。
CTR 是参与度指标,评估不了候选检索的完整性。
对;候选生成的成败在于相关视频有没有被召回进集合,Recall@K 正是这个。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is a performance constraint and does not measure whether the set captured all relevant videos.
NDCG measures ranking order, but candidate generation is not yet ranking, so recall matters more than order.
CTR is an engagement metric and cannot evaluate retrieval completeness of candidates.
Correct — candidate generation succeeds or fails on whether relevant videos got retrieved into the set, which Recall@K captures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前 K 个候选里覆盖了多少真正相关的视频,衡量候选生成的检索完整性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K measures how many truly relevant videos are covered in the top-K candidates, gauging candidate-generation retrieval completeness.

scenario: 团队决定纯粹优化「预测观看时长」这一个目标,没有任何护栏指标。
scenario_en: The team decides to purely optimize the single objective 'predicted watch time' with no guardrail metric.
q: 只追单一观看时长目标、不设护栏，会导致什么？
q_en: What happens if you chase watch time alone with no guardrail?
why: 会滑向标题党/诱导内容,并形成自我强化的反馈回路:模型学到什么留住人就多推什么,logged 数据又强化它,最终训练-服务偏差让质量悄悄退化。所以要在主目标旁并置护栏指标(多样性/满意度)。
why_en: It slides toward clickbait and a self-reinforcing feedback loop: the model recommends whatever retains, logged data reinforces it, and training-serving skew silently degrades quality, so place a guardrail (diversity/satisfaction) beside the primary objective.
options: 毫无风险,单目标最干净、最好优化
滑向标题党并形成自我强化回路,质量悄悄退化
会顺带提升多样性,是单目标的意外好处
会降低广告收入,因为时长与收入并不相关
options_en: No risk; a single objective is the cleanest thing to optimize.
It slides toward clickbait and a self-reinforcing loop that quietly degrades quality.
It incidentally improves diversity, a bonus of the single objective.
It lowers ad revenue, since watch time and revenue are unrelated.
optionExplanations: 单目标看似干净实则危险:没有护栏就会被观看时长这一维度带偏,牺牲长期体验。
对;纯观看时长会诱导标题党并经反馈回路自我强化,护栏指标是必备的平衡。
纯观看时长通常降低多样性(集中头部),不会意外提升。
观看时长恰恰驱动广告收入,单优化短期反而抬收入、伤长期,不是降收入。
optionExplanations_en: A single objective looks clean but is dangerous: with no guardrail, the watch-time dimension skews it and sacrifices long-term experience.
Correct — pure watch time invites clickbait and self-reinforces via the loop, so a guardrail metric is the necessary balance.
Pure watch time usually lowers diversity (concentrating on head content), not accidentally raising it.
Watch time drives ad revenue, so optimizing it alone raises short-term revenue while harming the long term, not lowering revenue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠夸张标题/缩略图诱导点击但内容低质,纯观看时长优化易奖励它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clickbait uses sensational titles/thumbnails to lure clicks with low-quality content, which pure watch-time optimization tends to reward.

scenario: 面试官问你两阶段各用什么指标,想看你能否把「检索完整性」和「排序质量」分清。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks which metric fits each stage, checking whether you separate retrieval completeness from ranking quality.
q: Recall@K 和 NDCG 分别评估两阶段的什么，核心区别是什么？
q_en: What do Recall@K and NDCG each evaluate across the two stages, and what is the core difference?
why: Recall@K 评估候选生成的检索完整性——相关视频有没有被捞进候选集,不管排第几;NDCG 评估排序阶段的位置质量——相关视频排得够不够靠前。前者只问「有没有」,后者问「排得对不对」。
why_en: Recall@K evaluates candidate generation's retrieval completeness (did relevant videos enter the set, regardless of rank), while NDCG evaluates ranking's position quality (are relevant videos near the top) — presence versus ordering.
tradeoff: Recall@K(候选阶段、只问有没有召回) vs NDCG(排序阶段、问排得对不对)
options: 两者都评排序阶段,只是打分公式不一样
Recall@K 评召回完整性,NDCG 评排序位置质量
Recall@K 评排序阶段,NDCG 评候选生成阶段
两者都只能离线算,线上服务时用不了
options_en: Both evaluate the ranking stage, just with different scoring formulas.
Recall@K measures retrieval completeness; NDCG measures ranking position quality.
Recall@K measures the ranking stage and NDCG the candidate-generation stage.
Both are offline-only and cannot be computed during live serving.
optionExplanations: 两者对应不同阶段:一个候选生成一个排序,不是都评排序。
对;检索完整性 vs 位置质量,正好切开两阶段各自的成功判据。
说反了:Recall@K 对应候选生成,NDCG 对应排序。
两者离线在线都可评估,不存在只能离线的限制。
optionExplanations_en: They map to different stages — one to candidate generation, one to ranking — not both to ranking.
Correct — retrieval completeness vs position quality cleanly splits each stage's success criterion.
Backwards: Recall@K maps to candidate generation and NDCG to ranking.
Both can be evaluated offline and online; there is no offline-only restriction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相关物品有没有被候选生成捞进集合,是候选阶段的成功判据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retrieval completeness is whether relevant items got pulled into the set by candidate generation, the success criterion of that stage.

scenario: 系统规模:数十亿视频、数十亿账号、数亿 DAU;每个会话有几十次请求,每次端到端要在 sub-100ms 内返回。
scenario_en: Scale: billions of videos and accounts, hundreds of millions of DAU; each session has dozens of requests, each returning end-to-end within sub-100ms.
q: 「sub-100ms 端到端」这个数字在设计里该怎么用？
q_en: How should the 'sub-100ms end-to-end' number be used in design?
why: sub-100ms 是给定的产品级 SLO(非公式推出),它约束架构:预算拆给候选生成~10-20ms、排序~50-80ms、特征查询单位数 ms,来不及查的特征须预计算或丢弃。
why_en: Sub-100ms is a given product-level SLO (not derived), and it constrains the architecture: the budget splits across candidate generation ~10-20ms, ranking ~50-80ms, and feature lookups single-digit ms, and any feature too slow to fetch must be precomputed or dropped.
options: sub-100ms 是要死记硬背的数字,面试时能背下 100 这个数字就算过关
sub-100ms 说明不用分两阶段,单模型实时打分也够快
sub-100ms 是给定 SLO,约束候选生成/排序/特征查询各自的预算切分
sub-100ms 只是前端动画的体验指标,不牵涉后端架构
options_en: sub-100ms is a number to memorize by rote; reciting the value 100 in the interview is enough to pass.
sub-100ms means you don’t need two stages; a single real-time model is fast enough.
sub-100ms is a given SLO that splits the budget across candidate generation, ranking, and feature lookups.
sub-100ms is just a frontend animation metric and doesn’t touch backend architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务水平目标:给定的延迟/可用性目标,是约束而非公式结果,用来倒逼架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given latency/availability target — a constraint, not a formula result — used to drive architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数,衡量规模的基数,影响吞吐与容量估算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU (Daily Active Users) is the daily active user count, a scale base affecting throughput and capacity estimates.

optionExplanations: 误把它当死记的数字——它其实是要拆解给候选生成/排序/特征查询的架构预算。
推错了:再快的单模型也扫不完数十亿视频,两阶段仍是必须的。
对;这是给定 SLO,倒逼把预算拆到候选生成、排序、特征查询三段,而不是背数字本身。
低估了它:后端每一段处理时间都要卡进这个预算,不只是前端体验。
optionExplanations_en: Treating it as a number to memorize misses the point — it's an architecture budget split across candidate generation, ranking, and feature lookups.
Wrong inference: no single model can score billions fast enough, so two stages are still required.
Correct — it is a given SLO that forces the budget to split across candidate generation, ranking, and feature lookups, not a number to recite.
Underestimates it: every backend stage must fit inside this budget, not just frontend animation.

scenario: 候选生成阶段要在大约 10-20ms 内把数十亿视频收窄到数百个。
scenario_en: Candidate generation must narrow billions of videos to hundreds within roughly 10-20ms.
q: 这个「10-20ms 内 billions→hundreds」的预算逼出什么架构选择？
q_en: What architecture does the '10-20ms, billions to hundreds' budget force?
why: 10-20ms 内不可能给数十亿视频逐个打分,所以必须用近似最近邻(ANN)检索或预过滤:把视频预先编码成向量存进 ANN 索引,查询时用用户向量近邻检索,毫秒级返回数百候选。这就是为什么候选生成用双塔+ANN 而非逐个打分。
why_en: Scoring billions in 10-20ms is impossible, so you need ANN search or pre-filtered retrieval: precompute video vectors into an ANN index and query with the user vector for millisecond top-hundreds retrieval, which is why candidate generation uses two-tower plus ANN, not per-item scoring.
options: 逼出 ANN 检索:视频预编码成向量存进索引,查询近邻取候选
逼出用一个大 Transformer,对每个视频都实时算一遍分数
逼出把全部视频读进内存,一条条遍历打分
逼出关掉个性化功能,只给所有人推全站热门榜
options_en: Forces ANN retrieval: precompute video vectors into an index, query nearest neighbors for candidates.
Forces one big Transformer to compute a real-time score for every single video.
Forces loading every video into memory and scanning through them one by one.
Forces turning off personalization and just showing everyone the sitewide trending list.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量条件(向量近邻/规则)快速圈出小候选集,再交给下游,避免逐个打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-filtered retrieval quickly narrows to a small candidate set with light conditions (vector nearest-neighbor/rules) before downstream, avoiding per-item scoring.

optionExplanations: 对;这个预算逼出向量化+ANN检索这条路,不是把每条视频都实时算一遍。
算力扛不住:大 Transformer 逐条实时打分,10-20ms 内跑不完数十亿次推理。
内存和时间都不够:加载全部视频再线性遍历,远超这个预算量级。
矫枉过正:关个性化只是回避问题,候选生成仍需要机制在预算内检索。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this budget forces vectorization plus ANN search, not scoring every video in real time.
Compute can't keep up: a big Transformer scoring each video live can't finish billions of inferences in 10-20ms.
Neither memory nor time allows it: loading and linearly scanning every video blows past this budget by orders of magnitude.
Overcorrection: disabling personalization dodges the problem — candidate generation still needs a mechanism that retrieves within budget.

scenario: 排序模型想用某个特征,但从特征仓库查它要几十 ms,而整条链路的特征查询预算只有单位数 ms。
scenario_en: The ranking model wants a feature, but fetching it from the feature store takes tens of ms while the feature-lookup budget is single-digit ms.
q: 面对这个查询太慢的特征，该怎么办？
q_en: What do you do with this too-slow feature?
why: 特征仓库必须在单位数 ms 内供给用户画像/视频元数据;查询超预算的特征只有两条路:提前预计算好存成可快查的形式,或直接从实时模型里丢弃。绝不能让一个慢特征拖垮 sub-100ms 预算。
why_en: The feature store must serve profiles/metadata within single-digit ms, so a feature too slow to fetch has only two options: precompute it into a fast-lookup form, or drop it from the real-time model — never let one slow feature blow the sub-100ms budget.
tradeoff: 预计算(快查但可能不够新鲜) vs 丢弃(省延迟但损失该特征信息)
options: 把整条链路的延迟预算放宽到几十 ms 迁就它
预计算成可快查形式,或从实时模型里丢弃
请求时同步现算这个特征,慢一点也认了
给每个用户开后台线程慢慢算,算完再返回
options_en: Loosen the whole pipeline’s latency budget to tens of ms to accommodate it.
Precompute it into a fast-lookup form, or drop it from the online model.
Compute it synchronously at request time and accept the slowdown.
Spin up a per-user background thread and wait for it to finish.
whenOtherWins: 若该特征既慢又对精度至关重要,宁可投入把它预计算到近实时(如流式更新到 Redis),而非直接丢弃。
whenOtherWins_en: If the feature is both slow and crucial for accuracy, invest in precomputing it to near-real-time (streamed into Redis) rather than dropping it.
optionExplanations: 放宽端到端预算违背 sub-100ms 这个产品 SLO,一个慢特征不该绑架全局。
对;超预算特征只能预计算或丢弃,这是延迟约束下的标准取舍。
同步现算会直接击穿延迟预算,让整次请求超时。
后台慢算的结果赶不上本次请求,等于这次没有该特征,还平白增复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Loosening the end-to-end budget violates the sub-100ms product SLO; one slow feature should not hold the whole system hostage.
Correct — an over-budget feature can only be precomputed or dropped, the standard tradeoff under a latency constraint.
Computing synchronously blows the latency budget and times out the whole request.
Background slow computation misses this request, so the feature is effectively absent while adding complexity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线服务用户画像/物品元数据的低延迟存储,须在单位数 ms 内返回特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store is low-latency online storage for user profiles/item metadata that must return features within single-digit ms.

scenario: 推荐模型用「过去展示并被互动的日志」训练,而这些日志本身就是模型自己之前推荐的结果。
scenario_en: The recommender trains on logs of past impressions and interactions, but those logs are themselves the model's own prior recommendations.
q: 为什么训练-服务偏差是推荐系统的头号失败模式，后果链是什么？
q_en: Why is training-serving skew the dominant failure mode in recsys, and what is the chain?
why: 模型只在自己推荐过的内容上得到反馈→训练数据只覆盖它已经surfacing的东西→强化已推、看不到没推的→质量在无监控时悄悄退化。这就是推荐里训练-服务偏差的自我强化,必须靠监控+探索+负反馈打破。
why_en: The model only gets feedback on what it already recommended, so training data covers only what it surfaced, reinforcing prior recs and never seeing the unshown, and quality silently degrades without monitoring — the self-reinforcing skew broken by monitoring, exploration, and negative feedback.
options: 只在已推内容上拿到反馈→强化已推、看不见没推的
训练数据太多导致过拟合,采样减少数据就能解决
只是标签回流有延迟,与自我强化回路没有关系
是网络带宽不足导致的特征传输偏差
options_en: Feedback arrives only on what was already shown, so the model reinforces prior recs and never sees the unshown.
Too much training data causes overfitting; downsampling the data fixes it.
It is just delayed label backfill, unrelated to any self-reinforcing loop.
It is a feature-transfer skew caused by insufficient network bandwidth.
optionExplanations: 对;推荐日志是模型自造的,只覆盖已推内容,回路自我强化,是训练-服务偏差在 recsys 的典型形态。
过拟合是容量问题,这里是数据覆盖偏差(只见已推),减数据不解决。
标签延迟只是其中一面,本题核心是自我强化的覆盖偏差,不能简化为延迟。
带宽是网络指标,与训练数据的自我强化偏差无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — recommendation logs are self-made and cover only recommended content, so the loop self-reinforces, the classic form of training-serving skew in recsys.
Overfitting is a capacity issue; here it is data-coverage bias (only seeing recommended), which reducing data does not fix.
Label delay is only one facet; the core here is self-reinforcing coverage bias, not reducible to delay.
Bandwidth is a network metric, unrelated to self-reinforcing training-data bias.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏差
termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐里模型只在自己推过的内容上获得反馈,训练分布被自身历史决策扭曲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In recsys, training-serving skew is the model getting feedback only on what it recommended, so the training distribution is warped by its own past decisions.

scenario: 开场做问题框定,你要覆盖哪些类别的澄清问题,且每个都要能驱动一个下游决策。
scenario_en: Framing at the start, which categories of clarifying questions must you cover, each driving a downstream decision?
q: 视频推荐框定阶段应覆盖哪些澄清类别？(多选)
q_en: Which clarifying-question categories should the framing stage cover? (multiple)
why: 六类各驱动一个下游决策:产品形态(候选策略)、用户类型(CF vs 内容/冷启动)、内容规模(要不要 ANN)、优化目标(标签/损失/护栏)、约束(延迟→实时 vs 预计算)、负反馈(训练含不含负样本)。每问一句都要能落到设计上。
why_en: Six categories each drive a downstream decision: product surface (candidate strategy), user type (CF vs content/cold start), content scale (ANN or not), objective (label/loss/guardrail), constraints (latency to real-time vs precompute), and negative feedback (negatives in training).
options: 产品形态(首页 feed vs watch-next)
用户类型(登录 vs 匿名)与内容规模(目录多大)
优化目标、延迟约束、是否采集负反馈
面试官爱喝什么咖啡
options_en: Product surface (homepage feed vs watch-next).
User type (logged-in vs anonymous) and content scale (catalog size).
Objective, latency constraint, and whether to capture negative feedback.
What coffee the interviewer likes.
optionExplanations: 对;产品形态决定候选生成走宽主题还是上下文锚定。
对;用户类型定 CF vs 内容信号,内容规模定要不要 ANN,都是关键澄清。
对;目标定标签/损失/护栏,延迟定实时 vs 预计算,负反馈定训练含不含负样本。
错;这是闲聊,不驱动任何设计决策,不属于框定问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — product surface decides broad-topic vs context-anchored candidate generation.
Correct — user type sets CF vs content signals and content scale sets whether ANN is needed, both key clarifications.
Correct — objective sets label/loss/guardrail, latency sets real-time vs precompute, negatives set whether training includes them.
Wrong — that is chitchat driving no design decision and is not a framing question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开场用来确定目标/用户/规模/约束的提问,每个都应能驱动一个下游设计决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clarifying question pins down objective/user/scale/constraints up front, each meant to drive a downstream design decision.

q: 把一次视频推荐请求在两阶段架构里的处理顺序排好:
q_en: Order how one video-recommendation request flows through the two-stage architecture:
steps: 候选生成用 ANN 把数十亿视频收窄到数百个(~10-20ms)
排序模型给这数百个候选精细打分(~50-80ms)
按分数取 top 排布最终列表并挂护栏(多样性)
把最终数十条返回给用户展示
why: 顺序是漏斗逐级收窄:先 ANN 候选生成把 billions→hundreds(轻、快),再重排序精打分,然后按分数成列表并挂多样性护栏,最后返回数十条。每一阶段的延迟预算之和必须落在 sub-100ms 内。
why_en: The order is a narrowing funnel: ANN candidate generation cuts billions to hundreds (light, fast), heavy ranking scores them, then top-scored items form the list with a diversity guardrail, and finally dozens are returned — the stage budgets summing under sub-100ms.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  B["数十亿"] --> CG["候选生成 ANN"]
  CG --> H["数百"]
  H --> RK["排序精打分"]
  RK --> L["top+多样性护栏"]
  L --> U["数十条返回"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐的逐级收窄结构:每一层用更重的模型处理更少的候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A funnel is the recommendation's progressive narrowing: each layer uses a heavier model on fewer candidates.

scenario: 同一道视频推荐题,L4(中级)和 L5(资深)的区别不在于会更多算法,而在于覆盖广度。
scenario_en: On the same prompt, the L4 (mid) vs L5 (senior) difference is not more algorithms but breadth of coverage.
q: 把 L5 与 L4 拉开差距的，主要是什么？
q_en: What mainly separates L5 from L4 on this question?
why: L5 主动覆盖负反馈、冷启动、多样性等盲区,并给出主指标+护栏且能讲清取舍;L4 只答基础产品+规模、一个主指标。差距在广度与取舍意识,不是更花哨的模型。
why_en: L5 proactively covers blind spots (negative feedback, cold start, diversity) and gives a primary metric plus guardrail with tradeoff reasoning, while L4 answers basic product+scale with one primary metric — the gap is breadth and tradeoff awareness, not fancier models.
tradeoff: L5(主动覆盖盲区+护栏+取舍) vs L4(基础产品/规模+单一主指标)
options: L5 会用更冷门的深度模型架构,L4 只会经典模型
L5 主动覆盖负反馈/冷启动/多样性,并给护栏和取舍
L5 写的代码行数和伪代码比 L4 多得多
L5 用更大的 batch size 和更多 GPU 训练
options_en: L5 uses more obscure deep architectures while L4 sticks to classic models.
L5 proactively covers negative feedback, cold start and diversity, with guardrails and tradeoffs.
L5 writes far more lines of code and pseudocode than L4.
L5 trains with a larger batch size and more GPUs.
whenOtherWins: 若题目本身是纯算法深挖(如让你推导 loss),那对具体建模细节的掌握才是区分点;但框定题的分层几乎总看广度与取舍意识。
whenOtherWins_en: If the prompt is a pure algorithm deep-dive (derive the loss), mastery of modeling detail is the differentiator; but for framing questions leveling almost always tracks breadth and tradeoff awareness.
optionExplanations: 分层不看模型花不花哨,用冷门架构不加分,覆盖广度和取舍才是关键。
对;主动覆盖盲区+主指标配护栏+讲清取舍,正是 L5 相对 L4 的分水岭。
代码行数与分层无关,系统设计看的是决策质量不是产量。
batch size 是训练细节,不构成 L4/L5 的能力区分。
optionExplanations_en: Leveling is not about fancy models; obscure architectures earn no credit — coverage breadth and tradeoffs are what count.
Correct — proactively covering blind spots plus a primary metric with a guardrail and clear tradeoffs is exactly the L5-over-L4 divide.
Lines of code are unrelated to leveling; system design tracks decision quality, not output volume.
Batch size is a training detail and does not distinguish L4 from L5 ability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试按候选人覆盖的广度(盲区、取舍、跨系统)而非算法数量来定级别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Level scoping grades a candidate by breadth of coverage (blind spots, tradeoffs, cross-system) rather than number of algorithms.

scenario: Staff+ 级别的回答里,面试官更想听你怎么把「短期参与提升」和「长期留存」区分开,而不只是画一张完美架构图。
scenario_en: At Staff+ level, the interviewer wants how you'd distinguish short-term engagement gains from long-term retention, not just a perfect architecture diagram.
q: 对 Staff+,花两分钟讲清什么，往往比完美架构图更有价值？
q_en: For Staff+, spending two minutes on what often beats a perfect architecture diagram?
why: 讲清 A/B 测试框架如何区分短期参与提升 vs 长期留存:观看时长这类短期指标可能靠标题党刷上去却伤留存,所以要设计能捕捉长期效应的实验(长观察窗、留存/回访指标、holdback 组)。这体现你懂指标会互相打架。
why_en: Explain how the A/B framework distinguishes short-term engagement from long-term retention: watch-time-style short metrics can be gamed by clickbait while hurting retention, so design experiments that capture long-term effects (long windows, retention metrics, holdback groups).
tradeoff: 重 A/B 框架分辨短期 vs 长期(抓住指标冲突) vs 只画完美架构(漏了指标会打架)
options: 多堆几层深度模型,把网络结构图画得更细
讲清 A/B 框架怎么区分短期参与与长期留存
把每个组件的 QPS 都算到小数点后两位
列出用过的所有开源库和它们的版本号
options_en: Stack more model layers and draw the network diagram in finer detail.
Explain how the A/B framework separates short-term engagement from long-term retention.
Compute every component’s QPS down to two decimal places.
List every open-source library used along with its version number.
whenOtherWins: 若面试还停在基础架构没搭起来(L4 阶段),那先把两阶段架构讲对更重要;A/B 深挖是架构已清晰后的 Staff+ 加分项。
whenOtherWins_en: If the interview is still at basic architecture (L4 stage), getting the two-stage design right comes first; the A/B deep-dive is a Staff+ bonus once the architecture is clear.
optionExplanations: 堆模型结构图不体现对指标冲突的理解,Staff+ 更看系统级判断。
对;短期 vs 长期的 A/B 设计恰恰暴露指标会打架这一 Staff+ 洞见,常比架构图更值钱。
把 QPS 算到小数点后两位是伪精确,不解决短期长期冲突。
列库版本号与设计判断无关,答不到 Staff+ 想听的取舍。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking model diagrams does not show understanding of metric conflict; Staff+ values system-level judgment.
Correct — short-vs-long A/B design exposes the Staff+ insight that metrics conflict, often worth more than an architecture diagram.
Computing QPS to two decimals is false precision and does not resolve short-vs-long conflict.
Listing library versions is unrelated to design judgment and misses the Staff+ tradeoff they want to hear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分组对比不同版本效果;要分辨短期参与与长期留存需长窗口和留存指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users to compare versions; distinguishing short-term engagement from long-term retention needs long windows and retention metrics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长期不接受新版本的一小撮用户,用来测量长期(留存)效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A holdback group is a small set of users kept on the old version long-term to measure long-run (retention) effects.

scenario: 复习「商业目标 → ML 指标」的四条映射。
scenario_en: Review the four business-goal to ML-metric mappings.
q: 补全视频推荐的商业目标到 ML 指标映射：
q_en: Fill in the business-goal to ML-metric mappings for video recommendation:
text: 观看时长→预测{{观看时长}}信号;用户满意度→{{NDCG}}(最满意视频是否靠前);内容多样性→{{覆盖率}}+列表内多样性;候选生成阶段→{{Recall@K}}(相关视频有没有被召回)。
text_en: Watch time → predicted {{watch time}} signal; user satisfaction → {{NDCG}} (are the most satisfying videos near the top); content diversity → {{coverage}} + intra-list diversity; candidate generation → {{Recall@K}} (were relevant videos retrieved).
why: 四条映射把商业语言翻成可优化的 ML 指标:时长→预测时长、满意度→NDCG、多样性→覆盖率、候选完整性→Recall@K。记住每条并配一个护栏,是框定的核心产出。
why_en: The four mappings translate business language into optimizable ML metrics: watch time to predicted time, satisfaction to NDCG, diversity to coverage, candidate completeness to Recall@K.

termDefinitions.meaning: 位置加权的排序质量指标,衡量最相关/最满意项是否靠前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a position-weighted ranking-quality metric for whether the most relevant items rank high.

scenario: 只按观看时长排,系统越来越集中推少数头部创作者,长尾创作者拿不到曝光、用户看到的越来越同质。
scenario_en: Ranking purely by watch time concentrates recommendations on a few head creators, starving the long tail of exposure while users see ever more homogeneous content.
q: 为什么要把「多样性」设成护栏，它护住的是什么？
q_en: Why make diversity a guardrail, and what does it protect?
why: 多样性护栏护住创作者生态(长尾也能被曝光,平台供给才健康)和用户体验(防信息茧房)。纯观看时长会向头部集中、窄化推荐;用覆盖率+列表内多样性当护栏,能在追参与的同时不牺牲生态与新鲜感。
why_en: A diversity guardrail protects the creator ecosystem (long-tail creators get exposure so supply stays healthy) and user experience (against filter bubbles), because pure watch time concentrates on head content and narrows recs.
options: 多样性护栏没必要,集中推头部对平台最划算
多样性护住创作者生态(长尾曝光)和用户体验
多样性只影响存储和 CDN 成本,与生态无关
多样性护栏的作用是提高 GPU 利用率和吞吐
options_en: A diversity guardrail is unnecessary; concentrating on head content pays best.
Diversity protects the creator ecosystem (long-tail exposure) and user experience.
Diversity only affects storage and CDN cost, unrelated to the ecosystem.
A diversity guardrail exists to raise GPU utilization and throughput.
optionExplanations: 集中推头部会饿死长尾创作者、把用户困进茧房,长期损害平台供给与体验。
对;多样性护栏同时保生态(长尾曝光)和体验(防茧房),是观看时长目标的必要平衡。
多样性关乎曝光分布与生态健康,不是存储成本问题。
GPU 利用率与推荐多样性无关,属无关项。
optionExplanations_en: Concentrating on head content starves long-tail creators and traps users in bubbles, harming platform supply and experience long-term.
Correct — a diversity guardrail protects both the ecosystem (long-tail exposure) and experience (against bubbles), the necessary balance to a watch-time objective.
Diversity concerns exposure distribution and ecosystem health, not storage cost.
GPU utilization is unrelated to recommendation diversity, an irrelevant option.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平台上创作者的整体供给健康度;长尾也需曝光才能持续产出内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The creator ecosystem is the overall supply health of a platform's creators; the long tail also needs exposure to keep producing content.

scenario: YouTube 规模下,不到 1% 的用户会去点赞/踩,显式反馈既稀疏又偏向有强烈意见的人。
scenario_en: At YouTube scale, under 1% of users ever tap thumbs up/down, so explicit feedback is both sparse and biased toward strong opinions.
q: 为什么视频推荐主要靠隐式反馈而非显式反馈来学习？
q_en: Why does video recommendation learn mainly from implicit rather than explicit feedback?
why: 显式反馈(赞/踩)只有 <1% 用户给,稀疏且偏向强意见人群,覆盖不了大多数用户。所以要从用户「做了什么」(看多久、重看、跳过、分享)这些隐式信号学习——它们海量、覆盖全、更能代表真实偏好。
why_en: Explicit feedback (likes/dislikes) comes from under 1% of users, sparse and skewed to strong opinions, so you learn from what users do — watch time, replays, skips, shares — which are abundant, cover everyone, and better represent real preference.
options: 隐式反馈稀疏、显式反馈充足,所以主要靠用户主动点的赞踩来训练排序模型,完全不需要看这些海量的观看时长、跳过、分享等行为数据
显式反馈 <1% 用户给、稀疏且偏强意见;隐式信号(看/重看/跳/分享)海量覆盖全,更代表真实偏好
两者都不用,直接让人工逐条打标
只用显式反馈,忽略所有观看行为
options_en: Implicit feedback is sparse and explicit is abundant, so train ranking mainly on likes/dislikes, with no need to look at the huge volume of watch-time, skip, and share behavior data at all.
Explicit comes from under 1% of users, sparse and strong-opinion-biased; implicit signals (watch/replay/skip/share) are abundant, cover everyone, and better represent real preference.
Use neither; have humans hand-label every item.
Use only explicit feedback, ignoring all watch behavior.
optionExplanations: 说反了:显式(赞/踩)才稀疏,隐式(观看行为)才海量,主要靠隐式。
对;显式稀疏偏置、隐式海量代表真实,这是数据策略的出发点。
人工逐条打标在数十亿量级不可行,也无法实时。
只用显式会丢掉 99% 用户的行为信号,严重欠拟合真实偏好。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: explicit (likes/dislikes) is the sparse one and implicit (watch behavior) is abundant, so rely on implicit.
Correct — explicit is sparse and biased while implicit is abundant and representative, the starting point of the data strategy.
Hand-labeling every item is infeasible at billions scale and not real-time.
Explicit-only discards the behavior of 99% of users, badly underfitting real preference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户行为(观看时长、重看、跳过、分享)推断偏好,而非直接问用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Implicit feedback infers preference from user behavior (watch time, replays, skips, shares) rather than asking directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户主动给的评价(赞/踩/评分),稀疏且偏向有强意见者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Explicit feedback is ratings users actively give (like/dislike/score), sparse and biased toward strong opinions.

category: Video Recommendation Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 你要用几种隐式信号一起代理「用户满意度」,每种信号刻画的是不同侧面。
scenario_en: You proxy user satisfaction with several implicit signals, each capturing a different facet.
q: 哪些是常用的隐式满意度信号，各代理什么？(多选)
q_en: Which are common implicit satisfaction signals, and what does each proxy? (multiple)
why: 四个核心信号各刻画一面:观看时长=参与深度、重看(replay)=重温意愿(very strong)、跳过(skip)=不感兴趣、分享(share)=社交背书(最强)。多信号互补,单一信号都有噪声与偏差。
why_en: Four core signals each capture a facet: watch time is engagement depth, replays are rewatch intent (very strong), skips are disinterest, and shares are social endorsement (strongest) — complementary because any single one has noise and bias.
options: 观看时长——参与深度
重看(replay)——重温意愿;分享(share)——社交背书(最强)
跳过(skip)——不感兴趣
视频文件的编码码率——用户满意度
options_en: Watch time — engagement depth.
Replays — rewatch intent; shares — social endorsement (strongest).
Skips — disinterest.
The video's encoding bitrate — user satisfaction.
optionExplanations: 对;观看时长代理参与深度,是最基础的隐式信号。
对;重看=强重温意愿,分享=最强的社交背书信号。
对;跳过代理不感兴趣,是重要的负向隐式信号。
错;码率是画质参数,与用户是否满意无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — watch time proxies engagement depth, the most basic implicit signal.
Correct — replays are strong rewatch intent and shares are the strongest social-endorsement signal.
Correct — skips proxy disinterest, an important negative implicit signal.
Wrong — bitrate is a video-quality parameter, unrelated to user satisfaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户重复观看同一视频,代理很强的重温意愿,但信号稀疏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replay is rewatching the same video, proxying strong rewatch intent but a sparse signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户把视频转发给他人,是最强的社交背书满意度信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A share is forwarding a video to others, the strongest social-endorsement satisfaction signal.

category: Video Recommendation Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 直接用绝对观看时长当标签,模型偏爱长视频:看 2 小时电影的 10% 也有 12 分钟,远超看完一个 30 秒短片。
scenario_en: Using absolute watch time as the label makes the model favor long videos: 10% of a 2-hour movie is 12 minutes, far more than fully watching a 30-second clip.
q: 该怎么处理观看时长这个信号，为什么？
q_en: How should you treat the watch-time signal, and why?
why: 按视频时长归一化成完成率(completion rate):看完 30 秒的 95% 比只看 2 小时电影的 10% 更能说明满意。绝对时长偏向长视频、混入内容长度这个混杂因素,归一化才让不同长度的视频可比。
why_en: Normalize by video duration into a completion rate: watching 95% of a 30-second clip signals more satisfaction than 10% of a 2-hour movie, since absolute time favors long videos and confounds length, while completion rate makes different lengths comparable.
tradeoff: 完成率(消除长度混杂、可比) vs 绝对时长(偏向长视频、被内容长度污染)
options: 直接用绝对观看时长当标签,越长越好,这样模型会天然更偏爱两小时的电影而不是三十秒的短视频,哪怕短视频完播率更高
按时长归一化成完成率:95% 的 30 秒 > 10% 的 2 小时,消除长度混杂让不同长度可比
只看是否点开,不看看多久
把观看时长取对数后再乘以文件大小
options_en: Use absolute watch time directly as the label; the longer the better, naturally biasing the model toward two-hour movies over 30-second clips, even when the clip has a much higher completion rate.
Normalize by duration into a completion rate: 95% of a 30s clip > 10% of a 2h movie, removing the length confound to compare across durations.
Only whether it was opened, not how long.
Take the log of watch time and multiply by file size.
whenOtherWins: 若产品就是要奖励长时长沉浸(如长播客/直播),绝对时长本身就是目标,这时不必强行归一成完成率。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product intends to reward long immersion (long podcasts/livestreams), absolute time is itself the goal and you need not force it into a completion rate.
optionExplanations: 绝对时长偏向长视频,把内容长度这个混杂当成偏好,系统会一味推长视频。
对;完成率把不同长度拉到同一尺度,才能公平比较满意度。
只看是否点开丢掉了参与深度,连长度混杂问题都没解决。
乘文件大小引入无关变量,反而制造新的偏差,毫无依据。
optionExplanations_en: Absolute time favors long videos, mistaking the length confound for preference, so the system just pushes long videos.
Correct — completion rate puts different lengths on one scale for a fair satisfaction comparison.
Only whether opened drops engagement depth and does not even address the length confound.
Multiplying by file size introduces an irrelevant variable and creates new bias with no basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 观看时长占视频总时长的比例,归一化后不同长度视频可比。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Completion rate is watch time as a fraction of total video duration, normalizing so different-length videos are comparable.

category: Video Recommendation Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 用户把视频放着当背景音、人却去干别的,系统记录到很长的观看时长。
scenario_en: A user leaves a video playing as background audio while doing something else, and the system logs a long watch time.
q: 这暴露了隐式信号的什么问题，属于哪类错误？
q_en: What implicit-signal problem does this expose, and which error type?
why: 这是背景播放导致的假阳性(false positive):长观看时长其实不代表满意。隐式信号普遍有噪声且相互关联——另一例是「已看过的视频被跳过」是假阴性(false negative)。所以要多信号交叉、并对背景播放等模式去偏。
why_en: This is a background-play false positive: long watch time does not actually mean satisfaction, and implicit signals are generally noisy and correlated (an already-watched skip is a false negative), so cross-check multiple signals and de-bias patterns like background play.
options: 背景播放假阳性:长时长≠满意;隐式信号普遍有噪声,需多信号交叉+对背景播放去偏
说明观看时长是完美无偏信号,可单独使用
属于概念漂移,与信号噪声无关
是硬件录制错误,是播放器采集观看时长的 bug,只要重启推荐服务、清空缓存就能解决
options_en: Background-play false positive: long time is not satisfaction; implicit signals are noisy, needing multi-signal cross-checks and de-biasing.
It shows watch time is a perfectly unbiased signal usable alone.
It is concept drift, unrelated to signal noise.
A hardware recording error in how the player logs watch time, fixed by restarting the recommendation service and clearing the cache.
optionExplanations: 对;背景播放让长时长变成假阳性,正说明单一隐式信号有噪声,需交叉验证与去偏。
背景播放恰恰证明观看时长有偏,不能单独当满意度真值。
这是信号噪声/假阳性,不是输入到标签映射变化的概念漂移。
记录本身没错,错在把背景播放的长时长误读为满意,不是硬件问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — background play turns long time into a false positive, showing a single implicit signal is noisy and needs cross-checks and de-biasing.
Background play is exactly why watch time is biased and cannot be used alone as satisfaction ground truth.
This is signal noise / a false positive, not concept drift (a changed input-to-label mapping).
The recording is correct; the error is misreading long background-play time as satisfaction, not a hardware fault.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把非满意行为(背景播放的长时长)误当成满意信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is mistaking a non-satisfaction behavior (long background-play time) for a satisfaction signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把非不满行为(跳过已看过的视频)误当成负信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative is mistaking a non-dislike behavior (skipping an already-watched video) for a negative signal.

category: Video Recommendation Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 两个跳过:一个是视频刚开头几秒就被跳,一个是看了大半才放弃。
scenario_en: Two skips: one in the first few seconds, one after watching most of it.
q: 早跳和晚弃的负向信号强度一样吗，为什么？
q_en: Do early skip and late abandonment carry the same negative weight, and why?
why: 不一样:开头几秒就跳,负向信号更强——用户几乎没给内容机会,基本是明确不感兴趣;看了大半才弃,负向弱得多——已经获得不少价值。建模时应给早跳更大的负权重。
why_en: No: an early skip in the first few seconds carries a stronger negative signal (the user barely gave it a chance, near-clear disinterest), while late abandonment is much weaker since they already got value, so weight early skips more negatively.
options: 一样,只要是跳过就同等负向,不管用户是刚看了 3 秒还是已经看了 10 分钟才放弃
不一样:早跳负向更强(几乎没给机会),晚弃负向弱(已获价值);早跳应给更大负权重
晚弃负向更强,因为看得久说明更失望
跳过一律是正信号,代表快速找到下一个
options_en: Same; any skip is equally negative, whether the user bailed after 3 seconds or already watched 10 minutes before giving up.
Different: early skip is stronger negative (barely gave it a chance), late abandonment weaker (already got value); weight early skips more negatively.
Late abandonment is stronger because watching long means more disappointment.
Skips are always positive, meaning quickly finding the next one.
optionExplanations: 把早跳和晚弃同等对待,抹掉了「给没给内容机会」这个关键差异。
对;早跳几乎没给机会是强负向,晚弃已获价值是弱负向,权重应有别。
看得久通常说明获得了价值,晚弃负向反而更弱,说反了。
跳过是负信号不是正信号,把它当正向会误导训练。
optionExplanations_en: Treating early skip and late abandonment equally erases the key difference of whether the content got a chance.
Correct — an early skip barely gave it a chance (strong negative) while late abandonment already got value (weak negative), so weights should differ.
Watching long usually means value was gained, so late abandonment is a weaker negative — backwards.
A skip is a negative signal, not positive, and treating it as positive misleads training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户放弃当前视频转下一个;早跳负向强、晚弃负向弱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skip is abandoning the current video for the next; early skips are strongly negative, late abandonment weakly so.

category: Video Recommendation Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 有了观看时长、重看、跳过、分享四个信号,你要把它们合成模型能优化的训练标签。
scenario_en: With watch time, replays, skips, and shares in hand, you must combine them into a trainable label.
q: 把多个隐式信号合成标签，「加权求和」与「多任务学习」的核心区别是什么？
q_en: Combining multiple implicit signals, what is the core difference between a weighted sum and multi-task learning?
why: 加权求和把多信号压成一个标量标签,简单但要手调权重、且抹掉了各信号语义;多任务学习给每个信号一个预测头、共享底座 backbone,保留各信号语义又共享表征。YouTube/TikTok 标准是多任务。
why_en: A weighted sum compresses signals into one scalar label — simple but needs hand-tuned weights and erases each signal's semantics — while multi-task learning gives each signal its own head over a shared backbone, keeping semantics while sharing representations; YouTube/TikTok default to multi-task.
tradeoff: 加权求和(单标量、简单但抹语义/需调权重) vs 多任务(多头共享底座、保语义但更复杂)

rows: 更复杂, 需平衡各头

options: 两者等价,只是命名不同,工程上换个名字调用同一套加权公式就行,模型结构、训练流程、预测头数量完全不用改
加权求和=多信号压成单标量(简单但抹语义/需调权重);多任务=每信号一头共享 backbone(保语义)
加权求和需要多个预测头,多任务只输出一个标量
多任务学习不能共享参数,每个信号完全独立训练
options_en: They are equivalent, just named differently — swapping the name still calls the same weighted formula, with no change needed to model architecture, training pipeline, or head count.
Weighted sum compresses signals into one scalar (simple but erases semantics/needs tuning); multi-task gives each signal a head over a shared backbone (keeps semantics).
Weighted sum needs multiple heads; multi-task outputs a single scalar.
Multi-task learning cannot share parameters; each signal trains fully independently.
optionExplanations: 两者机制不同:一个压标量一个多头,输出和可维护性都不一样,不等价。
对;单标量 vs 多头共享底座是二者的本质区别,后者保留信号语义。
说反了:加权求和才是单标量,多任务才用多个头。
多任务的核心正是共享 backbone,不是完全独立训练。
optionExplanations_en: The mechanisms differ: one compresses to a scalar, one uses multiple heads, with different outputs and maintainability — not equivalent.
Correct — single scalar vs multi-head over a shared backbone is the essential difference, the latter preserving signal semantics.
Backwards: the weighted sum is the single scalar and multi-task uses multiple heads.
Multi-task's essence is a shared backbone, not fully independent training.

termDefinitions.term: weighted sum label / 加权求和标签
termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个信号按权重加成一个标量标签,简单但需人工调权重、丢失各信号语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weighted-sum label combines signals by weights into one scalar, simple but needing hand-tuned weights and losing per-signal semantics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 共享一个底座 backbone、为每个信号设独立预测头,保留各信号语义又共享表征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-task learning shares one backbone with a separate head per signal, keeping each signal's semantics while sharing representations.

category: Video Recommendation Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 你想让模型同时兼顾观看时长、跳过、分享等信号,又不想手调一个脆弱的加权系数,还要在各信号间共享学到的表征。
scenario_en: You want the model to honor watch time, skips, shares at once without hand-tuning a brittle weight, while sharing learned representations across signals.
q: YouTube/TikTok 规模下的标准做法是什么，好处是什么？
q_en: What is the standard approach at YouTube/TikTok scale, and its benefit?
why: 标准是多任务学习:一个共享 backbone 学通用表征,每个信号挂一个预测头,既尊重每个信号的语义、又让它们共享底层特征。比加权求和更稳,不用手调一个把所有信号糊在一起的权重。
why_en: The standard is multi-task learning: a shared backbone learns general representations with one head per signal, respecting each signal's semantics while sharing lower-level features — more robust than a weighted sum and free of hand-tuning one blended weight.
tradeoff: 多任务(共享表征+保语义,YouTube/TikTok 标准) vs 加权求和(单标量,需手调、抹语义)
options: 只训一个观看时长的单一模型,其他信号丢掉
多任务学习:共享 backbone+每信号一头,保各信号语义又共享表征,免手调加权
给每个信号各训一个完全独立的模型,serving 时投票
把所有信号硬编码成 if-else 规则,比如观看时长大于 5 分钟就判定为满意,分享过就加分
options_en: Train a single watch-time model and drop the other signals.
Multi-task learning: shared backbone plus one head per signal, keeping semantics while sharing representations and avoiding hand-tuned weights.
Train a fully independent model per signal and vote at serving.
Hard-code all signals into if-else rules, e.g. mark satisfied whenever watch time exceeds 5 minutes or the video was shared.
whenOtherWins: 若信号很少、语义高度一致,一个精调的加权求和单标量更简单够用,不必上多任务的复杂度。
