options_en: Fix the model architecture and objective function first, then back out which features are needed.
First map raw data sources to business objectives, then derive features accordingly.
List as many feature names as possible first — the more you list, the smarter it looks.
Settle on the feature store and database choice first, then come back to discuss the features themselves.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官已明确锁定单一目标和数据源(例如「只用互动历史优化参与度」),可跳过全量映射,直接深入该源的特征。
optionExplanations: 先定架构和目标函数再倒推特征本末倒置,数据战略应先于架构。
对;源→目标映射是数据战略的核心动作,让每个特征都有归属和理由。
光罗列名称越多越显得没重点,反而暴露缺少战略。
先定存储选型是实现细节,不是数据战略;战略先于存储选型。
optionExplanations_en: Fixing architecture and objective function then backing out features is backwards; data strategy precedes architecture.
Correct — source-to-objective mapping is the core data-strategy move, giving each feature a home and a reason.
Listing more names shows less focus and exposes a lack of strategy.
Settling storage choice first is an implementation detail; strategy precedes storage choice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在列特征前,先把数据源映射到业务目标,让特征选择有依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data strategy maps data sources to business objectives before listing features, giving feature choices a rationale.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 社交图谱特征可以在不同粒度上抽取。
scenario_en: Social-graph features can be extracted at different granularities.
q: 社交图谱特征通常在哪些粒度上抽取?(多选)
q_en: At which granularities are social-graph features typically extracted? (multiple)
why: 三种粒度:节点(度数、关注/被关注比)、边(共同好友、连接时长)、邻域(共同社区、聚类系数)。它们从「这个人多活跃」「这两人多熟」到「他们所在社区多紧密」层层刻画关系。
why_en: Three granularities: node (degree, follower/following ratio), edge (mutual friends, time since connection), and neighborhood (shared community, clustering coefficient).
options: 节点级:度数、关注/被关注比
边级:共同好友数、连接建立时长
邻域级:共同社区、聚类系数
像素级:图片每个像素的 RGB 值
options_en: Node level: degree, follower/following ratio.
Edge level: mutual friends, time since connection.
Neighborhood level: shared community, clustering coefficient.
Pixel level: RGB values of each image pixel.
optionExplanations: 对;节点级刻画单个用户的图谱地位(多活跃、多受关注)。
对;边级刻画两个用户之间关系的强弱与历史。
对;邻域级刻画用户所在局部社区的结构紧密度。
错;像素 RGB 是图像内容特征,不属于社交图谱粒度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — node level captures a single user's graph standing (how active, how followed).
Correct — edge level captures the strength and history of a relationship between two users.
Correct — neighborhood level captures the structural tightness of a user's local community.
Wrong — pixel RGB is an image-content feature, not a social-graph granularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量一个节点的邻居之间彼此也相连的紧密程度,反映社区结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The clustering coefficient measures how tightly a node's neighbors are also connected to each other, reflecting community structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被关注数除以关注数,是节点级的图谱地位特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The follower/following ratio is followers divided by following, a node-level graph-standing feature.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 两个用户之间只有「是否好友」这个二元边太粗,想刻画关系强弱。
scenario_en: The binary 'are they friends' edge between two users is too coarse; you want relationship strength.
q: 互动历史怎么把二元的社交边变成连续的关系强度信号?
q_en: How does interaction history turn a binary social edge into a continuous relationship-strength signal?
why: 把每对「浏览者-发帖者」的点赞/评论/转发/私信/主页访问/故事浏览在 1d/7d/28d 滑动窗口上聚合。二元边(是否好友)因此变成随时间演化的连续强度,还能识别衰减中的关系(仍连着但不再互动→降权)。
why_en: Aggregate each viewer-poster pair's likes/comments/reshares/DMs/profile visits over 1d/7d/28d sliding windows, turning a binary edge into a time-evolving continuous strength and exposing decaying relationships.
options: 按 1d/7d/28d 窗口聚合互动,二元边变成随时间演化的连续强度
只记录两人之间是否曾经互动过这一件事,完全不看互动频率、时间衰减与近因
把点赞、评论、转发等所有互动类型合并成一个总数,不区分时间窗口
只保留最近一次互动的时间戳当作强度,不做任何滑动窗口聚合
options_en: Aggregate interactions over 1d/7d/28d sliding windows, turning the binary edge into a time-evolving continuous strength.
Record only whether the pair ever interacted at all, ignoring frequency, time decay, and recency entirely.
Merge likes, comments, reshares, and every interaction type into one total, with no time windows.
Keep only the timestamp of the last interaction as the strength, with no sliding-window aggregation at all.
optionExplanations: 对;多窗口滑动聚合是把关系从「有无」升级成「多强、趋势如何」的关键。
只记有无又退回二元,丢掉了频率和近因,刻画不了强度。
合并成一个总数丢了时间维度,看不出关系在增强还是衰减。
只用最近时间戳丢了频率,单点信息不足以刻画关系强度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — multi-window sliding aggregation upgrades a relationship from 'exists' to 'how strong, trending which way'.
Recording only existence reverts to binary, dropping frequency and recency, so it can't capture strength.
Merging into one total loses the time dimension, hiding whether the relationship is strengthening or decaying.
Using only the last timestamp loses frequency; a single point is insufficient for relationship strength.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间跨度(1d/7d/28d)上聚合事件,随时间滚动更新的统计口径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sliding window aggregates events over a fixed span (1d/7d/28d), rolling forward as time advances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由多窗口互动聚合得到的连续信号,替代二元好友边刻画亲疏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relationship strength is a continuous signal from multi-window interaction aggregation, replacing the binary friend edge.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 一次评论和一次被动点赞、一条私信和一次转发,携带的关系信息量并不相同。
scenario_en: A comment vs a passive like, a DM vs a reshare—each carries different relationship information.
q: 构造互动特征时,不同互动类型该怎么处理?
q_en: How should different interaction types be handled when building interaction features?
why: 不能一视同仁:评论比被动点赞更强,私信比转发更亲密。应给不同互动类型显式加权,让模型知道深度互动携带更强的关系信号(这正是 FB MSI 看重评论串深度的思路)。
why_en: Don't weight them equally: a comment outweighs a passive like and a DM implies more intimacy than a reshare, so weight interaction types explicitly, as Facebook's MSI favored comment-thread depth.
tradeoff: 按互动深度显式加权(信号更准) vs 所有互动等权(简单但糊平强弱)
options: 所有互动类型一律等权求和,评论和点赞算作同样强的信号
只统计点赞数,完全忽略评论和私信,因为点赞数据量最大
给互动类型随机分配权重,靠随机性增加特征多样性
按互动深度显式加权:评论>被动点赞、私信>转发
options_en: Sum all interaction types with equal weight — treat a comment and a like as the same strength of signal.
Count only the number of likes and fully ignore comments and DMs, since likes have the most volume.
Assign random weights to interaction types, relying on randomness to add feature variety.
Weight by interaction depth explicitly: comment > passive like, DM > reshare.
whenOtherWins: 若某产品的互动类型极单一(几乎只有点赞)或数据太稀疏撑不起分类型权重,等权聚合起步更稳,等信号够了再细分。
optionExplanations: 等权把强弱信号糊平,评论和点赞被当一回事,损失关系区分度。
只看点赞丢掉了最强的深度互动信号(评论/私信),明显欠采。
随机权重不可解释也不可优化,不是加权而是加噪。
对;按深度加权让深互动携带更强关系信号,是 MSI 式的正确做法。
optionExplanations_en: Equal weight smears strength signals, treating comments and likes alike and losing relationship discrimination.
Counting only likes drops the strongest deep-interaction signals (comments/DMs), clearly under-sampling.
Random weights are neither interpretable nor optimizable—adding noise, not weighting.
Correct — weighting by depth makes deep interactions carry stronger relationship signal, the MSI-style approach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按互动深度(评论>点赞、私信>转发)给不同类型赋不同权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interaction weighting assigns different weights by depth—comment > like, DM > reshare.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 提出的排序目标,强调评论串深度等深度互动信号,而非被动点赞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSI (Meaningful Social Interactions) is Facebook's ranking objective favoring deep-interaction signals like comment-thread depth over passive likes.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 要为数十亿条社交边各维护多窗口互动计数器。
scenario_en: You must maintain multi-window interaction counters for billions of social edges.
q: 给数十亿条边存互动计数器,会带来什么工程约束?
q_en: What engineering constraint arises from storing interaction counters for billions of edges?
why: 边数是数十亿量级,若每条边都长期保留全量事件,存储会爆。必须做聚合(只存窗口统计而非原始事件)+ TTL 过期(旧计数自动清理),把存储控制在可持续范围。
why_en: Billions of edges make storing raw events per edge explode, so you must aggregate (keep window stats, not raw events) and let old counters lapse via TTL to keep storage sustainable.
options: 边虽然数十亿条,但都能塞进内存,直接全量存原始事件也不会有问题
只能为最近一条边保留计数器,其余边的历史事件全部丢弃
数十亿边直接存储会爆,需聚合窗口统计 + TTL 清理旧计数
计数器必须做到强一致,哪怕多花延迟和成本也不能接受最终一致
options_en: Billions of edges still all fit in memory, so storing every raw event in full poses no problem.
Only the most recent edge can keep a counter; every other edge's history is discarded entirely.
Billions of edges would explode storage, so aggregate window stats plus TTL-based cleanup of old counters.
Counters must be strongly consistent, even at the cost of extra latency and spend — eventual consistency is unacceptable.
optionExplanations: 数十亿边远超内存容量,全量存原始事件正是会爆的做法,必须优化。
只存一条边是荒谬项,系统要为所有活跃边维护计数。
对;聚合+TTL 是把海量边计数控制在可持续存储的标准手段。
互动计数容忍最终一致(见后续卡),强一致是过度要求,反而拖慢。
optionExplanations_en: Billions of edges far exceed memory capacity; storing raw events for all of them is exactly what explodes and must be optimized.
Storing only one edge is absurd; the system must maintain counters for all active edges.
Correct — aggregation plus TTL is the standard way to keep massive edge counters within sustainable storage.
Interaction counts tolerate eventual consistency (see later card); strong consistency is over-engineering that slows things down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储项设过期时间,到点自动清理,控制海量计数器的存储增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) sets an expiry on stored items so old counters auto-purge, bounding storage growth.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 特征管线只用每 24 小时跑一次的批处理,一条帖子在创建 10 分钟后突然爆火。
scenario_en: The feature pipeline is batch-only, refreshing every 24h; a post goes viral 10 minutes after creation.
q: 只用日级批处理特征,这条刚爆火的帖会遇到什么失败模式?
q_en: With batch-only daily features, what failure mode hits this just-viral post?
why: 帖子的互动计数特征还停留在上次批处理跑出来的~0(创建才 10 分钟,没进批),模型据此系统性地把这条正在爆发的帖低排——恰好错过它最关键的分发窗口。所以快变信号必须走近实时流式。
why_en: Its engagement-count feature still reflects the last batch run's ~0 (only 10 min old, missed the batch), so the model systematically under-ranks the trending post during its critical distribution window.
options: 模型会正确识别爆火,因为批处理足够快
模型据~0 的旧计数把它系统性低排,错过关键分发窗口
帖子会被重复推给所有人,因为计数太高
陈旧计数只会拖慢存储层读写,不会波及排序结果的高低
options_en: The model correctly spots the viral post because batch is fast enough.
Using the stale ~0 count, the model systematically under-ranks it, missing the critical distribution window.
The post gets pushed to everyone repeatedly because the count is too high.
A stale count only slows storage reads/writes; it never spills over into ranking results.
optionExplanations: 24 小时批处理根本追不上 10 分钟的爆发,不可能及时识别。
对;旧计数~0 让模型低估这条帖,正好在它最该被分发时压住它。
计数还停在~0 不是过高,不会被重复狂推,方向反了。
特征陈旧直接决定排序低估,不只是存储问题。
optionExplanations_en: A 24h batch cannot keep up with a 10-minute burst and cannot spot it in time.
Correct — the stale ~0 count makes the model underestimate the post, suppressing it exactly when it should be distributed.
The count is still ~0, not too high, so it won't be over-pushed—the opposite direction.
Stale features directly cause ranking underestimation, not just a storage issue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条帖子刚发布、最有传播潜力的短暂时段,错过就难再起量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The distribution window is the brief early period when a post has the most spread potential; missing it caps its reach.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 特征有的慢变(图谱拓扑、用户画像),有的快变(点赞数、评论速度、转发爆发),要用一套管线覆盖。
scenario_en: Some features change slowly (graph topology, user profiles), some fast (like counts, comment velocity, reshare bursts); one pipeline must cover both.
q: 怎么设计特征管线同时覆盖慢变和快变特征?
q_en: How do you design a feature pipeline covering both slow and fast features?
why: 双管线:批处理(Spark + Airflow,日级)算慢变特征(图谱拓扑、用户聚合);流式(Flink + Kafka,实时)算快变特征(点赞数、评论速度、转发爆发)。用哪条按特征的变化速度分,不是一刀切。
why_en: A dual pipeline: batch (Spark + Airflow, daily) for slow features (graph topology, user aggregates) and streaming (Flink + Kafka, real-time) for fast features (like counts, comment velocity, reshare bursts).
tradeoff: 双管线按变化速度分工(各取所长) vs 全批处理(简单但快变滞后)/全流式(实时但慢变浪费)
options: 全部用批处理日级跑,连快变的点赞、评论、转发计数也只能跟着每天才更新一次
全部用流式实时跑,连慢变的图谱拓扑和用户画像特征也跟着每秒重算一遍
把所有原始特征不分快慢一股脑塞给模型,寄望模型自己慢慢学会区分时效,完全不做批流管线拆分
双管线:批处理(Spark+Airflow)算慢变,流式(Flink+Kafka)算快变
options_en: Run everything in daily batch, so even fast-changing like, comment, and reshare counts only update once a day.
Run everything in streaming, recomputing even slow-changing graph topology and user-profile features every second.
Dump every raw feature into the model regardless of speed and hope it slowly learns timeliness on its own, with no batch/streaming split at all.
Dual pipeline: batch (Spark+Airflow) for slow features, streaming (Flink+Kafka) for fast ones.
whenOtherWins: 若产品所有关键特征都慢变(如纯静态画像推荐),纯批处理就够,不必上流式的运维复杂度。
optionExplanations: 全批处理让快变计数滞后一天,爆火帖会被低排,不满足新鲜度。
全流式对慢变的图谱拓扑每秒重算是巨大浪费,拓扑一天变不了多少。
让模型自学时效解决不了特征本身陈旧的问题,数据进来就已经旧了。
对;按变化速度分工,慢的走批省成本,快的走流保新鲜,是标准双管线。
optionExplanations_en: All-batch lags fast counts by a day, under-ranking viral posts and failing freshness.
All-streaming recomputing slow graph topology every second is huge waste; topology barely changes in a day.
Letting the model self-learn timeliness cannot fix stale input; the data is already old when it arrives.
Correct — splitting by change speed (slow via batch to save cost, fast via streaming to stay fresh) is the standard dual pipeline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Spark+Airflow 定期(日级)批量算慢变特征,吞吐高但时效低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batch pipeline uses Spark+Airflow to periodically (daily) compute slow features in bulk—high throughput, low freshness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Flink+Kafka 实时算快变特征(点赞数、评论速度),低延迟但运维重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming pipeline uses Flink+Kafka to compute fast features (like counts, comment velocity) in real time—low latency, heavier ops.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 批处理和流式两条管线算出的特征,推理时要统一取用。
scenario_en: Features computed by the batch and streaming pipelines must be served uniformly at inference.
q: feature store 怎么统一批处理和流式两路特征?
q_en: How does a feature store unify batch and streaming features?
why: feature store 做统一层:批处理写离线存储再同步到在线存储;流式直接写在线存储并带 TTL 过期。推理时排序服务从在线存储(Redis/DynamoDB)读流式计数 + 批处理特征,一次取齐。
why_en: The feature store unifies both: batch writes to an offline store synced to the online store, streaming writes directly to the online store with TTL, and at inference the ranker reads streaming counters plus batch features from the online store (Redis/DynamoDB).
options: 批处理写离线存储同步在线;流式直接写在线带 TTL;推理一次读齐
两路特征分别存进两套不同的系统,推理时要分别发请求查询再自己手动拼接
只保留流式特征,丢弃批处理算出的慢变图谱和用户画像特征以简化系统
只保留批处理特征进排序,流式算出的实时互动计数仅用于后台监控看板
options_en: Batch writes an offline store synced online; streaming writes online directly with TTL; inference reads both in one shot.
Each pipeline stores into a separate system; at inference you query both separately and stitch the results together yourself.
Keep only streaming features, dropping the slow-changing graph and user-profile features batch computes, to simplify the system.
Keep only batch features in ranking; the real-time counts streaming computes are used only for a monitoring dashboard.
optionExplanations: 对;特征存储的价值就是统一读口,推理一次从在线存储取齐两路特征。
各存各的、推理时自己拼,正是特征存储要消除的碎片化。
丢批处理特征就失去慢变的图谱/画像信号,削足适履。
丢流式特征就回到批处理滞后问题,爆火帖被低排。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the feature store's value is a unified read path, fetching both feature sets from the online store in one inference call.
Storing separately and stitching at inference is exactly the fragmentation the feature store removes.
Dropping batch features loses slow graph/profile signals, cutting the foot to fit the shoe.
Dropping streaming features returns to batch lag, under-ranking viral posts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一管理离线/在线特征的系统,推理时提供低延迟点查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store manages offline/online features uniformly and serves low-latency point lookups at inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低延迟键值存储(Redis/DynamoDB),供推理实时读取特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The online store is a low-latency key-value store (Redis/DynamoDB) that serves features to inference in real time.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 互动计数只要大致新鲜就行,但拉黑名单(block list)绝不能让被拉黑内容漏出来。
scenario_en: Engagement counts only need to be roughly fresh, but a block list must never let blocked content slip through.
q: 哪些特征容忍最终一致,哪些必须强一致?
q_en: Which features tolerate eventual consistency, and which require strong consistency?
why: 互动计数容忍最终一致(晚个 10 秒无所谓,排序不会因此崩);但隐私敏感的拉黑/限制名单必须强一致——被拉黑的内容一旦漏出就是隐私事故。按「错了有多严重」区分一致性等级。
why_en: Engagement counters tolerate eventual consistency (10s stale is fine), but privacy-sensitive block/restricted lists must be strongly consistent, since blocked content leaking is a privacy incident.
tradeoff: 计数最终一致(省成本·可容忍旧) vs 拉黑名单强一致(必须·漏出即事故)
options: 所有特征包括互动计数和拉黑名单在内都统一做强一致,宁可拖慢延迟也不能有一丝错误
所有特征都统一用最终一致,连拉黑名单的生效延迟也完全可以容忍
计数容忍最终一致(10s 旧无妨);拉黑名单必须强一致(漏出即隐私事故)
一致性等级按特征类型随机分配,靠随机化均摊整个系统的读写压力
options_en: Make every feature, including engagement counts and block lists, strongly consistent — better to add latency than to ever be wrong.
Make every feature eventually consistent, including tolerating delay in when block lists take effect.
Counters tolerate eventual consistency (10s stale is fine); block lists must be strongly consistent (a leak is a privacy incident).
Assign consistency levels randomly by feature type, using randomness to spread the whole system's read/write load.
optionExplanations: 对计数强一致是过度设计,徒增延迟和成本,计数晚一点不影响排序质量。
对拉黑名单最终一致是危险的:延迟窗口里被拉黑内容会漏出,是隐私事故。
对;按错误后果分级——计数错一点无所谓,拉黑漏出不可接受,所以强一致。
随机分配一致性无视语义,既可能过度也可能失守,毫无依据。
optionExplanations_en: Strong consistency for counters is over-engineering that adds latency and cost; a slightly stale count doesn't hurt ranking.
Eventual consistency for block lists is dangerous: during the delay blocked content leaks, a privacy incident.
Correct — grade by consequence: a slightly wrong count is fine, but a block-list leak is unacceptable, so strong consistency.
Random consistency ignores semantics, risking both over-engineering and failure—baseless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短暂不一致、最终收敛,适合容忍轻微滞后的互动计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency permits brief inconsistency that converges later, fitting engagement counts that tolerate slight lag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写后立即对所有读可见,拉黑名单等安全关键特征需要它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency makes a write immediately visible to all reads, required for safety-critical features like block lists.

whenOtherWins: 若某类看似普通的特征一旦出错会牵连合规或金钱损失(不只是隐私),就该按更高一致性对待,不能只按「隐私漏出」一条线分级。
category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 社交 feed 排序:流式特征从事件到可读的 SLA 是 30–60 秒,批特征天级刷新。
scenario_en: Social feed ranking: streaming features are readable 30–60 seconds after the event, while batch features refresh daily.
q: 这条 30–60 秒 SLA 决定了哪类信号必须走流式?
q_en: Given that 30–60 second SLA, which kind of signal has to go through the streaming path?
why: 30–60 秒的额度只值得花在秒级会变的信号上:新帖计数晚一天就错过爆火窗口。慢变信号走批处理更省算力。
why_en: That 30–60 second budget is worth spending only on signals that change by the second, like counts on a fresh post, because a day of lag misses the trending window; slow-moving signals stay in batch to save compute.
options: 新帖发布后的实时点赞/评论计数,必须走流式
作者历史平均互动率,天级批处理刷新已足够
用户长期兴趣画像,应改成事件到达即重算
帖子文本 embedding,应每 30 秒重新推理一遍
options_en: Real-time like and comment counts on a freshly posted item must go through streaming.
The author historical average engagement rate, which a daily batch refresh already covers.
The long-term user interest profile, which should be recomputed on every incoming event.
The post text embedding, which should be re-inferred every 30 seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标,这里指事件发生到特征可被排序读取的端到端时延上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA here is the agreed upper bound on end-to-end delay from an event happening to its feature being readable by ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本或物品压成一个稠密向量,用来算相似度,内容不变时向量也不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector representation of text or an item used for similarity, and it stays fixed while the content stays fixed.

optionExplanations: 对;新帖的互动量在分钟级翻倍,只有秒级通道才追得上这种变化。
历史平均互动率按天缓慢漂移,占用流式额度只是浪费算力。
兴趣画像要聚合数周行为,每条事件重算既不稳定也扛不住 QPS。
文本内容不变则向量不变,反复推理徒增 GPU 成本,离线算一次即可。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — engagement on a new post can double within minutes, so only a seconds-scale path keeps up.
A historical average engagement rate drifts slowly by the day, so spending streaming budget on it wastes compute.
An interest profile aggregates weeks of behavior; recomputing it per event is both unstable and too expensive at this QPS.
If the text does not change the vector does not change, so repeated inference only burns GPU; compute it once offline.
category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 只用「发帖者单独」或「浏览者单独」的特征,抓不住这一对具体的人之间有多熟。
scenario_en: Poster-alone or viewer-alone features miss how close this specific pair of people are.
q: 为什么「发帖者×浏览者」交叉特征信号最强?
q_en: Why are poster×viewer cross-features the highest-signal?
why: 交叉特征刻画的是「这个浏览者对这个发帖者」的具体关系——频率、近因、互惠、社区重叠的复合,比任何一方单独的特征都更能预测这条帖对这个人是否相关。关系是成对的,单方特征丢了配对信息。
why_en: Cross-features capture this specific viewer's relationship to this poster—a composite of frequency, recency, reciprocity, and community overlap—predicting relevance better than either side alone, because relationships are pairwise.
tradeoff: 交叉特征(成对·最强信号·但最贵) vs 单方特征(便宜·但丢配对关系)
options: 因为发帖者单独的粉丝数、认证状态和历史发帖质量,已经最能预测这条帖的相关性
因为浏览者单独的历史点击率和长期兴趣画像,已经最能预测这条帖的相关性
因为交叉特征需要的参数最少、计算最快,比两个单方特征加起来还更省资源
因为它刻画这一对人的具体关系(频率/近因/互惠),比单方特征更能预测相关性
options_en: Because the poster's follower count, verified status, and historical post quality alone already best predict relevance.
Because the viewer's historical CTR and long-term interest profile alone already best predict relevance.
Because cross-features need the fewest params and compute fastest, using even less resource than the two single-side features combined.
Because they capture this pair's specific relationship (frequency/recency/reciprocity), predicting relevance better than either side alone.
whenOtherWins: 若某对用户之间历史互动极稀疏(冷启动、新关注),成对交叉特征无数据可算,这时只能退回单方特征起步。
optionExplanations: 发帖者粉丝数是单方特征,抓不到「他和你」的具体关系。
浏览者历史点击率也是单方特征,同样丢了配对信息。
交叉特征恰恰最贵(要成对算),不是最省算力,搞反了。
对;成对关系是最强预测信号,单方特征无论多强都丢了配对维度。
optionExplanations_en: Poster follower count is a single-side feature and misses the specific 'them and you' relationship.
Viewer historical CTR is also single-side, likewise losing the pairing information.
Cross-features are actually the most expensive (computed per pair), not the cheapest—reversed.
Correct — pairwise relationship is the strongest predictive signal; single-side features, however strong, drop the pairing dimension.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刻画某浏览者与某发帖者具体关系的成对特征,信号最强但最贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A poster×viewer cross-feature captures a specific viewer-poster relationship, the highest-signal but most expensive feature.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互动是单向还是双向,衡量关系是否对等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reciprocity is whether interaction is one-sided or mutual, gauging relationship symmetry.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 要为「发帖者×浏览者」这一对具体人构造复合交叉特征。
scenario_en: You need composite cross-features for a specific poster×viewer pair.
q: 下列哪些是合理的「发帖者×浏览者」交叉特征?(多选)
q_en: Which are reasonable poster×viewer cross-features? (multiple)
why: 四个合理特征各刻画这对人关系的一面:互动强度/互惠/共同兴趣/衰减;全站 DAU 是与具体人无关的全局标量,不算成对特征。
why_en: Each valid feature captures one facet of this pair's relationship — intent, reciprocity, shared interest, or decay — while site-wide DAU is a global scalar unrelated to any specific pair.
options: viewer_poster_comment_count_7d:7 天内该浏览者评论该发帖者的次数
reciprocal_interaction_ratio:双方互动的互惠比例
time_since_last_interaction:距上次互动的时间,刻画关系衰减
全站总 DAU:平台当天的日活总数
options_en: viewer_poster_comment_count_7d: the viewer's 7-day comment count on the poster.
reciprocal_interaction_ratio: the mutual share of their interactions.
time_since_last_interaction: time since their last interaction, capturing decay.
Site-wide total DAU: the platform's daily active user count.
optionExplanations: 对;7 天评论计数是最直接的成对互动意图信号。
对;互惠比例区分单向关注和双向互动,是关系对称性信号。
对;距上次互动的时间刻画关系是否在衰减,是近因维度。
错;全站 DAU 是全局标量,对所有帖都一样,区分不了任何一对具体关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 7-day comment count is the most direct pairwise interaction-intent signal.
Correct — the reciprocity ratio distinguishes one-sided follows from mutual interaction, a symmetry signal.
Correct — time since last interaction captures whether the relationship is decaying, a recency dimension.
Wrong — site-wide DAU is a global scalar identical for all posts and cannot distinguish any specific pair.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览者对该发帖者主打内容格式(视频/文本)的历史点击倾向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: content_type_affinity is the viewer's historical CTR tendency toward the poster's dominant content format.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 交叉特征要按(浏览者,发帖者)成对算,一次请求有几百个候选帖,全对预计算不现实。
scenario_en: Cross-features are computed per (viewer, poster) pair, hundreds of candidate posts per request, and precomputing all pairs is infeasible.
q: 既然全对预计算不可行,交叉特征在服务时怎么算?
q_en: Since all-pairs precompute is infeasible, how are cross-features computed at serving time?
why: 两条路:请求时只为候选集现算交叉特征,或缓存每个浏览者互动最多的 top-K 发帖者。都避开 N×N 全对预计算的组合爆炸,换成候选规模的按需计算。
why_en: Either compute cross-features on the fly for the candidate set, or cache each viewer's top-K most-interacted posters — both avoid the N×N all-pairs explosion.
tradeoff: 请求时按候选集现算(省存储·加读时算) vs 缓存 top-K 发帖者(读快·但覆盖有限)
options: 把数十亿用户对之间的交叉特征全部提前算好并长期存下来,读时直接查表
干脆放弃交叉特征,只用发帖者和浏览者各自的单方特征拼接起来打分
对每条候选帖只随机抽样几对用户来算交叉特征,凑够特征列就上线
请求时只为候选集现算,或缓存浏览者互动最多的 top-K 发帖者
options_en: Precompute cross-features for all billions of user pairs ahead of time and keep them in long-term storage, reading straight from the table.
Drop cross-features entirely and just concatenate the poster's and viewer's separate single-side features to score.
For each candidate post, randomly sample just a few user pairs to compute cross-features, enough to fill the feature column and ship it.
Compute on the fly only for the candidate set, or cache the top-K most-interacted posters per viewer.
whenOtherWins: 若浏览者的候选发帖者高度集中在少数熟人(如强社交圈产品),缓存 top-K 发帖者就能覆盖大部分请求,比每次现算更快。
optionExplanations: 全对预计算是 N×N 组合爆炸,数十亿用户根本存不下,正是不可行项。
丢掉交叉特征等于放弃最强信号,是因噎废食。
随机采样用户对算出的特征和当前候选无关,对排序没用。
对;只算召回候选或缓存 top-K 发帖者,把计算量从 N×N 降到候选规模,可行。
optionExplanations_en: All-pairs precompute is an N×N explosion; billions of users cannot be stored—exactly the infeasible option.
Dropping cross-features abandons the strongest signal, throwing the baby out with the bathwater.
Random user pairs yield features unrelated to the current candidates, useless for ranking.
Correct — computing only for retrieved candidates or caching top-K posters cuts work from N×N to candidate scale, feasible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按精确键(viewer_id, poster_id)在特征存储里 O(1) 取一条特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point lookup fetches one feature by an exact key (viewer_id, poster_id) in O(1) from the feature store.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 计算「A 和 B 的共同好友」要同时读 A 和 B 的好友列表,但 B 把好友列表设成了私密。
scenario_en: Computing 'mutual friends of A and B' reads both A's and B's friend lists, but B set their friend list private.
q: 图谱遍历算共同好友,可能造成什么隐私泄露?
q_en: What privacy leak can graph traversal for mutual friends cause?
why: 算共同好友要读双方好友列表,若 B 是私密的,这次遍历就间接暴露了 B 的部分关系——用户没同意公开的连接被泄露。所以隐私安全特征必须服务端算,绝不把原始图谱暴露给模型。
why_en: Computing mutual friends reads both friend lists, so if B is private, the traversal leaks part of B's connections the user never consented to expose—hence compute privacy-safe features server-side and never expose the raw graph.
options: 会泄露 B 未同意公开的部分关系,因为遍历读了 B 的私密好友列表
不会有任何泄露,因为共同好友这个计算结果本身对所有用户都是完全公开的信息
只会泄露 A 单方的关系信息,私密设置的 B 完全不受任何影响
只会拖慢一点计算延迟,不涉及任何隐私层面的问题
options_en: It leaks part of B's connections B never consented to expose, because the traversal read B's private friend list.
No leak at all, because the mutual-friends result itself is fully public information for every user.
It only leaks A's own relationship information; B, who set it private, is completely unaffected either way.
It only slows compute latency a bit and doesn't touch privacy at any level.
optionExplanations: 对;遍历读了 B 的私密列表,共同好友结果会反推出 B 未公开的连接,是隐私泄露。
B 已设私密,共同好友并非公开信息,断言无泄露是错的。
遍历读的是双方列表,泄露的正是私密方 B 的关系,不是只泄露 A。
这是实打实的关系泄露,不只是延迟问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the traversal read B's private list, and the mutual-friends result can reveal B's undisclosed connections, a leak.
B set it private, so mutual friends are not public; claiming no leak is wrong.
The traversal reads both lists, and the leak is precisely the private party B's relationships, not only A's.
This is a real relationship leak, not just a latency concern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沿社交图的边访问相邻节点(如读好友列表)来算特征,可能触及私密关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graph traversal walks the social graph's edges (e.g. reading friend lists) to compute features, potentially touching private relationships.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 想用图谱特征提升排序,又要保证无法从模型反推出任何单个用户的关系。
scenario_en: You want graph features to improve ranking while guaranteeing no single user's relationship can be inferred from the model.
q: 差分隐私(differential privacy)怎么在图谱特征上保护隐私,ε 起什么作用?
q_en: How does differential privacy protect graph features, and what role does ε play?
why: 差分隐私往特征里加校准过的噪声,使得任何单条数据在不在都无法被反推。隐私预算由 ε 控制:ε 越小噪声越大、隐私越强,但排序质量越差。生产常用 ε 在 1–10 之间权衡。
why_en: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so no single data point's presence is inferable, with the privacy budget controlled by ε—lower ε means more noise and stronger privacy but worse ranking, commonly 1–10 in production.
tradeoff: 小 ε(隐私强·噪声大·排序差) vs 大 ε(排序好·隐私弱)
options: 加校准噪声使单条数据不可反推;ε 越小隐私越强但排序越差
把所有图谱特征删掉,靠不用即隐私
把特征整体加密存储,推理时再解密使用,由 ε 决定密钥长度
只给管理员看图谱特征,普通模型不用
options_en: Add calibrated noise so no single data point is inferable; a smaller ε means stronger privacy but worse ranking.
Delete all graph features and rely on non-use as privacy.
Encrypt features at rest and decrypt them at inference time, with ε determining the key length.
Show graph features only to admins; ordinary models don't use them.
whenOtherWins: 若某特征根本不涉及可反推的个体关系(如纯内容元数据),不必上差分隐私加噪,直接用原值排序更准。
optionExplanations: 对;差分隐私用加噪 + ε 预算做隐私-效用权衡,是保图谱隐私的标准手段。
删掉全部图谱特征会丢最强信号,是过度的一刀切,不是差分隐私。
ε 是隐私预算,不是密钥长度;差分隐私靠加噪不是加密。
只给管理员看不解决模型使用时的反推风险,答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — differential privacy trades privacy for utility via added noise and an ε budget, the standard way to protect graph privacy.
Deleting all graph features drops the strongest signal, an over-broad measure, not differential privacy.
ε is a privacy budget, not key length; differential privacy adds noise, not encryption.
Admin-only viewing doesn't address inference risk during model use, off-topic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往数据/特征加校准噪声,使任何单条记录在不在都无法被反推。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so the presence or absence of any single record cannot be inferred.

termDefinitions.meaning: 差分隐私的隐私预算,越小噪声越大、隐私越强、效用越低;生产常用 1–10。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ε (epsilon) is the differential-privacy budget: smaller means more noise, stronger privacy, lower utility, commonly 1–10.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 差分隐私和 k-匿名是两种不同的图谱隐私保护思路。
scenario_en: Differential privacy and k-anonymity are two different graph-privacy approaches.
q: 差分隐私和 k-匿名(k-anonymity)在机制上有何区别,各自的代价是什么?
q_en: How do differential privacy and k-anonymity differ mechanically, and what is each one's cost?
why: 差分隐私靠加校准噪声让单点不可反推,代价是噪声降低排序质量;k-匿名要求每种子图模式至少匹配 k 个用户,代价是匿名化可能破坏关系特征依赖的社区结构。两者都是隐私↔质量的权衡,方式不同。
why_en: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so single points aren't inferable (cost: noise hurts ranking); k-anonymity requires every subgraph pattern to match ≥k users (cost: anonymization can destroy the community structure features rely on).
tradeoff: 差分隐私(加噪·损精度) vs k-匿名(泛化子图·毁社区结构)

rows: 加校准噪声,ε 控预算

options: 两者机制其实相同,只是 k(匿名集大小)和 ε(隐私预算)是同一参数的两种叫法
差分隐私加噪(代价降精度);k-匿名要求子图模式≥k 人(代价毁社区结构)
差分隐私要求任意子图模式匹配≥k 人;k-匿名则改成靠加噪声实现
两者都不需要付出任何代价,能同时做到完美隐私保护和完美排序质量
options_en: Mechanically the same — k (anonymity-set size) and ε (privacy budget) are just two names for the same parameter.
Differential privacy adds noise (cost: lower accuracy); k-anonymity requires subgraph patterns to match ≥k users (cost: destroys community structure).
Differential privacy requires any subgraph pattern to match ≥k users; k-anonymity instead relies on adding noise.
Neither has any cost at all — both achieve perfect privacy protection and perfect ranking quality simultaneously.
optionExplanations: k 和 ε 是不同机制的参数,一个是匿名集大小、一个是隐私预算,不是同一个。
对;加噪 vs 泛化子图是两种机制,代价分别是精度损失和社区结构破坏。
说反了:加噪是差分隐私,≥k 人是 k-匿名。
隐私保护必有代价(噪声/结构损失),无代价完美是幻想。
optionExplanations_en: k and ε are parameters of different mechanisms—anonymity-set size vs privacy budget—not the same thing.
Correct — adding noise vs generalizing subgraphs are two mechanisms, costing accuracy loss and community-structure destruction respectively.
Backwards: adding noise is differential privacy, and ≥k users is k-anonymity.
Privacy protection always has a cost (noise/structure loss); cost-free perfection is fantasy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让每种子图模式至少匹配 k 个用户,使个体不可单独识别,但会破坏社区结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: k-anonymity ensures every subgraph pattern matches at least k users so individuals can't be singled out, but it can destroy community structure.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 拉黑/限制名单属于隐私安全约束,被拉黑内容绝不能通过任何特征间接漏给用户。
scenario_en: Block/restricted lists are a privacy-safety constraint; blocked content must never leak to the user through any feature.
q: 拉黑名单在特征系统里该怎么处理,才能保证不通过交叉特征泄露?
q_en: How should block lists be handled in the feature system so they never leak through cross-features?
why: 拉黑名单要强一致(见前卡),且隐私安全特征在服务端计算、绝不把原始图谱暴露给模型——避免被拉黑关系通过交叉特征间接渗出。名单是硬约束,不是软信号,漏一次就是隐私事故。
why_en: Block lists must be strongly consistent, and privacy-safe features are computed server-side with the raw graph never exposed to the model, so blocked relationships can't seep through cross-features—a hard constraint where one leak is an incident.
tradeoff: 服务端算隐私安全特征+强一致名单(绝不泄露·更重) vs 把原始图谱喂模型(方便·会漏拉黑关系)
options: 把原始好友图和拉黑关系一起直接喂给模型,让模型自己学会避开拉黑内容
拉黑名单用最终一致就够了,延迟窗口内偶尔漏一点内容问题不大
只在客户端前端过滤拉黑内容,后端排序特征照常把它算进去
名单强一致,隐私安全特征服务端算,绝不把原始图谱暴露给模型
options_en: Feed the raw friend graph and block relationships straight into the model and let it learn to avoid blocked content on its own.
Eventual consistency for block lists is good enough; the occasional leak during the delay window is no big deal.
Filter blocked content only on the client-side frontend; backend ranking features compute it in as usual.
Keep the list strongly consistent, compute privacy-safe features server-side, and never expose the raw graph to the model.
whenOtherWins: 若某类内容并非隐私安全约束、只是「倾向少看」的偏好(如降低某话题),就不必上强一致名单,用软性降权即可。
optionExplanations: 把原始图喂模型正是泄露源头,模型可能通过特征间接暴露拉黑关系。
最终一致给了泄露窗口,拉黑是硬约束,漏一次就是隐私事故。
只在前端过滤,后端特征仍携带拉黑关系,交叉特征照样能渗出。
对;强一致名单 + 服务端算安全特征 + 不暴露原始图,才能堵住交叉特征泄露。
optionExplanations_en: Feeding the raw graph to the model is the leak source; the model can indirectly expose blocked relationships through features.
Eventual consistency opens a leak window; blocking is a hard constraint where one leak is an incident.
Frontend-only filtering leaves backend features carrying blocked relationships, which cross-features can still seep out.
Correct — a strongly consistent list plus server-side safe features plus not exposing the raw graph seals cross-feature leakage.

termDefinitions.term: block/restricted list / 拉黑限制名单
termDefinitions.meaning: 用户拉黑或限制的对象集合,隐私安全硬约束,内容绝不能漏出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A block/restricted list is the set a user blocked or restricted, a hard privacy-safety constraint whose content must never leak.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 对图谱特征做了差分隐私加噪或匿名化后,想知道排序质量掉了多少。
scenario_en: After applying differential privacy or anonymization to graph features, you want to know how much ranking quality dropped.
q: 怎么量化隐私变换对特征有用性的损害?
q_en: How do you quantify the damage a privacy transform does to feature usefulness?
why: 用信息损失指标(information-loss metrics):对比隐私变换前后特征的重要性/排序质量,量化掉了多少。Staff+ 会设定一个 ε 范围并持续追踪加噪后特征重要性的退化,把隐私-质量权衡变成可监控的数字。
why_en: Use information-loss metrics: compare feature importance/ranking quality before and after the privacy transform to quantify the drop, and Staff+ tracks feature-importance degradation across an ε range.
options: 只盯着隐私预算 ε 是否达标,完全不管排序质量因此掉了多少
用信息损失指标对比变换前后的特征重要性/排序质量,量化退化
假设加噪声不会影响特征质量,上线前不做任何量化测量
只等到用户投诉隐私问题时,才回头检查排序质量退化
options_en: Only watch whether the privacy budget ε is met, ignoring entirely how much ranking quality drops as a result.
Use information-loss metrics to compare feature importance/ranking quality before and after the transform, quantifying degradation.
Assume adding noise won't affect feature quality and run no quantified measurement before launch.
Only revisit ranking-quality degradation after users complain about privacy.
optionExplanations: 只看隐私不看质量,无法在隐私-效用之间做知情权衡。
对;信息损失指标把加噪/匿名的质量代价量化出来,支撑 ε 的选择。
假设加噪无害是危险的,噪声确实会降特征重要性,必须测。
等投诉太被动,质量退化早在投诉前就发生了。
optionExplanations_en: Checking privacy without quality can't make an informed privacy-utility trade-off.
Correct — information-loss metrics quantify the quality cost of noise/anonymization, supporting the choice of ε.
Assuming noise is harmless is dangerous; noise really lowers feature importance and must be measured.
Waiting for complaints is too passive; quality degradation happens well before complaints.

termDefinitions.term: information-loss metric / 信息损失指标
termDefinitions.meaning: 对比隐私变换前后特征重要性或排序质量,量化隐私带来的效用损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An information-loss metric compares feature importance or ranking quality before and after a privacy transform to quantify utility loss.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 一个点赞事件要在 30–60 秒内变成排序可读的新鲜特征。
scenario_en: A like event must become a fresh, ranking-readable feature within 30–60s.
q: 把互动事件经流式管线变成可用特征的步骤排序:
q_en: Order the steps by which an interaction event becomes a usable feature via the streaming pipeline:
steps: 用户点赞产生互动事件,写入 Kafka
Flink 实时消费事件,更新窗口互动计数
计数带 TTL 写入在线存储(Redis/DynamoDB)
排序服务推理时点查该计数 + 批处理特征
why: 流式链路:事件进 Kafka→Flink 消费更新计数→带 TTL 写在线存储→排序推理时点查。整条要压在 30–60 秒 SLA 内,快变信号才能及时进排序,爆火帖才不被低排。
why_en: Streaming flow: event into Kafka, Flink updates the count, write to the online store with TTL, then ranking point-looks it up at inference—all within the 30–60s SLA so fast signals reach ranking in time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["点赞事件→Kafka"] --> F["Flink 更新窗口计数"]
  F --> S["带 TTL 写在线存储"]
  S --> R["排序推理点查"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事件流平台,承接海量互动事件供流式管线消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform that ingests massive interaction events for the streaming pipeline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理引擎,实时消费事件、维护窗口聚合(如互动计数)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing engine that consumes events in real time and maintains windowed aggregates like interaction counts.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 把 feed 特征系统的三层设计讲成一条从慢到快再到隐私的完整叙事。
scenario_en: Explain the feed feature system's three-layer design as one narrative from slow to fast to privacy.
q: 把 feed 特征系统的三层设计按讲述顺序排好:
q_en: Order the feed feature system's three-layer design as you would present it:
steps: 批处理层:Spark+Airflow 日级算慢变的图谱/画像特征
流式层:Flink+Kafka 30–60s 算快变的参与/近因特征
隐私层:限定可行遍历 + 匿名化/差分隐私保护图谱
交叉特征最强但最贵、最敏感,喂给下一课的多任务模型
why: 三层叙事:批处理(慢变)→流式(快变)→隐私层(可行遍历+匿名化),最后点出交叉特征信号最强但最贵最敏感,承上启下接入多任务模型。这条链体现「先数据战略后建模」的成熟度。
why_en: Three-layer narrative: batch (slow) → streaming (fast) → privacy layer (permissible traversals + anonymization), closing on cross-features being highest-signal but most expensive and sensitive, feeding the multi-task model.

termDefinitions.term: three-layer feature design / 三层特征设计
termDefinitions.meaning: 批处理(慢变)+流式(快变)+隐私层(可行遍历与匿名化)的组合架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The three-layer feature design combines batch (slow), streaming (fast), and a privacy layer (permissible traversals and anonymization).

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 设计社交 feed 排序：一个模型要同时预测 P(点击)、P(转发)、P(有意义评论)、P(长停留) 和创作者公平分。
scenario_en: Designing social feed ranking: one model must jointly predict P(click), P(reshare), P(meaningful comment), P(long dwell), and a creator-equity score.
q: feed 排序模型的核心形态和三大支柱是什么？
q_en: What is the core shape and three pillars of the feed-ranking model?
why: 核心是一个模型对每个「观看者-发帖者-内容」三元组联合预测多个目标头（点击/转发/评论/停留/创作者公平）。三大支柱：多任务学习(MTL) 联合优化、专家混合(MoE) 处理内容异质、损失设计对抗指标蚕食。
why_en: The core is one model jointly predicting multiple heads (click/reshare/comment/dwell/creator equity) per viewer-poster-content triple, resting on three pillars: multi-task learning, mixture-of-experts for content heterogeneity, and loss design against cannibalization.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  F["特征: 三元组"] --> S["共享表示"]
  S --> MTL["多任务头"]
  MTL --> C["点击"]
  MTL --> R["转发"]
  MTL --> M["有意义评论"]
  MTL --> D["长停留"]
  MTL --> E["创作者公平"]
options: 每个目标各训一个独立模型，互不共享底座和特征表示，重复造轮子且多套上线
一个模型联合预测多目标头，三支柱=MTL+MoE+抗蚕食损失
只预测点击一个目标，其余目标用后置规则加分补齐
纯人工规则打分：按新鲜度、粉丝数、互动数排序
options_en: Train a separate model per objective, sharing no backbone or feature representation — duplicated work, multiple models to ship.
One model jointly predicts multiple heads; three pillars = MTL + MoE + anti-cannibalization loss.
Predict click only, then patch the other objectives with post-hoc rule bonuses.
Score by hand-written rules: recency, follower count, and interaction counts.
optionExplanations: 独立模型浪费算力、丢失共享表示，还要多套模型上线运维，正是本设计要避免的。
对；联合多头+MTL/MoE/损失设计三支柱，是 feed 排序的主流架构。
只预测点击会诱导 clickbait，忽略转发/评论/停留/公平等多目标。
纯规则无法个性化，也表达不了多目标权衡。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models waste compute, lose shared representation, and ship multiple models to run — exactly what this design avoids.
Correct — joint multi-head plus the MTL/MoE/loss-design trio is the mainstream feed-ranking architecture.
Predicting only click invites clickbait and ignores reshare/comment/dwell/equity.
Pure rules can't personalize or express multi-objective tradeoffs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务学习：一个模型共享表示同时优化多个目标，比每目标单独训模型更省且能互相受益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTL (Multi-Task Learning) trains one model with shared representation to optimize several objectives at once, cheaper than separate models and mutually beneficial.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分发是否公平覆盖不同创作者的分数，作为防止只追参与的护栏目标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator equity scores whether distribution fairly reaches diverse creators, a guardrail objective against pure engagement-chasing.

scenario: 有人主张给点击、转发、评论各训一个独立模型，分开上线打分。
scenario_en: Someone proposes training separate models for click, reshare, and comment and scoring them independently.
q: 为什么用一个多任务模型联合优化，而不是每任务一个独立模型？
q_en: Why one multi-task model instead of a separate model per task?
why: feed 排序本质多目标。分开训既浪费算力（重复造底座），又丢掉共享表示——会转发的用户通常先点了击，任务间有强相关信号，共享底座能互相受益。MTL 一个模型学共享表示 + 各任务头，更省也更准。
why_en: Feed ranking is inherently multi-objective, and separate models both waste compute and miss shared representation, since users who reshare usually clicked first, so a shared backbone lets tasks benefit each other.
tradeoff: MTL 共享底座（省算力+共享信号） vs 每任务独立模型（零干扰但重复造底座、丢共享）
options: 独立模型互不干扰，任何规模和目标数下都比共享更准，代价是重复造底座
feed 本质多目标：独立训浪费算力又丢共享表示，MTL 更省
MTL 只是省算力的妥协，各任务精度一定比独立训模型差
点击与评论之间毫无关联，共享表示只会引入额外噪声
options_en: Separate models never interfere and beat sharing at any scale or task count, at the cost of rebuilding the backbone each time.
Feed is inherently multi-objective: separate training wastes compute and loses shared representation, so MTL is cheaper.
MTL is only a compute-saving compromise and is always less accurate than separate models.
Click and comment are unrelated, so a shared representation only adds noise.
whenOtherWins: 如果两个任务本质完全无关（用户预测 vs 一个毫不相干的内容审核任务），强行共享底座反而互相污染，这时分开独立模型更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If two tasks are truly unrelated (user prediction vs a wholly unrelated moderation task), forcing a shared backbone mutually pollutes them, and separate models fit better.
optionExplanations: 独立模型确实零干扰，但重复造底座、丢共享信号，多数相关任务下更差。
对；相关任务共享底座能互相受益，还省算力，是 feed 多目标的标准解。
共享相关信号常常提升而非降低精度，不是纯省钱。
feed 任务高度相关（点击/转发/评论同源），共享很有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models are interference-free but rebuild backbones and lose shared signal, worse for most related tasks.
Correct — related tasks sharing a backbone benefit each other and save compute, the standard feed multi-objective solution.
Sharing related signal often raises accuracy, not lowers it — not just cost.
Feed tasks are highly related (click/reshare/comment same-source), so sharing is meaningful.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务共用的底层特征表示，让相关任务的信号互相增强、避免重复学习。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared representation is the common bottom feature layer across tasks, letting related signals reinforce each other and avoid relearning.

scenario: 多任务底座有两种：所有任务共用一个底座，或每个任务用自己的门控在一组专家上加权。
scenario_en: Two MTL backbones: all tasks share one bottom, or each task uses its own gating over a set of experts.
q: shared-bottom 和 MMoE 的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What's the core difference between shared-bottom and MMoE?
why: shared-bottom 一个共享底座接各任务塔，简单便宜但目标冲突时互相拖累；MMoE 用每任务门控对共享专家加权，选择性共享减少干扰。
why_en: Shared-bottom is one shared trunk feeding per-task towers — cheap but tasks drag each other when objectives conflict; MMoE gives each task its own gate over shared experts, so sharing is selective and interference drops.
tradeoff: shared-bottom（简单便宜但冲突时互拖） vs MMoE（选择性共享、减干扰但参数多、更难调）

rows: 每任务门控加权共享专家

options: shared-bottom 单底座简单但冲突时互拖；MMoE 每任务门控加权专家
两者结构完全相同，只是不同论文里给了不同的名字
shared-bottom 每任务一套专家，MMoE 只有单一共享底座，二者刚好说反
MMoE 不共享任何参数，等价于每个任务各训一个独立模型
options_en: Shared-bottom is a single simple bottom that interferes under conflict; MMoE gates shared experts per task.
They are structurally identical, just named differently in different papers.
Shared-bottom gives each task its own experts; MMoE has a single shared bottom — exactly backwards.
MMoE shares no parameters, which is equivalent to training a separate model per task.
optionExplanations: 对；一个是硬共享一个底座、一个是每任务门控软性挑专家，正是二者分野。
两者共享机制不同，不是叫法差异。
说反了：方向要记牢——单一底座属于前者，专家池加门控属于后者。
MMoE 共享的是专家池，只是门控各异，不等于独立模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one hard-shares a single bottom, the other lets each task softly gate experts, the dividing line.
Their sharing mechanisms differ; it's not naming.
Backwards — keep the direction straight: the single trunk belongs to the former, the expert pool with gates to the latter.
MMoE shares the expert pool with per-task gates — not separate models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组共享专家子网络，每个任务用独立门控网络对专家做 softmax 加权，实现选择性知识共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MMoE (Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts) has shared expert sub-networks, each task using its own gating network to softmax-weight experts for selective sharing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有任务共用一个 embedding+交互层，再接各任务塔，最简单的 MTL 结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shared-bottom has all tasks share one embedding+interaction layer feeding task-specific towers, the simplest MTL structure.

scenario: 一个 feed 内容类型单一、任务也不多且基本不冲突，团队想要最省算力、最好调的多任务结构。
scenario_en: A feed with homogeneous content, few tasks, and little conflict, wanting the cheapest, easiest-to-tune MTL structure.
q: 这种场景该选哪种多任务结构，为什么？
q_en: Which MTL structure fits this case, and why?
why: 选 shared-bottom：任务少、不冲突、内容同质时，一个共享底座就够，简单、低算力、好调。只有当目标开始互相冲突（clickbait 拉点击伤评论）时，才值得升级到 MMoE 的选择性共享。
why_en: Choose shared-bottom: with few non-conflicting tasks and homogeneous content, one shared bottom suffices — simple, cheap, easy to tune — upgrading to MMoE only when objectives start conflicting.
tradeoff: shared-bottom（任务少不冲突时最省最好调） vs MMoE（目标冲突时才值得的复杂度）
options: 选 MMoE：门控专家结构更复杂，复杂结构在任何场景都更强
选 shared-bottom：任务少不冲突、内容同质，共享底座够用
选每任务独立模型：零干扰最稳，服务成本和运维也不吃亏
选稀疏 MoE：top-K 路由天生就是为同质单一内容设计的，专家会闲置浪费
options_en: Pick MMoE: gated experts are more complex, and more complex always wins.
Pick shared-bottom: with few non-conflicting tasks and homogeneous content, one shared trunk is enough.
Pick a separate model per task: zero interference, and serving cost and ops are no worse.
Pick sparse MoE: top-K routing was designed for homogeneous single-type content, so experts would sit idle and go to waste.
whenOtherWins: 一旦任务目标明显冲突（点击 vs 有意义评论互相拉扯），shared-bottom 的硬共享会互相污染，这时 MMoE 的每任务门控选择性共享更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: Once objectives clearly conflict (click vs meaningful comment tug against each other), shared-bottom's hard sharing pollutes tasks, and MMoE's per-task gating fits better.
optionExplanations: 任务不冲突时上 MMoE 是过度工程，白增参数和调试成本。
对；同质少冲突场景 shared-bottom 最省最好调，是恰当的简单解。
独立模型丢共享、重复造底座，不是这里的最优。
稀疏 MoE 是为异质内容设计的，同质场景用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Using MMoE with non-conflicting tasks is over-engineering, adding params and tuning cost.
Correct — for homogeneous low-conflict cases shared-bottom is cheapest and easiest, the right simple solution.
Separate models lose sharing and rebuild backbones — not optimal here.
Sparse MoE is built for heterogeneous content, unneeded when homogeneous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务共享参数时，一个任务的更新损害另一个任务表现，尤其在目标冲突时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task interference is when shared-parameter updates for one task hurt another's performance, especially under conflicting objectives.

scenario: 点击有海量标签、有意义评论的标签却很稀疏，两者共用一个底座训练。
scenario_en: Clicks have abundant labels while meaningful-comment labels are sparse, and both share one backbone.
q: 标签量悬殊的任务共享底座会怎样，怎么缓解？
q_en: What happens when tasks with lopsided label counts share a backbone, and how to mitigate?
why: 标签多的强势任务（点击）会劫持共享层：梯度里它压倒性主导，把共享表示往自己方向拽，稀疏任务（评论）学不好。缓解：用同方差不确定性加权自动校准各任务影响，并给稀疏任务设权重下限，别让点击独吞底座。
why_en: The label-rich dominant task (clicks) hijacks the shared layers, dominating gradients and pulling the representation its way so the sparse task learns poorly — mitigated by uncertainty weighting and lower bounds on sparse tasks.
options: 点击劫持共享层、稀疏评论学不好；用不确定性加权+权重下限
毫无影响，优化器会让标签多与标签少的任务自动平衡，不需要额外加权
稀疏任务样本少、梯度更大，反而会自动主导压过点击
只影响训练的收敛速度，各任务最终质量并不会受影响
options_en: Click hijacks the shared layers so sparse comments learn poorly; use uncertainty weighting plus a weight floor.
No effect — the optimizer automatically balances label-rich and label-sparse tasks, no extra weighting needed.
The sparse task has fewer samples but larger gradients, so it automatically dominates click.
It only affects convergence speed, not the final quality of each task.
optionExplanations: 对；强势任务主导梯度会拽偏共享表示，需自动加权+下限保护稀疏任务。
标签量悬殊不会自动平衡，点击天然占主导。
稀疏任务信号弱，不可能自动压过标签海量的点击。
这是学到的表示被拽偏的质量问题，不只是速度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the dominant task's gradients skew the shared representation, needing auto-weighting plus lower bounds to protect the sparse task.
Lopsided labels don't auto-balance; clicks naturally dominate.
The sparse task's weak signal can't override label-rich clicks.
It's a quality issue of a skewed representation, not just speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签多或损失大的任务在共享层梯度中压倒其他任务，劫持共享表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task dominance is when a label-rich or high-loss task overwhelms others in shared-layer gradients, hijacking the shared representation.

scenario: 多任务损失里，点击和评论标签量、噪声都不同，你不想手工反复调各任务的固定权重。
scenario_en: In the multi-task loss, click and comment differ in label count and noise, and you don't want to hand-tune fixed weights.
q: 该用什么方法自动平衡各任务的损失权重？
q_en: Which method auto-balances the per-task loss weights?
why: 同方差不确定性加权给每任务学一个 σ_k：L=Σ(1/2σ_k²)L_k+log σ_k，σ 小则该任务被放大，log σ 项防 σ 无限膨胀。
why_en: Homoscedastic uncertainty weighting learns a per-task sigma: the loss is sum of L_k over two sigma squared plus log sigma, so a small sigma amplifies that task while the log term keeps sigma from blowing up.
tradeoff: 不确定性加权（自动校准、防噪声任务主导） vs 固定权重（简单但要反复手调、易失衡）
options: 手工给每个任务设固定权重，反复试跑直到指标看起来平衡
同方差不确定性加权：为每个任务学一个 σ_k 自动调权重
所有任务权重恒等于 1，训练全程从不调整任何一项
只保留标签最多的点击任务，其余稀疏任务直接不训
options_en: Hand-set a fixed weight per task and keep retrying until the metrics look balanced.
Homoscedastic uncertainty weighting: learn a per-task σ_k that tunes the weights automatically.
Keep every task weight at 1 and never adjust anything during training.
Keep only the label-richest click task and skip training the sparse ones.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务数很少、噪声水平相近且你已知合适权重，直接用手调的固定权重更简单，不必引入可学习 σ 的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If tasks are few with similar noise and you already know good weights, hand-tuned fixed weights are simpler than introducing learnable σ.
optionExplanations: 固定权重要反复手调、跟不上任务收敛速度差异，易失衡。
对；可学习 σ 让模型自动按不确定性校准各任务，log σ 防止 σ 一味变大逃避。
恒等权重忽视任务噪声/标签量差异，强势任务照样主导。
只留一个任务就放弃了多目标，违背 feed 排序初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed weights need repeated tuning and can't track differing convergence rates, easily imbalanced.
Correct — learnable σ auto-calibrates tasks by uncertainty, and log σ stops σ from just inflating to dodge loss.
Equal weights ignore noise/label differences, letting the dominant task win.
Keeping one task abandons multi-objective, defeating feed ranking.

termDefinitions.term: homoscedastic uncertainty weighting / 同方差不确定性加权
termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个任务学一个不确定性 σ，用 1/2σ² 自动加权损失，σ 越大权重越小，配 log σ 正则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Homoscedastic uncertainty weighting learns a per-task uncertainty σ, weighting loss by 1/2σ² (larger σ, smaller weight) with a log σ regularizer.

scenario: 监控发现点击任务的 σ_k 被学得非常小（点击标签太多、噪声低）。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows the click task's σ_k learned very small (abundant, low-noise click labels).
q: 点击 σ_k 变得很小意味着什么风险，怎么防？
q_en: What risk does a very small click σ_k signal, and how to guard?
why: σ 小→1/2σ²大→点击损失被放大、主导共享表示，这正是想防的失衡从另一端冒出来。防法：监控各任务 σ_k，给稀疏任务权重设下限，别让点击独吞底座。
why_en: Small σ means 1/2σ² is large, so click loss is up-weighted and dominates the shared representation, reintroducing the imbalance — guarded by monitoring per-task σ_k and setting explicit lower bounds on sparse tasks.
options: σ 小说明点击任务已被模型彻底忽略，可以放心不用管
σ 小→1/2σ² 大→点击损失放大并主导共享层；给稀疏任务设下限
σ 小只是数值溢出 bug，重启训练并调大 batch 就会恢复
σ 的大小只反映标注噪声，与各任务的损失权重完全无关
options_en: A small sigma means the click task is fully ignored, so you can relax.
Small sigma makes the coefficient large, so click loss is amplified and dominates the shared layers; put a floor on sparse tasks.
A small sigma is just a numeric overflow bug; restart training with a bigger batch.
Sigma only reflects label noise and has nothing to do with per-task loss weights.
optionExplanations: σ 小恰恰是权重被放大、点击更主导，不是被忽略。
对，这套自动加权确实可能让低噪声任务过度主导，需要监控+设下限兜底。
这不是 bug，是加权机制的真实副作用，重启不解决。
σ 直接决定 1/2σ² 权重，σ 小则权重大，绝非无关。
optionExplanations_en: Small σ actually up-weights and lets click dominate, not ignores it.
Correct — uncertainty weighting can over-favor low-noise tasks, needing monitoring plus lower bounds.
It's not a bug but a real side effect of the weighting; restarting won't fix it.
σ directly sets the 1/2σ² weight; small σ means large weight — far from unrelated.

termDefinitions.term: task lower bound / 任务权重下限
termDefinitions.meaning: 给稀疏或易被压制任务的损失权重设一个最小值，防止强势任务把它挤没。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A task lower bound sets a minimum loss weight for a sparse or easily-suppressed task, preventing a dominant task from squeezing it out.

scenario: 反向传播时不同任务的梯度方向互相打架，你要在两种梯度冲突处理法之间选。
scenario_en: During backprop, different tasks' gradients oppose each other, and you choose between two conflict-resolution methods.
q: PCGrad 和 GradNorm 分别怎么处理任务梯度冲突？
q_en: How do PCGrad and GradNorm each handle task-gradient conflict?
why: PCGrad（投影冲突梯度）：检测到两个梯度冲突时，把一个梯度投影到另一个的法平面上，去掉破坏性分量。GradNorm：动态重新平衡各任务的梯度幅度，让不同任务以相近速度学习。一个改方向、一个改幅度。
why_en: PCGrad detects conflict and projects one gradient onto the other's normal plane to remove the destructive component, while GradNorm dynamically rebalances gradient magnitudes so tasks learn at similar rates.
tradeoff: PCGrad（去掉冲突方向分量） vs GradNorm（重平衡梯度幅度）

rows: 投影到法平面去破坏分量
动态重平衡各任务幅度

options: 两者做法完全一样，只是不同论文里给出的不同命名
PCGrad 把冲突梯度投影到法平面；GradNorm 重平衡梯度幅度
PCGrad 改梯度幅度、GradNorm 改梯度方向，正好反过来
两者都只是自动调大学习率，与任务梯度冲突本身无关
options_en: They do exactly the same thing, just named differently in different papers.
PCGrad projects a conflicting gradient onto the normal plane; GradNorm rebalances gradient magnitudes.
PCGrad changes magnitude and GradNorm changes direction — the reverse.
Both merely raise the learning rate and have nothing to do with gradient conflict.
optionExplanations: 两者一个改方向一个改幅度，机制不同，非叫法差异。
对；PCGrad 处理方向冲突（投影），GradNorm 处理幅度失衡（重平衡），互补。
说反了：PCGrad 改方向，GradNorm 改幅度。
两者都不是简单调学习率，而是专门处理多任务梯度冲突。
optionExplanations_en: One changes direction, the other magnitude — different mechanisms, not naming.
Correct — PCGrad handles directional conflict (projection), GradNorm handles magnitude imbalance (rebalancing), complementary.
Backwards: PCGrad changes direction, GradNorm magnitude.
Neither merely tunes the learning rate; both target multi-task gradient conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测任务梯度冲突后，把一个梯度投影到另一个的法平面，去掉相互破坏的分量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PCGrad (Projecting Conflicting Gradients) detects conflicting task gradients and projects one onto the other's normal plane, removing the destructive component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态重平衡各任务梯度幅度，使不同任务以相近速度收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GradNorm dynamically rebalances per-task gradient magnitudes so tasks converge at similar rates.

scenario: 一个 feed 混杂文本、文章、图片、短视频、直播、链接预览，各类内容的特征分布和参与模式都不同（视频停留是强信号，文本停留可能只是读得慢）。
scenario_en: A feed mixes text, articles, images, short video, live, and link previews, each with different feature distributions and engagement patterns (video dwell is strong signal, text dwell may just mean slow reading).
q: 怎么让一个模型同时处理好这些异质内容？
q_en: How do you let one model handle these heterogeneous content types well?
why: 在共享骨干里插入稀疏激活的 MoE 层：一个学习到的路由器读内容类型 embedding，把每个样本路由到 top-K 个专家（如 8–16 里选 2），不同内容走不同专家、各自专精。只激活 K 个，推理算力恒定，不随专家数增长。
why_en: Insert sparsely-activated MoE layers into the shared backbone: a learned router reads content-type embeddings and sends each example to top-K experts (e.g. 2 of 8-16), so different content types get specialized experts at constant inference cost.
tradeoff: 稀疏 MoE（内容专精、推理算力恒定） vs 单一稠密骨干（异质内容互相拉平、学不专）
options: 给每种内容类型单独训一个完整模型，线上并行部署多套，服务成本翻倍
骨干里插稀疏 MoE 层：按内容路由到 top-K 专家
把图文、短视频、直播强行当成同一种内容统一处理
只保留短视频一种内容，其他内容类型直接不进召回
options_en: Train one full model per content type and serve several of them in parallel, doubling serving cost.
Insert sparse MoE layers in the backbone and route by content to top-K experts.
Force text posts, short video and live streams to be treated as one uniform content type.
Keep only short video and drop every other content type from retrieval.
whenOtherWins: 如果 feed 内容其实高度同质（如纯文本社区），稀疏 MoE 的专家专精没有用武之地，反而增加路由/负载均衡复杂度，普通稠密骨干更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If the feed is actually homogeneous (a text-only community), sparse MoE's specialization is wasted and adds routing/load-balancing complexity, so a plain dense backbone fits better.
optionExplanations: 每类一个完整模型服务成本高、丢共享，不如 MoE 在一个模型里专精。
对；稀疏 MoE 让路由器按内容类型挑专家，专精又保持推理算力恒定。
强行同质化会把视频停留和文本停留混为一谈，学不到内容差异。
丢掉其他内容类型直接放弃了 feed 的异质性，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: A full model per type is costly and loses sharing, worse than MoE specializing within one model.
Correct — sparse MoE routes by content type to experts, specializing while keeping inference cost constant.
Forcing homogeneity conflates video and text dwell, missing content differences.
Dropping content types abandons the feed's heterogeneity, missing the point.

termDefinitions.term: sparse MoE / 稀疏专家混合
termDefinitions.meaning: 在骨干里插入一组专家，路由器每次只激活 top-K 个专家，推理算力与专家总数无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse MoE inserts experts into the backbone where a router activates only top-K per example, so inference cost is independent of total expert count.

termDefinitions.meaning: MoE 里根据输入（内容类型/任务）决定把样本送给哪些专家的门控网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The router is the MoE gating network that decides which experts an example goes to, based on input like content type/task.

scenario: 同一个 feed 模型里既有 MMoE（任务级门控）也有稀疏 MoE（骨干内路由），你要说清两者插在哪、按什么路由。
scenario_en: The feed model has both MMoE (task-level gating) and sparse MoE (in-backbone routing); explain where each sits and how it routes.
q: 任务级 MMoE 和骨干内稀疏 MoE 的分工是什么？
q_en: How do task-level MMoE and in-backbone sparse MoE divide labor?
why: MMoE 在任务层：每个任务用自己的门控对共享专家加权，解决「任务间干扰」。稀疏 MoE 在共享骨干内：按内容类型（和任务）路由到 top-K 专家，解决「内容异质」。一个按任务分、一个按内容分，处理两种不同的异质性。
why_en: MMoE sits at the task level, each task gating shared experts to reduce task interference, while sparse MoE sits inside the backbone routing by content type (and task) to top-K experts for content heterogeneity.
tradeoff: MMoE（任务级门控、解任务干扰） vs 稀疏 MoE（骨干内路由、解内容异质）
options: 两者是同一个东西，只是插在网络的同一层上而已
MMoE 在任务层解任务干扰；稀疏 MoE 在骨干内解内容异质
MMoE 解内容异质、稀疏 MoE 解任务干扰，正好反过来
两者都只在推理时生效，训练阶段与它们完全无关
options_en: They are the same thing, just placed at the same layer of the network.
MMoE sits at the task level against task interference; sparse MoE sits inside the backbone against content heterogeneity.
MMoE handles content heterogeneity and sparse MoE handles task interference — the reverse.
Both take effect only at inference and are irrelevant during training.
optionExplanations: 两者位置和路由依据都不同，不是同一层的同一东西。
对；一个按任务分门控、一个按内容路由，分别解任务干扰与内容异质。
说反了：MMoE 解任务干扰，稀疏 MoE 解内容异质。
两者在训练时就参与学习门控/路由，不是只在推理。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in position and routing basis — not the same thing at one layer.
Correct — one gates by task, the other routes by content, addressing interference vs heterogeneity.
Backwards: MMoE addresses task interference, sparse MoE content heterogeneity.
Both learn gating/routing during training, not only at inference.

termDefinitions.term: task-aware gating / 任务感知门控
termDefinitions.meaning: 路由不仅看内容类型还看当前任务，防止一个任务的更新污染另一个任务依赖的专家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task-aware gating routes on content type and the current task, preventing one task's updates from corrupting experts another relies on.

scenario: 稀疏 MoE 上线后，你发现路由器几乎总是把样本送给固定的那 1–2 个专家，其他专家几乎不激活。
scenario_en: After deploying sparse MoE, the router almost always sends examples to the same 1-2 experts, leaving others idle.
q: 路由器坍缩到固定几个专家是什么问题，怎么修？
q_en: What's the router-collapse-to-few-experts problem, and how to fix it?
why: 没有负载均衡辅助损失，路由器会正反馈地坍缩到总选同 1–2 个专家：被选的专家越练越强、越发被选，其他专家荒废，MoE 退化成小稠密网、白养一堆专家。修法：加一个鼓励每 batch 内专家利用率均匀的惩罚项。
why_en: Without a load-balancing auxiliary loss the router collapses via positive feedback to always picking the same 1-2 experts, wasting the rest, fixed by a penalty encouraging even expert utilization per batch.
options: 毫无问题，路由器本来就该稳定地选那最好的一两个专家
缺负载均衡损失→坍缩到固定专家、其余荒废；加均衡惩罚项
说明专家总数太多，把专家数删到只剩两个就能解决
只是显存放不下的问题，扩显存或调小 batch 就没事了
options_en: No problem at all — the router should stably pick the best one or two experts.
Without a load-balancing loss the router collapses onto fixed experts while the rest idle; add a balancing penalty.
It means there are too many experts; cutting down to two fixes it.
It is only an out-of-memory issue; add memory or shrink the batch.
optionExplanations: 总用同一两个专家等于放弃了 MoE 的专精分工，不是理想状态。
对；负载均衡辅助损失打散路由、让专家都被用上，防止坍缩。
删专家治标不治本，坍缩根因是缺负载均衡而非专家多。
坍缩是路由分布问题，不是显存，加显存无关。
optionExplanations_en: Always using the same one or two experts abandons MoE's specialization — not ideal.
Correct — a load-balancing aux loss spreads routing so all experts are used, preventing collapse.
Cutting experts treats the symptom; the cause is missing load balancing, not too many experts.
Collapse is a routing-distribution issue, not memory; adding RAM is irrelevant.

termDefinitions.term: load-balancing auxiliary loss / 负载均衡辅助损失
termDefinitions.meaning: 鼓励每个 batch 里专家被均匀使用的惩罚项，防止路由器坍缩到少数专家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load-balancing auxiliary loss penalizes uneven expert use per batch, preventing the router from collapsing onto a few experts.

scenario: 每天数十亿次 feed 请求，要在 50ms p99 预算内做稀疏 MoE 排序。
scenario_en: Billions of daily feed requests, doing sparse MoE ranking within a 50ms p99 budget.
q: 「8 专家 + top-2 路由」这个配置在设计上意味着什么？
q_en: What does the '8 experts + top-2 routing' config imply for design?
why: 这是经验配置不是公式：8 个专家给够专精度，每次只激活 2 个让推理算力恒定、扛得住 50ms p99+数十亿请求。专家超过 16 个对排序收益递减、还更难部署。所以专家数是「专精 vs 部署/延迟」的经验平衡点。
why_en: It's empirical, not a formula: 8 experts give enough specialization and activating only 2 keeps inference cost constant to fit 50ms p99 at billions of requests, while beyond 16 experts gives diminishing returns and harder deployment.
options: 8 和 2 是要硬背的固定数字，换个延迟预算也不会变，没有设计逻辑
经验配置：8 专家保专精、top-2 保算力恒定
专家数量越多越好，冲到几百个
配置与延迟预算无关，只关准确率
options_en: 8 and 2 are fixed numbers to memorize, unchanged even if the latency budget shifts, with no design logic behind them.
Empirical config: 8 experts keep specialization, top-2 keeps compute constant.
More experts are always better; push to hundreds.
The config is unrelated to the latency budget, affects only accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个样本只激活得分最高的 K 个专家（如 top-2），使推理算力与专家总数无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K routing activates only the K highest-scoring experts per example (e.g. top-2), making inference cost independent of total experts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 请求延迟低于该值，这里 50ms 是给定的服务目标，约束模型算力预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value below which 99% of requests fall; here 50ms is a given target constraining the model's compute budget.

optionExplanations: 不是死记——8 和 2 是权衡专精度和延迟预算算出来的经验值，预算变了它们也会变。
对，这组数字是专精度和部署/延迟成本之间的权衡结果，不是要背的公式。
专家数不是越多越好：超过 16 左右调试和部署成本上升，收益却递减。
路由要跑的专家个数直接决定每次前向的计算量，这正是命中 p99 延迟的关键。
optionExplanations_en: Not for memorizing — 8 and 2 fall out of trading off specialization against the latency budget, and would shift if the budget changed.
Right — this pair is the tradeoff between specialization and deployment/latency cost, not a formula to recite.
More experts isn't always better: past roughly 16 the tuning and deployment cost climbs while gains flatten.
How many experts route per request directly sets the forward-pass compute, which is exactly what hits the p99 latency target.

scenario: 面试官让你横向比较 shared-bottom、MMoE、稀疏 MoE、每任务独立四种结构，说清各自最适合什么。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare shared-bottom, MMoE, sparse MoE, and separate-per-task, saying what each fits best.
q: 四种多任务/专家结构各自最适合什么场景？
q_en: What does each of the four MTL/expert structures fit best?
why: shared-bottom 适合同质内容、少任务；MMoE 适合多个部分冲突的目标；稀疏 MoE 适合异质 feed（推理算力恒定但需负载均衡）；每任务独立适合完全不相关的任务（零干扰但 N 倍服务成本）。按内容异质性和任务冲突程度选。
why_en: Shared-bottom fits homogeneous content with few tasks, MMoE fits several partially-conflicting objectives, sparse MoE fits heterogeneous feeds (constant inference but needs load balancing), and separate-per-task fits fully unrelated tasks (zero interference at N-times serving cost).

rows: 需负载均衡、有坍缩风险
无共享、N 倍服务成本

options: 同质少任务→shared-bottom；冲突目标→MMoE；异质→稀疏 MoE
四种结构的适用场景完全一样，选哪个只取决于团队熟悉度和成本
只有每任务独立模型可用，MMoE 和稀疏 MoE 门控在生产环境都会训不稳、梯度震荡
四种都只适合同质内容，遇到异质 feed 只能按类型拆成多个模型
options_en: Homogeneous with few tasks goes shared-bottom; conflicting objectives go MMoE; heterogeneous content goes sparse MoE.
All four fit exactly the same scenarios; the choice only depends on team familiarity and cost.
Only per-task separate models work; MMoE and sparse MoE gates both train unstably in production, with gradients oscillating.
All four only fit homogeneous content; a heterogeneous feed must be split into per-type models.
optionExplanations: 对；四种沿「内容异质×任务冲突」两轴各占一格，正好组成选型矩阵。
四种适用场景差别明显，不能随便选。
四种各有适用场景，独立模型只是其中一格，不是唯一。
稀疏 MoE 恰恰是为异质内容设计的，异质并非无解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the four span the 'content heterogeneity x task conflict' axes, forming the selection matrix.
Their fits differ clearly; you can't pick blindly.
Each fits a scenario; separate is just one cell, not the only choice.
Sparse MoE is built for heterogeneous content, so it's not unsolvable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组专家子网络加一个路由/门控，按输入选择性激活专家，兼顾容量与算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) combines expert sub-networks with a router/gate that selectively activates experts per input, balancing capacity and compute.

tradeoff: 共享程度 vs 任务隔离：越共享越省算力但干扰越大，越隔离越干净但服务成本按任务数翻倍。

scenario: 团队把排序目标设成最大化 P(点击)，A/B 里点击率短期确实涨了。
scenario_en: The team sets ranking to maximize P(click), and click-through rate does rise short-term in A/B.
q: 只最大化 P(点击) 会引发什么指标蚕食后果？
q_en: What metric-cannibalization consequence follows from maximizing only P(click)?
why: 只最大化点击会把标题党/激怒党排到最前：短期 A/B 点击赢了，但用户取关、28 天留存悄悄侵蚀。这就是指标蚕食——优化一个指标系统性损害另一个。Facebook 的「有意义社交互动」转向正是为纠此，压低被动参与、抬高评论深度。
why_en: Maximizing clicks ranks clickbait/rage-bait first — a short-term A/B click win — while users unfollow and 28-day retention silently erodes, the definition of cannibalization where optimizing one metric systematically harms another.
options: 毫无副作用，点击率涨了就是纯赢，可以直接全量上线不用观察留存
标题党被排前：短期点击赢但取关增加、28 天留存被侵蚀
点击涨会自动带动长期留存上升，是个意外的正向溢出
只影响推理服务器成本，对用户体验和留存都没有影响
options_en: No side effects — a click-rate win is a pure win, so ship it to everyone without watching retention.
Clickbait ranks first: short-term clicks win while unfollows rise and 28-day retention erodes.
Higher clicks automatically lift long-term retention, an accidental positive spillover.
It only affects inference server cost, with no impact on experience or retention.
optionExplanations: 短期点击赢掩盖了取关和留存下滑，不是纯赢。
对；单追点击奖励标题党、蚕食留存，MSI 转向正是压被动参与、抬评论深度来纠偏。
单追点击通常伤而非提升长期留存，不是好处。
这是用户体验/留存问题，不只是服务器成本。
optionExplanations_en: The short-term click win masks unfollows and falling retention — not a pure win.
Correct — chasing clicks rewards clickbait and cannibalizes retention; the MSI shift down-weights passive engagement to fix it.
Chasing clicks usually harms long-term retention, not helps it.
It's a UX/retention issue, not just server cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化一个指标（点击）系统性损害另一个（留存/满意度），短期赢长期输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric cannibalization is when optimizing one metric (clicks) systematically degrades another (retention/satisfaction), winning short-term while losing long-term.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 的排序转向，压低被动参与、抬高评论深度和回复链，对抗指标蚕食。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSI (Meaningful Social Interactions) is Facebook's ranking shift down-weighting passive engagement and up-weighting comment depth and reply chains.

scenario: 你想最大化参与度，但绝不能让创作者公平和有意义互动比例跌破底线。
scenario_en: You want to maximize engagement but must never let creator equity or meaningful-interaction ratio fall below a floor.
q: 该怎么把这个「有硬底线的多目标」落进损失/打分？
q_en: How do you encode this 'multi-objective with hard floors' into loss/scoring?
why: 用带护栏约束的多目标标量化：最大化参与度，同时约束「创作者公平 ≥ 阈值」「有意义互动比例 ≥ 底线」——这是约束优化，不是简单加权和。加权和会让参与度用高权重把护栏项换掉，约束式则强制底线不被牺牲。
why_en: Use multi-objective scalarization with guardrail constraints: maximize engagement subject to creator equity ≥ threshold and meaningful-interaction ratio ≥ floor, which is constrained optimization, not a plain weighted sum that would trade the guardrails away.
tradeoff: 带约束的标量化（护栏强制不被牺牲） vs 简单加权和（参与度可用权重换掉护栏）
options: 把所有目标直接加权求和，给参与度一个最大的权重，其余项权重压到很低
带护栏约束的标量化：最大化参与度，同时约束公平与互动≥底线
只保留参与度一个目标，护栏交给下游人工审核去兜底
每个目标各排一次序，再按随机权重把多个列表合并起来
options_en: Just weighted-sum all objectives, give engagement the biggest weight, and push the rest down low.
Scalarize with guardrail constraints: maximize engagement subject to equity and meaningful interaction staying above floors.
Keep engagement as the only objective and let downstream human review catch the rest.
Rank separately by each objective and merge the lists with random weights.
whenOtherWins: 如果各目标之间不冲突、也没有必须死守的硬底线，简单加权和更省事——约束优化的复杂度只在存在「不可牺牲的护栏」时才值得。
whenOtherWins_en: If objectives don't conflict and there's no hard floor to defend, a plain weighted sum is simpler — constrained optimization's complexity is only worth it when guardrails must not be sacrificed.
optionExplanations: 加权和里参与度用高权重就能把护栏项换掉，守不住硬底线。
对；约束式把护栏设成必须满足的下界，参与度无法用权重牺牲它。
删护栏就回到单追参与度、重新引发蚕食。
随机合并没有明确目标，无法保证护栏底线。
optionExplanations_en: In a weighted sum, a big engagement weight trades the guardrails away, failing the hard floor.
Correct — constraints set guardrails as must-satisfy lower bounds that engagement can't weight away.
Dropping guardrails returns to chasing engagement alone, re-triggering cannibalization.
Random merging has no clear objective and can't guarantee the floors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在满足护栏约束（如公平≥阈值）的前提下最大化主目标，而非简单加权求和。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constrained scalarization maximizes the primary objective subject to guardrail constraints (e.g. equity ≥ threshold), rather than a plain weighted sum.

scenario: 你手上有一批「点击率很高、但导致用户取关/静音」的帖子——典型的参与陷阱。
scenario_en: You have posts with high click rate that led to unfollows/mutes — classic engagement traps.
q: 怎么用这些蚕食案例直接改进排序？
q_en: How do you use these cannibalization cases to directly improve ranking?
why: 用对比损失从蚕食案例学：把「高点击但引发取关/静音」的帖子当硬负样本，加一个对比项，惩罚模型把这类「参与陷阱」排高。这样模型学会区分「真好」和「骗互动」，而不是只看点击。
why_en: Add a contrastive loss from cannibalization cases: use high-click-but-unfollow/mute posts as hard negatives with a contrastive term penalizing ranking such engagement traps high, teaching the model to tell genuine value from click-bait.
tradeoff: 对比损失惩罚参与陷阱（学会区分真好 vs 骗互动） vs 只用点击标签（把陷阱当好内容）
options: 把这些高点击帖子当正样本加权，进一步多推给用户
对比损失：把高点击却引发取关/静音的帖子当硬负样本
直接按关键词规则一刀切删掉所有高点击的帖子
忽略取关和静音信号，排序只相信点击这一个标签
options_en: Up-weight those high-click posts as positives and show them even more.
Contrastive loss: treat high-click-but-unfollow/mute posts as hard negatives.
Just delete every high-click post with a blanket keyword rule.
Ignore unfollow and mute signals and trust click as the only label.
whenOtherWins: 如果平台几乎没有可靠的取关/静音等负向长期信号，就没有蚕食案例可挖，只能先靠护栏约束或长期价值头兜底，而非对比损失。
whenOtherWins_en: If the platform lacks reliable negative long-term signals like unfollow/mute, there are no cannibalization cases to mine, so lean on guardrail constraints or a long-term-value head instead of contrastive loss.
optionExplanations: 当正样本会强化参与陷阱，恰恰放大蚕食，方向反了。
对；把参与陷阱当硬负样本、对比惩罚，让模型学会不被高点击骗。
一删了之丢掉信息，也无法让模型学到区分能力。
忽略取关就丢掉了纠正蚕食的关键负信号。
optionExplanations_en: Treating them as positives reinforces engagement traps, amplifying cannibalization — backwards.
Correct — engagement traps as hard negatives with contrastive penalty teach the model not to be fooled by high clicks.
Deleting them discards information and teaches the model no discrimination.
Ignoring unfollows drops the key negative signal for correcting cannibalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击/参与很高但损害长期体验的内容（标题党/激怒党），会引发取关静音。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An engagement trap is content with high clicks/engagement that harms long-term experience (clickbait/rage-bait), triggering unfollows/mutes.

scenario: 你想在最终打分里加入「这条帖子对 28 天留存的影响」，且希望不必每次都全量重训就能调短期 vs 长期的权衡。
scenario_en: You want to fold 'this post's 28-day retention impact' into the final score, tuning short vs long term without a full retrain each time.
q: 该用什么结构来注入长期价值？
q_en: Which structure injects long-term value?
why: 用长期价值头分解：一个独立塔预测每条帖子对 28 天留存的影响，用一个可调权重把它混进最终分。这样短期参与和长期价值解耦，调权重就能拨短期 vs 长期，不必全量重训整个模型。
why_en: Use a long-term value head decomposition: a separate tower predicts each post's 28-day retention impact, blended into the final score with a tunable weight, so you dial short vs long term by the weight without a full retrain.
tradeoff: 独立长期价值头+可调混合权重（解耦、免重训调权衡） vs 把长期目标硬塞主损失（每次调都要重训）
options: 把 28 天留存当成一个特征，直接塞进模型的输入层，训练服务两端都用
长期价值头：独立塔预测 28 天留存，可调权重混进最终分
只优化短期参与度，长期价值交给运营侧的活动去补
每次想调短长期权衡就把整个排序模型全量重训一遍
options_en: Feed 28-day retention in as just another input feature, used at both training and serving time.
A long-term value head: a separate tower predicts 28-day retention, blended in by a tunable weight.
Optimize short-term engagement only and let marketing campaigns cover long-term value.
Fully retrain the whole ranking model every time you want to shift the tradeoff.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品阶段明确只关心短期增长、长期留存暂不纳入优化，就可以先不加长期价值头，省掉延迟标签和额外塔的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product phase explicitly targets only short-term growth and defers long-term retention, you can skip the long-term value head, avoiding delayed-label and extra-tower complexity.
optionExplanations: 28 天留存是延迟标签、要预测的目标，当输入特征在服务时根本拿不到。
对；独立头预测长期影响、可调权重混合，短长期解耦，调权衡免重训。
不管长期价值就回到单追短期、重新蚕食留存。
每次全量重训成本高、迭代慢，正是解耦要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: 28-day retention is a delayed label to predict, unavailable as an input feature at serving.
Correct — a separate head predicts long-term impact and a tunable weight blends it, decoupling short/long term without retraining.
Ignoring long-term value returns to chasing short-term and re-cannibalizing retention.
Full retrains each time are costly and slow — exactly what decomposition avoids.

termDefinitions.term: long-term value head / 长期价值头
termDefinitions.meaning: 一个独立预测塔，估计每条内容对长期留存（如 28 天）的影响，混进最终打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-term value head is a separate prediction tower estimating each item's long-term retention (e.g. 28-day) impact, blended into the final score.

scenario: 长期价值头要预测 28 天留存，但 28 天留存的真标签只有等 28 天后才拿得到。
scenario_en: The long-term value head predicts 28-day retention, but the true label is only known after 28 days.
q: 延迟标签这个问题怎么解决，才能持续训练长期价值头？
q_en: How do you handle delayed labels to keep training the long-term value head?
why: 28 天留存是延迟标签，等满 28 天训练就太慢。用自举代理：先用早期信号（如 7 天回访）当近似标签立刻训起来，再定期用陆续成熟的真标签重训校准。这样既不停摆又能逐步逼近真实长期价值。
why_en: 28-day retention is a delayed label, so waiting 28 days is too slow — use bootstrapped proxies like 7-day return visits as approximate labels now, then periodically retrain on matured true labels to recalibrate.
options: 干等满 28 天，标签齐了之后再训一次长期价值头，中间完全不迭代
自举代理：先用 7 天回访当近似标签训，再用真标签重训校准
把 28 天留存当输入特征喂进去，绕开延迟标签的问题
放弃长期价值头，只用点击这类即时标签来做最终排序
options_en: Just wait the full 28 days and train the long-term head once labels land, with no iteration in between.
Bootstrapped proxies: train now on early signals like 7-day return, then recalibrate on matured true labels.
Feed 28-day retention in as an input feature to sidestep the delayed-label problem.
Drop the long-term value head and rank on immediate labels like clicks.
optionExplanations: 干等 28 天让模型迭代慢一个月，跟不上产品节奏。
对；7 天回访等代理先撑起训练，成熟真标签再定期校准，既快又逐步准。
延迟标签是要预测的目标，不能当输入特征（服务时拿不到）。
放弃长期价值头就回到单追短期、重新蚕食留存。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting 28 days slows iteration by a month, out of step with product pace.
Correct — proxies like 7-day return visits carry training now, and matured labels periodically recalibrate — fast and increasingly accurate.
The delayed label is the prediction target, not an input feature (unavailable at serving).
Abandoning the head returns to chasing short-term and re-cannibalizing retention.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要等一段时间才知道真值的标签（如 28 天留存），无法立即用于训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delayed label is one whose true value is known only after a delay (e.g. 28-day retention), unusable for immediate training.

termDefinitions.term: bootstrapped proxy / 自举代理标签
termDefinitions.meaning: 用早期可得信号（7 天回访）近似延迟标签先训练，待真标签成熟再校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bootstrapped proxy uses an early available signal (7-day return) to approximate a delayed label for training now, recalibrated when the true label matures.

scenario: 多任务训练里，点击任务的 σ_k 相对其他任务变得非常小。
scenario_en: In multi-task training, the click task's σ_k becomes very small relative to other tasks.
q: 点击 σ_k 相对变小，会对指标蚕食产生什么直接影响？
q_en: What's the direct cannibalization effect of a relatively small click σ_k?
why: σ 小 → 1/2σ² 大 → 点击损失被上调 → 点击主导共享表示 → 可能造成指标蚕食（把标题党排前，伤评论/留存）。所以监控 σ_k 不只是数值卫生，它直接关系到会不会重新滑向单追点击。
why_en: Small σ means the click loss is up-weighted, so click dominates the shared representation and can cause cannibalization, which is why monitoring σ_k directly bears on whether you slide back into chasing clicks.
tradeoff: 监控并约束点击 σ（防主导蚕食） vs 放任 σ 自由变小（点击独吞底座、蚕食其他目标）
options: 点击损失被上调、主导共享表示，可能直接引发指标蚕食
点击任务被彻底关掉，其他目标独占整个共享底座
对指标蚕食毫无影响，σ 只是训练内部的一个数值细节
所有任务的权重会同时变大，整体拟合能力一起变强
options_en: Click loss is up-weighted and dominates the shared representation, which can directly cause cannibalization.
The click task is switched off entirely, leaving the shared trunk to the other objectives.
No effect on cannibalization — sigma is just an internal training number.
All task weights grow together, so overall fitting capacity improves across the board.
whenOtherWins: 如果点击本就是当前阶段有意为之的主目标、且已有护栏约束顶住留存底线，那点击 σ 小可以接受——护栏在，就不会真的蚕食失控。
