termDefinitions.meaningEn: Near-real-time re-ranking uses an async worker on the engagement stream to refresh cached timelines within seconds, not per-read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 承载点赞、评论、点击等实时互动事件的消息流,供重排 worker 订阅。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The engagement stream is a message stream of real-time likes, comments, and clicks that the re-ranking worker subscribes to.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 流量突增,fan-out-on-write 的分发队列开始积压:帖子已提交但堆在队列里没分发出去。所有服务的 p99 延迟、错误率看着都正常。
scenario_en: Traffic spikes and the fan-out-on-write queue backs up: posts are submitted but sit undistributed. Every service's p99 latency and error rate look healthy.
q: 这个首要故障模式为什么危险,唯一可靠的发现手段是什么?
q_en: Why is this primary failure mode dangerous, and what is the only reliable way to catch it?
why: 危险在于系统看着健康(延迟/错误率都正常),但用户看到的是过时 feed——新帖卡在队列里没推到时间线。唯一可靠的捕捉是监控队列深度:队列积压是这个「静默过时」的直接信号。
why_en: It is dangerous because the system looks healthy (latency and errors normal) while users see stale feeds, and monitoring fan-out queue depth is the only reliable catch.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["发帖提交"] --> Q["fan-out 队列
积压"] Q -.卡住.-> T["粉丝时间线
未更新"] T --> U["用户看到过时 feed"] Q --> D["队列深度监控
唯一可靠信号"]
options: 危险在延迟飙升,靠 p99 latency 报警就能发现,报警一响就知道要处理
危险在系统看着健康、用户却见过时 feed,只有监控队列深度能可靠捕捉
危险在错误率上升,靠 5xx 计数就能发现,一看错误率曲线就清楚
危险在缓存命中率下降,靠命中率监控就能发现,命中率一跌就报警
options_en: The danger is latency spiking, and p99 latency alerts catch it the moment they fire.
The danger is the system looks healthy while users see stale feeds, and only monitoring queue depth reliably catches it.
The danger is error rate rising, and 5xx counts catch it as soon as the curve moves.
The danger is cache hit rate dropping, and hit-rate monitoring pages the moment it falls.
optionExplanations: 正因为延迟没飙升,p99 报警完全不会触发,这才是它隐蔽的原因。
对;积压不改变在线延迟/错误率,系统「看起来正常」,只有队列深度暴露新帖没被分发这个真相。
错误率也不升,请求都成功返回,只是返回的是旧内容,5xx 抓不到。
缓存照常命中(命中的是旧时间线),命中率监控看不出内容已过时。
optionExplanations_en: Precisely because latency does not spike, p99 alerts never fire — that is why it hides.
Correct — a backlog does not change online latency/errors, so the system 'looks fine'; only queue depth reveals undistributed posts.
Error rate does not rise either; requests succeed but return stale content, so 5xx misses it.
The cache still hits (on the stale timeline), so hit-rate monitoring cannot see the content is outdated.

termDefinitions.term: queue depth monitoring / 队列深度监控
termDefinitions.meaning: 跟踪 fan-out 分发队列里积压的消息数,是捕捉「静默过时 feed」的唯一可靠信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth monitoring tracks pending messages in the fan-out queue, the only reliable signal for silently stale feeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99 分位延迟:99% 的请求比这个值快,反映尾部最慢那批用户的体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the 99th-percentile response time — 99% of requests are faster — reflecting the slowest tail users' experience.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 监控显示 fan-out 队列深度 >10K 积压、用户报告 feed 过时,但完整重排模型的 p99 延迟仍在 SLA 之内。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows fan-out queue depth >10K and users report stale feeds, but the full re-ranker's p99 latency is still within SLA.
q: 该先动哪里?
q_en: Where should you act first?
why: 瓶颈在 fan-out 不在模型:模型 p99 正常说明排序算得动,问题是新帖卡在分发队列没进时间线。该扩 fan-out worker、并对「过时 feed 率」告警,而不是去动没问题的排序模型。
why_en: The bottleneck is fan-out, not the model — the re-ranker's p99 is fine, so scale up fan-out workers and alert on stale-feed rate rather than touching the healthy model.
tradeoff: 扩 fan-out worker(治真瓶颈、消积压) vs 优化排序模型(模型没问题、白费力)
whenOtherWins: 如果是模型 p99 超过 200ms 而队列深度正常,那瓶颈才在模型侧,该降级到轻量打分器或缩小候选集。
options: 扩容重排模型的 GPU,因为 feed 过时一定是排序太慢,先加卡再说
扩 fan-out worker 并对过时 feed 率告警,因为瓶颈在分发不在模型
回滚排序模型到上一版本,先止血再排查,反正模型换个版本总没错,完全不管队列到底有没有真正消退
提高缓存 TTL,让旧 feed 缓存更久以减压,先把队列压力糊过去
options_en: Scale up the re-ranker GPUs, since stale feeds must mean ranking is too slow — add cards first.
Scale up fan-out workers and alert on stale-feed rate, because the bottleneck is distribution, not the model.
Roll back the ranking model to the previous version to stop the bleeding first, on the theory any rollback is safe, completely ignoring whether the queue has actually drained at all.
Raise the cache TTL so stale feeds cache longer to relieve pressure, papering over the queue backlog.
optionExplanations: 模型 p99 在 SLA 内说明排序不慢,扩 GPU 治不了积压的分发队列,是找错了地方。
对;队列 >10K + 模型 p99 正常,明确指向 fan-out 分发瓶颈,扩 worker 消积压并对过时率告警才对症。
回滚模型无济于事,模型本来就健康,过时源自队列积压。
调高 TTL 只会让用户看到更旧的内容,是掩盖症状不是治瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: The model's p99 within SLA means ranking is not slow; scaling GPUs cannot clear a backed-up distribution queue — wrong target.
Correct — queue >10K with a healthy model p99 points squarely at the fan-out bottleneck, so scale workers and alert on stale rate.
Rolling back the model helps nothing; the model is healthy and staleness comes from the queue backlog.
Raising TTL just serves even older content, masking the symptom rather than fixing the bottleneck.

termDefinitions.term: fan-out worker / 分发工作进程
termDefinitions.meaning: 负责把新帖推进各粉丝时间线的后台进程,积压时可水平扩容来消化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fan-out worker is a background process pushing new posts into follower timelines, scaled horizontally to drain a backlog.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 一个排序模型不是突然崩,而是 CTR 每天悄悄跌 0.3%,没有任何单一硬阈值被击穿。
scenario_en: A ranking model does not crash; CTR quietly drops 0.3% per day with no single hard threshold ever breached.
q: 这种静默退化为什么难抓,该用什么监控?
q_en: Why is this silent degradation hard to catch, and what monitoring catches it?
why: 静默退化每天只跌一点、不触发任何硬阈值,盯单点阈值的告警看不见。要监控预测分数分布的漂移:把每小时打分直方图和 24 小时基线比,能提前抓到重训回归或特征管线故障导致的分布偏移。
why_en: Each day's tiny drop breaches no hard threshold, so threshold alerts miss it; monitor prediction score-distribution drift (hourly histogram vs 24h baseline) to catch it.
options: 靠 p99 延迟阈值,只要延迟没变就说明模型完全没有退化,盯着延迟曲线就够了
靠单一 CTR 硬阈值告警,跌破就报警,每天只跌一点永远不会触发
监控预测分数分布漂移:每小时直方图对比 24h 基线,抓分布偏移与重训回归
只看总请求量,量没跌就说明模型健康,量稳定时质量照样能烂掉
options_en: Rely on p99 latency thresholds; as long as latency is unchanged, watching the latency curve alone is enough to call the model completely healthy.
Rely on a single hard CTR threshold alert that fires on breach, but a tiny daily drop never trips it at all.
Monitor prediction score-distribution drift: hourly histogram vs a 24h baseline to catch distribution shift and retraining regressions.
Watch only total request volume; if volume holds, the model must be healthy, even while quality quietly rots.
optionExplanations: 延迟和模型质量退化无关,静默退化不会体现在延迟上。
单一硬阈值正是抓不到的原因——每天 0.3% 永远不会一次性击穿阈值。
对;分布漂移监控看的是形状变化而非单点越界,能在硬阈值被击穿前发现重训回归或特征故障。
请求量不反映排序质量,量稳定时 CTR 照样能慢慢烂掉。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is unrelated to quality degradation; silent decay does not show up in latency.
A single hard threshold is exactly why it is missed — 0.3% a day never breaches at once.
Correct — distribution-drift monitoring watches shape change, not a point breach, catching retraining regressions before any threshold trips.
Request volume does not reflect ranking quality; CTR can rot slowly while volume stays flat.

termDefinitions.term: score distribution drift / 分数分布漂移
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出分数的分布随时间偏离基线,常由重训回归或特征管线故障引起。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Score distribution drift is the model's output-score distribution moving away from baseline over time, often from retraining regressions or feature-pipeline failures.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 你要给 feed 排序搭一套三层监控,从系统健康一直看到业务生态。
scenario_en: You are building a three-layer monitoring stack for feed ranking, from system health to business ecosystem.
q: 这三层监控各看什么?
q_en: What does each of the three monitoring layers watch?
why: 三层各司其职:基建看延迟/队列/缓存/QPS,模型健康看分数漂移/特征新鲜度/null 率,业务看 unfollow/留存/创作者激活(7 天滚动窗)。
why_en: Infra watches latency/queue/cache/QPS, model health watches score drift/feature freshness/null rate, and business watches unfollow/retention/creator activation on 7-day windows.
options: 基建层看分数漂移、模型层看延迟、业务层看 CPU 使用率和内存占用,这是把三层各自该看的核心指标整个错配,谁都对不上号
基建看延迟/队列/缓存/QPS,模型健康看分数漂移/特征新鲜度/null 率,业务看 unfollow/留存/创作者激活
三层都只看 CTR,分别按分钟/小时/天聚合出三条一样的曲线,退化成单一指标反复看,看不出任何分层信息
基建看营收数字、模型看点击总数、业务看服务器数量和机房温度,三层量各归各错,完全没对上号
options_en: Infra watches score drift, model watches latency, and business watches CPU usage and memory — each layer's core metric is entirely mismatched with what it should watch, none lining up.
Infra watches latency/queue/cache/QPS, model health watches score drift/feature freshness/null rate, business watches unfollow/retention/creator activation.
All three watch only CTR, aggregated per minute/hour/day into three identical curves, reverting to one metric viewed three times with no layer-specific signal.
Infra watches revenue, model watches total clicks, business watches server count and datacenter temperature — every layer is paired with the wrong quantity.
optionExplanations: 层与指标错配:分数漂移属模型层、延迟属基建层,写反了。
对;基建管系统健康、模型管预测健康、业务管生态健康,三层各司其职、互不替代。
只看 CTR 就退回单指标监控,看不到延迟、漂移、创作者生态等不同层的问题。
营收/服务器数不是这三层的核心量,层与指标完全错位。
optionExplanations_en: Layers and metrics mismatched: score drift belongs to the model layer, latency to infra — reversed.
Correct — infra covers system health, model covers prediction health, business covers ecosystem health; each is distinct and non-substitutable.
Watching only CTR reverts to single-metric monitoring, missing latency, drift, and creator-ecosystem issues across layers.
Revenue/server count are not these layers' core quantities; layers and metrics are entirely misaligned.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征值距上次更新有多久,过时特征会让模型基于旧信息打分而悄悄退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature freshness is how recently a feature was updated; stale features make the model score on old information and degrade quietly.

termDefinitions.term: creator activation rate / 创作者激活率
termDefinitions.meaning: 创作者持续发帖/活跃的比例,反映内容供给侧生态健康。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator activation rate is the share of creators who keep posting and stay active, reflecting supply-side ecosystem health.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 线上给模型打分分布配了自动回滚:每小时算当前分数分布和 24 小时基线的差异,超阈值就自动回滚到上一版模型。
scenario_en: Production auto-rollback compares the current score distribution to a 24h baseline hourly and rolls back if it diverges past a threshold.
q: 用什么量衡量这个分布差异,阈值大概设在哪、触发后怎么办?
q_en: What measures this divergence, roughly what threshold, and what happens on trigger?
why: 用 KL 散度衡量当前分数分布相对 24h 基线的偏离,经验阈值约 >0.05 就自动回滚到上一版模型。这是自动止血:分布突变往往是重训回归或特征管线故障,先回滚再排查根因。
why_en: Use KL divergence of the current score distribution vs the 24h baseline, and a rule-of-thumb >0.05 triggers auto-rollback to the previous model.
options: 用准确率衡量,低于 90% 就回滚,但准确率需要标签、根本拿不到实时值
用 KL 散度衡量分布偏离,经验阈值约 >0.05 就自动回滚到上一版模型
用 p99 延迟衡量,超 200ms 就回滚模型,但延迟和分数分布是两回事
用 CTR 绝对值衡量,跌破历史均值就回滚,但季节和流量波动会天天误报
options_en: Measure with accuracy, roll back below 90% — but accuracy needs labels and is never available in real time.
Measure distribution divergence with KL divergence; a rule-of-thumb >0.05 auto-rolls back to the previous model.
Measure with p99 latency, roll back the model above 200ms — but latency and score distribution are unrelated signals.
Measure with absolute CTR, roll back when it drops below the historical mean, but seasonality and traffic noise would false-page daily.
optionExplanations: 准确率需要标签、有延迟,拿不到实时;这里要的是无标签就能算的分布偏离量。
对;KL 散度比较两个分布的距离,>0.05(经验阈值)触发自动回滚,先止血再查是重训回归还是特征故障。
延迟是基建层信号,和分数分布漂移是两回事,不该用来触发模型回滚。
CTR 绝对值受季节/流量波动干扰大,不如无标签的分布漂移灵敏且及时。
optionExplanations_en: Accuracy needs labels and is delayed, unavailable in real time; here you want a label-free distribution divergence.
Correct — KL divergence compares two distributions' distance, and >0.05 (rule of thumb) triggers auto-rollback to stop the bleeding before root-causing.
Latency is an infra signal, distinct from score-distribution drift, and should not trigger a model rollback.
Absolute CTR is noisy from seasonality/traffic; label-free distribution drift is more sensitive and timely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量两个概率分布差异的量,这里比较当前分数分布和 24h 基线,>0.05 触发回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KL (Kullback-Leibler) divergence measures the gap between two distributions, here current scores vs a 24h baseline, with >0.05 triggering rollback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控指标越界时自动切回上一个已知良好模型版本,先止血后排查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Auto-rollback automatically reverts to the last known-good model version when a monitored metric breaches, stopping harm before diagnosis.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 监控发现某个 top-10 重要特征的 null 率突然涨到超过 2%。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows a top-10 feature's null rate suddenly climbs past 2%.
q: 这通常意味着什么,该触发什么动作?
q_en: What does this usually mean, and what action should it trigger?
why: 重要特征 null 率飙升几乎总是上游特征管线出故障(数据源挂了、ETL 失败),模型只能拿缺失值打分、质量悄悄崩。动作:阻断本次模型更新并告警数据管线团队,先堵住坏特征进模型,再修上游。
why_en: A spiking null rate on a key feature almost always means an upstream feature-pipeline failure, so block the model update and alert the data-pipeline team.
options: 意味着用户变少了,应扩容服务器,但用户数和特征缺失完全是两件事
意味着上游特征管线故障,应阻断本次模型更新并告警数据管线团队
意味着模型过拟合,应立即重训一版,但过拟合不会表现成线上 null 率
意味着缓存过期,应清空缓存重建,但清缓存治不了特征值本身缺失
options_en: It means fewer users; scale up servers — but user count and missing features are unrelated problems.
It means an upstream feature-pipeline failure; block the model update and alert the data-pipeline team.
It means the model overfits; immediately retrain — but overfitting never shows up as a live null-rate spike.
It means the cache expired; flush and rebuild the cache — but a flush cannot fix values that are genuinely missing.
optionExplanations: null 率是特征质量信号,和用户数无关,扩容治不了缺失特征。
对;重要特征突然大量缺失指向上游数据源/ETL 故障,先阻断更新防坏特征进模型,再让数据团队修根因。
过拟合是训练问题,不会表现为线上特征 null 率突增,重训也不修上游故障。
缓存过期不会导致特征值为 null,清缓存无关这个数据管线故障。
optionExplanations_en: Null rate is a feature-quality signal unrelated to user count; scaling cannot fix missing features.
Correct — a key feature suddenly missing points to an upstream source/ETL failure; block the update to keep bad features out, then have data fix the root cause.
Overfitting is a training issue, not a live null-rate spike, and retraining does not fix an upstream failure.
Cache expiry does not null out feature values; flushing the cache is unrelated to this pipeline failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某特征取值为缺失/空的样本比例,突增通常暴露上游特征管线故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Null rate is the share of samples where a feature is missing; a spike usually exposes an upstream feature-pipeline failure.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 监控的业务结果层要在 7 天滚动窗上看 feed 排序对用户和创作者生态的长期影响。
scenario_en: The business-outcome layer watches feed ranking's long-term impact on the user and creator ecosystem on rolling 7-day windows.
q: 以下哪些属于业务结果层该监控的指标?(多选)
q_en: Which belong to the business-outcome monitoring layer? (multiple)
why: 业务结果层看关系和生态:unfollow 率、28 天留存、创作者激活率、创作者曝光 Gini,都在 7 天滚动窗上跑。推理 QPS 是基建层的吞吐信号,不属于业务结果。
why_en: The business layer watches relationships and ecosystem — unfollow rate, 28-day retention, creator activation, creator-impression Gini — on 7-day windows, while inference QPS is an infra metric.
options: unfollow 率——用户与创作者的关系流失
28 天留存——长期用户健康
创作者激活率与创作者曝光 Gini——供给侧生态健康与曝光公平
推理 QPS——每秒模型打分次数
options_en: Unfollow rate — user-creator relationship loss.
28-day retention — long-term user health.
Creator activation rate and creator-impression Gini — supply-side ecosystem health and exposure fairness.
Inference QPS — model scores per second.
optionExplanations: 对;unfollow 是关系流失的直接业务信号,7 天窗上看趋势。
对;28 天留存是长期用户健康的黄金指标,属业务结果层。
对;创作者激活率和曝光 Gini 守住供给侧生态,是业务层不可少的创作者视角。
错;推理 QPS 是基建层吞吐信号,反映系统压力而非业务生态结果。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — unfollow is a direct relationship-loss business signal, trended on a 7-day window.
Correct — 28-day retention is the gold long-term user-health metric, a business-layer concern.
Correct — creator activation and impression Gini guard supply-side ecosystem, the essential creator view at the business layer.
Wrong — inference QPS is an infra throughput signal reflecting system load, not a business-ecosystem outcome.

termDefinitions.meaning: 始终取最近 7 天数据聚合,平滑日间波动、看出中期趋势。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rolling 7-day window always aggregates the last 7 days to smooth daily noise and reveal medium-term trends.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 完整重排模型突然大量报错/超时,再等它恢复,用户就刷不出 feed 了。你要立刻止血。
scenario_en: The full re-ranker suddenly errors/times out en masse; waiting for recovery means users get no feed. You must stop the bleeding now.
q: 立即处置该怎么做?
q_en: What is the immediate response?
why: 立即处置两手:一是自动回滚到上一个已知良好 checkpoint;二是若完整排序器不健康,优雅降级到轻量首轮打分器——质量降一档但 feed 不断流。核心是先保可用,再中期排根因。
why_en: Auto-roll back to the last known-good checkpoint, and if the full ranker is unhealthy, gracefully degrade to the lightweight first-pass scorer so feeds keep flowing at lower quality.
tradeoff: 降级到轻量打分器(质量降一档但 feed 不断) vs 死等完整模型恢复(质量满但用户刷不出 feed)
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单次坏 checkpoint 上线、轻量打分器同样受影响,那直接回滚到上一版模型比降级更对症。
options: 停服等工程师查明根因后再恢复,避免降质,但用户直接刷不出 feed,可用性直接归零
自动回滚到已知良好 checkpoint;完整排序器不健康时降级到轻量首轮打分器,保 feed 不断流
把所有请求排队等完整模型恢复,宁慢不降质,结果延迟爆炸、请求堆积如山,用户照样刷不出 feed 来
直接关掉排序,给所有人按时间倒序展示,永久用这个兜底,放弃个性化,长期体验持续受损
options_en: Take the service down until engineers root-cause, avoiding any quality drop — but users get no feed at all and availability hits zero.
Auto-roll back to a known-good checkpoint; if the full ranker is unhealthy, degrade to the lightweight first-pass scorer to keep feeds flowing.
Queue all requests waiting for the full model to recover — slow but no quality loss — yet latency explodes, requests pile up like a mountain, and users still see nothing.
Turn off ranking and show everyone reverse-chronological permanently as the fallback, abandoning personalization and hurting experience for the long haul.
optionExplanations: 停服是最差止血,用户直接刷不出 feed,可用性归零。
对;先回滚到已知良好版本,不行就降级到轻量打分器,牺牲一档质量换 feed 持续可用,再中期查根因。
排队死等会让延迟爆炸、请求堆积,同样导致用户刷不出,不是止血。
永久退回时间倒序放弃了个性化,是长期损失;降级应是临时兜底而非永久方案。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the service down is the worst stop-gap; users get no feed and availability hits zero.
Correct — roll back to known-good, and if needed degrade to the light scorer, trading one quality tier for continuous availability, then root-cause.
Queuing and waiting explodes latency and piles up requests, also leaving users without a feed — not a fix.
Permanent reverse-chronological abandons personalization for a long-term loss; degradation should be a temporary fallback, not permanent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主组件故障时退到更简单但仍可用的组件(如轻量打分器),牺牲质量保可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation falls back to a simpler but still-working component (e.g. the light scorer) when the main one fails, trading quality for availability.

termDefinitions.term: known-good checkpoint / 已知良好检查点
termDefinitions.meaning: 此前验证过健康、可随时回滚到的模型版本快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A known-good checkpoint is a previously verified-healthy model snapshot you can roll back to at any time.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 止血之后进入中期处置,你要系统性地定位 feed 排序退化的根因。
scenario_en: After stopping the bleeding, the medium-term step is to systematically root-cause the ranking degradation.
q: 退化的根因通常落在哪三类?
q_en: Which three categories does the root cause usually fall into?
why: 三类根因:特征管线故障(特征过时/为 null)、数据分布漂移(如某类内容突然刷屏改变了输入分布)、模型回归(某次训练跑坏了但离线评估没抓到)。分门别类才能对症修复。
why_en: Three categories — feature-pipeline failure (stale/null), data distribution shift (a viral event flooding one content type), and model regression (a bad training run passing offline evaluation).
options: 特征管线故障、数据分布漂移、模型回归
服务器过热、网络抖动、磁盘写满
用户流失、营收下降、竞品上线
缓存击穿、DNS 解析失败、证书过期
options_en: Feature-pipeline failure, data distribution shift, model regression.
Server overheating, network jitter, disk full.
User churn, revenue decline, competitor launch.
Cache breakdown, DNS failure, certificate expiry.
optionExplanations: 对;这三类覆盖了模型退化的主要来源——输入坏(特征)、世界变(分布)、模型坏(回归),排查按此分流。
这些是通用基建故障,不针对排序模型质量退化,方向太泛。
这些是业务结果不是技术根因,回答不了「模型为什么变差」。
这些是网络/基建可用性故障,和排序模型的质量退化不是一类问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — these three cover the main sources of model degradation: bad inputs (features), a changed world (distribution), a broken model (regression).
These are generic infra failures, not specific to ranking-model quality degradation — too broad.
These are business outcomes, not technical root causes, and cannot explain why the model got worse.
These are network/infra availability failures, a different class from ranking-model quality degradation.

termDefinitions.term: data distribution shift / 数据分布漂移
termDefinitions.meaning: 线上输入分布偏离训练分布(如病毒事件让某类内容暴增),使模型预测失准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data distribution shift is live input drifting from training (e.g. a viral event flooding one content type), throwing off predictions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某次训练产出更差的模型却通过了离线评估,上线后才暴露质量下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model regression is a training run producing a worse model that passed offline eval, revealing degradation only in production.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 你想让 feed 更新鲜,于是提高近实时重排的频率,但工程师担心成本和尾延迟。
scenario_en: You want a fresher feed so you raise near-real-time re-ranking frequency, but engineers worry about cost and tail latency.
q: 新鲜度和延迟这个 dial 怎么权衡?
q_en: How does the freshness-vs-latency dial trade off?
why: 这是个连续 dial 不是开关:异步重排越频繁,feed 越新,但消耗更多算力、推高尾延迟(p99)和队列深度。要看着队列深度和 p99 去调这个旋钮,而不是一味求新。
why_en: It is a continuous dial — more async re-ranking means fresher feeds but more compute, higher tail latency, and deeper queues, tuned by watching queue depth and p99.
tradeoff: 重排更频繁(更新鲜) vs 更省算力/更低尾延迟(但稍旧)——看队列深度和 p99 调 dial
options: 新鲜度和延迟其实完全无关,可以同时拉满两者,不用看队列深度或 p99 这些监控指标
重排越频繁 feed 越新,但更耗算力、推高 p99 和队列深度,要看这两个指标调旋钮
只要加缓存就能同时做到最新鲜和最低延迟,没有权衡,权衡就此彻底消失不用再调
延迟只由网络决定,重排频率再高也不影响延迟,和算力、队列压力都无关
options_en: Freshness and latency are in fact entirely unrelated; you can max both at once without ever watching queue depth or p99.
More re-ranking means fresher feeds but more compute, higher p99, and deeper queues, tuned by watching those two.
Just add cache and you get both maximum freshness and minimum latency, no trade-off left, and the dial never needs tuning again.
Latency is set only by the network; re-ranking frequency does not affect it, unrelated to compute or queue pressure.
optionExplanations: 两者恰恰互相牵制,越追新鲜越费算力、越推高尾延迟,不能同时拉满。
对;这是连续 dial:频率↑→新鲜↑但算力/p99/队列↑,靠监控队列深度和 p99 找平衡点。
加缓存缓解读延迟,但更频繁的重排本身增加计算和尾延迟,权衡依然存在。
重排频率直接决定计算量和队列压力,进而影响 p99,不只是网络决定延迟。
optionExplanations_en: They constrain each other — chasing freshness costs compute and raises tail latency, so you cannot max both.
Correct — a continuous dial: higher frequency lifts freshness but also compute/p99/queue, balanced by watching queue depth and p99.
Cache eases read latency, but more frequent re-ranking itself adds compute and tail latency, so the trade-off remains.
Re-ranking frequency drives compute and queue pressure and thus p99; latency is not set by the network alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新鲜度与延迟的连续权衡:重排越勤越新但越费算力、尾延迟越高,是可调旋钮非开关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The freshness-vs-latency dial is a continuous trade-off: more re-ranking means fresher but costlier and higher-tail-latency, a knob not a switch.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 你想上一个更大的排序模型提升质量,但更大的模型推理更慢,可能击穿 200ms 的 p99 SLA。
scenario_en: You want a bigger ranking model for quality, but bigger means slower inference that may breach the 200ms p99 SLA.
q: 模型复杂度和服务预算这个 dial 怎么管?
q_en: How do you manage the model-complexity-vs-serving-budget dial?
why: 更大模型质量更好但更慢、易撑破 p99 SLA。用蒸馏(把大模型知识压进小模型)加两段式流水线来管这个 dial:让轻量首轮扫全量、只有 top-K 才跑重模型,在预算内拿到接近大模型的质量。
why_en: Bigger models give quality but risk the p99 SLA, so distillation plus a two-stage pipeline manage the dial — light scorer over all, heavy model only on top-K.
tradeoff: 更大模型(质量高但慢、险破 p99) vs 蒸馏+两段式(质量接近但守住延迟预算)
options: 无脑上最大模型,延迟问题靠加机器无限扩容解决,反正预算无上限
更大模型质量高但险破 p99,用蒸馏+两段式:轻量扫全量、重模型只跑 top-K
永远只用最小模型,牺牲质量换绝对最低延迟,不做任何两段式设计,彻底放弃质量上限
模型大小和延迟无关,选多大都不影响 p99,加卡也白加
options_en: Always ship the biggest model and solve latency by scaling machines infinitely, as if budget were unlimited.
Bigger models raise quality but risk p99, so use distillation plus two-stage: light scorer over all, heavy model only on top-K.
Always use the smallest model, sacrificing quality for the absolute lowest latency, with no two-stage design at all — completely forfeiting the quality ceiling.
Model size is unrelated to latency; any size leaves p99 unchanged, so adding GPUs would be pointless.
optionExplanations: 加机器降不了单请求的模型推理时间,p99 该破还是破,成本还爆炸。
对;蒸馏压缩计算、两段式让重模型只碰 top-K,既逼近大模型质量又守住 200ms 预算。
一味用最小模型放弃了质量上限,两段式本可在预算内兼顾质量,没必要走极端。
模型越大单次推理越慢,直接影响 p99,大小与延迟强相关。
optionExplanations_en: Adding machines does not cut per-request inference time; p99 still breaches and cost explodes.
Correct — distillation shrinks compute and two-stage runs the heavy model only on top-K, approaching big-model quality within the 200ms budget.
Always-smallest forfeits the quality ceiling; two-stage can balance both within budget, so the extreme is unnecessary.
Bigger models infer slower per request, directly affecting p99 — size strongly correlates with latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单请求可用的延迟/算力上限,模型复杂度必须被它约束住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving budget is the per-request latency/compute ceiling that model complexity must fit within.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 有人提议从「按用户各自时间线打分(local)」切换到「跨全平台内容统一打分(global)」以提升相关性。
scenario_en: A proposal switches from scoring within each user's timeline (local) to scoring across all platform content (global) for relevance.
q: 全局排序 vs 局部排序这个 dial,风险在哪?
q_en: For the global-vs-local ranking dial, where is the risk?
why: 全局排序常能提升相关性,但会把曝光分布推离小众创作者、拉高创作者 Gini,伤害多样性和公平——这是个带公平色彩的内容分发决策,不是纯技术开关。用创作者激活率来监测这种伤害。
why_en: Global ranking often lifts relevance but shifts impressions away from niche creators, raising Gini and harming fairness — a fairness-laden distribution decision, watched via creator activation rate.
tradeoff: 全局排序(相关性↑但曝光离开小众、Gini↑) vs 局部排序(多样性稳但相关性略低)
whenOtherWins: 如果平台正苦于内容同质、用户抱怨看不到全站好内容,且创作者 Gini 有余量,那切向全局排序换相关性是值得的。
options: 全局排序纯粹只提升相关性,没有任何副作用,应该无条件切换,不用看任何生态指标
全局排序提升相关性但把曝光推离小众创作者、拉高 Gini,是带公平色彩的分发决策
全局和局部排序结果完全一样,切换没意义,不影响相关性也不影响曝光
全局排序只影响延迟不影响曝光分布,是纯性能问题,和创作者公平无关
options_en: Global ranking purely and only improves relevance with no side effects at all, so switch unconditionally and skip watching any ecosystem metric.
Global ranking lifts relevance but shifts impressions away from niche creators and raises Gini — a fairness-laden distribution decision.
Global and local ranking give identical results, so switching is pointless — no change to relevance or exposure.
Global ranking affects only latency, not exposure distribution — a pure performance issue unrelated to creator fairness.
optionExplanations: 「无副作用」正是陷阱:全局排序会系统性地把曝光从小众挪向热门,损害多样性和公平。
对;相关性和创作者公平在这里对立,切全局要盯着 Gini 和创作者激活率,把它当分发决策而非纯技术选择。
两者结果不同——全局在更大候选集上比较,分布会明显偏移。
全局排序的核心影响是曝光分布(公平),不只是延迟,把它当纯性能问题会漏掉公平风险。
optionExplanations_en: 'No side effects' is the trap: global ranking systematically moves exposure from niche to popular, hurting diversity and fairness.
Correct — relevance and creator fairness conflict here, so switching to global demands watching Gini and creator activation as a distribution decision.
Results differ — global compares over a larger candidate set, visibly shifting the distribution.
Global ranking's core impact is exposure distribution (fairness), not just latency; treating it as pure performance misses the fairness risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: local 只在用户自己时间线内打分;global 跨全平台内容统一打分,相关性更高但易偏移曝光分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Local ranking scores within a user's own timeline; global scores across all platform content, lifting relevance but skewing exposure.

rows: 内容同质、用户抱怨看不到全站好内容
创作者 Gini 已偏高、需保多样性

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 一个实验显示 +2% CTR,像个明显的赢;但同一实验里创作者激活率 -1.5%。
scenario_en: An experiment shows +2% CTR (a clear win), but in the same experiment creator activation rate drops 1.5%.
q: 为什么必须同时看消费者侧和创作者侧指标?
q_en: Why must you monitor consumer-side and creator-side metrics jointly?
why: 只看消费者侧 CTR 会把它当赢,但创作者激活 -1.5% 说明供给侧生态在受损:创作者流失最终会掏空内容池、反噬长期消费体验。必须双侧联看,才能识破这种「看着赢、实则伤生态」。
why_en: CTR-only reads it as a win, but the -1.5% creator activation shows supply-side ecosystem harm that eventually hollows out content, so both sides must be watched together.
options: 只看 CTR 就已经够了,创作者指标是次要的,+2% 就该立刻上线,不用等创作者侧数据回来
双侧联看:+2% CTR 但创作者激活 -1.5% 说明供给侧受损,长期会反噬消费体验
只看创作者侧就够,消费者 CTR 不重要,消费体验可以先放一边慢慢再看
两侧指标独立无关,一个涨一个跌纯属巧合,和排序策略选择没有任何因果关系
options_en: CTR alone already suffices; creator metrics are secondary, so +2% should ship immediately without waiting for creator-side data to come back.
Watch both sides: +2% CTR but -1.5% creator activation signals supply-side harm that later hurts consumer experience.
Creator-side alone suffices; consumer CTR does not matter, so consumer experience can be set aside for later.
The two sides are independent; one up and one down is pure coincidence, with no causal link to the ranking policy chosen.
optionExplanations: 把创作者当次要正是踩坑：创作者流失会掏空内容供给，短期 CTR 赢换来长期崩。
对;消费和创作是同一生态的两端,创作者激活下降预示内容池萎缩,双侧联看才不被单侧假赢骗到。
只看创作者又走另一极端,消费者体验同样是平台命脉,不能偏废。
两者高度耦合:排序偏向刺激性内容常同时抬 CTR、压创作者激活,不是巧合。
optionExplanations_en: Treating creators as secondary is the trap: creator attrition hollows out content supply, trading a short-term CTR win for a long-term collapse.
Correct — consumers and creators are two ends of one ecosystem, and falling creator activation foretells a shrinking content pool, so joint monitoring avoids the one-sided false win.
Creator-only is the other extreme; consumer experience is equally the platform's lifeblood and cannot be ignored.
The two are tightly coupled: ranking toward sensational content often lifts CTR while suppressing creator activation — not coincidence.

termDefinitions.term: consumer-creator joint monitoring / 消费者-创作者联合监控
termDefinitions.meaning: 同时看用户侧 engagement 和创作者侧健康,识破「看着赢实则伤生态」的实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consumer-creator joint monitoring watches user engagement and creator health together to catch experiments that look like wins but harm the ecosystem.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: Staff+ 级答案不满足于「退化就回滚」,而是想让系统在创作者生态受损时自我纠偏。
scenario_en: A Staff+ answer is not content with 'roll back on degradation' and wants the system to self-correct when the creator ecosystem is harmed.
q: 面对创作者激活率持续下滑,Staff+ 会提出什么超越回滚的机制?
q_en: For a sustained drop in creator activation, what beyond-rollback mechanism does Staff+ propose?
why: Staff+ 提反馈回路:创作者激活率持续下滑时,自动触发重新校准目标函数的权重(比如上调创作者公平/多样性项),而不只是回滚到旧模型。这把公平从事后监控变成了目标函数里的闭环控制。
why_en: Propose a feedback loop where declining creator activation triggers re-calibrating the objective's weights (boosting fairness/diversity terms), not just rolling back to the old model.
options: 永远只回滚到旧模型,不改目标函数,下次遇到同样的创作者生态问题还会再退化
反馈回路:创作者激活持续下滑时自动重校目标函数权重(上调公平/多样性项),而非只回滚
直接关闭个性化排序,永久退回时间倒序,牺牲相关性也完全没解决目标函数权重失衡的问题
给所有创作者发放固定补贴,和排序目标解耦,治标不治本,权重照样失衡
options_en: Always just roll back to the old model without changing the objective, so the same creator-ecosystem problem degrades it again next time.
A feedback loop: sustained declining creator activation auto-recalibrates the objective weights (boosting fairness/diversity), not merely rollback.
Turn off personalized ranking and revert permanently to reverse-chronological, sacrificing relevance without ever fixing the imbalanced objective weights.
Give all creators a fixed subsidy, decoupled from the ranking objective, treating the symptom while the weights stay imbalanced.
optionExplanations: 只回滚是把系统拉回旧点,治不了「目标函数本身权重失衡」这个根因,下次照样退化。
对;把创作者激活当反馈信号去闭环调目标权重,让系统在生态受损时自动上调公平项,这才是 Staff+ 的生命周期视角。
关个性化是因噎废食,牺牲了相关性,也没解决目标权重问题。
发补贴是产品/运营手段,不改排序目标,治标不治本,和模型闭环无关。
optionExplanations_en: Rollback only returns to an old point and cannot fix the imbalanced objective weights, so it degrades again next time.
Correct — treating creator activation as feedback that auto-boosts fairness/diversity weights when the ecosystem suffers, not just rolling back — the Staff+ view.
Killing personalization overreacts, sacrifices relevance, and never addresses the objective-weight issue.
A subsidy is a product/ops lever that does not change the ranking objective — symptom relief, unrelated to a model feedback loop.

termDefinitions.term: objective re-calibration feedback loop / 目标校准反馈回路
termDefinitions.meaning: 用生态指标(如创作者激活)作反馈,自动上调目标函数里的公平/多样性权重,而非只回滚模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An objective-recalibration feedback loop uses ecosystem metrics like creator activation to auto-adjust fairness/diversity weights in the objective, beyond rollback.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 一场病毒事件让某一类内容(比如短视频)在几小时内暴增刷屏,排序质量随之走样。
scenario_en: A viral event floods one content type (say short video) within hours, and ranking quality warps.
q: 这属于哪类根因,为什么离线评估没提前抓到?
q_en: Which root-cause category is this, and why did offline evaluation miss it?
why: 属于数据分布漂移:线上输入分布突然偏离训练时的分布,模型没见过这种内容配比,预测失准。离线评估用的是历史静态数据,抓不到「未来才会出现的病毒式分布突变」,只能靠线上分布漂移监控发现。
why_en: It is data distribution shift — live input suddenly diverges from training — and offline evaluation on static historical data cannot foresee a future viral spike, so only online drift monitoring catches it.
options: 特征管线故障,因为特征值全变 null 了,是上游数据源或 ETL 挂了导致的
数据分布漂移:输入分布突变偏离训练分布;离线用历史静态数据,抓不到未来的病毒式突变
模型回归,因为训练脚本写错了,某次训练跑出了更差的权重却通过了离线评估
网络故障,因为流量太大打满带宽,是基建可用性问题而不是模型质量问题
options_en: Feature-pipeline failure, because all feature values turned null — the upstream data source or ETL job went down.
Data distribution shift: input distribution spikes away from training; offline uses static historical data and cannot foresee a future viral surge.
Model regression, because the training script had a bug and one run produced worse weights that still passed offline evaluation.
Network failure, because traffic saturated the bandwidth — an infra-availability problem, not a model-quality one.
optionExplanations: 特征没缺失,值是好的,只是内容配比变了,不是 null 问题。
对;病毒事件改变了输入分布,模型在训练时没见过这种配比;离线静态数据无法预见未来突变,得靠线上漂移监控。
训练脚本没错,模型本身是好的,退化来自世界变了不是模型坏了。
带宽满是基建可用性问题,和排序质量因分布突变而走样是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Features are not missing; values are fine — the content mix changed, not a null problem.
Correct — the viral event changed the input distribution the model never saw in training; static offline data cannot foresee it, so online drift monitoring is needed.
The training script is fine and the model is good; degradation is from the world changing, not a broken model.
Saturated bandwidth is an infra-availability issue, distinct from ranking quality warping from a distribution spike.

termDefinitions.term: viral distribution shift / 病毒式分布漂移
termDefinitions.meaning: 突发热点让某类内容短时暴增,线上输入分布偏离训练分布,模型预测失准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A viral distribution shift is a burst that floods one content type, moving live input off the training distribution and skewing predictions.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 同样是「设计 feed 排序的 serving 与监控」,L4 和 L5 答案差在哪。
scenario_en: For the same 'design feed-ranking serving and monitoring', how do L4 and L5 answers differ?
q: L5 答案比 L4 多了哪些关键要素?
q_en: What key elements does an L5 answer add over L4?
why: L4 泛谈 fan-out+缓存、点名 CTR/延迟,没有显式预算或自动回滚。L5 给出带明确预算(50/50/100ms)的三段式、写放大推理的混合 fan-out、含 KL 回滚的监控栈。
why_en: L4 vaguely names fan-out plus caching with no explicit budget or auto-rollback, while L5 gives budgeted staging (50/50/100ms), write-amplification-reasoned hybrid fan-out, and a monitoring stack with KL rollback.
tradeoff: L4(泛谈组件、serving 与监控分离) vs L5(显式预算、写放大推理、KL 回滚、护栏接告警)
options: L5 只是把 L4 的图画得更漂亮、配色排版更整齐一点,内容没有实质区别,面试官根本分不出高下
L5 加了显式延迟预算的三段式、按写放大推理的混合 fan-out、含 KL 回滚触发的监控栈、护栏接生产告警
L5 只多讲了用哪种编程语言、哪个前端框架去实现具体细节,和架构推理深度、取舍判断完全无关
L5 去掉了监控栈,专注把模型参数做得更大更贵,反而比 L4 讲得更少更空洞,整套监控闭环都彻底消失不见了
options_en: L5 just draws L4's diagram more nicely with tidier colors and layout, no substantive difference, and an interviewer could not tell them apart at all.
L5 adds budgeted three-stage pipeline, write-amplification-reasoned hybrid fan-out, a monitoring stack with KL rollback triggers, and guardrails wired to production alerting.
L5 only adds which programming language and frontend framework implement the details, entirely unrelated to architectural reasoning depth or trade-off judgment.
L5 drops the monitoring stack and focuses on making the model parameters bigger and pricier, ending up saying even less and emptier than L4, with the entire monitoring loop completely gone.
optionExplanations: 差别是实质性的推理深度,不是画图好看:L5 把每个选择的预算和触发条件都讲清了。
对;L5 的加分点是显式预算、写放大量化、自动回滚触发、护栏与告警联动,体现端到端的工程闭环。
语言选型不是分级依据,面试考的是架构推理与权衡。
L5 恰恰强化了监控(KL 回滚、护栏告警),不是去掉它。
optionExplanations_en: The gap is substantive reasoning depth, not prettier diagrams: L5 spells out each choice's budget and trigger.
Correct — L5's plus points are explicit budgets, quantified write amplification, auto-rollback triggers, and guardrail-alerting integration, showing an end-to-end loop.
Language choice is not a leveling criterion; interviews test architectural reasoning and trade-offs.
L5 strengthens monitoring (KL rollback, guardrail alerts) rather than dropping it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试评级:L4 讲基础组件,L5 加显式预算与监控闭环,Staff+ 跨生命周期推理生态权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leveling (L4/L5/Staff+) grades depth: L4 names components, L5 adds explicit budgets and monitoring loops, Staff+ reasons across the lifecycle and ecosystem trade-offs.

category: Social Feed Ranking Serving Monitoring Trade Offs

scenario: 广告平台为每个广告位取回一批候选广告,每个候选带有广告主出价 bid 和模型预测的点击率 pCTR,要决定谁胜出。
scenario_en: For each ad slot the platform retrieves candidate ads, each with an advertiser bid and a model-predicted click rate (pCTR), and must decide the winner.
q: 广告拍卖按什么排序、谁赢?这个量怎么算?
q_en: What quantity ranks the ad auction, who wins, and how is it computed?
why: 按 eCPM 排序、最高者胜,eCPM = pCTR × bid。它把「点击概率」和「愿付金额」乘起来,得到每次曝光的期望收入,平台据此选出对自己最有价值的广告。pCTR 只要差一点点,乘上巨量曝光就是数十亿营收的差别。
why_en: Rank by eCPM = pCTR × bid, highest wins — it multiplies click probability by willingness to pay into expected revenue per impression, so a tiny pCTR error scales to billions.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["候选广告
各带 pCTR, bid"] --> E["算 eCPM = pCTR × bid"] E --> R["按 eCPM 排序"] R --> W["最高者胜出展示"]
options: 按 bid 排序,出价最高者胜,pCTR 不参与拍卖
按 pCTR 排序,点击率最高者胜,bid 不参与拍卖
按 eCPM = pCTR × bid 排序,最高者胜
按广告主预算余额排序,余额最多的广告主胜出
options_en: Rank by bid, highest bidder wins, and pCTR does not enter the auction.
Rank by pCTR, highest click rate wins, and bid does not enter the auction.
Rank by eCPM = pCTR × bid, and the highest wins.
Rank by advertiser budget balance, and whoever has the most remaining budget wins.
optionExplanations: 只按 bid 会让高出价但没人点的广告霸屏,平台每次曝光的实际收入(要乘点击率)反而低。
只按 pCTR 忽略了广告主愿付多少,高点击但低价值的广告胜出,平台收入被压。
对;eCPM 把点击概率和出价相乘得到期望收入,兼顾「会不会被点」和「点了值多少钱」,这是拍卖的核心量。
预算余额是广告主的钱袋大小,不代表这次曝光的价值,不能用来排单次拍卖。
optionExplanations_en: Bid-only lets high-bid but never-clicked ads dominate, and the platform's actual per-impression revenue (times click rate) is lower.
pCTR-only ignores willingness to pay, so high-click low-value ads win and platform revenue is squeezed.
Correct — eCPM multiplies click probability by bid into expected revenue, balancing 'will it be clicked' and 'how much a click is worth', the auction's core quantity.
Budget balance is the advertiser's wallet size, not this impression's value, and cannot rank a single auction.

termDefinitions.fullName: effective Cost Per Mille (per thousand impressions)
termDefinitions.meaning: 每千次曝光的有效收入,eCPM = pCTR × bid,广告拍卖按它排序、最高者胜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: eCPM (effective Cost Per Mille) is expected revenue per thousand impressions, eCPM = pCTR × bid, ranking the auction with the highest winning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测的点击率,乘以出价得到 eCPM,是 CTR 系统的核心输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pCTR (predicted Click-Through Rate) is the model's predicted click probability, multiplied by bid to form eCPM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告主愿为一次点击或曝光支付的金额,拍卖里代表其对该展示的价值评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The bid is what an advertiser will pay per click or impression, representing their valuation of the placement.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 某个广告类目的 pCTR 被模型系统性高估。拍卖按 eCPM = pCTR × bid 排序。
scenario_en: A model systematically overestimates pCTR for an ad category. The auction ranks by eCPM = pCTR × bid.
q: 系统性高估 pCTR 最直接的后果是什么?
q_en: What is the most direct consequence of systematically overestimated pCTR?
why: 高估 pCTR 抬高了这类广告的 eCPM,让它们赢下本不该赢的拍卖,广告主为不转化的曝光付费、ROI 受损。这会侵蚀广告主信任,长期反噬平台营收,不是短期 eCPM 能弥补的。
why_en: Overestimated pCTR inflates that category's eCPM so it wins auctions it should not, and advertisers pay for non-converting impressions, eroding ROI and long-term trust.
options: 这类广告 eCPM 被抬高,赢下本不该赢的拍卖,广告主 ROI 受损
这类广告的曝光被系统性压制、排不上号,平台把该赚的营收留在桌上
对拍卖没有影响,因为排序只看广告间的相对高低,绝对值系统性偏差会自动抵消
只影响离线 AUC-ROC 这类排序指标,线上拍卖的分配结果完全不受影响
options_en: That category's eCPM is inflated, so it wins auctions it should not and advertiser ROI suffers.
That category's impressions are systematically suppressed and it can't rank, so the platform leaves revenue it should have earned on the table.
No effect on the auction, since ranking only looks at ads' relative standing and a systematic absolute bias cancels itself out.
Only offline ranking metrics like AUC-ROC are affected, while the live auction's allocation outcome is completely unchanged.
optionExplanations: 对;高估把 eCPM 顶上去,这类广告挤掉了真正更有价值的广告,广告主为白曝光买单、ROI 崩,信任受损。
这是「低估」的后果(压制、留营收在桌上),与高估方向相反。
高估不会抵消,因为不是所有类目都同等高估,被高估的类目会系统性挤占别人。
线上按 pCTR 定 eCPM 排序,高估直接改变谁胜出,分配一定受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — overestimation pushes eCPM up so this category crowds out genuinely more valuable ads, advertisers pay for wasted impressions, and ROI and trust collapse.
That is the consequence of underestimation (suppression, revenue left on the table), the opposite direction.
Overestimation does not cancel because not all categories are equally inflated; the overestimated one systematically crowds out others.
Live eCPM ranking uses pCTR, so overestimation directly changes who wins and definitely affects allocation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率与真实点击率不符;高估让广告赢下不该赢的拍卖,低估则压制好广告。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Miscalibration is predicted probabilities not matching true click rates; overestimation wins undue auctions, underestimation suppresses good ads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投资回报率,广告主视角=每花一块钱带来多少转化,pCTR 差会拉低它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ROI (Return On Investment) is conversions per dollar spent from the advertiser's view, degraded by poor pCTR.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 另一个广告类目的 pCTR 被模型系统性低估。
scenario_en: For another ad category, the model systematically underestimates pCTR.
q: 系统性低估 pCTR 会怎样,对谁不利?
q_en: What does systematically underestimated pCTR do, and who loses?
why: 低估 pCTR 压低了这类广告的 eCPM,让本该胜出的高价值广告被压制、拿不到曝光,平台把营收留在了桌上。它和高估是校准偏差的两个方向,都源自 pCTR 与真实点击率不符。
why_en: Underestimated pCTR lowers that category's eCPM, so genuinely high-value ads get suppressed and the platform leaves revenue on the table.
options: 这类广告 eCPM 被抬高,赢下本不该赢的拍卖,浪费广告主预算
这类高价值广告被压制、拿不到应有曝光,平台把营收留在了桌上
对拍卖无影响,低估会被其它类目自动补偿
只让广告主多赚,平台和用户都不受损
options_en: That category's eCPM is inflated, winning undue auctions and wasting advertiser budget.
These high-value ads are suppressed and lose deserved impressions, and the platform leaves revenue on the table.
No auction effect, since underestimation is auto-compensated by other categories.
It only helps advertisers earn more, with no loss to platform or users.
optionExplanations: 这是「高估」的后果(赢下不该赢、浪费预算),方向相反。
对;低估压低 eCPM,好广告排不上、失去曝光,平台少赚,这就是「营收留在桌上」。
不会自动补偿,被低估的类目会系统性地被别人挤下去。
低估让平台少赚、也可能让相关好广告触达不到用户,并非只利广告主。
optionExplanations_en: That is the overestimation consequence (winning undue auctions, wasting budget), the opposite direction.
Correct — underestimation lowers eCPM so good ads cannot rank and lose exposure, and the platform earns less — revenue left on the table.
No auto-compensation; the underestimated category gets systematically crowded out.
Underestimation costs the platform revenue and can starve relevant good ads from users, not merely helping advertisers.

termDefinitions.term: revenue left on the table / 留在桌上的营收
termDefinitions.meaning: 本可赚到却因定价/排序偏差没赚到的收入,低估 pCTR 是常见原因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Revenue left on the table is income the platform could have earned but did not due to pricing/ranking error, a common result of underestimating pCTR.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 候选说「我用 AUC-ROC 很高的模型,排序质量没问题」。但拍卖按 eCPM = pCTR × bid,pCTR 要当真实概率用。
scenario_en: A candidate says 'my model has high AUC-ROC, so ranking is fine.' But the auction uses eCPM = pCTR × bid, treating pCTR as a real probability.
q: 为什么光有高 AUC-ROC 不够,CTR 模型还必须满足什么?
q_en: Why is high AUC-ROC not enough, and what else must a CTR model satisfy?
why: AUC-ROC 只衡量排序/区分能力(能不能把会点的排前面),不管预测概率的绝对值对不对。拍卖要拿 pCTR 当真实点击率去乘 bid,所以模型必须校准良好(预测 0.05 就真是 5% 点击率),否则广告主 ROI 保证就崩了。
why_en: AUC-ROC measures only ranking/discrimination, not whether the predicted probability is right, but the auction uses pCTR as a true probability, so the model must be well-calibrated.
tradeoff: AUC-ROC(排序/区分,不看绝对值) vs log-loss/校准(绝对概率要对,拍卖必需)

rows: 预测 vs 观测对角线

options: 还必须校准良好——预测 0.05 就真是 5% 点击率,否则 eCPM 拍卖失真
还必须持续把 AUC-ROC 刷得更高,校准只是 AUC 提升后的副产品,无需单独处理
还必须把推理延迟压到两位数毫秒以内,校准和拍卖排序没有关系
不需要额外满足什么,AUC-ROC 高本身就代表预测概率一定准确可信
options_en: It must also be well-calibrated — a predicted 0.05 must mean a true 5% click rate, or the eCPM auction distorts.
It must keep pushing AUC-ROC even higher; calibration is just a by-product of higher AUC and needs no separate handling.
It must compress inference latency to double-digit milliseconds; calibration has nothing to do with auction ranking.
Nothing extra is needed — a high AUC-ROC by itself means the predicted probabilities are accurate and trustworthy.
optionExplanations: 对;拍卖把 pCTR 当真实概率乘 bid,所以绝对值必须准(校准),AUC 高但概率偏就会系统性错配 eCPM。
校准不是 AUC 的副产品:一个模型可以 AUC 完美却概率整体偏高/偏低,两者正交。
延迟是另一回事,这里的缺口是概率绝对值的准确性,即校准。
AUC 高只说明排序对,完全可能整体高估或低估概率,不能推出校准好。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the auction treats pCTR as a true probability times bid, so absolute values must be accurate (calibrated); high AUC with biased probabilities systematically misprices eCPM.
Calibration is not an AUC by-product: a model can have perfect AUC yet be globally over/under-confident — they are orthogonal.
Latency is separate; the gap here is the accuracy of absolute probabilities, i.e. calibration.
High AUC only means correct ranking and can still over/underestimate probabilities globally, so it does not imply calibration.

termDefinitions.fullName: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve
termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序/区分能力:随机取一正一负样本,正样本得分更高的概率;不反映绝对概率是否准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC-ROC measures ranking/discrimination — the chance a random positive outscores a random negative — and ignores whether absolute probabilities are right.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量预测概率与真实标签的差距,惩罚过度自信的错误,反映校准好坏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Log-loss (cross-entropy) measures the gap between predicted probabilities and true labels, penalizing overconfident errors and reflecting calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率与真实频率一致:预测 0.05 的那批曝光,实际点击率就是 5%。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration means predicted probabilities match true frequencies: impressions predicted at 0.05 truly click 5% of the time.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 面试官要你先讲清 CTR 系统里几方利益相关者的冲突,再谈架构。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to articulate the conflicting stakeholders in a CTR system before architecture.
q: CTR 系统的三方利益相关者及各自核心指标是什么?
q_en: Who are the three stakeholders in a CTR system and each one's core metric?
why: 三方三支柱:平台营收(总 eCPM/每千次曝光收入)、广告主 ROI(每次转化成本)、用户广告体验(负反馈率:隐藏/举报/不感兴趣)。三者利益冲突,讲清这张力和讲架构一样重要。
why_en: Three pillars — platform revenue (total eCPM), advertiser ROI (cost per conversion), and user ad experience (negative-feedback rate) — with conflicting interests.
options: 平台营收(eCPM)、广告主 ROI(转化成本)、用户负反馈率
算法团队、数据团队、运维团队三方,各自看的是模型迭代速度这类内部效率
GPU 成本、存储成本、带宽成本三项,反映的是基建开支占比而非业务指标
训练耗时、推理耗时、部署耗时三段,衡量的是工程流水线速度而非业务效果
options_en: Platform revenue (eCPM), advertiser ROI (cost per conversion), user negative-feedback rate.
Algorithm, data, and ops teams — three internal groups each tracked by model iteration speed.
GPU cost, storage cost, and bandwidth cost — three infrastructure spend shares, not business metrics.
Training time, inference time, and deployment time — three pipeline-speed metrics, not business outcomes.
optionExplanations: 对;平台、广告主、用户三方各有核心指标且彼此冲突,先点名这张力才是 framing 的重点。
内部团队不是产品的利益相关者维度,答不到业务张力。
基建成本是实现细节,不是三方业务利益冲突。
耗时是工程指标,和平台/广告主/用户的利益冲突无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — platform, advertiser, and user each have a core metric and conflict, and naming that tension is the point of framing.
Internal teams are not the product's stakeholder axis and miss the business tension.
Infra costs are implementation details, not the three-way business conflict.
Durations are engineering metrics, unrelated to platform/advertiser/user conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对广告点隐藏/举报/不感兴趣的比例,衡量广告相关性与体验损耗。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Negative-feedback rate is the share of users hiding/reporting/marking 'not interested', measuring ad relevance and experience harm.

termDefinitions.term: cost per conversion / 每次转化成本
termDefinitions.meaning: 广告主每获得一次转化所花的钱,衡量广告花费效率,pCTR 差会推高它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cost per conversion is what an advertiser spends per conversion, a spend-efficiency measure that poor pCTR inflates.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 产品想通过多塞广告、偏向高出价广告主来最大化本季度 eCPM,但你担心广告主 ROI 和用户体验。
scenario_en: The product wants to max this quarter's eCPM by serving more ads and favoring high-bidders, but you worry about advertiser ROI and user experience.
q: 为什么单纯最大化短期 eCPM 是危险的,该怎么补救?
q_en: Why is maximizing short-term eCPM alone dangerous, and how do you remedy it?
why: 短期塞满高价广告会拉低广告主 ROI(转化不划算)、拉高用户负反馈,广告主预算随之缩水、用户流失,长期营收反被反噬,不是短期 eCPM 能补的。补救是引入护栏指标,把广告主 ROI 和用户体验设成不可退化的约束。
why_en: Maxing short-term eCPM erodes advertiser ROI and user experience, shrinking budgets and retention so long-term revenue suffers, remedied by guardrail metrics on ROI and experience.
tradeoff: 最大化短期 eCPM(本季收入↑) vs 护栏保 ROI/体验(长期广告主预算与留存)
whenOtherWins: 如果是短期清库存/冲刺季度目标、且已知不会伤及核心广告主关系,适度提高广告负载去抓短期营收是可以接受的。
options: 危险:塞广告拉低 ROI、推高负反馈,反噬长期营收;补救=设护栏指标
不危险,eCPM 越高一定越好,广告主和用户会自动适应新的广告负载
危险只在于 GPU 推理成本上升,补救是买更多机器扩容
危险在模型 AUC 下降、精度不足,补救是换更大的排序模型
options_en: Danger: ad stuffing lowers ROI and raises negative feedback, hurting long-term revenue; remedy = guardrail metrics.
Not dangerous — higher eCPM is always better, and advertisers and users adapt to the new ad load.
The danger is only rising GPU inference cost, remedied by buying more machines to scale out.
The danger is falling AUC and weak accuracy, remedied by swapping in a bigger ranking model.
optionExplanations: 对;短期 eCPM 和长期健康冲突,塞广告伤 ROI 与体验→预算缩、用户走→长期营收受损,要用护栏把 ROI/体验钉成约束。
eCPM 无脑最大化正是坑:广告主和用户不会无限忍受低质高负载广告。
GPU 成本不是这里的核心张力,业务风险在广告主与用户侧。
AUC 是模型质量指标,这里的风险是业务层面的短期与长期营收冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — short-term eCPM conflicts with long-term health: ad stuffing hurts ROI and experience, shrinking budgets and churning users, so guardrails pin ROI/experience as constraints.
Blindly maxing eCPM is the trap; advertisers and users will not tolerate low-quality high-load ads indefinitely.
GPU cost is not the core tension here; the business risk is on the advertiser and user side.
AUC is a model-quality metric; the risk here is the business conflict between short- and long-term revenue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上线前预设的不可退化约束(如广告主 ROI、用户负反馈),防止短期营收透支长期健康。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a pre-set non-regression constraint (e.g. advertiser ROI, user negative feedback) preventing short-term revenue from mortgaging long-term health.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次会话展示的广告数量,过高会推高负反馈、损害留存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ad load is the number of ads shown per session; too high raises negative feedback and hurts retention.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 面试官提醒:把 log-loss 和 AUC-ROC 混为一谈会显得理解很浅。
scenario_en: The interviewer warns that conflating log-loss and AUC-ROC signals shallow understanding.
q: 补全两个离线指标各自衡量什么。
q_en: Complete what each offline metric measures.
text: log-loss(交叉熵)衡量的是 pCTR 的 {{校准}}(预测概率是否等于真实频率);AUC-ROC 衡量的是 {{排序}} 质量(能否把会点的排在前面)。拍卖要拿 pCTR 当真实概率,所以 {{log-loss}} 尤其关键。
text_en: Log-loss (cross-entropy) measures the {{calibration}} of pCTR (do predicted probabilities equal true frequencies); AUC-ROC measures {{ranking}} quality (are likely-clickers ordered first). Since the auction uses pCTR as a true probability, {{log-loss}} matters especially.
why: 一句话记牢:log-loss 管校准(绝对概率对不对)、AUC-ROC 管排序(相对顺序对不对)。拍卖乘 bid 用的是绝对概率,所以校准即 log-loss 是 CTR 的核心关切。
why_en: Log-loss governs calibration (absolute probability) and AUC-ROC governs ranking (relative order); the auction multiplies by bid using absolute probability, so calibration is core.

termDefinitions.meaning: log-loss 的别名,衡量预测概率分布与真实标签的差距,直接反映校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-entropy is another name for log-loss, measuring the gap between predicted probabilities and true labels and reflecting calibration.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 你要为 CTR 系统列一组指标,分别覆盖平台营收、模型质量、广告主和用户。
scenario_en: You are listing metrics for a CTR system covering platform revenue, model quality, advertiser, and user.
q: 以下哪些是合适的 CTR 系统评估指标?(多选)
q_en: Which are appropriate CTR system evaluation metrics? (multiple)
why: 合适的四个:总 eCPM/每千次曝光收入(平台营收)、log-loss(离线校准)、AUC-ROC(离线排序)、每次转化成本(广告主 ROI)。「模型参数量」是模型规模不是评估指标,不该混进来。
why_en: Appropriate: total eCPM (platform revenue), log-loss (offline calibration), AUC-ROC (offline ranking), cost per conversion (advertiser ROI); parameter count is model size, not a metric.
options: 总 eCPM / 每千次曝光收入——平台营收效率
log-loss 与 AUC-ROC——离线的校准与排序质量
每次转化成本——广告主花费效率与信任
模型参数量——模型有多少个权重
options_en: Total eCPM / revenue per 1K impressions — platform monetization efficiency.
Log-loss and AUC-ROC — offline calibration and ranking quality.
Cost per conversion — advertiser spend efficiency and trust.
Model parameter count — how many weights the model has.
optionExplanations: 对;总 eCPM 是平台营收效率的直接度量。
对;log-loss 管校准、AUC-ROC 管排序,是两个不能互相替代的离线质量指标。
对;每次转化成本反映广告主 ROI,差了会让预算缩水、伤长期营收。
错;参数量是模型规模,不衡量业务或质量效果,不是评估指标。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — total eCPM directly measures platform monetization efficiency.
Correct — log-loss governs calibration and AUC-ROC ranking, two non-substitutable offline quality metrics.
Correct — cost per conversion reflects advertiser ROI; a bad one shrinks budgets and hurts long-term revenue.
Wrong — parameter count is model size, measuring no business or quality outcome, so not an evaluation metric.

termDefinitions.term: revenue per 1K impressions / 每千次曝光收入
termDefinitions.meaning: 平台每展示一千次广告获得的收入,即 eCPM 的营收视角度量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Revenue per 1K impressions is what the platform earns per thousand ad shows, the revenue-side view of eCPM.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 从广告请求到返回胜出创意,整条管线必须在 100ms 内完成——这是 UX 和发布商合约给定的硬约束。
scenario_en: From ad request to returning the winning creative, the whole pipeline must finish under 100ms — a hard constraint from UX and publisher contracts.
q: 这个 <100ms 是怎么来的,它对架构意味着什么?
q_en: Where does the <100ms come from, and what does it mean for architecture?
why: <100ms 是 UX + 发布商合约给定的目标,不是算出来的。它是端到端墙钟预算,逼出一连串取舍:排除大 ensemble、把贵特征预计算进特征库、用两段式检索→排序,让重模型只打少量候选。
why_en: The <100ms is a given target from UX and publisher contracts, and as an end-to-end budget it rules out big ensembles, forces precomputed features, and motivates two-stage retrieval-then-ranking.
options: <100ms 是根据模型 FLOPs 反推出的算力物理下限,和业务体验无关
<100ms 是 UX/合约给定目标,作为端到端预算逼出预计算+两段式
<100ms 只是运维监控的告警阈值,超过了触发报警但不改变架构选型
<100ms 只是模型推理那一段的预算,和特征检索、拍卖序列化这些阶段无关
options_en: <100ms is a compute physical lower bound reverse-derived from model FLOPs, unrelated to business experience.
<100ms is a given UX/contract target, an end-to-end budget forcing precomputed features and two-stage serving.
<100ms is only an ops monitoring alert threshold — crossing it pages someone but does not change architecture choices.
<100ms is only the budget for the inference stage, unrelated to feature retrieval or auction serialization stages.
optionExplanations: 它不是算力推导,而是商务/体验给定的目标;架构要反向适配这个目标。
对;<100ms 是给定 SLO,端到端拆开后每一步都被压缩,直接导出排除大模型、预计算、两段式这些设计决策。
它是硬约束不是单纯告警线——正因为要卡 100ms,才决定了整套架构形态。
<100ms 是端到端预算,涵盖网络+渲染、特征检索、推理、拍卖序列化全部。
optionExplanations_en: It is not compute-derived but a business/experience target the architecture must fit backward.
Correct — <100ms is a given SLO; splitting it end-to-end squeezes every step, directly yielding no-big-model, precompute, and two-stage decisions.
It is a hard constraint, not a mere alert line — the 100ms cap shapes the whole architecture.
<100ms is an end-to-end budget spanning network+render, feature retrieval, inference, and auction serialization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告平台与展示广告的网站/App 之间的协议,常规定广告必须在多少 ms 内返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A publisher contract is the agreement between the ad platform and the site/app showing ads, often mandating the ad return within a latency bound.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 把 <100ms 的端到端预算拆到各阶段,你要说清每段大概花多少。
scenario_en: Splitting the <100ms end-to-end budget across stages, you must say roughly how much each takes.
q: 100ms 大致怎么分给各阶段,留给模型推理多少?
q_en: How is 100ms roughly split, and how much is left for model inference?
why: 大致:网络往返+渲染 ~60ms、特征检索 ~20ms、模型推理只剩 10-20ms、拍卖逻辑+序列化 ~10ms。推理窗口这么窄正是为什么要预计算特征、用两段式,把重模型省到只打几百个候选。
why_en: Roughly network+render ~60ms, feature retrieval ~20ms, inference only 10-20ms, auction+serialization ~10ms, and that tiny inference window forces precompute and two-stage.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  N["网络+渲染 ~60ms"] --> F["特征检索 ~20ms"]
  F --> M["模型推理 10-20ms"]
  M --> A["拍卖+序列化 ~10ms"]
options: 模型推理独占 80ms 的绝大部分预算,网络、特征检索和拍卖序列化全挤在剩下 20ms 内
网络+渲染 60ms、特征检索 20ms、推理 10-20ms、拍卖 10ms
全部 100ms 都算进模型推理的预算里,网络往返和页面渲染完全不占用时间
特征检索占掉 60ms,模型推理占 30ms,网络往返和渲染可以直接忽略不计
options_en: Model inference alone eats up 80ms of the budget, with network, feature retrieval, and auction serialization all squeezed into the remaining 20ms.
Network+render 60ms, feature retrieval 20ms, inference 10-20ms, auction 10ms.
All 100ms is counted toward the model-inference budget, and network round-trip and page rendering take up no time at all.
Feature retrieval eats up 60ms, model inference takes 30ms, and network round-trip and rendering can just be ignored.
optionExplanations: 推理拿不到 80ms;网络+渲染就吃掉约 60ms,推理只剩十几毫秒。
对;网络+渲染最重(~60ms)、特征检索~20ms、拍卖~10ms,推理被挤到 10-20ms,这决定了模型必须轻。
网络往返和渲染真实存在且占大头,不可能忽略。
特征检索约 20ms 不是 60ms;吃掉大头的是网络+渲染。
optionExplanations_en: Inference does not get 80ms; network+render alone eats ~60ms, leaving inference just over ten ms.
Correct — network+render dominates (~60ms), feature retrieval ~20ms, auction ~10ms, squeezing inference to 10-20ms, which forces a light model.
Network round-trip and rendering are real and dominant; they cannot be ignored.
Feature retrieval is ~20ms not 60ms; the dominant slice is network+render.

termDefinitions.meaning: 端到端预算里留给模型打分的时间(这里 10-20ms),窄到必须排除大 ensemble。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The inference window is the slice of the end-to-end budget left for model scoring (here 10-20ms), too narrow for big ensembles.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 模型推理只有 10-20ms 就要给几百个候选广告打分。有人想用一个大 ensemble 追求最高 AUC。
scenario_en: Inference has only 10-20ms to score hundreds of candidate ads. Someone wants a big ensemble for maximum AUC.
q: 大 ensemble 在这里为什么行不通?
q_en: Why won't a big ensemble work here?
why: 大 ensemble 单次推理慢,10-20ms 内给几百个候选打分根本跑不完,直接违反 <100ms 硬约束。serving 阶段要的是能在预算内打完全部候选的轻量模型,ensemble 的精度收益换不来超时的代价。
why_en: A big ensemble is too slow to score hundreds of candidates within 10-20ms, breaching the <100ms constraint, so serving needs a light model that finishes within budget.
options: ensemble 精度太低,融合后不如单个排序模型准
ensemble 推理太慢,10-20ms 打不完几百候选,超预算
ensemble 无法校准,概率永远不能用于 eCPM 拍卖
ensemble 只能离线训练评估,无法在线部署到 serving
options_en: Ensembles are too inaccurate — blending ends up worse than a single ranking model.
The ensemble is too slow — it cannot score hundreds of candidates in 10-20ms and blows the budget.
Ensembles cannot be calibrated, so their probabilities can never feed an eCPM auction.
Ensembles can only be trained and evaluated offline and cannot be deployed to online serving.
optionExplanations: ensemble 通常精度更高,问题不在精度而在延迟。
对;serving 卡 10-20ms 打几百候选,ensemble 的重推理跑不完,精度再高也超时,所以被排除。
ensemble 可以做校准,排除它的原因是延迟不是校准。
ensemble 可以在线部署,只是这里的延迟预算容不下它。
optionExplanations_en: Ensembles are usually more accurate; the issue is latency, not accuracy.
Correct — serving caps 10-20ms to score hundreds, and an ensemble's heavy inference cannot finish, so it is ruled out despite accuracy.
Ensembles can be calibrated; they are excluded for latency, not calibration.
Ensembles can be deployed online; here the latency budget simply cannot fit one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个模型的预测组合起来的方案,精度常更高但单次推理更慢,难满足严苛延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble combines several models' predictions for higher accuracy but slower inference, hard to fit tight latency budgets.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 一个强特征是用户过去 30 天的点击历史聚合,但在线现算它要扫大量日志,远超 20ms 的特征检索预算。
scenario_en: A strong feature is the user's aggregated 30-day click history, but computing it online scans huge logs, far beyond the 20ms retrieval budget.
q: 这类昂贵特征该怎么在线提供?
q_en: How should such expensive features be served online?
why: 把 30 天点击历史这类需要历史聚合的贵特征离线/流式预计算好,存进带 p99 保证的特征库,在线只做一次快速查表。请求路径上现算聚合会超时,预计算把重活挪到线下、在线只读。
why_en: Precompute expensive aggregations like 30-day click history into a feature store with p99 guarantees, so online serving is a fast lookup rather than an on-request scan.
tradeoff: 预计算进特征库(在线快查、但有新鲜度延迟) vs 在线现算(最新但超时,违反预算)
whenOtherWins: 如果一个特征完全由当前请求就能得出(如设备类型、时段),就该在线实时取,没必要预计算。
options: 预计算进带 p99 保证的特征库,在线只做快速查表,把聚合的重活挪到线下
每次请求都现算 30 天点击聚合,靠多加几台 CPU 机器硬扛,换取绝对最新
干脆放弃这个特征,只要计算成本高、拖慢延迟预算的特征就该整个丢弃
把用户 30 天点击历史整个塞进请求 payload,让客户端每次都上传
options_en: Precompute into a feature store with p99 guarantees and do a fast lookup online, moving the aggregation work offline.
Compute the 30-day click aggregation on every request, brute-forcing it with a few more CPU machines for absolute freshness.
Just drop this feature entirely — any feature whose compute cost eats into the latency budget should be discarded outright.
Stuff the user's whole 30-day click history into the request payload and have the client upload it every time.
optionExplanations: 对;历史聚合无法在 20ms 内现算,预计算存进特征库、在线快查,用 p99 保证读延迟,是标准解法。
现算聚合扫日志必然超时,加 CPU 也压不进 20ms 预算,代价和延迟都失控。
丢弃强特征白白损失精度;贵不等于该弃,预计算就是为了留住它。
让客户端上传 30 天历史不现实(数据量、隐私、可信度),也不是特征服务的路径。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a 30-day aggregation cannot be computed in 20ms, so precompute into a feature store and fast-lookup online with p99-guaranteed reads.
On-request aggregation scans logs and inevitably times out; more CPU cannot fit the 20ms budget, blowing cost and latency.
Dropping a strong feature forfeits accuracy; expensive does not mean discard — precompute keeps it.
Uploading 30-day history from the client is unrealistic (volume, privacy, trust) and is not the feature-serving path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中存储预计算特征、供在线低延迟读取的系统,常带 p99 读延迟保证(<5-10ms)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally holds precomputed features for low-latency online reads, often with a p99 read guarantee (<5-10ms).

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 每次广告请求有上千个候选,但推理只有 10-20ms,不可能用重模型给上千个都打分。
scenario_en: Each ad request has thousands of candidates, but inference is only 10-20ms — no way to score thousands with a heavy model.
q: 该用什么架构,各阶段分工是什么?
q_en: What architecture fits, and what does each stage do?
why: 两段式:轻量检索先用便宜信号把上千候选收窄到几百个,重排序模型再用更丰富特征给这几百个打分。它把昂贵计算限制在小候选集上,让整条管线卡进 <100ms。
why_en: Two-stage: lightweight retrieval narrows thousands to a few hundred with cheap signals, then a heavier ranking model scores the reduced set with richer features.
tradeoff: 两段式(重模型只打几百候选、进得了预算) vs 单段重模型(打上千候选、必超时)
whenOtherWins: 如果候选本来就只有几十个(小广告库、强定向),一段式重模型直接打完更简单也更准,不必两段。
diagram:
flowchart LR T["上千候选"] --> R["轻量检索
便宜信号收窄"] R --> H["几百候选"] H --> K["重排序模型
丰富特征打分"]
options: 单段:用一个重模型直接给上千候选全部打分,追求一次到位
两段式:轻量检索把上千收窄到几百,重排序模型再对这几百打分
随机采样几十个候选打分,其余全丢,省掉检索
把上千候选全发给客户端,让客户端本地排序
options_en: One stage: score all thousands of candidates with one heavy model for a one-shot result.
Two stages: lightweight retrieval narrows thousands to hundreds, then a heavier ranking model scores those.
Randomly sample a few dozen candidates to score and drop the rest, skipping retrieval.
Send all thousands to the client and let it rank locally.
optionExplanations: 重模型打上千候选在 10-20ms 内跑不完,单段方案直接违反延迟预算。
对;检索用便宜信号粗筛到几百,重模型只打这小集合,昂贵计算被限制住,整管线进得了 100ms。
随机采样会误杀好候选,粗筛应按信号保留最有希望的,不是靠运气。
客户端排序拿不到全量特征也无法保证一致与可信,不是可行架构。
optionExplanations_en: A heavy model over thousands cannot finish in 10-20ms; the one-stage plan breaches the budget.
Correct — retrieval coarse-filters to hundreds with cheap signals and the heavy model scores only that small set, fitting 100ms.
Random sampling kills good candidates; screening keeps the most promising by signal, not luck.
Client-side ranking lacks full features and consistency/trust — not a viable architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量检索把候选从上千收窄到几百,再用重排序模型精打分,兼顾延迟与精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage architecture narrows candidates from thousands to hundreds via light retrieval, then scores them with a heavier ranker, balancing latency and accuracy.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 用户在 2:00 看到广告,可能 2:15 才点、也可能永远不点。你在 2:05 用当时的标签重训模型。
scenario_en: A user sees an ad at 2:00, may click at 2:15 or never. You retrain at 2:05 using the labels available then.
q: 延迟反馈会让模型犯什么系统性错误?
q_en: What systematic error does delayed feedback cause?
why: 点击往往晚于曝光到达,近期曝光的正标签还没来,训练时被当成「没点击」。于是模型系统性低估近期曝光的 CTR,拍卖被扭曲,直到标签补齐才纠正。这是生产里的首要失效模式。
why_en: Clicks arrive after impressions, so recent positives are missing and counted as non-clicks, making the model systematically underestimate CTR for recent impressions until labels catch up.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  I["2:00 看到广告"] --> T["2:05 重训:标签未到"]
  T --> U["近期曝光被当未点击"]
  U --> B["系统性低估近期 CTR"]
  C["2:15 才点击"] -.补齐.-> B
options: 模型系统性高估近期曝光的 CTR,因为训练时把还没发生的未来点击提前算了进来
模型系统性低估近期曝光的 CTR,因为迟到的点击还没来、被当成没点击
模型完全不受延迟反馈影响,反正标签迟早会到,不影响当下这一轮训练
模型只是在离线评估指标上显得虚高,线上拍卖的分配结果不受任何影响
options_en: The model systematically overestimates recent CTR because training counts future clicks that haven't happened yet as if they already had.
The model systematically underestimates recent CTR because late clicks have not arrived and are treated as non-clicks.
The model is completely unaffected by delayed feedback; labels arrive eventually and this training round is unaffected.
The model only looks inflated on offline evaluation metrics; the live auction's allocation outcome is unaffected.
optionExplanations: 方向反了:迟到的是正标签(点击),缺失会让模型低估而非高估。
对;近期曝光的点击还在路上,训练时被记成负例,CTR 被系统性压低,直到标签补齐,拍卖期间被扭曲。
会影响:用不完整标签训练就是在用错误的负例,当下预测就偏了。
低估直接改变 pCTR→eCPM,线上分配一定受影响,不只是离线数字。
optionExplanations_en: Direction reversed — the late labels are positives (clicks), and their absence makes the model underestimate, not overestimate.
Correct — recent impressions' clicks are still in transit and counted as negatives, systematically depressing CTR until labels catch up, distorting the auction.
It does affect training: using incomplete labels means training on false negatives, biasing current predictions.
Underestimation changes pCTR→eCPM and definitely affects live allocation, not just an offline number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击/转化标签晚于曝光到达,近期曝光的正标签暂缺,使模型系统性低估近期 CTR。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delayed feedback is click/conversion labels arriving after impressions, so recent positives are missing and the model underestimates recent CTR.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 广告分布和用户兴趣快速变化,再叠加延迟反馈,一个训练好就不动的模型很快过时。
scenario_en: Ad distributions and user interests shift fast, and with delayed feedback a train-once model quickly goes stale.
q: 训练节奏该怎么定,为什么?
q_en: How should the training cadence be set, and why?
why: 小时级/天级持续重训:分布漂移快加上延迟反馈的标签补齐,都要求模型频繁吸收最新数据。太久不训,近期 CTR 低估和分布漂移会持续扭曲拍卖;频率过高则成本和不稳。
why_en: Retrain hourly/daily continuously, because fast distribution shift plus delayed-feedback label catch-up require frequently absorbing fresh data to keep the auction accurate.
tradeoff: 小时/天级重训(跟上漂移与标签补齐、但成本高) vs 训练一次不动(便宜但迅速过时、拍卖失真)
whenOtherWins: 如果某个广告场景分布极稳、几乎无新广告进入,拉长重训周期(如每周)可以省成本,不必小时级。
options: 训练一次永久部署,分布不会变,重训是浪费
小时级/天级持续重训,跟上分布漂移和标签补齐
只在 AUC 掉到某阈值以下才被动重训,平时完全不动
每分钟重训一次,越频繁一定越好、无副作用
options_en: Train once and deploy forever; distributions do not change, so retraining is waste.
Retrain continuously hourly or daily to keep up with distribution shift and late-arriving labels.
Retrain reactively only when AUC falls below a threshold, and otherwise leave the model untouched.
Retrain every minute; more frequent is always better with no downside.
optionExplanations: 广告分布和兴趣快速变化,训练一次很快过时,拍卖会被漂移和低估持续扭曲。
对;小时/天级重训让模型不断吸收最新数据和补齐的标签,是应对漂移+延迟反馈的标准节奏。
等 AUC 掉了才训是被动的,近期 CTR 低估在拍卖里已造成损失,应主动持续训练。
每分钟训成本高、易受噪声,过频不稳,小时/天级是成本与新鲜度的平衡点。
optionExplanations_en: Ad distributions and interests shift fast; a one-time model goes stale and the auction stays distorted by drift and underestimation.
Correct — hourly/daily retraining keeps absorbing fresh data and caught-up labels, the standard cadence for drift plus delayed feedback.
Waiting for AUC to drop is reactive; recent-CTR underestimation already costs the auction, so retrain proactively.
Per-minute retraining is costly and noise-prone; hourly/daily balances cost and freshness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按小时或天级节奏不断用最新数据重训模型,以跟上分布漂移和延迟反馈的标签补齐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous training retrains on fresh data at hourly/daily cadence to track distribution shift and delayed-feedback label catch-up.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 模型 AUC 不错,但预测概率整体偏高,拍卖里 eCPM 被系统性抬升。你要在几乎不加延迟的前提下修正校准。
scenario_en: The model has decent AUC but globally over-predicts, inflating eCPM in the auction. You must fix calibration with almost no added latency.
q: 该用什么后处理校准方法(L5 常见答案)?
q_en: Which post-hoc calibration method fits (a common L5 answer)?
why: 用 Platt scaling:在校准集上对模型 logits 拟合一个逻辑回归 p=σ(A·z+B),把整体偏移拉回对角线。它对单调型偏差有效、serving 只多一次 sigmoid,几乎零延迟,是默认首选。
why_en: Use Platt scaling — fit a logistic regression on the logits on a held-out set to pull predictions back to the diagonal, adding just one sigmoid at serving.
tradeoff: Platt scaling(单调偏差、几乎零延迟、默认) vs 复杂重训(更强但慢、常无必要)
whenOtherWins: 如果偏差是非单调的、Platt 拉不直,再上 isotonic regression(非参数单调阶梯),代价是更多数据和一张查表。
options: 重新从头训练一个参数更大的模型,期待它的预测概率能自然校准到对角线
Platt scaling:在校准集上对 logits 拟合逻辑回归
直接把所有 pCTR 乘上一个凭经验定的固定常数,不用校准集做任何拟合
干脆放弃后处理校准这一步,反正 AUC 已经很高、排序质量就没问题
options_en: Retrain a model with more parameters from scratch, hoping its predicted probabilities naturally land on the diagonal.
Platt scaling: fit a logistic regression on the logits over a held-out calibration set.
Just multiply every pCTR by a fixed constant chosen from experience, fitting nothing on a calibration set.
Just skip this post-hoc calibration step entirely, since AUC is already high and ranking quality is fine.
optionExplanations: 重训大模型成本高、也不保证校准,校准问题该用轻量后处理专门修。
对;Platt 在留出集上拟合 σ(A·z+B),把单调偏移拉回对角线,serving 只加一次 sigmoid,是默认低成本解。
乘固定常数不是拟合,救不了随分数变化的非线性偏移,还可能把概率推出 [0,1]。
AUC 高不代表校准好,拍卖乘 bid 用绝对概率,不校准会系统性错配 eCPM。
optionExplanations_en: Retraining a bigger model is costly and does not guarantee calibration; the fix should be a lightweight post-hoc step.
Correct — Platt fits σ(A·z+B) on a held-out set to pull monotonic bias back to the diagonal, adding just one sigmoid — the default low-cost fix.
A fixed constant is not a fit, cannot fix score-dependent nonlinear bias, and may push probabilities outside [0,1].
High AUC does not imply calibration; the auction multiplies by bid using absolute probability, so uncalibrated systematically misprices eCPM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后处理校准:在留出集上对模型 logits 拟合逻辑回归 p=σ(A·z+B),修单调型偏差,几乎零延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling is post-hoc calibration fitting a logistic regression p=σ(A·z+B) on logits over a held-out set, fixing monotonic bias at near-zero latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过 sigmoid 之前的原始分数,Platt scaling 就作用在它上面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A logit is the raw score before the sigmoid; Platt scaling operates on it.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 同一道 CTR 预测题,L4 和 Staff+ 的答案在框架深度上差别很大。
scenario_en: For the same CTR problem, L4 and Staff+ answers differ greatly in framing depth.
q: Staff+ 答案比 L4/L5 多出哪些框架要素?
q_en: What framing elements does a Staff+ answer add over L4/L5?
why: L4 定义问题+离线指标+简单模型;L5 加延迟-精度权衡、两段式、持续训练、校准。Staff+ 再加业务指标冲突、端到端基建、失效模式、监控护栏与组织级权衡。
why_en: Staff+ adds the business-metric hierarchy and stakeholder tensions, end-to-end infra, failure modes (delayed feedback, distribution shift), monitoring guardrails, and org trade-offs.
tradeoff: L4(定义+离线指标+基础模型) vs Staff+(业务层级+基建+失效模式+监控+组织权衡)
options: Staff+ 只是把 L4 的模型换成更大的深度网络,框架别无区别
Staff+ 加业务指标冲突、端到端基建、失效模式、监控护栏、组织权衡
Staff+ 只多讲用什么编程语言、训练框架和部署工具
Staff+ 反而省略 framing,直接上模型代码与实现细节
options_en: Staff+ just swaps L4's model for a bigger deep network, with no other framing difference.
Staff+ adds business-metric conflicts, end-to-end infra, failure modes, monitoring guardrails, and org trade-offs.
Staff+ only adds which programming language, training framework, and deployment tooling to use.
Staff+ actually skips framing and jumps straight into model code and implementation details.
optionExplanations: 差别不在模型大小,而在框架的广度与深度——业务、基建、失效、监控、组织。
对;Staff+ 的加分点是把技术决策接到业务利益冲突、失效模式、监控与组织权衡上,体现端到端 ownership。
语言/框架选型不是分级依据,考的是系统性推理。
Staff+ 恰恰更重 framing(可占 45 分钟的 10-15 分钟),不是跳过。
optionExplanations_en: The gap is not model size but framing breadth and depth — business, infra, failures, monitoring, org.
Correct — Staff+ ties technical choices to business conflicts, failure modes, monitoring, and org trade-offs, showing end-to-end ownership.
Language/framework choice is not a leveling criterion; systematic reasoning is tested.
Staff+ weights framing more (10-15 of 45 minutes), not less.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组织级选择:用一个共享 CTR 模型平台服务所有广告位,还是每个广告面各训一个模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An org trade-off is choosing a shared CTR model platform for all surfaces versus separate per-surface models.

rows: 共享 vs 各面独立

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 很多候选把 45 分钟几乎全花在画架构上,framing 一带而过。
scenario_en: Many candidates spend almost the whole 45 minutes on architecture and rush through framing.
q: 在 Staff+ 的 CTR 面试里,framing 大概该占多少时间,说明什么?
q_en: In a Staff+ CTR interview, roughly how much time should framing take, and what does that signal?
why: Staff+ 面试里光 framing 就可能占 45 分钟里的 10-15 分钟(经验目标,不是硬公式)。这说明评委看重「把问题定清楚」的能力:auction 数学、业务指标冲突、延迟约束,比急着画大架构更能体现级别。
why_en: Framing alone can take 10-15 of the 45 minutes (a rule of thumb), signaling that clearly defining the problem — auction math, business tensions, latency — matters more than rushing to architecture.
options: framing 应该压到 1-2 分钟以内,把剩下 40 多分钟全部留给画架构图
framing 可占 45 分钟里的 10-15 分钟,体现定义问题的能力
framing 应该占满 45 分钟里的 40 分钟,几乎不谈架构设计与深挖细节
framing 具体花多久由面试官临场抽签决定,和候选人的级别完全无关
options_en: Framing should be squeezed into 1-2 minutes at most, leaving the remaining 40-plus minutes entirely for drawing the architecture.
Framing can take 10-15 of the 45 minutes, showing you can define the problem.
Framing should fill 40 of the 45 minutes, leaving almost no time for architecture design or deep-dive detail.
How long framing takes is decided by the interviewer's mood on the spot, and has nothing to do with the candidate's level.
optionExplanations: 压到 1-2 分钟正是多数人的失误——跳过 framing 会暴露对问题理解的浅薄。
对;这段时间正好够把拍卖的乘法、三方指标张力、100ms 预算摆上台面,评委据此判级。
40 分钟只 framing 又走极端,架构与深挖同样重要,要平衡。
时间分配反映候选人的判断,不是随机,framing 深度与级别正相关。
optionExplanations_en: Squeezing to 1-2 minutes is exactly most people's mistake — skipping framing exposes shallow problem understanding.
Correct — that slice is just enough to put the auction multiplication, the three-way metric tension, and the 100ms budget on the table, which is what levels you.
40 minutes of only framing is the other extreme; architecture and deep-dives matter too, so balance.
Time allocation reflects the candidate's judgment, not randomness; framing depth correlates with level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在动手设计前先讲清目标、指标、约束和取舍,是高级别面试最被看重的环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Framing is clarifying goals, metrics, constraints, and trade-offs before designing, the most valued phase in senior interviews.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 面试官让你先把 CTR 模型的特征按来源和更新方式分门别类,再谈存储与服务。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to categorize CTR features by source and update pattern before discussing storage and serving.
q: CTR 特征通常分成哪四大家族?
q_en: What are the four feature families for CTR?
why: 四大家族:用户(user_id、CTR 等,基数达十亿)、广告(ad_id、类目等)、上下文(时段/设备,来自请求、实时)、交叉(user×类目,基数极高需 embedding)。来源、基数、更新频率不同,决定各自存储与服务方式。
why_en: User, Ad, Context, and Cross features — each differs in source, cardinality, and update frequency, which dictates how each is stored and served.
diagram:
flowchart TD F["CTR 特征"] --> U["用户
基数~十亿, 时/天更新"] F --> A["广告
基数~百万"] F --> C["上下文
来自请求, 实时"] F --> X["交叉
基数极高, 预计算/embedding"]
options: 训练集、验证集、测试集、线上集
用户特征、广告特征、上下文特征、交叉特征
数值特征、文本特征、图像特征、音频特征
整型、浮点、字符串、布尔四种数据类型
options_en: Training set, validation set, test set, online set.
User features, Ad features, Context features, Cross features.
Numeric, text, image, audio features.
Integer, float, string, boolean data types.
optionExplanations: 数据集划分不是特征家族,答非所问。
对;按语义来源分成用户/广告/上下文/交叉四类,每类的基数、来源、更新频率不同,直接决定存储与服务策略。
模态划分对广告 CTR 不合适,主体是类别与数值特征,不是图像音频。
数据类型是底层表示,不是按业务来源分的特征家族。
optionExplanations_en: Dataset splits are not feature families — off target.
Correct — by semantic source into User/Ad/Context/Cross, each with distinct cardinality, source, and update frequency driving storage and serving.
Modality splits do not fit ad CTR, which is mostly categorical and numeric, not image/audio.
Data types are low-level representations, not business-source feature families.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对某广告类目的历史偏好强度,是需历史聚合的预计算用户特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Category affinity is a user's historical preference strength for an ad category, a precomputed user feature needing history aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类别特征可取的不同值的总数,如 user_id 基数可达十亿。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of distinct values a categorical feature can take, e.g. user_id cardinality reaching a billion.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 单看用户特征和广告特征,模型抓不到「某类用户特别爱点某类广告」这种交互效应。
scenario_en: User and Ad features alone miss interaction effects like 'this user type especially clicks this ad type'.
q: 交叉特征解决什么问题,又带来什么代价?
q_en: What do cross features solve, and at what cost?
why: 交叉特征(如 user_id×广告主类目)捕捉单个家族看不到的交互效应,在 Wide & Deep 里是主要的记忆(memorization)机制。代价是它把特征空间组合式炸开、基数极高,这正是要用 embedding 去压的原因。
why_en: Cross features capture interaction effects individual families miss and are the main memorization mechanism in Wide & Deep, but they explode the feature space combinatorially, motivating embeddings.
tradeoff: 交叉特征(抓交互、强记忆) vs 组合爆炸(基数极高、需 embedding 压缩)
whenOtherWins: 如果两个字段之间没有真实交互(相互独立),硬造交叉只会加剧稀疏、白占空间,不如不做。
options: 交叉特征把 user_id 和广告主类目合并成一个联合 ID,借此降低整体基数,是节省存储的压缩手段
交叉特征捕捉家族间交互效应,是 Wide & Deep 的记忆机制,代价是特征空间组合式爆炸
交叉特征只把卷积网络提取的图像像素块编码进模型,只用于图像输入,和类别特征毫无关系
交叉特征只是加快了梯度反向传播、让模型更快收敛,不会带来任何额外的存储代价
options_en: Cross features merge user_id and advertiser_category into one joint ID, lowering overall cardinality — a storage-saving compression technique.
