Summing scores is meaningless: three weak signals added do not equal one strong signal and fake high confidence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分数分布的不确定度；类别分数越均匀熵越高，代表模型越困惑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entropy is the uncertainty of the score distribution; more even category scores give higher entropy and more model confusion.

scenario: 两条内容 Tier 1 违规分同为 0.6，一条无人问津，另一条正在被高速转发、触达飙升。
scenario_en: Two items both score 0.6, but one is ignored while the other is being rapidly reshared with surging reach.
q: 同样的违规分下，正在病毒式传播的内容路由该怎么处理？
q_en: At the same violation score, how should the router treat rapidly-spreading content?
why: 对病毒式内容路由要更快、更保守——降低升级/处置门槛，宁可多误升一点。因为传播速度放大危害：同样 0.6 分，扩散中的内容留着的期望代价高得多，等人工慢慢审就晚了。
why_en: Route viral content faster and more conservatively by lowering the action bar, because velocity amplifies harm and the expected cost of leaving it up rises with reach.
tradeoff: 病毒内容更保守（更快处置、少漏危害，但可能多误删）vs 一视同仁（省事，但高传播内容漏判代价大）
options: 两条都按 0.6 一样处理，传播速度不该影响审核判定
病毒的那条反而降优先级，等热度过了再慢慢审，省当下算力
对病毒内容更快更保守：降低处置/升级门槛，因传播放大危害
只要没超 0.9 就都放行，传播快只是自然流量、不必干预
options_en: Treat both the same at 0.6; spread velocity should not affect the moderation call.
Deprioritize the viral one and review it later once the hype cools, to save compute now.
Treat viral content faster and more conservatively by lowering the action/escalation bar, since spread amplifies harm.
Pass anything under 0.9; fast spread is just organic traffic and needs no intervention.
whenOtherWins: 若内容明确合规（低分低熵）或平台就是要鼓励传播（如已审核的官方公告），则不必因传播就更保守，避免误伤热门好内容。
optionExplanations: 忽略传播速度就是忽略危害的放大器：同分下扩散中的内容期望损害高得多。
越热越拖等于让危害在传播峰值时最大化，正好反了。
对；传播速度是危害的放大系数，路由要按期望代价而非静态分数来决策。
把病毒传播当中性流量，会让有害内容在扩散高峰期无人拦截。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring velocity ignores the harm amplifier: at the same score, spreading content has far higher expected damage.
Delaying the hotter item maximizes harm right at the peak of spread — exactly backwards.
Correct — velocity is a harm multiplier, so routing should decide by expected cost, not static score.
Treating viral spread as neutral traffic leaves harmful content unchecked at its peak reach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容已经或即将被多少用户看到，与危害规模成正比。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reach is how many users have or will see the content, proportional to the scale of harm.

scenario: 路由器还会看发帖账号本身：它是常年守规的老号，还是新注册、有违规史的可疑号。
scenario_en: The router also considers the posting account: a long-standing compliant one versus a new or previously-flagged suspicious one.
q: 路由特征里的「作者风险等级」是什么、怎么用？
q_en: What is the router's 'author risk tier' feature and how is it used?
why: 作者风险等级=从账号历史、账号年龄、行为模式推出的信任度。低信任作者（新号、有违规史）→ 路由更保守、更容易升级；高信任老号 → 同样分数可给更多自动放行的余地。它是内容分数之外的先验。
why_en: Author risk tier is a trust level derived from account history, age, and behavior, so low-trust authors get more conservative routing while trusted accounts earn more benefit of the doubt.
options: 从账号历史、年龄、行为推出的信任度，低信任→更保守路由
作者的粉丝数排名，粉丝越多内容越可信、越该自动放行
作者所在地区的法律风险等级，只用于决定内容存储在哪个数据中心
作者账号的付费订阅等级，付费用户内容免审
options_en: A trust level derived from account history, age, and behavior; lower trust means more conservative routing.
The author's follower-count rank; more followers means more trustworthy content and more auto-pass.
The legal-risk level of the author's region, used only to decide which data center stores the content.
The author's paid-subscription tier, exempting paying users from moderation.
optionExplanations: 对；账号信任度是内容分之外的先验，帮路由在同样分数下对可疑作者更谨慎。
粉丝多≠守规，大 V 反而传播广、危害大，不能用粉丝数当免审依据。
存储选址是合规/延迟问题，与「这条该不该升级」的路由判断无关。
按付费免审会被滥用，且与内容是否违规毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — account trust is a prior beyond the content score, helping the router be warier of suspicious authors at the same score.
More followers do not mean compliant; big accounts spread wider and can do more harm, so follower count is no exemption.
Storage location is a compliance/latency concern, unrelated to whether this item should escalate.
Exempting paying users invites abuse and has nothing to do with whether content violates policy.

termDefinitions.term: author risk tier / 作者风险等级
termDefinitions.meaning: 由账号历史、年龄、行为模式算出的信任分层，作为路由的先验信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Author risk tier is a trust bucket computed from account history, age, and behavior, used as a routing prior.

scenario: Meta 的路由用「置信走廊」决定升级：只有落在某个不确定区间内的分数才交给人工。
scenario_en: Meta's router uses a 'confidence corridor' for escalation: only scores inside an uncertainty band go to humans.
q: 置信走廊是怎么工作的，走廊宽度按什么定？
q_en: How does the confidence corridor work, and what sets its width?
why: 走廊=一段不确定带：分数低于带→明显合规、自动放行；高于带→明显违规、自动删除；落在带内→升级人工。走廊宽度按每类别成本比校准——误删代价高的类别把走廊调宽，宁可多送人工。
why_en: The corridor is an uncertainty band: below it auto-passes, above it auto-removes, and inside it escalates, with width per category calibrated from that category's cost ratio.
tradeoff: 走廊宽（多升级、少误判，但人工负载高）vs 走廊窄（少升级、省人工，但边界误判多）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  S["每类校准置信分"] --> B{"落在不确定走廊?"}
  B -->|低于走廊 明显合规| P["自动放行"]
  B -->|高于走廊 明显违规| R["自动删除"]
  B -->|走廊内| E["升级人工"]
options: 分数越高越升级，走廊就是一条越过就升级的单一上界
走廊是固定的全局区间，对所有类别用同一段带宽，按季度统一评审调整一次
带内升级、带外自动处置；走廊宽度按每类别的误删/误放成本比校准
走廊宽度按当前 GPU 余量动态调，算力多就调宽
options_en: The higher the score the more you escalate; the corridor is a single upper bound you escalate past.
The corridor is a fixed global band, the same width for every category, reviewed and adjusted once a quarter.
Inside the band escalate, outside auto-act; corridor width is calibrated per category from its false-positive/false-negative cost ratio.
Corridor width flexes with current GPU headroom, widening when compute is abundant.
whenOtherWins: 若某类别自动模型已极准、误判代价又低（如明显垃圾广告），可把走廊收到几乎为零，几乎全自动，不必留升级带。
optionExplanations: 升级不是「越高越升」，而是「越不确定越升」——明显违规的高分反而该自动删。
各类别成本比不同，用同一段全局走廊会在高危类别上要么漏放要么误升。
对；走廊是不确定带，宽度由成本比定，代价高的类别调宽多送人工。
走廊宽度是策略/成本决策，不该被临时算力余量牵着走，否则准确度随机波动。
optionExplanations_en: Escalation is not 'higher means escalate' but 'more uncertain means escalate'; clearly violating high scores should auto-remove.
Different categories have different cost ratios, so one global band mishandles high-severity ones.
Correct — the corridor is an uncertainty band whose width comes from the cost ratio, widening for costly categories to send more to humans.
Corridor width is a policy/cost decision and should not follow transient compute headroom, which would make accuracy fluctuate randomly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段不确定分数带：带内升级人工、带外自动处置，宽度按类别成本比定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A confidence corridor is an uncertainty band where in-band scores escalate and out-of-band scores auto-act, its width set by per-category cost ratio.

scenario: 路由器本质是在自动与人工之间连续分配审核产能这条边界。
scenario_en: The router essentially allocates review capacity along the boundary between automation and humans.
q: 路由偏得太自动、或太人工，各会带来什么后果？
q_en: What happens if routing leans too far toward automation, or too far toward humans?
why: 太偏自动→假阳性上升、误删好内容、侵蚀用户信任；太偏人工→审核队列过载、有害内容删除被延迟。路由器要持续优化这条产能分配边界，两头都是灾难。
why_en: Too far toward automation raises false positives and erodes trust; too far toward humans overwhelms the queue and delays removals, so the router continuously optimizes that capacity boundary.
tradeoff: 偏自动（快、省人工，但假阳性↑、信任↓）vs 偏人工（准，但队列过载、删除延迟）
diagram:
flowchart TB R["路由器 分配产能边界"] --> A["偏自动化过猛"] R --> H["偏人工过猛"] A --> AF["假阳性上升
误删好内容 侵蚀信任"] H --> HF["审核队列过载
有害内容删除被延迟"]
options: 两头都会让延迟下降，因为分配越极端、路由判断逻辑越简单、决策越快
太偏自动→假阳性↑误删侵蚀信任；太偏人工→队列过载、删除延迟
太偏自动只会漏判（假阴性），太偏人工只会误删（假阳性）
两头没有实质差别，路由怎么设结果都一样，是可忽略的旋钮
options_en: Both extremes lower latency, because a more extreme split makes the routing logic simpler and decisions faster.
Too automated raises false positives that erode trust; too human overwhelms the queue and delays removals.
Too automated only causes misses (false negatives); too human only causes wrongful removals (false positives).
There is no real difference; routing settings don't change outcomes, so it's a negligible knob.
optionExplanations: 偏人工恰恰让删除变慢、队列变长，说延迟一律下降是错的。
对；这是产能分配的两难，路由器要持续在两个失败模式间找平衡点。
方向搞混了：太偏自动是把模糊内容也强行处置→误删（假阳性）上升，不是只漏判。
路由直接决定误删率、删除时延和成本，是全系统最关键的旋钮之一。
optionExplanations_en: Leaning human actually slows removals and lengthens the queue, so claiming latency always drops is wrong.
Correct — it is a capacity dilemma, and the router must keep balancing between these two failure modes.
The direction is mixed up: too automated forces action on fuzzy content, raising wrongful removals, not just misses.
Routing directly sets wrongful-removal rate, removal latency, and cost — one of the most critical knobs in the system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在自动层与人工层之间分配处理量的决策，路由器持续优化这条边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Capacity allocation is dividing workload between the automated and human tiers, a boundary the router continuously optimizes.

scenario: 上线一个静态分类器后，团队想「先跑着，之后再说」。几个月后对抗性内容（新黑话、新规避手法）不断演变。
scenario_en: After shipping a static classifier, the team plans to 'just let it run', but months later adversarial content keeps evolving with new slang and evasions.
q: 为什么内容审核必须有反馈回路，没有会怎样？
q_en: Why must content moderation have a feedback loop, and what happens without one?
why: 反馈回路把静态分类器变成持续改进的系统：人工判定回流成标签→重训模型。没有它，对抗方不断演变新规避手法，分类器会随时间退化，越用越漏。回路是抵消这种漂移的引擎。
why_en: The feedback loop turns a static classifier into a continuously improving system by recycling human verdicts into labels, without which the model degrades as adversarial patterns evolve.
diagram:
flowchart LR M["静态分类器 打分"] --> D["Tier3 人工判定
确认/推翻/新类别"] D --> L["标签库 含元数据"] L --> Q["质量控制
多标注+仲裁+校准"] Q --> RT["按计划或漂移重训"] RT --> M
options: 没有反馈回路，分类器随对抗手法演变而退化、越用越漏
反馈回路只是可有可无的监控看板，不影响模型本身的准确度
静态分类器一旦训好就永久有效，反馈回路存在只是为了省算力开销
反馈回路的作用是加快推理延迟，把 100ms 压到更低
options_en: Without a feedback loop the classifier decays as adversarial tactics evolve and misses more over time.
The feedback loop is just an optional dashboard and doesn't affect the model's accuracy.
A static classifier stays valid forever once trained; the feedback loop only exists to save compute.
The feedback loop's job is to cut inference latency, pushing 100ms even lower.
optionExplanations: 对；对抗方持续进化，回路用人工标签重训是让模型不退化的唯一持续手段。
回路直接决定重训数据，是准确度的命脉，不只是看板。
「训好即永久」正是错的：分布漂移会让静态模型逐月失效。
回路管的是训练数据与模型更新，与单次推理延迟无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — adversaries keep evolving, so retraining on human labels via the loop is the only ongoing way to stop degradation.
The loop directly determines retraining data and is the lifeblood of accuracy, not just a dashboard.
'Trained means permanent' is exactly wrong: distribution drift makes a static model decay month over month.
The loop governs training data and model updates, not single-request inference latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把人工判定回收为标签、重训模型的闭环，让分类器随时间持续改进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The feedback loop recycles human verdicts into labels and retrains the model so the classifier keeps improving over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布随时间变化（如新对抗手法），使旧模型逐渐失准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift is the shift of live data distribution over time, such as new evasions, that gradually makes an old model inaccurate.

scenario: 反馈回路要有标签才能重训，而这些标签必须来自可信来源。
scenario_en: The feedback loop needs labels to retrain, and those labels must come from a trusted source.
q: 反馈回路的训练标签主要来自哪里、包含哪些取值？
q_en: Where do the feedback loop's training labels mainly come from, and what values do they take?
why: 标签来自 Tier-3 人工判定，取值有：确认（模型对了）、推翻（模型错了）、新类别（出现了未定义的违规）。这三种覆盖了模型该学的正误与盲区，是回路里质量最高的信号。
why_en: Labels come from Tier-3 human decisions taking values confirmed, overturned, or new-category, covering where the model was right, wrong, or blind.
options: 来自 Tier 1 分类器自己的高置信预测，模型确信就当标签
来自 Tier-3 人工判定：确认 / 推翻 / 新类别三种取值
来自用户举报的原始计数，举报多即判为违规标签
来自随机生成的合成样本，用规则模拟违规文本
options_en: From Tier 1's own high-confidence predictions, treating the model's certainty as the label.
From Tier-3 human decisions taking three values: confirmed / overturned / new-category.
From raw user-report counts, labeling as a violation whatever gets many reports.
From randomly generated synthetic samples simulating violating text by rules.
optionExplanations: 拿模型自己的预测当标签是自我强化，只会把现有偏差固化，学不到新东西。
对；人工判定是最可信的地面真值，三种取值覆盖正确、纠错、盲区。
举报数噪声大、可被刷，作为原始标签会灌进大量误判。
合成样本可作补充，但覆盖不了真实对抗演变，不能当主标签源。
optionExplanations_en: Using the model's own predictions as labels is self-reinforcing, freezing existing bias and learning nothing new.
Correct — human decisions are the most trusted ground truth, and the three values cover right, corrected, and blind spots.
Report counts are noisy and gameable, so as raw labels they inject many wrong verdicts.
Synthetic samples can supplement but can't cover real adversarial evolution, so they can't be the primary label source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工发现一种模型还没定义的违规类型，提示需要扩展分类体系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A new-category label is a human spotting a violation type the model hasn't defined yet, signaling the taxonomy needs extending.

scenario: 标签库不只存「这条是否违规」，还给每条标签挂了一堆元数据。
scenario_en: The label store keeps not just 'violation or not' but a bundle of metadata per label.
q: 标签为什么要连同 reviewer ID、审核时长、reviewer 置信、原始预测一起存？
q_en: Why store labels together with reviewer ID, review time, reviewer confidence, and the original prediction?
why: 这些元数据是为了调试和质控：reviewer ID 能追溯某人是否系统性偏差；审核时长与置信度标记出仓促/勉强的标签；原始预测让你分析模型在哪类内容上被推翻。没有它们，标签只是黑箱，出问题无从归因。
why_en: The metadata enables debugging and quality control — tracing reviewer bias, flagging rushed or low-confidence labels, and analyzing where the model gets overturned.
tradeoff: 存元数据（可调试、可归因，但存储与流程更重）vs 只存结论（省事，但出问题无从追溯）
options: 为了给 reviewer 按标注量发薪，元数据只用于计件结算
为了满足法规存档，元数据与模型训练和质控无关
为了调试与质控：追溯 reviewer 偏差、看模型在哪被推翻
为了压缩存储，把标签连同元数据打包成一条记录能省磁盘空间
options_en: To pay reviewers by labeling volume; the metadata is only for piece-rate payroll.
To satisfy regulatory archiving; the metadata is unrelated to training or quality control.
For debugging and QC: tracing reviewer bias and seeing where the model gets overturned.
To compress storage: bundling labels together with metadata into one record saves disk space.
whenOtherWins: 若只是临时打个小规模基准、标签用完即弃，可以只存结论、省掉元数据——但生产级反馈回路几乎总要留痕以便归因。
optionExplanations: 计件结算是行政副用途，不是存这些元数据的核心动机。
合规存档可能顺带需要，但元数据的主目的是喂给质控与模型分析。
对；元数据让标签可归因、可审计，是发现标注漂移和模型盲区的前提。
元数据只会增加而非减少存储，用它省空间说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Piece-rate payroll is an administrative side use, not the core reason to keep this metadata.
Compliance archiving may be incidental, but the metadata's main purpose is feeding QC and model analysis.
Correct — metadata makes labels attributable and auditable, the prerequisite for catching label drift and model blind spots.
Metadata increases storage, not decreases it, so using it to save space is backwards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 审核员对自己这次判定有多确定，低置信标签在重训时可降权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reviewer confidence is how sure a reviewer is about their verdict; low-confidence labels can be down-weighted in retraining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型当初给出的判定，与人工结论对比可定位模型在哪类内容出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The original prediction is the model's initial verdict, compared with the human's to locate where the model errs.

scenario: 人工标签本身也会有噪声——审核员之间会分歧、判定标准会随时间漂。
scenario_en: Human labels are themselves noisy: reviewers disagree and criteria drift over time.
q: 反馈回路里有哪些标签质量控制手段？（多选）
q_en: Which label-quality controls belong in the feedback loop? (multiple)
why: 三类质控：高危内容用 ≥2 名独立审核员看标注一致性；分歧走仲裁流程（资深审核员裁决）；定期校准会统一判定尺度、压住标签漂移。让单个审核员一票定高危、或让审核员互相看答案，都会引入而非消除偏差。
why_en: Use inter-annotator agreement with 2+ independent reviewers on high-severity, adjudication workflows for disagreements, and periodic calibration sessions to curb label drift.
options: 高危内容用 ≥2 名独立审核员，检查标注一致性
分歧走仲裁流程，由资深审核员裁决
定期校准会，统一判定尺度、压住标签漂移
让单个审核员一票定所有高危内容，以最快出标签
options_en: Use 2+ independent reviewers on high-severity content and check inter-annotator agreement.
Route disagreements through an adjudication workflow where a senior reviewer decides.
Hold periodic calibration sessions to align criteria and curb label drift.
Let a single reviewer unilaterally decide all high-severity content to produce labels fastest.
optionExplanations: 对；≥2 名独立审核员把单人噪声降下来，一致性低说明判据模糊、需修。
对；仲裁给分歧一个权威裁决，避免把矛盾标签直接灌进训练集。
对；不定期对齐，各人尺度会慢慢漂开，校准会把大家拉回同一刻度。
错；单人一票定高危正是要规避的做法——错误代价高的内容最不能靠一个人的噪声判定。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 2+ independent reviewers cut single-person noise, and low agreement flags vague criteria to fix.
Correct — adjudication gives disagreements an authoritative ruling instead of feeding conflicting labels into training.
Correct — without periodic alignment individual criteria drift apart, and calibration pulls everyone back to one scale.
Wrong — a single reviewer deciding high-severity is exactly what to avoid, since costly-error content should not ride on one person's noise.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不同审核员对同一内容给出相同判定的程度，衡量标签可信度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inter-annotator agreement measures how often different reviewers give the same verdict on the same item, gauging label reliability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 审核员分歧时由资深审核员做最终裁决的流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adjudication is a workflow where a senior reviewer makes the final call when reviewers disagree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期集体对齐判定标准、压住标签随时间漂移的会议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration session is a periodic meeting to realign judging criteria and curb label drift over time.

scenario: 自残与恐怖主义等高危类别，误判一条的代价极高，但每条内容都上多人审核又太贵。
scenario_en: For high-severity categories like self-harm or terrorism a single wrong call is very costly, yet multi-reviewing every item is expensive.
q: 为什么高危内容要用 ≥2 名独立审核员，而不是所有内容都上多人？
q_en: Why use 2+ independent reviewers on high-severity content rather than on everything?
why: 高危类别错误代价极高、且需要标注一致性来压单人噪声，所以值得花双人成本；低危高量内容单人足矣。这是把有限审核产能按错误代价分配——好钢用在刀刃上。
why_en: High-severity errors are so costly that paying for two independent reviewers to cut single-person noise is worth it, while low-severity high-volume content can ride on one reviewer.
tradeoff: 高危双人（更一致、更准，但成本翻倍）vs 全量单人（便宜，但高危类别噪声风险大）
options: 高危错误代价极高，双人独立审降单人噪声、提一致性，值得那份成本
所有内容都该上双人独立审核，成本从来不是审核系统设计要考虑的因素
高危内容其实更简单，多人只是走个形式、并无实际质量收益
用双人纯粹为了出标签更快，两个人并行比一个人快一倍
options_en: High-severity errors are so costly that two independent reviewers cut single-person noise and raise agreement, worth the cost.
Everything should get two independent reviewers; cost is never a factor to weigh in moderation system design.
High-severity content is actually simpler, so multiple reviewers are a formality with no real quality gain.
Two reviewers are purely to produce labels faster, since two in parallel are twice as fast as one.
whenOtherWins: 对低危、高量、判定明确的内容（如明显垃圾广告），单个审核员就够，硬上多人只是烧钱换不来质量。
optionExplanations: 对；按错误代价分配审核产能，高危值双人成本，低危单人即可。
全量双人成本翻倍且大多无收益，产能应按代价而非一刀切分配。
恰相反，高危往往更难更敏感，双人是为降噪不是走形式。
双人是串行复核降噪、不是并行提速，说快一倍搞错了目的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — allocate review capacity by error cost: high-severity earns two reviewers, low-severity rides on one.
Two reviewers everywhere doubles cost for little gain; capacity should follow cost, not a blanket rule.
On the contrary, high-severity is often harder and more sensitive; two reviewers reduce noise, not perform theater.
Two reviewers are for redundancy and noise reduction, not parallel speedup, so 'twice as fast' misses the point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误判代价极高的违规类型（自残、恐怖主义等），需更严格的标注质控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: High-severity categories are violation types whose misjudgment is very costly, like self-harm or terrorism, needing stricter label QC.

scenario: 要决定反馈回路多久重训一次模型：定死每周一次，还是等信号触发？
scenario_en: You must decide how often the feedback loop retrains: fixed weekly, or triggered by signals?
q: 重训该按固定周期，还是按漂移信号触发？
q_en: Should retraining fire on a fixed schedule or on drift signals?
why: 两者结合最稳：固定周期（如每周）保底吸收常规新标签；漂移触发抢跑——当升级率持续上升、或 reviewer-模型一致性下降，说明世界变了、模型正在过时，立刻重训。只靠周期会对突变反应慢，只靠漂移会漏掉缓慢退化。
why_en: Combine both: a fixed weekly schedule as a floor plus drift triggers (rising escalation rate, falling reviewer-model agreement) so sudden shifts don't wait for the next cycle.
tradeoff: 固定周期（可预测，但对突变反应慢）vs 漂移触发（响应快，但可能漏掉缓慢退化）→ 二者结合
options: 只按固定每周重训，简单可预测，突发对抗变化等下一周期再说
只在漂移信号出现时重训，省算力，缓慢退化就靠信号迟早会触发
两者结合：固定周期保底 + 漂移触发（升级率↑、一致性↓）抢跑
从不重训，静态模型足够稳，重训只会带来回归风险
options_en: Only retrain on a fixed weekly schedule; simple and predictable, and sudden adversarial shifts wait for next cycle.
Only retrain when a drift signal appears; saves compute, and slow degradation will eventually trip a signal.
Combine both: a fixed schedule as the floor plus drift triggers (escalation rate up, agreement down).
Never retrain; a static model is stable enough, and retraining only risks regressions.
optionExplanations: 纯周期对突发规避手法反应慢，一周内可能已被大量漏放。
纯漂移会漏掉缓慢、不触阈值的退化，等信号触发时可能已经积累很久。
对；周期保底 + 漂移抢跑，既可预测又能对突变快速响应。
从不重训正是静态分类器的死穴，分布漂移会让它逐月失效。
optionExplanations_en: Pure schedule reacts slowly to sudden evasions, and a week of misses can pile up in the meantime.
Pure drift misses slow, sub-threshold degradation that may accumulate before any signal fires.
Correct — a scheduled floor plus drift-triggered jumps is both predictable and responsive to sudden shifts.
Never retraining is the fatal flaw of a static classifier, which drift makes decay month over month.

termDefinitions.term: reviewer-model agreement / 审核-模型一致性
termDefinitions.meaning: 人工判定与模型预测一致的比例，持续下降说明模型正在过时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reviewer-model agreement is how often human verdicts match model predictions; a sustained drop signals the model is going stale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被路由升级到上层的内容占比，持续上升暗示模型对更多内容没把握。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Escalation rate is the share of content routed upward; a sustained rise hints the model is unsure about more content.

scenario: 模型只把「不确定」的内容升级给人工，于是回流的标签几乎全是边界模糊的样本。团队直接拿这些升级样本重训。
scenario_en: The model only escalates 'uncertain' items, so the returned labels are almost all borderline; the team retrains directly on these escalated items.
q: 只用升级样本重训，会带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem arises from retraining only on escalated items?
why: 选择偏差：升级样本不是随机抽样，全是决策边界附近的难例。只用它们重训，模型会过拟合边界、却在「明显合规/明显违规」这些从没升级过的内容上丢掉校准——越训越只会纠结中间地带。
why_en: Selection bias: escalated items aren't a random sample but cluster at the boundary, so retraining only on them overfits borderline cases while losing calibration on clearly benign or clearly harmful content.
options: 没问题，升级样本都是最难的例子，专攻它们模型只会更强
选择偏差：样本非随机、全在边界，模型过拟合边界，在明显合规/违规上丢校准
只会让模型变慢，因为难例更多、训练时间更长，但准确度不受影响
会导致模型只在垃圾广告这一类上变得更准，其他违规类别的判定完全不受影响
options_en: No problem; escalated items are the hardest cases, so focusing on them only makes the model stronger.
Selection bias: the sample isn't random but all borderline, so the model overfits the boundary and loses calibration on clearly benign/harmful content.
It only makes the model slower, since more hard cases mean longer training, but accuracy is unaffected.
It makes the model more accurate only on spam, and judgment on every other violation category is completely unaffected.
optionExplanations: 「专攻难例更强」忽略了训练分布已被扭曲——模型会忘掉怎么判简单内容。
对；升级样本是被模型自己筛出来的非随机子集，只训它们必然丢失全谱校准。
问题不在速度而在分布：偏差损害的是准确度与校准，不是训练时长。
偏差是全局的校准漂移，不是只影响某一个类别。
optionExplanations_en: 'Focus on hard cases makes it stronger' ignores that the training distribution is now skewed, so the model forgets how to judge easy content.
Correct — escalated items are a non-random subset the model itself selected, so training only on them loses full-spectrum calibration.
The issue is distribution, not speed: the bias hurts accuracy and calibration, not training time.
The bias is a global calibration shift, not something confined to a single category.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练样本不是随机抽取而是被某规则筛选，导致模型学到扭曲的分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Selection bias is when training samples are filtered by a rule rather than random, so the model learns a distorted distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出的置信分能否对应真实概率；丢校准=分数不再可信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is whether a model's confidence scores match true probabilities; losing calibration means the scores stop being trustworthy.

scenario: 反馈回路只回流升级样本，导致选择偏差；你要让训练分布重新覆盖全部置信度谱。
scenario_en: The loop only returns escalated items, causing selection bias; you need the training distribution to cover the full confidence spectrum again.
q: 怎么修复只训升级样本带来的选择偏差？
q_en: How do you fix the selection bias from training only on escalated items?
why: 随机审计：定期抽一小部分高置信的自动决策也送人工复核，把这些「模型本以为很确定」的样本补进训练集，训练分布就重新覆盖全置信度谱。它还顺带当作 Tier 1 的持续准确率评估——一箭双雕。
why_en: Random audit: periodically sample a small fraction of high-confidence auto-decisions and send them to human review, restoring full-spectrum coverage and doubling as a continuous Tier-1 accuracy check.
tradeoff: 随机审计（补全分布、兼作准确率评估，但占用人工产能）vs 只训升级样本（省人工，但偏差累积）
diagram:
flowchart TB T1["Tier1 高置信自动决策"] --> AU{"随机抽样 0.1-1%"} AU -->|抽中| HR["送人工复核"] AU -->|未抽中| KEEP["保持自动处置"] HR --> DS["训练集覆盖全置信度谱
兼作Tier1准确率评估"]
options: 加大升级比例，把更多不确定内容送人工，覆盖面自然变广
随机抽一小部分高置信自动决策也送人工，补全置信度谱
干脆停用反馈回路，避免任何偏差进入模型
只重训明显违规的样本，用极端样本抵消边界偏差
options_en: Escalate a larger share so more uncertain content reaches humans, naturally widening coverage.
Also send a small random sample of high-confidence auto-decisions to humans, restoring full-spectrum coverage.
Just disable the feedback loop to keep any bias out of the model.
Retrain only on clearly-violating samples, using extremes to offset the boundary bias.
whenOtherWins: 若你有充足的独立随机标注预算，可以直接周期性随机抽取全量内容做人工标注建基准，就不必特意只审高置信自动决策——但那样成本高得多。
optionExplanations: 加大升级只会让样本更集中在边界，偏差更重，不是补全高置信端。
对；专挑高置信自动决策来审，正好补上模型从不升级、因而从没被复核的那段谱。
停用回路等于放弃持续改进，模型会随对抗演变退化，得不偿失。
只训极端样本会走向另一种偏差，丢掉边界判别力，不能靠制造新偏差修旧偏差。
optionExplanations_en: Escalating more just concentrates samples at the boundary, worsening the bias rather than covering the high-confidence end.
Correct — auditing high-confidence auto-decisions fills exactly the spectrum the model never escalates and thus never gets reviewed.
Disabling the loop abandons continuous improvement, so the model degrades as adversaries evolve — a bad trade.
Training only on extremes creates the opposite bias and loses boundary discrimination; you can't fix bias by adding new bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期随机抽查一部分高置信自动决策送人工，用来补全训练分布并评估自动层准确率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A random audit periodically samples high-confidence auto-decisions for human review to restore training coverage and gauge automated accuracy.

scenario: 随机审计要抽查自动决策的一小部分，审核产能有限、又要统计上有意义。
scenario_en: The random audit samples a small fraction of auto-decisions, with limited reviewer capacity yet needing statistical meaning.
q: 随机审计的抽样率大约取多少、为什么是这个量级？
q_en: About what audit rate is used, and why that order of magnitude?
why: 取自动决策的 0.1%-1%——这是给定的运营目标、不是公式推导。下限要统计上有意义（能估出准确率与偏差），上限不能压垮人工：百万/分钟下即便 1% 也是每分钟上万条复核量，所以只能取这个很小的比例。
why_en: About 0.1%-1% of auto-decided content, a given operational target balancing statistical signal against reviewer capacity, since even 1% at millions per minute is a huge review load.
options: 约 0.1%-1%：统计上够用，又不压垮人工产能
约 50%：一半自动决策都要复核才能保证质量
恰好 5%：这是由错误率公式精确算出的唯一正确值
越高越好、没有上限，能审多少审多少直到人工排满
options_en: About 0.1%-1%: statistically meaningful yet still within reviewer capacity.
About 50%: half of all auto-decisions must be re-reviewed to guarantee quality.
Exactly 5%: the unique correct value computed precisely from an error-rate formula.
As high as possible with no ceiling; audit as much as you can until reviewers are saturated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机审计复核的自动决策占全部自动决策的比例，是运营权衡目标而非公式结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Audit rate is the share of auto-decisions sent to random review, an operational trade-off target rather than a formula output.

optionExplanations: 对，这个区间刚好卡在统计有意义和不压垮人工产能之间。
50% 复核率忽视了产能天花板：百万级流量下这相当于每分钟审几十万条，审核员根本扛不住。
没有公式能精确推出唯一阈值，「5%」只是编出来的假精确，实际是运营权衡出来的区间。
没有上限地审到排满，会把审计本身该省的产能全占光，压垮真正该处理的不确定内容。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — that band sits right where the sample stays statistically meaningful without overloading the review team.
A 50% recheck rate blows past the capacity ceiling — that's still hundreds of thousands of items every single minute for reviewers to handle.
There's no formula that pins down one exact number; '5%' is false precision, when it's really an operational trade-off band.
Auditing with no ceiling would burn through the very review bandwidth meant for genuinely uncertain escalations.

scenario: 随机审计除了修偏差，还有一个常被忽略的第二用途，可用一个类比记住。
scenario_en: Random audit has an often-missed second purpose, easy to remember by analogy.
q: 补全随机审计的第二用途与类比：
q_en: Fill in random audit's second purpose and analogy:
text: 随机审计抽查{{高置信}}的自动决策，除了给训练集补齐{{完整}}的置信度谱，还兼作对 Tier 1 的持续{{准确率}}评估。类比：卫生督查也会随机抽查{{零违规}}记录的餐厅，才能让评级系统保持可信。
text_en: Random audit reviews {{high-confidence}} auto-decisions, and besides restoring the {{full}} confidence spectrum for training it also serves as a continuous Tier-1 {{accuracy}} check. Analogy: a health inspector also randomly inspects {{spotless-record}} restaurants to keep the rating system trustworthy.
why: 随机审计一箭双雕：既补全训练分布、又持续监控自动层准确率。类比是卫生督查连零违规餐厅都随机查——不然「好评级」就没人信；同理不查高置信决策，就不知道模型是真准还是在悄悄退化。
why_en: Random audit both restores the training distribution and continuously monitors automated accuracy, like an inspector spot-checking spotless restaurants so the ratings stay trustworthy.

termDefinitions.term: Tier 1 accuracy eval / 自动层准确率评估
termDefinitions.meaning: 用人工复核高置信自动决策来持续测量自动层到底有多准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Tier-1 accuracy eval measures how accurate the automated tier really is by human-reviewing its high-confidence decisions.

scenario: 面试问 content moderation serving，你想给出 L5（高级/资深）而非 L4 级别的答案。
scenario_en: Asked about content-moderation serving, you want to give an L5 (senior) answer rather than an L4 one.
q: 什么样的回答把 L5 和 L4 区分开？
q_en: What distinguishes an L5 answer from an L4 one?
why: L4=单分类器+阈值、人工兜底、周期重训（路由静态、反馈是补充）。L5=显式三层架构 + 路由作为 ML（每类置信走廊）+ 反馈回路并意识到选择偏差 + 切片监控。区别在于是否把路由和反馈当成一等设计问题，而非事后补丁。
why_en: L4 is a single classifier with a threshold and human fallback; L5 makes routing an ML decision with per-category corridors, treats the feedback loop and selection bias explicitly, and adds slice-based monitoring.
tradeoff: L5（三层+ML路由+反馈+切片监控，系统更强但更复杂）vs L4（单分类器+人工兜底，简单但静态、易退化）
options: L4：单分类器+阈值、人工兜底、周期重训，把路由和反馈都当事后补丁
只把三层架构的框图画出来、术语堆满，但不谈路由和反馈怎么设计
L5：三层架构 + 路由做成 ML + 反馈回路与选择偏差 + 切片监控
直接跳到 Staff+ 的队列优先级排序模型，把它当成 L5 的分界线
options_en: L4: a single classifier plus threshold, human fallback, periodic retraining, treating routing and feedback as afterthoughts.
Just draw the three-tier diagram and pile on jargon without discussing how routing and feedback are designed.
L5: three-tier architecture, routing as ML, a feedback loop aware of selection bias, and slice-level monitoring.
Jump straight to Staff+ queue-prioritization ranking and treat it as the L5 dividing line.
whenOtherWins: 如果是早期原型或小规模平台，L4 的单分类器+人工兜底反而是合适答案——过早上三层+ML路由是过度设计。
optionExplanations: 这是 L4 基线：能跑但路由静态、反馈是补丁，缺少 L5 的系统性。
只画框图堆术语没有工程判断，面试官看得出你没真设计过。
对；把路由和反馈当一等问题、并意识到选择偏差与切片监控，正是 L5 的信号。
队列优先级是 Staff+ 的加分项，不是 L5 的分界，混淆层级反而露怯。
optionExplanations_en: This is the L4 baseline: it runs but routing is static and feedback is a patch, lacking L5's systemic view.
Just drawing a diagram and stacking terms shows no engineering judgment, and interviewers can tell you haven't designed one.
Correct — treating routing and feedback as first-class and being aware of selection bias and slice monitoring is the L5 signal.
Queue prioritization is a Staff+ bonus, not the L5 boundary, and conflating levels exposes the gap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把准确率按类别、语言、作者群等切片分别监控，发现整体指标掩盖的局部退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slice-based monitoring tracks accuracy separately per slice like category, language, or author group to catch local degradation hidden by aggregate metrics.

scenario: 要把答案从 L5 拔到 Staff+，需要展示更强的系统与组织权衡意识。
scenario_en: To lift the answer from L5 to Staff+, you must show stronger systemic and organizational trade-off awareness.
q: 以下哪些是 Staff+ 级别在 L5 之上额外该谈的点？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are Staff+ additions beyond L5? (multiple)
why: Staff+ 加分项：队列优先级做成独立排序模型、随机审计机制、减害 vs 模型改进的张力、金丝雀部署测回归、以及招人 vs 投自动化的组织权衡。把 Tier 1 延迟再压低不是分界线。
why_en: Staff+ adds queue prioritization as a separate ranking model, the random-audit mechanism, the harm-reduction-versus-model-improvement tension, canary deployments, and org trade-offs.
options: 把人工队列优先级做成一个独立的排序模型
随机审计机制 + 反馈回路里减害 vs 模型改进的张力
金丝雀部署：一部分内容同时用新旧模型打分以测回归
把 Tier 1 延迟从 100ms 再压到 10ms 作为主要 Staff+ 信号
options_en: Make human-queue prioritization a separate ranking model.
The random-audit mechanism plus the harm-reduction-versus-model-improvement tension in the loop.
Canary deployments: a fraction of content scored by both old and new models to measure regression.
Cutting Tier 1 latency from 100ms to 10ms as the primary Staff+ signal.
optionExplanations: 对；队列优先级本身是个排序问题，单独建模决定 reviewer 先看谁，是 Staff+ 视角。
对；随机审计 + 减害/改进张力显示你懂反馈回路的资源分配矛盾。
对；金丝雀部署是上线新模型不砸盘的标准做法，Staff+ 该主动提。
错；把延迟继续压低是局部优化，不是 Staff+ 的系统/组织级分界。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — queue prioritization is itself a ranking problem worth its own model deciding who reviewers see first, a Staff+ lens.
Correct — random audit plus the harm/improvement tension shows you grasp the loop's resource-allocation conflict.
Correct — canary deployment is the standard way to ship a new model without breakage, and Staff+ should raise it.
Wrong — shaving latency further is a local optimization, not the systemic/org-level Staff+ boundary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先让一小部分流量用新版本、与旧版本并行对比，确认无回归再全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canary deployment routes a small fraction to a new version alongside the old to check for regressions before full rollout.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定人工审核队列里先审哪些内容的排序，可用独立排序模型实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue prioritization orders which items human reviewers see first, implementable as a separate ranking model.

scenario: 审核模型要上一个新版本，直接全量替换风险太大——可能整体准确率反而回退。
scenario_en: A new moderation model version is ready, but swapping it in for everyone risks an overall accuracy regression.
q: 金丝雀部署在审核模型上线里具体怎么做、测什么？
q_en: How does canary deployment work when shipping a new moderation model, and what does it measure?
why: 金丝雀部署：让一部分内容同时用新旧模型打分，对比两者以量化回归，确认新模型没在某些切片上变差再逐步放量。它把「上线即全量」的赌博换成可测量、可回滚的渐进替换。
why_en: Canary deployment scores a fraction of content with both old and new models to quantify regression before gradually rolling out, turning an all-or-nothing swap into a measurable, reversible rollout.
options: 把新模型直接全量替换旧模型，出问题再整体回滚
只在测试集离线评估新模型，线上直接切，不做线上对比
让新模型只跑影子流量但从不看结果，纯粹热身预热缓存
一部分内容用新旧模型双打分、对比量化回归，无退步再放量
options_en: Swap the new model in for all traffic at once and roll back wholesale if problems appear.
Evaluate the new model only offline on a test set, then cut over live with no live comparison.
Run the new model on shadow traffic but never look at results, purely to warm caches.
Score a slice of content with both old and new models, quantify regression by comparison, then ramp up.
optionExplanations: 全量替换就是没有金丝雀：一旦回退已经影响所有内容，损失最大。
离线评估掩盖不了线上分布差异，缺了新旧并行对比就看不出真实回归。
影子流量不看结果等于白跑，金丝雀的核心正是对比新旧的线上结果。
对；新旧并行打分、量化回归、渐进放量，是可测量可回滚的安全上线方式。
optionExplanations_en: A full swap is the opposite of a canary: by the time you roll back, all content is already affected, maximizing damage.
Offline evaluation can't capture live distribution differences, and without an old-versus-new comparison real regressions stay hidden.
Shadow traffic you never inspect is wasted; the canary's whole point is comparing live old-versus-new results.
Correct — scoring both in parallel, quantifying regression, and ramping gradually is the measurable, reversible way to ship.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新版本在某些指标或切片上比旧版本更差，金丝雀部署就是为了提前发现它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is the new version performing worse than the old on some metric or slice, which canary deployment exists to catch early.

scenario: Tier 3 人工队列每天积压远超审核员产能，必须决定先审哪些内容。
scenario_en: The Tier 3 human queue backs up far beyond reviewer capacity, so you must decide which items to review first.
q: Staff+ 方案里怎么给人工审核队列排优先级？
q_en: In a Staff+ design, how do you prioritize the human review queue?
why: 用一个独立的排序模型，按危害严重度 × 触达 × 时效给队列排序，让审核员先处理高危、高传播、时效性强的内容。FIFO 或按时间排都忽略了「哪条现在最该先删」，在产能不足时会让最危险的内容干等。
why_en: Use a separate ranking model ordering the queue by harm severity × reach × time-sensitivity so reviewers hit the most dangerous, viral, time-critical items first, rather than FIFO.
tradeoff: 排序模型（把有限产能对准最高危内容，但要额外建模）vs FIFO（简单公平，但让最危险内容干等）
options: 用独立排序模型按危害×触达×时效排序
严格 FIFO 先到先审，保证绝对公平的处理顺序
随机抽取审核，避免审核员对某类内容产生偏见
只按内容创建时间倒序，永远先审最新发的
options_en: Use a separate ranking model ordering by harm severity times reach times time-sensitivity.
Strict FIFO, first-come-first-served, guaranteeing an absolutely fair processing order.
Review by random sampling to keep reviewers from developing bias toward certain content.
Order strictly by creation time descending, always reviewing the newest posts first.
whenOtherWins: 若队列量很小、审核产能充足、内容危害都差不多，简单 FIFO 就够公平高效，不必单独训一个排序模型。
optionExplanations: 对；产能不足时该把审核力量对准期望危害最大的内容，这正是一个排序问题。
FIFO 公平却盲目，会让高危高传播内容排在一堆无害内容后面干等。
随机审是给评估/审计用的，拿来排生产队列会让危险内容迟迟得不到处理。
按最新优先忽略危害与传播，热门旧帖的危害反而被无限延后。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — when capacity is short, aim review effort at the highest expected harm, which is exactly a ranking problem.
FIFO is fair but blind, leaving high-severity viral content stuck behind a pile of harmless items.
Random review is for evaluation/audit; using it to order the production queue starves dangerous content of attention.
Newest-first ignores harm and spread, indefinitely deferring harmful older posts that are going viral.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容危害随时间放大的紧迫度，越紧迫越该优先审核。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-sensitivity is how urgently harm grows over time, so more time-sensitive items should be reviewed first.

scenario: 同一条内容，自动层能在 100ms 内判完，人工层要分钟到小时但更准。
scenario_en: For the same item, automation decides within 100ms while humans take minutes-to-hours but are more accurate.
q: 内容审核里延迟与准确度这条取舍轴具体是什么？
q_en: What exactly is the latency-accuracy trade-off in content moderation?
why: 更快的自动决策牺牲准确度，更慢的人工决策换来准确度。整个三层架构就是在这条轴上分段：能自动判准的走 100ms，判不准的才用慢而准的人工——用分层把两端的好处都拿到一部分。
why_en: Faster automated decisions sacrifice accuracy while slower human ones buy it, and the three-tier design places each item along that axis by how confidently it can be judged.
tradeoff: 自动（100ms、快但边缘案例易错）vs 人工（分钟-小时、准但慢且贵）
options: 自动和人工其实一样准，差别只在成本，与准确度无关
更快的自动决策牺牲准确度，更慢的人工决策换来准确度，三层沿这条轴分段
延迟越低准确度越高，所以应把所有内容都塞进 100ms 的自动层
准确度只取决于模型大小，跟走自动还是人工没有关系
options_en: Automation and humans are equally accurate; the only difference is cost, not accuracy.
Faster automated decisions sacrifice accuracy while slower human ones buy it, and the three tiers split items along that axis.
Lower latency means higher accuracy, so push all content into the 100ms automated tier.
Accuracy depends only on model size and has nothing to do with going automated versus human.
optionExplanations: 自动与人工准确度并不相等，尤其在模糊边界上人工明显更准，这正是分层的理由。
对；这是这道题的核心取舍轴，三层架构就是沿它分配不同置信度的内容。
把「延迟低」当「准确高」正好搞反：自动快但在边缘案例上更容易出错。
准确度既受模型影响、也受是自动还是人工影响，人工在难例上系统性更准。
optionExplanations_en: Automation and humans aren't equally accurate; humans are clearly better on fuzzy boundaries, which is why tiers exist.
Correct — this is the core trade-off axis, and the three-tier design distributes content of different confidence along it.
Treating low latency as high accuracy is backwards: automation is fast but more error-prone on edge cases.
Accuracy depends on both the model and whether it's automated or human, with humans systematically better on hard cases.

termDefinitions.term: latency-accuracy tradeoff / 延迟-准确度取舍
termDefinitions.meaning: 更快的决策通常更不准、更慢的更准，分层架构沿这条轴分配内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The latency-accuracy tradeoff is that faster decisions are usually less accurate, and a tiered design distributes content along that axis.

scenario: 审核员产能固定，你既想审随机高置信决策拿更好训练数据，又想把人力用在真正不确定的内容上。
scenario_en: Reviewer capacity is fixed; you want to audit random high-confidence decisions for better training data, yet also spend humans on genuinely uncertain content.
q: 反馈回路里的探索-利用取舍具体指什么？
q_en: What is the exploration-exploitation trade-off in the feedback loop?
why: 探索=审那些高置信自动决策（随机审计），能拿到覆盖全谱的更好训练数据；利用=把人力都投给真正不确定的升级内容，最大化当下的删除质量。产能固定，多审计就少处理不确定案例——这就是探索与利用在抢同一批审核员。
why_en: Exploration is auditing high-confidence auto-decisions for better full-spectrum training data, while exploitation spends fixed reviewer capacity on genuinely uncertain items, and the two compete for the same reviewers.
tradeoff: 探索/审计高置信决策（更好训练数据，但占用产能）vs 利用/处理不确定内容（当下质量高，但不长远改进模型）
options: 指模型探索新类别 vs 利用旧类别，与审核员产能分配无关
探索=审随机高置信决策拿数据；利用=人力投给不确定内容
指是否要探索更大的模型，利用更多 GPU，纯粹是算力预算问题
探索和利用在这里没有冲突，两件事可以同时无成本地做
options_en: It's the model exploring new categories versus exploiting old ones, unrelated to reviewer capacity.
Exploration = auditing random high-confidence decisions for data; exploitation = spending humans on uncertain items.
It's whether to explore a bigger model and exploit more GPUs, purely a compute-budget question.
Exploration and exploitation don't conflict here; both can be done at once at no cost.
whenOtherWins: 当模型已很稳、漂移很慢时，可以少探索（少审计）、多利用（多处理不确定内容），把有限产能优先用于当下删除质量。
optionExplanations: 把它当模型内部的类别探索，忽略了真正冲突：审核员产能在审计与处理之间二选一。
对；探索（审计）换更好训练数据、利用（处理）换当下删除质量，产能固定就此消彼长。
这不是 GPU 预算问题，冲突发生在有限的人工审核产能上。
产能固定时二者天然冲突，说无成本并行是忽略了同一批审核员的排他占用。
optionExplanations_en: Framing it as internal category exploration misses the real conflict: reviewer capacity must choose between auditing and processing.
Correct — exploration (audit) buys better training data, exploitation (process) buys current removal quality, and fixed capacity trades one for the other.
It isn't a GPU-budget question; the conflict is over limited human review capacity.
With fixed capacity the two inherently conflict, and claiming free parallelism ignores that the same reviewers can't do both.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在收集更好信息（探索）与用现有信息取当下最优（利用）之间分配有限资源的取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exploration-exploitation is allocating limited resources between gathering better information (explore) and acting on current information for immediate payoff (exploit).

scenario: 面试官给的题是「给自动驾驶汽车(Waymo/Tesla/Amazon Robotics)设计一个物体检测系统」。
scenario_en: The interviewer says 'design an object detection system for an autonomous vehicle (Waymo/Tesla/Amazon Robotics)'.
q: 这道题真正在考什么？
q_en: What is this question really testing?
why: 别把它当调模型的题：它是完整系统设计——延迟预算、边缘硬件、安全认证、失败分析样样要答。真正拉开级别的是需求 scoping 的深度，不是模型选得多花哨。
why_en: Treat it as a full system-design problem with latency budget, edge hardware, safety certification, and failure analysis, where depth of requirements scoping, not model choice, separates the levels.
options: 主要是刷 mAP 分数，挑精度最高的检测网络、在公开数据集上调到 SOTA 就算通关
主要是训练技巧：靠数据增强、超参搜索、换更深的 backbone，模型堆得越大 mAP 分数就刷得越高
一个完整系统设计题：延迟预算、边缘硬件、安全认证、失败分析都要答，scoping 深浅区分级别
主要是标注工程：雇更多标注员画更多框，把数据集堆大就能覆盖所有长尾场景
options_en: Mostly chasing mAP scores: pick the most accurate detector and tune it to SOTA on a public dataset.
Mostly training tricks: augmentation, hyperparameter search, a deeper backbone — the bigger the model, the higher the mAP score climbs.
A full system-design question: latency budget, edge hardware, safety certification, failure analysis, where scoping depth sets the level.
Mostly labeling engineering: hire more annotators to draw more boxes and cover the long tail by piling up the dataset.
optionExplanations: mAP 只是精度一个侧面；这题重头在延迟、硬件、安全和失败分析，只刷分会被判成 L4。
训练技巧是模型内部细节；面试要系统级取舍，堆大模型反而违背边缘延迟预算。
对；它是端到端系统题，需求 scoping 的深浅(延迟/硬件/安全/失败)才是分级线。
堆数据解决不了长尾；这题先考需求框定，不是标注工程执行。
optionExplanations_en: mAP is only one slice of accuracy; this question centers on latency, hardware, safety, and failure, so score-chasing reads as L4.
Training tricks are model internals; the interview wants system-level tradeoffs, and bigger models fight the edge latency budget.
Correct — it is an end-to-end system question, and the depth of scoping across latency, hardware, safety, and failure is the leveling line.
More data cannot fix the long tail, and this question first tests requirement framing, not labeling execution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动驾驶车辆：靠传感器和感知模型自主行驶的车。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AV (Autonomous Vehicle) drives itself using sensors and perception models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨类别、跨 IoU 阈值综合的物体检测精度指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mAP (mean Average Precision) summarizes detection accuracy across classes and IoU thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把开放式题目拆成延迟、硬件、安全、数据等具体约束的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements scoping is breaking an open prompt into concrete constraints like latency, hardware, safety, and data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 失败可能致命的系统，检测漏报直接关系人身安全。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Safety-critical means failures can be fatal, so a missed detection directly risks human life.

scenario: 高速上以 30 m/s 行驶，从相机出帧到控制系统动作必须极快。
scenario_en: Cruising at 30 m/s on the highway, camera-frame-to-control action must be extremely fast.
q: 端到端 50ms 这个目标从哪来，它限定了哪些设计选择？
q_en: Where does the 50ms end-to-end target come from and what does it constrain?
why: 50ms 不是公式算出的，是给定的安全 SLO——30 m/s×50ms=1.5m 盲行距离，正好是紧急制动的最小余量。它是延迟预算总盘，逼推理只剩~30ms，从而排除顺序跑的两阶段检测。
why_en: The 50ms is a given safety SLO, not a computed number: at 30 m/s it means 1.5m of blind travel, the minimum emergency-braking margin, and it caps inference near 30ms which rules out sequential two-stage detectors.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["相机取帧
~5ms"] --> P["预处理 resize
~5ms"] P --> M["模型推理 edge GPU
~30ms 主导"] M --> N["NMS 后处理
~5ms"] N --> H["交给控制栈
~5ms"]
options: 50ms 只是 GPU 厂商标称的硬件上限，换更强芯片理论上就能突破，跟刹车距离无关
50ms 是物理推出的安全目标：30m/s×50ms≈1.5m 盲行，逼推理进 30ms，排除两阶段
50ms 是训练时每个 batch 的前向延迟指标，只影响训练吞吐速度，线上推理其实可以放宽到几百毫秒
50ms 指每帧必须在此时间内完成人工标注，是数据流水线时限，和实时推理完全无关
options_en: 50ms is just the GPU vendor's stated hardware ceiling; a stronger chip could, in theory, break it, unrelated to braking distance.
50ms is a physics-derived safety target: at 30 m/s it is about 1.5m of blind travel, which squeezes inference into 30ms and rules out two-stage.
50ms is a per-batch forward-pass training-latency metric that only affects training throughput; serving can actually relax to hundreds of ms.
50ms is the per-frame human-annotation deadline, a data-pipeline limit, completely unrelated to real-time inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给定的目标指标(如端到端 50ms)，不是公式推出的，而是安全/产品设定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given target like 50ms end-to-end, set by safety or product rather than derived.

termDefinitions.term: two-stage detector / 两阶段检测器
termDefinitions.meaning: 先出候选区域再逐个分类的检测器(如 Faster R-CNN)，两步串行、较慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage detector first proposes regions then classifies them, running serially and slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 速度单位，30 m/s≈108 km/h，用来把延迟换算成盲行距离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Meters per second; 30 m/s is about 108 km/h, used to convert latency into blind-travel distance.

q: 把 AV 检测端到端 50ms 延迟预算的 5 个阶段按执行顺序排好：
q_en: Order the five stages of the end-to-end 50ms AV-detection latency budget.
steps: NMS + 后处理：去掉重叠冗余框，~5ms
相机取帧 sensor capture：~5ms
把检测结果交给控制/规划栈：~5ms
预处理并 resize 到网络输入尺寸：~5ms
模型推理 edge GPU：~30ms，主导项
why: 顺序：取帧→预处理 resize→模型推理(~30ms 主导)→NMS 去重叠框→交给控制。五段相加~50ms，推理是唯一大头，优化都往它使劲。
why_en: The order is capture, preprocess/resize, inference at about 30ms as the dominant stage, NMS to drop overlaps, then handoff to control, summing to about 50ms with inference the only big chunk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非极大值抑制：同一物体上只保留置信度最高的框，删掉重叠冗余框。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression) keeps the highest-confidence box per object and removes overlapping duplicates.

scenario: 讨论为什么每多 50ms 延迟都危险。
scenario_en: Discussing why every extra 50ms of latency is dangerous.
q: 「30 m/s 下 100ms 延迟 ≈ 3m 盲行」这个数字对设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does '100ms of latency at 30 m/s is about 3m of blind travel' imply for design?
why: 车在你「看不见」的这段处理时间里一直在走：距离=速度×延迟。30 m/s×100ms=3m，×50ms=1.5m，这就是把延迟预算当安全指标压到 50ms 的物理依据。
why_en: The car keeps moving while it is 'blind': distance equals speed times latency, so 30 m/s over 100ms is 3m and over 50ms is 1.5m, which is why the latency budget is a safety metric pinned at 50ms.
options: 延迟直接换算成盲行距离：30 m/s×0.1s=3m，50ms 减半到 1.5m，延迟预算就是安全余量
3m 只是相机镜头本身的可视距离上限，与处理延迟完全无关，提高分辨率就能看更远更安全
3m 其实是检测框的平均定位误差数值，是精度问题，靠更大的模型把 mAP 提上去就能解决
3m 是两次相邻曝光帧之间产生的物体位移量，把相机帧率提高到 60fps 就能彻底消除掉，跟端到端延迟无关
options_en: Latency converts straight into blind-travel distance: 30 m/s times 0.1s is 3m, halving to 1.5m at 50ms, so the latency budget is the safety margin.
3m is just the camera lens's own visible-range ceiling, unrelated to processing latency; higher resolution sees farther and safer.
3m is actually the box's average localization error value, an accuracy issue solved by a bigger model with higher mAP.
3m is the object displacement between two adjacent exposure frames, fully removable by pushing the camera frame rate to 60fps, unrelated to end-to-end latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从相机出帧到系统做出反应的这段延迟里，车已经开过的距离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blind travel is the distance the car covers during the latency between a frame and the system's reaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒处理帧数，衡量实时速度；提高它并不能消掉端到端处理延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPS (Frames Per Second) measures real-time throughput; raising it does not remove end-to-end processing latency.

scenario: 50ms 预算里五个阶段：取帧 5、预处理 5、推理 30、NMS 5、控制 5(单位 ms)。
scenario_en: In the 50ms budget the five stages are capture 5, preprocess 5, inference 30, NMS 5, control 5 (ms).
q: 优化端到端延迟时，第一刀该砍哪个阶段？
q_en: When optimizing end-to-end latency, which stage do you cut first?
why: 五段里推理占 30/50，是唯一主导项；其余四段各~5ms，砍到 0 也只省 20ms。所以边缘优化(量化、TensorRT、选单阶段)全部集中在推理这一段。
why_en: Inference is 30 of the 50ms and the only dominant stage, so all edge optimization targets it, since the other four stages sum to just 20ms even if zeroed out.
options: 取帧阶段：换一块更快更贵的相机传感器，能省下流水线的大半预算
NMS 后处理：去重叠框其实才是整条流水线里最耗时的一步
控制交接：只要压缩车内 CAN 总线的通信与序列化耗时，就能省下整条流水线里最多的时间
模型推理：占~30ms 是主导项，量化/TensorRT/单阶段都压这里
options_en: Capture: swapping in a faster, pricier camera sensor could, in theory, save most of the pipeline's budget.
NMS post-processing: dropping overlapping boxes is actually the costliest step in the whole pipeline.
Control handoff: just trimming the in-vehicle CAN bus's communication and serialization time saves the most time in the whole pipeline.
Model inference: at ~30ms it is the dominant term, which is what quantization, TensorRT, and single-stage detection all attack.

termDefinitions.meaning: 装在车上的算力受限 GPU，推理就在它上面跑，不走云端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge GPU is the power-limited on-vehicle GPU where inference runs, not in the cloud.

optionExplanations: 取帧只占~5ms，不是拖累延迟的大头，换传感器省不出预算里的大半。
NMS 同样只占~5ms 的后处理，四个非主导阶段之一，谈不上最耗时。
控制交接也只占~5ms，压缩总线通信省不出多少，真正的大头在别处。
对；推理独占~30ms，是这条链路里唯一的大头，量化、TensorRT 编译、换单阶段检测都冲着它来。
optionExplanations_en: Capture is only about 5ms, not the latency hog, so a pricier sensor cannot buy back most of the budget.
NMS is likewise only ~5ms of post-processing, one of four minor stages, nowhere near the costliest step.
Control handoff is also just ~5ms; trimming bus communication saves little, since the real hog sits elsewhere.
Correct — inference alone eats ~30ms, the pipeline's one real hog, exactly what quantization, TensorRT compilation, and switching to single-stage detection all attack.

scenario: 推理只剩~30ms 的预算，要在这个窗口内检出所有物体。
scenario_en: Only ~30ms of budget is left for inference, and you must detect all objects inside that window.
q: 这个 30ms 窗口该选单阶段还是两阶段检测器？
q_en: Single-stage or two-stage detector for this 30ms window?
why: 30ms 排除了两阶段——区域提议→分类是顺序两步，跑不进预算；单阶段把检测当一次回归，多尺度特征图上直接出框和类别。
why_en: The 30ms budget rules out two-stage, whose region-proposal-then-classify runs sequentially, while single-stage treats detection as one regression pass that emits boxes and classes directly.
tradeoff: 单阶段(一次前向、够快) vs 两阶段(提议+分类两步、更准但顺序慢)
whenOtherWins: 离线场景(如高精地图标注、数据集预标)没有实时约束时，两阶段更高的定位精度更值得。
options: 两阶段 Faster R-CNN：先出区域提议再逐个分类，精度最高，30ms 也够用
先跑两阶段拿高精度，等实时性不够时再降分辨率临时补救
单阶段 YOLO/SSD：多尺度特征图上一次前向直接回归框+类别，卡进 30ms
30ms 内只能做图像分类，真正的物体检测必须放到云端去跑
options_en: Two-stage Faster R-CNN: propose regions then classify each; highest accuracy and 30ms is enough.
Run two-stage for accuracy first, then drop resolution as a patch when real-time fails.
Single-stage YOLO/SSD: one forward pass on multi-scale feature maps regresses boxes and classes, fitting 30ms.
In 30ms you can only do image classification; real object detection must run in the cloud.
optionExplanations: 两阶段的 RPN→分类是串行两步，延迟叠加，跑不进 30ms，精度再高也没用。
先慢后救本末倒置：降分辨率会掉召回，安全关键场景不能拿召回换速度。
对；单阶段一次前向就出框和类别，是把检测卡进 30ms 硬实时窗口的结构性选择。
把帧传云端往返延迟就爆预算，检测必须在车载边缘设备本地完成。
optionExplanations_en: Two-stage runs RPN then classification serially, stacking latency past 30ms, so accuracy cannot save it.
Slow-then-patch is backwards: dropping resolution costs recall, and safety-critical scenes cannot trade recall for speed.
Correct — single-stage emits boxes and classes in one pass, the structural choice that fits detection into the 30ms hard-real-time window.
Shipping frames to the cloud blows the budget on the round trip; detection must run locally on the edge device.

termDefinitions.term: single-stage detector / 单阶段检测器
termDefinitions.meaning: 一次前向从特征图直接回归框和类别的检测器(YOLO/SSD)，快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single-stage detector regresses boxes and classes from feature maps in one forward pass, making it fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典单阶段检测器，一次前向预测所有框和类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YOLO (You Only Look Once) is a classic single-stage detector predicting all boxes and classes in one pass.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款单阶段检测器，从多尺度特征图直接预测框。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSD (Single Shot MultiBox Detector) predicts boxes directly from multi-scale feature maps in one shot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段检测器：RPN 先提区域，再逐个分类，精度高但慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faster R-CNN is a two-stage detector whose RPN proposes regions then classifies each, accurate but slow.

scenario: 自动驾驶车载检测：相机 30fps，每帧只有 ~30ms 在车上边缘芯片里跑完推理。
scenario_en: On-vehicle detection for a self-driving car: the camera runs at 30fps, so each frame gets only about 30ms of inference on the car's edge chip.
q: 单阶段(YOLO/SSD)与两阶段(Faster R-CNN)在延迟上的根本差别是什么？
q_en: What is the fundamental latency difference between single-stage (YOLO/SSD) and two-stage (Faster R-CNN)?
why: 差别在流程结构：两阶段的 RPN→分类是串行两步，延迟叠加；单阶段把定位和分类压进一次前向，天然更适合 30ms 硬实时窗口。
why_en: The difference is pipeline structure: two-stage runs region proposals then classification serially so latencies stack, while single-stage folds localization and classification into one pass, fitting the 30ms window.
tradeoff: 单阶段(一次前向、低延迟) vs 两阶段(提议+分类、精度略高但慢)
diagram:
flowchart LR R["两阶段：区域提议"] --> Cl["再逐个分类
顺序慢"] F["单阶段：多尺度特征图"] --> O["一次直接回归
框+类别 快"]
options: 两阶段顺序两步：先 RPN 提区域、再逐个分类；单阶段一次前向直接出框+类别
单阶段要跑两遍网络、两阶段只跑一遍，所以两阶段反而更快更省
两者延迟基本相同，差别只在单阶段的定位精度天生更高
单阶段必须配 LiDAR 点云才能跑，两阶段只用纯相机图像，根本差别在传感器而不在流程
options_en: Two-stage is two serial steps: RPN proposes regions then classifies each; single-stage emits boxes and classes in one pass.
Single-stage runs the network twice and two-stage once, so two-stage is actually faster and cheaper.
Their latency is basically equal; the only difference is single-stage has inherently higher localization accuracy.
Single-stage needs a LiDAR point cloud to run while two-stage uses camera images only; the real difference is the sensor, not the pipeline.
optionExplanations: 对；两阶段串行叠加延迟，单阶段一次前向，这就是它能进 30ms 的根本原因。
说反了：单阶段只跑一遍、更快；两阶段多了区域提议这步反而更慢。
延迟并不相同：两阶段因串行步骤明显更慢，这正是被排除的原因。
两者都能用纯相机；差别在检测流程是几步，不在用什么传感器。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — two-stage stacks latency serially while single-stage runs one pass, which is exactly why it fits 30ms.
Backwards: single-stage runs once and is faster; two-stage adds the proposal step and is slower.
Latency is not equal: two-stage is clearly slower from its serial steps, which is why it is ruled out.
Both can run on cameras alone; the difference is how many steps the pipeline has, not the sensor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段检测器里先框出候选区域的子网络，是其额外的串行开销来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An RPN (Region Proposal Network) first proposes candidate regions in a two-stage detector, its extra serial cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用激光测距生成 3D 点云的传感器，可与相机融合，但不是单阶段检测的前提。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) uses laser ranging to build a 3D point cloud; useful for fusion but not required for single-stage detection.

scenario: 检测器在一个物体上常吐出好几个高度重叠的框。
scenario_en: The detector often emits several highly overlapping boxes on a single object.
q: 延迟预算里的 NMS 这一步是干什么的？
q_en: What does the NMS step in the latency budget do?
why: NMS=Non-Maximum Suppression，非极大值抑制：按置信度排序，抑制与最高分框 IoU 超阈值的重叠框，避免一个行人被报成五个。它在后处理占~5ms。
why_en: NMS, non-maximum suppression, keeps the highest-confidence box per object and suppresses overlaps above an IoU threshold, so one pedestrian is not reported five times, costing about 5ms.
options: 把图像 resize 到网络输入尺寸
去掉同一物体上重叠冗余的框，每类只留置信度最高的那个
把 FP32 权重量化成 INT8 整数以加速边缘推理
在多帧之间跟踪同一物体的 ID
options_en: Resize the image to the network's input dimensions.
Remove overlapping duplicate boxes on one object, keeping the highest-confidence box per class.
Quantize FP32 weights to INT8 integers to speed up edge inference.
Track the same object's ID across multiple frames.
optionExplanations: resize 是预处理阶段的事，和 NMS 无关。
对；NMS 按置信度+IoU 抑制重叠框，把一堆重复框收敛成每个物体一个。
量化是部署侧的权重压缩，NMS 不改精度格式。
跨帧跟踪是 tracking 模块的活，NMS 只在单帧内去重。
optionExplanations_en: Resizing happens in preprocessing and has nothing to do with NMS.
Correct — NMS suppresses overlaps by confidence and IoU, collapsing duplicate boxes into one per object.
Quantization is deployment-side weight compression; NMS does not change numeric format.
Cross-frame tracking is the tracker's job; NMS only deduplicates within a single frame.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非极大值抑制：抑制与最高分框重叠过多的冗余框，每物体留一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression) suppresses boxes that overlap the top-scoring one too much, leaving one per object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个框交集面积除以并集面积，衡量重叠程度，NMS 用它设阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IoU (Intersection over Union) is intersection area over union area, measuring box overlap; NMS thresholds on it.

scenario: 汇报检测系统效果时要同时给精度和速度两个指标。
scenario_en: Reporting the detector's results, you must give both an accuracy metric and a speed metric.
q: 物体检测最常用的精度与速度指标分别是什么？
q_en: What are the standard accuracy and speed metrics for object detection?
why: mAP=mean Average Precision，跨类别、跨 IoU 阈值综合的检测精度；FPS=Frames Per Second，每秒帧数即实时速度。L4 至少要同时给这两个，光有精度不谈速度过不了实时关。
why_en: mAP (mean average precision) summarizes accuracy across classes and IoU thresholds while FPS (frames per second) captures speed, and you must report both because accuracy without speed fails the real-time bar.
options: 用 BLEU 衡量精度、用 QPS 衡量速度
用准确率 accuracy 衡量精度、用 batch size 衡量速度
用困惑度 perplexity 衡量精度、用 epoch 数衡量速度
用 mAP 衡量精度、用 FPS 衡量速度
options_en: Use BLEU for accuracy and QPS for speed.
Use classification accuracy for precision and batch size for speed.
Use perplexity for accuracy and epoch count for speed.
Use mAP for accuracy and FPS for speed.
optionExplanations: BLEU 是机器翻译指标、QPS 是服务吞吐，都不是检测精度/速度的标准量。
单一 accuracy 不适合多框检测；batch size 是训练超参不是实时速度。
perplexity 是语言模型指标，epoch 是训练轮数，都跟检测无关。
对；mAP 综合定位与分类精度，FPS 表实时速度，是检测的标准双指标。
optionExplanations_en: BLEU is a translation metric and QPS is service throughput; neither is detection accuracy or speed.
Plain accuracy does not fit multi-box detection, and batch size is a training hyperparameter, not real-time speed.
Perplexity is a language-model metric and epochs are training rounds, both unrelated to detection.
Correct — mAP blends localization and classification accuracy while FPS is real-time speed, the standard pair.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨类别、跨 IoU 阈值平均的检测精度指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mAP (mean Average Precision) averages detection precision across classes and IoU thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒处理帧数，衡量实时推理速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPS (Frames Per Second) is how many frames are processed per second, measuring real-time speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器翻译文本相似度指标，与物体检测无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU is a machine-translation text-similarity metric, unrelated to object detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 语言模型预测下一个 token 的不确定度指标，与检测无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Perplexity measures a language model's uncertainty predicting the next token, unrelated to detection.

scenario: 模型不在云端 GPU 跑，而是装在车上的芯片里。
scenario_en: The model does not run on cloud GPUs but on a chip inside the vehicle.
q: AV 物体检测的部署环境有什么关键约束？
q_en: What is the key deployment constraint for AV object detection?
why: 车上是边缘设备，FLOPS、内存带宽都有限，还断不起网——不能把帧传云端(往返延迟就爆了 50ms 预算)。这逼你做量化、TensorRT 编译、选轻量单阶段模型。
why_en: The model runs on power- and bandwidth-limited edge chips and cannot offload frames to the cloud because the round trip alone blows the 50ms budget, which forces quantization, TensorRT, and lightweight single-stage models.
options: 跑在车载边缘设备(Jetson、Tesla FSD 芯片、ASIC)上，FLOPS 与带宽都受限
跑在数据中心的大规模 GPU 服务器集群上，算力几乎无限，只需要关心批处理吞吐量
跑在用户随身携带的手机上，靠车载 5G 蜂窝网络把每一帧实时上传到云端 GPU 推理、再把结果回传回来
跑在普通的服务器 CPU 上就行，物体检测对算力的要求本来就很低，不需要专用加速硬件
options_en: It runs on power- and bandwidth-limited in-vehicle edge devices (Jetson, Tesla FSD chip, ASICs).
It runs on a large-scale data-center GPU server cluster with near-unlimited compute, so only batch throughput matters.
It runs on the user's own phone, streaming every frame in real time over an onboard 5G cellular link to a cloud GPU for inference and back.
A plain server CPU suffices; object detection is inherently compute-light and needs no dedicated accelerator.
optionExplanations: 对；车载边缘算力/带宽有限，还得本地实时，这决定了所有部署侧优化。
云端集群的假设错了：车上没有无限算力，也承受不了云端往返延迟。
每帧上云往返延迟直接爆 50ms 预算，安全系统不能依赖网络。
实时多物体检测算力需求高，纯 CPU 达不到 30ms 推理，需专用加速。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — on-vehicle edge compute and bandwidth are limited and must run locally in real time, which drives every deployment optimization.
The cloud-cluster assumption is wrong: the car has no unlimited compute and cannot absorb cloud round-trip latency.
Uploading each frame blows the 50ms budget on the round trip, and a safety system cannot depend on the network.
Real-time multi-object detection is compute-heavy; a plain CPU cannot hit 30ms inference and needs an accelerator.

termDefinitions.meaning: 部署在数据产生现场(车上)的算力受限硬件，就地推理不依赖云。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge device is compute-limited hardware deployed where data is produced (the vehicle), inferring locally without the cloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒浮点运算次数，衡量算力；边缘设备的 FLOPS 有限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second) measures compute capacity, which is limited on edge devices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为特定任务(如推理)定制的专用芯片，能效比通用 GPU 高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ASIC (Application-Specific Integrated Circuit) is a chip customized for one task like inference, more efficient than a general GPU.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tesla 自研的车载自动驾驶推理芯片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The FSD (Full Self-Driving) chip is Tesla's in-house on-vehicle inference chip.

scenario: 边缘芯片内存和带宽有限，FP32 模型太大太慢。
scenario_en: Edge chip memory and bandwidth are limited, and the FP32 model is too big and slow.
q: 把模型从 FP32 量化到 FP16/INT8 有什么收益和代价？
q_en: What are the benefits and costs of quantizing the model from FP32 to FP16/INT8?
why: 量化用更少 bit 表示权重/激活(FP32→INT8 是 32→8 bit)，内存和带宽都降，还能用芯片的低精度计算单元加速；代价是数值精度下降，需校准防止掉点。
why_en: Quantization stores weights and activations in fewer bits (FP32 to INT8 is 32 down to 8), cutting memory and bandwidth and using the chip's low-precision units for speed, at the cost of accuracy you calibrate to protect.
options: 量化确实会增大模型的内存占用，但能换来更高的推理精度，很适合安全关键场景
量化只是改变了权重在磁盘上的存储格式而已，对实际推理速度和运行时内存占用都没有任何实质影响
FP32 降到 FP16/INT8：省内存、走低精度计算单元加速，代价是可能掉一点精度
量化本质上是把输入图片的分辨率主动降低以减少计算量，和模型权重完全无关
options_en: Quantization does increase memory footprint but buys higher inference accuracy, ideal for safety-critical use.
Quantization only changes how weights are stored on disk, with no real effect at all on actual inference speed or runtime memory footprint.
FP32 down to FP16/INT8: saves memory and uses low-precision compute units for speed, at the cost of some accuracy.
Quantization is essentially lowering the input image's resolution to cut compute, fundamentally unrelated to model weights.
optionExplanations: 反了：量化是减小内存、可能略降精度，不是增大内存换精度。
格式变了 bit 数就变了，内存和低精度算力都受益，不是没影响。
对；用更少 bit 换内存、带宽和速度，代价是精度略降，需校准。
量化改的是权重/激活的数值精度，不是图片分辨率，两者别混。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: quantization shrinks memory and may slightly cut accuracy, not the reverse.
Fewer bits changes memory and lets low-precision units help, so it is not a no-op.
Correct — fewer bits trade memory, bandwidth, and speed for a small accuracy drop you calibrate.
Quantization changes weight/activation numeric precision, not image resolution; do not conflate them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权重/激活从高精度浮点降到低 bit 表示，省内存、算力，略损精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers weights and activations from high-precision floats to fewer bits, saving memory and compute at some accuracy cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 32 位浮点数，训练默认精度，占内存大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP32 (32-bit Floating Point) is the default training precision and uses more memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 16 位浮点数，半精度，省一半内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP16 (16-bit Floating Point) is half precision, halving memory use.

termDefinitions.meaning: 8 位整数，量化最激进档，内存/算力最省但精度损失最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INT8 (8-bit Integer) is the most aggressive quantization, cheapest in memory and compute but with the largest accuracy loss.

scenario: 同一个模型直接跑和用厂商工具编译后跑，速度差很多。
scenario_en: The same model runs much faster after being compiled by the vendor's tool than run as-is.
q: TensorRT 在部署里起什么作用？
q_en: What role does TensorRT play in deployment?
why: TensorRT 是 NVIDIA 的推理优化编译器：把训练好的图针对目标 GPU 重编译——融合相邻层、删冗余算子、选最优 kernel，从而压低那 30ms 推理。它是部署侧优化，不改精度目标。
why_en: TensorRT is NVIDIA's inference compiler that re-optimizes a trained graph for the target GPU via layer fusion, redundancy elimination, and kernel selection to shrink that 30ms inference, without changing the accuracy target.
options: 一个数据标注工具，用来给训练帧画 3D 边界框
把计算图编译成硬件专属执行计划，做层融合、消冗余来加速推理
一种新的检测网络结构，用来替代 YOLO 充当特征提取主干网络
一个云端训练框架，负责多卡分布式训练调度
options_en: A data-annotation tool for drawing 3D bounding boxes on training frames.
It compiles the compute graph into a hardware-specific execution plan, fusing layers and cutting redundancy to speed inference.
A new detection architecture that replaces YOLO as the feature-extraction backbone.
A cloud training framework that schedules multi-GPU distributed training.
optionExplanations: 标注是数据侧工具，TensorRT 与画框无关。
对；它把图重编译成硬件专属计划，融合层+选优 kernel 压推理延迟。
TensorRT 不是网络结构，它优化的是已有模型的执行，不替代 backbone。
它做的是推理部署优化，不是训练调度框架。
optionExplanations_en: Annotation is a data-side tool; TensorRT has nothing to do with drawing boxes.
Correct — it recompiles the graph into a hardware-specific plan, fusing layers and picking optimal kernels to cut inference latency.
TensorRT is not an architecture; it optimizes an existing model's execution and does not replace a backbone.
It optimizes inference deployment, not training scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: NVIDIA 的推理优化编译器：把模型图针对目标 GPU 重编译加速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TensorRT is NVIDIA's inference compiler that recompiles a model graph for the target GPU to speed it up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相邻算子(如卷积+激活)合并成一个 kernel，减少内存往返、加速推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer fusion merges adjacent operators like conv and activation into one kernel, cutting memory traffic and speeding inference.

scenario: 一张街景图里绝大多数候选区域是背景，真正的前景物体极少。
scenario_en: In a street scene, the vast majority of candidate regions are background and true foreground objects are rare.
q: 训练检测器时用 focal loss 解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does focal loss solve when training a detector?
why: 一图里背景负样本压倒性多，普通交叉熵会被海量易分负样本淹没。focal loss 给已分对的样本乘一个衰减因子，down-weight 容易负样本，把梯度让给稀少难分的前景。
why_en: Backgrounds vastly outnumber objects so plain cross-entropy drowns in easy negatives; focal loss multiplies well-classified samples by a decay factor, down-weighting easy negatives so gradient focuses on rare hard foreground.
options: 它解决的是多机分布式训练时各节点之间的梯度同步问题，用来加快模型整体收敛速度
把输入图片压缩以适配边缘设备的有限内存，是一种部署侧的优化手段
给检测框做非极大值抑制处理，去掉同一个物体上重叠冗余的候选框
压低海量「容易的背景负样本」权重，让训练聚焦稀少前景，缓解前景-背景不平衡
options_en: It fixes gradient synchronization between nodes during multi-machine distributed training, to speed up overall model convergence.
It compresses input images to fit the edge device's limited memory, a deployment-side optimization.
It performs non-maximum suppression on boxes, removing overlapping redundant candidates on one object.
It down-weights the huge pool of easy background negatives so training focuses on the rare foreground, easing foreground-background imbalance.
optionExplanations: focal loss 是损失函数，与多机梯度同步无关。
它作用在训练损失上，不压缩图片，也不是部署优化。
去重叠框是 NMS 的活，发生在推理后处理，不是训练损失。
对；它衰减易分负样本、放大难分前景的梯度，专治极端类别不平衡。
optionExplanations_en: Focal loss is a loss function, unrelated to multi-machine gradient sync.
It acts on the training loss, not image compression, and is not a deployment optimization.
Removing overlaps is NMS at inference post-processing, not a training loss.
Correct — it decays easy negatives and amplifies gradient on hard foreground, targeting extreme class imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种给已分对样本加衰减因子的损失，down-weight 易分负样本、聚焦难例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Focal loss adds a decay factor on well-classified samples, down-weighting easy negatives to focus on hard examples.

termDefinitions.term: foreground-background imbalance / 前景-背景不平衡
termDefinitions.meaning: 一图里背景候选远多于前景物体，导致普通损失被背景淹没。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Foreground-background imbalance is when background candidates vastly outnumber objects, drowning ordinary loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类常用损失；在极端不平衡下会被大量易分负样本主导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-entropy is the standard classification loss, dominated by many easy negatives under extreme imbalance.

scenario: 想让答案从「只懂架构」升级到「懂部署」，该点名哪些手段压边缘推理开销。
scenario_en: To move the answer from 'architecture only' to 'deployment-aware', which techniques cut edge inference cost?
q: 哪些做法能压低边缘推理的延迟或内存？(多选)
q_en: Which techniques reduce edge inference latency or memory? (multiple)
why: 前三个都直接减少 FLOPS/内存或去掉顺序步骤，压的是那 30ms 推理；堆分辨率和加深网络只会推高延迟，方向相反。
why_en: The first three cut FLOPs, memory, or serial steps to shrink the 30ms inference, while cranking resolution and depth pushes latency the wrong way.
options: 量化 FP32→INT8，减少内存与带宽、走低精度计算单元
用 TensorRT 把图编译成硬件专属计划、融合层
选单阶段检测器(YOLO/SSD)避免两阶段的顺序开销
增大输入分辨率并加深 backbone，把 mAP 堆到最高
options_en: Quantize FP32 to INT8 to cut memory and bandwidth and use low-precision compute units.
Use TensorRT to compile the graph into a hardware-specific plan and fuse layers.
Pick a single-stage detector (YOLO/SSD) to avoid two-stage serial overhead.
Increase input resolution and deepen the backbone to maximize mAP.
optionExplanations: 对；INT8 权重更小、带宽更低，还能走芯片低精度单元，直接缩推理。
对；层融合+消冗余+选优 kernel 是部署侧提速核心，专压那 30ms。
对；单阶段一次前向省掉区域提议这步，是卡进 30ms 的结构性选择。
错；加大分辨率、加深网络会推高 FLOPS 和延迟，与边缘预算相反。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — INT8 weights are smaller with less bandwidth and use low-precision units, directly shrinking inference.
Correct — fusion, redundancy elimination, and kernel selection are core deployment speedups targeting that 30ms.
Correct — single-stage's one pass drops the proposal step, a structural choice to fit 30ms.
Wrong — bigger resolution and deeper networks raise FLOPs and latency, opposite to the edge budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测器提取特征的卷积网络主体；加深它会提高算力和延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The backbone is the detector's feature-extraction network; deepening it raises compute and latency.

scenario: 安全关键系统里，漏检和误检的后果完全不对等。
scenario_en: In a safety-critical system, the costs of a miss and a false alarm are not symmetric.
q: 在 AV 检测里，false negative 和 false positive 哪个更该被优先压低？
q_en: In AV detection, which should you prioritize reducing — false negatives or false positives?
why: 代价不对称：漏检行人=规划栈拿不到目标、永不减速，可能致命；误检=多刹一脚，不适但能活。所以安全关键类要往高召回调，宁可多几次幻影刹车。
why_en: The costs are asymmetric: a missed pedestrian means the planner never brakes and can be fatal, while a phantom detection just means an unnecessary brake, so safety-critical classes are tuned for high recall.
tradeoff: 高召回压 FN(防致命漏检) vs 高精度压 FP(防幻影刹车、代价较轻)
diagram:
flowchart TB D["检测器输出"] --> FN["漏检 FN
真行人当背景"] --> X["规划永不刹车
可能致命"] D --> FP["误检 FP
阴影当障碍"] --> Y["多刹一脚
不适但可生还"]
options: false positive 更严重：幻影刹车会被后车追尾撞上，必须优先彻底消除，哪怕因此漏检也值得
两者代价基本对称，用一个全局置信度阈值平衡精度和召回即可
false negative 更严重：漏检真行人规划栈永不刹车、可能致命，所以优先保召回
都不关键，检测错了后面还有 LiDAR 兜底，阈值随便设都行
options_en: False positives are worse: phantom braking risks being rear-ended, so eliminate them first even if it means missing objects.
The costs are basically symmetric; one global confidence threshold balances precision and recall.
False negatives are worse: missing a real pedestrian means the planner never brakes and can be fatal, so prioritize recall.
Neither matters; LiDAR backs up detection errors, so thresholds can be set arbitrarily.
optionExplanations: 反了：漏检可能致命，误检只是多刹一脚，不能为省 FP 牺牲召回。
代价并不对称，单一全局阈值恰恰无法照顾行人这类高危漏检。
对；漏检致命、误检可生还，所以安全关键类往高召回调。
把安全全押在 LiDAR 兜底上不成立，相机漏检本身就是核心风险。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: a miss can be fatal while a false alarm just brakes, so you cannot trade recall to cut FPs.
The costs are not symmetric, and one global threshold cannot protect high-risk misses like pedestrians.
Correct — a miss is fatal and a false alarm survivable, so safety-critical classes are tuned for high recall.
Betting safety on LiDAR backup fails; a camera miss is itself a core risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏检：真实存在的物体没被检出，在 AV 里可能致命。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative (FN) is a real object the detector misses, potentially fatal in an AV.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误检：把不存在的物体报成障碍，导致不必要刹车。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive (FP) is a phantom object flagged as an obstacle, causing an unnecessary brake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实物体中被成功检出的比例，越高漏检越少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of real objects successfully detected; higher means fewer misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 报出的检测里真为物体的比例，越高误检越少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of reported detections that are real; higher means fewer false alarms.

scenario: 行人检测器精度很高但偶尔漏人；有人提议调高阈值把误检清干净。
scenario_en: The pedestrian detector is high-precision but occasionally misses people; someone proposes raising the threshold to clean up false alarms.
q: 对行人这类安全关键类，该往哪个方向调？
q_en: For safety-critical classes like pedestrians, which way do you tune?
why: 安全关键类按不对称代价往高召回调：多几次幻影刹车可接受，漏一个行人不可接受。手段是给行人单独调低置信度阈值，而不是提高。
why_en: Safety-critical classes are tuned for high recall under asymmetric cost — extra phantom brakes are acceptable, a missed pedestrian is not — by lowering the pedestrian confidence threshold rather than raising it.
options: 往高召回调，宁可牺牲一点精度也不能漏人；漏检的代价远超多刹几脚
往高精度方向调，把行人的置信度阈值提高，彻底消除幻影刹车才是最重要的
保持默认全局阈值，行人和路锥一视同仁，避免偏袒
直接关掉行人类的检测，交给 LiDAR 专门处理最省事
options_en: Tune for high recall, accepting some precision loss rather than missing people, since a miss far outweighs a few extra brakes.
Tune toward high precision by raising the pedestrian confidence threshold; eliminating phantom braking is what matters most.
Keep the default global threshold, treating pedestrians and cones alike to avoid bias.
Just turn off the pedestrian class and let LiDAR handle it, the simplest option.
optionExplanations: 对；不对称代价下安全类要高召回，调低行人阈值防漏检。
提阈值会增加漏检，正好放大最致命的错误方向，不可取。
全局一视同仁做不到按类松紧，行人这类高危需要单独放宽。
关掉相机检测把安全全压在 LiDAR，冗余原则要求相机自身高召回。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — under asymmetric cost safety classes need high recall, so lower the pedestrian threshold to avoid misses.
Raising the threshold increases misses, amplifying the most fatal error direction.
A uniform global threshold cannot loosen per class, but high-risk pedestrians need their own relaxation.
Turning off camera detection bets all safety on LiDAR; redundancy demands the camera itself stay high-recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测分数高于它才被判为有物体；调低提高召回，调高提高精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A confidence threshold is the score above which a detection counts; lowering it raises recall, raising it raises precision.

scenario: 用一个全局置信度阈值时，要么行人漏检、要么路锥误报，顾此失彼。
scenario_en: With one global confidence threshold you either miss pedestrians or over-report traffic cones — you cannot win both.
q: 置信度阈值该怎么设？
q_en: How should you set the confidence thresholds?
why: 不同类代价不对称：漏行人致命、误报路锥只是多刹一脚，所以行人阈值调低(0.3)拉高召回、路锥调高(0.6)压误报。一个全局阈值做不到这种按类松紧。
why_en: Because class costs differ — a missed pedestrian is fatal, a false cone just brakes — you lower the pedestrian threshold to about 0.3 for recall and raise the cone threshold to about 0.6, which a single global threshold cannot express.
tradeoff: 类别专属阈值(贴合不对称代价、更安全) vs 全局阈值(简单但顾此失彼)
whenOtherWins: 当各类代价大致对称、且标注/调参预算有限时，单一全局阈值更简单可维护。
options: 用一个统一的全局阈值(如 0.5)对所有类别一视同仁地处理，简单、好维护、也好解释
按类别分设阈值：行人 0.3 就触发、路锥要 0.6，用不对称代价定每类松紧
把所有类别的阈值都提到 0.9，只保留最有把握的检测，看起来最安全
干脆不设任何阈值，把所有候选框都输出，让规划栈自己去筛选
options_en: Use one unified global threshold (e.g. 0.5) for all classes alike: simple, maintainable, and explainable.
Set per-class thresholds: pedestrian fires at 0.3, cone requires 0.6, letting asymmetric cost set each class's strictness.
Raise every class threshold to 0.9, keeping only the most confident detections, which looks safest.
Set no threshold at all, output every candidate box, and let the planner filter.
optionExplanations: 全局阈值简单，但没法同时满足行人要松、路锥要紧的相反需求。
对；按类别的不对称代价分别设阈值，行人放宽保召回、路锥收紧压误报。
把行人也提到 0.9 会大量漏检，正是安全关键类最不该做的。
不设阈值把海量低质框全丢给规划栈，制造噪声与延迟，规划无法承受。
optionExplanations_en: A global threshold is simple but cannot meet the opposite needs of loose pedestrians and strict cones.
Correct — per-class thresholds from asymmetric cost loosen pedestrians for recall and tighten cones against false alarms.
Pushing pedestrians to 0.9 causes many misses, exactly what safety-critical classes must not do.
No threshold dumps a flood of low-quality boxes on the planner, creating noise and latency it cannot handle.

termDefinitions.term: class-specific threshold / 类别专属阈值
termDefinitions.meaning: 每个类用自己的置信度门槛，按该类漏检/误检的代价单独调松紧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A class-specific threshold gives each class its own confidence cutoff, tuned to that class's miss and false-alarm costs.

scenario: 检测器对同一个物体给出中等置信度，但它离车的远近不同。
scenario_en: The detector gives medium confidence on the same object, but its distance to the car varies.
q: Time-to-Collision(TTC)怎么把置信度接到具体动作上？
q_en: How does Time-to-Collision (TTC) connect confidence to a concrete action?
why: TTC 把「多确信才动手」和「还剩多少时间」绑在一起：时间紧(0.5s)时即便置信不高也得先动、宁可误刹；时间宽(5s)时可以等跨帧确认降误报。同一置信度，动作因 TTC 不同。
why_en: TTC ties 'how sure before acting' to 'how much time is left': with 0.5s you act even on low confidence rather than wait, but with 5s you can hold for cross-frame confirmation, so the same confidence yields different actions.
diagram:
flowchart TB L["低置信 + TTC 0.5s"] --> A["立刻动作
来不及等确认"] S["同样置信 + TTC 5s"] --> W["等跨帧确认
再决定"]
options: TTC 只是用来粗略估算车辆当前刹车距离的一个辅助数值，跟检测置信度的高低其实完全没有任何关系
TTC 数值越大就代表当前路况情况越危险，应该立即刹车，完全不需要等待跨帧确认
低置信+TTC 0.5s→立刻动作，来不及等确认；同样置信+TTC 5s→等下一帧确认再决定
TTC 其实就是当前车载相机帧率的倒数，只是被用来决定每秒能处理多少帧而已
options_en: TTC is only an auxiliary number for roughly estimating the car's current braking distance, with no relation at all to detection confidence.
A larger TTC means more danger, so brake immediately with no need to wait for cross-frame confirmation.
Low confidence with TTC 0.5s means act now with no time to confirm; the same confidence with TTC 5s means wait for the next frame to confirm.
TTC is simply the reciprocal of the onboard camera's frame rate, just used to decide how many frames are processed per second.
optionExplanations: TTC 恰恰是把置信度接到动作的桥梁，不是与置信无关的距离计算。
说反了：TTC 越小才越紧急；大 TTC 反而有时间等确认。
对；TTC 短就先动、宁可误刹，TTC 长就等跨帧确认降误报。
TTC 是碰撞剩余时间，不是帧率倒数，别混。
optionExplanations_en: TTC is precisely the bridge from confidence to action, not a distance calc unrelated to confidence.
Backwards: smaller TTC is more urgent; a large TTC leaves time to confirm.
Correct — short TTC means act now even risking a false brake, long TTC means wait for cross-frame confirmation.
TTC is time-to-collision, not the reciprocal of frame rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按当前相对速度撞上物体还剩多少时间，短则必须立刻反应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTC (Time-to-Collision) is how long until impact at current closing speed; short TTC forces an immediate reaction.

scenario: 检测器老把阴影、路面标线、反光当成障碍物，误检不断。
