对；FID 比较生成图像和真实图像的分布距离，CLIP Score 比较图像和文本在语义空间的接近程度。
错；FID 恰好相反，分数越低代表和真实图像分布越接近、质量越好。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — GPU memory and latency are engineering metrics; these two scores measure image quality and alignment.
Incorrect — both are proxy metrics that can diverge from real user satisfaction, not an exact equivalence.
Correct — FID compares generated vs. real image distributions; CLIP Score compares image and text in a shared embedding space.
Incorrect — it's the opposite: a lower FID means the generated distribution is closer to real images.

termDefinitions.meaning: 比较生成图像和真实图像分布的相似度，越低越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FID compares the statistical distribution of generated images to real images; lower is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量生成图像与文本提示在语义空间里的对齐程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CLIP Score measures how well a generated image aligns with its text prompt in a shared embedding space.

scenario: 一个模型升级后主指标变好看了，但客服投诉和安全事件同时增多。
scenario_en: After a model upgrade, the primary metric improves, but support complaints and safety incidents also increase.
q: 为什么“没有单一指标能说明全部问题”是评估中的核心原则？
q_en: Why is 'no single metric captures everything' a core evaluation principle?
why: 单一数字会忽略某些失败模式；成熟评估要用主指标、guardrail 和切片指标组合着看。
why_en: No single metric captures all production tradeoffs, so evaluation needs primary metrics, guardrails, slices, and diagnostics.
options: 业务、体验、安全、成本和质量常互相冲突
评估指标定义得越少，结果就越真实可信
所有类型的任务都可以直接拿 accuracy 来衡量
线上系统一旦上线之后就再也不会发生漂移
options_en: Business, experience, safety, cost, and model quality often conflict with each other.
The fewer metrics you define, the more trustworthy the result is.
Every type of task can be measured directly with accuracy.
Once a production system has shipped, it will never drift again.
optionExplanations: 对；主指标变好时，安全或体验可能同时变差，必须多维一起看。
错；指标少反而容易漏掉某些失败模式，不代表更真实。
错；accuracy 在不平衡或生成类任务里常常失效或误导。
错；线上流量和内容会随时间变化，系统一定会漂移。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a rising primary metric can coexist with worsening safety or experience, so multiple views are needed.
Incorrect — fewer metrics tend to hide failure modes, not reveal more truth.
Incorrect — accuracy often fails or misleads on imbalanced or generative tasks.
Incorrect — live traffic and content change over time, so systems always drift eventually.

termDefinitions.meaning: 必须维持在某个门槛之上/之下才允许上线的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric must stay above or below a threshold before a change is allowed to ship.

scenario: 总体指标很好，但某些语言用户投诉搜索很差。
scenario_en: Overall metrics look good, but users in some languages complain that search quality is poor.
q: 最应该补什么评估？
q_en: What evaluation should be added first?
why: 总体平均会掩盖小群体或长尾 query 的失败；切片评估能定位特定用户群、语言或内容类型上的回归。
why_en: Slice evaluation exposes failures hidden by aggregate metrics, such as poor quality for a specific language or region.
tradeoff: 总体平均指标（简单但会掩盖问题）vs 按群体切片（更贵但能定位问题）
options: 只提高总样本量，不做切片
按语言、地区、意图切片的指标
直接删除被投诉的语言
只看训练 loss
options_en: Just increase the overall sample size without slicing.
Metrics sliced by language, locale, and intent.
Simply drop the language that is complaining.
Only look at training loss.
whenOtherWins: 如果投诉来自单个异常事件，先做事件级排查再扩展成长期切片。
optionExplanations: 错；总样本量再大，小语种占比还是低，问题一样被平均掉。
对；按语言/地区/意图切片才能看到总体平均掩盖的局部回归。
错；删掉投诉语言只是掩盖问题，不是修复评估或产品体验。
错；训练 loss 是模型训练信号，反映不出线上某语言的真实体验。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — a bigger overall sample still has a tiny share of that language, so it stays averaged out.
Correct — slicing by language, locale, and intent surfaces regressions the overall average hides.
Incorrect — dropping the complaining language hides the problem instead of fixing evaluation or the product.
Incorrect — training loss is a training-time signal and does not reflect real experience for one language.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按语言、地区或用户群体拆分指标，而不是只看总体平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slice evaluation breaks metrics down by language, locale, or user group instead of only looking at the overall average.

scenario: 违规内容自动删除要替掉一部分人工审核，人工审核员的判定准确率约 95%，低于人工的自动决策产品不接受。
scenario_en: An auto-removal model replaces part of manual moderation; human reviewers judge correctly about 95 percent of the time, and the product will not accept automation below human level.
q: 自动删除的 precision 操作点该定在哪？
q_en: Where should the precision operating point for auto-removal be fixed?
why: 把 precision 钉在人工审核水平 95%，系统才算不比人差、可以替换人工；代价是 recall 被压低，漏放的违规内容仍要人工兜底。
why_en: Fixing precision at the human review level makes the model at least as trustworthy as a reviewer, at the cost of lower recall that humans must still cover.
tradeoff: 对齐人工的高 precision（可替换人工但漏放多）vs 追 recall（少漏但误删激增）
options: 选 PR 曲线上 F1 最高的那个阈值点，让两类错误平衡
取 recall 最高的那个阈值，宁可多误删也绝不漏掉任何一条违规内容
对齐人工水平，把 precision 固定在 95% 再看 recall
先不定阈值直接放量上线，等用户投诉数据回来之后再回头补一个
options_en: Pick the threshold with the highest F1 on the precision-recall curve.
Take the highest-recall threshold and accept far more false removals so nothing violating slips through.
Fix precision at 95 percent to match human reviewers, then read recall there.
Ship with no threshold and set one later once user complaints come back.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型只做人工审核的排序队列、不直接删除，就该放松 precision 去追 recall。
optionExplanations: 错；F1 把误删和漏放同等看待，但自动删除的误删代价远高于漏放。
错；recall 优先会让大量正常内容被误删，直接推高申诉率和用户流失。
对；人工准确率就是产品能接受的下限，钉住它再报该点的 recall。
错；没有事前阈值就没有可对比的操作点，投诉数据也无法反推该调哪边。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — F1 weighs false removals and misses equally, but auto-removal punishes false removals far more.
Incorrect — a recall-first threshold removes lots of legitimate content, driving appeals and churn.
Correct — human accuracy is the floor the product accepts, so fix it there and read recall at that point.
Incorrect — with no prior operating point there is nothing to compare, and complaints cannot tell you which side to move.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型判为违规的内容中，真的违规的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the share of items flagged as violating that really are violating.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全部真实违规内容中，被模型抓到的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the share of all truly violating content that the model catches.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision 与 recall 的调和平均，把两类错误同等看待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, weighting both error types equally.

scenario: 推荐排序 NDCG@10 提升明显，但下游曝光预算系统直接把模型分数当成用户参与概率来分配展示位。
scenario_en: A recommender improves NDCG at 10, but a downstream budgeting system reads the model score directly as an engagement probability to allocate slots.
q: 推荐分数还必须补测哪个指标？
q_en: Which additional metric must the recommendation scores be checked against?
why: 排序指标只看相对顺序，分数整体偏高照样满分；下游按概率花钱时必须查 calibration，代价是要额外维护分桶统计并定期重校准。
why_en: Ranking metrics only judge relative order, so scores can be uniformly inflated and still look perfect; if a downstream system spends money on those scores you must check calibration.
tradeoff: 只优化排序（便宜但分数不可当概率用）vs 额外做校准（可当概率但要持续重校准）
options: 继续只看 NDCG@10 的排序质量，顺序对了下游怎么用这个分数都安全
Calibration：分数分布是否匹配实际参与率
Coverage：一段时间窗口内目录里有多少商品被展示过
MRR：第一个相关结果出现位置的平均倒数
options_en: Keep tracking only NDCG at 10, since correct ordering makes the raw score safe for any downstream use.
Calibration: does the score distribution match observed engagement rates?
Coverage: what share of the catalog gets surfaced over a time window.
MRR: the average reciprocal position of the first relevant result.
whenOtherWins: 如果分数只用来排序、从不被当成概率消费，排序指标就够，不必额外做校准。
optionExplanations: 错；顺序正确不代表数值正确，分数整体偏高会让预算系统系统性超配。
对；它比较预测分数分布与实际参与率，正是把分数当概率用的前提。
错；Coverage 衡量目录被展示的广度，管不到分数数值本身准不准。
错；MRR 只看第一个相关项的位置，同样是顺序指标而非数值指标。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — correct ordering does not make the numbers correct; inflated scores make the budget system systematically overspend.
Correct — it compares predicted score distribution against observed engagement rates, which is what treating scores as probabilities requires.
Incorrect — coverage measures how broadly the catalog is surfaced, not whether the score values are accurate.
Incorrect — MRR only looks at the first relevant item's position, another ordering metric rather than a value metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查预测分数分布是否与实际观测到的参与概率吻合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration checks whether the predicted score distribution matches observed engagement probabilities.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益：按位置折损相关性再归一化的排序指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG discounts relevance by log rank and normalizes against the ideal ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均倒数排名：只看第一个相关结果位置的倒数再平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MRR averages one over the position of the first relevant result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段时间内目录中被展示过的条目比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage is the proportion of the catalog surfaced over a time window.

scenario: 推荐系统真正的目标是六个月后的订阅续费，但一次线上实验最多只能跑几周。
scenario_en: The recommender's true objective is subscription renewal six months later, but a single experiment can only run for a few weeks.
q: 怎么在短实验里估计这个长周期目标？
q_en: How do you estimate that long-horizon objective inside a short experiment?
why: 长周期目标测不到时，用与之相关的代理指标加周期性 hold-out cohort 长期追踪来逼近；代价是代理与真目标的相关性本身要反复验证。
why_en: When the true objective is too far out to measure, combine proxy metrics with periodic hold-out cohorts, and keep re-validating that the proxy still tracks the real goal.
tradeoff: 短期代理指标（快但可能与真目标脱钩）vs 长期 hold-out cohort（准但慢且长期占流量）
options: 直接把点击率当作续费率的等价物，反正两者都是正向的用户参与信号
把实验一直跑满六个月，期间不做任何决策也不发布任何新模型
用代理指标加周期性 hold-out cohort 估计长期效应
只看离线 NDCG，线上长期指标交给业务团队自己去跟
options_en: Just treat click-through rate as equivalent to renewal rate, since both are positive engagement signals.
Run the experiment for a full six months and ship nothing while it runs.
Use proxy metrics plus periodic hold-out cohorts to estimate the long-range effect.
Track only offline NDCG and leave long-term metrics to the business team.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品目标本身就是即时转化（如单次购买），短期指标就是真目标，不需要 cohort。
optionExplanations: 错；短期点击常常靠标题党拿到，反而侵蚀满意度，和续费方向相反。
错；六个月冻结发布的机会成本极高，业务不可能接受这种迭代节奏。
对；代理指标给快速信号，hold-out cohort 给长期真值来校准代理。
错；离线 NDCG 连线上短期效果都只是近似，更够不到六个月后的续费。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — short-term clicks are often won with clickbait that erodes satisfaction, pushing renewal the other way.
Incorrect — freezing releases for six months costs far too much iteration speed for the business to accept.
Correct — proxies give a fast signal while hold-out cohorts supply the long-run ground truth that recalibrates them.
Incorrect — offline NDCG only approximates even short-term online effects, let alone renewal six months out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长期不接受新模型的一组用户，用来观察长周期真实效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hold-out cohort is a group of users kept off the new model for a long period so you can observe real long-range effects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以快速测量、且与真正业务目标相关的替代指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy metric is a fast-to-measure stand-in that correlates with the real business objective.

scenario: 推荐模型只在自己曝光过的物品上收到点击，训练日志越来越像模型自己的回音室，长尾内容再也进不来。
scenario_en: A recommender only ever gets clicks on items it already surfaced, so training logs become an echo chamber of its own output and long-tail items never re-enter.
q: 该往线上加哪种流量来打破这个循环？
q_en: What kind of traffic should you add online to break that loop?
why: 只有主动注入探索流量（ε-greedy 或 Thompson Sampling）才能拿到模型本来不会曝光的物品的反馈；代价是这部分流量的即时指标会变差。
why_en: Only deliberately injected exploration traffic, via epsilon-greedy or Thompson Sampling, produces feedback on items the model would never have shown, and it costs short-term metrics on that slice.
tradeoff: 纯利用当前最优（短期指标好但日志自我强化）vs 注入探索流量（短期掉点但日志无偏）
options: 把训练数据量加大，把过去两年的全部历史点击日志重新灌进模型里从头再完整训练一遍
注入 ε-greedy 或 Thompson Sampling 的探索流量
提高模型容量，用更深的网络去拟合现有点击日志里更细微的模式
把排序阈值调低，让更多物品进入候选集但仍按同一个模型分数排序
options_en: Add more training data by re-feeding two full years of historical click logs into the model.
Inject exploration traffic using epsilon-greedy or Thompson Sampling.
Increase model capacity with a deeper network to fit subtler patterns in the existing click logs.
Lower the ranking cutoff so more items enter the candidate set, still ordered by the same model score.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务处在大促之类不能容忍任何指标下滑的窗口，可先用离线反事实重加权替代在线探索。
optionExplanations: 错；历史日志同样是模型自己曝光的结果，加量只会放大同一个偏差。
对；随机或按不确定性展示非最优项，才能采到缺失区域的反馈。
错；模型再强也只能学到日志里有的信号，从未曝光的物品仍然没有标签。
错；候选集变大但排序仍由同一模型决定，最终曝光的还是同一批物品。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — historical logs are also the model's own output, so more of them just amplifies the same bias.
Correct — showing non-optimal items randomly or by uncertainty is the only way to collect feedback from the missing region.
Incorrect — a stronger model can only learn signals present in the logs; never-shown items still have no labels.
Incorrect — a bigger candidate set still gets ordered by the same model, so the same items end up exposed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以小概率 ε 随机展示非最优项，其余时间展示当前最优项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon-greedy shows a random non-optimal item with small probability epsilon and the current best item otherwise.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按各候选“可能是最优”的后验概率抽样展示，不确定性越大越常被试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson Sampling samples each candidate in proportion to its posterior probability of being best, so uncertain items get tried more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的曝光决定了未来训练数据，从而不断强化自身偏好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop means the model's own exposures shape future training data and keep reinforcing its existing preferences.

scenario: 推荐 A/B 中 treatment 换了候选生成逻辑，日志里只写最终展示出的排序列表，不记候选池和特征。
scenario_en: In a recommender A/B test the treatment changed candidate generation, but logs store only the final displayed ranking, not the candidate pool or features.
q: 这套日志方案会怎样让实验静默失败？
q_en: How does that logging scheme make the experiment fail silently?
why: treatment 召回到 control 从未见过的物品，事后既无法重放这些候选也无法区分收益来自召回还是排序，实验照常出数却不可信；补救只能重做，整轮流量白花。
why_en: The treatment surfaces candidates control never saw, so afterwards you cannot replay them or tell whether the lift came from retrieval or ranking; the test still reports numbers that mean nothing.
options: 日志体积随候选数线性膨胀，存储成本翻倍，最终被迫大幅缩短日志保留期
分流比例被随机数种子偏斜，treatment 桶的样本量长期达不到统计功效要求
control 从没见过 treatment 的候选，事后无法重放比较
写日志进入请求主路径，把搜索 p99 延迟推高到 SLO 之外并触发线上告警
options_en: Log volume grows linearly with candidate count, doubling storage cost and forcing a much shorter retention window.
The bucketing seed skews the split, so the treatment bucket never reaches statistical power.
Control never saw the treatment's candidates, so the comparison cannot be replayed afterwards.
Logging sits in the request path and pushes search p99 latency past the SLO, firing production alerts.
optionExplanations: 错；这是成本问题，实验结论仍然有效，缩短保留期也不影响本轮对比。
错；分流偏斜会被样本量监控直接发现，不属于“静默”失败模式。
对；候选池没落盘，treatment 独有的曝光无法在 control 侧复算，结论不可归因。
错；延迟劣化会被 p99 告警立刻暴露，属于显式故障而非隐性失效。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — that is a cost problem; the experiment's conclusion still holds and retention length does not affect this comparison.
Incorrect — a skewed split is caught immediately by sample-size monitoring, so it is not a silent failure.
Correct — with the candidate pool unlogged, treatment-only exposures cannot be recomputed on the control side, so nothing is attributable.
Incorrect — latency regressions trip p99 alerts right away, which makes it an explicit failure rather than a silent one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录全部候选和特征，使任一模型都能在同一批候选上事后重算排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replayability means logging all candidates and features so any model can be re-scored on the same candidate set afterwards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序之前从全量物料里召回一个小候选集的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the stage that retrieves a small candidate set from the full catalog before ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级别目标：对延迟或可用性设定的可量化承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO is a service level objective, a measurable target for latency or availability.

scenario: 新闻搜索里突发事件的报道要在几分钟内可被搜到，团队要给新鲜度定一组可监控的指标。
scenario_en: In news search, breaking coverage must be findable within minutes, and the team needs a monitorable set of freshness metrics.
q: 新鲜度评估该盯哪几类指标？（多选）
q_en: Which metric families should freshness evaluation track? (Select all that apply.)
why: 新鲜度可能坏在结果过期、抓取太慢、索引没更新三个不同环节，各要一个指标才能定位；只报总体相关性会把三者混成一次模糊的下降。
why_en: Freshness can break at three different places — stale relevance, slow crawling, or a lagging index — so each needs its own metric to localize the problem.
options: temporal relevance：不同类型 query 的结果多快变过期
crawl latency：内容产生到被抓取之间的延迟
index freshness：索引相对线上最新内容的滞后
训练时用的 GPU 显存占用峰值
options_en: Temporal relevance: how fast results go stale for each query type.
Crawl latency: the delay from content creation to it being crawled.
Index freshness: how far the index lags behind the latest live content.
Peak GPU memory used during training.
optionExplanations: 对；它告诉你哪些 query 需要按时间衰减相关性，哪些常青内容不用。
对；它把“搜不到新闻”定位到抓取环节，而不是排序模型的锅。
对；它暴露抓到了但还没进索引的滞后，也就是发了却搜不到的那段。
错；显存是训练资源指标，和用户能不能搜到刚发布的内容无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it tells you which queries need time decay on relevance and which evergreen ones do not.
Correct — it localizes a missing-news complaint to the crawler rather than the ranking model.
Correct — it exposes content that was crawled but not yet indexed, the classic published-but-unsearchable gap.
Incorrect — GPU memory is a training resource metric, unrelated to whether users can find newly published content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量某类查询的结果多快就变得过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal relevance measures how quickly results go stale for a given query type.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容被创建到被爬虫抓到之间的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Crawl latency is the time from content creation to the crawler fetching it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引内容相对线上最新内容的滞后程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index freshness measures how far the search index lags behind the latest live content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器：训练深度模型的主要算力硬件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU is the graphics processing unit hardware that does most deep model training.

scenario: 聊天助手上线一年后，BLEU 和自动事实检查通过率都稳定在 0.97 附近，两个候选模型分不出高下，但用户投诉仍在增加。
scenario_en: A year after launch, the chat assistant's BLEU and automated fact-check pass rate both sit near 0.97, two candidate models look identical, yet user complaints keep rising.
q: 这种指标停滞说明什么该改？
q_en: What does this metric stagnation tell you needs to change?
why: 指标会饱和：系统成熟后旧指标顶到天花板就失去区分度，必须换更难的测试集或更细的维度；代价是新旧版本的历史分数不再直接可比。
why_en: Metrics saturate — once a mature system tops out an old metric it stops discriminating, so evaluation itself must evolve, at the cost of breaking comparability with historical numbers.
options: 说明模型已经足够好了，可以停掉评估投入把资源全部转去做新功能开发
说明指标已经饱和，评估体系本身要随系统成熟而演进
说明测试集样本量不够，只要把同样分布的样本再扩大十倍就能重新分出差距
说明应该改用更宽松的通过阈值，这样两个模型之间的分数差异会被放大出来
options_en: It means the model is good enough, so evaluation spend can move to building new features.
It means the metrics have saturated and the evaluation suite must evolve as the system matures.
It means the test set is too small, and ten times more samples from the same distribution would separate them.
It means you should loosen the pass threshold so the gap between the two models gets amplified.
optionExplanations: 错；投诉还在涨说明失败模式真实存在，只是现有指标看不到它。
对；换更难的分层测试集或拆出新维度，才能重新获得区分度。
错；同分布样本再多也只是把同一个天花板测得更精确，差距依旧为零。
错；调阈值只是移动刻度，不会引入任何关于失败模式的新信息。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — complaints are still rising, so real failure modes exist; the current metrics just cannot see them.
Correct — a harder stratified test set or new sub-dimensions are what restore discriminating power.
Incorrect — more samples from the same distribution only measure the same ceiling more precisely; the gap stays zero.
Incorrect — moving the threshold just rescales the same numbers without adding information about failure modes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双语评估替补：按 n-gram 重合度衡量生成文本与参考答案的相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU scores generated text by n-gram overlap against reference answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标接近上限后不同模型的分数几乎一样，失去区分能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Saturation is when a metric nears its ceiling and stops separating different models.

scenario: 营销文案生成的人工评分只有一个 1-5 的好不好总分，两个评审经常给同一段文案打 2 分和 4 分，且说不清分歧在哪。
scenario_en: Human review of marketing copy uses a single 1-5 overall quality score; two reviewers often give the same text a 2 and a 4 and cannot say where they disagree.
q: 怎么让这个主观评分变得可测？
q_en: How do you make that subjective score measurable?
why: 把好不好拆成 fluency、coherence、style 等各自可判定的子维度，分歧才能定位到具体维度并写进标注规范；代价是每条样本的标注成本翻几倍。
why_en: Break overall quality into separately judgeable aspects like fluency, coherence, and style so disagreement localizes to one dimension, at the cost of several times more annotation work per sample.
tradeoff: 单一总分（便宜但评审一致性差）vs 拆分子维度（一致性高但标注成本翻几倍）
options: 把评审人数从 2 人加到 7 人，取中位数当最终分，用人数把噪声平均掉
拆成 fluency、coherence、style 等子维度分别打分
改用 BLEU 之类的自动重合度分数彻底取代人工评审，直接绕开一致性问题
只保留总分但把量表从 1-5 换成 1-100，让评审有更细的刻度可以选择
options_en: Raise the panel from two to seven reviewers and take the median so noise averages out.
Split the score into aspects such as fluency, coherence, and style.
Replace human review entirely with an automated overlap score like BLEU to sidestep agreement issues.
Keep one overall score but switch the scale from 1-5 to 1-100 for finer granularity.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要在两个候选之间排序而不需要诊断，成对偏好比较比拆维度更快也更一致。
optionExplanations: 错；人多只是摊薄噪声，评审心里的标准仍然不同，分歧原因照样查不出。
对；分歧落到具体维度后可以写进标注规范，也能定位模型弱在哪一项。
错；营销文案没有唯一参考答案，重合度分数对风格和语气几乎没有信号。
错；刻度更细只会让主观分更分散，没有解决在评什么这个根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — more reviewers only dilutes noise; their internal standards still differ and the cause of disagreement stays hidden.
Correct — once disagreement lands on a named aspect it can be written into the labeling guide and traced to a model weakness.
Incorrect — marketing copy has no single reference answer, so overlap scores carry almost no signal about tone or style.
Incorrect — a finer scale just spreads subjective scores further without fixing what is actually being judged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成文本的语法和用词是否自然通顺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fluency is whether the generated text reads naturally and grammatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整段内容前后逻辑是否一致、不自相矛盾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coherence is whether the passage stays logically consistent from start to end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让评审在固定档位（如 1-5）上给出主观程度评分的量表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Likert scale asks raters to score on a fixed set of levels such as one to five.

scenario: 面向青少年的助手，放出一条违法内容会引来监管处罚和品牌事故；误拦一条安全回答只会让用户重问一次。
scenario_en: For a teen-facing assistant, letting one illicit response through means regulatory penalties and brand damage, while wrongly blocking a safe answer just makes the user retry.
q: 安全评估的主指标该盯哪个？
q_en: Which metric should safety evaluation track as its primary number?
why: 漏放一条危险输出的代价远高于误伤一条安全输出，所以安全评估以 false-negative rate 为主指标；代价是拦截更激进，正常回答的误拦率随之上升。
why_en: Missing one harmful output costs far more than wrongly flagging a safe one, so safety evaluation leads with false-negative rate and accepts a higher false-positive rate as the price.
tradeoff: 压低 false-negative（少漏危险但误拦多）vs 压低 false-positive（体验顺但漏放风险高）
options: false-negative rate：危险输出被安全过滤器放过去的比例
整体 accuracy：安全分类器在全部样本上判断正确的比例有多高
prompt-response latency：用户发出请求到看到回答之间等待了多久
false-positive rate：安全输出被误拦下来、让用户不得不重问一次的比例
options_en: False-negative rate: the share of harmful outputs the safety filter lets through.
Overall accuracy: how often the safety classifier is correct across all samples.
Prompt-response latency: how long the user waits between asking and seeing an answer.
False-positive rate: the share of safe outputs wrongly blocked, forcing the user to ask again.
whenOtherWins: 如果场景是低风险的内部工具、误拦会直接卡住工作流，就该反过来先压 false-positive。
optionExplanations: 对；它直接对应危险内容流到青少年用户面前这个不可接受的后果。
错；危险样本占比极低，accuracy 会被大量安全样本主导而看起来很漂亮。
错；延迟是体验指标，和内容安不安全是两个正交的维度。
错；误拦只让用户重问一次，代价远低于放过一条违法内容。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it maps directly onto the unacceptable outcome of harmful content reaching teen users.
Incorrect — harmful samples are rare, so accuracy is dominated by safe ones and looks great regardless.
Incorrect — latency is an experience metric, orthogonal to whether the content is safe.
Incorrect — a wrongly blocked answer just costs one retry, far less than letting illicit content through.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实为危险内容却被模型判为安全的情况。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative is harmful content that the model wrongly judges to be safe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本来安全的内容被模型判为危险而拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is safe content that the model wrongly flags as harmful.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全部预测中判断正确的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Accuracy is the fraction of all predictions that are correct.

scenario: 助手的安全测试集是半年前写好的固定 prompt 集合，通过率一直 99.8%，但社区论坛上不断出现新的绕过写法。
scenario_en: The assistant's safety test set is a fixed prompt list written six months ago with a steady 99.8 percent pass rate, yet community forums keep posting new jailbreak phrasings.
q: 这套安全评估还缺哪一环？
q_en: What is missing from this safety evaluation?
why: 固定测试集只覆盖已知攻击面，新绕过写法天然不在集合里；要靠定期红队主动构造对抗输入找漏洞，代价是需要持续投入专门人力且结果不可复现。
why_en: A frozen test set only covers known attacks, so new jailbreaks are absent by construction; regular red-teaming actively hunts vulnerabilities, at the cost of ongoing specialist effort.
tradeoff: 固定回归集（可重复可比较但只盖已知攻击）vs 定期红队（能发现新漏洞但结果不可复现）
options: 定期红队与对抗性评估，主动构造新攻击找漏洞
把这个安全测试集的规模从一千条 prompt 扩大到一万条同类改写的 prompt
提高安全分类器的拦截阈值，把所有稍微沾边的敏感回答一律直接拒绝掉
把安全评估的运行频率从每周一次提高到每天一次，让同一套用例跑得更勤
options_en: Regular red-teaming and adversarial evaluation that actively construct new attacks.
Grow the safety test set from a thousand prompts to ten thousand rephrasings of the same ones.
Raise the safety classifier threshold and refuse anything remotely sensitive outright.
Run the same suite daily instead of weekly so the existing cases execute more often.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型和策略都冻结、只做上线前回归验证，固定测试集的可重复性反而更有用。
optionExplanations: 对；只有主动对抗才能覆盖还没出现在测试集里的新绕过方式。
错；同类改写扩十倍，覆盖的仍是同一批已知攻击面，通过率照样虚高。
错；一刀切拒绝会大量误伤正常问题，也测不出真正的漏洞在哪。
错；同一套用例跑得再勤，漏掉的攻击方式依然一次都不会被执行到。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — only adversarial probing reaches jailbreaks that are not yet in the test set at all.
Incorrect — ten times more rephrasings still cover the same known attack surface, keeping the pass rate falsely high.
Incorrect — blanket refusal harms many legitimate questions and still reveals nothing about real vulnerabilities.
Incorrect — running the same cases more often never executes the attack patterns they omit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门扮演攻击者、主动构造对抗输入去找系统漏洞的团队或流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A red team deliberately plays attacker, crafting adversarial inputs to find system vulnerabilities.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用特殊措辞诱导模型绕过安全策略输出被禁内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A jailbreak is a phrasing that tricks the model into bypassing its safety policy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入给生成模型的那段指令或问题文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prompt is the instruction or question text given to a generative model.

scenario: 客服机器人的测试集是从三年历史工单里随机抽的；新产品线上线后线上失败率翻倍，测试集通过率却纹丝不动。
scenario_en: A support bot's test set is randomly sampled from three years of tickets; after a new product line launches, live failure rate doubles while test-set pass rate does not move.
q: 测试集该怎么重建才能跟上分布漂移？
q_en: How should the test set be rebuilt to keep up with distribution shift?
why: 随机抽样把新旧工单混在一起，新产线只占极小比例；改成按时间 hold-out 并维护近期流量的滚动窗口，测试集才跟着用户漂移，代价是跨版本分数不再直接可比。
why_en: Random sampling drowns the new product line in three years of old tickets; hold out by time and keep a rolling window of recent traffic so the test set drifts with users.
tradeoff: 随机划分（分数稳定可比但滞后于真实流量）vs 时间 hold-out 加滚动窗口（跟得上漂移但历史分数不可比）
options: 按时间 hold-out，并维护一个近期流量的滚动窗口
把三年工单按产品线分层抽样，保证每条老产品线在测试集里的占比完全相同
把测试集扩大到十万条随机工单，用绝对样本量保证新产品线也能被抽到几条
固定不动这个测试集当长期基准，新产品线的问题交给线上监控去发现
options_en: Hold out by time and maintain a rolling window of recent traffic.
Stratify the three years of tickets by product line so every legacy line keeps an identical share.
Grow the set to a hundred thousand random tickets so sheer volume catches a few new-line cases.
Freeze the set as a long-term benchmark and let production monitoring catch new-product issues.
whenOtherWins: 作为漂移探针的 golden canary 集必须固定不动，那套集合就该冻结而不是滚动。
optionExplanations: 对；时间切分保证测试数据永远晚于训练数据，滚动窗口让它跟上当前流量。
错；按老产品线配平只会锁死旧分布，新产品线仍然拿不到任何配额。
错；十万条里新产线占比依旧很低，几条样本无法把失败率抬进指标。
错；等线上监控报警时用户已经受损，评估失去了上线前拦截的作用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a time split guarantees test data postdates training data, and the rolling window keeps it aligned with current traffic.
Incorrect — balancing legacy lines locks in the old distribution and still gives the new line no quota.
Incorrect — the new line's share stays tiny at any volume, and a handful of samples cannot move the metric.
Incorrect — by the time production monitoring alerts, users are already hurt, and evaluation loses its pre-release gate role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上输入的分布随时间变化，偏离训练和测试时的分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distribution shift is when live input patterns drift away from the training and test distribution over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从数据中划出一部分完全不参与训练、只用于评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hold-out is a slice of data kept out of training and used only for evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长期固定不变的一组样本，用来检测模型退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A golden canary set is a fixed sample set kept stable over time to detect model degradation.

scenario: 团队想用线上日志离线估计新排序器的效果，于是用 importance weighting 给每条历史曝光按新旧策略的概率比重新加权。
scenario_en: To estimate a new ranker offline from production logs, the team reweights each logged impression by the ratio of new-policy to logging-policy probability.
q: 这种反事实估计的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of this counterfactual estimate?
why: 新策略与日志策略差异越大，少数样本的权重越极端，估计量方差爆炸——同一批日志换个随机切片结论就翻转；只能靠截断权重或补探索流量缓解。
why_en: The more the new policy diverges from the logging policy, the more extreme a few sample weights become, so variance explodes and the same logs can flip the conclusion.
options: 少数样本权重极端，估计方差很高，结论不稳定
需要把线上流量的百分之十长期划给新排序器，实验成本与直接做 A/B 完全一样
只能用于分类任务，排序问题里没有办法为每条曝光定义倾向性得分
会引入时间泄漏，因为重加权用到了发生在曝光之后的未来点击信息
options_en: A few samples get extreme weights, so the estimate has high variance and is unstable.
It needs ten percent of live traffic long-term, costing exactly as much as running a real A/B test.
It only works for classification, since ranking impressions have no definable propensity score.
It leaks time, because the reweighting uses click information that happened after the impression.
optionExplanations: 对；权重是概率比，新旧策略分歧大时个别样本能主导整个估计值。
错；反事实估计的卖点恰恰是复用已有日志，不需要新开线上流量。
错；排序里可以用日志策略展示该项的概率作为倾向性得分。
错；重加权只用曝光当时的策略概率，不涉及曝光之后发生的信息。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the weights are probability ratios, so when policies diverge a few samples can dominate the whole estimate.
Incorrect — the whole point of counterfactual estimation is reusing existing logs without new live traffic.
Incorrect — in ranking you can use the logging policy's display probability as the propensity score.
Incorrect — reweighting uses only the policy probability at impression time, not anything that happened later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用旧策略产生的日志估计如果换成新策略会怎样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counterfactual evaluation uses logs from an old policy to estimate what a new policy would have done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按新旧策略选中同一条样本的概率之比给样本重新加权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Importance weighting rescales each logged sample by the ratio of new-policy to logging-policy probability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志策略当时展示该条目的概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A propensity score is the probability that the logging policy displayed that item at the time.

scenario: 新排序器离线指标很好，但它同时改动了候选生成，团队不敢直接把它的顺序推给真实用户。
scenario_en: A new ranker looks great offline but also changed candidate generation, and the team is not ready to serve its order to real users.
q: 上线前该先做哪种线上验证？
q_en: Which online validation should come first?
why: shadow-rank 让新模型重排但仍服务基线顺序，比较那些位次会变的物品上的点击，既拿到线上信号又零用户风险；代价是拿不到真实曝光后的行为。
why_en: Shadow-rank lets the new model reorder while the baseline order is still served, comparing clicks on items whose position would change — real online signal at zero user risk.
tradeoff: shadow-rank（零用户风险但拿不到真实曝光反馈）vs 直接 A/B（信号完整但坏模型会伤用户）
options: 跳过线上验证，直接把离线 NDCG 更高的模型全量替换掉现有的线上排序器
shadow-rank：模型重排但仍服务基线顺序，比较位次变化项的点击
把新旧模型的分数取平均后服务，用混合结果观察整体指标有没有下降
先只对内部员工开放新排序，等他们的主观反馈良好之后再考虑对外发布
options_en: Skip online validation and fully replace the live ranker with whichever model has higher offline NDCG.
Shadow-rank: the model reorders but the baseline order is still served, comparing clicks on items whose position changes.
Serve the average of both models' scores and watch whether the blended metrics drop.
Expose the new ranker to internal employees only and ship once their subjective feedback is good.
whenOtherWins: 如果改动很小且已有 shadow 结果，直接进 A/B 或 interleaving 更快拿到有统计功效的结论。
optionExplanations: 错；离线指标只是线上效用的近似，全量替换等于把风险直接压到用户身上。
对；用户看到的仍是基线顺序，却能收集到新模型判断有差异处的真实点击。
错；分数平均出来的是第三个模型，测不出新模型单独的效果。
错；员工不是目标用户分布，样本量和行为都无法代表线上流量。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — offline metrics only approximate online utility, so a full swap puts the risk straight onto users.
Correct — users still see the baseline order while you collect real clicks exactly where the new model disagrees.
Incorrect — averaging scores creates a third model and measures neither one on its own.
Incorrect — employees are not the target user distribution, so neither their volume nor behavior represents live traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新模型在线上打分排序但不对用户生效，只记录与基线的差异。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shadow-rank means the new model scores and ranks live but never affects users, only logging where it differs from the baseline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个排序器的结果混成一个列表给同一用户，形成成对比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving mixes two rankers' results into one list for the same user, turning the comparison into a paired test.

scenario: 电商搜索移动端首屏只显示 10 条结果，用户要滑动才能看到第 11 条以后；团队要选一个离线主排序指标。
scenario_en: Mobile product search shows 10 results above the fold, and users must scroll to reach the eleventh; the team must pick a primary offline ranking metric.
q: 离线排序指标的截断位 k 该由什么决定？
q_en: What should decide the cutoff k for the offline ranking metric?
why: 截断位 k 是产品参数而不是调参结果：首屏 10 条就优化 NDCG@10，指标才和用户实际看到的范围对齐；改版首屏条数时这个指标必须跟着改。
why_en: The cutoff k is a product parameter, not a tuning knob — ten results above the fold means optimize NDCG at 10 so the metric matches what users actually see.
tradeoff: k 对齐首屏（贴合用户实际所见）vs k 取更大值（数值更平滑但奖励了用户看不到的位置）
options: 产品界面首屏展示的结果条数，本例即 NDCG@10
让离线分数看起来最高的那个 k 值，通常取更大的 k 会让曲线更平滑好看
候选生成阶段召回回来的候选总数，一般是几百到上千条这个量级
训练集里每个 query 平均拥有的相关性标注条数，标了几条就取 k 等于几
options_en: The number of results the product UI shows above the fold, here NDCG at 10.
Whichever k makes the offline score look best, usually a larger k for a smoother curve.
The total number of candidates returned by candidate generation, typically hundreds to thousands.
The average number of graded relevance labels per query in the training set.
whenOtherWins: 如果界面是无限滚动、用户普遍会翻很深，就该取更大的 k 或改用不截断的 MAP。
optionExplanations: 对；用户看不到第 11 条，把它算进指标就是在优化没人看的位置。
错；按分数好看选 k 是自欺，指标会奖励用户根本触达不到的排名。
错；候选池大小是召回阶段的工程参数，和用户可见范围无关。
错；标注条数是数据集属性，改标注预算不该改变产品的成功定义。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — users never see the eleventh result, so counting it means optimizing positions nobody looks at.
Incorrect — picking k to flatter the score rewards ranks users cannot reach.
Incorrect — candidate pool size is a retrieval engineering parameter, unrelated to what users can see.
Incorrect — label count is a dataset property; changing the annotation budget should not redefine product success.

termDefinitions.fullName: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at k
termDefinitions.meaning: 只统计前 k 条结果、按位置折损相关性的归一化排序指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG at k scores only the top k results, discounting relevance by position and normalizing against the ideal order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均准确率均值：在每个相关结果处算 precision 再平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAP averages precision computed at each relevant result across queries.

scenario: 市场平台的推荐 NDCG 很高，但新入驻卖家几周都拿不到曝光，长尾商品几乎从不出现在任何推荐位上。
scenario_en: A marketplace recommender has strong NDCG, yet newly onboarded sellers get no impressions for weeks and long-tail items almost never appear.
q: 该补哪个产品指标来暴露这个问题？
q_en: Which product metric surfaces this problem?
why: 排序指标只衡量展示出的那几条排得对不对，完全看不见从没被展示过的目录部分；Coverage 统计时间窗内被展示过的目录比例，代价是提升它通常要牺牲短期 CTR。
why_en: Ranking metrics only judge the items that were shown and are blind to the catalog that was never surfaced; coverage measures the share of the catalog shown in a window.
tradeoff: 只优化排序质量（短期 CTR 高但长尾饿死）vs 纳入 Coverage（供给侧健康但短期指标下滑）
options: Coverage：时间窗内被展示过的目录比例
MRR：所有会话中第一个相关结果出现位置的平均倒数值有多高
响应延迟：从用户打开首页到推荐结果完成渲染之间的耗时
Recall@K：有多少比例的会话在前 K 条里至少命中了一个相关物品
options_en: Coverage: the share of the catalog surfaced within a time window.
MRR: the average reciprocal position of the first relevant result across all sessions.
Response latency: how long from opening the home page to recommendations rendering.
Recall at K: the share of sessions with at least one relevant item in the top K.
whenOtherWins: 如果目录很小且供给充足（例如只有几十部影片），Coverage 天然接近 100%，盯它没有信息量。
optionExplanations: 对；它直接统计目录被触达的广度，新卖家零曝光会立刻反映成低覆盖。
错；MRR 只看已展示结果里第一个相关项的位置，对没展示的商品无感。
错；延迟衡量渲染速度，和哪些商品被选中展示是两回事。
错；Recall@K 统计会话是否被满足，而会话可能全靠同一批热门品满足。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it measures how broadly the catalog is reached, so zero impressions for new sellers show up immediately as low coverage.
Incorrect — MRR only looks at the first relevant item among shown results and is blind to items never surfaced.
Incorrect — latency measures rendering speed, not which items get chosen for display.
Incorrect — recall at K asks whether sessions were satisfied, and they can be satisfied entirely by the same popular items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段时间窗口内被推荐展示过的目录条目比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage is the proportion of catalog items surfaced by recommendations over a time window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新卖家或新物品缺少交互数据，模型难以给它打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when a new seller or item has no interaction history for the model to score on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示出去的结果中被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR is click-through rate, the share of shown results that get clicked.

scenario: 短视频推荐把人均 dwell time 当作唯一北极星，模型上线后停留时长涨了 30%，三个月后次月留存却在持续下滑。
scenario_en: A short-video recommender uses dwell time as its single north star; dwell rose 30 percent after launch, but month-two retention has been sliding for three months.
q: 只优化 dwell time 会怎样反噬？
q_en: How does optimizing dwell time alone backfire?
why: 模型会学会制造 doom-scrolling：停留时长上去了但用户事后并不满意，短期指标吃掉长期留存；所以 dwell time 必须和留存这类长周期指标成对读。
why_en: The model learns to manufacture doom-scrolling — dwell goes up while satisfaction does not, so a short-term metric cannibalizes long-term retention.
options: 模型学会制造 doom-scrolling，停留变长但满意度和留存下滑
模型会偏向推荐时长更短的视频，因为短视频的完播率天然比长视频高得多
dwell time 无法按人群切片统计，所以任何分群上的回归都会被总体平均彻底掩盖
停留时长上升会直接推高推理成本，服务器扩容压力最终反噬到用户端的延迟
options_en: The model learns to manufacture doom-scrolling: dwell grows while satisfaction and retention fall.
The model favors shorter videos, since short clips naturally have far higher completion rates.
Dwell time cannot be sliced by audience, so any segment-level regression is hidden by the overall average.
Longer dwell drives up inference cost, and the scaling pressure eventually shows up as user-facing latency.
optionExplanations: 对；停留时长不区分看得投入和停不下来，模型只会挑更容易的那条路走。
错；优化停留时长的方向是拉长会话，不天然偏向更短的单条视频。
错；dwell time 完全可以按人群切片，切片不是这里的失败原因。
错；成本上升是运维问题，解释不了次月留存这个满意度信号在掉。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — dwell does not distinguish engaged watching from compulsive scrolling, and the model optimizes whichever is easier.
Incorrect — optimizing dwell pushes toward longer sessions, not inherently shorter individual clips.
Incorrect — dwell time can be sliced by audience segment, so slicing is not the failure here.
Incorrect — rising cost is an operations issue and does not explain a drop in month-two retention, a satisfaction signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在内容或页面上停留的时间长度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is how long a user stays on a piece of content or a page.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户停不下来地持续下滑浏览，事后满意度反而更低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doom-scrolling is compulsive continuous scrolling that leaves users less satisfied afterwards.

termDefinitions.term: north star metric / 北极星指标
termDefinitions.meaning: 团队长期对齐优化的那个唯一核心业务指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A north star metric is the single core business number a team aligns its optimization around.

scenario: 同一套推荐引擎要同时服务流媒体订阅站和零售商城；订阅站靠续费赚钱，商城按成交额抽佣且退货率高达两成。
scenario_en: One recommender engine serves both a subscription streaming site, which earns on renewals, and a retail marketplace, which takes a cut of sales with a 20 percent return rate.
q: 两边的北极星指标该分别选什么？
q_en: What should the north star metric be on each side?
why: 北极星要跟着钱走：订阅站的收入来自续费，completion rate 最能预测它；商城收入按成交抽佣，两成退货意味着必须扣掉退货后再算 GMV。
why_en: The north star follows the money — renewals make completion rate the right proxy for streaming, while commission on sales makes GMV net of returns the right one for retail.
tradeoff: completion rate（预测续费但对交易类业务无意义）vs 净退货后 GMV（贴合抽佣但对订阅制无意义）
options: 两边都用点击率，因为点击是所有推荐系统最通用也最容易采集的统一信号
流媒体看 completion rate，零售看净退货后的 GMV
两边都用总曝光量，曝光越多说明推荐引擎的服务吞吐和规模能力越强
流媒体看净退货后的 GMV，零售看 completion rate，交叉借鉴对方行业指标
options_en: Use click-through rate on both, since clicks are the most universal and easiest signal to collect.
Streaming tracks completion rate; retail tracks GMV net of returns.
Use total impressions on both, since more impressions show greater serving throughput.
Streaming tracks GMV net of returns and retail tracks completion rate, borrowing across industries.
whenOtherWins: 如果流媒体靠广告而不是订阅赚钱，观看时长和广告曝光就比 completion rate 更贴近收入。
optionExplanations: 错；点击既不代表看完一集，也不代表成交后没被退货，离两边的收入都很远。
对；各自选最接近收入的下游动作：看完一集预示续费，净成交额才是抽佣基数。
错；曝光量是系统吞吐指标，推得越多不代表用户价值或收入越高。
错；订阅制没有成交额可算，交易平台也没有看完这个动作。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — a click neither means an episode was finished nor that a purchase survived returns, so it is far from either revenue line.
Correct — each picks the downstream action closest to revenue: finishing an episode predicts renewal, and net sales is the commission base.
Incorrect — impressions measure system throughput; serving more does not mean more user value or revenue.
Incorrect — a subscription business has no sales total, and a marketplace has no completion action.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商品交易总额：平台上成交商品的总金额。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GMV is gross merchandise value, the total money value of goods transacted on the platform.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开始观看的内容中被看完的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Completion rate is the share of started content that viewers finish.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示结果中被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR is click-through rate, the share of shown results that get clicked.

scenario: 站内搜索里绝大多数 query 是一次性的长尾词，标注预算只够覆盖头部几千个 query。
scenario_en: In site search most queries are one-off long-tail terms, and the labeling budget only covers a few thousand head queries.
q: 长尾 query 的相关性怎么评估？
q_en: How do you evaluate relevance on long-tail queries?
why: 长尾 query 数量上不封顶，逐条人工标注在预算上不可能；用大模型做零样本相关性判定替代显式标注，代价是要定期用人工标注抽查校准它。
why_en: Long-tail queries are effectively unbounded, so per-query human labels are unaffordable; use a large model for zero-shot relevance judgments and calibrate it with human spot checks.
tradeoff: 人工标注（高精度但只覆盖头部）vs 大模型零样本判定（可覆盖长尾但需持续校准）
options: 只评估头部几千个 query，长尾部分默认与头部表现一致，不再单独衡量
用大模型做零样本相关性判定替代显式标注
把标注预算从头部转移到长尾，优先标注那些一年只出现过一次的稀有 query
把长尾 query 全部改写成最接近的头部 query 再评估，用改写后的分数代表长尾
options_en: Evaluate only the few thousand head queries and assume the tail performs the same.
Use a large language model for zero-shot relevance judgments instead of explicit labels.
Move the labeling budget from head to tail, prioritizing queries seen once a year.
Rewrite every tail query to its nearest head query and report the rewritten score.
whenOtherWins: 如果领域高度专业（如医疗、法律），模型判定不可信，仍要靠专家标注加 query 聚类共享判定。
optionExplanations: 错；长尾正是模型最弱的地方，用头部表现外推等于系统性高估质量。
对；零样本判定能低成本覆盖任意 query，再用人工抽查维持它的可信度。
错；一次性 query 标了也不会再出现，预算换不来可复用的评估资产。
错；改写会把长尾的真实意图抹平，测到的还是头部而不是长尾表现。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — the tail is where the model is weakest, so extrapolating from head performance systematically overstates quality.
Correct — zero-shot judgment covers arbitrary queries cheaply, with human spot-checks keeping it trustworthy.
Incorrect — a once-a-year query never recurs, so the budget buys no reusable evaluation asset.
Incorrect — rewriting erases the tail query's real intent, so you end up measuring head performance again.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出现频次极低但种类极多的那部分查询或内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The long tail is the huge variety of queries or items that each occur very rarely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不给任务专门的训练样本，直接让模型按指令做判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zero-shot means asking the model to judge from instructions alone, with no task-specific training examples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相似查询归到一组，让它们共享相关性标注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query clustering groups similar queries so they can share relevance judgments.

scenario: 内容审核模型分 12 个违规类别，报表只给一个整体 precision 0.94，运营却反馈某个小类几乎全靠人工兜底。
scenario_en: A moderation model covers 12 violation classes and reports a single overall precision of 0.94, yet operations says one small class is handled almost entirely by humans.
q: 只报总体指标会漏掉什么？
q_en: What does reporting only the overall metric miss?
why: 多分类系统必须报 per-class 性能：占比小的类别在总体平均里权重极低，可以整类崩掉而总分纹丝不动，运营的人工兜底量成了它唯一的外部信号。
why_en: Multi-class systems need per-class performance — a small class can fail completely while the overall average barely moves, leaving manual workload as its only visible signal.
options: 小类别整类崩掉也不会拉动总分，per-class 指标才能暴露
总体指标算不出 recall 只能算 precision，所以漏放情况天然无法被任何报表观察到
12 个类别之间存在标签重叠，任何总体指标在多标签设定下都不具备数学意义
总体指标只在测试集上成立，线上流量分布不同因此所有离线数字都不该被采信
options_en: A small class can fail entirely without moving the overall number; only per-class metrics expose it.
Overall metrics cannot produce recall, only precision, so misses are inherently unobservable in any report.
The 12 classes overlap, so no aggregate metric is mathematically meaningful in a multi-label setting.
Overall metrics hold only on the test set, so every offline number should be distrusted outright.
optionExplanations: 对；总体平均按样本量加权，占 1% 的类别几乎不影响那个 0.94。
错；总体 recall 完全可以计算，问题在于它同样被大类主导。
错；类别重叠是标签设计问题，与只报总体这个报表口径无关。
错；离线数字仍有价值，问题是粒度太粗而不是离线评估本身不可信。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the overall average is weighted by volume, so a class holding one percent of samples barely touches that 0.94.
Incorrect — overall recall is perfectly computable; the issue is that it too is dominated by large classes.
Incorrect — overlapping labels is a label-design question, unrelated to reporting only an aggregate.
Incorrect — offline numbers still have value; the problem is granularity, not offline evaluation itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对每个类别单独统计 precision、recall，而不是只看总体平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-class performance reports precision and recall separately for each class instead of one overall average.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输出要从三个以上互斥类别中选一个的分类任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-class classification picks one label from three or more mutually exclusive classes.

scenario: 欺诈检测里正例不到 1%，模型只在已知作案模式上表现好；一种全新手法出现时，它既不报警也几乎不会被随机抽样抽到。
scenario_en: In fraud detection positives are under 1 percent and the model only handles known patterns; a brand-new scheme neither triggers alerts nor gets caught by random sampling.
q: 该建一条什么样的循环来发现新型少数类？
q_en: What kind of loop should you build to discover new minority-class cases?
why: 新手法在训练数据里没有标签、模型分数天然偏低，随机抽样也几乎抽不到；靠主动学习优先送审不确定或新颖的样本再回灌训练集，代价是持续占用人工审核预算。
why_en: A new scheme has no labels and scores low by construction, and random sampling almost never hits it; active learning routes uncertain or novel cases to review and feeds findings back into training.
tradeoff: 随机抽样送审（无偏但对 1% 正例效率极低）vs 主动学习按不确定性送审（发现率高但引入采样偏差）
options: 主动学习：优先把不确定或新颖的样本送人工审核，结果回灌训练集
把模型的报警阈值整体调低，让更多交易被判为欺诈从而提高整体召回覆盖面
扩大随机抽样的规模，每天多抽十倍交易送人工复核以提高命中新手法的概率
在训练时对已知欺诈样本做过采样，让模型对现有欺诈模式学得更充分更敏感
options_en: Active learning: route uncertain or novel samples to human review and feed the results back into training.
Lower the alert threshold across the board so more transactions get flagged and overall recall rises.
Scale up random sampling, sending ten times more transactions to review each day to raise the odds of hitting new schemes.
Oversample known fraud during training so the model learns existing fraud patterns more sharply.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是无偏估计欺诈的真实发生率（prevalence），就必须用随机抽样而不是主动学习。
optionExplanations: 对；按不确定性和新颖度选样，把有限审核预算花在模型最可能出错的地方。
错；降阈值放大的是已知模式的边缘案例，新手法分数低照样被挡在阈值之下。
错；正例不到 1%，抽十倍只是把极低命中率线性放大，成本先撑不住。
错；过采样只会让模型对已知模式更自信，对没见过的手法毫无帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — selecting by uncertainty and novelty spends the limited review budget where the model is most likely wrong.
Incorrect — a lower threshold surfaces edge cases of known patterns, while a new scheme still scores below it.
Incorrect — with under one percent positives, ten times the sampling only scales a tiny hit rate linearly and the cost breaks first.
Incorrect — oversampling only makes the model more confident on known patterns and does nothing for unseen ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按标了最有信息量的原则挑样本送标注，而不是随机挑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Active learning picks the most informative samples to label instead of sampling randomly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 正负样本比例极度悬殊，正例只占很小一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Class imbalance is when positives make up only a tiny fraction of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据中真实正例所占的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prevalence is the true share of positive cases in production data.

q: 现代 ML 系统设计中，feature discussion 的重点更接近什么？
options: 手写尽可能多的 if-else 规则，逐条覆盖新用户、新地区等场景
想到哪个字段就报哪个，凑够三十个为止
识别信号来源、表示方式、新鲜度和 train/serve 一致性
只讨论模型有几层、参数有多大，不谈数据
options_en: Hand-write as many if-else rules as possible, one for every new-user or new-region case.
Name whatever field comes to mind until you hit thirty.
Identifying signal sources, representations, freshness, and train/serve parity.
Only discuss how many layers the model has and how many parameters, never the data.
optionExplanations: 老式规则手工穷举成本高，模型自己学不到没写过的新组合。
报字段名不等于讨论信号来源和一致性风险。
现代模型自己学交互，人要决定喂哪些信号、怎么保鲜。
层数是模型结构问题，不回答喂什么数据。
optionExplanations_en: Hand-written if-else rules are a pre-deep-learning approach the model can't extend on its own.
Naming thirty fields is not the same as discussing signal sources or consistency risk.
Modern models learn interactions themselves, but a human still decides which signals to feed and how to keep them fresh.
Layer count is a model-architecture question, not a data question.
why: 现代模型能吃文本、图像和序列，但喂哪些信号、怎么保鲜、训练服务是否一致仍由人决定。
why_en: Modern feature discussion is about choosing signal sources, representations, freshness, and train-serve parity, not hand-crafting fields.

termDefinitions.term: train/serve parity / 训练服务一致性
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时和线上服务时对同一特征算出相同的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Train-serve parity means training and online serving compute the same value for a feature.

q_en: In modern ML system design, what should the feature discussion mostly be about?
scenario: 你要为亿级用户的短视频推荐做排序，模型是能直接吃原始文本和图像的深度网络。
scenario_en: You're building ranking for a billion-user short-video feed, and the model is a deep net that eats raw text and images directly.

scenario: 面试进入数据/features 部分，你担心陷入无限 feature 列表。
q: 更好的组织方式是？
options: 按想到的顺序一直报字段
先按信号来源分桶，再每桶给代表性信号
只说“用所有数据”
跳过 features 直接上线
options_en: Keep listing fields in whatever order they come to mind.
Group by signal-source bucket first, then give a few representative signals per bucket.
Just say "use all the data."
Skip features entirely and go straight to launch.
optionExplanations: 想到哪说哪，容易变成无结构的字段流。
先给桶名再填代表信号，面试官能跟住结构。
没有取舍等于没有设计判断。
特征选择本身就是本轮考察重点。
optionExplanations_en: Free-associating fields turns into an unstructured stream with no natural stopping point.
Naming the buckets first lets the interviewer follow your structure before you fill in detail.
Saying 'use everything' skips the actual design decision.
Skipping features skips the exact thing this round is testing.
why: 按 content、actor、behavior、graph、context 等来源组织，面试官能跟住结构，你也能及时停止或深入。
why_en: Grouping features by signal source prevents an unstructured feature dump and makes the discussion easier to steer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Sources[Signal sources] --> Content[Content]
  Sources --> Actor[Actor]
  Sources --> Behavior[Behavior]
  Sources --> Graph[Graph]
  Sources --> Context[Context]
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官要求某个具体字段实现，再下钻编码和服务方式。
tradeoff: 结构化分桶讲清晰 vs 穷举字段显完整

termDefinitions.term: signal source bucket / 信号来源桶
termDefinitions.meaning: 按数据的来源（内容/用户/行为/图/上下文）划分特征的分组方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A signal-source bucket groups features by where the data comes from, such as content, actor, behavior, graph, or context.

q_en: What's a better way to organize it?
scenario_en: The interview has moved into the data/features section, and you're worried about spiraling into an endless feature list.

q: ML 系统设计面试中，候选人应该枚举哪些常见信号来源？（多选，注意排除干扰项）
options: 内容/物品信号
参与者/用户/作者信号
行为信号
网络/图信号
请求上下文信号
训练 batch size
options_en: Content / item signals
Actor / user / author signals
Behavioral signals
Network / graph signals
Request context signals
The training batch size
optionExplanations: 这是被打分的对象本身，如帖子文本、视频。
这是参与者本身，如观看者、发帖人。
这是发生过的事，如最近点击、浏览。
这是账号/设备间的关系，如共同关注。
这是请求本身的语境，如时间、设备。
batch size 是训练超参数，不是数据信号。
optionExplanations_en: This is the item being scored itself, like a post or video.
This is the participant, like the viewer or the author.
This is what happened, like recent clicks or views.
This is the relationship between accounts or devices.
This is the context of the request itself, like time or device.
Batch size is a training hyperparameter, not a data signal.
why: 真实系统反复用这五桶信号；不同问题里各桶权重不同，但都值得先枚举再挑重点。
why_en: Common ML signal sources include item content, actors, behavior, graph relationships, and request context.

termDefinitions.meaning: 来自账号、设备间关系（如共同关注、共享 IP）的信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A graph signal comes from relationships between accounts or devices, such as shared follows or shared IPs.

q_en: In an ML system design interview, which common signal sources should a candidate enumerate? (Select all; watch for the distractor.)
scenario: 为社交信息流排序建特征，模型既要解释「这条内容是什么」也要解释「这个用户此刻想要什么」。
scenario_en: You're building features for a social-feed ranker that must explain both what the content is and what this user wants right now.

scenario: 有害内容分类主要判断帖子文本和图片是否违规。
q: 最关键的信号来源通常是？
options: 内容/物品信号
数据库分片编号
服务器机房温度
用户界面颜色
options_en: Content / item signals.
The database shard number.
The data-center room temperature.
The app's UI color scheme.
optionExplanations: 判断本质是内容本身违不违规，内容信号信息量最大。
分片号只是存储位置，和内容语义无关。
运维指标，不参与预测目标的语义判断。
前端样式，不反映帖子本身是否违规。
optionExplanations_en: The label depends on what the content itself contains, so content is the highest-signal source here.
A shard number is a storage detail, not a semantic signal.
Datacenter temperature is an ops metric with no bearing on content meaning.
UI color is a front-end style choice, unrelated to whether the post is harmful.
why: 当问题本质是“这个东西看起来是什么”，内容本身通常最高信号，应作为一等输入进模型。
why_en: When the label depends on what the item contains, content signals are usually the first-class input.
whenOtherWins: 在推荐问题中，内容常不如行为强，因为用户是否喜欢不只由视频内容决定。
tradeoff: 内容信号信息量 vs 与标签的直接相关性

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接来自被判断对象本身的信号，如文本、图片、音频。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A content signal comes directly from the item being scored, such as its text, image, or audio.

q_en: Which signal source is usually most critical here?
scenario_en: A harmful-content classifier mainly judges whether a post's text and image violate policy.

q: actor/user 信号常采用哪种生产组合？
options: 只存用户昵称和注册邮箱，不接入任何历史行为数据
完全不用历史特征，每次请求都当成全新用户处理
每次请求都靠人工审核队列判定，不做自动化特征
长期 embedding + 实时显式属性
options_en: Store only the user's nickname and signup email, with no historical behavior data at all.
Use no historical features — treat every request as a brand-new user.
Send every request to a human review queue, with no automated features.
A long-term embedding plus real-time explicit attributes.
optionExplanations: 昵称几乎不携带行为或信誉信息。
丢弃历史等于放弃最强的个性化信号来源。
人工审核不是特征，是无法规模化的流程。
长期 embedding 稳但更新慢，实时属性补上最近异常。
optionExplanations_en: A nickname carries almost no behavioral or reputation signal.
Ignoring history throws away the strongest personalization signal.
Manual review isn't a feature — it's a process that doesn't scale.
A slow-moving embedding captures stable taste, while fast explicit attributes cover recent anomalies.
why: 长期 embedding 表达稳定偏好或信誉，实时属性表达近期异常、账号年龄、国家、举报等，两者互补。
why_en: Actor features often combine slow rich embeddings with fast explicit attributes for recent state.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Long[Long-term embedding] --> Join[Feature join]
  Fast[Real-time attributes] --> Join
  Join --> Model[Model input]
  Fast --> Alert[Recent anomaly]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把类别、用户或内容表示成模型学到的稠密向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector that a model learns to represent an entity such as a user or item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接记录的原始字段，如账号年龄、国家，而非学出来的向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An explicit attribute is a directly recorded field, like account age or country, rather than a learned vector.

q_en: What production combination do actor/user signals commonly use?
scenario: 为内容审核给账号打分：既要看长期信誉，也要抓 5 分钟内刚出现的举报激增。
scenario_en: You're scoring accounts for content moderation: you need long-term reputation and also a report spike from the last five minutes.

q: 现代系统处理行为序列时，轻 ranker 和重 ranker 常有什么区别？
options: 轻 ranker 只能读原始视频文件，重 ranker 只能执行 SQL 查询取特征
轻 ranker 用聚合特征，重 ranker 把序列喂 Transformer
两者都只依赖人工写死的 if-else 规则，完全不做参数学习
轻 ranker 不需要任何特征，直接对候选输出随机分数占位
options_en: Light rankers can only read raw video files, while heavy rankers can only pull features via SQL.
Light rankers use aggregated features; heavy rankers feed the sequence into a transformer.
Both rely purely on hand-written if-else rules and learn no parameters at all.
Light rankers need no features and just emit a random placeholder score.
optionExplanations: 视频原文件和 SQL 都不是序列的编码方式。
聚合便宜适合宽漏斗海量候选，完整序列适合候选变少后的重模型。
现代重 ranker 常用 self-attention 直接学时序，不靠手写规则。
轻 ranker 仍需要聚合特征，只是比重模型便宜。
optionExplanations_en: Raw video files and SQL are not sequence-encoding techniques at all.
Cheap aggregates fit the wide funnel's huge candidate set, while full sequences suit the narrow funnel's heavier model.
Modern heavy rankers learn temporal structure via self-attention, not hand-written rules.
Light rankers still need aggregated features, just cheaper ones.
why: 均值/时间衰减聚合便宜，适合宽漏斗；完整序列能学顺序和上下文，适合窄漏斗重模型。
why_en: Light rankers often use cheap aggregates, while heavy rankers can process event sequences directly with attention.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Seq[Event sequence] --> Agg[Mean or decay aggregate]
  Seq --> Tok[Sequence as tokens]
  Agg --> Light[Light ranker]
  Tok --> Heavy[Heavy ranker]
tradeoff: 聚合的低成本吞吐 vs 完整序列的时序表达力

termDefinitions.meaning: 让序列里每个元素都能关注其他元素来学习依赖关系的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Self-attention lets every element in a sequence attend to every other element to learn dependencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐流程里候选数量很大、需要低成本处理的早期阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The wide funnel is the early recommendation stage with a huge candidate set that needs cheap processing.

q_en: When modern systems process behavioral sequences, what's the typical difference between a light ranker and a heavy ranker?
scenario: 推荐漏斗第一层要在 20ms 内给 1 万候选打分，最后一层只给 100 个候选打分。
scenario_en: The first funnel stage must score ten thousand candidates in twenty milliseconds; the final stage scores only a hundred.

scenario: Bot detection 要识别协调账号、共享设备、关注关系异常。
q: 哪个信号桶最关键？
options: 只看帖子字数
只看浏览器主题
网络/图信号
只看训练 batch size
options_en: Only look at post length.
Only look at the browser color theme.
Network / graph signals.
Only look at the training batch size.
optionExplanations: 字数和是否协同作案没有因果关系。
界面偏好设置，与账号关系无关。
协调账号靠关系图和共享设备最容易暴露，比内容更难伪装。
batch size 是训练超参数，不是输入信号。
optionExplanations_en: Post length has no causal link to coordinated behavior.
Browser theme is a UI preference unrelated to account relationships.
Coordinated accounts show up in the relationship graph and shared devices, which are much harder to fake than content.
Batch size is a training hyperparameter, not an input signal.
why: 协调攻击和 botnet 往往在关系图、共享基础设施和相似活动中暴露。图信号比可伪装的内容更稳健。
why_en: Graph signals are critical for coordinated abuse because relationships and shared infrastructure are harder to fake than content.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务是单张商品图分类，图信号通常很少，内容信号会赢。
tradeoff: 图信号抗伪造 vs 内容信号采集成本低

termDefinitions.meaning: 来自账号、设备间关系（如共同关注、共享 IP）的信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A graph signal comes from relationships between accounts or devices, such as shared follows or shared IPs.

q_en: Which signal bucket matters most here?
scenario_en: Bot detection needs to spot coordinated accounts, shared devices, and abnormal follow relationships.

q: 请求上下文信号的特点是什么？
options: 便宜、实时，解释当次请求的特殊性
只能离线每月批量计算一次，无法实时取用
一定比内容信号更强，可以替代物品特征
属于日志字段，无法作为模型输入使用
options_en: Cheap and real-time — they explain what's special about this particular request.
They can only be computed offline in a monthly batch, never in real time.
They're always stronger than content signals and can replace item features.
They're log fields only and can't be used as model input.
optionExplanations: 时间、设备、位置几乎零成本获取，还原了这次请求的语境。
上下文特征恰恰相反，通常是请求时实时算出。
强弱取决于问题，上下文通常是补充信号而非主力。
上下文特征是最容易接入模型的一类输入。
optionExplanations_en: Time, device, and location are nearly free to compute and capture what is unique about this specific request.
Context features are the opposite — they are usually computed live at request time.
Strength depends on the problem; context is usually a supporting signal, not the main one.
Context features are among the easiest inputs to feed into a model.
why: 时间、设备、页面、当前位置或最近 query 往往容易获得且对当次意图有帮助。候选人常忘记这类信号。
why_en: Request context features are cheap real-time signals that explain what is special about the current request.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Req[Request] --> Time[Time of day]
  Req --> Device[Device type]
  Req --> Loc[Location]
  Time --> Model[Model input]
  Device --> Model
  Loc --> Model

termDefinitions.meaning: 必须等请求真正发生才能算出的特征，如当前设备。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A request-time feature can only be computed once the request actually happens, like the current device.

q_en: What are request-context signals like?
scenario: 外卖首页排序要区分「工作日午休的手机端用户」和「深夜网页端用户」。
scenario_en: A food-delivery home feed must tell a weekday-lunchtime mobile user apart from a late-night desktop one.

scenario: 同一个创作者既有“内容 embedding”又有“最近一小时举报率”两个特征。
q: 同一信号桶里的特征为什么仍要按更新频率区分？
options: 所有特征都必须做成实时计算，没有例外
更新频率只是特征命名习惯，不影响任何系统架构选型
特征算得越慢，代表的信息就一定越准确
静态、批量、流式、请求时特征的服务成本差异很大
options_en: Every feature must be computed in real time, with no exceptions.
Update frequency is just a naming convention for the feature name, with no effect on system architecture choices.
The slower a feature is computed, the more accurate it must be.
Static, batch, streaming, and request-time features have very different serving costs.
optionExplanations: 多数特征不需要实时，强上实时是浪费。
更新频率直接决定要不要建流式管线。
慢不等于准，只是反映数据本身变化的速度。
越靠近请求时刻计算，基础设施成本越高。
optionExplanations_en: Most features don't need to be real-time; forcing it wastes infrastructure.
Update frequency directly decides whether you need a streaming pipeline.
Slower isn't more accurate — it just reflects how fast the underlying data changes.
The closer to request time a feature is computed, the more infrastructure it costs.
why: 作者内容 embedding 可能每日刷新，最近一小时举报率需要流式聚合。越接近请求时计算，基础设施成本越高。
why_en: Feature freshness matters because static, batch, streaming, and request-time features have very different serving costs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过实时事件流持续聚合更新的特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming feature is continuously updated by aggregating a real-time event stream.

q_en: Why should features in the same signal bucket still be split by update frequency?
scenario_en: The same creator has both a 'content embedding' feature and a 'reports in the last hour' feature.

scenario: 你提出“最近 5 分钟举报率”作为审核特征。
q: 高级候选人下一句应该补什么？
options: 假设它免费实时可用，不讨论任何工程成本
确认是否值得建流式聚合和低延迟特征服务
把它放进每天跑一次的离线 CSV 就够了
删除所有历史特征，只保留这一个实时信号
options_en: Assume it's free and available in real time, without discussing engineering cost.
Check whether it's worth building streaming aggregation and a low-latency feature service.
Just drop it into an offline CSV that runs once a day.
Delete all historical features and keep only this real-time signal.
optionExplanations: 实时聚合从不是免费的，需要专门基础设施。
快变特征有用，但要主动权衡它值不值流式管线的成本。
5 分钟窗口放进日级离线管道就失去了时效性。
这里的问题是要不要建新管线，不是删旧特征。
optionExplanations_en: Real-time aggregation is never free — it needs dedicated infrastructure.
A fast-moving signal can help, but you should explicitly weigh whether it is worth a streaming pipeline.
A five-minute window loses its whole point inside a daily offline pipeline.
The question is whether to build a new pipeline, not whether to delete old features.
why: 快变特征有预测力但也有工程成本。面试里要说明为何它值这个成本，并如何保证训练/服务一致。
why_en: A fast-moving feature should trigger a discussion about whether a streaming pipeline is worth its cost.
whenOtherWins: 如果同等效果可由日级聚合得到，批处理特征会更简单稳健。
tradeoff: 快变信号的预测力 vs 流式管线的工程成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续处理实时事件、低延迟产出特征值的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming pipeline continuously processes real-time events to produce low-latency feature values.

q_en: What should a senior candidate add next?
scenario_en: You've proposed 'reports in the last 5 minutes' as a moderation feature.

q: 现代系统处理原始文本/图片的默认方式是什么？
options: 手工写二十个关键词计数特征，外加图片颜色直方图统计
把文本和图片全部转成 one-hot 用户 ID 向量再拼接
文本进 text encoder，图片进视觉 backbone
只保留文件大小和上传时间两个数字，丢掉全部内容
options_en: Hand-write twenty keyword-count features, plus image color-histogram statistics.
Convert both text and images into one-hot user-ID vectors and concatenate them.
Text goes into a text encoder; images go into a vision backbone.
Keep only file size and upload time as two numbers, discarding all the content.
optionExplanations: n-gram 计数和颜色直方图是深度学习前的老式做法。
one-hot 用于稀疏类别，不是文本或图片的编码方式。
让 encoder 直接学语义，不用手工穷举计数规则。
文件大小完全丢失了内容本身的语义信息。
optionExplanations_en: Keyword counts and color histograms are the pre-deep-learning way of doing this.
One-hot encoding is for sparse categories, not for representing text or images.
Modern systems let an encoder learn semantics directly instead of hand-counting features.
File size throws away all of the content's actual semantic information.
why: 大模型能从原始内容学语义和跨模态关系，手工 n-gram/颜色特征通常只是老式 baseline。关键是把原始内容正确暴露给模型。
why_en: Modern systems usually feed raw text and images through learned encoders instead of relying on many handcrafted counts.
tradeoff: 学习式编码器的语义表达力 vs 手工特征的可解释性

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本切成模型能处理的最小单元（token）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenizing splits text into the small units, called tokens, that a model can process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个类别一个只有一位为 1 的高维稀疏向量，类别间没有相似度信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding gives each category a sparse vector with a single 1, so it carries no similarity information between categories.

termDefinitions.term: vision backbone / 视觉骨干网络
termDefinitions.meaning: 负责从图片像素中提取特征的编码器，如 ViT。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vision backbone is the encoder that extracts features from image pixels, such as a ViT.

q_en: What's the modern system's default way to process raw text/images?
scenario: 要给百万级图文帖做语义理解，人工关键词表每月都被新说法绕过。
scenario_en: You need semantic understanding of millions of image-and-text posts, and hand-written keyword lists get bypassed by new phrasings every month.

scenario: 商品搜索要同时理解商品图片、标题和 query。
q: 更现代的表示方式是？
options: CLIP 对比学习，把图文和 query 对齐到共享空间
只按图片文件名字符串和标题做精确匹配
只用商品价格高低排序候选，忽略图文内容
只用用户输入 query 的字符长度当作排序模型的输入特征
options_en: CLIP-style contrastive learning that aligns images, text, and queries into one space.
Match only by exact string comparison on the image filename and title.
Rank candidates by price alone, ignoring the image and text entirely.
Use only the character length of the user's query as the ranking model's input feature.
optionExplanations: 对比学习让图片、文本、query 落进同一个向量空间可互相检索。
文件名是人工命名，和图片实际内容无关。
价格不表达图文语义是否匹配。
query 长度不携带语义信息。
optionExplanations_en: Contrastive training pulls images, text, and queries into one shared space so they can be matched or retrieved.
A filename is arbitrary and unrelated to what the image actually shows.
Price says nothing about whether the image and text semantically match.
Query length carries no semantic information at all.
why: 图文共同决定语义匹配，共享 embedding 空间能让图片、文本和 query 互相检索或作为 ranker 特征。
why_en: A CLIP-style shared embedding space is a modern way to align images, text, and queries.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有结构化库存和精确筛选需求，传统属性过滤可能更简单有效。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Image[Image] --> ImgEnc[Image encoder]
  Text[Title or query] --> TxtEnc[Text encoder]
  ImgEnc --> Space[Shared space]
  TxtEnc --> Space
  Space --> Match[Match or retrieve]
tradeoff: 跨模态语义对齐 vs 结构化属性过滤的简单性

termDefinitions.term: CLIP-style contrastive learning / CLIP 式对比学习
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练图文对，使匹配的图文向量更接近、不匹配的更远。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CLIP-style contrastive learning trains on image-text pairs so matching pairs land close together in the embedding space and mismatched pairs land far apart.

termDefinitions.term: shared embedding space / 共享向量空间
termDefinitions.meaning: 不同模态（图片、文本）的向量落在同一个可比较的空间里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared embedding space is where vectors from different modalities, like images and text, can be directly compared.

q_en: What's a more modern representation to use?
scenario_en: Product search needs to understand the product image, title, and query together.

q: 稀疏类别特征（user_id、item_id、枚举）常用什么表示？
options: 标准化成均值 0 方差 1 的浮点
把类别 ID 数值直接转换成一张图片矩阵输入
完全丢弃这个字段，不当作特征
embedding table 按 ID 查向量
options_en: Standardize it to zero mean, unit variance.
Convert the category ID's numeric value directly into an image-matrix input.
Drop the field entirely and don't use it as a feature at all.
An embedding table looked up by ID.
optionExplanations: 标准化是数值特征的处理方式，类别 ID 没有大小意义。
把 ID 转成图片没有任何表示学习的意义。
丢弃 ID 会丢失全部个性化和物品身份信息。
ID 之间没有大小顺序，改用查表方式给每个类别学一个独立向量，而不是套用数值处理。
optionExplanations_en: Standardization is for numeric features; category IDs have no magnitude to standardize.
Turning an ID into an image has no meaningful representation-learning purpose.
Dropping the ID throws away all personalization and item-identity signal.
IDs have no numeric ordering, so a lookup table learns an independent vector per category instead of treating it as a number.
why: 类别 ID 没有自然数值大小，embedding table 让模型学习每个类别的低维表示。高基数时要考虑参数规模。
why_en: Sparse categorical features are commonly represented by learned embedding-table lookups.

termDefinitions.term: sparse categorical / 稀疏类别特征
termDefinitions.meaning: 取值是离散类别（如用户 ID）而非连续数值的特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse categorical feature takes discrete category values, like a user ID, instead of a continuous number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按类别 ID 查表得到该类别可学习向量的结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding table is a lookup structure that returns a learned vector for a given category ID.

q_en: How are sparse categorical features (user_id, item_id, enums) commonly represented?
scenario: 推荐模型输入里有 1 亿个 user_id 和 5000 万个 item_id，ID 之间没有大小关系。
scenario_en: Your ranking model takes a hundred million user_ids and fifty million item_ids, and these IDs have no meaningful numeric ordering.

scenario: user_id embedding 表设 1B 行、64 维、float32，参数量约 256GB（还没算优化器状态）。
q: 这个参数量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 可以直接上线，不需要再做任何优化
长尾用户不该分配和头部用户同等大小的独立向量
模型精度还不够，应该继续增加 embedding 维度
应该完全放弃用户 embedding，改用其它特征
options_en: It can ship as-is, with no further optimization needed.
Long-tail users shouldn't get the same full-size independent vector as heavy users.
The model still lacks precision, so keep adding embedding dimensions.
User embeddings should be abandoned entirely in favor of other features.
why: 1B×64×4 bytes≈256GB，参数几乎都花在只出现过几次的长尾用户身上，付全价不划算。
why_en: A one-billion-row, sixty-four-dimensional float32 embedding table is about 256 gigabytes, and most of it pays for long-tail users who barely showed up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型学到的稠密向量，用来表示用户、物品或文本等对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a learned dense vector that represents an object such as a user, item, or text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按类别 ID 查表得到该类别可学习向量的结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding table is a lookup structure that returns a learned vector for a given category ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: 32 位浮点数，每个参数通常占 4 bytes。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Float32 is a 32-bit floating-point number, usually using four bytes per parameter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练优化器为每个参数额外保存的动量、方差等辅助张量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimizer state is extra per-parameter data, such as momentum or variance, kept by the training optimizer.

q_en: What design conclusion does this parameter count best support?
scenario_en: A user_id embedding table is 1B rows by 64 dimensions in float32, about 256GB of parameters before counting optimizer state.
optionExplanations: 256GB 还没算进优化器状态，规模这么大不代表可以不再优化就直接上线。
1B×64×4B≈256GB 里大部分参数花在长尾 ID 上，长尾不该和头部用户共享同等大小的独立向量。
只在明确欠拟合且资源可承受时才该加维度；这里先暴露的是参数预算爆炸，不是精度不够。
参数量大不等于该放弃用户 embedding，真正要做的是压缩表示，而不是整体丢弃这个信号。
optionExplanations_en: This is about 256GB before counting optimizer state — that scale alone doesn't mean it's ready to ship with no further work.
This 1B-row, 64-dim table is roughly 256GB, with the bulk spent on rarely-seen IDs, so they shouldn't get a full-size vector like heavy users get.
Add dimensions only once underfitting is clear and affordable; this number first exposes a parameter-budget problem, not a capacity gap.
A huge parameter count doesn't mean dropping user embeddings — the fix is compressing the representation, not discarding the signal.

scenario: 高基数 user_id 太多，完整 embedding 表参数爆炸，大量长尾用户只有几次出现。
q: 常见折中是什么？
options: 给每个用户单独训练一个独立的小模型，逐一微调参数
把所有低频长尾用户从训练集和线上数据里直接删除
hashing trick 到固定桶数后再 embedding
把 user_id 的数值直接当成一个连续数值特征输入排序模型
options_en: Train a separate small model for every user and fine-tune each one individually.
Delete every low-frequency long-tail user from both the training set and online data.
Apply the hashing trick into a fixed bucket count, then embed.
Feed the raw user_id number directly into the ranking model as a continuous numeric feature.
optionExplanations: 为每个用户训练模型完全不现实，成本爆炸。
删除长尾用户等于放弃给他们做个性化。
哈希进固定桶数，让多个长尾 ID 共享一行，重度用户仍主导自己的桶。
ID 大小没有数值意义，当成连续值会误导模型。
optionExplanations_en: Training a separate model per user is completely impractical at this scale.
Deleting long-tail users means giving up on personalizing for them at all.
Hashing into a fixed bucket count lets many long-tail IDs share one row, while heavy users still dominate their own bucket.
An ID's numeric value is meaningless, so treating it as continuous misleads the model.
why: 哈希桶让多个 ID 共享参数：参数量 = 桶数 × 维度，与用户总数脱钩。代价是碰撞，长尾用户退化到近似平均表示。
why_en: The hashing trick makes parameter count buckets times dimension instead of users times dimension, and pays for it with collisions that blur long-tail users into an average representation.
whenOtherWins: 如果 ID 数量不大且每个实体都有充足数据，完整 embedding 表质量更好。
tradeoff: 参数量大幅缩小 vs 少量 ID 哈希碰撞

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大量 ID 哈希进固定数量的桶，多个 ID 共享一个 embedding 行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The hashing trick maps many IDs into a fixed number of buckets so multiple IDs share one embedding row.

q_en: What's the common workaround?
scenario_en: There are too many high-cardinality user_ids — a full embedding table blows up in parameters, and most long-tail users only appear a few times.

q: 行为序列用均值聚合的主要代价是什么？
options: 丢失顺序、间隔和会话结构
无法降低成本
一定比 Transformer 更准
不能用于轻 ranker
options_en: It loses order, timing, and session structure.
It fails to reduce cost.
It is always more accurate than a Transformer.
It cannot be used in a light ranker.
optionExplanations: 取均值只留下整体趋势，谁先谁后、间隔多久全部丢掉。
均值聚合恰恰是最便宜的做法，说反了。
聚合更便宜但通常信息更少，不会比完整序列准。
均值聚合正是轻 ranker 最常用的表示方式。
optionExplanations_en: Averaging keeps only the overall trend and throws away order, timing, and session boundaries.
Mean aggregation is actually the cheapest option — this has it backwards.
Aggregation is cheaper but carries less information, not more accuracy than a full sequence.
Mean aggregation is exactly the go-to representation for light rankers.
why: 平均最近观看 embedding 便宜，但不知道先后顺序和时间间隔。完整序列模型能捕捉短期意图和模式转折。
why_en: Mean aggregation of event embeddings is cheap but loses order, timing, and session structure.
tradeoff: 聚合的低成本 vs 完整序列保留的时序信息

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次连续使用中事件的先后顺序和分组关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session structure is the order and grouping of events within one continuous usage session.

q_en: What's the main cost of mean-aggregating a behavioral sequence?
scenario: 用户这次会话先看健身再转做饭，轻 ranker 只把最近 50 次观看做了均值聚合。
scenario_en: A user switched from fitness to cooking within one session, and the light ranker only mean-pooled their last fifty watches.

scenario: 召回后的轻 ranker 要在 CPU 上快速处理百万候选。
q: 最近观看历史如何表示更合适？
options: 完整 16k 长度事件序列 Transformer 编码
每个候选人工检查
把历史视频原文件全部加载
最近若干视频 embedding 的均值或时间衰减聚合
options_en: A full 16k-length event-sequence Transformer encoder.
Manually review every candidate.
Load all the raw historical video files.
A mean or recency-weighted aggregate of the most recent video embeddings.
optionExplanations: 16k 事件 Transformer 对每候选算力太贵，撑不住百万级吞吐。
人工检查根本无法达到毫秒级、百万候选的吞吐。
加载视频原文件是巨大的 I/O 开销，不是特征表示。
百万候选要求吞吐优先，聚合便宜够用。
optionExplanations_en: A 16k-event transformer per candidate is far too expensive for million-scale throughput.
Manual review can't come close to millisecond, million-candidate throughput.
Loading raw video files is a huge I/O cost, not a feature representation.
Millions of candidates demand throughput first, and cheap aggregates are good enough here.
why: 宽漏斗阶段吞吐优先，便宜聚合能给出足够信号。完整序列适合候选数变少后的重 ranker。
why_en: A wide-funnel lightweight ranker should use cheap recency-weighted aggregates rather than a full sequence Transformer.
whenOtherWins: 当候选已缩小到百级、质量更重要时，完整序列模型会更有价值。
tradeoff: 宽漏斗吞吐优先 vs 窄漏斗表达力优先

termDefinitions.term: recency-weighted aggregation / 时间衰减聚合
termDefinitions.meaning: 给较近的事件更高权重后再取聚合统计量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recency-weighted aggregation gives more recent events higher weight before combining them into a summary statistic.

q_en: How should recent watch history be represented here?
scenario_en: After retrieval, a light ranker needs to process millions of candidates quickly on CPU.

q: 对 views、followers、金额这类 power-law 数值，默认变换是什么？
options: 保留原始数值，不做任何压缩
log-scaling
转成随机字符串
乘以用户 ID
options_en: Keep the raw value as-is, with no compression at all.
Log-scaling.
Convert it into a random string.
Multiply it by the user ID.
optionExplanations: 原值下 100 万浏览量的样本会完全压过其他信号。
取对数压缩幂律分布里少数极端值的影响。
转成字符串丢掉了数值本身的顺序信息。
和用户 ID 相乘没有任何统计学意义。
optionExplanations_en: Left raw, a million-view sample would swamp every other signal in training.
Log-scaling compresses the range so a handful of extreme values do not dominate training.
Turning it into a string throws away the value's numeric ordering.
Multiplying by a user ID has no statistical meaning whatsoever.
why: 幂律数值跨度巨大，原值会让少数超大样本支配模型。log 变换压缩尺度，让模型更稳。
why_en: Power-law numeric features are often log-scaled so a few huge values do not dominate the model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 少数值极大、大多数值很小的分布，如浏览量、粉丝数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A power-law distribution has a few very large values and many small ones, like view counts or follower counts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对数值取对数以压缩其数值范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Log-scaling applies a logarithm to a numeric value to compress its range.

q_en: What's the default transform for power-law numeric values like views, followers, or dollar amounts?
scenario: 视频 views 从 10 到 1 亿跨 7 个数量级，少数爆款样本会主导线性层。
scenario_en: Video view counts span seven orders of magnitude, from ten to a hundred million, and a few viral outliers dominate the model.

scenario: 某数值与标签关系明显非单调，例如年龄段中间最高、两端较低。
q: 比简单标准化更合适的表示是？
options: 强行线性标准化
只保留最大值
分桶后 embedding
当作文本 token 拼接
options_en: Force a linear standardization.
Keep only the maximum value.
Bucket the value, then embed each bucket.
