why_en: GraphSAGE is inductive, so it can embed brand-new nodes from their features and sampled neighborhoods at inference time instead of requiring retraining for every new account.
scenario: 需要识别新账号在社交图中的 botnet 关系，图持续增长。
options: 它是 inductive 的，能嵌入新节点
它只能处理训练时已经存在的固定节点
它不需要对邻居做任何采样
它会把整张社交图一次性全部载入内存后再计算
whenOtherWins: 如果图稳定且只做离线已知节点分析，node2vec 这类方法更简单。
tradeoff: 归纳式泛化到新节点 vs 只处理训练时已知节点

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种归纳式图神经网络，能给训练时没见过的新节点生成表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphSAGE is an inductive graph neural network that can embed new nodes it never saw during training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型学到的是一个函数，能泛化到新节点，而不是只记住训练图里的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inductive means the model learns a general function that works on new nodes instead of memorizing a fixed graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个节点连接的邻居数量，粉丝多的账号扇出会非常大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is how many neighbors a node has, so celebrity accounts have very large fan-out.

options_en: It is inductive, so it can embed new nodes directly.
It can only process the fixed set of nodes seen during training.
It requires no neighbor sampling at all.
It loads the entire social graph into memory at once before computing.
q_en: Why choose GraphSAGE for the graph branch?
scenario_en: You need to detect botnet relationships for new accounts in a social graph that keeps growing.
optionExplanations: GraphSAGE 是归纳式的，能直接用新节点的特征和邻域现算 embedding，正好匹配图持续增长、新账号频出的场景。
这描述的是只能处理固定图方法的局限，GraphSAGE 不受此限。
邻居采样正是 GraphSAGE 控制 fan-out 和延迟的关键设计。
恰恰相反，GraphSAGE 靠邻居采样只取局部子图，不需要整图载入内存。
optionExplanations_en: GraphSAGE is inductive, so it can compute an embedding for a brand-new node straight from its features and sampled neighborhood—exactly what a constantly growing graph needs.
That describes the limitation of fixed-graph methods; GraphSAGE isn't bound by it.
Neighbor sampling is precisely how GraphSAGE controls fan-out and latency.
The opposite—GraphSAGE samples a local subgraph and never loads the whole graph into memory.

scenario: 图分支默认只抓 2-hop 邻域；有人提议把邻域跳数改到 20-hop 看得更全。
q: 把邻域跳数从 2 大幅加深，对系统意味着什么？
why: 邻域规模随跳数迅速膨胀（尤其高粉丝账号），2-hop 已能看到局部协调关系；再加深收益递减但成本陡增。
why_en: Neighborhood size explodes with hop count, especially for high fan-out accounts, so a compact two-hop neighborhood already captures local coordination while deeper hops add cost with diminishing returns.
options: 计算和延迟会随跳数快速膨胀，收益却边际递减，通常不划算
跳数越深成本只是随之线性小幅增加，覆盖更全所以一直都很划算
跳数深浅完全不影响任何计算量或延迟
更深的跳数能自动让训练标签的数量变多
options_en: Compute and latency blow up with hop depth while returns diminish, so it's usually not worth it.
Deeper hops only add cost linearly while covering more, so it's always worth it.
Hop depth doesn't affect compute or latency in any way at all.
Deeper hops automatically produce a larger number of training labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图上距离账号 k 步以内能到达的节点集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-hop neighborhood is the set of nodes reachable within k edges of an account.

q_en: What does greatly increasing the graph-hop depth mean for the system?
scenario_en: The graph branch currently uses a 2-hop neighborhood; someone proposes 20 hops to see more context.
optionExplanations: 邻域规模随跳数指数级膨胀，粉丝多的账号尤其明显；两跳内就能看清本地的协同关系，再往深挖成本陡增但收获有限。
邻域规模随跳数指数级膨胀而非线性，高粉丝账号尤其爆炸，这里严重低估了成本。
跳数越深要遍历的节点越多，计算量必然跟着涨。
跳数深浅只影响邻域大小，不会凭空生出新的训练标签。
optionExplanations_en: Neighborhood size explodes roughly exponentially with hop count, especially for high fan-out accounts; two hops already captures local coordination, and going deeper adds cost for shrinking returns.
Neighborhood size grows exponentially with hops, not linearly—especially for high-follower accounts—so this badly underestimates cost.
Deeper hops always mean traversing more nodes, so compute necessarily rises.
Hop depth only changes neighborhood size; it can't manufacture new training labels out of nowhere.

q: 序列分支更合理的模型选择是什么？
why: GRU 能捕捉行为顺序和节奏，成本远低于 Transformer；这里建模的是事件序列的节奏，不是复杂自然语言语义。
why_en: A compact bidirectional GRU is enough to capture behavioral rhythm and order at a fraction of a Transformer's cost, since the task isn't about nuanced language understanding.
scenario: 要识别账号最近约 200 个事件的时间节奏，目标不是理解语言细节，计算也要省。
options: 小型双向 GRU/LSTM 类模型
超大规模文本 Transformer
只用平均发帖数这一个统计量
完全不建模事件的时间顺序
whenOtherWins: 如果需要捕捉很长距离复杂交互且候选很少，Transformer 序列模型可能赢。
tradeoff: 轻量 GRU 的低成本 vs Transformer 更强的长距离建模能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种轻量的循环神经网络，用来建模事件序列的先后顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GRU is a lightweight recurrent neural network used to model the order of a sequence of events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖自注意力机制处理序列，比 GRU 更贵但更擅长捕捉长距离依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Transformer uses self-attention to process sequences and is more expensive than a GRU but better at capturing long-range dependencies.

options_en: A small bidirectional GRU/LSTM-style model.
A very large text Transformer.
Just a single statistic like average posts per day.
Skip modeling event order entirely.
q_en: What model is a better fit for the sequence branch?
scenario_en: You need to model the timing of roughly the last 200 account events, not language semantics, and compute is limited.
optionExplanations: 目标是约 200 个事件的节奏而不是语言语义，小型双向 GRU 计算便宜，也足以捕捉顺序和节奏。
为语言细节设计的重型 Transformer 在这里算力花得远超所需。
压成一个平均值会抹掉顺序和节奏里的绝大部分信息。
顺序正是本题要建模的对象，放弃顺序就丢了核心信号。
optionExplanations_en: The goal is timing cadence over roughly 200 events, not language semantics, so a small bidirectional GRU is cheap and still enough to capture order and rhythm.
A heavyweight Transformer built for language nuance spends far more compute than this task needs.
Collapsing everything into one average erases nearly all order and rhythm information.
Order is exactly what this task needs to model—dropping it throws away the core signal.

scenario: 要把一个账号几个月的点击/发帖事件流喂进模型，原始时间戳精确到毫秒且分布长尾。
q: 序列分支是怎么编码用户事件的？
why: 事件类型、离散化的时间间隔和先后顺序共同表达人类/机器节奏；五分钟这类时间桶能让模型学到可比较的模式。
why_en: The sequence branch embeds recent event types and bucketed timestamps in order before feeding them into the sequence model, preserving both timing and order.
options: 分桶时间戳，embedding 事件类型
把原始 JSON 直接拼接成字符串输入
把事件按字母顺序重新排序
只保留最后一个事件
options_en: Bucket timestamps and embed event types.
Concatenate raw JSON logs as a string input.
Re-sort events alphabetically.
Keep only the very last event.
q_en: How does the sequence branch encode user events?
scenario_en: You need to feed months of an account click and post events into the model, with raw millisecond timestamps and a long-tail distribution.
optionExplanations: 序列分支把时间戳分桶、事件类型做 embedding，再按发生顺序喂给模型，同时保留时机和顺序信息。
原始 JSON 既没归一化也没向量化，模型用不了。
按字母重排会打乱事件本来的时间顺序，节奏信息就没了。
只留最后一个事件等于丢掉了整个序列的意义。
optionExplanations_en: The sequence branch buckets timestamps, embeds event types, and feeds them in order, preserving both timing and sequence.
Raw JSON is neither normalized nor vectorized, so the model can't consume it directly.
Alphabetical resorting scrambles the actual time order, destroying rhythm information.
Keeping only the last event throws away the entire point of having a sequence.

scenario: 单看时间线的高频账号可能是真人运营号，单看图上的密集互关可能只是同校同学。
q: 图分支和序列分支融合（fusion）的目的是什么？
why: 交叉注意力能回答「这个节奏是否在同一图簇里重复出现」，让时间线和图关系互相校验，比单看一边更强。
why_en: Cross-attention fusion lets the behavioral timeline query the graph and vice versa, so the two views cross-check each other for coordinated bot patterns.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Seq[Behavior timeline] --> Fuse[Fusion]
  Graph[Graph footprint] --> Fuse
  Fuse --> Risk[Bot risk]
  Risk --> Action[Action policy]
options: 让账号的时间线和网络足迹互相校验
只是为了减少传输的 JSON 大小
替代所有人工标签
直接删除低风险账号

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一路表示去查询另一路表示，找到与自己相关的部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-attention lets one sequence's representation query another sequence's representation for the parts relevant to it.

options_en: Let the account's timeline and network footprint cross-check each other.
Just to shrink the JSON payload size.
Replace the need for any human labels.
Directly delete low-risk accounts.
q_en: What is the purpose of fusing the graph and sequence branches?
scenario_en: A high-frequency timeline alone can be a real community manager, and a dense follow cluster alone can just be classmates.
optionExplanations: 交叉注意力让时间线表示去查询图表示、反过来也一样，两路信号互相校验，比单看一边更能发现协同 bot。
融合是表示层面的交互，不是数据传输优化。
融合只是产生更强的表示，产生不了标签，监督信号还得靠人工。
融合只输出风险分数，删账号是动作层的事，不是融合本身。
optionExplanations_en: Cross-attention lets the timeline representation query the graph representation and vice versa, so the two views cross-check each other and catch coordinated bots that either view alone would miss.
Fusion is a representation-level interaction, not a payload-size optimization.
Fusion produces a richer representation, not labels—supervision still comes from humans.
Fusion only outputs a risk score; deleting accounts is the action layer's job, not fusion's.

scenario: 图+序列双分支模型参数上亿，但每周只有几百条可信标签可用于监督训练。
q: 为什么 bot 主模型需要自监督预训练？
why: 标签少、模型较大，直接上二分类容易过拟合；先用自监督让图和序列分支学会平台的「语言」，监督阶段就更稳定。
why_en: With scarce labels and a fairly large model, jumping straight to supervised binary classification risks overfitting, so self-supervised pretraining lets each branch learn platform structure first.
options: 标签稀缺而模型较大，直接监督二分类容易过拟合
自监督预训练能彻底消除后续训练里出现的所有误判
预训练完全不需要用到任何真实数据
预训练只是为了单纯加速前端页面加载
options_en: Labels are scarce and the model is fairly large, so going straight to supervised classification risks overfitting.
Self-supervised pretraining fully eliminates all misclassifications in later training.
Pretraining needs no real data of any kind whatsoever.
Pretraining exists purely to speed up front-end page loading.
q_en: Why does the main bot model need self-supervised pretraining?
scenario_en: The graph-plus-sequence model has hundreds of millions of parameters, but only a few hundred trusted labels arrive each week.
optionExplanations: 标签少、模型又不小，直接上监督二分类容易过拟合；自监督预训练先让两个分支学会平台结构，监督阶段就更稳。
预训练只是给监督阶段更好的起点，改善不了标签本身，消不了所有误判。
预训练同样要吃大量真实行为/图数据，不是无中生有。
预训练服务的是建模质量，跟前端页面性能无关。
optionExplanations_en: With scarce labels and a fairly large model, going straight to supervised binary classification risks overfitting; self-supervised pretraining lets both branches learn platform structure first, stabilizing the supervised stage.
Pretraining only gives supervision a better starting point; it can't fix the labels or eliminate all errors.
Pretraining still consumes plenty of real behavior/graph data—it isn't free of data.
Pretraining serves modeling quality, unrelated to front-end page speed.

scenario: 预训练阶段不能碰调查员标签（要留作评估），手上只有海量无标签的图和事件流。
q: bot 主模型的自监督预训练任务包括哪些？（多选）
why: 这些任务让模型在没有标签的情况下学会正常社交图结构和行为「语言」；测试集标签必须留到评估阶段。
why_en: Masking graph attributes, predicting masked or next events, and contrasting same-user session clips all teach the model normal structure and rhythm without using any test labels.
options: 图侧遮蔽节点属性/丢边/辨别真假邻居
序列侧 masked event 和 next-event prediction
把同一用户的会话片段拉近，不同用户的片段推开
直接用测试集标签做监督训练
options_en: On the graph side: masking node attributes, dropping edges, and telling real neighbors from fake ones.
On the sequence side: masked-event and next-event prediction.
Contrastive learning: pull same-user session clips together, push different users' clips apart.
Train directly on the test-set labels.
q_en: Which self-supervised pretraining tasks fit the main bot model? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Pretraining cannot touch investigator labels, which are reserved for evaluation, so all you have is unlabeled graph and event data.
optionExplanations: 图侧靠遮蔽属性、丢边、辨别真假邻居这些自监督任务学正常图结构。
序列侧用掩码预测和下一事件预测学正常的行为节奏。
对比学习把同用户片段拉近、不同用户片段推远，学出账号级别的一致性表示。
测试集标签绝不能用于训练，否则评估会失去意义。
optionExplanations_en: On the graph side, masking attributes, dropping edges, and telling real neighbors from fake ones teaches normal graph structure self-supervised.
On the sequence side, masked-event and next-event prediction teaches normal behavioral rhythm.
Contrastive learning pulls same-user clips together and pushes different users' clips apart, learning an account-consistent representation.
Test-set labels must never be used for training, or the evaluation becomes meaningless.

scenario: 一个 bot 骚扰了 10 万用户，另一个只发了 3 条帖，业务目标是降低实际伤害。
q: bot 检测主模型的监督 loss 如何对齐「影响」这个目标？
why: 高影响 bot 更重要，所以按潜在受影响用户数加权；权重要设上限，避免单个爆款 spam 让梯度失控。
why_en: The loss is a weighted binary cross-entropy that emphasizes high-impact bot accounts, with weights capped so one viral spam post can't destabilize training.
options: 加权二元交叉熵，按影响力加权并设上限
只优化未加权的 accuracy
只优化生成文本的长度
只优化图节点的度数

termDefinitions.term: weighted binary cross-entropy / 加权二元交叉熵
termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个训练样本按重要性加权的二分类损失函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weighted binary cross-entropy is a binary classification loss that scales each example's contribution by an importance weight.

options_en: Weighted binary cross-entropy, weighted by impact and capped.
Optimize only unweighted accuracy.
Optimize only the length of generated text.
Optimize only the degree of a graph node.
q_en: How should the supervised loss align with user impact?
scenario_en: One bot reached 100k users while another posted three times, and the business goal is reducing actual harm.
optionExplanations: 用按潜在受影响用户数加权的二元交叉熵，并给权重设上限，让高影响 bot 更重要又不会让单个爆款样本主导梯度。
accuracy 反映不出谁受到了伤害，退回它就丢了「影响」这个目标。
文本长度和分类目标完全无关。
节点度数只是一个特征，不是训练要优化的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Weighting binary cross-entropy by potential affected-user count, with a cap, makes high-impact bots matter more without letting one viral sample dominate the gradient.
Accuracy doesn't reflect who got hurt, so falling back to it drops the 'impact' objective.
Text length has nothing to do with the classification target.
Node degree is a feature, not something the training loss should optimize.

q: 这段伪代码体现了什么设计？
why: 它把潜在伤害（受影响用户数）纳入训练目标提升召回，但 cap 防止单个爆款 spam 主导梯度。
why_en: The code shows impact-weighted binary cross-entropy where the weight is capped, so high-exposure accounts matter more without letting one viral post destabilize the gradient.
scenario: 你要解释 bot loss 如何重视高影响账号但避免梯度失控。
codeSample:
weight = min(users_exposed, cap)
loss = weight * BCE(label, bot_score)
options: 影响加权 BCE，并对权重做截断（cap）
无监督聚类损失
Platt scaling：把输出分数校准成概率
ANN 近邻检索
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求每个账号同等处理而不按影响优先，未加权或公平约束 loss 更合适。
tradeoff: 按影响力加权提升高危账号召回 vs 截断权重换取梯度稳定

termDefinitions.meaning: 给样本权重设的最大值，防止极端样本主导训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cap is a maximum value on a sample's weight so one extreme example can't dominate training.

options_en: Impact-weighted BCE with the weight capped.
An unsupervised clustering loss.
Platt scaling that calibrates output scores into probabilities.
ANN nearest-neighbor retrieval.
q_en: What design does this pseudocode express?
scenario_en: You need to explain how the bot loss emphasizes high-impact accounts without letting gradients blow up.
optionExplanations: `weight = min(users_exposed, cap)` 再乘 BCE，正是按受影响用户数加权、同时截断权重防止梯度失控的设计。
代码里没有任何聚类相关操作。
Platt scaling 是训练后把分数校准成概率的方法，不是这里的训练损失。
ANN 检索是找相似内容，不是损失函数。
optionExplanations_en: `weight = min(users_exposed, cap)` times BCE is exactly weighting by affected-user count while capping the weight to keep gradients stable.
There's no clustering operation anywhere in this code.
Platt scaling calibrates scores into probabilities after training; it isn't this training loss.
ANN retrieval finds similar content—it isn't a loss function.

q: 最重要的 serving 结构设计是什么？
why: 级联能把重模型调用量降到可控范围，轻模型的阈值还是个可调参数，能在资源和效果之间权衡。
why_en: A two-stage cascade reserves the expensive graph-sequence model for accounts that pass a cheap first-stage filter, keeping GPU cost bounded at billions of daily actions.
scenario: 每天有数十亿动作，重图序列模型需要 GPU。
options: 两阶段级联：轻模型过滤，重模型查可疑
对每一个动作都跑一遍完整的重图序列模型
只做离线的年度评分
取消所有缓存以简化架构
whenOtherWins: 如果流量很小或每次决策风险极高，直接跑重模型也可能合理。
tradeoff: 级联降低重模型调用量 vs 轻模型阈值可能漏掉部分可疑账号
diagram:
flowchart LR
  All[All accounts] --> Light[Light filter]
  Light --> Clear[Mostly normal]
  Light --> Suspicious[Suspicious]
  Suspicious --> Heavy[Graph sequence model]
  Heavy --> Action[Calibrated action]
options_en: A two-stage cascade: light model filters, heavy model checks suspects.
Run the full heavy graph-sequence model on every single action.
Only do offline scoring once a year.
Remove all caching to simplify the architecture.
q_en: What is the most important serving-architecture choice?
scenario_en: The platform has billions of daily actions, and the heavy graph-sequence model needs GPUs.
optionExplanations: 两阶段级联用便宜的轻模型先过滤，把重图序列模型的预算集中在可疑账号上，能把 GPU 调用量控制在可承受范围。
数十亿动作每个都跑重图序列模型，GPU 成本完全不可持续。
年度批处理完全跟不上风险变化的速度。
取消缓存只会让邻域和序列编码反复重算，成本更高。
optionExplanations_en: A cheap first stage filters traffic, concentrating the expensive graph-sequence model's budget on suspicious accounts, keeping GPU cost within a sustainable range.
Running the heavy graph-sequence model on all billions of actions is not GPU-sustainable.
A once-a-year offline batch can't keep up with how fast risk changes.
Dropping caching just forces repeated recomputation of neighborhood and sequence encodings, raising cost.

scenario: 重模型每次推理要拉整个图邻域，500M 账号全量跑不现实，得先筛掉明显正常的账号。
q: 轻量过滤模型如何与重模型的判断对齐？
why: 轻模型的目标不是独立最优，而是找出重模型可能打高分的账号；teacher/student 训练能省计算又少漏可疑样本。
why_en: The lightweight filter is trained in a teacher/student fashion to approximate the heavy model's score, which preserves recall while cutting the number of accounts sent to the expensive model.
options: 用 teacher/student 训练轻模型近似
让轻模型随机输出没有依据的分数结果
只在前端点击这一类信号上单独训练轻模型，不参考重模型输出
轻模型完全不使用任何形式的监督标签

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个大模型的输出去训练一个更小的模型来近似它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Teacher/student training trains a small model to approximate the outputs of a larger one.

options_en: Train the light model as a student to approximate the teacher.
Have the light model output ungrounded, random score results.
Train the light model alone on front-end click signals, ignoring the heavy model's output.
The light model uses no form of supervised label whatsoever.
q_en: How should the lightweight filter align with the heavy model?
scenario_en: The heavy model pulls a whole graph neighborhood per call, so scoring all 500M accounts is impossible without a cheap prefilter.
optionExplanations: 用师生蒸馏训练轻模型去近似重模型的判断，能省计算又不太漏掉重模型会打高分的账号。
随机分数没法近似重模型的判断。
只学前端点击信号且不看重模型输出，轻模型就学不到该逼近谁的判断。
没有对齐目标，轻模型就学不到该逼近谁。
optionExplanations_en: Training the light model teacher/student style to approximate the heavy model's judgment saves compute while preserving recall on what the heavy model would flag.
Random scores can't approximate the heavy model's judgment at all.
Training only on click signals without the heavy model's output leaves the light model no target to approximate.
Without an alignment target, the light model has nothing to learn to approximate.

scenario: 重模型 GPU 账单超预算，但多数账号的图邻域和活动序列在一天内几乎不变。
q: bot 检测重模型可用哪些推理优化？（多选）
why: 量化和缓存都能降低成本，但必须配合质量回归测试，尤其在图邻域没有明显变化时缓存最有效。
why_en: Quantization-aware training and caching graph or sequence encoders both cut serving cost, but they must be paired with quality regression testing.
options: quantization-aware training
缓存图 embedding
缓存活动序列编码
完全放弃模型质量评估

termDefinitions.term: quantization-aware training / 量化感知训练
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时就模拟低精度数值，让部署后用更少内存也能保持效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization-aware training simulates low-precision math during training so the deployed model stays accurate with less memory.

options_en: Quantization-aware training.
Caching graph embeddings.
Caching activity-sequence encodings.
Dropping model quality evaluation entirely.
q_en: Which inference optimizations can the heavy bot model use? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The heavy model blows the GPU budget, yet for most accounts the graph neighborhood and activity sequence barely change within a day.
optionExplanations: 训练时模拟低精度数值，部署后能用更少内存保持效果。
图邻域没大变化时，缓存图 embedding 能省下重复计算。
活动模式没大变化时，缓存序列编码同样能省计算。
推理优化必须配合质量回归测试，放弃评估会让人看不见质量退化。
optionExplanations_en: Simulating low-precision math during training keeps accuracy while using less memory at deployment.
When a graph neighborhood hasn't changed much, caching its embedding skips recomputation.
When activity patterns haven't changed much, caching the sequence encoding likewise skips recomputation.
Inference optimizations must pair with quality regression testing—dropping evaluation hides quality regressions.

scenario: 全量每天重算 500M 账号太贵，只想在账号风险可能真的变化时才重新打分。
q: 哪些事件适合触发 bot 风险重新评估？（多选）
why: 按事件触发重新评估比每个动作都全量重跑更省计算，也能在风险变化时更及时响应。
why_en: Re-scoring on registration, suspicious activity thresholds, joining a known bot cluster, or user reports is far cheaper than re-running every account on every action.
options: 账号注册
批量关注/快速发帖等活动阈值
加入已知的 bot 网络簇
收到用户举报
options_en: Account registration.
Crossing an activity threshold like bulk follows or rapid posting.
Joining a known bot cluster.
Receiving a user report.
q_en: Which events should trigger bot-risk reassessment? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Rescoring all 500M accounts daily is too expensive, so you only want to re-evaluate when an account risk plausibly changed.
optionExplanations: 新账号一出现就该先用元数据/早期行为打一次初始分。
越过批量关注、快速发帖这类活动阈值是典型的再评估触发点。
加入已知 bot 簇是很强的图协同信号，值得立刻重新评估。
用户举报应该优先触发重新评估。
optionExplanations_en: A brand-new account should get an initial score right away from metadata and early activity.
Crossing an activity threshold like bulk follows or rapid posting is a classic re-scoring trigger.
Joining a known bot cluster is a strong graph-coordination signal worth an immediate re-check.
A user report should trigger priority re-evaluation.

q: 这会带来什么风险？
why: 被及时拦截的正例缺少后续行为，模型可能学到「有完整行为数据=正常」，需要 holdout 或反事实样本来补足。
why_en: Because effective interception removes bots before they accumulate a full behavioral history, the model risks learning that having lots of history means legitimate.
scenario: 系统很快就拦截 bot，导致训练数据里高风险账号缺少后续完整行为。
options: 误学「有历史即正常」
模型判断会自动变得更公平
线上推理延迟会自动降低
训练标签会自动变成无偏
whenOtherWins: 如果模型只观察拦截前特征并严格按同一时间点训练，风险会小一些。
tradeoff: 越早拦截 bot（降低伤害）vs 训练数据里正例行为历史越不完整
options_en: Mislearning that having a history means legitimate.
Model judgments automatically become fairer.
Online inference latency automatically drops.
Training labels automatically become unbiased.
q_en: What risk does this create?
scenario_en: Fast interception means high-risk bot accounts often lack complete later behavior in the training logs.
optionExplanations: 被及时拦截的 bot 缺少后续行为，模型可能把「行为历史完整」错误地学成「正常」的信号。
这里的风险是标签偏差，跟公平性没有直接关系。
标签偏差和推理延迟是两回事，快速拦截不会自动改善延迟。
标签依然是有偏的，需要靠额外留一部分账号不处理来获取对照数据，或者构造反事实样本来补齐。
optionExplanations_en: Bots caught quickly never accumulate later behavior, so the model can mistakenly learn that having a full history equals legitimate.
The risk here is label bias, not fairness—the two aren't directly linked.
Label bias and inference latency are unrelated; fast interception doesn't automatically improve latency.
The labels stay biased and need dedicated fixes like holdouts or counterfactual samples.

q: 这类 holdout 的关键约束是什么？
why: holdout 能提供反事实数据，也能让攻击者更难反推检测逻辑，但绝不能造成明显用户伤害，需要小比例和严格风险控制。
why_en: Holdouts collect valuable counterfactual bot behavior and make detection logic harder to reverse-engineer, but they must stay small and tightly risk-controlled so bots aren't given free rein.
scenario: 为收集 bot 完整行为并隐藏检测规则，你考虑对少量疑似 bot 暂不立即处理。
options: 严格控制风险和流量，避免被攻击者反向利用
让所有被怀疑的 bot 都直接放行不管
完全不记录任何相关的操作日志
只把它用于前端的 A/B 实验场景
whenOtherWins: 如果风险极高（如恶意链接传播），软动作或沙盒比完全放行更合适。
tradeoff: 保留 holdout 换取反事实数据和隐藏检测逻辑 vs 放任 bot 造成的伤害规模
options_en: Tightly control risk and volume to avoid attackers exploiting it.
Let every suspected bot straight through with no oversight at all.
Keep absolutely no logs of any related activity.
Use it only for a front-end A/B experiment scenario.
q_en: What is the key constraint for this kind of holdout?
scenario_en: To collect complete bot behavior and hide detection logic, you consider delaying action on a tiny set of suspected bots.
optionExplanations: 把 holdout 限定在小比例、严格风险控制内，既能拿到反事实行为数据，又不会被攻击者规模化利用。
holdout 是小比例受控延迟，不是对所有 bot 全面放行。
日志记录正是 holdout 的价值所在，不留痕就白做了。
把用途限定在前端实验会错失收集完整 bot 行为这个核心目的。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the holdout small and tightly risk-controlled yields counterfactual behavior data without letting attackers exploit it at scale.
A holdout is a small, controlled delay, not a blanket pass-through for every bot.
Logging is exactly where a holdout's value comes from—no trace means wasted effort.
Limiting it to front-end experiments misses the whole point of collecting full bot behavior.

q: 在线评估应该怎么采样？
why: 边界和模型分歧处的样本信息量最大；低 prevalence 下纯随机标注效率太低，重加权能把这些样本还原成总体估计。
why_en: Online evaluation should use importance sampling weighted toward boundary and disagreement cases, then reweight, because with prevalence under 1% pure random sampling would need an enormous sample size.
scenario: 候选模型和旧模型标出的账号不同，bot prevalence 很低，人工标签很贵。
options: 按分数和分歧点采样，再重加权
均匀随机抽取少量样本且不重加权
只标最高分的账号并当成总体估计
完全不做人工验证
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是估计全站无条件 prevalence，仍需保留一部分随机样本。
tradeoff: 把标注预算集中在高信息量样本 vs 均匀随机采样的简单无偏性
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Scores[Model scores] --> Sample[Sample by score and disagreement]
  Sample --> Human[Investigator labels]
  Human --> Reweight[Reweight estimates]
  Reweight --> Metrics[Online metrics]

termDefinitions.meaning: 按信息量而非均匀概率抽样，再用权重修正估计结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Importance sampling draws samples in proportion to how informative they are, then reweights the results to correct for that bias.

options_en: Sample by score and disagreement, then reweight.
Sample a small number uniformly at random without reweighting.
Label only the highest-scoring accounts and treat that as the population.
Skip manual verification altogether.
q_en: How should online evaluation sample accounts?
scenario_en: The candidate and old models flag different accounts, bot prevalence is low, and human labels are expensive.
optionExplanations: 按模型分数和两模型分歧点采样再重加权，能把标注预算集中在信息量最高的账号上，还原成无偏的总体估计。
prevalence 低于 1% 时，均匀随机抽样需要巨大样本量才够稳定。
只看高分子集外推整体会系统性高估检出率，忽略假阴性。
不做人工验证就没法判断候选模型是否真的更好。
optionExplanations_en: Sampling by score and model disagreement, then reweighting, concentrates the label budget on the most informative accounts while still recovering an unbiased population estimate.
With prevalence under 1%, uniform random sampling needs a huge sample size to be stable.
Extrapolating from only the top-scoring subset systematically overestimates detection, ignoring false negatives.
Skipping manual verification leaves no way to tell whether the candidate model is actually better.

scenario: 上线评审要一个既能给产品也能给法务交代的线上指标，误封真实用户是硬红线。
q: bot detection 的主要在线业务指标可以概括为什么？
why: 这个指标直接衡量真实用户感受到的 bot 骚扰，并把误伤设成硬 guardrail，比抽象的模型分数更贴近业务目标。
why_en: The primary online metric is the reduction in bot interactions per legitimate user, subject to keeping the false-positive rate on account restrictions under 1%.
options: bot 互动量下降，且误伤率 <1%
模型 accuracy 达到最大
GPU 利用率达到最大
封禁账号数量达到最大

termDefinitions.meaning: 设定的硬性上限指标，防止优化方向跑偏、牺牲用户体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a hard limit that keeps optimization from drifting into an outcome that harms users.

options_en: Bot interactions per user drop, with false positives under 1%.
Maximum model accuracy.
Maximum GPU utilization.
The maximum number of banned accounts.
q_en: How can the main online business metric for bot detection be summarized?
scenario_en: The launch review needs one online metric that satisfies both product and legal, and wrongly banning real users is a hard red line.
optionExplanations: 把主指标定成真实用户感受到的 bot 互动量下降，同时给误伤率设 <1% 的硬护栏，比抽象分数更贴近业务目标。
accuracy 在类别不平衡下会失真，代表不了体验。
GPU 利用率是成本指标，不是用户体验指标。
只追封禁数量会激励系统宁可错杀。
optionExplanations_en: Setting the primary metric as the drop in bot interactions users actually feel, with a hard guardrail of under 1% false positives, tracks the business goal far better than an abstract score.
Accuracy gets distorted under class imbalance and doesn't represent user experience.
GPU utilization is a cost metric, not an experience metric.
Chasing raw ban counts rewards over-banning.

scenario: 人工标签一周才回来几百条，但 A/B 实验必须在几天内看出这版模型有没有变好。
q: bot detection 在线可以用哪些 proxy metric 快速迭代？（多选）
why: 这些信号能比人工标签更快反映用户体验和误伤情况，但都带噪声，应该和人工标签结合使用。
why_en: User reports, appeal success rates, and network interaction rates all give faster feedback than manual labels, though they're noisier and should be combined with investigator labels.
options: bot/spam/fake account 举报量
申诉成功率
好友请求接受率/消息回复率
代码提交行数
options_en: Volume of bot/spam/fake-account reports.
Appeal success rate.
Friend-request acceptance rate / message response rate.
Lines of code committed.
q_en: Which proxy metrics can speed up online iteration? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Human labels trickle in a few hundred a week, but the A/B test has to show whether this model version helped within days.
optionExplanations: 举报量是用户主动发出的信号，量大但带噪声，能快速反映体感变化。
申诉成功率能反映有多少误伤账号被纠正回来。
好友请求接受率和消息回复率反映真实用户对互动的接受程度，是网络健康度信号。
代码提交行数是工程活动指标，和检测效果毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Report volume is a user-initiated, noisy but high-volume signal that reflects experience shifts quickly.
Appeal success rate reflects how many wrongly flagged accounts get corrected.
Friend-request acceptance and message response rates reflect how willing real users are to interact—a network-health signal.
Lines of code committed is an engineering-activity metric with no bearing on detection quality.

scenario: 封禁阈值定在 recall 90% 那个操作点，离线评估要能预测上线后的真实表现。
q: bot detection 的离线评估应该包括哪些指标？（多选）
why: 离线指标既要看整体判别力（PR-AUC），也要看动作阈值处的精确率、影响加权效果和多早能抓到 bot。
why_en: Offline evaluation should include an operating-point metric like Precision@Recall90, overall PR-AUC, impact-weighted quality, and how early bots get caught.
options: Precision@Recall90 或类似操作点指标
PR-AUC
impact-weighted 指标
early detection rate

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall 曲线下的面积，类别不平衡时比 ROC-AUC 更能反映效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PR-AUC is the area under the precision-recall curve and is more informative than ROC-AUC when classes are imbalanced.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把召回率固定在 90% 时衡量精确率的操作点指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision at Recall 90 measures precision at the operating point where recall is fixed at ninety percent.

options_en: Precision@Recall90 or a similar operating-point metric.
PR-AUC.
Impact-weighted metrics.
Early detection rate.
q_en: Which offline metrics should bot-detection evaluation include? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The ban threshold sits at the 90%-recall operating point, and offline evaluation has to predict what happens in production.
optionExplanations: Precision@Recall90 这类操作点指标对齐了自动化动作实际用的阈值。
PR-AUC 衡量整体判别力，类别不平衡下比 ROC-AUC 更稳健。
impact-weighted 指标按潜在受影响用户数加权，对齐「减少伤害」这个业务目标。
early detection rate 衡量多快能在行为早期抓到 bot，抓得越早累积伤害越小。
optionExplanations_en: Precision@Recall90-style operating-point metrics align with the threshold automated actions actually use.
PR-AUC measures overall discriminative power and is more robust than ROC-AUC under class imbalance.
Impact-weighted metrics weigh quality by potential affected-user count, aligning with the 'reduce harm' business goal.
Early detection rate measures how soon bots get caught—the earlier, the less cumulative harm.

q: 验证集应该如何设计？
why: 对抗漂移意味着未来 bot 和过去不同；按时间分层留出未来行为，能让验证集更接近线上真实会遇到的新策略。
why_en: Because adversarial drift means future bot behavior differs from the past, time-stratified validation holds out future behavior so the test set better reflects unseen attack patterns.
scenario: bot 攻击策略随时间变化，你担心验证集过于容易。
options: 按时间分层，留出未来行为测试未见过的攻击模式
把所有时间点随机打散后再混合切分
只用最早期、最陈旧的历史样本做验证
只用训练集上的拟合效果来评估，完全不单独划分验证集
whenOtherWins: 如果只验证稳定的元数据 pipeline，随机抽样也可作为辅助。
tradeoff: 按时间切分更贴近真实漂移 vs 随机切分的方差更小、更容易
options_en: Time-stratify and hold out future behavior to test unseen attack patterns.
Randomly shuffle every timestamp together before splitting.
Validate only on the oldest, most dated historical samples.
Judge only by fit on the training set and never hold out a separate validation set.
q_en: How should the validation set be designed?
scenario_en: Bot attack strategies change over time, and you are worried the validation set is too easy.
optionExplanations: 按时间分层把未来的行为留出来做验证，能让测试集更贴近线上真正会遇到的新攻击策略。
随机切分会让模型「偷看」未来模式，验证结果会过于乐观。
最早期样本代表不了对抗漂移后的新策略。
只看训练集拟合无法反映泛化，尤其挡不住对抗漂移带来的新攻击。
optionExplanations_en: Time-stratifying and holding out future behavior makes the test set closer to the new attack strategies actually seen online.
Random splitting lets the model peek at future patterns, making validation results overly optimistic.
The earliest historical samples can't represent strategies that emerged after adversarial drift.
Training-set fit says nothing about generalization, least of all against drifting new attacks.

scenario: 新旧两个模型版本都输出 0.6 分，但切换后封禁阈值必须保持同样的误伤率。
q: bot 模型为什么需要做 calibration？
why: 0.6 分不一定代表 60% 是 bot；校准把分数映射成更可信的概率，动作阈值和模型版本切换才能稳定。
why_en: A raw score of 0.6 doesn't mean a 60% chance of being a bot, so calibration maps scores to trustworthy probabilities and keeps action thresholds stable across model versions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw score] --> Cal[Calibration]
  Cal --> Prob[Usable probability]
  Prob --> T1[Demote threshold]
  Prob --> T2[Ban threshold]
  Prob --> Monitor[Version comparison]
options: 原始分数不等于真实概率，需要校准才可信
校准能让模型永远不出错
校准只对生成式 AI 模型有意义，判别式分类器用不上
校准会自动消除所有误伤
options_en: Raw scores are not true probabilities, so they need calibration.
Calibration guarantees the model is never wrong.
Calibration only matters for generative AI models, not for discriminative classifiers.
Calibration automatically eliminates all false positives.
q_en: Why does a bot model need calibration?
scenario_en: Old and new model versions both output 0.6, yet after the swap the ban threshold has to keep the same false-positive rate.
optionExplanations: 模型给出的 0.6 分不代表 60% 的真实概率，校准是把分数变成可信数值，这样封禁/降权的界线换模型版本也不会跳变。
校准只是让分数更可信，不改变模型本身的判别力，消不了错误。
校准适用于任何输出分数的分类器，判别式 bot 模型同样需要。
校准不改变判别能力本身，也就消除不了误伤。
optionExplanations_en: A raw score of 0.6 doesn't mean a 60% chance of being a bot; calibration maps scores into trustworthy probabilities so action thresholds stay stable across model versions.
Calibration only makes scores more trustworthy—it doesn't change the model's underlying discriminative power or errors.
Calibration applies to any score-producing classifier; a discriminative bot model needs it too.
Calibration doesn't change discriminative power, so it can't eliminate false positives either.

scenario: 验证集只有几千条可信标签，要把模型原始风险分映射成可直接比较的真实概率。
q: bot 模型常用的校准方法包括哪些？（多选）
why: 直方分箱简单直接，isotonic 更灵活但需要更多数据，Platt scaling 用两参数 sigmoid，对少量关键点更实用。
why_en: Histogram binning, isotonic regression, and Platt scaling are the three calibration approaches discussed, trading off simplicity against data requirements.
options: histogram binning
isotonic regression
Platt scaling
数据库分片（sharding）

termDefinitions.term: histogram binning / 直方分箱校准
termDefinitions.meaning: 把预测概率分到等宽区间，用每个区间的真实命中率做校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Histogram binning buckets predicted scores into equal-width bins and calibrates using each bin's observed accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 学习一个单调的分段常数映射，不假设固定函数形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isotonic regression learns a monotonic step-wise mapping without assuming a fixed function shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个两参数的 sigmoid 函数把原始分数映射为概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling fits a two-parameter sigmoid function to map raw scores into probabilities.

options_en: Histogram binning.
Isotonic regression.
Platt scaling.
Database sharding.
q_en: Which calibration methods are commonly used for bot models? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The validation set holds only a few thousand trusted labels, and raw risk scores must become comparable real probabilities.
optionExplanations: 把预测分数分到等宽区间，用每个区间的真实命中率做校准，简单直接。
学一个单调分段常数映射，比固定函数形式更灵活，但需要更多数据。
用两参数 sigmoid 拟合分数到概率，标签少也能用。
分片是数据库扩容手段，和分数校准毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Bucketing scores into equal-width bins and calibrating by each bin's observed hit rate is simple and direct.
Learning a monotonic step-wise mapping is more flexible than a fixed function shape, but needs more data.
Fitting a two-parameter sigmoid works even with few labels.
Sharding is a database-scaling technique, unrelated to score calibration.

q: 更适合的简单校准方法是什么？
why: Platt scaling 只拟合两个 sigmoid 参数，在人工标签有限、只关心几个关键阈值时比 isotonic 更容易落地。
why_en: Platt scaling is attractive with limited labels because it fits just two sigmoid parameters on a small holdout set, unlike more data-hungry methods like isotonic regression.
scenario: 人工标签很少，只关心少数几个动作阈值附近的校准精度。
options: Platt scaling
另外训练一个超大模型专门做校准
完全不做校准
只看模型输出的最大分数
whenOtherWins: 如果有大量校准数据且分数-概率关系很不规则，isotonic 可能更准。
tradeoff: Platt scaling 的少参数、易落地 vs isotonic 在数据充足时更灵活
options_en: Platt scaling.
Train an entirely separate huge model just for calibration.
Skip calibration entirely.
Just look at the maximum score the model outputs.
q_en: What simple calibration method is a better fit here?
scenario_en: Human labels are scarce, and you only care about calibration near a few action thresholds.
optionExplanations: 这套校准方法只有两个自由参数（一条 sigmoid 曲线），标签少、只盯几个动作阈值时，落地明显比 isotonic 轻松。
标签量根本撑不起再训练一个大模型。
不校准会让误伤率 <1% 这类 guardrail 失去意义。
只看最大分数解决不了把分数映射成概率这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: This method fits just two free parameters on one sigmoid curve, so with scarce labels and only a few thresholds to watch, it lands far more easily than isotonic regression.
The label volume can't support training an entirely separate large model.
Skipping calibration makes a guardrail like 'false positives under 1%' meaningless.
Looking only at the max score doesn't solve the score-to-probability mapping problem.

scenario: 监督模型对已知 bot 家族 precision 很高，但新脚本模式要几周才被标注覆盖。
q: 异常检测在 bot 系统中主要起什么作用？
why: 攻击者不断制造新模式，异常检测能提出可疑账号供调查和扩充训练集，但要结合业务影响，而不是抓所有「怪」账号。
why_en: Anomaly detection helps surface new bot patterns that supervised labels haven't covered yet, feeding investigation and future training data.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Features[Behavior graph features] --> Anom[Anomaly detector]
  Anom --> Queue[Review queue]
  Queue --> Human[Investigator]
  Human --> Labels[New labels]
  Labels --> Train[Supervised update]
options: 发现未被监督标签覆盖的新型 bot 模式
完全替代所有监督模型
自动确认可疑账号，让系统不再需要任何人工审核
只用于数据可视化展示
options_en: Surfacing new bot patterns not yet covered by supervised labels.
Fully replacing every supervised model.
Auto-confirm suspicious accounts so the system needs no human review at all.
Serving only as a data-visualization tool.
q_en: What role does anomaly detection mainly play in the bot system?
scenario_en: The supervised model has high precision on known bot families, but new script patterns take weeks to reach the label set.
optionExplanations: 异常检测的定位是发现监督标签还没覆盖到的新型 bot 模式，把可疑账号送进调查队列扩充训练集。
异常检测的结果仍要靠调查/监督验证，替代不了监督模型。
异常只是线索，仍要调查员人工确认，消除不了人工审核这一环。
异常检测服务于发现新模式，不只是拿来做可视化。
optionExplanations_en: Anomaly detection's job is surfacing new bot patterns supervised labels haven't covered yet, feeding suspicious accounts into the investigation queue to grow training data.
Anomaly output still needs investigation and supervised verification—it can't replace supervised models.
Anomalies are only leads that still need investigator confirmation—human review can't be removed.
Anomaly detection is for finding new patterns, not just a visualization tool.

scenario: 完全没有标签，只有 500M 账号的高维行为特征，需要一个便宜的方法先挑出可疑账号。
q: isolation forest 识别异常的核心直觉是什么？
why: 多棵随机树里，越少切分就能被孤立的点越异常；这是无监督方法，不需要标签，计算效率也较高。
why_en: Isolation forests score anomalies by how quickly random feature splits isolate a point, since anomalies are rare and different from the bulk of the data.
options: 异常点少且不同，更容易被快速孤立
异常点总是聚集在特征均值附近
必须先有标签才能训练
它只能处理文本类特征

termDefinitions.meaning: 用多棵随机切分树，越容易被孤立的点越可能是异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An isolation forest randomly splits the feature space with many trees, and points that get isolated in fewer splits are scored as more anomalous.

options_en: Anomalies are rare and different, so they get isolated faster.
Anomalies always cluster near the feature mean.
It must have labels before it can be trained.
It can only handle text-type features.
q_en: What is the core intuition behind isolation forest anomaly detection?
scenario_en: With no labels at all, just high-dimensional behavior features for 500M accounts, you need a cheap way to surface suspects.
optionExplanations: 异常点数量少、和大多数样本不同，随机切分树只需要更少的切分次数就能把它孤立出来。
异常点通常远离大多数数据，不是靠近均值聚集。
它是无监督方法，不需要标签就能训练。
它适用于任意数值/类别特征，不限于文本。
optionExplanations_en: Anomalies are rare and different from the bulk of the data, so random split trees need fewer cuts to isolate them.
Anomalies are usually far from the bulk of the data, not clustered near the mean.
It's unsupervised—no labels are needed to train it.
It works on any numeric or categorical feature, not just text.

q: 更适合先用的方法是什么？
why: isolation forest 对高维表格异常计算高效，不需要强分布假设，适合作为第一道筛查。
why_en: Isolation forests are efficient first-pass detectors for point anomalies in metadata and simple activity features, without assuming a particular data distribution.
scenario: 要快速筛出账号元数据和基础活动特征里的孤立异常点。
options: Isolation forest
大型 sequence autoencoder
人工逐个审查全量账号
只用一个多模态 LLM
whenOtherWins: 如果异常是复杂时间序列模式，autoencoder 或序列模型更可能捕捉。
tradeoff: isolation forest 的效率 vs autoencoder 对复杂序列模式的表达力
options_en: Isolation forest.
A large sequence autoencoder.
Manually reviewing every account one by one.
Using a single multimodal LLM.
q_en: What should you try first for this anomaly screen?
scenario_en: You need to cheaply screen isolated anomalies in account metadata and basic activity features.
optionExplanations: 对高维表格特征来说，这类基于随机切分树的方法计算高效、不用假设特定的数据分布，适合拿来做元数据和基础活动特征的第一道快速筛查。
autoencoder 更适合复杂序列模式，成本远超「快速筛查」这个目标所需。
人工逐个审查在数十亿账号规模下完全不可扩展。
多模态 LLM 面向内容理解，不适合结构化的元数据特征。
optionExplanations_en: Isolation forest is efficient on high-dimensional tabular features without needing a strong distribution assumption, making it a good first-pass screen for metadata and basic activity features.
Autoencoders suit complex sequential patterns better, at a compute cost far beyond what a quick screen needs.
Manually reviewing every account one by one doesn't scale at billions of accounts.
A multimodal LLM targets content understanding, a poor fit for structured metadata features.

scenario: 要抓的异常是事件序列的节奏不像人：每个单独特征都正常，只有组合和顺序不对。
q: autoencoder 做异常检测相比 isolation forest 的优势是什么？
why: autoencoder 学习压缩重构正常行为，重构误差大代表异常；比 isolation forest 更贵，也有学会重构一切的「病理」风险。
why_en: Autoencoders can capture complex sequential and contextual patterns that isolation forests miss, at the cost of higher compute and the risk of learning to reconstruct anomalies too well.
options: 能捕捉更复杂的序列/上下文重构模式
成本永远比 isolation forest 更低
不需要定义任何重构损失
不会把异常也重构出来
tradeoff: autoencoder 的复杂模式表达力 vs isolation forest 的计算效率

termDefinitions.meaning: 学习压缩再重建正常数据，重建误差大的账号更可能异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An autoencoder learns to compress and reconstruct normal data, and a large reconstruction error flags an account as anomalous.

options_en: It can capture more complex sequential/contextual reconstruction patterns.
It is unconditionally cheaper than an isolation forest.
It needs no reconstruction loss defined at all.
It never ends up reconstructing anomalies too.
q_en: What advantage does an autoencoder have over isolation forest for anomaly detection?
scenario_en: The anomaly you need is a non-human rhythm in the event sequence: every single feature looks normal, only the combination and order are off.
optionExplanations: 压缩再重建正常行为是自编码器的强项，能捕捉基于随机切分树的筛查方法抓不住的复杂序列/上下文模式，代价是更贵。
实际成本关系是反的：跑一次自编码器通常比那种基于随机切分树的筛查方法更贵。
设计重构损失恰恰是用好 autoencoder 的关键难点。
学会把异常也重构得很好，正是 autoencoder 的已知病理风险。
optionExplanations_en: An autoencoder learns to compress and reconstruct normal behavior, catching complex sequential/contextual patterns isolation forest misses—at higher cost.
The cost relationship is actually reversed—autoencoders usually cost more than isolation forests.
Designing the reconstruction loss is exactly the hard part of using an autoencoder well.
Learning to reconstruct anomalies too well is a known pathology risk for autoencoders.

q: 更合理的异常检测组合方式是什么？
why: 级联利用 isolation forest 的效率做第一道筛查，再用 autoencoder 深查复杂模式，融合分数按置信度组合两者结果。
why_en: A cascaded setup uses isolation forests for cheap first-pass screening and autoencoders for deeper checks on complex sequential patterns, then combines their scores.
scenario: 你既要便宜筛查，又要捕捉复杂的协调行为。
options: isolation forest 先筛，再深入复核
只用成本最贵的那一个深度模型直接跑遍全部账号，不做分层
只依赖纯随机抽样的方式来筛查异常账号
彻底放弃整个异常检测这一处理环节
whenOtherWins: 如果流量很小且序列异常是唯一目标，可以直接用 autoencoder。
tradeoff: 级联组合的成本效率 vs 单一方法各自的局限
options_en: Isolation forest screens first, then a deeper recheck.
Run only the single most expensive deep model over every account with no tiered screening.
Rely purely on a random-sampling approach alone to screen for anomalies.
Drop the entire anomaly-detection processing step altogether.
q_en: What is the better way to combine anomaly detectors?
scenario_en: You need cheap first-pass screening and still want to catch complex coordinated behavior.
optionExplanations: 用基于随机切分树的方法先便宜地筛一遍，再用更贵的自编码模型深查复杂协调模式，融合两者结果，兼顾成本和表达力。
对全量账号都跑最贵的深度模型，又不分层筛查，计算成本不可持续。
随机抽样不是针对性筛查，抓不住真正的异常。
放弃异常检测等于丢了发现新型未知 bot 模式的渠道。
optionExplanations_en: Screening cheaply with isolation forest first, then running autoencoders on the flagged subset for complex coordinated patterns, balances cost against expressive power.
Running the priciest deep model on all accounts without tiered screening is computationally unsustainable.
Random sampling isn't targeted screening, so it misses real anomalies.
Dropping anomaly detection entirely gives up the channel for finding new, unknown bot patterns.

scenario: 异常检测每天报出 5 万个行为怪异的账号，里面有大量小众爱好者和真实运营号。
q: 为什么不能把所有「行为异常」的账号都当成 bot？
why: 异常只是调查信号，还要结合 bot 造成的实际伤害和人工验证，否则会误伤行为独特但合法的边缘真实用户。
why_en: Anomaly scores are just a signal for investigation, not proof of harm, so they must be combined with evidence of actual bot impact before any action is taken.
options: 业务关心造成 harm 的异常，而非单纯「奇怪」
统计上行为异常的账号一定百分之百都是恶意的攻击行为
异常检测在实践中完全不会产生任何误报
行为奇怪的账号不需要任何形式的保护
options_en: The business cares about harmful anomalies, not just weirdness.
A statistically anomalous account is necessarily 100% malicious attack behavior.
Anomaly detection in practice never produces any false positive.
Accounts that behave unusually deserve no protection of any kind.
q_en: Why not treat every behaviorally unusual account as a bot?
scenario_en: Anomaly detection surfaces 50k weird-looking accounts a day, including plenty of niche hobbyists and genuine community managers.
optionExplanations: 业务真正关心的是造成伤害的异常，「行为奇怪」只是调查线索，还要结合实际伤害证据和人工验证才能定性。
很多小众爱好者和运营号在统计上也异常，异常不能直接等同恶意。
isolation forest 和 autoencoder 都会产生误报。
把奇怪等同该被处置，会误伤只是行为独特的合法边缘用户。
optionExplanations_en: The business really cares about anomalies that cause harm—'looking weird' is just an investigation lead that still needs harm evidence and human verification.
Many niche hobbyists and operations accounts look statistically anomalous too—anomalous doesn't equal malicious.
Both isolation forests and autoencoders produce false positives.
Treating unusual as disposable ends up harming legitimate users who simply behave differently.

scenario: 算力有限，只有一小部分高风险账号值得跑昂贵的重模型，最后还要落到执行动作。
q: 按合理顺序排列 bot 检测系统主流程。
why: 先构造多源特征，再用轻模型省计算，重模型处理高风险集合，最后由动作层按置信度执行。
why_en: The bot pipeline gathers multi-source features, filters cheaply with a light model, scores the suspicious subset deeply, then applies calibrated actions.
steps: 根据校准风险采取封禁/降权/限流
轻量模型筛出可疑账号
收集活动、图、内容和元数据特征
重图序列模型深度评分
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Features[Activity graph content meta] --> Light[Light model]
  Light --> Heavy[Heavy score]
  Heavy --> Cal[Calibration]
  Cal --> Actions[Ban demote limit]
q_en: Put the main bot-detection system flow in the right order.
scenario_en: Compute is limited, only a small high-risk slice deserves the expensive heavy model, and everything must end in an enforcement action.

scenario: 每周只有几百条可信标签，但无标签的图和事件流海量，模型还必须输出可信概率。
q: 按正确顺序排列 bot 主模型训练策略。
why: 预训练先学平台结构，融合后再定义监督目标，最后用稀缺高质量标签微调与校准。
why_en: The training path pretrains graph and sequence encoders, aligns them, applies an impact-weighted objective, and fine-tunes with trusted labels.
steps: 用调查员标签微调并校准
图侧和序列侧自监督预训练
融合图/序列表示并做对齐
设计影响加权 BCE
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Pre[Self-supervised pretrain] --> Fuse[Graph sequence fusion]
  Fuse --> Loss[Impact-weighted BCE]
  Loss --> Fine[Fine-tune labels]
  Fine --> Cal[Calibrate]
q_en: Put the main bot-model training strategy in the right order.
scenario_en: Only a few hundred trusted labels arrive weekly against a mountain of unlabeled graph and event data, and the model still owes calibrated probabilities.

scenario: 业务目标写成「最大化 bot 检出，误封率 <1%」。线上算力大半花在刷猫图的低危 bot 上，散播恶意链接的账号却排在后面。
scenario_en: The stated goal is "maximize bot detections with false positives under 1%". Most compute now goes to harmless cat-picture bots while malware-link accounts wait in line.
q: 「最大化检出 + 误封 <1%」这个目标漏掉了什么？
q_en: What does a "maximize detections, keep false positives under 1%" objective miss?
options: 没有按每个 bot 造成的危害加权
没有给误封设上限，用户会被误伤
把 recall 和 precision 混为一谈，无法调阈值
检出率在生产环境里根本无法测量
options_en: It does not weight bots by the harm each one causes.
It sets no cap on false positives, so real users get hit.
It confuses recall with precision, so no threshold can be tuned.
Detection rate simply cannot be measured in production.
optionExplanations: 检出数把猫图 bot 和恶意链接 bot 各记一分，资源就流向最好抓而不是最该抓的账号。
误封上限恰恰已经写在目标里了，这不是它的缺口。
recall 与 precision 定义不同但都可算，阈值照样能调。
检出数、误封率都能用抽样标注在线上估计出来。
optionExplanations_en: Counting detections scores a cat-picture bot and a malware bot alike, so effort flows to the easiest catches rather than the most harmful ones.
The false-positive cap is already written into this objective, so that is not the gap.
Recall and precision are defined differently but both computable; thresholds remain tunable.
Both detection counts and false-positive rates can be estimated online via sampled labeling.
why: 按检出个数计分等于假设所有 bot 危害相同，资源会向易抓的低危账号倾斜。改成影响加权的代价是要额外设计伤害度量。
why_en: Counting detections treats every bot as equally harmful, so resources drift toward easy low-harm accounts; moving to an impact-weighted objective costs you a harm metric you now have to design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把真实用户误判成 bot 的情况。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is a legitimate user wrongly classified as a bot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有真实 bot 中被模型抓到的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of all real bots that the model actually catches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型判为 bot 的账号中真的是 bot 的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of flagged accounts that really are bots.

scenario: 真实用户被判 bot 后账号被限流，唯一出路是申诉；调查员每周只能查数百个账号，而 bot 作者同样熟练地批量提交申诉。
scenario_en: A real user flagged as a bot gets restricted and can only appeal; investigators handle just a few hundred accounts a week, and bot authors file appeals just as fluently.
q: 误封一个真实用户的代价链是怎么走完的？
q_en: How does the full cost chain of one wrongful ban play out?
options: 限流→申诉→占用稀缺人工，bot 也会刷申诉
只损失该用户当天一次会话，之后会自动恢复
申诉全部由模型自动裁决，不消耗人工预算
误封只影响离线指标，不改变真实用户行为
options_en: Restriction, then appeal, then scarce human review that bots also flood.
The user loses one session that day and recovers automatically after.
Appeals are all decided by a model, consuming no human budget.
Wrongful bans only move offline metrics, not real user behavior.
optionExplanations: 被限流的用户只能排进人工申诉队列，而这条队列同时被 bot 作者占用。
限制不会自己解除，用户得主动申诉才可能恢复访问。
判定是否误封需要人工调查，这正是稀缺资源所在。
被误封的用户会流失参与度甚至离开平台，影响是真实的。
optionExplanations_en: A restricted user can only join the human appeals queue, which bot authors are crowding at the same time.
Restrictions do not lift themselves; the user must appeal to regain access.
Deciding whether a ban was wrong needs human investigation, which is exactly the scarce resource.
Wrongly banned users lose engagement and may leave the platform, so the impact is real.
why: 误封把用户推进申诉队列，而队列消耗的正是每周只有数百个名额的调查员预算，bot 作者还会一起刷。代价：误伤越多，能查真 bot 的人工越少。
why_en: A wrongful ban pushes the user into an appeals queue that burns the same few-hundred-per-week investigator budget bots also exploit, so every false positive steals review capacity from real bot hunting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被处置的账号请求人工复核处置结果的流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An appeal is the process where a restricted account asks a human to review the enforcement decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由调查员人工确认的、可信度最高的账号标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ground truth label is the high-trust verdict an investigator produces by hand.

scenario: bot 若不治理会占平台一半以上动作。有人据此主张：既然治理省下的算力多于治理花掉的算力，检测链路就不必再优化。
scenario_en: Left alone, bots would drive over half of all platform actions. Someone argues that since remediation saves more compute than it burns, the detection path needs no further optimization.
q: 「bot 治理净 compute 为正」该怎么正确使用？
q_en: How should the "bot remediation is compute-positive" argument actually be used?
options: 它说明治理值得做，但不豁免效率要求
它说明检测链路可以随意堆重模型
它说明检测应该只放在离线批处理里做
它说明可以对每条内容都跑一次大模型
options_en: It shows remediation is worth doing, but does not excuse inefficiency.
It means the detection path can freely stack heavy models.
It means detection belongs only in offline batch jobs.
It means you can run a large model over every single piece of content.
optionExplanations: 净收益为正只回答「要不要做」，预算问题还得单独算。
检测跑在注册、发帖等高频交互面前，堆重模型会直接推高延迟与成本。
离线批处理抓不住新注册账号的即时风险，实时触发是必须的。
逐条内容跑大模型的开销远超收益，也谈不上净正。
optionExplanations_en: Being net-positive answers whether to do it at all; the budget question still has to be sized separately.
Detection sits in front of registration and posting, so stacking heavy models directly raises latency and cost.
Offline batches miss the immediate risk from freshly registered accounts, so real-time triggering is required.
Running a large model per item costs far more than it returns, and would not stay net-positive.
why: 净收益为正是「值不值得做」的答案，不是「能花多少」的答案；检测挡在大量用户交互面前，算力仍是硬约束。代价：得靠级联和缓存把成本压下来。
why_en: Compute-positive answers whether remediation is worth doing, not how much it may spend; detection sits in front of huge interaction volume, so you still pay for cascading and caching to keep it affordable.
tradeoff: 治理的净算力收益为正 vs 检测链路自身的算力预算
whenOtherWins: 如果某类攻击伤害极高且只是短期爆发，可以临时接受更贵的检测链路先止血，事后再优化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量模型过滤，只把可疑账号交给重模型，节省大部分算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascading inference filters with a cheap model first and sends only suspicious accounts to the heavy model.

scenario: 平台已有一支低质内容治理团队。bot 团队想把「减少 spam 曝光」当作自己的主指标，但两套系统会对同一批内容采取动作。
scenario_en: The platform already has a low-quality-content team. The bot team wants "reduced spam impressions" as its headline metric, but both systems act on the same content.
q: bot 治理与低质内容治理的职责边界怎么划？
q_en: How should responsibility split between bot remediation and low-quality-content systems?
options: 并非所有低质内容来自 bot，指标要能归因
两套系统合并成一套，用同一个模型判
bot 系统放弃影响类指标，只看封禁数量
低质内容系统停用，全部交给 bot 系统处理
options_en: Not all low-quality content comes from bots, so the metric must be attributable.
Merge the two systems and judge everything with one model.
The bot system drops impact metrics and tracks ban counts only.
Retire the low-quality-content system and hand everything to bot detection.
optionExplanations: 真人也会发垃圾内容，spam 曝光下降未必是 bot 系统的功劳。
两者的信号源和处置手段不同，强行合并会让账号级证据被内容级判断淹没。
封禁数量会重新激励过度封禁，回到被否掉的目标上。
停掉内容侧治理会放过全部由真人产出的低质内容。
optionExplanations_en: Real humans post junk too, so a drop in spam impressions is not automatically the bot system's win.
The two use different signals and enforcement levers; merging drowns account-level evidence in content-level judgement.
Ban counts re-create the over-enforcement incentive that was already rejected.
Shutting down content moderation lets through all the low-quality content produced by real people.
why: 影响类指标最贴近用户体验，但 spam 曝光同时被两套系统改动，不做归因就分不清是谁的效果。代价：要额外设计能归因到账号来源的指标口径。
why_en: Impact metrics track user experience best, but two systems move spam impressions at once, so without attribution you cannot tell whose change worked — and building attributable metric definitions costs extra design.
tradeoff: 指标贴近用户体验 vs 指标能归因到本系统
whenOtherWins: 如果平台上低质内容几乎全部由 botnet 产出，两套系统合并确实能省掉重复建设。

termDefinitions.meaning: 垃圾内容被真实用户看到的次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spam impression is one view of junk content by a real user.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由同一作者协同操控的一大批 bot 账号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A botnet is a large set of bot accounts operated together by one author.

scenario: 非参数分支把已知 bot 的内容和账号放进 ANN 索引，命中近邻就判风险；为了跟上新模式，系统把自己判出的 bot 也自动写回索引。
scenario_en: The non-parametric branch indexes known bot content and accounts in an ANN store and flags whatever lands near them; to keep up with new patterns it writes its own verdicts back into the index.
q: 把系统自判结果自动写回近邻索引，会怎么一步步失效？
q_en: How does auto-writing the system's own verdicts back into the neighbor index fail, step by step?
options: 误判进索引→更多相似账号被判中→索引越滚越偏
索引体积不变，只是近邻查询延迟缓慢升高
索引会拒绝新写入，导致新 bot 模式全部漏检
近邻距离保持恒定，模型分数只会整体下降
options_en: A false positive enters the index, pulls in more similar accounts, and the index drifts further each round.
Index size stays flat and only neighbor-query latency creeps upward.
The index refuses new writes, so every new bot pattern goes undetected.
Neighbor distances stay constant and scores merely shift downward overall.
optionExplanations: 一个误判的良性账号成为「已知 bot」样本后，会把和它相似的良性账号一起拖下水。
索引会持续变大，问题也不在延迟而在内容被污染。
写回路径是开着的，失效恰恰来自写进去的东西不可信。
索引内容变了，近邻距离必然跟着变，分数也不是单向下降。
optionExplanations_en: Once a wrongly flagged benign account becomes a "known bot" exemplar, it drags accounts similar to it down with it.
The index keeps growing, and the problem is contaminated content rather than latency.
The write path is open; the failure comes precisely from writing untrustworthy entries into it.
Index contents change, so neighbor distances change too, and scores do not simply drift one way.
why: 索引里存的是「什么算 bot」的定义，写回自判结果就让误判自我复制，良性数据被越索引越多，形成 runaway 反馈循环。修法：ground truth 标签与系统标签分开存并按可信度加权。
why_en: The index defines what counts as a bot, so feeding it the system's own verdicts lets false positives replicate and pull benign data in — which is why investigator labels must be stored and weighted separately from system-generated ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索：在向量库里快速找出与查询最像的若干条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN, Approximate Nearest Neighbor search, quickly finds the entries in a vector store most similar to a query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不训练固定参数，直接用检索到的相似样本来判断的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-parametric method makes decisions by retrieving similar stored examples instead of learning fixed parameters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统输出被当成输入回喂，偏差被一轮轮放大的循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A runaway feedback loop is when a system's own output is fed back as input, amplifying its bias each round.

scenario: 当前这批 bot 靠固定文案模板露馅，换个模板就抓不到；下一代 bot 已经在用 LLM 现生成内容。
scenario_en: Today's bots give themselves away with fixed copy templates and vanish the moment they rotate templates; the next generation already generates posts with an LLM.
q: 特征集怎么组合才不会 bot 一改招就失灵？
q_en: How should the feature set be composed so it does not die the moment bots change tactics?
options: 易得信号抓当下，行为节奏类信号抗漂移
只保留当前命中率最高的那批模板特征
全部换成最抽象的特征，放弃易得信号
每次 bot 变招就把模型整体重训一遍
options_en: Keep easy wins for today's bots plus rhythm-based signals that survive adaptation.
Keep only the template features with the best current hit rate.
Replace everything with the most abstract features and drop the easy wins.
Retrain the whole model from scratch every time bots change tactics.
optionExplanations: 两类特征分别覆盖「现在能抓到」和「明年还管用」，缺一边都会塌。
模板特征命中率高但寿命短，攻击者一改文案就整批失效。
放弃易得信号会牺牲眼下的召回，低级 bot 会立刻回流。
重训解决不了特征本身已经不含信息的问题。
optionExplanations_en: The two kinds cover "catches bots today" and "still works next year"; drop either side and coverage collapses.
Template features hit hard but die young — one copy rewrite retires the whole batch.
Dropping easy wins sacrifices near-term recall and low-effort bots flood straight back.
Retraining cannot fix features that no longer carry any signal at all.
why: 易得特征命中快但攻击者一改就废，作息与反应时间这类节奏信号难伪造却更弱，所以两类要同时留在特征集里。代价：维护两套特征的成本和复杂度都翻倍。
why_en: Easy features hit fast but die when attackers adapt, while rhythm signals like sleep cycles are hard to fake yet individually weaker, so you carry both — and pay double the feature-maintenance cost.
tradeoff: 抓当下 bot 的易得信号 vs 抗对抗漂移的根本信号
whenOtherWins: 如果面对的是一次性、短周期的攻击活动，先上易得的模板特征止血，比追求长期稳健更划算。

termDefinitions.meaning: 攻击者持续调整手法，导致模型学到的分布随时间失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adversarial drift is attackers continuously changing tactics so the distribution a model learned stops holding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，可用来批量生成看起来自然的帖子内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LLM, or Large Language Model, can mass-produce posts that read as naturally written.

scenario: 序列模型要读约 200 个事件才出分，但平台有 5 亿日活、每人 1-2 次会话，不可能对每个动作都跑一遍。
scenario_en: The sequence model reads roughly 200 events before scoring, but with 500M daily active users at one to two sessions each, it cannot run on every single action.
q: 活动节奏信号在实时链路上该怎么落地？
q_en: How should activity-rhythm signals be delivered on the real-time path?
options: 用多时间窗的手工统计特征做折中
对每个动作都实时跑一遍序列模型
干脆放弃活动节奏这一整类信号
把序列模型换成更大的 transformer
options_en: Compromise with hand-engineered statistics over multiple time windows.
Run the full sequence model on every action in real time.
Drop the entire activity-rhythm signal family.
Swap the sequence model for a larger transformer.
optionExplanations: 间隔分布、方差、熵按小时/天/周各算一份，成本是几个聚合而不是一次前向。
算力预算撑不住，检测又挡在高频交互面前，延迟会直接外溢给用户。
节奏类信号恰恰是最难伪造的一类，放弃等于把最稳的证据丢掉。
换更大的模型让每次推理更贵，与「跑不起」这个约束正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Inter-event gaps, variance and entropy computed hourly, daily and weekly cost a few aggregations instead of a forward pass.
The compute budget cannot absorb it, and since detection gates high-frequency interactions the latency lands on users.
Rhythm signals are the hardest to fake, so dropping them throws away the most durable evidence.
A bigger model makes each inference more expensive, which is the opposite of the binding constraint.
why: 理想情况这些节奏由序列模型自己学，但它跑不到每个动作上；多窗口的统计量是可负担的替代。代价：手工特征会漏掉模型才能学到的组合模式。
why_en: Ideally the sequence model learns these rhythms itself, but it cannot run per action, so multi-window statistics are the affordable stand-in — at the cost of missing combinations only a learned model would find.
tradeoff: 序列模型学到的时序细节 vs 手工统计特征的算力成本
whenOtherWins: 账号已被轻量模型判为可疑、进入级联的重模型阶段时，跑完整序列模型是值得的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量一组行为分布有多不规则，太低说明动作过于规律。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entropy measures how irregular a behavior distribution is; very low entropy means suspiciously regular actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于自注意力的序列模型，表达力强但推理成本高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transformer is a self-attention sequence model with high expressiveness and high inference cost.

scenario: 一批 bot 共用少量代理 IP 和同一台服务器，登录节奏也和真人不同。你要从账号元数据里挑出认证模式这一组特征。
scenario_en: A bot batch shares a handful of proxy IPs and one machine, and its login rhythm does not look human. You are picking the authentication-pattern group out of account metadata.
q: 账号元数据里的认证模式特征包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which account-metadata features belong to the authentication-pattern group? (Select all that apply.)
options: 登录频率
设备多样性
地理位置一致性
帖子的语义多样性
options_en: Login frequency.
Device diversity.
Location consistency.
Semantic diversity across posts.
optionExplanations: 登录频率：脚本化的登录节奏过于规律或过密，暴露非人操作。
设备多样性：一台机器批量控号时，设备指纹会异常集中。
地理位置一致性：同一账号短时间跨地登录，说明它被程序共用。
语义多样性属于内容信号那一组，不由认证行为产生。
optionExplanations_en: Login frequency: scripted logins are too regular or too dense, exposing non-human operation.
Device diversity: when one machine drives many accounts, device fingerprints cluster abnormally.
Location consistency: the same account logging in from far apart within minutes means a program is sharing it.
Semantic diversity belongs to the content-signal group and is not produced by authentication behavior.
why: 认证类特征刻画的是「谁在什么机器上、从哪里登进来」，对低成本批量控号的 bot 特别有效。代价：高级攻击者用住宅代理和指纹伪装就能削弱它们。
why_en: Authentication features describe who logs in from which machine and where, which catches cheap mass-controlled bots — though residential proxies and fingerprint spoofing weaken them against sophisticated attackers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由浏览器、系统、硬件属性拼出的设备标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A device fingerprint is an identifier assembled from browser, OS and hardware attributes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中转服务器的地址，用来隐藏账号真实来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy IP is a relay server address used to hide where an account really connects from.

scenario: 检测系统已经在线跑了一段时间，每个账号都积累了一份与检测系统交互的历史，这份历史本身可以回喂模型。
scenario_en: The detection system has been live for a while, so every account has a history of interacting with it, and that history can itself be fed back as features.
q: 哪些实时行为信号可以当特征回喂 bot 模型？（多选）
q_en: Which real-time behavioral signals can be fed back as features to the bot model? (Select all that apply.)
options: 被各模型标记的历史次数
被标记之后行为的变化
申诉的频率与成功率
注册时填写的生日
options_en: How often the account has been flagged across models.
How behavior changes after being flagged.
Appeal frequency and success rate.
The birthday entered at registration.
optionExplanations: 跨模型的累计标记次数：把多个模型各自的弱信号叠成一条强证据。
标记后的行为突变：说明账号在主动适应检测规则。
申诉频率与成功率：高频提交但极少成功，本身就是可疑模式。
生日是注册时的静态资料字段，不是与检测系统交互产生的信号。
optionExplanations_en: Cumulative cross-model flag counts stack several weak per-model signals into one strong piece of evidence.
A behavior jump right after a flag shows the account is actively adapting to the rules.
Filing appeals constantly while almost never winning is itself a suspicious pattern.
Birthday is a static registration field, not a signal generated by interacting with detection.
why: 这些信号只有在系统上线运行后才存在，价值在于它们记录的是账号对检测本身的反应。代价：新注册账号完全没有这类特征，模型必须容忍缺失值。
why_en: These signals only exist once the system has been running, and their value is that they record how an account reacts to detection itself — the cost being that brand-new accounts have none, so the model must tolerate missing values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 账号申诉被判定为误封的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Appeal success rate is the share of an account's appeals that are ruled wrongful enforcement.

scenario: 一个账号被限流后 24 小时内，把整点固定的发帖间隔改成随机抖动，还换掉了设备指纹；真实用户被限流时不会这样反应。
scenario_en: Within a day of being restricted, an account switches from posting on the hour to randomized jitter and swaps its device fingerprint — not how a real restricted user reacts.
q: 这种「被标记后行为突变」最好怎么用？
q_en: What is the best use of a behavior jump right after an account gets flagged?
options: 当成规避信号，作为特征喂回模型
当成账号已改邪归正，调低风险分
忽略它，只看被标记之前的行为
直接据此永久封禁，不再经过模型
options_en: Treat it as an evasion signal and feed it back to the model as a feature.
Read it as the account reforming and lower its risk score.
Ignore it and score only on pre-flag behavior.
Permanently ban on this alone, bypassing the model.
optionExplanations: 规避动作本身携带信息：只有知道自己被检测的一方才会这样调整。
风险分调低正中攻击者下怀，改一次参数就能洗白。
只看标记前行为等于自愿丢掉一整类对抗性证据。
单一信号直接触发永久处置，会绕过校准好的误封上限。
optionExplanations_en: The evasion move carries information: only someone who knows they were detected adjusts this way.
Lowering the score is exactly what the attacker wants — one parameter change and the account is clean.
Scoring only pre-flag behavior voluntarily discards an entire class of adversarial evidence.
Letting one signal trigger permanent enforcement bypasses the calibrated false-positive guardrail.
why: bot 的规避尝试反而证明它在适应检测，于是攻击者每躲一次就留下一条新证据，形成对抗反馈循环。代价：真实用户的正常行为变化会被误读，需要其他信号交叉验证。
why_en: A bot's evasion attempt proves it is adapting to detection, so every dodge leaves a fresh signal behind — the cost is that ordinary behavior changes by real users can be misread, so it needs corroborating signals.
tradeoff: 把规避动作读成证据 vs 读成账号行为改善
whenOtherWins: 如果限流本身来自模型误判，真实用户随之减少发帖就不该算规避，要结合申诉结果一起判断。

termDefinitions.meaning: 账号在察觉被检测后为躲避处置而做出的行为改变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An evasion pattern is how an account changes behavior once it senses it has been detected.

termDefinitions.meaning: 攻击者的躲避动作被系统采集成新的检测信号的循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An adversarial feedback loop is when the attacker's dodging itself becomes a new detection signal.

scenario: 面试官问你是否一开始就把图模型、序列模型、异常检测全部端上来。线上攻击手法每个季度都在变，你也说不准下一个缺口在哪。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether you would ship the graph model, sequence model and anomaly detection all at once. Attack tactics rotate every quarter and the next gap is unknown.
q: bot 检测的多层防御该怎么建立起来？
q_en: How should the layered defense of a bot-detection system be built up?
options: 先上简单一层，按真实攻击暴露的缺口加层
一次性把全部层级都设计完，再统一上线交付
只保留最强的那一层，其余全部删掉
每发现一种新攻击就把整套系统重写
options_en: Start with one simple layer and add layers where real attacks expose gaps.
Design every single layer up front, then launch them all together.
Keep only the single strongest layer and delete the rest.
Rewrite the whole system each time a new attack appears.
optionExplanations: 安全系统是被真实攻击喂出来的，先简单再补，才补在真的缺口上。
提前设计的层往往挡的是想象中的攻击，上线后仍要重做。
只留一层就没有安全网，这层被绕过时整套防线一起失守。
重写成本极高，而攻击手法的变化频率远高于系统能重写的频率。
optionExplanations_en: Security systems are grown by real attacks; starting simple and patching afterwards puts layers where the gaps truly are.
Layers designed up front tend to block imagined attacks and still get reworked after launch.
A single layer leaves no safety net, so the whole defense falls the moment it is bypassed.
Rewrites are expensive, and tactics change far faster than a system can be rewritten.
why: 攻击手法一直在变，提前设计的层挡不到真实缺口；多层的价值在于互为安全网，任何一层被绕过还有下一层接着。代价：层数越多，运维负担与推理延迟越高。
why_en: Tactics keep shifting so pre-designed layers rarely sit where the real gaps are; layers earn their keep as each other's safety net, at the price of more operational burden and inference latency.
tradeoff: 一次把防御设计到位 vs 按真实攻击有机分层生长
whenOtherWins: 如果面对的是已知成熟攻击面（比如批量注册），直接照搬业界成型的多层方案比从零试错更快。

termDefinitions.term: defense in depth / 纵深防御
termDefinitions.meaning: 安全原则：叠多层独立防线，任一层被突破仍有后续层兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Defense in depth is the security principle of stacking independent layers so a breach of one still meets another.

scenario: 图分支用 GraphSAGE 聚合 2 跳邻域。有人主张简化实现：把 follow 边和 reply 边当成同一种边一起聚合。
scenario_en: The graph branch aggregates a two-hop neighborhood with GraphSAGE. Someone proposes simplifying it by aggregating follow edges and reply edges as a single edge type.
q: 把 follow 边和 reply 边一视同仁会怎么坏事？
q_en: What breaks if follow edges and reply edges are aggregated as the same relation?
options: 自动关注上千人的账号会长得像社区核心
邻居采样会失效，fan-out 无法再封顶
模型会退化成 transductive，无法嵌入新节点
2 跳邻域会自动扩张成一次全图遍历
options_en: An account that auto-follows thousands starts to look like a well-connected community hub.
Neighbor sampling breaks and fan-out can no longer be capped.
The model degrades to transductive and cannot embed new nodes.
The two-hop neighborhood silently expands into a full graph traversal.
optionExplanations: follow 边可以单方面批量制造，堆够数量就把 spammer 的连接度顶上去了。
邻居采样按数量截断，和边类型区不区分无关。
GraphSAGE 的归纳性来自邻域聚合函数，不由边权决定。
跳数上限仍是 2，边类型合并不会改变遍历深度。
optionExplanations_en: Follow edges can be manufactured unilaterally in bulk, so enough of them push a spammer's connectivity right up.
Neighbor sampling truncates by count and is unaffected by whether edge types are distinguished.
GraphSAGE's inductive property comes from its aggregation function, not from edge weights.
The hop limit is still two; merging edge types does not change traversal depth.
why: follow 是单方面动作，reply 需要对方参与，可信度天然不同；一视同仁聚合时上千条自动关注就被读成社区核心的特征。relation-specific weights 让两类边分开加权。
why_en: A follow is unilateral while a reply needs the other side to engage, so relation-specific weights let GraphSAGE discount auto-follows instead of reading thousands of them as community centrality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归纳式图神经网络，靠采样邻居并聚合来生成节点表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphSAGE is an inductive graph neural network that embeds a node by sampling and aggregating its neighbors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按边的类型使用不同的聚合权重，让不同关系贡献不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relation-specific weights give each edge type its own aggregation weight so different relations contribute differently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只能处理训练时见过的节点、新节点需重训的图模型性质。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transductive means the model only handles nodes seen during training and needs retraining for new ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个节点连接的邻居数量，名人账号扇出极大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is how many neighbors a node has, and celebrity accounts have enormous fan-out.

scenario: 图编码器和序列编码器各自自监督预训练完毕，中间的 cross-attention 融合层还没训练，而调查员标签一条都还没舍得用。
scenario_en: The graph and sequence encoders finished self-supervised pretraining, the cross-attention fusion layer is untrained, and not a single investigator label has been spent yet.
q: 融合层的无标签对齐预训练目标是什么？
q_en: What is the objective of the label-free alignment pass over the fusion layer?
options: 同账号的两路表示靠近，不同账号推开
让两路表示完全相同，抹掉分支差异
直接用二分类交叉熵，标签取系统判定结果
冻结融合层，等到微调阶段再训练它
options_en: Pull the two views of one account together and push different accounts apart.
Force the two views to be identical, erasing branch differences.
Train binary cross-entropy directly, using system verdicts as labels.
Freeze the fusion layer and train it only during fine-tuning.
optionExplanations: 奖励一致、惩罚混淆，融合层就学会「这两路说的是同一个账号」。
两路完全相同就没有互补信息了，cross-attention 也失去意义。
拿系统判定当标签会把模型自身的偏差固化进融合层。
不训练融合层，稀缺的调查员标签就得同时承担对齐和判别两件事。
optionExplanations_en: Rewarding agreement and punishing confusion teaches the layer that both views describe one account.
If both views became identical there would be no complementary information left for cross-attention to use.
Using system verdicts as labels bakes the model's own bias into the fusion layer.
Skipping this pass makes the scarce investigator labels do alignment and discrimination at the same time.
why: 对齐先让融合层学会「同一个账号的图视角与时序视角是同一件事」，完全不消耗标签。代价：它只学到一致性，判别 bot 仍要靠后续的有标签微调和校准。
why_en: The alignment pass teaches the fusion layer that an account's graph view and timeline view describe the same entity without spending a label, but it only learns consistency — telling bots apart still needs supervised fine-tuning and calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一路表示去查询另一路表示的注意力机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-attention lets one representation query another so the two branches can inform each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把账号或事件压成的稠密向量表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector that represents an account or an event.

scenario: 账号收到用户举报需要重新评估。图 embedding 要拉 2 跳邻域重算，代价很高，但这个账号这周的关注关系几乎没有变动。
scenario_en: A user report triggers re-evaluation. Recomputing the graph embedding means pulling a two-hop neighborhood, which is expensive, yet this account's connections barely moved this week.
q: 重新触发评估时怎么压住重算成本？
q_en: How do you keep the cost of a re-triggered evaluation down?
options: 复用缓存的图 embedding，只刷新行为特征
两侧特征全部重算一遍，保证绝对新鲜
跳过这次评估，等每日批处理统一算
只重算图 embedding，行为特征沿用缓存
options_en: Reuse the cached graph embedding and refresh only the behavioral features.
Recompute both sides in full to guarantee absolute freshness.
Skip this evaluation and let the daily batch job handle it.
Recompute only the graph embedding and reuse cached behavioral features.
optionExplanations: 贵的那一半没变就不必重算，便宜的那一半才需要跟上最新动作。
全量重算把最贵的一步做成了每次触发的固定开销。
举报正是需要快速响应的信号，压到次日会放任伤害继续累积。
正好搞反了：变化快的是行为特征，图邻域反而相对稳定。
optionExplanations_en: The expensive half has not changed, so only the cheap half needs to catch up with recent actions.
Full recomputation turns the most expensive step into a fixed cost on every trigger.
A report is exactly the signal that needs a fast response; deferring it lets harm keep accumulating.
This inverts the picture: behavioral features move fast while the graph neighborhood is comparatively stable.
why: 行为特征几小时就变，图 embedding 只在邻域变动时才会变，所以邻域没明显变化时复用缓存能让重触发变得廉价。代价：邻域悄悄变化时用到的是过期的图表示。
why_en: Behavioral features shift within hours while a graph embedding only moves when the neighborhood does, so reusing the cache makes re-triggering cheap — at the risk of scoring on a stale graph view when the neighborhood quietly changed.
tradeoff: 重算带来的新鲜度 vs 图 embedding 的计算成本
whenOtherWins: 如果账号刚刚批量关注了一大批新账号，邻域已经变了，就必须重算图 embedding。

termDefinitions.meaning: 从目标节点出发最多走 k 步能到达的所有节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-hop neighborhood is every node reachable within k steps from the target node.

scenario: 图分支上线三个月，团队想知道「靠图连接」到底比单账号特征多抓到了什么，但 PR-AUC 只给出一个混在一起的总分。
scenario_en: Three months after the graph branch shipped, the team wants to know what graph connectivity actually added over per-account features, but PR-AUC returns one blended number.
q: 哪个离线诊断指标能回答这个问题？
q_en: Which offline diagnostic metric answers that question?
options: Network Coverage：靠图连接检出的 bot 簇比例
Early Detection Rate：24 小时内检出的比例
Precision@Recall90：操作点上的精确率
PR-AUC：precision-recall 曲线下的面积
options_en: Network Coverage: the share of bot clusters caught through graph connections.
Early Detection Rate: the share of bots caught within 24 hours.
Precision@Recall90: precision at the enforcement operating point.
PR-AUC: the area under the precision-recall curve.
optionExplanations: 它直接以「簇」为单位统计，正好对应协同 botnet 这个图分支要解决的问题。
它衡量的是抓得多早，与信号来自哪一路无关。
它对齐自动处置的阈值，回答的是能不能上线的问题。
它反映整体判别力，恰恰把各路信号的贡献混在了一起。
optionExplanations_en: It counts in clusters, which maps exactly onto the coordinated-botnet problem the graph branch exists to solve.
It measures how early bots are caught, regardless of which signal found them.
It aligns with the enforcement threshold and answers whether a model is shippable.
It reports overall discriminative power, which is precisely what blends the signal contributions together.
why: 总体指标把所有信号混成一个分数，答不出「图这一路值不值」；Network Coverage 直接度量有多少 bot 簇是通过图连接抓到的。代价：它只是诊断指标，不能单独决定上不上线。
why_en: Aggregate metrics blend every signal into one score and cannot say whether the graph branch earns its cost, while Network Coverage counts bot clusters found through graph links — but it is diagnostic only and cannot decide a launch alone.
tradeoff: 总体判别力指标 vs 定位单一信号贡献的诊断指标
whenOtherWins: 如果要判断模型整体是否变好、能不能上线，PR-AUC 这类总体指标才是该看的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线诊断指标：有多少比例的 bot 簇是靠图连接被检出的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Network Coverage is a diagnostic metric for the percentage of bot clusters detected through graph connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall 曲线下的面积，类别不平衡时比 ROC-AUC 更可靠。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PR-AUC, the area under the precision-recall curve, is more reliable than ROC-AUC under class imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: bot 在开始活动后 24 小时内被检出的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Early Detection Rate is the fraction of bots caught within their first 24 hours of activity.

scenario: 模型把「设备多样性低 + 地理位置跳变」当作强信号，而某些地区的用户大量共用网吧设备和运营商代理，整体误封率仍稳在 1% 以下。
scenario_en: The model leans on low device diversity plus location jumps, yet in some regions users share internet-cafe machines and carrier proxies — while the overall false-positive rate still reads under 1%.
q: 评估里必须加哪一项才能发现这个问题？
q_en: What must the evaluation add in order to surface this problem?
options: 按人群和地域分层，逐层看误封率
只确认整体误封率低于 1% 的红线
加大红队模拟规避样本在测试集中的占比
把验证集改成按时间先后分层切分
options_en: Break false-positive rate down by demographic and geography.
Just confirm the overall false-positive rate stays under the 1% line.
Raise the share of red-team evasion samples in the test set.
Re-split the validation set chronologically by time.
optionExplanations: 把误封率拆到人群和地域上，才看得见某个社群单独承担了全部配额。
总体数字达标恰恰是问题所在，它把局部集中的伤害平均掉了。
红队测的是模型挡不挡得住新攻击，不回答谁被误伤。
时间分层针对的是对抗漂移，与人群间的分布差异无关。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting the false-positive rate by community and region is what reveals that one group absorbs the entire quota.
The aggregate number passing is exactly the problem — it averages away harm that is concentrated locally.
Red-teaming tests whether the model withstands new attacks, not who gets wrongly hit.
Time-based splits target adversarial drift, not differences in distribution across populations.
why: 1% 的整体误封上限完全可以由某一个社群独自承担，聚合数字看不出来；按人群和地域分层评估才能暴露不成比例的误伤。代价：分层后每层样本变少，结论噪声更大。
why_en: A single community can absorb the entire 1% false-positive budget without the aggregate number moving, so you evaluate per demographic and geography — accepting that each slice has fewer samples and noisier conclusions.
tradeoff: 整体误封率达标 vs 各人群误封率均衡
whenOtherWins: 如果关心的是模型对未来新型 bot 的稳健性，按时间分层的验证集才是对的工具。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按人群、地域等切片检查模型表现是否存在系统性偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fairness evaluation checks model performance across demographic and geographic slices for systematic bias.

scenario: 模型在历史 bot 样本上表现很好，但攻击者每季度换一次手法，等新样本进测试集时那波攻击早已跑完。
scenario_en: The model scores well on historical bot samples, but attackers rotate tactics quarterly and by the time new samples reach the test set that wave is long over.
q: 怎么在新攻击到来之前评估模型的对抗鲁棒性？
