每条都新建连接直接放大了获取开销，跟批处理想省的成本正好反着来。
池设为 0 等于没有连接可用，写入直接没法进行。
关掉错误处理跟吞吐无关，只会让失败悄悄发生没人发现。
optionExplanations_en: Right — one acquire does a batch's worth of writes, amortizing 1000 acquire/release cycles down to a handful, boosting throughput.
Creating a new connection per record inflates the very acquire overhead batching is meant to reduce.
Setting the pool size to 0 leaves no connection available at all, so writes simply can't happen.
Disabling error handling has nothing to do with throughput; it just lets failures happen silently.

scenario: 固定 10 个连接在高峰不够、低峰浪费；团队愿意接受调参复杂度。
scenario_en: A fixed pool of 10 connections is too small at peak and wasteful off peak, and the team accepts extra tuning complexity.
q: 可以考虑哪种池策略？
q_en: What pool strategy could you consider?
options: adaptive sizing，根据利用率动态扩缩池
把连接池容量永远固定设置为 1 个连接
无界地不断创建新的数据库连接，完全不设任何数量上限
把要不要创建连接的决定权完全交给每一个请求自己
why: 自适应池根据需求增长和空闲收缩，能改善利用率。代价是调参困难，增长过快会压垮下游。
why_en: Adaptive pool sizing can improve utilization by growing under load and shrinking when idle, but it is harder to tune safely.
whenOtherWins: 面试基础实现应先用固定有界池，简单且可控。
options_en: Adaptive sizing that grows and shrinks the pool with utilization.
Permanently fix the connection pool's capacity at exactly 1 connection.
Keep creating new database connections without bound, with no cap on the count at all.
Hand the decision of whether to create a connection entirely over to each individual request.
tradeoff: 自适应池（贴合负载但调参复杂）vs 固定有界池（简单可控但峰值/低谷都不是最优）

termDefinitions.term: 自适应池 / adaptive pool sizing
termDefinitions.meaning: 根据当前利用率动态增加或收缩池的容量，而不是固定一个数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adaptive pool sizing grows or shrinks a pool's capacity based on current utilization instead of keeping it fixed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先创建并复用一组数据库连接对象，请求借用后归还，避免每次都重新建立昂贵连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool pre-creates a set of reusable database connection objects that requests borrow and return, avoiding the cost of establishing a new connection every time.

optionExplanations: 对，池随利用率增长而扩、空闲时收缩，能贴合负载起伏，代价是调参更复杂。
固定为 1 个连接在高峰会严重不够用，跟“想更好利用峰谷”这个诉求正好相反。
无界创建放弃了容量控制，增长过快反而会直接压垮下游数据库。
把决定权丢给每个请求会让池容量完全不可控，也就没有池化这回事了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the pool grows under load and shrinks when idle, tracking demand, at the cost of harder tuning.
Fixing the pool at exactly 1 connection would be badly undersized at peak, the opposite of improving utilization.
Unbounded creation abandons capacity control entirely and can slam the downstream database if it grows too fast.
Letting each request decide for itself makes pool size completely uncontrolled, which defeats pooling altogether.

q: 把稀缺性问题的工具选择链排好：
q_en: Put the scarcity-tool selection chain in order:
steps: 如果需要发放具体可复用对象，用 BlockingQueue 资源池
先判断限制的是操作个数、资源单位还是对象实例
如果限制同时运行数量，用 semaphore
如果操作消耗量不同，用许可代表资源单位
why: 稀缺性先看“缺的是什么”。许可适合数量或单位预算，队列适合具体对象复用。
why_en: Scarcity tool choice starts by identifying whether the scarce thing is operation slots, resource units, or reusable objects.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["need to cap concurrent use"] --> B{"resource reused?"}
  B -- no --> C["semaphore"]
  B -- yes --> D["resource pool"]
  D --> E["borrow, validate, return"]
tradeoff: 许可类工具（信号量，数量/单位预算）vs 对象池（阻塞队列，具体可复用对象）

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 拿到许可就减一，release 归还许可就加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads can run a section of code at once; acquire decrements the count and release increments it back, and the next acquire blocks once the count hits zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取（get/take）时如果队列为空会让线程等待，常用来同时充当“可用对象集合”和“等待机制”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking queue makes a get or take call wait when the queue is empty, so it doubles as both the set of available objects and the waiting mechanism.

q: 稀缺性设计的常见坑有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common pitfalls in scarcity design? (multi-select)
scenario: 压测跑到第 20 分钟，内存持续增长且部分请求永远不返回，要挑出制造这种故障的写法。
scenario_en: Twenty minutes into a load test memory keeps growing and some requests never return; pick the practices that cause this.
options: 忘记 release/归还资源
使用无界队列或无界池
请求路径无限等待资源
所有获取都设置合理超时并处理失败
why: 前三个会导致容量泄漏、OOM 或用户超时。合理超时和失败处理是修复方向。
why_en: Scarcity bugs usually come from leaked permits, unbounded queues, and unbounded waiting on request paths.
options_en: Forgetting to release or return the resource.
Using an unbounded queue or unbounded pool.
Waiting forever for a resource on the request path.
Setting a reasonable timeout on every acquire and handling failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有设置容量上限的队列，put 操作永远不会因为满而阻塞，可能无限增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unbounded queue has no capacity cap, so a put call never blocks for being full and the queue can keep growing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 进程或系统可用内存耗尽导致的错误，无界队列或无界池是常见诱因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOM, or Out Of Memory, is the failure when available memory runs out, and an unbounded queue or pool is a common cause.

optionExplanations: 忘记归还会让容量只减不增，挡不住的就是池慢慢被吃空的风险。
无界队列/池没有容量刹车，挡不住的是内存被无限占用直到 OOM 的风险。
请求路径无限等待挡不住线程被慢资源永久占用、用户早已放弃的风险。
这条恰恰是修复方向而不是坑：合理超时加失败处理正是用来防上面三个问题的。
optionExplanations_en: Forgetting to release only shrinks capacity, the risk it fails to guard against is the pool slowly draining to nothing.
An unbounded queue or pool has no capacity brake, the risk it fails to guard against is memory growing until OOM.
Waiting forever on the request path fails to guard against threads staying stuck on a slow resource the user already gave up on.
This one is the fix, not the pitfall — reasonable timeouts and failure handling are exactly what prevents the other three.

scenario: 资源竞争激烈，业务要求等待更久的请求优先拿到资源，即使吞吐略降也可以。
scenario_en: Resource contention is high, and the business wants older waiters to get the resource first even if throughput drops slightly.
q: 应关注什么特性？
q_en: What property should you pay attention to?
options: 公平/FIFO 等待策略
无界队列
随机释放许可
直接删除资源上限让请求随便进
why: 公平策略减少饥饿，通常以吞吐为代价。只有业务真的要求时才启用严格公平。
why_en: Fair or FIFO waiting can reduce starvation under contention, usually at some throughput cost.
whenOtherWins: 普通连接池大多近似公平就够，优先保持实现简单和吞吐稳定。
options_en: A fair or FIFO waiting policy.
An unbounded queue.
Releasing permits in random order.
Just remove the resource cap and let requests in freely.
tradeoff: 严格公平 FIFO（防止饥饿，吞吐通常下降）vs 近似公平（吞吐更好，可能有少量饥饿风险）

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：等待队列按到达顺序被服务，不允许后来者插队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO, or First In First Out, means waiters are served strictly in the order they arrived.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有设置容量上限的队列，put 操作永远不会因为满而阻塞，可能无限增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unbounded queue has no capacity cap, so a put call never blocks for being full and the queue can keep growing.

optionExplanations: 对，公平/FIFO 让等待更久的请求优先拿到资源，正好满足业务对饥饿的顾虑，代价是吞吐略降。
队列有界无界跟谁先拿到资源没关系，不能解决“等待更久的人优先”这个诉求。
随机释放许可反而会让等待最久的请求继续可能排不上，跟公平背道而驰。
删掉资源上限会让容量失控，不会让老等待者优先拿到资源。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a fair or FIFO policy serves the longest-waiting requester first, exactly what the business wants, at some throughput cost.
Whether the queue is bounded or not has nothing to do with who gets served first; it doesn't address starvation.
Releasing permits in random order can still leave the longest waiter unserved, the opposite of fairness.
Removing the resource cap loses capacity control; it does nothing to prioritize the oldest waiter.

q: 补全信号量口诀：
q_en: Complete the semaphore rule of thumb:
text: 信号量解决“最多同时 {{N}} 个操作”；线程进入前 {{acquire}}，结束后必须在 finally 或等价结构里 {{release}}。
why: 这句话覆盖了信号量的容量语义和最重要的泄漏防线。
why_en: A semaphore caps concurrent operations by acquiring before work and releasing afterward, preferably in a finally-like construct.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 拿到许可就减一，release 归还许可就加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads can run a section of code at once; acquire decrements the count and release increments it back, and the next acquire blocks once the count hits zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论 try 块是否抛出异常都会执行的代码块，常用来确保资源一定被释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finally block always runs whether or not the try block threw an exception, which is how code guarantees a resource is actually released.

q: 补全资源池口诀：
q_en: Complete the resource-pool rule of thumb:
text: 当线程需要拿到具体的可复用对象时，用 {{BlockingQueue}} 保存可用对象；{{get/take}} 借出，{{put}} 归还。
why: 资源池不是只数许可，而是管理对象生命周期。队列天然表达“没有可用对象就等”。
why_en: A resource pool uses a blocking queue to hand out concrete reusable objects and take them back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取（get/take）时如果队列为空会让线程等待，常用来同时充当“可用对象集合”和“等待机制”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking queue makes a get or take call wait when the queue is empty, so it doubles as both the set of available objects and the waiting mechanism.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先创建并复用一组数据库连接对象，请求借用后归还，避免每次都重新建立昂贵连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool pre-creates a set of reusable database connection objects that requests borrow and return, avoiding the cost of establishing a new connection every time.

scenario: 服务线程在等待资源时已经接近客户端超时；继续等可能让用户先断开但线程还占着。
scenario_en: A service thread is already close to the client timeout while waiting for a resource; if it keeps waiting, the user may disconnect while the thread remains occupied.
q: 更健康的行为是什么？
q_en: What is the healthier behavior?
options: 在小于客户端超时的边界内失败并释放请求线程
继续无限期地阻塞等待，直到资源终于重新出现为止
不设任何上限地创建新资源来救急
悄悄吞掉错误并假装请求已经成功
why: 请求路径要把过载转成明确失败，而不是让线程池被等待耗尽。超时应早于上游超时。
why_en: Request paths should fail before upstream timeouts so threads are not stuck waiting for resources the user has already given up on.
whenOtherWins: 后台批处理没有用户等待时，可以选择更长等待或排队。
options_en: Fail within a bound smaller than the client timeout and free the request thread.
Keep blocking indefinitely, with no bound, until the resource finally reappears.
Create brand-new resources without any cap at all just to relieve the pressure.
Quietly swallow the error and pretend the request actually succeeded.
tradeoff: 请求路径快速失败（保护线程和用户体验）vs 无限等待（用户已放弃，线程仍占用）

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器暂时无法处理请求的标准状态码，用来告诉客户端“稍后重试”而不是让它一直挂着等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable is the standard status code that tells a client to retry later instead of hanging indefinitely.

optionExplanations: 对，在客户端超时之前主动失败并放线程，过载变成一个明确错误，而不是线程被耗尽。
继续无限等待只会让线程卡在用户早已断开的请求上，白白占着资源。
无上限创建资源绕开了容量约束，高负载下反而会拖垮下游。
吞掉错误假装成功会让调用方以为操作成功了，其实数据可能根本没处理。
optionExplanations_en: Right — failing before the client timeout and freeing the thread turns overload into an explicit error instead of a stuck thread.
Waiting indefinitely just leaves the thread stuck on a request the user has probably already abandoned.
Creating resources without any cap sidesteps the constraint entirely and can drag down the downstream system under load.
Swallowing the error and pretending success tells the caller it worked when the operation may never have actually happened.

q: “最多 5 个下载同时进行”和“两个线程不能同时占同一个座位”的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between "at most 5 downloads at once" and "two threads cannot take the same seat"?
scenario: 订票系统既要把并发导出报表压到 5 个，又要保证同一个座位不会被两个用户同时占住。
scenario_en: A ticketing system caps concurrent report downloads at 5 while guaranteeing one seat is never held by two users at once.
options: 前者是容量限制，后者是共享状态正确性
两者都只需观察者模式
前者根本不能阻塞，后者则根本不能加锁
两者完全相同
why: 下载限制关心同时运行数，信号量可解。座位问题关心 seat owner 不变量，锁住检查和写入更关键。
why_en: A download cap is a scarcity capacity problem, while double booking is a correctness invariant problem.
options_en: The former is a capacity limit; the latter is shared-state correctness.
Both only need the Observer pattern.
The former can never block; the latter can never use a lock.
They are exactly the same thing.
tradeoff: 容量限制（信号量/池够不够用）vs 正确性不变量（锁保护共享状态不被破坏）

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种通知订阅者的设计模式：状态变化时通知所有监听者，跟限制并发数量无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern notifies subscribed listeners when state changes, and it has nothing to do with capping concurrency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持成立的约束，比如“一个座位最多属于一个订单”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a constraint that must hold at every point in time, such as a seat belonging to at most one order.

optionExplanations: 对，下载数是容量够不够的问题；座位不能重复占用是共享状态的正确性不变量，两者本质不同。
Observer 负责通知订阅者状态变化，既解决不了容量限制，也保证不了座位不被重复占用。
下载限制常靠信号量阻塞等待实现；座位问题恰恰需要锁住检查和写入这段临界区。
两者关注点完全不同：一个是数量够不够，一个是状态会不会被写坏。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the download cap is a capacity question; the seat rule is a correctness invariant on shared state, fundamentally different.
Observer just notifies subscribers of state changes; it solves neither a capacity cap nor a no-double-booking invariant.
Download limits commonly block via a semaphore; the seat problem is exactly where locking the check-and-write matters.
The two concerns are entirely different: one is about having enough capacity, the other about not corrupting shared state.

scenario: 面试官问“为什么不用 semaphore 实现连接池？”
scenario_en: The interviewer asks, "Why not implement the connection pool with only a semaphore?"
q: 最好的回答是什么？
q_en: What is the best answer?
options: semaphore 只能限制数量，还需要某处存放并发放 Connection 对象
semaphore 本身不会阻塞线程等待，所以线程只能不停地忙等直到许可可用为止
semaphore 会自动帮你创建并管理好数据库连接对象本身，不需要额外代码
连接池根本不需要设置任何容量上限，底层队列可以无限增长也完全没关系
why: 连接池问题有两层：容量上限和对象分发。阻塞队列同时保存可用连接并处理空池等待。
why_en: A semaphore can cap usage but does not store or hand out the actual connection objects.
whenOtherWins: 如果每次操作不需要具体对象，只需要并发许可，semaphore 就足够。
options_en: A semaphore only caps a count; you still need somewhere to store and hand out the actual Connection objects.
A semaphore itself never blocks a thread to wait, so threads would have to busy-wait in a loop until a permit frees up.
A semaphore automatically creates and fully manages the database connection objects itself, with no extra code needed.
A connection pool fundamentally does not need any capacity cap at all; the underlying queue can grow without limit and that's completely fine.
tradeoff: 信号量（只管数量上限）vs 阻塞队列资源池（既管数量又发放具体连接对象）

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 拿到许可就减一，release 归还许可就加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads can run a section of code at once; acquire decrements the count and release increments it back, and the next acquire blocks once the count hits zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先创建并复用一组数据库连接对象，请求借用后归还，避免每次都重新建立昂贵连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool pre-creates a set of reusable database connection objects that requests borrow and return, avoiding the cost of establishing a new connection every time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取（get/take）时如果队列为空会让线程等待，常用来同时充当“可用对象集合”和“等待机制”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking queue makes a get or take call wait when the queue is empty, so it doubles as both the set of available objects and the waiting mechanism.

optionExplanations: 对，semaphore 只回答“能不能进”，连接池还得有个地方存实际 Connection 对象再发出去。
semaphore 本身就是阻塞原语，acquire 拿不到许可会挂起线程等待，不是忙等。
semaphore 只是许可计数器，不会自己创建或管理任何连接对象。
无界队列会让连接数跟着请求量一直涨，内存和下游数据库都会被压垮。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a semaphore only answers 'may I proceed'; the pool still needs somewhere to store and hand out real Connection objects.
A semaphore is itself a blocking primitive — acquire suspends the thread when no permit is free, it doesn't busy-wait.
A semaphore is just a permit counter; it doesn't create or manage any connection object by itself.
An unbounded queue would let connection count keep growing with request volume, straining memory and the downstream database.

q: 把安全执行一次池化连接查询的步骤排好：
q_en: Put the steps for safely running one pooled-connection query in order:
steps: 在 finally 中把连接放回池
从池中带超时获取连接
执行查询或调用资源操作
如果获取超时，向调用方返回可处理错误
why: 严格说获取成功才会执行查询并进入 finally；获取失败走错误路径。核心顺序是限时获取、使用、必归还。
why_en: A safe pool operation bounds acquisition time, uses the resource only after success, and always returns it in a finally path.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[acquire] --> B[use resource]
  B --> C{success?}
  C -->|yes| D[return result]
  C -->|error| E[throw]
  D --> F[finally release]
  E --> F
tradeoff: 限时获取+finally 归还（防泄漏且请求路径有边界）vs 无限期获取（简单但可能拖垮请求线程）

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先创建并复用一组数据库连接对象，请求借用后归还，避免每次都重新建立昂贵连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool pre-creates a set of reusable database connection objects that requests borrow and return, avoiding the cost of establishing a new connection every time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论 try 块是否抛出异常都会执行的代码块，常用来确保资源一定被释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finally block always runs whether or not the try block threw an exception, which is how code guarantees a resource is actually released.

q: 当面试官从“别超过限制”转向“如何保持资源满载”时，哪些技术可以提？（多选）
q_en: When the interviewer shifts from "do not exceed the limit" to "keep resources fully utilized," which techniques can you mention? (multi-select)
scenario: GPU 池平均利用率只有 40%，任务时长从几十毫秒到几十秒不等，面试官问怎么把空闲吃掉。
scenario_en: A GPU pool averages 40% utilization with task durations from tens of milliseconds to tens of seconds, and the interviewer asks how to soak up the idle time.
options: work stealing
batching
adaptive pool sizing
忘记 release 让资源一直忙
why: 前三个都是提高利用率的常见方向。泄漏资源只会制造假忙和阻塞。
why_en: Work stealing, batching, and adaptive sizing are utilization techniques, while leaked resources only create blockage.
options_en: Work stealing.
Batching.
Adaptive pool sizing.
Forgetting to release so the resource looks permanently busy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 worker 有自己的任务队列，空闲 worker 去偷别的 worker 队列里的任务，避免任务时长不均导致的空闲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Work stealing gives each worker its own task queue, and an idle worker steals tasks from another worker's queue so uneven task lengths do not leave it idle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多次小操作合并成一次操作执行，摊薄每次操作的固定协调开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batching groups many small operations into one larger operation so the fixed per-operation coordination cost is paid only once.

termDefinitions.term: 自适应池 / adaptive pool sizing
termDefinitions.meaning: 根据当前利用率动态增加或收缩池的容量，而不是固定一个数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adaptive pool sizing grows or shrinks a pool's capacity based on current utilization instead of keeping it fixed.

optionExplanations: 空闲 worker 主动分担长任务的压力，挡住的是有的 worker 闲着、有的忙死的不均衡。
把多次小操作合成一次，减掉的是重复获取/归还连接的协调开销。
池随负载动态扩缩，减掉的是峰值不够用、低谷又浪费的两头压力。
忘记 release 只是制造假忙，资源看着被占用其实是泄漏，不是真正的利用率提升。
optionExplanations_en: An idle worker shares the load of long tasks, relieving the imbalance of some workers idle while others are swamped.
Combining many small operations into one cuts the repeated coordination cost of acquiring and releasing a connection.
The pool grows and shrinks with load, relieving the pressure of being undersized at peak and wasteful when idle.
Forgetting to release just fakes busyness — the resource looks occupied because it's leaked, not because it's truly utilized.

scenario: 题目是“设计一个连接池”，你已经说明 BlockingQueue 存连接。面试官继续问边界条件。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design a connection pool," and you have already explained using a BlockingQueue to store connections; the interviewer now asks about edge cases.
q: 最应该补充哪组点？
q_en: Which set of points should you add first?
options: finally 归还、获取超时、容量有界、可选验证连接这四点
把类改造成很深的继承树，用继承表达连接和 worker 的关系
把所有方法都改成 static 方法，去掉实例状态
换成无界队列，并且不处理任何异常，让它自己重试
why: 连接池面试主要看资源不会泄漏、请求不会无限等、池不会无限增长，以及坏连接不会被反复发放。
why_en: A strong connection-pool answer covers return-in-finally, bounded capacity, acquire timeouts, and optional resource validation.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只是限制并发 API 调用，连接验证这类对象池细节不需要展开。
options_en: Return-in-finally, acquire timeouts, bounded capacity, and optional connection validation.
Restructure the class into a deep inheritance tree to model connections and workers.
Turn every method into a static method and drop all instance state.
Switch to an unbounded queue and skip all exception handling, letting it retry on its own.
tradeoff: 完整边界清单（归还/超时/容量/校验）vs 只讲核心存取（面试官会继续追问遗漏点）

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论 try 块是否抛出异常都会执行的代码块，常用来确保资源一定被释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finally block always runs whether or not the try block threw an exception, which is how code guarantees a resource is actually released.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有设置容量上限的队列，put 操作永远不会因为满而阻塞，可能无限增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unbounded queue has no capacity cap, so a put call never blocks for being full and the queue can keep growing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象里子类复用父类结构的机制，跟“资源够不够用”的并发稀缺性问题无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance is the object-oriented mechanism where a subclass reuses a parent class's structure, unrelated to a scarcity problem about whether there is enough of a resource.

termDefinitions.meaning: 绑定在类本身而不是实例上的方法，跟资源池要不要有容量上限、超时这些工程问题无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A static method is bound to the class itself rather than an instance, and it has nothing to do with engineering concerns like pool capacity or timeouts.

optionExplanations: 对，归还兜底、获取超时、容量有界、连接校验正好覆盖泄漏、无限等待、无限增长、坏连接这四类坑。
深继承树描述的是类结构关系，回答不了资源会不会泄漏或等待有没有边界。
全改成 static 方法只是去掉实例状态，跟连接池要不要设边界毫无关系。
无界队列加不处理异常正好是这四个坑里最容易踩的两个，会让池失控。
optionExplanations_en: Right — always returning the connection in finally, bounding how long acquire waits, capping the pool size, and optionally validating connections together cover those four failure modes.
A deep inheritance tree is about class structure; it says nothing about whether resources leak or waits are bounded.
Making everything static just removes instance state, unrelated to whether the pool has any bounds at all.
An unbounded queue with no exception handling walks straight into two of the exact pitfalls a strong answer should cover.

q: 补全稀缺性总结：
q_en: Complete the scarcity summary:
text: 稀缺性题先问缺的是：{{操作槽位}}、{{资源单位}}，还是{{具体对象}}；分别对应普通信号量、单位许可预算、阻塞队列资源池。
why: 这个三分法能快速区分下载限并发、内存预算和连接池。
why_en: Scarcity maps to operation slots, resource units, or concrete objects, which correspond to semaphores, unit permits, or queue-backed pools.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 拿到许可就减一，release 归还许可就加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads can run a section of code at once; acquire decrements the count and release increments it back, and the next acquire blocks once the count hits zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取（get/take）时如果队列为空会让线程等待，常用来同时充当“可用对象集合”和“等待机制”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking queue makes a get or take call wait when the queue is empty, so it doubles as both the set of available objects and the waiting mechanism.

scenario: 磁盘写入器总预算 100MB，1 个许可代表 1MB；一次写入必须一次性拿到 permits 个单位，不够就等。
scenario_en: A disk writer has a 100MB budget where one permit means 1MB, and a write must take all of its permits at once or wait.
q: 预算不足时为什么用 Condition 加 while 循环，而不是 if 判断一次？
q_en: Why guard the budget with a Condition plus a while loop instead of a single if check?
codeSample:
with self._condition:
    while self._available < permits:   # 复查，不是只查一次
        self._condition.wait()        # 挂起，同时让出锁
    self._available -= permits        # 额度确实够才扣减
options: 被唤醒后重新复查预算，不够就接着等
if 判断一次就够，被唤醒时额度必然够用
while 是忙等轮询，靠 CPU 空转扫描剩余额度
Condition 会自动把 permits 拆成几次部分获取
options_en: It re-checks the budget after each wake-up and keeps waiting if it is still short.
A single if is enough, since a woken thread is guaranteed to have enough budget.
The while loop is a busy-wait that burns CPU scanning the remaining budget.
Condition automatically splits the permits into several partial acquisitions.
why: 被唤醒只说明有人归还过额度，不代表还轮得到你——可能已被别的线程抢走。while 复查保证只在够用时扣减，代价是可能空醒几轮。
why_en: Waking up only means someone released permits, not that enough are still left for you, so the while loop re-checks before deducting.
whenOtherWins: 如果每次固定只取 1 个单位，标准 Semaphore 的 acquire 本身就原子完成了检查加占用，不必手写 Condition。
tradeoff: 手写 Condition + while（能一次原子拿走 N 个单位）vs 单次 if 判断（代码短，但唤醒后额度可能已被抢走）

termDefinitions.meaning: 配合一把锁使用的等待机制：wait 会释放锁并挂起线程，别人改完共享状态后 notify 把它叫醒重新拿锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A condition variable pairs with a lock: wait releases the lock and suspends the thread, and another thread notifies it to wake up and re-acquire the lock after changing shared state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预算的最小记账单位，这里一个许可代表 1MB 在途数据，拿走就减、归还就加。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A permit is the unit of budget accounting; here one permit stands for 1MB of in-flight data, decremented on acquire and restored on release.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 减一、release 加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads run a section at once; acquire decrements it, release increments it, and the next acquire blocks at zero.

optionExplanations: 对，wait 返回只代表被 notify 过，额度可能已被别人抢走，必须再看一眼。
唤醒和拿到额度是两件事，只查一次就扣减会在不够时冲破 100MB 上限。
wait() 会把线程挂起并交出 CPU，循环体只在每次被叫醒后跑一遍，不空转。
部分获取会让线程握着半截额度继续等，容易互相卡死，这段代码没这么做。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a return from wait only means someone notified, and the budget may already be taken again.
Being woken and having enough budget are different things; one check can deduct past the 100MB cap.
wait() suspends the thread and yields the CPU; the loop body runs only once per wake-up.
Partial acquisition would leave a thread holding half a budget while waiting, risking deadlock.

scenario: 磁盘写预算 100 许可（1 许可 = 1MB）。一个要 60 许可的写和一个要 5 许可的写都在等，此时一个 70MB 的写完成并归还 70 许可。
scenario_en: A disk-write budget holds 100 permits (1 permit = 1MB). One writer needs 60 permits and another needs 5; a finished 70MB write now returns 70 permits.
q: 释放时把 notify_all 换成 notify，会出什么问题？
q_en: What breaks if the release path calls notify instead of notify_all?
options: 可能只叫醒 5 许可那个，60 许可的写继续睡
所有等待线程照样都被叫醒，只是顺序变随机
归还的许可会被算错，available 加成两倍
被叫醒的线程会跳过 while 复查，直接扣减额度
options_en: It may wake only the 5-permit writer, leaving the 60-permit writer asleep.
Every waiting thread still wakes up; only the order becomes random.
The returned permits are miscounted and available is increased twice.
The woken thread skips the while re-check and deducts the budget anyway.
why: notify 只挑一个等待者，而等待者要的额度不同：被挑中的小写拿走额度后预算又变紧，大额度的写可能永远等不到自己那次唤醒。notify_all 让所有人复查，代价是惊群空醒。
why_en: notify wakes just one waiter, and since waiters need different amounts, the large writer can starve; notify_all makes everyone re-check at the cost of spurious wake-ups.
tradeoff: notify_all（人人复查，不漏掉大额度等待者）vs notify（唤醒少更省，但可能永远叫不到该醒的那个）

termDefinitions.meaning: 叫醒所有在这个条件变量上等待的线程，让它们各自重新检查条件是否满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: notify_all wakes every thread waiting on the condition variable so each one re-checks whether its condition now holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次唤醒把大量线程同时叫起来抢同一份资源，多数复查失败后又睡回去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd is when one signal wakes many threads to contend for the same resource, and most re-check, fail, and go back to sleep.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个线程虽然一直在等，却因为调度或唤醒策略长期拿不到资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Starvation is when a thread waits indefinitely because the scheduling or wake-up policy keeps passing it over.

optionExplanations: 对，唤醒对象是任意一个，小写被叫醒拿走 5 许可后，大写这次机会就白白错过。
notify 的定义就是只叫醒一个等待者，不是把所有人叫醒后打乱顺序。
唤醒策略只影响叫谁起来，available += permits 这行算术完全不受影响。
复查逻辑写在 while 里，被叫醒的线程照样要过这道检查，不会跳过。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the wake target is arbitrary, so the small writer takes 5 permits and the big one loses its chance.
notify is defined as waking a single waiter, not waking everyone in shuffled order.
The wake policy only picks who gets up; the available += permits arithmetic is untouched.
The re-check lives in the while loop, so a woken thread still has to pass it.

scenario: 连接池报告 10 个连接全部 in use，但数据库那端吞吐极低。池里既有 1ms 跑完的快查询，也有占住连接 500ms 的分析查询。
scenario_en: A pool reports all 10 connections in use, yet database throughput is minimal; it mixes 1ms queries with analytics queries that hold a connection for 500ms.
q: 池显示满载但数据库很闲，最可能是什么状态？
q_en: The pool looks saturated but the database is idle — what state is the system actually in?
options: 连接被应用代码占着空转，in-use 不等于在干活
数据库正在主动限流，把大部分查询挡了回去
池容量设小了，把 10 调到 100 就能解决问题
池里的连接已经全部失效，握手失败发不出查询
options_en: The connections are checked out but idling in application code — in use is not the same as busy.
The database is throttling and rejecting most of the incoming queries.
The pool is undersized and simply raising it from 10 to 100 fixes it.
Every pooled connection has gone stale, so handshakes fail and no query is sent.
why: in-use 只说明连接被借走了，借走后线程可能在处理结果集或等别的 IO，数据库那一端是闲的。所以要看利用率而不是占用率，扩池只会把更多连接一起晾着。
why_en: In use only means the connection is checked out; the borrowing thread may be chewing on results, so measure utilisation rather than occupancy.
tradeoff: 看占用率（好采集，但会把空转当成满载）vs 看数据库侧吞吐与利用率（更真实，但要额外埋点）

termDefinitions.meaning: 资源真正在做有效工作的时间占比，区别于只是被谁借走的占用率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Utilisation is the share of time a resource spends doing useful work, as opposed to merely being checked out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 池里那些已被数据库或网络单方面关掉、但池还以为可用的连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stale connection is one the database or network already closed while the pool still believes it is usable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端主动拒绝或延迟超出配额的请求，用来保护自己不被压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throttling is a server deliberately rejecting or delaying requests beyond a quota to protect itself from overload.

optionExplanations: 对，10 条里多数只是被借着，线程在处理结果集，数据库端并没有活要干。
限流会让查询返回错误或明显变慢，而这里症状是数据库端根本收不到请求。
连接空转时扩池只是让更多连接一起闲着，还多占数据库内存和描述符。
连接失效会表现为借出后报错或重连，而不是安静地一直显示为使用中。
optionExplanations_en: Right — most of the ten are merely borrowed while threads chew on results, so the database has nothing to do.
Throttling would surface as errors or clear slowdowns, but here the database sees almost no requests at all.
Growing the pool while connections idle just parks more of them, costing extra database memory and descriptors.
Stale connections show up as errors or reconnects on checkout, not as quietly in-use connections.

scenario: 10 连接的池被所有租户共用。一个批量导数租户长期把池占满，交互式租户的请求排在后面，多数等到超时。
scenario_en: One 10-connection pool is shared by all tenants; a bulk-import tenant keeps it saturated and interactive tenants queue behind it until they time out.
q: 怎么改才能让交互式租户不被批量租户长期饿死？
q_en: How do you keep interactive tenants from being starved by the bulk tenant?
options: 按租户或优先级把池切成几份，各自有配额
把池换成严格公平队列，按到达顺序发放连接
把池容量从 10 调到 100，让大家都能拿到
去掉获取超时，让交互式请求一直等到有连接
options_en: Partition the pool by tenant or priority so each class gets its own quota.
Switch to a strictly fair queue that hands out connections in arrival order.
Raise the pool from 10 to 100 connections so everyone can get one.
Drop the acquire timeout so interactive requests wait until a connection frees up.
why: 竞争压垮吞吐时，公平只保证排队顺序，救不了大户长期霸占容量；按租户分区让每类请求有各自的额度。代价是分区之间的空闲额度不能互相借用。
why_en: Fairness only fixes ordering, not a tenant that holds capacity for long stretches, so partition the pool per tenant at the cost of stranded idle capacity.
whenOtherWins: 如果各租户负载相近、只是偶尔有人排在后面，严格公平 FIFO 更简单，不用给每个分区单独调容量。
tradeoff: 按租户分区（防饿死，但空闲额度不共享）vs 单一共享池（利用率高，但大户能长期占满）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一份共享资源拆成若干独立配额，各自只能用自己那份，互不挤占。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning splits one shared resource into separate quotas so each class can only consume its own share.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：等待者严格按到达顺序被服务，不允许插队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO, or First In First Out, serves waiters strictly in the order they arrived.

termDefinitions.meaning: 等资源的时间上限，超过就放弃并向上返回失败，而不是继续挂着。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acquire timeout caps how long a thread waits for a resource before giving up and returning an error.

optionExplanations: 对，交互式租户有专属的那几条连接，批量任务再忙也吃不到这部分额度。
公平只解决“谁先排上”，批量租户仍会一轮一轮把连接全借走。
扩容让批量任务跑得更凶，数据库内存和描述符先扛不住，比例问题没变。
去掉超时只会把请求线程一起耗尽，用户看到的还是超时，只是更晚。
optionExplanations_en: Right — interactive tenants own a slice of connections that the bulk job can never take.
Fairness only decides who queues first; the bulk tenant still takes every connection round after round.
More connections just let the bulk job run harder while the database runs out of memory and descriptors.
Removing the timeout only exhausts request threads too; users still see timeouts, just later.

scenario: 限并发的代码不加锁：先读 active < 5 判断有没有余量，再执行 active += 1。5 个线程几乎同时到达，都读到 active = 4。
scenario_en: Concurrency limiting code checks active < 5 and then does active += 1 without a lock; five threads arrive together and all read active = 4.
q: 这种 check-then-act 会把系统带到什么状态？
q_en: What state does this check-then-act pattern leave the system in?
options: 五个线程都通过检查，active 冲到 9 超出限额
五个线程全被拒绝，因为读到的值已经过期作废
active 会被减成负数，计数器从此永久损坏
结果仍然正确，只是有些线程要多等一两轮调度才能通过
options_en: All five pass the check and active climbs to 9, above the limit.
All five are rejected because the value they read is already stale.
active is decremented below zero and the counter is permanently corrupted.
The result stays correct; some threads merely wait an extra scheduling round or two.
why: 读和写之间没有锁，5 个线程都基于同一个 4 各加一，上限 5 被冲到 9，下游实际收到 9 路并发就是超载。修法是用 semaphore 的 acquire 把检查和占用做成一个原子动作。
why_en: With no lock between the read and the write, all five threads act on the same stale 4 and push concurrency to 9, so use a semaphore acquire to make check and take atomic.
tradeoff: semaphore 原子 acquire（检查与占用不可分割）vs 裸计数器 check-then-act（代码直观，但限额形同虚设）

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读共享状态做判断、再基于判断修改它；两步之间没有锁的话，状态可能已被别人改掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Check-then-act reads shared state, decides, then mutates it; without a lock in between, the state can change between the two steps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外表现为不可分割的一步，其他线程看不到它的中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation appears indivisible to other threads, which never observe an intermediate state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 减一、release 加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads run a section at once; acquire decrements it, release increments it, and the next acquire blocks at zero.

optionExplanations: 对，每个线程都拿着自己那份过期的 4 做判断，五次自增全部生效，限额被静默突破。
过期的值不会自动作废，代码照样当真，判断结果是“还有余量”而不是拒绝。
这里只有自增没有配对的自减，计数只会偏大，不会掉到负数。
调度顺序不同只让超限出现得或早或晚，缺锁这件事本身不会被调度修好。
optionExplanations_en: Right — each thread decides on its own stale 4, all five increments land, and the cap is silently breached.
A stale value is not invalidated automatically; the code trusts it and concludes there is room.
There is only an increment here with no paired decrement, so the count skews high, never negative.
Different scheduling only changes when the overshoot appears; it cannot repair the missing lock.

scenario: 图片处理用 5 许可的信号量限并发。上游 HTTP 客户端 2 秒就超时，但高峰期请求线程挂在 acquire 上一直不返回。
scenario_en: Image processing caps concurrency with a 5-permit semaphore; the upstream HTTP client times out after 2 seconds, yet request threads hang forever inside acquire.
q: 信号量这一侧该怎么改，才不会让请求线程永久阻塞？
q_en: What change on the semaphore side stops request threads from blocking forever?
options: 改用 tryAcquire(timeout)，等不到就返回失败
把许可数从 5 加到 50，降低线程阻塞的概率
改用队列的 poll(timeout)，因为信号量没有超时变体
在 acquire 外面套一层重试循环，直到拿到许可为止
options_en: Use tryAcquire with a timeout and fail when no permit arrives in time.
Raise the permits from 5 to 50 so threads are less likely to block.
Use the queue's poll with a timeout, since semaphores have no timed variant.
Wrap acquire in a retry loop that keeps trying until a permit is obtained.
why: 阻塞版 acquire 会一直等下去，请求线程被耗光；tryAcquire(timeout) 在窗口内拿不到就返回 false，调用方可以回 503。代价是高峰期会主动丢掉一些本可成功的请求。
why_en: A plain acquire waits indefinitely and drains the request threads, while tryAcquire with a timeout fails fast so the caller can return a 503.
whenOtherWins: 后台批处理没有用户在等响应时，阻塞版 acquire 更简单：让任务排队比直接丢弃它更划算。
tradeoff: tryAcquire(timeout) 快速失败（保住线程，但会误杀请求）vs acquire 无限等待（不丢请求，但线程会被耗光）

termDefinitions.meaning: 信号量的限时获取：在给定时间内拿到许可就返回真，超时则返回假而不是继续等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: tryAcquire with a timeout returns true if a permit arrives within the window and false when it expires, instead of waiting on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 阻塞队列的限时取元素：等到超时还没有元素就放弃，返回空值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: poll with a timeout takes an item from a blocking queue but gives up and returns empty once the timeout expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 状态码 Service Unavailable，告诉调用方服务当前没有容量、可以稍后重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable tells the caller the service currently has no capacity and the request may be retried later.

optionExplanations: 对，超时窗口设在客户端 2 秒之内，线程能及时脱身并把过载变成明确错误。
加许可只是把过载放行到下游，CPU 打满之后线程照样堆在那里等。
信号量本身就有 tryAcquire 的限时变体，不必为了超时改造成队列。
重试循环等价于换个写法的无限等待，线程一样回不来，还多烧 CPU。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a timeout inside the client's 2 seconds lets the thread escape and turns overload into an explicit error.
More permits just admit the overload downstream; once the CPU saturates, threads pile up again.
Semaphores already offer a timed tryAcquire, so there is no need to convert this into a queue.
A retry loop is unbounded waiting in disguise: the thread still never returns and burns CPU.

scenario: 磁盘写预算 100 许可、1 许可 = 1MB，代码算 permits = max(1, ceil(字节数/MB))。这台服务上大量写入只有 4KB。
scenario_en: A disk-write budget has 100 permits at 1MB each, computing permits = max(1, ceil(bytes/MB)); most writes on this service are only 4KB.
q: 如果去掉 max(1, ...) 这层地板，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the max(1, ...) floor is removed from the permit calculation?
options: 4KB 的写各算 0 个许可，可无限并发绕过预算
4KB 的写会被向上并成 1MB，预算反而算得偏多
可用许可会被减成负数，之后的写永远拿不到许可
大写入会拿不到许可，因为小写入先把额度全抢走了
options_en: Each 4KB write costs 0 permits and unlimited tiny writes bypass the budget.
Each 4KB write rounds up to 1MB, so the budget is over-counted instead.
Available permits go negative and later writes can never acquire again.
Large writes starve because the small writes grabbed all the budget first.
why: 不设地板时 4KB 除以 1MB 取整就是 0，这些写既不减预算也不用等，几千个可以同时压到磁盘上，限流对最常见的负载完全失效。地板 1 保证每次写至少记一笔账。
why_en: Without the floor a 4KB write rounds to zero permits, so it neither consumes budget nor waits, and thousands can hit the disk at once.
tradeoff: 地板 1 许可（小写也记账，但对 4KB 明显高估）vs 按真实比例计（更精确，但 0 许可等于不限流）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不满一个单位的余数也算作一个单位，例如 1.1MB 按 2MB 计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ceiling rounds any partial unit up to a whole one, so 1.1MB is charged as 2MB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预算的最小记账单位，这里一个许可代表 1MB 在途数据，拿走就减、归还就加。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A permit is the unit of budget accounting; here one permit stands for 1MB of in-flight data, decremented on acquire and restored on release.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经开始但还没完成的操作正占用的数据量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-flight data is the amount held by operations that have started but not yet finished.

optionExplanations: 对，占 0 个许可的写永远满足条件，while 循环一次都不会挡住它们。
并成 1MB 正是保留地板后的行为，去掉它得到的是 0 而不是 1。
扣减 0 不会改变计数，可用许可停在原地，不存在被减成负数一说。
小写入压根不占额度，也就谈不上把大写入的额度抢走。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a write costing zero permits always satisfies the condition, so the while loop never blocks it.
Rounding up to 1MB is exactly what keeping the floor does; removing it yields 0, not 1.
Subtracting zero leaves the counter unchanged, so it never drifts below zero.
Tiny writes consume no budget at all, so they cannot take anything away from large ones.

scenario: 磁盘写预算 100 许可，1 许可 = 1MB，permits = ceil(字节数 / 1MB)。实际负载里有不少 1.1MB 这种刚过整数的文件。
scenario_en: A disk-write budget holds 100 permits at 1MB each with permits = ceil(bytes / 1MB), and the real workload contains many files just over a whole megabyte, like 1.1MB.
q: 这种向上取整的许可粒度带来什么后果？
q_en: What is the consequence of this ceiling-based permit granularity?
options: 多记的零头累积，真实在途约 98MB 就开始阻塞
少记的零头累积，真实在途悄悄超过 100MB 才阻塞
取整只影响统计口径，阻塞时刻仍精确卡在 100MB
取整会让大文件优先被调度，1.1MB 的文件排到最后
options_en: The over-charged remainders add up, so writes start blocking around 98MB of real data.
The under-charged remainders add up, so real in-flight data quietly exceeds 100MB.
Rounding only affects reporting; blocking still happens exactly at 100MB.
Rounding prioritises large files and pushes 1.1MB files to the back of the queue.
why: 许可数 = ceil(字节数 / 1MB)，MB 是 1024×1024 字节；1.1MB 记 2 个许可，多记的零头累积后真实在途约 98MB 就用光 100 许可。这个 100 是保守上界，用来定阻塞点，不是精确在途量。
why_en: Permits equal the byte count divided by one megabyte rounded up, so a 1.1MB file is charged 2 and blocking kicks in near 98MB of real data — a deliberately conservative bound.
tradeoff: 整数许可粒度（实现简单，只做加减法）vs 按字节精确记账（预算准，但计数更细、竞争更多）

termDefinitions.meaning: 兆字节，这里按 1024×1024 = 1048576 字节计，是许可的换算单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MB, or megabyte, is taken here as 1024 by 1024 bytes and is the conversion unit for one permit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不满一个单位的余数也算作一个单位，例如 1.1MB 按 2MB 计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ceiling rounds any partial unit up to a whole one, so 1.1MB is charged as 2MB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 故意估得比真实值大一点的限额，宁可提前挡住也不愿超出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conservative bound deliberately over-estimates usage so the system blocks early rather than overshooting.

optionExplanations: 对，2 个许可只装 1.1MB 真数据，约 50 个文件就用完 100 许可，阻塞点提前到 98MB 左右。
取整方向反了：ceil 只会多记不会少记，所以真实在途永远小于等于许可数。
记账单位是整数许可，1.1MB 记 2 个的那 0.9MB 差额是真实存在的，不只是报表口径。
许可只决定谁能开始写，不排序也不区分文件大小，先到的先拿。
optionExplanations_en: Right — two permits cover only 1.1MB of real data, so about 50 files exhaust 100 permits near 98MB.
The rounding goes the other way: ceil only over-charges, so real in-flight data never exceeds the permit count.
Accounting happens in whole permits, so the 0.9MB charged beyond a 1.1MB file is a real gap, not a reporting artifact.
Permits only decide who may start writing; they impose no ordering and no preference by file size.

scenario: 10 连接的池已被借空，第 11 个线程调 queue.get() 等连接。这台机器在 3 万 QPS 下 CPU 已经吃紧。
scenario_en: All 10 pooled connections are checked out and an eleventh thread calls queue.get(); the box is already CPU-bound at 30k QPS.
q: 这个线程在等待期间对 CPU 做了什么？
q_en: What does that waiting thread do to the CPU while it waits?
options: 被 OS 挂起，不占 CPU，归还连接时再被唤醒
在循环里反复检查队列是否非空，占满一个核心
每隔 10ms sleep 一次再查一遍，延迟取决于间隔
立刻返回空值，由调用方自己决定什么时候重试
options_en: It is suspended by the OS, uses no CPU, and is woken when a connection returns.
It spins in a loop checking whether the queue is non-empty, pinning one core.
It sleeps 10ms and polls again, so latency depends on the polling interval.
It returns empty immediately and leaves the caller to decide when to retry.
why: 阻塞队列的 get 走 OS 的挂起唤醒原语：线程让出 CPU，直到 put 把它叫醒。这正是选阻塞队列而不是自旋或 sleep 轮询的效率理由，代价是唤醒要过一次调度延迟。
why_en: A blocking queue's get uses OS suspend and wake primitives, so the thread yields the CPU until a put wakes it, at the price of one scheduling delay.
tradeoff: OS 挂起唤醒（等待期间零 CPU，但唤醒有调度延迟）vs 自旋或轮询（反应更快，但持续烧 CPU 或引入固定间隔）

termDefinitions.meaning: 取元素时如果队列为空会让线程等待，同时充当可用对象集合和等待机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking queue makes a take wait while it is empty, serving as both the pool of available objects and the waiting mechanism.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程在循环里不停重读条件，不释放 CPU，等待期间一直烧一个核。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spin-waiting keeps re-reading a condition in a loop without yielding, burning a core for the whole wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量服务每秒处理多少请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or Queries Per Second, measures how many requests a service handles each second.

optionExplanations: 对，线程进入内核的等待队列，直到有人 put 才被调度回来，期间不消耗 CPU。
自旋在 3 万 QPS 这种场景下会把本就紧张的核心烧掉，队列并没有这么实现。
sleep 轮询会带来最多一个间隔的额外延迟，也没必要——队列自己会精确唤醒。
立刻返回是不带超时的 poll 语义，get 的默认行为是等下去而不是放弃。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the thread parks in a kernel wait queue and is rescheduled only when someone puts a connection back.
Spinning would burn an already scarce core at 30k QPS, and that is not how the queue is implemented.
Sleep-and-poll adds up to one interval of extra latency and is unnecessary since the queue wakes precisely.
Returning immediately is the semantics of a non-blocking poll; get waits by default rather than giving up.

scenario: 低层设计面里你说“用 5 许可的信号量限制并发下载”，面试官追问：它到底是怎么把线程阻塞住的？
scenario_en: In a low-level design round you say you'll cap downloads with a 5-permit semaphore, and the interviewer asks how it actually blocks a thread.
q: 面对这个追问，最稳的回答策略是什么？
q_en: What is the safest way to answer that follow-up?
options: 说它用 OS 原语挂起和唤醒线程，标准库已实现
现场手写一个基于自旋锁的信号量内部实现给他看
承认不清楚，改口说不用信号量，换成加锁计数器
说它内部就是一个 while 循环，不停地检查计数器
options_en: Say it uses OS primitives to park and wake threads, and the standard library handles that.
Whiteboard your own spin-lock-based implementation of a semaphore on the spot.
Admit you don't know and switch to a lock-protected counter instead.
Say that internally it is just a while loop constantly re-checking the counter.
why: 这类追问考的是你知不知道抽象边界：讲清 acquire/release 的语义，加一句挂起唤醒由 OS 做就够了。硬讲内部容易讲错，还会把话题从设计带偏到实现。
why_en: The follow-up tests whether you know the abstraction boundary, so state the acquire and release semantics plus OS park and wake, and leave the internals to the library.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮明确是操作系统或并发原语实现岗，面试官要的就是内部结构，那才该展开等待队列的细节。
tradeoff: 答 API 语义（聚焦设计判断，稳）vs 答内部实现（显得深入，但容易讲错且偏题）

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统提供的底层机制，这里指把线程挂起进等待队列、有事件时再唤醒的调度能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An OS primitive is a low-level kernel facility, here the ability to park a thread in a wait queue and wake it when an event occurs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拿不到锁就在循环里反复重试的锁，等待期间不让出 CPU。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spin lock retries in a tight loop when the lock is unavailable, never yielding the CPU while it waits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 你负责说清语义、把实现交给底层库的那条线，答题时要主动点明它在哪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstraction boundary is the line where you own the semantics and the library owns the implementation.

optionExplanations: 对，一句“挂起唤醒由 OS 做，Java 的 Semaphore 已经封装好”就答到位了。
手写内部实现风险高：写错一处就变成考实现细节，设计讨论也被打断。
追问实现不等于方案有问题，换掉信号量反而暴露对工具的不自信。
说成 while 循环等于把它讲成自旋忙等，与真实的挂起唤醒语义相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right — saying the OS parks and wakes threads and Java's Semaphore wraps that is a complete answer.
Writing the internals live is risky: one slip turns the round into an implementation quiz and derails the design talk.
A follow-up about internals is not a sign the design is wrong; swapping the tool signals low confidence.
Describing it as a while loop turns it into busy-waiting, the opposite of real park-and-wake semantics.

scenario: 服务每秒 1000 个请求，每个请求都要查一次数据库。有人提议每来一个请求就现开一条连接、用完关掉。
scenario_en: A service takes 1,000 requests per second and each one queries the database; someone proposes opening a fresh connection per request and closing it after.
q: 哪些代价说明数据库连接必须池化复用？（多选）
q_en: Which costs explain why database connections must be pooled and reused? (multi-select)
options: 每条连接都占数据库服务端的一块内存
每条连接占一个文件描述符，OS 有硬上限
建立连接要走一次握手，耗时加在每个请求上
连接对象是无状态的，复用能省掉序列化开销
options_en: Every connection consumes memory on the database server.
Every connection holds a file descriptor, and the OS caps how many exist.
Establishing a connection costs a handshake, added to every single request.
Connections are stateless objects, so reusing them saves serialization work.
why: 连接贵在三处：数据库端内存、文件描述符、握手耗时。1000 QPS 下每请求新建等于把这三笔成本乘一千；池化把它们摊到启动那一次，代价是并发被池容量卡住。
why_en: Connections are expensive in three ways — server memory, file descriptors, and handshake time — so pooling pays those costs once at startup and caps concurrency instead.
tradeoff: 池化复用（摊掉建连成本，但并发被池容量卡死）vs 每请求新建（并发不受限，但内存、描述符和握手全线爆炸）

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统给每个打开的文件或套接字分配的整数句柄，每个进程能同时持有的数量有上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A file descriptor is the integer handle the OS assigns to each open file or socket, and each process can hold only a limited number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建连时的往返协商过程，包含网络往返和认证，耗时通常是毫秒级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A handshake is the round-trip negotiation that sets up a connection, including network round trips and authentication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不保存任何跨调用的上下文；数据库连接恰恰相反，它带着套接字、认证和事务状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stateless means keeping no context between calls, which a database connection is not: it carries a socket, credentials, and transaction state.

optionExplanations: 是，每条连接在数据库进程里都有会话缓冲区，连接一多先压垮的是数据库内存。
是，描述符用尽后整个进程连新文件都打不开，故障范围远超数据库这条路径。
是，握手的毫秒级往返直接叠进每个请求延迟，1000 QPS 下这笔账最刺眼。
不是，连接恰恰有状态：套接字、凭据、事务上下文都挂在上面，正因如此才要复用。
optionExplanations_en: Yes — each connection keeps session buffers inside the database process, so memory there is the first thing to break.
Yes — once descriptors run out the whole process cannot open new files, so the blast radius exceeds the database path.
Yes — the millisecond handshake round trip lands directly in every request's latency, which hurts most at 1,000 QPS.
No — connections are stateful, carrying a socket, credentials, and transaction context, which is exactly why they are reused.

q: 把 LLD 设计流程五个阶段按依赖顺序排好：
q_en: Put the five LLD design phases in dependency order.
steps: 实现核心方法并验证场景
澄清需求
讨论可扩展性追问
提取实体和关系
设计类的状态和行为
why: 先澄清范围，再把需求落到实体、类状态和核心方法；最后用走查和 follow-up 检查设计是否站得住。
why_en: Clarify scope first, then derive entities, classes, and core methods before validating the design with a walkthrough.
tradeoff: 先建立结构与契约 vs 直接写代码或先聊扩展
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确跳到某个 follow-up，就先回答它，再把主线拉回剩余阶段。

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计面试，重点是把小范围需求拆成类、状态、方法和核心逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design focuses on turning a small scoped problem into classes, state, methods, and core logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试官在主设计后追加的变化或扩展问题，用来检查设计能否演进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follow-up is an added change or extension question used to test whether the design can evolve.

diagram:
flowchart TD
A["clarify requirements"] --> B["extract entities"]
B --> C["design class state and behavior"]
C --> D["implement core method"]
D --> E["walk through scenario"]
E --> F["discuss follow-ups"]

scenario: 你正在把「设计 Tic Tac Toe」这句话需求变成可设计的 spec，逐条追问细节。
scenario_en: You are turning the prompt "Design Tic Tac Toe" into a designable spec by asking clarifying questions.
q: 下面哪些追问的答案会直接改变实体或类的设计？（多选）
q_en: Which clarifying answers would directly change the entity or class design? (Select all that apply.)
options: 落子按钮用什么颜色（不影响任何实体或方法签名）
是否要支持 AI 对手（决定要不要为落子逻辑引入 Strategy 接口）
怎样判定获胜或平局（决定 Board 要实现哪些检查方法）
非法操作返回 false 还是抛异常（决定方法的错误处理契约）
options_en: What color the move button is (does not affect any entity or method signature).
Whether an AI opponent is needed (decides if move selection needs a Strategy interface).
How a win or draw is determined (decides which check methods Board must implement).
Whether invalid moves return false or throw (decides the method's error-handling contract).
why: 会改变状态、规则或错误契约的问题才会改类模型；按钮颜色这类展示细节不该挤进核心设计。
why_en: Questions about state, rules, or error contracts change the model; button colors usually do not.

rows: 方法返回值或异常设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能能力；在这题里指系统是否要自己选择下一步落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Artificial Intelligence means the system can choose moves on its own in this problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法或策略封装成独立接口，运行时可以互换实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface so implementations can be swapped at runtime.

optionExplanations: 按钮颜色只影响样式渲染，不涉及任何字段、状态或方法签名，所以不该问它来定型。
有没有 AI 对手决定落子选择要不要抽象成可替换的 Strategy 接口，直接改变类结构。
胜负判定规则决定 Board 要实现哪些检查方法，是这道题里改动最大的一条追问。
非法操作是返回 false 还是抛异常，会直接写进方法的错误处理契约，所以要先问清楚。
optionExplanations_en: Button color only affects rendering, not any field or method signature, so it shouldn't drive the design.
Whether there's an AI opponent decides if move selection needs a swappable Strategy interface.
Win/draw rules decide which check methods Board must implement, the biggest design lever here.
Whether invalid moves return false or throw becomes part of the method's error-handling contract.

scenario: 题目只给一句话「设计 Tic Tac Toe」，你要把它变成可设计的 spec。
scenario_en: The prompt only says "Design Tic Tac Toe," and you need to turn it into a designable spec.
q: 先追问哪组问题最能定义系统的规则和边界？
q_en: Which set of questions best defines the system rules and scope first?
options: 数据库要分几个分片、CDN 要几个节点
轮流、胜负判定、非法操作、UI/AI 范围
落子逻辑该用哪种设计模式实现
棋盘格子用什么颜色的边框
options_en: How many database shards or CDN nodes to use.
Turn order, win/draw rules, invalid-move handling, and whether UI or AI is in scope.
Which design pattern to use for move logic.
What border color the board cells should have.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确是在线多人游戏平台，才需要讨论网络、分片和部署。
tradeoff: 规则与范围澄清 vs 过早跳到实现细节或视觉样式
why: 第一轮要先锁定轮流规则、结束条件和非法输入；模式、分片和视觉样式都依赖这些边界。
why_en: Lock down turns, end states, and invalid moves first; patterns, sharding, and visuals come after scope is clear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把静态内容缓存到离用户更近的节点，和游戏规则无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on servers closer to users and has nothing to do with game rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，负责展示和输入，不应该先决定核心游戏规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input, and it should not define the core game rules first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能能力；如果纳入范围，会影响落子策略和类边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Artificial Intelligence would affect move-selection strategy and class boundaries if it is in scope.

optionExplanations: 分片和 CDN 节点数属于扩展性问题，游戏规则还没定就先问部署规模，是本末倒置。
轮流、胜负、非法操作和 UI/AI 范围一次性锁定了规则边界，后续设计都建立在它上面。
该用哪种设计模式是实现细节，规则都还没定，先讨论模式只会分散注意力。
格子边框颜色是纯视觉样式，不会影响任何一个方法或状态字段。
optionExplanations_en: Shard count and CDN nodes are scaling concerns; asking about deployment before rules are set is backwards.
Turn order, win/draw, invalid moves, and UI/AI scope lock down the rule boundary everything else depends on.
Which design pattern to use is an implementation detail, pointless before the rules even exist.
Cell border color is pure visual styling and touches no method or state field.

q: 补全需求阶段产出：
q_en: Complete the requirement-phase output:
text: 需求阶段要写下核心 Requirements，也要写下明确的 {{Out of Scope}}——被排除的功能不需要设计对应的实体或接口，这样类模型才不会{{膨胀}}。
why: Out of Scope 是防膨胀用的边界：排除网络对战，就不要为它建 NetworkManager 或协议接口。
why_en: Out-of-scope boundaries keep the model lean; if networking is excluded, skip NetworkManager and protocol APIs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 明确不在本轮设计范围内的功能，面试中先记下但不为它建核心实体或接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Out of scope means a feature is explicitly excluded from this design round, so you note it but do not model core entities or APIs for it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责网络连接或消息收发的组件；网络对战不在范围内时不需要设计它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A NetworkManager handles network connections or messages; it is unnecessary when networked play is out of scope.

scenario: 你正在把一份需求文档拆解成候选类，需要决定哪些名词值得单独建模成实体。
scenario_en: You are splitting a requirements document into candidate classes and deciding which nouns deserve their own entity.
q: 判断一个名词是否该单独建成实体时，哪些提问有帮助？（多选）
q_en: Which questions help decide whether a noun should become its own entity? (Select all that apply.)
options: 它是否维护会变化的状态
它被其他类引用的次数是否够多
它是否执行或约束重要规则
它是否只是别的对象上的一个字段
options_en: Does it hold state that changes over time?
Is it referenced by enough other classes?
Does it enforce or constrain an important rule?
Is it really just a field on another object?
why: 我会看它是否拥有会变状态或规则；如果只是别的对象上的值，就留成字段，别因为被引用多就硬拆类。
why_en: Model it as an entity when it owns changing state or rules; leave simple attached data as a field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在设计里有独立身份、状态或规则归属的业务对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entity is a domain object with its own identity, state, or rule ownership.

optionExplanations: 会随时间变化的状态是最强的实体信号，说明它需要自己的生命周期管理。
被引用次数多不代表该拆成类，一个常量或简单值也可能被到处引用。
如果它执行或约束一条重要规则，把规则和状态绑在一起才是它该独立成实体的理由。
如果它只是挂在别的对象上的一个值，硬拆成实体反而制造多余的类。
optionExplanations_en: State that changes over time is the strongest entity signal; it needs its own lifecycle.
Being referenced a lot doesn't make something an entity; a plain constant can be widely referenced too.
If it enforces or constrains an important rule, bundling that rule with its state is reason enough to model it separately.
If it's really just a value attached to another object, splitting it out only creates an extra class.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 的需求已经确认：两个玩家、3x3 棋盘、落子、胜负和平局。
scenario_en: The Tic Tac Toe requirements are confirmed: two players, a 3x3 board, moves, wins, and draws.
q: 最合理的初始实体集合是？
q_en: What is the most reasonable initial set of entities?
options: DatabaseShard、Cache、CDN
MouseEvent、Pixel、Theme
Game、Board、Player
Factory、Builder、Singleton
options_en: DatabaseShard, Cache, and CDN.
MouseEvent, Pixel, and Theme.
Game, Board, and Player.
Factory, Builder, and Singleton.
tradeoff: 职责清晰的领域实体 vs 把基础设施组件或设计模式名当成实体
whenOtherWins: 如果后续加入 AI、网络或可变棋盘尺寸，才考虑额外实体。
why: Game 管流程，Board 管棋盘和胜负检查，Player 表示参与者；这三类正好覆盖需求里的状态所有权。
why_en: Game owns the flow, Board owns the grid and win checks, and Player represents each participant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库分片，把数据按规则拆到多台数据库上，是基础设施扩展手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database shard is one partition of data placed on a separate database for scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存保存常用数据副本以减少读取延迟，不是 Tic Tac Toe 的领域实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stores frequently used data copies to reduce read latency; it is not a Tic Tac Toe domain entity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，是基础设施组件，不是游戏领域的业务实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is infrastructure for caching content, not a business entity in the game domain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 鼠标输入事件，属于 UI 交互细节，不是核心游戏领域对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A MouseEvent is a UI input event, not a core game-domain object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于封装对象创建逻辑的设计模式，不是一个业务实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern encapsulates object-creation logic; it is not a business entity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过分步骤设置参数来构造复杂对象的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Builder pattern constructs a complex object through a step-by-step configuration process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证一个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

optionExplanations: DatabaseShard、Cache、CDN 是基础设施扩展手段，跟这道题的游戏规则完全无关。
MouseEvent、Pixel、Theme 都是 UI 交互细节，不是承载游戏状态的领域对象。
Game 驱动流程、Board 管棋盘和判胜、Player 代表参与者，三者正好覆盖需求里的状态归属。
Factory、Builder、Singleton 是创建对象的手段，本身不是业务领域里的实体。
optionExplanations_en: DatabaseShard, Cache, and CDN are infrastructure scaling tools unrelated to this game's rules.
MouseEvent, Pixel, and Theme are UI interaction details, not domain objects that own game state.
Game drives the flow, Board owns the grid and win checks, and Player represents each participant, together covering state ownership.
Factory, Builder, and Singleton are ways to construct objects, not business entities themselves.

scenario: 35 分钟的 Tic Tac Toe LLD 面试，已列出 Game、Board、Player，要先画清关系再写代码。
scenario_en: In a 35-minute Tic Tac Toe design interview you already have Game, Board, and Player, and the relationships must be settled before any code.
q: 定义实体关系时，最重要的问题之一是什么？
q_en: What is one of the most important questions when defining entity relationships?
options: 谁在继承体系里继承的类数量最多，越多说明职责越重
谁对外暴露的 public 方法数量最多，方法越多说明越核心
谁在运行时被实例化的次数最频繁，出现越多说明越重要
谁是 orchestrator，谁拥有持久状态，谁依赖谁
options_en: Whether a class inherits from the most classes — more inheritance is assumed to mean more responsibility.
Whether a class exposes the most public methods — more methods is assumed to mean it's more central.
Whether a class gets instantiated most often at runtime — appearing more is assumed to mean it matters more.
Who is the orchestrator, who owns durable state, and who depends on whom.
why: 关系图要回答谁驱动流程、谁拥有状态、谁依赖谁；这些边界决定后面每个类该暴露什么。
why_en: Relationships show who drives the flow, who owns state, and what each class must expose.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动主流程、调用其他对象完成整体行为的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator is the class that drives the main workflow by coordinating other objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类对外可调用的方法，数量多少不等于职责是否清晰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A public method is callable from outside the class; method count alone does not prove clear responsibility.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象需要长期保存并影响后续行为的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durable state is data an object keeps over time and uses to drive later behavior.

optionExplanations: 继承的类数量多少只是结构指标，不代表职责更重，也不会告诉你谁该拥有状态或驱动流程。
public 方法数量多不代表这个类更核心，可能只是接口设计得臃肿。
实例化次数多通常只说明这个类轻量常被复用，不代表它更重要或该拥有状态。
这条问题直接点名了主控流程的类、保存长期状态的类，以及各类之间的依赖方向。
optionExplanations_en: How many classes it inherits from is just a structural stat; more doesn't mean more responsibility, and it doesn't tell you who should own state or drive the flow.
A high public-method count doesn't mean the class is more central; it might just mean a bloated interface.
Getting instantiated often usually just means the class is lightweight and reused a lot, not that it matters more or should own state.
This question names the class that drives the flow, the one holding long-lived state, and how the classes depend on each other.

scenario: 你已经有 Game、Board、Player 三个实体，要开始展开类。
scenario_en: You already have Game, Board, and Player as entities, and now you need to expand them into classes.
q: 通常应先从哪个类开始？
q_en: Which class should you usually start with?
options: 依赖最少的辅助类，比如 Player
orchestrator，例如 Game
最复杂的支持类，比如 Board 的判胜逻辑
所有工具类和辅助方法
options_en: The supporting class with the fewest dependencies, such as Player.
The orchestrator, such as Game.
The most complex supporting class, such as Board's win-checking logic.
All utility classes and helper methods.
tradeoff: 先定驱动主流程的类 vs 先钻进某个支持类的实现细节
whenOtherWins: 如果某个支持类的规则极其复杂，也可以先展开它以尽早暴露风险。
why: 先从 Game 这种 orchestrator 开始，因为它串起主流程；定下它的调用点，Board 和 Player 才知道要暴露什么。
why_en: Start with Game because it coordinates the flow and reveals what Board and Player need to expose.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动主流程、调用其他对象完成整体行为的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator is the class that drives the main workflow by coordinating other objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 棋盘对象，通常负责保存格子状态并提供落子和判胜相关能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the grid object that usually stores cells and supports move and win checks.

optionExplanations: 先画 Player 这种依赖最少的辅助类，反而定不出它要配合谁、该暴露什么方法。
Game 是整条主流程的入口，先框出它要调用谁、传什么参数，两个支持类才知道自己该开放什么接口。
一上来就钻进 Board 判胜逻辑的细节，容易在主流程还没定的情况下白改设计。
把所有工具类和辅助方法都列一遍，抓不到谁在驱动整个游戏往前走。
optionExplanations_en: Starting with a low-dependency helper like Player leaves you unable to tell what it needs to expose or to whom.
Game is the entry point for the whole flow — pin down who it calls and what it passes first, and the two supporting classes know what to expose.
Diving straight into Board's win-check details risks reworking it once the main flow is finally set.
Listing every utility and helper class first doesn't reveal which class actually drives the game forward.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 面试进入类设计阶段，只剩十分钟定完每个类的字段与方法，之后直接写实现。
scenario_en: You reach the class-design step of a Tic Tac Toe interview with ten minutes left to fix each class fields and methods before coding.
q: 为每个类设计时，应回答哪两个问题？（多选）
q_en: Which two questions should you answer when designing each class? (Select all that apply.)
options: 它是否该直接读写别的类的私有字段
它需要记住什么状态
它能否负责所有事情
它需要提供什么行为或查询
options_en: Should it directly read and write another class's private fields?
What state does it need to remember?
Can it be made responsible for everything?
What behavior or queries does it need to expose?
why: 每个类只先回答两件事：记住什么状态、暴露什么行为；跨类改私有字段或做万能类都会打破职责边界。
why_en: For each class, define its state and behavior; private-field access and god objects break ownership boundaries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读取对象内部状态的方法；它不应该替代真正的业务行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter reads an object's internal state, but it should not replace real domain behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只应由本类内部访问和维护的字段，用来保护封装边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A private field should be accessed and maintained only inside its own class to preserve encapsulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 承担过多职责的类，通常会让规则、状态和修改点集中失控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A god object takes on too many responsibilities, making rules, state, and changes hard to control.

optionExplanations: 跨类直接读写别人的私有字段会绕开封装，让状态变更散落在调用方手里。
先问它要记住什么状态，是划出这个类边界的第一步。
让一个类能负责所有事情，就是典型的万能类，会让规则和状态全挤在一起。
再问它要对外提供什么行为或查询，状态和行为合起来才是完整的类设计。
optionExplanations_en: Reaching into another class's private fields bypasses encapsulation and scatters state changes into callers.
Asking what state it must remember is the first step in drawing that class's boundary.
Letting one class be responsible for everything is exactly how you end up with a god object.
Asking what behavior or queries it should expose completes the class design alongside its state.

scenario: 需求说“两名玩家轮流落子，游戏胜利或平局后结束”。
scenario_en: The requirements say two players take turns, and the game ends on a win or draw.
q: Game 类至少需要哪些状态？
q_en: What state does the Game class need at minimum?
options: board、两个 player、gameState，但省略 currentPlayer 和 winner
只有 board 和 winner，其余用临时变量代替
board、两个 player、currentPlayer、gameState、winner
board、currentPlayer、gameState、winner，但省略两个 player 的引用
options_en: board, both players, and gameState — but missing currentPlayer and winner.
Only board and winner, with everything else in temporary variables.
board, both players, currentPlayer, gameState, and winner.
board, currentPlayer, gameState, and winner — but missing references to both players.
whenOtherWins: 如果不需要单独查询 winner，可由 board 状态推导；但显式字段更不容易漏判胜负。
tradeoff: 状态完备覆盖判定条件 vs 用临时变量或省略字段图省事
why: 状态要从规则倒推：currentPlayer 决定轮到谁，两个 player 引用让 Game 能切换回合并记录赢家。
why_en: Derive state from the rules: currentPlayer controls turns, and player references let Game switch turns and record the winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前轮到落子的玩家引用，用来校验出手者并决定下一回合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer points to the player whose turn it is and is used to validate and advance moves.

termDefinitions.meaning: 游戏当前所处的状态，例如进行中、获胜或平局。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gameState tracks whether the game is in progress, won, or drawn.

termDefinitions.meaning: 获胜玩家的引用；没有赢家时通常为空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: winner points to the winning player, or stays null when nobody has won.

optionExplanations: 缺了 currentPlayer 就没法知道该轮到谁落子，缺了 winner 就没法记录结果。
只留 board 和 winner，靠临时变量凑轮次和进度，逻辑会散落在方法之间。
board、两个 player、currentPlayer、gameState、winner 齐了，正好覆盖轮次、进度和结果三件事。
省掉两个 player 的引用，Game 就没法在切换回合或判定赢家时拿到具体玩家对象。
optionExplanations_en: Without currentPlayer you can't tell whose turn it is, and without winner you can't record the result.
Keeping only board and winner forces turn and progress tracking into scattered temp variables.
board, both players, currentPlayer, gameState, and winner together cover turns, progress, and the result.
Dropping the player references leaves Game with no actual player object to switch turns or record a winner.

scenario: 需求需要玩家落子、查询当前玩家、查看游戏状态和赢家。
scenario_en: The requirements need players to move, query the current player, and inspect the game state and winner.
q: Game API 的合理方法集合是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable method set for the Game API?
options: makeMove 和 getBoard 两个方法，UI 没法查到该谁落子或赢家
makeMove、getCurrentPlayer、getGameState 三个方法，游戏结束却查不到赢家是谁
只保留 makeMove 一个方法，调用方连该谁落子都问不到
makeMove、getCurrentPlayer、getGameState、getWinner、getBoard
options_en: makeMove and getBoard — the UI can't tell whose turn it is or who won.
makeMove, getCurrentPlayer, and getGameState — but once the game ends there's still no way to query the winner.
Only the single method makeMove — callers can't even ask whose turn it is.
makeMove, getCurrentPlayer, getGameState, getWinner, and getBoard.
tradeoff: 覆盖需求隐含的全部操作和查询 vs 只实现动作、遗漏查询方法
whenOtherWins: 如果只要求展示核心行为，可以先只实现 makeMove，getter 留到有时间再补。
why: API 要覆盖需求里的动作和查询；少 getCurrentPlayer 或 getWinner，调用方就查不到轮次或结果。
why_en: The API must cover required actions and queries; without getCurrentPlayer or getWinner, callers cannot read turn or result state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类对外暴露的方法集合，调用方通过它与该类交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the set of methods a class exposes for other code to interact with it.

optionExplanations: 只有 makeMove 和 getBoard，调用方查不到轮到谁、也查不到赢家。
补了轮次和状态查询，却漏了 getWinner，游戏结束后调用方拿不到结果。
只暴露 makeMove，调用方连当前该谁落子都问不到，几乎没法驱动 UI。
makeMove 加四个查询方法，正好覆盖需求里要问的轮次、状态、赢家和棋盘。
optionExplanations_en: With only makeMove and getBoard, callers can't tell whose turn it is or who won.
Turn and state queries are covered, but missing getWinner leaves callers with no result once the game ends.
Exposing only makeMove means callers can't even ask whose turn it is, which barely drives a UI.
makeMove plus four query methods covers exactly what the requirements need: turn, state, winner, and board.

scenario: Tic Tac Toe 里多处都要校验落子合法性，规则被放进拥有格子矩阵的 Board，而非各自取 grid 判断。
scenario_en: Several call sites in Tic Tac Toe must validate a move, so the rule lives inside Board, which owns the grid, instead of each caller reading the grid.
q: “规则放在拥有相关状态的实体里”体现了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle is shown by putting rules inside the entity that owns the relevant state?
options: 封装（Tell, Don't Ask 原则）
遇事都用全局变量，图省事绕开类边界，谁都能改
干脆把所有业务逻辑都塞进 UI 层里
不断叠加继承层级，靠子类复用代码来解决
options_en: Encapsulation (the Tell, Don't Ask principle).
Reaching for global variables so any code can dodge class boundaries and mutate state.
Dumping all the business logic straight into the UI layer.
Piling on inheritance layers to reuse code through subclassing.
why: 拥有状态的对象也该执行相关规则；不要把内部数据交给外部调用方拼判断，否则 bug 会散在多处。
why_en: The object that owns the state should enforce the rule; leaking data outward scatters bugs across callers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把状态和操作该状态的逻辑绑定在同一个类里，不对外暴露内部细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation bundles state with the logic that operates on it and hides internal details from callers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让对象自己执行操作，而不是先问出它的内部状态再由外部决定怎么做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tell, Don't Ask means telling an object to perform an action instead of asking for its internal state and deciding externally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，负责展示和输入，不应承载核心业务规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input, and should not own core business rules.

optionExplanations: 谁拥有状态谁就执行相关规则，这正是封装和 Tell, Don't Ask 的做法。
全局变量会让任何代码都能改状态，规则反而无处安身。
把逻辑全塞进 UI，会让核心规则跟着界面变化一起被改坏。
过度继承是在拿类层级解决状态归属问题，跟这条原则没关系。
optionExplanations_en: The object that owns the state enforces its own rules, exactly what encapsulation and Tell, Don't Ask mean.
Global variables let any code mutate state, leaving the rule with no real owner.
Cramming all logic into the UI ties core rules to whatever the interface happens to do.
Over-inheritance tries to solve state ownership with a class hierarchy, a different problem entirely.

rows: 调用方取 grid 判断

q: 把实现核心方法的推荐顺序排好：
q_en: Put the recommended core-method implementation sequence in order.
steps: 枚举非法输入、非法状态等边界情况
把正常流程写成清晰伪代码
先口头走 happy path
必要时补充返回值和状态变化
why: 先口头跑主流程，让面试官知道方法正常怎么走；再补非法输入和非法状态，最后写成伪代码和状态变化。
why_en: Walk the happy path first, then add invalid inputs and states before writing pseudocode and state changes.
tradeoff: 先讲主流程再补边界 vs 一开始陷入分支细节
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官要求直接写代码，就边写边口头标出 happy path 和边界检查。
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["walk happy path"] --> B["list invalid states and inputs"]
B --> C["write clear pseudocode"]
C --> D["name return values"]
D --> E["show state changes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有异常或错误发生时的主流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the main flow when nothing goes wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接近代码结构但不绑定具体语言语法的表达方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudocode describes code-like logic without committing to a specific programming language syntax.

scenario: 你要实现 Tic Tac Toe 的 makeMove，展示状态检查、落子、胜负和平局处理。
scenario_en: You are implementing Tic Tac Toe's makeMove to show state checks, placing a mark, win handling, and draw handling.
q: 这段伪代码最重要的结构特征是什么？
q_en: What is the most important structural feature of this pseudocode?
codeSample:
makeMove(player, row, col):
    if state != IN_PROGRESS or player != currentPlayer: return false
    if not board.canPlace(row, col): return false
    board.placeMark(row, col, player.mark)
    if board.checkWin(row, col, player.mark):
        state, winner = WON, player
    elif board.isFull():
        state = DRAW
    else:
        currentPlayer = otherPlayer()
    return true
options: 把所有规则放到 UI
先拒绝非法状态和动作，再执行状态转换
忽略 currentPlayer
只实现 reset
options_en: Put all the rules in the UI layer.
Reject illegal state or moves first, then apply the state transition.
Ignore currentPlayer entirely.
Only implement reset.
tradeoff: 前置校验保证不变量 vs 直接改状态、事后再补校验
whenOtherWins: 如果要用异常表达失败而不是布尔返回值，可以把 return false 换成 throw，但校验-变更-判定终局的顺序不变。
why: 这段代码先用 guard clause 拒绝非法状态和动作，再落子、判胜负、切回合；顺序清楚才不容易破坏不变量。
why_en: Use guard clauses first, then place the mark, check terminal states, and switch turns so invariants stay intact.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS --> WON : checkWin
IN_PROGRESS --> DRAW : board full
IN_PROGRESS --> IN_PROGRESS : valid non-terminal move
WON --> [*]
DRAW --> [*]

termDefinitions.meaning: 函数开头用来提前拒绝非法输入或非法状态的判断语句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guard clause is an early check that rejects invalid input or state before the main logic runs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层，只负责展示和输入，不应该保存 Tic Tac Toe 的核心规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input, and should not store Tic Tac Toe's core rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前轮到落子的玩家，用来拒绝非本回合玩家的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the player whose turn it is and is used to reject out-of-turn moves.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 的三种状态：进行中、已获胜、已平局。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IN_PROGRESS, WON, and DRAW are the three states a Game can be in.

optionExplanations: 代码里根本没有 UI，规则全在 makeMove 里执行，这个说法对不上代码结构。
方法开头的 guard clause 先把不合法的状态和越权动作挡在外面，然后才推进落子、判定和换手。
代码第一行就用 currentPlayer 校验出手者，说忽略它跟代码直接矛盾。
这段代码根本没有 reset 方法，只实现了落子和终局判断。
optionExplanations_en: There's no UI in this snippet at all; every rule runs inside makeMove, so this doesn't match the structure.
The guard clauses up front block illegal state or out-of-turn moves, then the code moves on to placing the mark, checking the result, and switching turns.
The very first check validates currentPlayer, so claiming it's ignored contradicts the code.
This snippet has no reset method at all; it only implements placing a move and checking terminal states.

scenario: 45 分钟的 LLD 面试只剩 15 分钟实现核心 makeMove，你在犹豫要不要先加一层 Factory。
scenario_en: With 15 minutes left in a 45-minute design interview to implement the core makeMove, you are debating whether to add a Factory layer first.
q: 在实现阶段强行塞 Singleton、Factory、Builder 等模式的常见风险是什么？
q_en: What is the common risk of forcing Singleton, Factory, or Builder into the implementation phase?
options: 一定提升可读性
能替代需求澄清
过度设计，浪费时间并模糊核心逻辑
保证所有 follow-up 自动解决
options_en: It always improves readability.
It can substitute for requirements clarification.
Overengineering — it wastes time and obscures the core logic.
It guarantees every follow-up question is automatically handled.
why: 模式要服务真实变化点；如果只是为了显得高级，反而会拖慢实现并遮住核心状态转换。
why_en: Patterns help only when they solve real variation; forced patterns hide the core state transition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证一个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装对象创建逻辑，让调用方不用关心具体子类的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern encapsulates object-creation logic so callers do not depend on concrete subclasses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过分步骤设置参数构造复杂对象的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Builder pattern constructs a complex object through a step-by-step configuration process.

optionExplanations: 硬套模式不一定更好读，反而经常让核心状态转换被多一层抽象包住。
模式解决的是代码结构问题，不能替代需求还没澄清这件事。
为了显得高级硬塞 Singleton、Factory，会占用时间还把核心状态转换埋进抽象层。
模式跟 follow-up 是否被覆盖没有必然关系，能不能应对全看设计本身。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing a pattern in doesn't automatically read better; it often buries the core state transition under an extra layer.
Patterns solve structural problems; they can't substitute for requirements that were never clarified.
Forcing in Singleton or Factory just to look sophisticated burns time and buries the core state transition.
Whether follow-ups get handled has nothing to do with using a pattern; that depends on the design itself.

scenario: 你刚写完 makeMove 的伪代码，要用一个具体走查来验证逻辑，而不是只读代码。
scenario_en: You just wrote makeMove pseudocode and need a concrete walkthrough to verify the logic, not just read the code.
q: 一次好的走查应该覆盖哪些内容？（多选）
q_en: What should a good walkthrough cover? (Select all that apply.)
options: 初始状态
只口头描述，不用具体输入输出
每一步操作发生了什么
每步后状态如何变化
options_en: The initial state.
Only a verbal description without concrete inputs and outputs.
What happens on each operation.
How state changes after each step.
why: 走查要从具体初始状态开始，逐步核对每次操作后的状态；这样才能发现没切回合、没触发胜负这类逻辑 bug。
why_en: Start from a concrete initial state and check state after each move to catch missed turn switches or win checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tic Tac Toe 的核心落子方法，负责校验、更新棋盘并推进游戏状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove is the core Tic Tac Toe method that validates a move, updates the board, and advances game state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用具体输入一步步模拟方法执行，检查每一步后的状态是否正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A walkthrough simulates concrete inputs step by step and checks the state after each operation.

optionExplanations: 从一个具体的初始状态开始，走查才有一个可核对的起点。
只靠口头描述、不带具体输入输出，很容易漏掉边界情况却察觉不到。
逐步说清每一步操作做了什么，才能对上代码实际执行的逻辑。
每步后核对状态变化，才抓得到没切回合、没触发胜负这类隐藏 bug。
optionExplanations_en: Starting from a concrete initial state gives the walkthrough a checkable baseline.
A purely verbal description with no concrete input or output makes edge cases easy to miss unnoticed.
Spelling out what each operation actually does is what lets you match it against the real code.
Checking the state after each step is what catches hidden bugs like a missed turn switch or win check.

scenario: 新增需求：Tic Tac Toe 要支持撤销最近一步棋（undo）。
scenario_en: New requirement: Tic Tac Toe must support undoing the most recent move.
q: 最直接的实现方向是什么？
q_en: What is the most direct implementation direction?
options: 把所有类和方法都推倒重写，连带删掉 Board 里已验证过的落子记录方式
在 UI 按钮的点击处理函数里直接改字段，完全跳过 Game 的方法和校验逻辑
给每一个方法都加事务日志，undo 时回滚整个应用状态而不只是棋盘
状态变化集中在 makeMove，加命令历史栈记录落子前状态，undo 弹栈回滚
options_en: Rewrite every class and method from scratch, including how Board already tracks placed marks.
Mutate fields directly inside the UI button's click handler, completely bypassing Game's methods and validation logic.
Add a transaction log to every method and roll back the entire application state, not just the board.
Since state changes are centralized in makeMove, add a command history stack recording the state before each move, and undo pops it.
tradeoff: 复用集中式状态变更点 vs 为 undo 重建应用级事务机制
whenOtherWins: 如果状态很大或历史很多，需要讨论快照、命令差量和内存成本。
why: undo 能自然接上，是因为状态变化都经过 makeMove；在这个入口记录旧状态，回滚就不用改散落的字段。
why_en: Undo fits cleanly because all mutation goes through makeMove, so one history stack can restore the prior state.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["makeMove is the only state-changing path"] --> B["record successful move"]
B --> C["push prior state to history"]
C --> D["undo pops history"]
D --> E["restore board, turn, state, winner"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面层；直接在按钮处理函数里改状态会绕开 Game 的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User Interface handles display and input; mutating state in a button handler bypasses Game's rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录状态变更以便恢复或回滚的日志；本题只需要棋局级历史，不需要应用级事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction log records state changes for recovery or rollback; this problem only needs game-level history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每次操作前状态的栈结构，undo 时弹出最近一条记录来回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A command history stack records the state before each action so undo can pop the most recent entry and roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次操作封装成对象，可以记录、排队或撤销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Command pattern encapsulates an action as an object so it can be logged, queued, or undone.

optionExplanations: 把类推倒重写还顺带删掉 Board 记录落子的方式，等于把已验证的设计全部作废。
在 UI 点击处理函数里直接改字段会绕开 Game 的规则，状态变更就不再只经过一个入口。
给每个方法都加事务日志、回滚整个应用状态，远超 undo 一步棋所需要的范围。
makeMove 是棋局里唯一改状态的地方，把落子前的快照存进一个栈，undo 直接弹栈还原即可，改动量最小。
optionExplanations_en: Rewriting every class and deleting how Board tracks marks throws away a design that already works.
Mutating fields directly in a UI click handler bypasses Game's rules, so state changes no longer flow through one entry point.
Adding a transaction log to every method and rolling back the whole app is far more than undoing one move needs.
Since state only ever changes inside makeMove, saving a snapshot there before each move and popping it on undo keeps the change minimal.

q: 补全类设计口诀：
q_en: Complete the class-design rule of thumb:
text: 逐个实体回答两个问题：这个类要记住什么{{状态}}，以及它要提供什么{{行为}}。
why: 状态和行为都要从需求推出来；这样类既不会只是空壳，也不会变成什么都管的万能对象。
why_en: Derive both state and behavior from requirements so the class is neither empty nor a god object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象需要记住并影响后续行为的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State is data an object remembers and uses to drive later behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象对外提供的操作或查询，通常来自需求里的动作。
