why_en: This is the biggest professionalism tell: method/variable casing follows the language — the camelCase camp (Java/JS/TS/C#/Kotlin/Swift) vs the snake_case camp (Python/Ruby/Rust). Class names are PascalCase everywhere, but do not mix methods: get_user in Java or getUser in Python instantly looks amateur.
tradeoff: camelCase 阵营(Java/JS/C#/Kotlin/Swift) vs snake_case 阵营(Python/Ruby/Rust)——方法/变量随语言,类名恒 PascalCase

scenario: 定义一个「最大重试次数」的常量。
scenario_en: Defining a "max retries" constant.
q: 常量通常怎么命名？
q_en: How are constants typically named?
options: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE：MAX_RETRIES
camelCase：maxRetries
PascalCase：MaxRetries（在多数语言里看起来像个类名）
随便，常量命名没约定
options_en: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: MAX_RETRIES
camelCase: maxRetries
PascalCase: MaxRetries (looks like a class name in most languages)
Anything; constants have no convention
optionExplanations: 对：全大写下划线在一屏代码里自成一类,读者立刻知道不该在运行时改它。
错：camelCase 是普通变量,读者分不出它是常量。
错：PascalCase 在多数语言里像类名(C# 是例外)。
错：常量有明确约定,不能随便。
optionExplanations_en: Right: all-caps-underscore stands out on screen, so readers instantly know it must not be mutated at runtime.
Wrong: camelCase reads as an ordinary variable; readers cannot tell it is constant.
Wrong: PascalCase looks like a class name in most languages (C# is the exception).
Wrong: constants do have a clear convention.
why: 常量用 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE(全大写+下划线):MAX_RETRIES。通行于 Java/JS/Python/C++,一眼传达「不可变配置值」。(Go/C# 例外,用 PascalCase。)
why_en: Constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (all-caps + underscores): MAX_RETRIES, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS. Common in Java/JS/Python/C++; it signals "immutable config value" at a glance. (Go/C# are exceptions, using PascalCase.)

scenario: 给类和方法起名时的语义规则。
scenario_en: The semantic rule when naming classes and methods.
q: 类名和方法名在词性上应该是？
q_en: What part of speech should class vs method names be?
options: 类=名词，方法=动词短语
类名用动词、方法名用名词
类名和方法名都统一用名词就行，不用区分词性
词性无所谓，能跑就行
options_en: class = noun, method = verb phrase
Class names are verbs; method names are nouns
Both class and method names can just be nouns, no need to distinguish
Part of speech does not matter as long as it runs
optionExplanations: 对：类=事物(名词)、方法=动作(动词),读代码像读句子,意图自明。
错：反过来会让 API 读起来别扭(order.paymentProcessor() ？)。
错：方法用名词(order.payment())读者不知道它「做」什么。
错：词性直接决定可读性,不是能跑就行。
optionExplanations_en: Right: class = thing (noun), method = action (verb); code reads like sentences and intent is self-evident.
Wrong: reversing makes APIs awkward (order.paymentProcessor()?).
Wrong: a noun method (order.payment()) hides what it does.
Wrong: part of speech drives readability; "it runs" is not enough.
why: 类名用名词(是什么:Order、PaymentProcessor),方法名用动词短语(做什么:createOrder、chargeCard、isExpired)。这样 order.charge(card) 读起来就是一句话,意图自明。
why_en: Class names are nouns (what it is: Order, PaymentProcessor); method names are verb phrases (what it does: createOrder, chargeCard, isExpired). Then `order.charge(card)` reads like a sentence with self-evident intent. Query methods often start with get/is/has.
tradeoff: 类=名词、方法=动词(调用处读成一句话) vs 词性混用(order.paymentProcessor() 这类别扭 API)

scenario: 给一个表示「账号是否激活」的布尔字段/方法命名。
scenario_en: Naming a boolean field/method for "is the account active".
q: 布尔值怎么命名最专业？
q_en: How to name a boolean most professionally?
options: 用 is/has/can 前缀：isActive、hasPermission
用名词：active、permission、dispense，读到时再自己判断
用 flag1、flag2 这类通用名
用动词命令式：activate、dispense
options_en: is/has/can prefix: isActive, hasPermission
Nouns: active, permission, dispense — judge for yourself when reading
Use generic names like flag1, flag2
Use imperative verbs: activate, dispense
optionExplanations: 对：is/has/can 前缀让 `if (user.isActive)` 读起来就是个真假判断,一眼知道是布尔。
错：裸名词读者分不清是布尔还是对象。
错：flag1/flag2 毫无表意。
错：activate 像个会改状态的动作方法,不是布尔查询。
optionExplanations_en: Right: an is/has/can prefix makes `if (user.isActive)` read as a truth test — obviously boolean.
Wrong: a bare noun leaves readers unsure if it is a boolean or an object.
Wrong: flag1/flag2 conveys nothing.
Wrong: activate looks like a state-changing action, not a boolean query.
why: 布尔用 is/has/can 前缀,让它读起来像个是非判断:isActive、canDispense。if(order.isPaid) 一眼可读;裸名词 if(order.paid) 就含糊,分不清布尔还是对象。
why_en: Booleans take an is/has/can/should prefix so they read as a yes/no test: isActive, hasPermission, canDispense, isExpired. `if (order.isPaid)` reads clearly; a bare noun `if (order.paid)` is ambiguous about whether it is a boolean or an object.
tradeoff: is/has/can 前缀(读作是非判断) vs 裸名词 paid(短一点·代价是分不清布尔还是对象)

scenario: 给「校验规则」的接口/抽象基类命名。
scenario_en: Naming the interface/abstract base for a "validation rule".
q: 接口该怎么命名？
q_en: How should you name an interface?
options: PascalCase 名词或 -able：ValidationRule、Comparable
统一加匈牙利前缀 I：IValidationRule、IPaymentMethod（多数语言不推荐）
用小写 snake_case：validation_rule
在名字里带上具体实现：CreditCardValidationRuleImpl
options_en: PascalCase noun or -able: ValidationRule, Comparable
Prefix everything with Hungarian I: IValidationRule, IPaymentMethod (discouraged in most languages)
Lowercase snake_case: validation_rule
Bake the concrete impl into the name: CreditCardValidationRuleImpl
optionExplanations: 对：接口是 PascalCase 名词或能力形容词(-able);它描述「能力/角色」,不该暴露实现。
错：I 前缀是 C#/旧 COM 习惯,Java/Python/Go/Swift 里不地道。
错：接口不用 snake_case,类型名恒 PascalCase。
错：接口名不该带 Impl/具体实现,那是给实现类留的。
optionExplanations_en: Right: an interface is a PascalCase noun or capability adjective (-able); it names a capability/role and should not leak the implementation.
Wrong: the I prefix is a C#/legacy-COM habit, non-idiomatic in Java/Python/Go/Swift.
Wrong: interfaces are not snake_case; type names are always PascalCase.
Wrong: an interface name should not contain Impl/a concrete implementation — that is for the impl class.
why: 接口/抽象类用 PascalCase,取名反映能力或角色:名词(ValidationRule)或 -able(Comparable)。别用匈牙利 IFoo(除 C#),也别把具体实现塞进接口名。
why_en: Interfaces/abstract classes are PascalCase, named for a capability or role: a noun (ValidationRule, PaymentMethod) or an -able adjective (Comparable, Iterable). Avoid Hungarian IFoo (outside the C# ecosystem) and do not bake a concrete implementation into the interface name. The impl class carries specificity: CreditCardPayment implements PaymentMethod.
tradeoff: 名词/-able 接口名(表能力·跨语言地道) vs I 前缀(C# 习惯·他处不地道)
whenOtherWins: 如果代码库在 C#/.NET 生态里,IValidationRule 这种 I 前缀反而是官方与团队既定惯例,跟着写才地道;新写 Java/Go/Python 则不用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在标识符前加类型/用途前缀的老习惯(如接口 IFoo、成员 m_x、字符串 strName)。现代多数语言(Java/Python/Go/Swift)不推荐,认为它冗余且易过时;C# 生态仍保留接口 I 前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hungarian notation prefixes identifiers with their type/role (e.g. interface IFoo, member m_x, string strName). Most modern languages (Java/Python/Go/Swift) discourage it as redundant and stale-prone; the C# ecosystem still keeps the interface I prefix.

scenario: 给变量和方法起名时要不要缩写。
scenario_en: Whether to abbreviate when naming variables and methods.
q: 关于缩写和表意，哪种做法更专业？
q_en: On abbreviations and intent, which is more professional?
options: 名字表意、不含糊缩写：elapsedMs、userCount
尽量缩短，能省字母就省：usr、cnt、calc
用 data、info、manager、handler 这类万能空词就够
变量都叫 a、b、c，反正自己看得懂
options_en: Intent-revealing, no cryptic abbreviations: elapsedMs, userCount
Shorten aggressively, drop letters where you can: usr, cnt, calc
Generic empty words like data, info, manager, handler are enough
Name variables a, b, c — you understand them yourself
optionExplanations: 对：表意命名让读者无需猜;循环里的 i 等公认短名可以,但业务变量要说人话。
错：省字母省不了多少,却大幅增加理解成本。
错：这类词放到任何类上都成立,等于没描述职责。
错：a/b/c 只有你当下懂,面试官和未来的你都要重新猜。
optionExplanations_en: Right: intent-revealing names spare the reader guessing; well-known short names like loop i are fine, but business variables should read plainly.
Wrong: dropping letters saves little but greatly raises comprehension cost.
Wrong: such words fit any class, so they describe no responsibility at all.
Wrong: a/b/c only you understand right now; the interviewer and future-you must re-guess.
why: 名字要表达意图,别含糊缩写:elapsedMs 胜过 e、userCount 胜过 cnt。例外是公认惯例(循环 i/j、坐标 x/y)。也避开 data/info/manager 这类万能空词。清晰 > 简短。
why_en: Names should reveal intent, not use cryptic abbreviations: elapsedMs beats e, userCount beats cnt, retryAttempt beats r. Exceptions are well-known idioms (loop i/j, coordinates x/y). Also avoid catch-all empty words like data/info/manager. Clear > short — an interviewer understanding it at first glance is what reads as professional.
tradeoff: 表意全名 elapsedMs(读者不用猜) vs 短缩写 e/cnt(少敲几个字母·换来理解成本)——清晰 > 简短

scenario: 设计取某个用户的 REST 端点。
scenario_en: Designing the REST endpoint to fetch a user.
q: 资源路径该怎么写？
q_en: How should you write the resource path?
options: 复数名词、无动词：GET /users/123、GET /users/123/orders
路径里带动词：GET /getUser?id=123
单数名词：GET /user/123、POST /user
每个操作一个独立路径：/createUser、/deleteUser、/updateUser
options_en: Plural nouns, no verbs: GET /users/123, GET /users/123/orders
Verbs in the path: GET /getUser?id=123
Singular nouns: GET /user/123, POST /user
One path per operation: /createUser, /deleteUser, /updateUser
optionExplanations: 对：资源用复数名词,同一 /users 既表集合也表其下的 /users/123,动作交给 HTTP 方法。
错：路径带动词是 RPC 风格,不是 REST;/getUser 里 GET 已表意。
错：单复数混用不一致;主流约定是集合用复数。
错：为每个动作建路径正是 REST 要避免的,动作应由方法承载。
optionExplanations_en: Right: resources are plural nouns; the same /users covers the collection and /users/123 under it, with actions handled by HTTP methods.
Wrong: verbs in the path are RPC-style, not REST; GET already conveys the action in /getUser.
Wrong: mixing singular/plural is inconsistent; the mainstream convention is plural for collections.
Wrong: a path per action is exactly what REST avoids; actions belong to methods.
why: REST 资源路径用复数名词、不带动词:GET /users/123、POST /users、GET /users/123/orders。同一个 /users 既是集合又派生单个资源,一致可预测。动词交给 HTTP 方法,不写进 URL。
why_en: REST resource paths use plural nouns and no verbs: GET /users/123, POST /users, GET /users/123/orders. The same /users is both the collection and the base for a single resource — consistent and predictable. Verbs (create/delete) go to HTTP methods, not the URL.
tradeoff: 复数名词资源路径(动作交给 HTTP 方法) vs 动词路径 /getUser(RPC 风格·端点数随操作膨胀)

scenario: 路径里出现多词资源，比如「用户档案」。
scenario_en: A multi-word resource in the path, e.g. "user profiles".
q: URL 路径段的大小写该怎么写？
q_en: What casing do URL path segments use?
options: 全小写 + kebab-case：/user-profiles
camelCase：/userProfiles
snake_case：/user_profiles（下划线，更像数据库风格）
PascalCase：/UserProfiles
options_en: All-lowercase + kebab-case: /user-profiles
camelCase: /userProfiles
snake_case: /user_profiles (underscores, more of a database style)
PascalCase: /UserProfiles
optionExplanations: 对：URL 惯例是全小写 + 连字符,清晰且避开大小写敏感带来的坑。
错：camelCase 在 URL 里别扭,还可能因大小写敏感出问题。
错：下划线更像数据库/JSON 约定,URL 里少见,还容易被下划线装饰遮住。
错：URL 里用 PascalCase 极不常见。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the URL convention is all-lowercase + hyphens — clear and avoids case-sensitivity pitfalls.
Wrong: camelCase looks awkward in URLs and can break on case sensitivity.
Wrong: underscores are more of a database/JSON convention, rare in URLs, and can hide under link underlines.
Wrong: PascalCase in URLs is highly unusual.
why: URL 路径段用全小写 + kebab-case(连字符):/user-profiles。web 标准约定,比 camelCase(大小写敏感)、snake_case(更像 DB/JSON)都清晰。注意跟 JSON 字段约定不同,别混。
why_en: URL path segments use all-lowercase + kebab-case (hyphens): /user-profiles, /shipping-addresses. This is the web-standard convention — clearer than camelCase (case-sensitivity risk) or snake_case (more DB/JSON). Note this differs from the JSON-field convention; do not mix them.
tradeoff: URL 用 kebab-case(全小写·避开大小写敏感) vs camelCase/snake_case(更像代码标识符或 DB 字段)

termDefinitions.meaning: 全小写、单词间用连字符 - 连接(user-profiles)。因为形似串在扦子上的烤串(kebab)得名。是 URL 路径段的通行约定:清晰、无大小写敏感问题;但不能用于多数编程语言的标识符(- 会被当成减号)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: kebab-case is all-lowercase with words joined by hyphens (user-profiles), named for looking like items on a skewer (kebab). It is the standard for URL path segments — clear and case-insensitive-safe — but cannot be used for identifiers in most languages (the hyphen parses as minus).

scenario: 要「创建一个订单」和「取消一个订单」。
scenario_en: You need to "create an order" and "cancel an order".
q: 「动作」应该体现在哪里？
q_en: Where should the "action" live?
options: 动作放 HTTP 方法：POST /orders、DELETE /orders/9
体现在 URL 上：POST /createOrder、POST /cancelOrder
全用 GET，动作放在查询参数里：GET /orders?action=create
每个动作用不同端口区分
options_en: Action in the HTTP method: POST /orders, DELETE /orders/9
In the URL: POST /createOrder, POST /cancelOrder
All GET, action in a query param: GET /orders?action=create
Distinguish each action by a different port
optionExplanations: 对：方法本身就是动作词表,客户端与网关看方法即知语义(GET 可缓存、DELETE 幂等)。
错：把动词塞进 URL 是 RPC 风格,丢掉了 HTTP 方法的语义。
错：全 GET 违反语义(GET 应无副作用),还会被缓存/预取误伤。
错：用端口区分动作是奇技淫巧,毫无必要。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the method set is the action vocabulary — clients and gateways read semantics off it (GET cacheable, DELETE idempotent).
Wrong: putting verbs in the URL is RPC-style and discards HTTP-method semantics.
Wrong: all-GET violates semantics (GET must be side-effect-free) and gets hit by caching/prefetch.
Wrong: distinguishing actions by port is a hack with no benefit.
why: REST 里动作由 HTTP 方法承载,不写进 URL:POST 建、GET 读、PATCH 改、DELETE 删。URL 始终只描述资源。所以路径里几乎不该出现 create/get/update/delete 这类动词。
why_en: In REST the action is carried by the HTTP method, not the URL: POST /orders to create, GET /orders/9 to read, PATCH /orders/9 to update, DELETE /orders/9 to delete. The URL always names the resource only. So you should almost never see verbs like create/get/update/delete in a path.
tradeoff: 动作放 HTTP 方法(REST·URL 只指资源) vs 动词写进 URL(RPC 风格·丢方法语义)

scenario: 设计 API 返回的 JSON body 字段名。
scenario_en: Designing the field names in an API JSON body.
q: JSON 字段大小写怎么定最专业？
q_en: How to decide JSON field casing professionally?
options: camelCase 或 snake_case 选一种，全程一致
每个端点随手用不同风格，反正字段名能对上就行
JSON 字段必须和 URL 保持一样，统一都用 kebab-case
JSON 字段必须用 PascalCase
options_en: Pick camelCase or snake_case, stay consistent throughout
Use a different style per endpoint at will, as long as field names match up
JSON fields must match URLs and all use kebab-case
JSON fields must use PascalCase
optionExplanations: 对：camelCase(常见于 JS/Node 系)和 snake_case(Stripe/Twitter 等)都可,关键是全程一致。
错：风格不一致会让客户端解析混乱、显得业余。
错：kebab-case 的连字符在多数语言里不能直接做字段名(obj.user-name 报错)。
错：PascalCase 不是 JSON 字段的通行约定(.NET 老风格除外)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: both camelCase (common in JS/Node) and snake_case (Stripe/Twitter) are fine; what matters is consistency throughout.
Wrong: inconsistent styles confuse client parsing and read as amateur.
Wrong: kebab-case hyphens cannot be field names directly in most languages (obj.user-name errors).
Wrong: PascalCase is not the common JSON-field convention (legacy .NET aside).
why: JSON 字段 camelCase 或 snake_case 都行,关键是选一种、全 API 一致。别用 kebab-case(连字符不能当字段名)。注意 URL 用 kebab、JSON 用 camel/snake,两层不同别混。
why_en: JSON body fields can be camelCase or snake_case (camelCase is common in JS/Node; snake_case appears in Stripe, Twitter, etc.) — the key is picking one and staying consistent across the whole API. Do not use kebab-case (hyphens cannot be field names in most languages). Note: URLs use kebab-case while JSON fields use camel/snake — two different layers, do not mix.
tradeoff: JSON 字段 camelCase vs snake_case——两者都专业,取舍不在选哪个,而在全 API 是否一致
whenOtherWins: 如果 API 要兼容 .NET 老客户端,PascalCase 字段可能早已是既定契约——这时保持现有契约优先于换成 camelCase。

scenario: 要「取第 2 页、状态为 active、按创建时间倒序」的用户。
scenario_en: Fetch users on page 2, status active, sorted by creation time descending.
q: 过滤 / 排序 / 分页这些参数放哪？
q_en: Where do filter/sort/pagination params go?
options: 查询参数：?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at
编进路径：GET /users/active/page/2/sort/created-desc
放进请求体，即使是 GET
放 HTTP 头里传
options_en: Query params: ?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at
Encoded into the path: GET /users/active/page/2/sort/created-desc
In the request body, even for GET
Passed in HTTP headers
optionExplanations: 对：过滤/排序/分页是对同一集合的「修饰」,用查询参数最贴切、可组合、可省略。
错：把这些编进路径会让路径爆炸,且语义上它们不是资源层级。
错：GET 一般不带 body,很多客户端/代理会忽略它。
错：这类业务参数放 header 不合常规,难发现难调试。
optionExplanations_en: Right: filter/sort/pagination modify the same collection, so query params fit best — composable and optional.
Wrong: encoding them into the path explodes the path and misrepresents them as resource hierarchy.
Wrong: GET usually carries no body; many clients/proxies ignore it.
Wrong: putting business params in headers is unconventional, hard to discover and debug.
why: 过滤、排序、分页用查询参数,不进路径:GET /users?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at。它们是对集合的「修饰」,可组合可省略。路径表达资源层级,query 表达对集合的筛选与视图。
why_en: Filtering, sorting, and pagination go in the query string, not the path: GET /users?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at. They modify the same collection resource — composable and optional. The path expresses resource hierarchy (/users/123/orders); the query expresses filtering and views over a collection.
tradeoff: 过滤/排序/分页放 query(可组合可省略) vs 编进路径(路径组合爆炸·把筛选伪装成资源层级)

scenario: 复盘让 OOD/API 代码显得业余的命名失误。
scenario_en: Review naming mistakes that make OOD/API code look amateur.
q: 下面哪些会让你的代码一眼显得业余？（多选）
q_en: Which make your code look amateur at a glance? (multi-select)
options: 在 Java 里给方法用 snake_case、或在 Python 里给方法用 camelCase
REST 路径写成动词：POST /createUser、GET /getOrder
同一个 API 里 JSON 字段一会儿 camelCase 一会儿 snake_case
类名用 PascalCase、方法名跟随语言惯例、常量用 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
options_en: snake_case methods in Java, or camelCase methods in Python
REST paths written as verbs: POST /createUser, GET /getOrder
JSON fields flip-flopping between camelCase and snake_case within one API
PascalCase classes, methods following the language idiom, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants
optionExplanations: 错误:方法大小写用错语言的惯例,是最刺眼的外行信号。
错误:动词进 URL 是 RPC 风格,丢掉 HTTP 方法语义。
错误:同一 API 内 JSON 风格不一致,客户端解析混乱、显得随意。
这是对的:类 PascalCase + 方法随语言 + 常量全大写,正是专业基线。
optionExplanations_en: Mistake: wrong-language method casing is the most glaring amateur signal.
Mistake: verbs in the URL are RPC-style and discard HTTP-method semantics.
Mistake: inconsistent JSON style within one API confuses clients and reads as careless.
This is correct: PascalCase classes + language-idiomatic methods + all-caps constants is the professional baseline.
why: 三个高频失分:①方法大小写用错语言惯例(Java 写 snake_case)②REST 路径带动词(/createUser)③同一 API 内 JSON 字段风格不一致。正解见前面各卡的组合。
why_en: Four common losses: (1) wrong-language method casing (snake_case in Java); (2) verbs in REST paths (/createUser); (3) inconsistent JSON field style within one API; (4) (the fix) PascalCase classes + language-idiomatic methods + SCREAMING_SNAKE constants + kebab-case URLs. Consistent + idiomatic = professional.
tradeoff: 跟随语言惯例与 REST 约定(专业基线) vs 自创混用风格(省下查约定的时间·换来一眼外行的印象)

q: 设计原则和 OOP 概念在 LLD 里各自负责什么？
q_en: In low-level design, what job does each of design principles and OOP concepts do?
options: 两者是互不相关的两套独立知识
OOP 概念只在系统设计面试才会考，LLD 白板题只考数据结构和算法
设计原则决定取舍方向，OOP 概念是实现这些取舍的语言机制
设计原则的内容只适用于前端框架代码
options_en: The two pages are unrelated, independent topics.
OOP concepts are only tested in system-design interviews — LLD whiteboard rounds only test data structures and algorithms.
Design principles decide the direction of a tradeoff, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that implement it.
Design principles only apply to frontend framework code.
why: 设计原则回答“该怎么取舍”，封装、抽象、多态、继承回答“怎么把取舍写进类和接口里”。两者是同一决策链的上下游。
why_en: Design principles decide what tradeoff to make, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that turn that tradeoff into classes and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层次设计（LLD）：面试中要求把需求落到具体类、接口和方法的设计环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage that asks you to turn requirements into concrete classes, interfaces, and methods.

optionExplanations: 把两者当成孤立知识会让你在面试里各说各话；实际上原则给方向，OOP 概念给落地方式。
LLD 白板题不只考数据结构和算法，还要求把取舍落成类和接口，OOP 概念天天用到。
对：原则先定取舍方向，接口、封装、继承再把这个方向落成具体代码结构。
设计原则同样适用于后端类设计，把它限定在前端框架是范围搞错了。
optionExplanations_en: Treating them as unrelated leaves you unable to connect tradeoffs to code in an interview — principles set direction, OOP concepts implement it.
LLD whiteboard rounds test more than data structures and algorithms — they require turning tradeoffs into classes and interfaces, where OOP concepts show up constantly.
Correct: principles set the tradeoff direction first, then encapsulation, interfaces, and inheritance turn that into class structure.
Design principles apply just as much to backend class design, not only frontend framework code.
scenario: LLD 面试设计支付网关：先定下"新增支付渠道不改旧代码"，接着要落成具体的类与接口。
scenario_en: In an LLD interview for a payment gateway, you first settle on "adding a new channel must not touch old code", then you have to turn that into actual classes and interfaces.

q: 补全四个核心 OOP 概念：
q_en: Fill in the four core OOP concepts:
text: LLD 面试中最重要的四个 OOP 概念是：{{封装}}、{{抽象}}、{{多态}}、{{继承}}。
why: 不需要死背术语，但要能在类设计里自然应用它们。
why_en: The four core OOP concepts are encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

q: 封装的核心含义是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of encapsulation?
options: 隐藏对象内部数据，通过方法控制访问和修改
把所有字段都设为 public，方便外部直接读写
让每个类都必须继承一个公共父类
只写静态函数，不定义任何实例方法
options_en: Hide an object's internal data and control access and changes through methods.
Make every field public so external code can read and write it directly.
Force every class to inherit from a common parent class.
Write only static functions and define no instance methods.
why: 封装让对象自己维护规则，例如余额不能为负、停车位不能被外部随意改。调用方通过行为而不是直接改字段来交互。
why_en: Encapsulation hides internal data and exposes controlled behavior so the object itself can enforce its own rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

optionExplanations: 对：把状态藏起来、只开放受控方法，是封装的核心动作。
全部字段设为 public 正好是封装要防止的做法，外部能绕开校验直接改状态。
强制继承公共父类说的是继承而不是封装，两个概念被混在一起了。
只写静态函数会让对象没有自己的状态可藏，根本谈不上封装。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: hiding internal data and only allowing controlled methods to touch it is exactly what encapsulation does.
Making every field public is the exact failure mode encapsulation prevents — callers can bypass validation.
Forcing every class to inherit a common parent describes inheritance, not encapsulation — a different concept.
Static-only functions leave no instance state to hide, so there's nothing to encapsulate.
scenario: 银行账户类要求余额永不为负，而调用方分散在转账、结算、对账三处代码里。
scenario_en: A bank account class must guarantee the balance never goes negative, but callers live in three different places: transfer, settlement, and reconciliation.

scenario: ParkingLot 暴露 public spots: list[ParkingSpot]，任何调用方都能直接增删停车位。
scenario_en: ParkingLot exposes a public spots: list[ParkingSpot] field, so any caller can add or remove parking spots directly.
q: 主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem here?
options: 列表本身不能用来存对象，得换成字典
外部代码可以绕过 ParkingLot 的规则，直接增删内部车位列表
每个 ParkingSpot 都必须实现成 Singleton 才安全
问题在于 Python 语言本身不支持 private 约定
options_en: Lists simply cannot hold objects, so it must become a dict.
External code can bypass ParkingLot's rules and mutate the internal spot list directly.
Every ParkingSpot must be implemented as a Singleton to be safe.
The real problem is that Python has no private-field convention.
why: 公开可变集合会让调用方绕过 park_vehicle 等受控方法直接改内部状态，破坏不变量。应提供受控方法并返回副本或只读视图。
why_en: Exposing a mutable internal collection lets callers bypass ParkingLot's rules and mutate its internal state directly, breaking its invariants.
whenOtherWins: 只读 DTO 或测试夹具可以直接暴露简单字段，但核心领域对象应保护可变状态。
tradeoff: 私有集合 + 受控方法 vs 公开可变集合：前者安全但多一层方法调用，后者简单但任何人都能破坏不变量。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the domain object in this example that manages the collection of parking spots and the parking logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton：一种保证某个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Singleton is a design pattern that guarantees a class has only one instance across the whole program.

termDefinitions.meaning: private：一种把字段/方法标记为只能在类内部访问的可见性约定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Private is a visibility convention that marks a field or method as accessible only from inside its own class.

optionExplanations: 列表完全可以存对象，问题不在数据结构类型，是暴露方式本身。
对：公开可变列表让外部绕开 park_vehicle 直接改车位，破坏了内部不变量。
车位对象要不要唯一实例和这里的问题无关，Singleton 解决的是另一件事。
Python 用下划线前缀和 @property 就能表达受保护/私有，语言并不缺这个能力。
optionExplanations_en: Lists can absolutely hold objects — the real issue is exposure, not the data structure choice.
Correct: a public mutable list lets callers skip park_vehicle and mutate spots directly, breaking invariants.
Whether a spot needs a single instance is unrelated here — Singleton solves a different problem.
Python expresses private/protected fine via underscore prefixes and @property; the language isn't missing this.

scenario: 调用方需要查看停车位列表，但不应能修改 ParkingLot 内部列表。
scenario_en: A caller needs to view the parking spot list, but must not be able to modify ParkingLot's internal list.
q: 这段 getter 的关键目的是什么？
q_en: What is the key purpose of this getter?
options: 让外部更容易删除内部元素
把 ParkingLot 变成不可实例化的类
自动给每次调用加锁
返回列表的副本，避免外部直接改动内部集合
options_en: Make it easier for external code to delete internal elements.
Turn ParkingLot into a class that can never be instantiated.
Automatically lock every call to this property.
Return a copy of the list so external code can't mutate the internal collection.
why: @property 返回 list(self._spots) 的副本，调用方可以读取结果，但无法通过引用篡改内部状态。
why_en: Returning a copy of the list preserves encapsulation because callers can read the result but cannot mutate the internal state through a shared reference.
whenOtherWins: 如果集合很大，复制成本高，可能改用只读视图、迭代器或查询方法代替整体复制。
tradeoff: 返回副本 vs 返回内部引用：副本安全但有复制开销，直接返回引用零开销但会泄漏可变状态。

termDefinitions.meaning: getter：用于读取对象内部字段的只读访问方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter is a method that provides read-only access to an object's internal field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the domain object in this example that manages the collection of parking spots and the parking logic.

optionExplanations: getter 返回的是副本，删除副本里的元素不会影响内部列表，达不到这个效果。
@property 只是暴露一个只读视图，跟类能不能被实例化没有关系。
这段代码没有任何加锁逻辑，getter 只是做了复制，不涉及并发控制。
对：这个 property 每次调用都产出一份新拷贝，调用方拿到的只是快照，动不了内部集合本身。
optionExplanations_en: The getter returns a copy, so deleting from that copy never touches the internal list — this doesn't happen.
The @property just exposes a read-only view; it has nothing to do with whether the class can be instantiated.
There's no locking here at all — the getter is just a copy, not a concurrency mechanism.
Correct: this property produces a fresh copy on every call, so the caller only ever holds a snapshot, never the internal collection itself.

q: 抽象的核心含义是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of abstraction?
options: 暴露必要能力，隐藏实现细节
把所有内部字段都暴露给调用方
让每个类都改写成公共父类
只使用全局函数，不定义接口
options_en: Expose only the essential capability and hide the implementation details.
Expose all internal fields to every caller.
Rewrite every class to be a shared parent class.
Use only global functions and never define an interface.
why: 抽象定义“能做什么”，不泄露“怎么做”。调用方依赖清晰接口，具体实现可以替换。
why_en: Abstraction exposes essential capabilities while hiding implementation details behind a clear contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接口（Interface）：只声明方法契约、不含实现，供多个类各自实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface declares a method contract with no implementation, which multiple classes can implement independently.

optionExplanations: 对：只给调用方需要的能力契约，具体怎么实现留在类内部。
全部字段暴露出去正是抽象要避免的，调用方会直接依赖内部实现。
让每个类共享一个父类说的是继承的做法，跟隐藏实现细节没关系。
只用全局函数反而丢掉了契约的边界，没有接口就没法约束调用方依赖什么。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: expose only the capability contract the caller needs, and keep the how inside the class.
Exposing every internal field is exactly what abstraction avoids — callers end up depending on internals.
Sharing one parent class across every type describes inheritance, not hiding implementation.
Global-only functions actually remove the contract boundary — no interface means nothing constrains what callers depend on.
scenario: 支付服务今天走 Stripe，半年后可能换 Adyen，上游下单代码不想跟着一起改。
scenario_en: The payment service runs on Stripe today and may switch to Adyen in six months, and the upstream checkout code must not have to change with it.

scenario: OrderService 直接调用 StripeAPI.set_api_key() 和 create_charge()，以后换 PayPal 要改 OrderService。
scenario_en: OrderService calls StripeAPI.set_api_key() and create_charge() directly, so switching to PayPal later would require changing OrderService.
q: 更好的抽象是什么？
q_en: What would be a better abstraction here?
options: 让 OrderService 直接继承 StripeAPI 类
把 StripeAPI 实例设为 OrderService 的 public 字段
定义 PaymentMethod 接口，只暴露 process(amount) 方法
把支付调用逻辑整体搬到前端 UI 层去写
options_en: Have OrderService directly inherit from the StripeAPI class.
Make the StripeAPI instance a public field on OrderService.
Define a PaymentMethod interface that only exposes process(amount).
Move all payment logic into the frontend UI layer.
why: 订单服务只需要“处理支付”这个能力，不该绑定 Stripe 的具体 API 细节。接口让支付实现可替换。
why_en: A PaymentMethod abstraction lets OrderService depend on the ability to process a payment instead of Stripe-specific details.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统永远只用一个支付实现且代码很小，直接调用可能符合 KISS。
tradeoff: PaymentMethod 接口 vs 直接调用 StripeAPI：接口多一层抽象但换供应商不用改 OrderService；直接调用更省事但换 PayPal 要重写调用方。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中负责结账流程的订单服务类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OrderService is the class in this example responsible for the checkout flow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方支付服务商 Stripe 的具体 API 客户端类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: StripeAPI is the concrete client class for the third-party payment provider Stripe.

termDefinitions.meaning: PaymentMethod：本例中定义“处理支付”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentMethod is the interface in this example that defines the capability to process a payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS：保持设计足够简单、不要过度设计的原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, and it means don't over-engineer a design.

diagram:
classDiagram
  class OrderService
  class PaymentProcessor {
    +process(amount)
  }
  class StripeProcessor
  class PayPalProcessor
  OrderService --> PaymentProcessor
  PaymentProcessor <|.. StripeProcessor
  PaymentProcessor <|.. PayPalProcessor
optionExplanations: 继承会把 OrderService 和 Stripe 的具体实现焊死在一起，换供应商时要动订单服务本身。
public 字段等于把 Stripe 细节直接摊开给调用方，谁都能绕开抽象直接摆弄 Stripe 对象。
对：接口只留 process(amount) 一个方法，OrderService 不用关心背后是 Stripe 还是别的供应商。
支付涉及密钥和金额校验，搬到前端等于把敏感逻辑暴露给客户端，安全上不可行。
optionExplanations_en: Inheriting from StripeAPI welds OrderService to Stripe's concrete implementation, so switching providers means editing OrderService itself.
A public field just hands Stripe's details straight to callers, letting anyone bypass the abstraction and poke at the Stripe object.
Correct: the interface only exposes process(amount), so OrderService never needs to know whether it's Stripe or another provider.
Payment involves secret keys and amount validation — moving it to the frontend exposes sensitive logic to the client, which isn't safe.

q: 好的抽象层级应该围绕什么设计？
q_en: What should a good abstraction level be designed around?
options: 把接口做到越泛越好，比如只留一个 doWork()
围绕调用方真正需要执行的业务操作来设计
把内部实现的每个小步骤都单独暴露出来
把接口做到越具体越好，比如 callStripeCreateChargeOnly()
options_en: Make the interface as generic as possible, like a single doWork().
Design it around the actual operation the caller needs to perform.
Expose every small internal implementation step separately.
Make the interface as specific as possible, like callStripeCreateChargeOnly().
why: 接口太泛没有语义，太细又泄露实现。合适的抽象层级来自调用方的业务需要，而不是实现的步骤数。
why_en: A good abstraction is shaped around what the caller needs to do, not how many internal steps the implementation happens to have.
tradeoff: 过泛接口 vs 过细接口：doWork() 太泛让实现自己猜意图，callStripeCreateChargeOnly() 太细则泄漏了具体供应商，两者都不是调用方真正需要的契约。

termDefinitions.meaning: doWork(request)：一个只有动词、没有业务语义的过泛接口方法名示例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: doWork(request) is an example of an overly generic method signature that carries no real business meaning.

optionExplanations: doWork() 这种万能接口只在真的通用到没有业务语义时才有意义，多数场景下它把猜意图的负担甩给了实现者。
对：接口方法名对应调用方真正要做的业务动作，比如 processPayment(amount)，层级不多不少。
把内部每一步都单独暴露，调用方要自己拼装步骤顺序，这其实是把实现细节泄露成了接口。
callStripeCreateChargeOnly() 把供应商名字焊进了方法签名，换一家支付商就得改调用方代码。
optionExplanations_en: A catch-all doWork() only makes sense when the operation is truly generic; in most cases it just pushes the guessing of intent onto the implementation.
Correct: the interface names the actual business operation the caller performs, like processPayment(amount) — not too broad, not too granular.
Exposing every internal step forces the caller to assemble the sequence itself, which leaks implementation detail into the interface.
callStripeCreateChargeOnly() bakes the vendor name into the method signature, so switching payment providers forces callers to change too.
scenario: 订单服务要调支付网关：接口既要能换供应商，又要让调用方一眼看懂它在做什么业务。
scenario_en: The order service calls a payment gateway: the interface has to survive swapping vendors and still make it obvious to the caller what business action it performs.

q: 多态在 LLD 中通常用来替代什么？
q_en: What does polymorphism usually replace in LLD?
options: 所有对象初始化时执行的构造函数逻辑
所有字段声明时使用的默认初始值
所有异常捕获与错误处理相关代码
根据对象类型走不同分支的判断逻辑
options_en: Every constructor's logic for initializing a new object.
The default initial value assigned to every declared field.
All exception-catching and error-handling related code.
Branching logic that dispatches based on an object's type.
why: 当行为随类型变化时，让每个对象实现同一接口并自己处理，比到处写 type 判断更可扩展。
why_en: Polymorphism replaces type-checking branches by letting each implementation handle the same operation in its own way.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层次设计（LLD）：面试中要求把需求落到具体类、接口和方法的设计环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage that asks you to turn requirements into concrete classes, interfaces, and methods.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[type switch] --> B{vehicle type}
  B --> C[car logic]
  B --> D[bike logic]
  B --> E[truck logic]
  F[Vehicle.park] --> G[object decides]
optionExplanations: 构造函数负责初始化对象，跟“同一方法不同实现”这件事没有直接关系。
字段默认值是初始化数据，多态解决的是行为分派，不是给字段赋初值。
异常处理是错误路径的机制，跟按类型选择行为的问题不是一回事。
对：多态让每个类型自己实现同一方法，取代到处写 if vehicle.type == 'car' 这种判断。
optionExplanations_en: Constructors handle object initialization, which isn't the same problem as dispatching behavior by type.
Default field values are just initialization data — polymorphism is about dispatching behavior, not defaulting fields.
Exception handling is an error-path mechanism, a different concern from choosing behavior by type.
Correct: polymorphism lets each type implement the same method, replacing scattered if vehicle.type == 'car' checks.
scenario: 停车场要支持轿车/摩托/卡车，收费规则各不相同，下季度还会再加新车型。
scenario_en: A parking lot must handle cars, motorcycles and trucks with different fee rules, and more vehicle types are coming next quarter.

scenario: ParkingLot.park_vehicle() 根据 vehicle.type 判断 car、motorcycle、truck，分支越来越多。
scenario_en: ParkingLot.park_vehicle() branches on vehicle.type to handle car, motorcycle, and truck, and the branches keep growing.
q: 多态式改法是什么？
q_en: What is the polymorphic way to fix this?
options: 给 Vehicle 加统一的取尺寸方法，让子类各自返回自己的答案
继续在 if/elif 分支里不断添加新的车辆类型判断逻辑
让 ParkingLot 自己读取车辆的每个字段、自行猜测车辆类型是什么
干脆把所有车辆类型都统一当成 car 来处理，不做任何区分对待
options_en: Add a shared spot-size method to Vehicle and let each subclass return its own answer.
Keep adding more if/elif branches for each new vehicle type, without bound.
Have ParkingLot read every field itself and guess what the vehicle type actually is.
Just treat every vehicle the same way as a car, with no distinction at all.
why: 车辆知道自己需要什么车位，ParkingLot 只调用统一方法。新增车辆类型时尽量不改 ParkingLot。
why_en: Let each Vehicle implementation report its own required spot size so ParkingLot never branches on vehicle type.
whenOtherWins: 如果类型只有两种且明确不会增加，简单分支可能更直白易读。
tradeoff: 多态方法 vs 类型分支：前者新增车辆类型不用改 ParkingLot，但要多定义一个接口方法；后者写起来快，但每加一种车都要回来改 park_vehicle。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中 Vehicle 定义的方法，返回该车辆所需的车位尺寸。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: get_required_spot_size is the method Vehicle defines to report the parking-spot size that vehicle needs.

optionExplanations: 对：车辆知道自己需要什么尺寸的车位，把这件事交给 Vehicle 自己回答，新增车型不用碰这段停车逻辑。
继续加分支只会让 park_vehicle 越来越长，每加一种车都要回来改这同一个函数。
让 ParkingLot 猜车辆类型等于把判断逻辑搬到了错误的一边，车辆自己才最清楚自己是什么。
把所有车都当 car 处理会让大车占用小车位或反过来，直接破坏车位分配的正确性。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the vehicle itself knows what size spot it needs, so Vehicle answers that question and adding a new type never touches this parking logic.
Keep adding branches and park_vehicle only keeps growing — every new vehicle type means editing this same function again.
Having ParkingLot guess the vehicle type puts the judgment on the wrong side — the vehicle itself knows best what it is.
Treating every vehicle as a car means large vehicles get undersized spots or vice versa, breaking spot allocation correctness.

scenario: 你要展示车辆类型扩展时 ParkingLot 不用知道所有具体类型。
scenario_en: You want to show that ParkingLot doesn't need to know every concrete vehicle type as vehicle types get added.
q: 下面代码体现的 OOP 概念是什么？
q_en: Which OOP concept does this code demonstrate?
options: Singleton：全局只允许存在一个 Vehicle 实例，不能创建第二个
多态：ParkingLot 调用同一个方法，具体行为由子类决定
Builder：分步骤设置字段，最后再构造出一个复杂的 Vehicle 对象
Law of Demeter：避免写太长的链式方法调用、只跟直接对象交互
options_en: Singleton: only one Vehicle instance is allowed to exist globally, ever.
Polymorphism: ParkingLot calls one method, and the subclass decides the behavior.
Builder: set fields step by step, then finally construct a complex Vehicle object.
Law of Demeter: avoid long chained calls and only talk to direct collaborators.
why: ParkingLot 依赖 Vehicle 的统一契约 get_required_spot_size()，不依赖具体车种分支。行为差异被封装到具体实现里。
why_en: This is polymorphism because ParkingLot calls one method and the concrete vehicle subclass supplies the behavior.
whenOtherWins: 若停车规则还依赖更复杂的策略选择，可能再把 spot selection 抽成 Strategy 模式。
tradeoff: 多态 vs Singleton/Builder：这里的关键行为是“同一方法、不同实现”，不是“限制实例数量”或“分步构造对象”，所以后两个模式名词对不上这段代码在解决的问题。

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton：一种保证某个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Singleton is a design pattern that guarantees a class has only one instance across the whole program.

termDefinitions.meaning: Builder：一种通过链式方法逐步构造复杂对象的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Builder is a design pattern that constructs a complex object step by step through chained method calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter：只和直接相邻对象交互、避免链式深访问的设计原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says an object should only talk to its immediate collaborators and avoid deep chained calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

optionExplanations: 代码里没有限制 Vehicle 实例数量的逻辑，跟 Singleton 要解决的问题对不上。
对：ParkingLot 调用的是这同一个尺寸方法，Car 和 Truck 各自返回自己的答案，行为差异全封装在子类里。
代码里没有分步骤设置字段再返回对象的过程，跟 Builder 的构造方式对不上。
代码里也没有出现链式调用，Law of Demeter 关心的是调用链长度，不是这里的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing here limits how many Vehicle instances can exist — that's not the problem Singleton solves.
Correct: ParkingLot calls that one shared method, and Car and Truck each return their own answer — the difference lives entirely in the subclasses.
There's no step-by-step field-setting process before returning an object here, which is what Builder is about.
There's no chained method call in this snippet either — Law of Demeter is about call-chain length, not this.

scenario: 团队在停车场系统里给 Vehicle 定义了多态接口，随着 Car、Truck、Motorcycle 等实现类越来越多。
scenario_en: The team defined a polymorphic Vehicle interface in the parking-lot system, and the number of implementations like Car, Truck, and Motorcycle keeps growing.
q: 这时多态调用可能带来什么代价？
q_en: What cost can this growing set of polymorphic implementations bring?
options: 多态天生比 if/else 慢到无法接受
多态没办法配合接口一起使用
使用多态之后就没法写单元测试了
实现类一多，调用流程会更难追踪和调试
options_en: Polymorphism is inherently too slow compared to if/else to be usable.
Polymorphism can't be combined with interfaces at all.
Once you use polymorphism, you can no longer write unit tests.
As the number of implementations grows, the call flow becomes harder to trace and debug.
why: 多态提升扩展性，但把行为分散到多个实现类里。不同公司对多态的接受度不同，面试里要能解释这个取舍。
why_en: Polymorphism improves extensibility but scatters behavior across many implementation classes, which can make control flow harder to trace.
tradeoff: 扩展性 vs 可追踪性：多态让新增类型不用改调用方，但调试时要跳进具体实现类才能看到真实行为。

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

optionExplanations: 多态确实多一次虚方法查找，但这点开销在大多数业务系统里完全不是瓶颈。
多态恰恰是靠接口才能生效——子类实现同一接口，接口是多态成立的前提。
多态反而更利于测试，每个实现类可以单独 mock 和验证，不是没法测。
对：实现类越来越多，读代码的人得跳进每个具体子类才能看到真实执行的行为。
optionExplanations_en: Polymorphism does add one virtual dispatch, but that cost is nowhere near a bottleneck in most business systems.
Polymorphism actually depends on interfaces to work — subclasses implementing a shared interface is what makes it possible.
Polymorphism actually helps testing, since each implementation can be mocked and verified independently — it's not untestable.
Correct: as implementations multiply, readers have to jump into each concrete subclass to see what actually runs.

q: 继承最主要的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of inheritance?
options: 继承完全无法共享任何实现代码
继承只能用来实现接口，不能共享代码
父类的变化可能破坏所有子类，形成紧耦合
使用继承会自动提升代码的可维护性
options_en: Inheritance can never share any implementation code at all.
Inheritance can only be used to implement interfaces, never to share code.
A change in the parent class can break every subclass, creating tight coupling.
Using inheritance automatically improves maintainability.
why: 子类继承父类字段和方法，父类内部变化会影响整棵层次。这就是“脆弱基类”问题。
why_en: Inheritance tightly couples subclasses to the base class's implementation, so a base-class change can break the whole hierarchy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 脆弱基类问题：父类实现的一次改动，意外破坏了多个子类行为的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The fragile base class problem is when a single change to the parent implementation unexpectedly breaks multiple subclasses.

optionExplanations: 继承恰恰就是为了共享父类的字段和方法，说它完全不能共享代码正好说反了。
继承和实现接口是两件事，继承本身就是共享代码的手段之一。
对：子类紧耦合父类实现，父类一改，所有子类的行为都可能跟着变。
继承提高的是复用速度，不是可维护性，用不好反而会让改动牵一发动全身。
optionExplanations_en: Inheritance exists precisely to share a parent's fields and methods — saying it shares no code at all is backwards.
Inheriting and implementing an interface are different things; inheritance is itself one way to share code.
Correct: subclasses are tightly coupled to the parent's implementation, so one parent change can ripple through every subclass.
Inheritance speeds up reuse, not maintainability — used poorly it makes one change ripple through the whole hierarchy.
scenario: 支付基类被 6 个渠道子类继承，风控团队每个月都要改基类里的校验逻辑。
scenario_en: A payment base class is inherited by six channel subclasses, and the risk team edits the validation logic inside that base class every month.

scenario: SavingsAccount 和 CheckingAccount 都确实共享余额、存款、取款和交易历史逻辑。
scenario_en: SavingsAccount and CheckingAccount genuinely share balance, deposit, withdraw, and transaction-history logic.
q: 这里继承为什么可能合理？
q_en: Why might inheritance be a reasonable fit here?
options: 共享的余额和交易逻辑稳定，两者都是 BankAccount 的特殊形式
只要两个类名字都带 Account 后缀、听起来相似，就足够构成继承的理由
因为组合这种设计手法根本没办法用来复用任何共享的实现代码
因为这两个子类打算把父类的所有行为逻辑完全推翻并重写一遍
options_en: The shared balance and transaction logic is stable, and both are genuine specializations of BankAccount.
Two classes merely sharing the Account suffix and sounding similar is already enough reason to reach for inheritance.
Composition as a technique simply has no way to reuse any shared implementation code at all.
The two subclasses intend to completely override and rewrite every single parent behavior.
why: 继承适合稳定、真实的 is-a 关系和共享实现。账户例子中核心余额行为一致，子类只是增加特定字段。
why_en: Inheritance fits when subclasses truly share stable implementation and are genuine specializations of the base class.
whenOtherWins: 如果差异主要是可替换的行为而非共享状态，组合接口通常更稳。
tradeoff: 继承 vs 组合：账户例子里核心逻辑稳定共享，继承省事；若账户类型未来行为差异很大，组合会更抗变化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的银行账户基类，持有余额并实现存取款逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BankAccount is the base class in this example that holds the balance and implements deposit/withdraw logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组合（Composition）：一个类持有并委托给另一个对象，而不是继承它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition means a class holds a reference to another object and delegates to it instead of inheriting from it.

optionExplanations: 对：余额、存取款、交易记录这些行为两个子类完全一致，这是真正稳定的 is-a 关系。
光凭 Account 后缀相似就用继承很危险，两个类名字像但行为可能完全不共享，会强行绑死不该绑的东西。
组合同样能复用代码，只是通过持有对象委托调用，而不是通过继承字段方法。
如果子类要推翻父类几乎所有行为，说明它根本不是父类的合法特例，继承反而不合适。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: balance, deposit/withdraw, and transaction history are genuinely identical across both subclasses — a real stable is-a relationship.
Using inheritance just because two names share the Account suffix is risky — similar names can hide completely different, non-shared behavior.
Composition can reuse code too, just through holding and delegating to an object instead of inheriting fields and methods.
If a subclass has to override nearly every parent behavior, it isn't a legitimate specialization, so inheritance doesn't fit.

scenario: Car 有 gasoline engine，ElectricCar 没有 engine，却继承 Car 并重写 start_engine 为完全不同逻辑。
scenario_en: Car has a gasoline engine, but ElectricCar has no engine at all — yet it inherits from Car and overrides start_engine with completely different logic.
q: 更好的设计方向是什么？
q_en: What is a better design direction here?
options: 让 ElectricCar 继承 Car 后在 start_engine 里直接抛出异常来拒绝执行
把 start_engine 的具体实现逻辑整体搬到一个全局函数里去写
抽出 Drivetrain 接口，用组合方式接入 GasEngine/ElectricMotor
继续给 Car 家族加更多子类，每个子类都要重写一遍 start_engine
options_en: Have ElectricCar inherit from Car anyway, then throw an exception inside start_engine to reject the call.
Move the entire start_engine implementation logic into one global function.
Extract a Drivetrain interface and compose in GasEngine/ElectricMotor.
Keep adding more Car subclasses, each one overriding start_engine again.
why: 行为要被整个推翻就不是 is-a：把启动动作抽成 Drivetrain 接口、组合注入。加混动只需新写一个 Drivetrain，Car 一行不改。
why_en: When behavior varies, composing a Drivetrain abstraction is cleaner than forcing the variation into a Car subclass.
whenOtherWins: 如果子类真的共享大量稳定实现且不破坏父类契约，继承仍然可用。
tradeoff: 组合 Drivetrain vs 继承 Car：组合让新增动力类型不用碰 Car，但多一层委托；继承写起来快，但每种动力都要新开一个子类并重写 start_engine。

termDefinitions.meaning: Drivetrain：本例中定义“启动动力系统”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drivetrain is the interface in this example that defines the capability to start the car's power system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中错误地继承 Car、但没有汽油引擎的电动车子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ElectricCar is the subclass in this example that inherits from Car even though it has no gasoline engine to share.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组合（Composition）：一个类持有并委托给另一个对象，而不是继承它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition means a class holds a reference to another object and delegates to it instead of inheriting from it.

optionExplanations: 抛异常等于承认 ElectricCar 不是合法的 Car 子类，已经违反了继承的替换原则，是在掩盖设计问题。
搬进全局函数丢掉了每种动力各自的状态和实现，不同车型的启动细节没地方放了。
对：Drivetrain 接口让 Car 组合 GasEngine 或 ElectricMotor，新增混动类型不用碰 Car 本身。
每种动力都新开一个 Car 子类，子类数量会跟着动力类型线性增长，行为差异其实和“是不是车”无关。
optionExplanations_en: Throwing an exception admits ElectricCar isn't a valid Car subtype at all — that already breaks substitutability and just hides the design problem.
Moving it into a global function drops each drivetrain's own state and implementation — there's nowhere to put type-specific start-up details.
Correct: a Drivetrain interface lets Car compose GasEngine or ElectricMotor, so adding hybrid support never touches Car itself.
Opening a new Car subclass per drivetrain grows the subclass count with every power type, even though the variation has nothing to do with 'being a car.'

scenario: 你要让不同车的启动方式可替换，并避免 ElectricCar 继承不适合的 engine 行为。
scenario_en: You want to make each car's start-up mechanism swappable, without ElectricCar inheriting engine behavior that doesn't fit it.
q: 这段代码体现了什么取舍？
q_en: What tradeoff does this code demonstrate?
options: 用 Singleton 确保全局只有一辆 Car
用组合承载可变的启动行为，避免脆弱的继承层次
用 Builder 分步骤设置 Car 的可选字段
用 Observer 在价格变化时通知订阅者
options_en: Use Singleton to ensure only one Car exists globally.
Use composition to hold the variable start-up behavior and avoid a fragile inheritance hierarchy.
Use Builder to set Car's optional fields step by step.
Use Observer to notify subscribers when the price changes.
why: Car 依赖 Drivetrain 抽象，具体启动细节由组件实现。新增动力系统不需要改 Car。
why_en: The design composes a Drivetrain abstraction so engine start-up behavior can vary without changing Car.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有车辆共享同一启动实现且差异很小，简单继承或单一字段可能更简单。
tradeoff: 组合 vs 继承：组合让 Car 不用管具体是燃油还是电动，代价是多一层 self.drivetrain.start() 委托。

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton：一种保证某个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Singleton is a design pattern that guarantees a class has only one instance across the whole program.

termDefinitions.meaning: Builder：一种通过链式方法逐步构造复杂对象的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Builder is a design pattern that constructs a complex object step by step through chained method calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer：一种让订阅者在被观察对象状态变化时自动收到通知的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Observer is a design pattern where subscribers are automatically notified when the observed object's state changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Drivetrain：本例中定义“启动动力系统”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drivetrain is the interface in this example that defines the capability to start the car's power system.

optionExplanations: 代码里 Car 可以创建任意多个实例，没有限制唯一性的逻辑，不是 Singleton。
对：Car 持有一个 drivetrain 字段并委托给它，这就是组合，避开了继承带来的脆弱层次。
代码里 Car 的构造只接收一个 drivetrain 参数，没有分步骤设置多个可选字段的过程。
代码里完全没有价格变化或订阅通知的逻辑，跟 Observer 要解决的问题不沾边。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing here limits how many Car instances can exist — Car can be created freely, so this isn't Singleton.
Correct: Car holds a drivetrain field and delegates to it, which is composition — it sidesteps the fragile inheritance hierarchy.
Car's constructor just takes one drivetrain argument; there's no step-by-step setting of multiple optional fields here.
There's no price-change or subscriber-notification logic anywhere in this snippet — that's not what's happening.

scenario: 你在设计一批需要复用部分逻辑的类，正在纠结先用继承还是先用组合+接口。
scenario_en: You're designing a group of classes that need to reuse some logic, and you're deciding between reaching for inheritance first or composition plus an interface first.
q: 默认情况下应该先选哪一个？
q_en: Which should you default to first?
options: 默认使用又深又长的继承层次，共享实现出问题了才回头改组合
任何情况下都完全禁止使用继承
任何情况下都完全禁止使用接口
默认接口 + 组合，只有共享实现真正稳定时才用继承
options_en: Default to a deep inheritance hierarchy, and only switch to composition once the shared implementation turns out to be a problem.
Completely forbid inheritance under any circumstance.
Completely forbid interfaces under any circumstance.
Default to interfaces plus composition, and reach for inheritance only when the shared implementation is genuinely stable.
why: 组合能复用行为并降低父子类耦合。继承不是禁忌，但应保留给真正稳定的共享实现。
why_en: Default to interfaces and composition, and reserve inheritance for implementation that is genuinely stable and shared.
tradeoff: 接口+组合 vs 深继承：前者默认更灵活但每个能力都要多写一层委托；后者短期少写代码，但父类一变就牵连所有子类。

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组合（Composition）：一个类持有并委托给另一个对象，而不是继承它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition means a class holds a reference to another object and delegates to it instead of inheriting from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接口（Interface）：只声明方法契约、不含实现，供多个类各自实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface declares a method contract with no implementation, which multiple classes can implement independently.

optionExplanations: 先建深继承层次再等出问题才改，代价是问题往往到后期才暴露，返工成本更高。
继承不是禁忌，真正稳定共享的实现（如账户余额逻辑）用继承依然合适，一刀切禁止太绝对。
接口是表达契约最轻量的方式，完全禁用接口会让抽象和多态都失去落脚点。
对：默认用接口加组合更灵活，只有实现确实稳定共享时才升级为继承。
optionExplanations_en: Building a deep hierarchy first and fixing it only when it breaks means problems surface late, when rework is more expensive.
Inheritance isn't forbidden — genuinely stable shared implementation, like account balance logic, still fits it fine; an outright ban is too absolute.
Interfaces are the lightest way to express a contract; banning them entirely removes the foundation abstraction and polymorphism need.
Correct: default to interfaces plus composition, and only promote to inheritance once implementation is genuinely stable and shared.

q: 哪些做法体现封装？（多选）
q_en: Which of these practices demonstrate encapsulation? (multi-select)
options: 允许任何调用方直接写 balance 字段
把字段设为私有或受保护
通过 deposit/withdraw 等方法修改状态
返回内部可变集合的副本或只读视图
options_en: Allow any caller to write the balance field directly.
Make fields private or protected.
Change state only through methods like deposit/withdraw.
Return a copy or read-only view of an internal mutable collection.
why: 封装的目标是让对象守住自己的规则。直接写 balance 会绕过校验和关联逻辑，破坏不变量。
why_en: Encapsulation uses private state, controlled methods, and safe views of collections rather than direct external mutation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: balance：本例中账户对象持有的余额字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Balance is the account object's stored balance field in this example.

optionExplanations: 直接暴露可写字段等于放弃校验，任何调用方都能把余额改成负数或非法状态。
字段私有/受保护挡住了外部绕过方法直接改状态的路径，规则只能通过对象自己的方法生效。
只通过 deposit/withdraw 修改状态，把余额校验和记账逻辑锁在方法内部，杜绝跳过检查的写入。
返回副本或只读视图挡住了调用方通过引用篡改内部集合的可能，读没问题，写不到内部数据。
optionExplanations_en: Exposing a writable field directly means giving up validation — any caller can set balance to negative or invalid values.
Making fields private/protected blocks external code from bypassing methods to mutate state directly — rules only apply through the object's own methods.
Changing state only via deposit/withdraw locks balance validation and bookkeeping inside those methods, closing off writes that skip checks.
Returning a copy or read-only view blocks callers from mutating the internal collection through a shared reference — reads work, writes to internals don't.
scenario: 账户类要求余额永不为负，而且内部持仓列表不能被调用方在对象外偷偷改掉。
scenario_en: An account class must keep the balance non-negative, and its internal holdings list must not be mutated behind the object’s back.

q: 哪些信号说明可能需要抽象？（多选）
q_en: Which signals suggest you might need an abstraction? (multi-select)
options: 同一能力存在多个不同的实现
这块逻辑只有一个字段、并且以后也不会变化
某块逻辑里藏着很多变化的规则
调用方本不应该知道外部 API 的实现细节
options_en: The same capability has multiple different implementations.
This logic has only one field and it will never change.
A piece of logic hides a lot of varying rules.
Callers shouldn't need to know the implementation details of an external API.
why: 抽象适合隐藏复杂性和变化点。没有变化也不复杂的地方，抽象往往只是额外成本。
why_en: Abstraction helps when there are multiple implementations, complex variation, or details callers should not know about.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: API：应用程序编程接口，供调用方使用的一组预定义方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: API stands for Application Programming Interface, a predefined set of methods a caller can use.

optionExplanations: 同一能力有多个实现时，抽象挡住了调用方硬编码某一种实现的风险，换实现不用改调用方。
只有一个字段且永不变化，说明这里没有变化点要隐藏，硬加抽象反而多了一层没用的间接。
规则藏得越多，抽象把这些变化规则收进实现内部，调用方不用被每条规则牵连。
调用方不该知道外部 API 细节时，抽象挡住了供应商变更（如换支付商）传导到调用方代码的风险。
optionExplanations_en: When one capability has multiple implementations, abstraction blocks callers from hardcoding a specific one, so swapping implementations doesn't touch callers.
A single field that never changes has no variation to hide, so adding abstraction here is just an extra layer with no payoff.
The more varying rules hide inside a piece of logic, the more abstraction shields callers from being coupled to every one of those rules.
When callers shouldn't know external API details, abstraction blocks a vendor change (like switching payment providers) from rippling into caller code.
scenario: 订单系统里有一段通知逻辑，未来要支持短信、邮件、推送三种发送方式。
scenario_en: An order system has a notification step that will need to support SMS, email and push in the future.

scenario: 你看到 checkout 里根据 payment_type 字符串 switch 到不同支付逻辑。
scenario_en: You see checkout switch on a payment_type string to branch into different payment logic.
q: 这通常提示你使用什么概念？
q_en: What concept does this usually signal you should use?
options: 继承一个巨大的 PaymentProcessor 基类
把每种支付方式的字段都公开出来
定义 PaymentMethod 接口，让多态处理每种支付方式
在 checkout 里继续往 switch 加分支，新增支付方式还要跟着改这段代码
options_en: Inherit from one giant PaymentProcessor base class.
Expose every payment method's fields publicly.
Define a PaymentMethod interface and let polymorphism handle each payment type.
Keep adding branches to the switch inside checkout, so every new payment method means editing this same code again.
why: 支付方式是行为变化点。接口让每种支付自己实现 process，checkout 只调用统一方法。
why_en: A payment-type switch is a cue to use polymorphism through a shared PaymentMethod interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一种支付方式且没有扩展信号，先保持简单实现也可以。
tradeoff: PaymentMethod 多态 vs switch 分支：接口让新增支付方式不用改 checkout，但多定义一层接口；switch 写起来快，但每加一种支付都要回来改这段代码。

termDefinitions.meaning: PaymentMethod：本例中定义“处理支付”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentMethod is the interface in this example that defines the capability to process a payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中一个试图把所有支付方式塞进同一个继承体系的巨大基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentProcessor here is a giant base class that tries to cram every payment method into one inheritance hierarchy.

optionExplanations: 继承一个巨大基类会把所有支付方式的字段和方法都塞进一棵层次，父类一改全体遭殃。
把字段全公开出来，调用方就要自己判断该用哪个字段，等于把分支判断从代码搬进了脑子里。
对：每种支付类型自己实现同一个 process 方法，checkout 端不用判断具体是哪种支付，直接调用即可。
继续往 switch 加分支，每新增一种支付方式都要回来改这同一段 checkout 代码。
optionExplanations_en: Inheriting one giant base class crams every payment method's fields and behavior into one hierarchy — a parent change hits everyone.
Exposing every field publicly just pushes the branching into the caller's head — it now has to know which fields apply to which method.
Correct: each payment type implements the same process method on its own, so checkout never has to branch — it just calls it.
Keep adding switch branches and every new payment method means editing this same checkout code again.

q: 用继承表达行为差异时，常见后果是什么？
q_en: What commonly happens when you use inheritance to express behavior differences?
options: 所有的变化都会自动变得更容易处理
子类会大量覆写父类方法，父类的契约变得脆弱
用继承之后就再也不需要接口了
只要用了继承，子类覆写父类的所有方法就自动被认为是正确的
options_en: Every future change automatically becomes easier to make.
Subclasses end up overriding many parent methods, and the parent's contract becomes fragile.
Once you use inheritance, you never need interfaces again.
Using inheritance automatically makes every method a subclass overrides correct.
why: 当子类只是为了不同实现而覆写父类方法，说明共享父类可能不是合适的抽象。组合可变行为通常更稳。
why_en: Using inheritance to express behavior variation often leads to many overrides and a fragile base-class contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

optionExplanations: 继承本身不会让变化自动变简单，用来表达行为差异时反而经常让改动更难追踪。
对：子类为了不同行为不停覆写父类方法，父类原本承诺的契约慢慢就不成立了。
继承和接口解决的是不同问题，用了继承之后该定义的契约接口通常还是要有。
继承只是复用了字段和方法，方法本身对不对跟有没有用继承没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: Inheritance doesn't automatically make change easier — using it to express behavior differences often makes changes harder to trace.
Correct: subclasses keep overriding parent methods for different behavior, and the parent's original contract gradually stops holding.
Inheritance and interfaces solve different problems — you typically still need a contract interface even after adding inheritance.
Inheritance just reuses fields and methods; whether a method is correct has no causal link to whether inheritance was used.
scenario: 为 5 种支付渠道建了统一 Payment 基类，结果每个子类都把 charge 和 refund 重写了一遍。
scenario_en: You built one shared Payment base class for five payment channels, and every subclass ended up overriding both charge and refund.

q: 把从 type-check 到多态停车的重构步骤排好：
q_en: Put the steps of refactoring from type-checks to polymorphic parking in the correct order:
steps: 让 ParkingLot 调用 vehicle.get_required_spot_size()
为 Vehicle 定义所需车位尺寸契约
识别 switch/if 基于 vehicle.type 分支
为 Car/Motorcycle/Truck 实现各自尺寸
why: 先识别行为随类型变化，再把变化移进类型本身，最后调用方依赖统一契约。
why_en: Refactor type checks by identifying type-varying behavior, defining a contract, implementing it per type, and calling the contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the domain object in this example that manages the collection of parking spots and the parking logic.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[type checks] --> B[define interface]
