optionExplanations_en: Scale is worth asking, but 3 vs 30 elevators changes how much dispatch tuning pays off, not the class structure.
In a simulation you advance time by calling step(); in real control software floor sensors advance it, and the two lead to fundamentally different class structures.
That is a scoping question whose answer is "no" — it saves time but does not decide how you model time.
Language is an execution detail the interviewer usually leaves to you; asking it yields no design information.
why: 仿真里你写 currentFloor++ 并自己调 step()；真实控制软件里是 onFloorReached(floor) 回调驱动。代价是仿真绕开了硬件异步，只能谈对象建模。
why_en: In a simulation you increment currentFloor yourself inside step, while real control software is driven by onFloorReached callbacks — the simulation buys determinism at the cost of ignoring hardware asynchrony.
tradeoff: 自己用 step() 推进时间的仿真 vs 硬件中断回调驱动的控制软件
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明说要做真实控制软件，就得按 onFloorReached(floor) 这类硬件事件回调组织类，step() 根本不存在。

termDefinitions.meaning: 仿真里手动推进一个离散时间单位的方法，调一次代表过去一个 tick。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: step() is the method you call to advance the simulation by one discrete time unit, or tick.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实电梯控制软件里由楼层传感器触发的回调，通知软件轿厢已到达某层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: onFloorReached is a callback fired by a floor sensor in real control software to tell the program the car has arrived at a floor.

scenario: 电梯在 5 楼向上，请求在 3、7、8 楼。nearest-first 一共走 7 层，SCAN 一共走 8 层。
scenario_en: An elevator sits at floor 5 heading up with requests at floors 3, 7 and 8: nearest-first travels 7 floors in total, SCAN travels 8.
q: 为什么仍然选走得更远的 SCAN？
q_en: Why still pick SCAN even though it travels farther?
options: SCAN 在任何请求分布下总距离都不会更长
优化目标是方向可预期和等待体验，不是总距离
nearest-first 会漏掉反方向的 pickup 请求不停
SCAN 每 tick 只走一层，nearest-first 可以跳层
options_en: SCAN never travels farther than nearest-first for any request distribution.
The goal we optimize is predictable direction and waiting experience, not total distance.
Nearest-first would skip opposite-direction pickup requests and never stop for them.
SCAN moves one floor per tick while nearest-first is allowed to jump floors.
optionExplanations: 这个例子本身就是反例：8 > 7，SCAN 在这里确实更远。
多走的这一层买的是「电梯朝我来」这个可预期性，繁忙楼里还能顺路批量接人、避免在近楼层之间反复折返。
该不该停由 Request 的类型决定，两种移动算法用的是同一套停靠规则，跟谁先谁后无关。
两种算法都是一 tick 一层，区别只在下一层朝哪边走。
optionExplanations_en: This very example is the counterexample: 8 is more than 7, so SCAN really is farther here.
That extra floor buys the "it's coming toward me" predictability, and in a busy building it also batches nearby pickups instead of thrashing between close floors.
Whether to stop is decided by the Request type, and both movement algorithms share that same stopping rule.
Both algorithms move exactly one floor per tick; they differ only in which way the next floor is.
why: 多走的那 1 层换的是方向可预期：nearest-first 先下到 3 楼，7 楼乘客眼睁睁看电梯走反方向。代价就是总行程略长。
why_en: That one extra floor buys directional predictability — with nearest-first the person on floor 7 watches the car head down to 3 first — and the cost is a slightly longer trip.
tradeoff: 总行走层数最短 vs 方向可预期、少折返
whenOtherWins: 如果楼里几乎没人、同时只有一两个请求且没人在别的楼层等，最短距离的 nearest-first 就不用付可预期性的代价。

termDefinitions.meaning: 沿当前方向一路服务所有顺路请求，前方没有请求了才反向的扫掠式调度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in one direction serving every request along the way, and only reverses once nothing is left ahead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每一步都朝距离当前楼层最近的那个请求走，不考虑当前方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nearest-first always heads toward whichever pending request is closest, ignoring the current direction of travel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：严格按请求到达顺序逐个服务，完全不考虑楼层位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO, first in first out, serves requests strictly in arrival order regardless of where those floors are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯在几个相邻楼层之间反复来回，谁都服务不痛快的抖动状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thrashing is when the car keeps bouncing back and forth between nearby floors without serving anyone well.

scenario: 35 分钟的面试还剩 12 分钟，方向感知版 selectBestElevator 已经跑通，request-aware 版还没写。
scenario_en: Twelve minutes remain in a 35-minute interview; the direction-aware selectBestElevator works, but the request-aware version is unwritten.
q: 剩下的时间最该花在哪？
q_en: Where should you spend the remaining time?
options: 把 request-aware 版硬写完，写不完就留 TODO 注释
主动说出没检查请求队列这个局限，再问要不要写
改用 priority queue，一次把调度做到最优
先补一遍所有非法楼层的输入校验和单元测试
options_en: Push through and finish the request-aware version, leaving TODO comments if you run out of time.
Proactively name the limitation that you don't check the request queue, then ask if they want it coded.
Switch to a priority queue so the scheduling is optimal in one shot.
Go back and add input validation plus unit tests for every invalid floor number.
optionExplanations: 半截代码既证明不了你会写，又占掉了本可以谈扩展和并发的时间。
面试官要的信号是「你知道这个 edge case 存在」，说出来和写出来拿到的是同一个分。
priority queue 会打散沿一个方向扫掠的行为，属于换掉移动算法，不是补一个调度短板。
校验在 addRequest 里已经写过了，重复补它拿不到新的评分点。
optionExplanations_en: Half-finished code proves neither that you can write it nor leaves time to discuss extensions and concurrency.
The signal the interviewer wants is that you know the edge case exists, and saying it earns the same credit as coding it.
A priority queue breaks the sweep-in-one-direction behavior — that replaces the movement algorithm rather than patching a dispatch gap.
Validation already lives in addRequest, so redoing it earns no new points.
why: 剩余时间不够写完 hasRequestsAtOrBeyond，而口述局限拿到的是同一个 senior 信号。代价是这段逻辑确实没被验证过。
why_en: There isn't time to finish hasRequestsAtOrBeyond, and naming the limitation earns the same senior signal — the cost is that the logic stays unverified.
tradeoff: 花时间实现 request-aware 版 vs 口述局限保住扩展性和并发的讨论时间
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说「我想看这段实现」，或者你还剩 20 分钟以上，就该真的把 hasRequestsAtOrBeyond 写出来。

termDefinitions.meaning: 派梯前不仅看电梯方向，还检查它队列里的请求会不会带它经过目标楼层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request-aware dispatch checks not only the elevator's direction but whether its queued stops will actually carry it to or past the requested floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elevator 上的查询方法，回答「我队列里有没有在这层或更远的同向停靠」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: hasRequestsAtOrBeyond is a query on Elevator answering whether it has a same-direction stop at or beyond a given floor.

scenario: 5 楼有人按「上」。最近的电梯在 6 楼，但它正向下开往 1 楼。nearest 策略照样把它派了过去。
scenario_en: Someone on floor 5 presses up; the nearest car is on floor 6 but heading down to floor 1, and the nearest strategy dispatches it anyway.
q: 这位乘客实际会经历什么？
q_en: What does that passenger actually experience?
options: 电梯到 5 楼就停，乘客被载着一路开到 1 楼
向下经过 5 楼不停，到 1 楼反向后才回来接
请求被 addRequest 拒绝，直接返回 false
电梯在 6 楼立即掉头放弃原有请求，向上接人
options_en: The car stops at floor 5 and carries the passenger all the way down to floor 1.
It passes floor 5 going down, reaches floor 1, reverses, and only then comes back up.
The request is rejected by addRequest, which simply returns false.
The car reverses at floor 6 immediately, abandoning its existing stops to pick them up.
optionExplanations: 这正是只存楼层数字时会发生的错接——有了 PICKUP_UP 类型，向下的电梯不会停。
停靠是方向敏感的，行进不是：电梯会朝任何请求走，但只为同向的乘客开门。
楼层 5 合法、类型也是合法的 hall call，校验层没有理由拒绝它。
step 只在前方没有请求时才反向，1 楼的请求还在前面，掉不了头。
optionExplanations_en: That is exactly the mis-pickup you get when you store bare floor numbers; with a PICKUP_UP type the downward car simply does not stop.
Stopping is direction-aware while travelling is not: the car moves toward any request but only opens for passengers going its way.
Floor 5 is valid and so is the hall call type, so validation has no reason to reject it.
step only reverses when nothing is left ahead, and the floor 1 stop is still ahead.
why: Request 带方向类型兜住了正确性——不会把人往反方向拉；但兜住的只是「不接错人」，代价是他要等完整的下行加返程。
why_en: The direction-typed Request keeps correctness — nobody is carried the wrong way — but all it guarantees is no wrong pickup, at the cost of a full trip down and back.
tradeoff: nearest 实现成本低 vs 派错方向带来的极长等待
whenOtherWins: 小楼、轻流量、电梯大多处于 IDLE 时，nearest 派出去的基本就是空闲电梯，方向判断带来的收益很小。

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼梯按钮产生的请求，只带上或下的方向，不带目的楼层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is the request created by the up or down button outside the elevator; it carries a direction but no destination floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: RequestType 之一，表示这层有人要往上走，只有向上的电梯才应为它停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is the request type meaning someone on that floor wants to go up, so only an upward-moving car should stop.

scenario: 澄清阶段你问呼梯面板是哪种，面试官答「经典上/下两键 hall call，不是选层派梯」。
scenario_en: During clarification you ask which call panel is used and the interviewer answers "classic two-button up/down hall calls, not destination dispatch".
q: 这个回答如何改变请求建模？
q_en: How does that answer change the way you model requests?
options: 呼梯只带方向，目的楼层进轿厢后再单独按
呼梯时就要带上目的楼层，系统当场分配轿厢
Floor 必须建成类，用来保存面板的分配结果
Controller 派梯时要把目的楼层一起写进队列
options_en: The hall call carries only a direction; destinations are pressed separately once inside the car.
The call itself carries a destination floor and the system assigns a car on the spot.
Floor has to become a class so it can hold what the panel assigned.
The controller must write the destination floor into the elevator's queue when dispatching.
optionExplanations: 所以 RequestType 才需要 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN、DESTINATION 三种，而不是一个「目的楼层」字段。
这是 destination dispatch 的模型：呼梯即知终点，调度可以按终点把人分组塞进同一部轿厢。
楼层在本题里始终只是整数编号，它不保存状态也不执行规则。
两键面板下 Controller 根本不知道乘客要去哪，写不进任何目的楼层。
optionExplanations_en: That is why RequestType needs PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN and DESTINATION rather than a destination field.
That describes destination dispatch, where knowing the endpoint up front lets the scheduler group passengers into one car.
A floor here is just an integer label — it holds no state and enforces no rules.
With two-button panels the controller has no idea where the passenger is going, so it cannot write a destination anywhere.
why: 两键面板只给方向，所以电梯必须靠请求类型判断该不该停；代价是调度看不见终点，没法把同终点的人成组分配。
why_en: Two-button panels give only a direction, so the car must use the request type to decide whether to stop — the cost is that dispatch can't group passengers by shared destination.
tradeoff: hall call 两键模型简单 vs destination dispatch 信息更全但调度更复杂
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官要的是高层写字楼的 destination dispatch，Request 就要带目的楼层，调度目标变成按终点成组分车。

termDefinitions.meaning: 选层派梯：乘客在楼层面板上直接选目的楼层，系统当场告诉他坐哪一部。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Destination dispatch lets passengers pick their target floor at a lobby panel, and the system tells them which car to board.

termDefinitions.meaning: 区分 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN、DESTINATION 三种停靠原因的枚举。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is the enum distinguishing the three reasons to stop: pickup going up, pickup going down, and an in-car destination.

scenario: 35 分钟的面试里你问要不要考虑称重、门机构、急停，面试官说「不用，聚焦调度和移动」。
scenario_en: In a 35-minute interview you ask about weight limits, door mechanics and emergency stops, and the interviewer says "skip them, focus on scheduling and movement".
q: 这句话直接省掉了哪一块设计？
q_en: Which piece of design does that answer let you drop?
options: 门状态机可以不写，当前楼层请求直接算已服务
Direction 里的 IDLE 状态可以删掉，电梯不用停
Controller 可以删掉，电梯自己接收 hall call
请求去重可以不做，Set 换成简单的 List
options_en: No door state machine, and a request for the current floor counts as already served.
The IDLE value in Direction can be dropped since the car never stops.
The controller can be removed and each elevator can take hall calls itself.
Deduplication can be skipped and the Set replaced with a plain List.
optionExplanations: 没有门模型就没有「开门中」这个中间状态，addRequest 遇到当前楼层可以直接返回 true。
IDLE 表示的是「没有请求」，跟门无关，删了电梯就会一直往某个方向漂。
多部电梯之间的派发仍在范围内，这正是被明确保留的部分。
同一层同一类型的重复按钮仍然要合并，去重靠的是 Request 的 equals，不是门。
optionExplanations_en: With no door model there is no "doors opening" intermediate state, so addRequest can just return true for the current floor.
IDLE means "no requests" and has nothing to do with doors; drop it and the car drifts in one direction forever.
Dispatching across multiple elevators is exactly the part that was explicitly kept in scope.
Repeated presses on the same floor and type still have to collapse, and that dedup comes from Request.equals, not doors.
why: 「当前楼层视为已服务」这条规则只有在没有门模型时才成立。代价是这套设计答不出「门被挡住怎么办」。
why_en: Treating a request for the current floor as already served only holds because doors are out of scope, and the cost is that this design can't answer what happens when a door is blocked.
tradeoff: 排除门与称重换来 35 分钟内跑通调度 vs 系统无法描述真实停靠过程
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官后来加一句「开门要占 3 秒」，no-op 规则就不成立了，得引入开门状态和停留 tick 计数。

termDefinitions.meaning: 空操作：接受这次调用但什么状态都不改，本题里指请求自己所在的楼层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A no-op accepts the call but changes no state — here, requesting the floor you are already on.

termDefinitions.meaning: Direction 枚举里表示「当前没有任何请求、电梯不动」的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE is the Direction value meaning the elevator has no pending requests and is not moving.

scenario: 实体已经定成 ElevatorController、Elevator、Request，接下来 10 分钟要展开类设计。
scenario_en: The entities are settled as ElevatorController, Elevator and Request, and you have ten minutes to flesh out the class design.
q: 应该先展开哪个类的接口？
q_en: Whose interface should you flesh out first?
options: 先写 Elevator.step 的移动算法，跑通了再往上包
先定 Controller 的对外方法，再钻进 Elevator
先把三个类的字段一次性全部列出来再挑
先写 Request 的 equals 和 hashCode 保证去重
options_en: Start with the movement algorithm in Elevator.step and wrap a controller around it once it works.
Pin down the controller's public methods first, then drill into Elevator.
List every field on all three classes at once, then decide what matters.
Write Request's equals and hashCode first so dedup is guaranteed.
optionExplanations: 自底向上容易写出一个没人调得动的 step：外界拿不到入口，方法签名后面还得返工。
外部代码只碰 Controller，所以 requestElevator(floor, type) 和 step() 是必须先钉死的公共契约。
字段是从需求推出来的结果，先列字段等于跳过「为什么需要它」。
equals/hashCode 是 Request 定型之后的实现细节，此刻连要不要建这个类都还没定。
optionExplanations_en: Bottom-up tends to produce a step nobody can call: there is no entry point yet, and signatures get reworked later.
External code only touches the controller, so requestElevator and step are the public contract to nail down first.
Fields are the output of tracing requirements, so listing them first skips the "why do we need this" step.
equals and hashCode are implementation details that come after Request exists, and that decision is still open.
why: 自顶向下先钉住公共契约，让讨论停在「外面怎么用」而不是先陷进移动细节。代价是移动算法要更晚才验证得到。
why_en: Top-down pins the public contract first so the discussion stays on how the system is used rather than sinking into movement details, at the cost of validating the algorithm later.
tradeoff: 自顶向下先定公共契约 vs 自底向上先跑通移动算法
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官直接说「我只想看 step() 的移动逻辑」，就从 Elevator 开始写，Controller 留一个空壳即可。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类暴露给外部调用方的方法签名集合，决定别人能对它做什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The public contract is the set of method signatures a class exposes, defining what callers are allowed to do with it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收 hall call、决定派哪部电梯并推进整体时间的协调类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ElevatorController receives hall calls, decides which car to dispatch, and advances time for the whole system.

scenario: 你要决定 Elevator 存哪些字段，手上只有一条需求：「沿当前方向继续服务，前方无请求才反向」。
scenario_en: You must decide Elevator's fields with only one requirement in hand: "keep serving in the current direction and reverse only when nothing is ahead".
q: 这条需求直接推出哪个字段？
q_en: Which field does that single requirement force?
options: direction 字段：不记住方向就判断不了「继续」
requestHistory 列表，用来回放走过的每一层
reverseCount 计数器，记录一共反向了几次
targetFloor 字段，指向本趟最终要去的楼层
options_en: A direction field — without remembering direction you cannot decide what "continue" means.
A requestHistory list so you can replay every floor the car has passed.
A reverseCount counter recording how many times it has turned around.
A targetFloor field pointing at the final floor of this trip.
optionExplanations: 问法是「要记住什么才能执行这条需求」，答案就是当前行进方向，UP/DOWN/IDLE 三态。
历史轨迹只服务调试和统计，需求里没有任何规则读它。
反向次数是可以从行为里观察出来的指标，不是执行规则所需的状态。
SCAN 沿途会不断加入新请求，本趟没有固定终点，硬存一个终点反而会打架。
optionExplanations_en: The question is what must be remembered to execute this rule, and the answer is the current travel direction with its three states.
A history trail only serves debugging and analytics; no rule in the requirements reads it.
Reversal count is a metric you can observe from behavior, not state needed to execute a rule.
SCAN keeps absorbing new requests along the way, so a trip has no fixed endpoint and a stored one would conflict.
why: 逐条需求问「要记住什么才能执行它」，状态就被需求推出来而不是拍脑袋加；「可选多个目的楼层」同样推出 requests 集合。
why_en: Ask of each requirement what must be remembered to enforce it, and the state falls out of the requirements instead of being guessed.
tradeoff: 逐条需求反推状态 vs 先凭直觉列字段再回头删
whenOtherWins: 如果需求里出现「显示预计到达时间」，同样的问法会额外推出一个已规划路径或到达时间的缓存字段。

termDefinitions.meaning: 取值 UP、DOWN、IDLE 的枚举，表示电梯此刻的行进方向或静止。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is the enum with values UP, DOWN and IDLE describing how the car is currently moving, or that it is not.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elevator 内部保存所有待停靠 Request 的集合，是它的事实来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The requests set holds every pending stop inside an Elevator and is its source of truth.

scenario: Elevator 的 currentFloor、direction、requests 都是私有字段，队友问要不要统统加上 getter。
scenario_en: Elevator keeps currentFloor, direction and requests private, and a teammate asks whether every one of them should get a getter.
q: 该对外暴露哪些读方法？
q_en: Which read methods should the elevator expose?
options: 三个字段都配 getter 和 setter，方便写测试
只暴露 Controller 派发时要读的楼层和方向
什么都不暴露，Controller 用反射读私有字段
额外暴露 requests 集合本身，方便外部改队列
options_en: Give all three fields getters and setters so tests are easy to write.
Expose only the floor and direction the controller reads when dispatching.
Expose nothing and let the controller read private fields by reflection.
Also expose the requests set itself so callers can edit the queue.
optionExplanations: setter 会让外部直接改 currentFloor，电梯瞬移到别层，step 的不变量当场失效。
getCurrentFloor 和 getDirection 存在的唯一理由就是 selectBestElevator 要读它们。
反射绕过封装还破坏可读性，本质上是把耦合藏起来而不是消除。
交出集合等于让外部绕过 addRequest 的楼层校验和去重，直接写脏状态。
optionExplanations_en: Setters let callers rewrite currentFloor, teleporting the car and breaking step's invariants outright.
getCurrentFloor and getDirection exist for exactly one reason: selectBestElevator has to read them.
Reflection sidesteps encapsulation and hurts readability — it hides the coupling instead of removing it.
Handing out the set lets callers bypass addRequest's floor validation and dedup and write bad state directly.
why: 接口大小由调用方的真实需要决定：Controller 只需要位置和方向两个只读值。多暴露一个集合就多一条绕过校验的路。
why_en: Interface size is decided by what callers truly need — the controller needs only position and direction — and every extra exposure adds another path around validation.
tradeoff: 最小暴露保住封装 vs 全量 getter/setter 方便但状态可被外部改坏
whenOtherWins: 升级到 request-aware 调度时，Controller 还需要 hasRequestsAtOrBeyond 这类只读查询，但仍不该把集合本身交出去。

termDefinitions.meaning: Controller 内部按位置、方向挑出最合适电梯的派发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: selectBestElevator is the controller's dispatch method that picks the most suitable car from position and direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把状态和改动它的规则关在同一个类里，外部只能通过受控方法交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation keeps state and the rules that change it inside one class, so outsiders interact only through controlled methods.

scenario: hall call 由 Controller 派发进来，destination 由轿厢内按钮产生，两条来源都要落到同一部电梯上。
scenario_en: Hall calls arrive via the controller while destinations come from buttons inside the car, and both must land on the same elevator.
q: Elevator 该给几个写入口？
q_en: How many write entry points should Elevator offer?
options: 两个：addHallCall 和 addDestination 各管一边
一个 addRequest(request)，来源信息写在 Request 里
一个 addFloor(int)，方向由电梯自己推断出来
三个：按 PICKUP_UP / PICKUP_DOWN / DESTINATION 各一个
options_en: Two: addHallCall and addDestination, one for each source.
One addRequest(request), with the source encoded inside the Request.
One addFloor(int), letting the elevator infer the direction itself.
Three, one per request type: PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN and DESTINATION.
optionExplanations: 两个方法里的楼层校验、去重、当前楼层 no-op 会被复制两份，改一处就漏一处。
电梯不关心请求为什么来，只关心停在哪层、以什么方向停，类型放进 Request 就够了。
电梯推断不出方向：站在 7 楼的人想上还是想下，只有按钮知道。
三个方法只是把 enum 的分支搬到方法名上，新增一种类型就得再加一个方法。
optionExplanations_en: Floor validation, dedup and the current-floor no-op get duplicated across both methods, so fixing one always misses the other.
The elevator doesn't care why a request arrived, only which floor and which direction, so the type belongs inside Request.
The car cannot infer direction: only the button knows whether the person on floor 7 wants up or down.
Three methods just move an enum branch into method names, and every new type forces another method.
why: 统一入口让校验、去重、no-op 只写一遍，请求来源被 RequestType 吸收。代价是调用方必须自己构造正确的类型。
why_en: A single entry point keeps validation, dedup and the no-op rule in one place, with the source absorbed into RequestType — the cost is that callers must build the right type themselves.
tradeoff: 统一 addRequest 入口 vs 按请求来源拆成多个方法
whenOtherWins: 如果 hall call 以后要额外记等待起始时间做统计，可以包一层专用方法，但底层仍应落回同一个 addRequest。

termDefinitions.meaning: Elevator 上唯一的请求写入方法，负责楼层校验、当前楼层 no-op 和入集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: addRequest is the single write method on Elevator, handling floor validation, the current-floor no-op, and insertion into the set.

termDefinitions.meaning: RequestType 之一，表示轿厢内按下的目的楼层，无论电梯朝哪走都要停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is the request type for a floor button pressed inside the car, and the elevator stops there regardless of direction.

scenario: 新增一部 express 电梯只停 0、5、9 层。有人在 5 楼按「上」，此时 express 正在向下送人。
scenario_en: A new express elevator stops only at floors 0, 5 and 9; someone presses up on floor 5 while the express car is heading down with passengers.
q: Controller 该把这次呼梯派给谁？
q_en: Which car should the controller dispatch for this call?
options: 强行派 express，让它先把车上乘客放下再折返上来
express 不 idle 时回落普通选择逻辑
把请求挂起排队，等 express 空下来再派给它
express 和普通电梯各派一部，谁先到就算谁
options_en: Force the express car anyway and let it drop its current passengers first.
If the express car isn't idle, fall back to normal elevator selection.
Park the request in a queue until the express car frees up.
Dispatch both an express and a normal car and let whichever arrives first win.
optionExplanations: 打断在途行程会让车上乘客先被拉去别的方向，为了一个优先楼层牺牲了一车人。
只在 express 处于 IDLE 时优先它，其余情况完全走原来的分层选择，不需要新数据结构。
挂起会让 5 楼的人在高峰期一直等，而旁边可能就有空闲的普通电梯。
重复派发浪费一部电梯的行程，还要额外写「另一部已服务」的撤销逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Interrupting a trip in progress drags the passengers already aboard the wrong way for the sake of one priority floor.
Prefer the express car only when it is IDLE and otherwise fall straight back to the existing tiered selection, with no new data structures.
Queuing leaves the person on floor 5 waiting through rush hour while an idle normal car may be right there.
Double dispatch wastes a whole car's trip and forces extra cancel logic once one of them arrives.
why: 只在 express 空闲时优先它，是为了不打断在途行程；代价是高峰期 express 很少 idle，优先楼层的收益退化成普通调度。
why_en: Preferring the express car only while it is idle avoids interrupting a trip in progress, at the cost that during rush hour it is rarely idle and priority floors degrade to normal dispatch.
tradeoff: express 优先派发 vs 回落普通选择保证请求不被饿死
whenOtherWins: 如果优先楼层有硬性的等待上限，就得允许打断在途行程或维护 pending 队列，而不是简单回落。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在少数主要楼层停靠的快梯，本题里限定为 0、5、9 层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An express elevator stops only at a few major floors — here 0, 5 and 9.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被指定优先服务的楼层，通常是大堂或换乘层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority floor is one designated for preferential service, typically a lobby or transfer level.

scenario: 乘客按错楼层后点了取消，代码调 removeRequest(Request(7, DESTINATION))，但这一 tick 电梯已经在 7 楼停过了。
scenario_en: A passenger cancels a mis-pressed floor, so the code calls removeRequest for floor 7, but the car already stopped at floor 7 this tick.
q: 这次取消会发生什么？
q_en: What happens on that cancel?
options: 会抛异常，因为要删的元素已经不在集合里
集合里已经没有它，删除是空操作
电梯会掉头再回 7 楼一次补这次服务
requests 变空，电梯会立刻错误地转成 IDLE
options_en: It throws, because the element being removed is no longer in the set.
The set no longer holds it, so the removal is a no-op.
The car turns around and revisits floor 7 to redo the stop.
requests goes empty and the elevator wrongly flips to IDLE right away.
optionExplanations: Set.remove 对不存在的元素返回 false 而不是抛错，这正是它适合做撤销的原因。
停靠那一刻请求就已经被移除，再删一次只是确认它不在。
移动逻辑只读 requests 集合，集合里没有 7 楼就没有任何理由回去。
取消并没有额外删掉别的请求，其它待停靠请求还在，方向也不变。
optionExplanations_en: Set.remove returns false for a missing element rather than throwing, which is exactly why it suits undo.
The request was already removed at the moment of the stop, so removing again just confirms it is gone.
Movement logic reads only the requests set, and with floor 7 absent there is no reason to go back.
The cancel removed nothing extra, so the remaining stops and the current direction are untouched.
why: 正常路径是 addRequest 进集合、停靠时移除；取消晚到只是重复移除同一个 Request，step 一行都不用改。代价是分不清「取消成功」和「早就到过」。
why_en: Requests enter the set through addRequest and leave when the car stops, so a late cancel is just a repeat removal and step needs no change — the cost is you cannot tell a successful cancel from an already-served stop.
tradeoff: removeRequest 幂等实现最简单 vs 无法区分取消成功与请求早已服务
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要按按钮灯反馈取消是否生效，removeRequest 就得返回布尔值，并区分「从未存在」和「已服务」。

termDefinitions.meaning: addRequest 的逆操作，从电梯的 requests 集合里删掉一个请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: removeRequest is the inverse of addRequest, deleting one request from the elevator's set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个操作执行一次和执行多次，系统最终状态完全相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An operation is idempotent when running it once and running it many times leave the system in the same final state.

scenario: 实体阶段已经定下 Elevator 和 Controller，轮到 Request 时你还看不出存一个楼层整数够不够。
scenario_en: Elevator and Controller are settled, but when you reach Request you cannot yet tell whether a bare floor integer suffices.
q: 此刻最好的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle that uncertainty?
options: 当场拍板用 Set<Integer>，简单优先
当场拍板建 Request 类，反正更灵活
说明先搁置，等移动逻辑清楚再定
两种都建，运行时按配置切换实现
options_en: Commit now to a Set of integers and keep it simple.
Commit now to a Request class since it is more flexible anyway.
Say you're deferring it until the movement logic makes the answer clear.
Build both and switch implementations by configuration at runtime.
optionExplanations: 楼层数字会让向下等梯的人被向上的电梯接走，但这个坑要写完停靠逻辑才暴露。
还没有证据说明需要它，此时建类就是凭偏好而非需求做决定。
把「这个决定依赖什么」讲出来，面试官看到的是判断顺序而不是犹豫。
为一个尚未确定的问题同时维护两套实现，是典型的过度设计。
optionExplanations_en: Bare floor numbers let an upward car pick up someone waiting to go down, but that trap only surfaces once the stopping logic is written.
There is no evidence yet that it is needed, so committing now is a preference rather than a requirement.
Saying out loud what the decision depends on shows the interviewer your ordering of judgements, not hesitation.
Maintaining two implementations for an undecided question is textbook over-engineering.
why: 楼层整数够不够，取决于停靠要不要区分方向——这要等 step 的停靠规则才看得清。提前拍板不是过度设计就是返工。
why_en: Whether a bare floor number suffices depends on whether stopping must be direction-aware, and that only becomes visible once step's stopping rule exists.
tradeoff: 提前建 Request 类的灵活 vs 等移动逻辑明朗再定带来的返工风险
whenOtherWins: 如果需求里已经明说 hall call 必须带方向，就不用搁置了，当场建 Request 类是正确的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示一次待停靠的请求，携带楼层和 RequestType 两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request represents one pending stop and carries a floor plus a RequestType.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为还没出现的需求提前引入抽象，换来更高的理解与维护成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-engineering means adding abstraction for requirements that have not appeared yet, paying in comprehension and maintenance cost.

scenario: 面试官只给一句『设计一个电梯控制系统』，开口前要把问题范围钉牢。
scenario_en: The interviewer just says "design an elevator control system" — you must pin down scope before writing anything.
q: 结构化澄清应覆盖哪四个方面？（多选）
q_en: Which four areas should structured clarifying questions cover? (select all)
options: 核心动作是什么（比如呼梯、选层如何触发）
错误情况怎么处理（比如非法楼层、重复请求）
系统边界在哪（比如要不要做称重、开关门）
要不要为将来的扩展留空间（比如未来加 express）
面试官希望用什么编程语言写代码
options_en: What the core actions are (e.g., how a hall call or floor selection gets triggered)
How errors should be handled (e.g., invalid floors, duplicate requests)
Where the system boundary is (e.g., whether to model weight or doors)
Whether to leave room for future extensions (e.g., adding an express car later)
Which programming language the interviewer wants for the code
optionExplanations: 核心动作决定了要建哪些实体和方法，是四象限里最先问的一块。
错误处理划清了 addRequest/requestElevator 该拒绝哪些输入。
系统边界（称重、开关门）划出去，才能把 35 分钟花在调度和移动上。
未来扩展决定当前设计要不要为 Strategy 模式这类改动留缝。
这是实现方式的偏好，属于『怎么写代码』，不属于需求范围本身。
optionExplanations_en: Core actions determine which entities and methods you need — usually the first thing to ask.
Error handling defines what addRequest/requestElevator must reject.
Carving out the boundary (weight, doors) frees the 35 minutes for scheduling and movement.
Future extensions decide whether today's design should leave room for something like the Strategy pattern.
This is an implementation-style preference, not a question about the scope of the requirements.
why: 四象限把模糊题拆成可执行的澄清清单；语言/代码风格属于实现方式，不属于需求范围本身。
why_en: The four areas turn a vague prompt into an actionable clarification checklist; language or pseudocode preference is an implementation question, not a scope question.

scenario: 面试官出的是电梯题，但这类『自己控制时间』的模式在停车场、售货机、红绿灯题里反复出现。
scenario_en: This is an elevator problem, but the "you control time yourself" pattern recurs in parking-lot, vending-machine, and traffic-light problems.
q: 这类 LLD 题的通用处理模式是什么？
q_en: What is the general pattern for handling this class of LLD problems?
options: 尽量还原真实硬件中断，展示系统编程能力
抽象掉硬件，自己用 step() 推进时间
为每种题单独设计一套推进机制，互不复用
把时间处理留给面试官决定，自己只写业务逻辑
options_en: Faithfully reproduce real hardware interrupts to show systems-programming skill
Abstract away the hardware and advance time yourself with step()
Design a fresh time-advancement mechanism per problem, with no reuse
Leave time handling for the interviewer to decide and just write business logic
optionExplanations: 面试想看对象建模和算法，不是异步中断和线程编排能力。
跨题型复用同一个思路：自己控制时间比对接真实硬件事件更省时间、更好测。
每题重新发明时间推进方式，浪费本该花在算法上的 35 分钟。
时间推进是核心设计的一部分，主动提出并确认，不该丢给面试官决定。
optionExplanations_en: The interview wants to see object modeling and algorithms, not async interrupts or thread orchestration.
The same idea reuses across problem types: controlling time yourself is faster to build and easier to test than real hardware events.
Reinventing time-advancement for every problem wastes the 35 minutes that should go to algorithms.
Time-advancement is a core design decision you should raise yourself, not leave for the interviewer.
why: 这些 LLD 题都用 step()/tick() 抽象掉硬件，让仿真确定、可测试，35 分钟内聚焦对象建模而不是异步事件。
why_en: These LLD problems all abstract hardware away with step()/tick(), keeping the simulation deterministic and testable within 35 minutes.
tradeoff: 自控 step()/tick() 的可测试性 vs 对接真实硬件事件驱动的真实性
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说要设计真实控制软件而不是仿真，才需要转向硬件中断和异步回调模型。

scenario: 面试官说『3 部电梯服务 10 层，先固定，不用支持配置』。
scenario_en: The interviewer says "3 elevators serving 10 floors, keep it fixed for now, no need to support configuration."
q: 这个规模假设对实现方式有什么影响？
q_en: What design implication follows from this scale assumption?
options: 3 部电梯也要用最小堆维护楼层顺序才能正确调度
遍历 3 部电梯做线性扫描已经够用，不必建调度索引结构
这个规模已经很大，必须先做数据分片才能继续设计
既然电梯数量固定，楼层边界也能写成 10 个 if 分支
options_en: Even 3 elevators need a min-heap over floors to dispatch correctly
A linear scan over 3 elevators is already fast enough — no index structure needed
The scale is already large enough that data sharding is required first
Since the elevator count is fixed, floor boundaries can be hardcoded as 10 if-branches
optionExplanations: 堆的优势体现在大规模排序上，3 个元素的堆反而增加不必要的复杂度。
3 是常量级，for 循环找最近/顺路的线性扫描足够快，不必上索引结构。
3 部电梯、10 层是很小的规模，数据分片是完全不成比例的过度设计。
楼层边界应由请求集合驱动，硬编码 if 反而会引入新 bug。
optionExplanations_en: Heaps pay off at large scale; wrapping 3 elements in a heap only adds needless complexity.
3 is a constant-size scale — a for-loop scan for nearest/committed elevators is fast enough without an index.
3 elevators and 10 floors is a tiny scale — sharding data would be wildly disproportionate over-engineering.
Floor boundaries should fall out of the request set; hardcoding an if-branch introduces new bugs instead.
why: 3 部电梯、10 层是给定的小规模，遍历比建索引结构更省时间；这类假设决定要不要为规模优化数据结构。
why_en: With only 3 elevators and 10 floors, a linear scan beats building an index — the scale assumption decides whether you need scale-optimized structures.
tradeoff: 线性扫描的简单实现 vs 索引结构在大规模下才有的收益
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官把规模改成几百部电梯、上千楼层，线性扫描就该换成按位置索引的结构。

scenario: 高峰期电梯不断收到新 hall call，nearest-first 每次都改追最新最近的请求。
scenario_en: During rush hour new hall calls keep arriving, and nearest-first keeps re-targeting whichever request is currently closest.
q: 繁忙楼里 SCAN 相对 nearest-first 的关键优势是什么？
q_en: In a busy building, what is SCAN's key advantage over nearest-first?
options: SCAN 每次都重新计算全局最优路径，适应新请求
SCAN 只服务先到的请求，新请求一律排到队尾
SCAN 沿方向扫掠顺路接人，不会因新请求反复折返
SCAN 会把所有请求先收集满，再一次性统一调度
options_en: SCAN recomputes a globally optimal route on every new request
SCAN only serves requests in arrival order, pushing new ones to the back
SCAN sweeps in one direction and picks up along the way, so new requests don't force reversals
SCAN waits to collect all requests before dispatching in one batch
optionExplanations: 全局最优要枚举请求组合，随请求数指数级增长，不是 SCAN 的做法。
SCAN 按位置和方向决定服务顺序，不是按到达时间排队的 FIFO。
扫掠中顺路的新请求会被自然捎带，方向切换次数被压到最多一次。
SCAN 逐 tick 推进，不会等请求收集满才开始移动。
optionExplanations_en: Global optimality means enumerating request permutations, which blows up with request count — not what SCAN does.
SCAN orders service by position and direction, not by arrival order like FIFO.
Same-direction requests along the sweep get picked up naturally, capping reversals at roughly one.
SCAN advances one tick at a time and never waits for requests to accumulate first.
why: SCAN 一次扫掠顺带服务同向新请求，方向切换被压到最多一次；这正是繁忙楼里防止来回震荡的原理。
why_en: SCAN sweeps one direction and batches same-direction pickups along the way, capping reversals — that's what prevents thrashing under heavy load.
tradeoff: SCAN 扫掠批量顺路 vs nearest-first 贴近但方向反复震荡
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单部电梯、请求很稀疏，两者差别很小，可以先用更简单的 nearest-first。

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: 沿当前方向持续服务请求，直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps serving requests in the current direction and only reverses once nothing remains ahead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调度反复来回改变方向、效率被震荡掉的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thrashing is when a scheduler keeps flipping direction back and forth, burning efficiency on the reversals.

scenario: 候选人实现的电梯会先冲到 8 楼，再折回 3 楼，最后又爬回 7 楼，来回摆动但最终服务了所有请求。
scenario_en: The candidate's elevator rushes to floor 8, doubles back to floor 3, then climbs to floor 7 — it bounces but eventually serves every request.
q: 这段实现达到了哪个候选人级别的标准？
q_en: Which candidate-level bar does this implementation clear?
options: 达到 Junior 标准，未达 Mid-level 要求
已经达到 Mid-level 标准，可以直接进入并发讨论
连 Junior 标准都不够，因为没能服务所有楼层
达到 Senior 标准，因为展示了完整的移动轨迹
options_en: Clears the Junior bar, but not the Mid-level bar
It already clears the Mid-level bar and is ready to move on to concurrency
It doesn't even clear the Junior bar because it fails to serve every floor
It clears the Senior bar because it shows a complete movement trace
optionExplanations: 文章原话：junior 可以摆动，重要的是最终服务完；mid 要求核心循环无需提示就写对。
Mid-level 标准正是要消除这种反复摆动，这段实现还没做到。
题面已说明『最终服务了所有请求』，满足 junior 的底线要求。
Senior 关注调度权衡和并发风险，不是单纯展示移动轨迹。
optionExplanations_en: The article says junior can bounce as long as every request eventually gets served; mid must get the core loop right with minimal hints.
The Mid-level bar is exactly to eliminate this kind of back-and-forth bouncing, which this implementation hasn't done.
The scenario already states every request was eventually served, which meets the junior floor.
Senior focus is on dispatch tradeoffs and concurrency risk, not just showing a full movement trace.
why: Junior 只要求最终服务完所有请求；Mid-level 要求『沿一个方向服务到底才反向』的核心循环无需提示就写对。
why_en: Junior only needs every request eventually served; Mid-level must get the "keep going one direction, then reverse" core loop right with minimal hints.
tradeoff: Junior 的『最终正确』 vs Mid-level 的『无提示写对核心循环』

scenario: 候选人只用 Set<Integer> 存楼层号，不区分 hall call 方向，电梯偶尔接错方向的乘客。
scenario_en: The candidate stores only Set<Integer> floor numbers, ignoring hall-call direction, so the elevator occasionally picks up passengers going the wrong way.
q: 文章认为这种简化在什么情况下可以接受？
q_en: Under what condition does the article consider this simplification acceptable?
options: 任何级别都可以接受，反正乘客最终能到目的地
只在 Junior 面试里可以接受，更高标准应该改用 Request 类
只有电梯少于 2 部时才可以接受
只要没有 hall call、只有 destination 请求时才可以接受
options_en: Acceptable at any level since the passenger eventually reaches their destination
Acceptable only in a Junior interview; a higher bar expects the Request class
Acceptable only when there are fewer than 2 elevators
Acceptable only when there are no hall calls, just in-cab destinations
optionExplanations: 接错方向乘客本身就是文章点名的体验问题，不该被『最终到达』抹平。
这正好点出标准分层：初级先跑通简化模型，更高标准要主动升级方向感知。
电梯数量和方向识别是否需要区分请求类型无关。
hall call 恰恰是方向感知的来源，没有 hall call 时这个问题反而不存在。
optionExplanations_en: Picking up the wrong-direction passenger is exactly the experience problem the article calls out — "eventually arrives" doesn't erase it.
This marks the level split: junior can ship the simplified model first, a higher bar upgrades to direction awareness on its own.
The elevator count has nothing to do with whether request types need to be direction-aware.
Hall calls are exactly where the direction problem comes from — without them the issue wouldn't exist.
why: 文章原话：该简化对 junior 级别的面试可能可以接受，但『我们可以做得更好』——更高标准应升级为区分方向的 Request 类。
why_en: The article's own words: this simplification may be acceptable for a junior interview, but "we can do better" — a higher bar upgrades to the direction-aware Request class.
tradeoff: 实现速度（Set<Integer>） vs 乘客体验正确性（Request 类）

scenario: 要加一部只停 0、5、9 层的 express 电梯，同时不想牵动其余电梯的设计。
scenario_en: You're adding an express elevator that only stops at floors 0, 5, 9, without touching the rest of the design.
q: Request 类本身需要为此改动吗？
q_en: Does the Request class itself need to change for this?
options: 需要给 Request 加一个 isExpress 字段跟着请求走
不需要，Elevator 加 isExpress 标志和限定楼层集合即可
需要把 Request 拆成 ExpressRequest 和 NormalRequest 两个子类
需要让 Controller 直接在 Request 里写死允许楼层列表
options_en: Yes — add an isExpress field to Request so it travels with the request
No — just add an isExpress flag and an allowed-floor set to Elevator
Yes — split Request into ExpressRequest and NormalRequest subclasses
Yes — have Controller hardcode the allowed floor list inside Request
optionExplanations: 请求本身不知道自己会被派给哪部电梯，isExpress 字段对它没有意义。
楼层限制是电梯的能力，不是请求的属性，改 Elevator 就够。
子类化 Request 会让 equals/hashCode 和现有 Set 逻辑复杂化，且没必要。
Request 是数据类，写死楼层列表混入了电梯的能力信息，职责不清。
optionExplanations_en: A request doesn't know which elevator it will be dispatched to, so isExpress on it carries no meaning.
The floor restriction is a capability of the elevator, not a property of the request — Elevator alone needs the change.
Subclassing Request complicates equals/hashCode and the existing Set logic for no real benefit.
Request is a data class; baking a floor list into it mixes in elevator-capability information it shouldn't own.
why: express 是电梯这一层的能力约束（哪些楼层可停），不是请求本身的属性；Request 仍只存 floor 和 type，改动全部留在 Elevator。
why_en: Express is a capability constraint of the elevator (which floors it can stop at), not a property of the request itself — Request still only stores floor and type.
tradeoff: 改 Elevator（能力约束局部化） vs 改 Request（把状态摊给所有请求）
whenOtherWins: 如果未来要按乘客类型做更复杂的路由规则，那时才值得把类型信息挪回 Request。

scenario: 需求明确把『动态增删电梯配置』划为范围外，电梯数量在构造函数里写死为 3。
scenario_en: Requirements explicitly put "dynamic floor/elevator configuration" out of scope, and the elevator count is hardcoded to 3 in the constructor.
q: 这个范围排除对 ElevatorController 的实现有什么直接影响？
q_en: What is the direct implementation impact of that scope exclusion on ElevatorController?
options: elevators 必须换成支持动态扩容的线程安全集合
elevators 用构造时建好的固定列表即可
Controller 需要支持运行时动态增删电梯的接口
每次 step() 都要先检查电梯列表是否发生变化
options_en: elevators must become a thread-safe collection that supports dynamic growth
elevators can be a fixed list built once at construction
Controller needs an interface for adding/removing elevators at runtime
step() must first check whether the elevator list changed on every call
optionExplanations: 动态扩容的并发安全集合是为『支持配置』准备的，本题范围外，属于过度设计。
3 部电梯的初始化只在构造函数跑一次，后续也不需要再处理上线下线。
运行时增删电梯的接口只有在数量可变时才有意义，这里数量固定不变。
elevators 结构本身不会在运行中变化，step() 不需要为此多做检查。
optionExplanations_en: A dynamically growable, concurrency-safe collection is built for configurability, which is explicitly out of scope here — over-engineering.
The 3 elevators are built once inside the constructor; there's no online/offline handling to do afterward.
An add/remove-at-runtime interface only matters if the elevator count can change, which it can't here.
The elevators structure never changes during a run, so step() doesn't need an extra check for it.
why: 范围排除『动态配置』意味着 elevators 是一次性初始化的固定列表，不用为运行时增删多写并发安全代码。
why_en: Excluding dynamic configuration from scope means elevators is a fixed list built once — no need for extra concurrency-safe code to add or remove cars at runtime.
tradeoff: 固定列表的简单 vs 动态扩容结构的通用性

scenario: Elevator 类的设计描述写明『不知道其他电梯的存在』，只管自己的位置和请求。
scenario_en: The Elevator class is described as not knowing about other elevators — it only manages its own position and requests.
q: Elevator 持有其他 Elevator 引用的最直接坏处？
q_en: If Elevator held references to other Elevators internally, what's the most direct downside?
options: Elevator 的 step() 会因此运行得明显更慢
调度逻辑会泄漏进 Elevator，职责边界被打破
Request 类的 equals/hashCode 判断会因此失效
仿真会因此无法再用 step()/tick() 离散推进
options_en: Elevator's step() would run noticeably slower as a result
Dispatch logic would leak into Elevator, breaking the responsibility boundary
Request's equals/hashCode comparisons would stop working
The simulation would no longer be able to advance via step()/tick()
optionExplanations: 持有额外引用本身不会显著拖慢单个 elevator 的一次 step 调用。
职责边界一旦被打破，替换或测试调度算法都会牵连到 Elevator 内部实现。
equals/hashCode 只依赖 Request 自己的 floor 和 type，跟 Elevator 互相持有引用无关。
离散推进由 Controller.step() 依次调用每部 Elevator.step() 保证，跟引用无关。
optionExplanations_en: Holding an extra reference doesn't meaningfully slow down a single elevator's own step call.
Once the boundary breaks, swapping or testing the dispatch algorithm ends up dragging in Elevator's internals.
equals/hashCode depend only on Request's own floor and type, unrelated to whether elevators reference each other.
Discrete advancement is guaranteed by Controller.step() calling each Elevator.step() in turn, independent of references.
why: 调度（看全局选电梯）和移动（管自己位置）是两种职责；Elevator 拿到别的电梯引用后很容易开始做调度判断，边界就模糊了。
why_en: Dispatch and movement are separate jobs; giving Elevator sibling references invites it to start making dispatch decisions, blurring the boundary.
tradeoff: Elevator 只管自己（可独立测试） vs 持有全局视图（方便但耦合）
whenOtherWins: 如果要做电梯间协同（比如互相避让、负载均衡），那部分逻辑也该放进 Controller，而不是让 Elevator 互相持有引用。

scenario: FIFO 移动策略用 Queue<Request> 按到达顺序处理；SCAN 实现最终改用了 Set<Request>。
scenario_en: The FIFO movement strategy used Queue<Request> in arrival order; the final SCAN implementation switched to Set<Request>.
q: SCAN 为什么改用 Set 而不是沿用 Queue？
q_en: Why does SCAN switch to a Set instead of keeping the Queue?
options: Set 比 Queue 占用内存更少，性能更好
SCAN 按位置和方向挑请求，Set 不强加到达顺序
Queue 无法存储 Request 对象，只能存整数
Set 能自动按楼层从小到大排序，方便扫描
options_en: Set uses less memory than Queue and performs better
SCAN picks by position and direction, and Set imposes no arrival order
Queue can't store Request objects, only integers
Set automatically sorts by floor ascending, which is convenient for the sweep
optionExplanations: 两者存放的数据量相同（未服务请求数），内存差异不是这里的决定因素。
SCAN 每步都要重新判断『离我最近/顺路的是谁』，跟入队顺序无关，无序的 Set 更贴合。
Queue 同样可以存对象，问题不在于能不能存，而在于它强加了到达顺序。
HashSet 本身不保证任何顺序，扫描时仍要遍历比较，不会自动排好序。
optionExplanations_en: Both hold the same amount of data (unserved requests) — memory isn't the deciding factor here.
SCAN re-evaluates "who is closest/committed" every step, unrelated to enqueue order, so an unordered Set fits better.
Queue can store objects fine too; the issue is that it imposes arrival order, not storage capability.
A HashSet guarantees no ordering at all — the sweep still has to iterate and compare, it isn't pre-sorted.
why: FIFO 靠 Queue 的到达顺序驱动；SCAN 靠位置和方向挑下一个目标，跟到达顺序无关，所以换成不排序的 Set，顺带靠 equals/hashCode 去重。
why_en: FIFO is driven by arrival order; SCAN picks its next target by position and direction instead, so it switches to an unordered Set that also dedupes via equals/hashCode.
tradeoff: Queue 的到达顺序 vs Set 的位置/方向驱动加天然去重

scenario: 多个 hall call 并发调用 requestElevator，同时 step() 正在遍历同一个 Elevator 的 requests 集合并做删除。
scenario_en: Multiple hall calls call requestElevator concurrently while step() is iterating and removing from the same Elevator's requests set.
q: 不加任何同步机制时，实际会发生什么？
q_en: With no synchronization at all, what actually happens?
options: Set 内部会自动帮并发读写排好队，完全不需要额外处理
addRequest 撞上 step() 遍历/删除，产生未定义修改
两次 hall call 会互相覆盖楼层号，只服务后到的那次请求
step() 发现集合被修改后自动跳过当前 tick，下一 tick 重试
options_en: The Set internally serializes concurrent access for you, no extra handling needed
addRequest collides with step()'s iterate/remove, causing undefined modification
The two hall calls overwrite each other's floor number; only the later one gets served
step() detects the modified set and auto-skips this tick, retrying next tick
optionExplanations: HashSet/普通集合都不是线程安全的，并发读写没有任何自动串行化保证。
两个操作都改同一个共享 Set 却没有互斥，这正是需要锁或队列缓冲的经典竞态。
两次 hall call 各自生成不同的 Request 对象，不会互相覆盖成一个楼层号。
并发修改的后果是未定义行为，不能假设运行时会优雅地跳过重试。
optionExplanations_en: Plain HashSet-style collections are not thread-safe; concurrent access has no automatic serialization guarantee.
Both operations mutate the same shared Set without mutual exclusion — the textbook race that needs a lock or queue buffer.
The two hall calls produce separate Request objects; they don't overwrite each other into a single floor number.
Concurrent modification produces undefined behavior — you can't assume the runtime gracefully skips and retries.
why: addRequest 写入撞上 step() 正在遍历的同一个 Set，产生未定义的并发修改；锁互斥或『先入队列再 drain』能恢复，代价是阻塞或多一 tick 延迟。
why_en: addRequest's write collides with step()'s in-progress iteration, causing undefined concurrent modification; a lock or queue-drain pattern recovers it, at a blocking or latency cost.
tradeoff: 全局锁的简单可控 vs 并发队列的低阻塞但多一 tick 延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果并发量很低（比如仿真本来就单线程跑），根本不需要锁或队列，直接单线程处理最简单。

scenario: 电梯在 tick 6 服务完所有请求后进入 IDLE，一直停到 tick 7 才因新请求开始移动。
scenario_en: The elevator goes IDLE at tick 6 after serving every request, and doesn't move again until tick 7 when a new request arrives.
q: IDLE 状态在 tick 6 到 tick 7 之间起了什么作用？
q_en: What role does the IDLE state play between tick 6 and tick 7?
options: 让电梯提前预测下一个可能的请求楼层，主动靠近
让电梯在没有请求时保持静止，直到新请求真正到达才决定方向并移动
让电梯在原地继续沿上一次方向缓慢漂移
让 Controller 在 IDLE 期间跳过对这部电梯的 step() 调用
options_en: It lets the elevator predict the next likely request floor and move toward it early
It keeps the elevator still while there are no requests, until a new one actually arrives to pick a direction and move
It lets the elevator keep drifting slowly in its last direction while idle
It makes Controller skip calling step() on this elevator while it's IDLE
optionExplanations: 仿真不做预测，电梯只对已经存在的请求做反应，不会主动靠近假想的请求。
文中验证片段正是如此：tick 6 进入 IDLE，直到 tick 7 收到新请求才重新判断方向。
IDLE 的意义正是不再移动，『缓慢漂移』违反了这个状态的定义。
Controller.step() 依然会调用每部电梯的 step()，只是 IDLE 分支让它什么都不做。
optionExplanations_en: The simulation doesn't predict; the elevator only reacts to requests that already exist, never moving toward a hypothetical one.
That's exactly the article's trace: IDLE at tick 6, and direction is only re-decided once a new request arrives at tick 7.
The whole point of IDLE is to stop moving — "slow drift" would violate that definition.
Controller.step() still calls every elevator's step(); the IDLE branch just makes it a no-op.
why: 没有 IDLE，无请求的电梯会继续按上次方向漂移；IDLE 让它原地等待，直到 tick 7 新请求进来才重新判断方向、开始移动。
why_en: Without IDLE, a requestless elevator would keep drifting in its last direction; IDLE holds it still until tick 7's new request makes it re-decide direction and move.

scenario: 并发方案已经选定候选：给 requestElevator 和 step() 加同一把锁，或改成线程安全队列由 step() 每 tick drain。
scenario_en: Two concurrency options are on the table: one shared lock around requestElevator and step(), or a thread-safe queue that step() drains each tick.
q: 两种方案的核心取舍轴是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff axis between the two approaches?
options: 锁的性能天生更高，队列实现天生更复杂，没有真正折中
锁简单但阻塞；队列不阻塞但新请求晚一 tick 生效
锁只能防止读冲突，队列只能防止写冲突，需要两者都用
锁和队列在这个场景下完全等价，选哪个都不影响运行行为
options_en: Lock is inherently faster; queue is inherently more complex, no real tradeoff
Lock is simple but blocking; queue doesn't block but delays a new request by one tick
Lock only prevents read conflicts, queue only prevents write conflicts, so you need both
Lock and queue are fully equivalent here, either choice behaves the same
optionExplanations: 锁不是天生更快，反而因为互斥牺牲了并发度；队列的复杂度也不是没有折中,代价是延迟。
文章原话：两种都对，锁简单但阻塞，队列更优雅，代价是要等下一 tick 才 drain 到位。
两个方案要解决的都是同一组『读+写同一共享状态』的竞态，不是分别对应读/写冲突。
队列引入了最多一 tick 的处理延迟，行为上并不完全等价于锁。
optionExplanations_en: A lock isn't inherently faster — mutual exclusion trades away concurrency; the queue's complexity also comes with a latency cost.
The article's own take: both are valid, the lock is simple but blocks, the queue is more elegant but delays a new request by one tick.
Both approaches address the same race on shared state being read and written at once, not separate read vs write conflicts.
The queue introduces up to one tick of processing latency, so its behavior isn't fully equivalent to the lock.
why: 锁让 requestElevator 和 step() 互斥，简单但会阻塞彼此；队列让生产者和 step() 分离，不阻塞，但新请求要等下一 tick 才被处理。
why_en: A lock makes requestElevator and step() mutually exclusive — simple but blocking; a queue separates them with no blocking, at the cost of one extra tick before a new request is processed.
tradeoff: 锁的简单实现 vs 队列的低阻塞但多一 tick 延迟

rows: hall call 与 step 互相等待
互不阻塞，多一 tick 延迟
并发量大，要求低延迟响应

scenario: 面试官追问：如果 hall call 要加上方向语义，你的哪部分代码要跟着改？
scenario_en: The interviewer follows up: if hall calls need direction semantics, which part of your code has to change?
q: 良好封装下，这个改动应该局限在哪？
q_en: Under good encapsulation, where should this change stay contained?
options: step() 的循环结构要整体重写，多了一个方向维度
只改 requests 数据结构，step 控制流骨架不变
Controller 对外方法签名要全部废弃重写
需要新增 DirectionManager 类接管移动逻辑
options_en: step()'s loop structure needs a full rewrite for the new direction dimension
Only the requests data structure changes; step's control-flow skeleton stays the same
All of Controller's public method signatures need to be deprecated and rewritten
A new DirectionManager class is needed to take over movement logic
optionExplanations: 循环骨架（idle/停靠/反向/移动五个 case）保持不变，只是停靠判断变得更精细。
数据结构从 Integer 换成 Request，判断条件跟着变，但 tick 的宏观结构没变。
requestElevator(floor, type) 的签名本来就带 type，不需要废弃重写。
这是不必要的新增类，方向逻辑放在 Request 和 step 的判断里就够。
optionExplanations_en: The loop skeleton (idle/stop/reverse/move cases) stays the same; only the stop-check condition gets more precise.
The data structure swaps Integer for Request and the check conditions follow, but the tick's macro structure is unchanged.
requestElevator(floor, type) already carries type in its signature, so nothing needs deprecating.
This is an unnecessary new class — direction logic already fits inside Request and step's checks.
why: 方向信息只改变『存什么请求、停靠时比对什么』，不改变 step 的整体节奏（idle→定向→停靠检查→反向检查→移动）。
why_en: Direction information only changes what gets stored and compared at a stop, not step's overall rhythm (idle → pick direction → stop check → reverse check → move).
tradeoff: 改数据结构（局部）vs 改控制流骨架（全局）

scenario: 为支持 VIP 优先，把所有请求塞进 priority queue 按优先级弹出，替代 SCAN 的方向扫掠。
scenario_en: To support VIP priority, all requests go into a priority queue popped by priority, replacing SCAN's directional sweep.
q: 这个替代方案实际运行时会出现什么问题？
q_en: What actually goes wrong when this replacement runs?
options: 优先级队列会让电梯完全停止响应普通请求，直到程序重启
电梯为了服务高优先级请求频繁掉头，顺路的普通请求被反复搁置
这只是实现细节的变化，扫掠行为和 SCAN 完全一样
优先级队列没法存储 Request 对象，编译都通不过
options_en: The priority queue makes the elevator stop responding to normal requests entirely until restart
The elevator reverses direction repeatedly to serve high-priority requests, stranding same-direction normal ones
This is just an implementation detail change — sweep behavior stays identical to SCAN
A priority queue can't store Request objects, so it won't even compile
optionExplanations: 队列不会让电梯停摆，只是牺牲了移动的连贯性，不是彻底无响应。
高优先级请求随时能插队打断当前扫掠方向，普通乘客的等待时间因此变得不可预测。
SCAN 靠『前方无请求才反向』维持最多一次反向；优先级队列没有这个约束，行为并不相同。
优先级队列可以存任何带比较器的对象，Request 一样能存，这不是技术障碍。
optionExplanations_en: The queue doesn't stop the elevator — it sacrifices movement continuity, not responsiveness altogether.
A high-priority request can cut in and interrupt the current sweep at any moment, making normal wait times unpredictable.
SCAN caps reversals near one via "reverse only when nothing remains ahead"; the priority queue has no such constraint, so behavior differs.
A priority queue can hold any comparable object; Request is no exception — this isn't a technical blocker.
why: 队列每次弹出的是优先级最高而不是顺路的请求，电梯可能刚经过某层又要为高优先级请求折返，这正是文章说的『跳来跳去而不是高效移动』。
why_en: The queue always pops by priority, not by sweep order, so the elevator may pass a floor then reverse for it — the "jumping around" the article warns about.
tradeoff: 优先级响应速度 vs 移动路径的连贯性（方向反转次数）
whenOtherWins: 如果 VIP 请求极少且允许电梯短暂脱离正常扫掠，优先级抢占反而能让 VIP 更快，这时候取舍就反过来了。

scenario: 面试官说：设计一个支持创建文件/目录、路径导航和基本文件操作的内存文件系统，只保留单根目录树。
q: 这个内存文件系统的基础能力包含哪些？（多选）
options: 单根目录的层级树
文件存储字符串内容
创建、删除、列出、重命名、移动文件或文件夹
支持相对路径、权限、持久化和符号链接
why: 范围是内存中的单根绝对路径树：创建、删除、列出、重命名、移动加内容存储。相对路径、权限、持久化、符号链接都被面试官明确排除。
why_en: The base file system is an in-memory, single-root, absolute-path tree with string content plus five core mutation operations.
options_en: A hierarchical tree under a single root.
Files store string content.
Create, delete, list, rename, and move files or folders.
Support relative paths, permissions, persistence, and symlinks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从根目录 / 开始书写的完整路径，如 /home/user/notes.txt。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An absolute path is a full path written from the root, such as /home/user/notes.txt.

q_en: Which base capabilities does this in-memory file system support? (multi-select)
scenario_en: The interviewer says: design an in-memory file system that supports creating files/folders, path navigation, and basic file operations, keeping just a single-root tree.
optionExplanations: 单根树是这套内存文件系统的骨架，后续所有路径都从这一个 root 出发解析。
文件不区分类型，统一按字符串存内容，省去序列化和类型系统的复杂度。
这五个操作对应最终需求清单，是这版实现必须跑通的最小操作集。
这四项每个都单独被面试官划出范围，实现里不用为它们预留接口。
optionExplanations_en: The single root gives this in-memory tree one entry point that every path resolves from.
Files skip type distinctions and just hold string content, avoiding serialization overhead.
These five operations are the minimum command set this version has to support end to end.
Each of these four was explicitly carved out by the interviewer, so there's no need to design for them here.

scenario: 需求中反复出现 /home/user/docs 这类路径。
q: Path 应该如何建模？
options: 作为独立实体，自己保存全局状态和子节点列表
定义成 Folder 的子类类型
字符串输入，由 FileSystem 解析
定义成 File 的父类类型
why: 路径是定位输入，不拥有生命周期或可变状态；把解析逻辑集中在 FileSystem helper 里就够。
why_en: Path is just an input string to resolve, not a domain entity with its own state.
tradeoff: Path 作为无状态输入字符串 vs 独立 Path/Resolver 实体
whenOtherWins: 如果支持相对路径、规范化、符号链接、挂载点和权限检查，Path/Resolver 可能值得独立建模。
options_en: A standalone entity that holds its own global state and list of children.
Defined as a subclass of Folder.
A string input that FileSystem resolves.
Defined as a superclass of File.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识树中某个位置的字符串，例如 /home/user/docs。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A path is a string that identifies a location in the tree, such as /home/user/docs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持有 root 并对外提供路径 API 的入口类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystem is the entry-point class that owns the root and exposes the path-based API.

q_en: How should Path be modeled?
scenario_en: The requirements repeatedly reference paths like /home/user/docs.
optionExplanations: 把 Path 做成有状态的实体会引入生命周期管理，但这里连规范化都不需要，纯属过度设计。
路径和文件夹是两种不同的概念，硬塞进 Folder 继承体系会让类型语义变乱。
路径只是定位输入，交给 FileSystem 统一解析成 parent+name，不用为它单独建模。
File 不该从一个字符串概念派生，这个继承方向在语义上说不通。
optionExplanations_en: Turning Path into a stateful object with its own identity is over-engineering when you don't even need normalization yet.
A path and a folder are different concepts, so wedging Path under Folder's hierarchy corrupts the type semantics.
Path is just a location input that FileSystem resolves into parent and name, so it doesn't need its own model.
File shouldn't derive from a string-like concept — that inheritance direction doesn't make sense here.

scenario: 调用方想 createFile('/home/user/notes.txt','hi')，不想手动从 root 一层层导航。
q: 为什么需要 FileSystem 类？
options: 因为 Folder 不能包含 File
因为 FileSystem 存储每个文件内容
为了完全替代 Folder 和 File 这两个类
作为 facade，集中处理路径解析和公共 API
why: FileSystem 隐藏路径拆分、导航和校验细节，避免每个调用方重复实现；它是系统入口，不是叶子节点。
why_en: FileSystem acts as a facade over root navigation, centralizing path parsing behind one public API.
tradeoff: 集中路径解析的 facade 入口 vs 调用方各自手写导航逻辑
whenOtherWins: 如果 API 只面向已持有 Folder 引用的内部代码，直接操作 Folder 也可以；但用户级路径 API 需要 facade。
options_en: Because Folder cannot contain File.
Because FileSystem stores every file's content.
To fully replace both Folder and File as classes.
As a facade that centralizes path parsing and the public API.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个简单入口类隐藏子系统内部复杂性的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Facade pattern hides a subsystem's internal complexity behind one simple entry-point class.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持有 root 并对外提供路径 API 的入口类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystem is the entry-point class that owns the root and exposes the path-based API.

q_en: Why do we need a FileSystem class?
scenario_en: A caller wants to call createFile('/home/user/notes.txt','hi') without manually navigating from root.
optionExplanations: Folder 本来就能通过 addChild 装 File，这从来不是引入 FileSystem 的原因。
内容其实存在 File.content 上，FileSystem 并不代管每个文件的字节。
Folder 和 File 仍然各司其职，FileSystem 只是在它们之上加一层编排，不是替代品。
FileSystem 拥有 root，把路径拆分和逐级导航都收在一个入口，调用方只用记一个 API。
optionExplanations_en: Folder can already hold File via addChild, so that was never the reason FileSystem exists.
Content actually lives on File.content — FileSystem doesn't stash every file's bytes itself.
Folder and File still keep their own jobs; FileSystem just orchestrates on top, it doesn't replace them.
FileSystem owns root and folds path-splitting and step-by-step navigation into one entry point, so callers only need one API.

q: 这个内存文件系统的类设计要落地哪些类型？（多选）
options: FileSystem
FileSystemEntry
Folder
File
Path
why: FileSystem 负责编排，FileSystemEntry 抽取共享身份，Folder 是 composite，File 是 leaf；Path 不作为实体，只是解析输入。
why_en: The design uses FileSystem, a shared FileSystemEntry abstraction, Folder composites, and File leaves — Path stays a plain string.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class FileSystem
  class FileSystemEntry
  class Folder
  class File
  FileSystem --> Folder : root
  FileSystemEntry <|-- Folder
  FileSystemEntry <|-- File
  Folder --> FileSystemEntry : children
options_en: FileSystem
FileSystemEntry
Folder
File
Path

termDefinitions.meaning: File 和 Folder 共同的抽象基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystemEntry is the shared abstract base class for File and Folder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以包含子节点的容器类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite is a container type that can hold child nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不能再包含子节点的树末端节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaf is a tree node that cannot contain further children.

q_en: Which types does this in-memory file system actually implement? (multi-select)
optionExplanations: FileSystem 是持有 root 并对外暴露公共 API 的入口类，属于最终类型清单。
它把 File 和 Folder 共有的 name/parent 字段抽成一个共享基类。
Folder 是能装子节点的 composite 容器，是树里唯一有 children 的类型。
File 是叶子节点，只多带一个字符串内容字段，没有子节点。
Path 从没被当成一个类来实现，它只是传给 FileSystem 方法的字符串参数。
optionExplanations_en: FileSystem is the entry-point class that owns root and exposes the public API, so it's on the final type list.
It pulls the shared name/parent fields off File and Folder into one common base class.
Folder is the composite container that can hold children — the only type in the tree with a children map.
File is the leaf node, carrying just one extra string content field and no children.
Path was never implemented as a class — it's just a string argument passed into FileSystem's methods.
scenario: 设计内存文件系统：目录可任意深度嵌套，所有 API 只接收 "/a/b/c" 字符串来定位节点。
scenario_en: We are designing an in-memory file system: folders nest to any depth, and every API call locates a node with a "/a/b/c" string.

scenario: File 和 Folder 各自实现了几乎相同的 name、parent、getPath、isDirectory，代码明显重复。
q: FileSystemEntry 抽象解决了什么问题？
options: 它让 File 也能像 Folder 一样包含并管理子节点
File/Folder 共享字段与方法，children 需统一类型
它替代了 FileSystem 里的路径解析器，不再需要 resolvePath
它负责对每个文件的内容做全文关键词搜索和索引
why: 文件树里 leaf 和 composite 都是 entry；共享抽象减少重复，并让 Folder.children 的类型可以统一。
why_en: FileSystemEntry captures the shared node identity for both files and folders in the tree.
tradeoff: 共享基类统一身份 vs 各自独立类型省去继承耦合
options_en: It lets File contain and manage children like Folder does.
File/Folder share fields and methods, and children need one shared type.
It replaces FileSystem's path resolver, so resolvePath is no longer needed.
It handles full-text keyword search and indexing over every file's content.

termDefinitions.meaning: File 和 Folder 共同的抽象基类，封装 name/parent/getPath。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystemEntry is the shared abstract base class holding name, parent, and getPath for both files and folders.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来区分一个 entry 是文件夹还是文件的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isDirectory is the method that tells whether an entry is a folder or a file.

q_en: What problem does the FileSystemEntry abstraction solve?
scenario_en: File and Folder each implement almost identical name, parent, getPath, and isDirectory, and the duplication is obvious.
optionExplanations: File 依然是叶子节点，这个抽象并不会给它加上管理子节点的能力。
File 和 Folder 共享 name/parent/getPath 等字段方法，抽出基类还能让 children 用统一类型存两种节点。
路径解析仍是 FileSystem.resolvePath 的职责，这个抽象跟它无关。
全文搜索是完全独立的功能扩展，跟节点身份抽象没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: File stays a leaf — this abstraction doesn't give it any child-managing power.
File and Folder share fields like name/parent/getPath, and the shared base also lets children hold one uniform type covering both.
Path resolution still belongs to FileSystem.resolvePath — this abstraction has nothing to do with it.
Full-text search is a completely separate extension, unrelated to node identity.

scenario: File 和 Folder 都稳定共享 name、parent、getPath 行为。
q: 为什么 abstract class 比只有 interface 更合适？
options: 能共享字段和 getPath 实现，interface 只有契约
interface 从 Java 8 起也有 default method，能共享方法体
abstract class 能自动把 File/Folder 状态持久化到磁盘
Folder 只是容器，用组合代替继承也能达到同样效果
why: 这里共享的不只是方法名，还有稳定实现；继承在真实 is-a 关系且共享行为稳定时是合理选择。
why_en: An abstract class is justified because File and Folder share stable state and behavior, not just a method contract.
tradeoff: 共享实现的 abstract class vs 只共享契约的 interface
whenOtherWins: 如果语言偏组合，或两者只共享很少契约，interface 加工具函数也可以。
options_en: It can share fields and the getPath implementation, while an interface only has a contract.
Since Java 8, interfaces also have default methods that can share a method body.
An abstract class can automatically persist File/Folder state to disk.
Folder is just a container; composition instead of inheritance can achieve the same effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以包含共享字段和默认实现、但不能直接实例化的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class can hold shared fields and default implementations but cannot be instantiated directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: interface 里可以提供默认实现、但仍不能持有实例字段的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A default method lets an interface provide a default implementation, but the interface still cannot hold instance fields.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只定义方法契约、不提供共享实现的类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface defines a method contract without providing shared implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用统一类型引用不同子类对象，并调用各自实现的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets code refer to different subclass objects through one shared type and call their own implementations.

q_en: Why is an abstract class a better fit here than a plain interface?
scenario_en: File and Folder both stably share name, parent, and getPath behavior.
optionExplanations: File 和 Folder 能直接继承 getPath 等方法实现，不用各自重写一遍，这正是选 abstract class 的理由。
default method 能共享方法体，但接口仍不能持有实例字段，abstract class 才能两者都要。
抽象类本身跟磁盘持久化毫无关系，这版设计里 File/Folder 状态只存在内存中。
组合确实是候选方案，但 File/Folder 是稳定的 is-a 关系且共享字段，继承在这里更直接。
optionExplanations_en: File and Folder can inherit getPath's real implementation instead of each rewriting it — that's the actual case for an abstract class.
A default method can share a method body, but an interface still can't hold instance fields — only an abstract class gives you both.
An abstract class has nothing to do with disk persistence — in this design, File/Folder state only ever lives in memory.
Composition is a real alternative, but File and Folder have a stable is-a relationship and share fields, so inheritance is the more direct fit here.

q: 补全 Composite 结构：
text: File 是不能包含 children 的 {{leaf}}；Folder 是可以包含 FileSystemEntry 的 {{composite}}；FileSystemEntry 是二者共同的 {{节点抽象}}。
why: 文件系统天然是树；统一节点抽象让外层代码可以把文件和文件夹当作 entry 统一处理。
why_en: The file system naturally fits the Composite pattern: File is the leaf and Folder is the composite, sharing one entry abstraction.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class FileSystemEntry
  class Folder
  class FileEntry
  FileSystemEntry <|-- Folder
  FileSystemEntry <|-- FileEntry
  Folder --> FileSystemEntry

termDefinitions.meaning: 让叶子节点和容器节点共用同一接口的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Composite pattern lets leaf and container nodes share one common interface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不能再包含子节点的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaf node cannot contain further children.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以包含子节点的容器节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite node can contain child nodes.

q_en: Fill in the Composite structure:

scenario: 需要从任意 File 或 Folder 引用得到完整路径，并支持 rename/move。
q: 为什么优先存 parent 指针而不是每个 entry 存 full path 字符串？
options: getPath 无论目录树多深，都必须保持 O(1) 常数时间返回
parent 指针除了定位还能自动搜索文件内容
rename/move 只改 name/parent，路径按需计算
full path 字符串无法正确显示中文文件名
why: 存 full path 会让重命名大目录时必须更新所有后代路径；parent 指针把 rename/move 降为局部更新，getPath 付出 O(depth)。
why_en: Parent pointers avoid cascading path updates on rename or move, trading O(1) getPath for O(depth).
tradeoff: parent 指针的局部更新 vs full path 字符串的级联更新
whenOtherWins: 如果几乎只读路径且很少 move/rename，可缓存路径字符串，但要有失效策略。
options_en: getPath must return in O(1) constant time no matter how deep the directory tree gets.
Parent pointers can also automatically search file content.
Rename/move only changes name/parent; the path is computed on demand.
Full path strings cannot correctly display Chinese file names.

termDefinitions.meaning: 子节点保存的指向父节点的引用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parent pointer is the reference a child node keeps back to its parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时随树的深度增长，而不是随节点总数增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(depth) means the operation's cost grows with the tree's depth, not with the total number of nodes.

q_en: Why store a parent pointer instead of a full path string on every entry?
scenario_en: You need to compute the full path from any File or Folder reference, and support rename/move.
optionExplanations: getPath 用 parent 指针其实是 O(depth) 而非 O(1)，这不是这里权衡的目标。
parent 指针只负责定位和导航，不做任何内容层面的搜索。
重命名或移动时只需要改这一个 entry 的 name/parent，getPath 再按需要往上拼一次。
路径字符串本身跟字符集无关，这不是工程上真实存在的限制。
optionExplanations_en: getPath over parent pointers is actually O(depth), not O(1) — that's not the tradeoff being made here.
Parent pointers only handle locating and navigating, never any content-level search.
Rename or move only touches that one entry's name/parent, and getPath just walks up on demand afterward.
A path string's encoding has nothing to do with the character set — that's not a real engineering constraint.

q: 按顺序排列存 full path 字符串导致的问题：
steps: 如果 /home 被重命名为 /house，所有后代路径前缀都变了。
每个 entry 持有自己的 path 字符串。
必须遍历整个子树更新每个 path。
一次 rename/move 从局部操作变成 O(descendants)。
why: 这就是 parent 指针方案胜出的主要理由：深层目录下路径字符串冗余会让简单操作变复杂。
why_en: Storing full paths on every entry turns a folder rename or move into a cascading update across all descendants.
tradeoff: 存 full path 读取简单 vs parent 指针写入简单但读取要递归

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 entry 自己保存的完整路径字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full path is the complete path string stored directly on each entry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个节点子树下所有更深层的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A descendant is any node deeper in the subtree rooted at a given node.

scenario: 多个 public 方法都需要把绝对路径转成树节点。
q: 这段 resolvePath 伪代码体现了什么？
codeSample:
resolvePath(path)
    if path == null || !path.startsWith('/') throw InvalidPath
    if path == '/' return root
    parts = path.substring(1).split('/')
    current = root
    for part in parts
        if part == '' throw InvalidPath
        if !current.isDirectory() throw NotADirectory
        current = current.getChild(part)
        if current == null throw NotFound
    return current
options: 每个调用方都要自己解析路径
只检查 root 下第一层 child 是否存在
集中处理绝对路径校验、逐级下降和错误情况
支持 ../ 相对路径解析和 symlink 跳转
why: resolvePath 是路径 API 的核心 helper，它把无效路径、文件中途被当目录、缺失 child 都统一处理。
why_en: resolvePath centralizes absolute-path validation and level-by-level tree traversal in one helper.
tradeoff: 集中式路径 helper vs 每个方法各自解析路径
whenOtherWins: 支持相对路径或符号链接时，需要更复杂的 resolver 和循环检测。
options_en: Every caller must parse the path itself.
It only checks whether a direct child under root exists.
It centralizes absolute-path validation, level-by-level descent, and error handling.
It supports ../ relative-path resolution and symlink jumps.

scenario: 实现 rename 时要避免 name collision 并维护 map key。
q: 这段伪代码的关键不变量是什么？
codeSample:
rename(path, newName)
    parent = resolveParent(path)
    oldName = extractName(path)
    if parent.hasChild(newName) throw AlreadyExists
    entry = parent.removeChild(oldName)
    if entry == null throw NotFound
    entry.setName(newName)
    parent.addChild(entry)

key 要跟 entry.name 保持一致
rename 应该把整个子树都完整复制一份
parent 指针在这整个操作里都并不重要
why: remove/add 让 map key 和 entry.name 同步，同时 addChild 会重新设置 parent 指针。
why_en: Rename must keep the entry's name and the parent's map key synchronized on every update.
tradeoff: remove→rename→add 保持不变量 vs 直接改字段留下不一致的 key
whenOtherWins: 若 newName 等于 oldName，可选择直接返回成功；但仍要先定义清楚语义。
options_en: rename should skip the entire name-collision check step.
The key must stay consistent with entry.name.
rename should make a full, complete copy of the entire subtree.
The parent pointer doesn't matter anywhere in this whole operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序运行过程中必须始终保持成立的结构性约束。

q_en: What is the key invariant in this pseudocode?

改名不涉及复制，原 entry 应该原地更新，不产生副本。
addChild 执行时会把 parent 指针指向新的容器，指针错了 getPath 会跟着算错。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the collision check lets a rename silently clobber someone else's entry when newName already exists.
Removing the old key and re-adding the new one is exactly what keeps the map's key matching entry.name.
Renaming doesn't involve copying — the original entry should update in place with no duplicate created.
When addChild runs it points the parent pointer at the new container, and a wrong pointer would throw off getPath's calculation.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["resolve source"] --> B["resolve destination folder"]
  B --> C["reject cycles"]
  C --> D["remove from old parent"]
  D --> E["add to new parent"]
  E --> F["update parent pointer"]

Only change entry.name but never update its parent pointer.
Remove from the source parent, rename it, then add to the destination parent.
Use the destination path string directly as the content.

q_en: What are the core steps of move?
scenario_en: Calling move('/home/user/notes.txt','/home/notes.txt').

Remove from the source parent, rename it, then add to the destination parent — both containers get updated.
A path string and a file's content are two completely unrelated fields.

scenario: 用户尝试 move('/home','/home/user/stuff')。
q: 为什么必须拒绝？
options: home 名称太短
'stuff' 是系统保留字，不能用作普通文件名
文件夹不能移动
会把文件夹移入自己的后代，形成树循环
why: 父指针和 children 引用会形成环，getPath 和遍历都可能无限循环；必须从 destParent 向上检查是否遇到源 entry。
why_en: Moving a folder into its own descendant creates a cycle and breaks the acyclic-tree invariant.
tradeoff: 拒绝会成环的移动 vs 允许任意移动但让树结构失效
whenOtherWins: 文件移动不需要此检查，因为文件没有 descendants；目录移动必须做祖先检查。
options_en: The name 'home' is too short.
'stuff' is a system-reserved word and cannot be used as a regular file name.
Folders cannot be moved at all.
It would move the folder into its own descendant, creating a cycle in the tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 树结构里某节点通过 parent/children 引用又指回自己祖先的错误状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cycle is a broken tree state where following parent or child references eventually loops back to an ancestor.

q_en: Why must this be rejected?
scenario_en: A user tries move('/home','/home/user/stuff').
optionExplanations: 路径长度跟这个操作能不能执行完全无关，这是编造的限制。
'stuff' 不是保留字，就是个普通合法的名称组件，跟环检测无关。
move 明确支持移动文件夹，问题只出在这一种特定的移动方向上。
把 home 移进它自己的后代会让 parent/children 互相矛盾，遍历可能无限递归。
optionExplanations_en: Name length has nothing to do with whether this move can proceed — that constraint is made up.
'stuff' isn't a reserved word — it's just an ordinary valid name component, unrelated to cycle detection.
move explicitly supports folders — the problem is only with this one particular move direction.
Moving home into its own descendant makes parent and children contradict each other, and traversal can recurse forever.

q: 按顺序排列 move 的 cycle detection 逻辑：
steps: 如果 current == entry，拒绝移动。
只在 entry.isDirectory() 时做检查。
从 destParent 开始。
不断 current = current.getParent() 向根走。
走到 null 还没遇到 entry，则不会形成环。
why: 从目标父目录向上看祖先，可以判断目标是否在源目录子树里；命中源目录就说明会形成环。
why_en: Cycle detection walks up from the destination parent's ancestors to see whether the moved folder is one of them.
tradeoff: 只对文件夹做祖先检查 vs 对所有 move 都检查（文件没有后代，检查是浪费）
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[move folder X] --> B[target parent]
  B --> C[walk parents]
  C --> D{hit X?}
  D -->|yes| E[reject cycle]
  D -->|no| F[unlink and attach]

termDefinitions.meaning: 沿 parent 指针一路向上能到达的所有节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ancestor is any node reachable by walking parent pointers upward from a given node.

termDefinitions.meaning: move 操作里目标位置所在的父 Folder。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: destParent is the destination parent Folder in a move operation.

q_en: Order the cycle-detection logic inside move:

scenario: move 同时触碰源父目录和目标父目录两处树结构，任何一步失败都必须在修改前发现。
q: move 应处理哪些边界情况？（多选）
options: 不能移动 root
源不存在
目标父目录不存在或不是目录
目标位置重名
目录移入自身后代
把文件移动到另一个独立的 FileSystem 实例
why: move 是最复杂操作，因为同时触碰两处树结构并可能破坏树不变量；每个失败都应在修改前发现。
why_en: Move must validate root, source, destination parent, name collisions, and cycles before mutating anything.
options_en: Cannot move root.
Source does not exist.
Destination parent does not exist or is not a directory.
Name collision at the destination.
Moving a folder into its own descendant.
Moving a file into a separate, independent FileSystem instance.

termDefinitions.meaning: move 目标路径最后一级所在的父 Folder。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The destination parent is the parent Folder implied by the final component of the destination path.

q_en: Which edge cases should move handle? (multi-select)
scenario_en: move touches two places in the tree at once, the source and destination parents, so every failure must be caught before mutating anything.
optionExplanations: root 是唯一入口，不能被移出或替换，跟 delete('/') 的拒绝逻辑一致。
resolveParent 或 getChild 找不到源 entry 时应该直接抛错，不能静默跳过。
目标父目录不存在或本身是文件时，后续的 addChild 根本无法进行。
目标位置已有同名 entry 时，addChild 会覆盖数据，必须提前拒绝。
文件夹移入自身后代会形成结构环，这正是环检测要拦住的情况。
这版设计里只存在一棵树，压根不存在跨 FileSystem 实例移动这个概念。
optionExplanations_en: root is the one entry point and can't be moved out or replaced, matching how delete('/') gets rejected.
If resolveParent or getChild can't find the source entry, it should throw right away instead of silently skipping.
If the destination parent doesn't exist or is itself a file, the later addChild simply can't happen.
If the destination already has a same-named entry, addChild would overwrite data, so it must be rejected up front.
Moving a folder into its own descendant creates a structural cycle — exactly what cycle detection has to catch.
This design only ever has one tree; there's no such thing as moving across separate FileSystem instances.

scenario: notes.txt 的 parent 是 user，user 的 parent 是 home，home 的 parent 是 root('/')。
q: getPath() 应如何计算？
options: 向上递归取 parent 路径，root 特判避免双斜杠
返回创建时就保存好的旧路径字符串
从 root 出发对整棵树做遍历搜索来定位自己
把它自己所有 child 的名字依次拼接成一个字符串
why: parent 指针让路径动态反映当前树位置；root 特判能生成 /home 而不是 //home。
why_en: getPath walks parent pointers up to root, special-casing root to avoid a leading double slash.
tradeoff: 每次动态计算路径 vs 缓存路径字符串换取 O(1) 但要处理失效
whenOtherWins: 如果频繁调用 getPath，可缓存结果，但 rename/move 时要让后代缓存失效。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["entry"] --> P1["parent"]
  P1 --> P2["parent"]
  P2 --> R["root"]
  R --> J["reverse names into path"]
options_en: Recursively take the parent's path, special-casing root to avoid a double slash.
Return the exact old path string saved back at creation time.
Start from root and search through the entire tree to locate itself.
Concatenate the names of all of its own children, one after another, into a string.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沿 parent 指针向上走、拼出完整绝对路径的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: getPath is the method that walks parent pointers upward to build the full absolute path.

q_en: How should getPath() be computed?
scenario_en: notes.txt's parent is user, user's parent is home, and home's parent is root('/').
optionExplanations: 沿 parent 一路往上拼段，遇到 root 特殊处理一下就不会拼出双斜杠。
缓存的旧路径字符串在 rename/move 之后就过期了，这正是要避免的坑。
从 root 全树搜索自己既没必要又低效，parent 指针已经能直接定位。
子节点的名字跟这个 entry 自己的路径没有任何关系。
optionExplanations_en: Walk up through parent, joining each segment, and special-case root so you don't end up with a double slash.
A cached old path string goes stale the moment a rename or move happens — that's exactly the trap to avoid.
Searching the whole tree from root to find yourself is both unnecessary and slow when parent pointers already locate you directly.
The names of an entry's own children have nothing to do with that entry's own path.

q: 补全 Folder.addChild/removeChild 的关键副作用：
text: addChild(entry) 成功后要 entry.setParent({{this}})；removeChild(name) 成功后要 entry.setParent({{null}})。
why: children map 和 parent 指针是双向关系；任何一边更新时都要维护另一边，否则 move 和 getPath 会出错。
why_en: Folder mutations must keep the children map and the parent pointer consistent on both sides.

termDefinitions.meaning: 父节点通过 children 指向子节点，子节点又通过 parent 指回父节点的相互引用关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bidirectional reference means the parent points to the child via children while the child points back via parent.

q_en: Fill in the key side effects of Folder.addChild/removeChild:

scenario: 调用 getChildren() 列目录内容。
q: 为什么返回 children values 的副本，而不是内部 map？
options: 返回副本单纯是为了让查找速度更快
Folder 内部的 map 结构完全不能被遍历
防止调用方绕开 addChild/removeChild 破坏内部约束
FileSystemEntry 类型的对象不能被放进任何 List 集合里
why: Folder 需要控制自己的不变量；暴露内部 map 会让外部代码直接修改 children 而不维护 parent。
why_en: Returning a copy of the children protects Folder's invariants from uncontrolled external mutation.
tradeoff: 返回副本保护不变量 vs 直接暴露内部结构换取零拷贝
whenOtherWins: 如果 Folder 只在受信任的内部代码里被使用，直接暴露引用也可以接受，但会失去这层保护。
options_en: Returning a copy is purely to make lookups faster.
Folder's internal map cannot be iterated at all.
It stops callers from bypassing addChild/removeChild and breaking internal invariants.
A FileSystemEntry object can never be stored inside any List collection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内部状态隐藏起来，只通过受控方法修改的设计原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides internal state and only allows changes through controlled methods.

q_en: Why does getChildren() return a copy of the values instead of the internal map?
scenario_en: Calling getChildren() to list a directory's contents.
optionExplanations: 返回副本这件事本身跟查找速度无关，这不是暴露内部 map 的真正风险点。
Map 本来就可以用 values() 遍历，这个断言站不住。
暴露内部 map 会让外部代码绕开 addChild/removeChild 直接改结构，破坏 parent 一致性。
List 完全能存放包括 FileSystemEntry 在内的任意对象。
optionExplanations_en: Returning a copy has nothing to do with lookup speed — that's not the real risk of exposing the internal map.
A map can already be iterated via values(); that claim doesn't hold up.
