whenOtherWins: 真要保调用方延迟，正确的做法是给每个 destination 加有界队列和 worker 线程，而不是给锁加超时。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个已配置的输出目标，组合 minLevel、Formatter 和 Sink，负责过滤、格式化、加锁写入的完整流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Destination is one configured output target that composes a threshold, a formatter, and a sink to filter, format, and write under a lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 尝试获取锁并立即返回成功或失败的调用，不会让线程挂起等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TryLock attempts to take a lock and returns success or failure immediately instead of parking the thread.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个线程同时争抢同一把锁，未抢到的线程必须等待，等待时间等于持有者的临界区长度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock contention is several threads racing for the same lock, where losers wait as long as the holder's critical section.

scenario: PlainTextFormatter 现在把 timestamp、level、threadName、message 硬编码拼成一行。运维希望去掉线程名、换个分隔符，而且不想为此发一次版本。
scenario_en: PlainTextFormatter currently hardcodes the concatenation of timestamp, level, thread name, and message. Operators want the thread name dropped and the separator changed without shipping a new build.
q: 生产实现应该怎么支持这种排版变化？
q_en: How should a production implementation absorb that layout change?
options: 每种排版写一个 Formatter 子类，运维要什么就加一个类
构造函数接受一个模板字符串，例如 {timestamp} {level} [{thread}] {message}
把排版交给 Sink，写入前由它决定字段顺序，因为 sink 最贴近输出目标的格式约定
让 LogRecord 自己实现 toString，排版跟着记录走，所有 formatter 都调用同一个方法拿到最终字符串
options_en: One Formatter subclass per layout; add a class whenever operators want a change.
Take a template string in the constructor, e.g. {timestamp} {level} [{thread}] {message}.
Let the Sink decide field order before writing, since it is closest to the target's conventions.
Give LogRecord a toString so layout travels with the record and every formatter calls that one method.
optionExplanations: 排版是配置维度，用类来表达会让类数量随运维口味无限增长。
模板把「哪些字段、什么顺序、什么分隔符」变成一个可外部配置的参数。
Sink 的职责窄到只把字符串变成字节，让它排版会把格式和目的地重新耦合。
值对象不该决定展示形式，否则 JSON 格式化也会被这一个 toString 绑住。
optionExplanations_en: Layout is a configuration dimension; expressing it as classes makes the class count grow with operator taste.
A template turns which fields, in what order, with which separators into one externally configurable parameter.
A Sink's job is narrowly turning a string into bytes; laying out fields there re-couples format with target.
A value object should not decide presentation, or the JSON formatter gets bound to that same toString.
why: 排版是配置不是代码，模板字符串让输出形状改变而不改类；代价是多一层模板解析，面试范围内直接硬编码并说明这一点即可。
why_en: Layout is configuration rather than code, so a template string lets the output shape change without touching the class, at the cost of one parsing layer.
tradeoff: 模板字符串换免改代码 vs 硬编码换实现最简单
whenOtherWins: 面试时间紧就硬编码拼接，口头说明真实实现会在构造函数里接一个模板字符串，同样拿分。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 LogRecord 序列化成字符串的纯函数接口，现有 PlainText 和 Json 两个实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Formatter is a pure-function interface that serializes a LogRecord into a string; plain text and JSON are the two implementations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次 log 调用生成的不可变值对象，携带 timestamp、level、message、threadName 四个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A LogRecord is the immutable value object created per log call, carrying timestamp, level, message, and thread name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只负责把已格式化好的字符串写到具体目标（stdout、文件、未来的网络）的窄接口，不做过滤或格式化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sink is a narrow interface that only writes an already formatted string to a target like stdout, a file, or the network.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带占位符的排版字符串，运行时把占位符替换成记录字段，改排版不用改代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A template string is a layout string with placeholders that are substituted with record fields at runtime, so changing layout needs no code change.

scenario: 团队用 Formatter 序列化、Sink 输出字节、Destination 组合两者的方案已经定稿，有人质疑这是不是为了显得复杂多加的一层。
scenario_en: The team has settled on Formatter for serialization, Sink for bytes, and Destination composing both; someone asks whether that's just extra layering for its own sake.
q: 这个组合形状对应哪套已知框架的真实收敛结果？
q_en: Which real framework already converged on this same shape?
options: 同一套分离形状已在 Log4j 和 Python logging 里各自出现过
这是本设计独创的形状，主流生产日志库为了性能通常把格式和目标写死耦合进同一个类里
Log4j 和 Python logging 都是靠继承层级实现格式与目标的组合，而不是这种组合形状
这是 ELK 这类跨服务网络日志聚合系统常见的拆分方式，和进程内日志库的场景完全无关
options_en: This same split shape already exists in both Log4j and Python logging.
This shape is unique to this exercise; production loggers usually hardcode format and target into one class for speed.
Log4j and Python logging both use inheritance hierarchies for this composition, not this shape.
This is how network log aggregators like ELK typically split responsibilities, completely unrelated to an in-process logger.
optionExplanations: Appender 对应 Sink，Layout 对应 Formatter，两个生态各自独立收敛到同一形状。
真实反了：耦合格式和目标才会撞上 N×M 类爆炸，主流框架正是为了躲开它才分离。
两个框架用的正是组合（接口 + 构造参数），不是继承层级。
ELK 处理的是跨服务网络聚合，这里明确是进程内库，场景不同。
optionExplanations_en: Appender maps to Sink and Layout maps to Formatter; two separate ecosystems converged on the same shape.
Backwards: coupling format and target is exactly what causes the N×M class explosion frameworks avoid.
Both frameworks use composition (an interface plus a constructor argument), not an inheritance hierarchy.
ELK is about cross-service network aggregation; this design is explicitly an in-process library.
why: Log4j 的 Appender/Layout 和 Python logging 的 handler/formatter 都是同一种格式-目标分离，说明这不是本设计独创，是三个生态收敛到的答案。
why_en: Log4j's Appender/Layout and Python's handler/formatter are the same format-target split, so this shape is a convergent answer, not an invention.
tradeoff: 对齐已验证过的生产形状 vs 每个团队各自造一套耦合类
whenOtherWins: 面试官明确说是纯练习不必对齐真实框架时，直接讲清楚组合的收益即可，不必刻意点名 Log4j。

termDefinitions.meaning: Log4j 中把日志事件写到具体目标（文件/控制台/网络）的组件，对应本设计的 Sink。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Appender is Log4j's component that writes a log event to a concrete target, playing the role of this design's Sink.

termDefinitions.meaning: Log4j 中把日志事件格式化成字符串的组件，对应本设计的 Formatter。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Layout is Log4j's component that formats a log event into a string, playing the role of this design's Formatter.

scenario: 你在白板上选了 Sink 组合方案，面试官追问：如果我坚持要用继承版本（abstract Destination + ConsoleDestination/FileDestination），你觉得那样不行吗？
scenario_en: You picked the Sink composition design; the interviewer pushes back: what if I insist on the inheritance version — abstract Destination plus ConsoleDestination/FileDestination — is that wrong?
q: 面对这个追问，回答应该走哪条线？
q_en: How should you respond to that pushback?
options: 说继承版本本身也可辩护，讲清楚两边取舍，只有讲不出为什么没选它才是问题
立刻改口承认继承更好，现场把整个设计从头切换成继承版本
坚持组合是唯一正确答案，断言继承版本在任何生产系统里都不会被用到
回避这个追问，说时间不够先跳过，打算等面试全部结束后再私下补充说明
options_en: Say the inheritance version is defensible too, and walk through both tradeoffs — the only failure is not being able to explain the choice.
Immediately concede inheritance is better and switch the whole design over live from scratch.
Insist composition is the only correct answer, claiming inheritance is never used in any production system.
Dodge this pushback, cite time pressure, and plan to follow up privately after the whole interview ends.
optionExplanations: 文章明说继承变体同样可辩护，senior 信号是能讲清楚为什么没选它。
现场改口会显得没有主见，也丢了刚才组合方案的推理过程。
过度绝对化：template method 版本同样能正确工作，只是包装场景更弱。
回避追问本身就是没能力论证选择，比讲错答案更扣分。
optionExplanations_en: The article says the inheritance variant is equally defensible; the senior signal is explaining the choice, not memorizing one answer.
Flip-flopping live looks indecisive and abandons the reasoning you just built for composition.
Overclaiming: the template-method version is still correct, it's just weaker once wrapping is needed.
Dodging the pushback is itself a failure to argue for your choice, worse than a wrong answer.
why: 两种方案都能自圆其说，senior 信号是主动讲清楚取舍，而不是靠一个背好的标准答案护身。
why_en: Both designs are defensible; the senior signal is walking through the tradeoff yourself, not reciting a memorized answer.
tradeoff: 继承版本更省一层接口 vs 组合版本能干净叠加缓冲/重试等包装
whenOtherWins: 目标数量小且确定不会叠加装饰器（缓冲/重试/多路）时，继承版本同样是够用且可辩护的答案。

termDefinitions.meaning: 父类固定流程骨架、子类只填一步实现的模式，这里是继承版本 Destination 的做法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Template Method is a pattern where the base class fixes the workflow and subclasses fill in one step, used by the inheritance version of Destination.

scenario: 需求澄清阶段面试官明确说异步写、热更新配置、远程目的地这版都不做。
scenario_en: During clarification the interviewer says async writes, hot-reload config, and remote destinations are all out of scope for this version.
q: 拿到这个答复后应该怎么处理？
q_en: What should you do with that answer?
options: 在白板上显式列出 out-of-scope 清单，点名这些是有意排除、之后会作为扩展回归
既然不做就不用写下来，直接跳到下一节以节省时间
把它们混进 in-scope 的 Requirements 需求列表里，反正后面都要提一句
只留到实现阶段口头一提，不在需求阶段的白板上单独区分
options_en: Write an explicit out-of-scope list on the board, naming them as deliberately excluded, likely to return as extensions.
Skip writing them down since they're not being built, and move straight to the next section.
Mix them into the in-scope Requirements list since they'll get a mention there anyway.
Only mention them verbally during implementation instead of separating them on the board during requirements.
optionExplanations: 显式点名让面试官看到你考虑过、主动排除，而不是没想到。
省下十秒的代价是面试官分不清'考虑过排除'还是'压根没想到'。
混进 in-scope 列表会让当前要构建的核心模型边界变得模糊。
需求阶段就该定范围；拖到实现阶段才提，边界感已经晚了。
optionExplanations_en: Naming them explicitly shows you considered and deliberately excluded them, not that you missed them.
Saving ten seconds costs the interviewer the ability to tell 'considered and excluded' from 'never occurred to you'.
Mixing them into the in-scope list blurs the boundary of the core model you're about to build.
Scope belongs at the requirements stage; raising it only during implementation is too late for that signal.
why: 显式点名'考虑过但不做'和'压根没想到'在面试官那里是两种完全不同的读感，而且大多数功能后面会在 Extensibility 环节自然回归。
why_en: Explicitly naming 'considered but excluded' versus never mentioning it reads very differently, and most of those items resurface naturally in the extensibility discussion.
tradeoff: 花几秒写清单换来'考虑过'的读感 vs 省时间但显得没想到
whenOtherWins: 时间极度紧张时至少口头点名一句，也比完全不提要好。

scenario: 45 分钟 LLD 面试快结束，面试官还没主动问'你的设计有什么问题'。
scenario_en: A 45-minute LLD interview is winding down and the interviewer hasn't yet asked 'what's wrong with your design'.
q: 主动验证设计时应该覆盖哪几类场景？（多选）
q_en: Which categories of scenarios should you proactively walk through? (Select all)
options: 单线程正常路径：不同 destination 按各自 minLevel 独立过滤
并发场景：两个线程同时写同一个 destination
故障场景：某个 sink 写入失败时其它目的地是否受影响
把能想到的全部 edge case（20 个以上）逐一念给面试官听
why: 主动用'过滤/并发/故障'三类场景走查一遍，比等面试官发现漏洞更能体现 senior 信号；堆大量 edge case 不是目标，覆盖有代表性的几类才是。
why_en: Proactively walking filtering, concurrency, and failure scenarios beats waiting for the interviewer to find a hole; a long edge-case list is not the goal.
optionExplanations: 对应 Scenario 1：验证不同 destination 按各自阈值独立决定写或不写。
对应 Scenario 2：验证同一 destination 被多线程写时字节不交错。
对应 Scenario 3：验证单个 sink 出问题不会拖垮其它目的地或调用方。
数量不是目标，能覆盖前三类的代表性场景就够，堆边界案例边际收益很低。
optionExplanations_en: Maps to scenario 1: each destination independently decides to write based on its own threshold.
Maps to scenario 2: bytes never interleave when multiple threads write the same destination.
Maps to scenario 3: one broken sink never drags down other destinations or the caller.
Count isn't the goal; a few representative scenarios beat piling on marginal edge cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 destination 自己配置的最低级别阈值，记录级别低于它就被静默丢弃。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: minLevel is the per-destination threshold below which a record is silently dropped.

options_en: Single-thread happy path: each destination filters independently by its own minLevel.
Concurrent scenario: two threads writing the same destination at once.
Failure scenario: one sink write fails — do other destinations stay unaffected?
Reading out every edge case you can think of, twenty or more, one by one.

scenario: Logger.log() 目前顺序遍历 destinations 调用 write。你想'每次调用起一个线程并行写各个目的地'，让 log() 更快返回。
scenario_en: Logger.log() currently iterates destinations sequentially. You consider spinning up one thread per destination on every call so log() returns faster.
q: 这个'提速'想法在这套设计里会带来什么后果？
q_en: What actually happens if you adopt this per-call parallel-fanout idea?
options: destination 已各自独立加锁，并行只换来更快的 log() 返回，代价是每次调用都要管理线程生命周期
并行写各个 destination 后不再需要 per-destination 锁，因为每个线程只碰自己的目的地
这就等价于文章后面讲的异步扩展方案，提前做等于直接实现了 bounded queue
线程池能把这个开销摊薄到可以忽略，所以应该把它设成默认行为
options_en: Destinations already have independent locks; parallelizing only speeds up log() itself, at the cost of managing a thread's lifecycle every call.
Parallel writes mean you no longer need per-destination locks, since each thread only touches its own target.
This is equivalent to the async extension described later — doing it early is the same as implementing the bounded queue.
A thread pool amortizes the cost to negligible, so this should become the default behavior.
optionExplanations: 锁保护的是同目标被多次不同调用并发写，和这次调用内部并行无关，仍需保留。
锁保护跨调用的并发写，不是这次调用内部的并发，去掉锁会重新引入字节交错。
每次调用起线程和'每个 destination 一个持久 worker + 队列'是完全不同的机制。
线程池能摊薄创建成本，但没解决顺序保证和管理复杂度，也不该默认打开。
optionExplanations_en: The lock guards a target being written by different calls concurrently, unrelated to fan-out within one call, and still applies.
The lock protects cross-call concurrency, not the fan-out inside one call; removing it reintroduces byte interleaving.
Spawning a thread per call is a different mechanism from a persistent worker plus a queue per destination.
A pool amortizes creation cost but doesn't solve ordering guarantees or lifecycle complexity, and shouldn't be the default.
why: destination 已经各自独立加锁，并行写只换来更快的 log() 返回，代价是每次调用一个线程的生命周期与顺序保证复杂度；真正的非阻塞方案是异步扩展里的持久 worker。
why_en: Destinations already lock independently, so parallelizing only speeds up log() itself at the cost of per-call thread lifecycle and ordering complexity; the real non-blocking answer is the persistent worker from the async extension.
tradeoff: 顺序遍历简单可靠 vs 每次调用起线程换轻微延迟收益
whenOtherWins: 只有 destination 数量很多且个个都慢、又能接受线程池管理成本时才值得评估，且应该用线程池而不是每次 new 线程。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次调用把同一份数据分发给多个下游（这里是多个 destination）处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means dispatching the same data from one call out to multiple downstream consumers, here the destinations.

scenario: 每个 Destination 配了 bounded queue 和后台 worker 线程做异步写。业务在没有优雅关闭逻辑的情况下直接 kill 进程。
scenario_en: Each Destination now has a bounded queue and a background worker thread for async writes. The process gets killed with no graceful-shutdown logic in place.
q: 会发生什么，该如何补救？
q_en: What happens, and how do you fix it?
options: 队列里还没被 worker 取走的记录随进程丢失；需先停止入队、drain、再等 worker 结束
队列其实是一种持久化存储，进程被 kill 之后下次启动还能自动接着处理剩下的记录
worker 线程会在进程收到 kill 信号的那一刻自动把队列内容全部刷盘，不需要写额外代码
只要把 bounded queue 的容量设置得足够小，记录就永远不会因为进程被 kill 而丢失
options_en: Records still sitting in the queue when the worker hasn't drained them are lost with the process; stop enqueueing, drain, then wait for the worker.
The queue is actually durable storage, so records survive a kill and automatically resume processing on the next startup.
The worker thread automatically flushes the entire queue to disk the instant a kill signal arrives, no extra code needed.
Making the bounded queue's capacity small enough guarantees records can never be lost when the process is killed.
optionExplanations: 内存队列没有持久化，未消费部分随进程消失，唯一救法是显式 drain 再退出。
BlockingQueue 是内存结构，进程结束时内容直接消失，不会跨重启保留。
操作系统不会替你做优雅关闭；drain 逻辑必须由 shutdown hook 显式实现。
队列大小和是否优雅关闭无关，再小的队列也可能有几条还没被 worker 取走。
optionExplanations_en: An in-memory queue has no durability; the unconsumed remainder vanishes with the process, so an explicit drain is the only fix.
A BlockingQueue is in-memory; its contents disappear when the process ends and are not preserved across restarts.
The OS does not perform graceful shutdown for you; draining must be implemented explicitly as a shutdown hook.
Queue size is unrelated to graceful shutdown — even a tiny queue can hold a few records the worker hasn't taken yet.
why: 正常运行 → kill 信号到达 → worker 还没消费的队列内容随进程消失 → 补救靠显式 shutdown：停止入队、drain 剩余、等待 worker 完成 → 代价是关闭变慢。
why_en: Normal operation → kill signal arrives → whatever the worker hasn't consumed disappears with the process → the fix is an explicit shutdown that stops enqueueing, drains the rest, and waits for the worker — at the cost of a slower shutdown.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程安全、有界容量的队列，满时 put 会阻塞，是异步 Destination 用来解耦调用方和 worker 的结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BlockingQueue is a thread-safe, bounded-capacity queue whose put blocks when full, used to decouple the caller from the worker in async destinations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一从队列取记录并写 sink 的后台线程，单消费者所以不需要额外锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The worker is the single background thread that pulls records from the queue and writes the sink, so no extra lock is needed.

scenario: 上线异步 Destination 后，一次 FileSink.write 因磁盘满抛出异常，值班同学想根据堆栈定位是哪次业务调用触发的。
scenario_en: After shipping the async Destination, a FileSink.write throws because the disk is full, and the on-call engineer tries to trace the stack back to the triggering business call.
q: 这时候会遇到什么麻烦？
q_en: What problem shows up here?
options: 异常发生在 worker 线程上，堆栈不再指向真正调用 log() 的业务代码，定位变难
异步化之后异常反而会被自动附加上完整的原始调用栈，定位变得更容易
因为记录本身是不可变的，所以 worker 线程抛出的异常必然和调用时刻的堆栈完全一致
bounded queue 会在异常发生时自动把出问题的记录连同调用栈一起持久化
options_en: The exception fires on the worker thread, whose stack no longer points back to the business code that called log(), making it harder to locate.
Going async automatically attaches the full original call stack to the exception, making tracing easier.
Because the record is immutable, the exception thrown on the worker thread must exactly match the call-site stack.
The bounded queue automatically persists the failing record together with its call stack when an exception occurs.
optionExplanations: 写入现在发生在另一个线程上，原调用点的堆栈信息已经不在异常路径里。
反了：异步恰恰切断了堆栈和调用点的直接关联，不会自动补全。
不可变只保证记录内容一致，不会让异常携带另一个线程当初的调用栈。
队列本身不做持久化也不附加堆栈，这是需要额外设计的能力，不是默认行为。
optionExplanations_en: The write now happens on a different thread, so the original call-site stack is no longer part of the exception path.
Backwards: going async is exactly what severs the stack from the call site; nothing restores it automatically.
Immutability only guarantees the record's content, not that the exception carries the original caller's stack.
The queue itself neither persists records nor attaches stacks — that's extra design work, not default behavior.
why: 写入挪到 worker 线程后，失败时的堆栈只指向 worker 的取任务循环，不再指向业务调用点；缓解手段是把调用点信息写进记录本身随诊断一起打印。
why_en: Once writes run on the worker, a failure's stack only points into the worker's pull loop, not the business call site; mitigation is embedding call-site info in the record and printing it with the diagnostic.

scenario: 团队要给 Destination.write() 写单元测试，覆盖过滤/格式化/加锁全流程，但不想真的往 stdout 或磁盘写东西。
scenario_en: The team wants to unit-test Destination.write() end to end — filter, format, lock — without actually writing to stdout or disk.
q: Sink 接口在这里带来了什么好处？
q_en: What benefit does the Sink interface bring here?
options: 可以传入一个只记录调用参数的 fake Sink，测试不用真的碰 stdout 或文件系统
Sink 接口能自动帮 Destination 生成单元测试用例，不用手写断言
有了 Sink 之后 Destination 就不再需要处理 minLevel 过滤，交给测试环境判断
fake Sink 会让 lock 在测试环境下自动变成 no-op，加快测试运行速度
options_en: You can pass a fake Sink that just records the calls it received, so tests never touch stdout or the filesystem.
The Sink interface automatically generates unit tests for Destination without hand-written assertions.
Once Sink exists, Destination no longer needs to apply the minLevel filter — the test environment decides that.
A fake Sink silently turns the lock into a no-op in test environments to speed up test runs.
optionExplanations: 接口把'写字节'这一步换成可替换实现，fake Sink 记调用即可断言而不触碰真实资源。
接口只提供替换点，测试用例和断言仍要工程师自己写。
minLevel 过滤是 Destination 的职责，和输出目标是否是 fake 无关，不会被跳过。
锁保护的是共享资源写入，替换 Sink 不改变 Destination 里的加锁逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: The interface swaps 'write bytes' for a replaceable implementation; a fake Sink can just record calls for assertions.
The interface only provides a substitution point; test cases and assertions still have to be written by hand.
minLevel filtering is Destination's own responsibility, independent of whether the sink is fake, so it's never skipped.
The lock protects the shared write path; swapping the Sink doesn't change Destination's locking logic at all.
why: Sink 是一个窄接口，测试可以传一个只记录调用参数的 fake 实现，验证过滤/格式化/加锁逻辑而不碰真实 stdout 或文件。
why_en: Sink is a narrow interface, so tests can pass a fake that just records calls, verifying the filter/format/lock logic without touching real stdout or files.
tradeoff: 多一层接口间接换来隔离测试 vs 直接写 stdout/文件更省一层代码但测试变慢变脏
whenOtherWins: 写一次性脚本、不打算长期维护测试时，直接对着真实 stdout 断言也够用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只记录收到的字符串、不真正写任何目标的 Sink 测试替身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fake Sink is a test double that just records the strings it receives instead of actually writing to any target.

scenario: 扩展成层级 logger 后，com.app.service.payments 没有单独配置 minLevel，父级 com.app.service 配了 WARN，根 logger 配了 INFO。
scenario_en: After extending to hierarchical loggers, com.app.service.payments has no minLevel of its own; its parent com.app.service is set to WARN and the root is set to INFO.
q: 该 logger 的 effective level 应该怎么算？
q_en: How should this logger's effective level be resolved?
options: 自己没配置就沿 dotted-name 的 parent 链往上找，第一个显式配置的祖先值生效
没配置就报错，要求每个新建的 named logger 必须显式设置自己的 level
没配置就直接用最严格的 FATAL，防止意外打印过多日志
子 logger 永远覆盖父 logger 的配置，找不到任何配置就退回硬编码默认值 DEBUG
options_en: With none set locally, walk up the dotted-name parent chain; the first ancestor with an explicit value wins.
Error out and require every newly created named logger to set its own level explicitly.
Fall back to the strictest level, FATAL, so nothing is over-printed by accident.
A child always overrides its parent, and one with nothing set falls back to a hardcoded default of DEBUG.
optionExplanations: 文章明说 effective level 在未设置时沿 parent chain 走，直到找到显式值。
要求每个 logger 都强制设置违背了'父级设一次、子级继承'这个层级设计的初衷。
FATAL 会让大量该打印的 WARN/ERROR 消失，和父级 WARN 的意图不符。
子级只有'自己配置了才覆盖'，没配置时不是覆盖而是继承父级。
optionExplanations_en: The article states effective level walks the parent chain until an explicit value is found when unset locally.
Forcing every logger to set its own level defeats the point of 'set once on a parent, children inherit'.
FATAL would suppress WARN/ERROR that the WARN-level parent clearly intends to keep, the opposite of intent.
A child only overrides when it has its own setting; an unset child inherits rather than reverting to a hardcoded default.
why: com.app.service.payments 没有自己的 level，就沿 dotted-name 向上走到 com.app.service 的 WARN，找到第一个显式值就停。
why_en: With no level of its own, com.app.service.payments walks up to com.app.service's WARN and stops at the first explicit ancestor value.
tradeoff: 父级设一次全树继承 vs 每个 logger 都显式配置更明确但维护成本高
whenOtherWins: 少数几个 logger 需要和父级完全不同的行为时，直接在那个 logger 上显式覆盖即可，不影响其它子树。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用点分隔层级的 logger 命名方式，如 com.app.service.payments，隐含父子关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dotted-name is a period-separated hierarchical logger naming scheme, like com.app.service.payments, that implies parent-child relationships.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 logger 实际生效的级别阈值，可能来自自己或沿链继承自某个祖先。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The effective level is the threshold that actually applies to a logger, either its own setting or inherited up the chain from an ancestor.

scenario: 为了让 log() 热路径别每次都走 parent chain，你在每个 logger 上缓存了 effective level。运维随后把 com.app.service 的配置从 WARN 改成 DEBUG。
scenario_en: To keep log() off the parent-chain walk on every call, you cache each logger's effective level. Operators then change com.app.service's config from WARN to DEBUG.
q: 如果缓存没有失效机制，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the cache has no invalidation path?
options: 子 logger 仍用旧的缓存 effective level，DEBUG 记录按旧 WARN 被丢弃
缓存值会在配置变更事件里被 JVM/运行时自动重新计算，不用额外处理
缓存只影响性能不影响正确性，因为 minLevel 判断仍然会读最新配置
只要客户端重新调用一次 getLogger(name)，就一定能拿到刷新之后的 effective level
options_en: Child loggers keep using the stale cached effective level, so DEBUG records still get dropped under the old WARN threshold.
Cached values get automatically recomputed by the runtime whenever configuration changes, no extra work needed.
The cache only affects performance, not correctness, because the minLevel check always reads the latest config.
Simply calling getLogger(name) again is guaranteed to hand back a logger with the freshly refreshed effective level.
optionExplanations: 缓存的意义就是不再每次查 parent chain；不主动失效，它就会一直返回旧值。
没有运行时会替你监听配置变更并自动重算缓存，这必须是显式失效逻辑。
缓存值本身就是 minLevel 判断要用的数，缓存过期直接等于判断用了旧配置。
工厂返回的是同一个已存在的 logger 实例，getLogger 不会顺带刷新它的缓存。
optionExplanations_en: The whole point of the cache is skipping the parent-chain lookup; without explicit invalidation it just keeps returning the stale value.
No runtime watches config changes and recomputes the cache for you automatically — that has to be explicit invalidation logic.
The cached value is exactly what the minLevel check reads, so a stale cache directly means a stale decision.
The factory returns the same existing logger instance; calling getLogger again does not refresh its cache as a side effect.
why: 正常运行 → 配置从 WARN 改成 DEBUG → 已缓存的 effective level 没跟着更新 → DEBUG 记录仍按旧阈值被丢 → 补救是配置变更时显式让相关 logger 的缓存失效。
why_en: Normal operation → config changes from WARN to DEBUG → the cached effective level is not updated → DEBUG records are still dropped under the old threshold → the fix is explicitly invalidating affected loggers' caches on config change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 logger 实际生效的级别阈值，可能来自自己或沿链继承自某个祖先。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The effective level is the threshold that actually applies to a logger, either its own setting or inherited up the chain from an ancestor.

scenario: 面试官按 Junior 标准评估候选人，候选人第一版把格式和目的地耦合成一个 JsonFileDestination 类，还没意识到 N×M 类爆炸问题。
scenario_en: The interviewer is grading at the Junior bar; the candidate's first cut couples format and destination into one JsonFileDestination class and hasn't yet noticed the N×M explosion.
q: 这在 Junior 级别应该如何被评价？
q_en: How should this be evaluated at the Junior bar?
options: 可以接受，Junior 只需先给出一个能跑的对象模型，2D 爆炸问题可以在面试官追问后才发现
直接判定失败，任何耦合格式与目的地的设计在任何面试级别下都不能通过
只有把 Formatter 独立成单独接口的候选人，才算完成了 Junior 级别的基本要求
Junior 候选人必须在没有提示的情况下自己想到组合优于继承，否则算不合格
options_en: It's acceptable — a Junior only needs a working object model first; noticing the 2D explosion can come after the interviewer pushes.
It should be an automatic fail — coupling format and destination is disqualifying at any interview level.
Only a candidate who separates Formatter out into its own interface has met the basic Junior bar.
A Junior candidate must independently realize composition beats inheritance without any hint, or they fail.
optionExplanations: 文章原话：Junior 第一版耦合格式和目的地是可以的，只在被追问后才需要看到爆炸问题。
耦合本身在 Junior 级别是可接受的起点，不是失败项，这是 Mid/Senior 才要求分离。
把 Formatter 独立出来是 Mid-level 的期望，不是 Junior 的门槛。
自主发现组合优于继承是 Mid/Senior 信号；Junior 允许在提示下才想到。
optionExplanations_en: The article says explicitly: a Junior's first cut coupling format and destination is fine, as long as they see the explosion once pushed.
Coupling is an acceptable starting point at the Junior bar, not a fail item; separation is the Mid/Senior expectation.
Pulling Formatter out into its own interface is the Mid-level expectation, not the Junior bar.
Independently discovering composition over inheritance is a Mid/Senior signal; Juniors are allowed to need a hint.
why: Junior 的门槛是能把一句话需求拆成能跑的对象模型和基本错误处理；耦合格式与目的地、只在被追问后才看到 2D 爆炸，都在预期范围内。
why_en: The Junior bar is turning a one-line prompt into a working object model with basic error handling; coupling format and destination and only noticing the 2D explosion when pushed are both within expectations.
tradeoff: Junior 看模型是否能跑 vs Mid/Senior 看是否主动分离变化轴
whenOtherWins: 同一份耦合设计放到 Mid-level 评估时就不再够用，需要主动提出格式-目的地分离。

scenario: 在实体阶段列出 Logger/LogRecord/Formatter/Destination 四个类时，你注意到 ConsoleDestination 和 FileDestination 迟早要共享'写字节'这个动作，想在这一步就直接抽出 Sink 接口。
scenario_en: While listing the four entities Logger, LogRecord, Formatter, and Destination, you notice ConsoleDestination and FileDestination will share a 'write bytes' step and consider pulling out a Sink interface right there.
q: 这个抽象应该在实体阶段就定下来吗？
q_en: Should that abstraction be locked in during the entity stage?
options: 不急；等 Class Design 比完继承 vs 组合后，Sink 作为组合方案的产物自然浮现更有说服力
应该立刻定，实体阶段就该把所有类列完，越早锁定抽象越能避免后面大量返工
不需要 Sink 这个接口，Destination 从一开始写死 console/file 分支处理即可
应该在实体阶段就把 Sink 和 Formatter 合并成一个接口，用来减少系统类的总数
options_en: No rush — let Sink emerge naturally as the product of the inheritance-vs-composition comparison during class design, which makes the case stronger.
Lock it in immediately; the entity stage should list every class as early as possible, since locking abstractions early avoids rework later.
Skip the Sink interface entirely and just hardcode console/file branches in Destination from the start.
Merge Sink and Formatter into one interface right at the entity stage in order to reduce the system's total class count.
optionExplanations: 文章原文建议先走完两种方案的对比，Sink 是那次对比得出的结论而非起点。
过早定下抽象会跳过'为什么不用继承'这段论证，讲不出取舍反而扣分。
不加 Sink 就是最初的 type-switch/继承方案，正是文章要否掉的两个选项。
Sink 写字节、Formatter 序列化是两个不同职责，合并会重新引入耦合问题。
optionExplanations_en: The article says forcing Sink into the entity stage skips the most valuable reasoning: the inheritance-vs-composition discussion.
Locking the abstraction in too early skips the 'why not inheritance' argument, and not being able to explain it costs points.
Skipping Sink is exactly the type-switch or inheritance starting point the article walks through and rejects.
Sink writes bytes and Formatter serializes — two different responsibilities; merging them reintroduces coupling.
why: 把 Sink 提前塞进实体阶段会跳过继承-组合这段最有价值的推理；让它在 Class Design 比较完两个方案后自然浮现，论证更完整。
why_en: Forcing Sink into the entity stage skips the most valuable inheritance-vs-composition reasoning; letting it emerge after that comparison makes the argument complete.
tradeoff: 延后抽象换完整论证 vs 提前定下抽象换省时间但讲不出取舍
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官直接要求先看完整类图再讨论取舍，也可以先画出 Sink 再回头补充理由。

scenario: Destination 的构造函数接收 Formatter 和 Sink 两个接口类型的参数，而不是直接 new 一个 ConsoleSink 或 JsonFormatter。
scenario_en: Destination's constructor takes Formatter and Sink as interface-typed parameters, instead of internally new-ing a ConsoleSink or JsonFormatter itself.
q: 这体现的是哪条设计原则，换来什么好处？
q_en: Which design principle is this, and what does it buy you?
options: 依赖倒置：Destination 依赖抽象接口，换 RemoteSink 不用改代码
单一职责：Destination 只做一件事，所以构造函数的参数应该越少越好越简洁
开闭原则：只要构造函数签名不变，Destination 内部实现逻辑就永远不需要修改
接口隔离：把 Sink 和 Formatter 拆成两个独立参数，是为了压低单个接口暴露的方法数量
options_en: Dependency Inversion: Destination depends on abstract interfaces, so swapping in RemoteSink needs no code change.
Single Responsibility: Destination does one thing, so its constructor parameters should be kept as few and simple as possible.
Open/Closed: as long as the constructor's signature stays unchanged, Destination's internal implementation never needs modification.
Interface Segregation: Sink and Formatter are split into two separate parameters to keep each single interface's exposed method count low.
optionExplanations: 高层类只认接口，不认具体实现；后续想接入新目标，换一个构造参数就够。
参数数量和单一职责无关，这里两个参数对应两个真实变化轴，不是为了'越少越好'。
开闭原则讲的是对扩展开放、对修改关闭，不是'构造函数不变逻辑就不用改'。
拆成两个参数是因为格式和输出是两条独立变化轴，不是为了压低单个接口的方法数。
optionExplanations_en: The high-level workflow class depends on abstractions, not concretions; adding RemoteSink is just passing a different instance.
Parameter count is unrelated to single responsibility; the two parameters map to two real axes of variation, not a minimalism goal.
Open/Closed is about open for extension, closed for modification, not 'unchanged constructor means untouched internals'.
The split into two parameters reflects two independent variation axes, not a method-count minimization goal for one interface.
why: Destination 依赖 Sink 和 Formatter 这两个抽象而不是具体类，新增 RemoteSink 时只是构造时传入不同实例，Destination 本身零改动。
why_en: Destination depends on the Sink and Formatter abstractions rather than concrete classes, so a new RemoteSink is just a different constructor argument, with zero changes to Destination itself.
tradeoff: 依赖抽象换来无痛扩展 vs 依赖具体类实现起来更直白但换目标要改代码
whenOtherWins: 系统里只会存在一种输出目标、终身不变时，直接依赖具体类也能少一层接口的间接成本。

termDefinitions.meaning: 高层模块依赖抽象接口而不是具体实现，具体实现反过来依赖抽象，是 SOLID 里的 D。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dependency Inversion means high-level modules depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations, which in turn depend on those abstractions; it's the D in SOLID.

scenario: 有人建议跳过 LogRecord 类，让 Logger.log() 直接把 (timestamp, level, message, threadName) 四个参数原样传给每个 destination.write()。半年后要新增 requestId 字段。
scenario_en: Someone proposes skipping the LogRecord class and having Logger.log() pass the four raw parameters (timestamp, level, message, threadName) straight to every destination.write(). Six months later a requestId field needs to be added.
q: 这时候会发生什么？
q_en: What happens at that point?
options: Destination.write 和每个 Formatter.format 签名都要跟着改，改动面覆盖整个系统
因为四个参数已经是原始类型，新增 requestId 只需要在 Logger.log 内部加一行局部变量即可
不需要改任何方法签名，requestId 可以通过全局变量在各方法间隐式传递
只需要给 write 方法加一个可选参数，其它已有调用点不用同步修改
options_en: Every Destination.write and Formatter.format signature has to change, and the blast radius covers the whole system.
Since the four are primitives already, adding requestId only needs one local variable inside Logger.log.
No signatures need to change at all — requestId can be passed implicitly through a global variable.
Just add one optional parameter to write, and existing call sites don't need to be touched.
optionExplanations: 四个参数到处传意味着新字段要跟着改遍每个消费它们的方法签名，这正是 LogRecord 要避免的。
requestId 要被 destination 和 formatter 用到，只加在 Logger.log 内部没用，还是得往下传。
全局变量会让并发调用互相踩踏，且违背了记录应随调用方走的语义。
可选参数依然是签名变化，且暗改语义会让老调用点静默丢失新字段而不报错，更危险。
optionExplanations_en: Passing four raw parameters everywhere means the new field has to be threaded through every consuming signature, exactly what LogRecord avoids.
requestId needs to reach destinations and formatters, so a local variable inside Logger.log alone doesn't get it there.
A global variable would let concurrent calls stomp on each other and breaks the idea that a record travels with its call.
An optional parameter is still a signature change, and silently missing the new field at old call sites is worse, not safer.
why: 四参数方案下，新增 requestId 要改 Destination.write、每个 Formatter.format 的签名，改动面覆盖整个系统；LogRecord 把这些字段收进一个类，加字段只改一处。
why_en: With four raw parameters, adding requestId means changing Destination.write and every Formatter.format signature across the whole system; LogRecord groups the fields so a new field touches only one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次 log 调用生成的不可变值对象，携带 timestamp、level、message、threadName 四个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A LogRecord is the immutable value object created per log call, carrying timestamp, level, message, and thread name.

scenario: 另一道 LLD 题：支付方式（信用卡/钱包/银行转账）和币种（USD/EUR/JPY）可以任意组合，且两者各自独立扩展。
scenario_en: A different LLD prompt: payment methods (credit card / wallet / bank transfer) and currencies (USD/EUR/JPY) can combine freely and each expands independently.
q: 看到这种'两个维度各自独立变化'的信号，第一反应该往哪个方向设计？
q_en: Seeing this 'two independently varying dimensions' signal, which design direction should you reach for first?
options: 把两个维度各自抽成接口，用组合而不是继承，避免 N×M 个具体类
为每一种（支付方式, 币种）组合单独建一个类，保证每种情况都能精确定制
选一个维度做成抽象基类，另一个维度作为该基类的字段硬编码进去
两个维度都不建模，运行时用字符串比较分支处理，减少类的数量
options_en: Turn each dimension into its own interface and compose them, avoiding N times M concrete classes.
Create one class per (payment method, currency) combination so every case can be precisely customized.
Make one dimension an abstract base class and hardcode the other dimension as a field on it.
Don't model either dimension — branch on string comparisons at runtime to keep the class count down.
optionExplanations: 这正是 Formatter/Sink 分离用到的同一条heuristic：两个独立变化轴用组合，新增一边不影响另一边。
M×N 建类正是 Formatter 和 Destination 耦合时会撞上的 2D 爆炸，是这条heuristic要避免的结果。
把一个维度硬编码进基类字段，等于只解决了一半问题，另一维度扩展时仍要改这个基类。
字符串分支会重演 Destination 最初 type-switch 方案的 Open/Closed 违反问题，规模变大后更难维护。
optionExplanations_en: This is the exact same heuristic behind separating Formatter from Sink: two independent axes get composed, and extending one never touches the other.
Building an M-by-N class per combination is exactly the 2D explosion that coupling format and destination caused — the outcome this heuristic avoids.
Hardcoding one dimension as a field on the base class solves only half the problem; extending it still means editing that base class.
String-branching repeats the Open/Closed violation of Destination's original type-switch approach, and gets worse as it scales.
why: 两个维度各自独立变化，是组合优于继承的通用信号，不只出现在 logging 里；每个维度抽成接口、构造时组合，新增一边不改另一边。
why_en: Two independently varying dimensions is a general signal for composition over inheritance, not unique to logging; make each dimension an interface and compose at construction so extending one never touches the other.
tradeoff: 两个接口 + 组合换零改动扩展 vs 少建一层接口但撞上 N×M 类爆炸
whenOtherWins: 如果其中一个维度基本不会再扩展（比如只有一种币种），直接把它硬编码为字段也是合理的简化。

scenario: FileSink 在构造时打开文件并持有 writer 句柄，程序会长时间运行并持续调用 log()。
scenario_en: FileSink opens the file and holds the writer handle at construction time, and the application runs for a long time, calling log() continuously.
q: 这个文件句柄该由谁负责关闭，什么时候关？
q_en: Who is responsible for closing that file handle, and when?
options: 应用整体关闭时关闭，或者提供一个显式 close() 方法走优雅关闭路径
FileSink 每次 write 完就立刻 close，下次 write 前再重新 open
由调用 log() 的业务代码负责在每次打日志后手动调用 close()
永远不关闭，让操作系统在进程结束时强制回收文件句柄即可
options_en: Close it when the application shuts down, or expose an explicit close() for a graceful shutdown path.
FileSink should close right after every write and reopen before the next one.
The business code calling log() should manually call close() after every log call.
Never close it explicitly — let the OS forcibly reclaim the handle when the process ends.
optionExplanations: 文章明说句柄在应用关闭时释放，或提供显式 close() 走优雅路径，和 flush 的收尾时机呼应。
每次 open/close 会把本该省下来的 open syscall 成本重新加回每条日志，正是要避免的代价。
业务代码不该知道 FileSink 内部持有文件句柄这件事，这会打破 Sink 的封装边界。
从不显式关闭会让最后写入的内容留在 OS 缓冲区未刷盘，遇到崩溃更容易丢失最近日志。
optionExplanations_en: The article says the handle closes at app shutdown, or via an explicit close() for a graceful path, echoing the flush timing decision.
Opening and closing per write reintroduces the exact open-syscall cost per record that keeping the handle open was meant to avoid.
Business code shouldn't need to know FileSink holds a file handle at all — that breaks the Sink's encapsulation boundary.
Never closing explicitly leaves the last writes sitting in an OS buffer unflushed, more likely to be lost on a crash.
why: FileSink 构造时打开、复用同一个 writer；关闭要么随应用整体关闭，要么走一个显式 close() 的优雅路径，不该每次写完就关。
why_en: FileSink opens once at construction and reuses the same writer; closing happens at app shutdown or via an explicit graceful close(), never per write.
tradeoff: 常驻句柄换高吞吐 vs 每次开关换零状态但成本高
whenOtherWins: 极低频写入、且完全不在意 open 的 syscall 成本时，每次开关也能简化状态管理。

scenario: 异步 Destination 的 bounded queue 满了。团队在 block/drop-newest/drop-oldest/throw 四个策略里选默认值。
scenario_en: An async Destination's bounded queue is full. The team is picking a default from four choices: block, drop-newest, drop-oldest, or throw.
q: 四个策略里，production 默认最常见的是哪一个，为什么？
q_en: Which of the four is the most common production default, and why?
options: drop-newest 配 stderr 诊断：换取不丢历史，代价是最新记录可能丢失
block：让业务线程阻塞等待队列腾出空间，因为这样才能保证一条记录都不丢失
throw：让调用方自己捕获异常并决定是否重试，因为这被认为是最诚实的做法
drop-oldest：优先保留最新写入的记录，因为运维通常只关心刚刚发生的事情
options_en: Drop-newest with a stderr diagnostic: keep history, at the cost of possibly losing the newest record.
Block: make the business thread wait for space, since this is regarded as the only way to guarantee zero record loss.
Throw: let the caller catch the exception itself and decide whether to retry, since this is seen as the most honest option.
Drop-oldest: prioritize the most recently written record, since operators usually only care about what just happened.
optionExplanations: 文章点名生产默认多是 drop-newest + stderr 诊断，在不阻塞调用方和不完全静默之间取平衡。
block 恰好抵消了异步化想要的效果——调用方本该立刻返回，block 又把它拖住。
throw 会把调用方重新拖回处理日志异常的负担，正是要避免的场景。
drop-oldest 会连续覆盖旧记录，正常运行下反而更常见的是保留旧的、牺牲最新那一条。
optionExplanations_en: The article names drop-newest with a stderr diagnostic as the common production default, balancing caller latency against total silence.
Blocking cancels out the point of going async — the caller was supposed to return immediately, and blocking holds it up again.
Throwing pushes the log-failure-handling burden right back onto the caller, exactly what async writes were meant to avoid.
Drop-oldest keeps overwriting older records; the more common default actually keeps the old ones and sacrifices the newest instead.
why: 四个策略各自代价不同：block 抵消异步收益，throw 把负担还给调用方，drop-oldest 丢历史；多数生产日志库默认 drop-newest 加 stderr 诊断。
why_en: Each policy has a distinct cost: block cancels the point of async, throw hands the burden back to the caller, drop-oldest loses history; most production loggers default to drop-newest with a stderr diagnostic.
tradeoff: drop-newest 保历史丢最新 vs block 零丢失但拖慢调用方
whenOtherWins: 如果业务绝对不能丢任何一条记录、且能接受偶尔的调用延迟，block 才是更合适的默认。

termDefinitions.meaning: 容量固定的队列，满了之后必须按策略处理新写入，不能无限增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bounded queue has a fixed capacity; once full, new writes must be handled by a policy instead of growing without limit.

scenario: Implementation 阶段只剩十分钟，你要决定优先手写哪些方法体的完整伪代码。
scenario_en: Only ten minutes are left in the implementation phase, and you need to decide which method bodies to write out in full pseudocode first.
q: 该优先完整写出哪两个方法？
q_en: Which two methods deserve full pseudocode first?
options: Logger.log()（capture+fan-out）和 Destination.write()（全流程）
PlainTextFormatter.format() 和 JsonFormatter.format()，因为格式化逻辑被认为最容易写错
LogRecord 的构造函数和 getter，因为它是被所有类共享引用的核心数据结构
ConsoleSink.write() 和 FileSink.write()，因为它们直接决定字节最终写到哪里去
options_en: Logger.log() (capture+fan-out) and Destination.write() (the full flow).
PlainTextFormatter.format() and JsonFormatter.format(), since formatting logic is thought to be the easiest to get wrong.
LogRecord's constructor and getters, since it's the core data structure referenced and shared by every other class.
ConsoleSink.write() and FileSink.write(), since they directly decide where the final bytes end up landing.
optionExplanations: 文章明说面试官通常盯这两个方法：一个展示 capture+fan-out，一个展示完整加锁写入链路。
两个 formatter 被描述为纯函数、illustrative 实现，结构简单，不是信息量最高的部分。
getter 在现代语言里'折叠成一行'，构造函数也是直白赋值，不值得占用有限时间。
两个 Sink 被描述为'dumb on purpose'的一行委托，没有值得展开的设计决策。
optionExplanations_en: The article says interviewers usually focus on exactly these two: one showing capture-and-fan-out, one showing the full filter-format-lock-write chain.
Both formatters are described as pure, illustrative implementations — straightforward, not the highest-information part to write out.
Getters 'collapse to one line' in a modern language and the constructor is plain assignment, not worth the limited time.
Both sinks are described as one-line delegations, 'dumb on purpose', with no design decision worth spelling out.
why: 面试官通常盯这两个信息量最高的方法：Logger.log 和 Destination.write；formatter/sink/getter 结构简单，口述带过即可。
why_en: Interviewers usually focus on the two highest-signal methods: Logger.log for capture-and-fan-out, Destination.write for the full filter-format-lock-write chain; formatter/sink/getters are simple enough to describe verbally.
tradeoff: 手写两个高价值方法讲清决策 vs 面面俱到但时间不够
whenOtherWins: 面试官明确要求全部方法都写出可编译代码时，再按顺序补完 formatter/sink 这些简单实现。

q: Parking Lot 基础需求包含哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: Which capabilities belong in the base Parking Lot requirements? (Select all that apply.)
options: 支持 Motorcycle、Car、Large Vehicle 三类车
入场时自动分配兼容车位并发 ticket
出场时用 ticketId 校验、计费、释放车位
支付处理、摄像头、预约和 UI
why: 基础系统只覆盖入场分配、票据、出场计费和释放车位；支付、摄像头、预约在需求澄清阶段被明确划为范围外。
why_en: The base parking lot handles compatible spot assignment, ticket issuance, ticket-based exit, and fee calculation, while payment, cameras, and reservations stay out of scope.
options_en: Support three vehicle types: motorcycle, car, and large vehicle.
Automatically assign a compatible spot and issue a ticket on entry.
Validate the ticket ID, charge a fee, and free the spot on exit.
Payment processing, cameras, reservations, and UI.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在入场时生成的停车会话凭证，出场时用它校验和计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ticket is the record the system creates at entry to represent one active parking session.

optionExplanations: 车型分类决定车位匹配规则，是入场分配必须支持的三类车。
入场是核心流程起点，车位匹配和发票必须自动完成，不用等人工分配。
出场校验、计费、释放车位三件事同时发生，是维持车位库存准确的关键闭环。
这些是需求澄清阶段被排除的功能，纳入会让基础版本失焦，属于后续迭代范围。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle classification drives spot matching, so all three types have to be supported from day one.
Entry is the core workflow, so spot assignment and ticket issuance must happen automatically without a human in the loop.
Exit needs validation, billing, and spot release to happen together to keep the spot inventory accurate.
These were explicitly ruled out during requirements clarification — folding them in would blow the scope of the base design.
scenario: 45 分钟白板 LLD 面试要设计单层停车场，面试官要求先交付能跑通入场到出场的最小闭环。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute whiteboard LLD round, you have to ship a single-floor parking lot that closes the loop from entry to exit first.

scenario: 系统只需要知道车辆是 motorcycle、car 还是 large 来匹配车位，不追踪车主、车牌或车辆状态。
scenario_en: The lot only needs to know whether a vehicle is a motorcycle, car, or large vehicle to match a spot; it does not track owner, plate, or vehicle state.
q: Vehicle（车辆）在 Parking Lot 设计中应如何建模？
q_en: How should Vehicle be modeled in this Parking Lot design?
options: VehicleType enum，而不是 Vehicle 类
完整 Vehicle 类，含车牌、车主、保险字段
把 Vehicle 定义为 Ticket 的父类
把 Vehicle 定义为 ParkingSpot 的子类
why: 车辆是外部对象，系统不追踪它的状态，只需要一个分类标签匹配车位类型；建成类会引入系统不需要管理的状态。
why_en: Vehicle stays a type enum because the lot only needs the vehicle category for spot compatibility, not an entity with tracked state.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求加入车牌识别、黑名单、常客账户或车辆历史，Vehicle 才可能成为实体。
tradeoff: 轻量分类枚举 vs 承载状态的完整实体
options_en: A VehicleType enum instead of a Vehicle class.
A full Vehicle class with license plate, owner, and insurance fields.
Define Vehicle as a parent class of Ticket.
Define Vehicle as a subclass of ParkingSpot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 枚举类型，用一组预定义的常量表示分类，例如车辆类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An enum is a fixed set of named constant values used to represent a category, like a vehicle type.

optionExplanations: 车辆只是车位匹配用的分类标签，枚举足够表达，不需要建成有状态的类。
把车主、保险这些系统不追踪的字段塞进类，是把外部对象误当成需要持久化的实体。
把 Vehicle 设成 Ticket 的父类颠倒了包含关系——票据描述一次会话，不该被车辆继承。
车辆不是车位的特化，两者是完全不同的领域概念，继承关系在语义上不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle is only a classification label for matching spots, so a plain enum already carries what a class would.
Loading owner and insurance fields onto Vehicle mistakes an external object for a stateful entity the system needs to persist.
Making Vehicle a parent of Ticket inverts the relationship — a ticket describes one session, it shouldn't be inherited from a vehicle.
A vehicle is not a specialization of a spot; treating it as a ParkingSpot subclass doesn't hold up semantically.

q: 最终设计中的核心实体/分类有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities or classifications are in the final design? (Select all that apply.)
options: ParkingLot（编排者，管理索引与流程）
ParkingSpot（物理车位数据）
Ticket（停车会话记录）
Vehicle 完整类（车主、保险等状态）
why: ParkingLot 编排，ParkingSpot 存物理属性，Ticket 记会话；Vehicle 只是外部分类标签，没有被建成类。
why_en: The model centers on ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket as classes, while Vehicle stays a classification label rather than a class.
options_en: ParkingLot: the orchestrator that manages indexes and the workflow.
ParkingSpot: physical spot data.
Ticket: the record of one parking session.
A full Vehicle class holding owner and insurance state.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class ParkingLot
  class ParkingSpot
  class Ticket
  ParkingLot --> ParkingSpot
  ParkingLot --> Ticket
  Ticket --> ParkingSpot : spotId

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多个对象、驱动主流程的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator is the component that coordinates other objects and drives the main workflow.

optionExplanations: 编排者持有索引和主流程，是入场出场逻辑真正跑起来的地方。
只存物理属性和车位类型，是无状态的纯数据对象，不掺业务逻辑。
记录一次停车会话的关键字段，出场计费和释放车位都靠它。
车主、保险这类持久状态从未被系统追踪，建成完整类是过度设计。
optionExplanations_en: The orchestrator holds the indexes and drives the actual entry/exit workflow.
It's a stateless data holder for physical properties and spot type only, with no business logic mixed in.
It records the key fields of one parking session, which both fee calculation and spot release depend on.
Owner and insurance data were never something the system tracks, so building a full class here is over-engineering.
scenario: 停车场系统只需保证车位库存准确和按时长计费，不存车主身份、保险这类持久数据。
scenario_en: The parking lot only has to keep spot inventory accurate and bill by duration; it never stores owner identity or insurance data.

scenario: 车辆入场时 ticket 一生成，该 spot 就被分配，即使车还没物理开到车位。
scenario_en: Once a ticket is issued at entry, that spot is assigned even before the car physically reaches it.
q: 本设计选择如何表示 occupied（占用）状态？
q_en: How does this design represent occupied state?
options: ParkingSpot 自己保存 occupied boolean
ParkingLot 维护 occupiedSpotIds Set 索引
不维护索引，每次都遍历 activeTickets 重新推导占用集合
让每个 Ticket 自己在出场时释放对应车位
why: 占用被视为系统管理的 assignment 关系而非车位固有属性，由 ParkingLot 维护索引；Set 是受控冗余，换来 O(1) 查找和清晰的加锁边界。
why_en: ParkingLot tracks occupancy as an assignment relationship through an occupiedSpotIds Set, trading small redundancy for O(1) lookups and a clean locking boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果更强调物理车位状态，ParkingSpot.occupied 也可行；Amazon Locker 就用了实体持有物理占用状态的方案。
tradeoff: 受控冗余换 O(1) 查找和并发边界 vs 零冗余但重复计算
options_en: ParkingSpot stores its own occupied boolean.
ParkingLot maintains an occupiedSpotIds Set as an index.
Derive occupancy from activeTickets on every lookup.
The Ticket itself frees the spot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存储唯一元素、支持快速成员判断的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Set stores unique elements and supports a fast membership check.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时不随数据规模增长，例如 Set 的成员判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means an operation's cost does not grow with the size of the input, like a Set membership check.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份信息在多处保存，需要额外维护同步，换取查询速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization keeps the same information in more than one place, trading extra sync work for faster reads.

optionExplanations: 车位自己存 boolean 更直观，但要跟 ticket 状态两处同步，容易出现两个真相不一致的风险。
把占用看成系统维护的分配关系，用 Set 索引换 O(1) 查找，还能把加锁范围收紧到一个集合。
彻底不冗余，但每次分配都要扫全部 tickets，规模变大或写多读多时代价会显现。
释放车位应该是编排者的职责；让 Ticket 反过来操作 Spot，会打破谁拥有谁的边界。
optionExplanations_en: A boolean on the spot itself feels direct, but it has to stay synced with ticket state, so the two sources can drift apart.
Occupancy is treated as an assignment relationship rather than an intrinsic spot property, so a maintained Set buys O(1) lookups and a tight locking boundary.
Deriving from tickets on every lookup removes redundancy entirely, but the cost shows up once ticket volume or read frequency grows.
Freeing a spot is the orchestrator's job; letting Ticket reach back into Spot blurs who owns what.

q: Parking Lot 和 Amazon Locker 在占用状态建模上的核心差异是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between Parking Lot and Amazon Locker occupancy modeling?
options: 两者都把占用看作车辆/包裹的物理存在状态
Parking Lot 和 Locker 都在编排者里用同一个共享 Set 维护占用
两者占用状态都由 Ticket/Token 自己持有并释放
Parking Lot 占用=ticket 分配关系，Locker 占用=物理包裹存在
why: 车位被分配给 ticket 是关系状态，包裹是否在格口是物理状态；这个语义差异解释了两套系统不同的占用建模。
why_en: Parking occupancy is assignment-like since a ticket references a spot, while locker occupancy is physical package presence, which explains the different modeling choices.
tradeoff: 关系型占用（assignment） vs 物理型占用（presence）
options_en: Both systems treat occupancy as the physical presence of a vehicle or package.
Both parking lot and locker maintain occupancy with the same Set on the orchestrator.
In both systems the ticket or token itself holds and releases the state.
Parking lot occupancy is a ticket-assignment relationship; locker occupancy is physical package presence.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon Locker 里用来验证取件人身份的一次性凭证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the one-time credential Amazon Locker uses to verify who may open a compartment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个电影订票系统案例，这里用来类比座位预订的占用关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BookMyShow is a movie-ticket booking case used here to compare seat-reservation occupancy.

optionExplanations: 包裹确实是物理进出格口，但车位靠 ticket 分配来表达占用，两者的语义并不相同。
Parking Lot 和 Locker 各自维护自己的占用索引，并不是共享同一个 Set。
Ticket 和 Token 是凭证，真正持有和清理占用状态的是各自的编排者，不是凭证自己。
关系型占用和物理型占用是两套不同语义：车位跟着 ticket 走，格口跟着包裹是否还在里面走。
optionExplanations_en: A package really is physically inside the compartment, but a spot's occupancy comes from a ticket assignment — the two aren't the same kind of state.
Parking Lot and Locker each maintain their own occupancy index; they don't share one Set.
Tickets and tokens are credentials — the orchestrator on each side actually holds and clears occupancy, not the credential itself.
These are two different kinds of occupancy: a spot follows its ticket assignment, while a compartment follows whether the package is still physically inside.
scenario: 同一套 LLD 模板要复用到停车场和 Amazon Locker，先决定占用状态该怎么建模。
scenario_en: You are reusing one LLD template for both a parking lot and Amazon Locker, so you must first decide how occupancy is modeled.

scenario: 系统不维护 occupiedSpotIds 索引，而是每次入场都从 activeTickets 动态计算哪些 spot 被占用。
scenario_en: The system does not maintain an occupiedSpotIds index; each entry request derives occupied spots from activeTickets.
q: 完全从 activeTickets 推导 occupiedSpotIds 的优点和缺点是什么？
q_en: What are the pros and cons of deriving occupiedSpotIds entirely from activeTickets?
options: 推导后无法知道 ticket 对应哪个 spot
推导版本反而比维护 Set 的写法运行起来更快，且完全没有任何额外代价
推导会自动避免所有并发 race
最少冗余，但每次分配要扫描 tickets，且并发时要锁整个 map
why: 推导状态概念上干净、没有冗余，但每次分配都要重复扫描 tickets，并发时还要锁住整个 activeTickets map；维护 Set 是受控冗余，换来清晰边界。
why_en: Deriving occupancy avoids redundancy but repeats the scan on every allocation and forces locking the whole ticket map under concurrency.
tradeoff: 零冗余的动态推导 vs 受控冗余的维护索引
options_en: Deriving occupancy makes it impossible to know which spot a ticket maps to.
The derived version is strictly faster than a maintained Set and carries no downside at all, in theory.
Deriving occupancy automatically prevents all race conditions.
It has the least redundancy, but allocation must scan tickets and concurrent access needs to lock the whole map.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多线程同时读写共享状态，导致结果依赖执行顺序的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition happens when concurrent threads read and write shared state and the outcome depends on timing.

optionExplanations: ticket 本身还留着 spotId 字段，推导 occupied 集合并不会丢失这层映射。
扫描代替索引通常更慢不是更快，这个说法把工程代价说反了。
推导只是换了个读的方式，找空位和占用之间的 race 窗口照样存在。
没有额外索引要同步，但每次分配都要扫 tickets，并发下还得锁住整个 map，读写都变重。
optionExplanations_en: Ticket still stores its own spotId field, so deriving the occupied set doesn't lose that mapping.
Scanning in place of an index is typically slower, not faster — this claim has the tradeoff backwards.
Deriving just changes how you read state; the race window between finding and claiming a spot is still there.
There's no extra index to keep in sync, but every allocation scans tickets and concurrent access needs to lock the whole map, making both paths heavier.

q: 补全状态归属心法：
q_en: Fill in the state-ownership rule of thumb:
text: 判断状态属于实体还是 orchestrator，可问它是实体的{{内在属性}}，还是系统管理的{{关系/分配}}。
why: 车位大小是内在属性，当前被哪个 ticket 占用是关系状态；这个判断能解释很多 LLD 设计里的状态归属取舍。
why_en: State ownership depends on whether the state is intrinsic to an entity or a relationship the system manages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实体本身固有、不依赖外部关系的属性，比如车位的大小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An intrinsic property belongs to the entity itself and does not depend on an external relationship, like a spot's size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由系统在多个对象之间维护的关系，比如车位当前分配给哪张 ticket。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relational state is a relationship the system maintains between objects, like which ticket a spot is currently assigned to.

scenario: 入场成功后，系统要在出场时识别停车会话、车位、车型和入场时间。
scenario_en: After entry succeeds, exit needs to identify the parking session, spot, vehicle type, and entry time.
q: Ticket 应保存哪些核心字段？
q_en: Which core fields should Ticket store?
options: id、spotId、vehicleType、entryTime
完整 ParkingSpot 引用、支付卡号和摄像头抓拍图片
只保存 vehicleType，spotId 和 entryTime 都现查
只保存 hourlyRate 费率，不存 entryTime 时间
why: Ticket 是一次停车会话的不可变记录，出场计费和释放车位都依赖这四个字段，不多不少。
why_en: Ticket records the parking session with an ID, spot ID, vehicle type, and entry time, which is exactly what exit needs.
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持车牌识别或黑名单，需要新增专门实体，而不是把这些字段塞进 Ticket。
tradeoff: 只存最小必要字段 vs 塞进冗余引用和无关数据
options_en: id, spotId, vehicleType, and entryTime.
A full ParkingSpot reference, a payment card number, and a camera image.
Only vehicleType, looking everything else up later.
Only hourlyRate, without any timestamp.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class Ticket
  class Vehicle
  class ParkingSpot
  Ticket --> Vehicle
  Ticket --> ParkingSpot
  Ticket : spotId
  Ticket : entryTime

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接持有另一个对象的指针，可以调用它的方法或修改它的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An object reference directly points to another object, letting you call its methods or change its state.

optionExplanations: 这四个字段刚好覆盖出场要做的事：认票、找车位、算车型费率、算时长，不多不少。
支付卡号和摄像头图片跟停车会话记录无关，把它们塞进 Ticket 会让职责边界模糊。
丢了 spotId 和 entryTime，出场时无法知道该放哪个车位、该收多少钱。
没有 entryTime 就算不出停了多久，只存费率没法完成计费。
optionExplanations_en: These four fields cover exactly what exit needs: identify the ticket, locate the spot, know the rate, and compute duration — nothing extra.
A card number and camera image have nothing to do with the parking session record; folding them in blurs what Ticket is responsible for.
Without spotId and entryTime, exit has no way to know which spot to release or how long the car was parked.
Without an entry timestamp there's no way to compute duration, so storing only a rate can't produce a fee.

scenario: Ticket 需要在出场时告诉 ParkingLot 释放哪个车位，但不应该直接操作 ParkingSpot 对象。
scenario_en: Ticket must tell ParkingLot which spot to release at exit, but it should not mutate the ParkingSpot object directly.
q: Ticket 为什么存 spotId 字符串，而不是 ParkingSpot 对象引用？
q_en: Why should Ticket store a spotId string instead of a ParkingSpot object reference?
options: ParkingSpot 这个类本身完全不允许拥有一个 id 字段
Ticket 是记录，存 ID 更简单，避免它导航或修改 Spot
spotId 字符串无法用来释放车位
Ticket 必须自己负责定价计算
why: Ticket 不应该伸手修改领域对象。ParkingLot 用 spotId 更新 occupiedSpotIds 即可，符合 Law of Demeter。
why_en: Ticket stores a spot ID to remain a simple record rather than a navigational object that reaches into ParkingSpot.
tradeoff: 存 ID 的简单记录 vs 存对象引用带来的导航能力
options_en: ParkingSpot as a class is not allowed to have an id field at all.
Ticket is a record, and storing an ID is simpler and keeps it from navigating into or mutating Spot.
A spotId string cannot be used to free the spot.
Ticket must own the fee-calculation logic itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象只应该跟直接协作者通信，不应该链式访问别的对象内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says an object should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through them into other objects.

optionExplanations: ParkingSpot 完全可以有自己的 id 字段，这个说法本身站不住脚。
Ticket 只是记录一次会话的事实，存字符串 ID 就够用，还能防止它反过来伸手修改 Spot 对象。
ParkingLot 拿到 spotId 就能在自己的索引里定位并释放对应车位，字符串完全够用。
计费是 ParkingLot 的职责，跟 Ticket 该存 ID 还是引用没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: ParkingSpot can absolutely have its own id field — this claim doesn't hold up.
Ticket only needs to record the facts of a session, so a string ID is enough, and it keeps Ticket from reaching back in to mutate Spot.
ParkingLot can look up and release the right spot from just the ID in its own index — a string is all it needs.
Fee calculation belongs to ParkingLot; it has nothing to do with whether Ticket stores an ID or a reference.

scenario: 需求只有一条定价规则：所有车型同一 hourly rate，按小时向上取整。
scenario_en: The only pricing rule is one hourly rate for all vehicle types, rounded up to whole hours.
q: 计费逻辑应放在哪个类里？
q_en: Which class should own the fee-calculation logic?
options: Ticket.calculateFee，并让 Ticket 自己保存 rate
ParkingLot.computeFee
ParkingSpot.getSpotType 顺带算价
VehicleType enum 内部计算
why: 计费是停车场业务政策，不是 ticket 记录本身的职责；简单需求下放在 ParkingLot 足够，也符合单一职责。
why_en: Fee calculation is a parking lot business policy, not behavior of the ticket record, so it belongs on ParkingLot.
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持多种复杂定价模型，可抽 PricingStrategy，而不是一开始就过度设计。
tradeoff: 定价放在业务编排者 vs 定价放在数据记录里
options_en: Ticket.calculateFee, with the ticket storing its own rate.
ParkingLot.computeFee.
ParkingSpot.getSpotType, computing price on the side.
Inside the VehicleType enum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Single Responsibility Principle says a class should have only one reason to change.

optionExplanations: 让 Ticket 自己存费率会让一条会话记录背上业务政策，改价格时还要改每张已发 ticket 的逻辑。
计费是停车场的业务政策，不是某条记录或某个车位的职责，放在编排者身上最直接，也符合单一职责。
getSpotType 只该回答车位类型是什么，顺带算价会让一个方法承担两件不相关的事。
enum 只是分类值的集合，让它内部计算费用会把数据类型和业务逻辑混在一起。
optionExplanations_en: Having Ticket store its own rate saddles a session record with business policy, so a price change means touching every ticket's logic.
Fee calculation is a business policy of the lot, not the job of a single record or spot, so it fits naturally on the orchestrator and keeps a single responsibility.
getSpotType should only answer what type a spot is; tacking on pricing makes one method do two unrelated things.
An enum is just a set of classification values; making it compute fees mixes a data type with business logic.

scenario: 系统要把 $5.47 这样的金额存成整数，并按小时向上取整计费。
scenario_en: The system stores amounts like $5.47 as integers and bills parking time by rounding up to whole hours.
q: 补全计费锚点：
q_en: Fill in the billing anchor:
text: 金额应以最小货币单位如 {{cents}} 的整数保存；时长按小时计费并 {{向上取整}}，所以 5 分钟也算 1 小时。
why: 金额用 cents 整数存储避免浮点误差（$5.47→547 cents）；时长向上取整这条规则直接决定 computeFee 的返回值。
why_en: Money is stored as integer cents to avoid floating-point error, and duration rounds up to whole hours, which directly drives computeFee's output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用整数分表示金额，避免浮点小数误差累积。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Storing money as integer cents avoids the rounding errors that accumulate with floating-point fractions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不足一个整小时也按一整小时计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rounding up means any partial hour is still billed as a full hour.

scenario: 出场 API 收到 ticketId，需要快速验证票据并找到 entryTime 和 spotId。
scenario_en: The exit API receives a ticketId and must quickly validate the ticket and find entryTime and spotId.
q: activeTickets 应该用什么结构存储？
q_en: What data structure should store activeTickets?
options: List<Ticket>，每次查票都要做一遍线性扫描，是唯一能用的选择
Map<String, Ticket>，以 ticketId 为 key
Set<ParkingSpot>，按车位去重
单个 currentTicket 字段
why: map 让『按 ticketId 查票』的意图显式化；200 张票时 benchmark 显示 map 0.12μs、list 扫描 1.93μs，但这个差距在停车场规模下不重要，map 的价值主要在代码可读性。
why_en: A map makes lookup-by-ticket-ID explicit, and even though it benchmarks faster than a list scan, the real win at parking-lot scale is code clarity.
whenOtherWins: 极小系统用 list 扫描也能工作，但没有 map 语义清楚。
tradeoff: 查找语义清晰的 Map vs 实现简单但要线性扫描的 List
options_en: List<Ticket>, where a full linear scan every time is the only option available.
Map<String, Ticket>, keyed by ticket ID.
Set<ParkingSpot>, deduplicated by spot.
A single currentTicket field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键值对集合，可以通过 key 直接查找 value。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Map stores key-value pairs and lets you look up a value directly by its key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时不随数据规模增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means an operation's cost does not grow with the size of the input.

optionExplanations: 线性扫描能跑通，但用循环代替按键查找，会把查询逻辑藏起来，可读性不如直接查表。
用 ticketId 做 key，查找意图一目了然，还顺带拿到近乎 O(1) 的性能，规模变大后差距更明显。
这里要按 ticketId 找票据，不是按车位去重，Set<ParkingSpot> 从数据结构上就答非所问。
系统同时有多张有效票据在场，单个字段连基本的多会话场景都装不下。
optionExplanations_en: A linear scan can work, but looping instead of keying by ID buries the lookup logic, which reads worse than a direct lookup.
Keying by ticketId makes the lookup intent obvious and happens to run near O(1), and that gap only widens as ticket volume grows.
The job here is finding a ticket by ID, not deduplicating spots, so a Set<ParkingSpot> answers a different question entirely.
Multiple sessions are active at once, so a single field can't even represent the basic case of more than one ticket.

scenario: 车辆入场，系统要找兼容空位并发票。
scenario_en: A vehicle enters, and the system must find a compatible free spot and issue a ticket.
q: 这段 enter 伪代码体现的状态变化顺序是什么？
q_en: What state-change order does this enter pseudocode show?
codeSample:
enter(vehicleType)
    spot = findAvailableSpot(vehicleType)
    if spot == null throw NoSpace
    occupiedSpotIds.add(spot.id)
    ticket = Ticket(generateId(), spot.id, vehicleType, now())
    activeTickets[ticket.id] = ticket
    return ticket
options: 先创建 ticket，稍后再决定占不占车位
只更新 ParkingSpot.occupied，不碰 ticket
先占用 spotId，再创建并保存 ticket，最后返回 ticket
把车位分配推迟到出场时才做
why: 入场成功要同时建立车位占用索引和票据索引；找不到兼容空位时不能改变任何状态。
why_en: Entry claims a compatible spot, creates a ticket, stores it, and returns it, keeping both indexes in sync.
whenOtherWins: 多入口并发下，这段 find+add 必须放在同一把锁内，否则两辆车可能拿到同一个车位。
tradeoff: 先占位后发票保证不变量 vs 反过来可能留下幽灵占用
options_en: Create the ticket first and decide whether to claim a spot later.
Only update ParkingSpot.occupied, without touching the ticket.
Claim the spot ID first, then create and store the ticket, then return it.
Defer spot assignment until exit time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["vehicle arrives"] --> B["find spot"]
  B --> C["mark spot occupied"]
  C --> D["create ticket"]
  D --> E["store active ticket"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持成立的约束，例如 occupied 集合和 ticket 集合同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a condition the system must always keep true, such as keeping the occupied set and ticket map in sync.

optionExplanations: 先发票据再决定占位，会让系统一度出现有效 ticket 却没对应车位的中间态。
只改 occupied 不建票据，出场时就没有 ticket 可查，出场流程直接断裂。
占位、建票、存票、返回，四步顺序保证两个索引在任何时刻都同步，不会留下半成品状态。
入场就是要当场确定车位，推到出场才分配等于让 ticket 在整个停车期间都指不到具体车位。
optionExplanations_en: Issuing the ticket before deciding on a spot leaves a window where a valid ticket exists with no spot behind it.
Updating only occupied without creating a ticket means exit has nothing to look up, breaking the exit flow entirely.
Claim the spot, build the ticket, store it, then return it — that order keeps both indexes in sync with no half-finished state in between.
Entry is exactly when the spot has to be pinned down; deferring it to exit means the ticket points nowhere for the whole stay.

scenario: 基础需求要求 exact compatible spot，不提『摩托可停汽车位』等 fallback。
scenario_en: The base requirement asks for an exact compatible spot and does not mention fallback rules like letting motorcycles use car spots.
q: findAvailableSpot 默认应如何查找空位？
q_en: How should findAvailableSpot look for a free spot by default?
options: 扫描 spots，找 spotType 匹配且不在 occupiedSpotIds 中的空位
任意一个空位都可以直接随便分配给任何一种车型，完全不检查 spotType 是否兼容匹配
优先把停车场里最大的车位分配给所有车型，不管实际需要
按车辆到最近出口的实时距离做复杂路径排序后再分配
why: 基础规则是兼容类型精确匹配。没有需求提出 fallback 时不引入复杂分配策略。
why_en: The base allocation scans for an unoccupied spot with the required compatible type, nothing more.
whenOtherWins: 如果扩展允许 motorcycle 用 car spot，映射逻辑或分配策略需要支持 fallback 顺序。
tradeoff: 精确类型匹配的简单扫描 vs 提前引入的复杂分配策略
options_en: Scan spots for a matching spotType whose id is not in occupiedSpotIds.
Any single free spot at all can be handed to any vehicle type freely, without ever checking spotType.
Always give the largest spot in the lot to every vehicle type.
Sort candidate spots by real-time distance to the nearest exit.
optionExplanations: 基础规则就是类型精确匹配加空闲检查，两个条件缺一不可，逻辑最直接对应需求。
跳过类型检查会让摩托车占用汽车位这种情况随意发生，违反了『兼容车位』这个前提。
把大车位都给小车会白白浪费本该留给大车的稀缺资源，也不是需求要的规则。
需求根本没提出口距离或路径优化，提前引入这套排序是没有依据的复杂化。
optionExplanations_en: The base rule is exact type match plus a free check — both conditions map directly to what was actually asked for, nothing more.
Skipping the type check would let a motorcycle claim a car spot at will, which breaks the compatible-spot requirement.
Handing large spots to every vehicle wastes a resource that should stay reserved for large vehicles, and nothing in scope asked for that.
Nothing in the requirement mentions exit distance or path optimization, so adding that sorting logic now has no basis.

scenario: 用户出场提供 ticketId，ticket 存在且未使用过。
scenario_en: A user exits with a ticketId, and the ticket exists and has not been used before.
q: exit 的正确执行顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct execution order for exit?
options: 出场时先把 activeTickets 里对应的那张 ticket 直接删除掉，然后再拿它去计算最终的 fee
查 ticket → 计算 fee → 释放 spot → 删除 active ticket → 返回 fee
只计算 fee 返回给用户，不释放 spot，占用状态一直保留
把该车位所在楼层的所有同类型车位全部释放，而不是只放这一个
why: 出场完成后车位可再次分配，ticket 不能再次使用；顺序必须保证 ticket 数据还在时先完成计费。
why_en: Exit looks up the ticket, computes the fee, frees the spot, removes the active ticket, and returns the fee, in that order.
whenOtherWins: 如果计费失败需要重试，删除 ticket 这一步应该放到计费和释放都确认成功之后再做。
tradeoff: 先读数据再清理状态 vs 先清理导致计费数据丢失
options_en: Delete the matching ticket from activeTickets first, and only afterward try to use it to compute the fee.
Look up the ticket, compute the fee, free the spot, remove the active ticket, then return the fee.
Only compute the fee without freeing the spot, leaving occupancy untouched.
Free every same-type spot on that floor, not just this one.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant V as Vehicle
  participant L as ParkingLot
  participant T as Ticket
  V->>L: exit(ticketId)
  L->>T: load active ticket
  L->>L: calculate fee
  L->>L: free spot
  L->>L: remove active ticket
optionExplanations: 计费需要用到 ticket 里的 entryTime，先删掉它就等于把算 fee 需要的数据先扔了。
先读票再算钱，最后才清理两个索引，保证每一步都还能拿到上一步留下的数据。
不释放车位等于让这个车位在系统里永远显示占用，下一辆车永远排不上它。
出场只该影响这一个车位，把整层同类型全放掉会错误地清空别人正在用的车位。
optionExplanations_en: Fee calculation needs the entryTime stored on the ticket, so deleting it first throws away the data the fee math depends on.
Read the ticket, compute the fee, then only afterward clean up both indexes — each step still has the data the previous one needs.
Skipping the release leaves that spot permanently marked occupied, so no future car can ever be assigned to it.
Exit should only touch this one spot; freeing every same-type spot on the floor would wrongly clear spots other vehicles are still using.

scenario: 用户可能重复使用同一张 ticket 出场。
scenario_en: A user may try to exit more than once with the same ticket.
q: 这段 exit 伪代码如何防止 double exit？
q_en: How does this exit pseudocode prevent a double exit?
codeSample:
exit(ticketId)
    if ticketId == null || ticketId == '' throw InvalidTicket
    ticket = activeTickets[ticketId]
    if ticket == null throw InvalidTicket
    fee = computeFee(ticket.entryTime, now())
    occupiedSpotIds.remove(ticket.spotId)
    activeTickets.remove(ticketId)
    return fee
options: 在 Ticket 上增加 usedCount 字段计数
允许重复计费，只记录日志
成功出场后删除 activeTickets 项，下一次查不到同一 ticket
只删除 occupiedSpotIds 这一个索引，但仍然把 ticket 本身保留着
why: activeTickets 是当前有效票据集合，移除后已使用票据和随机无效票据都表现为同一种 invalid。
why_en: Removing the ticket from activeTickets makes any repeated exit with the same ticket ID come back invalid.
whenOtherWins: 如果要区分『从未存在』和『已使用』这两种错误，需要额外维护 usedTickets 或历史记录。
tradeoff: 用集合成员资格表达有效性 vs 额外状态字段表达已用
options_en: Add a usedCount field on the Ticket to count exits.
Allow repeated billing and only log it.
Remove the entry from activeTickets on success, so the next lookup finds nothing.
Only remove the occupiedSpotIds index entry, while still keeping the ticket itself around.
optionExplanations: 加计数字段能记录次数，但没有真正拒绝第二次出场，还得再加一层判断逻辑才有用。
记日志只是留证据，不能阻止用户被重复扣费，风险没有被真正堵住。
出场成功就把票从有效集合里摘掉，第二次查询天然查不到，问题在根上被消除。
留着 ticket 但删了占用记录，第二次出场还能查到同一张票，重复扣费的口子没堵上。
optionExplanations_en: A counter can log how many times exit ran, but it doesn't actually reject the second attempt — you'd still need extra logic on top.
Logging keeps a record but does nothing to stop the user from being billed twice; the actual risk stays open.
Once exit succeeds, the ticket disappears from the valid set, so a second lookup naturally finds nothing — the problem is removed at the source.
Keeping the ticket while only clearing occupancy still lets a second exit find the same ticket, so double billing stays possible.

scenario: 系统用 durationMillis 表示停车时长，按小时向上取整计费，hourlyRateCents=500。
scenario_en: The system represents parking duration as durationMillis, bills by rounding up to whole hours, and uses hourlyRateCents = 500.
q: computeFee 应该如何处理 2.5 小时这类不足整数小时的时长？
q_en: How should computeFee handle a partial-hour duration such as 2.5 hours?
options: 把算出来的小数 durationHours 四舍五入到最近整数小时
durationMillis 对 3600000 取模，余数 > 0 就 hours+1，再乘费率
忽略不足一小时的余量，只按整除后的小时数收费
直接用浮点数 durationMillis 除以 3600000.0 之后再乘以小时费率算出最终结果
why: 需求是不足一小时也按一小时收费，只有『余数>0则hours+1』能保证任何非零余量都进位；四舍五入和向下取整都会算错 2.5 小时的场景。
why_en: The rule is that any partial hour still bills a full hour, so only the remainder-then-increment check gets a 2.5-hour stay right.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要求首小时免费或按分钟计费，这段取整逻辑要整体替换。
tradeoff: 余数判断的整数取整 vs 四舍五入或浮点近似
options_en: Round the fractional durationHours to the nearest whole hour.
Take durationMillis modulo 3600000; if the remainder is greater than 0, add one hour before multiplying by the rate.
Ignore the partial-hour remainder and bill only the floored whole hours.
Directly multiply the raw floating-point durationMillis/3600000.0 by the hourly rate to compute the final result.
codeSample:
computeFee(entryMs, exitMs)
    durationMs = exitMs - entryMs
    hours = durationMs / 3600000
    if durationMs % 3600000 > 0
        hours = hours + 1
    return hours * hourlyRateCents

termDefinitions.meaning: 两数相除后的余数运算，用 % 表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo is the remainder operation after division, written with the % operator.

optionExplanations: 四舍五入会把 2.5 小时收成 2 小时，恰好违反了『不足一小时也要收一小时』这条规则。
只要余数不为零就进一位，这是唯一能保证任何非零零头都被收费的写法。
向下取整等于把不到一小时的零头当成免费送出，跟计费规则直接冲突。
浮点除法在边界值上可能因精度误差算错临界小时，整数取模不会有这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Rounding to nearest would bill 2.5 hours as 2, directly violating the rule that any partial hour still bills a full hour.
Bumping the hour count whenever the remainder is nonzero is the only version that guarantees every partial hour gets billed.
Flooring effectively gives the leftover partial hour away for free, which contradicts the billing rule outright.
Floating-point division can misjudge a boundary hour due to precision error near the edge; integer modulo avoids that entirely.

q: ParkingLot 应处理哪些基础错误？（多选）
q_en: Which base errors should ParkingLot handle? (Select all that apply.)
options: 无兼容空位时拒绝入场
ticketId 空或不存在时拒绝出场
已使用 ticket 再次出场时拒绝
金额用浮点数导致精度误差
why: 前三个是业务错误处理要求，最后一个是实现风险；金额用整数 cents 存储能避开浮点精度问题。
why_en: The design rejects full-lot entry, invalid or reused tickets, and uses integer money to avoid floating-point precision errors.
options_en: Reject entry when no compatible spot is available.
Reject exit when the ticket ID is empty or does not exist.
Reject exit when a used ticket is presented again.
Using floating-point money causes precision drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浮点数用二进制近似小数，反复运算会累积微小误差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Floating-point numbers approximate decimals in binary, so repeated arithmetic accumulates small errors.

optionExplanations: 车位满了还硬发票据会留下无法兑现的记录，入场必须在这一步就拦住。
空字符串或不存在的 ID 如果放行，出场逻辑会在查表那一步直接崩掉或返回垃圾数据。
重复出场如果不拦，同一张票能被反复计费和反复释放，账和车位都会乱。
浮点数做加减乘除会累积舍入误差，金额算错几分钱这种 bug 很难被单元测试抓到。
optionExplanations_en: Issuing a ticket when the lot is full would create a record with no spot behind it, so entry has to be blocked right here.
Letting an empty or nonexistent ID through would crash or return garbage at the lookup step in the exit flow.
If a used ticket isn't rejected, the same ticket could be billed and released more than once, corrupting both money and spot state.
Floating-point arithmetic accumulates rounding error, so a fee that's off by a few cents is exactly the kind of bug unit tests tend to miss.
scenario: 入口无人值守的停车场按小时计费，非法票据只能靠代码拦住，一次错账就直接变成钱的差错。
scenario_en: An unattended parking lot bills by the hour, so only code can reject bad tickets — one bad ticket is a real money error.

scenario: VehicleType 和 SpotType 目前都只有 MOTORCYCLE/CAR/LARGE 三个值，取值完全相同。
scenario_en: VehicleType and SpotType currently both contain MOTORCYCLE, CAR, and LARGE, with identical values.
q: 为什么 VehicleType 和 SpotType 即使值相同也要分成两个 enum？
q_en: Why keep VehicleType and SpotType as separate enums even when their values match?
options: 车辆类型和车位类型是不同概念，未来兼容关系可能变化
编程语言不允许两个类复用同一组常量
只是为了增加类的数量，方便面试展示
因为 Ticket 类型上不能存 VehicleType 字段
why: 分开建模让『摩托可停汽车位』这类兼容逻辑更清晰；相同标签不代表两者是同一个领域概念。
why_en: Vehicle type and spot type are different concepts even though their current labels match, which keeps future compatibility rules clean.
tradeoff: 语义分离换未来兼容逻辑的清晰 vs 合并 enum 省一个类型定义
options_en: Vehicle type and spot type are different concepts, and their compatibility rules may diverge later.
The programming language forbids two classes from reusing the same constants.
It is only done to add more classes for the interview to look impressive.
Because Ticket cannot store a VehicleType field.
optionExplanations: 车辆类型和车位类型现在恰好同值，但一个描述车、一个描述车位，摩托停汽车位这类规则出现时会先分家。
任何主流语言都能让两个类型各自定义相同的常量集合，这条限制并不存在。
拆成两个 enum 是为了让兼容规则以后能独立演化，不是单纯凑类的数量。
Ticket 存 VehicleType 字段完全没问题，这跟要不要拆分 enum 没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle type and spot type happen to share the same values today, but one describes a car and the other a spot — once fallback rules like motorcycle-in-car-spot show up, they diverge first.
Any mainstream language lets two types define their own matching sets of constants; that restriction doesn't exist.
Splitting them into two enums is about letting compatibility rules evolve independently, not padding the class count.
Ticket storing a VehicleType field is completely fine and has nothing to do with whether the enums are split.

scenario: ParkingSpot 在当前设计中只表示物理车位的固有属性，不参与占用或计费逻辑。
scenario_en: In the current design, ParkingSpot only represents intrinsic physical spot properties and does not own occupancy or pricing logic.
q: ParkingSpot 需要哪些字段？
q_en: Which fields does ParkingSpot need?
options: occupied boolean、ticket map、hourlyRate
id 和 spotType
entryTime 和 fee
全部 activeTickets 的引用
why: ParkingSpot 是纯数据对象，只保存物理身份和兼容类型；占用和票据由 ParkingLot 管理。
why_en: ParkingSpot stores only intrinsic properties: its ID and spot type.
whenOtherWins: 如果选用实体自管物理占用的方案，可以在 ParkingSpot 上加 occupied/status 字段。
tradeoff: 只存内在属性的纯数据对象 vs 把关系状态也塞进实体
options_en: An occupied boolean, a ticket map, and an hourly rate.
id and spotType.
entryTime and fee.
A reference to every entry in activeTickets.
optionExplanations: occupied、ticket map、rate 都是关系或业务状态，ParkingSpot 只该管自己的物理属性。
身份和车位类型是车位真正内在、不依赖任何关系就存在的属性，其余都该由编排者管理。
entryTime 和 fee 属于某一次会话，是 Ticket 的字段，跟车位本身的固有属性无关。
让每个车位持有全部票据引用会造出严重冗余，而且车位根本不需要知道别的会话。
optionExplanations_en: occupied, a ticket map, and rate are all relationship or business state — ParkingSpot should only own its own physical properties.
Identity and spot type are the only things truly intrinsic to a spot, independent of any relationship; everything else belongs to the orchestrator.
entryTime and fee belong to a specific session, which is Ticket's job, not an intrinsic property of the spot itself.
Giving every spot a reference to all tickets creates massive redundancy, and a spot has no reason to know about sessions it isn't part of.

q: 按顺序排列一次停车会话的状态变化：
q_en: Put one parking session's state changes in order:
steps: findAvailableSpot 找到空车位 B。
occupiedSpotIds 加入 B。
创建 Ticket(T123,B,CAR,entryTime) 并放入 activeTickets。
exit(T123) 计算 fee。
occupiedSpotIds 删除 B，activeTickets 删除 T123。
why: 同一会话由 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两个索引共同表达，出场必须同时清理两者。
why_en: A parking session claims a spot, stores a ticket, computes a fee on exit, and clears both indexes together.
tradeoff: 双索引同步表达一次会话 vs 单一来源每次动态推导
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Gate
  participant Lot
  participant Ticket
  Gate->>Lot: enter(CAR)
  Lot->>Lot: claim spot B
  Lot->>Ticket: create T123
  Gate->>Lot: exit(T123)
  Lot->>Lot: fee and release B

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了快速查找而额外维护的数据结构，需要和源数据保持同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is extra data maintained purely to make lookups fast, and it must stay in sync with the source data.

scenario: Ticket 已经发给用户，后续会用来计费和释放车位。
scenario_en: The ticket has already been issued to the user and will later be used for billing and releasing the spot.
q: Ticket 字段应如何设计？
q_en: How should Ticket fields be designed?
options: 允许用户修改 entryTime
让 ParkingSpot 反过来修改 ticketId
构造后只读，不暴露任何修改方法
每次出场前随机重写 spotId
why: Ticket 是会话记录，应稳定反映入场事实；不可变让计费和验证更可靠，避免被意外篡改。
why_en: Ticket should be immutable because it records the facts of the parking session and must stay reliable for billing and validation.
whenOtherWins: 如果未来要支持改签停车时段，才需要给 Ticket 加受控的状态转换方法，而不是暴露 setter。
