tradeoff: 不可变记录保证计费可靠 vs 可变字段带来的一致性风险
options_en: Allow the user to modify entryTime.
Let ParkingSpot modify the ticketId in return.
Read-only after construction, with no exposed mutation methods.
Randomly rewrite spotId before every exit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象创建后字段不能再被修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An immutable object cannot have its fields changed after it is created.

optionExplanations: entryTime 是入场那一刻的事实，允许改写就等于允许伪造停车时长，直接威胁计费的可靠性。
Ticket 的 spotId 应该是它记录的既成事实，反过来让 Spot 改写它会打破谁描述谁的方向。
创建后不可变，让票据能稳定反映入场事实，计费和出场验证都能放心信任它不会被中途篡改。
spotId 一旦写入就不该再变，随机重写会让票据跟真实占用的车位对不上。
optionExplanations_en: entryTime is the fact of the moment entry happened; letting it be edited is letting someone fake how long they parked, which undermines billing directly.
spotId on the ticket should be a fact the ticket records; letting Spot rewrite it backwards breaks the direction of who describes whom.
Being read-only after construction means the ticket reliably reflects the entry fact, so billing and exit validation can trust it wasn't tampered with mid-session.
Once spotId is written it shouldn't change again; randomly rewriting it would make the ticket point at the wrong spot.

scenario: 后续要求 motorcycle 3 美元/小时，car 5 美元/小时，large 8 美元/小时。
scenario_en: A later requirement sets different hourly rates: motorcycle $3, car $5, and large vehicle $8.
q: 最简单合理的扩展方式是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest reasonable extension?
options: 立刻抽出 PricingStrategy 接口，为单一规则做多态扩展
让 Ticket 自己保存三档价格并在内部计算费用
为每一种不同的 SpotType 都各自单独实例化出一整套完整的 ParkingLot 系统来处理
ParkingLot 存 Map<VehicleType,rate>，computeFee 按车型查表
why: 只有按车型不同费率这一条规则时，一个 map 就足够简单；Strategy 模式留给更复杂、可动态替换的定价规则。
why_en: A map from vehicle type to hourly rate is enough for simple per-type pricing, without introducing a strategy interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持动态定价、折扣、会员或节假日策略，PricingStrategy 才更合适。
tradeoff: 按车型查表的简单扩展 vs 提前上 Strategy 模式的过度设计
options_en: Introduce a PricingStrategy interface right away for a single rule.
Let the Ticket store all three price tiers and compute its own fee.
Instantiate a whole separate ParkingLot system entirely on its own for every single distinct SpotType out there.
ParkingLot stores a Map<VehicleType, rate> and computeFee looks it up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键值对集合，这里键是 VehicleType，值是对应费率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Map<K,V> stores key-value pairs — here the key is a vehicle type and the value is its hourly rate.

optionExplanations: 只是三档固定费率，还没出现『需要在运行时切换算法』这种情况，上接口是提前买单。
费率是停车场的业务政策，让每张票各存一份价格表，改价时要挨个改，维护成本更高。
车型不是停车场的分区维度，为每种车型复制一整套系统会带来无意义的重复状态。
按车型查表就能表达三档费率这条规则，改动小、意图清楚，不需要引入额外的抽象层。
optionExplanations_en: It's just three fixed tiers — there's no case yet where the algorithm needs to be swapped at runtime, so an interface is paying for complexity too early.
Rate is a business policy of the lot; having every ticket carry its own price table means updating each one separately whenever prices change.
Vehicle type isn't a partition of the lot itself, so spinning up a whole separate system per type duplicates state for no reason.
A lookup keyed by vehicle type expresses the three-tier rule directly, with a small change and clear intent, no extra abstraction needed.

scenario: 当前需求只有一条简单的『所有车型同一 hourly rate』定价规则，没有折扣或动态定价。
scenario_en: The current requirement has only one simple pricing rule: the same hourly rate for every vehicle type, with no discounts or dynamic pricing.
q: 为什么基础需求下不一开始就抽 PricingStrategy？
q_en: Why not introduce PricingStrategy at the start for the base requirement?
options: 只有一个简单 hourly rule，提前抽象违反 YAGNI
Strategy 模式在任何真实场景下都用不上、也没有价值
Ticket 对象无法传给策略对象
费用计算逻辑不需要写测试
why: 抽象要为真实存在的变化付费；当前只有单一计费规则，直接在 ParkingLot.computeFee 里实现更直接。
why_en: A pricing strategy is premature when the only requirement is one simple hourly rule, which is exactly what YAGNI warns against.
tradeoff: 为当下唯一规则保持直接实现 vs 为假设的未来复杂度提前抽象
options_en: There is only one simple hourly rule, so abstracting early violates YAGNI.
The Strategy pattern is never useful in any scenario.
A Ticket object cannot be passed into a strategy object.
Fee-calculation logic does not need tests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不要为还不存在的需求提前构建抽象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI means you should not build abstraction for a requirement that does not exist yet.

optionExplanations: 目前只有一条统一费率规则，还没有真正的变化要适应，抽出接口只是在为假设的未来付费。
Strategy 模式在规则真的会替换或动态切换时很有用，只是当下这道题还没到那一步。
把 Ticket 传给策略对象在设计上完全可行，这不是不引入 Strategy 的理由。
要不要写测试跟该不该抽象出策略模式是两件不相关的事。
optionExplanations_en: There's only one uniform rate rule right now, with no real variation to accommodate yet, so pulling out an interface pays for a hypothetical future.
The Strategy pattern earns its keep once rules genuinely need to swap or change at runtime — this problem just isn't there yet.
Passing a Ticket into a strategy object is entirely workable in design terms; that isn't the reason to skip Strategy here.
Whether to write tests has nothing to do with whether a strategy pattern is warranted.

scenario: 后续扩展为 10 层商场停车楼。
scenario_en: The design later expands to a ten-floor shopping-mall parking garage.
q: 最自然的新增实体是什么？
q_en: What is the most natural new entity?
options: 把 floorNumber 这个楼层号硬编码塞进 hourlyRate 这个每小时计费字段里表示
每层建一个独立系统，且不能共享 ticket
ParkingFloor：ParkingLot 持有 floors，Floor 持有 spots
直接删除 ParkingSpot，改用坐标数组
why: ParkingFloor 是 ParkingLot 和 ParkingSpot 之间自然的容器层，spotId 可以顺便携带楼层信息，如 3-A15。
why_en: A multi-floor garage introduces ParkingFloor as a container between ParkingLot and ParkingSpot.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需显示楼层而没有楼层级别的逻辑，也可以把 floorNumber 直接放在 ParkingSpot 上。
tradeoff: 新增中间层容器 vs 把楼层信息硬塞进不相关字段
options_en: Hard-code the floorNumber value by cramming it inside the hourlyRate billing field.
Build an independent system per floor that cannot share tickets.
ParkingFloor: ParkingLot holds floors, and each floor holds spots.
Delete ParkingSpot entirely and use a coordinate array instead.
optionExplanations: 楼层号和费率是两个不相关的字段，把一个编码进另一个会让两者都变得难以理解。
多层楼共享同一批入口和票据体系，拆成互不相通的独立系统会让跨楼层查询无从下手。
在编排者和车位之间加一层容器，正对应现实中的楼层结构，spotId 还能顺便带上楼层号。
坐标数组能表示位置，但丢掉了显式的楼层实体，楼层级别的统计和策略都失去了落脚点。
optionExplanations_en: Floor number and hourly rate are unrelated fields; encoding one inside the other makes both harder to reason about.
A multi-floor garage shares one set of entrances and one ticket system; splitting into isolated per-floor systems breaks any cross-floor query.
Inserting a container layer between the orchestrator and the spots mirrors the physical floor hierarchy directly, and spotId can even carry the floor number along.
A coordinate array can express position, but it drops the explicit floor entity, leaving floor-level stats and policy with nowhere natural to live.

q: 多层扩展后可采用哪些车位分配策略？（多选）
q_en: Which spot-allocation strategies can a multi-floor extension use? (Select all that apply.)
options: 低楼层优先分配
按各层可用车位数量做均衡分配
按目的地或入口距离选择楼层
永远随机选择离入口最远的楼层
why: 不同策略优化不同体验：靠近出口、避免单层拥堵、或靠近目的地；复杂到一定程度可以抽 AllocationStrategy。
why_en: Multi-floor allocation can prioritize lower floors, balance capacity across floors, or optimize for destination proximity.
options_en: Fill lower floors first.
Balance allocation by the number of available spots per floor.
Choose a floor by destination or entrance proximity.
Always randomly pick the floor farthest from the entrance.
optionExplanations: 让车尽量停在离出入口更近的楼层，减少步行距离，是最直接的一种优化目标。
避免某一层被挤爆而其他层空着，均衡分配能把车流压力摊开。
按用户要去的地方选楼层，优化的是从车位到目的地的整体路径，而不只是车位本身。
刻意选最远楼层不服务任何真实目标，只会拉长步行和寻位时间，不是合理策略。
optionExplanations_en: Putting cars on floors closer to the entrance minimizes walking distance — the most direct optimization target.
Balancing spots across floors avoids one floor jamming up while others sit empty, spreading traffic pressure out.
Choosing a floor by where the user is headed optimizes the whole path from spot to destination, not just spot availability.
Deliberately picking the farthest floor serves no real goal — it only lengthens walking and search time, so it isn't a reasonable strategy.
scenario: 500 个车位分 5 层，高峰期低层排队而高层空着，要选一个分配策略。
scenario_en: A 500-spot lot spread over 5 floors queues up on the lower levels at peak while upper floors sit empty, so you must pick an allocation policy.

scenario: 多个入口同时调用 enter(CAR)，两个线程都看到同一个 spot 空闲。
scenario_en: Multiple entrances call enter(CAR) at the same time, and two threads both see the same spot as free.
q: 这是哪类问题，最简单的修复方式是什么？
q_en: What kind of problem is this, and what is the simplest fix?
options: 内存泄漏问题；重启服务进程就能解决
check-then-act race；同步整个 enter 关键区
浮点精度误差问题；把金额改成整数 cents
路径解析出错的问题；应该改用 resolvePath 这个工具函数
why: findAvailableSpot 和 occupiedSpotIds.add 必须原子化。同步整个 enter 足够简单，且停车场入场吞吐通常远低于锁能处理的量级。
why_en: Concurrent entries can race between finding and claiming a spot, so the critical section should be synchronized as a whole.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单一入口，本来就不存在并发，加锁没有必要。
tradeoff: 简单的方法级锁 vs 更细粒度但更复杂的并发方案
options_en: A memory leak; restarting the service process fixes it.
A check-then-act race; synchronize the whole enter critical section.
A floating-point precision bug; switch money to integer cents.
A path-parsing error; the fix should be switching to a resolvePath utility function.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检查条件再执行动作，中间如果被其他线程插入就会产生竞态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Check-then-act means checking a condition and then acting on it, which races if another thread intervenes in between.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次只能被一个线程执行的代码区域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is a block of code that only one thread may execute at a time.

optionExplanations: 内存泄漏是长期占用不释放的问题，两个线程同时看到同一个空位跟内存管理无关。
先检查空闲再写入占用之间有个窗口，两个线程都能钻进去；把查找和占用合成一个临界区能堵住这个窗口。
这里出错的是并发时序，不是数值计算，浮点精度问题不会导致两辆车抢到同一个车位。
场景里没有涉及任何路径或字符串解析逻辑，这个诊断跟症状对不上。
optionExplanations_en: A memory leak is about state never being released over time; two threads seeing the same free spot has nothing to do with memory management.
There's a window between checking free and writing occupied that both threads can slip into; merging the check and the claim into one critical section closes it.
The bug here is concurrency timing, not numeric computation — floating-point precision wouldn't cause two cars to claim the same spot.
Nothing in the scenario involves path or string parsing logic, so this diagnosis doesn't match the symptom.

scenario: 实现多入口并发下的入场分配。
scenario_en: The entry allocation must work correctly when multiple entrances operate concurrently.
q: 这段 synchronized 锁的作用是什么？
q_en: What does this synchronized lock do?
codeSample:
enter(vehicleType)
    synchronized(this)
        spot = findAvailableSpot(vehicleType)
        if spot == null throw NoSpace
        occupiedSpotIds.add(spot.id)
        ticket = Ticket(generateId(), spot.id, vehicleType, now())
        activeTickets[ticket.id] = ticket
        return ticket
options: 只保护 fee 计算这一步
故意设计成让两个入口都能拿到同一个 spot 才对
替代 ticketId 的生成逻辑
把查找空位、占用和保存 ticket 做成一个原子操作
why: 锁住整个关键区能防止两个线程分配同一车位；这个粒度在停车场规模下通常足够。
why_en: The lock makes spot search, claim, and ticket creation atomic across entrances, preventing two threads from claiming the same spot.
whenOtherWins: 如果持久化到数据库，应改用事务和唯一约束，或 SELECT FOR UPDATE，而不是内存锁。
tradeoff: 粗粒度互斥保证正确 vs 更高并发但更复杂的方案
options_en: It only protects the fee-calculation step.
It is deliberately designed to let two entrances claim the same spot.
It replaces ticket ID generation logic.
It makes spot search, claim, and ticket save one atomic operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要么完整执行，要么完全不执行，不会被其他线程看到中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation either completes fully or not at all, with no other thread able to observe a partial result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，同一时刻只允许一个线程进入被保护的代码块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mutex lock allows only one thread at a time to enter the protected section of code.

optionExplanations: 这段代码里没有出现计费逻辑，锁包住的是找位、占位和建票，不是 fee 计算。
加锁的目的正相反，是要阻止两个入口拿到同一个 spot，不是制造这个问题。
generateId() 本来就在锁里被调用，锁不是用来替代它，只是保证它和其他步骤一起原子执行。
锁把找空位、标记占用、创建保存票据这三步合成一个不可分割的操作，别的线程看不到中间状态。
optionExplanations_en: There's no fee-calculation logic in this snippet at all — the lock wraps the search, claim, and ticket steps, not a fee computation.
The whole point of the lock is the opposite — preventing two entrances from claiming the same spot, not causing it.
generateId() is already called inside the lock; the lock isn't replacing it, it's just making it atomic alongside the other steps.
The lock fuses finding a spot, marking it occupied, and creating/storing the ticket into one indivisible operation no other thread can observe mid-way.

scenario: 想让多个入口并发搜索空位，只在真正占用车位时短暂互斥。
scenario_en: We want multiple entrances to search for free spots concurrently and only take a short exclusive lock when claiming a spot.
q: 支持并发搜索、只在占用时短暂独占的更细粒度方案是什么？
q_en: What finer-grained approach supports concurrent search and short exclusive claiming?
options: 读锁搜索，写锁内 double-check 后占用，冲突则重试
完全不加任何锁，读写都自由进行
只锁 activeTickets，不锁 occupiedSpotIds
给每个 ticket 单独分配一把锁
why: 读写锁允许多个搜索并行，但 read 和 write 之间可能被别的线程抢先，所以写锁内要二次检查后再占用。
why_en: A read-write approach searches concurrently, then double-checks and claims the spot under the write lock, retrying on conflict.
whenOtherWins: 对 3-5 个入口的普通停车场，方法级互斥更简单，性能也已经足够。
tradeoff: 读写锁提高并发但要 double-check vs 单一互斥锁简单但完全串行
options_en: Search under a read lock, then double-check and claim under a write lock, retrying on conflict.
Use no locking at all for reads or writes.
Lock only activeTickets and leave occupiedSpotIds unlocked.
Give every ticket its own separate lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许多个读操作并发进行，但写操作需要独占访问的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-write lock lets multiple readers run concurrently but gives a writer exclusive access.

optionExplanations: 读多写少的场景下，多个搜索可以并发跑，真正占用车位那一刻才切到写锁并二次确认，兼顾并发度和正确性。
不加锁能获得最大并发，但代价是彻底放弃正确性，check-then-act 的窗口会天天暴露。
占用状态实际记在 occupiedSpotIds 里，只锁 activeTickets 完全保护不到真正会冲突的数据。
冲突发生在多个线程抢同一个 spot，而不是抢同一张 ticket，按 ticket 分锁根本锁不住这场竞争。
optionExplanations_en: When reads dominate, multiple searches can run concurrently and only the moment of claiming switches to a write lock with a re-check, balancing concurrency against correctness.
No locking at all buys maximum concurrency, but at the cost of correctness entirely — the check-then-act window gets exposed every time.
Occupancy actually lives in occupiedSpotIds; locking only activeTickets doesn't protect the data that can actually conflict.
The conflict is multiple threads racing for the same spot, not the same ticket, so a per-ticket lock doesn't guard against that race at all.

q: 按顺序排列多入口 race 的发生过程：
q_en: Put the multi-entrance race in order:
steps: 入口 A 和 B 同时调用 findAvailableSpot。
二者都看到 spot B 不在 occupiedSpotIds 里。
A 创建 ticket 指向 spot B。
B 也创建 ticket 指向 spot B。
两辆车拿到了同一个车位。
why: 问题窗口在『检查空闲』和『写入占用』之间；必须把两步合并成同一个临界区才能消除这个 race。
why_en: The race occurs because two entrances observe the same free spot before either one claims it, so the check and the claim must become one critical section.
tradeoff: 分离的检查与占用步骤 vs 合并成一个原子临界区
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Gate A
  participant S as spot B
  participant B as Gate B
  A->>S: sees free
  B->>S: sees free
  A->>S: claim
  B->>S: claim

termDefinitions.meaning: 多线程同时读写共享状态导致结果依赖执行顺序的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition happens when concurrent threads read and write shared state and the outcome depends on timing.

scenario: 停车场有 3-5 个入口，单次 enter 处理约 100 毫秒；200 个车位平均每 2 小时周转一次。
scenario_en: The lot has 3 to 5 entrances, one enter call takes about 100 ms, and 200 spots turn over about once every 2 hours on average.
q: 为什么同步整个 enter() 方法在现实停车场规模下通常足够？
q_en: Why is synchronizing the whole enter() method usually enough at real parking-lot scale?
options: 因为加锁本身会让车位的物理数量凭空增加
因为这类题目里假设停车场永远只有一个车位
因为 ticket map 的按 ID 查找操作本身就非常慢
入场频率远低于锁可处理的吞吐，车通过闸机/支付耗时远大于内存操作
why: 工程取舍要看数量级：停车场的真实入场频率很低，简单正确的方案应该优先于过早优化。
why_en: A coarse enter lock is usually fine because parking-lot arrival rates are tiny compared with in-memory critical-section throughput.
tradeoff: 按数量级判断是否需要优化 vs 不看数量级就上复杂并发方案
options_en: Because locking itself somehow makes the physical spot count grow.
Because this kind of problem always assumes only one spot exists.
Because ticket-map lookup by ID is itself extremely slow.
Arrival frequency is far below what the lock can handle, since gate and payment time dwarf in-memory work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内系统能处理的请求数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is the number of requests a system can process per unit of time.

optionExplanations: 加锁只是控制并发访问顺序，不会改变车位这类物理资源的数量，这个因果关系不成立。
题目场景是 200 个车位、3-5 个入口，不是只有一个车位的极端情况。
map 查找是微秒级操作，慢的从来不是查找本身。
锁能处理的吞吐是微秒到毫秒级，而真实入场受限于闸机和支付这些慢得多的物理环节，锁根本不是瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Locking only controls the order of concurrent access; it can't change how many physical spots exist — that causal link doesn't hold.
The scenario is 200 spots and 3-5 entrances, not the degenerate case of a single spot.
Map lookup runs in microseconds — lookup speed was never the slow part here.
The lock can handle throughput on the order of microseconds to milliseconds, while real entries are bottlenecked by gates and payment, which are far slower — the lock is never the constraint.

scenario: 有人说 Node.js 单线程就完全不会有 race condition。
scenario_en: Someone claims Node.js is single-threaded, so race conditions cannot happen at all.
q: 面对这个说法应该如何回应？
q_en: How should you respond to that claim?
options: 单线程模型下永远不会出现逻辑上的 race
异步 await 之间仍可能交错，持久化时要靠数据库事务或分布式锁保证原子性
Node.js 这门编程语言本身根本就完全不适合拿来实现这样的停车场系统
只要用 Set 存状态就自动获得事务保证
why: 单线程事件循环避免了同一时刻执行两段 JS，但异步 I/O 会在 await 点把请求流程切开，数据库层仍要保证 check-and-claim 原子。
why_en: Single-threaded event loops can still interleave async workflows at await points, so persistence still needs transactional protection.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有状态更新都在同一个不跨越 await 的同步代码块里，才真的不需要额外加锁。
tradeoff: 单线程避免同一时刻双执行 vs 异步交错仍需事务或分布式锁
options_en: A single-threaded model can never have a logical race.
Async await points can still interleave, so persistence needs database transactions or a distributed lock.
Node.js as a programming language is simply never suited at all for building a system like this parking lot.
Storing state in a Set automatically gives you transaction guarantees.

termDefinitions.meaning: Node.js 单线程调度模型，在 I/O 等待点切换执行其他任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event loop is Node.js's single-threaded scheduler that switches to other work while one task waits on I/O.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个进程或服务器协调、只允许一个持有者继续执行的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across multiple processes or servers so only one holder can proceed at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库锁定被查询的行，防止其他事务并发修改它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE locks the selected database rows so no other transaction can modify them concurrently.

optionExplanations: 单线程只保证同一时刻只有一段 JS 在跑，但 await 会把一次操作拆成好几段，中间照样能被别的请求插进来。
两个 await 之间事件循环会去处理别的任务，状态要落库时还是得靠数据库事务或分布式锁保证检查和占用是一体的。
语言的并发模型只影响要不要额外加锁，跟这门语言适不适合实现某个系统是两件事。
Set 只是一种数据结构，本身不提供任何跨请求的原子性或回滚能力。
optionExplanations_en: Single-threaded only guarantees one piece of JS runs at a time — await splits one operation into several steps, and another request can still slip in between them.
Between two await points the event loop can go handle other work, so if state is persisted, it still needs a database transaction or distributed lock to keep check-and-claim atomic.
The language's concurrency model only affects whether extra locking is needed — that's a separate question from whether it's suited to building the system at all.
A Set is just a data structure; it provides no cross-request atomicity or rollback on its own.

scenario: ticketId 从未存在过，或者已经出场使用过一次。
scenario_en: The ticketId either never existed or was already used once at exit.
q: 基础 exit 应该对这两种情况返回什么语义？
q_en: What semantic result should base exit return for these two cases?
options: 必须区分成两个不同的复杂错误码
自动为这个用户重新补发一张新的 ticket
两种情况都统一视为 invalid ticket
照常释放一个任意车位再报错
why: activeTickets 只表示当前有效票据集合，不存在和已使用对出场流程都是不可用，没必要区分。
why_en: A ticket not present in activeTickets is invalid whether it never existed or was already used, so exit treats them the same.
whenOtherWins: 如果客服或审计需要区分这两种情况，可以额外保存历史 used tickets 和状态。
tradeoff: 统一 invalid 语义换实现简单 vs 区分两种错误换更精确反馈
options_en: The two cases must be distinguished with two different complex error codes.
Automatically issue the user a brand-new ticket.
Treat both cases uniformly as an invalid ticket.
Free some arbitrary spot anyway before reporting an error.
optionExplanations: 两种情况对出场流程的结果都一样——都不能继续，区分成两个错误码是给基础流程增加不必要的分支。
无效票据不该被系统当成新会话来处理，自动补发一张票会掩盖真正的问题。
系统只用『当前有效』这一个状态描述票据，不在这个集合里的票据不管原因是什么，对出场来说都是同一种结果。
错误的票据本来就没有对应的正确车位，随便释放一个反而会破坏别的会话的占用状态。
optionExplanations_en: Both cases lead to the same outcome for exit — neither can proceed — so splitting them into two error codes adds branching the base flow doesn't need.
An invalid ticket shouldn't be treated as the start of a new session; auto-issuing a replacement would paper over the real problem.
The system expresses only one state, currently valid; anything missing from that set produces the same result for exit, regardless of why.
An invalid ticket has no spot it actually corresponds to, so releasing some arbitrary one would corrupt another session's occupancy instead.

scenario: 后续要支持车位维修或临时封闭。
scenario_en: A later requirement adds spot maintenance or temporary closure.
q: 在当前占用建模（occupiedSpotIds Set）下，新增维修状态最自然放在哪里？
q_en: With the current occupiedSpotIds Set model, where should maintenance state go?
options: ParkingSpot 加 status 字段，或 ParkingLot 加 disabledSpotIds 过滤
在 Ticket 记录上增加一个记录维修人员姓名和联系方式的字段
往 VehicleType 这个车辆分类的 enum 类型里硬加一个 BROKEN 取值来表示这个新的车位状态
把这个车位的 hourlyRate 计费字段直接改成 0 表示不可用
why: 维修是车位自身或可用性约束，不是 ticket 会话的一部分；基础设计没有实现，但可以沿分配过滤自然扩展。
why_en: Maintenance can be modeled as spot status or a disabled-spot-ID set that allocation simply skips.
whenOtherWins: 如果车位物理状态很多，ParkingSpot.status enum 更适合；只是临时屏蔽少数车位，用 disabled set 更轻量。
tradeoff: 维护性状态放进车位可用性过滤 vs 混进车辆分类或计价字段
options_en: Add a status field to ParkingSpot, or a disabledSpotIds filter on ParkingLot.
Add a field on the Ticket record storing the maintenance worker's name and contact info.
Hard-add a brand-new BROKEN value into the VehicleType vehicle-classification enum type just to represent this new state.
Change that spot's hourlyRate billing field directly to zero to mark it unusable.
optionExplanations: 维修状态描述的是车位本身能不能用，跟 ParkingSpot 的固有属性天然是一类，扩展起来最顺。
Ticket 描述的是一次停车会话，跟车位要不要维修是完全不相关的两条线。
VehicleType 分类的是车辆而不是车位，BROKEN 描述的是车位状态，塞进这个 enum 混淆了两个维度。
费率是计价字段，把它改成 0 只是掩盖了『不可用』这件事，还会让计费逻辑读到假价格。
optionExplanations_en: Maintenance status describes whether the spot itself can be used, which naturally belongs alongside ParkingSpot's own properties — the easiest place to extend.
Ticket describes one parking session; whether a spot needs maintenance is an entirely unrelated concern.
VehicleType classifies vehicles, not spots — BROKEN describes spot state, so cramming it into that enum conflates two different dimensions.
Rate is a pricing field; zeroing it out only hides the 'unavailable' fact and leaves fee logic reading a fake price.

scenario: 监控或前端目前都没有提出『查询实时车位状态』的需求。
scenario_en: Neither monitoring nor the frontend currently requires querying real-time spot status.
q: 为什么基础 API 不主动加 getAvailableSpots 或 getParkingStatus？
q_en: Why should the base API not proactively add getAvailableSpots or getParkingStatus?
options: 这两个方法在技术上根本无法实现
需求没有要求，暴露内部状态会扩大 API；监控需求来了再加
加了这两个只读方法会破坏 ticketId 的全局唯一性
使用者必须提前知道全部车位信息
why: 接口应该围绕核心工作流最小化；过早暴露内部集合会增加耦合，等真正的监控需求出现再加不迟。
why_en: The base API stays focused on entry and exit until status queries are explicitly required, to avoid premature coupling.
tradeoff: 接口按需最小化 vs 提前暴露内部状态换『可能有用』
options_en: These two methods are technically impossible to implement.
There is no requirement for them, and exposing internal state widens the API; add them when monitoring is actually needed.
Adding them would break the uniqueness of ticketId.
Callers must already know the full spot inventory in advance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只暴露必要的公开接口，隐藏内部实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means exposing only the necessary public interface while hiding internal implementation details.

optionExplanations: 查询车位状态在技术上没有任何障碍，说做不到是站不住脚的。
没有监控或前端提出这个需求，先加上等于提前把内部索引暴露成公开接口，真需要时再加不迟。
这两个方法是只读查询，跟 ticketId 怎么生成、是否唯一完全没有关系。
现在的入场出场流程不要求调用方提前知道任何车位库存信息。
optionExplanations_en: There's no technical obstacle to querying spot status; claiming it's impossible doesn't hold up.
Neither monitoring nor the frontend has asked for this yet, so adding it now means turning an internal index into a public API early — it can be added the moment it's actually needed.
These are read-only queries and have nothing to do with how ticketId is generated or whether it stays unique.
The current entry/exit flow doesn't require a caller to know anything about spot inventory ahead of time.

q: 出场计费的正确执行顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order for exit fee calculation?
steps: 从 activeTickets 取出 ticket。
计算 exitTime - entryTime。
按小时向上取整。
乘以 hourlyRateCents。
释放 spot 并删除 ticket。
why: 必须先有 ticket 才能知道 entryTime 和 spotId；删除 ticket 前要先取够计费和释放所需的数据。
why_en: Exit fee calculation uses the active ticket's entry time, rounds duration up, multiplies by the rate, and only then clears state.
tradeoff: 先读后清理保证数据完整 vs 先清理导致计费数据丢失

scenario: 所有 car spotId 都已经在 occupiedSpotIds 中，此时来了一辆车，车辆类型为 CAR。
scenario_en: All car spot IDs are already in occupiedSpotIds, and now a CAR arrives.
q: enter(CAR) 应该如何处理？
q_en: How should enter(CAR) behave?
options: 发一张 ticket，但 spotId 留空
拒绝入场，且不创建 ticket
临时占用一个 motorcycle spot
把最早入场的旧 ticket 强制删除
why: 没有兼容空位时不能创建停车会话；创建一张没有 spot 的 ticket 会破坏 exit 释放逻辑的不变量。
why_en: Entry must fail without creating a ticket when no compatible spot is available.
whenOtherWins: 如果支持候补排队，可以创建一个 WaitingRequest，但那不是基础 ticket 流程。
tradeoff: 无空位时拒绝并保持状态不变 vs 创建残缺 ticket 破坏不变量
options_en: Issue a ticket but leave spotId empty.
Reject entry and create no ticket at all.
Temporarily occupy a motorcycle spot instead.
Force-remove the oldest active ticket to make room.
optionExplanations: spotId 留空的票据后面没法出场释放车位，等于制造了一条无法闭环的记录。
没有兼容空位时最直接的做法就是不创建任何状态、直接拒绝，保持系统状态一致。
car 不兼容 motorcycle spot，临时借用会破坏『按车型精确匹配』这条基础规则。
强制清退别人正在使用的合法车位，本质上是抢别人的车位来解决自己的容量问题。
optionExplanations_en: A ticket with an empty spotId has no spot to release at exit later — it creates a record that can never close cleanly.
With no compatible spot available, the most direct move is to create no state at all and simply reject, keeping the system consistent.
A car isn't compatible with a motorcycle spot; borrowing one anyway breaks the exact-type-match rule the base design relies on.
Force-evicting someone else's legitimate, still-active session is really just stealing their spot to solve your own capacity problem.

scenario: 多层停车楼希望根据不同目标（靠近出口/均衡/靠近目的地）选择不同分配策略。
scenario_en: A multi-floor garage wants to switch allocation policies based on goals such as nearest exit, load balancing, or destination proximity.
q: 何时应该引入 AllocationStrategy？
q_en: When should AllocationStrategy be introduced?
options: 单层 exact-match 场景从一开始就必须引入它
当 Ticket 没有 entryTime 字段时
当金额改用 cents 存储时
当分配规则会在低楼层优先、均衡、目的地接近等策略间切换时
why: Strategy 模式适合真实存在、可能被替换的算法；基础单一规则下直接实现更简洁。
why_en: AllocationStrategy earns its complexity when spot-selection policy genuinely varies and needs to be swapped.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单层、单一规则，不必引入 Strategy，直接 inline 实现更清楚。
tradeoff: 真实可替换算法才上 Strategy vs 单一规则直接内联实现
options_en: The single-floor exact-match case must introduce it right away.
When the Ticket has no entryTime field.
When money switches to storing cents.
When allocation policy genuinely switches among lowest-floor-first, balanced, and destination-proximity strategies.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["one simple allocation rule"] --> B["inline method"]
  C["multiple changing policies"] --> D["AllocationStrategy"]
  D --> E["nearest, cheapest, level aware"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法封装成独立类，运行时可以互换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms as separate classes that can be swapped at runtime.

optionExplanations: 只有一条精确匹配规则时还没有『多种算法互换』这个需求，一开始就上 Strategy 是提前抽象。
entryTime 缺不缺跟怎么选车位是两回事，这个条件跟分配策略没有因果关系。
金额存储方式是计费问题，跟车位该怎么分配是完全不相关的两条逻辑。
当低楼层优先、均衡、目的地接近这些规则会互相替换或组合时，『可插拔算法』的需求才真正出现，Strategy 才值回复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: With only one exact-match rule, there's no 'swap between algorithms' need yet — introducing Strategy at the start is abstracting too early.
Whether entryTime exists is unrelated to how a spot gets chosen; that condition has no causal link to allocation policy.
How money is stored is a billing concern, entirely separate from the logic of choosing a spot.
Once rules like lowest-floor-first, balanced, and destination-proximity actually need to swap or combine, a genuine 'pluggable algorithm' need shows up — that's when Strategy earns its complexity.

q: 补全三类对象的职责：
q_en: Fill in the responsibilities of the three object types:
text: ParkingLot 管 {{分配、activeTickets、occupiedSpotIds、计费}}；ParkingSpot 管 {{id 和 spotType}}；Ticket 管 {{ticketId、spotId、vehicleType、entryTime}}。
why: 职责边界清晰后，入场和出场流程都变成 orchestrator 对简单记录和物理资源的协调。
why_en: ParkingLot owns workflows and indexes, ParkingSpot owns intrinsic spot properties, and Ticket records a session.

q: Senior 级 Parking Lot 回答应主动覆盖哪些技术要点？（多选）
q_en: Which technical points should a senior-level Parking Lot answer cover proactively? (Select all that apply.)
options: Vehicle 不建实体的理由
occupied flag / derived / Set 三种方案的权衡
Ticket 用 map 按 ID 查找的理由
金额用整数 cents 存储
多入口并发 race 的成因和加锁方案
why: 高级答案要能主动解释状态归属、数据结构选择和并发正确性，而不仅仅是列出类图。
why_en: Senior answers explain entity pruning, occupancy tradeoffs, ticket lookup, integer money, and multi-entrance races without being prompted.
options_en: Why Vehicle is not modeled as an entity.
The tradeoffs among flag, derived, and Set approaches to occupancy.
Why Ticket lookup uses a map keyed by ID.
Storing money as integer cents.
The cause of multi-entrance races and how to lock against them.
optionExplanations: 能主动说清车辆为什么只是分类标签而不是实体，说明理解状态归属这条主线。
能对比三种占用方案的查找成本和加锁边界，说明不是死记答案，而是懂权衡。
能说出用 map 而不是 list 的原因，展示的是对数据结构选择背后意图的理解。
主动提到用整数分存钱，说明对精度这类容易被单独追问的细节有防备。
能主动指出多入口下的 race 窗口并给出加锁方案，是这道题体现并发意识的关键得分点。
optionExplanations_en: Being able to explain unprompted why Vehicle stays a label instead of an entity shows the candidate follows the state-modeling thread.
Comparing lookup cost and locking boundaries across the three occupancy approaches shows real tradeoff understanding, not a memorized answer.
Explaining why a map beats a list demonstrates understanding of the intent behind a data-structure choice, not just the choice itself.
Volunteering integer-cent storage shows the candidate is ahead of a precision question the interviewer might otherwise probe separately.
Proactively naming the multi-entrance race window and its fix is the key signal of concurrency awareness in this problem.
scenario: 45 分钟 LLD 面试里类图只占 10 分钟，剩下的时间靠你主动抛出的技术点拿 senior 信号。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute LLD round the class diagram takes only ten minutes; the senior signal comes from what you raise unprompted after that.

q: 按顺序排列 Parking Lot 的主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main Parking Lot design argument in order:
steps: ParkingLot 作为入口，持有 spots、occupiedSpotIds、activeTickets、hourlyRateCents。
澄清三类车、自动兼容分配、ticket、出场计费和释放。
Vehicle 降级为 enum，Ticket 建成不可变会话记录。
占用建模为 ParkingLot 维护的关系索引 Set。
enter/exit 分别原子维护 ticket 和 occupied spot 状态。
why: 从范围澄清到实体裁剪，再到状态归属和流程不变量，是这道题的主要论证路径。
why_en: The design chain moves from scoped requirements to entity pruning, orchestrator state, occupancy indexing, and lifecycle updates.
tradeoff: 范围裁剪先行再定状态归属 vs 一上来就画类图

scenario: 系统需要同时用 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两个索引描述同一次停车会话，两者必须保持同步。
scenario_en: The system uses both occupiedSpotIds and activeTickets to describe the same parking session, and the two indexes must stay in sync.
q: 面试收尾时，哪一句最准确地总结这个不变量？
q_en: Which closing sentence best summarizes this invariant in an interview?
options: 系统里每一辆曾经进出过的车辆，不管它现在是否已经离开车场，都必须始终对应一个持久化保存了完整状态的 Vehicle 实体类
active ticket 指向的 spotId 必须在 occupiedSpotIds 中；成功 exit 后二者都要被删除
所有车位的编号命名必须在整个停车场范围内按楼层严格连续排序
所有发出的 ticket 只要生成成功就永久有效，理论上永远不会失效或过期
why: ParkingLot 用两个索引表达同一会话；入场同时创建两者，出场同时清理两者，才能避免重复出场或重复分配。
why_en: The key invariant is that active tickets and occupied spot IDs stay in sync for every parking session.
whenOtherWins: 如果从 activeTickets 推导 occupancy，就不需要维护 Set，但分配时要保护对 tickets 的读取和修改。
tradeoff: 双索引同步的不变量 vs 单一来源但需要每次重新推导
options_en: Every single vehicle that has ever entered, whether or not it has already left the lot by now, must always have a persisted, fully stateful Vehicle entity class.
The spotId an active ticket points to must be in occupiedSpotIds, and a successful exit removes both.
Spot numbers must be strictly and continuously sorted by floor across the entire lot.
Every issued ticket stays valid forever once created, theoretically never expiring or timing out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持成立的约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a condition the system must always keep true.

optionExplanations: 车辆从头到尾都只是分类标签，这句总结把它错误地升级成了需要持久化的实体。
两个索引描述同一件事，出场那一刻必须同时清理，这才是真正撑住系统的不变量。
车位编号怎么命名是展示细节，不是这道题真正要保护的正确性约束。
如果票据永远有效，重复出场和重复释放的风险就无法被排除，这跟不变量的方向正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: A vehicle was only ever a classification label; this statement wrongly promotes it to something requiring persisted entity state.
Both indexes describe the same fact and must always agree, with exit clearing both at the same moment — that's what actually holds the system together.
How spot numbers are labeled is a display detail, not the correctness constraint this problem is protecting.
If a ticket stayed valid forever, double-exit and double-release risk could never be ruled out — the opposite of what the invariant guarantees.

scenario: 面试官按中级候选人的标准评估这道 Parking Lot 设计。
scenario_en: The interviewer evaluates this Parking Lot design at the mid-level candidate bar.
q: 中级候选人在本题应能稳定说明什么？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate be able to explain reliably in this problem?
options: 必须一次性实现多层楼分配策略并处理跨楼层并发锁
无论如何都必须使用数据库事务加上 SELECT FOR UPDATE 语句来保证跨请求的强一致性
必须把 Vehicle 建成完整类并存车主、车牌信息
ParkingLot 编排、ParkingSpot 存属性、Ticket 是记录，能处理三类边界情况
why: 中级重点是职责清晰和关键边界情况；多层策略和并发多入口是高级候选人再深入的部分。
why_en: A mid-level answer should clearly separate ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket and handle the key entry and exit edge cases.
tradeoff: 中级看职责分离与边界情况 vs 高级才要求的并发/多层深挖
options_en: Implement multi-floor allocation and cross-floor concurrency locking in one pass.
Database transactions plus a SELECT FOR UPDATE statement must always be used no matter what, to guarantee strong consistency.
Build Vehicle as a full class storing owner and license-plate information.
ParkingLot orchestrates, ParkingSpot stores properties, Ticket is a record, and it handles the three key edge cases.
optionExplanations: 多层分配和跨楼层并发是这道题深挖之后才出现的加分项，不是中级候选人一次要做完的基线。
题目场景是内存态设计，数据库事务是持久化层的加分项，不是中级候选人的硬性门槛。
把 Vehicle 建成完整类恰好是这道题要避免的过度设计，中级候选人应反过来说明为什么不这么做。
分清谁编排、谁存属性、谁是记录，再处理满位、无效票据、重复出场三类边界情况，是中级候选人真正的及格线。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-floor allocation and cross-floor concurrency only show up once the problem gets pushed deeper — they aren't the mid-level baseline for a single pass.
This scenario is an in-memory design; database transactions are a persistence-layer bonus, not a hard bar for a mid-level candidate.
Building Vehicle as a full class is exactly the over-engineering this problem wants avoided — a mid-level candidate should explain why not, if anything.
Separating who orchestrates, who stores properties, and who is a record, plus handling the full-lot, invalid-ticket, and double-exit edge cases, is the actual mid-level bar here.

scenario: entryTime 和 exitTime 相同，车辆几乎立刻出场。
scenario_en: entryTime and exitTime are the same because the vehicle exits almost immediately.
q: 按『hourly rounded up』规则，durationMillis 为 0 时应如何思考？
q_en: Under an hourly-rounded-up rule, how should you reason about durationMillis = 0?
options: 永远都应该直接收取 0，完全不去追问产品是否需要设定一个最低消费的门槛
永远收 24 小时，把这种情况当成整天处理
是否收 0 或 1 小时要先向产品澄清；非零但不足一小时仍向上收 1 小时
认为这种边界情况在数学上根本无法算出费用
why: 计费规则强调部分小时向上取整，但 0 分钟是否有最低收费属于产品语义，面试中应该主动澄清或明确定义，而不是自己假设。
why_en: Partial hours clearly round up, but the exact zero-duration minimum charge is a product rule that should be clarified rather than assumed.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确规定最低一小时收费，那么 duration 为 0 时也直接返回一小时的费用。
tradeoff: 边界语义需要产品澄清 vs 默认套用向上取整规则
options_en: It should always just charge exactly 0 outright every time, without ever asking product whether a minimum charge applies.
Always charge 24 hours, treating this edge case as a full day.
Clarify with product whether 0 or 1 hour applies; any nonzero partial hour still rounds up to 1.
Claim this edge case is mathematically impossible to bill at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论实际使用多短，至少收取的费用下限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A minimum charge is the smallest fee charged regardless of how briefly the resource was used.

optionExplanations: 直接收 0 是自己替产品做了『不设最低消费』的决定，边界语义没有被真正澄清。
把瞬间出场当成整天收费缺乏依据，跟计费规则里『向上取整到小时』的粒度完全对不上。
取整规则本身很清楚，但零时长要不要收最低一小时是产品语义，主动提出澄清比自己瞎猜更稳妥。
取模加乘法就能算出 0，这个边界情况在数学上没有任何障碍。
optionExplanations_en: Charging 0 outright silently decides on the product's behalf that there's no minimum charge — the edge case was never actually clarified.
Billing a full day for an instant exit has no basis; it doesn't match the hourly rounding granularity the rule actually describes.
The rounding rule itself is clear, but whether zero duration still hits a one-hour minimum is a product decision — raising it beats guessing.
Modulo plus multiplication computes 0 without issue; there's no mathematical obstacle in this edge case at all.

scenario: 某实现把占用同时记在两处：ParkingSpot 上的 occupied 布尔位，以及 ParkingLot.activeTickets（有票引用即占用）。enter 写了票据，但某个分支忘了把 flag 置为 true。
scenario_en: One implementation stores occupancy twice: an occupied boolean on ParkingSpot, and ParkingLot.activeTickets (a ticket referencing a spot means it is taken). enter writes the ticket but one branch forgets to set the flag to true.
q: 这个漏同步接下来会怎么演变成用户看得见的故障？
q_en: How does that missed sync turn into a failure the customer actually sees?
options: 该位仍被判为空闲，第二辆车拿到同一 spotId，两车争一个车位
两张票的 ticketId 会哈希冲突，exit 时后一张票覆盖掉前一张的记录
系统会在下一次 enter 时察觉两处真相不一致，直接抛异常拒绝本次入场
只有空位统计数字偏大，实际分配路径读的是票据所以仍然是安全的
options_en: The spot still reads as free, so a second car gets the same spotId and two cars fight over one space.
The two ticket IDs collide in the hash map, so on exit the later ticket overwrites the earlier record.
The next enter call notices the two sources of truth disagree and throws, rejecting that entry outright.
Only the free-spot count is inflated; the allocation path reads tickets, so it stays safe.
why: 占用被反规范化到两处真相，任何一处漏更新就分叉；代价是每条改状态的路径都得手工维持这个不变量。
why_en: Once occupancy lives in two places, one missed write makes them diverge, and the cost is that every state-changing path has to keep that invariant by hand.
tradeoff: 反规范化后读取直观 vs 双真相手工同步带来的正确性风险
whenOtherWins: 如果占用只在一个地方被写入（如 Amazon Locker 放包时置位），flag 不会分叉，反而更好读。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一份事实冗余存到多处以换取读取方便，代价是要自己维持一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization stores the same fact in more than one place for easier reads, at the cost of keeping copies in sync yourself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须成立的条件，这里是「flag 与票据表说的是同一件事」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a condition that must hold at every moment, here that the flag and the ticket map always agree.

optionExplanations: flag 仍是 false，findAvailableSpot 照样返回它，同一 spotId 被发出两次。
票据 id 是 UUID，撞车概率可忽略；这里坏掉的是占用真相不是 id。
两处真相没有任何自动比对，分叉会静默存在直到有人被分错车位。
搜索走的正是 flag 这一路，所以分配路径本身就已经不安全了。
optionExplanations_en: The flag is still false, so findAvailableSpot keeps returning it and the same spotId goes out twice.
Ticket ids are UUIDs, so collisions are negligible; what broke here is occupancy, not identity.
Nothing cross-checks the two sources, so the divergence stays silent until someone is misassigned.
The search reads the flag itself, so the allocation path is exactly what is already unsafe.

scenario: 同事主张把 occupied 布尔位直接放回 ParkingSpot，理由是代码更好读。本题里占用是在闸口发票那一刻确立的，车还没开到车位。
scenario_en: A teammate wants the occupied boolean put back on ParkingSpot because it reads better. In this problem occupancy is established the moment the ticket is issued at the gate, before the car reaches the space.
q: 对这个 occupied flag 提议，最准确的评价是什么？
q_en: What is the fairest assessment of that occupied-flag proposal?
options: 搜索时直接问 spot.isFree() 很直观，但本题占用是票据关系而非固有属性
flag 方案在任何问题里都不该采用，Amazon Locker 用它属于设计上的历史包袱
flag 让 ParkingSpot 变成可变对象，这一点本身就违反单一职责，必须无条件拒绝
flag 和 Set 在所有维度上完全等价，选哪个纯看个人口味，不需要给出任何理由
options_en: Asking spot.isFree() directly is clean, but here occupancy is a ticket relationship, not an intrinsic property.
The flag approach should never be used anywhere; Amazon Locker only has it as historical baggage.
The flag makes ParkingSpot mutable, which alone violates single responsibility, so it must be rejected outright.
Flag and Set are equivalent on every dimension, so it is pure personal taste and needs no justification.
why: flag 的真实收益是搜索逻辑一行读懂、车位自己知道状态；代价是把「被分配给哪张票」当成了车位的固有属性。
why_en: The flag genuinely buys you a one-line readable search where the spot knows its own state; the cost is treating a ticket assignment as if it were a permanent property of the space.
tradeoff: 车位自持状态的可读性 vs 编排者集中管理关系状态
whenOtherWins: 当占用代表物理存在（Amazon Locker 里包裹已经放进格口）时，它就是固有属性，放实体上更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 属于实体本身、不随外部关系变化的状态，如车位 id 和尺寸。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Intrinsic state belongs to the entity itself and does not change with outside relationships, like a spot id or size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由系统维护的实体之间的关系，如「这个车位当前分配给票 X」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relational state is a relationship the system maintains between entities, such as this spot currently being assigned to ticket X.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一职责原则：一个类只应有一个变化的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Single Responsibility Principle says a class should have only one reason to change.

optionExplanations: 优点是真的，但本题占用在发票时就成立，性质上属于票据关系。
Amazon Locker 的占用是包裹的物理存在，用 flag 是经过论证的选择。
可变本身不等于违反 SRP，加个状态位并没有给车位第二个变化理由。
两者在同步风险和并发加锁边界上明显不同，不是口味问题。
optionExplanations_en: The upside is real, but here occupancy starts at ticket issue, which makes it relational.
In Amazon Locker occupancy is the package physically sitting there, so the flag is a reasoned choice.
Being mutable is not the same as breaking SRP; one status bit gives the spot no second reason to change.
They differ clearly on sync risk and on where you can put a concurrency lock, so taste is not the issue.

scenario: 开场澄清阶段，你已问清车辆类型、票据形式、按小时计费、满位与无效票怎么报错。四个提问维度里还有一个没覆盖。
scenario_en: In the clarification phase you have already pinned down vehicle types, the ticket, hourly pricing, and how full-lot and invalid-ticket errors behave. One of the four question axes is still uncovered.
q: 还该补问哪一类问题，它会影响哪个设计决定？
q_en: Which axis is still missing, and which design decision does it drive?
options: 问「以后可能变什么」——例如分车型定价，决定 Ticket 存不存 vehicleType
问「闸口硬件用哪种通信协议」——决定入场信号要怎么被解析成一次 enter 调用
问「每天车流量有多大」——决定 activeTickets 应该换成哪一种数据库表结构存储
问「车主 App 的界面长什么样」——决定入场之后返回的那张票据该带上哪些展示字段
options_en: Ask what might change later, like per-vehicle-type pricing, which decides whether Ticket stores vehicleType.
Ask which wire protocol the gate hardware speaks, which decides how an entry signal becomes an enter call.
Ask how much daily traffic there is, which decides which database table shape activeTickets should become.
Ask what the driver app screen looks like, which decides which display fields the returned ticket carries.
why: 四维提问是系统做什么 / 出错怎么办 / 什么在范围外 / 未来可能变什么；最后一维决定现在就要留哪些字段和扩展点。
why_en: The four axes are what the system does, what happens on errors, what is out of scope, and what might change later — and that last one decides which fields you leave room for now.
tradeoff: 为未来变化预留扩展点 vs 只按当前需求最小实现
whenOtherWins: 面试官已明说「别考虑未来变化，先做这一版」时，继续追问未来只会占掉实现时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: Ticket 上记录的车辆分类枚举，基础计费用不到，但按车型定价时要靠它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: vehicleType is the vehicle category stored on the ticket; base pricing ignores it, but per-type pricing needs it.

optionExplanations: 未来变化维度直接落到字段上：留了 vehicleType，分车型定价就不用改 Ticket。
闸口硬件已被划出范围，问它不会改变任何类的状态或方法。
本题是单机内存对象设计，没有到选表结构那一层。
UI 同样在范围外，票据字段由计费和验证需求决定，不由界面决定。
optionExplanations_en: The future-change axis lands straight on a field: keep vehicleType and per-type pricing needs no Ticket change.
Gate hardware is explicitly out of scope, so it changes no class state or method here.
This is an in-memory object design; choosing a table shape is a layer this problem never reaches.
UI is out of scope too; ticket fields follow from billing and validation, not from a screen.

scenario: 你已问过满位怎么办、无效票怎么办、丢票怎么办，面试官答「丢票先不考虑，保持简单」。白板上还剩大约三十分钟要写类设计和实现。
scenario_en: You have asked about a full lot, an invalid ticket, and a lost ticket, and the interviewer said to keep it simple and skip lost tickets. About thirty minutes remain for class design and implementation.
q: 接下来继续追问边界情况的正确尺度是什么？
q_en: How far should you keep pushing on edge cases from here?
options: 停下并收敛到需求清单，进入实体设计；已问到的失败模式足够体现思考
继续把二十个边界情况都列到白板上，覆盖得越全越能体现工程严谨性
既然丢票被划出范围，满位和无效票也不必处理，直接实现快乐路径就行
给每个想到的边界情况都先预留一个异常类型，把异常体系建好再写主流程
options_en: Stop, converge on the requirements list, and move into entities; the failure modes you raised already show the thinking.
Keep listing all twenty edge cases on the whiteboard, since broader coverage shows more engineering rigor.
Since lost tickets are out of scope, drop full-lot and invalid-ticket handling too and just build the happy path.
Reserve an exception type for every edge case you can think of and build the exception hierarchy before the main flow.
why: 主动问失败模式是成熟信号，但收益递减；「保持简单」就是收敛信号，代价是主动放弃一部分边界覆盖度。
why_en: Asking about failure modes is a maturity signal, but it has diminishing returns, and keep it simple is your cue to converge and deliberately give up some coverage.
tradeoff: 边界情况覆盖度 vs 有限的白板时间
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说想看你穷举错误路径（比如健壮性专题），那就该继续往下展开。

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统偏离正常路径的具体方式，如满位入场、票据无效、重复出场。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A failure mode is a concrete way the system leaves its normal path, such as entering a full lot or reusing a ticket.

optionExplanations: 三个失败模式已经建立了信号，再问下去挤压的是实现时间。
二十个边界情况会淹没主设计，面试官看到的是不会取舍。
满位和无效票是需求里写死要拒绝的，属于必须实现的部分。
异常体系是为未知变化做的抽象，当前需求只需要两种错误。
optionExplanations_en: Three failure modes already send the signal; more of them only eats into implementation time.
Twenty edge cases bury the main design, and what the interviewer sees is an inability to prioritize.
Full lot and invalid ticket are written into the requirements as rejections, so they must be implemented.
An exception hierarchy is abstraction for unknown change, while the current spec needs only two errors.

scenario: 需求已定稿，你要给 ParkingLot、ParkingSpot、Ticket 三个类各自定出字段和接口，但不知道该从哪个角度切入。
scenario_en: Requirements are locked and you must define fields and methods for ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket, but you are unsure where to start.
q: 对每个类都应该固定问哪两个问题？
q_en: Which two questions should you ask of every class?
options: 它要记住什么才能强制需求，以及它需要支持哪些对外操作
它会被哪些设计模式套用，以及它应该继承哪个基类来复用代码
它在数据库里对应哪张表，以及它的主键和索引要怎么建才够快
它大概有多少行代码，以及它的方法数是否落在单一职责的经验区间内
options_en: What it must remember to enforce the requirements, and which operations it needs to support.
Which design patterns it will fit into, and which base class it should extend to reuse code.
Which database table it maps to, and how its primary key and indexes should be built for speed.
Roughly how many lines it will be, and whether its method count lands in the usual single-responsibility range.
why: state 从需求逐条倒推，methods 从外部真正要发起的动作倒推；两问问完 ParkingLot 就只剩 enter 和 exit 两个公开方法。
why_en: You derive state by walking the requirements one by one and methods from what the outside world actually needs to call, which is how ParkingLot ends up with just enter and exit.
tradeoff: 从需求倒推接口 vs 先套设计模式再找用途
whenOtherWins: 已经有强制的框架契约（必须实现某个接口）时，先看契约再补 state 更省时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类为了强制需求必须长期记住的字段集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State is the set of fields a class must remember over time in order to enforce its requirements.

optionExplanations: 需求→必须记住的字段，外部动作→方法，两条线推完接口就闭合了。
先想模式容易做出没有需求支撑的抽象，本题的 Strategy 就是这样被否掉的。
本题是内存对象建模，持久化不在范围内，这两问推不出字段。
行数和方法数是结果不是依据，按它们裁类会切错边界。
optionExplanations_en: Requirements give you the fields and outside actions give you the methods, which closes the interface.
Leading with patterns produces abstractions nothing asked for, which is exactly why Strategy was cut here.
This is in-memory modelling with persistence out of scope, so those questions derive no fields.
Line and method counts are outputs, not inputs; slicing classes by them cuts the wrong boundaries.

scenario: 你在白板上把需求逐条映射成 ParkingLot 必须追踪的字段，已经推出 spots 和 occupiedSpotIds 两项。
scenario_en: On the whiteboard you are mapping each requirement to a field ParkingLot must track, and you already have spots and occupiedSpotIds.
q: 「出场时要验证票据有效」这条需求推出哪个字段？
q_en: Which field does the requirement that exit validates the ticket derive?
options: activeTickets：入场写入、出场删除，查不到就是无效或已用过
usedTicketIds：只记录已经出过场的票，用它反查一张票是否还有效
ticketCounter：一个自增计数器，用序号区间判断票据是否属于本停车场
entryLog：把每次入场追加成不可变日志，验证时扫描日志推出当前状态
options_en: activeTickets: written on entry, deleted on exit, so a miss means invalid or already used.
usedTicketIds: record only tickets that have already exited and check validity against that.
ticketCounter: an incrementing counter, using id ranges to tell whether a ticket belongs to this lot.
entryLog: append every entry as an immutable log and scan it to derive current state at validation.
why: 验证要能立刻回答「这张票现在是否在场」，只有活跃票据表能同时支撑验证、取 entryTime 计费和防重复出场三件事。
why_en: Validation has to answer instantly whether this ticket is still inside, and only the active-ticket map serves validation, the entry time for billing, and double-exit prevention at once.
tradeoff: 维护活跃集合 vs 从历史日志推导当前状态
whenOtherWins: 若要求把「票不存在」和「票已用过」分成两种错误返回，就得额外再存一份已用票集合。

termDefinitions.meaning: Ticket 上记录的入场时间戳，出场时用它减出停车时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: entryTime is the entry timestamp stored on the ticket, subtracted at exit to get the parked duration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一张票被使用两次出场，正确设计应在第二次直接报错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A double exit is the same ticket being used to leave twice, which a correct design rejects the second time.

optionExplanations: 删除票据这一个动作同时完成了释放车位和作废票据两件事。
只存已用票就无法证明一张没见过的票曾经合法入场。
序号区间只能判断票像不像本场发的，判断不了它此刻是否有效。
日志可以复原状态，但每次出场都要扫全量，也没解决重复出场判定。
optionExplanations_en: Deleting the ticket does two jobs at once: it frees the spot and voids the ticket.
Storing only used tickets cannot prove that an unseen ticket was ever legitimately issued.
An id range tells you a ticket looks like ours, not whether it is valid right now.
A log can rebuild state, but every exit rescans everything and double exits still need extra work.

scenario: 有人提议把 hourlyRateCents 从 ParkingLot 拿掉，改成 exit(ticketId, hourlyRateCents)，让调用方每次出场都传入费率。
scenario_en: Someone proposes removing hourlyRateCents from ParkingLot and changing the signature to exit(ticketId, hourlyRateCents) so the caller passes the rate on every exit.
q: 这个改动的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with that change?
options: 调用方被迫知道定价规则，封装被打破，同一个场还可能传出不同费率
多传一个 long 参数会显著抬高 exit 的调用开销，出场路径的延迟变得不可接受
费率一旦作为参数就没法再用整数分来表示，只能退回浮点数，从而引入精度误差
参数化之后 ParkingLot 就不能再实例化多个对象，多停车场的场景反而无法支持
options_en: The caller is forced to know the pricing rule, encapsulation breaks, and one lot can be charged inconsistently.
Passing one extra long noticeably raises the cost of calling exit, making the exit path latency unacceptable.
Once the rate is a parameter it can no longer be integer cents and must fall back to floats, adding rounding error.
After parameterizing, ParkingLot can no longer be instantiated more than once, so multiple lots stop working.
why: 定价是停车场级策略：放在 ParkingLot 里既能给不同 lot 实例化不同费率，也不必全局硬编码；代价只是构造函数多一个参数。
why_en: Pricing is a lot-level policy, so keeping it on ParkingLot lets you instantiate different lots at different rates without hardcoding a global, and the only cost is one more constructor argument.
tradeoff: 编排者持有定价策略 vs 调用方每次出场传参
whenOtherWins: 若费率确实由外部系统按次下发（平台动态定价），把它作为参数或注入 PricingStrategy 才是合理的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内部规则藏在类里，只暴露必要接口，调用方不必知道规则细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation keeps internal rules inside the class and exposes only what callers need, so they need not know the rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把计费算法抽成可替换接口的模式，用于需要多种定价模型时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PricingStrategy is a swappable interface for the fee algorithm, used when several pricing models are needed.

optionExplanations: 费率一旦由外部传，两个入口传不同数字就没人能拦住。
一个 long 参数的开销远小于出场时的物理动作，性能不是这里的矛盾。
参数类型仍然可以是 long 分，与放在哪里无关。
实例化能力恰恰是把费率留在 ParkingLot 才获得的好处。
optionExplanations_en: Once the rate comes from outside, nothing stops two entrances from passing different numbers.
One long argument costs far less than the physical exit itself, so performance is not the tension here.
The parameter can still be a long in cents; storage location has nothing to do with the type.
Being able to instantiate several lots is precisely the benefit of keeping the rate on ParkingLot.

scenario: 有人把 hourlyRateCents 存进 Ticket，让 Ticket 自己算费。某辆车还停在场内时，停车场上调了小时费率。
scenario_en: Someone stores hourlyRateCents on Ticket so the ticket computes its own fee. While a car is still parked, the lot raises its hourly rate.
q: 除了违反单一职责，这个设计还引出什么额外状态问题？
q_en: Beyond breaking single responsibility, what extra state problem does this create?
options: 必须决定是否冻结入场费率，Ticket 从不可变记录变成要维护的状态
Ticket 会因此持有 ParkingSpot 的对象引用，违反迪米特法则，让票据能改车位状态
费率变化会让已经发出的 Ticket 的 id 失效，出场时必须重新给车主签发一张新票据
向上取整的计费公式会失效，不足一小时的停车时长将不能再按整整一小时来收费
options_en: You must decide whether to freeze the entry rate, turning Ticket from an immutable record into managed state.
The ticket ends up holding a ParkingSpot reference, breaking the Law of Demeter and letting it mutate the spot.
The rate change invalidates the ids of already-issued tickets, so a fresh ticket must be reissued at exit.
The round-up formula stops working, so a partial hour can no longer be billed as a full hour.
why: 把定价搬进 Ticket 会让它同时是记录和计算器，还得回答「中途涨价按哪个费率」——这是本可以不存在的状态。
why_en: Moving pricing into the ticket makes it both a record and a calculator, and forces you to answer which rate applies after a mid-stay change, which is state you never needed.
tradeoff: 票据自算费用的内聚 vs 保持票据不可变的简单
whenOtherWins: 若业务要求入场即锁定价格并写进凭证（合同价、预付券），那就该把当时费率快照进票据。

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象构造后字段不再改变，读起来永远是发放那一刻的事实。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An immutable object never changes after construction, so it always reads as the fact recorded at creation time.

termDefinitions.term: 迪米特法则 / Law of Demeter
termDefinitions.meaning: 对象只跟直接邻居说话，不要顺着引用链去调别人的内部对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says an object should talk only to its immediate neighbors, not reach through references into others.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一职责原则：一个类只应有一个变化的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Single Responsibility Principle says a class should have only one reason to change.

optionExplanations: 一旦票上有费率，涨价就变成必须回答的语义问题而不是实现细节。
存 spotId 字符串本来就避开了引用问题，跟费率放哪里无关。
票据 id 是身份标识，费率变化不会让身份失效。
取整逻辑只依赖时长，跟费率存在哪个类上完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: The moment a rate sits on the ticket, a price change becomes a semantic question you must answer.
Storing spotId as a string already avoids reference reach-through; that is unrelated to where the rate lives.
The ticket id is an identity, and changing a rate does not invalidate an identity.
Rounding depends only on duration, so it is untouched by which class holds the rate.

scenario: 类设计讲完，白板上还剩大约十分钟，你准备开始写 ParkingLot 的 enter 和 exit。
scenario_en: Class design is done and about ten minutes remain; you are about to write ParkingLot.enter and exit.
q: 动手之前该先和面试官确认什么？
q_en: What should you confirm with the interviewer before writing anything?
options: 要伪代码、可运行代码还是口头讲，如果写代码用哪种语言
是否可以使用 IDE 和自动补全功能，以免手写时出现语法错误
这段代码会不会被留档，作为后续几轮面试的评分依据之一
要不要连同单元测试一起写完，以及测试覆盖率大致要求多少
options_en: Whether they want pseudocode, runnable code, or just a verbal walkthrough, and in which language.
Whether you may use an IDE with autocomplete so you do not make syntax mistakes by hand.
Whether this code will be kept on file and used as a grading input for later interview rounds.
Whether unit tests should be written alongside it, and roughly what coverage they expect.
why: 各家期望不同：有人要特定语言的可运行代码，有人只要伪代码或口述；一句确认就决定这十分钟花在哪个粒度上。
why_en: Expectations vary a lot: some want runnable code in a specific language, others just pseudocode or a verbal pass, and one question decides how you spend those ten minutes.
tradeoff: 可运行代码的可信度 vs 伪代码的覆盖速度
whenOtherWins: 题面里已经指定语言并要求代码能跑时，直接开写，再确认只是浪费时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: 不绑定语言的结构化描述，够表达控制流和状态变化即可。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudocode is a language-agnostic structured sketch, precise enough to show control flow and state changes.

optionExplanations: 粒度和语言是唯一会改变你这十分钟产出的两个变量。
工具问题不改变要写什么，通常也不是白板轮的关注点。
评分流程与本轮如何作答无关，问了不会改变你的写法。
基础需求没有提测试，主动加会挤掉核心流程的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Granularity and language are the only two variables that change what those ten minutes produce.
Tooling does not change what you write and is rarely the point of a whiteboard round.
How grading works downstream does not change how you should answer this round.
The base requirements never mention tests, and adding them squeezes out the core flows.

scenario: enter 与 exit 的伪代码刚写完，占用记在 occupiedSpotIds，票据记在 activeTickets。还剩几分钟，你想赶在面试官之前自己发现 bug。
scenario_en: You just finished the enter and exit pseudocode, with occupancy in occupiedSpotIds and tickets in activeTickets. A few minutes remain and you want to find bugs before the interviewer does.
q: 该 trace 哪个场景最能暴露状态管理的 bug？
q_en: Which scenario should you trace to expose state-management bugs?
options: 同一张票入场→出场→再出场，看两个集合是否归零、第二次是否报错
连续调用一百次 enter，观察平均耗时是否随 spots 数量呈线性增长趋势
只 trace 一次成功入场，确认返回票据上的四个字段都被正确填满就够了
手算停 2.5 小时应该收 3 小时的钱，验证取整公式没有把方向写反掉
options_en: One ticket entering, exiting, then exiting again — check both sets return to empty and the second exit errors.
Call enter a hundred times in a row and watch whether average latency grows linearly with the spot count.
Trace just one successful entry and confirm all four fields on the returned ticket are filled correctly.
Hand-compute that a 2.5 hour stay bills three hours, verifying the rounding formula is not inverted.
why: 完整会话把 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两处状态的增与删都走了一遍，再出场一次则检验删除是否真的生效。
why_en: A full session exercises both adds and removes on occupiedSpotIds and activeTickets, and the repeat exit proves the removal actually took effect.
tradeoff: 走完整状态闭环 vs 只验证单点公式
whenOtherWins: 如果只够 trace 一件事，而计费取整规则刚刚被改过，那先手算费用更划算。

termDefinitions.meaning: 手工把一个具体场景在设计上逐步走一遍，检查每步状态是否正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trace-through is manually walking one concrete scenario through the design step by step, checking state at each point.

optionExplanations: 一次会话就覆盖了加入、删除、以及删除后的拒绝三种状态转移。
这个规模下的耗时差距只有微秒级，测不出设计层面的问题。
只走快乐路径查不出释放遗漏，而遗漏正是最常见的 bug。
取整只是纯函数，验它不涉及任何跨调用的状态。
optionExplanations_en: One session covers three transitions: adding, removing, and rejecting after removal.
At this scale timing differences are microseconds and reveal nothing about the design.
A happy-path-only trace cannot catch a missed release, which is the most common bug here.
Rounding is a pure function, so checking it touches no state that spans calls.

scenario: 你以 Junior 岗位面这道 Parking Lot 题，时间只够写出能跑通的 enter 与 exit，扩展性一节完全没时间讲。
scenario_en: You are interviewing for a junior role on this parking lot problem, with only enough time to get enter and exit working and none left for extensibility.
q: Junior 档评估看重什么，允许你在哪里被提示？
q_en: What does the junior bar measure, and where are hints acceptable?
options: 看入场出场能否跑通并处理满位与无效票；定价放哪里被提示是允许的
看能否主动讲出反规范化取舍与并发方案；实体划分需要被提示是可以接受的
看能否先给出 PricingStrategy 抽象，再顺势展开多层车库的分配策略讨论
看代码是否零 bug 并附带完整单元测试；设计取舍完全不在这一档评估范围内
options_en: Whether entry and exit work and handle a full lot and invalid tickets; a hint on where pricing lives is fine.
Whether you volunteer the denormalization tradeoff and a concurrency plan; needing hints on entities is fine.
Whether you present a PricingStrategy abstraction first and then open up multi-floor allocation strategies.
Whether the code is bug-free with full unit tests; design tradeoffs are outside this bar entirely.
why: Junior 档的门槛是识别出车位、票据、编排者三样并让流程真的跑通；主动的取舍论证属于 Senior 加分项，不是这一档的下限。
why_en: The junior bar is spotting that you need spots, tickets, and an orchestrator, and getting the flow to actually work; volunteering tradeoffs is a senior signal, not the floor here.
tradeoff: 先做出能工作的系统 vs 先讲清设计取舍
whenOtherWins: 面 Senior 档时同样一份能跑的实现就不够了，要主动摆出反规范化、O(1) 查找、枚举分离这些取舍。

termDefinitions.meaning: 统筹整个流程的类，这里是 ParkingLot，唯一对外暴露 enter 和 exit。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The orchestrator is the class that coordinates the whole flow — here ParkingLot, the only public entry point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一份事实冗余存到多处以换取读取方便，代价是要自己维持一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization stores the same fact in more than one place for easier reads, at the cost of keeping copies in sync yourself.

optionExplanations: 两条主流程加两种拒绝就是可工作系统的最小完整形态。
这是把 Senior 的主动论证和 Junior 的被提示项对调了。
基础需求只有一种费率，先抽策略在任何档位都属于过度设计。
零 bug 加测试不是白板轮的标准，取舍讨论也从未被完全排除。
optionExplanations_en: Two main flows plus two rejections is the smallest complete shape of a working system.
This swaps the senior expectation of volunteering tradeoffs with the junior allowance for hints.
The base spec has a single rate, so leading with a strategy abstraction is over-design at any level.
Bug-free code with tests is not the whiteboard bar, and tradeoffs are never fully excluded.

scenario: 3-5 个入口共用一把方法级锁，你要用数字说服面试官粗粒度锁不是瓶颈。
scenario_en: With 3-5 entrances sharing one method-level lock, you need numbers to show the coarse lock isn't a bottleneck.
q: 补全并发容量的余量估算：
q_en: Fill in the concurrency headroom estimate:
text: 每次 enter 耗时 100 毫秒 → 吞吐 1000÷100 = {{10}} 辆/秒；200 个车位每 2 小时周转一轮 → 需求约 200÷7200 ≈ {{0.03}} 辆/秒；两者相除得到约 {{300}} 倍余量。
why: 吞吐=1000ms÷100ms/次=10 次/秒（entries per second）；需求=200 spots÷7200 秒≈0.03 辆/秒；10÷0.03≈300 倍。这个数字用来判断方法级锁够不够，不必一开始就上读写锁。
why_en: Throughput is 1000ms / 100ms per entry = 10 entries/sec; demand is 200 spots / 7200 seconds ≈ 0.03 vehicles/sec, giving about 300x headroom — enough to justify a simple method-level lock over a read-write lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统实际吞吐超出真实需求的倍数，数字越大代表越不用担心这条路径先成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Headroom is how many times over actual demand your capacity sits — a bigger number means this path is unlikely to be the first bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内系统能处理的请求数，这里是每秒能完成几次 enter。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is how many requests a system can process per unit time — here, how many enter calls per second.

scenario: 系统选了『不存索引，每次现算 occupancy』的方案，随后要支持多入口并发。
scenario_en: The system picked the derive-on-demand occupancy approach, then needs to support multiple concurrent entrances.
q: 按顺序排列推导方案在并发下失效的过程：
q_en: Put the derive-on-demand approach's concurrency failure in order:
steps: occupancy 不单独存，每次入场都遍历 activeTickets 现算。
新增需求：多个入口要能同时处理车辆。
遍历 tickets 求 occupancy 时，不能有别的线程正在改 activeTickets。
只能把整个 activeTickets map 锁起来，读和写都互斥。
所有入口排队等同一把大锁，比只锁一个 Set 索引的粒度粗得多。
why: 推导方案没有冗余数据，但并发下必须把整张 map 锁起来做读写互斥；省下的存储换来了比维护 Set 索引更差的并发粒度。
why_en: The derive-on-demand approach has no redundant state, but under concurrency it forces a lock on the entire ticket map for both reads and writes — trading storage savings for worse concurrency granularity than a maintained Set index.
tradeoff: 无冗余、逻辑最干净 vs 并发时锁粒度粗、吞吐更差

termDefinitions.meaning: 一把锁保护的数据范围大小；锁的范围越大，能并行执行的操作就越少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock granularity is how much data one lock protects — the bigger the scope, the less can run in parallel.

scenario: 3 个车位的场，B 位被 CAR 占用 2.5 小时后正常出场，随后用同一张票再出场一次。
scenario_en: In a 3-spot lot, spot B is claimed by a car for 2.5 hours then exits normally, and the same ticket is used to exit a second time.
q: 按顺序排列这次会话从入场到二次出场的状态变化：
q_en: Put this session's states in order, from entry through the second exit attempt:
steps: 初始：occupiedSpotIds={}，activeTickets={}。
enter(CAR) 找到 spot B → occupiedSpotIds={"B"}，activeTickets 存入 T123。
2.5 小时后 exit("T123")：向上取整按 3 小时收 1500 分，两个索引清空。
再次 exit("T123")：activeTickets 查不到 T123，抛出 invalid ticket 错误，状态不变。
why: 正常入场占位发票、出场按取整计费并清空两个索引，再出场时查不到票直接报错且不改状态——这条 trace 同时验证了计费公式和防重复出场。
why_en: Normal entry claims a spot and issues a ticket, exit bills with round-up and clears both indexes, and a second exit finds nothing and errors without touching state — this trace verifies both the fee formula and double-exit prevention in one pass.
tradeoff: 手动 trace 一次完整场景 vs 等面试官找到 bug 才修

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写完流程后手动带入一组具体数值，逐步核对状态是否符合预期，抢在面试官之前自己发现 bug。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trace-through is manually walking a concrete scenario through your pseudocode step by step to catch bugs before your interviewer does.

scenario: 扩展成多层车库后，你要用『两问法』给新增的 ParkingFloor 类定出状态和方法。
scenario_en: After extending to a multi-floor garage, you apply the two-question method to design the new ParkingFloor class.
q: ParkingFloor 应该记住什么、暴露哪些方法？
q_en: What should ParkingFloor remember, and what methods should it expose?
options: floorNumber 和本层 spots；暴露 findAvailableSpot 和 getAvailableSpotCount 两个方法
只存 floorNumber，本层车位仍留在 ParkingLot 里统一遍历，Floor 不持有 spots
存本层已入场的 Ticket 列表，出场校验也交给 ParkingFloor 处理
只暴露 getAvailableSpotCount，不提供 findAvailableSpot，具体车位靠 ParkingLot 直接读 spots
why: 两问法用在 ParkingFloor 上：要记住 floorNumber 和本层 spots，要支持按类型找空位和统计可用数量，这样 ParkingLot 才能委托给每层而不必直接摸 spots 内部列表。
why_en: Applying the two-question method to ParkingFloor: it should remember its floorNumber and spots, and expose finding a spot by type plus counting availability, so ParkingLot can delegate instead of reaching into each floor's internal list.
tradeoff: Floor 自持 spots 并暴露查找方法 vs ParkingLot 继续统一遍历所有楼层的车位
whenOtherWins: 如果楼层数量很少（比如只有 2 层）且不需要按楼层统计，直接让 ParkingLot 扁平遍历所有 spots 也够用，不必新增 Floor 类。
options_en: floorNumber and this floor's spots as state; expose the findAvailableSpot and getAvailableSpotCount methods.
Store only floorNumber; keep spots in ParkingLot and scan them there, so Floor never owns spots.
Store this floor's active tickets and hand exit validation to ParkingFloor too.
Expose only getAvailableSpotCount, no findAvailableSpot, so ParkingLot reads each floor's spots directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个操作的具体执行交给下层对象自己完成，上层只调用接口而不碰内部细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delegation means handing an operation to a subordinate object to actually perform, while the caller only touches its interface.

optionExplanations: 两问法直接得出的形状：状态是楼层号和本层车位，方法是按类型查找和计数，ParkingLot 只需调用接口。
Floor 不持有 spots，找空位还是要靠 ParkingLot 扁平扫描全部车位，引入 Floor 这一层就没有意义。
出场校验属于编排者职责，票据也不该按楼层拆开存，这会让『查一张票』变成要先知道它在哪层。
少了 findAvailableSpot，ParkingLot 拿到计数后还是得自己遍历该层 spots，Floor 没有真正封装查找逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what the two-question method yields: state is floor number and spots, methods are find-by-type and count.
Without owning spots, Floor adds a layer that does nothing — ParkingLot still has to flat-scan every spot itself.
Exit validation belongs to the orchestrator, and splitting tickets by floor turns 'look up one ticket' into a per-floor search.
Without findAvailableSpot, ParkingLot still has to walk that floor's spots itself after getting the count — no real encapsulation.

scenario: 多层扩展后 spotId 变成 "3-A15" 这种带楼层信息的复合格式。
scenario_en: After the multi-floor extension, spotId becomes a composite like "3-A15" that embeds the floor.
q: 为什么 Ticket 类可以完全不加字段？
q_en: Why can the Ticket class stay unchanged with no new field?
options: spotId 隐式带上楼层，exit 仍按 spotId 查找释放，无需改 Ticket
楼层信息其实从不需要保留，多层扩展后旧的单层 spotId 编号方式继续沿用
Ticket 应该新增 floorNumber 字段，否则出场时无法定位车辆所在楼层
spotId 编码楼层后，Ticket 反而必须改成可变对象才能追加这个信息
why: spotId 从 "B" 变成 "3-A15" 就把楼层信息编码进已有字段，exit 查找逻辑不用改；Ticket 保持不可变、字段不增加。
why_en: Once spotId itself becomes "3-A15", floor information rides along in an existing field, so the exit lookup logic is unchanged and Ticket stays immutable with no new field.
tradeoff: 复合 spotId 隐式带楼层 vs Ticket 显式加 Floor 字段
options_en: spotId implicitly carries the floor, and exit still looks up and frees by spotId, so Ticket doesn't need to change.
Floor information is never actually needed, so the old single-floor spotId scheme just keeps being used unchanged.
Ticket should gain a floorNumber field, or exit can't locate which floor the vehicle is on.
Encoding the floor into spotId actually forces Ticket to become mutable to append that information.
optionExplanations: 字符串本身就是新的复合标识符，找车位、释放车位的逻辑照旧按 id 查找，不需要改 Ticket 的字段。
多层结构下 spot 本来就要按楼层区分身份，"B" 这种旧编号在 10 层车库里会撞号，站不住。
这是本设计选择不做的做法：只有需要在收据上直接展示楼层文字、不想解析字符串时才值得加。
spotId 只是构造时确定的一个字符串值，编码楼层信息不需要让 Ticket 本身变成可变对象。
optionExplanations_en: The string is itself the new composite identifier — lookup and release logic still works by id, no Ticket field needed.
In a multi-floor building, spots need floor-qualified identity or the old scheme like "B" collides across floors.
This is the alternative the design didn't take — only worth it if a receipt must show the floor as text without parsing.
spotId is just a string fixed at construction; encoding the floor into it doesn't require Ticket to become mutable.

scenario: 500 个车位分 5 层，高峰期低层排队而高层空着，你换成按可用车位数选楼层。
scenario_en: 500 spots across 5 floors, with lower floors congested and upper floors empty at peak, so you switch to picking the floor with the most availability.
q: 这段均衡分配伪代码比『第一个匹配楼层』多付出什么代价？
q_en: What extra cost does this balanced-allocation pseudocode pay compared to first-match?
codeSample:
findAvailableSpot(vehicleType)
    requiredType = mapVehicleTypeToSpotType(vehicleType)
    bestFloor = null
    maxAvailable = 0
    for floor in floors
        available = floor.getAvailableSpotCount(requiredType)
        if available > maxAvailable
            maxAvailable = available
            bestFloor = floor
    if bestFloor == null
        return null
    return bestFloor.findAvailableSpot(requiredType)
options: 每次入场都要扫一遍全部楼层求最大可用数，换来车位分布更均衡，避免单层拥堵
会漏掉某些楼层完全不参与遍历，换来的是入场处理速度更快
只查一次就直接返回第一层，换来的是完全没有均衡效果
把车位统计逻辑搬到了 ParkingSpot 内部，换来的是 Floor 类可以整个删掉
why: 每次入场要遍历所有楼层取最大可用数，比第一个匹配楼层多一轮 O(floors) 扫描；换来的是车流不再堆积在低楼层。
why_en: Every entry now scans all floors to find the maximum availability, an extra O(floors) pass compared to first-match — the payoff is traffic no longer piles up on the lower floors.
tradeoff: 先匹配即返回，最快但可能堵低楼层 vs 全楼层扫描选最优，稍慢但分布均衡
whenOtherWins: 楼层很少或车流本就稀疏时，第一个匹配楼层的简单遍历已经够用，不值得为均衡多付这轮扫描。
options_en: It scans every floor each entry to find the max availability, trading extra work for a more even spot distribution.
It skips some floors from the scan entirely, trading correctness for faster entry processing.
It checks once and returns the first floor, trading away any real balancing effect.
It moves spot counting into ParkingSpot itself, letting the Floor class be deleted entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算法开销随楼层数量线性增长；这里指每次入场都要遍历一遍全部楼层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(floors) means the cost grows linearly with the number of floors — here, every entry walks the full floor list.

optionExplanations: 代码里 for floor in floors 遍历了全部楼层再挑 maxAvailable，这一轮全量扫描就是换取均衡的代价。
代码没有跳过任何楼层，for 循环覆盖 floors 里的每一个元素，不存在漏扫描的情况。
代码明确记录 maxAvailable 并持续更新 bestFloor，不是找到第一个非空楼层就直接返回。
getAvailableSpotCount 仍在 ParkingFloor 上，代码没挪到 ParkingSpot，也没删 Floor 类。
optionExplanations_en: The for-loop walks every floor to track maxAvailable — that full scan is exactly the cost paid for balance.
The loop doesn't skip any floor; it iterates the whole floors list, so nothing is left out.
The code keeps updating maxAvailable and bestFloor, so it isn't just returning the first non-empty floor.
getAvailableSpotCount stays a ParkingFloor method here — the code neither moves it nor removes the Floor class.

scenario: 写 findAvailableSpot 时你想加一条『优先分配靠近入口的车位』的规则，但需求里没提过。
scenario_en: While writing findAvailableSpot, you're tempted to add a rule preferring spots near the entrance, even though requirements never mentioned it.
q: 这种情况下该怎么处理这条额外规则？
q_en: What should you do with this extra allocation rule?
options: 不主动实现，除非面试官提出或你先问一句是否需要
直接实现，展示的分配逻辑越复杂越能体现工程能力
把它写进 ParkingSpot 的构造函数参数里，默认对所有车位生效
跳过 findAvailableSpot 的实现，先把这条规则的设计文档写清楚
why: 需求没提的分配策略先不做，这是在往未被要求的地方烧时间；真要展示可以先问面试官是否要延伸讨论。
why_en: Don't build allocation logic nobody asked for — that burns time on unrequested features; if you want to show it, ask the interviewer whether they want that extension.
tradeoff: 先写需求内的简单线性扫描 vs 主动加需求外的分配优化
whenOtherWins: 面试官在扩展性环节主动问『如何做更聪明的分配』时，这才是展开 Strategy 模式或就近分配的时机。
options_en: Don't build it proactively — wait for the interviewer to ask, or ask them first whether it's needed.
Implement it right away; the more sophisticated the allocation logic looks, the more it signals skill.
Bake it into ParkingSpot's constructor arguments so it applies to every spot by default.
Skip implementing findAvailableSpot and write up the design for this rule first instead.
optionExplanations: 基础版只需匹配类型并按 O(n) 扫描找到第一个空位，额外偏好逻辑要等被要求才加。
复杂度不等于工程能力，未被要求的功能是在燃烧白板时间，反而显得没有把握好范围。
偏好逻辑是分配策略问题，不是车位固有属性，塞进 ParkingSpot 构造函数混淆了状态归属。
跳过核心方法的实现去写没被要求的文档，本末倒置，交付不出能跑的系统。
optionExplanations_en: The base version only needs to match type and scan for the first free spot; extra preference logic waits until asked.
Complexity isn't skill — building unrequested features burns whiteboard time and signals poor scoping.
Preference is an allocation-policy concern, not an intrinsic spot property; stuffing it into the constructor mixes up which class should hold that state.
Skipping the core method to document an unrequested rule is backwards — you'd have nothing working to show.

scenario: findAvailableSpot 在 enter 中找不到任何兼容空位。
scenario_en: findAvailableSpot finds no compatible free spot inside enter.
q: 此时 enter 应该先做什么？
q_en: What should enter do at this point?
options: 直接返回错误，不改动 occupiedSpotIds 或 activeTickets
先生成一张没有 spotId 的 ticket 占位，等真正有空位时再补上
把某个已经被别人占用的 spot 强制标记为空闲，让这次入场也侥幸成功
先把 occupiedSpotIds 加上一个占位 ID 记录，之后再决定要不要报错
why: 找不到空位就必须在改变任何状态之前返回错误，这样失败路径不会留下半成品的 ticket 或占用记录。
why_en: When no spot is found, enter must return the error before touching any state, so the failure path never leaves a half-written ticket or occupancy record.
tradeoff: 失败路径零副作用 vs 先分配再回滚更复杂但看似更灵活
whenOtherWins: 如果系统未来要支持排队等位，才需要在没有空位时也创建某种『等待中』记录，那已经不是这道题的基础需求。
options_en: Return the error immediately without touching occupiedSpotIds or activeTickets.
Issue a ticket with no spotId as a placeholder and fill it in once a spot opens up.
Force-mark some other vehicle's already-occupied spot as free so this entry can luck into succeeding.
Add a placeholder ID record to occupiedSpotIds first, then decide afterward whether to error.
optionExplanations: 两个索引在失败路径上完全不动，保证下一次入场看到的状态和这次失败前一致。
半成品 ticket 会让 activeTickets 里出现一张指不到真实车位的记录，出场时无法正确释放。
抢占别人车位是更严重的错误，会让原本合法占用的那辆车凭空丢失车位。
占位 ID 会让 occupiedSpotIds 出现一个不对应任何真实 spot 的假条目，污染后续的空位统计。
optionExplanations_en: Neither index moves on the failure path, so the next entry sees exactly the state it would have seen before this attempt.
A half-written ticket leaves an entry in activeTickets pointing at no real spot, so exit can never free it correctly.
Stealing another vehicle's spot is a worse bug — the car that legitimately holds it now has no spot at all.
A placeholder ID pollutes occupiedSpotIds with an entry that maps to no real spot, corrupting later availability checks.

q: 限流器基础设计的需求范围，哪些正确？
options: 配置只在系统启动时加载一次
请求只携带 clientId 和 endpoint 两个字符串
每个 endpoint 可以指定不同算法和参数
结果包含 allowed、remaining、retryAfterMs 三个字段
支持运行时动态更新已加载的配置
options_en: Configuration is loaded exactly once at startup.
A request carries only two strings: clientId and endpoint.
Each endpoint can specify its own algorithm and parameters.
The result has three fields: allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs.
The system supports hot-reloading configuration at runtime.
why: 基础设计把配置加载、请求输入、endpoint 策略和结构化结果先固定下来；运行时热更新会引入原子替换或保状态更新，不在这版范围内。
why_en: The base design fixes startup config, simple request keys, per-endpoint policies, and structured results; hot reload is out of scope.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识发起请求客户端的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clientId is the string that uniquely identifies the caller making a request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被限流的 API 路径标识，用作查配置的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: endpoint is the API path used as the lookup key for its rate-limit config.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求被拒绝时，建议客户端等待多少毫秒后重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: retryAfterMs tells a denied caller how many milliseconds to wait before retrying.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务不重启的情况下加载并应用新配置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot reload applies new configuration without restarting the service.

q_en: Which requirements are in scope for the base rate limiter design? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 启动时读一次配置就够，构造阶段可以直接创建好所有 limiter，不用为运行中 reload 铺路。
clientId 和 endpoint 这两个字符串就是查表和限流 key 的全部输入，不需要更复杂的请求对象。
algorithm 字段按 endpoint 区分，Factory 才能给不同 endpoint 建不同的 Limiter 实现。
allowed/remaining/retryAfterMs 一起返回，调用方才能设置响应头、显示剩余额度和重试提示。
热更新配置属于后续扩展题——基础版本里配置只在启动时加载，改这条会牵出原子替换或保状态更新的复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Startup-only config load means the constructor can create every limiter once, with no live-reload path to build for.
clientId and endpoint are the only two strings needed to look up a policy and key a limiter — nothing more elaborate.
The algorithm field varies per endpoint, so the factory builds a different Limiter for each one.
allowed, remaining, and retryAfterMs travel together so callers can set headers, show quota, or hint a retry.
Hot-reloading config is a later extension — the base design loads config once at startup, and adding this pulls in atomic swap or state-preserving update complexity.
scenario: 45 分钟白板题：单机 Java 进程内限流器，只做能跑通的最小版本，扩展项留到 follow-up。
scenario_en: A 45-minute whiteboard task: an in-process rate limiter for one Java service, minimum working version only, extensions deferred to follow-ups.

scenario: 请求只以 clientId 和 endpoint 两个字符串进入系统，处理后立即用于查 limiter 和 key。
scenario_en: Requests enter only as clientId and endpoint strings, then immediately route to a limiter and key.
q: Request/Client/Endpoint 应如何建模？
q_en: How should Request, Client, and Endpoint be modeled?
options: 都保持为输入字符串或 key，不建实体
三者都建成复杂类
Endpoint 继承 Limiter
Client 保存所有算法状态
options_en: Keep all three as plain input strings or lookup keys — no entity classes.
Turn all three into full-blown classes.
Make Endpoint inherit from Limiter.
Let Client hold all algorithm state.
why: 这些对象在系统内没有生命周期或行为。真正有状态的是具体 Limiter 的 per-key 记录。
why_en: Request, client, and endpoint are input keys, while limiter implementations own the rate-limit state.
whenOtherWins: 如果要管理客户端套餐、endpoint 元数据或请求上下文，才可能新增实体。
tradeoff: 建实体便于未来扩展 vs YAGNI 精简（无行为就不建类）

termDefinitions.meaning: “你不会需要它”，即不要为不存在的需求预先构建功能的设计原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for "you aren't gonna need it," meaning don't build for requirements that don't exist yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

optionExplanations: clientId/endpoint 没有行为也没有生命周期，直接当 map key 用就够，不用为它们建实体类。
假设每个名词都得有类，会造出三个没有行为的空壳类，违反 YAGNI。
把纯标签误当成算法子类型——Endpoint 和 Limiter 语义完全不同，继承在这里是误用。
把 per-key 算法状态错放进 Client，会让 Client 要感知每种算法的字段，职责被搞乱。
optionExplanations_en: clientId and endpoint have no behavior or lifecycle, so they stay plain lookup keys instead of becoming entity classes.
This assumes every noun needs a class, producing three empty shells that violate YAGNI.
This treats a plain label as an algorithm subtype — Endpoint and Limiter mean completely different things, so inheritance misuses it here.
This puts per-key algorithm state in Client, forcing it to know every algorithm's fields and blurring ownership.

q: 最终设计中的核心类型有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core types are in the final design? (Select all that apply.)
options: RateLimiter
Limiter interface
LimiterFactory
RateLimitResult
TokenBucketLimiter / SlidingWindowLogLimiter
Client 类持有该用户的完整请求历史
options_en: RateLimiter.
Limiter interface.
LimiterFactory.
RateLimitResult.
TokenBucketLimiter / SlidingWindowLogLimiter.
A Client class holds the user's full request history.
why: 编排、算法契约、创建、结果封装、具体实现各占一个类型；把用户的请求历史挂到 Client 上会放错状态所有者。
