why_en: A B-tree only helps prefix or reversed-suffix matches, so a pattern that can appear anywhere in the text forces a full scan of every row's content.
codeSample:
SELECT * FROM posts WHERE content LIKE '%database%';
-- B 树只能加速前缀匹配 'database%'，中缀匹配只能全表扫描
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Text"] --> B["Tokens"]
  B --> C["Inverted index"]
  C --> D["Posting lists"]
options_en: A B-tree only speeds up prefix or suffix matches; anything else forces a character scan.
The LIKE syntax itself forbids using an index.
B-trees do not support string types at all.
Because this query has no WHERE filter clause at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 里做模式匹配的操作符，如 LIKE '%database%'。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LIKE is the SQL operator for pattern matching, as in LIKE '%database%'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只匹配字符串开头部分的模式，如 'database%'。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prefix match is a pattern matching only the start of a string, like 'database%'.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 中用来过滤行的条件子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The WHERE clause is the SQL condition that filters rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: Why can a B-tree index not help a LIKE "%database%" query?
scenario_en: An articles table holds a million bodies with a B-tree on the body column, and the product searches for the word database anywhere inside them.
optionExplanations: 对，中缀匹配用不上 B 树的有序性，数据库只能把内容整篇读进来逐字符找，文本越多越慢。
LIKE 本身不禁止用索引——前缀匹配（如 'db%'）就能用上 B 树，只是中缀（%xx%）用不上。
B 树完全支持字符串类型的键，问题不在类型支持，而在中缀匹配破坏了有序性。
有没有 WHERE 子句跟索引能不能用得上无关，问题出在 LIKE 的匹配模式（前缀 vs 中缀）。
optionExplanations_en: Right — infix matching can't use a B-tree's sortedness at all, so it has to load the whole text and scan character by character.
LIKE itself doesn't ban index use — a prefix pattern like 'db%' can still use a B-tree; only an infix pattern (%xx%) can't.
A B-tree fully supports string-typed keys — the issue is infix matching destroys the sortedness a B-tree relies on, not type support.
Whether there's a WHERE clause has nothing to do with index usability — the real issue is LIKE's pattern, prefix versus infix.

scenario: 要支持全文搜索：给一个词，立刻拿到含它的文档列表，不能逐篇把正文读进内存。
q: 倒排索引「倒排」的是什么？
options: 把整棵 B 树结构从根到叶彻底颠倒过来重新存储一遍
把文本内容从头到尾整体做倒序编码处理
翻转文档与词的关系：从「文档→词」变成「词→文档列表」
把新写入的数据排列在旧数据的前面存放
why: 与其读每一页找「ACID」，不如在书后索引直接查「ACID」出现在哪些页。倒排索引存的就是 word → [doc1, doc3] 这样的映射。
why_en: An inverted index flips the relationship to store each word with the list of documents containing it, like the index at the back of a textbook.
options_en: Flip the entire B-tree structure upside down from root to leaf and store it all over again.
Reverse-encode the entire text content from end to start.
Flip the document-word relationship: from "document maps to words" to "word maps to a list of documents."
Place newly written data ahead of older data in storage order.
codeSample:
-- 倒排索引：词 -> 文档列表
b-trees  -> [doc1, doc3]
fast     -> [doc1, doc2]
handle   -> [doc3]
-- 查 "b-trees" 直接拿到 [doc1, doc3]，不必读全部文档

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

q_en: What is inverted in an inverted index?
scenario_en: You need full-text search: given one word, return the list of documents containing it immediately, without reading every body into memory.
optionExplanations: B 树是有序结构，不存在「整个倒过来存储」这种操作，跟倒排索引的「倒排」不是一回事。
倒排索引处理的是词与文档的映射关系，不是把文本内容整体倒序存储。
对，倒排索引把「文档→词」的关系翻转成「词→文档列表」，查一个词直接拿到它出现的文档，不用逐页翻找。
写入顺序跟倒排索引的「倒排」无关，那描述的是插入策略，不是索引存储的映射方向。
optionExplanations_en: A B-tree is an ordered structure — there's no such thing as flipping the whole structure over; that's not what "inverted" means here.
An inverted index deals with the mapping between words and documents, not reversing the order of the raw text.
Right — an inverted index flips "document maps to words" into "word maps to a list of documents," so a lookup goes straight to where it appears.
Write ordering has nothing to do with what "inverted" means here — that describes an insertion policy, not the mapping direction.

scenario: 用户搜「Databases」要能命中正文里的「database」「DATABASE」甚至「database's」。
q: Elasticsearch 这类系统索引文本前的分析管道包含哪些步骤？（多选）
options: 把文本切分成 token（词或子词）
统一转小写
去掉 "the"、"and" 等停用词，并常做词干化（还原词根）
给每个词单独建一棵 B 树
why: 分词、小写化、去停用词、词干化让搜 "Databases" 也能命中 "database"、"DATABASE" 甚至 "database's"——这正是全文搜索显得自然的原因。
why_en: Text is tokenized, lowercased, stripped of stop words, and often stemmed, which is why searching one form of a word matches its variants.
options_en: Split text into tokens (words or subwords).
Convert everything to lowercase.
Remove stop words like "the" and "and", and often apply stemming.
Build a separate B-tree for every single word.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的开源全文搜索与分析引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an open-source full-text search and analytics engine built on inverted indexes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文本切分后的最小单位，通常是一个词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit text is split into, usually a word.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把词还原成词根形式，如 running 还原成 run。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stemming reduces a word to its root form, like turning running into run.

termDefinitions.meaning: the、and 这类过于常见、通常从索引中剔除的词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stop word is a very common word, like the or and, typically stripped out before indexing.

q_en: Which steps are in the text analysis pipeline before Elasticsearch-style indexing? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: A search for Databases has to also hit database, DATABASE, and even database's in the body text.
optionExplanations: 对，分词把一段文本切成独立的词或子词单元，是整条分析管道的第一步。
对，统一小写让「Database」和「database」被当成同一个词处理，不会因大小写分裂成两个索引条目。
对，去停用词减少无意义索引项，词干化把 running/ran 还原成 run，让搜索更宽容。
错——倒排索引是一张词到文档列表的映射表，不是给每个词单独建一整棵 B 树。
optionExplanations_en: Right — tokenization splits a piece of text into individual word or subword units, the first stage of the pipeline.
Right — lowercasing means "Database" and "database" are treated as the same word, instead of splitting into two index entries.
Right — removing stop words cuts meaningless index entries, and stemming folds running/ran down to run, making search more forgiving.
Wrong — an inverted index is one mapping table from word to a list of documents, not a separate B-tree built per word.

scenario: 搜索框里用户手滑打成「databas」，系统仍要返回 database 相关的文档。
q: 用户打错字搜 "databas" 也能找到 "database" 相关文档，靠的是现代搜索系统的哪个特性？
options: 词频分析，统计词出现次数
模糊匹配，容忍拼写误差
短语查询，匹配精确词序
相关性评分，给结果排序
why: Elasticsearch/Lucene 在倒排索引之上叠了词频分析、相关性评分、模糊匹配、短语查询等功能；容错找近似词的是 fuzzy matching。
why_en: Fuzzy matching is the feature that finds close matches like a misspelled word, built on top of the inverted index alongside relevance scoring and phrase queries.
options_en: Term frequency analysis, counting how often a word appears.
Fuzzy matching, which tolerates spelling errors.
Phrase queries, matching an exact word sequence.
Relevance scoring, ranking the results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 容忍拼写误差、仍能找到相近词的搜索能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fuzzy matching finds close matches even when the search term is slightly misspelled.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个词在文档中出现的次数统计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Term frequency is a count of how many times a word appears in a document.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给搜索结果按匹配程度打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relevance scoring ranks search results by how well they match the query.

q_en: If a user searches for "databas" and still finds documents about "database", which modern search feature is doing that?
scenario_en: A user fat-fingers databas in the search box, and the system still has to return documents about database.
optionExplanations: 词频统计的是一个词出现多少次，用来算相关性分数，不负责容忍拼写错误。
对，模糊匹配专门用编辑距离一类算法容忍拼写误差，让「databas」也能匹配上「database」。
短语查询要求词序完全匹配，反而对拼写误差更敏感，不是它的作用。
相关性评分负责给已匹配的结果排序，不负责把拼错的词先匹配上。
optionExplanations_en: Term frequency counts how often a word appears, feeding relevance scoring — it doesn't handle spelling tolerance.
Right — fuzzy matching uses something like edit distance specifically to tolerate spelling errors, so "databas" can still match "database."
A phrase query requires exact word order, which makes it more sensitive to spelling errors, not less.
Relevance scoring ranks results that already matched — it doesn't help match a misspelled word in the first place.

scenario: 一个 CMS 每天改动 10 万篇文档、每篇几百个词，全都进了倒排索引。
q: 倒排索引的主要代价是什么？
options: 倒排索引目前在技术上被认为只能支持英文文本内容
查询延迟反而会比全表扫描还要变得更高
倒排索引完全没办法实现相关性排序功能
存储开销可观，文档一变更就要更新其含的每个词条
why: 一篇文档几百个词就对应几百个索引项，改动一次要同步更新所有相关词条，存储也不便宜。但为了让文本真正可搜索，这些代价值得付。
why_en: Inverted indexes need substantial storage and careful updating, since changing a document means updating the entry for every term it contains.
options_en: An inverted index is technically thought to only support English-language text.
Query latency actually ends up higher than a full table scan.
An inverted index supposedly can't implement relevance ranking at all.
Storage overhead is real, and one document edit means updating every word entry it contains.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

q_en: What is the main cost of an inverted index?
scenario_en: A CMS edits a hundred thousand documents a day, each a few hundred words, and all of them live in the inverted index.
optionExplanations: 现代倒排索引对语言无关，中文、日文等一样能分词建索引，不是只支持英文。
查询延迟恰恰是倒排索引要优化的目标，正常情况下比全表扫描快得多，不是更高。
相关性排序正是倒排索引叠加的常见能力（配合词频、TF-IDF 等），不是做不到。
对，一份文档动辄几百个词，等于几百条索引记录，编辑一次就要同步这些记录，存储和更新都不便宜。
optionExplanations_en: A modern inverted index isn't language-locked — Chinese, Japanese, and others can be tokenized and indexed too, not just English.
Query latency is exactly what an inverted index is built to optimize — normally much faster than a full scan, not higher.
Relevance ranking is a common capability layered on top of an inverted index, using term frequency or TF-IDF — not something it can't do.
Right — a document with a few hundred words means a few hundred index entries, and one edit means syncing all of them, a real storage and update cost.

scenario: 社交 feed 查询：WHERE user_id = 123 AND created_at > '2024-01-01' ORDER BY created_at DESC，这是最高频的查询。
q: 最优的索引方案是？
options: 分别在 user_id 和 created_at 上各建一个独立索引，查询时再合并结果
只在 created_at 一列上建索引，靠它过滤全部用户的数据
一个复合索引 (user_id, created_at)：一次遍历完成过滤和排序
只在 user_id 上建一个哈希索引，不管时间范围
why: 复合索引让数据库定位到 user 123 的第一条，然后顺序扫描到日期边界——条目在每个 user 内天然按 created_at 有序，过滤和排序一次拿到。
why_en: A composite index on user id and created at lets the database find the user's first entry and scan sequentially, getting both filtering and sorting for free.
whenOtherWins: 如果还存在大量「只按 created_at 过滤全表」的查询，这个复合索引帮不上（最左前缀限制），得为那类查询另建索引。
options_en: Build two independent single-column indexes on user_id and created_at, then merge the results at query time.
Index only created_at, and use it to filter across every user's rows.
One composite index (user_id, created_at): a single pass handles both filtering and sorting.
Build a hash index on user_id alone, ignoring the time range.
tradeoff: 单次有序遍历 vs 两次单列检索再求交集

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个列拼成一个键的单个 B 树索引，键先按第一列排序、再按后续列排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is a single B-tree index whose key concatenates multiple columns, sorted by the first column and then the rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 中按某列排序结果的子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ORDER BY is the SQL clause that sorts query results by a column.

q_en: What is the best index for this feed query?
scenario_en: A social feed repeatedly runs WHERE user_id = 123 AND created_at > '2024-01-01' ORDER BY created_at DESC; this is the hottest query.
optionExplanations: 两个独立索引各自只覆盖一个维度，查询时还要额外做交集运算，比复合索引多一步。
只按 created_at 建索引会让每次查询先扫全部用户的数据再按 user_id 过滤，白白多扫很多行。
对，复合索引把 user_id、created_at 压成一个二维有序序列，定位到该用户后顺着 created_at 顺序扫，过滤和排序一次搞定。
哈希索引只能做等值查找，扛不住 created_at 的范围过滤和排序需求。
optionExplanations_en: Two separate indexes each cover only one dimension, so the query still has to intersect them afterward — one more step than a composite index.
Indexing only created_at means every query first scans across all users' rows before filtering by user_id, scanning far more rows than needed.
Right — a composite index packs user_id and created_at into one sorted sequence; once it lands on the user, it scans forward in created_at order, one pass.
A hash index only supports equality lookups — it can't serve the range filter and sort that created_at needs here.

scenario: feed 查询是 WHERE user_id=? AND created_at>? ORDER BY created_at，表上只有两个单列索引。
q: 对上面的 feed 查询用两个单列索引（idx_user、idx_time），数据库要做哪些额外工作？
options: 两个索引各查一遍、结果集求交集、最后还要再排序
数据库会自动合并成一个复合索引
只用其中任意一个单列索引就等价于复合索引的效果
数据库会直接报错拒绝执行
why: 两个单列索引意味着两次大范围检索 + 交集 + 显式排序，比复合索引的单次有序遍历贵得多——这正是复合索引成为最常见优化的原因。
why_en: With two separate indexes the database must fetch both large result sets, intersect them, and then sort, instead of one ordered traversal of a composite index.
options_en: Query each index separately, intersect the two large result sets, and then sort them.
The database automatically merges them into a composite index.
Using just one of the single-column indexes is equivalent to a composite index.
The database simply throws an error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个列拼成一个键的单个 B 树索引，键先按第一列排序、再按后续列排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is a single B-tree index whose key concatenates multiple columns, sorted by the first column and then the rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分别用多个单列索引查询后再取结果集的交集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index intersection means querying multiple single-column indexes separately, then intersecting their result sets.

q_en: For the feed query above, what extra work does the database do with two single-column indexes?
scenario_en: The feed query filters on user_id and created_at and orders by created_at, and the table only has two single-column indexes.
optionExplanations: 对，两个单列索引各自扫一遍范围结果、再求交集、最后还要单独排序，比复合索引的单次有序遍历多好几步。
数据库不会自动把两个独立索引合并成一个复合索引，那是需要显式建的另一种索引。
单独用其中一个索引只能覆盖一个过滤条件，另一条件还是要逐行核对，效果达不到复合索引的水平。
两个单列索引是合法查询计划，数据库会执行、只是效率更低，不会直接报错拒绝。
optionExplanations_en: Right — two single-column indexes each get scanned for a range, then intersected, then still need an explicit sort — several more steps than a composite index.
A database doesn't automatically merge two independent indexes into a composite one — that's a separate index you'd have to create explicitly.
Using just one of the two indexes only covers one filter condition; the other still needs row-by-row checking.
Two single-column indexes make a valid, if slower, query plan — the database executes it, it doesn't error out and refuse.

scenario: 为 feed 查询建了复合索引 (user_id, created_at)，要看清它在 B 树里按什么顺序排。
q: 复合索引 (user_id, created_at) 在 B 树内部长什么样？
options: 会变成两棵完全独立的 B 树结构
键是两列元组，先按 user_id、组内再按 created_at 排序
一张哈希表里还嵌套着一棵 B 树
如果只按时间列排序，那就变成单列索引了，跟本题问的这种两列复合索引是两回事
why_en: Each B-tree key is effectively a tuple of both columns, sorted by user id first and then created at within each user, turning a 2D query into a 1D scan.
options_en: It becomes two completely independent B-tree structures.
Each key is a two-column tuple, sorted by user_id then created_at within each group.
A hash table with a B-tree nested inside it.
If it were sorted only by the time column, that would just be a single-column index — a different thing from the two-column composite index this question asks about.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个列拼成一个键的单个 B 树索引，键先按第一列排序、再按后续列排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is a single B-tree index whose key concatenates multiple columns, sorted by the first column and then the rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个值按固定顺序打包成一个整体的组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tuple bundles multiple values together in a fixed order.

q_en: What does the composite index (user_id, created_at) look like inside a B-tree?
scenario_en: You built the composite index (user_id, created_at) for the feed query and want to see what order it's laid out in inside the B-tree.
optionExplanations: 复合索引不是两棵独立的树，而是一棵树，键是两列拼成的元组，这正是它能一次搞定两个维度的原因。
对，键是 (user_id, created_at) 这样的元组，先按第一列排、组内再按第二列排，二维查询被压成一维有序扫描。
复合索引底层还是 B 树，不会额外嵌套一张哈希表；哈希和 B 树是两种不同的结构。
如果只按 created_at 排序，就成了单列索引，跟这里问的两列复合索引是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: A composite index isn't two separate trees — it's one tree whose key is the two columns combined into a tuple, which handles both dimensions in one pass.
Right — the key is a tuple like (user_id, created_at): sorted by the first column, then the second within each group, one ordered scan for a 2D query.
A composite index is still just a B-tree underneath — no hash table nested inside; hash and B-tree are different structures.
Sorting only by created_at would just be a single-column index, a different thing from the two-column composite index here.

scenario: 表上只有复合索引 (user_id, created_at)，现在来了个只按时间范围查全站的报表查询。
q: 复合索引 (user_id, created_at) 对「只按 created_at 过滤」的查询有帮助吗？
options: 有，任何用到这个索引里任意一列的查询都会自动被加速
有帮助，但速度只能提升大约一半左右
有没有帮助其实取决于这张表本身的大小
没有——B 树只服务列清单的前缀；跳过第一列就用不上
why: 这是最左前缀规则：索引按 user_id 优先排序，只查 created_at 时条目对它而言是乱序的。列的顺序至关重要。
why_en: No, because a B-tree composite index only serves prefixes of its column list, so skipping the leading user id column makes it useless.
options_en: Yes — any query touching any column in this index gets automatically sped up.
It helps, but only speeds things up by roughly half.
Whether it helps actually depends on how big the table itself is.
No — a B-tree only serves prefixes of its column list; skip the first column and it can't be used.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复合索引只能高效服务包含最左侧列的查询前缀，跳过第一列就用不上索引排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The leftmost-prefix rule means a composite index only helps queries that include its leading column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个列拼成一个键的单个 B 树索引，键先按第一列排序、再按后续列排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is a single B-tree index whose key concatenates multiple columns, sorted by the first column and then the rest.

q_en: Does the composite index (user_id, created_at) help a query that filters only by created_at?
scenario_en: The table only has the composite index (user_id, created_at), and now a reporting query filters site-wide by time range alone.
optionExplanations: 夸大了：复合索引只服务「从第一列开始」的查询前缀，不是任何包含索引列的查询都能沾光。
「快一半」是拍脑袋的估计——真实情况是完全用不上索引，要退化成扫描不含 user_id 过滤的那部分数据。
表大小只影响「用不上索引」这件事有多疼，不影响用不用得上——结构决定的事，不是数据量决定的。
对，最左前缀规则：跳过第一列 user_id，剩下的 created_at 在索引里其实是乱序的，帮不上忙。
optionExplanations_en: Overstated — a composite index only serves query prefixes starting from its first column, not any query that merely mentions an indexed column.
"About half as fast" is a made-up number — the real outcome is the index is unusable at all, degrading toward a scan without the user_id filter.
Table size only affects how painful it is that the index can't be used — whether it can be used is a structural fact, not a data-volume one.
Right — the leftmost-prefix rule: skipping user_id means the remaining created_at values are effectively unordered inside the index, so it can't help.

scenario: 要建复合索引：status 只有 3 个取值、user_id 上百万种，查询还总要 ORDER BY created_at。
q: 「复合索引列怎么排」的经验法则及其例外是？
options: 永远按字母表顺序把索引列排列，不用管查询模式
把数据类型占用字节数最长的列放在最前面
选择性最高的列在前；但常排序列纳入索引能省排序
顺序其实无所谓，查询优化器会自动帮你重新排列
why: 「most selective first」是常见口诀，但查询模式可以推翻它：频繁 ORDER BY 的列进索引能直接消掉排序操作。按真实查询设计而非教条。
why_en: The rule of thumb is most selective column first, but query patterns can trump selectivity, such as including a frequently sorted column to eliminate sort operations.
options_en: Always order index columns alphabetically, regardless of query pattern.
Put whichever column's data type takes the most bytes first.
Most selective column first; but a column frequently sorted on can be included to skip a sort step.
Order doesn't actually matter — the query optimizer automatically rearranges it for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一列里不同值的比例，值越独特选择性越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Selectivity is the proportion of distinct values in a column; more unique values means higher selectivity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个列拼成一个键的单个 B 树索引，键先按第一列排序、再按后续列排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is a single B-tree index whose key concatenates multiple columns, sorted by the first column and then the rest.

q_en: What is the rule of thumb for ordering composite-index columns, and what is the exception?
scenario_en: You're designing a composite index where status has three distinct values, user_id has millions, and the query always orders by created_at.
optionExplanations: 字母顺序完全跟查询模式无关，是拍脑袋的规则，不是真实经验法则。
字段类型长度和索引效率没有必然关系，决定顺序的应该是选择性和查询模式。
对，「选择性最高的列在前」是常见口诀，但如果某列经常出现在 ORDER BY 里，把它纳入索引能直接省掉一次排序，这个例外要看真实查询。
索引列的物理顺序是建索引时就固定的，优化器不会替你重排索引结构。
optionExplanations_en: Alphabetical order has nothing to do with query patterns — an arbitrary rule, not a real heuristic.
A column's data-type byte length has no real bearing on index efficiency — selectivity and query pattern should decide order.
Right — "most selective column first" is the common rule of thumb, but a column frequently in ORDER BY can skip a sort step if included — depends on the real query.
The physical order of index columns is fixed at creation time — the optimizer doesn't rearrange that structure for you.

q: 补全面试常见的复合索引设计：
text: 订单历史查询：({{customer_id}}, order_date)；事件处理：(status, {{priority}}, created_at)；活动流：({{user_id}}, type, timestamp)。
why: 三个经典模板都遵循同一套路：先按「谁/什么状态」定位，再按时间或优先级有序扫描——过滤列在前、排序列在后。
why_en: Classic composite indexes pair an identifying column like customer id, status, or user id with ordering columns like date, priority, or timestamp.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个列拼成一个键的单个 B 树索引，键先按第一列排序、再按后续列排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is a single B-tree index whose key concatenates multiple columns, sorted by the first column and then the rest.

q_en: Fill in common composite-index designs for interviews:

scenario: feed 查询只取 user_id、created_at、likes 三列，但每条命中都要回主表读一次数据页。
q: 什么是覆盖索引（covering index）？
options: 把查询需要的列都放进索引，跳过回表直接返回
覆盖整张表所有列的一个索引
一种号称能自动覆盖所有查询模式的万能智能索引
只是主键索引的另一个别名
why: 如 (user_id, created_at) INCLUDE (likes)：feed 要显示点赞数时不必再逐条回表读数据页，索引本身就答完了查询——对只取少数列的高频查询特别猛。
why_en: A covering index includes every column the query needs, so the database answers purely from the index and skips the expensive table-page lookups.
options_en: It includes every column the query needs, skipping the table lookup entirely.
An index covering every column of the whole table.
A supposedly all-purpose smart index that automatically covers every query pattern.
Just another name for the primary key index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引命中后还要去主表数据页取出索引未包含的列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A table lookup, or heap fetch, is the extra step of visiting the main table page for columns the index doesn't include.

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 里给索引附加非键列的语法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCLUDE is PostgreSQL syntax for attaching non-key columns to an index.

q_en: What is a covering index?
scenario_en: The feed query needs only user_id, created_at, and likes, yet every match still costs a trip back to the main table's data page.
optionExplanations: 对，把查询要用的列直接塞进索引（比如再包一个 likes 字段），数据就能直接从索引返回，不用再回表读数据页。
覆盖整表所有列既没必要也不现实，覆盖索引只包含某个查询实际需要的那几列。
没有「自动覆盖所有查询」的智能索引，覆盖索引是针对某个具体查询模式手动设计出来的。
覆盖索引是普通索引的一种设计方式（把用到的列都放进去），不是主键索引的别名。
optionExplanations_en: Right — pack the columns a query needs straight into the index (say, tucking in a likes column too), so it returns from the index alone, no table lookup needed.
Covering every column in the whole table is neither necessary nor practical — a covering index only holds the columns one query actually needs.
There's no such thing as a smart index that automatically covers every query — a covering index is deliberately designed for one query pattern.
A covering index is a design choice for a regular index (including the columns a query needs), not another name for the primary-key index.

scenario: 一张读密集的表已有普通索引，有人提议把所有热查询都改成覆盖索引。
q: 2026 年的现实里，覆盖索引该怎么定位？
options: 所有读查询都该用的默认方案
偏小众优化：普通索引已高效，覆盖索引更贵
已被数据库厂商移除的过时特性
覆盖索引只适用于 NoSQL 数据库
why: 覆盖索引在特定场景（读密集、列少的表）收益显著，但存储和维护成本是真的。现代查询优化器已经很聪明，面试建议优先讲简单索引策略。
why_en: Covering indexes are now a niche optimization with real maintenance and storage costs, so favor simpler strategies unless you have a strong specific reason.
options_en: The default choice for every read query.
A niche optimization: regular indexes already do well, and covering indexes cost more.
A deprecated feature removed by database vendors.
It only applies to NoSQL databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库里决定如何执行一条查询的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query optimizer is the database component that decides how to execute a query.

q_en: How should you position covering indexes in real systems in 2026?
scenario_en: A read-heavy table already has ordinary indexes, and someone proposes converting every hot query over to covering indexes.
optionExplanations: 覆盖索引不是所有读查询的默认方案——它有真实的存储和维护成本，得挑读密集、列少的场景用。
对，覆盖索引在读密集、列少的表上收益明显，但存储和维护是真代价，属于偏小众的优化手段。
覆盖索引没有被厂商移除，主流数据库（Postgres、MySQL）现在都还支持这个特性。
覆盖索引不是 NoSQL 专属概念，关系型数据库的索引 INCLUDE 列同样是覆盖索引的实现。
optionExplanations_en: A covering index isn't the default for every read query — it has real storage and upkeep costs, so it's reserved for read-heavy, narrow tables.
Right — a covering index pays off clearly on read-heavy, narrow tables, but storage and maintenance are real costs, a fairly niche optimization.
Covering indexes haven't been removed by any vendor — mainstream databases like Postgres and MySQL still support the feature today.
A covering index isn't a NoSQL-only idea — a relational index's INCLUDE columns are exactly the same covering-index technique.

scenario: 面试被问「这个场景该用什么类型的索引」，需要一句话给出通用决策规则。
q: 正确的默认决策流是？
options: 永远回答哈希索引最快，闭眼选它
遇到就先去问公司的 DBA
不管什么场景都上 Elasticsearch
默认 B 树；例外：邻近用地理索引，全文用倒排
why: 拿不准就 B 树（等值+范围通吃、各数据库的默认）；空间数据换 geohash 系空间索引，大规模文本搜索换倒排索引。这三板斧覆盖绝大多数索引问题。
why_en: Default to B-trees, switch to a geospatial index like geohash for lat-lng proximity, and use an inverted index for full-text search.
whenOtherWins: 极端写入摄入（指标、日志、IoT）时再引入 LSM 存储引擎的讨论；纯内存等值查找才轮到哈希结构。
options_en: Always answer hash index because it's fastest, no matter what.
Whenever asked, go ask the DBA first.
Reach for Elasticsearch no matter the scenario.
Default to B-trees; exceptions are geospatial for proximity and inverted for full text.
tradeoff: 通用默认覆盖大多数场景 vs 特化索引服务少数场景

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库管理员，负责数据库运维和优化的角色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DBA stands for Database Administrator, the role responsible for operating and tuning databases.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: What is the right default decision flow for choosing an index type?
scenario_en: In an interview, you are asked which index type fits a scenario and need a one-sentence general decision rule.
optionExplanations: 把哈希索引当默认答案风险很高——一旦场景需要范围查询或排序，这个答案立刻站不住。
面试现场没有 DBA 可问，面试官想看的是你自己能不能推出一个合理默认，不是回避决策。
Elasticsearch 是为全文搜索定制的重型方案，普通等值/范围查询场景直接上它是杀鸡用牛刀。
对，拿不准先默认 B 树；邻近查询换地理空间索引，全文检索换倒排索引，这三板斧覆盖了大多数场景。
optionExplanations_en: Treating a hash index as the default answer is risky — the moment the scenario needs range queries or sorting, that answer falls apart.
There's no DBA to ask in an interview — the interviewer wants to see you reason your way to a sensible default yourself, not dodge the decision.
Elasticsearch is a heavyweight tool purpose-built for full-text search — reaching for it on an ordinary equality/range query is overkill.
Right — default to B-tree when unsure; swap to a geospatial index for proximity queries and an inverted index for full-text search.

scenario: DynamoDB 聊天表按 user_id 分区，最常见的查询是「查某个用户在某时间段内的消息」，需要按时间区间取。
scenario_en: A DynamoDB chat table is partitioned by user_id, and the hottest query is 'a given user's messages in a time window', needing a time range.
q: 怎么建模才能让「单用户 + 时间区间」这类查询走连续扫描？
q_en: How do you model the table so a single-user time-range query becomes a contiguous scan?
options: 把 timestamp 设为该表的 sort key，让分区内 item 有序
另建一个只以 timestamp 为键的 GSI，靠它做时间区间扫描
依赖底层 B 树索引，直接对 timestamp 列做范围扫描
用 Scan 把整个分区读出来，再用 FilterExpression 过滤掉区间外的项
options_en: Make timestamp the table's sort key so items within the partition are stored in order.
Build a separate GSI keyed only on timestamp and use it for the time-range scan.
Rely on the underlying B-tree index to range-scan the timestamp column directly.
Use Scan to read the whole partition, then FilterExpression to drop items outside the window.
why: 同分区内 item 按 sort key 有序存放，所以「固定 partition key + sort key 区间」是一次连续读，代价接近顺序扫描。代价：这份有序只在单个 partition key 内成立。
why_en: DynamoDB keeps items within a partition ordered by sort key, so a fixed partition key plus a sort-key range is one contiguous read, close to a sequential scan in cost. The catch: that ordering only holds inside a single partition key.
whenOtherWins: 当查询不带 user_id、要跨所有用户按时间全局排序或取区间时，分区内 sort key 帮不上，得建一个以 time 为分区/排序键的 GSI。
tradeoff: 分区内 sort-key 区间（单分区有序、最省）vs GSI（跨分区但另建结构）vs Scan（全读再过滤）

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 复合主键的第二部分；同一 partition key 下的 item 按 sort key 有序存放，因此支持分区内区间查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sort key is the second part of a DynamoDB composite primary key; items under one partition key are stored in sort-key order, enabling in-partition range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复合主键的第一部分，决定 item 落在哪个物理分区；有序区间查询只在同一个 partition key 内成立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the first part of the primary key and decides which physical partition an item lands in; ordered range queries only hold within one partition key.

termDefinitions.fullName: Global Secondary Index（全局二级索引）
termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 用另一套键（可跨分区）重新组织数据的附加索引，供主键之外的查询模式使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is an extra DynamoDB index that reorganizes data under a different key, possibly across partitions, for query patterns beyond the primary key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 追加写、后台合并的存储结构；DynamoDB 被普遍认为用 LSM 式底座而非 B 树，因此没有用户可范围扫描的 B 树索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is an append-and-merge storage structure; DynamoDB is widely understood to use an LSM-style engine rather than B-trees, so there is no user-facing B-tree to range-scan.

termDefinitions.meaning: Scan 读遍整张表或整个分区，FilterExpression 只在读完之后丢弃不匹配项——不减少读取量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scan reads the whole table or partition, and FilterExpression only discards non-matching items after reading — it does not reduce how much is read.

optionExplanations: 对，这正是把 timestamp 放进 sort key 的目的：同一 user_id 下的时间区间落成一段相邻磁盘读，而非逐条随机点查。
以 timestamp 为键的 GSI 是把数据跨分区重排，适合「跨用户按时间查」，但对「单用户区间」是绕远路。
DynamoDB 被普遍认为用 LSM 式底座、不是 B 树，没有可供用户对 timestamp 做范围扫描的 B 树索引。
Scan 会把整个分区都读出来再过滤，读取量不随区间收窄——正是 sort key 有序想避免的浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Right — items sit in sort-key order within the partition, so a fixed user_id plus a timestamp range is one contiguous read.
A GSI keyed on timestamp reorders data across partitions, good for 'time across all users' but a detour for a single user's range.
DynamoDB is understood to use an LSM-style engine, not B-trees, so there's no user B-tree to range-scan on timestamp.
Scan reads the entire partition then filters, so the read volume doesn't shrink with the window — the waste sort-key ordering avoids.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 用四叉树（把二维空间递归四等分的树）做「找我附近 1 公里的餐厅」，你已经下钻到自己所在的叶象限。
scenario_en: Using a quadtree (a tree that recursively quarters 2D space) for 'restaurants within 1 km of me', you've drilled down to your own leaf quadrant.
q: 为什么只返回这个叶象限里的点会漏掉最近的餐厅？
q_en: Why does returning only the points inside this leaf quadrant miss the nearest restaurant?
options: 最近的点可能就贴在象限边界另一侧的相邻象限里
本象限里的点没有按到我的距离排好序，结果顺序是乱的
四叉树不平衡，我所在的这个叶象限有可能恰好是空的
象限用 geohash 字符串编号，前缀比较有时会把邻居判成远点
options_en: The nearest point may sit just across the boundary in an adjacent quadrant.
Points in this quadrant aren't sorted by distance to me, so the order is scrambled.
A quadtree is unbalanced, so my leaf quadrant might happen to be empty.
Quadrants are labeled by geohash strings, and prefix comparison sometimes misjudges neighbors as far.
why: 下钻只覆盖了一块方格，真正的最近邻可能落在紧贴边界的相邻象限。所以邻近查询要走完整链：定位目标象限 → 检查同层相邻象限 → 按搜索半径上钻覆盖更大范围或下钻更精细。代价：一次邻近查询要触碰多个象限节点，不是单点查找。
why_en: Drilling down only covers one cell, but the true nearest neighbor can fall in an adjacent quadrant hugging the boundary. So a proximity search runs the full loop: find the target quadrant, check same-level neighbors, then move up or down levels by the search radius. The cost: one query touches several quadrant nodes, not a single lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维空间递归四等分成象限的树；点太密就继续四分，稀疏区保留大格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree is a tree that recursively splits 2D space into four quadrants; dense areas keep subdividing while sparse areas keep large cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 四叉树一次四等分得到的一块方格区域，对应树里的一个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadrant is one of the four cells produced by a quadtree split, corresponding to one node in the tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 找「距某点半径内的所有对象」的查询；在四叉树里需要跨相邻象限、按半径调层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proximity search finds all objects within a radius of a point; in a quadtree it must cross neighboring quadrants and adjust levels by radius.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维坐标编码成保留邻近性的字符串（另一种空间索引路线），靠前缀匹配做邻近查询——不是四叉树的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash encodes 2D coordinates into a proximity-preserving string (a different spatial-index path) and uses prefix matching, not the quadtree's mechanism.

optionExplanations: 对，边界是人为切的，最近邻可能就在隔壁象限，所以必须再查同层相邻象限并按半径调层。
排序不是问题——问题是完整性：漏了相邻象限里更近的点，排不排序都补不回来。
四叉树按点密度自适应细分，空象限不是漏点的原因；漏点来自没查边界外的邻居。
把坐标编成前缀字符串是 geohash 的做法；四叉树直接切分空间、用树导航，不靠前缀比较。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the boundary is arbitrary, the nearest neighbor may be next door, so you must also check same-level neighbors and adjust levels by radius.
Ordering isn't the issue — completeness is: a closer point in an adjacent quadrant is missed whether or not you sort.
A quadtree subdivides adaptively by point density; an empty quadrant isn't why points are missed — skipping boundary neighbors is.
Encoding coordinates into prefix strings is geohash's approach; a quadtree partitions space directly and navigates the tree, not by prefixes.

scenario: 线上一个查询突然变慢，表上已经有几个索引，团队不确定到底该给哪列再加索引。
scenario_en: A production query suddenly got slow; the table already has a few indexes, and the team isn't sure which column to index next.
q: 定位「该加什么索引」的第一步应该是什么？
q_en: What should the first step be to figure out which index to add?
options: 跑 EXPLAIN 看查询计划，确认它卡在哪个谓词、有没有 seq scan
给 WHERE 子句里出现的每一列都单独建一个索引，用数量硬覆盖所有过滤组合
按表的行数决定：行多就加索引，行少就先不加
直接把表迁到写入更快的 LSM 引擎上
options_en: Run EXPLAIN to read the query plan and see which predicate it stalls on and whether it's doing a seq scan.
Add an index to every column that appears in the WHERE clause to cover all possibilities.
Decide by row count: index if the table is big, skip it if the table is small.
Migrate the table onto an LSM engine that writes faster.
why: 索引不是免费的——每建一个都加写放大和存储，盲目加还可能既不命中慢查询又拖慢写入。先用 EXPLAIN/查询计划加数据库指标找到真正的瓶颈谓词，再针对性建索引。代价：多一步诊断，换来不建无效索引。
why_en: Indexes aren't free — each one adds write amplification and storage, and blind ones may miss the slow query while slowing writes. First use EXPLAIN plus database metrics to find the real bottleneck predicate, then index for it. The cost: one extra diagnosis step, in exchange for not building dead indexes.
whenOtherWins: 当查询模式一开始就明确（例如登录永远按 email 精确匹配），建表时直接把索引建好即可，不必先跑 EXPLAIN 诊断。
tradeoff: 先诊断后建索引（多一步、只加有用的）vs 盲目全列建索引（省诊断、堆写入成本）

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库命令，打印某条查询的执行计划——它打算用哪些索引、要不要全表扫描、各步预估代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXPLAIN is a database command that prints a query's execution plan — which indexes it will use, whether it will scan the whole table, and the estimated cost of each step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库为一条查询选定的执行方案（用哪个索引、按什么顺序连接、扫描方式），是判断瓶颈的入口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query plan is the execution strategy the database picks for a query — which index, join order, and scan method — and is the entry point for spotting bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Sequential scan，数据库逐行读遍整张表；查询计划里出现它往往意味着某个谓词缺可用索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A seq (sequential) scan reads every row of the table in order; seeing it in a plan often means a predicate lacks a usable index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询里的过滤条件（如 WHERE user_id=123）；诊断的目标是找出哪个谓词没走索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A predicate is a filter condition in a query (like WHERE user_id=123); diagnosis aims to find which predicate isn't using an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写入被放大成多次物理写：每多一个索引，插入/更新就要多改一份结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is one logical write turning into several physical writes: each extra index means an insert or update must modify one more structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向高写入的追加写存储结构；换引擎解决的是写吞吐，不是「哪列该建索引」的读诊断问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is an append-oriented storage structure for high write throughput; switching engines addresses write throughput, not the read-side question of which column to index.

optionExplanations: 对，先看查询计划才知道慢在哪个谓词、是不是在做 seq scan，再据此选列建索引最省。
给每列都建索引会堆高写放大和存储，还可能建了一堆没命中慢查询的死索引。
行数只是粗略信号——真正决定要不要索引的是访问模式，光看大小会误判。
换 LSM 引擎解决的是写吞吐，和「哪个读谓词缺索引」是两根轴，跑偏了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — read the plan first to see which predicate is slow and whether it's a seq scan, then index that column.
Indexing every column piles on write amplification and storage, and may create dead indexes that never hit the slow query.
Row count is only a rough signal — access pattern decides whether an index helps; size alone misleads.
Switching to LSM addresses write throughput, a different axis from which read predicate lacks an index.

scenario: 你要给一个日活千万的 Web 应用写请求代码，工期两周，不可能自己实现丢包重传。
scenario_en: You have two weeks to ship request code for a web app with ten million daily users, so reimplementing packet retransmission yourself is off the table.
q: 网络分层（OSI 模型）对应用开发者的根本意义是什么？
q_en: What is the core value of network layering, or the OSI model, for application developers?
options: 规定了所有协议的字节格式
分层是抽象：只需和下一层打交道
让网络传输更快
强制所有系统用 7 层协议
why: 分层就是抽象——像用语言里的 open 而不是手动指挥磁盘读字节。请求网页时你不需要懂物理层，只要会用下一层即可。
why_en: Network layers are abstractions that let developers reason about communication at their own level without knowing how lower layers move the bits.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["应用层 L7"] --> B["传输层 L4"]
    B --> C["网络层 L3"]
    C --> D["更底层细节"]
    A -.只依赖下一层.-> B
options_en: It dictates the exact byte format every protocol must use.
Layering is an abstraction — you deal only with the layer below you.
It makes network transmission inherently faster.
It forces every system to implement all seven OSI layers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把网络通信拆成 7 层的参考模型，每层只依赖它下面那一层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OSI is the reference model that splits network communication into seven layers, each depending only on the layer below it.

optionExplanations: 分层从没规定过字节格式，那是具体协议自己的事，分层只是把复杂度切开。
分层的价值就是抽象——你只需要弄懂和你相邻的下一层，不用管物理层怎么搬比特。
分层不会让传输本身变快，它换来的是可维护性和职责隔离，不是性能。
没有系统被强制走满 7 层，很多实现会跳过或合并某些层。
optionExplanations_en: layering never dictates byte formats; that's each protocol's own job, layering just splits up complexity.
layering's value is abstraction — you only need the layer right below you, not how bits move on the wire.
layering doesn't speed up transmission itself; it buys maintainability, not performance.
no system is forced to implement all seven layers; real stacks skip or merge layers freely.

q: 补全面试最常涉及的三个网络层：
q_en: Fill in the three network layers that come up most often in interviews.
text: 第 3 层网络层：{{IP}}，负责路由与寻址；第 4 层传输层：{{TCP}}、UDP、QUIC，提供端到端通信；第 7 层应用层：DNS、{{HTTP}}、WebSocket、WebRTC。
why: 面试聚焦三层：L3 管「送到哪台机器」，L4 管「可靠性/顺序等端到端保证」，L7 是开发者天天用的应用协议。
why_en: Interviews focus on layer three with IP for routing, layer four with TCP and UDP for end-to-end guarantees, and layer seven application protocols like HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上提供持久、双向通信的协议，通过 HTTP upgrade 建立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent, bidirectional channel over one TCP connection, established via an HTTP upgrade.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

scenario: 排查跨机房服务调用：包都到了但顺序全乱，你要定位这属于哪一层该管的事。
scenario_en: You're debugging cross-datacenter service calls where every packet arrives but the order is scrambled, and you need to know which layer owns that.
q: 网络层（L3）的 IP 协议负责什么？
q_en: What is IP responsible for at the network layer, or L3?
options: 保证数据按序到达
加密通信内容
把数据切成包并尽力而为投递
维护客户端与服务器的会话
why: IP 只管路由和寻址：切包、转发、尽力送达——不保证可靠或有序，那是 L4 的事。ML 训练场景还会见到 InfiniBand，但面试以 IP 为主。
why_en: IP handles routing and addressing by breaking data into packets and forwarding them with best-effort delivery to any destination address.
options_en: It guarantees packets arrive in order.
It encrypts the contents of the communication.
It breaks data into packets and delivers them best-effort.
It maintains session state between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里负责路由和寻址的网络层，主角是 IP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 3, the network layer, handles routing and addressing and is dominated by IP.

optionExplanations: 按序到达是 L4（TCP）的职责，IP 本身不做排序或重传保证。
加密属于更上层（如 TLS），IP 只负责路由寻址，不碰内容加解密。
IP 的职责就是把数据切片打包、尽力路由投递，可靠性和顺序留给上层去做。
会话状态由应用层或传输层维护，IP 是无状态的逐包转发。
optionExplanations_en: ordered delivery is TCP's job at L4 — IP makes no ordering or retransmission promise.
encryption belongs to a higher layer like TLS; IP only routes and addresses, never touches content.
IP's job is chopping data into packets and best-effort routing them, leaving reliability to the layer above.
session state is tracked by transport or application layers, not by stateless, per-packet IP.

scenario: 你的服务直接基于 IP 收发，拿到的是一堆乱序、可能重复的包，要决定补哪一层。
scenario_en: Your service talks straight over IP and gets back an unordered, possibly duplicated pile of packets, so you have to decide which layer to add.
q: 传输层（L4）在网络层之上补充了什么？
q_en: What does the transport layer, or L4, add on top of the network layer?
options: 端到端通信服务：可靠性、有序性等特性
域名解析：把主机名翻译成目标 IP 地址
HTML 页面渲染引擎
物理层的信号调制与编码
why: L3 只把包尽力扔到目的地；TCP/QUIC/UDP 这层决定要不要在其上提供可靠、有序、流控等保证——否则你拿到的就是一堆乱序的包。
why_en: The transport layer adds end-to-end services like reliability, ordering, and flow control on top of the network layer's raw packet delivery.
options_en: End-to-end services like reliability and ordering.
Resolving a hostname into a destination IP address.
The browser's HTML rendering engine.
Modulating and encoding the physical-layer signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里提供端到端保证（可靠性、顺序、流控）的传输层，主角是 TCP/UDP/QUIC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

optionExplanations: 传输层在 L3 之上加了端到端保证——要不要可靠、要不要保序，由 TCP/UDP/QUIC 决定。
域名解析是 DNS 在应用层做的事，跟传输层没关系。
HTML 渲染发生在浏览器的应用层，传输层根本看不到内容格式。
物理信号调制属于物理层（L1），传输层只处理逻辑上的字节流。
optionExplanations_en: the transport layer adds end-to-end guarantees above L3 — TCP, UDP, or QUIC decide reliability and ordering.
domain resolution is DNS's job at the application layer, unrelated to transport.
HTML rendering happens in the browser's application layer; transport never sees content format.
signal modulation belongs to the physical layer (L1); transport only handles logical byte streams.

scenario: 设计一个浏览器聊天应用，你只在应用层选协议，传输可靠性交给下面的 TCP/UDP。
scenario_en: You're designing a browser chat app and only pick protocols at the application layer, leaving transport reliability to TCP or UDP underneath.
q: 以下哪组全是应用层（L7）协议？
q_en: Which group contains only application-layer, or L7, protocols?
options: IP、InfiniBand（网络层）
TCP、UDP、QUIC（传输层）
SYN、ACK、FIN、RST（TCP 报文标志位）
DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC
why: 应用层协议构建在 TCP（或 WebRTC 的 UDP）之上，为 Web 应用的各类数据提供抽象。SYN/ACK/FIN 只是 TCP 的报文标志，不是协议。
why_en: DNS, HTTP, WebSockets, and WebRTC are application-layer protocols built on top of TCP or, in WebRTC's case, UDP.
options_en: IP and InfiniBand (network layer).
TCP, UDP, and QUIC (transport layer).
SYN, ACK, FIN, and RST (TCP segment flag bits).
DNS, HTTP, WebSocket, and WebRTC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层的高速互联协议，常用于大规模机器学习训练集群，不是面试常考的重点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InfiniBand is a high-speed network-layer interconnect mostly seen in large machine-learning training clusters, rarely the interview's focus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 报文里的控制标志位，分别用于发起连接、确认收到、结束连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SYN, ACK, and FIN are TCP control flags used to open a connection, acknowledge receipt, and close a connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上提供持久、双向通信的协议，通过 HTTP upgrade 建立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent, bidirectional channel over one TCP connection, established via an HTTP upgrade.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

optionExplanations: IP 和 InfiniBand 都是网络层/更底层的东西，不是应用层协议。
TCP、UDP、QUIC 是传输层协议，应用层协议是建在它们之上的。
SYN、ACK、FIN、RST 都是 TCP 报文的标志位，本身并不构成一种独立协议。
DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC 都跑在传输层之上，为具体应用场景提供数据抽象。
optionExplanations_en: IP and InfiniBand sit at the network layer or below, not the application layer.
TCP, UDP, QUIC are transport protocols — application protocols are built on top of them.
SYN/ACK/FIN/RST are just flag bits inside a TCP segment, not protocols at all.
DNS, HTTP, WebSocket, and WebRTC all run above transport, giving each app its own data abstraction.

q: 把「浏览器输入 URL 到拿到网页」的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the browser-to-webpage request flow in the correct order.
steps: TCP 三次握手建立连接
DNS 把域名解析成 IP 地址
服务器处理请求并准备响应
客户端发送 HTTP GET 请求
TCP 四次挥手关闭连接
服务器发回 HTTP 响应
why: DNS 解析 → TCP 握手 → 发请求 → 服务器处理（多数工程师唯一控制的延迟）→ 回响应 → 挥手断开。一次「简单」请求背后是多轮包交换，层层都有延迟。
why_en: A web request resolves DNS, performs the TCP handshake, sends the HTTP request, waits for server processing, receives the response, and tears the connection down.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant D as DNS
    participant S as 服务器
    C->>D: 域名解析
    D-->>C: IP 地址
    C->>S: SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK（三次握手）
    C->>S: HTTP GET
    S-->>C: HTTP 响应
    C->>S: FIN / ACK / FIN / ACK（四次挥手）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

q: 补全 TCP 三次握手：
q_en: Complete the TCP three-way handshake.
text: 客户端发 {{SYN}} 请求连接；服务器回 {{SYN-ACK}} 确认请求；客户端再发 {{ACK}} 完成连接建立。断开则用 FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK 四次挥手。
why: 三次握手建立、四次挥手拆除——每个不复用连接的请求都要重复这套流程，这是后面讨论持久连接和负载均衡的伏笔。
why_en: TCP opens with a SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake and closes with a four-way FIN and ACK exchange.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: SYN
    S-->>C: SYN-ACK
    C->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 连接已建立

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 报文里的控制标志位，分别用于发起连接、确认收到、结束连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SYN, ACK, and FIN are TCP control flags used to open a connection, acknowledge receipt, and close a connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

scenario: 一个 API 网关每秒处理 5 万次短请求，你想把每请求的连接建立开销压下来。
scenario_en: An API gateway handles fifty thousand short requests per second, and you want to cut the per-request connection setup cost.
q: TCP 连接是客户端和服务器都要维护的状态：这一事实带来什么设计影响？
q_en: What design consequence follows from TCP connection state living on both client and server?
options: 连接一旦建立就永远免费
连接状态只由服务器端维护，客户端无需保存
不用 keep-alive 就要重建连接
TCP 连接不占用任何资源
why: 连接即状态，双方都要维护；不复用就得每请求重建，开销可观。设计实时更新类系统（持久连接）时这一点会反复出现。
why_en: Because a connection is state both sides maintain, every request repeats the costly setup unless you use keep-alive or multiplexing, which matters for realtime systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["请求 1"] --> B["建连"]
    B --> C["响应"]
    C --> D["断开"]
    D --> E["请求 2 再建连"]
    C -.keep-alive.-> F["复用连接"]
options_en: Once established, a connection is free forever.
The connection state is kept only on the server, and the client stores nothing.
Without keep-alive you rebuild the connection every time.
A TCP connection consumes no resources at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一条 TCP 连接被多个 HTTP 请求复用，省去重复握手的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP keep-alive lets one TCP connection serve multiple HTTP requests, avoiding repeated handshake overhead.

optionExplanations: 维护连接本身要占内存和文件描述符，从来不是免费的，只是分摊到了每次请求。
TCP 是双方对等维护状态，客户端和服务器都要记住序号、窗口，不是只有服务器。
连接状态双方都要维护，不复用连接（没有 keep-alive）就得每次请求重新握手，开销明显。
每条 TCP 连接都占用服务器内存和文件描述符，大量并发连接会实实在在压垮资源。
optionExplanations_en: keeping a connection alive still costs memory and file descriptors — it's amortized, not free.
TCP state is kept by both sides; client and server both track sequence numbers, not just the server.
both sides hold connection state, so without keep-alive you pay a fresh handshake on every request.
every TCP connection consumes real memory and file descriptors; enough of them exhaust resources.

scenario: 你把自建服务部署在公司内网，现在要让互联网上的外部用户直接访问它。
scenario_en: You deployed a self-hosted service inside the corporate network, and now external users on the internet need to reach it directly.
q: 关于公网 IP，正确的说法是？
q_en: Which statement about public IP addresses is correct?
options: 任何人可以随便自封公网 IP 并被全网路由
公网 IP 由 RIR 分配，全网可路由
公网 IP 只在局域网内部有效，出不了本地网络
公网 IP 由 DNS 服务器直接分配给客户端
why: 私有网络里 IP 随便定，但要让互联网流量找到你，必须用 RIR 分配的可路由地址。互联网路由基础设施针对公网 IP 之间的转发做了优化。
why_en: Public IPs are allocated by regional internet registries and are routable, so the internet backbone knows for example that addresses starting with 17 belong to Apple.
options_en: Anyone can self-assign a public IP and have it routed by the whole internet.
Public IPs are allocated by a RIR and are globally routable.
A public IP only works inside a local network and never leaves it.
Public IPs are assigned directly to clients by DNS servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责分配可在公网路由的 IP 地址段的区域机构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A RIR is the regional authority that allocates blocks of publicly routable IP addresses.

optionExplanations: 自己乱定的地址不会被互联网骨干路由接受，必须走正规分配才能被全网识别。
公网 IP 由 RIR 统一分配，保证全球唯一、可被互联网路由基础设施转发。
只在局域网内有效的是私有地址段，公网 IP 恰恰是要能被外部路由的地址。
DNS 只负责把域名解析成已有的 IP，它不分配 IP 地址本身。
optionExplanations_en: a self-assigned address won't be accepted by the internet backbone without proper allocation.
public IPs are allocated by RIRs, guaranteeing global uniqueness so routing infrastructure can forward them.
addresses valid only inside a LAN are private ranges — a public IP is exactly one that routes outside.
DNS only resolves a name to an existing IP; it never assigns the IP address itself.

scenario: 为多人对战游戏选传输协议：位置更新每秒 60 次，晚到的包不如直接丢掉。
scenario_en: You're picking a transport for a multiplayer game where position updates fire sixty times a second, and a late packet is worse than a dropped one.
q: UDP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does UDP have?
options: 无连接：没有握手和连接建立，开销小、延迟低
不保证送达：丢包不会有任何通知
不保证顺序：包可能乱序到达
自动去重，保证恰好一次投递
why: UDP 是「机枪式」spray and pray：在 IP 之上几乎不加功能，换来速度。无连接、可能丢、可能乱序，也没有重复保护——收到的就是一坨二进制加上来源/目的地址端口。
why_en: UDP is connectionless with no handshake, offers no delivery or ordering guarantees, and has lower latency precisely because it adds so little on top of IP.
options_en: Connectionless: no handshake or setup, so overhead and latency are lower.
No delivery guarantee: a lost packet triggers no notification.
No ordering guarantee: packets can arrive out of order.
Automatic deduplication with exactly-once delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: 省掉握手意味着发送前不用建立连接状态，直接把开销和延迟降到最低。
丢包发生时发送方和接收方都不会收到提示，应用层必须自己检测和处理丢失。
包可能各走各的路径，到达顺序可能和发送顺序对不上，接收方要自己排序。
UDP 不做任何去重，重复包会原样交给上层，恰好一次投递是应用自己要保证的事。
optionExplanations_en: skipping the handshake means no setup before sending, keeping overhead and latency low.
on loss, neither sender nor receiver is notified — the application must detect and handle it itself.
packets can take different paths, so arrival order can differ from send order; receivers reorder them.
UDP does no deduplication — duplicates pass straight through; exactly-once is the app's job.

scenario: 设计 VoIP 语音通话：偶尔丢一个包只是音频轻微卡顿、对话依然可懂；重传丢失的包反而会用 ACK 堵塞网络。
scenario_en: You are designing a VoIP call: losing one audio packet causes a tiny glitch, but retransmitting it would block newer audio behind ACKs.
q: 传输层该选？
q_en: Which transport protocol should you choose for this VoIP audio call?
options: TCP：靠重传保证每个音频包都送达
QUIC，等它普及
UDP：速度优先，客户端自己扛丢包
HTTP 轮询
why: 实时音视频、在线游戏、DNS 查询都是 UDP 的主场：应用能自行处理偶发丢包/乱序，低延迟远比完整重传值钱。
why_en: UDP fits VoIP because dropping an occasional packet is a minor hiccup, while retransmitting old audio would only clog the network.
whenOtherWins: 数据完整性关键的场景（支付、文件传输、几乎一切非实时业务）用 TCP——凡是 UDP 不合适的地方基本都是 TCP。
options_en: TCP, retransmitting to guarantee every audio packet arrives.
QUIC, and wait for it to become mainstream.
UDP: speed over reliability, and the client absorbs the occasional loss.
HTTP polling.
tradeoff: UDP 低延迟可丢包 vs TCP 可靠重传

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: TCP 适合数据必须完整到达的场景（文件传输、支付），但这里重传会让新音频排在旧音频后面，加剧卡顿。
QUIC 具备类似能力且底层用 UDP，值得关注，但客户端/中间件支持还不够普及，直接依赖它超出本题约束。
偶发丢包只造成轻微卡顿，重传反而堵塞后续音频；UDP 让客户端自己容忍丢包，换来实时语音要的低延迟。
轮询天然有请求间隔造成的延迟，不是持续推送，撑不起语音这种连续实时流。
optionExplanations_en: TCP suits data that must arrive whole, but retransmitting audio here queues fresh sound behind stale sound.
QUIC offers similar guarantees over UDP, but support isn't mainstream yet, so betting on it here goes too far.
a dropped packet is a minor glitch, but retransmitting clogs newer audio — UDP trades loss for low latency.
Polling has built-in gaps between requests instead of continuous delivery, so it can't sustain a voice stream.

scenario: Facebook Live 的点赞刷屏要推给浏览器观众端，你想用 UDP 换更低的延迟。
scenario_en: Facebook Live reaction bursts have to reach viewers in the browser, and you want UDP to get lower latency.
q: 你想用 UDP（User Datagram Protocol）给 Facebook Live 评论的刷屏点赞做实时推送，要注意什么现实限制？
q_en: What real-world limitation matters if you want to use UDP for Facebook Live reactions in the browser?
options: UDP 无法承载表情数据
浏览器基本只有 WebRTC 支持 UDP
UDP 在蜂窝移动网络下会被运营商直接完全封锁
点赞数必须做到强一致
why: 浏览器除 WebRTC 外基本用不了 UDP。常见设计：App 端吃实时 UDP 流，浏览器端退化为分批 HTTP 流、在 UI 里摊开播放。
why_en: Browsers barely support UDP outside WebRTC, so a UDP-based design needs a fallback like a slower batched HTTP stream for browser users.
options_en: UDP cannot carry emoji/reaction data.
Browsers only really support UDP through WebRTC.
UDP is outright blocked by carriers on cellular mobile networks.
Like counts must be strongly consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: UDP 只是个传输协议，不关心载荷内容，表情、文本、二进制都能装进去。
普通浏览器 JS 没有裸 UDP socket 接口，除了 WebRTC 这个特例，浏览器端基本走不了 UDP。
运营商并不会封锁 UDP，UDP 在移动网络能用，真正的限制来自浏览器 API。
点赞数是可以容忍短暂不一致、最终收敛的计数，不需要强一致，这不是选 UDP 的顾虑点。
optionExplanations_en: UDP just moves bytes and doesn't care about payload — emoji, text, or binary all fit fine.
plain browser JS has no raw UDP socket API; aside from WebRTC, browsers basically can't speak UDP.
Carriers don't block UDP; it works on mobile — the real constraint is the browser API.
like counts tolerate brief inconsistency and converge eventually; strong consistency isn't the issue.

scenario: 聊天系统要求同一会话内的消息在接收端按发送顺序显示，漏一条都不行。
scenario_en: A chat system requires messages in one conversation to show up in send order on the receiving side, with none dropped.
q: TCP 的「流（stream）」意味着什么？
q_en: What does it mean that TCP exposes a stream?
options: 数据以视频流的形式传输
服务器可以不经客户端请求就主动推送数据
连接是完全无状态的
有状态连接：同流内消息保序，未确认会重传
why: TCP 流是有状态连接，给了我们谈「顺序」的基础：同流内消息保序，接收方必须 ACK，否则发送方重传。可靠、有序、有错误校验。
why_en: A TCP stream is a stateful connection where messages arrive in the order sent and unacknowledged messages are retransmitted until confirmed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["发送端字节流"] --> B["TCP 分段"]
    B --> C["确认 ACK"]
    C -.丢包.-> D["重传"]
    C --> E["接收端按序读"]
options_en: Data is transmitted like a video stream.
The server can push data on its own without any client request.
The connection carries no state at all.
A stateful connection: messages on the same stream stay ordered, and unacknowledged ones get retransmitted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: 这里的「流」指字节流这个抽象概念，跟视频流媒体没有关系。
服务器主动推送需要 WebSocket 之类机制，普通 TCP 流本身不代表服务器能不请自来发数据。
恰恰相反，TCP 连接是有状态的——双方要记住序号、窗口、未确认的数据。
TCP 的流是有状态连接，同一条流内消息保证顺序，没收到 ACK 的数据会被重传。
optionExplanations_en: 'stream' here means the byte-stream abstraction, unrelated to video streaming.
unsolicited server push needs something like WebSocket; a plain TCP stream alone doesn't grant that.
it's the opposite — TCP is stateful, with both sides tracking sequence numbers and unacked data.
a TCP stream is stateful; messages within it stay ordered, and unacknowledged data gets retransmitted.

scenario: 为银行转账接口选传输协议：任何一条报文丢失或乱序都会让账目算错。
scenario_en: You're choosing a transport for a bank transfer API where any lost or reordered segment corrupts the ledger.
q: TCP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does TCP provide?
options: 面向连接：传数据前先建立专用连接
可靠投递：保证数据按序、无错到达
流量控制防止淹没接收方 + 拥塞控制适应网络拥堵
头部固定只有 8 字节
why: TCP 四大件：面向连接、可靠有序、流控、拥塞控制——这就是它比 UDP 慢的原因，也是互联网的主力马。8 字节头是 UDP 的，TCP 头是 20-60 字节。
why_en: TCP is connection-oriented with reliable in-order delivery, flow control, and congestion control, while the tiny eight-byte header belongs to UDP.
options_en: Connection-oriented: it establishes a dedicated connection before transferring data.
Reliable delivery: it guarantees data arrives in order and without errors.
Flow control to avoid overwhelming the receiver, plus congestion control to adapt to a congested network.
A fixed 8-byte header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: TCP 在传数据前先做三次握手，建立起一条双方都认可的专用连接。
TCP 靠序号和 ACK/重传机制保证数据按顺序、无差错地到达接收方。
流量控制防止发送方压垮接收方缓冲区，拥塞控制则根据网络状况动态调整发送速率。
8 字节固定头是 UDP 的特征；TCP 基础头是 20 字节，带 options 能到 60 字节。
optionExplanations_en: TCP does a three-way handshake before sending data, establishing a dedicated agreed-upon connection.
sequence numbers plus ACK-and-retransmit guarantee data arrives in order and without corruption.
flow control stops the sender overrunning the receiver's buffer; congestion control adapts send rate.
an 8-byte header is UDP's trait — TCP's base header is 20 bytes, up to 60 with options.

scenario: 你在解释实时音视频为什么常偏向 UDP：单包头部开销不是主瓶颈，但能反映协议是否在传输层替你记可靠性状态。
scenario_en: You are explaining why real-time media often leans toward UDP: packet-header overhead is not the main bottleneck, but it shows whether the transport layer tracks reliability state for you.
q: UDP/TCP 头部大小差异说明哪个传输层取舍？
q_en: What transport-layer tradeoff does the UDP/TCP header-size difference illustrate?
options: 8B vs 20-60B：少记账、低开销
20-60B vs 8B：把顺序反了
同为 20B：只按带宽选协议
无固定含义：可靠性不需要状态
why: UDP 头固定 8B；TCP 基础头 20B，带 options 可到 60B。这个数字的用途不是背诵，而是提醒你：TCP 用额外字节和状态换可靠性、流控、拥塞控制。
why_en: UDP's 8-byte header versus TCP's 20-to-60-byte header is a reminder that TCP pays extra bookkeeping for reliability, flow control, and congestion control.
options_en: 8B versus 20-60B: less bookkeeping and lower overhead.
20-60B versus 8B: the order is reversed.
Both are 20B: choose only by bandwidth.
No fixed meaning: reliability needs no state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: UDP 头只需 8 字节记账，TCP 为维护可靠性状态把头部撑到 20-60 字节，这条差距就是「省记账 vs 换可靠」的体现。
把两个协议的头部数字对调了，实际是 UDP 更小（8B）、TCP 更大（20-60B），不是反过来。
两者头部大小并不相等，协议选择的关键也不是带宽，是要不要传输层帮你维护可靠性状态。
头部大小的差异恰恰说明可靠性需要额外状态字段去维护，不是无成本的。
optionExplanations_en: UDP needs only 8 bytes of bookkeeping, while TCP grows to 20-60 bytes to carry reliability state.
this swaps the two numbers — UDP is the smaller one (8B), TCP the larger (20-60B), not reversed.
the headers aren't equal, and the choice driver isn't bandwidth — it's transport-layer reliability.
the header-size gap shows reliability needs extra state fields to maintain — it isn't free.

scenario: 系统设计面试中选择传输层协议，没有特别的实时性要求。
scenario_en: In a system design interview, you need to choose a transport protocol and there is no special real-time requirement.
q: 正确的默认姿势是？
q_en: What is the default transport-protocol stance in a system design interview?
options: 每个连接都明确声明改用 QUIC 协议
默认 UDP，快
默认 TCP：面试官通常已假设你在用
TCP 和 UDP 各占一半
why: TCP 是默认，通常不用点名。加分方式是识别出真正适合 UDP 的用例并把细节讲对，而不是为了炫技乱用 UDP。
why_en: Interviewers assume TCP by default, and you earn extra points by correctly making the case for UDP only where it genuinely fits.
whenOtherWins: 低延迟至上、可容忍丢包的实时媒体/游戏/遥测才切 UDP，并要交代浏览器端怎么办。
options_en: Explicitly declare QUIC as the protocol for every connection.
Default to UDP because it's fast.
Default to TCP — interviewers usually assume it already.
Split every connection 50/50 between TCP and UDP.
tradeoff: 默认 TCP 省心 vs 论证清楚才切 UDP

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: QUIC 值得了解，但面试里主动点名每条连接都用它显得刻意——它还不是通用默认。
只有真正需要低延迟且能容忍丢包时才该默认选 UDP，无脑当默认反而暴露没抓住取舍。
面试官通常默认你的连接走 TCP，除非题目明确要求实时/容忍丢包，不用特意声明。
把协议对半分没有对应任何真实约束，只会显得是在凑答案而不是做技术判断。
optionExplanations_en: QUIC is worth knowing, but naming it for every connection looks forced — it isn't the universal default yet.
UDP earns default status only with a real low-latency, loss-tolerant need; picking it blindly looks careless.
interviewers usually assume TCP unless the problem calls for real-time or loss-tolerant traffic.
Splitting protocols 50/50 maps to no real constraint — it reads as guessing, not making a technical call.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么主链路不上 QUIC，你要给出一个关于采用面成熟度的判断。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you didn't put QUIC on the main link, and you need an answer about adoption maturity.
q: 面试语境下该怎么看 QUIC？
q_en: How should you think about QUIC in interview settings?
options: 它已经完全取代了 TCP，成为新标准
现代化、性能更好的 TCP，但采用面还不够广
它只是 UDP 换了个名字，本质完全相同
它只能用于内部数据库之间的通信
why: QUIC 提供 TCP 式的保证外加现代化性能优化，但还没有同等的普及基线。面试的真实选择题仍是 TCP vs UDP。
why_en: Treat QUIC as a better modernized TCP that lacks broad adoption, so the real interview choice remains TCP versus UDP.
options_en: It has already fully replaced TCP as the new standard.
A modernized, better-performing TCP that isn't broadly adopted yet.
It's just UDP renamed, functionally identical underneath.
It's only ever used for database-to-database communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: QUIC 还远没有取代 TCP，面试里默认协议依然是 TCP。
QUIC 提供接近 TCP 的可靠性保证并做了现代化性能优化，但普及度还没到能当默认答案的程度。
QUIC 是构建在 UDP 之上的独立协议，有自己的可靠性和拥塞控制机制，不只是换个名字。
QUIC 是通用传输协议，HTTP/3 等多种应用都在用，不是数据库专用协议。
optionExplanations_en: QUIC is nowhere near replacing TCP — TCP is still the default protocol to assume.
QUIC gives TCP-like reliability with modern performance gains, but adoption isn't broad enough to default to.
QUIC is its own protocol built on UDP with its own reliability and congestion control, not a rename.
QUIC is general-purpose, used by things like HTTP/3, not specific to databases.

scenario: 为文件上传服务选传输层：丢一个字节文件就损坏、校验和对不上。
scenario_en: You're picking a transport for a file upload service where one lost byte corrupts the file and breaks its checksum.
q: 在可靠性（reliability）这一维度上，TCP 与 UDP 的对比是？
q_en: How do TCP and UDP compare on reliability?
options: 两者都保证送达
UDP 保证送达，TCP 尽力而为
两者都不保证送达
TCP 保证送达，UDP 尽力而为
why: 一句话对照表：可靠性上 TCP 保证、UDP 尽力而为；顺序上 TCP 保序、UDP 不保；流控/拥塞控制 TCP 有、UDP 没有；速度上 UDP 更快。
why_en: On reliability TCP offers guaranteed delivery while UDP is best-effort with no notification of loss.
options_en: Both guarantee delivery.
UDP guarantees delivery, TCP is best-effort.
Neither guarantees delivery.
TCP offers guaranteed delivery, UDP is best-effort.
tradeoff: TCP 可靠有序但更重 vs UDP 更快但尽力而为

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: UDP 从设计上就不做确认和重传，根本不满足「两者都保证」。
这是把两个协议的可靠性描述完全对调了，真实情况正相反。
TCP 的握手和重传机制正是为保证送达而生，不是「两者都不保证」。
TCP 靠 ACK 和重传保证送达，UDP 发出去就不管了，可靠性正是两者的核心差异。
optionExplanations_en: UDP has no acknowledgment or retransmission by design, so 'both guarantee delivery' can't be right.
this flips the two protocols' reliability descriptions — the real picture is the opposite.
TCP's handshake and retransmission exist precisely to guarantee delivery, not to guarantee neither.
TCP guarantees delivery via ACKs and retransmission, while UDP fires and forgets — that's the core gap.

scenario: 你在评估哪些业务能从 TCP 换到 UDP，前提是端到端延迟预算被压到 50ms 内。
scenario_en: You're evaluating which workloads can move from TCP to UDP now that the end-to-end latency budget is squeezed under fifty milliseconds.
q: 哪些信号提示你可以选 UDP？（多选）
q_en: Which signals tell you UDP may be the right choice?
options: 低延迟是硬要求（实时应用、游戏）
能接受部分数据丢失（媒体流）
高量遥测/日志，偶尔丢一点无所谓
不需要支持浏览器，或已为浏览器准备了替代通道
why: 四个信号齐了 UDP 就很香。现代应用常两者混用：视频会议用 TCP/HTTP 做信令鉴权、UDP/WebRTC 传音视频流。
why_en: Choose UDP when low latency is critical, some loss is acceptable, you handle high-volume telemetry, and you either skip browsers or have an alternative for them.
options_en: Low latency is a hard requirement (real-time apps, gaming).
Some data loss is acceptable (media streaming).
High-volume telemetry or logs where the occasional loss doesn't matter.
You don't need browser support, or you already have an alternative channel for browsers.
tradeoff: 低延迟可丢包 vs 可靠交付需保序

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: 延迟是硬指标时，UDP 省掉握手和重传等待，直接把延迟压到最低。
媒体流丢一帧只是轻微卡顿，能容忍丢失就没必要为完整性支付重传的延迟代价。
遥测/日志量大且偶尔丢几条不影响整体判断时，UDP 的低开销比逐条可靠投递更划算。
浏览器原生不支持裸 UDP，选它前要确认目标端不是普通浏览器，或已准备好替代通道。
optionExplanations_en: when latency is a hard requirement, UDP skips handshake and retransmission waits, keeping it lowest.
losing a media frame is a minor glitch, so tolerable loss removes any reason to pay retransmission latency.
with high-volume telemetry where a few dropped entries don't skew the picture, UDP's low overhead wins.
browsers lack a native raw-UDP API, so confirm the target isn't a plain browser or has a fallback channel.

scenario: 做浏览器视频会议：登录鉴权一次都不能错，音视频帧可以丢但必须低延迟。
scenario_en: You're building a browser video meeting product where login and auth can never fail, but media frames may drop as long as latency stays low.
q: 一个基于 Web 的视频会议应用，典型的协议组合是？
q_en: What protocol mix is typical for a web-based video meeting app?
options: TCP 管信令鉴权，UDP 传音视频
全部走 UDP，包括登录
全部走 TCP，包括视频帧
信令走 UDP 图省事，视频帧走 TCP
why: 现代应用经常混搭：控制面（信令、鉴权）要可靠所以走 TCP/HTTP；媒体面要低延迟、容忍丢帧所以走 UDP/WebRTC。
why_en: A web conferencing app typically uses TCP and HTTP for signaling and authentication but UDP via WebRTC for the audio and video streams.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["客户端"] -->|HTTP/TCP
信令 鉴权| S["服务端"] C <-->|WebRTC/UDP
音视频| P["对端"] P -->|HTTP/TCP
信令| S
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
    A["登录/信令"] -->|TCP/HTTP| S["服务端"]
    A <-->|UDP/WebRTC| B["音视频对端"]

flowchart LR
    A["登录"] -->|UDP| S["服务端"]
    A -->|UDP| V["视频"]

flowchart LR
    A["视频帧"] -->|TCP 排队| S["服务端"]

flowchart LR
    A["信令"] -->|UDP| S["服务端"]
    A -->|TCP| V["视频"]
options_en: TCP handles signaling and auth, UDP carries the audio and video.
Everything over UDP, including login.
Everything over TCP, including video frames.
Signaling over UDP for simplicity, video frames over TCP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

optionExplanations: 登录、鉴权这些控制信息必须完整送达，走可靠的 TCP/HTTP；画面能丢帧换低延迟，走 UDP/WebRTC。
登录鉴权这类必须完整到达的数据不适合 UDP，丢包会直接导致登录失败或状态不一致。
视频帧全走 TCP 会让丢包变成重传排队，卡顿反而更严重，不符合实时媒体的取舍。
这把信令和视频该用的协议完全说反了——信令要可靠该用 TCP，视频要低延迟该用 UDP。
optionExplanations_en: the control plane (login, auth, signaling) needs TCP/HTTP; the media plane needs low-latency UDP/WebRTC.
login and auth data must arrive intact, so UDP isn't suitable — a dropped packet breaks login state.
sending every video frame over TCP turns loss into retransmission queuing, making glitches worse.
this swaps the two — signaling needs TCP's reliability, video needs UDP's low latency.

scenario: 你的 Web 服务要在高峰时从 10 台自动扩到 200 台，实例随时可能被杀掉重建。
scenario_en: Your web service has to autoscale from ten to two hundred instances at peak, with any instance killed and replaced at any moment.
q: 「HTTP 是无状态协议」意味着什么？为什么这是好事？
q_en: What does it mean that HTTP is stateless, and why is that useful?
options: 无状态意味着 HTTP 不能携带任何 cookie
每个请求彼此独立，服务器无需记住之前的请求
服务器不能存任何数据
请求之间必须间隔一秒
why: 无状态让服务器可以随意横向扩展、随意替换。系统设计的一般原则：能无状态就无状态，把有状态的表面积压到最小。
why_en: HTTP is stateless because each request is independent, which is good since you want to minimize the stateful surface area of your system.
options_en: Statelessness means HTTP cannot carry any cookies at all.
Each request is independent and the server doesn't need to remember prior requests.
The server cannot store any data.
Requests must be spaced at least a second apart.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: 无状态跟能不能带 cookie 无关，cookie 只是客户端自己保存、随请求带上的数据。
无状态指每个请求都独立，服务器不用记住上一个请求的上下文，这才让服务器能随意扩展替换。
无状态是「协议不替你记会话」，服务器完全可以存数据，只是不能靠协议本身记住谁是谁。
HTTP 协议本身对请求间隔没有任何强制要求，这条限制根本不存在。
optionExplanations_en: statelessness has nothing to do with cookies — cookies are client-stored data sent with requests.
statelessness means each request stands alone with no remembered context, letting servers scale freely.
statelessness means the protocol itself doesn't track sessions; the server can still store data.
HTTP itself imposes no required gap between requests — that constraint doesn't exist.

scenario: 你在设计公开 API，网关会自动重试「可安全重复」的方法，方法语义必须选对。
scenario_en: You're designing a public API where the gateway auto-retries methods that are safe to repeat, so the method semantics have to be right.
q: 关于 HTTP 请求方法的约定，正确的是？
q_en: Which convention for HTTP methods is correct?
options: POST 按约定应该是幂等的
PUT 是用来删除资源的方法
PATCH 是用来整体替换整个资源的方法
GET 幂等无请求体；DELETE 也幂等
why: GET 取数据（幂等、无 body）、POST 提交、PUT 更新、PATCH 部分更新、DELETE 删除（幂等）。方法和状态码像枚举一样标准化。
why_en: GET requests should be idempotent and carry no body, and DELETE requests should be idempotent as well.
options_en: POST should conventionally be idempotent.
PUT is the method used to delete a resource.
PATCH is the method used to fully replace the entire resource.
GET is idempotent with no body; DELETE is idempotent too.
codeSample:
GET    /orders/42        HTTP/1.1   # 幂等，无 body，重复调用结果一致
POST   /orders           HTTP/1.1   # 创建新资源，不是幂等的
DELETE /orders/42        HTTP/1.1   # 幂等：删一次和删十次效果相同

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: POST 按约定是非幂等的，重复提交会创建多个资源，这正是它和 PUT 的关键区别。
PUT 是整体更新（或创建）资源，删除资源对应的是 DELETE。
整体替换资源是 PUT 的职责，PATCH 按约定是部分更新。
GET 只读无请求体、重复调用不产生副作用；DELETE 重复调用效果一样，两者都是幂等操作。
