q: 关于 DynamoDB 的加密，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about DynamoDB's encryption is correct?
options: 需要手动开启静态加密
静态加密默认开启，TLS 强制传输。
只加密传输途中的数据，落盘存储时并不加密
加密需要额外付费开通
why: 静态加密和传输加密是两件事：数据写入持久存储前默认已加密；TLS 则保护到 DynamoDB API 路上的请求和响应。
why_en: Split it into two layers: encryption at rest is on by default before data reaches durable storage, and TLS protects requests and responses on the way to the DynamoDB API.
options_en: You must manually enable encryption at rest.
Encryption at rest is on by default and TLS is enforced in transit.
Only data in transit is encrypted; data at rest on disk is not.
Encryption requires an extra paid add-on.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTPS 底层的传输加密协议:在客户端和 DynamoDB API 之间建加密通道,防请求/响应在网络上被窃听或篡改
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the transport encryption under HTTPS: it builds an encrypted channel between the client and the DynamoDB API so requests/responses cannot be sniffed or tampered with in transit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 静态加密:数据落盘存储时被加密。DynamoDB 从建表起默认开、不能关、不额外收费,底层用信封加密+KMS。防的是「磁盘/备份被拿走」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encryption at rest: data is encrypted when stored on disk. DynamoDB has it on by default from table creation, cannot disable, no extra cost, using envelope encryption + KMS. Protects against stolen disks/backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输加密:数据在网络上传输时被加密,靠 TLS。DynamoDB API 强制 HTTPS。防的是「网络路上被窃听/篡改」。和静态加密是两个阶段:一个存着时、一个传输时
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encryption in transit: data is encrypted while moving over the network, via TLS. The DynamoDB API is HTTPS-only. Protects against eavesdropping/tampering on the wire — a different stage from at-rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 信封加密(密钥分两层):①用一把「数据密钥(DEK)」加密真正的数据 ②再用「主密钥(在 KMS 里)」把这把数据密钥加密(=「装进信封」)③加密后的数据密钥跟数据存一起。好处:主密钥永不离开 KMS;轮换主密钥只需重新加密那些小小的数据密钥、不用重加密全部数据;数据密钥做大批量对称加密(快)、主密钥只封套
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Envelope encryption (two key layers): (1) a data key (DEK) encrypts the actual data; (2) a master key (in KMS) encrypts that data key ("wrapped in an envelope"); (3) the encrypted data key is stored with the data. Benefits: the master key never leaves KMS; rotating it only re-encrypts the small data keys, not all data; the data key does fast bulk symmetric encryption.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真正用来加密数据的那把密钥。它本身以「被主密钥加密后」的形态存着(信封加密);读数据时先用 KMS 里的主密钥把它解开,再用它解数据
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data key (DEK) is the key that actually encrypts the data. It is stored in encrypted form (wrapped by the master key); to read, the master key in KMS unwraps it, then it decrypts the data.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  App["应用/服务"] -->|"TLS / HTTPS\n传输中加密"| API["DynamoDB API"]
  API -->|"服务端静态加密\n写入前加密"| Store["密文数据\n表 / 索引 / 备份"]
  KMS["KMS / wrapping key"] -->|"加密 data key"| DK["encrypted data key"]
  DK -.-> Store
scenario: 系统里存有用户的敏感信息。
scenario_en: The system stores sensitive user information.
optionExplanations: 静态加密其实从建表起就默认打开，不需要用户手动做任何配置。
落盘前默认做静态加密，加上 API 路上强制走 TLS，两层保护同时覆盖存储和传输。
这只说对了一半，静态加密同样是默认行为，不是只加密传输。
两层加密都不额外收费，是服务默认自带的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Encryption at rest is actually on by default from the moment the table is created -- no manual setup required.
Data is encrypted by default before it's written to storage, and TLS is enforced for every API call, covering both storage and transit.
This only gets half right -- encryption at rest is equally the default, not just transit.
Neither layer costs extra -- both come included with the service by default.

q: DynamoDB 提供哪些访问控制/网络安全手段？（多选）

内置用户名密码表

scenario: 两个业务：A 流量高度不可预测、忽高忽低；B 流量稳定可预测、长期在线。分别选 DynamoDB 计费模式。

q: 正确的搭配是？
q_en: What's the right pairing?
options: A 用 on-demand，B 用 provisioned。
都用 on-demand
A 用 provisioned；B 用 on-demand
都用 provisioned
why: on-demand 按请求计费，适合不可预测的负载；provisioned 预先指定 RCU/WCU 按小时计费，可预测负载下更省，但低谷期会有闲置容量。
why_en: On-demand per-request pricing suits unpredictable workloads while provisioned capacity is more cost-effective for predictable steady traffic.
whenOtherWins: 稳定负载硬用 on-demand 会明显更贵；波动负载用 provisioned 则要么限流要么大量闲置。
options_en: A uses on-demand, B uses provisioned capacity.
Both use on-demand.
A uses provisioned; B uses on-demand.
Both use provisioned capacity.
tradeoff: 按请求付费应对波动 vs 预置容量应对稳定负载

termDefinitions.meaning: 按实际请求量计费的容量模式，适合不可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-demand capacity bills per request, which suits unpredictable traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先指定读写容量单位、按小时计费的模式，适合稳定可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provisioned capacity bills hourly for pre-specified read and write units, which suits steady, predictable traffic.

optionExplanations: A 波动就按请求付费，避免为峰值预留浪费；B 稳定就用预置容量，按小时计费更省钱。
稳定负载 B 硬用 on-demand 会持续按请求单价付费，比预置容量明显更贵。
把两种负载和计费模式的搭配整个对调了，波动负载用 provisioned 要么限流要么闲置，两头都不划算。
波动负载 A 硬用 provisioned，遇到尖峰会限流、遇到低谷又浪费闲置容量。
optionExplanations_en: A is bursty, so pay-per-request avoids over-provisioning for peaks; B is steady, so hourly provisioned capacity is cheaper.
Forcing steady-load B onto on-demand keeps paying the per-request premium continuously, clearly costlier than provisioned.
This swaps the two workload-to-mode pairings entirely -- provisioned under bursty load throttles or sits idle either way.
Forcing bursty A onto provisioned capacity means throttling at peaks and wasted idle capacity in the quiet periods.

q: 补全容量单位的定义：
q_en: Fill in the definitions of the capacity units:
text: 1 个 RCU = 每秒读取最多 {{4KB}} 数据（强一致 1 次 / 最终一致 2 次）；1 个 WCU = 每秒写入最多 {{1KB}} 数据。
why: RCU 以 4KB 为读取单位、WCU 以 1KB 为写入单位；同一个 RCU 能换 2 次最终一致读，这是最终一致省一半钱的由来。
why_en: One read capacity unit covers four kilobytes per second and one write capacity unit covers one kilobyte per second.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

q: DynamoDB 底层会怎么应对这个写入需求？
q_en: How will DynamoDB handle this write load under the hood?
options: 自动把数据横向拆分到足够多的分区，让总吞吐超过单分区上限
让单个分区独自扛下全部吞吐，靠换用更快的 SSD 磁盘硬顶住上限

why_en: A single partition caps out around three thousand RCUs and one thousand WCUs, so DynamoDB automatically splits data across more partitions once demand exceeds that limit.
scenario: 一张表预计需要持续 5,000 WCU 的写入吞吐（已知单分区写入上限约 1,000 WCU）。

options_en: Automatically split the data horizontally across enough partitions so total throughput exceeds the single-partition cap.
Let a single partition absorb all the throughput by swapping in faster SSD disks.
Require a manual capacity-expansion ticket before AWS will split the partition.
Automatically downgrade reads to eventual consistency to save throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

optionExplanations: 单分区吞吐撞到约 1,000 WCU 的天花板后，系统会自动把数据横向拆到更多分区并重新分布，让总吞吐突破这个限制。

全托管的意义就是消灭这种人工工单，拆分是自动完成的，不需要申请。

A single partition's read/write ceiling is fixed -- no disk speed can sustain throughput past it indefinitely.
Being fully managed exists to eliminate this kind of manual ticket -- splitting happens automatically, no request needed.

q: 用 DynamoDB 记 YouTube 播放数，每次写只有几十字节，为什么每次写仍消耗 1 个完整 WCU？

WCU 向上取整到 1KB
因为每次写要复制三份副本
因为表上没有开启压缩选项

options_en: Because the play count is a numeric type, which bills higher.
A WCU rounds up to 1KB.
Because every write is replicated to three copies.
Because compression is not enabled on the table.

scenario: 在 DynamoDB 里记录一个高频但单条数据很小的计数器，比如播放数。
scenario_en: Recording a high-frequency but tiny counter in DynamoDB, such as a view count.

WCU 按字节大小向上取整到 1KB，哪怕只写几十字节也要吃满整整 1 个 WCU。

计费单位就是字节大小向上取整，压缩不是计费维度，开不开都一样。

A WCU rounds byte size up to the nearest kilobyte, so even a write of a few dozen bytes still consumes a full WCU.
Three-way replication is a durability mechanism -- users pay per logical write, not per replica.
The billing unit is simply byte size rounded up; compression isn't a billing dimension either way.

q: 假设 1,000 万写/秒的负载跑在 DynamoDB 上（预置容量约 $0.00065/WCU-小时），日成本量级大约是？
q_en: Assuming a load of ten million writes per second on DynamoDB (provisioned pricing around $0.00065 per WCU-hour), roughly what order of magnitude is the daily cost?
options: 约 $150 一天，几乎可以忽略
约 $1,500 一天，属于小额开销
约 $15.6 万一天
落在免费额度内，无需付费
why: 这笔账的意义在于「gut check」：超高写入量在 DynamoDB 上成本可能高到不现实，这正是「成本效率」成为不选它的理由之一。
why_en: Ten million writes per second costs roughly one hundred fifty six thousand dollars a day on provisioned capacity, a sanity check on feasibility.
options_en: About $150 a day -- basically negligible.
About $1,500 a day -- a small line item.
About $156,000 a day.
It falls inside the free tier, so nothing to pay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先指定读写容量单位、按小时计费的模式，适合稳定可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provisioned capacity bills hourly for pre-specified read and write units, which suits steady, predictable traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按实际请求量计费的容量模式，适合不可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-demand capacity bills per request, which suits unpredictable traffic.

scenario: 团队评估把 YouTube 播放量写入 DynamoDB 是否现实，负载假设为 1,000 万写/秒。
scenario_en: The team is evaluating whether writing YouTube view counts into DynamoDB is realistic, assuming a load of ten million writes per second.
optionExplanations: 这个量级低了三个数量级，跟 1,000 万写/秒的规模完全对不上。
这个量级还是低了两个数量级，撑不起千万级写入的真实账单。
1,000 万 WCU × $0.00065/小时 × 24 小时，算下来是十万美元量级，这笔账是判断该不该用它的 gut check。
免费额度只覆盖很小的用量，千万级写入早就远远超出这个范围。
optionExplanations_en: This is off by three orders of magnitude from what ten million writes per second actually costs.
This is still off by two orders of magnitude -- nowhere near the real bill at that write volume.
Ten million WCUs times $0.00065 per hour times 24 hours lands in six figures -- this math is the gut check for whether the load is even feasible.
The free tier only covers a tiny volume, and ten-million-per-second writes blow far past it.

scenario: 读多写少的 DynamoDB 应用想加缓存把读延迟降到微秒级，同时尽量不引入新的第三方组件。
scenario_en: A read-heavy DynamoDB app wants to add caching to push read latency down to microseconds, while avoiding introducing a new third-party component if possible.
q: 最顺手的方案是？
q_en: What's the most convenient option?
options: 自建 Memcached 集群
DAX，专属缓存微秒响应。
把数据全量导入应用内存
开启强一致读
why: DAX 是 DynamoDB 专用内存缓存，读多且访问模式贴合 DynamoDB API 时可拿到很低延迟，并减少自行维护 Redis/Memcached 的复杂度。它不是通用缓存，强一致读也不能靠 DAX 提速。
why_en: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond reads without adding a general-purpose cache like Redis.
whenOtherWins: 如果缓存还要服务 DynamoDB 之外的数据、或要用丰富数据结构（排行榜、pub/sub），通用的 Redis 更合适。
options_en: Self-host a Memcached cluster.
DAX, a purpose-built cache with microsecond response.
Load the entire dataset into application memory.
Turn on strongly consistent reads.
tradeoff: DynamoDB 专属缓存的低运维 vs 通用缓存的更广能力

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 专属的内存缓存服务，提供微秒级读延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond read latency.

optionExplanations: 自建 Memcached 要自己运维集群、写失效逻辑，违反了「不想引入新组件」的约束。
换个 SDK 接入就能把读延迟压到微秒级，专为 DynamoDB 打造，不用额外运维一套通用缓存。
数据量涨起来应用内存装不下，也没有跨实例共享和淘汰机制，不可扩展。
强一致读实际消耗双倍 RCU、延迟更高，跟「降低延迟」的目标正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Self-hosting Memcached means running your own cluster and invalidation logic -- it breaks the 'no new component' constraint.
Swapping in the SDK alone drives read latency down to microseconds, purpose-built for DynamoDB with no extra general-purpose cache to run.
As data grows it stops fitting in application memory, and there's no cross-instance sharing or eviction -- it doesn't scale.
Strong consistency actually costs double the RCUs and adds latency, the opposite of the latency goal.

q: 接入 DAX 对应用代码的要求是？
q_en: What does adopting DAX require from the application code?
options: 完全透明，零改动
需要把应用里的每一条查询语句都逐条重写一遍
换 DAX 客户端 SDK，改动很小。
只能通过 REST API 访问
why: DAX 通过替换客户端 SDK 接入：API 兼容、改动少，但确实要换客户端——「不是完全透明」是常被追问的细节。
why_en: Using DAX means swapping in the DAX client SDK, which is API compatible but not completely transparent.
options_en: Fully transparent -- zero code changes.
You must rewrite every single query statement in the application one by one.
Swap in the DAX client SDK -- a small change.
It can only be accessed through a REST API.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 专属的内存缓存服务，提供微秒级读延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的客户端库，用于以编程方式调用 DynamoDB API。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The SDK is AWS's client library used to call the DynamoDB API programmatically.

optionExplanations: 至少要把客户端换成 DAX SDK，并不是纯配置开关式的零改动。
Query/Scan 这些调用方式不用变，只是底层客户端换了，谈不上重写全部查询。
API 兼容、只需替换客户端 SDK，改动小但确实要动代码和重新部署。
DAX 提供的是各语言的客户端 SDK，不是通用 REST 接口。
optionExplanations_en: At minimum the client has to be swapped to the DAX SDK -- it's not a pure config toggle with zero changes.
Query and Scan calls stay the same; only the underlying client changes, nowhere near rewriting every query.
API-compatible, just swap the client SDK -- a small change, but it does mean touching code and redeploying.
DAX ships as per-language client SDKs, not a generic REST interface.
scenario: 线上服务读延迟要从毫秒压到微秒，团队打算加 DAX，先要知道改动量。
scenario_en: To take read latency from milliseconds to microseconds the team wants DAX, and needs to know how much code changes.

q: DAX 是读穿透 + 写穿透缓存，但有一个失效陷阱是？
q_en: DAX is a read-through-plus-write-through cache, but what's one staleness trap?
options: 只失效经过 DAX 的写，旁路直写留旧数据。
DAX 每次写入都会把整个缓存里的条目全部清空失效
DAX 不支持 TTL
DAX 写入不会落到 DynamoDB
why: write-through 只覆盖走 DAX 的路径：任何旁路直写 DynamoDB 的服务都会造成缓存陈旧，需要靠 TTL/淘汰兜底或统一所有写路径。
why_en: DAX only invalidates entries for writes that go through DAX itself, so direct writes to DynamoDB leave stale cache entries until TTL or eviction.
options_en: Only invalidates writes that go through DAX; a bypassed direct write leaves stale data.
DAX wipes and invalidates every entry in its whole cache on each write.
DAX does not support TTL at all.
Writes through DAX never actually reach DynamoDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 专属的内存缓存服务，提供微秒级读延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生存时间：数据到期后自动过期/淘汰的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the lifespan after which a stored item automatically expires.

optionExplanations: 写穿透只覆盖经过 DAX 的那条写路径，任何绕开它直接写库的服务都会让缓存跟数据库脱节。
DAX 只精确失效被写入的那个 key，不会波及缓存里的其他条目，说全量清空夸大了范围。
DAX 支持给条目设置 TTL，到期后自动淘汰，这个说法低估了它的能力。
DAX 是写穿透缓存，写操作会同时落到缓存和 DynamoDB，二者是一起完成的。
optionExplanations_en: Write-through only covers writes that pass through DAX -- any service that bypasses it and writes DynamoDB directly leaves the cache out of sync.
DAX invalidates only the exact key that was written, not the rest of the cache -- claiming a full wipe overstates the scope.
DAX does support setting a TTL so entries lapse automatically, so this undersells its capability.
DAX is a write-through cache -- a write lands in both the cache and DynamoDB together.
scenario: 读路径走 DAX，但另有一个批处理作业直接写 DynamoDB 主表。
scenario_en: Reads go through DAX, but a separate batch job writes straight to the DynamoDB table.

q: DAX 内部维护哪两个缓存？如何配置二选一？
q_en: What two caches does DAX maintain internally, and how do you pick between them?
options: 读缓存和写缓存两种，可以按需要任选其中一个开启
item 缓存与 query 缓存，均常开
本地缓存和远程缓存，默认只开本地
冷缓存和热缓存，按小时自动切换
why: 两个缓存各管一类操作、恒常开启：item cache 缓存单条读取，query cache 缓存查询/扫描结果——没有开关可选。
why_en: DAX always runs both an item cache for single-item gets and a query cache for query and scan results, with no configuration to choose one.
options_en: A read cache and a write cache, and you enable whichever one you need.
An item cache and a query cache, both always on.
A local cache and a remote cache, with local on by default.
A cold cache and a hot cache, switched hourly.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 专属的内存缓存服务，提供微秒级读延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按完整主键读取单个 item 的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GetItem reads a single item by its full primary key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求批量读取多个 item（可跨表）的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BatchGetItem reads multiple items, even across tables, in a single request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读全表或全索引每个 item 的操作，代价随数据量线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Scan reads every item in a table or index, so its cost grows linearly with data size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按主键或索引键条件读取匹配 item 的操作，比 Scan 高效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Query reads only items matching a key condition, which is far more efficient than a Scan.

optionExplanations: DAX 没有「读缓存/写缓存二选一」这种配置项，这是编出来的分类。
item cache 管单条读取、query cache 管查询和扫描结果，两个缓存按操作类型分工、始终一起开着，没有开关可选。
DAX 是独立部署的集群式缓存层，不存在本地/远程二选一这种架构。
DAX 的两个缓存不存在按小时冷热切换的机制，这个说法是编造的。
optionExplanations_en: DAX has no 'pick a read cache or a write cache' setting -- that category is invented.
The item cache handles single-item reads and the query cache handles query/scan results, split by operation type and always both running with nothing to toggle.
DAX is a standalone, cluster-deployed caching layer, not a local-versus-remote architecture.
DAX's two caches have no hourly hot/cold swap mechanism -- that's fabricated.
scenario: 接入 DAX 后既有 GetItem 单条读，也有大量 Query，想知道缓存怎么覆盖。
scenario_en: After adopting DAX you have both single-item GetItems and heavy Query traffic, and need to know what gets cached.

q: 通过 DAX 发起强一致读会发生什么？
q_en: What happens when you issue a strongly consistent read through DAX?
options: DAX 返回缓存值并标记为强一致
请求被拒绝
DAX 会静默地把它偷偷降级成最终一致读返回
不缓存，直接透传给 DynamoDB。
why: 强一致读必须来自 leader，缓存无法保证，所以 DAX 直接透传、不缓存——设计强一致路径时别指望 DAX 提速。
why_en: DAX passes strongly consistent reads straight through to DynamoDB and does not cache the results.
options_en: DAX returns a cached value and just labels it as strongly consistent.
The request is rejected outright.
DAX quietly downgrades it to an eventually consistent read and returns that.
Not cached -- passed straight through to DynamoDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 专属的内存缓存服务，提供微秒级读延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读请求里的参数，设为 true 即要求强一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ConsistentRead is a per-request parameter that, when set to true, requires a strongly consistent read.

optionExplanations: 缓存没法保证反映此前所有成功写入，给它贴「强一致」标签只是自欺欺人。
请求会被正常处理，只是跳过缓存，不存在被拒绝这回事。
擅自降级会违反调用方明确要求的一致性语义，DAX 不会这么做。
既然强一致的答案只能来自主副本、缓存没法打这个包票，DAX 索性把这类请求原样转给 DynamoDB，跳过缓存这一层。
optionExplanations_en: A cache can't guarantee it reflects every prior successful write, so labeling it 'strongly consistent' is just self-deception.
The request proceeds normally, just skipping the cache -- there's no rejection involved.
Silently downgrading would violate the consistency the caller explicitly asked for, so DAX doesn't do that.
A strong read has to come from the leader, which a cache can't guarantee, so DAX simply passes it straight through to DynamoDB, skipping the cache layer.
scenario: 把一条要求强一致的余额读也指向了 DAX 集群，期待它同样被加速。
scenario_en: You point a strongly consistent balance read at the DAX cluster, expecting the same speedup.

q: DynamoDB Streams 是什么？
q_en: What is DynamoDB Streams?
options: 视频流媒体服务
内置 CDC，记录变更事件。
把表数据流式导出为 CSV
只用于备份的日志
why: Streams 是 DynamoDB 自带的 CDC：item 变更会进入流，下游可以触发 Lambda、同步派生索引或做近实时分析。它是异步变更出口，不等于跨存储强一致事务。
why_en: DynamoDB Streams is built-in change data capture that lets downstream systems react to item changes in near real time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    T[("DynamoDB table")] --> S["Streams shard"]
    S --> L["Lambda consumer"]
    S --> K["Kinesis adapter"]
    L --> D["derived view or side effect"]
    K --> A["analytics pipeline"]
options_en: A video streaming media service.
Built-in CDC that records change events.
A feature that streams the table out to CSV files.
A log used only for backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库变更事件（增删改）供下游实时消费的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture streams a database's insert, update, and delete events to downstream consumers in real time.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 内置的 CDC 功能，把表变更记录成可消费的 stream record。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is the built-in CDC feature that records table changes as consumable stream records.

scenario: 想知道 DynamoDB 表的数据变化能不能被下游系统实时感知到。
scenario_en: Wondering whether downstream systems can react to a DynamoDB table's data changes in near real time.
optionExplanations: 这里的「Stream」指的是数据变更事件流，跟视频媒体毫无关系，是望文生义。
item 的每次增删改都会被记成一条事件进入这条流，下游服务订阅后就能各自响应。
stream record 是结构化事件，不是 CSV 文件，消费方式也完全不同。
它是一个通用的异步变更出口，典型用途包括搜索同步、实时分析、变更通知，不只是备份。
optionExplanations_en: 'Stream' here refers to a change-event stream, entirely unrelated to video media -- a literal misreading.
Every item insert, update, and delete lands in this stream, letting downstream systems trigger Lambda, sync derived indexes, or run near-real-time analytics.
A stream record is a structured event, not a CSV file, and it's consumed in a completely different way.
It's a general-purpose async change outlet used for search sync, real-time analytics, and change notifications, not just backups.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: DynamoDB Streams 的典型用法有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the typical use cases for DynamoDB Streams? (select all)
options: 保持 Elasticsearch 索引与 DynamoDB 表同步，在其上构建搜索功能
通过 Kinesis 管道把变更数据送进 S3/Redshift/OpenSearch 做实时分析
触发 Lambda 响应数据变化（发通知、更新缓存等）
替代 IAM 做权限控制
why: Streams 的三大经典场景：搜索索引同步、实时分析管道、变更触发的 Lambda。它是数据变更的出口，不是权限系统。
why_en: Streams commonly sync Elasticsearch indexes, feed real-time analytics pipelines, and trigger Lambda functions on data changes.
options_en: Keep an Elasticsearch index in sync with the DynamoDB table to power search.
Pipe change data through Kinesis into S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch for real-time analytics.
Trigger Lambda functions in response to data changes, such as sending notifications or updating caches.
Replace IAM as the access-control mechanism.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源全文搜索与分析引擎，常与 DynamoDB Streams 搭配做搜索索引同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an open-source full-text search engine often kept in sync with DynamoDB via Streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的实时数据流服务，常作为 DynamoDB Streams 与 Firehose 之间的中间层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis Data Streams is AWS's real-time streaming service, often bridging DynamoDB Streams and Firehose.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流数据自动批量加载进 S3/Redshift/OpenSearch 的托管服务，不能直接读 DynamoDB Streams。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis Data Firehose loads streaming data into S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch, but cannot read DynamoDB Streams directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，常作为分析管道或备份的落地存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service, often used as the destination for analytics pipelines or backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的数据仓库服务，用于大规模分析查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redshift is AWS's data warehouse service for large-scale analytical queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 Elasticsearch 兼容搜索与分析服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OpenSearch is AWS's managed, Elasticsearch-compatible search and analytics service.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的无服务器函数计算服务，常被 Streams 事件触发执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lambda is AWS's serverless compute service, often triggered by DynamoDB Streams events.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的身份与权限管理服务，用策略控制谁能访问哪些资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IAM is AWS's identity and access management service, controlling who can access which resources.

tradeoff: 实时变更驱动的派生系统 vs 定期批量重建
optionExplanations: DynamoDB 作为事实源，ES 跟着 Streams 事件走就能保持同步，省掉应用层双写的一致性风险。
变更经 Kinesis 实时流入分析系统，比定期批量导出更及时，也更省一次性全量拉取的开销。
典型例子是订单状态变化触发通知，或写操作后失效相关缓存，都是靠事件驱动而不是轮询。
权限控制是 IAM 的职责，Streams 只负责把变更事件暴露出去，两者不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: With DynamoDB as the source of truth, Elasticsearch stays in sync just by following Streams events, sidestepping the consistency risk of double writes.
Changes flow through Kinesis into the analytics system in real time, more current than periodic batch exports and cheaper than one-off full pulls.
A typical example is triggering a notification on an order-status change or invalidating a cache after a write -- event-driven, not polling.
Access control is IAM's job; Streams only exposes change events -- the two aren't the same thing.
scenario: 订单表的变更要驱动下游：搜索索引、数据仓库、通知，全都要近实时。
scenario_en: Order-table changes must drive downstream search indexing, the warehouse, and notifications, all in near real time.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 想用 Kinesis Data Firehose 把 DynamoDB 变更载入 S3/Redshift，管道上要注意什么？
q_en: You want to use Kinesis Data Firehose to load DynamoDB changes into S3/Redshift -- what should you watch out for in the pipeline?
options: Firehose 可以直接读 DynamoDB Streams
必须先导出全表快照
Firehose 不能直连，需 Kinesis 中转。
只能通过人工导出 CSV
why: 常见误区：Firehose 与 DynamoDB Streams 不直连，中间必须有 Kinesis Data Streams（在表上启用）或一个 Lambda 做搬运。
why_en: Kinesis Data Firehose cannot read DynamoDB Streams directly and needs Kinesis Data Streams or a Lambda function as the intermediary.
options_en: Firehose can read DynamoDB Streams directly.
You must first export a full table snapshot.
Firehose cannot connect directly -- it needs Kinesis as a relay.
The only path is a manual CSV export.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全托管的「投递」服务:把流式数据批量缓冲后载入 S3/Redshift/ES,不用写代码、不用管消费者——「把流倒进存储」的管子。它的数据源是 Kinesis Data Streams(或直接 PUT),不能直连 DynamoDB Streams
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully-managed delivery service that buffers and loads streaming data into S3/Redshift/ES with no code and no consumers to manage. Its source is a Kinesis Data Stream (or direct PUT); it cannot read DynamoDB Streams directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 自己的变更流(CDC):捕获 item 增/改/删,由 Lambda/KCL 消费,保留 24 小时。注意它不能被 Firehose 直接读
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is DynamoDB's own change feed (CDC), capturing item inserts/updates/deletes, consumed by Lambda/KCL, retained 24h. Firehose cannot read it directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 通用的实时流服务(类似 Kafka):可分片、可多消费者、可回放。DynamoDB 能把变更直接推到它(表上开启「Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB」),再由 Firehose 读它载入 S3
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis Data Streams is AWS's general real-time streaming service (Kafka-like): shardable, multi-consumer, replayable. DynamoDB can push changes to it (enable "Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB"), then Firehose reads it into S3.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS serverless 函数,可作为「胶水」消费 DynamoDB Streams、再把记录塞进 Firehose——Firehose 不能直连 DynamoDB Streams 时的另一种中转
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS Lambda (serverless function) can act as glue: consume DynamoDB Streams and push records into Firehose — the other way to bridge when Firehose cannot read DynamoDB Streams directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB Streams 不能直连 Firehose。两种接法:①表上开 Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB → Firehose → S3(原生、无代码);②Lambda 读 DynamoDB Streams → 塞进 Firehose → S3(写胶水)。都是要「中转」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams cannot connect to Firehose directly. Two bridges: (1) enable Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB → Firehose → S3 (native, no code); (2) Lambda reads DynamoDB Streams → pushes to Firehose → S3 (glue code).

scenario: 打算把 DynamoDB 的变更实时同步进数据仓库做分析。
scenario_en: Planning to sync DynamoDB changes into a data warehouse for analytics in near real time.
optionExplanations: 这是个常见误区，按这个理解搭建管道会直接失败，因为两者根本没有直连路径。
先导出全量快照违背了「实时」管道的初衷，会把它退化成批量导出。
对，管道要多一跳中转：先在表上开启 Streams，再挂一个搬运组件，Firehose 只负责最后一段投递。
人工导出跟「实时分析」的目标完全相悖，Streams 本身就是自动实时的。
optionExplanations_en: This is a common misconception, and building the pipeline on it fails outright since no such direct connection exists.
Exporting a full snapshot first defeats the point of a 'real-time' pipeline, degrading it into batch export.
Right -- the pipeline needs an extra hop: enable Streams on the table, hang a relay off it, and Firehose only does the final delivery.
Manual export directly contradicts the real-time analytics goal -- Streams itself is already automatic.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 系统用 DynamoDB 存业务数据，同时要在 Elasticsearch 上提供全文搜索，两个存储必须保持同步。
scenario_en: The system stores business data in DynamoDB and also needs full-text search on Elasticsearch; the two stores must stay in sync.
q: 推荐的同步方案是？
q_en: What's the recommended way to keep them in sync?
options: 应用层双写 DynamoDB 和 ES
每晚全量重建 ES 索引
让 ES 直接查询 DynamoDB
用 Streams 消费变更同步 ES。
why: CDC 方案让 DynamoDB 作为单一事实源、ES 跟随变更流：避免应用层双写的部分失败不一致，也比全量重建实时。
why_en: Consuming DynamoDB Streams to update Elasticsearch keeps the search index in sync without dual writes from the application.
whenOtherWins: 若搜索数据量极小且更新极少，定期批量重建索引反而简单，不必上流式管道。
options_en: Have the application double-write to both DynamoDB and Elasticsearch.
Rebuild the entire Elasticsearch index from scratch every night.
Let Elasticsearch query DynamoDB directly.
Consume Streams events to keep Elasticsearch in sync.
tradeoff: 单一事实源+CDC 同步 vs 应用层双写的一致性风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源全文搜索与分析引擎，常与 DynamoDB Streams 搭配做搜索索引同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an open-source full-text search engine often kept in sync with DynamoDB via Streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 内置的 CDC 功能，把表变更记录成可消费的 stream record。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is the built-in CDC feature that records table changes as consumable stream records.

optionExplanations: 双写引入了「两次写入部分失败」的经典一致性风险，还得自己写补偿逻辑。
两次重建之间用户搜到的都是旧数据，全量重建本身也很耗资源，实时性差。
ES 和 DynamoDB 是两套独立系统，查询协议和数据模型完全不同，不存在这种直连方式。
让 DynamoDB 保持权威数据源、ES 跟着 Streams 事件走，避免应用层维护两份写逻辑，也比全量重建更及时。
optionExplanations_en: Double-writing introduces the classic 'one of two writes partially fails' consistency risk, plus you have to build your own compensation logic.
Between rebuilds users search against stale data, and a full rebuild itself burns significant resources -- poor freshness.
Elasticsearch and DynamoDB are separate systems with entirely different query protocols and data models -- no such direct link exists.
Keeping DynamoDB authoritative with Elasticsearch following Streams events avoids duplicating write logic in the app, and stays fresher than a full rebuild.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 为什么在面试里 DynamoDB「几乎可以胜任任何持久层」？（多选）
q_en: Why is DynamoDB 'good for nearly any persistence layer' in an interview? (select all)
options: 高可扩展、高持久
支持 ACID 事务（含跨表）
单毫秒级延迟，配 DAX 可到微秒级
自带 DAX 缓存和 Streams，方便做低延迟读与异步派生视图/CDC
免费且无供应商锁定
why: 扩展、事务、低延迟、附带缓存与 CDC——这套组合覆盖很多持久层需求；但 DAX/Streams 分别是缓存和异步变更流，不提供跨存储强一致，且 DynamoDB 不免费、也深度绑定 AWS。
why_en: DynamoDB pairs high scalability and durability with transactions and single-digit-millisecond latency, though it is not free and still ties you to AWS.
options_en: Highly scalable and highly durable.
Supports ACID transactions, including across tables.
Single-digit-millisecond latency, down to microseconds with DAX.
Ships with DAX caching and Streams, making low-latency reads and async derived views or CDC easy.
Free and has no vendor lock-in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专给 DynamoDB 用的全托管「内存缓存」,挡在 DynamoDB 前面:命中的读从毫秒降到微秒级、还省 RCU。是「加速读」的缓存,不是变更流
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) is a fully-managed in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB: cached reads drop from milliseconds to microseconds and save RCUs. It is a read cache, not a change stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的 CDC:把每次 item 的增/改/删按顺序变成一串变更事件,供下游(Lambda/Kinesis)实时消费——用来做异步派生视图(更新搜索索引、维护聚合、复制、触发通知)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is CDC: every item insert/update/delete becomes an ordered stream of change events for downstream consumers (Lambda/Kinesis) to build async derived views (search index, aggregates, replication, notifications).

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 支持 ACID 事务(TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems):可对多个 item(含跨表)原子写入,要么全成要么全回滚。预订/下单可一步原子完成,不必自己写 saga 补偿。代价:2 倍容量、单事务最多 100 item
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB supports ACID transactions (TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems): atomically write multiple items, even across tables, all-or-nothing. Booking/order flows become one atomic step with no manual saga. Cost: 2x capacity, up to 100 items per transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库的变更(增/改/删)并变成一串事件、供下游实时消费的机制——下游不用轮询,DB 把变更「推」出来。常用来把变更喂给 Elasticsearch 建索引、维护物化视图、复制数据。DynamoDB Streams、Debezium(读 MySQL/PG 的 binlog/WAL)都是 CDC
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC (Change Data Capture) captures a database inserts/updates/deletes as a stream of events for downstream real-time consumption — no polling; the DB pushes its changes. Often used to feed Elasticsearch, maintain materialized views, or replicate. DynamoDB Streams and Debezium (MySQL/PG binlog/WAL) are CDC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 别混:DAX=缓存,加速「读」(毫秒→微秒);Streams=CDC,把「写/变更」变成事件流给下游。一个管读得快、一个管变更传播,方向不同
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Do not confuse: DAX is a cache that speeds up reads (ms→μs); Streams is CDC that turns writes/changes into an event stream for downstream. One is read speed, the other is change propagation.

tradeoff: 全托管强能力 vs 成本与供应商锁定的代价
optionExplanations: 扩展和持久是几乎任何持久层都要的底线诉求，DynamoDB 天然满足，不用自己搭分片方案。
跨表原子写入让预订、下单这类场景不必自己实现补偿逻辑。
默认单毫秒级延迟已经很快，配 DAX 还能进一步压到微秒级，覆盖大部分低延迟诉求。
不用额外引入 Redis 做缓存，也不用自建 CDC 管道去同步搜索索引或做实时分析。
这把「功能强大」和「免费无锁定」混为一谈了，DynamoDB 是收费的托管服务，且深度绑定 AWS。
optionExplanations_en: Scalability and durability are baseline needs for almost any persistence layer, and DynamoDB meets them natively without hand-rolling sharding.
Atomic cross-table writes mean booking or checkout flows don't need their own compensation logic.
The default single-digit-millisecond latency is already fast, and DAX pushes it further down to microseconds, covering most low-latency needs.
No need to bring in Redis separately for caching or build a custom CDC pipeline to sync search indexes or feed real-time analytics.
This conflates 'feature-rich' with 'free and lock-in-free' -- DynamoDB is a paid managed service deeply tied to AWS.
scenario: 面试里为一个已在 AWS 上的新系统选主存储，规模、低延迟、事务需求都有。
scenario_en: In an interview you're picking the primary datastore for a new AWS system with scale, low latency, and transactions.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 哪些情况会让你不选 DynamoDB？（多选）
q_en: Which situations should make you avoid DynamoDB? (select all)
options: 成本：每秒几十万写的高量负载下，按读写计费可能贵得离谱
复杂查询：需要 JOIN、ad-hoc 聚合等灵活查询能力
建模信号：发现自己频繁依赖大量 GSI/LSI——说明关系型（如 PostgreSQL）可能更合适
供应商锁定：面试官要求保持 vendor-neutral
需要毫秒级读延迟
why: 四大不选理由：成本、查询灵活性、建模约束（索引泛滥是换关系库的信号）、AWS 锁定。毫秒级延迟恰恰是它的强项，不是短板。
why_en: Avoid DynamoDB for cost-heavy write volumes, complex query needs, index-heavy modeling better served by Postgres, or when vendor neutrality is required.
options_en: Cost: at hundreds of thousands of writes per second, pay-per-request billing can get absurdly expensive.
Complex queries: the system needs joins or ad-hoc aggregation that flexible querying provides.
A modeling signal: leaning on a pile of GSIs and LSIs suggests a relational database like PostgreSQL may fit better.
Vendor lock-in: the interviewer wants a vendor-neutral, open-source choice.
Needing millisecond-level read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 JOIN 和灵活查询，是 DynamoDB 建模复杂时的常见替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that supports joins and flexible queries, a common alternative when DynamoDB modeling gets too complex.

tradeoff: 键值建模的高效 vs 关系型查询的灵活
optionExplanations: 几十万写/秒的量级下，按请求计费可能高到不现实，这时候要重新算一笔账。
DynamoDB 支持跨表事务，但没有 SQL 式的灵活联表和即席聚合能力，复杂报表类查询会很吃力。
索引堆到七八个说明访问模式本质上是关系型的，硬撑不如直接换库。
有些面试官明确要求避免绑定单一云厂商，这时该考虑开源的替代方案。
这把它的强项当成了弱项——毫秒甚至微秒级（配 DAX）延迟恰恰是选它的理由，不是避开它的理由。
optionExplanations_en: At hundreds of thousands of writes per second, pay-per-request billing can get unrealistically expensive, worth re-running the numbers.
DynamoDB supports cross-table transactions but lacks SQL-style flexible joins and ad-hoc aggregation, so complex reporting queries get painful.
Piling on seven or eight indexes signals the access patterns are fundamentally relational -- better to switch databases than force it.
Some interviewers explicitly want to avoid single-vendor lock-in, which points toward open-source alternatives.
This turns a strength into a weakness -- millisecond, even microsecond with DAX, latency is a reason to pick it, not avoid it.
scenario: 一个跑在 DynamoDB 上的后台，报表要做多表 JOIN 和临时聚合，写入量也在飙升。
scenario_en: A backend on DynamoDB now needs multi-table joins and ad-hoc aggregation, and write volume is climbing fast.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 设计过程中发现：为了支撑各种查询，一张 DynamoDB 表上已经挂了七八个 GSI 和多个 LSI。
scenario_en: While designing the system, you notice a DynamoDB table already carries seven or eight GSIs plus several LSIs to support various queries.
q: 这个信号说明什么？
q_en: What does this signal mean?
options: 说明设计很成功，索引建得越多查询就越灵活越好
应该把所有查询改成 Scan
访问模式关系化，超出键值建模舒适区。
应该删掉所有索引
why: DynamoDB 要求围绕少数明确访问模式精心建模；索引堆到这个程度说明查询需求本质上是关系型的，硬撑不如换关系库。
why_en: Leaning heavily on many GSIs and LSIs signals relational access patterns that a database like PostgreSQL would serve better.
whenOtherWins: 若只是两三个清晰的次要访问模式，正常使用 GSI/LSI 完全合理，不必换库。
options_en: The design is a success -- the more indexes you build, the more flexible the queries.
Every query should be switched to a Scan.
The access patterns are relational, past key-value modeling's comfort zone.
All the indexes should simply be deleted.
tradeoff: 硬撑键值建模的索引堆积 vs 换用关系库的灵活查询

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 JOIN 和灵活查询，是 DynamoDB 建模复杂时的常见替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that supports joins and flexible queries, a common alternative when DynamoDB modeling gets too complex.

optionExplanations: 索引越多通常意味着写入时要多付好几倍的维护开销、运维和账单一起被拖累，不是越多越好。
把所有查询都换成 Scan 会让每次查询代价随表增长线性上升，是明显的反模式，跟索引堆积的问题无关。
索引堆到七八个说明查询需求本质上已经关系化了，超出了键值建模能舒服覆盖的范围，这时候该考虑换关系库而不是硬撑。
如果这些查询模式仍是真实需求，删掉索引只会让它们变得低效或彻底不可用，治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: More indexes usually means paying several times the write-time maintenance overhead, dragging down operations and cost -- not simply better.
Switching every query to a Scan makes each query's cost grow linearly with the table, a clear anti-pattern unrelated to the actual index-pileup problem.

Piling up to seven or eight indexes means the query needs have effectively gone relational, past what key-value modeling can comfortably cover -- time to consider a relational database instead of forcing it.
If those query patterns are still genuinely needed, deleting the indexes only makes them inefficient or unusable -- treating the symptom, not the cause.

q: 把「选用 DynamoDB」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for 'choosing DynamoDB' in the correct order:
steps: 代价：按量计费在超高写入下昂贵、查询灵活性差、绑定 AWS
需求：海量数据 + 高可用 + 低延迟，团队不想管运维
缓解：围绕访问模式精心建模、控制索引数量、用估算核对成本
选型：DynamoDB
决定性属性：全托管、自动分片扩缩、单毫秒延迟、支持事务
why: 决策链：需求（大规模+免运维）→ 决定性属性（托管、自动扩展、事务）→ 选 DynamoDB → 代价（成本/查询/锁定）→ 缓解（建模+成本估算）。
why_en: Massive scale with no ops burden points to DynamoDB's managed auto-scaling and transactions, whose cost and query limits are mitigated by careful modeling and estimation.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Access patterns known"] --> K["design PK and SK"]
    K --> I["add GSI or LSI only if needed"]
    I --> C["choose consistency per path"]
    C --> S["check hot keys and cost"]
tradeoff: 全托管免运维 vs 成本/查询灵活性/供应商锁定的代价

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 补全「一致性按路径拆分」这条 DynamoDB 推理：
q_en: Fill in this DynamoDB reasoning about splitting consistency by path:
text: 预订/下单这类关键路径用 {{ConsistentRead=true}} 的强一致读（走 {{leader}} 节点、消耗 2 倍 RCU）；读多、延迟敏感的路径默认{{最终}}一致（任意副本可服务、0.5 RCU/4KB）。
why: 按请求可调一致性让一个系统里两类路径各取所需：正确性优先的花钱买强一致，性能优先的享受默认的便宜和快。
why_en: Critical paths request strongly consistent reads from the leader at double cost while latency-sensitive paths keep the cheap eventually consistent default.
tradeoff: 强一致读的正确性优先 vs 最终一致读的性能优先

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读的一致性开关。默认 false=最终一致(任意副本服务、可能读到略旧、0.5 RCU/4KB);设 true=强一致(必须读 leader 副本、保证最新、1 RCU/4KB=2倍)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB read consistency flag. Default false = eventually consistent (any replica, may be slightly stale, 0.5 RCU/4KB); true = strongly consistent (must read the leader replica, latest data, 1 RCU/4KB = double).

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读容量单位。1 RCU=每秒一次强一致读(≤4KB)=每秒两次最终一致读(≤4KB)。所以强一致读花 1 RCU、最终一致只花 0.5 RCU→强一致=2倍成本
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read Capacity Unit. 1 RCU = one strongly-consistent read/sec (≤4KB) = two eventually-consistent reads/sec; a strong read costs 1 RCU, an eventual read 0.5 — strong is 2x.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 每个 item 存多个副本(通常 3 个跨 AZ),其中一个是 leader:写先落 leader 再复制给 follower。强一致读必须读 leader(它一定有最新写);最终一致读可读任意副本(follower 可能略滞后→读到旧值)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB stores each item on multiple replicas (usually 3 across AZs); one is the leader — writes hit it first, then replicate. A strongly consistent read must read the leader (it has the latest write); an eventually consistent read may read any replica (a follower may lag).

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 在「分区内索引结构」上，DynamoDB 与 Cassandra 的对比是？
q_en: On 'in-partition index structure', how do DynamoDB and Cassandra compare?
options: 两者都用 LSM 树
前者 B-tree，后者 LSM（写优化）。
DynamoDB 用 LSM，Cassandra 用 B-tree
两者都不用索引
why: DynamoDB 走 B-tree 路线（读写均衡、范围查询高效），Cassandra 走 LSM 路线（极致写吞吐）——同为宽列/键值家族但存储引擎哲学不同。
why_en: DynamoDB indexes each partition with a B-tree by sort key while Cassandra relies on an LSM tree optimized for writes.
options_en: Both use LSM trees.
The former uses a B-tree, the latter a write-optimized LSM tree.
DynamoDB uses LSM, Cassandra uses a B-tree.
Neither uses any index structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平衡树索引结构，支持高效的有序遍历和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced tree index that supports efficient ordered traversal and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化的树形存储结构：先写内存再顺序刷盘合并，Cassandra 等系统使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized storage structure that buffers writes in memory and merges them to disk sequentially.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源宽列存储数据库，分区内用 LSM 树、面向高写入吞吐设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is an open-source wide-column database that uses LSM trees internally and is optimized for high write throughput.

tradeoff: DynamoDB 读写均衡的 B-tree vs Cassandra 写优化的 LSM

options_en: An eventually consistent read saves half the read capacity.

Only strongly consistent reads consume read capacity; eventual reads are not billed at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向宽列存储的分布式 NoSQL 数据库，擅长海量写入和线性扩展。

q_en: Which search component should this system add?
scenario_en: An e-commerce product search needs full-text matching, relevance ranking, multi-field filters, and faceting over a large, complex dataset.
optionExplanations: 数据小、只做简单包含匹配时能先用它，但排序和 faceting 都要应用层手写，规模一大就撑不住。
Redis 适合按已知 key 读取或缓存热门结果，但撑不起相关性排序和分面统计，本质不是搜索引擎。
倒排索引加聚合原生覆盖打分排序、字段过滤和分面统计，复合搜索到这规模就该用它。
写入扩展优先、查询按分区键固定时 Cassandra 合适，但它的二级索引扛不住这里的复合过滤和相关性排序。
optionExplanations_en: Fine when data is small and matching is a simple substring check, but ranking and faceting end up hand-rolled in the app layer and slow down at scale.
Redis speeds up known-key reads or cached popular results, but it can't carry relevance ranking or faceting — it's not a search engine.
The inverted index plus native aggregations natively cover ranking, filtering, and faceting once search gets this compound.
Cassandra fits when write scaling matters most and queries follow fixed partition keys, but its secondary indexes can't handle compound filtering and relevance here.

q: Elasticsearch 里的「document」最准确的理解是？
options: 必须是网页或博客文章这类可被爬取的长文本
任意 JSON 对象，检索的最小单元
一张关系型数据库表
一个二进制文件
options_en: It must be long crawlable text like a web page or blog post
Any JSON object — the smallest unit you search over
A relational database table
A binary file
why: 别被字面意思误导：document 就是任意 JSON 对象（比如一本书的记录），是搜索的基本单元。
why_en: A document in Elasticsearch is just any JSON object, the basic unit of data you search over.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

q_en: In Elasticsearch, what is a document?
optionExplanations: 别被字面意思带偏：document 不局限于网页，图书、订单等结构化记录都能作为 document。
它就是任意一个 JSON 对象，是被搜索的最小单元——书、订单、日志都算数。
document 对应的其实是表里的一行，「表」这个类比留给 index，两者不是一回事。
document 存的是结构化 JSON，不是二进制文件，二进制附件要单独处理。
optionExplanations_en: Don't take the name literally — documents aren't limited to web pages; books, orders, and other structured records all qualify.
It's simply any JSON object, the smallest searchable unit — a book, an order, a log line, all count.
A document actually maps to a single row; the table analogy belongs to the index, not the document.
A document holds structured JSON, not binary data — binary attachments need separate handling.
scenario: 书店搜索：每本书的标题、作者、价格要作为一条记录写进 Elasticsearch 供检索。
scenario_en: In a bookstore search service, each book's title, author, and price goes into Elasticsearch as one searchable record.

q: Elasticsearch 的「index」类比关系型数据库里的什么？
options: 一行记录
一个字段
加速查询的 B-tree 辅助索引
一张表（文档的集合）
options_en: A single row
A single field
A B-tree auxiliary index for speeding up lookups
A table, a collection of documents
why: index 是文档的集合，搜索针对 index 执行——类比数据库表；注意这和「加速查询的辅助索引」是两个概念，术语被重载了。
why_en: An Elasticsearch index is a collection of documents that searches run against, analogous to a database table rather than an auxiliary index structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档的集合，类比关系型数据库里的一张表；注意与「加速查询的辅助索引」是两个概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a collection of documents, roughly analogous to a database table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

q_en: What does an Elasticsearch index map to in a relational database?
optionExplanations: index 对应的其实是 document 这一行，不是 index 本身，这里把两个概念搞混了。
字段对应的是 mapping 里的 field，不是 index 这一级抽象。
这是「索引」在数据库里的另一层含义（加速查询的结构），和 Elasticsearch 的 index 不是一回事。
它是文档的集合：一次搜索请求作用在某个 index 上，返回匹配的那些文档，最贴近数据库里的表。
optionExplanations_en: A single row actually corresponds to a document, not an index — the two get conflated here.
A field maps to a field definition inside mapping, not to the index level.
This is the other database meaning of 'index' — a lookup structure — a different, overloaded sense from Elasticsearch's index.
It's a collection of documents: a search runs scoped to one index and returns the matching documents — closest to a database table.
scenario: 书店系统要把 10 万本书的记录放进 Elasticsearch，先得决定用什么容器装这批文档。
scenario_en: A bookstore needs to put a hundred thousand book records into Elasticsearch and must first decide what container holds them.

q: 补全 Elasticsearch 客户端视角的核心概念：
text: 客户端四概念：{{document}} 是被搜索的 JSON 数据单元；{{index}} 是文档的集合（类比表）；{{mapping}} 是索引的 schema，定义每个可搜索 {{field}} 的类型与处理方式。
why: documents / indices / mappings / fields 是使用 ES 的第一层词汇表，mapping 决定「哪些字段可搜、按什么类型搜」。
why_en: Documents are the JSON units of data, indices are collections of documents, and the mapping is the schema defining each searchable field's type.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档的集合，类比关系型数据库里的一张表；注意与「加速查询的辅助索引」是两个概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a collection of documents, roughly analogous to a database table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引的 schema，定义每个字段的类型和处理方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mapping is the index's schema, defining each field's type and how it is processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档里的一个键值对，mapping 决定它是否可搜索、按什么类型搜索。

q_en: Fill in the core Elasticsearch concepts from a client point of view:

q: mapping 里 keyword 类型和 text 类型的关键区别是？
options: keyword 整值精确匹配、不分词；text 会分词进倒排索引，支持包含式查询
keyword 只能存储数字类型的数据，text 只能存储字符串类型的数据
无论字段内容长什么样，text 字段的全文查询速度总是比 keyword 的精确匹配更快
两者在底层实现上完全等价，只是取名习惯不同而已
options_en: Keyword is exact-match on the whole value and not tokenized; text is tokenized into the inverted index for contains-style search
Keyword can only store numeric-typed data and text can only store string-typed data
No matter what the field holds, text full-text queries are always faster than keyword exact matching
The two are completely equivalent under the hood, just named differently by convention
tradeoff: keyword 精确匹配 vs text 全文包含匹配
why: id、作者名这类要精确匹配的字段用 keyword（想成 hash 表）；标题这类要判断「是否包含某词」的字段用 text，会被分词进倒排索引。
why_en: Use keyword for exact-match fields like an id, and text for fields that need contains-style full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整值精确匹配的字段类型，不分词，适合 ID、状态这类值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A keyword field stores the whole value for exact matching without tokenization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 会被分词进倒排索引的字段类型，支持包含式全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A text field is tokenized into the inverted index to support full-text contains queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

q_en: In a mapping, what is the key difference between keyword and text fields?
optionExplanations: 同一字段既要精确过滤又要全文搜索时，会拆成 keyword 和 text 两个子字段分别处理。
两者都能存字符串，区别不在数据类型，而在是否分词进倒排索引。
没有单纯的快慢：精确过滤通常 keyword 更省，全文包含查询才需要 text。
若真的等价，mapping 就没必要区分这两种类型——本质区别是分词与否。
optionExplanations_en: When a field needs both exact filtering and full-text search, split it into a keyword sub-field and a text sub-field.
Both can store strings; the real difference isn't data type, it's whether the value gets tokenized into the inverted index.
There's no universal winner: keyword is usually cheaper for exact filters, while text is what you need for substring/full-text queries.
If they were truly equivalent, mapping wouldn't need two separate types — the real distinction is tokenization.
scenario: 书的 isbn 要精确匹配、title 要支持「包含某个词」的检索，mapping 得给两者选类型。
scenario_en: A book's isbn must match exactly while its title needs contains-style search, so the mapping must pick a type for each.

q: User 对象有 10 个字段，实际只按 2 个搜索，却把整个对象都映射进 mapping。后果是？
options: 多余字段会稀释相关性打分，让搜索返回错误的排序结果
写入请求会被直接拒绝，索引因此创建失败
8 个用不到的字段白占索引内存，性能变差、成本变高
完全没有任何影响，可以放心这样处理
options_en: The extra fields dilute relevance scoring and make search return the wrong ranking
Write requests would be rejected outright, failing to create the index
The eight unused fields waste index memory, hurting performance and raising cost
There would be no effect at all, and it is fine to do this
why: mapping 里每个字段都有索引和内存代价；只映射真正要搜索的字段，查询性能很大程度上就靠调 mapping。
why_en: Every mapped field costs index and memory overhead, so map only the fields you actually search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引的 schema，定义每个字段的类型和处理方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mapping is the index's schema, defining each field's type and how it is processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档里的一个键值对，mapping 决定它是否可搜索、按什么类型搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A field is a key-value pair in a document, whose searchability and type are set by the mapping.

q_en: What happens if a User object has 10 fields but only 2 are searched, and all 10 are mapped?
optionExplanations: mapping 大小不影响算分正确性，它带来的是资源开销问题，不是排序算错。
多余字段不会导致写入被拒绝，只是白白占用了内存。
8 个用不到的字段一样占索引和内存，query 性能和成本都会被拖累。
每个映射字段都有实打实的内存代价，「完全没影响」不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Mapping size doesn't affect scoring correctness — the real cost is resource overhead, not broken ranking.
Extra fields don't get writes rejected; they just waste memory silently.
Those 8 unused fields still get indexed and held in memory, dragging down query performance and driving up cost.
Every mapped field carries real memory cost — 'no impact at all' isn't true here.
scenario: User 文档每天写入千万条，线上只按 email 和 city 搜索，集群内存成本很敏感。
scenario_en: Ten million User documents land daily, only email and city are ever searched, and memory cost is tight.

q: 用一个不带参数的简单 PUT 创建索引时，默认配置是？
options: 无 mapping、5 个 shard、0 个 replica
动态 mapping、1 个 shard、1 个 replica（之后可再改）
创建索引前必须先手动写出完整的 mapping，否则这次 PUT 会直接报错失败
动态 mapping、10 个 shard、3 个 replica
options_en: No mapping, five shards, zero replicas
Dynamic mapping, one shard, one replica, all adjustable later
You must hand-write a complete mapping before creating the index, or the PUT will fail outright
Dynamic mapping, ten shards, three replicas
why: 默认是动态 mapping + 1 分片 + 1 副本，这些参数创建后还能更新；多数字段不该被搜索时就该显式设置 mapping。
why_en: A bare PUT creates an index with dynamic mapping, one shard, and one replica, all adjustable later.
codeSample:
PUT /books
# 不带 body：动态 mapping + 1 shard + 1 replica
# 等价于显式指定：
PUT /books
{ "settings": { "number_of_shards": 1, "number_of_replicas": 1 } }

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引的 schema，定义每个字段的类型和处理方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mapping is the index's schema, defining each field's type and how it is processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引水平拆分出的一份数据与索引结构，1:1 对应一个 Lucene 索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is a horizontal slice of an index's data and index structures, mapping one-to-one to a Lucene index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a full copy of a shard, used for failover and to share query load.

q_en: What are the defaults when you create an index with a simple PUT and no extra parameters?
optionExplanations: 默认不是 5 个分片、0 副本，这个数字记错了。
没给参数时会先套上动态 mapping、1 个分片和 1 个副本这三项起步配置，之后都能再调整。
mapping 可以留给动态推断，不是创建索引前必须先手写的东西。
10 个分片、3 个副本不是默认值，要显式配置才会有。
optionExplanations_en: The default isn't 5 shards and 0 replicas — that number is just wrong.
Leave the parameters out and you start with dynamic mapping, 1 shard, and 1 replica — all three stay adjustable later.
Mapping can be left to dynamic inference — it isn't a prerequisite you must hand-write before creating an index.
10 shards and 3 replicas aren't the default; you'd have to configure that explicitly.
scenario: 运维直接 PUT /books 建索引，没带任何 settings 或 mapping，现在要评估默认行为。
scenario_en: An operator creates an index with a bare PUT /books, no settings and no mapping, and now needs to know the defaults.

scenario: 书店系统：评论(review)很少被更新，但查书时经常要带着评论条件一起查。要决定评论放哪。
q: 更合适的建模是？
options: 把评论作为 nested 字段嵌进 book 文档
把评论拆分出来，单独建一个 review 专属 index
把评论整体存进 Redis 这样的键值缓存里
评论只落地在文件系统里，不做任何索引
options_en: Nest reviews as a nested field inside the book document
Split reviews out into their own dedicated review index
Store the whole reviews blob in a key-value cache like Redis
Land reviews only on the file system with no indexing at all
tradeoff: 查询效率（嵌套一起查）vs 更新代价（改评论要重写整个文档）
why: 评论「少更新、常随书一起查」时嵌套进 book 文档更高效——这是搜索版的范式化/反范式化取舍。
why_en: When reviews are rarely updated but frequently queried with books, nesting them inside the book document is the more efficient call.
whenOtherWins: 评论更新频繁时应单独建 index——嵌套方案每次改一条评论都要重写整个 book 文档，更新代价大。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把子文档数组当作独立文档索引的字段类型，保证多条件命中同一个子对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A nested field indexes each array element as its own hidden document so multiple conditions can match the same sub-object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

q_en: Which data model is the better fit?
scenario_en: In a bookstore system, reviews are rarely updated but are often queried together with books, so you need to decide where reviews should live.
optionExplanations: 评论少更新、又常跟书一起查时，嵌进 book 文档最省事：一次查询就拿到书和评论。
评论更新很频繁，或者要单独搜索评论本身时，才值得拆成独立 index。
Redis 能缓存热点读，但撑不起这里需要的全文和多条件搜索。
纯文件存储没有倒排索引，做不了条件过滤，等于放弃搜索能力。
optionExplanations_en: When reviews change rarely and are almost always queried alongside the book, nesting them in is simplest — one query returns both.
It's worth splitting reviews into their own index only when they update frequently or need to be searched independently.
Redis can cache hot reads, but it can't carry the full-text and multi-condition search this needs.
Plain file storage has no inverted index and can't do conditional filtering — that gives up search entirely.

scenario: 只想把某本书的 price 改成 14.99，不想读取和重发整个文档。
q: 该用哪个 API 调用？
options: PUT /books/_doc/{id} 并附上完整文档，把 title、author 等没改的字段一起重写
DELETE 后重新 POST 整个文档，中间会有短暂的数据空档期
POST /books/_update/{id}，body 只带 {"doc":{"price":14.99}}
PUT /books/_mapping 修改 price，但这改的是字段类型定义不是具体值
options_en: PUT the full document to /books/_doc/{id}, rewriting title, author, and every other unchanged field too
DELETE the document then POST the whole thing again, leaving a brief gap with no document
POST to /books/_update/{id} with only {"doc":{"price":14.99}}
PUT /books/_mapping to change price, but that changes the field's type definition, not its value
tradeoff: 部分字段更新（_update）vs 整文档替换（PUT）
why: _update 端点支持只传变更字段，不必先取整个文档；ES 是分布式、异步、并发系统，显式的更新语义能保证结果符合预期。
why_en: The update endpoint patches only the given fields without fetching the whole document first, which matters in a distributed, concurrent system.
whenOtherWins: 如果本来就要整体替换文档（全字段重建），直接 PUT 完整文档更直接，但要注意并发覆盖风险。

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

q_en: Which API call should you use?
scenario_en: You only want to change one book’s price to 14.99, without reading and resending the full document.
optionExplanations: 要整体替换文档、且手上已有完整内容时才用 PUT；这里只改一个字段，白白多一次读。
先删后建等于人为制造一个数据空档期，纯粹是更差的写法。
_update 端点只传变更字段，不用先取整份文档，就是为这种局部改动设计的。
_mapping 改的是字段类型定义，不是某篇文档里的具体值。
optionExplanations_en: PUT the full document only when you're replacing it wholesale and already have the complete content — here it's one field, so that's a wasted round trip.
Delete-then-recreate manufactures a gap where the document doesn't exist — strictly worse than updating in place.
The _update endpoint only needs the changed field, no need to fetch the whole document first — built exactly for a partial edit like this.
_mapping changes a field's type definition, not the value inside one document.

q: 写入返回的 _version 字段配合 ?version=N 更新，实现的是什么机制？
options: 悲观锁：更新前必须先锁住整份文档，其他并发写入排队等待
乐观并发控制：版本不匹配就报错，客户端处理冲突后重试
服务端自动合并两个并发写入的冲突内容
只是写入成功后的持久化确认回执而已
options_en: Pessimistic locking: it must lock the entire document first while other concurrent writes queue up
Optimistic concurrency control: a version mismatch fails the write for the client to retry
The server automatically merges the conflicting content of two concurrent writes
Merely a durability acknowledgment sent back after the write succeeds
why: 带版本条件的更新只在版本匹配时生效，否则抛错——这是乐观并发控制的典型例子，把冲突交给客户端重试。
why_en: Conditional updates on the version field are optimistic concurrency control: a mismatch fails the write and lets the client retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 给每个文档维护的版本号，配合乐观并发控制使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The version field is a per-document counter Elasticsearch uses for optimistic concurrency control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先假设不会冲突，写入时校验版本号，不匹配就报错让客户端重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency control assumes no conflict and lets a version mismatch fail the write for the client to retry.

q_en: What mechanism do _version and ?version=N implement for updates?
optionExplanations: 校验不持锁，不会阻塞其他并发写入，这不是悲观锁。
版本号对不上就直接报错，冲突交给客户端处理后重试——典型的乐观并发控制。
ES 不会替你合并两个并发写，它只拒绝携带过期版本号的那次写。
持久化确认是另一件事，跟这里的版本校验无关。
optionExplanations_en: The check doesn't hold a lock and won't block other concurrent writers — this isn't pessimistic locking.
A version mismatch just errors out and pushes conflict resolution back to the client to retry — textbook optimistic concurrency control.
Elasticsearch won't merge two concurrent writes for you; it only rejects the one carrying a stale version.
Durability confirmation is a separate concern, unrelated to this version check.
scenario: 两个后台任务可能同时改同一本书的库存字段，后写的不能静默盖掉先写的。
scenario_en: Two background jobs may update the same book's stock field at once, and the later write must not silently clobber the earlier one.

q: 不带版本条件、直接 PUT 整个文档来更新，主要风险是？
options: 文档会被拆成两份互相独立的副本
索引会损坏，必须整体重建才能恢复
写入会立刻失败并返回一个版本冲突错误
并发更新时悄悄覆盖别人的修改（丢更新）
options_en: The document gets split into two independent copies
The index becomes corrupted and needs a full rebuild to recover
The write immediately fails and returns a version conflict error
It silently overwrites a concurrent writer's changes, a lost update
why: 另一个进程同时更新同一文档时，不带版本条件的整文档 PUT 会把对方的修改直接覆盖；用 _version 条件更新能防住。
why_en: A full-document PUT without a version check can silently overwrite a concurrent writer's changes.

q: 要按「计算出来的值」排序（比如打折后的价格），Elasticsearch 提供什么机制？
options: 服务端不支持计算排序，只能把数据全部拉到客户端排序
必须先在数据库层建好物化视图才能按此排序
直接借用关系型数据库 SQL 里的 ORDER BY 表达式语法
_script 排序：用 Painless 脚本算出排序值
options_en: The server has no computed sort, so all data must be pulled to the client to sort
You must first build a materialized view at the database layer before sorting this way
Directly borrow the ORDER BY expression syntax from relational SQL
Script-based sorting: compute the sort value with a Painless script
why: 脚本排序用 Painless 语言按文档字段计算排序值（如 price * 0.9），适合按派生值排序的场景。
why_en: Script-based sorting uses the Painless language to sort by a computed value such as a discounted price.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 内置的脚本语言，用于按计算值排序等场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Painless is Elasticsearch's built-in scripting language, used for things like sorting by a computed value.

q_en: What Elasticsearch mechanism sorts by a computed value, such as a discounted price?
optionExplanations: ES 原生就支持服务端计算排序，不用把全量数据拉到客户端处理。
物化视图是数据库层的手段，不是 ES 提供的排序机制。
ES 查询 DSL 是 JSON，没有 SQL 的 ORDER BY 表达式语法。
_script 排序用 Painless 脚本按文档字段现算排序值，比如 price * 0.9。
optionExplanations_en: Elasticsearch natively supports server-side computed sorting — you don't need to pull everything to the client.
A materialized view is a database-layer trick, not something Elasticsearch offers for sorting.
The ES query DSL is JSON — there's no SQL-style ORDER BY expression syntax.
_script sorting runs a Painless script over document fields to compute the sort value on the fly, like price * 0.9.
scenario: 商品列表要按「打折后价格 = price × 0.9」排序，但索引里只存了原价字段。
scenario_en: A product list must sort by the discounted price, price times 0.9, but only the original price field is indexed.

q: 按 nested 字段排序（如按书的最高评论评分）时，为什么必须用 nested sort（带 path + mode）？
options: 不这样写查询请求会直接被服务端拒绝并报语法错误
保证排序值来自同一个嵌套对象，并用 mode（如 max）决定多条评论取哪个值
带上 path 和 mode 只是为了让排序性能更好而已
nested 类型的字段在 Elasticsearch 里默认根本不能参与排序
options_en: Without it, the server rejects the request outright with a syntax error
It scopes the sort values to one nested object and uses a mode like max to pick a value
Adding path and mode is purely a performance nicety, nothing semantic
Nested-typed fields cannot take part in sorting at all by default in Elasticsearch
why: nested sort 指定 path 进入嵌套文档，mode: max 表示取每本书评论里的最高分作为排序值。
why_en: A nested sort scopes the sort values to the same nested object and uses a mode like max to pick one value per parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把子文档数组当作独立文档索引的字段类型，保证多条件命中同一个子对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A nested field indexes each array element as its own hidden document so multiple conditions can match the same sub-object.

q_en: Why does sorting by a nested field require nested sort with path and mode?
optionExplanations: 不带 path 未必直接报语法错，但排序语义会算错，问题不在报错本身。
path 限定排序值必须来自同一条嵌套评论，mode（如 max）再决定多条评论时取哪个值。
这里关键是语义正确，不只是为了让查询跑得更快。
nested 字段其实可以参与排序，只是必须显式带上 path 和 mode。
optionExplanations_en: Omitting path won't necessarily throw a syntax error, but the sort semantics come out wrong — the issue isn't a parse failure.
path pins the sort value to a single nested review, and mode (like max) decides which value wins when a book has several.
The point here is semantic correctness, not just making the query faster.
Nested fields can actually be sorted — it just requires explicitly specifying path and mode.
scenario: 一本书挂着多条 nested 评论，列表要按「这本书最高的一条评论评分」排序。
scenario_en: A book carries many nested reviews, and the listing must sort by the highest review rating on that book.

scenario: 商品列表用 from/size 分页，产品要求支持翻到很深的历史结果页。
q: from/size 分页的性能拐点在什么规模？超过后该怎么应对？
options: 性能拐点在 100 条左右，超过这个规模就要马上换游标分页
拐点约 10,000 条，之后该换 search_after 游标分页
拐点要到 1,000 万条以上才出现，在那之前完全不必处理分页深度
分页效率跟深度完全无关，压根不存在这样一个拐点
options_en: The tipping point is around one hundred results, past which you must switch to cursor pagination right away
The tipping point is around ten thousand results, after which you switch to search_after cursor pagination
The tipping point only appears past ten million results, so nothing about page depth needs handling before that
Pagination efficiency has nothing whatsoever to do with depth, so no such tipping point exists at all
why: 超过约 10,000 条后，集群每次都要取回并排序前面所有文档，代价高得难以接受——这个规模起就该换 search_after 之类的游标分页。
why_en: Beyond roughly ten thousand results, from-size pagination becomes prohibitively expensive because all preceding documents must be fetched and sorted, which is the point to switch to a cursor like search_after.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最简单的分页方式，from 是起始偏移，size 是每页条数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: From-size pagination specifies a starting offset and a page size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search-after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the starting point for the next page.

q_en: At what scale does from/size pagination become painful, and what should replace it?
scenario_en: A product list uses from/size pagination, and the product requirement says users can jump deep into historical result pages.
optionExplanations: 100 条量级远没到深分页真正变贵的地方，拐点被大幅低估。
约 10,000 条起，取回排序前面全部文档的代价就明显爬升，该换游标分页。
拖到 1,000 万条才处理，中间已经积累了大量深分页请求，代价被严重低估。
深度其实直接决定了要排序和丢弃多少文档，不存在「和深度无关」这回事。
optionExplanations_en: 100 rows is well below where deep paging actually gets expensive — this understates the threshold badly.
Past roughly 10,000 rows, the cost of retrieving and sorting everything before that page climbs sharply — time to switch to cursor-based paging.
Waiting until 10 million rows lets a huge number of expensive deep-page requests pile up first — this threshold is way too high.
Depth is exactly what determines how many documents get sorted and discarded — there's no such thing as depth not mattering.

q: from/size 深分页为什么昂贵？
options: 每次都要取回并排序目标页之前的全部文档再丢弃
深分页查询会给整张索引加写锁，阻塞其他写入
翻到很深的页会主动触发一次代价高昂的段合并
客户端必须在本地缓存住之前翻过的全部页结果
options_en: Each request retrieves and sorts every document before the target page, then throws them away
A deep-page query takes a write lock on the whole index, blocking other writes
Paging very deep proactively triggers an expensive segment merge
The client must cache every previously fetched page locally
why: 取第 1000 页意味着先算出前 999 页再丢弃，排序和取回的开销随深度线性增长。
why_en: Fetching a deep page forces the cluster to retrieve and sort every preceding document on each request and then discard them.
diagram:
flowchart LR

termDefinitions.meaning: 最简单的分页方式，from 是起始偏移，size 是每页条数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: From-size pagination specifies a starting offset and a page size.

q_en: Why is deep pagination with from/size expensive?
optionExplanations: 取第 1000 页要先算出并排好前 999 页再丢弃，开销随深度线性增长。
Elasticsearch 的搜索不会给整张索引加行级锁。
分页查询本身不会主动触发段合并。
这是服务端重复计算的问题，不是要客户端在本地缓存全部翻页结果。
optionExplanations_en: Getting page 1000 means computing and sorting all 999 pages before it, then discarding them — cost grows linearly with depth.
Elasticsearch search doesn't take a row-level lock across the whole index.
Pagination itself doesn't trigger a segment merge.
This is server-side repeated computation, not a requirement for the client to cache every prior page locally.
scenario: 搜索结果页要让用户翻到第 1000 页，每页 20 条，请求写 from=19980&size=20。
scenario_en: A results page lets users jump to page 1000 at twenty per page, issuing from=19980 and size=20.

scenario: 结果列表可能翻到几万条深，不需要随机跳页，只要顺序往后翻且高效。
q: 该用哪种分页方式？
options: 继续用最基础的 from/size 分页，靠加大 size 硬扛
每翻一页都重新执行一次全量查询再截取
search_after：用上一页最后一条的 sort 值做起点
干脆把几万条结果一次性全部拉回客户端
options_en: Keep basic from/size pagination and just crank up the page size
Re-run the full query from scratch and slice it on every page
search_after, starting from the previous page's last sort values
Just pull all tens of thousands of results back to the client at once
tradeoff: 深分页效率 vs 是否支持随机跳页
why: search_after 用上一页末尾的 sort 值圈定「之后的文档」，逐页收缩搜索集，深分页依然高效。
why_en: Search-after starts each page from the previous page's last sort values, staying efficient even for very deep pagination.
whenOtherWins: 需要随机跳到任意页且深度很浅时，from/size 更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 最简单的分页方式，from 是起始偏移，size 是每页条数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: From-size pagination specifies a starting offset and a page size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search-after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the starting point for the next page.

q_en: Which pagination method should you use?
scenario_en: The result list may go tens of thousands of hits deep, does not need random page jumps, and only needs efficient forward paging.
optionExplanations: 浅分页、需要随机跳页时 from/size 还行，但翻到几万条深时会明显变慢，不满足这里的要求。
每页都重新付出一次全量查询的代价，比 from/size 还差，没利用上一页的信息。
search_after 拿上一页最后一条的排序值当起点，逐页收缩搜索集，深度不影响单页成本。
几万条一次性拉回客户端不现实，也违背了做分页的初衷。
optionExplanations_en: from/size is fine for shallow, random-access paging, but it visibly slows down tens of thousands of rows deep — doesn't fit here.
Re-running the full query every page pays even more than from/size and wastes what the previous page already told you.
search_after starts from the last row's sort value and shrinks the search window page by page — depth doesn't raise the per-page cost.
Pulling tens of thousands of rows back in one shot isn't practical, and it defeats the point of paging at all.

q: search_after 参数的值从哪里来？
options: 服务端生成并下发给客户端的、带过期时间的一次性随机 token
上一页最后一条的 sort 字段值（如 [时间戳, _id]）
用页码乘以每页大小算出的一个偏移量
上一次请求返回的 PIT 快照 ID
options_en: A one-time random token with an expiry that the server generates and hands to the client
The sort field values of the previous page's last document, such as [timestamp, _id]
An offset computed by multiplying the page number by the page size
The PIT snapshot id returned by the previous request
why: 首次查询不带 search_after；之后每页把上一页最后一条的 sort 值（例如 date + _id）作为下一页起点。
why_en: Each next page passes the sort values of the previous page's last document, such as its timestamp and id.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search-after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the starting point for the next page.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定一个时间点的数据快照，配合 search_after 实现一致的深分页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point-in-time snapshot fixes a consistent view of the data for paging with search-after.

q_en: Where does the search_after value come from?
optionExplanations: search_after 是无状态机制，服务端不会为它生成 token 下发。
客户端从上一页结果里取出最后一条的 sort 字段值（比如时间戳+_id），下次请求传回去。
按页码乘每页大小算偏移量是 from/size 的算法，不是 search_after 的原理。
PIT 快照 ID 是另一个独立参数，search_after 本身不依赖它。
optionExplanations_en: search_after is stateless — the server doesn't hand out a token for it.
The client pulls the last hit's sort values from the previous page (say, timestamp plus _id) and sends them back on the next request.
Multiplying page number by page size is the from/size algorithm, not how search_after works.
A PIT snapshot ID is a separate parameter — search_after doesn't depend on it by itself.
scenario: 结果按 [时间戳, _id] 排序，要用 search_after 取下一页，客户端得知道游标值从哪来。
scenario_en: Results are sorted by timestamp and _id, and to fetch the next page with search_after the client must know where the cursor value comes from.

q: 关于 search_after 分页，哪些说法正确？（多选）
options: 深分页高效：每页只取上一页之后的文档
只能向前翻页，不能随机跳到第 N 页
服务端为每个客户端保存游标状态
客户端要自己记住上一页最后一条的 sort 值
options_en: Deep paging stays efficient because each page only fetches documents after the previous one
You can only page forward, never jump to page N
The server keeps per-client cursor state
The client must remember the previous page's last sort values
why: search_after 把状态放在客户端（记 sort 值）、只能前进；若底层数据更新删除，之前页的文档还可能被漏掉——要一致快照得用 PIT。
why_en: Search-after is efficient and duplicate-free but forward-only, with the client keeping the last sort values rather than the server holding cursor state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search-after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the starting point for the next page.

q_en: Which statements about search_after pagination are correct? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 深分页高效：每页只处理上一页之后的增量部分，不用重新排前面的文档。
只能往前翻，不支持随机跳到第 N 页——这是它比 from/size 少的能力。
实际上服务端不保存游标状态，是无状态机制，这个说法反了。
游标状态在客户端：要自己记住并传回上一页最后一条的 sort 值。
optionExplanations_en: Deep paging stays fast because each page only processes the increment after the last one — no re-sorting everything before it.
It's forward-only — no jumping to page N — that's the capability it trades away versus from/size.
The server actually doesn't hold cursor state — search_after is stateless, so this claim is backwards.
The cursor state lives on the client: it has to remember and resend the previous page's last sort value.
scenario: 日志检索要顺序翻几十万条结果，客户端是不保存会话状态的 Web 前端。
scenario_en: A log search pages sequentially through hundreds of thousands of results from a stateless web front end.

scenario: 要在索引持续写入的同时完整导出一批搜索结果，翻页过程中不能因数据变动而漏掉或重复文档。
q: 最合适的分页机制是？
options: 继续沿用最基础的 from/size 分页
不带 PIT 的纯 search_after 游标，翻页时完全靠客户端自己做结果去重
每翻一页都独立重新跑一次搜索查询
PIT（point in time）+ search_after 游标
options_en: Keep using the most basic from/size pagination
Plain search_after with no PIT, relying entirely on the client to dedupe results while paging
Independently re-run the search query fresh on every page
A PIT (point in time) cursor combined with search_after
tradeoff: 一致性快照的额外开销 vs 翻页期间数据可能变动
why: PIT 固定一个时间点视图（keep_alive 续期，用完 DELETE 释放），配合 search_after 翻页，即使索引在更新也能保持一致——代价是更多服务端开销。
why_en: A point-in-time snapshot combined with search-after gives a consistent view across pages even while the index is being updated.
whenOtherWins: 不要求一致快照时，纯 search_after 更轻量——PIT 的状态维持是实打实的额外开销。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point-in-time snapshot fixes a consistent view of the data for paging with search-after.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。

q_en: Which pagination mechanism best fits this export job?
scenario_en: You need to export a full batch of search results while the index is still receiving writes, without missing or duplicating documents during paging.
optionExplanations: 浅分页、索引不太变时还能用，但这里翻页又慢又不保证一致，不满足要求。
只要高效前进、不要求跨页一致时可以单用它，但索引更新期间仍可能漏掉或重复文档。
每页独立重新查询，不同页可能基于不同时刻的数据，结果会漂移。
PIT 固定住一个时间点视图，配合游标翻页，导出全程基于同一份快照，索引更新也不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Fine for shallow paging with a stable index, but here it's both slow and non-consistent — doesn't meet the requirement.
Good enough alone when you only need forward efficiency, not cross-page consistency — index updates mid-export can still drop or duplicate rows.
Re-running the query independently each page means different pages can reflect different moments — the result drifts.
PIT pins a fixed point-in-time view, and paging through it with a forward cursor means the whole export runs against one consistent snapshot even while the index keeps changing.

q: Elasticsearch 与 Apache Lucene 的分工是？
options: Elasticsearch 是 Lucene 之上的分布式编排层：集群协调、聚合；搜索内核归 Lucene
Elasticsearch 从零自研了一整套倒排索引与搜索内核，完全不依赖 Lucene 这个第三方库
Lucene 承担分布式集群协调的职责，Elasticsearch 负责底层倒排索引
Elasticsearch 和 Lucene 是市场上互相竞争的两款独立产品
options_en: Elasticsearch is a distributed orchestration layer over Lucene handling cluster coordination and aggregations, while Lucene provides the search core
Elasticsearch built its own full inverted index and search core from scratch and does not depend on the Lucene third-party library at all
Lucene takes on distributed cluster coordination while Elasticsearch handles the underlying inverted index

q_en: How do Elasticsearch and Apache Lucene split responsibilities?
optionExplanations: 它是搭在 Lucene 之上的分布式编排层：集群协调、接口、聚合和实时能力归它管，核心搜索交给 Lucene 完成。
实际上 ES 深度依赖 Lucene 做底层搜索，不是从零自研的内核。
分布式协调是 ES 的职责，倒排索引才是 Lucene 的活，这里说反了。
Lucene 是被嵌入使用的库，不是和 ES 竞争的独立产品。
optionExplanations_en: It's the distributed orchestration layer sitting on top of Lucene — cluster coordination, the API surface, aggregations, and real-time features are its job, while core search execution belongs to Lucene.
Elasticsearch actually depends heavily on Lucene for search internals — it isn't a from-scratch engine.
Distributed coordination is Elasticsearch's job and the inverted index is Lucene's — this has it backwards.
Lucene is an embedded library, not an independent product competing with Elasticsearch.

q: 以下哪些是 Elasticsearch 的节点类型？（多选）

Gateway 节点
Coordinating 节点
Ingest 节点
options_en: Master node
Gateway node
Coordinating node
Ingest node
why: 五种节点类型：Master（集群管理）、Data（存数据）、Coordinating（请求协调）、Ingest（数据摄入转换）、Machine Learning；没有 Gateway 节点。
why_en: Elasticsearch nodes come in five types: master, data, coordinating, ingest, and machine learning.

专门负责跑机器学习模型的推理任务
options_en: Storing every document in the cluster on its own local disk
Cluster-level operations like adding nodes and creating indices — the cluster's admin
Single-handedly executing every search request in the cluster
Dedicated to running machine learning model inference jobs
why: Master 是唯一能执行集群级操作的节点；数据存储在 Data 节点，搜索入口在 Coordinating 节点。
why_en: The master node is the cluster admin, the only node that performs cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices.

It's the only node type that can add/remove nodes or create/delete indices — the cluster's admin.
Receiving and dispatching search requests is the coordinating node's work, not Master's.
ML inference is handled by dedicated ML nodes, unrelated to Master.

Taking part in the leader-election vote among master-eligible nodes to decide who becomes master
The cluster's front end: receiving requests, parsing queries, routing, and merging results
Handling only write requests, never search requests
why: Coordinating 节点是用户请求的入口：解析查询、决定该问哪些节点、汇总排序结果——搜索的「前台」。

q_en: Which node role handles transformation and preprocessing before indexing?
optionExplanations: 它负责摄入管道里的转换和预处理，处理完的数据才轮到 Data 节点落盘索引。

Coordinating 负责查询路径，不负责写入前的预处理。

Coordinating handles the query path, not pre-write processing.
