  C -->|"no"| B
  C -->|"yes"| D["DLQ"]
optionExplanations: 有些任务无论重试多少次都会失败，DLQ 就是把它们隔离出去，别再占用 worker。
响应太快从来不是问题，这个选项本身就不是长任务系统会遇到的场景。
job_id 是提交时系统返回给客户端的，跟 DLQ 要解决的问题完全无关。
缺字段是数据库设计问题，跟隔离反复失败任务的 DLQ 机制不是一码事。
optionExplanations_en: Some jobs will fail no matter how many times you retry them; a DLQ isolates them so they stop eating up worker capacity.
Responding too fast was never the issue — this scenario doesn't even come up in a long-running task system.
The job_id is handed back to the client at submission time, which has nothing to do with what a DLQ solves.
A missing column is a database-design problem, not what the DLQ mechanism for isolating repeatedly failing jobs addresses.

scenario: DLQ 的重试上限要选一个具体数字；这个数字本身不是重点，重点是选 0、选很小、选很大分别会带来什么后果。
scenario_en: A DLQ needs a concrete retry limit; the important part is what happens if that number is zero, tiny, or unlimited.
q: 为什么 DLQ 的重试上限通常设在 3-5 次，而不是 0 次或无限次？
q_en: Why are DLQ retry limits often around 3-5 attempts instead of zero or unlimited?
options: 0 次误杀抖动，无限次被 poison job 占满
重试次数必须和 worker 机器数量保持严格一致
重试次数越多永远越安全，完全没有任何代价
DLQ 只是用来存放已经成功完成的历史任务
options_en: 0 retries kills jobs on any brief blip; unlimited retries lets a poison job hog every worker.
The retry count must always match the number of worker machines.
More retries is always strictly safer with no downside.
A dead letter queue is only where already-completed jobs are stored.
why: 3-5 次能覆盖短暂错误（网络抖动、临时限流），又不会让永久坏数据无限占用 worker。这个次数是后续告警和 DLQ 容量规划的基数，具体值取决于任务成本和错误类型。
why_en: Jobs commonly move to a dead letter queue after about three to five failed attempts, balancing transient-error tolerance against wasted worker time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络或依赖服务的短暂、偶发性失败，重试一两次通常就能恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blip is a brief, transient failure in the network or a dependency that usually recovers after one or two retries.

optionExplanations: 两个极端都不行：0 次会把可自愈的临时抖动直接判死，无限次又养着坏任务耗光 worker。
重试次数是任务层面的策略，跟当前有多少台 worker 机器没有绑定关系。
重试越多代价越高——占用 worker 时间更久，故障恢复也拖得更慢。
DLQ 存的是反复失败的坏任务，不是处理完成的历史记录，两者用途相反。
optionExplanations_en: Neither extreme works: 0 retries kills a self-healing blip outright, unlimited retries lets a bad job hog workers forever.
The retry count is a per-task policy choice, with no inherent tie to how many worker machines happen to exist.
More retries isn't free — it burns more worker time and drags out recovery from real failures.
A DLQ holds jobs that keep failing, not a record of completed history — those are opposite purposes.

scenario: 支付回调队列刚接上 DLQ，运维要决定给它配哪些常驻告警。
scenario_en: The payment callback queue just got a DLQ, and ops has to decide which standing alerts to put on it.
q: DLQ 设计中应该持续监控哪些信号？（多选）
q_en: Which signals should you keep monitoring in a DLQ design? (Select all that apply.)
options: DLQ depth 是否在持续增长
失败原因的分布情况
从 DLQ 修复后重新投递回主队列的流程
完全忽略 DLQ，因为它只存垃圾数据
options_en: Whether DLQ depth keeps growing over time.
The distribution of failure reasons.
The process for redriving fixed jobs from the DLQ back to the main queue.
Ignore the DLQ entirely since it only holds garbage.
why: DLQ 是生产故障信号，不是垃圾桶。持续增长意味着系统需要人工调查、代码修复或数据清洗。
why_en: A growing dead letter queue is an operational signal that needs investigation and repair.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 DLQ 里已经修复的任务重新投递回主队列继续处理的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A redrive moves a fixed job from the dead letter queue back into the main queue for reprocessing.

optionExplanations: 持续增长说明有东西在系统性地坏掉，而不是偶发的一两次抖动。
同一种失败原因扎堆出现，往往指向一个具体的代码 bug 或坏数据源。
问题修好后要有明确路径把任务放回主队列，不然它们永远卡在 DLQ 里。
DLQ 增长恰恰是要调查的生产信号，当垃圾桶忽略只会让故障越滚越大。
optionExplanations_en: Steady growth signals something is breaking systematically, not just an occasional blip.
A cluster of the same failure reason usually points to one specific bug or a bad data source.
Once the underlying issue is fixed, there needs to be a clear path to put jobs back on the main queue, or they sit stuck forever.
Growth in the DLQ is exactly the production signal worth investigating; treating it as trash just lets the failure snowball.

scenario: 用户不耐烦，连续点击“Generate Report”三次，三个请求的输入参数完全一样。
scenario_en: An impatient user clicks Generate Report three times in a row, and all three requests have the same input parameters.
q: 如何避免为同一个业务意图重复创建三个 job？
q_en: How do you avoid creating three jobs for the same business intent?
options: idempotency key 命中就返回旧 job_id
盲目地为这三次连续点击分别创建三个互相独立的 job 记录
只在前端禁用按钮防重复，后端完全不做校验
随机丢弃两个请求且不给出任何响应状态
options_en: If a job with the same idempotency key already exists, return its old job_id.
Blindly create three separate, independent job records for the three consecutive clicks.
Only disable the button on the frontend, with zero backend validation.
Randomly drop two of the requests and return no response status for them.
why: idempotency key 把同一次业务意图映射到同一个 job。前端防抖有帮助，但后端必须兜底。
why_en: An idempotency key maps repeated submissions of the same operation to the existing job.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本来就允许多次独立执行且每次结果互不影响，可以不用合并，但仍要明确语义。
tradeoff: 去重换来一次性执行 vs 不去重更简单但可能重复扣款/发信

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识同一次业务操作的唯一键，重复提交带同样 key 的请求时用来判重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key uniquely identifies one business operation so repeated submissions can be deduplicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前端在短时间内合并/抑制重复触发的技巧，例如点击后禁用按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Debouncing is a frontend technique that suppresses duplicate triggers in a short window, like disabling a button after a click.

optionExplanations: 同一个 key 代表同一次业务意图，命中就直接把已有的 job_id 递回去。
三个请求参数完全一样却建三个 job，等于让同一份报表生成三遍。
前端禁用按钮能防手抖，但接口本身没校验，绕过前端照样能重复提交。
静默丢请求且不给状态，用户搞不清哪次点击成功了、哪次没反应。
optionExplanations_en: The same key means the same business intent, so a hit just hands back the existing job_id.
Three identical requests spawning three jobs means generating the same report three times over.
Disabling the button helps with an itchy trigger finger, but with no backend check, bypassing the frontend still duplicates.
Silently dropping requests with no status leaves the user unsure which click actually succeeded.

scenario: 队列是 at-least-once 交付，而任务内容是给用户扣款并发一封确认邮件。
scenario_en: The queue delivers at-least-once, and the job charges the user and sends a confirmation email.
q: 为什么 worker 执行本身也要尽量做成 idempotent？（多选）
q_en: Why should the worker execution itself be as idempotent as possible? (Select all that apply.)
options: worker 处理中崩溃后，job 很可能被别的 worker 重试
queue 交付语义通常是 at-least-once，本来就可能重复投递
重复发送邮件、重复扣款等 side effect 一旦发生代价很高
idempotent 设计能让任务从此永远不会失败
options_en: A worker that crashes mid-job will very likely have its job retried by another worker.
Queue delivery is typically at-least-once, so redelivery can happen on its own.
Side effects like duplicate emails or duplicate charges are expensive once they happen.
Being idempotent means the task can never fail from then on.
why: 异步系统里重复执行很正常。worker 应在发送邮件、写文件、扣款前检查是否已完成，或使用外部服务的 idempotency key。
why_en: Workers should be idempotent because retries and at-least-once delivery can repeat side effects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息交付语义：消息至少会被投递一次，可能重复，但不会丢失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery guarantees a message arrives one or more times — never lost, but possibly duplicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务执行过程中产生的外部可见影响，例如发邮件、扣款、写文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A side effect is an externally visible result of running a job, such as sending an email or charging a card.

optionExplanations: 崩溃后的重试是常态而不是意外，worker 的逻辑必须扛得住被再跑一次。
队列本身就承诺“至少一次”，这不是 bug，是它的设计契约。
邮件多发一封是烦，扣款多扣一次是真金白银的损失，代价不对等。
幂等解决的是重复执行的后果，不是让任务本身变得不会失败。
optionExplanations_en: A retry after a crash is the norm, not an edge case — worker logic has to survive being run again.
The queue itself only promises at-least-once delivery; duplication isn't a bug, it's the design contract.
One extra email is annoying, one extra charge is real money lost — the stakes aren't equal.
Idempotency handles the consequences of running twice; it doesn't make the task itself immune to failing.

scenario: 提交 job 时，客户端传入 idempotency_key，你要避免重复 job。
scenario_en: When submitting a job, the client sends an idempotency_key, and you need to avoid duplicate jobs.
q: 这段 submit_job 伪代码的关键语义是什么？
q_en: What is the key behavior in this submit_job pseudocode?
options: 先查 key，存在就返回旧 job_id，不存在才创建入队
每次调用都无条件创建一个新 job
key 只存在内存变量里，进程重启后就丢失
函数完全忽略 user_id 和 job_type 参数
options_en: Look up the key first; if it exists, return the old job_id — only create and enqueue when it doesn't.
Unconditionally create a brand-new job on every call.
Keep the key only in an in-memory variable that's lost on process restart.
The function completely ignores the user_id and job_type parameters.
codeSample:
def submit_job(user_id, job_type, data, key):
    existing = db.get_job_by_key(key)
    if existing:
        return existing.id
    job_id = db.create_job(user_id, job_type, data)
    db.store_idempotency_key(key, job_id)
    queue.push(job_id)
    return job_id
why: 幂等入口要在持久存储里建立 key -> job_id 映射。否则重复点击或网络重试会创建重复任务。
why_en: The idempotency key is persisted so repeated submissions return the same job instead of creating duplicates.
whenOtherWins: 实际实现还需要数据库唯一约束或事务，避免并发提交同一个 key 时竞态创建两个 job。
tradeoff: 持久化 key->job_id 映射防重复 vs 只在内存判重、重启即失效

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和它对应的 job_id 持久写入数据库，供后续查重使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: This call persists the key together with its job_id in the database so future submissions can be deduplicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个并发请求几乎同时执行同一段判重逻辑，都没查到已存在的 key，从而各自创建了一个 job。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is when two concurrent requests both check the key before either has written it, so each creates its own job.

optionExplanations: 代码先查库里有没有这个 key，命中直接复用旧 job，没命中才真正创建。
这段代码明明先做了 db.get_job_by_key 检查，并不是无脑每次都建。
代码用的是 db.store_idempotency_key 落库，不是内存变量，这个说法读错了实现。
两个参数都被传进 db.create_job 用来建立任务记录，并没有被忽略。
optionExplanations_en: The code checks the store for the key first — a hit reuses the old job, and only a miss creates a new one.
This misreads the code — it does call db.get_job_by_key first, it isn't creating unconditionally every time.
The code persists via db.store_idempotency_key, not an in-memory variable — this misreads what the implementation does.
Both parameters are passed straight into db.create_job to build the record; neither is ignored.

scenario: 促销期间入队速率是 worker 消费能力的 5 倍，队列占用的内存已逼近上限。
scenario_en: During a promotion, jobs arrive five times faster than workers can drain them, and the queue is close to its memory limit.
q: Backpressure 在 async worker 系统中具体指什么？
q_en: What does backpressure mean in an async worker system?
options: workers 忙不过来时，主动放慢或拒绝新 job
让 queue 无限增长，来者不拒
只在前端页面加一行 loading 提示文案，后端照旧全盘接收所有请求
让所有 worker 同时停止发送心跳
options_en: Actively slowing or rejecting new job intake when workers can't keep up.
Letting the queue grow without bound and accepting everything.
Just add a loading message on the frontend while the backend keeps accepting every request as before.
Having every worker stop sending heartbeats at the same time.
why: Backpressure 防止系统接受超过处理能力的工作。否则 queue 深度、等待时间和内存/存储成本都会失控。
why_en: Backpressure slows or rejects new job intake when workers cannot keep up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当下游处理能力跟不上时，主动放慢或拒绝新请求，防止队列无限堆积。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure slows or rejects new intake when downstream workers cannot keep up, preventing unbounded queue growth.

optionExplanations: 处理能力跟不上时主动踩刹车，宁可拒绝也不让积压无限扩大。
来者不拒看似友好，实际是把问题往后拖，queue 深度和等待时间会失控。
loading 文案只是遮住症状，系统内部该有的限流机制一个都没做。
停心跳只会让系统误判 worker 全体死亡，跟控制接入速率毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: When capacity can't keep up, actively hit the brakes — better to reject than let the backlog grow unbounded.
Accepting everything looks friendly but just defers the problem — queue depth and wait time spiral out of control.
A loading message only masks the symptom; none of the actual rate-limiting machinery gets built.
Stopping heartbeats just makes the system misjudge every worker as dead — it has nothing to do with throttling intake.

scenario: Black Friday 时 job 流量突然 10x，queue 已经堆到几百万，用户等待时间变成数小时。
scenario_en: During Black Friday, job traffic suddenly grows 10x; the queue has millions of items and users now wait for hours.
q: 应优先讨论哪些应对措施？
q_en: Which mitigations should you discuss first?
options: 按 queue depth autoscale，过深时限流/返回 busy
继续无条件接收所有新 job，队列先堆着再处理
只盯着单机 CPU 使用率，完全忽略 queue depth 这个真正的积压信号
直接删除队列里全部 pending 状态的 job
options_en: Autoscale on queue depth, and rate-limit or return busy once it's too deep.
Keep accepting every new job unconditionally and let the queue pile up first.
Watch only single-machine CPU usage and completely ignore queue depth, the signal that actually reflects backlog.
Simply delete every pending job in the queue.
why: queue depth 是 worker 系统的关键扩容指标。处理不过来时，扩容和限流要同时考虑。
why_en: Use queue depth for autoscaling and apply rate limits or busy responses when the backlog is too deep.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务可延迟数小时且用户可接受，可以继续排队，但仍要明确 SLA 和容量上限。
tradeoff: 扩容+限流保护系统吞吐 vs 无条件接收但拖垮延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列里还未被处理的任务数量，是衡量积压程度的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth is the number of unprocessed jobs waiting in the queue, the key backlog signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务承诺的量化指标，例如任务处理延迟的上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is a quantified service promise, such as a cap on job processing latency.

optionExplanations: 既扩容缓解压力，又在深度过高时限流兜底，两个手段一起上才稳。
堆积十倍流量不处理，等待时间只会从分钟变成小时，用户先崩溃。
CPU 高说明机器在忙，但排队多久要看 queue depth，光看 CPU 会踏空信号。
直接删掉排队中的任务等于让用户的报表请求凭空消失，代价太大。
optionExplanations_en: Scale out to relieve pressure and rate-limit once depth is too high — doing both together is what keeps it stable.
Letting a 10x spike pile up unprocessed turns wait time from minutes into hours, and users bail first.
High CPU shows the machine is busy, but how long jobs wait depends on queue depth — watching CPU alone misses the real signal.
Simply deleting queued jobs makes users' report requests vanish without a trace, which is too costly.

scenario: worker 大半时间在等外部 API，CPU 只有 30%，但用户抱怨任务要排半小时。
scenario_en: Workers spend most of their time waiting on an external API so CPU sits at 30%, yet users complain jobs queue for half an hour.
q: 为什么 worker pool 扩容通常看 queue depth，而不是只看 CPU 使用率？
q_en: Why does worker-pool scaling usually watch queue depth instead of only CPU usage?
options: queue depth 直接反映积压和等待时间，CPU 高时可能已经排队很久了
CPU 指标对系统来说完全没有任何参考价值
queue depth 这个概念只适用于 Web server，不适用于 worker
worker 进程运行时不会消耗任何 CPU 资源
options_en: Queue depth directly reflects backlog and wait time; by the time CPU is high, the queue may already be badly backed up.
The CPU metric has no reference value for the system whatsoever.
The concept of queue depth only applies to web servers, not to workers.
Worker processes consume no CPU resources while running.
why: 异步系统的用户体验取决于排队时延。CPU 是资源利用率信号，queue depth 才是工作积压信号。
why_en: Queue depth better captures backlog and wait time, while CPU alone can lag the actual service-level problem.
tradeoff: queue depth 反映积压/等待时间 vs CPU 只反映资源利用率

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器（CPU），CPU 使用率高只说明机器在忙，不直接说明有多少任务在排队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU is the processor; high CPU usage only shows the machine is busy, not how much work is backlogged.

optionExplanations: 用户体验取决于排多久队，而不是机器忙不忙，queue depth 才直接对应等待时间。
CPU 不是没用，它反映资源利用率，只是不能替代积压信号来做扩容判断。
queue depth 恰恰是给 worker 系统看的核心指标，跟 Web server 没关系。
worker 执行任务当然要吃 CPU，这个说法直接违背了进程运行的基本常识。
optionExplanations_en: User experience depends on how long jobs wait, not on how busy the machine looks — queue depth maps directly to wait time.
CPU isn't useless — it shows resource utilization, it just can't substitute for a backlog signal when deciding to scale.
Queue depth is precisely the core metric worker systems watch; it has nothing to do with being web-server-only.
Workers obviously burn CPU while executing jobs — this claim contradicts basic facts about how processes run.

scenario: 财务系统承诺 PDF 导出 1 分钟内出结果，而年终报表一跑就是 5 小时。
scenario_en: The finance system promises PDF exports within one minute, while the annual report takes five hours to run.
q: 把 5 秒 PDF 和 5 小时年终报表放进同一个 FIFO queue，会有什么问题？
q_en: What goes wrong if 5-second PDFs and 5-hour annual reports share one FIFO queue?
options: 短任务被拖成 head-of-line blocking
短任务因为体积小，一定会被优先处理完
worker 会自动感知任务耗时并识别出它们之间的优先级顺序
所有进入这个队列的任务都会变成 5 秒完成
options_en: Short jobs get stuck behind long ones, causing head-of-line blocking.
Short jobs are guaranteed to finish first just because they're smaller.
Workers automatically sense each job's duration and infer the priority order among them.
Every job entering this queue magically finishes in 5 seconds.
why: 长任务占住 worker，短任务排在后面会等很久。混合耗时任务需要分队列、优先级或拆分长任务。
why_en: Mixed short and very long jobs in one queue can cause head-of-line blocking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出队列，任务按到达顺序被处理，不区分耗时长短。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A FIFO queue processes jobs strictly in arrival order regardless of how long each one takes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队首的大任务卡住通道，后面排队的小任务被迫跟着等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Head-of-line blocking is when a big job at the front of the queue delays all the smaller jobs waiting behind it.

optionExplanations: 先到先服务的队列不管任务轻重，5 小时的任务堵在前面，后面的 5 秒任务只能干等。
FIFO 队列只看到达顺序，完全不看任务大小，这个说法搞反了排队规则。
worker 不会自己判断优先级，除非系统显式设计了优先级队列或调度逻辑。
队列不会改变任务本身的耗时，5 小时的报表进了 queue 还是要跑 5 小时。
optionExplanations_en: A strict first-come queue doesn't care about job size, so a 5-hour job at the front blocks a 5-second one stuck behind it.
A FIFO queue only looks at arrival order, never size — this gets the queuing rule backwards.
Workers don't infer priority on their own unless the system explicitly builds a priority queue or scheduler.
A queue doesn't shrink a job's actual runtime — a 5-hour report still takes 5 hours once it's in there.

scenario: 有些报告 5 秒完成，有些报告要跑 5 小时，你想保持 fast queue 的响应始终很快。
scenario_en: Some reports finish in 5 seconds and others run for 5 hours; you want the fast queue to stay responsive.
q: 应如何拆分 worker/queue？
q_en: How should you split the workers and queues?
options: 按耗时拆 fast/slow queue 分别配置
不管耗时长短，所有任务都塞进同一个 queue
先集中跑完所有 5 小时任务，再处理 5 秒任务
干脆取消对所有任务的状态跟踪机制
options_en: Split into a fast queue and a slow queue by duration, each with its own worker count.
Put every job into the same single queue no matter how long it takes.
Run all the 5-hour jobs to completion first, then handle the 5-second ones.
Simply stop tracking status for any task at all.
why: 拆队列能隔离不同 SLA 和资源需求。无法提前预测时，可先进入 fast queue，超过时间限制再迁移到 slow queue。
why_en: Separate queues by job type or expected duration to keep short jobs responsive and tune workers independently.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有任务耗时相近，单队列更简单，不用维护两套配置。
tradeoff: 拆分 fast/slow queue 隔离 SLA vs 单队列简单但短任务被拖累
codeSample:
queues:
  fast:
    max_duration: 60s   # keep this responsive
    worker_count: 50
  slow:
    max_duration: 6h    # fewer, beefier workers
    worker_count: 10

termDefinitions.meaning: 配给短任务、worker 数量多的队列，保证低延迟响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fast queue is dedicated to short jobs and staffed with many workers to keep latency low.

termDefinitions.meaning: 配给长任务、机器规格更强但 worker 数量较少的队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slow queue handles long jobs with beefier machines but fewer workers.

optionExplanations: 按耗时分流，fast queue 配多个轻量 worker，slow queue 配少量重型机器。
单队列正是长短任务互相拖累的根源，这个选项等于没解决问题。
先跑完所有长任务，短任务的用户要一直饿等，体验反而更糟。
取消状态跟踪跟拆队列毫无关系，还会让用户彻底看不到任何进度。
optionExplanations_en: Split by duration — the fast queue gets many light workers, the slow queue gets fewer, beefier machines.
A single shared queue is exactly the root cause of long jobs dragging down short ones; this doesn't fix anything.
Running every long job first just leaves short-job users starving even longer — the experience gets worse.
Dropping status tracking has nothing to do with splitting queues, and it also blinds users to any progress at all.

scenario: 生成报告需要 fetch data -> generate PDF -> email user 三个步骤，且每一步可能都要单独重试。
scenario_en: Report generation has three steps: fetch data, generate PDF, and email the user, and each step may need its own retry.
q: 这种简单链式依赖可以怎么实现？
q_en: How can you implement this simple chain of dependent jobs?
options: worker 完成后自排下一步，带上 workflow_id
把整条链的中间状态只保存在某个 worker 进程的内存变量里
任何一步失败都从第一步重新开始，且不记录失败原因
让客户端手动逐步触发链条中的每一个步骤
options_en: Each worker enqueues the next step itself, carrying a workflow_id in the context.
Keep the whole chain's intermediate state only in one worker process's in-memory variable.
Restart the entire chain from step one on any failure, without recording why.
Have the client manually trigger each step of the chain in sequence.
why: 简单链可以由前一步显式排下一步，并携带可重试上下文。复杂分支/并行流程再考虑 workflow orchestrator。
why_en: For simple chains, each worker can enqueue the next step with workflow context and retryable outputs.
whenOtherWins: 如果有复杂分支、并行、补偿或长期等待，用 Step Functions、Temporal 或 Airflow 更清晰。
tradeoff: worker 显式排下一步简单上线快 vs orchestrator 换来分支/可视化能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一整条多步骤任务链的 ID，各步骤 worker 用它关联上下游产物。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A workflow_id ties together every step of a multi-step job chain so workers can associate upstream and downstream outputs.

optionExplanations: 上一步做完就顺手把下一步入队，workflow_id 把整条链的产物串起来。
内存变量随 worker 进程消亡，这条链的状态一崩溃就彻底丢失。
从头重跑又不记原因，等于每次失败都要把已经成功的步骤白跑一遍。
让客户端手动驱动多步流程，网络一断或用户一走链条就卡死了。
optionExplanations_en: Each finished step simply enqueues the next, with the workflow_id threading the outputs together across the chain.
An in-memory variable dies with the worker process, so a crash wipes out the whole chain's state.
Restarting from step one with no recorded reason means redoing already-successful steps every single time it fails.
Having the client manually drive each step means the chain stalls the moment the connection drops or the user leaves.

scenario: 任务依赖出现分支、并行步骤、每步独立 retry 和可视化状态的需求，worker 之间互相 queue 下一步变得越来越乱。
scenario_en: Job dependencies now include branches, parallel steps, per-step retries, and visible state, so workers queueing each other is getting messy.
q: 这种情况下一步应该考虑引入什么？
q_en: What should you consider introducing next?
options: 引入 orchestrator（如 Temporal）
继续让流程分支逻辑散落在各个 worker 代码里维护
干脆删掉现有重试逻辑，让失败任务直接静默丢弃
把整条流程压缩成一个巨大的同步 HTTP 请求处理
options_en: Bring in a workflow orchestrator, such as Temporal.
Keep letting the branching logic stay scattered across worker code.
Just delete the existing retry logic and let failed jobs silently vanish.
Squeeze the entire flow into one giant synchronous HTTP request.
why: 复杂依赖会让手写链式 queue 变成 spaghetti。工作流系统集中表达流程、重试和状态可见性。
why_en: Complex branching or parallel job dependencies justify a workflow orchestrator.
whenOtherWins: 单步任务或简单线性链条用 queue + worker 就足够，不必引入 orchestrator。
tradeoff: 引入 orchestrator 换取分支/可视化能力 vs 增加一层基础设施复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的工作流编排服务，用状态机描述步骤、重试和分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS Step Functions is a managed workflow orchestrator that models steps, retries, and branching as a state machine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源工作流编排引擎，用普通代码定义长时间运行、可重试的业务流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is an open-source workflow engine that lets you define long-running, retryable business processes in ordinary code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用于数据管道调度的开源工作流编排工具，以 DAG 描述任务依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Airflow is an open-source workflow tool commonly used for data-pipeline scheduling, expressing task dependencies as a DAG.

optionExplanations: 分支、并行和可视化状态正是 orchestrator 的强项，把流程集中管理起来。
逻辑越散落在各处 worker 代码里，改一条分支就要满仓库找地方改。
删掉重试等于放弃故障恢复能力，失败任务从此没人知道也没人处理。
压成一个同步请求会立刻撞上超时问题，这正是本模式一开始要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: Branching, parallelism, and visible state are exactly what an orchestrator is built for — it centralizes the flow.
The more scattered the logic across worker code, the more files you have to hunt through to change one branch.
Dropping retries throws away fault recovery entirely — failed jobs vanish with nobody noticing or handling them.
Squeezing it into one synchronous request runs straight into the timeout problem this whole pattern exists to avoid.

scenario: 异步导出上线后 API latency 一直很漂亮，但用户投诉任务几小时不出结果。
scenario_en: After async exports shipped, API latency looks great, yet users complain results take hours to appear.
q: 异步 worker 系统必须监控哪些指标？（多选）
q_en: Which metrics must an async worker system monitor? (Select all that apply.)
options: queue depth / oldest job age
worker health / heartbeat
job failure rate / retry rate / DLQ depth
只监控前端页面的访问量
options_en: Queue depth and the age of the oldest job.
Worker health and heartbeat.
Job failure rate, retry rate, and DLQ depth.
Only frontend page view counts.
why: 异步系统的故障常表现为队列堆积、worker 死亡、失败重试或 DLQ 增长。只看 API latency 会漏掉后台问题。
why_en: Async systems need monitoring for backlog, worker health, failures, retries, and dead-letter queues.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列里等待最久的那个任务已经排队多长时间，直接体现最坏等待延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Oldest job age is how long the longest-waiting job has sat in the queue, showing the worst-case delay.

optionExplanations: 反映积压程度和最坏等待时长，是判断是否要扩容的第一信号。
worker 集体沉默往往意味着部署出问题或某个依赖挂了，得第一时间发现。
失败和重试变多、DLQ 变深，通常指向代码 bug 或某个下游依赖不稳定。
前端页面访问量跟后台任务是否堆积、失败毫无关系，看它会完全漏掉故障。
optionExplanations_en: It reflects backlog size and worst-case wait time — the first signal for deciding whether to scale.
Workers going silent as a group often means a bad deploy or a dead dependency, and needs catching immediately.
Rising failures and retries with a deepening DLQ usually point to a code bug or a flaky downstream dependency.
Frontend page views have nothing to do with whether background jobs are backing up or failing — watching only this misses the outage entirely.

scenario: 面试官说“我们每天处理 100 万张图片，每张处理耗时 10 秒”。
scenario_en: The interviewer says, "We process 1 million images per day, and each image takes 10 seconds to process."
q: 你应该如何主动用这两个数字推导架构结论？
q_en: How should you use those two numbers to derive an architecture conclusion?
options: 算出约 120 并发，需异步 worker pool
跳过任何吞吐量计算，直接断言现有单机硬件资源肯定够用
把所有图片处理逻辑都同步塞进登录服务器里去做
让用户干脆排队等上一整天，完全不做任何架构调整
options_en: Compute about 12 images/sec times 10 seconds, roughly 120 concurrent — needs an async worker pool.
Skip the math and just assert a single machine has plenty of headroom.
Process every image synchronously inside the login server.
Just make the user queue and wait an entire day, no architecture change.
why: 把规模和处理时间乘起来能暴露资源不匹配：日处理量转成每秒到达率，再乘处理时长就是同一时刻所需的并发工作量。这个数字是决定要不要上 worker pool 及配多少 worker 的依据。
why_en: Doing the throughput math shows image processing would saturate the web tier and should move to async workers.
whenOtherWins: 如果处理耗时只有几毫秒且流量低，同步路径可能仍可接受。
tradeoff: 提前用规模计算暴露瓶颈 vs 等 latency 恶化才被动处理

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一时刻正在被处理、还未完成的任务数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrency is the number of tasks being processed at the same instant, not yet finished.

optionExplanations: 到达率乘处理时长就能算出同一时刻的并发量，这是判断要不要拆异步 worker 的关键量级。
跳过计算直接下结论，等真上线撞上延迟暴涨才发现判断错了，代价更高。
图片处理跟登录服务本该分开扩容，硬塞一起会让登录也被拖慢。
面试官给你数字就是想看你怎么用它推导架构，放弃计算等于放弃这个信号。
optionExplanations_en: Arrival rate times processing time gives the concurrent load at any instant — that number is what decides whether you need a worker pool.
Skipping the math and just asserting it'll be fine means finding out you were wrong only after latency blows up in production.
Image processing and login should scale independently; cramming them together drags login down too.
When an interviewer hands you numbers, they want to see how you turn them into an architecture decision — skipping the math throws that signal away.

scenario: 面试白板上要判断：哪些题的核心操作慢到用户不能同步等着它返回。
scenario_en: On the interview whiteboard you have to judge which prompts have a core operation too slow for the user to wait on synchronously.
q: 哪些系统设计题里经常会用到 long-running tasks 模式？（多选）
q_en: Which system-design prompts commonly use the long-running tasks pattern? (Select all that apply.)
options: YouTube 的视频转码和缩略图生成
Instagram 的图片处理和 feed fanout
Dropbox 的文件病毒扫描、索引、预览生成
只读取用户昵称这一个字段
options_en: YouTube's video transcoding and thumbnail generation.
Instagram's image processing and feed fanout.
Dropbox's file virus scanning, indexing, and preview generation.
Reading just a single user nickname field.
why: 媒体处理、fanout、文件扫描/索引都耗时且可异步。简单读取用户昵称不需要 long-running task 模式。
why_en: Media processing, feed fanout, and file scanning are common long-running task scenarios.

termDefinitions.meaning: 作者发帖后把内容写扩散到大量粉丝各自 feed 里的过程，粉丝多时很耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feed fanout is writing a new post out to every follower's individual feed, which gets slow when follower counts are huge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从原始图片/视频派生出的小尺寸预览图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thumbnail is a small preview image derived from the original photo or video.

optionExplanations: 转码要产出多种分辨率/编码，缩略图生成也要解码渲染，都是分钟级计算。
粉丝多的账号一发帖，fanout 要写扩散到海量 feed，处理和分发都不是瞬时的。
扫描病毒、建索引、生成预览都要整份读取文件内容，体积一大就慢下来。
读一个昵称字段是索引命中的毫秒级查询，跟这些重计算场景完全不是一类。
optionExplanations_en: Transcoding produces multiple resolutions and encodings, and thumbnails need decode-and-render — both are minutes of compute.
When a high-follower account posts, fanout has to write the update to a huge number of feeds — neither the processing nor the distribution is instant.
Virus scanning, indexing, and preview generation all have to read the entire file, which gets slow as size grows.
Reading one nickname field is a millisecond indexed lookup, nothing like these heavy-compute scenarios.

scenario: 支付系统中，基础 card authorization 同步很快，但 fraud detection、3DS、webhook 通知和延迟结算会持续较久。
scenario_en: In a payments system, basic card authorization is fast, but fraud detection, 3DS, webhooks, and delayed settlement take longer.
q: 如何拆分这个系统的同步/异步边界？
q_en: How should you split the synchronous and asynchronous boundary in this system?
options: 授权同步返回，风控/通知/结算走 async
让支付的每一步都同步卡住用户，直到全部完成
让支付的每一步都异步，且永远不返回任何初始状态
完全不记录 payment 的处理状态
options_en: Keep the critical authorization synchronous, and move fraud checks, webhooks, and settlement to async workers.
Make every payment step synchronous and block the user until all of it completes.
Make every payment step async and never return any initial status at all.
Don't record the payment's processing status at all.
why: 支付经常混合同步和异步：用户需要及时知道初始状态，但后续风控、webhook 和 settlement 可以后台推进。
why_en: Payments often keep the immediate authorization synchronous while moving fraud checks, webhooks, and settlement to async workers.
whenOtherWins: 如果某一步影响用户是否可以继续下单且必须强一致，就不能随意把它异步化。
tradeoff: 关键授权同步保证即时反馈 vs 风控/结算异步换取可扩展性

termDefinitions.meaning: 银行卡在线支付的额外身份验证流程，常见于欧洲监管要求，会引入额外耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 3DS, or 3-D Secure, is an extra identity-verification step for online card payments that adds processing time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统间通过 HTTP 回调异步通知事件的机制，例如支付渠道通知结算结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback one system uses to asynchronously notify another of an event, like a settlement result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支付渠道之间真正完成资金转移和对账的后续流程，通常比授权慢得多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Settlement is the later process where money actually moves between payment parties and gets reconciled, much slower than authorization.

optionExplanations: 用户马上需要知道授权成不成功，风控和结算晚一点完成用户感知不到。
3DS、风控这些步骤本身就慢，全程同步等于让用户对着页面卡好几秒到几十秒。
授权结果不能异步——用户下一步要不要继续下单，取决于这个初始状态。
不记录状态等于支付出问题后没法排查，也没法给用户任何反馈。
optionExplanations_en: Users need to know right away whether authorization succeeded; fraud checks and settlement finishing a bit later is invisible to them.
Steps like 3DS and fraud checks are inherently slow, so going fully synchronous means the user stares at the page for seconds to tens of seconds.
Authorization can't be async — whether the user proceeds with the order depends on that immediate status.
Not recording status means there's nothing to investigate when a payment breaks, and nothing to show the user either.

q: 补全 long-running task 的一句话模式：
q_en: Fill in the one-sentence pattern for a long-running task.
text: 先{{接受并入队}}，立即返回{{job_id}}，再由{{worker pool}}异步处理，并更新{{job status}}。
why: 这是该模式的核心闭环：快速确认、后台执行、状态可查。
why_en: The pattern is accept and enqueue, return a job ID, process in workers, and update job status.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久化记录任务当前处于 pending/processing/completed/failed 中哪个阶段的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Job status is the persisted field tracking which stage — pending, processing, completed, or failed — a task is in.

scenario: Queue 服务短暂宕机的几秒内，Web server 仍然校验通过请求并在数据库里创建了 status='pending' 的 job 记录，但没能把 job_id 推进 queue。
scenario_en: For a few seconds while the queue is down, the web server still validates requests and creates status='pending' job rows, but cannot enqueue their job_ids.
q: 这批“卡在 pending”的任务后续要怎样才能被处理到？
q_en: How can these jobs stuck in pending get processed later?
options: 需要 poller 扫描 pending 记录，补偿逻辑重新入队
worker 会自动扫描数据库表，完全不需要额外机制
这些 pending 记录应该直接从数据库删除，让用户重新提交
queue 恢复正常后会自动找回所有丢失的 job_id
options_en: A poller needs to periodically scan pending records, or a compensation path re-enqueues them.
Workers will automatically scan the database table, no extra mechanism needed.
These pending records should just be deleted from the database, forcing users to resubmit.
Once the queue recovers, it will automatically recover all the lost job_ids on its own.
why: 如果接受请求和入队不是同一个原子动作，就要设计补偿路径。否则 pending job 可能永远不被处理。
why_en: If job creation can succeed while queueing fails, a poller or repair path must enqueue pending jobs later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期扫描数据库、把该处理但还没入队的记录重新补推给 queue 的后台进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A poller is a background process that periodically scans the database and re-enqueues records that should be processed but never made it to the queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要么全部成功要么全部失败、不会停在中间状态的一次操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic action either fully succeeds or fully fails, never leaving the system in a half-done state.

optionExplanations: 创建记录和入队不是一个原子操作，缺的那一步得靠专门的补偿机制补上。
worker 只消费 queue 里的消息，它默认不会主动去扫数据库表找漏掉的任务。
删掉记录等于让用户白白重新走一遍流程，浪费的是已经做完的校验工作。
queue 只知道自己收到过什么，它没办法凭空找回从未被推进来的 job_id。
optionExplanations_en: Creating the record and enqueueing it aren't one atomic step, so the missing piece needs a dedicated compensation path to fill in.
Workers only consume messages off the queue; by default they never proactively scan the database for jobs that slipped through.
Deleting the records just forces the user to redo the whole flow, wasting validation work that was already done.
The queue only knows what it actually received; it has no way to conjure up a job_id that was never enqueued in the first place.

scenario: 一个 API 查询用户 profile，耗时 30ms，用户必须立即看到结果。
scenario_en: An API reads the user's profile in 30ms, and the user must see the result immediately.
q: 这种场景是否应该引入 queue + worker？
q_en: Should this scenario introduce a queue plus workers?
options: 不应该，保持同步请求更简单、延迟也更低
必须无条件引入 queue
必须给这个请求返回 job_id
必须用 GPU worker 来处理这次查询
options_en: No — staying synchronous is simpler and has lower latency.
Yes, a queue must be introduced unconditionally.
Yes, this request must return a job_id.
Yes, a GPU worker must handle this lookup.
why: 长任务模式是为“超过几秒、资源不匹配或失败恢复复杂”的工作服务。30ms 的轻量同步读取不该被过度设计。
why_en: A 30-millisecond profile read should remain synchronous because queueing would add needless complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果 profile 请求背后触发了昂贵的 recomputation，可以把 recomputation 异步化，但读取本身仍应快返。
tradeoff: 同步简单直接、延迟最低 vs 引入 queue+worker 换来的扩展性此处用不上

termDefinitions.meaning: 为一个不需要额外复杂度的场景引入不必要的架构组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-engineering is adding architectural components a scenario doesn't actually need.

optionExplanations: 30ms 的读取本来就很快，同步直接返回结果，没有引入队列的必要。
无条件上 queue 是过度设计，给一个毫秒级查询增加了完全不必要的复杂度。
job_id 是给需要异步跟踪的长任务用的，套在瞬时完成的请求上没有意义。
读一行 profile 数据用不上 GPU，这个选项把资源类型完全用错了地方。
optionExplanations_en: A 30ms read is already fast; returning the result synchronously needs no queue at all.
Adding a queue unconditionally is over-engineering — it bolts needless complexity onto a millisecond-scale lookup.
A job_id is for long tasks that need async tracking; wrapping it around an instantly-finished request serves no purpose.
Reading one profile row has no use for a GPU — this option pairs the wrong resource type with the task entirely.

q: 按正确顺序排列一个失败 job 的处理生命周期：
q_en: Put the lifecycle of a failed job in the correct order.
steps: 超过最大次数后移入 DLQ，并报警/等待人工调查
Worker 崩溃或任务执行抛错
队列根据 heartbeat/visibility timeout 判定并重新投递
Worker 重试处理，job attempt count 增加
why: 异步失败处理要可控：先重试 transient failure，持续失败才隔离到 DLQ，避免拖垮整个 worker 队伍。
why_en: A failed job is redelivered, retried with an attempt count, and eventually isolated in a dead letter queue.
tradeoff: 先重试挽救短暂故障 vs 超限后隔离进 DLQ 保护 worker

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录一个 job 已经被重试过多少次的计数字段，用来判断是否该移入 DLQ。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Attempt count tracks how many times a job has been retried, used to decide when it should move to the DLQ.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Run job"] --> B["Fail"]
  B --> C["Record error"]
  C --> D["Retry with backoff"]
  D --> E["DLQ or success"]

scenario: 后台任务完成后，你希望用户不用手动刷新页面就能收到结果。
scenario_en: After a background job completes, you want the user to receive the result without manually refreshing the page.
q: 可以使用哪些方式主动通知用户？
q_en: What are good ways to proactively notify the user?
options: Email、push 或 WebSocket 推送
只把结果写进服务器日志，不告诉用户
只把最终结果保存在处理它的那个 worker 进程的内存里
什么都不做，让用户自己猜测完成时间
options_en: Email, push, or a realtime WebSocket/SSE update.
Only write the result to server logs and never tell the user.
Only keep the final result in the memory of the worker process that produced it.
Do nothing and let the user guess when it's done.
why: 异步任务完成和用户页面不在同一个请求里，需要额外通知或状态查询机制。实时需求高时可接入 realtime updates 模式。
why_en: Async job completion should notify users through email, push, or realtime updates, or be visible through status polling.
whenOtherWins: 低优先级任务可只提供状态页和邮件，不必上实时推送。
tradeoff: 主动实时推送体验好 vs 只提供状态页更轻量但要用户主动查

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器推送事件，服务器通过一条长连接单向持续推送更新给浏览器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, or Server-Sent Events, lets a server continuously push updates to the browser over one long-lived connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许服务器和浏览器保持长连接、双向实时推送消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that keeps a persistent, two-way connection open between server and browser for realtime pushes.

optionExplanations: 三种渠道覆盖不同紧急度：邮件适合不急的，push 适合移动端，WebSocket 适合实时更新。
日志是给工程师排查用的，普通用户根本看不到，等于没有通知。
worker 进程一重启或崩溃，存在内存里的结果就彻底没了。
什么都不做等于把等待和焦虑全部丢给用户自己承受。
optionExplanations_en: Three channels for different urgency levels — email for non-urgent, push for mobile, WebSocket for realtime updates.
Logs are for engineers to debug, not something an ordinary user ever sees — that's effectively no notification at all.
The moment the worker process restarts or crashes, anything held only in memory is gone for good.
Doing nothing just dumps all the waiting and anxiety onto the user to deal with alone.

scenario: 45 分钟的系统设计面试里你提出用 queue + worker 做异步处理，面试官立刻开始追问。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute system design interview you propose a queue plus workers, and the interviewer immediately starts drilling in.
q: 面试里主动提出 long-running task 模式时，应准备回答哪些 deep dive？（多选）
q_en: When you bring up the long-running task pattern in an interview, which deep dives should you be ready for? (Select all that apply.)
options: worker 崩溃后如何被重新分配和重试
poison message 如何最终被隔离进 DLQ
重复点击如何用 idempotency key 去重
queue 堆积时如何 backpressure/autoscale
options_en: How a crashed worker's job gets reassigned and retried.
How a poison message eventually gets isolated in the DLQ.
How repeated clicks get deduplicated with an idempotency key.
How to apply backpressure and autoscale when the queue backs up.
why: 提出 async workers 后，常见追问就是失败、重复、积压和混合任务。提前准备这些会显得设计成熟。
why_en: The common deep dives are crash retry, poison messages, idempotency, and backpressure.
optionExplanations: 面试官几乎必问：worker 说挂就挂，重试和重新分配的细节要讲得出来。
反复失败的坏任务怎么被发现、怎么被隔离，是故障处理成熟度的体现。
用户手抖点击三次，你的设计能不能保证只生成一份结果。
流量突然涨十倍，你是先扩容还是先限流，还是两个一起上。
optionExplanations_en: Interviewers almost always ask this: workers do crash, so be ready to walk through reassignment and retry.
How a repeatedly failing job gets detected and isolated shows maturity in your failure-handling design.
If a user fumbles and clicks three times, can your design guarantee only one result gets produced.
When traffic spikes 10x, do you scale first, throttle first, or do both at once.

scenario: 团队既有单步的缩略图生成，也有带分支和补偿回滚的多步订单流程，要选工具。
scenario_en: The team has both single-step thumbnail generation and a multi-step order flow with branching and compensation, and must pick a tool.
q: Long-running task queue 和 workflow orchestrator 的边界大致在哪？
q_en: Where is the rough boundary between a long-running task queue and a workflow orchestrator?
options: 单步/线性异步用 queue+worker；复杂分支/并行用 orchestrator
所有异步任务都必须无条件上 Temporal 这类系统
queue+worker 这套组合完全无法处理任何任务
workflow orchestrator 这类编排系统只能用来处理同步的 HTTP 请求
options_en: Single-step or linear async work uses queue plus worker; complex branching or parallelism uses an orchestrator.
Every async task must unconditionally be built on something like Temporal.
The queue-plus-worker combo can't handle any task at all.
A workflow orchestrator, as a class of system, can only be used for synchronous HTTP requests.
why: 不要为了一个单步任务引入工作流引擎；也不要把复杂状态机硬塞进 workers 互相排队的 spaghetti。
why_en: Use queues for simple async work and workflow systems for complex branching, retries, and compensation.
tradeoff: queue+worker 简单直接 vs orchestrator 换取分支/并行可视化能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 工作流某一步失败后，撤销/修正之前已完成步骤造成的影响的逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compensation is the logic that undoes or corrects the effects of earlier completed steps after a later step fails.

optionExplanations: 简单场景用 queue+worker 就够，一旦出现分支、并行或要可视化状态才值得上 orchestrator。
单步任务上 Temporal 纯属杀鸡用牛刀，白白多背一层基础设施。
queue+worker 恰恰是最基础、最常用的异步组合，这个说法明显不成立。
orchestrator 管理的是异步多步工作流，跟同步 HTTP 请求完全是两个次元。
optionExplanations_en: Simple cases are fine with queue plus worker; branching, parallelism, or visible state is when an orchestrator earns its keep.
Putting a single-step job on Temporal is overkill — you carry an extra layer of infrastructure for nothing.
Queue plus worker is precisely the most basic, most common async combo — this claim plainly doesn't hold.
An orchestrator manages async multi-step workflows, which is a completely different world from synchronous HTTP requests.

q: 按正确顺序排列面试中引入 long-running tasks 的表达：
q_en: Put the interview explanation for introducing long-running tasks in the right order.
steps: 说明用户体验：返回 job_id，支持状态查询和完成通知
指出该操作会超过同步请求可接受时长，或资源不适合放 Web tier
提出 queue + worker pool，Web server 快速入队
补充失败处理：retry、DLQ、idempotency、backpressure
why: 先证明为什么需要异步，再给架构和用户体验，最后主动处理生产 failure modes。
why_en: A strong interview answer motivates async processing, proposes queue workers, explains UX, and covers failure modes.
tradeoff: 先论证异步必要性再给架构 vs 直接上架构显得想当然

scenario: 报表服务规定：同一用户 5 分钟内的重复提交算同一次业务意图，超过 5 分钟的再次提交要真的重新生成。
scenario_en: A report service treats repeat submissions from the same user within five minutes as one intent, but a resubmission after that window must really regenerate.
q: 用户发起的任务，idempotency key 该怎么构造？
q_en: How should you build the idempotency key for a user-initiated job?
options: user_id + action + 按 5 分钟取整的 timestamp
每次提交由客户端现场生成一个随机 UUID 当 key
只用 user_id，同一用户的任何任务都算重复
user_id + action + 毫秒精度的原始 timestamp
options_en: user_id plus action plus a timestamp rounded down to the five-minute window.
Have the client mint a fresh random UUID for every submission as the key.
Use the user_id alone, so any job from that user counts as a duplicate.
user_id plus action plus the raw millisecond-precision timestamp.
optionExplanations: 取整粒度就是去重窗口：同窗口内的连点算出同一个 key，跨窗口自然分开。
随机值每次都不同，服务端永远查不到已存在的 key，防重复形同虚设。
粒度太粗：用户下午想重跑同一份报表也会被判成重复，直接拿到旧结果。
毫秒精度下两次点击几乎不可能撞上同一个值，等于没有去重窗口。
optionExplanations_en: The rounding granularity is the dedup window: clicks inside one window hash to the same key.
A fresh random value never matches an existing key, so dedup never fires.
Too coarse: a legitimate rerun later in the day is also judged a duplicate.
At millisecond precision two clicks almost never collide, so there is no window.
why: 去重窗口决定 timestamp 的取整粒度，取整到 5 分钟，窗口内的连点才会算出同一个 key。代价是刚好跨过窗口边界的两次点击仍会变成两个 job。
why_en: The dedup window sets how coarsely you round the timestamp, so repeated clicks inside the window produce one key; the cost is that clicks straddling a window boundary still create two jobs.
tradeoff: 窗口取大点防重复 vs 取小点不误杀正常重跑
whenOtherWins: 系统自动产生的任务没有"用户点击"语义，这时改用输入数据的 deterministic ID（例如源文件内容 hash）当 key 更准确。

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表一次业务意图的唯一标识，命中已存在的 key 就返回旧 job 而不新建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key uniquely identifies one business intent, so a repeat submission returns the existing job instead of creating a new one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一识别码：一个几乎不会重复的随机标识符。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID, or Universally Unique Identifier, is a random identifier that is practically never generated twice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由输入数据本身算出的标识，相同输入永远得到相同的 ID。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deterministic ID is derived from the input data itself, so identical input always yields the same identifier.

scenario: 一个 200 万 follower 的账号发帖，单个 fanout job 要写几十分钟，把后面的普通 fanout 全堵住；团队不想再养第二组 slow queue 机器。
scenario_en: A post from an account with two million followers turns into one fanout job that runs for tens of minutes and blocks every ordinary fanout behind it, and the team does not want to run a second fleet of slow-queue machines.
q: 除了拆 fast/slow 队列，还能怎么消除这个 head-of-line blocking？
q_en: Besides splitting into fast and slow queues, how else can you remove this head-of-line blocking?
options: 把 fanout 按 follower 分批，拆成许多小 job 进同一队列
给这个大 job 单独留一台高内存机器长期常驻
把这个 job 的 retry 上限调高，让它慢慢跑完
让 Web server 同步执行 fanout，绕过队列直接写完所有 feed
options_en: Chunk the fanout by batches of followers into many small jobs on the same queue.
Reserve one permanently running high-memory machine just for this big job.
Raise the retry limit on this job and let it grind through slowly.
Let the web server run the fanout synchronously and write every feed directly.
optionExplanations: 每个小 job 只写一批 follower，占用 worker 的时间回到秒级，队头不再被独占。
专机方案就是变相的 slow queue，机器闲着也要付钱，正是场景里要避开的。
retry 次数管的是失败重试，跟一个成功但极慢的任务堵队列毫无关系。
同步执行会让 HTTP 请求跑满几十分钟，先撞上 30-60 秒的网关超时。
optionExplanations_en: Each small job writes only one batch, so worker occupancy drops back to seconds.
A dedicated box is a slow queue in disguise, and you pay for it while it idles.
Retry limits govern failures, not one successful-but-slow job clogging the line.
Running it inline holds the HTTP request for tens of minutes and hits the gateway timeout first.
why: 把长任务切成小 chunk 后，它复用同一套队列和 worker，不必再维护第二组机器。代价是要自己记录分批进度，并想清楚失败时只重跑哪一批。
why_en: Chunking the long job lets it reuse the same queue and worker pool instead of a second fleet; the cost is tracking batch progress yourself and deciding which batch to redo on failure.
tradeoff: 切 chunk 复用单队列 vs 新建 slow queue 独立调优
whenOtherWins: 任务本身切不开时（一次要扫全表聚合的 5 小时年终报表），只能拆 fast/slow 队列，用更少更壮的机器扛。

termDefinitions.meaning: 队头一个慢任务占住 worker，后面所有任务被迫排队等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Head-of-line blocking is when one slow job at the front of the queue holds the worker and stalls everything behind it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条内容写进大量关注者各自的 feed 的扩散动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is the work of writing one piece of content into the feeds of many followers.

scenario: 你用一张数据库表当队列：每个 worker 先 SELECT 最早那条 pending 行，再 UPDATE 成 processing，20 个 worker 并发轮询。
scenario_en: You use a database table as the queue: each worker SELECTs the oldest pending row and then UPDATEs it to processing, with twenty workers polling concurrently.
q: 这个自制队列在并发消费下会怎么坏掉？
q_en: How does this hand-rolled queue break under concurrent consumption?
options: 两个 worker 取到同一行，任务被执行两次
数据库表存不住任务，重启后 pending 行会全部丢失
任务只会在 worker 崩溃之后才可能被重复执行
数据库会自动给每个 worker 分到互不重叠的行
options_en: Two workers grab the same row and the job runs twice.
A table cannot persist jobs, so pending rows vanish after a restart.
Jobs can only ever be re-executed after a worker crashes.
The database automatically hands each worker a non-overlapping set of rows.
optionExplanations: SELECT 和 UPDATE 之间没有互斥，两个 worker 都读到 pending 就各跑一遍。
恰恰相反：行是持久化的，这方案的问题不在丢失而在重复。
把重复投递只归因于崩溃，漏掉了没有消息锁时正常路径上就会重复。
普通 SELECT 不会为并发读者分区，要 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED 才有这效果。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing is mutually exclusive between the SELECT and the UPDATE, so both workers run it.
The opposite: rows are durable here; the flaw is duplication, not loss.
That blames only crashes and misses the duplication on the normal path.
A plain SELECT does not partition rows among readers; you need FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
why: 正常路径是取一条→标 processing→执行，但取和标之间没有锁，两个 worker 各发一封同样的邮件。成熟队列在投递瞬间就用消息锁把消息藏起来，代价是锁超时设短了又会重复投递。
why_en: The normal path is claim, mark processing, execute, but with no lock between claim and mark two workers each send the same email; real queues hide a message at delivery time with a lock, at the cost of redelivery if that lock times out too early.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息被投递给某个 worker 后对其他 worker 暂时不可见的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message lock makes a delivered message temporarily invisible to all other workers.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS 里消息被隐藏的时长，超时未确认就重新对其他 worker 可见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A visibility timeout is how long SQS hides a delivered message before making it visible again if it was not acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 里跳过已被别的事务锁住的行，用来让并发读者不抢同一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SKIP LOCKED tells SQL to skip rows already locked by another transaction so concurrent readers do not contend.

scenario: 转码 worker 产出一个 800MB 的 mp4，外加清晰度、时长、缩略图路径这类小 metadata；queue 消息和 job 行都要保持小。
scenario_en: A transcoding worker produces an 800 MB mp4 plus small metadata such as resolution, duration and thumbnail paths, while the queue message and job row must stay small.
q: 任务完成后这两类结果分别落在哪里？
q_en: Where should each of these two kinds of result be stored when the job finishes?
options: 文件写 S3，metadata 写数据库，job 行只存指针
文件和 metadata 一起塞进 job 行的一个大字段
把产物 base64 编码后作为完成消息推回 queue
产物留在 worker 本地磁盘，等用户下载时回源读
options_en: Write the file to S3 and the metadata to the database; the job row holds only pointers.
Stuff both the file and the metadata into one big column on the job row.
Base64-encode the artifact and push it back through the queue as a completion message.
Leave the artifact on the worker local disk and read from there when the user downloads.
optionExplanations: 大产物交给对象存储，库里只留 URL，job 行和消息体都保持在几百字节。
800MB 的 BLOB 会让每次读 job 状态都拖着巨大 payload，备份也跟着膨胀。
base64 还会把体积放大三分之一，直接撞穿 SQS 的 1MB 消息上限。
本地磁盘随 worker 一起消失：实例被回收，用户点下载就 404。
optionExplanations_en: The object store takes the artifact and the row keeps a URL, so both stay tiny.
An 800 MB BLOB drags a huge payload into every status read and bloats backups.
Base64 also inflates size by a third and blows through the 1 MB SQS message limit.
Local disk dies with the worker: once the instance is reclaimed the download 404s.
why: 大产物走对象存储、库里只落 URL 和 metadata，能让 queue 消息和 job 行始终保持小而稳定。代价是多一次 S3 往返，且过期产物的清理策略要自己管。
why_en: Sending the artifact to object storage and keeping only a URL plus metadata in the database keeps queue messages and job rows small and predictable, at the cost of an extra S3 round trip and a cleanup policy you own.
tradeoff: 大产物放 S3 只存指针 vs 全部塞进数据库行
whenOtherWins: 产物本身只有几 KB 的纯文本（比如一段 JSON 摘要），直接写进数据库列反而省掉一个外部依赖和一次网络往返。

termDefinitions.meaning: 简单存储服务：AWS 的对象存储，适合存大文件并按 URL 取回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3, or Simple Storage Service, is the AWS object store used to hold large files and serve them by URL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述产物本身的小字段，如时长、清晰度、文件路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metadata is the small descriptive fields about an artifact, such as duration, resolution and file path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二进制大对象：数据库里存放大段二进制数据的列类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BLOB, or Binary Large Object, is a database column type that stores a large chunk of binary data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二进制编码成文本的方式，体积会膨胀约三分之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base64 encodes binary data as text and inflates its size by about a third.

scenario: 5 秒的 PDF 和 5 小时的年终报表混在同一个 queue，你按 queue depth 配了自动扩缩容，但扩容总是要么太晚要么过头。
scenario_en: Five-second PDFs and five-hour year-end reports share one queue, and although you autoscale on queue depth the scaling is always either too late or too aggressive.
q: 除了短任务排队变长，混合耗时还带来什么后果？
q_en: Beyond longer waits for short jobs, what else does a mixed-duration workload cause?
options: 时长不可预测，queue depth 换算不出该加几个 worker
queue depth 会彻底失效，只能改看 worker 的 CPU 使用率
长任务会被队列自动降优先级，短任务因此提前完成
所有 worker 的利用率会自动趋于一致，扩容因此变简单
options_en: Duration is unpredictable, so queue depth no longer converts into a worker count.
Queue depth becomes useless and you must switch to watching worker CPU instead.
The queue automatically deprioritises long jobs so short ones finish sooner.
Worker utilisation evens out on its own, which makes scaling decisions easy.
optionExplanations: 同样是 1000 条积压，可能是 1000 个 5 秒任务也可能是 1000 个 5 小时任务。
换 CPU 指标更糟：等 CPU 飙高时积压早已堆了几个小时。
普通 FIFO 队列不认识任务时长，不会替你重排顺序。
事实相反：有的 worker 刷完几百条短任务，有的被一条长任务占死。
optionExplanations_en: A backlog of a thousand could be a thousand five-second jobs or a thousand five-hour ones.
Switching to CPU is worse: by the time CPU spikes the backlog is hours deep.
A plain FIFO queue knows nothing about duration and will not reorder for you.
The opposite happens: some workers churn hundreds of short jobs, others sit on one long one.
why: 任务时长不可预测时，同一个 queue depth 对应的所需 worker 数可以差几百倍，autoscaling 的阈值根本调不准。同时 worker 利用率严重不均：有的空转，有的被单个长任务占死。
why_en: When job duration is unpredictable the same queue depth can imply wildly different worker counts, so autoscaling thresholds cannot be tuned, and utilisation is badly uneven because some workers churn short jobs while others sit on a single long one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列里等待处理的消息条数，是扩缩容最常用的触发指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth is the number of messages waiting to be processed, the usual trigger metric for scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按指标自动增减 worker 实例数量的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoscaling automatically adds or removes worker instances based on a metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：先入队的消息先被取走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO, or First In First Out, means the message enqueued earliest is delivered first.

scenario: 任务已经跑在 SQS 上，另一条链路跑在 RabbitMQ 上。你要让失败 5 次的消息自动离开主队列，不再一遍遍拖垮 worker。
scenario_en: One pipeline runs on SQS and another on RabbitMQ, and you need messages that have failed five times to leave the main queue automatically instead of repeatedly killing workers.
q: SQS 与 RabbitMQ 上分别靠哪个内置配置实现 DLQ？
q_en: Which built-in configuration gives you a DLQ on SQS and on RabbitMQ respectively?
options: SQS 用 redrive policy，RabbitMQ 用 dead letter exchange
SQS 用 visibility timeout，RabbitMQ 用 prefetch count 限制
SQS 用 S3 的过期规则，RabbitMQ 用 TTL 索引来做转移
两者都没有内置支持，只能由 worker 代码自己转投队列
options_en: On SQS a redrive policy, on RabbitMQ a dead letter exchange.
On SQS the visibility timeout, on RabbitMQ a prefetch count limit.
On SQS an S3 expiry rule, on RabbitMQ a TTL index to move messages.
Neither has built-in support, so worker code must republish the message itself.
optionExplanations: 前者填 maxReceiveCount 和目标队列，后者按路由规则接走被拒消息。
visibility timeout 管的是单次投递隐藏多久，prefetch 管一次预取几条，都不做转移。
对象存储的过期规则只删文件，TTL 索引是数据库概念，都不转移消息。
两个产品都内置了这条路径，自己写转投代码等于重复造轮子还容易漏。
optionExplanations_en: The former sets a max receive count and target queue; the latter routes rejected messages by binding.
Visibility timeout controls how long one delivery is hidden and prefetch how many are pulled at once.
Object-store expiry only deletes files and a TTL index is a database concept; neither moves messages.
Both products ship this path, so hand-rolled republishing just duplicates it badly.
why: DLQ 在这两个产品里是队列侧的配置而不是应用代码：SQS 的 redrive policy 指定重投上限和目标队列，RabbitMQ 用 dead letter exchange 把被拒消息路由走。
why_en: On both products the dead letter path is queue configuration rather than application code: SQS uses a redrive policy with a max receive count and a target queue, while RabbitMQ routes rejected messages through a dead letter exchange.

termDefinitions.meaning: 死信队列：反复失败的消息被移到这里，等人排查而不再重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DLQ, or Dead Letter Queue, holds repeatedly failing messages so a human can investigate instead of retrying forever.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS 上配置"失败几次后转投到哪个队列"的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A redrive policy is the SQS setting that says after how many failed receives a message moves to which queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: RabbitMQ 里接收被拒绝或过期消息并按路由规则转发的交换机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead letter exchange is the RabbitMQ exchange that receives rejected or expired messages and routes them onward.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS 里消息被投递后对其他 worker 隐藏的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A visibility timeout is how long SQS hides a message from other workers after delivering it.

termDefinitions.meaning: RabbitMQ 里一个 consumer 一次最多预取多少条未确认消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefetch count caps how many unacknowledged messages a RabbitMQ consumer may hold at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生存时间：数据在被自动清除前允许存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL, or Time To Live, is how long a piece of data may live before it is automatically removed.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["生产者"] --> Q["主队列 jobs"]
  Q --> W["worker"]
  W -->|"成功: 删除 / ack"| OK["完成"]
  W -->|"失败: 不删 / nack"| Q
  Q -->|"失败次数达上限"| DLQ["死信队列 jobs-dlq"]
  DLQ --> H["人工排查 / 重放"]
codeSample:
# ── SQS：redrive policy 是【挂在主队列上的属性】，指向 DLQ + 重收上限 ──
aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url $MAIN_Q --attributes '{
  "RedrivePolicy": "{\"deadLetterTargetArn\":\"arn:aws:sqs:...:jobs-dlq\",
                       \"maxReceiveCount\":\"5\"}"
}'
# worker 失败时【不删除】消息；SQS 自动重投。
# 同一条被收满 5 次仍没删 → SQS 自动搬去 jobs-dlq。全程零应用代码。

# ── RabbitMQ：dead letter exchange 是【单独声明的交换机】，主队列指过去 ──
ch.exchange_declare('dlx', 'direct')            # 1. 死信交换机
ch.queue_declare('jobs-dlq')                    # 2. 死信队列
ch.queue_bind('jobs-dlq', 'dlx', 'jobs')        # 3. 绑定路由键

ch.queue_declare('jobs', arguments={            # 4. 主队列指向 DLX
    'x-dead-letter-exchange': 'dlx',
    'x-dead-letter-routing-key': 'jobs',
    'x-delivery-limit': 5,       # quorum queue：投递超 5 次 → 死信
})
# worker 失败时 basic_nack(requeue=False) → 消息被死信到 dlx → jobs-dlq。

scenario: 一条消息已经失败到达重收上限,马上要离开主队列。你在「送进 DLQ」和「直接 drop」之间选。
scenario_en: A message has failed up to the receive limit and is about to leave the main queue. You choose between routing it to a DLQ and just dropping it.
q: 反复失败的消息为什么应该进 DLQ,而不是直接 drop 掉?
q_en: Why should a repeatedly failing message go to a DLQ instead of just being dropped?
options: DLQ 只是把消息挪到一边:保留数据、可查根因、修复后可重放、堆积可告警;drop 是静默永久丢失
drop 更好,反复失败的消息一定是坏消息,留着也没用
DLQ 会自动重试直到成功,所以永远不需要人工介入
两者其实一样,DLQ 只是延迟几秒后再把消息 drop 掉
options_en: A DLQ just sets the message aside — data is kept, root cause is inspectable, it can be replayed after a fix, and buildup can alert; dropping loses it silently and forever
Dropping is better because a repeatedly failing message must be a bad message with no further use
A DLQ auto-retries until success, so a human never has to get involved
They are effectively the same — a DLQ just drops the message a few seconds later
why: 离开主队列是为了不让毒消息反复重试拖垮 worker,但「离开」不等于「删除」。DLQ 把消息挪到一边,换来四样东西:①数据不丢(常常只是下游暂时故障,恢复后可重放);②可诊断(失败样本就是排查根因的证据);③可恢复(修好后 re-drive 回主队列);④可告警(DLQ 深度是监控信号)。直接 drop 则是静默、永久、无痕地丢掉用户的真实请求。只有当消息本身可丢弃(如 metrics 心跳)时,drop 才合理。
why_en: Leaving the main queue keeps a poison message from killing workers on endless retries, but leaving is not deleting. Routing to a DLQ buys four things: data is preserved (failures are often just a transient downstream outage that can be replayed after recovery), the failures are diagnosable evidence of root cause, they can be re-driven back after a fix, and DLQ depth is an alertable signal. Dropping instead loses a real user request silently and permanently; it is only reasonable when the message itself is disposable, like a metrics heartbeat.
whenOtherWins: 消息本身可丢弃、价值低且量大(metrics 心跳、缓存预热提示这类噪声)→ 直接 drop 甚至不配 DLQ。
tradeoff: DLQ 的少量存储/运维成本 vs 直接 drop 丢掉的数据、可诊断性与可恢复性

rows: 无证据,不知丢了啥/为啥
没了就没了,需重新提交
修好后 re-drive 回主队列

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条无论重试多少次都会失败的消息(如格式损坏),会反复拖垮 worker,所以要移出主队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A poison message is one that keeps failing no matter how many times it is retried (e.g. malformed), so it must be moved off the main queue before it starves workers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 DLQ 里的消息重新投回主队列再处理一次,常在修复 bug 或下游恢复后做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-drive (replay) means pushing DLQ messages back onto the main queue to be processed again, typically after a bug fix or downstream recovery.

optionExplanations: 这正是取舍:DLQ 用一点点存储换来数据不丢、可诊断、可重放、可告警,而 drop 把这些全丢了。
失败常常只是下游暂时故障,消息本身没坏——一刀 drop 会把一批好任务永久丢掉。
DLQ 不会自动重试,它恰恰是「停止重试、挪到一边等人处理」的地方;重放要显式触发。
DLQ 不会自己 drop 消息,它把消息留存下来等排查/重放,和延迟 drop 是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the trade-off: a DLQ spends a little storage to keep data, diagnosability, replayability, and alerting, all of which dropping throws away.
Failures are often just a transient downstream outage with a perfectly good message — blanket dropping permanently loses a batch of valid work.
A DLQ does not auto-retry; it is precisely where retries stop and the message waits for a human, and replay must be triggered explicitly.
A DLQ does not drop the message on its own — it retains it for investigation or replay, which is not the same as a delayed drop.

scenario: 打车 App 的匹配要评估周边司机、算路线和定价，需要数秒；同时每台司机手机每几秒上报一次位置，量非常大。
scenario_en: In a ridesharing app, matching evaluates nearby drivers, routes and pricing and takes seconds, while every driver phone reports its location every few seconds at huge volume.
q: 这两条链路各自该走同步还是异步？
q_en: Should each of these two paths be synchronous or asynchronous?
options: 匹配后台跑、先返回"正在寻找司机"；位置更新走 async worker
两条都同步：乘客请求一直阻塞到匹配完成，位置更新也直接打进主 API
匹配同步返回最终结果，位置更新也由主 API 同步落库
两条都异步，且不给乘客任何中间状态提示
options_en: Run matching in the background behind a "finding drivers" state and push location updates through async workers.
Make both synchronous: the rider request blocks until matching finishes and locations write straight into the main API.
Return the final match synchronously and also write location updates through the main API.
Make both asynchronous and show the rider no intermediate state at all.
optionExplanations: 乘客立刻看到有反馈，主 API 也不用替海量位置写入扛压力。
阻塞几秒会让每个乘客占住一条请求线程，高峰时 Web 层先被占满。
位置上报的频率比乘客下单高一到两个数量级，同步写会挤掉正常请求。
没有中间状态，乘客只会看到空白页面并反复重开，制造更多重复请求。
optionExplanations_en: The rider gets instant feedback and the main API never absorbs the location write volume.
Blocking for seconds pins a request thread per rider and saturates the web tier at peak.
Location reports arrive one or two orders of magnitude more often than ride requests and crowd them out.
With no intermediate state the rider sees a blank screen and keeps retrying, adding duplicate requests.
why: 匹配要数秒但乘客需要即时反馈，所以先返回一个"寻找中"的状态由后台推进；位置更新量大且能容忍秒级延迟，走 worker 才不会把主 API 压垮。
why_en: Matching takes seconds but the rider needs instant feedback, so you return a finding state and let workers finish it, and location updates are high volume yet tolerant of a few seconds of lag, so routing them through workers keeps the main API healthy.
tradeoff: 先返回中间状态异步匹配 vs 阻塞等待最终结果
whenOtherWins: 如果匹配能稳定在 200ms 内完成（司机很少的小城市），同步直接返回结果反而省掉一轮状态轮询和 UI 状态机。

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数：衡量请求速率的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or Queries Per Second, measures how many requests a system handles each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从队列取任务、在后台执行的独立进程，不占用请求线程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An async worker is a separate process that pulls jobs from a queue and runs them in the background.

scenario: job 数据库主库正在做故障切换，约 3 分钟不可写。某个 worker 刚跑完转码，正要把 status 从 processing 改成 completed。
scenario_en: The job database is failing over and will reject writes for about three minutes, just as a worker finishes transcoding and tries to move its status from processing to completed.
q: 这 3 分钟里 worker 该怎么处置手上这条消息？
q_en: What should the worker do with the message it holds during those three minutes?
options: 持续重试写入，DB 恢复后再 ack 消息
把 job 标记为 failed，立刻投进 DLQ 等人处理
直接 ack 消息跳过状态更新，继续取下一条
让 worker 进程自行退出，等运维手动重启补跑
options_en: Keep retrying the write and acknowledge the message only once the database recovers.
Mark the job failed and push it straight to the DLQ for a human.
Acknowledge the message, skip the status update and move to the next job.
Let the worker process exit and wait for an operator to restart and backfill.
optionExplanations: 数据库故障是暂时的，消息没 ack 就还在队列里，恢复后能正常收尾。
把基础设施抖动当成任务本身有问题，DLQ 会被一堆其实没错的 job 灌满。
ack 之后消息就消失了，这个 job 会永远停在 processing，用户等不到结果。
退出进程既丢了整台机器的处理能力，又把恢复动作压到人身上。
optionExplanations_en: The outage is transient and an unacknowledged message stays queued, so it can finish after recovery.
That treats an infrastructure blip as a bad job and floods the dead letter queue with healthy work.
Once acknowledged the message is gone and the job is stuck in processing forever.
Exiting throws away a whole machine of capacity and pushes recovery onto a human.
why: 正常路径是干完活→写 completed→ack；DB 不可写时 worker 只重试不 ack，消息留在队列里，恢复后再收尾。代价是这几分钟积压变深，而且可见性超时一到任务可能被另一台 worker 重做，所以工作本身必须幂等。
why_en: Normally the worker finishes, writes completed and acknowledges, but while the database is down it retries without acknowledging so the message stays queued until recovery; the cost is a deeper backlog and possible re-execution by another worker once the visibility timeout expires, which is why the work must be idempotent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 确认：worker 告诉队列这条消息已处理完，可以删除了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack, short for acknowledgement, tells the queue a message is fully processed and can be deleted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 死信队列：反复失败的消息移到这里等人排查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DLQ, or Dead Letter Queue, collects repeatedly failing messages for human investigation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 故障切换：主库出问题时把写流量切到备库的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover is the process of switching write traffic to a standby when the primary database fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次的结果与执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it is repeated.

scenario: 一次营销活动会一次性产生 20 万条短信通知，但第三方短信网关只允许 50 请求/秒，超了就返回 429，且通知一条都不能丢。
scenario_en: A marketing campaign generates 200,000 SMS notifications at once, but the third-party gateway allows only 50 requests per second and returns 429 above that, and no notification may be dropped.
q: 怎么在不丢通知的前提下满足对方的限流？
q_en: How do you respect that rate limit without dropping any notification?
options: 全部入队，worker 按 50/秒 匀速消费
直接全量并发调用，被 429 拒绝的就丢掉不再发
把 20 万条分给 20 万个线程同时发出去
在用户的 Web 请求里同步发送，靠请求到达速度自然限流
options_en: Enqueue everything and let workers drain it at a steady fifty per second.
Fire them all concurrently and drop whatever comes back as a 429.
Hand the 200,000 messages to 200,000 threads and send them all at once.
Send inline in the user web request and let arrival rate act as the limiter.
optionExplanations: 队列把突发削平成稳定速率，worker 并发数就是那个限速旋钮。
丢弃被拒的消息直接违反"一条都不能丢"，而且重试风暴会让限流更严重。
20 万并发只会把 429 打成一片，网关还可能整体封禁你的账号。
营销触发的是后台批量，根本没有对应的用户请求可以搭车。
optionExplanations_en: The queue flattens the burst into a steady rate, and worker concurrency is the throttle knob.
Dropping rejected messages violates the no-loss rule and the retry storm worsens throttling.
Two hundred thousand concurrent calls just produce a wall of 429s and risk an account-level ban.
A campaign is a background batch; there is no matching user request to piggyback on.
why: 队列把 20 万条突发摊平成第三方能接受的稳定速率，worker 数量就是限速旋钮。代价是最后一条要等 200000 ÷ 50 = 4000 秒（约 67 分钟）才发出，产品必须接受这个尾延迟。
why_en: The queue shapes a burst of 200,000 into a steady rate the third party accepts, with worker count as the throttle; the cost is that the last message goes out after 200,000 divided by 50, or 4,000 seconds, so the product must accept that tail delay.
tradeoff: 排队整形保证不丢 vs 直接并发求最快送达
whenOtherWins: 通知有强时效时（一次性验证码），宁可不排队直接发，超限就快速失败并让用户手动重发，而不是让他等一小时。

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流：接口对单位时间内允许的请求数设的上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limit is the cap an API sets on how many requests it accepts per unit of time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超出限流时服务端返回的状态码，表示请求过多需退避。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests is the status code a server returns when you exceed its rate limit and must back off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把突发流量摊平成稳定速率再送出去的做法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate shaping smooths a burst of traffic into a steady outbound rate.

scenario: 电商平台的订单履约要跨支付、库存、仓储三个服务，任一步都可能超时失败。
scenario_en: You're designing order fulfillment for an e-commerce site: it spans payment, inventory, and warehouse services, and any step can time out.
q: Multi-step processes 模式主要解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does the multi-step processes pattern mainly solve?
options: 跨服务的长流程如何在失败点可靠地推进、重试和补偿
单条数据库查询如何选择合适索引
静态图片资源如何用 CDN 分发并配置边缘节点的缓存过期时间
单个用户的偏好字段如何持久化存储
options_en: How to reliably drive a long cross-service flow through failure points with retries and compensation.
How to pick the right index for a single database query.
How to distribute static image assets over a CDN and configure edge-node cache expiry.
How to persist a single user's preference field.
why: 真实业务流程常包含支付、库存、发货、人审、邮件等多步操作，任何一步都可能失败或超时。该模式关注 durable state、retry、compensation 和 orchestration。
why_en: Multi-step process patterns make long, failure-prone workflows across services reliable through durable state, retries, and compensation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN, or Content Delivery Network, caches content on edge servers close to users.

optionExplanations: 这正是本模式关注的核心：跨服务多步骤在失败点能可靠恢复、重试和补偿。
把它当索引选择题就搞混了——这是单库查询优化，不是跨服务多步骤编排的问题。
静态资源缓存分发是 CDN 的职责，跟跨服务失败恢复完全是两回事。
单字段持久化只是普通写操作，没有多步骤、跨服务失败恢复这些编排诉求。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what the pattern targets: keeping a multi-service flow recoverable and retryable at any failure point.
Confusing this with index tuning misses the point — that's single-query optimization, not cross-service orchestration.
CDN caching just distributes static assets; it has nothing to do with recovering a failed multi-step flow.
Persisting one field is a simple write, with no multi-step or cross-service recovery concerns at all.

scenario: 订单履约的四个步骤全写在一个 API server 函数里，扣款成功后进程被重启。
scenario_en: All four fulfillment steps live in one API server function, and the process gets restarted right after the charge succeeds.
q: 把订单履约流程只写成单个 API server 函数有什么致命问题？
q_en: What is the fatal flaw in implementing order fulfillment as one API server function?
options: 只要用 try/catch 包住整个流程，崩溃重启后就能自动恢复到中断点
server 在扣款成功后崩溃重启，内存中的进度全部丢失，不知道该继续还是补偿
只要每一步都打印日志，重启后就能从日志读出流程进度
只要用 async/await 写步骤，Node 崩溃重启后会自动重放未完成的调用
options_en: Wrapping the whole flow in try/catch means it auto-recovers to the crash point after a restart.
The server crashes after charging succeeds, all in-memory progress is lost, and it has no way to know whether to resume or compensate.
Printing a log line at every step means the process can read its progress back from the logs after restart.
Writing each step with async/await means Node automatically replays unfinished calls after a crash.
why: 单机内存不是 durable progress。跨服务流程必须把已完成步骤记录到可恢复的存储，否则崩溃后会留下半完成状态。
why_en: A single in-memory function loses progress on crash, leaving the system unable to resume or compensate safely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理请求逻辑的应用服务器进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API server is the application process that handles request logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编程语言里捕获运行时异常的语法，只处理程序内错误，不提供跨进程持久化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: try/catch is a language construct for catching runtime exceptions; it does not persist state across process crashes.

termDefinitions.meaning: JavaScript 里编写异步代码的语法糖，本身不提供崩溃后自动重放的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: async/await is JavaScript syntax for writing asynchronous code; it does not by itself provide crash replay.

optionExplanations: try/catch 只能捕获同一进程内的异常，进程本身重启后这段内存状态照样清零。
崩溃发生在内存里，没有落盘的进度记录，恢复时根本不知道该续跑还是退款。
日志是给人读的文本流，没有结构化恢复点，进程不会自动从日志里续跑逻辑。
async/await 只是异步语法糖，进程重启后未完成的调用链不会被自动重放。
optionExplanations_en: try/catch only catches exceptions inside the same live process; a real restart wipes that memory regardless.
The crash happens in memory with no durable checkpoint, so recovery can't tell whether to resume or refund.
Logs are just text for humans — they aren't structured checkpoints a process can resume from automatically.
async/await is just async syntax; a restart does not replay unfinished promise chains on its own.

scenario: 面试要你列出电商下单后的履约步骤，流程跨多个服务并含仓库人工拣货等待。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to enumerate the fulfillment steps after checkout, spanning services and a human warehouse pick.
q: 电商订单履约 workflow 可能包含哪些步骤？（多选）
q_en: Which steps can appear in an e-commerce order fulfillment workflow? (Select all)
options: charge payment
reserve inventory
create shipping label / wait for warehouse pick
send confirmation email
options_en: Charge the customer's payment.
Reserve inventory for the order.
Create a shipping label and wait for the warehouse to pick the item.
Send the confirmation email.
why: 这些步骤跨多个服务和人类等待点，正是 workflow/saga 的典型场景。
why_en: Order fulfillment spans payment, inventory, shipping, human work, and notification steps.
optionExplanations: 扣款要先于发货动作，避免钱货两空，也是补偿链条要保护的第一步。
库存要在下单时锁定，防止两个订单抢同一件商品导致超卖。
履约要等仓库真实拣货完成，不能假设下单后商品立刻能发出。
确认邮件让用户知道进度，避免用户在等待期间反复问客服或重复下单。
optionExplanations_en: Charging comes before shipping so the customer is never billed without getting the goods — the first step compensation must protect.
Inventory must be locked at order time, or two orders can grab the same item and cause overselling.
Fulfillment waits on the real warehouse pick — you can't assume the item ships the instant the order is placed.
The confirmation email keeps the customer informed so they don't spam support or place a duplicate order.

scenario: 支付走异步 webhook 回调，API server 扩到十台并挂在 load balancer 后面。
scenario_en: Payment confirms through an async webhook, and your API tier is scaled to ten instances behind a load balancer.
q: 为什么支付网关 webhook 会让单服务器内存编排更不可靠？
q_en: Why does a payment gateway webhook make in-memory orchestration on one server less reliable?
options: webhook 请求本身完全不会携带任何订单标识字段，所以回调回来后永远无法关联到具体订单
支付网关一定会立刻同步返回最终结果，根本不存在异步回调这种情况
callback 可能落在负载均衡后的另一台 server 上，那台机器没有原来的内存状态
load balancer 在流量高峰时会直接清空后端数据库里保存的所有记录
options_en: Webhook requests fundamentally never carry any order identifier, so after the callback returns nothing can be linked to a specific order.
The payment gateway always immediately responds synchronously with the final result, so there is no such thing as an async callback.
The callback can land on a different server behind the load balancer that has no memory of the original flow.
The load balancer directly wipes every record stored in the backend database during traffic spikes.
why: 扩容后请求不一定回到同一台机器。流程状态必须通过 durable store 和 workflow ID 关联，而不能靠某台服务器记忆。
why_en: Webhook callbacks may land on a different host, so workflow state must be durable and addressable by ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: 外部系统在事件发生后主动 HTTP 回调你服务的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback an external system makes to your service when an event happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers.

optionExplanations: 把 webhook 想成匿名请求是个误解——网关几乎总会把商户订单号原样带回来。
支付网关普遍靠异步回调确认结果，真把它当纯同步接口会漏掉后续状态变化。
负载均衡后请求可能落到任意一台机器，那台机器的内存里根本没有原来的上下文。
负载均衡只负责转发流量，不会去清空数据库记录，这个说法混淆了两个组件的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Treating the webhook as anonymous is the misconception — gateways almost always echo back your order id.
Gateways commonly confirm results through async callbacks; assuming a pure sync reply misses later state changes.
After load balancing, the callback can land on any instance, whose memory has none of the original context.
A load balancer only routes traffic — it never wipes database records; that mixes up two unrelated jobs.

scenario: 订单流程跨支付、库存、物流三个各自独立的数据库，开不出一个共享事务。
scenario_en: The order flow spans three services with separate databases, so a single shared transaction isn't available.
q: Saga pattern 的核心定义是什么？
q_en: What is the core definition of the saga pattern?
options: 跨所有参与服务加一把全局分布式锁，一直锁到最后一步成功提交之后才肯释放
只在读路径加一层缓存，用来加速那些被重复发起的查询请求
把所有跨服务步骤压缩成一次原子 SQL 事务来强行保证一致性
一系列本地提交的步骤，每一步都有对应的补偿动作；失败时按反方向执行补偿
options_en: Take a single global distributed lock across every participating service and hold it until the last step successfully commits.
Add only a cache layer on the read path to speed up queries that get repeated often.
Squeeze every cross-service step into one atomic SQL transaction to force consistency.
A sequence of locally committed steps, each with a matching compensating action, undone in reverse order on failure.
why: Saga 不保证所有步骤原子同时提交，而是保证已提交的步骤可以被补偿。它接受短暂不一致。
why_en: A saga is a sequence of local steps with compensating actions that undo completed work if a later step fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一系列本地事务加补偿动作的模式，用于跨服务保证最终一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga is a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions that keep cross-service work eventually consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个进程/服务共享的锁，用来阻止并发修改同一资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a lock shared across processes or services that prevents concurrent modification of the same resource.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单个数据库内保证原子性的一组操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SQL transaction is a set of operations inside a single database guaranteed to be atomic together.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Step one succeeds]
  B[Step two fails]
  C[Compensate step one]
  D[End in known state]
  A --> B --> C --> D
optionExplanations: 全局锁会把所有参与者锁住直到最后一步，这正是 saga 想避开的强耦合方案。
缓存解决的是读路径加速问题，跟跨服务写操作的一致性协调没有关系。
多服务往往分属不同数据库，压不进一次原子 SQL 事务里去。
每步本地提交后立刻可见，出错时靠反向补偿把已完成的动作撤销回去。
optionExplanations_en: A global lock holds every participant until the last step finishes — the tight coupling sagas try to avoid.
Caching speeds up reads; it has nothing to do with coordinating consistency across separate write services.
Multiple services usually sit on different databases, so they can't fit inside one atomic SQL transaction.
Each local step commits and becomes visible right away; a failure is undone by running compensations backward.

scenario: 履约链路里支付网关是第三方、仓库拣货要等几小时，不能长时间持有锁。
scenario_en: In this flow the payment gateway is third-party and the warehouse pick takes hours, so you can't hold locks that long.
q: 为什么很多跨服务业务流程不用 Two-Phase Commit，而用 saga？
q_en: Why do many cross-service business workflows use a saga instead of Two-Phase Commit?
options: 2PC 长时间锁住所有参与者，外部系统未必支持事务协议
2PC 在任何跨服务场景下都一定比 saga 更快、更可靠、更省心
saga 要求所有步骤都同步加锁直到全部完成
外部支付网关天生就支持你数据库的事务协议
options_en: 2PC holds a lock on every participant for a long time, and external systems often don't speak your transaction protocol.
2PC is always faster, more reliable, and less trouble than a saga in every cross-service scenario.
A saga requires every step to be synchronously locked until the whole flow finishes.
External payment gateways natively support your database's transaction protocol.
tradeoff: 长事务加锁的原子性 vs 补偿式的最终一致性
why: 支付、人审、发货等步骤可能很慢或不受你控制，不能靠长事务锁住全部资源。Saga 更适合现实中的异步业务流程。
why_en: Sagas avoid long distributed locks and work with external systems by compensating committed steps instead of atomically locking everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交协议，参与者先投票再统一提交或回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where participants vote, then all commit or all roll back together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一系列本地事务加补偿动作的模式，用于跨服务保证最终一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga is a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions that keep cross-service work eventually consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理信用卡/银行扣款的第三方服务，通常不支持你的数据库事务协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A payment gateway is the third-party service that processes card or bank charges, and it usually does not speak your database's transaction protocol.

optionExplanations: 2PC 要求所有参与者投票并保持锁定直到提交，第三方网关通常不实现这套协议，长事务在这行不通。
2PC 在同库强一致场景确实更简单，但跨系统异步等待时锁越拖越久，谈不上任何场景都更快。
把 saga 想成也要全程加锁就误解了它——saga 恰恰是用分步本地提交替代长时间持锁。
外部支付网关是独立系统，不会加入你数据库的两阶段提交协议，这个假设不成立。
optionExplanations_en: 2PC needs every participant to vote and stay locked until commit; gateways rarely implement that protocol.
2PC can be simpler in one strongly-consistent database, but across flaky async steps the lock just drags on.
