Every index removed is one less structure to maintain on write — the tradeoff is that the matching queries get slower.
Misconception: more secondary indexes means more index pages to update on every write — that adds load, it doesn't reduce it.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 面试里你想表达「换个写优化的数据库」，需要展示对取舍的理解而不是丢名词。
scenario_en: In the interview you want to argue for "switch to a write-optimized database", and need to show you understand the trade-off, not just drop a product name.
q: 哪种说法最能拿分？
q_en: Which phrasing earns the most credit?
options: 「我们把数据库换成社区里口碑更好、性能评测更亮眼的那一个就行了」
「说清 Cassandra 追加写更快在哪，或时序库为何适合指标采集」
「NoSQL 反正不用维护表结构，所以写入场景里永远比关系型数据库快」
「数据库选型其实不重要，只要不断加机器、堆更多实例就能解决」
options_en: "We'll just switch to whichever database has the best reputation and flashiest benchmarks."
"Explain why Cassandra's append-only writes are faster, or why a time-series store fits metrics."
"NoSQL never has to maintain a schema, so it's always faster than relational databases for writes."
"Database choice doesn't really matter, just keep adding more machines and more instances."
why: 别只说「用更快的库」——要讲机制：追加写 vs B-tree 更新、时序库为何适合 metrics。展示你懂取舍，而不是背名词。
why_en: Do not just say use a faster database; explain why append-only writes beat B-tree updates or why a time-series store fits metrics.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入量估算下来单库完全扛得住，那连换库都不必提——一个调优过的通用数据库就够了。
tradeoff: 讲清写机制取舍 vs 只报数据库品牌名

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: MySQL 等关系库常用的索引结构，更新时通常要原地改写页面，带来随机磁盘寻道。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is the balanced index structure MySQL and similar databases use, and updating it usually means rewriting pages in place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为带时间戳的高频顺序写入优化的数据库，如 InfluxDB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-series database is optimized for high-frequency, timestamped sequential writes, such as InfluxDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见关系型数据库，默认面向通用 OLTP 负载，而不是极端写入吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MySQL is a common relational database aimed at general OLTP workloads rather than extreme write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组非传统关系模型数据库的统称，不等于所有场景都比关系库写得快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL, or Not Only SQL, is a broad family of non-relational databases, not a guarantee of faster writes in every case.

optionExplanations: 只报品牌和评测分数，没讲写路径为什么变快，面试官听不出你是真懂还是在复述广告词。
点名具体机制——追加写 vs B-tree 原地更新、时序库为何契合指标采集——这才是面试官要的判断力证据。
误解：NoSQL 确实少了严格 schema 校验，但查询能力和一致性模型的取舍才是决定因素，不是「永远更快」。
误解：只讲堆机器，跳过了分片键和写机制这些真正决定收益的细节，等于回避了这道题在考的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Naming a brand and a benchmark score without explaining why the write path gets faster leaves the interviewer unsure if you actually understand it.
Naming the actual mechanism — append-only vs in-place B-tree updates, why a time-series store fits metrics — is the judgment signal interviewers are listening for.
Misconception: NoSQL does skip strict schema checks, but query capability and consistency tradeoffs are what actually decide speed, not a blanket "always faster".
Misconception: talking about adding machines alone skips the partition key and write-mechanism details that actually determine the payoff — it avoids the question.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 水平分片的基本承诺是什么？
q_en: What's the basic promise of horizontal sharding?
scenario: 单台 MySQL 在 1,000 写/秒打满，团队想加到 10 台来扛 10 倍写量，先确认这个承诺是什么。
scenario_en: One MySQL box saturates at 1,000 writes per second and the team wants ten boxes to carry ten times the load, so be clear about what sharding actually promises.
options: 单机 1,000 写/秒，10 台「应该」到 10,000——写量分摊，各扛一份
只要给数据分了片，原本集中在少数热门用户身上的写入热点就会自动被分片机制完全拉平
分片之后，读请求就不再需要考虑数据在哪个分片上，性能自动比单机时更快
把数据切成多片分开存放在不同机器上，能让原本存储的数据总量因此直接变小
options_en: If one server handles 1,000 writes/sec, 10 servers "should" reach 10,000 by spreading writes into a share each
Simply sharding the data automatically and completely flattens out write hot spots concentrated on a few popular users, thanks to the sharding mechanism itself
After sharding, reads no longer need to think about which shard the data lives on and automatically get faster than on one machine
Splitting data into multiple shards across different machines directly shrinks the total amount of data stored
why: 分片的理想态是线性扩展：写量均匀分摊，每台只扛可控的一份。多台服务器组成一个逻辑数据库，对应用（基本）透明。
why_en: Sharding promises near-linear scaling by spreading writes across servers so each handles a manageable portion, hidden behind one logical database.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    W[写入流量] --> H[按 partition key 哈希]
    H --> A[(Shard A)]
    H --> B[(Shard B)]
    H --> C[(Shard C)]
    A --> DBA[(DB A)]
    B --> DBB[(DB B)]
    C --> DBC[(DB C)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一份数据横向拆到多台服务器，每台只处理一部分写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across multiple servers so each one only handles a portion of the writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分片承受远超其他分片的流量，即使整体分片均匀也可能出现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot spot is a single shard taking far more traffic than the others, which can still happen even with an evenly designed scheme.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器数增加 N 倍时，总吞吐也接近增加 N 倍；真实系统通常只能逼近它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linear scaling means N times as many machines gives close to N times the throughput, though real systems only approximate it.

optionExplanations: 这是分片的理想线性扩展承诺：N 倍机器摊平写量，每台只扛可控的一份，多台组成一个逻辑数据库。
误解：分了片只是把 key 分散存放，热点用户依然可能都落在同一个分片上，需要专门选好分区键才能拉平。
误解：分片后读请求要么打对分片、要么 scatter-gather 打多个分片，分布问题只会更需要设计，不会自动消失。
误解：分片改变的是数据存放的位置，不是总量；总数据量该多大还是多大，只是被摊开存放了。
optionExplanations_en: This is sharding's ideal linear-scaling promise: N times the machines spreads the writes so each handles a controlled share, all hidden behind one logical database.
Misconception: sharding alone just spreads keys across nodes; a hot user can still land entirely on one shard unless the partition key is chosen to spread that load too.
Misconception: after sharding, reads either have to hit the right shard or scatter-gather across several — distribution needs more design, not less.
Misconception: sharding relocates data, it doesn't shrink it; total data volume stays the same, just spread across machines.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: Redis Cluster 是怎么决定一个 key 写到哪个节点的？
q_en: How does Redis Cluster decide which node a key gets written to?
scenario: 六节点 Redis Cluster 扛百万计数写/秒，客户端必须一跳内找到 key 的归属节点。
scenario_en: A six-node Redis Cluster absorbs a million counter writes per second, and the client has to reach the owning node for a key in a single hop.
options: 客户端按固定顺序依次把写请求发给每一个节点，不管 key 是什么
把 key 按字母表位置切成几段区间，落在哪段就写到对应节点
key 经 CRC 哈希成 slot，查路由表后直写目标节点
所有写入请求先统一发给一个中心代理，再由它转发给具体节点
options_en: The client sends writes to every node in a fixed round-robin order regardless of the key
Split keys into ranges by alphabetical position, and write to whichever node owns that range
Hash the key with CRC into a slot, then look up the routing table and write directly to the owning node
Every write first goes to one central proxy, which then forwards it to the right node
why: Redis Cluster 用简单 CRC 函数把 key 哈希成 slot 号，slot 分配给节点；客户端自己维护 slot→节点映射，直接把写发给负责的节点。
why_en: Redis Cluster hashes each key with a CRC function to a slot number, slots map to nodes, and clients route writes directly to the responsible node.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant N1 as 节点A (slots 0-5460)
    participant N2 as 节点B (slots 5461-10922)
    C->>C: CRC(key) → slot 7000
    C->>N2: 直接写到负责 slot 7000 的节点B
    N2-->>C: OK
codeSample:
# 客户端先算 key 属于哪个 slot
> CLUSTER KEYSLOT user:1000
(integer) 3999
# 查路由表得知 slot 3999 归节点A，直接写它
> SET user:1000:profile '{"name":"Ann"}'
OK

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的分片集群模式，用 slot 把 key 空间分配到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster is Redis's sharded cluster mode, assigning key-space slots across multiple nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种快速哈希校验算法，Redis Cluster 用它把 key 映射到 slot 号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRC, or Cyclic Redundancy Check, is a fast hashing algorithm Redis Cluster uses to map a key to a slot number.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 把 key 空间切成 16384 个槽位，每个槽位固定分配给某个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot is one of Redis Cluster's fixed key-space buckets, and each slot is assigned to exactly one node.

optionExplanations: 客户端并不会挨个节点广播写请求——Redis 集群只把写发给负责该 key 所在 slot 的那一个节点。
字母表区间切分不是 Redis 集群的分片方式，那样切很容易让负载集中到某几个字母段。
CRC 把 key 映射成槽位，槽位固定分给节点，客户端缓存路由表后直连目标节点，不必经过中转。
所有写入不会先经过一个中心代理转发——Redis 集群本身没有强制的中心代理这一跳。
optionExplanations_en: The client doesn't broadcast to every node — Redis Cluster sends a write only to the single node owning that key's slot.
Alphabetical range slicing isn't how Redis Cluster shards; that scheme would easily concentrate load on a few letter ranges.
CRC maps the key to a slot, slots are pinned to nodes, and the client caches the routing table to write straight to the owning node with no extra hop.
Writes don't funnel through one central proxy first — Redis Cluster has no mandatory central-proxy hop.

scenario: 面试里你说了「sharding」，面试官追问「具体怎么分」。你要给出最关键的那个细节。
scenario_en: You said "we'll shard it" in the interview, and the interviewer follows up with "shard it how, exactly". You need the one detail that matters most.
q: 分片方案里最重要、必须主动讲清的细节是？
q_en: What's the most important sharding detail you must proactively spell out?
options: 先确定用哪家云厂商，再决定机房区域和可用区，把延迟和容灾定下来
先确定每台机器该配多大容量、什么型号的磁盘，把硬件规格提前定好
先确定分片之间多久互相发一次心跳，检测节点是否存活并及时摘除
如何选 partitioning key，让数据均匀铺开
options_en: First decide which cloud vendor to use, then the data center region and availability zone, to lock in latency and disaster recovery
First decide how much capacity and which disk model each machine should have, to lock in the hardware spec upfront
First decide how often shards send heartbeats to each other, to detect and evict dead nodes in time
How you pick the partitioning key so data spreads evenly
why: 面试官期待的不是「sharding」这个词，而是分区键怎么选：选好了（比如 hash userID），数据均匀分布，10 台机器才能真正拿到 10 倍收益。
why_en: The most important sharding detail is selecting a partitioning key that spreads data evenly, which is what actually realizes the ten-times gain.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官继续深挖「客户端怎么找到正确的分片」，就要展开 consistent hashing、虚拟节点、slot 分配这些路由机制。
tradeoff: 分区键选择 vs 其它次要实现细节

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片的字段，选得好坏直接决定负载是否均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partitioning key is the field that decides which shard a row lands on, and picking it well or poorly directly determines whether load is even.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种分片路由算法，节点增减时只需重新分配少量 key，而不是全量重哈希。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing is a sharding scheme where adding or removing a node only reshuffles a small slice of keys instead of rehashing everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希环上的虚拟分片点，用来让真实节点承接多个小范围，减轻倾斜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node is a logical point on a consistent-hash ring that lets real nodes own many smaller ranges and reduces skew.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片系统把 key 空间切出的固定槽位，槽位再分配给具体节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot is a fixed bucket of key space in a sharded system, later assigned to a concrete node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户的唯一标识符，常被选作分片或分区的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: userID is a user's unique identifier, commonly used as a sharding or partition key.

optionExplanations: 云厂商和可用区决定延迟与容灾能力，但回答不了一条写入到底该落到哪个分片。
机器容量和磁盘型号是硬件规格规划，分区键选错时再大的机器也会被热点压垮。
心跳间隔只用来判断节点是否存活，不参与决定一条写入该路由到哪个分片。
分区键决定每条写入的去向，选得好坏直接决定 10 台机器能不能真拿到接近 10 倍的收益。
optionExplanations_en: Cloud vendor and availability zone shape latency and disaster recovery, but they don't answer which shard a given write should land on.
Machine capacity and disk model are hardware sizing decisions; even a huge machine gets crushed by a hot shard if the partition key is wrong.
Heartbeat interval only decides whether a node is judged alive — it plays no part in routing a write to a shard.
The partition key decides where every write lands; getting it right is what actually lets 10 machines realize something close to a 10x gain.

q: 用「用户所在国家」当分区键，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if you use "user's country" as the partition key?
scenario: 全球社交 App 按「用户所在国家」分片，中国用户占四成、新西兰不到 1%。
scenario_en: A global social app shards by the user’s country, where China is about forty percent of users and New Zealand is under one percent.
options: 中国这类人口大国的分片过载，新西兰这类分片闲置——负载严重倾斜
选错分区键只会让数据变得难以查询，不会导致数据丢失或写入被拒绝
只要用了分片这个技术，负载天然就会在各节点间完全均匀分布
分区键只影响读路径查询的速度，跟写入请求的分布完全无关
options_en: A populous-country shard like China gets overloaded while a sparse-country shard like New Zealand sits idle — badly skewed load
Picking the wrong partition key only makes data harder to query, it doesn't cause data loss or rejected writes
As long as you use sharding as a technique, load naturally ends up perfectly even across nodes
The partition key only affects read-path query speed and has nothing to do with write request distribution
why: 国家这种低基数、分布不均的键会造成倾斜：写量涌向人口大国的分片，小国分片闲着。这就是坏分区键的经典画像。
why_en: Partitioning by country skews load badly, overloading the China shard while the New Zealand shard sits idle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片的字段，基数太低或分布不均会造成倾斜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which shard a row lands on, and a low-cardinality or unevenly distributed key causes skew.

optionExplanations: 这就是坏分区键的经典画像——像 userID 这种高基数字段通常比国家这种粗粒度字段更能把写量摊匀。
误解：选错分区键不只是查询变难，热点分片过载还可能导致超时、拒绝写入甚至丢数据。
误解：分片只是把数据切开存放，负载是否均匀完全取决于分区键选得好不好，不是自动的。
误解：分区键直接决定每条写入落到哪个分片，天然影响写入分布，不只是影响读路径。
optionExplanations_en: This is the textbook bad-partition-key picture — a high-cardinality field like userID usually spreads writes far more evenly than a coarse field like country.
Misconception: a bad partition key isn't just a query inconvenience — an overloaded hot shard can also mean timeouts, rejected writes, or even data loss.
Misconception: sharding only splits where data lives; whether load ends up even depends entirely on how good the partition key is, it isn't automatic.
Misconception: the partition key directly decides which shard each write lands on, so it shapes write distribution too, not just reads.

q: 补全选分区键的原则：
q_en: Fill in the principle for choosing a partition key:
text: 好的分区键要{{最小化}}各分片写入量的方差——图上「{{平}}即是好」；常见做法是对主要标识符（如 {{userId}} 或 postId）取{{哈希}}。
text_en: A good partition key should {{minimize}} the variance in writes per shard — "{{flat}} is good" on the chart; a common approach is to {{hash}} a primary identifier such as {{userId}} or postId.
why: 选键原则：让各分片写入量的方差最小，即每片 ≈ 总写量 / 分片数。对高基数主标识符取哈希通常就能做到。
why_en: Pick the key that minimizes variance in writes per shard, so each shard carries roughly total writes divided by shard count — hashing a high-cardinality identifier usually gets you there.
whenOtherWins: 如果主要查询总是按另一个实体聚合，就要优先评估那个实体是否该做分区键，避免高频读跨片。
tradeoff: 写入均匀分布 vs 高频读是否跨片

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意输入映射成固定范围数值的函数，用来把 key 均匀打散到各分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash function maps arbitrary input to a fixed-range value, used here to spread keys evenly across shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户的唯一标识符，是最常见的分区键候选之一，基数高、分布均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: userId is a user's unique identifier, one of the most common partition-key candidates because it has high cardinality and even distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帖子的唯一标识符，也常作为按帖子维度分布数据的分区键候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: postId is a post's unique identifier and a common partition-key candidate for post-centered data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量各分片写入量离平均值有多远的统计量；越小表示越均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Variance measures how far each shard's write count is from the average; lower variance means more even load.

q: 写入完全均匀铺开了，但每个读请求都要跨所有分片收集数据，后果是？
q_en: Writes are perfectly spread out, but every read has to collect data from all shards — what's the consequence?
scenario: 按随机 UUID 分片后写入完全均匀，但用户主页每次要一口气拉出自己的全部帖子。
scenario_en: After sharding by random UUID the writes spread perfectly evenly, but the user home page still has to pull all of that user’s posts in one go.
options: 读请求命中缓存的概率会因为分片布局自动提高
读写各自独立进行，分片布局对读延迟没有任何影响
每个读者都要向集群所有分片发网络调用，读开销巨大
分片把数据摊开后，写入吞吐反而会因此下降
options_en: The cache hit rate for reads automatically improves because of the sharding layout
Reads and writes are fully independent, so the sharding layout has no effect on read latency
Every reader has to make a network call to every shard in the cluster, so read overhead is huge
Spreading data across shards actually makes write throughput go down
why: 分区键不能只看写：如果读要打到每个分片（scatter-gather），网络调用的开销会吃掉分片收益。要同时问「这个请求要打几个分片？发生得多频繁？」
why_en: If every read must fan out to all shards, the network overhead can erase your sharding gains, so consider the read path when picking a key.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R[读请求] --> G[聚合层]
    G -->|scatter| S1[(Shard A)]
    G -->|scatter| S2[(Shard B)]
    G -->|scatter| S3[(Shard C)]
    S1 -->|partial| M[合并结果]
    S2 -->|partial| M
    S3 -->|partial| M
    M --> Resp[响应]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求同时向多个分片发起子请求，再合并所有结果的读取模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather is a read pattern where one request fans out to many shards and then merges all the partial results.

optionExplanations: 误解：分片布局本身不提高缓存命中率，命中率取决于访问模式和缓存策略，跟分片无关。
误解：跨分片的读请求确实会并发打到多个分片，网络往返直接叠加进读延迟，不是无关。
每次读都要给集群里每个分片各发一次网络调用再合并结果，开销随分片数线性增长——这正是跨分片扇出读的代价。
误解：写吞吐取决于分片是否分散了写量，跟读路径要打几个分片是两个独立的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the sharding layout itself doesn't raise cache hit rate; hit rate depends on access pattern and caching policy, not sharding.
Misconception: a cross-shard read really does fan out to several shards concurrently, adding real network round trips to read latency — it's not independent of the layout.
Each read makes one network call per shard in the cluster and then merges the results, so overhead grows linearly with shard count — that's the cost of fanning a read out across shards.
Misconception: write throughput depends on whether writes are spread out; how many shards a read must hit is a separate question.

scenario: 在为读写最频繁的「最快」数据设计物理布局，需要一套判断分区方案是否会形成瓶颈的自检问题。
scenario_en: You're designing the physical layout for the "hottest" data — the rows with the most reads and writes — and need a self-check for whether the partitioning scheme creates a bottleneck.
q: 该问自己哪两个问题？
q_en: What two questions should you ask yourself?
options: 「这个请求要打几个分片？」和「这个请求发生得多频繁？」
「用 SQL 还是 NoSQL？」和「要不要加缓存？」
「机器多少核？」和「磁盘多大？」
「团队会不会运维？」和「预算多少？」
options_en: "How many shards does this request have to hit?" and "how often does this request happen?"
"SQL or NoSQL?" and "should we add a cache?"
"How many CPU cores?" and "how big is the disk?"
"Can the team operate it?" and "what's the budget?"
why: 目标是读写都尽量均匀铺开、同时把常一起访问的数据放一起。用「打几个分片 × 多频繁」来判断有没有造出瓶颈。
why_en: Ask how many shards each request must hit and how often that request happens to decide whether your layout creates a bottleneck.
whenOtherWins: 对低频请求，跨全部分片的 scatter-gather 可以接受；只有高频请求跨多分片时才必须重新设计布局。
tradeoff: 写均匀铺开 vs 读的 scatter-gather 成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求同时向多个分片发起子请求，再合并所有结果的读取模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather is a read pattern where one request fans out to many shards and then merges all the partial results.

optionExplanations: 打几个分片和多频繁两个维度相乘，才能算出这条访问路径会不会变成瓶颈。
SQL/NoSQL 和要不要加缓存是选型和加速层的问题，回答不了这条路径会打几个分片。
核数和磁盘大小是容量规划，跟一条请求要跨几个分片、多久发生一次是两回事。
团队运维能力和预算影响能不能落地，但判断不出具体某条访问路径是否会成为瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Multiplying "how many shards" by "how often" is what actually tells you whether this access path becomes a bottleneck.
SQL vs NoSQL and whether to add a cache are technology and acceleration questions — they don't answer how many shards a request hits.
Core count and disk size are capacity planning, a separate question from how many shards one request crosses and how often.
Team ops capability and budget affect feasibility, but they don't tell you whether a specific access path is about to bottleneck.

q: 水平分片和垂直分区的区别是？
q_en: What's the difference between horizontal sharding and vertical partitioning?
scenario: 帖子表写入撞顶：正文字段很大、计数器又高频更新，要决定按行铺开还是按列拆表。
scenario_en: A posts table is maxed out on writes — large body fields plus hot counters — so you must choose between spreading rows out or splitting the columns apart.
options: 水平分片和垂直分区其实是同一种技术换了个说法
水平分片切行，垂直分区切列——按访问模式拆开不同数据
水平分片把表按列切开，垂直分区把表按行切开
垂直分区这种拆表方式只能用在缓存层，不能用在主存储
options_en: Horizontal sharding and vertical partitioning are really just two names for the same technique
Horizontal sharding splits rows, vertical partitioning splits columns — separating data by access pattern
Horizontal sharding splits tables by column; vertical partitioning splits tables by row
Vertical partitioning as a table-splitting technique only applies to the caching layer, never primary storage
why: 水平分片按行把同一张表铺到多台；垂直分区按列/类型拆表，把访问模式和扩展需求不同的数据分开存放。
why_en: Horizontal sharding splits rows across servers while vertical partitioning splits columns by access pattern.
tradeoff: 水平分片（按行扩展吞吐） vs 垂直分区（按列隔离访问模式）

rows: 不同访问模式互相干扰

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一张表的不同行分布到多台机器上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal sharding distributes different rows of one table across multiple machines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一张表的不同列拆成多张表，按访问模式分开存放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical partitioning splits one table's columns into multiple tables, separated by access pattern.

optionExplanations: 误解：两者切分的维度完全不同——一个按行铺到多机，一个按列拆到多表，不是同一技术的两个名字。
水平分片按行铺到多台机器解决单表写吞吐；垂直分区按列拆表，把不同访问模式的数据分开存放。
误解：这里把两者的切分方向说反了——水平分片按行切，垂直分区才是按列切。
误解：垂直分区在主存储里同样常见，比如把内容表和高频计数表拆开，不是缓存层专属手法。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the two split along completely different dimensions — one spreads rows across machines, the other splits columns into tables; they're not the same technique renamed.
Horizontal sharding spreads rows across machines to fix single-table write throughput; vertical partitioning splits columns into separate tables by access pattern.
Misconception: this reverses the split direction — horizontal sharding splits by row, and vertical partitioning is the one that splits by column.
Misconception: vertical partitioning is common in primary storage too, like separating a content table from a high-frequency counter table — it's not cache-layer-only.

scenario: 社交帖子的单张大表被三类操作互相干扰：用户写内容、系统高频更新互动计数、分析查询扫大量数据。要做垂直分区。
scenario_en: One monolithic post table is being hammered by three interfering workloads: users writing content, the system updating engagement counts constantly, and analytics scanning huge volumes. Time to vertically partition it.
q: 最合理的拆法是？
q_en: What's the most sensible way to split it?
options: 按帖子 ID 的奇偶把同一份带全部字段的大表复制成两张结构一模一样的表
把 content、like_count、view_count 等所有列统统塞进一个 JSONB 字段里存起来
拆成 post_content、post_metrics、post_analytics 三张表，按访问模式分开存放
什么都不拆分，就在被三种操作互相干扰的大表上继续叠加更多二级索引
options_en: Split the same full-column table into two structurally identical copies by odd/even post ID
Cram every column — content, like_count, view_count, and the rest — into one single JSONB column
Split into post_content, post_metrics, and post_analytics — three tables separated by access pattern
Don't split anything, and just keep adding more secondary indexes to the table three workloads are already fighting over
why: 按访问模式拆：内容表写一次读多次、指标表高频更新、分析表只追加。拆开后互不干扰，还能各自搬到最适合的数据库。
why_en: Split the monolithic table into content, metrics, and analytics tables so each access pattern stops interfering with the others.
whenOtherWins: 如果三类访问的量都不大，单表加索引就够了——垂直分区带来的多库运维成本只有在互相干扰成为真实瓶颈时才值得。
tradeoff: 拆表隔离访问模式 vs 单表加索引的运维简单

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 里以二进制格式存储 JSON 的列类型，查询灵活但不是关系建模的替代品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSONB is PostgreSQL's binary JSON column type — flexible to query, but not a substitute for proper relational schema design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一张表的不同列拆成多张表，按访问模式分开存放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical partitioning splits one table's columns into multiple tables, separated by access pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主键之外为加速特定查询而建的额外索引；在这张大表上继续加会放大写入干扰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A secondary index is extra structure beyond the primary key; adding more here would increase write interference.

optionExplanations: 误解：奇偶复制成两张结构相同的表只是又做了一次水平分片，三种访问模式还是全部挤在同一张表结构里互相干扰。
误解：塞进一个 JSONB 字段等于放弃了列级的独立索引和存储优化，三种访问照样共享同一行、同一份锁。
按访问模式拆成三张表：内容写一次读多次、指标高频小更新、分析只追加，拆开后互不干扰还能各自换合适的存储。
误解：继续叠加索引只会让本就冲突的三种操作在同一张表上多付出更多维护成本，不解决互相干扰的根问题。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: cloning into two structurally identical tables by odd/even ID is just another horizontal split — all three access patterns still share the same row structure and interfere.
Misconception: cramming everything into one JSONB column gives up per-column indexing and storage tuning; all three access patterns still share the same row and lock.
Splitting by access pattern — content written once and read often, metrics updated at high frequency, analytics append-only — removes the interference and lets each move to the storage that fits it.
Misconception: piling on more indexes just adds more upkeep to the same table where three workloads already collide; it doesn't fix the underlying interference.

q: 垂直分区后把三张表搬到不同数据库实例，哪些「表 → 优化方向」的搭配是对的？（多选）
q_en: After vertically partitioning into three tables and moving each to its own database instance, which "table → optimization" pairings are correct? (select all)
scenario: 帖子拆成 content / metrics / analytics 三表，三者访问模式差别很大，可各自选库。
scenario_en: Posts are split into content, metrics, and analytics tables whose access patterns differ sharply, so each one can pick its own database.
options: post_content → 传统 B-tree 索引，为读性能优化
post_metrics → 内存存储或专用计数器，扛高频更新
post_analytics → 时序优化存储或列式压缩数据库
三张表必须留在同一个实例里才正确
options_en: post_content → traditional B-tree indexes, optimized for read performance
post_metrics → in-memory storage or specialized counters, to absorb high-frequency updates
post_analytics → time-series-optimized storage or a column-compressed database
All three tables must stay on the same instance to be correct
why: 垂直分区的收益之一：每张表可以搬到为它的访问模式优化的数据库。内容配 B-tree 读优化、指标配内存计数、分析配时序/列存。
why_en: Each partition can move to a database optimized for it: B-tree indexes for content, in-memory counters for metrics, and columnar or time-series storage for analytics.
whenOtherWins: 如果三张表的访问量都低、事务还常跨列更新，留在同一个实例里更简单，避免分布式事务和运维成本。
tradeoff: 专用存储换性能 vs 多实例的运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库常用的索引结构，适合点查和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is the balanced index structure relational databases commonly use, well suited to point lookups and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列存储相似值再压缩，适合分析表的大范围扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Columnar compression stores similar values by column and compresses them, which suits large analytical scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高频加减计数优化的存储或组件，用来减少通用关系库的行锁和写放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialized counter is storage or logic optimized for frequent increments and decrements, reducing row locks and write amplification.

optionExplanations: 内容表写一次读多次，B-tree 索引能把按 post_id/user_id 的点查和范围查都做快。
互动计数高频加减，内存存储或专用计数器能省掉关系库行锁带来的写等待。
分析事件只追加、常做大范围扫描，列存或时序库的压缩和顺序扫描正好对上这种模式。
误解：强行留在同一实例，三种访问模式还是会继续抢 CPU、锁和磁盘 I/O，没解决拆分想解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: The content table is written once and read often, so B-tree indexes make point and range lookups on post_id/user_id fast.
Engagement counts get updated at high frequency, so in-memory storage or a specialized counter avoids the row-lock waits a relational table would incur.
Analytics events are append-only and usually scanned in bulk, which is exactly what columnar or time-series storage compresses and scans well.
Misconception: forcing all three onto one instance still leaves them fighting over CPU, locks, and disk I/O — it undoes the point of splitting them apart.

scenario: 订单系统平时容量刚好够用，团队要求黑五当天必须能扛住平日 4 倍的下单写入量而不掉线。
scenario_en: The order system's normal capacity is just enough day to day, but the team requires it to absorb 4x the usual write volume on Black Friday without falling over.
q: 如果系统必须能扛峰值 4 倍的写入量，平时的容量利用率意味着什么？
q_en: If the system must always be able to absorb a 4x peak in write volume, what does that imply about normal-time capacity utilization?
options: 平时只能用到约 25% 的总容量，多出的 75% 是为峰值预留的
平时能用到 90% 也没问题，因为峰值来的时候还有缓冲时间去扩容
利用率高低跟系统要扛的峰值倍数完全没有关系
不管会不会遇到峰值，平时都必须把容量用满 100% 才划算
why: 公式是平时利用率 ≤ 1 / 峰值倍数；4 倍峰值就是 ≤25%。多数系统不会长期付 75% 闲置成本，所以会用队列或 load shedding 处理突发。
why_en: Normal utilization must be at most one divided by the peak multiplier, so a four-times peak means twenty-five percent utilization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统实际使用的容量占总配置容量的比例；公式是当前负载 / 总容量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Capacity utilization is the current load divided by total provisioned capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动丢弃部分不重要写入，保住整体可用性的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately dropping some low-value writes when the system is overloaded, to keep the rest of it available.

options_en: Normal-time usage is capped at roughly 25% of total capacity, with the other 75% reserved for the peak
Running at 90% normally is fine too, since there is buffer time to scale up when the peak hits
Utilization has nothing to do with how large the peak multiplier is
Regardless of whether a peak happens, normal-time capacity must be run at 100% to be worth it
optionExplanations: 公式是平时利用率 ≤ 1/峰值倍数：4 倍峰值意味着平时最多只能吃 25% 容量，留 75% 缓冲。
误解：数据库扩容常伴随停机或吞吐下降，等峰值来了才扩容早就来不及，90% 利用率没有安全边际。
误解：峰值倍数正是决定利用率上限的那个变量——倍数越大，平时能用的比例反而越小。
误解：跑满 100% 意味着没有任何缓冲，一旦有峰值或抖动，系统立刻过载。
optionExplanations_en: The formula is normal utilization ≤ 1 / peak multiplier: a 4x peak means normal-time usage caps at 25%, leaving 75% as headroom.
Misconception: database scaling often means downtime or a throughput dip, so waiting for the peak to scale up is already too late — 90% utilization leaves no safety margin.
Misconception: the peak multiplier is exactly the variable that sets the utilization ceiling — a bigger multiplier means a smaller normal-time share.
Misconception: running at 100% leaves zero headroom, so any peak or jitter immediately overloads the system.

q: 为什么「autoscaling」不是写突发的万能药？
q_en: Why isn't "autoscaling" a silver bullet for write bursts?
scenario: 票务系统开售瞬间写入涨 50 倍、只持续两分钟，团队想靠自动扩容扛过去。
scenario_en: A ticketing system sees writes spike fifty times for just two minutes when sales open, and the team wants autoscaling to absorb it.
options: autoscaling 只对无状态的读流量生效，对有状态的写完全没用
扩容需要时间，数据库扩容常有停机或吞吐下降，正撞上业务最忙时
autoscaling 是需要额外单独付费开通的功能，不开就不生效
autoscaling 触发扩容时会主动删除旧数据来腾出空间
options_en: Autoscaling only works for stateless read traffic and does nothing for stateful writes
Scaling takes time, and database scaling often means downtime or a throughput dip — right when the business is busiest
Autoscaling is a feature that needs to be separately enabled and paid for extra, or it simply doesn't kick in
Autoscaling deletes old data to free up space when it triggers
why: 扩容不是瞬时的，数据库系统扩容时常有停机或吞吐降级，正好撞上流量高峰。所以突发要靠缓冲（队列）或舍弃（load shedding），不能只赌 autoscaling。
why_en: Autoscaling takes time and database scaling often means downtime or reduced throughput exactly when traffic is spiking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据负载自动增减计算资源的机制；数据库层的自动扩容通常伴随停机或降速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoscaling automatically adds or removes compute based on load, but database autoscaling often causes downtime or a throughput dip.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动丢弃部分不重要写入，保住整体可用性的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately dropping some low-value writes when the system is overloaded, to keep the rest of it available.

optionExplanations: 这其实对读写都能生效——真正的限制不在读写之分，而在数据库扩容这个动作本身有代价。
扩容不是瞬时的，数据库层的扩容常伴随停机或吞吐下降，而这恰好撞上流量高峰最需要稳定的时刻。
误解：是否收费是成本问题，跟它能不能瞬时应对写突发是两回事，不是这里的核心限制。
误解：autoscaling 触发的是资源增减，不会主动删数据；把资源伸缩和数据保留混为一谈了。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: autoscaling can apply to both reads and writes; the real limit isn't a read/write split, it's the cost of the database-scaling action itself.
Scaling isn't instant, and database-level scaling often brings downtime or a throughput dip — exactly when traffic is spiking and stability matters most.
Misconception: whether it costs extra is a budget question, unrelated to whether it can instantly absorb a write burst — not the core limit here.
Misconception: autoscaling adjusts resources, it doesn't delete data — this conflates resource scaling with data retention.

scenario: 写请求偶尔突发到数据库瞬时扛不住，团队考虑在应用和数据库之间插一层消息队列。
scenario_en: Write requests occasionally burst past what the database can instantly absorb, so the team considers putting a message queue between the app and the database.
q: 在写路径中加入 Kafka/SQS 队列，本质上解耦的是什么？
q_en: Adding a Kafka/SQS queue to the write path fundamentally decouples what?
options: 队列把原本一条链路的读请求和写请求彻底分成两条独立的路径
队列的作用是让客户端不用先经过 DNS 解析就能直接建立连接
写入的「接收」与「处理」分开——入队要快，数据库按稳定速率消费
队列把应用进程和它运行所在的操作系统内核彻底隔离开
options_en: The queue splits what used to be one path into a fully separate read path and write path
The queue lets the client establish a connection directly, skipping DNS resolution entirely
Decouples write "acceptance" from "processing" — enqueueing is fast, while the database drains at its own steady rate
The queue completely isolates the application process from the operating system kernel it runs on
why: 队列把「收下写请求」和「真正写库」分开：突发先进队列缓冲，数据库以稳定速率处理，这就是 burst absorption。
why_en: A write queue decouples write acceptance from write processing so the database drains at a steady rate while the queue absorbs bursts.
diagram:
flowchart LR C[客户端突发写] --> A[App Server] A --> Q[(Kafka / SQS 队列
缓冲突发)] Q -->|稳定速率| W[Worker] W --> D[(数据库)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管消息队列服务，作用和 Kafka 类似，用于缓冲异步写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue, used similarly to Kafka to buffer asynchronous writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列充当缓冲区，吸收短时间的流量尖峰，让下游以稳定速率处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Burst absorption is the queue acting as a buffer that soaks up short traffic spikes so downstream systems can process at a steady rate.

optionExplanations: 误解：队列解耦的不是读写两条链路，本题问的是写路径内部「收下」和「处理」这两步的解耦。
误解：DNS 解析发生在客户端建立连接的更早阶段，跟写路径里加不加队列没有关系。
接收写请求只要求快速入队，数据库则按自己的稳定速率慢慢消费，这正是队列吸收突发流量的方式。
误解：队列是应用层组件，不涉及进程和操作系统内核之间的隔离，这个说法混淆了两个不同层面。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the queue doesn't decouple two separate read/write paths; this question is about decoupling "accept" from "process" within the write path itself.
Misconception: DNS resolution happens earlier, at connection setup, and has nothing to do with whether a queue sits in the write path.
Accepting a write only needs a fast enqueue, while the database drains at its own steady rate — that's exactly how the queue soaks up bursts.
Misconception: the queue is an application-layer component; it has nothing to do with process/kernel isolation — this conflates two different layers.

q: 队列天然是异步的，这给客户端带来什么直接影响？
q_en: A queue is inherently asynchronous — what's the direct consequence for the client?
scenario: 为削峰在写路径前加了 Kafka，但移动端仍要立刻给用户显示「已保存」。
scenario_en: You put Kafka in front of the write path to smooth out spikes, but the mobile app still has to show the user a “saved” confirmation right away.
options: 客户端的写入请求经过队列缓冲之后反而会更快地落进数据库
应用只知道写进了队列，不知道是否已落库，常需要回查确认
客户端必须放弃短连接、改用长期保持的连接才能往队列写数据
队列这一层的引入对客户端的调用方式完全没有任何影响
options_en: Buffering through the queue actually makes the client's write land in the database faster
The app only knows the write reached the queue, not whether it reached the database, so it often needs a way to check back
The client must give up short-lived connections and switch to a long-held connection just to write to the queue
Introducing this queue layer has absolutely no effect on how the client calls the API
why: 入队成功 ≠ 落库成功。异步意味着确认语义变弱，很多场景要给客户端提供回查/回调机制来确认写入最终生效。
why_en: With an async queue the app only knows the write was enqueued, so clients often need a way to check back that it eventually reached the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调用者提交请求后不等待结果立即返回，结果稍后才确定，需要额外机制去确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asynchronous means the caller submits a request and returns immediately without waiting for the result, so confirming the outcome needs a separate mechanism.

optionExplanations: 误解：队列缓冲改变的是何时被处理，不是让落库变快；数据库还是按自己的速率消费。
入队成功不等于落库成功，异步弱化了确认语义，客户端往往要另加回查或回调才能确认写入真正完成。
误解：连接是否长连是客户端和队列服务之间的实现细节，跟写入是不是异步没有必然绑定。
误解：调用方式其实要变——至少要接受「已接受」和「已处理」是两个不同的状态，不能假装没区别。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: buffering through the queue changes when a write gets processed, not that it lands faster — the database still drains at its own rate.
An enqueued write isn't a durable write yet; async weakens the confirmation semantics, so clients often need a poll-back or callback to confirm it truly landed.
Misconception: whether the connection is long-lived is an implementation detail between client and queue service, not something async writes force.
Misconception: the calling pattern does change — clients now have to treat "accepted" and "processed" as two different states, not the same thing.

q: 如果生产者持续以超过数据库消费能力的速率写入队列，会怎样？
q_en: If producers keep writing to the queue faster than the database can consume it, what happens?
scenario: 队列前端持续接 10 万写/秒，后端数据库稳定只能消费 3 万/秒，且这样持续一整天。
scenario_en: The queue takes in a hundred thousand writes per second while the database steadily drains only thirty thousand, and it stays that way all day.
options: 只要接了队列，生产者的写入速率就会被自动限制住
数据库消费速度会随着队列积压自动加快，追上生产速率
超出处理能力的写会被队列静默丢弃，用户完全察觉不到
队列持续无界增长，处理延迟越拖越长，用户体验跟着变差
options_en: Just having a queue in place automatically throttles how fast producers can write
Database consumption speed automatically increases as the backlog grows, catching up to the producer rate
Writes beyond capacity get silently dropped by the queue, and users notice nothing at all
The queue keeps growing without bound, processing delay keeps stretching out, and the user experience keeps getting worse
why: 队列只是缓冲不是产能：入队速率长期大于出队速率就是无界积压，延迟不断攀升。此时即便扩库去追积压，用户体验往往已经恶化。
why_en: If writes enter the queue faster than the database can drain it, the queue grows without bound and processing delay keeps increasing.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[生产者 10k/s] --> Q[(队列积压增长)]
    Q -->|消费者 4k/s| W[Worker]
    W --> D[(数据库)]
    Q -.延迟上升.-> U[用户等待]

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游跟不上时让上游减速或拒绝新请求的机制；没有它，队列就会持续积压。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is a mechanism that slows or rejects producers when downstream can't keep up; without it, the queue keeps backing up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经入队但还没被消费的消息数量；入队长期快于出队时会不断增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue backlog is the number of enqueued messages not yet consumed; it grows when enqueue rate stays above drain rate.

optionExplanations: 误解：队列本身不自带限速，没有额外背压机制的话，生产者可以一直往里写。
误解：数据库的处理速率由自己的硬件和配置决定，不会因为队列堆积就自动提速。
误解：没有背压和限流时，写入不会被悄悄丢弃，而是持续排队，用户会等得越来越久。
生产者写入速度持续超过数据库消费速度时，队列长度会一路走高，用户感知到的延迟也跟着一路变差。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: a queue doesn't throttle by itself; without an added backpressure mechanism, producers can keep writing indefinitely.
Misconception: the database's processing rate is set by its own hardware and config, it doesn't speed up automatically just because the backlog grows.
Misconception: without backpressure or rate limiting, writes aren't quietly dropped — they keep queuing, and users wait longer and longer.
When producers keep writing faster than the database can drain, the queue keeps growing and the delay users feel keeps getting worse.

scenario: 数据库连平峰的稳态负载都扛不住，有人提议「加个 Kafka 队列解决写入问题」。
scenario_en: The database can't even handle normal steady-state load at average traffic, and someone proposes "just add a Kafka queue to fix the write problem".
q: 对这个提议的正确判断是？
q_en: What's the right judgment on this proposal?
options: 队列只该缓冲短暂突发；拿它掩盖稳态容量不足，队列终将被打爆
只要上了队列，就可以从此不再考虑数据库要不要扩容这件事
队列本身能让数据库处理写入的速度变得更快
只要把队列的容量配置得足够大，积压的问题就自然不存在
options_en: A queue should only buffer short-lived bursts; using it to mask insufficient steady-state capacity just hides the real problem, and it will eventually blow up
Once a queue is in place, you never have to think about scaling the database again
A queue by itself makes the database process writes faster
As long as the queue's capacity is configured big enough, backlog simply stops being a problem
why: 队列的正确用法是吸收短暂突发；如果稳态负载就超过数据库产能，队列只会积压成灾。候选人常犯的错就是拿队列糊底层问题。
why_en: Use queues for short-lived bursts, not to patch a database that cannot handle the steady-state load.
whenOtherWins: 如果负载真的是间歇性尖峰、稳态在产能之内，队列就是正确工具——先在需求阶段确认对延迟写入的容忍度。
tradeoff: 队列吸收短暂突发 vs 用它掩盖稳态容量不足

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在非峰值时段的正常持续负载水平，是判断容量是否够用的基准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Steady-state load is the system's normal ongoing load outside of peaks, the baseline for judging whether capacity is sufficient.

optionExplanations: 队列的本职是吸收短暂尖峰；如果稳态负载本身就超过数据库产能，队列只是把积压往后拖，迟早被打爆。
误解：队列不能替代容量规划，数据库依然要按自己的吞吐消费，该扩容还是得扩容。
误解：队列只改变写入到达的时间，不改变数据库每秒实际能处理多少条，处理速度不会变快。
误解：队列容量再大也只是把爆掉的时间往后推，不会修复长期入队快于出队这个根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: A queue's real job is absorbing short spikes; if steady-state load already exceeds database capacity, the queue just postpones the backlog until it eventually blows up.
Misconception: a queue is not a substitute for capacity planning — the database still drains at its own throughput, so it still needs to be scaled if that's the real gap.
Misconception: a queue only changes when a write arrives, not how many the database can actually process per second — processing speed itself doesn't increase.
Misconception: a bigger queue only delays when it blows up, it doesn't fix the underlying problem of enqueue rate staying above drain rate indefinitely.

scenario: 你在考虑给写路径加队列，但还没和面试官对齐需求。
scenario_en: You're considering adding a queue to the write path, but haven't yet aligned with the interviewer on requirements.
q: 加队列之前必须先在需求阶段确认什么？
q_en: Before adding a queue, what must you confirm at the requirements stage?
options: 先纠结队列中间件具体该选 Kafka 还是 SQS 这类产品细节
系统对延迟写入和不一致读的容忍度，确保队列不破坏关键需求
先把队列要开几个分区这种容量参数早早定下来
先确定消费者服务打算用哪种编程语言去实现
options_en: Getting hung up on whether the queue product should be Kafka or SQS
How much tolerance the system has for delayed writes and inconsistent reads, so the queue doesn't break key requirements
Locking in how many partitions the queue should have this early
Deciding upfront which programming language the consumer service will be written in
why: 队列引入异步和最终一致。先确认业务能否容忍写延迟和读到旧数据——多数系统在最高峰能容忍一点延迟，但不能想当然。
why_en: Before adding a queue, confirm at the requirements stage how much write delay and read inconsistency the system can tolerate.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求要求写后立读、强一致确认（如支付扣款），队列这种异步缓冲就不合适，得靠分片/扩容硬扛。
tradeoff: 异步缓冲换吞吐 vs 写后立读的强一致需求

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管消息队列服务，作用和 Kafka 类似。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue, used similarly to Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内读可能读到旧值，但最终会收敛到最新值的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read right after a write may see a stale value, but the system eventually converges to the latest one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端写入成功后，后续读取必须立刻看到自己的最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes means that after a client writes successfully, its later reads must immediately see that write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统确认写入后，后续读取都必须看到最新值，不能短暂读到旧数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means once a write is acknowledged, later reads must see the latest value, not a stale one.

optionExplanations: 误解：Kafka 还是 SQS 是产品选型细节，晚点定都不影响先把一致性边界谈清楚这件事。
队列一旦引入就带来异步和最终一致，必须先确认业务能不能忍受写延迟和读到旧值，这是决定队列能不能用的前提。
误解：分区数是容量实现参数，可以晚点再调，不影响这道题问的一致性容忍边界。
误解：消费者用什么语言是实现细节，不会改变队列带来的延迟写入和最终一致这两个业务后果。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: Kafka vs SQS is a product-choice detail; deciding it later doesn't block settling the consistency boundary first.
Adding a queue introduces async and eventual consistency, so you must first confirm the business can tolerate delayed writes and stale reads — that's the gate on whether a queue is usable at all.
Misconception: partition count is an implementation-capacity parameter that can be tuned later; it doesn't touch the consistency-tolerance question this asks.
Misconception: the consumer's programming language is an implementation detail — it doesn't change the delayed-write, eventual-consistency consequences the queue introduces.

scenario: Strava 位置上报服务跨年夜过载，写入速率持续超过数据库消费能力；用户客户端每几秒就会再上报一次新位置。
scenario_en: Strava's location-reporting service is overloaded on New Year's Eve: write rate exceeds what the database can absorb, and every client reports a fresh location again within seconds.
q: 过载时该怎么处理这批位置写入？
q_en: How should you handle the location writes while overloaded?
options: 加一层 Kafka 队列，把所有位置写全部缓冲下来让数据库慢慢追
主动丢掉距上次上报只有几秒的重复位置写，保住系统不崩
对全部写请求统一返回 503，等负载退下去以后再恢复接收写入
临时把数据库实例垂直扩容到更大规格，靠 autoscaling 顶过峰值窗口
options_en: Add a Kafka queue and buffer every location write so the database can catch up slowly
Deliberately drop location writes that arrive seconds after the previous one, keeping the system alive
Return 503 to all write requests and resume accepting writes once load subsides
Vertically scale the database instance up temporarily and ride out the peak with autoscaling
why: 过载时主动决定接受哪些写、拒绝哪些写，这就是 load shedding。位置上报可重放，牺牲重复上报换来关键写不被拖垮；代价是过载期轨迹变粗。
why_en: Load shedding means deciding which writes to accept and which to drop when overloaded — a dropped location is replaced by a fresher one seconds later, at the cost of coarser tracks during the peak.
tradeoff: 保住部分写的可用性 vs 数据完整性
whenOtherWins: 如果每条写都不可重放（支付扣款、下单），丢弃不可接受，只能靠队列缓冲或提前扩容硬扛。

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动拒绝一部分请求，以保证剩余请求能被正常处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding means deliberately rejecting some requests when a system is overloaded so the remaining ones still get served.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 状态码，表示服务当前不可用、请求未被处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 503, Service Unavailable, tells the client the service could not handle the request right now.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据负载自动增减实例数量的机制，扩缩容本身需要时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoscaling automatically adds or removes instances based on load, but the scaling itself takes time.

optionExplanations: 误解：持续超载下队列只会无界积压，位置数据越排越旧，缓冲并没有解决吞吐缺口。
客户端每几秒自己重发一次，等于自带重试，丢掉的那条几乎立刻被补上。
误解：全量拒绝把「过载」直接升级成「全员不可用」，正是 load shedding 想避免的结果。
误解：数据库扩容通常伴随停机或吞吐降级，正好撞在流量最高的那一刻发生。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: under sustained overload a queue just grows without bound and the locations in it get staler — buffering does not close the throughput gap.
The client resends every few seconds on its own, effectively self-retrying, so a dropped report is replaced almost immediately.
Misconception: rejecting everything escalates overload into a full outage, which is exactly what load shedding avoids.
Misconception: scaling a database usually brings downtime or reduced throughput, landing exactly at the traffic peak.

scenario: Uber 跨年夜在路司机数三倍，位置写入速率持续高于数据库消费速率；团队在写路径前加了 Kafka 队列吸收流量。
scenario_en: On New Year's Eve Uber has 3x drivers on the road and location writes stay above what the database can consume; the team puts a Kafka queue in front of the write path.
q: 持续过载下这个写队列会怎样一步步失效？
q_en: Under sustained overload, how does this write queue fail step by step?
options: 队列无上限积压，写延迟越拖越长，库里的位置全是过期轨迹
队列会自动丢弃最老的消息，系统始终只保留最新位置，不会积压
队列写满后生产者立刻收到强一致的失败回执，客户端可以马上重试
扩容数据库消费端后积压立刻清空，用户侧感知不到延迟，问题自愈
options_en: The queue backlog grows without bound, write latency stretches out, and the database holds only stale positions
The queue automatically discards the oldest messages, so only the newest positions survive and no backlog forms
Once the queue fills, producers get a strongly consistent failure receipt and clients can retry immediately
Scaling the consumer side instantly drains the backlog and users notice no delay, so it self-heals
why: 正常时队列吸收短突发；生产持续快于消费则积压无界增长，写延迟不断变长，数据库里的位置越来越旧。队列治短突发，治不了稳态吞吐不足。
why_en: A queue absorbs short bursts, but when producers stay faster than consumers the backlog grows unbounded and writes land later and later — it masks a steady-state throughput gap instead of fixing it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 放在写路径前的缓冲，把「接受写」和「处理写」解耦。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write queue sits in front of the write path and decouples accepting a write from processing it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产速率长期高于消费速率时，队列中未处理消息数量持续增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unbounded backlog is what happens when the produce rate stays above the consume rate and unprocessed messages keep piling up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

optionExplanations: 积压增长没有天花板，等待时间随之增长，用户看到的位置永远落后于真实位置。
误解：普通消息队列默认保序保留，不会替你挑「最新的留下」，那是 load shedding 的活。
误解：队列的价值恰恰是异步接受，生产者拿到的只是「已入队」，不是写库成功的确认。
误解：数据库扩容期间常有吞吐降级，还要先追完历史积压，用户等待反而更久。
optionExplanations_en: The backlog has no ceiling, wait time grows with it, and the position users see always lags reality.
Misconception: an ordinary message queue keeps messages in order by default and will not pick "keep the freshest" for you — that is load shedding.
Misconception: the queue exists precisely to accept asynchronously; the producer only learns the write was enqueued, not committed.
Misconception: scaling the database often degrades throughput first, and the accumulated backlog still has to be drained, so users wait longer.

scenario: 广告分析系统同时写 impression（曝光）和 click（点击）两类事件，写量约 100:1；峰值超出写入容量，必须丢一部分。
scenario_en: An ad analytics system writes impression and click events at roughly 100:1, and at peak the write volume exceeds capacity so something must be dropped.
q: 过载时该优先丢哪一类事件？
q_en: Which event type should be shed first under overload?
options: 对两类事件按同一比例随机采样丢弃，维持统计口径不偏斜
暂停写入 impression，把容量让给对营收判定更关键的 click
把 click 也压进同一个队列排队，等负载退下去再统一落库
先丢 click，因为 click 数量本来就少，丢掉对整体统计总量影响最小
options_en: Randomly sample both event types at the same rate so the statistics stay unbiased
Stop writing impressions and give the capacity to clicks, which matter more to revenue
Push clicks into the same queue as well and commit everything once load subsides
Drop clicks first, since there are few of them and losing them barely moves the totals
why: 分级丢弃按业务价值排序：click 直接决定计费与转化归因，impression 丢一段时间只损失曝光估算精度。代价是这段窗口的曝光量有缺口。
why_en: Tiered shedding ranks writes by business value: clicks drive billing and attribution, while dropping impressions for a while only blurs reach estimates — at the cost of a gap in impression counts.
tradeoff: 保住高价值写 vs 指标完整性
whenOtherWins: 如果下游主要看 CTR（点击率），分母缺失会让比率失真，这时对两类同比例采样才是对的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告被展示一次的事件，量大但单条价值低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one event recording that an ad was displayed — high volume, low value per record.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点击广告的事件，直接关联计费和转化归因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A click event records that a user clicked an ad, and it ties directly to billing and conversion attribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率，等于点击数除以曝光数，衡量广告效果的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR, or click-through rate, is clicks divided by impressions and is the core measure of ad effectiveness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次成交归到具体哪次广告点击上的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Conversion attribution assigns a purchase back to the specific ad click that produced it.

optionExplanations: 同比例采样保住了比率，却让高价值的 click 也一起丢，计费和归因直接出现漏账。
click 与钱直接挂钩，impression 只是估算基数，按价值排序就该先牺牲后者。
误解：排队不减总量，超出稳态吞吐时队列只会积压，click 的落库反而更晚。
误解：判断依据是业务价值不是数量，click 稀少恰恰说明每条都更贵重。
optionExplanations_en: Uniform sampling preserves the ratio but throws away high-value clicks too, punching holes in billing and attribution.
Clicks map straight to money while impressions are only an estimation base, so value ordering sacrifices impressions first.
Misconception: queueing does not reduce total volume — past steady-state capacity the backlog just grows and clicks land even later.
Misconception: the criterion is business value, not count; clicks being rare is exactly why each one is worth more.

scenario: 订单分析服务已经分了片、加了队列，数据库仍是写瓶颈；每条写都要一次网络往返、一次事务建立和一轮索引更新。
scenario_en: An order-analytics service is already sharded and queued but the database is still the write bottleneck; every single write costs a network round trip, a transaction setup, and an index update.
q: 除了接受既有写量之外还有哪条路？
q_en: Beyond accepting the existing write volume, what other lever is left?
options: 改变写的结构，把多条写合成一批，摊薄每条写的固定开销
继续增加分片数量，把同样多的写摊到更多机器上面去
给数据库加只读副本，把压力从主库整体转移出去处理
把队列的分区数继续调大，提高消费者并行度，让积压更快被排空
options_en: Change the shape of the writes: merge many writes into one batch to amortize the per-write fixed cost
Keep adding shards so the same write volume is spread across more machines
Add read replicas so pressure is moved off the primary database
Raise the queue partition count to increase consumer parallelism and drain the backlog faster
why: 分片和队列都只是把既有写量搬来搬去；批处理直接减少写的条数——网络往返、事务建立、索引更新是每条写的固定开销，合批即摊薄。代价是多一层延迟。
why_en: Sharding and queueing only move a fixed write volume around, while batching reduces the number of writes so the fixed per-write cost is amortized — at the price of added latency.
tradeoff: 合批摊薄固定开销 vs 引入缓冲延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果写是互不相关的单键随机写、根本攒不出同键批，合批毫无压缩，只能靠分片继续摊。

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条写都要付的一次性成本：网络往返、事务建立、索引更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fixed per-write overhead is the cost every single write pays: a network round trip, transaction setup, and index maintenance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库为一次写开启事务、加锁、写日志的准备工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transaction setup is the work a database does to open a transaction, take locks, and log before a write commits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库的只读复制实例，用来分摊读流量，不能分摊写提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the primary that offloads reads but cannot offload write commits.

optionExplanations: 合批把 N 次事务建立和索引更新压成 1 次，减少的是写的条数本身，不是分布位置。
误解：分片只改变写落在哪台机器，每条写的固定开销一分不少地照付。
误解：副本只能分摊读，写提交仍全部落在主库，写瓶颈原样不动。
误解：调分区数提高的是消费并行度，数据库仍要逐条承接同样多的写。
optionExplanations_en: Batching collapses N transaction setups and index updates into one, cutting the write count itself rather than relocating it.
Misconception: sharding only changes which machine a write lands on; each write still pays its full fixed overhead.
Misconception: replicas offload reads only — every commit still hits the primary, so the write bottleneck is untouched.
Misconception: more partitions raise consumer parallelism, but the database still absorbs the same number of individual writes.

scenario: 一个服务从 Kafka topic 读事件、处理后写库。有人提议在应用进程内先攒 500 条再一次性提交数据库。
scenario_en: A service reads events from a Kafka topic, processes them, and writes to a database; someone proposes buffering 500 writes in the process before committing them together.
q: 这个应用层批处理为什么可以安全采用？
q_en: Why is this application-layer batching safe to adopt?
options: 应用不是权威数据源，崩了重读 Kafka 就能恢复这一批
批量提交在数据库里是原子的，所以任何崩溃都不可能造成丢数据
Kafka 已经把消息持久化了，所以数据库这边不需要再关心提交顺序
攒批只是把写延后，应用崩溃时操作系统会把缓冲区自动刷进数据库里
options_en: The app is not the authoritative store, so after a crash it re-reads Kafka to rebuild the batch
A batch commit is atomic in the database, so no crash can ever lose data
Kafka already persisted the messages, so the database side no longer has to care about commit ordering
Batching only delays writes, and on a crash the OS flushes the buffer into the database automatically
why: 攒批安不安全取决于谁是 source of truth：数据还在 Kafka 里，进程崩了从 offset 重读即可。代价是重放会重复投递，写入必须幂等。
why_en: Whether batching is safe depends on who owns the source of truth: the data still lives in Kafka, so a crashed process just re-reads from its offset — at the cost of needing idempotent writes.
tradeoff: 攒批省下的提交次数 vs 崩溃后重放与幂等要求
whenOtherWins: 如果应用本身就是 source of truth（直接接用户请求并已回执成功），应用层攒批就不安全，得改用中间批处理进程。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据的权威副本所在处，丢了就无处可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is where the authoritative copy of data lives — if it is lost, there is nowhere to recover it from.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 分区中每条消息的位置编号，消费者靠它记住读到哪了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka offset is the position number of a message in a partition, letting a consumer remember where it left off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个操作重复执行多次，结果与执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating the same operation many times leaves the same result as doing it once.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 中一类消息的持久化日志通道，可按 offset 重复读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka topic is a durable log channel of messages that can be re-read from any offset.

optionExplanations: 上游日志保留了原始事件，重启后从上次 offset 重读就能补齐未提交的那批。
误解：原子的是「已发出的那次提交」，还没发出的内存批不在数据库的保护范围内。
误解：这题问的是丢不丢数据，提交顺序是另一个话题，不能解释为什么安全。
误解：内存里的应用级缓冲不是操作系统页缓存，进程一没，这批数据就没了。
optionExplanations_en: The upstream log still holds the raw events, so on restart the service re-reads from its last offset and rebuilds the uncommitted batch.
Misconception: atomicity covers a commit that was actually issued; an in-memory batch never sent is outside the database protection.
Misconception: the question is about data loss — commit ordering is a separate topic and does not explain safety.
Misconception: an application-level buffer is not the OS page cache; when the process dies the batch dies with it.

scenario: 一个直接接收用户下单请求的服务，收到请求就返回成功，并把写攒进内存批，每 2 秒提交一次数据库。
scenario_en: A service takes user order requests directly, returns success immediately, buffers writes in an in-memory batch, and commits to the database every 2 seconds.
q: 进程在提交前崩溃会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the process crashes before the batch commits?
options: 已向用户确认成功的那批写随进程一起消失，且无处可重放
写会留在数据库连接池的缓冲里，进程重启后自动补提交上去
客户端会收到超时错误，因此可以安全重试，不存在丢数据窗口
数据库的 WAL（预写日志）里已有这批写的记录，重启后可回放恢复
options_en: The batch already acknowledged to users vanishes with the process, and there is nothing upstream to replay
The writes stay in the connection pool buffer and are committed automatically after restart
Clients get a timeout error and can safely retry, so there is no data-loss window
The database write-ahead log already holds these writes, so a restart can replay them
why: 正常路径：用户拿到成功回执但写只在内存。进程崩溃 → 这批写既没入库也没有上游日志可重读 → 用户看到订单凭空消失。应用是 source of truth 时不能无脑攒批。
why_en: The user already holds a success receipt while the write lives only in memory, so a crash leaves it neither committed nor replayable and the order simply disappears — never batch blindly when the app is the source of truth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据的权威副本所在处，丢了就无处可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is where the authoritative copy of data lives — if it is lost, there is nowhere to recover it from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库在改数据页之前先写的持久化日志，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log, or WAL, is the durable log a database writes before touching data pages, used for crash recovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用数据库连接的客户端组件，只管连接，不保证写的持久化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool reuses database connections on the client side; it manages connections and guarantees nothing about durability.

optionExplanations: 成功回执已经发出，数据却只在进程内存里，上游又没有日志可重读，这是真正的丢数据。
误解：连接池只复用 TCP 连接，不缓存也不重发未提交的业务写。
误解：客户端早已拿到 200 成功回执，压根不会重试，问题正出在这里。
误解：WAL 只保护「已经到达数据库」的写，还在应用内存里的批从没到过数据库。
optionExplanations_en: The success receipt is already out while the data sits only in process memory with no upstream log to replay — that is genuine data loss.
Misconception: a connection pool reuses TCP connections; it neither caches nor resends uncommitted business writes.
Misconception: the client already got a 200 success and will never retry — that is precisely the problem.
Misconception: the WAL only protects writes that reached the database; a batch still in application memory never got there.

scenario: Like Batcher 是写路径上的中间聚合进程：它收 Like 事件，在窗口内按帖子累加计数，再写库。某热帖 1 分钟收到 100 个赞，窗口设为 1 分钟。
scenario_en: A Like Batcher is an intermediate process on the write path: it consumes like events, tallies counts per post inside a window, then writes to the database. One hot post gets 100 likes in a minute with a 1-minute window.
q: 这一分钟里落到数据库的写次数是多少？
q_en: How many database writes land during that minute?
options: 压到 1 次：窗口内 100 个赞聚合成一条计数更新，压缩比 100:1
仍然是 100 次：中间批处理只是把写延后，并不会减少最终落库的写次数
变成 0 次：计数只留在批处理进程内存里，靠读时再实时算
变成 101 次：100 条原始事件加 1 条聚合结果全都要写库
options_en: Down to one: the 100 likes in the window collapse into a single count update, a 100:1 compression ratio
Still one hundred: intermediate batching only defers writes and never reduces how many finally land
Down to zero: the count stays in the batcher memory and is computed at read time
Up to one hundred and one: the 100 raw events plus the aggregate all get written
why: 库写次数 = 帖子数 × 窗口数，与赞的条数无关：1 帖 × 1 窗口 = 1 次写；压缩比 = 100 赞 ÷ 1 次写 = 100:1。这个比值是判断批处理值不值得做的依据。
why_en: Database writes equal posts times windows, not likes: one post times one window is one write, so the compression ratio is 100 likes over 1 write — that ratio is what tells you whether batching is worth it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径上的中间进程，在时间窗口内把同一帖子的点赞累加成一次计数更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Like Batcher is an intermediate process that tallies likes for the same post inside a time window into one count update.

termDefinitions.meaning: 窗口内进来的事件数除以实际落库的写次数，衡量批处理收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The compression ratio is events entering a window divided by writes actually committed, measuring how much batching buys you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 批处理器攒事件的时间长度，窗口越长压缩越多、延迟越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The batching window is how long the batcher accumulates events; longer windows compress more but add latency.

optionExplanations: 同一帖子的赞在窗口内累加，只有最终计数需要落库，所以是 1 次写。
误解：中间批处理不是延后逐条写，而是把同键事件合并成一条计数更新。
误解：批处理器只是缓冲，窗口结束必须把结果写库，否则崩了计数就没了。
误解：原始事件在这条路径上并不落库，Like Batcher 保留的是计数不是明细。
optionExplanations_en: Likes for the same post accumulate inside the window and only the final count is committed, so it is a single write.
Misconception: intermediate batching does not defer per-event writes, it merges same-key events into one count update.
Misconception: the batcher is only a buffer — at window close it must commit, or the count dies with a crash.
Misconception: raw events are not persisted on this path; the Like Batcher keeps the count, not the detail rows.

scenario: 同一套 Like Batcher 换个场景：绝大多数帖子每小时才收到 1 个赞，聚合窗口仍设为 1 分钟。
scenario_en: The same Like Batcher in a different setting: most posts get just one like per hour, while the aggregation window is still one minute.
q: 这时批处理带来的收益是多少？
q_en: How much benefit does batching deliver here?
options: 几乎为零：每个窗口通常只有 1 个赞，聚合不掉任何写
仍有 60 倍收益，因为一小时的赞会被压成 1 次写入操作
收益更大，帖子越冷批处理器内存占用越低，压缩得越充分
收益不变，批处理的压缩比只取决于窗口长度，与事件到达速率无关
options_en: Almost none: each window usually holds a single like, so nothing gets merged away
Still a 60x win, because an hour of likes collapses into one write
Even better: colder posts use less batcher memory and therefore compress more
Unchanged: the compression ratio depends only on window length, not on arrival rate
why: 压缩比 = 窗口内同键事件数；到达率低于每窗口 1 条时压缩比约等于 1，等于白加了一分钟延迟。上批处理之前必须先验证到达率。
why_en: Compression equals same-key events per window, so when arrivals fall below one per window the ratio is about one and you have bought only a minute of latency — validate arrival rate before batching.
tradeoff: 写次数压缩 vs 额外延迟与多一个活动组件
whenOtherWins: 把窗口拉到 1 小时压缩比才起来，但写入可见延迟也变成 1 小时，实时计数场景不可接受。

termDefinitions.meaning: 窗口内进来的事件数除以实际落库的写次数，衡量批处理收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The compression ratio is events entering a window divided by writes actually committed, measuring how much batching buys you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内某个键收到的事件条数，决定窗口内能攒到几条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Arrival rate is how many events a given key receives per unit time, which decides how many can accumulate in a window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要部署、监控和故障处理的额外运行进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A moving part is an extra running component that must be deployed, monitored, and recovered when it fails.

optionExplanations: 窗口内攒不到第二条同键事件，1 条进 1 条出，写次数一点没少。
误解：60 倍要求这一小时的赞落在同一个窗口里，1 分钟窗口根本装不下一小时。
误解：省内存不等于省写入，这题问的是落库写次数有没有减少。
误解：压缩比是「窗口长度 × 到达率」，到达率趋近 0 时窗口再长也压不动。
optionExplanations_en: No second same-key event ever lands in the window, so one in means one out and the write count is unchanged.
Misconception: a 60x win requires an hour of likes inside one window, and a one-minute window cannot span an hour.
Misconception: saving memory is not saving writes — the question is whether committed write count drops.
Misconception: compression is window length times arrival rate; as arrivals approach zero, no window length helps.

scenario: 写吞吐仍不够，有人提议直接调数据库自身的刷盘频率（Redis 默认每 100ms 把写刷一次盘）来吸收写压力。
scenario_en: Throughput is still short and someone proposes tuning the database own flush interval — Redis flushes writes to disk every 100ms by default — to absorb the pressure.
q: 该怎么评价这个数据库层批处理？
q_en: How should you judge this database-layer batching?
options: 可行但是「大锤」：它改的是全库持久化行为，只留给极端情况
首选方案：不用改任何应用代码，风险最低，应当第一个尝试
无效：刷盘频率只影响读延迟，对写入吞吐没有任何实际影响
等价于应用层批处理，只是换个地方做，收益和风险其实完全一样
options_en: Workable but a big hammer: it changes durability for the whole database, so reserve it for extreme cases
The first choice: no application code changes, lowest risk, so try it first
Useless: flush frequency only affects read latency and does nothing for write throughput
Equivalent to application-layer batching, just done elsewhere, with identical benefit and risk
why: 调刷盘频率把攒批下沉到存储引擎，影响的是整库的持久化窗口——崩溃会丢掉这 100ms 内所有键的写。粒度最粗，所以是最后手段。
why_en: Tuning flush interval pushes batching down into the storage engine and widens the durability window for the entire database, so a crash loses every key written in those 100ms — it is a last resort.
tradeoff: 拉长刷盘间隔换写吞吐 vs 崩溃丢失窗口变大
whenOtherWins: 当上游写来自大量互不相关的键、根本攒不出同键批时，数据库层反而是唯一还能调的地方。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内存中已接受的写真正落到磁盘的动作，多数系统的吞吐瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk flush pushes accepted in-memory writes onto durable storage, and it is the throughput bottleneck for most systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存数据结构存储，常用作缓存和高频计数器，可配置刷盘频率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory data-structure store used for caching and high-frequency counters, with a configurable flush interval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写被接受但尚未落盘的时间段，崩溃时这段内的写会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The durability window is the span in which writes are accepted but not yet on disk, and a crash loses everything inside it.

optionExplanations: 这个旋钮一拧全库都受影响，没法只对热点键生效，所以只在别的层都用尽后才动。
误解：不改代码不等于低风险，它换来的是全库范围的数据丢失窗口变大。
误解：刷盘正是多数系统的写瓶颈，攒批刷盘直接影响可持续写入速率。
误解：应用层能挑哪些写攒批，数据库层只能一刀切，风险面完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: This knob affects the entire database and cannot be scoped to hot keys, so it comes only after the other layers are exhausted.
Misconception: not touching code is not low risk — it buys a wider data-loss window across the whole database.
Misconception: disk flushing is exactly the write bottleneck for most systems, so batching flushes moves sustainable write rate.
Misconception: the application layer chooses which writes to batch; the database layer is all-or-nothing, a very different risk surface.

scenario: 直播平台每秒收到数百万条点赞与评论事件，产品只需要展示实时的总计数和最新评论列表，不需要回放每条原始事件。
scenario_en: A live-streaming platform takes millions of like and comment events per second, and the product only needs live totals and the latest comments — never a replay of each raw event.
q: 为什么这里可以做层级聚合？
q_en: Why does hierarchical aggregation apply here?
options: 因为只需要聚合视图，而聚合视图能分阶段增量构建，逐级减量
因为事件量大到必须完整保存每条原始事件，聚合只是加速读取用的索引
因为聚合能保证强一致，比直接写原始事件的一致性更好一些
因为观众数量少于事件数量，所以扇出天然不构成瓶颈问题
options_en: Because only an aggregated view is needed, and such a view can be built incrementally, shrinking volume at each stage
Because the volume forces you to keep every raw event, and the aggregate is just an index that speeds reads up
Because aggregation guarantees strong consistency, which beats writing raw events directly
Because there are fewer viewers than events, so fan-out is not a bottleneck to begin with
why: 高量流数据的前提是下游只要聚合结果、不要每条明细，于是每一级都能先减量再上送。代价是每加一级就多一跳延迟。
why_en: The premise for high-volume stream data is that downstream only needs the aggregate, so each stage can reduce volume before forwarding — each extra stage costs one more hop of latency.
tradeoff: 逐级减量的吞吐 vs 多跳带来的延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要审计或回放每条原始事件（合规、计费明细），中间层就不能丢明细，只能全量落库。

termDefinitions.meaning: 分多级处理数据，每级把事件量减少后再转给上一级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hierarchical aggregation processes data in stages, reducing event volume at each level before forwarding it upward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只保留统计结果（计数、总和）而不保留每条原始事件的数据视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregated view keeps only summary results like counts and sums rather than every raw event.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每来一批新事件就在已有结果上累加，而不是重算全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Incremental build adds each new batch onto the existing result instead of recomputing everything from scratch.

optionExplanations: 计数和最新评论都能在上送前先在本级合并，量级一级比一级小，这正是分层的前提。
误解：正好相反，能丢掉原始明细才是层级聚合成立的条件。
误解：分层聚合走的是最终一致路线，多加几跳只会让收敛更晚，不会更强一致。
误解：直播的痛点恰恰是百万观众对百万写者的全对全扇出，扇出正是瓶颈本身。
optionExplanations_en: Counts and latest comments can both be merged locally before forwarding, so volume shrinks stage by stage — that is the precondition.
Misconception: the opposite is true — being allowed to discard raw detail is what makes hierarchical aggregation possible.
Misconception: staged aggregation is an eventually-consistent design; extra hops delay convergence rather than strengthening consistency.
Misconception: the pain in live streams is exactly the all-to-all fan-out among millions of viewers, so fan-out is the bottleneck.

scenario: 直播间百万观众，每人发的评论都要推给所有其他人，构成全对全扇出；所有观众要的是同一份最终一致的视图。
scenario_en: A live room with a million viewers needs every comment pushed to everyone else, an all-to-all fan-out, and all viewers want the same eventually consistent view.
q: 怎么把读侧的全对全扇出降下来？
q_en: How do you cut down the all-to-all fan-out on the read side?
options: 写到 M 个广播节点，由它们各自扇出给名下的观众
给每个观众各建一条独立投递队列，逐个精确推送每一条新评论
让观众定时轮询数据库拉最新评论，把扇出压力整体转成读压力
按观众 ID 把评论分片存储，让每个观众只从自己那一片读所需数据
options_en: Write to M broadcast nodes and let each fan out to the viewers assigned to it
Give every viewer a dedicated delivery queue and push each new comment to them one by one
Have viewers poll the database periodically, converting all fan-out pressure into read pressure
Shard comments by viewer ID so each viewer reads only from their own slice of the data
why: 全对全的前提是每个写者直接找每个读者；改成写 M 个广播节点后写扇出从 N 降到 M，观众用 consistent hashing 分配到节点。代价是多一跳延迟。
why_en: All-to-all assumes every writer reaches every reader; writing to M broadcast nodes instead drops fan-out from N to M, with viewers assigned by consistent hashing, at the cost of one more hop.
tradeoff: 写扇出从 N 降到 M vs 多一跳延迟与广播节点运维
whenOtherWins: 如果每个观众要的是各自不同的定制视图，广播节点无法复用同一份更新，逐人投递反而更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收更新后转发给挂在自己名下那批观众的中间节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broadcast node receives updates and forwards them to the set of viewers assigned to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把键映射到环上节点的哈希方式，增删节点时只需搬动少量映射。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys onto a ring of nodes so that adding or removing a node moves only a small share of the mappings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条写需要投递到多少个接收方，接收方越多写放大越严重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is how many recipients one write must be delivered to; more recipients means more write amplification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内读可能读到旧值，但最终会收敛到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read right after a write may be stale, but the system converges to the latest value.

optionExplanations: 观众都要同一份视图，所以一份更新可以在广播节点上复用给它名下的所有人。
误解：每人一条队列就是把 N 路扇出原样写下来，一点没减少写放大。
误解：百万观众高频轮询会把压力搬到数据库上，扇出并没有消失只是换了受害者。
误解：按观众 ID 分片要求同一条评论复制进每个观众的分片，写放大反而更大。
optionExplanations_en: All viewers want the same view, so one update can be reused on a broadcast node for everyone assigned to it.
Misconception: a queue per viewer just spells out the N-way fan-out literally and removes no write amplification.
Misconception: a million viewers polling frequently moves the load onto the database — fan-out did not vanish, it changed victims.
Misconception: sharding by viewer ID requires copying each comment into every viewer slice, which amplifies writes further.

scenario: 直播评论加了广播节点后读侧扇出解决了，但所有观众的评论与点赞事件仍然全部打到同一个 root processor。
scenario_en: Broadcast nodes fixed the read-side fan-out for live comments, but every viewer comment and like event still lands on the single root processor.
q: 上游该怎么再减一层写压力？
q_en: How do you shed one more layer of write pressure upstream?
options: 上游加一层 write processor，按评论 ID 路由并窗口聚合后上送
给 root processor 加只读副本，把聚合压力分摊到副本上面去做
让广播节点直接互相同步，彻底去掉 root processor 这个角色
把 root processor 垂直扩容到更大机型，并在它前面加一层写队列做缓冲
options_en: Add a write-processor tier upstream that routes by comment ID and forwards window aggregates
Add read replicas to the root processor so the aggregation load spreads onto the replicas
Let broadcast nodes sync directly with each other and drop the root processor entirely
Vertically scale the root processor to a bigger instance and put a write queue in front of it as a buffer
why: 事件按评论 ID 路由到固定的 write processor，它在窗口内聚合该评论的点赞与评论数，批量上送，root 只做 merge。代价是又多一跳延迟。
why_en: Events route by comment ID to a fixed write processor that aggregates that comment over a window and forwards batches, leaving the root to merely merge — at the cost of another hop of latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按键路由接收事件、在窗口内聚合后再上送的中间处理节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write processor receives events routed by key, aggregates them over a window, and forwards the result upward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 层级聚合最顶层的节点，负责合并各下级送上来的聚合结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The root processor sits at the top of the hierarchy and merges the aggregates sent up by lower tiers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个已聚合的部分结果合并成一份全局结果的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Merging combines several partially aggregated results into one global result.

optionExplanations: 按评论 ID 路由保证同一条评论的事件落在同一个处理器，才能在本级先合并再上送。
误解：副本只帮读，聚合是写路径上的工作，root 收到的事件条数一条不少。
误解：去掉 root 后每个广播节点都要和其它所有节点同步，又变回全对全。
误解：更大机型和队列都不减少事件条数，稳态超载时只是把积压换个地方存。
optionExplanations_en: Routing by comment ID keeps all events for one comment on the same processor, which is what lets it merge locally before forwarding.
Misconception: replicas only help reads; aggregation is write-path work and the root still receives every event.
Misconception: dropping the root forces every broadcast node to sync with every other one, recreating all-to-all.
Misconception: a bigger box and a queue reduce no events — under sustained overload they only relocate the backlog.

scenario: 你打算在设计里同时用上队列、分区和批处理，面试官要求先讲清每项各自的代价再动手。
scenario_en: You plan to use queues, partitioning, and batching together in one design, and the interviewer asks you to state each cost before you propose it.
q: 下面哪些「策略 → 代价」的搭配是对的？（多选）
q_en: Which strategy-to-cost pairings are correct? (select all)
options: 队列：写入变最终一致，客户端要另外回查确认写是否落库
分区：读路径可能受损，跨分区查询要扇出到所有分片再合并结果
批处理：引入额外延迟，并多出一个必须部署和监控的活动组件
队列：能同时提升写吞吐和读一致性，几乎没有需要说明的代价
options_en: Queues: writes become eventually consistent, so clients need a callback to confirm the write landed
Partitioning: the read path can suffer, since cross-partition queries fan out to every shard and merge
Batching: it adds latency and introduces one more moving part to deploy and monitor
Queues: they raise write throughput and read consistency at once, with essentially no cost to mention
why: 三条路都在减少单个组件承担的吞吐，代价各不相同：队列=最终一致+延迟，分区=读路径受损，批处理=延迟+活动组件。先讲代价再提方案。
why_en: All three reduce throughput per component but each has its own cost: queues bring eventual consistency and delay, partitioning compromises the read path, batching adds latency and moving parts — name the cost before proposing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内读可能读到旧值，但最终会收敛到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read right after a write may be stale, but the system converges to the latest value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次查询要发到所有分片再把结果合并，延迟取决于最慢的那片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scatter-gather query goes to every shard and merges results, so its latency is set by the slowest shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要部署、监控和故障处理的额外运行进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A moving part is an extra running component that must be deployed, monitored, and recovered when it fails.

optionExplanations: 队列把「接受写」和「写库」解耦，压力削峰了，但客户端只知入队，需要回查确认。
分区按写均匀铺开，代价是不按分区键的查询要打到每一片，延迟取决于最慢分片。
批处理减的是写的条数，代价是要等窗口关闭，还多一个进程要运维。
误解：队列不改善一致性，它恰恰把强一致确认换成了异步的最终一致。
optionExplanations_en: A queue decouples accepting a write from committing it, smoothing peaks, but the client only knows it was enqueued and must check back.
Partitioning spreads writes evenly at the cost of queries off the partition key hitting every shard, with latency set by the slowest.
Batching cuts the number of writes, paying with the wait for the window to close plus one more process to operate.
Misconception: queues do not improve consistency — they trade a strongly consistent acknowledgment for asynchronous eventual consistency.

scenario: 线上 8 个分片写满要扩到 16 个。有人提议停服，把全量数据按新的 hash 重算后搬到新分片，再开服。
scenario_en: Eight shards are saturated and must become sixteen; someone proposes taking the system offline, rehashing all data onto the new shards, then reopening.
q: 这个朴素 resharding 在大数据集上会怎么破？
q_en: How does this naive resharding break on a large dataset?
options: hash 结果几乎全变，绝大多数数据都要搬，大数据集意味着数小时停机
只有一半的数据需要搬动，因此停机时间可以控制在分钟级别里面
数据不用搬，客户端换个 hash 函数就能直接找到新分片上的数据
搬迁期间写入会自动排队缓冲，服务不中断，用户完全感知不到影响
options_en: Nearly every hash result changes, so almost all data must move, and a large dataset means hours of downtime
Only half the data needs to move, so downtime stays in the minutes range
No data moves at all: clients just switch hash functions and find data on the new shards
Writes are queued automatically during the move, service stays up, and users notice nothing
why: 分片数从 8 变 16，key 到分片的映射对绝大多数 key 都变了，等于全量重排；停服期间读写全不可用，数据集越大停机越久。这就是朴素方案不能上生产的原因。
why_en: Going from 8 shards to 16 changes the key-to-shard mapping for almost every key, so it is a full reshuffle with reads and writes unavailable throughout, and the bigger the dataset the longer the outage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改变分片数量并把数据重新分配到新分片集合的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resharding changes the number of shards and redistributes data across the new set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按新的分片数重新计算每个 key 归属哪个分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rehashing recomputes which shard each key belongs to under the new shard count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务对外完全不可用的时间段，迁移期间读写都被拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Downtime is the period when the service is fully unavailable and both reads and writes are refused.

optionExplanations: 映射变了就得逐条搬，数据量决定搬迁时长，期间服务是彻底关着的。
误解：分片数一变，取模结果对大部分 key 都会落到不同分片，不是只动一半。
误解：换 hash 函数只改「该去哪找」，数据本身还躺在旧分片上，找不到。
误解：这个方案的前提就是停服，没有双写也没有缓冲，写请求直接被拒。
optionExplanations_en: Once the mapping changes every row must be moved, dataset size sets the duration, and the service is fully closed throughout.
Misconception: changing the shard count sends most keys to a different shard under modulo, not just half of them.
Misconception: swapping the hash function only changes where you look; the data still sits on the old shards and is not found.
Misconception: this plan is defined by going offline — there is no dual write and no buffer, so writes are simply rejected.

scenario: 同一次 8→16 分片扩容，业务要求迁移期间不停服、不丢任何写。
scenario_en: The same 8-to-16 shard expansion, but the business requires zero downtime and zero lost writes during migration.
q: 生产环境该怎么迁这批数据？
q_en: How should production migrate this data?
options: 渐进迁移：迁移期间向新旧分片双写，读优先走新分片
先把流量整体切到新分片，再后台把旧数据慢慢补过去，读写都只打新分片
只对新写入使用新分片，旧数据永远留在旧分片上，不做任何迁移动作
对全库加只读锁，边搬边只允许读，搬完之后再统一放开写入口
options_en: Gradual migration: dual-write to both old and new shards during the move, and read with preference for the new shard
Cut all traffic to the new shards first, then backfill old data in the background while reads and writes hit only the new shards
Send only new writes to the new shards and leave old data on the old shards forever, migrating nothing
Take a read-only lock on the whole database, allow reads while copying, then reopen writes when the copy finishes
