scenario: 每个 Redis shard 约能处理 100k checks/sec；目标总吞吐是 1M checks/sec。
scenario_en: Each Redis shard handles about 100k checks/sec, and the target total throughput is 1M checks/sec.
q: 要达到这个目标吞吐，Redis 状态应该怎么部署？
q_en: How should Redis state be deployed to hit this target throughput?
options: 继续用单实例，靠升级硬件解决
关闭一部分限流规则来降低压力
按 client key 分片到约 10 个实例
把全部限流状态复制到每一个 gateway 节点上做本地判断
why: 1M / 100k ≈ 10，量级上需要十几个 shard 而不是一个大实例；真实生产还要再加副本和余量。
why_en: One million divided by about 100k checks per shard is roughly ten shards, plus replicas and headroom in production.
options_en: Keep a single instance and just upgrade hardware
Turn off some rate-limit rules to reduce load
Shard state by client key across about ten instances
Replicate all rate-limit state to every gateway node and decide locally on each one
optionExplanations: 硬件升级能小幅提升单实例的吞吐上限，但离 10 倍差距还差得远，量级上解决不了问题。
关掉规则等于放弃限流本身要保护的东西，不是解决吞吐瓶颈的办法。
用目标吞吐除以单 shard 能力，先得到约 10 个 shard 的量级，再另加副本和余量。
把所有数据复制到每个节点，写入要同步到所有副本，反而会把单点的写入压力放大成全网压力。
optionExplanations_en: Upgrading hardware can nudge a single instance's ceiling up a bit, but it's nowhere close to a 10x gap — it doesn't fix the order-of-magnitude problem.
Turning off rules gives up the very protection rate limiting exists for — it doesn't address the throughput bottleneck.
Divide target throughput by per-shard capacity to get roughly ten shards first, then add replicas and headroom.
Copying all data to every node means each write has to sync to every replica, turning what was one instance's write pressure into pressure across the whole cluster.

q: 把分片限流检查流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the sharded rate-limit check flow into the correct order:
steps: gateway 提取 userId/IP/API key 作为 identifier
Redis shard 内原子执行 Token Bucket 判断
对 identifier 做 consistent hash 或计算 Redis slot
根据结果返回 passes/remaining/resetTime
把请求路由到负责该 identifier 的 Redis shard
why: identifier 是分片键，必须稳定映射到同一 shard。到达 shard 后，算法本身和单实例 Token Bucket 基本一样。
why_en: The gateway extracts a stable identifier, routes it to the owning Redis shard, and runs the token-bucket decision there atomically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Req[Request key] --> Hash[Hash key]
Hash --> Shard[Redis shard]
Shard --> Lua[Atomic check]
Lua --> Decision[Allow or 429]

scenario: Redis 挂了，gateway 拿不到任何 bucket 状态，必须立刻决定这批请求怎么办。
scenario_en: Redis is down, the gateway can't read any bucket state, and it has to decide right now what to do with incoming requests.
q: fail-closed 的含义是什么？
q_en: What does fail-closed mean?
options: 限流器故障时改为放行所有请求
只对已付费的用户执行限流
把无法判断的请求先排队缓存，等 Redis 恢复后再处理
无法判断时拒绝请求，保护后端但牺牲可用性
why: fail-closed 保守：判断不了就拒绝，保护后端但会牺牲可用性——健康的请求也可能被挡在门外。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects requests it cannot verify, protecting backends at the cost of rejecting some healthy traffic too.
tradeoff: 保护后端优先 vs 可用性优先
options_en: Switch to allowing all requests when the limiter fails
Only rate-limit paying customers
Buffer the unverifiable requests in a queue until Redis recovers and process them then
Reject requests it cannot verify, protecting the backend at the cost of availability
optionExplanations: 故障时改成放行所有请求，说的其实是 fail-open 的定义，跟这里问的正好相反。
只挑付费用户限流是一个业务规则的选择，跟「故障时怎么办」这个 fail-closed 的定义没有关系。
把无法判断的请求挂起排队等 Redis 恢复，是另一种处理策略，不是 fail-closed 这个术语本身的定义。
判断不了配额时选择拒绝而不是放行，这样能护住后端，但代价是一些本该通过的健康请求也会被挡在门外。
optionExplanations_en: Switching to allow everything on failure is actually the definition of fail-open — the opposite of what's being asked here.
Rate-limiting only paying users is a business-rule choice, unrelated to what fail-closed means about handling a failure.
Queuing the unverifiable requests until Redis recovers is a different handling strategy, not the definition of the term fail-closed itself.
Choosing to reject rather than allow when quota can't be verified protects the backend, at the cost of also blocking some healthy requests that should have gone through.

scenario: Redis 在流量高峰时不可用，gateway 选择照常放行所有请求。
scenario_en: Redis becomes unavailable during a traffic spike, and the gateway chooses to let every request through.
q: fail-open 的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of fail-open?
options: Redis 挂掉后流量直通后端，高峰易级联故障
它会把所有健康请求也一起拒绝掉
它反而让限流判断更加精确
它要求每个客户端自己实现 Lua 限流脚本
why: fail-open 保住了可用性，但暂时失去限流保护；如果 Redis 正是因为流量或攻击才出问题，放开闸门可能直接压垮后端。
why_en: Fail-open keeps the API available but removes protection at the exact moment traffic or an attack may already be overwhelming the backend.
tradeoff: 可用性优先 vs 失去保护窗口
options_en: With Redis down, traffic passes straight to the backend and can cascade in a spike
It rejects every healthy request as well
It makes rate-limit decisions more precise
It requires every client to write its own Lua limiting script
optionExplanations: Redis 不可用时流量直通后端，如果高峰或攻击流量正好赶上这个时候，后端可能被直接压垮，引发级联故障。
拒绝所有健康请求说的是 fail-closed 的行为，fail-open 恰恰相反，是继续放行。
fail-open 时限流器已经不工作了，谈不上判断更精确，反而是完全没有判断。
Lua 脚本是服务端 Redis 里的实现细节，跟客户端要不要自己实现什么完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: When Redis is down, traffic passes straight through, and if that coincides with a traffic spike or an attack, the backend can get overwhelmed, triggering a cascading failure.
Rejecting every healthy request describes fail-closed behavior — fail-open does the opposite and keeps letting traffic through.
Under fail-open the limiter has effectively stopped working, so there's no decision being made at all, let alone a more precise one.
The Lua script is a server-side Redis implementation detail, unrelated to whether clients need to implement anything themselves.

scenario: 社交平台在 viral 事件中流量突增；Redis-based 限流层故障或超时，系统无法可靠读取/更新计数，而后端数据库和应用也可能已经接近容量上限。
scenario_en: A social platform sees a traffic surge during a viral event; the Redis-based limiter fails or times out so counts can't be reliably read or updated, and the backend database and app are already near capacity.
q: 此时最直接选择哪种失败模式？
q_en: Which failure mode is the right call here?
options: fail-open
fail-closed
无限排队
客户端自觉限流即可
why: fail-closed = 限流器不可用时默认拒绝或降级拦截；在后端已接近容量时，它牺牲一部分可用性来避免流量绕过限流打爆数据库。fail-open = 限流器不可用时默认放行，用户可用性更高，但可能把 Redis 故障放大成级联故障。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects or degrades requests when the limiter is unavailable, protecting a near-capacity backend from a Redis outage becoming a cascading failure.
whenOtherWins: 如果后端余量很大、限流只是软配额或非关键保护，fail-open 更适合，因为它优先保证用户请求继续成功。
tradeoff: 下游保护/防级联故障 vs 用户可用性
options_en: Fail-open
Fail-closed
Queue requests indefinitely
Rely on client-side limiting alone

termDefinitions.meaning: 保护组件故障时默认放行请求；在限流场景里，就是 Redis/限流器超时或不可用时仍让请求进入后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-open means allowing requests by default when the protective component fails, such as letting traffic through when Redis rate limiting times out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保护组件故障时默认拒绝或降级拦截请求；在限流场景里，就是无法判断配额时返回 429/503 或走保守拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-closed means rejecting or degrading requests by default when the protective component fails, such as returning 429 or 503 when quota cannot be checked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个组件故障后，流量、重试或负载转移继续压垮下游组件，导致故障范围扩大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascading failure is when one component failure shifts load or retries onto downstream components until more of the system fails.

optionExplanations: fail-open 会在限流器故障时默认放行，用户成功率更高，但这里后端已经接近容量，放行会让绕过限流的流量直接冲垮它，级联风险太大。
fail-closed 在无法判断配额时默认拒绝，会挡住一部分健康请求，但优先保护已经吃紧的后端不被打垮，是这里更安全的选择。
把请求无限期挂起等 Redis 恢复，只会在入口层堆积连接、线程和内存，往往比直接快速失败更危险。
把限流责任丢给客户端本身不难实现，但攻击者或异常客户端不会乖乖配合，服务端失去了强制手段。
optionExplanations_en: Fail-open keeps the API available by default when the limiter breaks, but here the backend is already near capacity, so letting traffic bypass the limiter risks tipping it into cascading failure.
Fail-closed rejects requests it can't verify, blocking some healthy traffic, but that protects an already-stressed backend from being overwhelmed — the safer call here.
Queuing requests indefinitely until Redis recovers just piles up connections, threads, and memory at the entry layer, usually more dangerous than failing fast.
Handing rate limiting to the client is easy to build, but attackers or buggy clients won't reliably cooperate, so the server loses its only enforcement point.

scenario: Redis 已按 client 分片，但任一 shard 挂掉会影响其负责的一批用户；希望自动恢复写能力。
scenario_en: Redis is already sharded by client, but any shard going down affects the batch of users it owns; the goal is automatic recovery of write capability.
q: 标准高可用方案是什么？
q_en: What is the standard high-availability approach?
options: 只用单 master，完全不配副本
把 bucket 状态写进浏览器本地存储
每个 shard 配副本，故障时自动提升
每次故障都靠人工手动切换 Redis
why: master-replica 复制加自动 failover 是标准做法，Redis Cluster 能自动探测故障并提升副本；代价是成本和短暂复制延迟。
why_en: Standard Redis high availability uses master-replica replication with automatic promotion on failure, at the cost of extra infrastructure and brief replication lag.
whenOtherWins: 极小系统能接受单实例故障；跨地域强隔离需求可能要每区域独立集群加更复杂策略。
tradeoff: 自动故障恢复 vs 额外副本成本和复制延迟
options_en: Use a single master with no replicas at all
Write bucket state into the browser's local storage
Give every shard a replica and auto-promote it on failure
Fail over by hand every single time
optionExplanations: 只有一个 master、不配副本，它一旦挂掉，负责的那批用户的限流状态就直接不可用了。
把状态存进用户浏览器本地，用户换设备、清缓存都能重置额度，根本挡不住真正想绕过限流的人。
每个 shard 配副本，master 挂了副本自动顶上，恢复写能力不用等人来手动切换。
每次故障都靠人手动切，从发现到真正切换完的这段时间，那批用户的限流写入完全没人管。
optionExplanations_en: A single master with no replica means the moment it dies, the whole batch of users it owned lose their rate-limit state entirely.
Storing state in the user's browser local storage lets them reset their quota just by switching devices or clearing cache — no real barrier against someone trying to dodge the limit.
Giving every shard a replica that auto-promotes on failure restores write capability without waiting for a human to step in.
Failing over by hand leaves a gap between the moment a shard dies and someone actually completing the switch, during which that batch of users has no working rate-limit writes at all.

scenario: 限流器挡在所有 API 流量入口，它一旦异常，API 要么被误杀要么裸奔。
scenario_en: The limiter sits in front of all API traffic, so when it misbehaves the API either blocks good users or runs completely unprotected.
q: 限流系统应监控哪些指标？（多选）
q_en: Which metrics should a rate-limiting system monitor? (multi-select)
options: Redis CPU、内存、网络连通性
限流检查成功率和延迟
进入 fail-open/fail-closed 降级模式的事件
每个用户的头像颜色
why: 限流器挡在请求入口，必须能快速发现 Redis 异常、决策延迟升高或降级模式被触发；跟限流健康无关的指标不该混进来。
why_en: Rate-limiter observability should cover Redis health, check latency and success rate, and transitions into fail-open or fail-closed.
options_en: Redis CPU, memory, and network connectivity
Rate-limit check success rate and latency
Events entering fail-open or fail-closed degraded mode
Every user's avatar color
optionExplanations: Redis CPU、内存、网络这些底层健康指标出问题，限流检查会先变慢甚至直接失败。
限流检查成功率和延迟直接反映这道入口关卡本身有没有在正常工作。
进入 fail-open/fail-closed 的事件要单独监控，因为一旦触发就意味着系统正在用降级模式运行。
用户头像颜色跟限流系统健不健康没有任何关系，混进监控面板只会增加噪音。
optionExplanations_en: Redis CPU, memory, and network health degrading is usually the first sign a rate-limit check is about to slow down or fail.
Check success rate and latency directly show whether this entry-point gate is working normally.
Transitions into fail-open or fail-closed deserve their own alert, because hitting either one means the system is already running in a degraded mode.
A user's avatar color has nothing to do with whether the limiter is healthy — it's just noise on the dashboard.

scenario: 每次限流检查都要访问 Redis；如果 gateway 每次都新建 TCP 连接，额外握手会让请求延迟不可接受。
scenario_en: Every rate-limit check hits Redis; if the gateway opens a new TCP connection each time, the extra handshake makes request latency unacceptable.
q: 最重要的低延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the single most important low-latency optimization?
options: 每次请求都新建一条 TCP 连接，用完立刻关闭
把限流检查改成离线批处理
删除所有 headers
连接池 / 持久 Redis 连接
why: 连接池复用已建立的 TCP 连接，省掉每次 20-50ms 级别的握手开销；Redis 操作本身很快，连接管理常常才是主要延迟来源。
why_en: Connection pooling reuses established TCP connections and avoids repeated handshake overhead on the hot path.
whenOtherWins: 很低频的管理接口可以用简单短连接；核心请求路径必须复用连接。
tradeoff: 复用连接省握手延迟 vs 每次新建连接的简单但慢
options_en: Open a brand-new TCP connection per request and close it right after
Turn rate-limit checks into an offline batch job
Strip out all response headers
Connection pooling with persistent Redis connections

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用一组已建立的连接，而不是每次请求都重新握手。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connection pooling reuses a set of already-open connections instead of opening a new one per request.

optionExplanations: 每个请求都开新连接，意味着每次都要重新走一次 TCP 握手，这正是要避免的延迟来源，不是优化。
把限流检查改成离线批处理，请求进来时根本等不到判断结果，这跟「低延迟在线检查」的前提直接冲突。
删掉 headers 省不了访问 Redis 的那次网络往返，跟连接开销完全不是一回事。
连接池复用已经建立好的 TCP 连接，省掉每次新建连接的握手开销，而 Redis 操作本身已经够快，连接管理常常才是真正的延迟大头。
optionExplanations_en: Opening a fresh connection per request means redoing the TCP handshake every single time — that's exactly the latency source to avoid, not an optimization.
Turning the check into an offline batch job means a live request has nothing to wait on for its answer — it directly conflicts with needing a low-latency online check.
Stripping out headers doesn't save the network round trip to Redis at all — that's an unrelated cost from connection overhead.

Connection pooling reuses TCP connections that are already open, skipping the handshake each time, and since the Redis operation itself is already fast, connection management is often the real latency driver.

scenario: 用户分布全球；东京用户如果每次限流都访问弗吉尼亚 Redis，会多出明显网络延迟。
scenario_en: Users are distributed globally; if a Tokyo user's every rate-limit check hits Redis in Virginia, that adds noticeable network latency.
q: 最大的地理延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest optimization for geographic latency?
options: 多区域部署 Gateway 和 Redis，就近完成限流
把所有流量强制回源到单一区域
只在 HTTP 429 响应的 body 里多返回几个诊断字段
直接关闭 TLS 加密传输
why: 限流状态放到离用户近的区域能省掉跨洋 RTT；代价是跨区域一致性更复杂，但限流通常可以接受区域间最终一致。
why_en: Deploying gateways and Redis regionally keeps rate-limit checks close to users and avoids cross-continent round trips.
whenOtherWins: 如果必须全局强一致限额，需要单一权威区域或分层协调，但会牺牲延迟。
options_en: Deploy gateways and Redis regionally, so checks stay local
Force all traffic back to a single origin region
Just return a few more diagnostic fields in the 429 response body
Simply turn off TLS encryption
optionExplanations: 把 Gateway 和 Redis 都部署到离用户近的区域，限流检查就不用跨洋来回，直接省掉大部分 RTT。
把所有流量强制送回单一区域处理，等于把每个东京用户的请求都拖上一趟跨洋往返，延迟问题完全没解决。
只改 429 响应体里的字段跟网络距离毫无关系，请求依然要先跑到远端 Redis 才能拿到判断结果。
去掉传输层加密顶多省一点点握手开销，跨大洲的物理传播时延才是真正的瓶颈，这里根本没打中点子。
optionExplanations_en: Deploying gateways and Redis regionally keeps each check local, so it skips most of that cross-ocean round trip.
Forcing all traffic back to one origin region still sends every Tokyo request on the same long round trip — it doesn't fix the latency.
Changing a field in the 429 response body has nothing to do with network distance; the request still has to reach the far-away Redis first.
Turning off TLS only trims a bit of handshake time — the real bottleneck is physical propagation delay across continents, so this misses the point.

scenario: 每次限流检查都要访问 Redis，端到端只有 10ms 预算，你想再压掉网络往返成本。
scenario_en: Every rate-limit check hits Redis inside a ten-millisecond end-to-end budget, and you want to squeeze more cost out of the round trips.
q: 除连接池和地理部署外，文章提到哪些可选优化？（多选）
q_en: Besides connection pooling and geographic deployment, which optional optimizations does the article mention? (multi-select)
options: 每次请求都查询中央配置数据库
Redis pipelining 或 Lua scripts 减少往返
同用户突发请求的 request batching
本地缓存限流状态但要小心 stale
why: pipelining/Lua 减少往返，batching 摊薄热点请求，本地缓存要小心 stale；但每次查中央配置库会直接拖垮延迟目标，不该走这条路。
why_en: Pipelining, Lua scripts, careful batching, and cautious local caching can cut latency, while querying a central config database on every request would not.
options_en: Querying a central config database on every request
Redis pipelining or Lua scripts to cut round trips
Batching a burst of requests from the same user
Local caching of rate-limit state, done carefully to avoid staleness
optionExplanations: 每个请求都去查一次中央配置库，等于给本来要省的那次 Redis 往返重新加回一次数据库往返，直接违背低延迟目标。
pipelining 或 Lua 脚本把多条命令并成一次往返，省掉网络本身的排队和握手开销。
把同一用户短时间内的多个请求合并检查，能摊薄高频突发场景下的调用次数。
本地缓存限流状态能省掉一次网络调用，但要设好较短的刷新间隔，否则本地看到的配额会跟 Redis 里的真实值脱节。
optionExplanations_en: Querying a central config database on every request just re-adds the round trip you were trying to save, working against the latency goal.
Pipelining or Lua scripts fold several commands into one round trip, cutting network queueing and handshake overhead.
Batching several of the same user's requests together thins out the call count during a high-frequency burst.
Caching rate-limit state locally saves a network call, but needs a short refresh interval, or the local view drifts away from what Redis actually has.

scenario: 限流状态按 client key 分片，监控发现某一个 shard 的 CPU 远高于其他 shard。
scenario_en: Rate-limit state is sharded by client key, and monitoring shows one shard running far hotter than all the others.
q: Rate Limiter 中的 hot key 通常意味着什么？
q_en: What does a hot key usually mean in a rate limiter?
options: 某篇帖子被非常多不同用户同时读取
单个 client 请求量极高，压垮所在 shard
某张数据库表的 schema 设计得不好，导致查询变得很慢
所有用户的请求量都完全均匀
why: 限流状态按 client key 分片，所以 hot key 就是某一个 client 自己的请求量极大；可能是滥用攻击，也可能是合法高流量客户或 NAT 聚合。
why_en: A rate-limiter hot key is one client identifier sending enough traffic to overload the single shard that owns it.
options_en: One post is being read by many different users
One client sends extreme traffic and overloads its shard
A database table has a poorly designed schema that makes queries slow
Every user's request volume is perfectly even
optionExplanations: 很多人读同一篇帖子是缓存场景里的热点 key，跟这里按 client 分片的限流状态是两回事。
因为分片键就是 client identifier，这个 identifier 的全部计数都会打到同一个 owner shard。
hot key 是流量分布的问题，跟数据库表结构设计得好不好没有关系。
如果所有用户请求量都完全均匀，压根就不会出现某个 shard 被压垮的 hot key 问题。
optionExplanations_en: Many people reading the same post is the hot-key pattern in a caching scenario, a different thing from rate-limit state sharded by client.
Because the shard key is the client identifier, all counter operations for that identifier hit the one owner shard.
A hot key is about traffic distribution, unrelated to whether a database table's schema is well designed.
If every user's traffic were perfectly even, there'd be no hot-key problem overloading a single shard in the first place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 key 承受了不成比例的巨量请求。限流里=某个 client(状态按其 key 分片)请求量极大,所有计数都砸向它所在的那一个 shard、把该 shard 压垮(别的 shard 却闲着)。成因:合法大客户 / 攻击滥用 / NAT 把很多人聚成一个 IP。缓解:各 gateway 本地预计数+周期同步,或把热 key 拆成 key+随机后缀分散到多 shard 再求和
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key takes a disproportionate share of traffic. In rate limiting it means one client (sharded by its key) sends huge volume, so all its counter ops hit the single shard owning it and overload it while others idle. Causes: a big legit customer, an attacker, or NAT aggregating many users into one IP. Mitigate with local pre-counting + periodic sync, or splitting the hot key into key+random-suffix sub-keys across shards and summing.

scenario: 某企业客户流量极大但完全合法，你要保住 shard，又不想赶走这个付费客户。
scenario_en: One enterprise customer sends huge but entirely legitimate traffic; you need to protect the shard without driving away a paying customer.
q: 对合法高流量 client，文章建议哪些处理方式？（多选）
q_en: For legitimate high-volume clients, which approaches does the article recommend? (multi-select)
options: 鼓励 client-side rate limiting 平滑流量
立刻永久封禁所有高流量 client
提供 batch API 减少检查次数
premium tiers 或 dedicated infrastructure
why: 合法高流量要引导承载，不是一刀切封禁：客户端限流平滑流量，批处理减少检查次数，付费/专用资源隔离压力。
why_en: Legitimate high-volume clients are handled with client-side limiting, batch APIs, or premium and dedicated infrastructure rather than blanket bans.
options_en: Encourage client-side rate limiting to smooth traffic
Permanently ban every high-volume client immediately
Offer a batch API to cut the number of checks
Offer premium tiers or dedicated infrastructure
optionExplanations: 鼓励客户端自己做限流，能把突发请求磨平成平滑曲线，减少一上来就撞限额被拒的情况。
对合法高流量客户直接永久封禁，等于把付费大客户当攻击者处理，业务上根本行不通。
提供 batch API 把多次调用合成一次，直接减少要检查的请求数量本身。
给这类客户开 premium tier 或专用基础设施，把它们的压力从共享资源池里挪出去。
optionExplanations_en: Encouraging client-side limiting smooths out bursts into a steadier curve, so fewer requests slam straight into the limit and bounce.
Permanently banning a legitimate high-volume client immediately treats a paying customer like an attacker, which doesn't work as a business move.
A batch API folds several calls into one, cutting the actual number of requests that need checking.
Giving these clients a premium tier or dedicated infrastructure moves their load out of the shared resource pool entirely.

scenario: 有 client 持续以攻击级速率打你的 API，而且部分流量来自共享 NAT 出口 IP。
scenario_en: A client keeps hitting your API at attack-level rates, and some of that traffic comes from a shared NAT egress IP.
q: 对滥用或攻击流量，哪些策略合理？（多选）
q_en: For abusive or attack traffic, which strategies are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 持续触发限流后临时加入 blocklist
使用 Cloudflare/AWS Shield 等 DDoS 防护在更前面挡流量
完全依赖客户端自觉
降低 IP-based 规则对 NAT 的误伤并更多依赖 authenticated user limit
why: 恶意流量不能指望客户端自觉，应尽早用 blocklist 和上游 DDoS 防护挡住；共享 IP 也可能是合法 NAT，IP 规则要谨慎、多依赖已登录用户限额。
why_en: Abusive traffic needs blocklists and upstream DDoS protection, while IP-based rules must stay cautious about shared NATs.
options_en: Temporarily blocklist a client after it repeatedly hits limits
Use upstream DDoS protection such as Cloudflare or AWS Shield
Rely entirely on client good behavior
Ease IP-based rules for NAT and lean more on authenticated user limits
optionExplanations: 持续触发限流的 client 先临时拉黑一段时间，比每次都放行再拒绝更省资源。
Cloudflare/AWS Shield 这类上游防护能在流量到达自己的 Redis 之前就先挡一层，减轻后面限流的压力。
完全指望客户端自觉遵守，对真正的攻击者毫无约束力，服务端必须自己强制执行。
公共 WiFi、公司网络这类共享 IP 容易被误伤，所以要放松 IP 规则、更依赖已登录用户的限额。
optionExplanations_en: Temporarily blocklisting a client after repeated violations is cheaper than letting it hit the limiter over and over.
Upstream protection like Cloudflare or AWS Shield blocks a layer of traffic before it ever reaches your own Redis, easing pressure on the limiter behind it.
Relying entirely on client good behavior puts zero constraint on an actual attacker — enforcement has to live on the server.
Shared IPs from public WiFi or corporate networks get falsely caught by strict IP rules, so easing those and leaning on authenticated user limits avoids punishing real users.

scenario: 你已经在自家 SDK 里加了客户端限流，但攻击者可以直接用 curl 绕开 SDK。
scenario_en: You've built client-side limiting into your own SDK, but an attacker can just bypass the SDK with curl.
q: client-side rate limiting 在本设计中的定位是什么？
q_en: What role does client-side rate limiting play in this design?
options: 完全替代服务端限流
只用于数据库内部
有价值的补充，但不能当安全边界
会让 HTTP 429 不再需要
why: 客户端限流能减少误伤和基础设施压力，但恶意客户端不会自觉遵守；服务端限流仍是保护系统必须有的边界。
why_en: Client-side limiting is a useful complement for well-behaved clients, but it cannot replace server-side enforcement.
tradeoff: 降低基础设施压力 vs 无法充当安全边界
options_en: A full replacement for server-side rate limiting
Something only used inside the database
A useful complement, but never the security boundary
Something that makes HTTP 429 unnecessary
optionExplanations: 如果只靠客户端自己限流，恶意或改过的客户端可以直接跳过检查，服务端就完全没有保护了。
限流本来就发生在请求进入系统之前，跟数据库内部操作没有关系，这个选项文不对题。
客户端限流能提前劝退好公民的重试风暴，减轻网络和基础设施压力，但它管不住不听话的客户端，所以服务端限流仍然是唯一硬边界。
客户端主动少发请求不代表服务端就不会再拒绝超限请求，429 该返回还是要返回。
optionExplanations_en: If enforcement lives only on the client, a malicious or modified client can just skip the check, and the server has no protection left.
Rate limiting happens before a request even reaches the system — it has nothing to do with database internals, so this option is off-topic.
Client-side limiting can head off well-behaved clients' retry storms and ease load on the network, but it can't control a client that ignores it, so server-side limiting stays the only real boundary.
Sending fewer requests voluntarily doesn't stop the server from rejecting ones that still go over the limit — 429 still has to fire.

scenario: 限流规则偶尔调整，例如产品发布时临时提高 limit；允许几十秒内逐步生效，想保持实现简单。
scenario_en: Rate-limit rules change occasionally, such as temporarily raising a limit for a product launch; taking tens of seconds to propagate is fine, and the team wants a simple implementation.
q: 最常见的动态配置方案是什么？
q_en: What is the most common approach for dynamic configuration?
options: 每次改限额都要重新构建镜像并重新部署所有 gateway 实例
把规则直接写进客户端代码里
只靠人工 SSH 登录改内存
规则存配置库，gateway 定期 polling
why: 配置服务/数据库存规则，gateway 周期性 polling 并本地缓存，实现简单、够用；代价是变更到全网生效有延迟，比如最多 30 秒。
why_en: Polling a configuration store and caching results locally is simple and good enough when rule changes can take up to about 30 seconds to propagate.
whenOtherWins: 安全事件或高频交易等需要秒级强推配置时，push-based 方案更合适。
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 变更生效有延迟
diagram:
flowchart LR
Admin[Admin config] --> Store[Config store]
Store --> Watch[Watch or poll]
Watch --> Gateway[Gateway cache]
Gateway --> Checks[Limiter checks]
options_en: Rebuild the image and redeploy every gateway instance whenever a limit changes
Hard-code the rules directly into client code
Only change memory by hand over SSH
Rules live in a config store that gateways poll periodically
optionExplanations: 每个请求都触发一次重新部署，部署本身要几十秒到几分钟，这比要改的限额生效速度慢了好几个数量级。
规则写死在客户端代码里，改一次限额要等所有客户端升级完才生效，跟「临时调整」这个诉求正好相反。
靠人工登录改内存，改一台生效一台，规模一大根本没法保证所有 gateway 同步更新。
规则存进配置库，gateway 周期性拉取并本地缓存，实现简单，几十秒内传播完成也在这里能接受的范围内。
optionExplanations_en: Triggering a redeploy on every single request means waiting tens of seconds to minutes for the deploy itself — orders of magnitude slower than the limit needs to take effect.
Hard-coding rules into client code means a limit change only takes effect once every client has been upgraded — the opposite of a quick, temporary adjustment.
Changing memory by hand over SSH updates one gateway at a time, which doesn't scale to keeping every gateway in sync.
Storing rules in a config store that gateways poll and cache locally is simple to build, and propagating within tens of seconds is exactly what this scenario can tolerate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把配置(限流规则)发到各 gateway 的两种方式:poll=每台定期去配置库拉+本地缓存(简单,生效延迟=拉取间隔,如30秒);push=配置变了主动推给各台(实时,但要推送/订阅设施,更复杂)。容忍几十秒→选 poll(更简单),这题正是
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two ways to distribute config (rate-limit rules) to gateways: poll = each gateway periodically fetches from a config store and caches (simple; propagation delay = poll interval, e.g. 30s); push = the store pushes changes (real-time but needs pub/sub infra). If tens of seconds is acceptable, poll is simpler.

termDefinitions.meaning: 安全地远程登录到另一台服务器命令行的协议/工具。你在自己电脑上敲 ssh user@服务器IP,连接被加密,然后就像坐在那台服务器前一样敲命令(看日志、改配置、重启服务)。服务器在机房/云里没接键盘,运维就靠 SSH 进去操作。「人工 SSH 改内存」=工程师手动登进每台机器改 → 不 scale
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSH (Secure Shell) securely logs you into a remote server command line. You run ssh user@host from your laptop; the connection is encrypted and you get a shell on that server (view logs, edit config, restart). Servers sit in data centers with no keyboard, so ops use SSH to operate them. Manually SSH-ing to edit memory means logging into each machine by hand, which does not scale.

scenario: 安全事件中需要几秒内把新 limit 推到所有 gateway，不能等下一轮 30 秒 polling。
scenario_en: During a security incident, a new limit must reach all gateways within seconds — it can't wait for the next 30-second polling cycle.
q: 应考虑哪种配置分发？
q_en: Which configuration-distribution approach should be considered?
options: ZooKeeper/Pub-Sub push 配置变更
每天定点人工重启所有 gateway 实例来让新的配置生效
把规则直接写死在部署镜像里
只手动更新其中一台 gateway
why: push-based 配置能立刻通知所有连接的 gateway，适合紧急规则变更；代价是要处理连接故障、部分更新和 fallback，复杂度更高。
why_en: Push-based configuration notifies every connected gateway immediately, which suits urgent changes but adds connection and partial-failure handling complexity.
whenOtherWins: 普通业务规则调整用 polling 更简单；push 只在对传播延迟敏感时才值得付出复杂度。
tradeoff: 秒级生效 vs 连接管理和部分失败的复杂度
options_en: Push config changes out via ZooKeeper or Pub/Sub
Restart every gateway instance by hand at a fixed time each day to apply new config
Bake the rules directly into the deployment image
Manually update just one single gateway

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式协调服务，能在配置变化时主动推送通知给所有连接的客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a distributed coordination service that can push configuration changes to all connected clients immediately.

optionExplanations: ZooKeeper 或 Pub/Sub 能在配置一变就主动推给所有连着的 gateway，秒级生效，正好赶上安全事件的时间要求。
每天定时重启才生效，意味着安全事件发生后最多要等快一整天，跟「几秒内」这个要求差了几个数量级。
规则写进部署镜像意味着改一次限额要重新构建、发布整个镜像，速度上完全跟不上紧急变更。
只手动更新一台 gateway，其余的还在用旧规则，攻击者绕过没更新的那些实例照样能打进来。
optionExplanations_en: ZooKeeper or Pub/Sub can push a config change out to every connected gateway the moment it happens, hitting seconds-level propagation — exactly what a security incident needs.
Restarting on a daily schedule means an incident-time change could wait almost a full day to take effect, off by orders of magnitude from a few seconds.
Baking rules into the deployment image means every limit change needs a full rebuild and rollout — far too slow for an urgent change.
Manually updating just one gateway leaves the rest running old rules, so traffic can still slip through the ones that never got updated.

q: 把“选择 API Gateway + Redis Token Bucket”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for choosing API Gateway plus Redis Token Bucket into the correct order:
steps: 用 Token Bucket 兼顾 burst 和 sustained rate
需求：每个请求前低延迟判断并保护后端
把限流放在 API Gateway，先于业务服务拒绝
用 Redis 共享各 gateway 的 bucket 状态
用 Lua 保证 read-calculate-update 原子
why: 先确定入口保护位置，再选算法，然后补共享状态和原子性；这条链覆盖了功能、延迟和正确性三层。
why_en: The gateway-plus-Redis decision starts with edge protection, chooses Token Bucket, and adds shared atomic state.

q: 把“扩展到 1M RPS”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for scaling to 1M RPS into the correct order:
steps: 每个 shard 做 master-replica 和 failover
用 Redis Cluster / consistent hashing 按 client key 分片
需求：单 Redis 实例只能处理约 50k-100k checks/sec
在 gateway 侧复用连接并尽量区域内访问
约十个 shard 才能达到 1M checks/sec 量级
why: 先由单实例瓶颈推出分片，再估算 shard 数，之后补高可用和低延迟；顺序体现容量、可用性、延迟三层约束。
why_en: Scaling to one million checks requires Redis sharding by client key, enough shards, replica failover, and low-latency connections.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Scale[1M checks per sec] --> Shard[Redis Cluster]
Shard --> Pool[Connection pools]
Pool --> Local[Regional deploy]
Local --> Metrics[Monitor hot keys]

scenario: 45 分钟的系统设计面试，中级候选人只来得及把限流器的主路径讲清楚。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute system design interview, a mid-level candidate only has time to get the rate limiter’s main path right.
q: 中级候选人在这题里至少应讲清楚什么？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate clearly cover at minimum in this question?
options: 从零手写一遍完整的 ZooKeeper 分布式协调实现
选对部署位置、讲清一种算法、知道要分片 Redis
背出 Lua 虚拟机的内部源码
只讨论前端错误提示文案
why: 中级重点是高层设计和核心组件理解：放在哪里、怎么算、状态放哪、怎么返回 429；分布式细节可以留到追问再展开。
why_en: A mid-level answer should place the limiter sensibly, explain one algorithm like Token Bucket, and recognize that Redis state needs sharding.
options_en: Hand-write a complete ZooKeeper distributed-coordination implementation from scratch
Place the limiter well, explain one algorithm, and know Redis needs sharding
Recite the internal source of the Lua VM
Only discuss frontend error copy
optionExplanations: 从零手写 ZooKeeper 远超中级面试的期望深度，属于过度工程。
选对部署位置、讲清一种算法、知道 Redis 要分片，覆盖了中级候选人该讲清楚的高层设计。
背 Lua 虚拟机内部源码是无关的实现细节，不是系统设计面试考察的内容。
只谈前端错误提示文案完全没碰到这道题真正的技术判断——放哪里、怎么算、状态怎么共享。
optionExplanations_en: Implementing ZooKeeper from scratch goes far beyond what a mid-level interview expects — over-engineering for this scope.
Placing the limiter well, explaining one algorithm clearly, and knowing Redis needs sharding covers the high-level design a mid-level candidate should nail.
Reciting the Lua VM's internal source is an unrelated implementation detail, not what a system-design interview is testing.
Only discussing frontend error copy never touches the actual technical judgment this question is testing — placement, algorithm, shared state.

scenario: 面试官让你设计 1M rps 的 distributed rate limiter。你已经说了 API Gateway + Redis + Token Bucket，接下来要体现 senior 深度。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design a distributed rate limiter for 1M rps. You've already said API Gateway + Redis + Token Bucket, and now need to show senior-level depth.
q: 下一步最应该主动展开什么？
q_en: What should you proactively expand on next?
options: 只是把固定窗口算法的定义原封不动地背下来
假装系统完全没有故障模式
讲清原子更新、按 key 分片、降级
把限流丢给客户端就当结束
why: Senior 深度不是多背算法名，而是说明限流状态在并发、容量和故障下是否仍正确：原子更新、按 key 分片、故障降级。
why_en: Senior depth means explaining whether shared rate-limit state remains correct under concurrency, scale, and Redis failure, not merely naming more algorithms.
options_en: Just memorize the fixed-window algorithm's definition word for word
Pretend the system has no failure modes
Explain atomic updates, sharding, and failure degradation
Hand rate limiting to the client and stop there

termDefinitions.meaning: 这里指一次限流判断里的“读 token、补 token、扣 token、写回状态”必须像一个不可拆开的步骤执行；否则多个 gateway 并发请求会互相覆盖，导致多放行或误拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Here atomicity means the read-refill-decrement-write rate-limit update runs as one indivisible step, so concurrent gateways cannot overwrite each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同 client 的 bucket 状态分散到多个 Redis shard；同一个 user/IP/API key 必须稳定落到同一个 shard，否则它的计数会被拆散，限流失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding spreads different clients' bucket state across Redis shards while keeping the same client key on the same shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 慢、超时或 shard 挂掉时系统如何反应：fail-open 是放行保可用性但可能打爆后端，fail-closed 是拒绝保护后端但会挡住正常用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A failure mode is how the system behaves when Redis is slow or down, such as fail-open for availability or fail-closed for backend protection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当限流依赖(Redis)故障/超时、判不了限额时,系统「优雅退化」到一个后备行为而不是崩溃。两个主选:fail-open(放行,保可用、失保护)、fail-closed(拒绝,保后端、牺牲可用);更软的还有:退回本地内存近似计数、用上次缓存的规则、临时上一个粗粒度全局限流。所以「降级」=故障时怎么优雅后备,fail-open/close 是它最主要的两个选项
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation: when the rate-limit dependency (Redis) fails/times out and you cannot check limits, the system falls back to a safe behavior instead of crashing. Two main choices: fail-open (allow — keep availability, lose protection) and fail-closed (reject — protect backend, lose availability); softer options include local approximate counting, using last cached rules, or a coarse global cap.

rows: Lua 保证读改写不中断
按 key 分散到多个 shard

optionExplanations: 只讲固定窗口的定义还停留在 junior/mid 的算法背诵，讲不出并发更新同一个 bucket 时会不会出错。
假装系统没有故障模式太危险——分布式限流必须讲清 Redis 超时、shard 挂掉、重试风暴时后端怎么保护。
senior 深度要能讲清三件事：多个 gateway 并发更新会不会踩坏同一份状态、Redis 单点会不会成为新的瓶颈、故障时怎么在保护后端和放行用户之间做取舍。
把限流全丢给客户端只能当补充，攻击者或异常客户端不会可靠配合，服务端还是需要强制手段。
optionExplanations_en: Only reciting the fixed-window definition is still junior/mid-level recall — it doesn't explain whether concurrent gateways can corrupt the same bucket.
Pretending there are no failure modes is risky — a distributed limiter has to explain what happens when Redis times out, a shard dies, or retries spike.

Covering atomic updates, per-key sharding, and failure degradation shows the depth interviewers want, because those are exactly where state gets lost, Redis becomes a single point of failure, or the backend gets overloaded.
Handing everything to the client only works as a complement — attackers or buggy clients won't reliably cooperate, so the server still needs enforcement.

scenario: 同样 45 分钟的限流题，Staff+ 候选人被期待比中级多讲出一层东西。
scenario_en: Same 45-minute rate-limiter question, but a Staff+ candidate is expected to go one level deeper than mid-level.
q: Staff+ 答案通常应体现什么？
q_en: What should a Staff+ answer typically demonstrate?
options: 只是把更多限流算法的名字一个接一个地罗列出来
完全回避任何权衡取舍的讨论
假设所有客户端天生值得信任
强调生产深度：多区域、可观测性、真实容量
why: Staff+ 重点是生产经验和边界条件，能把限流系统放进真实平台运维中思考，而不是更长的术语列表。
why_en: Staff-level answers emphasize production operations, multi-region behavior, observability, and real capacity judgment from experience.
options_en: Just rattle off the names of even more rate-limiting algorithms one after another
Avoid any discussion of trade-offs entirely
Assume every client is inherently trustworthy
Emphasize production depth: multi-region, observability, real capacity
optionExplanations: 多报几个算法名字只是知识广度，staff+ 更想听到的是怎么把这套系统在生产里跑稳。
回避权衡取舍恰恰是资历不够的信号——每个方案都有代价，staff+ 应该主动点出来。
假设所有客户端天生可信，等于把安全边界让给了不可控的一方，这在生产系统里是个隐患。
多区域延迟、可观测性、真实容量数字，这些是只有真在生产系统里踩过坑才会主动讲到的深度。
optionExplanations_en: Naming a few more algorithms is just breadth of knowledge — what a staff+ answer needs to show is how the system stays stable in production.
Avoiding tradeoffs is itself a sign of shallower experience — every option has a cost, and a staff+ answer should call it out unprompted.
Assuming every client is inherently trustworthy hands the security boundary over to a party you don't control — a real production risk.
Multi-region latency, observability, and real capacity numbers are exactly the depth that only shows up once you've actually run a system like this in production.

scenario: 限流决策在 1M requests/sec 的请求路径上同步发生，多一跳就吃掉延迟预算。
scenario_en: The rate-limit decision happens synchronously on a request path doing a million requests a second, where any extra hop eats the latency budget.
q: 最终 rate limiter 设计的关键组成包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are the key components of the final rate limiter design? (multi-select)
options: API Gateway 执行限流并返回 429 headers
Redis Cluster 分片存 token bucket 状态
Lua 原子执行 bucket 更新
每个请求长期写入分析数据库后再决定是否放行
why: 最终主路径要短：gateway 提取标识、命中对应 Redis shard、脚本原子判断，超限就快速返回 429；长期分析不该阻塞在线决策。
why_en: The final design keeps the hot path short: extract identity, hit the right Redis shard, decide atomically, and return 429 fast when over the limit.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> GW[API Gateway]
GW -->|extract id| Router[Shard Router]
Router --> R1[(Redis Shard A)]
Router --> R2[(Redis Shard B)]
Router --> R3[(Redis Shard C)]
R1 --> Rep1[Replica]
GW -->|allow| App[Backend API]
GW -->|429 headers| Client
options_en: The API Gateway enforces limits and returns 429 headers
Redis Cluster shards store token-bucket state
Lua executes bucket updates atomically
Every request is written to an analytics database before deciding
optionExplanations: gateway 执行限流并回传 429 headers，是用户能直接感知到的那一层。
Redis Cluster 按 shard 存 token bucket 状态，把单实例扛不住的量级摊开。
Lua 保证一次 bucket 更新的读改写不被拆开，是并发正确性的关键。
先把每个请求写进分析数据库再决定放不放行，等于把在线判断路径接上一个离线系统的延迟，跟低延迟目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: The gateway enforcing the limit and returning 429 headers is the layer users actually feel.
Redis Cluster sharding token-bucket state spreads out the load a single instance couldn't handle.
Lua keeps a single bucket update's read-modify-write from being split apart, which is what keeps it correct under concurrency.
Writing every request to an analytics database before deciding whether to allow it bolts an offline system's latency onto the online decision path, working against the low-latency goal.

scenario: Token Bucket 里一个 client 好几天没发请求;bucket 按流逝时间持续 refill,早已加满到 capacity 上限。
scenario_en: In Token Bucket a client hasn't sent a request for days; the bucket kept refilling with elapsed time and is now full at capacity.
q: 这个满桶的 idle client 一上线会发生什么失效?
q_en: What goes wrong when this idle, full-bucket client comes back online?
options: 他被立刻拒绝,因为长期闲置会先扣掉一整窗配额
他能一次放行整桶(capacity)请求,形成不受控的突发
refill rate 自动清零,他只能发出一个请求就被限
bucket 会一直拒绝,直到下一个整分钟窗口对齐才放行
why: bucket 随时间 refill 并封顶在 capacity;闲置很久的 client 一上线就是满桶,能一次放行整桶突发。代价:capacity 要按可容忍的最大突发来定,定大了冷启动就冲击后端。
why_en: An idle client's bucket refills to full capacity, so its first request can release a whole bucket as one uncontrolled burst; size capacity to the largest burst you can tolerate.
options_en: It is rejected immediately, since long idleness first deducts a full window of quota
It can release a whole bucket (capacity) of requests at once as an uncontrolled burst
The refill rate resets to zero, so it gets throttled after a single request
The bucket keeps rejecting until the next whole-minute window aligns
optionExplanations: Token Bucket 不惩罚闲置;闲置只会让桶累积到满,不会先扣配额。
elapsed 越久桶补得越满、封顶在 capacity,冷启动时满桶被瞬间放光=一整桶突发。
refill 只做加法且封顶,不会清零;这是把机制方向搞反了。
整点对齐是 Fixed Window 的行为,Token Bucket 靠 refill 连续补,不看整分钟。
optionExplanations_en: Token Bucket doesn't penalize idleness; idling only lets the bucket fill up, it never pre-deducts quota.
The longer the elapsed time, the fuller the bucket up to capacity; a full bucket drained at once is one whole burst.
Refill only adds and caps out — it never zeroes; this reverses the mechanism.
Boundary alignment is Fixed Window behavior; Token Bucket refills continuously and ignores minute marks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 client 一个桶,按 refill rate 匀速加 token、封顶 capacity;每请求扣 1,没 token 就拒。只存 (tokens, last_refill) 两个字段
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Each client has a bucket that gains tokens at a steady refill rate up to capacity; each request spends one, and an empty bucket rejects. It stores just (tokens, last_refill).

termDefinitions.meaning: 桶能容纳的最大 token 数,等于允许的最大瞬时突发量;冷启动时满桶=这么多突发
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The maximum tokens a bucket holds, i.e. the largest instantaneous burst allowed; a full bucket at cold start equals exactly that burst.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每单位时间往桶里加多少 token,决定长期允许的平均速率
termDefinitions.meaningEn: How many tokens are added per unit time; it sets the long-run average rate allowed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长期闲置的 client 突然上线,bucket 早已补满,第一波请求可放行整桶突发的问题
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-idle client returning with an already-full bucket, so its first wave can release a whole bucket burst.

scenario: Fixed Window 每分钟限 100 次;某 client 在 12:00:03 就把 100 次打满,离窗口结束还有 57 秒。
scenario_en: A fixed window allows 100/min; a client burns all 100 by 12:00:03, with 57 seconds left in the window.
q: 打满后剩余的 57 秒里这个 client 会怎样?
q_en: What happens to this client for the remaining 57 seconds of the window?
options: 整个剩余窗口都会被拒绝,即使流量已回落正常
计数器立即重置归零,他可以继续按正常速率发请求
系统按已流逝的时间比例,退还一部分配额给他
多余请求进入队列,等窗口一到就自动重放出去
why: 固定窗口只在整点重置计数、不平滑;client 在窗口早期打满后,整个剩余窗口都被一刀切拒绝,哪怕后面流量很低。代价:体验是「用完即全停」,平滑要靠滑动窗口或 Token Bucket。
why_en: A fixed window resets only on the boundary, so a client that burns its quota early is starved for the rest of the window even after traffic calms; token bucket smooths this out.
options_en: The whole rest of the window is rejected, even once traffic returns to normal
The counter immediately resets to 0, so it can keep sending at a normal rate
The system refunds part of its quota in proportion to elapsed time
Excess requests are queued and automatically replayed when the window ticks over
optionExplanations: 计数只在整点归零,窗口内一旦达上限就全拒到底=对早期爆量用户的饿死。
窗口中途不会重置,这正是 Fixed Window 不平滑的根源。
固定窗口没有按比例退还机制;那更像 Sliding Window Counter 的加权,机制不同。
Fixed Window 直接丢弃超限请求,不排队重放;排队是另一种被否决的方案。
optionExplanations_en: The count only zeroes on the boundary, so hitting the cap mid-window rejects everything after — starving an early spender.
The window never resets mid-way; that is exactly why Fixed Window isn't smooth.
Fixed Window has no proportional refund; that resembles Sliding Window Counter's weighting, a different mechanism.
Fixed Window simply drops over-limit requests rather than queuing them; queuing is a separate, rejected approach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间切成固定窗口(如每分钟),每 client 一个计数器,窗口切换时归零;超限即拒。简单但边界不平滑
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slices time into fixed windows (e.g. per minute) with one counter per client that zeroes at the window switch; over-limit requests are rejected. Simple but not smooth at boundaries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在窗口早期就打满配额,导致整个剩余窗口的请求都被拒绝,即使实际流量已很低
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A user exhausts its quota early in the window, so all its requests for the rest of the window are rejected even when actual traffic is low.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用当前窗口和上一窗口两个计数器,按已过去比例加权估算真实滑动速率,比固定窗口平滑
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Uses the current and previous window counters, weighting by how far into the window you are, to approximate a true sliding rate more smoothly than fixed windows.

scenario: Sliding Window Counter 用「当前窗口已过去比例」加权上一窗口计数来估速率;某 client 的请求全挤在上一窗口最后几秒。
scenario_en: Sliding Window Counter weights the previous window by how far into the current window you are; a client's requests all cluster in the last few seconds of the previous window.
q: 这种边缘集中的流量下,加权估算会怎样出错?
q_en: With traffic clustered at the edge, how does the weighted estimate go wrong?
options: 它假设窗口内流量均匀,请求挤在边缘时估算失真、会漏放本该拒的请求
它总是高估速率,导致系统性地误拒大量本该放行的合法请求
加权数学一旦写错就退化成精确的 Sliding Window Log,内存暴涨
两个窗口的计数器会互相覆盖,最终导致 client 的状态直接丢失
why: 加权公式(上一窗×剩余比例 + 当前窗)默认流量在窗口内均匀分布;请求集中在某一端时,真实速率被系统性错估,近似失真。代价:换来的是每 client 只存两个计数器的省内存,要精确得用 Log。
why_en: The weighted estimate assumes even traffic across the window; when requests cluster at one edge it misjudges the true rate and can let through requests it should block.
options_en: It assumes even traffic in the window, so edge-clustered requests distort the estimate and slip past
It always overestimates the rate, systematically rejecting many legitimate requests it should pass
One wrong line of weighting math degrades it into an exact Sliding Window Log with huge memory
The two window counters overwrite each other and eventually lose the client's state entirely
optionExplanations: 加权按均匀分布折算上一窗;流量集中在边缘时折算值偏离真实,漏放或误拒都可能。
它不是单向高估;取决于请求落在窗口哪端,可能高估也可能低估。
写错数学得到的是错误近似,不会变成 Log;Log 是逐条存 timestamp 的另一算法。
两个计数器各自独立累加,不会互相覆盖;状态丢失是无中生有的说法。
optionExplanations_en: The weighting prorates the previous window as if traffic were even; edge-clustered traffic makes that proration miss.
It is not one-directional overestimation; depending on which edge requests land, it can over- or under-count.
Bad math gives a wrong approximation, not a Log; the Log is a separate algorithm storing each timestamp.
The two counters accumulate independently and don't overwrite each other; lost state is fabricated here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用当前+上一窗口两个计数器,按当前窗已过去比例加权上一窗,近似真实滑动窗口;只存两个计数器很省内存
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Uses current plus previous window counters, weighting the previous by how far into the current window you are, to approximate a true sliding window using just two counters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐条记录每次请求的 timestamp,精确统计过去 N 分钟的请求数;精确但热点 client 内存开销大
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stores every request's timestamp to count exactly how many happened in the last N minutes; perfectly accurate but memory-heavy for hot clients.

scenario: Redis 挂了,gateway 选 fail-closed 给所有请求回 429/503;而大多数客户端没实现退避,一看到失败就立刻重试。
scenario_en: Redis is down; the gateway fail-closes and returns 429/503 to every request, but most clients have no backoff and retry the instant they see a failure.
q: fail-closed 在这种客户端行为下会引发什么连锁副作用?
q_en: With clients like this, what knock-on side effect does fail-closed trigger?
options: 客户端激进重试,失败的请求反而把入站负载推得更高
重试请求会自动绕过限流器,直接打到后端服务上
收到 429 后客户端会永久停止发请求,负载归零
Redis 会因为承接这些重试流量而自动恢复上线
why: fail-closed 拒掉请求,但不做退避的客户端看到 429/503 会立刻重试;失败请求本身变成新负载,在故障期把入站流量推得更高。代价:必须靠 Retry-After 头引导退避才缓解。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects requests, but clients without backoff retry immediately on a 429/503, so the rejections become fresh load exactly when the system is already struggling.
options_en: Clients retry aggressively, so the rejected requests themselves push inbound load even higher
Retried requests automatically bypass the rate limiter and hit backend services directly
After a 429 the client permanently stops sending, dropping load to zero
Redis automatically recovers because it absorbs the retry traffic
optionExplanations: 拒绝不等于减负;无退避客户端把每次拒绝立刻变成一次新请求,叠成重试风暴。
重试仍走同一条 gateway 路径、仍被 fail-closed 拦,不会绕过限流器。
429 只是一次拒绝,不会让客户端永久停发;真实客户端多半会重试。
重试只会加重 Redis 负载,不会让它自愈;恢复要靠 failover/扩容。
optionExplanations_en: Rejecting isn't shedding load; a no-backoff client turns each rejection into a fresh request, stacking into a retry storm.
Retries still take the same gateway path and are still fail-closed; they don't bypass the limiter.
A 429 is one rejection, not a permanent stop; real clients mostly retry.
Retries only add load to Redis, they don't heal it; recovery needs failover or scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器拿不到状态时默认拒绝请求;保护后端但牺牲可用性,健康请求也会被挡
termDefinitions.meaningEn: When the limiter can't read state it defaults to rejecting requests; this protects the backend but sacrifices availability, blocking even healthy requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超出限额时返回的 HTTP 状态码,通常带 Retry-After 告诉客户端多久后可重试
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The HTTP status returned when a limit is exceeded, usually with a Retry-After telling the client when to retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端暂时不可用时返回的 HTTP 状态码,fail-closed 时表示限流器本身故障
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The HTTP status returned when the server is temporarily unavailable; under fail-closed it signals the limiter itself is down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随 429/503 一起发的响应头,告诉客户端等多少秒再重试,用来引导退避、避免重试风暴
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A response header sent with 429/503 telling the client how many seconds to wait before retrying, used to guide backoff and prevent retry storms.

scenario: 一个支付/金融 API,限流器(Redis)故障时要在 fail-open 和 fail-closed 之间选;这里「无限流地放行」比「短暂拒绝」后果严重得多。
scenario_en: A payments/financial API must pick fail-open vs fail-closed when the limiter (Redis) fails; here letting requests through unlimited is far worse than briefly rejecting them.
q: 这种系统在限流器故障时该选哪种失败模式?
q_en: Which failure mode should this system pick when the limiter fails?
options: fail-open,优先保住可用性,让所有交易照常通过
fail-closed,宁可拒绝也不放行无法核验限额的交易
关闭服务端限流,改完全依赖客户端自己限流
把交易全部排队,等 Redis 恢复后再统一处理
why: 支付/高安全系统里「无限流放行」比停机更糟:放行可能带来欺诈、超额扣款等不可逆损失。fail-closed 用短暂拒绝换掉这个风险。
why_en: In payments or high-security systems, unlimited pass-through is worse than downtime because unchecked access risks irreversible harm, so fail-closed trades brief rejection for safety.
whenOtherWins: 若是内容展示类 API、放行的最坏后果只是后端多扛点读压力,fail-open 更好,避免把限流器故障放大成全站不可用。
tradeoff: 可用性(fail-open) vs 不可逆损失防护(fail-closed)
options_en: Fail-open, prioritize availability and let all transactions go through as usual
Fail-closed, reject rather than pass transactions whose limits can't be verified
Turn off server-side limiting and rely entirely on client-side rate limiting
Queue all transactions and process them together once Redis recovers
optionExplanations: 对普通读服务可以,但支付里放行一笔无法核验的交易可能造成不可逆资金损失。
无核验的交易被拦下,用短暂拒绝换掉欺诈/超额扣款等不可逆风险,契合金融语义。
客户端不可信,安全场景恰恰不能把限流交给客户端;这等于放弃防护。
排队让交易延迟不可预测、还占内存,金融路径通常要求快速确定的失败。
optionExplanations_en: Fine for ordinary reads, but in payments letting an unverifiable transaction through can cause irreversible money loss.
Unverifiable transactions are blocked, trading brief rejection for irreversible fraud/overcharge risk — the right fit for finance.
Clients aren't trustworthy; security cases must not delegate limiting to the client, which abandons protection.
Queuing makes transaction latency unpredictable and eats memory; financial paths usually want fast, definite failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器不可用时默认拒绝请求;牺牲可用性换安全,金融/高安全场景常用
termDefinitions.meaningEn: When the limiter is unavailable it defaults to rejecting requests, trading availability for safety — common in financial or high-security settings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器不可用时默认放行所有请求;保住可用性但暂时失去限流保护,可能被打爆
termDefinitions.meaningEn: When the limiter is unavailable it defaults to allowing all requests, keeping availability but temporarily losing protection and risking overload.

scenario: Redis 挂了、限流器无法核验任何配额,gateway 决定 fail-closed 拒绝请求;现在要选回 429 还是 503。
scenario_en: Redis is down and the limiter can't verify any quota; the gateway fail-closes and now must choose between returning 429 or 503.
q: 限流器自身故障导致的拒绝,更贴切的状态码是哪个?
q_en: For a rejection caused by the limiter's own outage, which status code fits better?
options: 429 Too Many Requests,暗示是客户端自己请求太多、超出了配额上限
503 Service Unavailable,是限流器故障而非客户端超限
200 OK 附带一个警告头,把放行与否交给客户端自己决定
403 Forbidden,表示这个客户端根本无权访问该接口
why: 429 的语义是「你超配额了」,但限流器故障时客户端并没超限、是服务端问题;503 更诚实地表达「限流器暂时不可用」,并可配 Retry-After。代价:客户端要能区分对待 503。
why_en: 429 says the client exceeded its quota, but in a limiter outage the client hasn't — the fault is server-side, so 503 more honestly signals the limiter is temporarily down.
whenOtherWins: 若你希望客户端对两种情况用同一套退避逻辑、不想在客户端多加分支,统一回 429 + Retry-After 也可接受,只是语义不够精确。
tradeoff: 语义诚实(503=服务端故障) vs 复用已有退避码(429)
options_en: 429 Too Many Requests, implying the client itself exceeded its quota ceiling
503 Service Unavailable, since the rejection stems from a limiter outage, not the client over-limit
200 OK with a warning header, leaving the allow/deny decision to the client itself
403 Forbidden, meaning this client has no permission to access the endpoint at all
optionExplanations: 429 把责任归到客户端超限,但这次是限流器坏了、客户端没超,语义误导。
拒绝的真实原因是服务端(限流器)不可用,503 正好表达这层、并可带 Retry-After。
200 表示成功放行,把限流决定推给不可信客户端,既不安全也误导。
403 表示鉴权/权限问题,和限流器临时故障是两回事,语义不符。
optionExplanations_en: 429 blames the client for over-limit, but here the limiter broke and the client didn't exceed — misleading.
The real cause is a server-side (limiter) outage, which 503 expresses exactly and can carry Retry-After.
200 means success; pushing the limit decision to an untrusted client is both unsafe and misleading.
403 signals an auth/permission problem, not a transient limiter outage — the semantics don't match.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端超出限额时返回的 HTTP 状态码,语义是「是你请求太多了」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The HTTP status returned when a client exceeds its limit; it means "you sent too many requests".

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端暂时不可用时返回的 HTTP 状态码,把责任归到服务端而非客户端
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The HTTP status returned when the server is temporarily unavailable; it attributes the fault to the server, not the client.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端已被识别但无权访问该资源时返回的 HTTP 状态码,属于鉴权/权限问题
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The HTTP status returned when a client is identified but not allowed to access the resource; an auth/permission problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随 429/503 一起发的响应头,告诉客户端等多少秒再重试
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A response header sent with 429/503 telling the client how many seconds to wait before retrying.

scenario: app server 调用独立限流服务,但限流器响应变慢、甚至和 app server 之间出现网络分区;每个请求只有 <10ms 延迟预算。
scenario_en: App servers call a dedicated limiter, but it responds slowly or a network partition appears between them; each request has a sub-10ms latency budget.
q: 限流器迟迟不回时,更稳妥的处理策略是什么?
q_en: When the limiter is slow to answer, what's the safer handling strategy?
options: 一直同步等它回,保证每次限流判断都精确无误
设超时,到点就按预设失败模式猜一个决定
让请求线程原地自旋重试,直到最终拿到限流答案
直接丢弃该请求,并且不给客户端返回任何响应
why: 每请求只有 <10ms 预算,无限等会把限流器的慢叠加到用户延迟、甚至耗尽 app server 线程;设超时后按 fail-open/closed 预案猜一个决定,把可用性与精确性的取舍显式化。代价:超时期间判断不精确。
why_en: With a sub-10ms per-request budget, blocking on a slow limiter adds its latency to every request and can exhaust app-server threads — set a timeout and fall back to your fail-open/closed policy.
whenOtherWins: 只有能容忍高延迟的离线/批处理路径才值得多等一会儿换精确判断;交互式 API 必须超时后快速降级。
tradeoff: 等待换判断精确 vs 超时换低延迟与可用性
options_en: Block synchronously until it answers, guaranteeing every limit decision is exact
Set a timeout and, when it fires, guess a decision per the preset failure-mode policy
Have the request thread spin-retry in place until it finally gets the limiter's answer
Just drop the request and return no response at all to the client
optionExplanations: 无限等把限流器的慢直接叠到每个请求延迟上,还可能耗尽线程池,拖垮 app server。
超时上限先护住延迟预算,拿不到答案就走预设降级策略,取舍显式可控。
自旋重试和无限等一样占着线程、烧 CPU,只是换了个卡住的方式。
不给响应会让客户端一直挂起、超时重试,体验和负载都更糟。
optionExplanations_en: Unbounded waiting stacks the limiter's slowness onto every request and can exhaust the thread pool, dragging the app server down.
A timeout ceiling first protects the latency budget, then a preset degradation policy backstops it — explicit and controlled.
Spin-retry holds threads and burns CPU just like unbounded waiting, only in a different stuck form.
Returning nothing leaves clients hanging until they time out and retry, worsening both experience and load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络分区:两个组件之间的网络断开或不可达,谁也收不到对方的消息,请求会一直等到超时
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is when the network between two components breaks or becomes unreachable, so neither hears the other and requests hang until they time out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器不可用时默认放行所有请求,保可用性但暂失保护
termDefinitions.meaningEn: When the limiter is unavailable it defaults to allowing all requests, keeping availability but temporarily losing protection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器不可用时默认拒绝请求,保护后端但牺牲可用性
termDefinitions.meaningEn: When the limiter is unavailable it defaults to rejecting requests, protecting the backend but sacrificing availability.

scenario: 面试官澄清这是个 startup 的 API,每天只有几千请求(不是 1M/sec);你要据此定限流器的架构。
scenario_en: The interviewer clarifies this is a startup API doing a few thousand requests per day (not 1M/sec); you must size the limiter's architecture to that.
q: 这个量级下,相比百万级设计可以砍掉哪些东西?
q_en: At this scale, what can you cut compared with the millions-per-second design?
options: 单机 in-process 计数即可,不必上 Redis 分片和一致性哈希
仍必须部署多个 Redis 分片,以防未来流量增长
必须引入 Redis Cluster 的自动 failover 来保高可用
需要跨区域多活部署来把限流延迟压到最低
why: 每天几千请求下单机就装得下全部状态,in-process 计数的近似误差也无所谓;Redis 分片、一致性哈希、跨区都是为百万级吞吐准备的,提前上就是过度设计。代价:一旦增长要迁到共享状态。
why_en: At a few thousand requests a day, one box holds all state and in-process counting is fine; sharding, consistent hashing, and multi-region are for millions per second, so adding them now over-engineers it.
whenOtherWins: 一旦流量涨到单机吞吐上限或需要多实例部署,in-process 的近似误差和协调问题就绷不住,必须迁到 Redis 共享状态。
tradeoff: 小规模的单机简单 vs 大规模的分布式分片
options_en: In-process counting on one box is enough; skip Redis sharding and consistent hashing
You still must deploy multiple Redis shards to guard against future growth
You must bring in Redis Cluster automatic failover for high availability
You need multi-region active-active deployment to minimize limiter latency
optionExplanations: 几千/天全落在一台机器上,in-process 的跨节点误差根本不存在,不需要共享状态。
为「未来可能增长」现在就分片是过度设计;等真的接近单机上限再迁不迟。
Redis Cluster failover 是给分片后每个 shard 保命用的,这个量级还没有分片。
跨区多活解决的是全球用户的延迟与容量,几千/天的 startup 用不上。
optionExplanations_en: A few thousand a day all land on one machine, so cross-node error vanishes and no shared state is needed.
Sharding now for possible future growth is over-engineering; migrate when you actually near one box's limit.
Redis Cluster failover exists to keep each shard alive after sharding, and there's no sharding at this scale.
Multi-region active-active solves latency and capacity for global users, which a few-thousand/day startup doesn't have.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流计数直接放在应用/网关进程的本地内存里,无网络调用、最快;但每个实例只看到自己那部分流量
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate-limit counters kept in the app/gateway process's local memory — fastest, no network call — but each instance only sees its own slice of traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希:把 key 映射到一圈哈希槽上,增删节点时只搬动少量 key,用来把某 client 稳定路由到同一 Redis shard
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys onto a hash ring so adding/removing nodes moves few keys; used to route a client consistently to the same Redis shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 官方分片方案,把 key 分到 16384 个 hash slot、自动路由并内建 failover
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis's built-in sharding: it spreads keys across 16384 hash slots, routes automatically, and has built-in failover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 故障转移:master 挂掉后自动把某个 replica 提升为新 master,恢复写能力
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover automatically promotes a replica to new master when the master dies, restoring write capability.

q: Dropbox 设计题的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
options: 从任意设备上传文件
从任意设备下载文件
分享文件并查看别人分享给自己的文件
自动跨设备同步文件
options_en: Upload a file from any device
Download a file from any device
Share a file and view files others have shared with you
Automatically sync files across devices
why: 这题覆盖上传、下载、分享和同步四条用户主路径；编辑文件和免下载预览属于范围外。
why_en: The core Dropbox requirements are upload, download, sharing, and automatic cross-device sync.
q_en: Which core functional requirements are in the Dropbox design? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 如果做不到从任意设备上传，用户只能困在装了客户端的那台机器上传文件，跨设备协作无从谈起。
下载权限缺了这条，用户换个设备就拿不到自己的文件，“随处访问”的承诺就落空。
分享和查看别人分享的文件是协作场景的核心，没有它 Dropbox 只是个人网盘，做不成团队工具。
自动跨设备同步区别于纯粹的手动上传下载——没有它，用户得自己记得去同步，体验退化成传统网盘。
optionExplanations_en: Without upload from any device, a user is stuck uploading only from the one machine with the client installed, killing multi-device use.
Without download from any device, switching devices means losing access to your own files — the 'access anywhere' promise breaks.
Sharing and viewing what's shared with you is what turns this from a personal drive into a collaboration tool.
Automatic sync is what separates this from manual upload/download — without it, users have to remember to sync themselves.
scenario: 45 分钟的 Dropbox 面试，只画跨设备存取与协作的主路径，在线编辑和预览留到最后再谈。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute Dropbox interview you only draw the cross-device access and collaboration paths; in-app editing and preview come last.

q: Dropbox 设计题里，以下哪些被明确列为 below the line（范围外）？（多选）
options: 文件编辑
无需下载即可预览文件
每用户存储上限
病毒/恶意软件扫描
options_en: File editing
Previewing files without downloading them
A per-user storage limit
Virus / malware scanning
why: 这些是真实产品能力，但不是本设计主线；范围收紧后重点转向大文件传输、同步和可靠性。
why_en: Editing, previewing without download, storage limits, and malware scanning are out of scope for this design.
q_en: Which capabilities are below the line for this Dropbox design? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 文件编辑要动到内容本身和多人协作合并逻辑，是完全独立的一套系统，这道题先不展开。
免下载预览需要额外的转码/渲染服务，属于锦上添花，不影响核心的存储和同步链路。
每用户存储上限是产品计费策略问题，不影响文件怎么存、怎么传，可以后置。
病毒扫描是安全增强项，加在上传管线的某一环即可，不改变整体架构，所以先放到范围外。
optionExplanations_en: Editing touches content itself and multi-user merge logic — a whole separate system, not needed for this pass.
Rendering a preview before the file downloads needs its own transcoding/rendering service; a nice-to-have that doesn't touch core storage or sync.
A per-user storage cap is a billing/product policy question, not something that changes how files are stored or transferred.
Scanning uploads for malware is a security add-on that can slot into the pipeline later without reshaping the core architecture.
scenario: 同一场 45 分钟面试：时间只够设计大文件传输、同步和可靠性，其余能力先划到线下。
scenario_en: Same 45-minute interview: there is only time for large-file transfer, sync, and reliability, so everything else gets pushed below the line.

q: Dropbox 的核心非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
options: 高可用，优先 availability over consistency
支持超大文件（数百 GB 到 TB 级）
安全可靠，文件丢失或损坏后可恢复
上传、下载、同步尽量低延迟
options_en: High availability, favoring availability over strict consistency
Support very large files, from hundreds of GB up to TB scale
Be secure and reliable, recovering files if they are lost or corrupted
Keep upload, download, and sync latency as low as possible
why: 文件系统能接受几秒同步延迟，但不能频繁不可用或丢文件；大文件量级直接驱动分块和续传设计。
why_en: Dropbox prioritizes high availability, very large file support, reliability, and low latency.
q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for Dropbox? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 高可用换来的代价是接受短暂的跨区域旧值——用户能接受多等几秒看到新文件，但不能接受服务打不开。
大文件支持直接决定了要不要做分块上传和断点续传，这条约束贯穿整个设计。
文件丢失或损坏是网盘最不能犯的错，可靠性要求直接推动多副本存储和校验机制。
低延迟决定了用户体验——上传下载卡顿会让产品显得不专业，即使数据最终正确。
optionExplanations_en: Favoring uptime trades off strict freshness — users tolerate a few seconds of delay before seeing a new file, but not downtime.
Large-file support is what forces the chunking and resumable-upload design later in the interview.
Losing or corrupting a file is the one thing a storage product can't do, which drives replication and checksums.
Low latency shapes the felt experience — sluggish upload/download makes the product feel broken even when data is correct.
scenario: Dropbox 要托管数百 GB 到 TB 级文件、跨设备同步，几秒延迟可接受，但文件绝不能丢。
scenario_en: Dropbox must hold files from hundreds of GB up to terabytes and sync them across devices; a few seconds of lag is fine, losing a file is not.

scenario: 面试给出设计假设：Dropbox 系统要支持单个文件最大 50GB。
q: 这个 50GB 假设主要决定了哪个设计判断？
options: 这意味着要给 users 表和 files 表重新建索引
文件已经很大，索性放弃所有缓存层
下载可以完全交给数据库处理，不必接入 CDN
单次 POST 不现实，必须做客户端分块和断点续传
options_en: This means the users and files tables need new indexes.
The file is already large, so drop every cache layer entirely.
Downloads can be handled entirely by the database, no CDN needed.
A single POST isn't realistic; the client must chunk and support resumable upload.
why: 50GB 远超单请求的超时和请求体限制，这个量级直接把设计推向客户端分块、进度展示和断点续传。
why_en: A 50GB file makes single-request upload impractical, forcing client-side chunking, progress tracking, and resumable uploads.
q_en: What design decision does the 50GB file-size assumption force?
scenario_en: The interview assumption is that Dropbox must support a maximum single-file size of 50GB.
optionExplanations: 50GB 只是文件体积，跟 users/files 表要不要建索引是两回事，这个推论跑偏了主题。
文件大不等于放弃缓存——metadata 和小文件仍然受益于缓存，只是大文件字节走别的路径。
CDN 恰恰是加速这类大文件下载最直接的手段，跳过它反而是反方向。
这才是 50GB 直接逼出来的判断——单次请求扛不住这个体量。
optionExplanations_en: 50GB is just file size — unrelated to whether the users/files tables need new indexes; a non sequitur.
A large file doesn't mean dropping caching altogether — metadata and small files still benefit even if big bytes take a different path.
A CDN is exactly the tool for speeding up large downloads, so skipping it points the wrong direction.
This is the one conclusion the 50GB number actually forces — a single request just can't carry that much.

q: 为什么 Dropbox 通常优先可用性而不是强一致？
options: 用户能接受另一地区几秒后才看到新文件
文件系统不需要任何安全机制
Blob Storage 无法跨区域复制
强一致性反而会让下载更快
options_en: Users can accept seeing a file uploaded elsewhere only a few seconds later.
A file system does not need any security controls.
Blob storage cannot replicate across regions.
Strong consistency actually makes downloads faster.
why: 文件同步允许几秒级延迟，不必像交易系统那样保证全局强一致读到最新写。
why_en: File sync can tolerate a few seconds of delay, unlike transactional systems that must guarantee every read sees the latest write.
tradeoff: 可用性优先（容忍短暂延迟） vs 强一致（每次读最新写）
q_en: Why does Dropbox usually favor availability over strong consistency?
optionExplanations: 这就是可用性优先要付的代价——用户能接受另一地区晚几秒才看到新文件。
安全机制和一致性模型是两条正交的轴，该加密、该做权限控制跟选可用性还是强一致没关系。
Blob Storage 恰恰擅长跨区域复制，这不是它的短板。
强一致往往要等多副本写入确认，会拖慢而不是加快下载。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the cost of favoring availability — users accept seeing a file several seconds behind in another region.
Security and the consistency model are orthogonal — a file system still needs encryption and access control no matter which one you pick.
Blob storage is actually good at cross-region replication; that's not a real limitation.
Strong consistency usually waits on replica acknowledgments, which slows downloads down, not up.
scenario: Dropbox 同步：北美用户传完文件，欧洲同事几秒后才看到没问题，但网盘不能打不开。
scenario_en: For Dropbox sync, a teammate in Europe seeing a newly uploaded file a few seconds late is fine, but the drive being unavailable is not.

q: 补全 Dropbox 的核心实体：
text: 核心实体包括 {{File}}（原始字节）、{{FileMetadata}}（name/size/mimeType/uploadedBy 等元数据）、{{User}}（系统用户）。
why: 原始文件和元数据必须分开思考：前者走 Blob Storage/CDN 大对象路径，后者走数据库和权限查询。
why_en: The core entities are File bytes, FileMetadata, and User, because bytes and metadata follow different storage paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存储大二进制对象（如文件、图片）的存储服务，例如 S3。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is a service for storing large binary objects such as files, for example S3.

q_en: Fill in the core Dropbox entities.

q: Dropbox 初版 API 需要覆盖哪些接口？（多选）
options: POST /files 上传文件和 metadata
GET /files/{fileId} 下载文件和 metadata
POST /files/{fileId}/share 分享给用户
GET /files/changes?since={timestamp} 查询同步变化
options_en: POST /files uploads a file and its metadata
GET /files/{fileId} downloads a file and its metadata
POST /files/{fileId}/share shares the file with other users
GET /files/changes?since={timestamp} polls for sync changes
why: 这些接口对应上传、下载、分享和同步四个功能需求；上传/下载 API 之后会演进为 signed URL 流程。
why_en: The initial API covers upload, download, sharing, and change polling for sync.
q_en: Which endpoints should the first Dropbox API cover? (Select all that apply)
optionExplanations: 上传接口是整个系统的入口——没有它文件根本进不了系统，后面的下载分享都无从谈起。
下载接口直接对应用户能不能拿回自己的文件，是最基础的读路径。
分享接口把单人存储变成协作场景，是把网盘升级成协作工具的关键一环。
变化查询接口是同步机制的基础——没有它，客户端不知道该拉取哪些远端更新。
optionExplanations_en: The upload endpoint is the entry point for the whole system — without it, nothing gets into storage for download or sharing to build on.
The download endpoint is the basic read path — it's literally whether a user can get their file back.
The share endpoint is what turns single-user storage into a collaboration feature.
The changes-polling endpoint is the backbone of sync — without it, a client has no way to know what remote updates to pull.
scenario: Dropbox 第一版 API 只服务上传、下载、分享、跨设备同步这四条功能需求，先不谈优化。
scenario_en: The first cut of the Dropbox API only has to serve four functional requirements: upload, download, share, and cross-device sync.

q: 为什么请求体里不应让客户端直接传 user 信息作为授权依据？
options: HTTP 请求体这种格式没办法装下 JSON 数据
客户端内容可伪造，身份应来自 session/JWT
上传时文件名字符会变得越来越长
这个云存储 S3 完全不支持保存任何 metadata 字段
options_en: An HTTP request body cannot hold JSON data.
Client-supplied content can be forged; identity should come from a session or JWT.
File name characters would grow longer over time.
This cloud storage, S3, does not support saving metadata fields.
why: 用户身份要来自可信认证上下文（session/JWT），请求体内容客户端可随意伪造。
why_en: User identity should come from a trusted auth context like a session or JWT, not from a forgeable request body.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON Web Token，一种自包含、可验证签名的身份令牌。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a self-contained, signed token used to represent an authenticated identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、代表已登录用户身份的凭证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session token is a credential issued by the server that represents a logged-in user's identity.

q_en: Why should the request body not be trusted for user identity?
optionExplanations: HTTP 请求体完全能装 JSON，这个说法本身就站不住脚。
关键在于信任边界——客户端传的任何字段都能被篡改，身份得来自服务端签发的凭证。
文件名长度跟这道题要判断的授权来源完全是两码事。
这个云存储 S3 存不存 metadata 字段跟要不要信任客户端传的身份信息毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: An HTTP body can absolutely carry JSON — that claim doesn't hold up.
The real issue is trust boundary — any field the client sends can be forged, so identity must come from a server-issued credential instead.
File name length has no bearing on how the server determines identity.
Whether S3 stores metadata fields is unrelated to whether the request payload can be trusted for identity.
scenario: Dropbox 上传接口收到一个请求体里自带 userId 的 POST /files，服务端要据此判断谁能写。
scenario_en: The Dropbox upload endpoint gets a POST /files whose body carries its own userId, and the server has to decide from that who may write.

scenario: 文件 metadata 结构简单、关系少，主要查询模式是按用户列出文件和根据 fileId 做权限检查。
q: 默认最适合选哪类存储？
options: 把 metadata 全存进 S3 object body 里
浏览器 localStorage
DynamoDB 这类 NoSQL metadata DB
Elasticsearch 作为唯一真相
options_en: Store metadata only inside the S3 object body.
Browser localStorage.
DynamoDB, a managed NoSQL store.
Elasticsearch as the single source of truth.
why: 简单 document、按 user 查询的场景下，NoSQL 如 DynamoDB 是顺手默认；SQL 数据库同样可行。
why_en: For simple documents queried mainly by user, a NoSQL store like DynamoDB is a sensible default, though a relational database works too.
whenOtherWins: 共享关系和事务查询变复杂时，Postgres 等关系型数据库同样合理。
tradeoff: 简单文档快速上手 vs 关系型数据库的事务与复杂查询能力

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的全托管 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service from AWS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向全文检索和聚合分析的搜索引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine built for full-text search and analytics.

q_en: Which storage type is the best default for Dropbox metadata?
scenario_en: File metadata is simple, has few relationships, and is mainly queried by user or by fileId for permission checks.
optionExplanations: 把 metadata 全部塞进 S3 object body，意味着每次查询都要下载整个对象才能读字段，完全没法索引。
localStorage 是浏览器本地存储，只服务当前设备的当前用户，撑不起服务端要处理的多设备查询。
结构简单、主要按 user 查询时，DynamoDB 这类 NoSQL 能直接按 key 查，上手快、扩展省心。
Elasticsearch 的强项是全文检索和聚合分析，把它当唯一真相来源会牺牲事务性和一致性保证。
optionExplanations_en: Putting metadata inside the S3 object body means every query has to fetch the whole object just to read a field — no indexing at all.
localStorage lives in one browser on one device; it can't serve the multi-device queries a backend needs to answer.
When the schema is simple and most lookups are scoped to one user, a managed NoSQL database such as DynamoDB gives fast key lookups with easy scaling.
Elasticsearch is built for full-text search and aggregation — using it as the source of truth gives up transactional guarantees.

scenario: 用户文件可能很多很大，应用服务器本地磁盘无法可靠、弹性地保存所有原始字节。
q: 原始文件内容应该存在哪里？
options: File Service 本地文件系统
Metadata DB 里新增一个二进制 BLOB 大字段列
Redis Pub/Sub
S3 / GCS 这类 Blob Storage
options_en: The File Service's local file system.
A dedicated binary BLOB column added to the metadata database.
Redis Pub/Sub.
Blob storage such as S3 or GCS.
why: 大对象需要弹性扩展和可靠性，Blob Storage 专为此设计；应用服务器本地磁盘扛不住容量和可靠性要求。
why_en: Large file bytes need elastic, reliable storage, which is exactly what blob storage like S3 provides.
whenOtherWins: 极小原型可以先用本地磁盘；生产级大文件和多设备访问才需要托管对象存储。
tradeoff: 托管对象存储的弹性与可靠性 vs 本地磁盘的简单实现

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon 和 Google 提供的对象存储服务，用于保存大文件字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 and GCS are cloud object storage services used to hold large file bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 提供的发布订阅消息机制，不做持久化对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe messaging mechanism, not persistent object storage.

q_en: Where should the raw file bytes live?
scenario_en: Users can store many large files, and local disks on app servers cannot hold all raw bytes reliably or elastically.
optionExplanations: 本地文件系统跟着单台机器走，机器一宕机或要扩容，文件就跟着没了或拆不动。
把大字节塞进数据库列，哪怕只查文件名也要驮着几十 GB 的负载，拖垮整个查询层。
Redis Pub/Sub 是消息广播通道，消息不落盘、不持久化，根本不是用来存文件的。
大文件需要弹性容量和持久性，这正是 S3/GCS 这类对象存储从设计之初就要解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Local disk is tied to one machine — if it dies or you need to scale out, the files go with it or can't move.
Stuffing large bytes into a database column means every query, even one that only needs the file name, drags along tens of GB.
Redis Pub/Sub is a broadcast channel — messages aren't persisted, so it was never meant to hold files.
Large files need scalable, durable capacity, exactly the problem an object store such as S3/GCS was built to solve.

q: 客户端先上传到 File Service，再由 File Service 上传到 S3 的主要问题是什么？
options: 文件穿后端两次，又慢又贵，还压垮应用服务器
这个云存储 S3 拒绝接收后端发起的上传
metadata 记录这时候没法正常保存
用户看不到自己上传文件的名字
options_en: The file crosses the backend twice, which is slow, costly, and overloads app servers.
This cloud storage, S3, refuses uploads issued from a backend.
The metadata record cannot be saved properly at this point.
Users cannot see the name of the file they uploaded.
why: 客户端到后端、后端再到 S3，等于传两遍大文件；应用服务器还要扛大对象流量成为瓶颈。
why_en: Routing through the backend sends the file twice and turns application servers into a large-object bottleneck.
q_en: What is the main problem with proxying uploads through the File Service?
optionExplanations: 问题就在双跳传输——先到 File Service 再到 S3，同一份大文件走了两遍网络，还占满应用服务器的连接。
S3 完全接受来自服务端的上传请求，这不是它拒绝的场景。
metadata 的保存跟字节走哪条路径是两件独立的事，不会因为代理上传就存不进去。
文件名是 metadata 里的一个字段，跟传输路径无关，用户照样能看到。
optionExplanations_en: The problem is the double hop — client to backend, then backend to S3 sends the same large file across the network twice and saturates app-server connections.
S3 fully accepts uploads issued from a backend; that's not what breaks here.
Saving metadata is independent of which path the bytes take — proxying doesn't stop it from being saved.
The file name is just a metadata field, unrelated to the transfer path — users still see it fine.
scenario: Dropbox 用户上传 50GB 视频，File Service 跑在按出入流量计费的应用服务器上。
scenario_en: A Dropbox user uploads a 50GB video while the File Service runs on app servers billed by bandwidth in and out.

scenario: 要让客户端绕过应用服务器直接上传到 S3，同时仍限制只能上传到授权位置和对象。
q: 最合适的机制是什么？
options: 把 AWS root key 发给客户端
预签名上传 URL
让用户手动登录 S3 控制台
把文件先 base64 放进 JSON body
options_en: Send the AWS root key to the client.
A presigned upload URL.
Have the user log into the S3 console manually.
Base64-encode the file into a JSON body.
why: File Service 用自己的云凭证本地签一个限时限路径的 URL，客户端直接 PUT 到 S3，后端不进数据路径。
why_en: The File Service signs a time-limited, path-scoped URL with its own credentials, so the client can PUT directly to S3 without the backend touching the bytes.
whenOtherWins: 内部管理工具或很小文件可以直接走后端上传；面向用户的大文件路径应绕开后端。
tradeoff: 客户端直传的速度与解耦 vs 后端代理上传的集中控制

termDefinitions.meaning: 由服务端用云凭证签名、限时限路径的 URL，持有者可直接对该对象操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, path-scoped URL signed by the server that lets the holder access that specific object directly.

q_en: What mechanism lets clients upload directly to S3 safely?
scenario_en: Clients should bypass app servers and upload directly to S3, while still being limited to an authorized object path.
optionExplanations: 把 root key 发给客户端等于把整个云账户的钥匙交出去，一旦泄露攻击者能为所欲为。
既要客户端直传又要限制范围时，预签名 URL 刚好卡在中间——限时限路径，客户端拿到就能直接 PUT。
让用户手动登录 S3 控制台没法自动化，也完全破坏产品的上传体验。
50GB 文件 base64 编码后体积更大，还得塞进 JSON body，会直接撞穿几乎所有请求体大小限制。
optionExplanations_en: Handing the client the root key hands over the entire cloud account — one leak and an attacker can do anything.
When clients need to upload directly but stay scoped, a presigned URL sits right in the middle — short-lived and path-restricted, no long-lived credential exposed.
Making users log into the S3 console manually can't be automated and wrecks the upload experience.
Base64-encoding a 50GB file only makes it bigger, and stuffing it into a JSON body blows past nearly every request-size limit.

q: 把普通 direct-to-S3 上传流程排成正确顺序：
steps: 客户端用 URL 直接 PUT 文件到 Blob Storage
File Service 生成 presigned URL 并把 metadata 标记为 uploading
客户端请求 POST /files/presigned-url 并提交 metadata
S3 通知后端文件已上传
后端把 metadata 状态更新为 uploaded
why: 控制面先建 metadata 和签名 URL，数据面直传 S3；对象到位后再把状态从 uploading 推进到 uploaded。
why_en: The control plane creates metadata and a signed URL first, the client uploads bytes straight to S3, then the backend marks metadata uploaded.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] -->|init upload| FileSvc[File Service]
FileSvc -->|signed URL| Client
Client -->|PUT bytes| Blob[(Blob Storage)]
Client -->|complete| FileSvc
FileSvc --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 由服务端用云凭证签名、限时限路径的 URL，持有者可直接对该对象操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, path-scoped URL signed by the server that lets the holder access that specific object directly.

q_en: Put the direct-to-S3 upload flow in the right order.

scenario: 上传 API 已从单个 POST /files 演进为先申请上传权限，再把字节直传对象存储。
q: 第一步 control-plane API 应该是什么？
options: GET /files/{fileId}/bytes -> all bytes through backend
DELETE /users/me
POST /files/presigned-url -> PresignedUrl
POST /files/search
options_en: GET /files/{fileId}/bytes streams all bytes through the backend.
DELETE /users/me.
POST /files/presigned-url returns a PresignedUrl.
POST /files/search.
why: 这个接口只处理 metadata、鉴权和签名，不接收文件字节，把应用服务器留在控制面。
why_en: This endpoint only handles metadata, authorization, and signing, keeping large bytes off the application server.
whenOtherWins: 文件很小且赶工期时，单个 POST 上传可以先用；生产级大文件路径必须拆开。
tradeoff: 控制面/数据面分离 vs 单接口实现简单
q_en: What should the first control-plane upload API be?
scenario_en: The upload API has evolved from one POST /files call into requesting upload permission first, then sending bytes to object storage.
optionExplanations: GET 全量字节走后端正是要绕开的老路径，字节应该走 S3 直传。
删除用户账号跟上传流程完全不搭边，选项本身就跑题了。
第一步只需要处理鉴权和签名，字节完全不经过这个接口，应用服务器留在控制面上。
搜索接口是后续功能，不属于最初这版上传 API 要解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: GET-ing all the bytes through the backend is exactly the old path this design avoids — bytes should go straight to S3.
Deleting a user account has nothing to do with the upload flow; the option is simply off-topic.
The first step only needs to handle auth checks and URL signing — no bytes touch this endpoint, keeping the app server on the control plane.
A search endpoint is a later feature, not something the initial upload API needs to solve.

q: 使用 Blob Storage 后，metadata 和 file bytes 之间会出现什么一致性问题？
options: S3 写入和 metadata 写在同一个事务里，不会不一致
上传后文件名字段直接就无法保存
S3 上传成功就代表 metadata 那条记录一定也写好了
文件传上去了但 metadata 没存，或者反过来
options_en: The S3 write and the metadata write share one transaction, so they can't diverge.
The file name field simply cannot be saved after upload.
A successful S3 upload guarantees the metadata row was already written too.
The file uploaded but metadata wasn't saved, or the reverse happened.
why: 大对象和元数据分处两个系统，没有单一事务；需要 status 字段和补偿清理来处理中间态。
why_en: Blob bytes and metadata live in two separate systems with no single transaction, creating partial-success states that need a status field and cleanup.
q_en: What consistency problem appears when metadata and file bytes live separately?
optionExplanations: S3 和数据库是两个独立系统，没有跨系统事务，正因如此才会出现中间态。
文件名字段的保存跟这里讨论的一致性问题无关，完全能正常写入。
S3 只知道自己的字节，管不到 metadata 那张表写没写成功，两者各自成败。
两个系统各自独立成功或失败，就会留下“字节到了但记录没写”或反过来的中间态。
