URL query tokens routinely end up in browser history, proxies, and access logs — a much larger leak surface than a header.
Re-entering a password on every call is unusable, and defeats the point of stateless token auth in the first place.

scenario: 标准 signed URL 5 分钟内谁拿到都能下载；某些内部合规文件需要比这更强的下载控制。
scenario_en: A standard signed URL lets anyone who has it download within 5 minutes; some internal compliance files need stronger control than that.
q: 还能加什么限制来收紧下载权限？
q_en: What extra restriction can tighten download access further?
options: 把过期时间从 5 分钟延长到 24 小时
加 IP 绑定，或搭配认证 cookie
彻底取消过期时间，换成永久有效链接
把 URL 打印出来通过内部邮件群发确认身份
options_en: Extend the expiry from 5 minutes to 24 hours.
Add IP binding, or pair it with an authentication cookie.
Remove the expiration entirely and make the link permanent.
Print the URL and mass-email it internally to confirm identity.
why: 短过期只收窄泄露窗口，挡不住持有者转发；IP 绑定或搭配认证 cookie 能把裸 URL 这一单一凭证变成多因子校验。
why_en: A short expiry only narrows the leak window and can't stop a holder from forwarding it; IP binding or pairing with an auth cookie turns the bare URL into a multi-factor check.
whenOtherWins: 普通用户下载场景不需要这层额外摩擦，短期 signed URL 已经够用。
tradeoff: 多一层绑定挡住更多泄露路径 vs 增加客户端集成复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 把访问凭证和请求来源 IP 绑定，非绑定 IP 发起的请求即使拿到凭证也会被拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP binding ties a credential to a specific source IP, so a request from any other IP is rejected even with a valid credential.

optionExplanations: 延长过期时间是反方向操作，泄露窗口只会变得更大，不是更小。
IP 绑定把凭证和请求来源锁死，配合认证 cookie 就不再是单靠一个 URL 就能用的裸凭证。
永久链接等于彻底放弃访问控制，任何人拿到都能一直用。
人工邮件核实完全没法自动化，也不是这道题在讨论的技术方案。
optionExplanations_en: Lengthening the expiry runs backwards — it widens the leak window instead of narrowing it.
IP binding ties the credential to where the request comes from, and pairing it with an auth cookie means the bare URL alone is no longer enough.
A permanent link gives up access control entirely — anyone who gets it can use it forever.
Manual email verification can't be automated and isn't the technical control this question is asking about.

scenario: S3 对存储的文件做静态加密：用一个独立的密钥加密文件，密钥本身不和文件放在一起。
scenario_en: S3 encrypts stored files at rest, using a separate key that is not stored alongside the file itself.
q: 把密钥和文件分开存放，防的是哪种风险？
q_en: What risk does storing the key separately from the file guard against?
options: 防止文件在传输过程中被窃听
拿到存储介质/文件本身，没密钥也解不开内容
防止文件的 MIME type 被篡改
让 CDN 边缘节点可以跳过鉴权直接缓存
options_en: It stops eavesdropping on the file while it's in transit.
Getting the storage medium or the file itself isn't enough to decrypt it without the key.
It stops the file's MIME type from being tampered with.
It lets CDN edge nodes skip authorization and cache directly.
why: 静态加密防的是存储介质本身被拿走/越权访问的风险；密钥单独存放意味着光有文件字节仍解不开内容，多一层纵深防御。
why_en: Encryption at rest guards against the storage medium itself being taken or improperly accessed; keeping the key apart means raw bytes alone still can't be decrypted, adding defense in depth.
optionExplanations: 传输中的窃听是 HTTPS 要挡的，跟这里说的静态加密是两道独立防线。
密钥单独存放正是这里的设计意图——拿到文件字节不等于能读懂里面的内容。
MIME type 是文件元数据的一个字段，跟密钥怎么存放没有关系。
CDN 缓存策略和访问鉴权是另一套机制，密钥分开存放不会影响它。
optionExplanations_en: Eavesdropping in transit is what HTTPS guards against — a separate line of defense from encryption at rest.
Storing the key apart is exactly the point — having the raw bytes doesn't mean you can read the content.
MIME type is just a metadata field, unrelated to where the encryption key lives.
CDN caching and authorization are a separate mechanism untouched by where the encryption key is stored.

scenario: 客户端上传前，既算了整个文件的 fingerprint，也给每个 chunk 单独算了 fingerprint。
scenario_en: Before uploading, the client computes a fingerprint for the whole file and a separate fingerprint for each chunk.
q: 这两级 fingerprint 分别解决什么问题？
q_en: What does each level of fingerprint actually solve?
options: 全文件级判断能否续传，chunk 级判断哪些块还没传
两个其实是同一个值，算两遍只是为了双重确认
全文件级用来压缩，chunk 级用来加密
chunk 级决定文件存哪个区域，全文件级只用来生成文件名
options_en: The whole-file fingerprint checks resumability, while chunk fingerprints pinpoint which pieces are still missing.
They're actually the same value; computing it twice is just double-checking.
The file-level one drives compression, the chunk-level one drives encryption.
The chunk-level one picks the storage region, the file-level one only generates the file name.
why: 全文件 fingerprint 先回答“这份内容传过吗、能不能续传”，chunk fingerprint 再精确到“哪几块已经在远端了”，两级问题不同。
why_en: The whole-file fingerprint answers whether this content was uploaded before and is resumable, while chunk fingerprints pinpoint exactly which pieces already made it — two different questions.
tradeoff: 两级都算：判断精确 vs 每级都要多一次哈希计算的开销
optionExplanations: 先用全文件指纹判断要不要走续传逻辑，再用 chunk 指纹精确定位缺哪几块。
内容不同、哈希输入范围不同，两个值本来就不会相等。
压缩和加密都是独立步骤，跟计算哪种粒度的哈希没有因果关系。
存储区域由部署策略决定，文件名通常来自用户输入或 metadata，不是哈希值决定的。
optionExplanations_en: The whole-file hash first decides whether to take the resume path; the chunk hash then pinpoints exactly which pieces are missing.
Different input ranges hash to different values — the two were never going to match.
Compression and encryption are separate steps unrelated to which granularity of hash gets computed.
Storage region comes from deployment policy, and the file name usually comes from user input or metadata — neither is decided by a hash.

scenario: 客户端靠 WebSocket 实时接收远端变更；网络抖动导致连接断开了几分钟又重连。
scenario_en: The client relies on WebSocket to receive remote changes in real time, then a network blip drops the connection for a few minutes before it reconnects.
q: 这几分钟里错过的变更事件，最终怎么补回来？
q_en: How do the change events missed during that gap eventually get recovered?
options: 永久丢失，除非用户手动触发一次全量重新下载
重连后靠周期 poll 补齐
服务端会把断线期间的事件重新逐条推送到新连接上
客户端应该把心跳间隔缩短到毫秒级来避免断线
options_en: Permanently lost unless the user manually triggers a full redownload.
A periodic poll after reconnecting catches up.
The server replays every missed event one by one onto the new connection.
The client should shrink its heartbeat interval to milliseconds to avoid drops.
why: 正常路径靠推送；断线是异常态，客户端本地视图变旧但不自知；下一次周期性 poll 用 since timestamp 补齐，代价是最多等一个轮询周期才追平。
why_en: Push handles the normal path; a drop is the failure state where the local view goes stale unnoticed, and the next periodic poll with a since timestamp catches up — the cost is waiting up to one poll interval to reconcile.
optionExplanations: 混合方案就是为了避免这种永久丢失，轮询兜底本来就是为了不必用户手动介入。
推送负责实时性，轮询负责兜底；重连后下一次 poll 自然会把断线期间的变更捞回来。
设计里服务端并不逐条重放历史事件，兜底手段是客户端主动用 since 参数去问。
缩短心跳只能更快发现断线，挡不住断线期间本来就会漏事件这件事。
optionExplanations_en: The hybrid design exists precisely to avoid this permanent loss — polling is the fallback so users never have to step in manually.
Push handles real-time delivery and polling handles the safety net; the next poll after reconnecting naturally pulls in whatever was missed.
The design doesn't have the server replay history event-by-event; the fallback is the client actively asking with a since parameter.
A shorter heartbeat only detects the drop faster — it doesn't stop events from being missed during the drop itself.

scenario: 有人提议：下载链接不设过期时间，方便用户随时点开，权限只在生成链接那一刻检查一次。
scenario_en: Someone proposes a download link with no expiration, checking permission only once at generation time so users can click it anytime.
q: 这个方案会在什么情况下出问题？
q_en: When does this proposal break down?
options: 链接一旦被转发到公开论坛，任何人可永久下载
文件本身的内容会因为链接不过期而逐渐损坏
S3 会拒绝生成不设过期时间的链接
永久链接会让 CDN 完全没办法缓存这个文件
options_en: Once the link gets forwarded to a public forum, anyone can download it forever.
The file's content itself gradually degrades because the link never expires.
S3 refuses to generate a link that has no expiration.
A permanent link makes it impossible for the CDN to cache the file at all.
why: 权限只在生成那一刻检查过，链接本身之后就是裸凭证；一旦意外或故意流出到公开渠道，没有过期时间就没有任何东西能自动收回访问权。
why_en: Permission is checked only once at generation, so the link itself becomes a bare credential afterward — if it leaks to a public channel, nothing without an expiry can automatically revoke access.
optionExplanations: 生成后不过期意味着链接一旦泄露，没有任何自动机制能让它失效，只能靠人工事后补救。
链接的有效期跟文件字节本身是否损坏完全无关。
S3 允许生成任意过期时间（包括很长）的签名 URL，不会主动拒绝。
CDN 缓存内容看的是 cache-control 策略，不是链接过不过期。
optionExplanations_en: Once generated, nothing auto-revokes it — if it leaks accidentally or on purpose, only manual cleanup can undo the exposure.
How long a link stays valid has nothing to do with whether the file's bytes degrade.
S3 will happily sign a URL with any expiry, including a very long one — it doesn't refuse this.
CDN caching is governed by cache-control policy, not by whether the link itself expires.

scenario: 所有 part 都通过 ListParts 校验后，后端还没调用 CompleteMultipartUpload，就先把 metadata 状态改成了 uploaded。
scenario_en: All parts pass ListParts verification, but before calling CompleteMultipartUpload the backend already flips metadata status to uploaded.
q: 提前改状态最可能带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem does marking the status early most likely cause?
options: 没问题，ListParts 通过就等于文件已经可以下载
组装若失败，metadata 仍显示 uploaded
这会导致 presigned URL 的签名立刻失效
这会让 fingerprint 计算出错误的哈希值
options_en: No problem — passing ListParts already means the file is downloadable.
If assembly later fails, metadata still says uploaded.
It immediately invalidates the presigned URL's signature.
It causes the fingerprint calculation to produce the wrong hash.
why: ListParts 只确认各 part 已到 S3，还没组装成一个对象；只有 CompleteMultipartUpload 成功后对象才真实存在，提前标记会造成“metadata 说传完了、下载却失败”的中间态。
why_en: ListParts only confirms parts landed on S3, not that they're assembled into one object; only a successful CompleteMultipartUpload makes the object real, so marking early creates a state where metadata says done but the download fails.
optionExplanations: part 都在不等于已经组装成一个可下载的对象，这正是提前标记会踩的坑。
组装这一步可能失败（比如某个 part 缺失或校验不过），提前标记就制造出状态不一致的中间态。
presigned URL 的签名有效期是独立设置的，跟 metadata 状态字段无关。
fingerprint 在上传前就已经算好，跟后端什么时候更新状态字段没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: All parts present doesn't mean they're assembled into a downloadable object yet — exactly the trap in marking early.
Assembly can still fail, e.g. a missing or mismatched part, so marking early creates a state mismatch.
A presigned URL's signature validity is set independently and has nothing to do with the metadata status field.
The fingerprint is computed before upload even starts, unrelated to when the backend flips the status field.

q: 端到端延迟目标定为 < 200ms，这个数字的依据是什么？
options: 建立连接的三次握手大约耗时 200ms 左右
本设计选定的体验目标，不是协议强制值
服务器推流协议规范里规定的最大间隔
内容分发网络边缘缓存的默认刷新周期
why: 200ms 不是硬分界，而是本设计采用的实时体验目标：低于这个量级通常会被感知为很快、接近即时。更严格的交互目标常会用 100ms 量级。
why_en: Two hundred milliseconds is a practical realtime target rather than a hard perception boundary; interactions under that range usually feel very fast, while stricter instant-feedback targets are often closer to 100ms.
options_en: The connection three-way handshake takes about 200ms.
This design's chosen target, not a protocol requirement.
The maximum interval defined by the server-push spec.
The default refresh period for the content delivery network cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么把端到端延迟目标定在 200ms，而不是直接照抄某个协议或基础设施参数。
q_en: Why is the end-to-end latency target set below 200ms?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why the end-to-end latency target is 200ms instead of copying a protocol or infrastructure number.
optionExplanations: 建立连接的三次握手通常几十毫秒量级，跟 200ms 这个体验目标没有因果关系，是无关的巧合数字。
对，200ms 是团队自己定的体验目标，不是照抄某个协议或基础设施参数。
SSE 协议本身不规定端到端延迟上限，把协议条文当成体验目标的依据是张冠李戴。
CDN 边缘缓存的刷新周期是另一层的运维参数，跟评论要多快到达观众无关。
optionExplanations_en: The handshake takes tens of milliseconds, but that has no causal link to a chosen UX latency target.
Right — 200ms is the team's own experience target, not copied from a protocol or infra spec.
SSE itself sets no end-to-end latency ceiling, so citing the spec here confuses protocol with product goal.
A CDN's cache refresh interval is an unrelated ops parameter, not the reason for a comment latency target.

scenario: 直播评论系统：不同观众看到同一条评论的时间略有先后完全无伤大雅，但评论区整体不可用会毁掉直播体验。
q: 非功能需求上该怎么做 CAP 取舍？
options: 一致性优先：所有观众必须在同一瞬间看到同一条评论
放弃分区容忍，假设网络永不分区
可用性优先、接受最终一致：评论晚几百毫秒到达没关系
用分布式事务同时保证强一致和高可用
why: 评论属于典型的可容忍短暂不同步的数据，所以可用性优先、最终一致即可。这条取舍直接决定了后面能用 DynamoDB、Redis pub/sub 这类偏可用的组件。
why_en: Live comments tolerate brief staleness, so the system prioritizes availability over consistency and accepts eventual consistency.
whenOtherWins: 涉及钱、库存扣减、订单这类不能读到旧值的业务必须倒向强一致，宁可短暂拒绝服务。
tradeoff: 可用性优先(最终一致) vs 强一致性
options_en: Consistency first: every viewer must see a comment at the exact same instant.
Drop partition tolerance and assume the network never partitions.
Availability first with eventual consistency: comments landing a few hundred ms late is fine.
Use distributed transactions to guarantee strong consistency and high availability together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统里一致性、可用性、分区容忍性三者的取舍框架
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the tradeoff among consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短暂不同步，但保证副本最终收敛到相同值
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows brief staleness but guarantees replicas converge over time.

q_en: How should we make the CAP tradeoff for live comments?
scenario_en: In live comments, viewers can see the same comment slightly apart in time, but an unavailable comment experience ruins the live stream.
optionExplanations: 转账、扣库存这类不能读到旧值的场景才该一致性优先；评论慢半秒没人在意，为此牺牲可用性不值。
现实网络会分区，是分布式系统必须面对的常态，假设它不存在直接违背 CAP 的前提。
对，几百毫秒的到达差异对观众无伤；把服务保持在线，比让所有人同一刻看到同一条更重要。
CAP 下强一致和高可用不可兼得，分布式事务只是把代价转嫁成延迟或阻塞，不是真的兼得。
optionExplanations_en: Consistency-first fits money or inventory flows that can't read stale values; comments arriving late is harmless, so paying for it here is wasteful.
Real networks do partition, so assuming they never will breaks the basic premise CAP is built on.
Right — a few hundred milliseconds of skew is harmless here; keeping the experience online matters more than synchronized delivery.
CAP says you can't have both strong consistency and high availability; distributed transactions just hide the cost as extra latency or blocking.

q: FB Live Comments 的规模（scale）目标是？
options: 数百万路并发直播，热门场每秒数千条评论
全平台只有几千路直播，每场每秒也就几条评论
只有一路超级直播，累计百万条评论总量
只需支撑工作日高峰的几万观众，无并发压力
why: 规模需求是双重的：横向是数百万路并发视频，纵向是热门单场每秒数千条评论。后面的分层方案（pub/sub、采样、CDN）就是围绕这两个维度展开的。
why_en: The system must scale to millions of concurrent live videos with thousands of comments per second on a single hot video.
options_en: Millions of concurrent live videos, thousands of comments per second on a hot one.
Only a few thousand live videos platform-wide, a handful of comments per second each.
A single mega live video with a million comments in total.
Only needs weekday-peak traffic of a few tens of thousands of viewers.
scenario: 面试官让你先说清楚这套评论系统要扛住的规模量级，再继续往下设计。
q_en: What scale should FB Live Comments be designed for?
scenario_en: Before designing further, the interviewer asks you to state the order of magnitude the comment system must handle.
optionExplanations: 对，横向数百万路并发视频、纵向热门单场每秒数千条评论，这两个维度撑起了后面的分层方案。
几千路、每场几条评论这个量级远小于题目要求，撑不起后面对推送层和采样的深挖。
把总量压缩成单路直播的百万评论，漏掉了并发路数这个维度，规模判断会整个偏小。
只按工作日高峰的几万观众来设计，会让后面的横向扩展和采样方案变得没有必要。
optionExplanations_en: Right — millions of concurrent videos plus thousands of comments per second on a hot one drives everything that follows.
A few thousand videos with a handful of comments each is far below the stated scale and skips the reason for push and sampling.
Collapsing it to one video with a million comments total drops the concurrency dimension entirely.
Sizing only for tens of thousands of weekday-peak viewers makes the later horizontal scaling and sampling work unnecessary.

q: 对这类 product 风格的系统设计题，推荐的推进策略是？
options: 先把所有深挖点讲完，最后再补高层架构图
先做完整容量估算，数字齐了再动手设计
从完整的数据库 schema 开始，自底向上推
按功能需求逐条推进，再用非功能需求叠深度
why: 策略是顺序推进：一条条满足功能需求，保证不迷失在细节里；功能齐了以后，再让非功能需求引导深挖和复杂度。
why_en: Build the design sequentially through each functional requirement, then use the non-functional requirements to layer on depth.
options_en: Cover every deep dive first and only then draw the high-level diagram.
Do a full capacity estimate and start designing once the numbers are in.
Start from a complete database schema and build bottom-up.
Work through the functional requirements in order, then layer depth from the non-functional ones.
q_en: How should you approach this product-style system design interview?
optionExplanations: 先讲深挖点会让面试官看不到全局，一头扎进细节容易迷路，拖慢整体节奏。
容量估算通常按需插入设计过程中，不必在动手前做一次完整估算。
过早定死 schema 会在后续需求逐步展开时被迫返工，字段还没到该确定的阶段。
对，先逐条满足功能需求打好地基，再让非功能需求引导深挖，是稳妥的推进节奏。
optionExplanations_en: Leading with deep dives buries the interviewer in detail before they see the big picture and stalls momentum.
Capacity estimates are usually folded in as the design needs them, not done wholesale before anything else.
Locking the schema too early forces rework once later requirements reshape which fields you actually need.
Right — work through each functional requirement first to build a foundation, then let non-functional needs drive the depth.
scenario: 45 分钟面试设计 FB Live 评论区，功能需求已列全，非功能需求还没深挖，时间必须省着花。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes for Facebook Live comments: the functional requirements are listed, the non-functional ones aren't explored yet, and time is tight.

q: 补全三个核心实体：
text: 本题只有三个核心实体：{{User}}（既可以是观众也可以是主播）、{{Live Video}}（由其他团队管理、需要集成的直播视频）、{{Comment}}（用户发在直播上的消息）。
why: 实体是系统的「名词」：User、Live Video、Comment。其中 Live Video 归别的团队所有，我们只做集成。
why_en: The three core entities are the user, the live video owned by another team, and the comment posted on it.
q_en: Fill in the three core entities.

q: 为什么开局只列核心实体、而不直接给完整数据模型？
options: 早期定不准字段，先立核心名词打地基，schema 随设计补全
数据模型在面试里不重要，可以全程跳过不谈
面试官通常不会看你的 schema 设计，写了也白写
实体列表和完整 schema 本质是同一件事，写哪个都行
why: 开局阶段还无法准确枚举所有列/字段，硬写只会返工。先立住核心实体来引导思路，数据模型随设计逐步长出来。
why_en: Early in the design you cannot enumerate every column yet, so you start with core entities and grow the data model as the design progresses.
options_en: You can't pin down fields this early, so name the core entities first and let the schema fill in as the design grows.
The data model doesn't matter in interviews, so you can skip it entirely.
Interviewers never look at your schema, so writing one is wasted effort.
An entity list and a full schema are the same thing, so either one will do.
q_en: Why start with core entities instead of a full data model?
optionExplanations: 对，设计早期还定不准每个字段，先立住核心名词打地基，字段随设计逐步长出来。
数据模型仍然要在设计推进中补全，跳过它会让后续讨论缺了地基。
面试官通常会追问字段细节，说他们不关心 schema 不成立。
实体列表只是「名词」清单，完整 schema 需要更多信息才能定，两者不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Right — you can't pin down every field yet, so naming the core entities first gives the design a foundation to grow from.
The data model still gets filled in as the design progresses; skipping it entirely leaves no foundation.
Interviewers routinely probe field-level detail, so claiming they don't care about the schema doesn't hold.
An entity list is just the noun list; a full schema needs information you don't have yet, so the two aren't the same thing.
scenario: FB Live 评论区设计的第 5 分钟：后面还要加分页、推送、CDN，字段肯定还会反复变。
scenario_en: Five minutes into the Facebook Live comments design — pagination, push and CDN are still coming, so the fields will keep changing.

scenario: 设计发评论的 POST 接口，必须防止用户篡改请求、冒充他人发评论。
q: userId 应该从哪里来？
options: 放进请求体，由客户端自行填写 userId 字段
作为 URL 查询参数随请求传入
服务端从头部令牌中解析出身份
从 cookie 里直接读取明文 userId
why: 客户端只负责携带令牌，服务端校验令牌并从中提取 userId。身份不走请求体，用户就无法伪造 userId 冒充别人，这是现代 Web 应用的通用做法。
why_en: The server extracts the user id from a validated JWT or session token in the header, which prevents users from tampering with the request to impersonate others.
whenOtherWins: 内部受信服务间调用或管理后台代用户操作时，可以在请求体里显式传目标 userId，但仍要有服务级鉴权。
options_en: Put userId in the request body for the client to fill in.
Pass userId as a URL query parameter.
Server parses identity from the header token.
Read plaintext userId straight from a cookie.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON Web Token，一种把用户身份编码进已签名令牌的方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity claims.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、代表已登录会话的令牌
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session token represents an authenticated session issued by the server.

tradeoff: 令牌解出身份 vs 请求体自报身份
q_en: Where should the userId come from?
scenario_en: You are designing the POST API for comments and must prevent users from tampering with the request to impersonate someone else.
optionExplanations: 内部受信服务之间可以显式在请求体传目标 userId，但面向普通用户时任何人都能改这个字段冒充别人。
URL 查询参数和请求体一样是客户端能直接编辑的内容，同样挡不住伪造身份。
对，签名令牌把身份绑定在服务端可校验的数据里，客户端没有密钥就不能改成别人。
明文 cookie 没有签名校验，用户或中间人一样能直接改写里面的 userId。
optionExplanations_en: Trusted internal services can pass a target userId explicitly in the body, but a public client can edit that same field to impersonate anyone.
A URL query parameter is just as editable by the client as the body, so it offers no real protection either.
Right — the signed token binds identity to data the server can verify, and the client can't rewrite it as another user.
A plaintext cookie carries no signature check, so a user or a man-in-the-middle can rewrite the userId just as easily.

q: 读这个创建评论的请求，正确的说法是？
options: userId 应补进请求体，方便服务器直接识别用户
liveVideoId 应该放进请求体而不是路径
这个 POST 请求会顺带返回该视频最近一页的历史评论
视频 ID 走路径参数，评论内容走请求体，身份从令牌头解析
why: 写接口极简：路径定位视频，body 只带 message，身份由头部令牌承载。查历史评论是另一个 GET 接口的职责。
why_en: The create-comment endpoint takes the video id in the path, the message in the body, and the user identity from the auth token header.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant M as Comment Service
    participant D as Comment DB
    participant P as Push path
    C->>A: POST /comments
    A->>M: auth user + liveVideoId
    M->>D: append comment
    M->>P: publish new comment
options_en: userId should be added to the body so the server can identify the user directly.
liveVideoId should live in the request body instead of the path.
This POST also returns the video's latest page of comment history.
The video id goes in the path, the message in the body, and identity comes from the auth token header.
q_en: What is the correct read of this create-comment request?
optionExplanations: 身份应该来自已签名令牌，让客户端自报 userId 会重新打开伪造身份的口子。
liveVideoId 本就是要定位的资源，属于路径参数，不需要塞进请求体。
历史列表属于读取历史的接口；这条 POST 只表达「新增一条评论」这个动作。
对，视频 ID 走路径定位资源、评论内容走 body、身份从令牌头解析，三者各司其职。
optionExplanations_en: Identity should come from a signed token, not from letting the client self-report userId — that reopens the impersonation hole.
liveVideoId identifies the resource being addressed, so it belongs in the path, not stuffed into the body.
History belongs to the read-history endpoint; this POST only represents appending one new comment.
Right — the video id locates the resource in the path, the message goes in the body, and identity comes from the token header.
scenario: FB Live 写评论接口：观众在直播页发一条评论，身份已由网关校验过的 JWT 令牌承载。
scenario_en: The Facebook Live create-comment endpoint: a viewer posts on the live page and identity already rides in a gateway-validated JWT.

scenario: 用户刚加入直播，页面要先显示加入之前最近的一页评论；之后如果继续往上滚，才加载更早的历史评论。
q: 加载「加入直播之前的历史评论」时，为什么不用已有的 since 参数？
options: since 参数本身查询效率太慢
since 参数不支持设置每页返回多少条评论
since 只能配合写路径一起使用
since 给的是比锚点更新的评论，方向反了
why: 对，历史评论应该用 cursor/before + limit。since 是「给我锚点之后的新评论」，适合断线后追赶；历史回看要「锚点之前的 N 条」，方向相反。
why_en: Yes: historical comments should use cursor/before plus limit. since means comments newer than the anchor, which is useful for catching up after disconnects; history loading needs the N comments before an anchor.
codeSample:
GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?limit=20
# 返回最近 20 条历史评论 + nextCursor

GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?before={nextCursor}&limit=20
# 往上滚时，继续取更早的 20 条

GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?since={lastSeenCommentId}
# 断线重连时，追赶更新的评论

scenario: 评论是结构简单的记录，没有复杂关系和事务需求，但要求快、可水平扩展、高可用。

why_en: DynamoDB fits because comments are simple records without complex relationships or transactions, and it is fast, scalable, and highly available.
whenOtherWins: 文章明说 Postgres / MySQL 也完全可行；如果后续要复杂关系查询或事务，关系库反而更顺手。
options_en: DynamoDB: high-throughput access to simple records, scalable and highly available.
Neo4j graph database: comments are naturally parent-child graph relationships.
Keep everything in Redis memory for maximum read and write speed.

q_en: Which database should store comments?
scenario_en: Comments are simple records with no complex relationships or transactions, but they need fast reads and writes, horizontal scale, and high availability.

纯内存存储掉电易失，评论这种要长期保留的数据不能只放 Redis。

Comments have no inherent graph relationships to traverse, so a graph database pays for a query pattern that isn't there.
Pure in-memory storage loses data on restart, and comments need to persist, so Redis alone isn't enough.
Comments don't need cross-row transactions, so insisting Postgres is mandatory overconstrains the choice.

q: 「客户端每隔几秒轮询新评论」这个朴素方案的核心缺陷是？
options: 客户端实现轮询与去重逻辑太复杂
近实时要毫秒级轮询，数据库扛不住且多是空跑
轮询无法携带 since 这类增量参数
轮询和无限滚动分页天然互相冲突
why: 观众和评论一多，轮询频率就得跟着涨，数据库压力暴增；而大部分轮询是空手而归的浪费。要满足近实时得毫秒级轮询，不可行。
why_en: Polling cannot scale because near-real-time delivery would require millisecond-level polling that hammers the database while most requests return nothing new.
options_en: Polling plus dedup logic is too complex to implement on the client.
Near-real-time would need millisecond polling, which the database can't sustain and which mostly returns nothing.
Polling cannot carry an incremental parameter like since.
Polling and infinite-scroll pagination are inherently incompatible.
q_en: What is the core flaw in polling for new comments every few seconds?
optionExplanations: 轮询本身实现并不复杂，真正的问题不在客户端代码难度上。
对，要做到近实时就得压到毫秒级轮询，数据库扛不住而且大部分请求都是空手而归。
轮询完全可以带 since 参数，这不是它的短板。
轮询和分页可以配合使用，两者并不天然冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Polling logic itself isn't hard to implement; that's not where the real problem lives.
Right — near-real-time needs millisecond-level polling, which the database can't sustain, and most requests come back empty.
Polling can absolutely carry a since parameter, so that isn't the limitation.
Polling and pagination work fine together; they aren't inherently at odds.
scenario: 一场 100 万观众的直播，新评论要求 200ms 内可见；朴素方案是客户端每几秒轮询一次。
scenario_en: A live video with a million viewers needs new comments visible within 200ms; the naive plan is clients polling every few seconds.

Jump straight to the better solution, but justify the decision and spell out the trade-offs.
Let the interviewer decide which approach to start from.
Skip the high-level design and go straight into deep dives.
q_en: How should you present the starting design?
scenario_en: In the interview, you already know this problem well and know that push beats polling for the realtime comment path.
optionExplanations: 真的是第一次遇到这题时，从轮询起步打地基才合理；已经很熟就没必要装作不会。
对，已经知道更优解就可以直接上，关键是把决策理由和取舍讲清楚，不用为了表演绕远路。

q: 用户刚加入一场直播时，评论区要同时满足哪两件事？（多选）
options: 立即开始实时收到新发布的评论
能往上滚动、逐步加载更早的历史评论（无限滚动）
自动回放整场直播视频
把全部旧评论一次性推到屏幕上
why: 加入直播的用户需要两条路径：实时流拿新评论 + 分页拉历史评论。历史部分用聊天应用常见的无限滚动交互。
why_en: A joining viewer needs both a real-time stream of new comments and paginated history loaded through infinite scrolling.
options_en: Immediately start receiving new comments in real time.
Scroll up to progressively load older history via infinite scroll.
Automatically replay the entire live video.
Dump every old comment onto the screen at once.
q_en: When a user joins a live video, what two things must the comment UI handle?
optionExplanations: 挡住的是「错过现场」的风险：实时流让刚加入的观众马上跟上正在发生的讨论。
挡住的是「一次性拉全量」的压力：无限滚动按需分页加载历史，减轻服务器和带宽负担。
自动回放整场视频是播放器的职责，不属于评论区要解决的问题。
一次性推送全部旧评论会在加入瞬间打爆带宽和渲染，跟无限滚动的按需加载正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: It blocks the risk of missing the live moment: a real-time stream lets a joining viewer catch up to the conversation immediately.
It relieves the pressure of loading everything at once: infinite scroll paginates history on demand instead.
Auto-replaying the entire video is the player's job, not something the comment UI needs to solve.
Dumping every old comment at join time spikes bandwidth and rendering — the opposite of on-demand infinite scroll.
scenario: 观众中途点进一场已经播了 40 分钟的直播，评论区此刻是空白的。
scenario_en: A viewer joins a live video 40 minutes in, and the comment pane is currently blank.

q: 在高速滚动的评论流里，offset 分页有哪两大问题？
options: 要数过 offset 之前的所有行，增删还会让偏移错位
offset 不支持自定义的排序方向
offset 分页天生无法配合无限滚动这种交互模式
offset 值本身会泄露用户的隐私信息
why: offset 分页既低效（每页都要扫过前面所有行）又不稳定（滚动期间的新增/删除让偏移失准）。快速变化的评论流正好把两个短板都踩中。
why_en: Offset pagination is slow because the database counts all preceding rows, and unstable because inserts or deletes shift the offset and cause duplicated or missing comments.
options_en: The database counts every row before the offset, and inserts or deletes shift that offset out of place.
Offset does not support a custom sort direction.
Offset pagination inherently cannot work with an infinite-scroll interaction.
The offset value itself leaks user privacy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用数字偏移量跳过前面若干行的分页方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset pagination skips a fixed number of preceding rows using a numeric offset.

q_en: What are the two big problems with offset pagination in a fast comment stream?
optionExplanations: 对，每页都要扫过前面所有行效率低，滚动期间的增删又让偏移错位，快速变化的流正好踩中两个短板。
排序方向和分页方式是两回事，跟 offset 本身无关。
offset 技术上仍能配合滚动加载，问题不在交互模式的兼容性。
offset 只是个数字偏移量，本身不携带任何隐私信息。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the database has to count every row before the offset, and inserts or deletes during scroll shift it out of place, hitting both weaknesses in a fast-moving stream.
Sort direction is a separate concern from pagination style, unrelated to offset itself.
Offset pagination can technically still drive infinite scroll, so compatibility isn't the issue.
An offset is just a numeric position; it carries no privacy information on its own.
scenario: 热门直播每秒新增上千条评论，客户端要一页 20 条地往上翻历史。
scenario_en: A hot live video adds a thousand comments per second while the client pages backwards 20 at a time.

scenario: 高吞吐、评论持续插入的无限滚动列表，要求翻页高效且不会因新评论到来而错位。
q: 分页方案选什么？
options: offset 分页，实现简单直接、前端也好写
每次全量拉取评论，交给客户端自己裁剪
cursor 分页：用评论 ID 做翻页锚点
随机抽取一页评论展示给用户，减少扫描
why: 游标锚定到具体一条评论上：配合索引不用扫过前面的行，增删也不影响游标指向，性能随数据量增长保持稳定，还天然契合 DynamoDB 的 key 查询。
why_en: Cursor pagination anchors on a unique comment id, staying efficient with an index and stable under concurrent inserts, which suits a fast-moving feed.
whenOtherWins: 数据集小、基本静态，或产品需要「跳到第 N 页」时，offset 只传数字偏移，更简单够用。

graph LR
    Client[Join live] --> API[GET comments before cursor]
    API --> DB[(Comments by liveVideoId)]
    DB --> Page[Recent page]
    Page --> SSE[Start live SSE]
    SSE --> Client

Fetch every comment each time and let the client trim the list itself.
Cursor pagination anchored on the comment id.
Randomly sample a page of comments to cut down scanning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用某条记录的唯一 ID 作为翻页锚点的分页方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination anchors each page on a unique record id.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用数字偏移量跳过前面若干行；评论仍可有 ID，只是不用 ID 当翻页锚点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset pagination skips a numeric number of rows; comments can still have ids, but ids are not the page anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值数据库，按主键查询扩展性好
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that scales well for key-based queries.

tradeoff: cursor 稳定高效 vs offset 简单但会错位
q_en: Which pagination strategy should we use?
scenario_en: An infinite comment list keeps receiving inserts at high throughput, and pagination must stay efficient without shifting under new writes.
optionExplanations: 数据量小、基本静态或需要跳到第 N 页时，offset 只传两个数字确实更省事，但持续插入的流里它会错位。
把裁剪工作丢给客户端意味着每次都要传全量数据，热门直播下带宽和数据库都扛不住。
对，用评论 ID 当锚点，查询可以从索引位置继续走；持续插入也不会改变这个锚点。
随机抽样丢掉了按时间顺序回看的能力，跟无限滚动翻历史的交互需求正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: When data is small, mostly static, or you need to jump to page N, offset's two plain integers are genuinely simpler, but it shifts under a stream that keeps inserting.
Handing trimming to the client means shipping the full comment set every time, which neither bandwidth nor the database survives for a hot video.
Right — using comment id as the anchor lets the query continue from an indexed position, and new inserts do not move that anchor.
Random sampling throws away chronological order, the opposite of what scrolling back through history needs.

q: 读这个 DynamoDB（NoSQL 键值库）查询，它返回的是什么？
options: lv_42 中比 c_1088 更新的最近 10 条评论
lv_42 中早于 c_1088 的最近 10 条，新→旧
对整表做全量扫描后任取 10 条
恰好等于 c_1088 的那一条评论
why: commentId < :cursor 限定「比游标更早」，ScanIndexForward=false 表示按 key 倒序（新→旧），Limit 取一页。这正是无限滚动往上翻历史的查询。
why_en: The query fetches the ten most recent comments older than the cursor for that video, sorted newest first, which is exactly one page of history.
options_en: The 10 most recent comments in lv_42 that are newer than c_1088.
The 10 most recent comments in lv_42 older than c_1088, newest first.
Ten arbitrary rows from a full table scan.
The single comment whose id equals c_1088.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值数据库，按主键查询扩展性好
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that scales well for key-based queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用某条记录的唯一 ID 作为翻页锚点的分页方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination anchors each page on a unique record id.

q_en: What does this DynamoDB query return?
optionExplanations: 这里的范围条件把结果限制在锚点之前，所以把它解释成更新评论是读错方向。
对，范围条件取旧记录，倒序返回最近的一页；这是往上滚动时需要的结果。
查询带着明确的 KeyConditionExpression 过滤条件，不是无差别的全表扫描。
< 是范围条件，会匹配一批记录，不是精确匹配单条评论。
optionExplanations_en: The range predicate selects records before the anchor, so treating the result as newer comments reads the direction backwards.
Right — the range selects older records and returns the nearest page in descending order, exactly what upward scrolling needs.
The query carries an explicit KeyConditionExpression filter, not an unfiltered full-table scan.
< is a range condition matching a batch of records, not an exact match on a single comment.
scenario: 无限滚动往上翻历史评论：客户端手上只有当前屏幕最旧的一条 commentId = c_1088。
scenario_en: Infinite scroll going back in history: all the client holds is the oldest comment id on screen, c_1088.

q: 补全 cursor 分页的优点：
text: cursor 分页更{{高效}}（有索引时不用数过游标之前的行）、更{{稳定}}（滚动期间的增删不会让游标错位）、契合 DynamoDB 的 {{key}} 式查询，且评论量增长时性能保持{{一致}}。
why: 这四点就是选 cursor 而不是 offset 的完整理由：效率、稳定性、与存储引擎的契合、规模下的性能一致性。
why_en: Cursor pagination is efficient, stable under concurrent changes, a natural fit for key-based queries, and keeps consistent performance as volume grows.
q_en: Fill in the benefits of cursor pagination.

q: 从轮询升级到推送模型，本质上改变了什么？
options: 从客户端猜时机反复问，变成服务端主动推送
把评论从数据库挪到了内存里存放
把底层传输协议从 HTTP 换成了 UDP
把普通的读请求改成了批处理任务
why: 拉模型靠客户端猜时机，猜错就是浪费；推模型让服务端掌握主动权，评论一创建就推出去。这也是协作编辑、实时看板、游戏等实时更新场景的通用模式。
why_en: Instead of clients guessing when to ask, a push model lets the server deliver each comment the moment it is created, the core of the real-time updates pattern.
tradeoff: 服务端主动推送 vs 客户端反复轮询
options_en: From clients guessing and repeatedly asking, to the server pushing proactively.
Moving comments from the database into memory.
Swapping the transport protocol from HTTP to UDP.
Turning normal read requests into batch jobs.
q_en: What fundamentally changes when we move from polling to push?
optionExplanations: 对，拉模型靠客户端猜时机反复问，推模型让服务端一创建评论就主动推出去，主动权换了边。
评论仍然持久化在数据库里，推送模型没有改变存储位置。
SSE 依然跑在标准 HTTP 之上，传输协议并没有换成 UDP。
这跟批处理没有关系，变化的是谁发起动作，不是请求怎么被处理。
optionExplanations_en: Right — instead of clients guessing and asking repeatedly, the server now pushes each comment the moment it's created; the initiative moved sides.
Comments are still persisted in the database; push didn't relocate storage.
SSE still runs over plain HTTP, so the transport wasn't swapped to UDP.
This has nothing to do with batch processing; what changed is who initiates, not how requests get processed.
scenario: 100 万观众的直播要求评论 200ms 内送达，而客户端根本猜不到下一条评论何时产生。
scenario_en: A million-viewer live video needs comments delivered within 200ms, and the client cannot guess when the next one appears.

q: 一句话区分 WebSocket 和 SSE（Server-Sent Events）这两种推送技术？
options: WebSocket 只能单向、SSE 才双向，方向刚好说反了
两者都是双向通道，只是握手方式不同
WebSocket 双向长连接，SSE 单向 HTTP 推流
SSE 不是持久连接，每条消息都要重新建连
why: WebSocket 打开一条双向通道并保持；SSE 只做服务器到客户端的单向推送，且跑在标准 HTTP 上、实现更简单，客户端要发消息就走普通请求。
why_en: WebSockets provide a persistent two-way channel, while SSE is a one-way server-to-client stream over standard HTTP with client messages sent as normal requests.
tradeoff: 双向长连接 vs 单向 HTTP 推流
options_en: WebSocket can only go one-way, SSE is the two-way one — the direction is backwards.
Both are two-way channels, only the handshake differs.
WebSocket is two-way persistent; SSE is one-way over HTTP.
SSE is not persistent, every message needs a new connection.

q_en: How do WebSocket and SSE differ in one sentence?
optionExplanations: 事实正好相反：WebSocket 才是双向，SSE 是单向服务器推流。
SSE 是单向流，不是双向通道，这个说法把两者都判错了。
对，前者适合双向收发；后者是一条 HTTP 响应流，专门承接服务端连续推给浏览器。
SSE 连接本身是持久的，不需要每条消息都重新建连。
optionExplanations_en: The facts are reversed: WebSocket is the two-way one, SSE is the one-way server push.
SSE is a one-way stream, not a two-way channel, so calling both bidirectional misreads them both.
Right — the former fits two-way traffic; the latter is one HTTP response stream for continuous server-to-browser delivery.
An SSE connection is itself persistent; it doesn't need a fresh connection per message.
scenario: FB Live 评论区：观众绝大多数时间只读评论，偶尔才发一条，要在两种推送技术里选。
scenario_en: In Facebook Live comments viewers mostly just read and only occasionally post, and we have to pick between two push technologies.

scenario: 直播评论的读写极不均衡：绝大多数观众从不发评论，却要持续接收所有评论；发评论本身是低频事件。
q: 推送技术选哪个？
options: WebSocket：为每个观众开一条双向通道
SSE：观众单向收流，发评论走普通 POST
长轮询：兼容性最好，不用引入新协议
gRPC 双向流：性能最强、二进制帧
why: 为几乎只读的观众维护双向通道是白付的开销。SSE 的单向流正好承接高频读，低频写继续用普通 POST，各得其所。
why_en: With reads vastly outnumbering writes, SSE's one-way stream serves viewers efficiently while infrequent comment posts go over plain HTTP.
whenOtherWins: 读写均衡的真双向场景——比如互相频繁收发消息的聊天室——WebSocket 才是最优解。
diagram:
graph LR
    Viewer[Browser viewer] --> SSE[SSE connection]
    Comment[New comment] --> PubSub[Pub/Sub]
    PubSub --> SSE
    SSE --> Viewer
options_en: WebSocket: open a two-way channel for every viewer.
SSE: viewers receive a one-way stream and post comments over plain HTTP POST.
Long polling: best compatibility, no new protocol needed.
Bidirectional gRPC streaming: strongest performance with binary frames.

q_en: Which push technology should we choose?
scenario_en: Live comments are heavily read-biased: most viewers never comment, but they continuously receive comments; posting is low-frequency.
optionExplanations: 互相频繁收发的聊天室这类真双向场景才该选 WebSocket；这里几乎只读，双向通道是白付的开销。
对，观众侧主要消费事件，用一条服务器到浏览器的流；少量发言仍用普通写接口。
长轮询是 SSE/WebSocket 出现前的兼容方案，效率不如原生推送。
gRPC 双向流面向服务间调用，不是为海量浏览器长连接设计的。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket earns its keep in truly two-way, high-frequency chat; here viewers mostly just read, so a two-way channel is overkill.
Right — viewers mainly consume events over one server-to-browser stream, while the rare comment post stays on the normal write API.
Long polling predates SSE and WebSocket as a compatibility fallback and is less efficient than native push.
Bidirectional gRPC streaming targets service-to-service calls, not millions of browser long connections.

q: 选了 SSE 之后要正视哪些基础设施挑战？（多选）
options: 部分代理和负载均衡器不支持流式响应，产生难排查的缓冲问题
浏览器限制每个域名的并发 SSE 连接数，多开直播会有麻烦
长生命周期连接让监控和调试更复杂
SSE 无法在普通 HTTP 上运行，必须自定义协议
why: SSE 的三大坑：中间层缓冲流式响应、浏览器每域连接数上限、长连接的可观测性难题。SSE 恰恰是跑在标准 HTTP 上的，这正是它的优点。
why_en: SSE brings proxy buffering issues, browser per-domain connection limits, and harder monitoring of long-lived connections, even though it runs on plain HTTP.
options_en: Some proxies and load balancers don't support streaming responses, causing hard-to-debug buffering.
Browsers cap concurrent SSE connections per domain, causing trouble with multiple live tabs.
Long-lived connections make monitoring and debugging harder.
SSE cannot run over plain HTTP and needs a custom protocol.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: After choosing SSE, which infrastructure issues must we handle?
optionExplanations: 挡不住的风险是中间层默默缓冲整个响应，评论会成批延迟到达而不是逐条流式送达。
挡不住的风险是浏览器每域并发连接数有上限，用户多开几个直播标签页就可能连不上。
减不掉的压力是长生命周期连接让排障更难：一条连接可能活好几个小时，问题定位得靠专门的可观测性。
这个说法反了：EventSource 使用普通 HTTP 响应流，部署优势正来自不发明新协议。
optionExplanations_en: The risk it doesn't block: an intermediate proxy silently buffers the whole response, so comments land in delayed batches instead of streaming one by one.
The risk it doesn't block: browsers cap concurrent connections per domain, so opening several live tabs can fail to connect.
The pressure it doesn't relieve: long-lived connections make debugging harder since one connection can run for hours before a problem surfaces.
This is backwards: EventSource uses a normal HTTP response stream, and its deployment advantage comes from not inventing a new protocol.
scenario: 决定用 SSE 给百万观众推评论，流量要穿过公司现有的 NGINX 代理和用户的浏览器。
scenario_en: We chose SSE to push comments to a million viewers, and the traffic must cross our existing NGINX proxies and the user browser.

q: 读这段响应，哪一行把它变成浏览器认可的 SSE（服务器推流）流？
codeSample:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive

id: c_1042
event: comment
data: {"user":"amy","message":"lets go!"}
options: Content-Type: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
Cache-Control: no-cache
data: {"user":"amy","message":"lets go!"}
why: text/event-stream 这个 MIME 类型告诉浏览器这是一条持续的事件流，EventSource 会保持连接并逐条解析 id/event/data 块。其余头只是配合项。
why_en: The text/event-stream content type is what tells the browser to treat the response as a continuous server-sent event stream.
options_en: Content-Type: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
Cache-Control: no-cache
data: {"user":"amy","message":"lets go!"}

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识响应内容类型的头部，如 text/event-stream
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-Type is the header that labels a response's media type, such as text/event-stream.

q_en: Which line makes this response a browser-recognized SSE stream?
optionExplanations: 对，这个 MIME 类型告诉浏览器把响应当持续事件流处理，EventSource 才会保持连接逐条解析。
keep-alive 只是配合长连接的通用头，不是浏览器识别 SSE 的关键。
no-cache 只是控制缓存行为，不决定这是不是一条 SSE 流。
data 行只装单条评论的负载，浏览器得先认出流类型才会去逐条解析它。
optionExplanations_en: Right — this MIME type tells the browser to treat the response as a continuous event stream, which is what makes EventSource keep the connection open.
keep-alive is just a generic header supporting long connections, not what makes the browser recognize SSE.
no-cache only controls caching behavior; it doesn't determine whether this is an SSE stream.
The data line only carries one comment payload; the browser must first recognize the stream type before it parses those lines.
scenario: 服务端要把评论推给浏览器原生的 EventSource，下面是准备返回的响应头与首个事件。
scenario_en: The server wants to feed comments to the browser native EventSource; here are the response headers and the first event.

q: 「Comment Management Service 直接给所有观众推 SSE（服务器推流）长连接」，这个初版方案的遗留问题是？
options: 评论没有被持久化写入数据库
SSE 协议无法传输 JSON 格式的数据
客户端无法把评论渲染进列表里
单机扛不住所有连接，暴露跨服务器协调问题
why: SSE 要求每个观众一条常开连接，单机注定扛不住百万级观众。加机器之后，「同一直播的观众分散在不同服务器」就成了下一个要解的题。
why_en: A single server cannot hold millions of persistent SSE connections, so we must scale horizontally, which creates the cross-server coordination problem.
options_en: Comments are not persisted to the database.
SSE cannot transmit JSON-formatted data.
The client cannot render comments into the list.
A single server cannot hold every connection, exposing coordination.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: What problem remains if the Comment Management Service directly holds every SSE connection?
optionExplanations: 写路径已经完成了持久化，这跟推送方案是否单机部署无关。
SSE 的 data 字段能传任意文本，JSON 字符串完全没问题。
渲染是前端已经解决的问题，跟推送服务器怎么部署无关。
对，单机扛不住百万级观众的常开连接，加机器之后同一直播的观众分散到多台，跨服务器协调就成了新问题。
optionExplanations_en: Persistence already happens on the write path, unrelated to whether the push layer runs on one server.
SSE's data field carries arbitrary text, so JSON payloads work fine over it.
Rendering is already solved on the client and has nothing to do with how push servers are deployed.
Right — one server can't hold millions of persistent connections, so scaling out scatters viewers of the same video across machines, creating a cross-server coordination problem.
scenario: 初版：单个 Comment Management Service 直接给一场 100 万观众的直播维持 SSE 连接。
scenario_en: First cut: one Comment Management Service holds SSE connections for a live video with a million viewers.

q: 单台现代服务器大致能维持多少并发长连接？瓶颈在哪？
options: 常见在 10 万量级，瓶颈是系统资源而非协议
最多 65,535 条，因为端口号已经用尽
大约只能维持 1,000 条并发连接
理论上没有任何上限，可以无限增长
why: 10 万级并发连接是常见量级，真正的限制是系统资源而不是协议理论值。所以支撑数百万观众必须靠加机器。
why_en: A modern server commonly handles on the order of one hundred thousand concurrent connections, limited by CPU, memory, and file descriptors rather than any theoretical cap.
options_en: On the order of 100k; the bottleneck is system resources.
At most 65,535, because ports run out.
Only about 1,000 concurrent connections.
No limit at all in theory, it can grow forever.

q_en: Roughly how many long-lived connections can one modern server hold, and what is the bottleneck?
scenario_en: You plan to support millions of viewers with long-lived SSE connections, and the interviewer asks what one server can actually handle.
optionExplanations: 对，粗略按每连接占 fd、缓冲区和调度开销估；到十万量级后通常先碰系统资源。
65,535 是端口号空间，不是单机能维持的连接数上限，这里把两个概念搞混了。
1,000 这个量级远低于现代服务器实际能撑住的连接数，明显低估了。
连接数不可能无限增长，服务器的内存和文件描述符总会先见底。
optionExplanations_en: Right — count file descriptors, buffers, and scheduling cost per connection; around the 100k order, system resources usually bite first.
65,535 is the port number space, not a cap on how many connections one server can hold — that conflates two different concepts.
1,000 is far below what a modern server can actually sustain, a clear underestimate.
Connections can't grow forever; memory and file descriptors will always run out first.

scenario: SSE/WebSocket 这类长连接通常都连到同一个服务端监听端口，例如 server_ip:443；面试官追问 65,535 这个数字是不是单机连接上限。
q: 「单服务器最多 65,535 条连接」这个流行说法错在哪？
options: 真实上限其实是 32,768 条，不是 65,535
这只是端口号范围，不是连接数上限
这个数字是浏览器端限制，与服务器无关
这个限制只对 SSE 这一个协议生效
why: 65,535 是端口号空间，不是单机连接上限。TCP 连接由四元组区分；同一个 server:443 可服务大量不同客户端，真实瓶颈是 fd、内存、CPU、带宽。
why_en: 65,535 is the port number space, not a server connection cap. TCP connections are identified by a four-tuple, so one server port can serve many clients; real limits are fd, memory, CPU, and bandwidth.
options_en: The real cap is actually 32,768, not 65,535.
It's just the port number range, not a connection cap.
This number is a browser-side limit unrelated to servers.
This limit applies only to the SSE protocol.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一条 TCP 连接的四个值：源 IP、源端口、目标 IP、目标端口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The four-tuple identifies one TCP connection: source IP, source port, destination IP, and destination port.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发起连接时临时使用的源端口；它可能限制单个客户端到同一目标的连接数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral port is a temporary client source port; it can limit connections from one client to the same destination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统为打开的文件或 socket 分配的句柄；大量连接会消耗它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A file descriptor is an OS handle for an open file or socket; many connections consume many descriptors.

q_en: What is wrong with saying one server can only hold 65,535 connections?
scenario_en: SSE or WebSocket clients usually connect to one listening endpoint such as server_ip:443; the interviewer asks whether 65,535 is the single-server connection limit.
optionExplanations: 换一个数字仍然没解决问题，32,768 同样不是单机连接总数的上限。
对，端口只是 16 位编号；连接真正由源/目的 IP 与端口组合区分，上限看机器资源。
浏览器确实有每域连接数限制，但那是另一层约束，不是 65,535 这个数字的来源。
SSE、WebSocket、普通 HTTP 长连接都要占用连接资源，这个误解不只针对某一个协议。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping in a different number doesn't fix it — 32,768 still isn't the real cap on total server connections.
Right — the port is just a 16-bit number; connections are distinguished by the source and destination IP-port tuple, and the cap is resource-based.
Browsers do cap per-domain connections, but that's a separate constraint, not where the 65,535 number comes from.
SSE, WebSocket, and plain long-lived HTTP all consume connection resources, so this isn't a protocol-specific limit.

q: 横向扩展推送服务器后，出现的核心协调难题是什么？
options: 写入压力变大，数据库必须跟着一起分片
同视频观众分散在不同机器，评论送不到全部人
负载均衡器本身开始变成单点故障
SSE 协议本身不支持多台服务器同时部署
why: 观众被负载均衡到不同机器后，收到新评论的那台服务器只认识自己本机的连接。必须设计一套机制，让评论无论落到哪台都能到达所有观众。
why_en: After horizontal scaling, viewers of the same video sit on different servers, so the server receiving a comment cannot reach viewers connected elsewhere.

SSE itself does not support multi-server deployment.

q_en: After horizontally scaling push servers, what coordination problem appears?
optionExplanations: 分片压力出现在写路径，跟推送层横向扩展后暴露的问题不是一回事。
对，观众被分散到不同机器后，收到评论的那台服务器只认识本机连接，必须有机制让评论到达全部观众。

Right — once viewers are spread across machines, the server that receives a comment only knows its own local connections, so something must fan it out to all of them.
Load balancers are typically deployed with redundancy, so that isn't the core problem this exposes.
SSE is just an application-layer protocol and has no conflict with running on multiple servers.

scenario: 发评论的写流量远小于收评论推送的读流量，两侧需要独立扩缩容。
q: 架构上第一步该怎么拆？
options: 读写继续放同一组服务器，整体一起扩容
把推送逻辑塞进数据库触发器里执行
让客户端之间直接 P2P 转发评论
拆出独立的推送服务器层，写入路径不变
why: 读写流量差着数量级，绑在一起就得按读的峰值给写侧买单。拆出实时推送层后，两侧各自按需扩缩。
why_en: Separating dedicated realtime messaging servers from the write path lets the read-heavy push traffic scale independently of the much smaller write traffic.
whenOtherWins: 规模小或读写大致均衡时，单一服务同时承担读写更简单，没必要提前拆分。

options_en: Keep read and write on the same server pool and scale together.
Put the push logic inside a database trigger.
Have clients forward comments to each other peer-to-peer.
Split off a dedicated push server layer, keep the write path unchanged.
tradeoff: 读写分层独立扩缩 vs 单一服务简单但要为读买单
q_en: What is the first architectural split we should make?
scenario_en: Comment writes are far smaller than comment-push reads, so the two sides need to scale independently.
optionExplanations: 规模小或读写量级接近时，一个服务同时扛读写确实更简单，但这里读写差着数量级，绑在一起就得为读的峰值给写侧买单。
数据库触发器不是为大规模消息扇出设计的，用它驱动推送很快就会撑不住。
客户端之间直接转发没有服务端兜底送达和一致体验，评论会变得不可控。
对，拆出独立的推送服务器层后，读写各自按自己的负载扩缩，写入路径完全不受读侧压力影响。
optionExplanations_en: When scale is small or reads and writes are close in volume, one service handling both is genuinely simpler, but here they differ by orders of magnitude, so bundling them makes the write side pay for read-side peaks.
Database triggers weren't built for large-scale fan-out, so driving push through them buckles quickly under load.
Direct client-to-client forwarding has no server-side delivery guarantee, so comments become uncontrollable.
Right — splitting off a dedicated push server layer lets reads and writes scale independently, so the write path stays untouched by read-side load.

q: Realtime Messaging Server 在本机内存里维护这张映射表，用途是？
options: 把评论内容持久化写入磁盘存储
记录本机每个直播对应哪些 SSE 连接
把本机负载情况上报给负载均衡器
缓存每个视频的历史评论，供断线用户重连后重放
why: 客户端建连时告知自己看的 liveVideoId，服务器把连接挂到对应视频名下。之后该视频的新评论一到，直接遍历这份列表推送。
why_en: Each realtime server keeps an in-memory map from live video id to its local SSE connections so it can push an incoming comment to the right viewers.
options_en: Persist comment content to disk storage.
Track which local SSE connections belong to which video.
Report local load back to the load balancer.
Cache each video's historical comments for disconnected users to replay.
q_en: Why does a Realtime Messaging Server keep this in-memory mapping?
optionExplanations: 持久化写入磁盘是数据库的职责，不是这张内存表要解决的问题。
对，连接建立时把 socket 放进对应直播的本地列表；收到新评论后查这张表推给当前观众。
负载权重上报是另一套机制，跟这张按视频分组连接的映射表无关。
这张表不是历史缓存，它只记录当前活跃连接，不负责重放旧评论。
optionExplanations_en: Persisting to disk is the database's job, not what this in-memory table exists for.
Right — on connect, the server puts the socket into the local list for that live video, then uses that list to fan out each new comment.
Reporting load weight to the balancer is a separate mechanism, unrelated to this per-video connection map.
This table isn't a history cache — it only tracks currently active connections, not replay of old comments.
scenario: 一台 Realtime Messaging Server 上挂着 5 万条 SSE 连接，分属上千场不同直播。
scenario_en: A single realtime messaging server holds fifty thousand SSE connections spread over a thousand different live videos.

scenario: 多台推送服务器都需要在「新评论创建」的瞬间得到通知，然后各自推给本机相关观众。
q: 最常用的通知机制是？
options: 每台推送服务器高频轮询数据库查新评论
服务器之间两两建立 TCP 网格互相转发
pub/sub：评论服务发布，推送服务器订阅
把评论写入共享文件，由各服务器 tail 读取
why: 发布/订阅是跨服务器扇出的标准解：写路径只管发布一次，订阅方各自消费并推给本机观众，彼此解耦。
why_en: Pub/sub is the standard answer: the comment service publishes each new comment to a channel that every realtime server subscribes to.
whenOtherWins: 想要集中式路由逻辑、能按负载做智能路由时，Dispatcher 服务直接点对点转发是另一个成立的选项。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    CMS["评论服务"] -->|PUBLISH| CH["pub/sub 频道"]
    CH -->|SUBSCRIBE| R1["推送服务器 1"]
    CH -->|SUBSCRIBE| R2["推送服务器 2"]
    R1 --> V1["本机观众 SSE"]
    R2 --> V2["本机观众 SSE"]
tradeoff: 解耦的发布/订阅 vs 集中式 Dispatcher 转发
options_en: Each push server polls the database frequently for new comments.
Servers form a pairwise TCP mesh to forward to each other.
Pub/sub: the comment service publishes, push servers subscribe.
Write comments to a shared file that each server tails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布/订阅消息模式：发布者广播消息，订阅者各自接收
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/sub is a messaging pattern where publishers broadcast messages that subscribers receive.

q_en: What notification mechanism is most commonly used here?
scenario_en: Several push servers must learn about a new comment as soon as it is created, then push it to their own relevant viewers.
optionExplanations: 轮询数据库延迟高，还有大量空查，跟推送要求的实时性正好相反。
两两互连的网格连接数会随服务器数量的平方增长，规模一大就没法维护。
对，评论服务只需发布一次，各推送服务器订阅后各自消费再推给本机观众，写路径和推送方彼此解耦；若还想要集中路由和负载感知规则，Dispatcher 服务是另一个成立的方向。
共享文件当消息总线既不可靠也难扩展，tail 读取本身就有延迟和一致性问题。
optionExplanations_en: Polling the database is high-latency and mostly comes back empty, the opposite of what push needs.
A pairwise mesh's connection count grows with the square of server count, becoming unmanageable at scale.

Right — the comment service publishes once, each push server subscribes and consumes independently, decoupling writers from pushers; if you also want centralized routing or load-aware rules, a dispatcher service is the other valid direction.
A shared file as a message bus is neither reliable nor scalable, and tailing it introduces its own latency and consistency issues.

q: 「所有推送服务器订阅同一个频道」的朴素 pub/sub 在规模上为什么不行？
options: pub/sub 机制本身不保证送达，一定会丢消息
单一频道会把不同视频的评论顺序打乱
订阅方越多，端到端延迟必然超过 200ms
每台服务器都要消费全网评论，本机没观众也一样
why: 单一频道意味着全量广播：一台只服务视频 A 观众的机器，也要消费视频 B、C、D 的所有评论再丢弃。规模一大这份无效功耗就压垮系统。
why_en: With one global channel every server processes every comment across all videos even when none of its viewers care, wasting compute at scale.
options_en: Pub/sub itself guarantees nothing and is bound to drop messages.
A single channel scrambles the ordering of comments from different videos.
More subscribers necessarily push end-to-end latency past 200ms.
Every server has to consume the whole platform comment firehose even when none of its viewers care.
q_en: Why does one global pub/sub channel fail at scale?
optionExplanations: 丢消息不是全局广播模型的症结，跟频道数量的设计没有关系。
pub/sub 不天然打乱消息顺序，单频道的问题不在乱序上。
延迟是否超标取决于具体实现，不是订阅方越多就必然超标。
对，单一频道意味着全量广播，只服务视频 A 观众的机器也要消费并丢弃视频 B、C、D 的评论，规模一大就压垮系统。
optionExplanations_en: Losing messages isn't the flaw in global broadcast — it's unrelated to channel design.
Pub/sub doesn't inherently scramble order, so that isn't what breaks a single channel.
Whether latency crosses 200ms depends on the implementation, not automatically on subscriber count.
Right — one global channel means full broadcast: a server serving only video A's viewers still has to consume and discard every comment from B, C, D, which collapses at scale.
scenario: 全平台同时有上万场直播、每秒几十万条评论，而每台推送服务器只服务其中几十场。
scenario_en: The platform runs tens of thousands of live videos and hundreds of thousands of comments per second, but each push server serves only dozens of them.

q: 为什么用 hash(liveVideoId) % N 分频道，而不是每个直播一个频道？
options: 取模哈希还能保证消息按发布顺序送达每个观众
取模把频道数压到固定上限，避免开无数频道
一个视频一个频道会导致哈希计算冲突
N 个频道能让底层传输延迟天然更低
why: 频道本身有成本，按视频开频道数量失控。哈希取模把任意多的视频装进固定 N 个频道，服务器只订阅自己观众涉及的那几个。
why_en: Hashing video ids into a fixed number of channels bounds the channel count, since one channel per video would be resource-prohibitive for systems like Kafka.
options_en: Modulo hashing also guarantees in-order delivery to every viewer.
Hashing bounds the channel count instead of opening unlimited channels.
One channel per video would cause hash collisions.
N channels inherently lower the underlying transport latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对哈希值取模，把任意多个 key 映射进固定数量的桶
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hashing a key modulo N maps an unbounded number of keys into a fixed number of buckets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

q_en: Why shard channels with hash(liveVideoId) % N instead of one channel per live video?
optionExplanations: 取模哈希不保证消息顺序，这不是它要解决的问题。
对，按视频一对一开频道数量会失控，哈希取模把任意多视频装进固定 N 个桶，服务器只订阅涉及自己观众的那几个。
一个视频一个频道不存在哈希冲突的说法，频道数和碰撞是两回事。
频道数量和底层传输延迟没有直接关系，这是无关的联想。
optionExplanations_en: Modulo hashing doesn't guarantee ordering; that's not the problem it's solving.
Right — one channel per video would let the count spiral, so hashing packs an unbounded number of videos into a fixed N buckets, and each server only subscribes to the few touching its own viewers.
One channel per video wouldn't cause hash collisions — channel count and collisions are unrelated concepts here.
Channel count has no direct bearing on underlying transport latency; that's an unrelated leap.
scenario: 同时进行的直播从几千涨到几十万，而 Redis 频道本身有内存与订阅开销，不能无限开。
scenario_en: Concurrent live videos grow from thousands to hundreds of thousands, and Redis channels cost memory and subscriptions, so we cannot open them without limit.

q: 分好频道之后，round-robin 负载均衡为什么会把效率优化毁掉？
options: 轮询把各视频观众混在一台机上，订阅集合又膨胀
round-robin 分配的流量本身就不均匀
round-robin 会让频道的哈希计算失效
负载均衡器会因此变成写入瓶颈
why: 频道分区的收益取决于「一台服务器只需要少数频道」；而 round-robin 把观众随机撒开，每台机器的观众什么都看，订阅集合又膨胀回去。解法是智能路由。
why_en: Round-robin scatters viewers of many different videos onto each server, forcing it to subscribe to many channels and reintroducing the inefficiency.
options_en: Round-robin mixes viewers of many videos onto each server, so the subscription set balloons again.
Round-robin distributes traffic unevenly in the first place.
Round-robin breaks the channel hash calculation.
The load balancer turns into a write bottleneck.
q_en: Why does round-robin load balancing ruin the channel optimization?
optionExplanations: 对，轮询把观众随机撒到各台机器，每台都混着各种视频的观众，订阅集合又膨胀回全量。
流量分配是否均匀是另一个话题，不是这里效率被毁掉的原因。
round-robin 只影响观众落在哪台机器，跟频道哈希计算没有关系。
round-robin 影响的是读路径的连接分配，不会让负载均衡器变成写入瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Right — round-robin scatters viewers randomly across machines, so each one ends up with a mix of every video's viewers and the subscription set balloons back out.
Whether traffic lands evenly is a separate question from what breaks the channel optimization here.
Round-robin only decides which machine a viewer lands on; it has nothing to do with the channel hash itself.
Round-robin affects read-path connection placement, not the load balancer's write-side throughput.
scenario: 已按 hash(liveVideoId) % 1000 分好频道，观众连接仍由负载均衡 round-robin 分配。
scenario_en: Channels are already sharded by hash(liveVideoId) % 1000, but viewer connections are still handed out round-robin by the load balancer.

scenario: 希望同一直播的观众尽量落到同一台推送服务器上，让每台服务器只订阅极少数频道。
q: 路由层怎么做？
options: L4 负载均衡只按源 IP 做哈希，四层转发看不到内容
客户端连接失败后随机换一台机器重试
L7 负载均衡按 liveVideoId 做一致性哈希
DNS 轮询把域名解析到不同的服务器 IP
why: 只有 L7 才能看见 liveVideoId 这类应用层信息；按它做一致性哈希，同一视频的观众自然聚到同一台机器，订阅集合就收敛了。
why_en: A layer-7 load balancer can consistent-hash on the video id in the request, keeping viewers of the same video together on the same server.
whenOtherWins: 把 liveVideoId→server 的动态映射放进 Zookeeper 这类协调服务更灵活（可自定义迁移），代价是更高的运维复杂度。
options_en: Layer-4 load balancing hashes only on source IP and forwards without seeing content.
The client retries on a random server after a failed connection.
Layer-7 load balancing that consistent-hashes on liveVideoId.
DNS round-robin resolving the domain to different server IPs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能读取应用层信息（如请求路径）来路由流量的负载均衡器
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-7 load balancer routes traffic using application-level data such as the request path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让同一个 key 稳定映射到同一节点、扩缩容影响小的哈希方法
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps the same key to the same node stably, minimizing disruption when nodes change.

q_en: How should the routing layer work?
scenario_en: We want viewers of the same live video to land on the same push server when possible, so each server subscribes to only a few channels.
optionExplanations: L4 只能按 IP/端口等网络信息转发，无法按正在观看的直播来聚合观众。
随机重试完全不保证同一视频的观众会聚到同一台机器上。
对，只有 L7 才能读懂请求内容按 liveVideoId 做一致性哈希，让同一视频的观众自然聚合；想要更灵活的自定义迁移，代价是把映射放进 Zookeeper 这类协调服务、运维更复杂。
DNS 解析粒度太粗，做不到按单个视频这个维度路由。
optionExplanations_en: L4 can route by network fields like IP and port, but it cannot group viewers by the live video they are watching.
Random retries give no guarantee that viewers of the same video converge on one machine.

Right — only layer-7 can read the request content to consistent-hash on liveVideoId, naturally clustering viewers of the same video; wanting custom migration flexibility instead means pushing the mapping into something like Zookeeper at the cost of more ops complexity.
DNS resolution is too coarse-grained to route by an individual video.

q: 观众协同定位（co-location）方案的主要持续性挑战是？
options: 一致性哈希本身的计算开销太大
NGINX 这类代理不支持处理流式响应
观众会因此完全无法切换到别的直播
观众和服务器都在变化，订阅要持续同步
why: 难点不在建立映射而在维护映射：观众来去、机器增减，负载均衡与 pub/sub 订阅两边的状态要持续对齐。
why_en: The ongoing challenge is coordination: subscriptions must track each server's changing viewer mix, and routing maps must stay in sync as servers scale.
options_en: The computational cost of consistent hashing itself is too high.
NGINX-style proxies do not support streaming responses.
Viewers become completely unable to switch to a different video.
Both viewers and servers keep changing, so subscriptions need constant sync.
q_en: What is the main ongoing challenge with viewer co-location?
optionExplanations: 哈希计算本身很轻量，开销不是持续维护阶段的真正瓶颈。
NGINX 这类代理完全支持流式响应，这个说法与事实相反。
切换到别的直播不受这套路由方案的影响，观众依然能自由换台。
对，关系表会随观众迁移和机器伸缩不停变化；路由层与订阅层必须一起更新。
optionExplanations_en: Hashing itself is computationally light, so that overhead isn't the real bottleneck during ongoing operation.
NGINX-style proxies fully support streaming responses; this claim is the opposite of reality.
Switching to a different stream is unaffected by this routing scheme — viewers can still freely change channels.
Right — the mapping keeps changing as viewers move and servers scale, so routing and subscriptions must be updated together.
scenario: 用一致性哈希把同一场直播的观众固定到少数几台机器，但观众随时进出、机器随时扩缩容。
scenario_en: Consistent hashing pins one video viewers onto a few machines, yet viewers come and go and the fleet scales up and down constantly.

scenario: 不想管理 pub/sub 订阅关系，希望把路由逻辑集中在一处，还想以后加「按服务器负载路由」这类高级规则。
q: 哪种模型正中需求？
options: Dispatcher：按映射转发给目标服务器
把每条新评论无差别广播给系统里所有推送服务器
让客户端定期自己主动拉取新评论
用数据库触发器来驱动评论推送逻辑
why: Dispatcher 把 pub/sub 模型整个反转：服务器不再订阅，由中心组件查映射后点对点投递。路由逻辑集中、好推理，加负载感知等规则也不用改推送服务器。
why_en: A dispatcher service inverts pub/sub by keeping a live map of which servers own which videos and forwarding each comment directly, centralizing the routing logic.
whenOtherWins: pub/sub 通常更简单、边角情况更少，是面试里作者优先推荐的方案。
tradeoff: 集中式 Dispatcher 路由 vs 去中心化 pub/sub 订阅
options_en: Dispatcher: keeps one map, forwards straight to the right server.
Broadcast every new comment indiscriminately to all push servers.
Have clients periodically pull new comments themselves.
Use a database trigger to drive the push logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护路由映射、把消息直接转发到目标服务器的中心组件
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dispatcher is a central component that keeps a routing map and forwards messages directly to servers.

q_en: Which model best matches these requirements?
scenario_en: You want to avoid managing pub/sub subscriptions, centralize routing logic, and later add rules such as routing by server load.
optionExplanations: 对，把转发决策收拢到一个专门组件维护一份映射表，扩展负载感知等新路由规则时只改这一处，不必逐台改推送服务器；不过 pub/sub 通常更简单、边角情况更少，更常被优先推荐。
全量广播给所有服务器正是想避免的浪费，跟集中路由的目标相反。
客户端定期拉取会退化回轮询，满足不了实时推送的需求。
数据库触发器难以承载持续变化的路由逻辑，不是可扩展的推送机制。
optionExplanations_en: Right — routing decisions move into one dedicated component holding a single map, so adding rules like load-aware routing later only touches that one place instead of every push server; pub/sub is usually simpler with fewer edge cases though, so it's the more commonly favored default.
Broadcasting to every server is exactly the waste you're trying to avoid, the opposite of centralized routing.
Having clients pull periodically degrades back into polling, which can't meet the real-time requirement.
A database trigger can't carry constantly-changing routing logic; it isn't a scalable push mechanism.

q: Dispatcher 自己如何避免成为单点？
options: 只能部署单实例，靠快速重启来兜底
多实例共享同一份协调存储中的映射
每个实例各自维护独立映射、互不通信
把映射直接硬编码写进配置文件里
why: Dispatcher 无状态化：映射的权威副本放在 Zookeeper/etcd 里，多实例共享同一份真相，挂一个不影响整体。
why_en: Multiple dispatcher instances run behind a load balancer and all consult the same coordination store like Zookeeper or etcd for consistency.
options_en: Deploy only a single instance and rely on fast restarts.
Multiple instances share one map from a coordination store.
Each instance keeps its own independent map with no sync.
Hard-code the mapping directly into a config file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式协调服务，用来保存和同步共享状态或映射
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zookeeper or etcd is a distributed coordination service for storing and syncing shared state.

q_en: How does the Dispatcher avoid becoming a single point of failure?
optionExplanations: 单实例本身就是单点故障，快速重启解决不了这个结构性问题。
对，把权威映射外置到协调存储，路由节点只做计算和缓存；任一实例挂掉可由其他实例接手。
各实例互不通信会导致映射不一致，路由结果因实例而异。
映射随观众和服务器持续变化，硬编码进静态配置文件跟不上变化。
optionExplanations_en: A single instance is itself the single point of failure; fast restarts don't fix that structural problem.
Right — store the authoritative mapping in coordination storage, let dispatchers compute and cache, and any instance can fail over.
Instances that never sync end up with inconsistent maps, so routing results differ by which instance you hit.
The mapping keeps changing as viewers and servers change, so hard-coding it into static config can't keep up.
scenario: Dispatcher 持有「哪台推送服务器负责哪场直播」的映射，所有评论都要经它转发。
scenario_en: The dispatcher holds the map of which push server owns which live video, and every comment is routed through it.

q: Dispatcher 模型最大的运行期难点是？
options: 转发路径的延迟必然比 pub/sub 更高
Dispatcher 模型无法水平扩展
观众洪流下映射秒级变动，需高频刷新加协同失效
Dispatcher 与 SSE 长连接不兼容
why: 映射的新鲜度就是 Dispatcher 的命门：viral 场景下服务器负责关系秒级变动，任何一份陈旧缓存都会把评论投错地方。
why_en: The dispatcher's hard part is keeping its routing map accurate during rapid change, requiring frequent refreshes and coordinated cache invalidation across instances.
options_en: The forwarding path necessarily has higher latency than pub/sub.
The dispatcher model cannot scale horizontally.
Under viewer churn the map shifts by the second, needing frequent refresh plus coordinated invalidation.
The dispatcher is incompatible with SSE long connections.
q_en: What is the hardest runtime problem in the Dispatcher model?
optionExplanations: 转发延迟高低取决于具体实现，不是 Dispatcher 模型必然的代价。
多实例部署本身就是为了水平扩展，这个说法与实际设计相反。
对，观众换台会让归属关系按秒变化，Dispatcher 得靠心跳或 TTL 主动踢掉过期路由，而不是等转发失败才发现服务器已经不对。
Dispatcher 只负责路由决策，跟 SSE 这类连接协议本身互不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Whether forwarding latency is higher depends on the implementation, not an inherent cost of the dispatcher model.
Running multiple instances is precisely how it scales horizontally, the opposite of this claim.

Right — as viewers hop between videos, ownership shifts by the second, so the dispatcher needs heartbeats or a TTL to actively evict stale entries instead of discovering a bad route only after a forward fails.
The dispatcher only handles routing decisions and has no conflict with a connection protocol like SSE.
scenario: 一场直播突然爆红，观众从 1 万涨到 100 万，推送服务器不停扩容、负责关系秒级变动。
scenario_en: A video goes viral from ten thousand to a million viewers, push servers keep scaling, and ownership changes by the second.

q: 在这个场景下，为什么 Redis pub/sub（发布订阅广播）比 Kafka 更顺手？
options: Kafka 的延迟天生比 Redis pub/sub 更低
Redis 能持久化消息而 Kafka 反而不能
Kafka 能支持的订阅方数量比 Redis 更少
Kafka 应付动态订阅吃力，Redis 更灵活
why: 这里的订阅关系随观众换台不断变动，正是 Kafka 的短板、Redis pub/sub 的长处。维度是「动态订阅的灵活性」，不是吞吐。
why_en: Kafka is scalable and fault-tolerant but struggles with dynamic subscription churn, while Redis pub/sub offers low latency and handles viewers switching videos gracefully.
options_en: Kafka inherently has lower latency than Redis pub/sub.
Redis persists messages while Kafka cannot.
Kafka supports fewer subscribers than Redis.
Kafka struggles with dynamic subscriptions; Redis handles them better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

tradeoff: 动态订阅的灵活性 vs 吞吐与持久化保证
scenario: 推送服务器需要感知观众正在观看哪些直播，而观众会频繁在不同直播间切换，订阅关系持续变动。
q_en: Why is Redis pub/sub a better fit than Kafka in this scenario?
scenario_en: Push servers need to track which live videos their viewers are watching, and viewers switch between live rooms frequently.
optionExplanations: 延迟对比与事实相反：Redis pub/sub 通常比 Kafka 更低延迟，不是 Kafka 更快。
持久化能力的说法正好反了：Kafka 才是能持久化事件日志的一方，Redis pub/sub 是即发即弃。
订阅方数量不是这里的决定因素，两者都能支撑大量订阅者。
对，观众换台会频繁增删订阅；轻量频道订阅更合适，若要持久日志和重放再换 Kafka。
optionExplanations_en: The latency comparison is backwards: Redis pub/sub is typically lower latency than Kafka, not the other way around.
The durability claim is reversed too — Kafka is the one built for a durable event log, while Redis pub/sub is fire-and-forget.
Subscriber count isn't the deciding factor here; both can support large numbers of subscribers.
Right — channel membership changes constantly as viewers switch streams; lightweight subscriptions fit, while durable replay points back to Kafka.

q: Redis pub/sub 是 fire-and-forget（不保证送达），为什么在这里不致命？
options: 评论已持久化在库里，漏掉的靠重连追赶从库或缓存补回
Redis pub/sub 其实内置了消息重试，不会丢
因为还有 Kafka 在后面做兜底队列
观众永远不会感知到任何消息丢失
why: pub/sub 在这里只是「热路径通知」，不是唯一事实来源。数据库兜底 + 追赶机制，让偶发丢消息只是短暂延迟而非数据丢失。
why_en: Fire-and-forget is acceptable because comments are already persisted in the database and the catch-up mechanism recovers anything missed during a brief disconnect.
options_en: Comments are already persisted, so anything missed is refetched from storage or cache by the reconnect catch-up.
Redis pub/sub actually retries internally and never loses messages.
Because Kafka sits behind it as a backup queue.
Viewers will never notice any message loss at all.
q_en: Why is Redis pub/sub being fire-and-forget not fatal here?
optionExplanations: 对，数据库才是唯一事实来源，掉线漏掉的评论靠断线追赶机制从库或缓存补回，pub/sub 只是热路径通知。
Redis pub/sub 本身就是 fire-and-forget，没有内置消息重试。
本设计没有引入 Kafka 做兜底，这里只用了 Redis pub/sub。
短暂断线仍可能让观众错过一两条评论，说完全不会感知太乐观。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the database is the true source of record, so anything missed on a disconnect gets recovered by the catch-up mechanism from storage or cache; pub/sub is only the hot-path notification.
Redis pub/sub is fire-and-forget by design; it has no built-in message retry.
This design never introduced Kafka as a backup — only Redis pub/sub is used here.
A brief disconnect can still cost a viewer a comment or two, so claiming zero perceived loss is overly optimistic.
scenario: 评论先持久化进 DynamoDB 再经 Redis pub/sub 通知推送机；客户端重连时会走追赶补课。
scenario_en: Comments are persisted to DynamoDB first and only then announced over Redis pub/sub, and clients run a catch-up fetch on reconnect.

scenario: 评论服务要把新评论广播出去，推送服务器只想收到与本机观众相关的那部分分片频道的消息。
q: 这组 Redis 命令实现的是什么？
codeSample:
# 推送服务器：按本机观众需要订阅分片频道
SUBSCRIBE comments:shard:7

# 评论服务：hash("lv_42") % 100 = 7，发布到对应分片
PUBLISH comments:shard:7 '{"liveVideoId":"lv_42","commentId":"c_9","message":"nice!"}'
options: 把评论持久化写入数据库存储
分片频道上的发布/订阅广播机制
带延迟投递功能的持久化消息队列
基于 SETNX 命令实现的分布式锁
why: SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH 是 Redis 的 pub/sub 原语；按 hash 分片的频道名让每台服务器只消费自己需要的流量，而不是全网广播。
why_en: These Redis commands implement sharded pub/sub, where only servers subscribed to that hash shard receive the published comment.
whenOtherWins: 需要可回放的持久日志、消费组和严格的吞吐保证时，应该用 Kafka topic 而不是 Redis 频道。
options_en: Persisting the comment write to the database.
A publish/subscribe broadcast on a sharded channel.
A durable message queue with delayed delivery.
A distributed lock built on the SETNX command.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子命令：key 不存在时才写入，常用于实现锁
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SETNX is a Redis command that sets a key only if it is absent, often used to build locks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

q_en: What do these Redis commands implement?
scenario_en: The comment service needs to broadcast new comments, while push servers only want messages from the shard channels relevant to their local viewers.
optionExplanations: 这组命令不落磁盘；评论持久化应该在数据库写路径完成。
对，按 hash 分片的频道名让服务器只订阅自己需要的那部分流量，是分片广播；要可回放的持久日志和消费组保证时才该换 Kafka。
Redis pub/sub 没有内置的延迟投递能力，这两个命令做不到定时发送。
加锁关注互斥和租约，这里是在频道上广播消息，语义完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: These commands do not write to disk; durable comment storage belongs on the database write path.

Right — the hash-sharded channel name means each server only subscribes to the slice of traffic it needs, i.e. sharded broadcast; switch to Kafka once you need a durable, replayable log with consumer groups.
Redis pub/sub has no built-in delayed delivery; these two commands can't schedule a future send.
Locking is about mutual exclusion and leases; this is channel broadcast, a completely different operation.

scenario: 面试里要在「pub/sub + 观众协同定位」与「Dispatcher 服务」之间选一个作为主推的协调方案。
q: 作者建议优先押哪个？
options: 选 Dispatcher，因为听起来更高级一些
两个方案都完整展开讲，不做取舍
都不选，直接跳到讲 CDN 方案
pub/sub 更简单、边角情况更少，优先押它
why: 两个方案都成立，但 pub/sub 的实现路径更平、坑更少，面试时更容易讲稳。Dispatcher 留作对比加分项。
why_en: Both approaches solve coordination, but pub/sub is typically simpler with fewer corner cases, making it the one to reach for in an interview.
whenOtherWins: 需要集中式路由逻辑、负载感知路由等高级规则时，Dispatcher 的可控性更强。
options_en: Pick dispatcher because it sounds more advanced.
Fully present both without choosing between them.
Skip both and jump straight to the CDN approach.
Pub/sub is simpler with fewer edge cases, so lead with it.
q_en: Which coordination approach should you lead with?
scenario_en: In the interview, you need to choose between pub/sub plus viewer co-location and a Dispatcher service as the primary coordination plan.
optionExplanations: 选型理由应该是工程权衡，不是「听起来高级」这种印象分。
面试时间有限，两个方案都完整展开会显得没有聚焦和判断力。
CDN 方案是另一个独立话题，跳过协调问题本身解决不了跨服务器送达。
对，pub/sub 实现路径更平、边角情况更少，更容易讲稳；需要集中式路由逻辑或负载感知规则时，Dispatcher 的可控性更强，可以留作对比加分项。
optionExplanations_en: The reason to choose should be engineering trade-offs, not that one option merely sounds more advanced.
Interview time is limited; fully presenting both without ever choosing reads as unfocused and indecisive.
The CDN approach is a separate topic; skipping past coordination doesn't actually solve cross-server delivery.

Right — pub/sub has a flatter path with fewer corner cases and is easier to defend under time pressure; when you need centralized routing or load-aware rules, the dispatcher's extra control is worth raising as a bonus comparison.

q: 超级直播每秒 5,000 条评论（平均 4 词一条）意味着什么？
options: 相当于不到 30 秒读完一整本《战争与和平》
数据库会因此先于推送层崩溃宕机
延迟会因此自动涨到 1 秒以上
每条评论平均能在屏幕上停留约 1 秒，足够看清读完
why: 这组数字证明了一个质变：评论流快到超出人类阅读能力时，「每条必达、低延迟」的传统目标失去了意义。
why_en: At five thousand comments per second each message survives about four milliseconds on screen, far beyond human reading speed.
options_en: Equivalent to reading all of War and Peace in under 30 seconds.
The database would crash before the push layer does.
Latency automatically rises above 1 second as a result.
Each comment stays on screen about 1 second on average, long enough to read.
scenario: 世界杯决赛级别的超级直播，评论以每秒 5,000 条的速度涌入，面试官问这组数字说明了什么。
q_en: What does 5,000 comments per second, averaging four words each, imply?
scenario_en: For a World Cup final level live stream, comments arrive at 5,000 per second, and the interviewer asks what that number tells you.
optionExplanations: 对，5,000 条/秒 × 4 词约等于每秒 20,000 词；人眼已无法逐条消费，目标要改成现场感。
先崩溃的说法缺乏依据，这道题的重点是需求本身的质变，不是哪层先扛不住。
延迟涨到多少取决于具体实现，不是数字本身自动导致的结果。
每条评论实际停留的时间远不到 1 秒，这个估算明显偏乐观。
optionExplanations_en: Right — 5,000 comments per second times four words is about 20,000 words per second; people cannot read that, so the target becomes ambience.
Claiming the database crashes first has no basis; the point here is that requirements themselves change, not which layer fails.
How much latency rises depends on the implementation, not something the raw number forces automatically.
Each comment actually survives on screen far less than a second — this estimate is overly optimistic.

q: 评论快到没人能逐条阅读时，系统的设计目标发生了什么变化？
options: 延迟要求反而变得比之前更严格了
必须给每条评论增加送达确认机制
低延迟逐条送达退位，用户要的是氛围
需要把公开评论功能改成私信功能
why: 这是本题最重要的洞察：极端规模下需求本身变了。用户要的是感受到人群的能量，这为采样和 CDN 快照两个方案打开了大门。
why_en: At mega-scale the requirements themselves change: users experience a collective vibe rather than reading individual comments, so strict per-message delivery stops mattering.
options_en: Latency requirements actually get stricter than before.
Every comment now needs a delivery confirmation mechanism.
Reliable per-message delivery gives way to a collective vibe.
Public comments need to be turned into private messages.
q_en: How does the design goal change when comments arrive too fast to read one by one?
optionExplanations: 延迟要求实际上是放宽了，不是变得更严格，这个方向说反了。
逐条确认反而违背了「氛围优先」这个洞察，是加了不必要的强保证。
对，量级过高时产品目标从逐条阅读转成感知热度，采样和快照才合理。
私信是完全不同的功能形态，跟群体评论区的体验诉求无关。
optionExplanations_en: Latency requirements actually loosen, not tighten — this points the wrong direction.
Requiring per-message confirmation actually fights the 'vibe over accuracy' insight by adding an unneeded strong guarantee.
Right — at that scale the product goal shifts from reading every line to sensing crowd energy, which makes sampling and snapshots reasonable.
Private messaging is an entirely different feature and unrelated to what a shared comment section needs to deliver.
scenario: 一场超级直播峰值每秒上万条评论，一秒钟就刷过几百条，人眼根本读不完。
scenario_en: A mega live video peaks at tens of thousands of comments per second, hundreds flying by every second, far more than anyone can read.

scenario: 单场超级直播评论如洪水，观众只需要看到「足够多」的评论来感受人群能量，不需要每条都看到。
q: 第一个减负手段是？
options: 无脑加推送服务器，硬扛全量评论
直接关闭该直播的评论功能来止损
改成每分钟把这一分钟全部评论批量投递一次
对评论流做采样：每个观众只收一小部分
why: 既然没人读得完，就没必要全量投递。采样让每个观众收到可读数量的评论，同时保留现场感。
why_en: Since nobody can read them all, sampling delivers only a subset of comments to each viewer while preserving the feeling of crowd energy.
whenOtherWins: 普通流量的直播必须逐条投递——采样只在评论量超出人类阅读能力的超级流里才合理。
options_en: Blindly add push servers and brute-force the full volume.
Just turn off comments on that live video to stop the bleeding.
Switch to delivering that minute's full batch of comments once a minute.
Sample the comment stream so each viewer receives only a subset.
tradeoff: 采样保留现场感 vs 全量投递保证不丢条
q_en: What is the first way to reduce load?
scenario_en: In a super-hot live stream, comments arrive like a flood; viewers need enough comments to feel the crowd, not every single comment.
