需求：爆款帖子头几小时读量巨大，而 DynamoDB 只有负载均匀才能高吞吐
升级：换成复制式缓存+负载均衡，任何实例都能服务任何帖子
选型：在 Post 表前加分布式缓存，长 TTL + LRU
why: 链条完整走一遍：热读需求 → 加缓存 → 缓存自己也热 → 复制式缓存摊平 → 接受少量回源。
why_en: The chain runs from a hot-read requirement, to adding a cache, to the cache itself getting hot, to replication spreading the load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 复制式缓存能装下的『不同帖子总数』比分片式少，为什么可以接受？
q_en: Why is it acceptable that a replicated cache holds fewer distinct posts than a sharded cache?
options: 因为帖子会自动压缩
因为可以无限加内存
因为旧帖子几乎根本没人会去读，不缓存它们也没什么影响
DynamoDB 兜得住这点额外 miss
options_en: Because posts get automatically compressed.
Because memory can be added without limit.
Because almost nobody ever reads old posts anyway, so not caching them makes no real difference.
Because the DynamoDB backend can absorb some read-throughput variability, and the small extra misses fall well within that.
why: 复制牺牲了有效容量，换来热 key 吞吐；落库的 miss 变多一点没关系，DynamoDB 不是不能读，只是不能被单点打爆。
why_en: Replication trades away effective capacity for hot-key throughput, and the extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed.
optionExplanations: 帖子并不会自动压缩，这是编出来的机制。
内存可以加但成本会跟着线性上涨，不是『无限』就没代价。
『旧帖子根本没人读』说得太绝对，只是读得少，不是完全没有。
对：复制牺牲的是有效容量，多出来的 miss 落回 DynamoDB 完全兜得住，不是被单点打爆。
optionExplanations_en: Posts don't actually get auto-compressed — that's a fabricated mechanism.
Memory can be added, but cost keeps scaling linearly with it; 'unlimited' doesn't mean free.
'Nobody reads old posts' overstates it — they're read less often, not never.
Correct: replication trades away effective capacity, and the resulting extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed, not a single-point overload.
scenario: 复制缓存把同一批热帖复制到每个节点，能缓存的不同帖子数因此变少；后端是 DynamoDB。
scenario_en: A replicated cache copies the same hot posts onto every node, so it holds fewer distinct posts, and DynamoDB sits behind it.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 45 分钟面试，你刚画完 naive feed（读时现查关注列表再逐个拉帖），自己清楚它扛不住大扇出，可分页、存储等需求都还没铺。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute interview you've just drawn the naive feed (query the follow list at read time, then pull each user's posts), you know it won't survive large fan-out, and pagination and storage are still unbuilt.
q: 面对这个明显不 scale 的 naive 方案，此刻最该怎么处理？
q_en: Facing this obviously non-scaling naive design, what's the right move right now?
options: 口头声明『我知道这版不 scale，先铺完再单独解决扩展』，然后继续铺其余需求
默默擦掉 naive 方案，直接重画一个能 scale 的最终设计，免得被看出方案不成熟
当场为方案不成熟道歉，坦白自己一时只能想到这么多
立刻停下把扇出优化到位，确认这块彻底没问题再回来做别的需求
options_en: Say out loud 'I know this won't scale; I'll lay it out first and fix scaling separately,' then keep covering the rest.
Quietly erase the naive design and redraw a scalable final version so the interviewer never sees anything unpolished.
Apologize on the spot for an immature design and admit this is all you can think of for now.
Stop immediately and perfect the fan-out until it's fully solved before returning to the other requirements.
why: 主动说『我知道这不 scale』证明你已识别瓶颈，比藏起来更得分；代价是白板上暂留一个已知不完善的方案，靠后半程补回来。
why_en: Announcing 'I know this won't scale' proves you already spotted the bottleneck and scores better than hiding it, at the cost of leaving a known-incomplete design on the board to fix later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次写或读要触发的下游操作数量；关注多则读扇出大，被关注多则写扇出大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is the number of downstream operations one read or write triggers; following many people means large read fan-out, being followed by many means large write fan-out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最直白但不考虑扩展的第一版设计，用来先铺通功能、之后再单独优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A naive solution is the simplest first-pass design that ignores scale, used to make the flow work before optimizing separately.

optionExplanations: 对：显式标注已识别瓶颈，再按广度优先把其余需求铺完，时间才够。
擦掉重画会让面试官看不到你识别问题的过程，反而丢掉『发现瓶颈』这一分。
道歉传递不自信，naive 起步是标准打法，不是需要致歉的失误。
还没铺完广度就深挖单点，正是最常见的失败模式，容易时间失控。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: flag the known bottleneck out loud, then keep covering breadth first so time holds up.
Erasing and redrawing hides your problem-spotting, costing you the 'found the bottleneck' credit.
Apologizing signals low confidence; a naive start is standard practice, not a mistake to atone for.
Deep-diving one spot before breadth is done is the classic failure mode and blows the clock.

scenario: 同样 45 分钟，你刚发现 naive feed 的扇出瓶颈，很想立刻把它优化到完美；可分页、follow、存储等需求都还空着。
scenario_en: Same 45 minutes: you've just found the naive feed's fan-out bottleneck and want to perfect it immediately, but pagination, follow, and storage are all still empty.
q: 如果现在一头扎进扇出细节、不先铺完广度，最可能的失败结局是？
q_en: If you dive straight into fan-out details before covering breadth, what's the most likely failure outcome?
options: 时间被这一处深挖吃光，收尾时多个功能需求仍无任何设计，面试官看到残缺系统
越深入越好，深度分永远压过广度分，所以提前扎进去其实稳赚不亏
面试官一定会及时喊停并把你拉回来，所以无论扎多深都能被纠正、根本不用自己控节奏
没先把数据模型定死就深挖，方案会因为缺少前置依赖而根本推进不下去
options_en: The clock gets eaten by that one deep dive, and at wrap-up several requirements still have no design, so the interviewer sees a half-built system.
Deeper is always better and depth points always beat breadth points, so diving in early is a sure win.
The interviewer will always stop you in time and pull you back, so any depth self-corrects and you never need to pace yourself.
Deep-diving before nailing the data model means the plan can't move forward for lack of prerequisites.
why: 广度没铺完就深挖，时间预算被单点吃光，收尾时多个需求还空着——而 mid/senior 的评分底线正是『完整且满足需求的高层设计』。
why_en: Deep-diving before breadth is done drains the time budget on one spot and leaves requirements empty at wrap-up, yet the passing bar for mid and senior is a complete high-level design that meets the requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个组件或瓶颈做深入的方案讨论，展开取舍与实现细节，而非停在高层框图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is an in-depth discussion of one component or bottleneck, working through trade-offs and implementation instead of staying at the high-level diagram.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把所有功能需求都对应到高层组件、先铺通整套系统的宽度，而非某一处的深度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Breadth means mapping every functional requirement to high-level components and covering the whole system's width before going deep anywhere.

optionExplanations: 对：时间是零和的，深挖吃掉预算就没有收尾，残缺系统直接触底评分线。
深度确实值钱，但缺了广度会连基础及格线都够不到，谈不上稳赚。
指望面试官救场是把节奏交给别人，控时是候选人自己的责任。
没有完整数据模型也能口头讨论扇出方向，这不是深挖失败的真正原因。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: time is zero-sum, and a deep dive that eats the budget leaves no wrap-up, hitting the floor of the score.
Depth is valuable, but missing breadth fails even the base bar, so it's no sure win.
Relying on the interviewer to rescue you hands over pacing, which is the candidate's own job.
You can discuss fan-out direction verbally without a full data model, so this isn't the real cause.

scenario: 你面的是 mid-level（E4）后端岗，45 分钟设计 News Feed；级别决定了这一轮的评分重心。
scenario_en: You're interviewing for a mid-level (E4) backend role, 45 minutes to design News Feed; the level sets what this round grades on.
q: E4 这一轮，面试官的评分方式和你的精力分配该是怎样？
q_en: At E4, how does the interviewer grade and how should you split your effort?
options: 广度为主（约 80/20），会逐个追问基础组件『它是做什么的』，但不指望你主动发现所有扩展瓶颈
深度为主（约 40/60），默认你懂基础，只想听你把复杂场景深挖透彻
广度深度各半，还要求你在毫无提示的情况下就主动暴露所有的性能瓶颈，并至少把其中两处深挖到底
只要画出组件框图就够，不必解释每个组件到底负责什么
options_en: Mostly breadth (about 80/20); they'll probe each basic component with 'what does it do?' but don't expect you to surface every scaling bottleneck yourself.
Mostly depth (about 40/60); they assume you know the basics and just want to hear you deep-dive the hard scenarios.
Half breadth half depth, and you must proactively expose every performance bottleneck fully unprompted and deep-dive at least two of them.
Just drawing the component boxes is enough; you don't need to explain what each component actually does.
why: E4 底线是『功能完整、满足需求的高层设计』，约 80% 广度；面试官不指望你自查瓶颈，会接手后半程并逐个盘问基础组件的作用。
why_en: The E4 bar is a functional high-level design that meets the requirements, roughly 80% breadth; the interviewer doesn't expect you to self-audit bottlenecks and will drive the later stages while probing each basic component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中级工程师职级；系统设计轮以广度为主，约 80% 广度 20% 深度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E4 is the mid-level engineer tier; its system-design round is breadth-first, about 80% breadth and 20% depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把功能需求映射成组件与数据流的整体框图，还未展开到深挖细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A high-level design maps functional requirements onto components and data flow as an overall diagram, before any deep-dive detail.

optionExplanations: 对：E4 求完整可用的高层设计，面试官会盘问基础组件并驱动后半程。
深度为主是 staff+ 的标准，E4 阶段不会这样压深度。
无提示暴露瓶颈并深挖两处，是 senior（E5）的要求，超出 E4 及格线。
面试官恰恰会追问每个组件的职责，画框图不解释会被判为只知其名。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: E4 wants a complete, functional high-level design; the interviewer probes basics and drives the back half.
Depth-first is the staff+ standard; E4 isn't pushed on depth like this.
Surfacing bottlenecks unprompted and deep-diving two is the senior (E5) bar, above E4.
The interviewer will in fact ask each component's role, so unexplained boxes read as name-only knowledge.

scenario: 同一道 News Feed，这次面的是 senior（E5）后端岗，还是 45 分钟；级别抬高改变了及格线。
scenario_en: Same News Feed, this time for a senior (E5) backend role, still 45 minutes; the higher level moves the passing bar.
q: 相比 E4，E5 把这道题的及格线抬到了哪里？
q_en: Compared with E4, where does E5 raise the passing bar on this question?
options: 约 60/40 广度深度：快速掠过高层设计，主动（不靠提示）点出扇出瓶颈，并至少深挖两个 deep dive
和 E4 一样 80/20，只是要求组件图画得更工整、命名更规范一些
纯深度 40/60，面试官全程只在真正需要聚焦时才短暂介入，期待你完全独立地发现、预防并解决一切潜在问题
只要能背出扇出读、扇出写两种策略的定义，不必落到本题具体怎么用
options_en: About 60/40 breadth to depth: speed through the high-level design, proactively (unprompted) name the fan-out bottleneck, and deep-dive at least two areas.
Same 80/20 as E4, just with a tidier component diagram and more standardized naming.
Pure depth at 40/60, with the interviewer briefly stepping in only to focus, expecting you to fully independently find and prevent every potential issue.
Just reciting the definitions of fan-out-on-read and fan-out-on-write is enough, without applying them to this problem.
why: E5 要证明有 hands-on 深度：因此快速铺完广度、主动暴露扇出瓶颈，并挑至少两处深挖到能讲清 pros/cons；代价是广度必须提速。
why_en: E5 must show hands-on depth, so you cover breadth fast, proactively surface the fan-out bottleneck, and deep-dive at least two areas enough to explain the pros and cons, at the cost of speeding up breadth to free time for depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高级工程师职级；系统设计轮约 60% 广度 40% 深度，需主动暴露瓶颈并深挖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5 is the senior engineer tier; its system-design round is about 60% breadth and 40% depth, requiring you to surface bottlenecks proactively and deep-dive.

termDefinitions.term: 扇出读/扇出写 / fan-out on read vs write
termDefinitions.meaning: 读时现查合并各账号的帖子叫扇出读；发帖时预先写进每个粉丝的 feed 叫扇出写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read merges each account's posts at read time; fan-out on write pushes a new post into every follower's feed when it's created.

optionExplanations: 对：E5 要主动暴露扇出并深挖至少两处，快速走完广度以腾出深度时间。
只把图画整齐仍停在 E4 的广度水平，够不到 E5 对深度的要求。
只在聚焦时介入、独立预防一切，是 staff+ 的标准，比 E5 更高。
背定义而不落到本题，正是 E5 面试官想淘汰的『纸上谈兵』。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: E5 must proactively surface fan-out and deep-dive at least two, racing through breadth to free depth time.
A tidier diagram still sits at E4's breadth level and misses E5's depth requirement.
Intervening only to focus and preventing everything independently is the staff+ standard, above E5.
Reciting definitions without applying them is exactly the paper-only answer E5 interviewers screen out.

q: 面试官禁止使用 Elasticsearch / Postgres 全文索引后，设计上你被迫要亲手做的核心工作是？
q_en: When Elasticsearch and Postgres full-text search are off limits, what core work must you build yourself?
options: 亲手设计数据布局与倒排索引
改用 NoSQL 自带的搜索功能
放弃关键词搜索改做前缀匹配
把过滤逻辑全放到客户端本地
why: 没有现成全文索引可依赖，你必须自己决定数据如何布局、如何构建倒排索引、如何扩展——这正是这类题要考的底层功。
why_en: With no off-the-shelf full-text index available, you must design the data layout, build the inverted index, and scale it yourself.
options_en: Hand-build the data layout and an inverted index yourself.
Rely on a NoSQL database's built-in search.
Drop keyword search and only do prefix matching.
Push all filtering to the client side.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开箱即用的分布式搜索引擎，内部本身就用倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an off-the-shelf search engine built on inverted indexes.

optionExplanations: 禁用现成引擎后，唯一出路就是这个：自己定布局、建索引、想扩展。
误以为 NoSQL 自带全文检索能绕过限制，但题目已经排除了这类现成搜索方案。
把关键词搜索偷换成前缀匹配，其实是在悄悄阉割功能需求，题目并未允许。
客户端拿不到全量帖子数据，把过滤全丢给它做不出真正的搜索匹配。
optionExplanations_en: With Elasticsearch and native full-text search off the table, you're the one deciding the data layout, the index shape, and how it scales.
NoSQL's built-in search is exactly the kind of off-the-shelf engine this problem rules out, so it doesn't get you out of building your own.
Swapping keyword search for prefix matching quietly drops a stated requirement instead of solving the indexing problem.
The client never sees the full post corpus, so pushing filtering there can't reproduce real keyword search.
scenario: 面试官禁掉 Elasticsearch 和 Postgres 全文索引，你仍要在万亿级帖子上支持关键词搜索。
scenario_en: The interviewer takes Elasticsearch and Postgres full-text search off the table, but you still need keyword search over a trillion posts.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 为 FB 帖子搜索定义需求时，哪些属于核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: When defining requirements for FB Post Search, which are core functional requirements?
options: 用户能创建和点赞帖子
用户能按关键词搜索帖子
搜索结果能按时间或点赞数排序
搜索结果按用户兴趣做个性化排序
why: 核心需求只有三条：创建/点赞、关键词搜索、按时间或赞数排序；个性化被明确划出范围，这个决定让后面的缓存设计大为简化。
why_en: The core requirements are creating and liking posts, keyword search, and sorting by recency or like count, while personalization is explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Users can create and like posts.
Users can search posts by keyword.
Results can be sorted by recency or like count.
Results are personalized to each user's interests.
optionExplanations: 创建和点赞是搜索得以运作的前提动作，属于核心功能需求。
关键词搜索是本题唯一被点名的核心检索方式，必须支持。
结果排序是明确列出的核心需求，为后面的双索引设计埋下伏笔。
个性化听起来像加分项，但被题目明确划出范围，不是核心需求。
optionExplanations_en: Creating and liking posts are the baseline actions the whole search feature depends on, so they're core requirements.
Keyword search is the one retrieval mode this problem names explicitly, so it has to be supported.
Sorting results is called out as a core requirement, which is what later motivates the dual-index design.
Personalization sounds like a nice add-on, but the problem explicitly puts it out of scope, not a core requirement.
scenario: 为 FB 帖子搜索划需求：10 亿用户 × 每天 1 帖 ≈ 10k 帖/秒，40 分钟白板只能设计最小可用集。
scenario_en: Scoping FB Post Search: 1B users times one post a day is roughly 10K posts per second, and on a 40-minute whiteboard you can only design the minimum viable set.

q: FB 帖子搜索里，下列哪些被划为范围外（out of scope）？（多选）
q_en: In FB Post Search, which items are out of scope?
options: 模糊匹配（搜 bird 命中 ostrich）
隐私规则与过滤
新帖 1 分钟内可被搜索
搜索页对新帖做实时推送更新
why: 模糊匹配、个性化、隐私、复杂相关性排序、多媒体、实时更新都在范围外；「新帖 1 分钟内可搜」恰恰是核心非功能需求，不是范围外。
why_en: Fuzzy matching, privacy filters, and realtime result updates are out of scope, whereas making new posts searchable within a minute is a core requirement.
options_en: Fuzzy matching (searching bird also matches ostrich).
Privacy rules and filtering.
New posts searchable within one minute.
Realtime push updates to the search page.
optionExplanations: 模糊匹配要理解语义相近词，这类高级检索能力被划出了范围。
隐私规则涉及权限体系，这道题聚焦索引和检索，不含在内。
这条其实是核心非功能需求（新帖可搜的时限），不是范围外项目。
实时推送要额外的长连接和通知系统，本题只做拉取式搜索。
optionExplanations_en: Fuzzy matching needs semantic-similarity understanding, an advanced capability this problem puts out of scope.
Privacy rules are an authorization concern; this problem stays focused on indexing and retrieval, not access control.
This is actually a core non-functional requirement — the new-post visibility deadline — not an out-of-scope item.
Realtime push needs long-lived connections and a notification system; this design only does pull-based search.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索定范围：万亿帖、40 分钟白板，多留一项能力就要挤掉索引设计的时间。
scenario_en: Scoping FB Post Search over a trillion posts on a 40-minute whiteboard — every extra capability you keep eats into index-design time.

scenario: 需求阶段决定是否保留「搜索结果个性化」：10 亿用户 × 每天 1 次搜索 ≈ 10k 查询/秒，且重复查询极多。
scenario_en: During requirements you decide whether personalized results stay in scope: 1B users times one search a day is about 10K queries per second, and the same queries repeat constantly.
q: 把个性化划出范围，对系统设计最大的红利是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest system-design benefit of making personalization out of scope?
options: 数据库可以少建一个索引来省空间
读写请求都不再需要 API 网关拦截
相同查询人人同结果，查询级缓存极其有效
写入路径可以完全省掉
why: 没有个性化意味着搜索结果只取决于查询本身、人人相同，结果可以进缓存和 CDN 被海量复用；所以值得当面问「个性化是不是硬需求」。
why_en: Dropping personalization means identical queries return identical results for everyone, which makes query-level caching and CDN reuse dramatically more effective.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品硬性要求千人千面的搜索结果，查询级缓存基本失效，只能退到缓存更底层的索引数据、在线上做个性化重排。
options_en: The database needs one fewer index.
You no longer need an API gateway.
Identical queries return identical results, so query-level caching becomes extremely effective.
The write path can be dropped entirely.
tradeoff: 无个性化换来缓存高复用 vs 千人千面的相关性

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径最前端的入口，负责鉴权、限流后转发给后端服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway authenticates and rate-limits requests before forwarding them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

optionExplanations: 少建索引只是锦上添花的小事，撑不起「舍弃个性化」这么大的取舍。
API 网关管的是鉴权限流，跟结果是否因人而异毫无关系。
无个性化时同一查询谁来查结果都一样，缓存可以被海量请求复用，这才是真正的红利。
发帖点赞的写入路径跟个性化无关，砍掉个性化也不会让写入消失。
optionExplanations_en: Trimming one database index is a footnote, not the payoff big enough to justify dropping personalization.
The API gateway just handles auth and rate limiting, unrelated to whether results differ per user.
Without personalization, identical queries return identical results for everyone, so a shared cache absorbs massive request volume — that's the real win.
The write path for posts and likes has nothing to do with personalization; dropping it doesn't remove writes.

scenario: FB Post Search 面试先给定两个目标：中位搜索延迟 <500ms，新帖 <1分钟可搜。这些是 SLO/SLA 目标，不是由帖子量公式算出的结果。
scenario_en: In the FB Post Search interview, median search latency under 500 ms and new posts searchable within one minute are given SLO/SLA targets, not capacity-derived numbers.
q: 这些 NFR 数字分别约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Which design paths do these NFR numbers constrain?
text: 500ms 约束{{查询路径}}，推动内存索引、缓存和避免请求时全量排序；1分钟约束{{新帖可见性}}，反推索引流水线延迟和缓存 TTL 上限。
why: 这两个数不是算出来的容量结果，而是面试中先约定的用户体验目标。真正的计算发生在后面：用它们倒推索引、缓存、冷热分层和写入流水线。
why_en: The five-hundred-millisecond and one-minute numbers are service targets, not derived constants, and they constrain the query path and freshness path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟、吞吐、可用性这类衡量系统「好不好」的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover latency, throughput, and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队希望系统达到的内部目标，如中位搜索 <500ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level objective is an internal target for system behavior, such as median search latency under five hundred milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议：对外承诺的服务指标，如新帖 1 分钟内可搜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level agreement is a promised service level, such as new posts being searchable within a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存存活时间。超过 TTL 后缓存条目过期，系统必须重新取或重算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time to live is how long a cache entry may live before it expires and must be refreshed.

q: 「老帖、冷门帖也要可搜索，但允许更慢」这条需求在为哪个设计决策埋伏笔？
q_en: Which later design decision is hinted by the requirement that old and unpopular posts are searchable but slower?
options: 放弃高可用目标
冷热分层：热数据进内存、冷数据下沉廉价存储
换一台内存更大的单机数据库来扛全部数据
把所有索引都搬进 CDN
why: 大数据量系统天然有热/冷数据之分：热数据高频访问要内存级速度，冷数据低频访问可放磁盘、远端库甚至磁带；这条 NFR 正是后面「冷索引下沉 S3」的伏笔。
why_en: Allowing old or unpopular posts to be slower foreshadows a hot-cold split where hot data lives in memory and cold data moves to cheaper, slower storage.
options_en: Abandon the high-availability goal.
A hot-cold split: hot data in memory, cold data on cheaper storage.
Switch to a single bigger database machine.
Move all indexes into the CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: 允许冷帖慢一点跟放弃高可用是两码事，系统仍要保持可用。
这正是后面冷索引下沉 blob 存储的伏笔：热数据留内存，冷数据可以慢。
单机再大也扛不住海量冷热数据，纵向扩容不是长久之计。
CDN 缓存的是响应结果，不是拿来放整份可写索引的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Tolerating slower cold posts is not the same as giving up on availability; the system still has to stay up.
This is exactly what later motivates demoting cold indexes to blob storage: hot data stays in memory, cold data can be slower.
No single machine, however large, absorbs unbounded hot-and-cold data growth; vertical scaling doesn't hold up.
A CDN caches response payloads, not a place to host a live, writable index.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索里绝大多数查询命中近期热帖，但万亿老帖也要能搜到，全放内存的成本不可接受。
scenario_en: In FB Post Search almost every query hits recent hot posts, yet a trillion old posts must stay searchable and keeping them all in memory is unaffordable.

q: 补全写入侧的规模估算（10 亿用户，每天按约 10 万秒取整）：
q_en: Fill in the write-side scale estimate for 1B users and roughly 100K seconds per day.
text: 每人每天 1 帖 → 约 {{10k}} posts/秒；每人每天 10 个赞 → 约 {{100k}} likes/秒；点赞写入量是发帖的 {{10}} 倍。
why: 用 1B ÷ 100k 秒的快捷除法得出发帖 10k/s、点赞 100k/s；点赞比发帖多一个数量级，这个观察直接决定了后面必须重点优化点赞写入。
why_en: A billion users produce roughly ten thousand posts and one hundred thousand likes per second, so likes outnumber post creations ten to one.
scenario: 规模估算：10 亿用户，每天约 10 万秒，估算写入侧的量级。
scenario_en: Estimate write-side order of magnitude from 1B users and about 100K seconds per day.

q: 由这个读规模，读路径最该具备的能力是？
q_en: Given this read scale, what capability does the read path need most?
options: 读会突发到 10 倍，重复查询要能被缓存/CDN 吸收
读量极小，单台普通机器就足以稳稳承载全部流量
读远大于写，应把机器全都堆到读路径上、给倒排索引不断扩容
读流量根本无法估算，直接跳过这步
why: 搜索读约 10k/s 但可能突发 10 倍；因为无个性化、查询重复度高，读路径靠结果缓存和 CDN 吸收峰值，而不是一味加索引机器。
why_en: Search reads run about ten thousand per second but can spike tenfold, so the read path leans on result caching and a CDN to absorb bursts.
scenario: 10 亿用户 × 每人每天约 1 次搜索 ≈ 10k 查询/秒，还可能突发到平时的 10 倍。
scenario_en: A billion users times about one search a day is roughly 10K queries per second, and it can burst to ten times that.
options_en: Reads can spike 10x, so repeated queries must be absorbable by a cache/CDN.
Read volume is tiny; a single machine can carry all traffic.
Reads dominate writes, so pile machines onto the read path and keep scaling up the inverted index.
Read traffic can't be estimated, so skip this step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

optionExplanations: 10k/s 的常态读量还可能突发到 10 倍，读路径得靠缓存和 CDN 顶住峰值。
1 万/秒已经不是单机量级，读量并不小。
前面已经算出写才是大头，这里反而说读碾压写，判断反了。
估算恰恰是这一步的意义所在，「无法估算」是在回避该做的工作。
optionExplanations_en: A steady ten thousand reads a second can still burst tenfold, so the read path leans on cache and CDN to absorb spikes.
Ten thousand requests a second is well past what a single box handles; the volume isn't tiny.
The earlier estimate already showed writes dominate; claiming reads crush writes gets the comparison backwards.
Estimating scale is the whole point of this step; skipping it dodges the work instead of doing it.

q: 对比估算结果（写约 110k/s vs 搜索 10k/s），关于系统性质最重要的结论是？
q_en: Comparing about 110K writes/s with 10K searches/s, what is the key system takeaway?
options: 系统读多写少，应重点优化读路径、把大部分机器投在查询侧
系统写多读少——别被「搜索」二字骗成读为主
读写均衡，无需特别优化
数据量不大，单机即可承载
why: 这题最容易犯的错是被「搜索系统」带偏、假设读是大头；估算揭示写入（尤其点赞）远超读，写路径才是主要瓶颈。
why_en: The estimates reveal a write-heavy system, overturning the common assumption that a search problem must be read-heavy.
options_en: The system is read-heavy, so focus optimization on the read path and put most machines on the query side.
The system is write-heavy—don't let the word 'search' fool you into assuming reads dominate.
Reads and writes are balanced; no special optimization.
The data is small; one machine suffices.
optionExplanations: 这正是「搜索」二字带来的常见误判，估算结果其实相反。
110k/s 写 vs 10k/s 读，写才是十倍量级的大头。
两者相差一个数量级，说「均衡」低估了真实的写入压力。
十亿用户规模下的写入量早已远超单机承载能力。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the misread the word 'search' invites; the estimate actually points the other way.
At roughly 110K writes/s versus 10K reads/s, writes outweigh reads by a full order of magnitude.
The two differ by 10x, so calling it 'balanced' understates the real write pressure.
At a billion-user scale, write volume already far exceeds what one machine can carry.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索：10 亿用户每天发 1 帖、点 10 个赞、搜 1 次，你要决定先优化哪条路径。
scenario_en: FB Post Search: a billion users each post once, like ten times, and search once a day — you decide which path to optimize first.

q: 这个存储量级对搜索系统提出的设计要求是？
q_en: What does this storage scale force the search system to do?
options: 内存放不下 3.6PB，索引要设上限、冷数据下沉便宜存储
数据量不大，一台大内存机器即可
把全部帖子原文连同索引都整份塞进 Redis 内存里加速查询
存储不是问题，无需特别处理
why: 3.6 万亿帖 × 1kb ≈ 3.6PB，全量放内存/单机不可行；这直接催生后面给索引设上限、把冷门关键词下沉 blob 存储的设计。
why_en: Ten years of a billion posts a day is about 3.6 petabytes, far too much to keep in memory, which forces index caps and cold blob storage.
scenario: FB 运营 10 年、每天约 10 亿帖、每帖元数据约 1kb，原始存储估算约 3.6 PB。
scenario_en: After 10 years at roughly 1B posts per day and 1 KB metadata per post, raw storage is about 3.6 PB.
options_en: 3.6 PB won't fit in memory, so indexes must be capped and cold data pushed to cheap storage.
The data is small; one big-memory machine is enough.
Stuff every post's full text and index into Redis memory to speed up queries.
Storage isn't a concern; no special handling needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

optionExplanations: 3.6PB 远超任何单机内存容量，索引必须设上限、冷数据另找便宜去处。
3.6PB 早已超出「一台大内存机器」能装下的范围。
把原文塞进内存型的 Redis，成本和容量都撑不住 PB 级数据。
3.6PB 正是逼出「索引设上限+冷数据下沉」设计的根源，不能忽视。
optionExplanations_en: 3.6 petabytes dwarfs any single machine's memory, so indexes need a cap and cold data needs a cheaper home.
3.6 petabytes is already far beyond what one big-memory box can hold.
Stuffing raw post text into memory-priced Redis can't afford petabyte-scale cost or capacity.
3.6 petabytes is precisely what forces the index-cap-plus-cold-storage design; it can't be waved away.

q: FB 帖子搜索的核心实体（User/Post/Like）里，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about the core User/Post/Like entities in FB Post Search are correct?
options: User——发帖的主体
Post——被搜索的对象，有内容、作者，隐含点赞数
Like——我们主要关心它的计数而非每条记录
Comment——搜索的主要目标
why: 实体刻意简单：User、Post、Like 三个，且对 Like 只关心 count；实体简单就不必恋战，快速推进到 API 和设计。
why_en: The entities are just User, Post, and Like, and for likes we mostly care about the count rather than individual records.
options_en: User — the author who creates posts.
Post — the searchable object with content, author, and an implicit like count.
Like — we mostly care about its count, not each record.
Comment — the primary search target.
optionExplanations: User 只是发帖的主体，本题不深挖用户模型本身。
Post 是搜索真正的目标对象，携带内容、作者和点赞数。
点赞我们只关心总数用于排序，单条点赞记录不重要。
评论从未出现在本题的核心实体里，搜索的目标始终是帖子。
optionExplanations_en: User is just the actor who creates posts; this problem doesn't dig into the user model itself.
Post is the actual object being searched, carrying content, author, and an implicit like count.
For likes we only care about the running total for sorting, not each individual like record.
Comments never appear among this problem's core entities; the search target is always the post.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索白板只有 40 分钟，核心实体这一步该压到 2 分钟，多写实体就少了深挖时间。
scenario_en: You have 40 minutes on the FB Post Search whiteboard; core entities should take two of them, and extra entities cost you deep-dive time.

q: FB 帖子搜索的 API 应该是什么形状？
q_en: What shape should the FB Post Search API have?
options: 单一搜索端点，写入直连数据库
全部收敛为一个 GraphQL 端点
搜索直接复用写入端点，读写全部共用同一条 API 路径
写路径（发帖/点赞）+ 查询路径（搜索）两条腿
why: API 分两条腿：写入端点接帖子与点赞、搜索端点服务查询；并向面试官说明真实系统中写入多半来自事件总线，独立端点只是为了讲解清晰。
why_en: The system exposes a write path for posts and likes plus a search query path, and in production the writes would likely arrive via an event stream like Kafka.
options_en: A single search endpoint, with writes going straight to the database.
Everything collapsed into one GraphQL endpoint.
Search just reuses the write endpoint, sharing one API path for reads and writes.
A write path (create post / like) plus a query path (search) — two legs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让客户端按需声明字段的单端点查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a single-endpoint query language where clients request exact fields.

optionExplanations: 写入直连数据库跳过了摄取和索引构建这一整套流程。
GraphQL 收敛所有查询字段，跟这里读写分离的架构无关。
写入和搜索的负载特征完全不同，合用一个端点会互相拖累。
写路径喂事件建索引、查询路径服务搜索，各司其职最清晰。
optionExplanations_en: Writing straight to the database skips the whole ingestion and index-building pipeline this design needs.
GraphQL collapses query fields into one endpoint, which has nothing to do with separating reads from writes here.
Writes and searches have completely different load shapes; cramming them into one endpoint makes each worse.
The write path feeds events into the index while the query path serves search — a clean separation of concerns.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索的写入来自发帖/点赞事件、读取来自用户查询，两者流量差一个数量级且要独立扩展。
scenario_en: In FB Post Search, writes arrive as post and like events while reads come from user queries — an order of magnitude apart and scaled independently.

q: 设计只聚焦「搜索」时，对上游 Post Service / Like Service 的正确处理方式是？
q_en: If the design focuses only on search, how should you treat upstream Post and Like services?
options: 假设它们已存在且正常工作，只从它们接收事件
必须从零开始重新设计发帖和点赞这两个上游服务
把它们合并进搜索服务统一实现
忽略它们，让客户端直连索引
why: 搜索只是整个社交产品的一部分，合理做法是假设上游发帖/点赞服务存在并工作正常，我们的摄取层从它们接事件；把边界说清楚能省下宝贵时间。
why_en: Since we are only designing search, we assume the upstream post and like services already exist and feed our ingestion pipeline.
options_en: Assume they already exist and work; just consume their events.
Design both the post and like upstream services from scratch.
Merge them into the search service.
Ignore them and let clients hit the index directly.
optionExplanations: 搜索只是整个产品的一部分，划清边界后专心做摄取和索引。
重新设计发帖/点赞服务偏离了「只做搜索」的题目边界。
合并服务混淆了职责边界，搜索不该兼管发帖点赞的业务逻辑。
跳过上游服务，索引就没有数据来源，搜索无从谈起。
optionExplanations_en: Search is only one slice of the product, so drawing that boundary lets you focus on ingestion and indexing.
Redesigning the post and like services strays outside the 'search only' scope this problem sets.
Merging the services blurs ownership; search shouldn't also own posting and liking business logic.
Skip the upstream services and the index has no data source at all — there's nothing left to search.
scenario: 你只负责 Facebook 的搜索子系统，发帖和点赞由别的团队的服务拥有，40 分钟不够重画整个社交产品。
scenario_en: You own only Facebook's search subsystem; posting and liking belong to other teams' services, and 40 minutes isn't enough to redraw the whole product.

q: 用这条 SQL 直接在 PB 级帖子表上做关键词搜索，最根本的问题是？
q_en: What is the fundamental problem with running this SQL keyword search directly on a PB-scale posts table?
options: 语法不合法，无法执行
没有索引，查询时要逐帖全表扫描，PB 级下太慢
返回的结果不正确
LIKE 这条语法本身并不支持中文内容匹配
why: 前置通配符的 LIKE 无法走索引，每次查询都要在查询时刻扫描每一帖；结果正确但在万亿帖、PB 级数据上是灾难——数据组织必须匹配请求模式。
why_en: A leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use an index, so every query scans every post at query time, which is hopeless at petabyte scale.
options_en: The syntax is invalid and won't run.
No index is usable, so every query scans all posts — hopeless at petabyte scale.
The returned results are incorrect.
LIKE doesn't support non-English text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

optionExplanations: 这条 SQL 语法完全合法，能正常执行，只是慢到不可用。
前置通配符的 LIKE 走不了索引，每次查询都要扫全表。
结果本身是对的，问题出在扫描代价，不是结果错误。
LIKE 对语言无感知，真正的病根是缺索引而非语言支持。
optionExplanations_en: The SQL syntax is perfectly valid and runs fine; the problem is that it's unusably slow.
A leading-wildcard LIKE can't use an index, so every query scans the entire table.
The results themselves are correct; the issue is scan cost, not wrong output.
LIKE has no awareness of language at all; the real defect is the missing index, not text support.
scenario: 在万亿行、PB 级的 posts 表上直接用 LIKE '%keyword%' 查询，中位延迟目标 500ms。
scenario_en: Running LIKE '%keyword%' straight against a petabyte-scale posts table of a trillion rows, with a 500ms median latency target.

q: 对全表扫描方案做分片/复制（M 个节点各扫 N/M 帖），结论是？
q_en: If you shard and replicate the full-table scan across M nodes, what is the conclusion?
options: 分片能彻底解决扫描慢的问题
只要把节点数 M 撑到足够大，每片扫描量小到就能达标
只是边际改善：每节点仍要扫海量，依旧太慢，死路
分片反而会让结果不正确
why: 分片把扫描量从 N 降到 N/M，但面对万亿级帖子这只是把「不可能」变成「依然不可能」；正确出路是改变数据组织方式，而不是堆机器硬扫。
why_en: Sharding the naive scan only cuts each node's work to N over M posts, which is still far too slow and a dead end.
options_en: Sharding fully solves the slow-scan problem.
It's fine as long as node count M is large enough that each shard's scan is tiny.
Only a marginal gain: each node still scans a huge amount — still too slow, a dead end.
Sharding makes the results incorrect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

optionExplanations: 分片只是把慢均摊到多台机器，扫描这件事本身没有变快。
把 M 堆得再大，万亿级数据下每片仍是海量，撑不起亚秒级。
分片只把总扫描量摊薄成 N/M，量级依旧巨大，唯一出路是重新组织数据。
分片只影响谁去扫，不影响扫描逻辑本身，结果依旧正确。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding just spreads the slowness across machines; scanning itself doesn't get any faster.
However large M gets, each shard of a trillion-row table is still huge and can't hit sub-second latency.
Cutting N down to N/M only turns 'impossible' into 'still impossible' — the fix has to be reorganizing the data itself.
Sharding only changes who does the scanning, not the scan logic, so results stay correct.
scenario: 万亿帖全表扫描太慢，有人提议扩到 1000 个节点各扫 N/M 帖，延迟仍要压在 500ms 内。
scenario_en: Full scans over a trillion posts are too slow, so someone proposes a thousand nodes each scanning N/M posts — still inside a 500ms budget.

scenario: 万亿级帖子，要求按关键词找出所有包含该词的帖子，查询延迟中位数 <500ms，且不允许使用现成搜索引擎。
scenario_en: Across trillions of posts, you need sub-500 ms keyword lookup without using an off-the-shelf search engine.
q: 应该采用的核心数据结构是？
q_en: What core data structure should you use?
options: 倒排索引：关键词 → 包含它的帖子 ID 列表
对 content 列建 B-tree 索引
分片后的并行全表扫描
用布隆过滤器直接返回结果
why: 倒排索引把工作移到写入时：发帖时拆词并把帖子 ID 挂到每个词的列表下，查询就变成一次按 key 取列表的快速查找，这是关键词搜索的教科书解法。
why_en: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of posts containing it, turning search into a fast key lookup instead of a scan.
whenOtherWins: 若查询是前缀或范围查询，B-tree 类索引才有用武之地；若允许用 Elasticsearch，直接用它内置的倒排索引省去自建成本。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["新帖: I saw Taylor"] --> T["拆词 tokenization"]
    T --> A["key: i ← post9"]
    T --> B["key: saw ← post9"]
    T --> C["key: taylor ← post9"]
    Q["搜索 taylor"] -. 直接取列表 .-> C
options_en: An inverted index: keyword → list of post IDs containing it.
A B-tree index on the content column.
Parallel full-table scan after sharding.
Use a Bloom filter to return results directly.
tradeoff: 写时预组织(倒排索引) vs 查询时扫描/过滤

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库常用的按值排序索引，擅长前缀和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index sorts values for fast prefix and range lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用位数组做概率性成员判断，只能答「可能存在/一定不存在」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter probabilistically tests set membership with no false negatives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开箱即用的分布式搜索引擎，内部本身就用倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an off-the-shelf search engine built on inverted indexes.

optionExplanations: 把词到帖子的映射提前建在写入阶段，检索时只是一次哈希查找，天然扛得住亚秒级要求。
B-tree 擅长前缀和范围查询，但整词精确匹配靠它仍要扫描，帮不上这里的忙。
并行扫描把 N 降到 N/M，可万亿级数据下每片仍太大，赶不上 500ms。
布隆过滤器只能答「可能存在」，给不出完整的帖子列表，满足不了搜索需求。
optionExplanations_en: Pre-building the keyword-to-post mapping turns every query into a single key lookup, which is what makes sub-second latency possible.
A B-tree shines at prefix and range lookups, but exact whole-word matching still forces a scan, so it doesn't help here.
Parallel scanning cuts N down to N/M, but each shard of a trillion posts is still too large to hit 500ms.
A Bloom filter can only answer 'maybe present,' not hand back the actual list of matching posts search needs.

q: 补全倒排索引的写入流程：
q_en: Fill in the write flow for building an inverted index:
text: 帖子创建后，Ingestion 服务把内容拆解成一个个可匹配的关键词，这个过程叫 {{tokenization}}；随后把该帖的 {{post ID}} 追加到每个关键词对应的列表里。
why: 倒排索引的构建就是「拆词 + 挂 ID」：一帖可能含 10-1000 个词，意味着一次发帖触发多个 key 的写入，这也是后面写扩展问题的根源。
why_en: Ingestion tokenizes each post into keywords and appends the post ID to every keyword's list in the index.
diagram:
graph LR
    Post[New post] --> Tokenize[Tokenize text]
    Tokenize --> Terms[Terms]
    Terms --> Index[Update inverted index]
    Index --> Redis[(Redis lists or sets)]
    Post --> Store[(Post store)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把帖子内容拆解成一个个可匹配关键词的过程，中文叫分词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization breaks a post into individual searchable keywords.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

scenario: 倒排索引位于中位 <500ms 的核心查询路径上，需要极快的读取，同时你接受用替代方案弥补持久性短板。
scenario_en: The inverted index sits on the sub-500 ms query path, needs very fast reads, and can address durability through another option.
q: 这个倒排索引应该放在什么存储里？
q_en: Where should this inverted index live?
options: 磁盘上的 MySQL 表——最耐久但随机读取偏慢、难达亚 500ms
本地文件——最简单但单机无法扩展
Redis 内存——查询极快，MemoryDB 补持久
S3 对象存储——最便宜但延迟太高
why: 索引放 Redis 内存里查询飞快，满足亚 500ms 的核心诉求；内存的持久性短板是可解的——换 MemoryDB 等持久化兼容方案或留到深挖处理。
why_en: The index lives in Redis for blazing-fast in-memory lookups, with durability concerns addressed by a persistent alternative like MemoryDB.
whenOtherWins: 若索引重建代价不可接受、持久性是硬约束，一开始就选 MemoryDB 或磁盘型存储；冷门关键词后面也会下沉到便宜的 blob 存储。
options_en: A MySQL table on disk — most durable but random reads are too slow for sub-500ms.
Local files — simplest but a single box that can't scale.
Redis in memory — blazing-fast reads, with MemoryDB covering durability.
S3 object storage — cheapest but latency is too high.
tradeoff: 内存读取速度 vs 持久性/成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 兼容 Redis 接口但带持久化的内存数据库，可弥补纯内存的易失性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MemoryDB is a durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: MySQL 落盘最耐久，但磁盘读取撑不住亚 500ms 的核心查询路径。
本地文件简单直接，可惜是单机存储，没法随索引规模水平扩展。
内存读取满足亚 500ms 的核心诉求，持久性短板换成 MemoryDB 之类方案来补。
S3 便宜、容量大，但延迟太高，只适合放冷门数据而非热查询路径。
optionExplanations_en: MySQL on disk is the most durable option, but disk reads can't keep up with the sub-500ms query path.
Local files are simple, but they live on one box and can't scale horizontally as the index grows.
In-memory reads meet the sub-500ms requirement, and a durable variant like MemoryDB covers the persistence gap.
S3 is cheap and huge, but its latency is too high for the hot query path — better suited to cold data.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: Redis 倒排索引方案从第一天起就自带哪些挑战？（多选）
q_en: Which challenges come with a Redis inverted-index design from day one?
options: 常见关键词的 post ID 列表会变得非常大
一帖含 10-1000 个关键词，每次发帖要写很多个 key
Redis 完全无法水平扩展
内存存储天生有持久性顾虑
why: 三大隐患：热词列表巨大（后面用截断+冷存储解决）、发帖写放大（用 Kafka+分片解决）、内存持久性（用 MemoryDB 解决）；Redis 本身完全可以通过分片水平扩展。
why_en: Common keywords produce huge ID lists, each post fans out into many key writes, and in-memory storage raises durability concerns.
options_en: Post-ID lists for common keywords grow very large.
A post has 10-1000 keywords, so each post writes many keys.
Redis can't scale horizontally at all.
In-memory storage inherently raises durability concerns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写在底层被放大成多次物理写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification turns one logical write into many physical writes.

optionExplanations: 热词列表膨胀会拖慢读取、吃光内存，后面得靠截断和冷存储控制。
拆词后一帖变成几十上百次写，是写路径压力的直接来源。
Redis 完全可以按关键词分片水平扩展，这不是它的真实短板。
内存易失意味着宕机可能丢索引，必须换持久化方案兜底。
optionExplanations_en: Hot-keyword lists ballooning drags down reads and eats memory, which later forces caps and cold storage.
Tokenizing one post into dozens or hundreds of writes is the direct source of write-path pressure.
Redis actually scales out fine by sharding on keyword; horizontal scaling isn't its real weakness.
In-memory storage can lose the index on a crash, so it needs a durable fallback.
scenario: 用 Redis 存倒排索引服务 FB 帖子搜索：10k 帖/秒写入，热词如 'the' 覆盖上亿帖。
scenario_en: Using Redis for the FB Post Search inverted index: 10K posts a second coming in, and hot terms like 'the' appearing in hundreds of millions of posts.

q: 把「选择倒排索引」的完整决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full decision chain for choosing an inverted index in the correct order:
steps: 代价：每帖拆出几十上百个词、每个词都要写 key；热词的 postId 列表巨大
需求：万亿帖中按关键词亚秒级找到所有匹配帖子
缓解写放大：Kafka 缓冲写入 + 索引按关键词分片
决定性质：查询时全量扫描必死，必须在写入时按查询模式预组织数据
选型：Redis 内存倒排索引（关键词 → postId 列表）
缓解大列表：截断到 1k-10k 条 + 冷词下沉 blob 存储
why: 完整链条 = 需求 → 决定性质（写时预组织）→ 选型（Redis 倒排索引）→ 代价（写放大、大列表）→ 两条缓解各自对应一个代价；两个缓解之间先说哪个都成立。
why_en: The chain runs from the sub-second keyword search requirement, through organizing data at write time, to a Redis inverted index whose write amplification and huge lists are mitigated by buffering, sharding, capping, and cold storage.
diagram:
graph TD
    Scan[Full table scan too slow] --> Inverted[Use inverted index]
    Inverted --> Redis[Fast posting lists]
    Redis --> Challenges[Memory and ranking challenges]
    Challenges --> Tiering[Hot Redis plus cold storage]
tradeoff: 写时预组织 vs 查询时扫描

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

q: 「请求时排序」（取出关键词全部 postId → 逐个查时间戳 → 内存排序）有哪些致命问题？（多选）
q_en: What fatal problems come from request-time sorting after fetching all post IDs and timestamps?
options: 热词可能有千万级 postId，索引返回的载荷可达数百 MB
每个 postId 都要一次查找，累计上千万次查询
请求时排序百万级条目，平添不必要的延迟
排序结果一定是错误的
why: 三重打击：网络传输巨量 ID、海量逐条查找、请求时全量排序，500ms 的 SLA 完全无望；结果本身是对的，但代价不可接受。
why_en: Request-time sorting suffers from hundreds of megabytes of IDs, tens of millions of lookups, and expensive in-memory sorts on every query.
options_en: Popular keywords can have tens of millions of post IDs, payloads up to hundreds of MB.
Each post ID needs a lookup — tens of millions of them.
Sorting millions of items at request time adds needless latency.
The sorted result is guaranteed to be wrong.
optionExplanations: 千万级 ID 的载荷光传输就吃掉大量带宽和时间预算。
上千万次逐条查找的延迟叠加起来，远超 500ms 的预算。
把百万条目的排序留到请求时做，等于每次查询都白白多花时间。
排序算法本身没有错，问题全在代价高昂，不在结果对不对。
optionExplanations_en: A payload of tens of millions of IDs alone burns through bandwidth and time budget just being transferred.
Tens of millions of individual lookups stack up latency far past the 500ms budget.
Leaving a million-item sort for request time means every query pays that cost for nothing.
The sorting logic itself isn't wrong; the entire problem is the cost, not correctness.
scenario: 热词 'Taylor' 的 postId 列表上千万条，搜索仍要在 500ms 内返回按时间排序的前 10 条。
scenario_en: A hot term like 'Taylor' has tens of millions of post IDs, yet search still must return the top ten by recency within 500ms.

scenario: 搜索结果必须支持「按最新」和「按点赞数」两种排序，且查询时不能做大规模排序运算。
scenario_en: Search results must support recency and like-count sorting, but queries cannot perform large sorts at request time.
q: 怎么同时支持按时间和按赞数排序，又不在查询时做大排序？
q_en: How do you support both recency and like-count sorting without large query-time sorts?
options: 每次查询后在搜索服务里排序
只支持按时间排序，直接砍掉按点赞数排序这个功能需求
把排序交给客户端处理
每个关键词维护两份预排序索引：按时间、按赞数
why: 用空间换时间：每个关键词同时维护按时间和按赞数两份预排序索引，查询直接取已排序的头部；代价是索引存储翻倍，但换来查询性能的巨大提升。
why_en: Each keyword gets two pre-sorted indexes, one by creation time and one by like count, so queries read already-ordered results.
whenOtherWins: 若数据量小或查询稀少，请求时排序能省下一半索引存储；简单系统未必需要预排序双索引。
options_en: Sort in the search service after each query.
Support only recency sorting and drop the like-count sort requirement entirely.
Offload sorting to the client.
Keep two pre-sorted indexes per keyword: one by time, one by like count.
tradeoff: 索引存储翻倍 vs 查询时零排序

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

optionExplanations: 候选可能有百万条，查询时才排序会拖垮延迟。
砍掉按赞排序不满足需求，属于悄悄削减功能而非解决问题。
客户端既没有全量数据也没有算力，排不出正确结果。
空间换时间：查询直接取预排序好的头部，零排序开销。
optionExplanations_en: Candidates can run into the millions, so sorting them at query time wrecks latency.
Dropping like-count sorting fails the requirement — it's quietly cutting a feature, not solving the problem.
The client has neither the full dataset nor the compute to produce a correct order.
Trading space for time: queries just read the already-sorted head, with zero sort cost.

scenario: creation index 只会不断追加新帖，查询永远只取最新的若干条，需要为每个关键词选一个 Redis 结构。
scenario_en: The creation index only appends new posts and queries always take the newest few items, so choose a Redis structure per keyword.
q: 哪组命令符合 creation index 的正确用法？
q_en: Which command pattern is correct for the creation index?
codeSample:
# 发帖时间索引：按到达顺序追加
RPUSH kw:taylor:by_time post123
# 查询：只取列表尾部最新 10 条
LRANGE kw:taylor:by_time -10 -1
options: RPUSH 追加写入；LRANGE 取列表尾部最新 N 条
ZADD 按时间戳写入 sorted set；ZRANGE 取出全量再逐条过滤
SET 每次覆盖写入最新一条
SADD 写入集合；SMEMBERS 全量取出
why: 发帖天然按时间到达，用普通 Redis list 尾部追加即可免费保持时间序；查询只读尾部最新元素，写入和读取都很便宜。
why_en: Posts arrive in time order, so a plain Redis list with tail appends and tail reads keeps the creation index sorted for free.
whenOtherWins: 需要按会变化的分数（点赞数）排序时 list 无能为力，必须换 sorted set 按 score 动态维序。
options_en: RPUSH to append; LRANGE to read the newest N from the tail.
ZADD into a sorted set keyed by timestamp; ZRANGE to read everything then filter.
SET to overwrite with the latest one each time.
SADD into a set; SMEMBERS to read everything.
tradeoff: 追加即有序的 list vs 需按分数维序的 sorted set

termDefinitions.meaning: RPUSH 向列表尾部追加，LRANGE 按区间读取列表元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPUSH appends to a list tail and LRANGE reads a range of elements.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

optionExplanations: 发帖天然按时间到达，普通 list 尾部追加免费维持时间序。
sorted set 的按分数维序能力这里用不上，时间序不需要它。
SET 只能存一条，历史帖子全被覆盖丢失。
集合无序，取不出「最新 N 条」这种有顺序的结果。
optionExplanations_en: Posts arrive in time order naturally, so a plain list's tail append keeps that order for free.
A sorted set's score-based ordering is overkill here; time order doesn't need it.
SET holds only one value, so every earlier post gets overwritten and lost.
A set has no order, so it can't produce an ordered 'newest N' result.

scenario: likes index 需要按「会不断变化的点赞数」维持排序，要像优先队列一样支持按分数插入与按名次查询。
scenario_en: The likes index must maintain order by a constantly changing like count, like a priority queue with score updates and ranked reads.
q: 哪组命令符合 likes index 的正确用法？
q_en: Which command pattern is correct for the likes index?
codeSample:
# 点赞事件：给帖子的 score 加 1
ZINCRBY kw:taylor:by_likes 1 post123
# 查询：取点赞最高的前 10
ZREVRANGE kw:taylor:by_likes 0 9
options: RPUSH 命令负责把元素追加到普通列表的尾部并保持插入顺序
LPUSH 插到普通列表的头部
GET 直接读取一个字符串键
ZINCRBY 加分；ZREVRANGE 取最高前 N
why: Redis sorted set 按 score 维持有序，插入/更新/按名次查询的复杂度与优先队列相当，天然适合「按点赞数排序」的索引。
why_en: A Redis sorted set keeps posts ordered by like-count score, supporting priority-queue-like insertion and ranked queries.
whenOtherWins: 若排序键是不可变的到达时间，普通 list 追加更省内存也更简单。
options_en: RPUSH to append elements to the tail of a plain list, preserving insertion order.
LPUSH to prepend to the head of a plain list.
GET to read a single string key.
ZINCRBY to bump the score; ZREVRANGE to read the top-N.
tradeoff: 可变分数维序(sorted set) vs 固定顺序(list)

termDefinitions.meaning: ZINCRBY 给有序集合成员的分数加值，ZREVRANGE 取分数最高的前 N 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZINCRBY increases a member score and ZREVRANGE reads the highest-scoring N.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

optionExplanations: 普通列表只能保留插入顺序，赞数一变就没法重新排序。
头插和尾插都只是顺序不同，同样解决不了「按分数排序」。
单个字符串键存不下一份排行结构。
sorted set 每次点赞都能重新排序，天然适合按赞数排名。
optionExplanations_en: A plain list only preserves insertion order; it can't reorder itself when a like count changes.
Head versus tail insertion is just direction — neither solves ordering by a changing score.
A single string key can't hold a ranked structure at all.
A sorted set re-orders on every like, making it the natural fit for ranking by like count.

q: 双索引方案下，发帖和点赞分别触发什么索引操作？
q_en: In the dual-index design, what index operations do posts and likes trigger?
options: 发帖只写 creation；点赞只新增 likes 条目
发帖和点赞都触发全量重建索引
发帖写两份索引(每词)；点赞更新 likes 的 score
发帖和点赞都只修改 likes index
why: 新帖要在它的每个关键词下同时进两份索引（时间序列表 + 赞数 sorted set）；点赞只需给 likes index 对应 score 加一，但高频点赞会带来巨大更新压力。
why_en: A new post is added to both indexes for every keyword it contains, while each like updates the post's score in the likes index.
options_en: A post writes only creation; a like just adds a likes entry.

A post writes both indexes (per keyword); a like updates that post's score in likes.

q: 应对读流量的第一个显而易见的工具是？
q_en: What is the first obvious tool for handling read traffic?

升级更大内存的 Redis 机器

why: 判断缓存是否合适的两个信号在这全中：能容忍陈旧（1 分钟 SLA）+ 大量重复请求（无个性化），于是在搜索服务旁加分布式结果缓存。

Upgrade to a Redis box with more memory.

q: 搜索结果缓存的 TTL 应该设为多少，为什么？
q_en: What TTL should the search-result cache use, and why?
options: 小于 1 分钟——贴着新帖可见 SLA
24 小时——尽量拉长缓存寿命把命中率做到最高

why: TTL 由业务 SLA 反推：新帖必须 1 分钟内可见，缓存最长只能存活不到 1 分钟，这样即使命中旧缓存也不会违反可见性承诺。

24 hours — stretch cache lifetime to push the hit rate as high as possible.
1 second — to keep results as fresh as possible.
Never expire — least operational effort.

1 秒白白牺牲命中率，1 分钟内的陈旧本就被业务允许。

24 hours blows past the one-minute promise, so a cache hit could be badly out of date.

Never lapsing means a new post could stay unsearchable forever, breaking the SLA outright.

q: 在 Redis 结果缓存之外还能加什么？

options: 再多加几台无状态的搜索服务实例、纯靠横向扩容硬扛读流量
CDN 边缘缓存：就近节点缓存 /search 响应

CDN edge cache: geographically local nodes cache the /search response.
Have clients keep polling and retrying.
Add several read replicas to the database.

Edge nodes sit closest to the user, so a hit returns in tens of milliseconds without ever reaching the data center.
Polling and retrying only manufactures more duplicate requests and does nothing for latency.
Read replicas relieve database read pressure, not the physical distance between the user and your data center.

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=59

why: public 允许共享缓存（CDN）存储，max-age=59 让缓存寿命 <1 分钟、贴着 SLA 上限拿最高命中率；no-store 直接放弃缓存，3600 秒则违反 SLA。

Set Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600.
Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=59.

q: 把「交集法」回答 Taylor Swift 短语查询的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the intersection-method steps for answering a Taylor Swift phrase query in the correct order:
steps: 拉取候选帖原文，验证确实包含连续短语 Taylor Swift，而不是 Taylor made a swift exit 这种散装匹配
分别取出 Taylor 和 Swift 两个关键词的 postId 列表
把通过验证的帖子按排序要求返回
求两个列表的交集，得到同时含两个词的 postId
why: 交集法四步：取各词列表 → 求交 → 原文验证短语连续性（过滤「碰巧都含这两个词」的假阳性）→ 返回；不改索引结构，是侵入最小的多词方案。

    Query --> T2[term swift]
    T1 --> Intersect[Intersect postIds]

q: 交集法处理短语查询的最大痛点是？
q_en: What is the biggest pain point when using intersection for phrase queries?

why_en: Popular keywords yield huge ID sets that are expensive to transfer and intersect within the latency budget, and overlapping but nonadjacent words force wasteful filtering.
options_en: It can't return correct results.
Redis doesn't support set-intersection operations, forcing app-side computation.
Popular keywords have huge sets — transfer and intersection are costly, hard within 500ms.
It only supports two-word queries.

q: 应该怎么改进索引？
q_en: How should you improve the index?
options: 索引 bigram/shingle：相邻词对当 key
把一整句完整的话原样当成唯一的索引 key 去做精确命中

why: 每句的 bigram 数量线性增长，但像 Swift at 这种词对在别的帖子里几乎不复现，key 空间因此暴涨一个数量级，存储成本急剧上升。
why_en: Bigrams are far more unique than single words, so the index can balloon from ten million keys to over a hundred million.
options_en: Phrase queries actually get slower.
Key explosion: bigrams are sparse, so keys can grow by an order of magnitude.
A bigram index can't coexist with the existing single-word inverted index.
Like scores can no longer be updated.

optionExplanations: bigram 索引让短语查询变成一次命中，反而更快而非更慢。
词对比单词稀有得多，key 空间可能暴涨一个数量级，存储成本随之飙升。

bigram 只影响短语索引，跟点赞分数更新完全是两回事。

Word pairs are far rarer than single words, so the key space can balloon by an order of magnitude, driving storage costs up.
Single-word and bigram indexes coexist fine; they don't conflict.
Bigrams only touch the phrase index and have nothing to do with updating like scores.

scenario_en: To speed up phrase queries you index bigrams: 10K posts a second times about a hundred word pairs each, and you pay for that key space.

scenario_en: A full bigram index is too expensive, so you only want to pay index cost for phrases people actually search.
q: 合理的折衷方案是？
q_en: What is a reasonable compromise?
options: 彻底放弃短语查询
把所有 bigram 索引都直接下沉到 S3 对象存储省钱
只给高频 bigram 建索引，其余回退交集法
每天全量重建一次索引
why: 用概率计数结构（如 count-min sketch）廉价地找出高频 bigram、只为它们建索引；冷门短语回退交集法，兼顾成本与常见查询的速度。
why_en: Index only the popular bigrams identified with a probabilistic counter like count-min sketch, and fall back to intersection for the rare ones.
whenOtherWins: 若存储预算充足且短语查询延迟至上，全量 bigram 索引更简单，也没有回退路径带来的复杂度。
options_en: Abandon phrase queries entirely.
Dump every bigram index straight into S3 object storage to save cost.
Index only popular bigrams; fall back to intersection for the rest.
Fully rebuild the whole index daily.
tradeoff: 索引膨胀 vs 命中率——只为高频短语付索引成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率计数结构，用很小的内存估算元素出现频率。

optionExplanations: 放弃短语查询丢掉了明确的功能需求，代价太大。
全量冷存意味着连高频短语也要付延迟代价，得不偿失。
只为常被搜的短语付索引成本，冷门短语靠交集法兜底，两头兼顾。
周期性全量重建既昂贵又留有陈旧窗口，治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping phrase search entirely throws away a stated requirement — too costly a trade.
Cold-storing every bigram makes even popular phrases pay the latency penalty, which defeats the point.
Only popular phrases pay index cost, while rare ones fall back to intersection — the best of both.
A daily full rebuild is expensive and still leaves a stale window in between.

q: 为什么说发帖在索引侧存在「写放大」？
q_en: Why does posting create write amplification on the index side?
options: 每帖都要同步写主库和备库
Redis 会自动把每帖数据复制成三份副本从而放大写入
每帖都要重建全量索引
每帖拆成 10-100+ 个词，每词一次索引写
why: 倒排索引把一次发帖放大成「每个关键词一次写」，双索引下还要乘 2；10k 帖/秒的创建流量在索引层就成了百万级写/秒的压力源。
why_en: Tokenization fans a single hundred-word post out into a hundred or more index writes, massively amplifying the write load.
options_en: Every post must be written synchronously to primary and replica.
Redis automatically replicates each post's data into three copies, amplifying writes.
Every post rebuilds the whole index.
Each post splits into 10-100+ keywords, one index write each.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把帖子内容拆解成一个个可匹配关键词的过程，中文叫分词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization breaks a post into individual searchable keywords.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写在底层被放大成多次物理写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification turns one logical write into many physical writes.

optionExplanations: 主备同步写是存储的复制策略，跟拆词写放大是两回事。
Redis 的复制份数是运维配置，不是「写放大」这个概念说的事。
重建索引代价大到不可接受，倒排索引从不需要靠重建维护。
分词把一帖拆成几十上百个关键词，每个词都触发一次索引写。
optionExplanations_en: Primary-replica sync is a storage replication policy, not what tokenization write amplification is about.
Redis's replica count is an ops configuration, not what 'write amplification' refers to here.
Rebuilding the index is prohibitively expensive; an inverted index is never maintained by rebuilding.
Tokenizing a post into dozens or hundreds of keywords triggers one index write per keyword.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索写路径吃 10k 帖/秒，每帖含 10-100 个关键词，且每个关键词都要进两份索引。
scenario_en: The FB Post Search write path takes 10K posts a second, each carrying 10 to 100 keywords, and every keyword lands in two indexes.

q: 发帖洪峰打爆 ingestion 服务的最坏后果是？
q_en: What is the worst outcome if a post-creation surge overwhelms the ingestion service?
options: 事件被丢失，那些帖子将永远搜不到
查询延迟会稍微变慢一点
搜索结果缓存的命中率会随之明显下降
CDN 边缘缓存被清空失效
why: ingestion 是帖子进入索引的唯一通道，过载丢事件意味着帖子永远不可搜——直接违反「所有帖子可发现」的核心 NFR，所以必须加缓冲。
why_en: An overwhelmed ingestion service can drop post or like events, leaving those posts permanently unsearchable.
options_en: Events are dropped, and those posts become permanently unsearchable.
Query latency gets slightly worse.
The search-result cache hit rate noticeably drops as a result.
The CDN edge cache gets invalidated.
optionExplanations: 作为帖子进入索引的唯一通道，一旦事件被丢，那些帖子就永远搜不到。
「稍微变慢」严重低估了丢事件对可发现性的致命影响。
缓存命中率下降是读路径的小问题，跟丢失写事件不在一个量级。
CDN 缓存跟发帖洪峰打爆的是写路径，两者互不相干。
optionExplanations_en: Ingestion is the only door into the index, so a dropped event means that post is unsearchable forever.
'Slightly slower' badly understates how fatal dropping events is for discoverability.
A dip in cache hit rate is a minor read-path issue, nowhere near as severe as losing write events.
CDN caching lives on the read path; a write-side ingestion surge has nothing to do with it.
scenario: 名人事件让发帖量瞬间涨 10 倍，而 ingestion 是帖子进索引的唯一通道，NFR 要求新帖 1 分钟可搜。
scenario_en: A celebrity event spikes posting tenfold; ingestion is the only path a post takes into the index, and the SLA says new posts are searchable within a minute.

scenario: 发帖 10k/s 且有突发流量，ingestion 需要扩容、削峰，并把负载分摊到多个实例上。
scenario_en: At 10K posts/s with bursts, ingestion needs scaling, smoothing, and load distribution across instances.
q: 标准解法是？
q_en: What is the standard solution?
options: 让客户端不断重试直到成功
给每台 ingestion 配更大内存
用关系型数据库充当消息队列来缓冲并暂存这些高频写入事件
用 Kafka 日志/流：分区摊负载 + 缓冲突发
why: Kafka 一石三鸟：分区把负载分摊到多实例、日志天然缓冲突发流量、事件持久化避免丢失；这是写扩展的标准工具。
why_en: A Kafka log fans requests out across partitioned ingestion instances while buffering bursts so no events are lost.
whenOtherWins: 流量小且无突发时，直接同步调用 ingestion 更简单，省去引入消息系统的运维成本。
diagram:
flowchart LR PS[Post Service] --> K["Kafka 日志
分区 + 缓冲突发"] LS[Like Service] --> K K --> I1["Ingestion 实例 1"] K --> IN["Ingestion 实例 N"] I1 --> R["Redis 索引
按 keyword 分片"] IN --> R
options_en: Have clients keep retrying until they succeed.
Give each ingestion box more memory.
Use a relational database as the message queue to buffer and hold these high-frequency write events.
Use a Kafka log/stream: partition to spread load and buffer bursts.
tradeoff: 引入消息系统的运维成本 vs 削峰/分区/不丢事件

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

optionExplanations: 客户端重试在洪峰下只会叠加更多请求，火上浇油。
堆内存只是纵向扩容，单机终究还是瓶颈。
关系型数据库的吞吐撑不住高频事件流，当队列用会先垮。
分区把负载摊到多实例，日志天然缓冲突发，还顺带持久化不丢事件。
optionExplanations_en: Client-side retries during a surge only pile on more requests, making the flood worse.
More memory is just vertical scaling; one box remains the eventual bottleneck.
A relational database's throughput can't sustain a high-frequency event stream as a queue — it buckles first.
Partitioning spreads load across instances, the log naturally buffers bursts, and persistence keeps events from being lost.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 索引写入量巨大，单个 Redis 实例吃不下所有关键词的写入与存储。
scenario_en: Index write volume is huge, and one Redis instance cannot hold all keyword writes and storage.
q: 索引层的扩展方式是？
q_en: How should the index layer scale?
options: 直接换用一台内存更大的单机
让每一个 Redis 实例都各自保存一份完整的全量索引副本
按 keyword 分片到多个 Redis 实例
把索引整体搬回关系型数据库
why: 按关键词分片后，每个 Redis 实例只负责一部分词的索引，写入和存储都水平摊开；查询按词路由到对应分片即可。
why_en: Sharding the inverted index by keyword spreads writes and storage across many Redis instances, with each query routed to its keyword's shard.
whenOtherWins: 全量复制适合读扩展而非写扩展；若单个超热关键词本身超过一个节点的承载，还需要对该 key 再做拆分或复制。
options_en: Just switch to a single box with more memory.
Have every Redis instance keep its own full copy of the entire index.
Shard by keyword across multiple Redis instances.
Move the index entirely back to a relational database.
tradeoff: 按词分片摊写 vs 全量复制只摊读

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

optionExplanations: 单机内存总有上限，纵向扩容撑不住持续增长的写入和存储。
全量复制摊的是读压力，写入还是全部打在同一份数据上。
按词分片后每个实例只扛一部分词，写入和存储都水平摊开。
关系型数据库不是为这种高频 key-value 写入设计的，会成为新瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: A single box's memory has a ceiling; vertical scaling can't keep up with ever-growing writes and storage.
Full replication spreads read load, but every write still lands on the same copy of the data.
Sharding by keyword lets each instance carry only part of the terms, spreading both writes and storage.
A relational database isn't built for this kind of high-frequency key-value write pattern and becomes the new bottleneck.

q: 在「写入频率」这个维度上，点赞和发帖的关系是？
q_en: On write frequency, how do likes compare with posts?
options: 点赞约是发帖的 10 倍，点赞更新才是大象
发帖的频率反而是点赞的 10 倍，写优化重心该放在发帖上
两者数量级相当
点赞量小到可以忽略
why: 每人每天 10 赞 vs 1 帖，点赞写入量高一个数量级；而且每个赞都要更新多个关键词的 sorted set score，是写路径优化的头号目标。
why_en: Likes arrive ten times more often than posts and each one touches many index keys, making like ingestion the elephant in the room.
options_en: Likes run about 10x posts, so like updates are the elephant in the room.
Posts run 10x likes, so write optimization should center on posting.
They're the same order of magnitude.
Likes are negligibly small.
tradeoff: 点赞高频(100k/s) vs 发帖低频(10k/s)——写优化重心在点赞
optionExplanations: 每人每天 10 赞对 1 帖，点赞写入量高出一个数量级，是写优化的头号目标。
估算方向刚好说反了，实际是点赞远多于发帖。
一个数量级的差距称不上「相当」，点赞明显更重。
点赞恰恰是写路径里量级最大的一块，谈不上可以忽略。
optionExplanations_en: At 10 likes versus 1 post per person per day, likes run a full order of magnitude higher — the prime target for write optimization.
This has the direction backwards; likes actually far outnumber posts.
A full order of magnitude apart isn't 'comparable' — likes are clearly the heavier load.
Likes are in fact the single largest chunk of write volume, nowhere close to negligible.
scenario: 10 亿用户每人每天发 1 帖、点 10 个赞，你要决定写路径先优化哪一类事件。
scenario_en: A billion users each post once and like ten times a day — you decide which write type the write path should optimize first.

scenario: 爆款帖 30 秒内涌入 500 个赞，每个赞都要单独更新它所有关键词的索引，写入量不可接受。
scenario_en: A viral post gets 500 likes in 30 seconds, and every like would update every keyword index for that post.
q: 第一步优化是？
q_en: What is the first optimization?
options: 随机丢弃掉其中一部分点赞事件
把点赞改成每天只在固定时刻统一结算一次总数
加 batcher：30 秒窗口聚合同帖点赞
直接砍掉按点赞数排序的功能
why: batcher 在 30 秒窗口内把同一帖的赞合并成一次增量更新，爆款帖从 500 次写变 1 次；聚合结果回写 Kafka 保持管道统一。
why_en: A batcher aggregates likes per post over a thirty-second window and emits one summed update, collapsing five hundred writes into one.
whenOtherWins: 对点赞稀疏均匀的普通帖（每分钟 1 赞），窗口内只有 1 个事件、无从合并，batcher 反而白添延迟和组件。
options_en: Randomly drop some of the incoming like events.
Change likes to settle just once a day at a fixed time.
Add a batcher: aggregate a post's likes over a 30-second window.
Just cut the sort-by-like-count feature.
tradeoff: 多写 30 秒延迟换爆款帖的写入合并 vs 每赞即写

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间窗口内聚合同一帖的点赞，再一次性写回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batcher aggregates the likes for one post over a time window into a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

optionExplanations: 丢事件会让赞数失真，牺牲正确性换性能不可取。
日结算的陈旧程度远超 1 分钟可见性承诺，会击穿 SLA。
窗口内合并同帖的赞，爆款帖从 500 次写变成 1 次，立竿见影。
砍掉按赞排序是丢功能，没有真正解决写入压力。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping events makes like counts wrong; trading correctness for speed isn't acceptable.
Settling once a day is far staler than the one-minute visibility promise and would break the SLA.
Merging a post's likes within a window collapses five hundred writes into one for a viral post — an immediate win.
Cutting sort-by-likes just removes a feature instead of actually solving the write pressure.

q: batcher 方案的关键局限是？
q_en: What is the key limitation of the batcher approach?
options: 会永久丢失点赞总数
消息系统在架构设计上完全不支持二次重复写入
排序会彻底错乱
多数帖不爆款：均匀点赞窗口内无可合并，总量没降
why: 合并只对「窗口内多次点赞同一帖」有效；一天 1440 赞若均匀分布，批处理照样要写 1440 次——整体写入量由长尾普通帖决定，而它们恰恰无从批起。
why_en: Since most posts are not viral, evenly spaced likes offer nothing to batch, so overall write volume barely drops while overhead grows.
options_en: It permanently loses the total like count.
The messaging system doesn't support writing twice.
Sorting gets completely scrambled.
Most posts aren't viral: evenly spaced likes can't be batched, so total volume barely drops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间窗口内聚合同一帖的点赞，再一次性写回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batcher aggregates the likes for one post over a time window into a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

optionExplanations: batcher 只是延迟合并写入，总数依然被完整统计，不会丢失。
消息系统完全能承受重复写入，这不是 batcher 的限制来源。
batcher 只改变写入时机，不动排序逻辑，排序不会乱。
普通帖点赞稀疏均匀，窗口内往往只有 1 个事件，合并无从谈起。
optionExplanations_en: The batcher just delays and merges writes; the total count is still fully tallied, never lost.
Messaging systems handle repeated writes fine — that's not where the batcher's limitation comes from.
The batcher only changes write timing, not sort logic, so ordering doesn't get scrambled.
Most posts get likes sparsely and evenly, so a window usually holds just one event — nothing to merge.
scenario: 有人提议用 batcher 把 1 秒窗口内对同一帖的点赞合并，但绝大多数帖子一天只有零星几个赞。
scenario_en: Someone proposes a batcher that merges likes on the same post within a one-second window, but the vast majority of posts get only a handful of likes all day.

scenario: 想让点赞的索引写入量随点赞数指数级下降，且可以接受索引里的计数不精确。
scenario_en: You want like-index writes to fall exponentially with like count, and approximate indexed counts are acceptable.
q: 更好的方案是？
q_en: What is the better approach?
options: 固定每 100 个赞写一次
从今往后彻底不再更新 likes 这份索引、任由计数停在初始值
只统计每帖前 1000 个赞
只在跨越 2 的幂里程碑时更新，1000 赞≈10 次写
why: 按 2 的幂打点，写入次数从与点赞数成正比降到对数级——1000 赞只要约 10 次写；对所有帖子生效，不依赖「是否爆款」。
why_en: Updating the index only when likes cross powers of two cuts writes exponentially, so a thousand likes cost about ten index updates.
whenOtherWins: 若产品要求索引里的数字直接精确展示给用户，里程碑打点不可用，只能回到全量或批量更新。
options_en: Write once per fixed 100 likes.
Stop updating the likes index entirely, letting counts freeze at their initial value.
Only count the first 1000 likes per post.
Update only when likes cross powers of two — 1000 likes about 10 writes.
tradeoff: 索引计数精确性 vs 写入次数(对数级)

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在计数跨过阈值（如 2 的幂）时才写索引，把写入降为对数级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Milestone updates only write when a count crosses thresholds like powers of two.

optionExplanations: 固定间隔对爆款帖仍是线性写入次数，没有真正压低量级。
彻底不更新会让按赞排序失效，等于放弃这个需求。
只统计前 1000 赞让排序在超过阈值后失真，不够普适。
按 2 的幂打点把写入次数压到对数级，1000 赞只需约 10 次写。
optionExplanations_en: A fixed interval still means linear write counts for viral posts — it doesn't really cut the order of magnitude.
Stopping updates entirely breaks sort-by-likes, effectively abandoning that requirement.
Capping the count at 1000 distorts ordering once posts pass that threshold — not a universal fix.
Marking updates at powers of two drops write counts to logarithmic — about 10 writes for 1000 likes.

q: 里程碑更新给索引带来的本质变化是？
q_en: What does milestone updating fundamentally change about the index?
options: 索引从此彻底不可用
结果排序会变得完全随机、失去参考价值
赞数天生陈旧，但排序近似正确
只有新发布的帖会受影响
why: 计数只在跨里程碑时更新，所以永远滞后真实值；但相对大小关系基本保持、排序「近似正确」——这正是可以用第二阶段精排修复的那类误差。
why_en: The indexed like counts become inherently stale, yet the ordering stays approximately correct since a post with ten thousand likes still ranks far above one with a single like.
options_en: The index becomes completely unusable.
Result ordering becomes fully random and loses all reference value.
Counts are inherently stale, but ordering stays approximately correct.
Only newly published posts are affected.
optionExplanations: 索引依然可用，只是计数不再是精确实时值。
相对大小关系基本保持，排序不会变成随机。
计数永远滞后真实值，但量级差距仍能撑起大致正确的名次。
所有帖子的赞数都按里程碑打点，新老帖一视同仁。
optionExplanations_en: The index is still perfectly usable; it's just the count that's no longer exact and live.
Relative magnitudes mostly hold, so ordering doesn't turn random.
Counts always lag the true value, but the gap in magnitude still keeps ranking roughly right.
Every post's like count follows the same milestone rule — old and new posts alike.
scenario: 点赞索引改成只在 1、10、100、1000… 这些里程碑上更新 score，而排序结果仍要可用。
scenario_en: The likes index only bumps its score at milestones like 1, 10, 100 and 1000, yet the ranking still has to be usable.

scenario: likes index 里的计数是近似值，但返回给用户的排序和数字必须基于最新数据。
scenario_en: The likes index stores approximate counts, but returned ordering and numbers must use fresh data.
q: 查询时怎么补救？
q_en: How do you fix this at query time?
options: 直接把索引里的近似值原封不动返回给用户展示
取 2N 候选，用实时赞数重排，返回前 N
每次查询前重建索引
给近似值乘一个修正系数
why: 近似索引负责「把对的帖子捞进候选集」（多取一倍留冗余），实时计数负责精排；存储是近似的，最终结果却是精确的。
why_en: Fetch twice as many candidates from the approximate index, look up fresh like counts from the like service, re-sort, and return the top N.
whenOtherWins: 若近似排序对产品已经够用（不展示精确数字），跳过重排少一次服务调用，延迟更低。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Search Service
    participant I as 近似 Likes Index
    participant L as Like Service
    S->>I: 取 top 2N 候选
    I-->>S: 近似排序的 postIds
    S->>L: 批量查实时赞数
    L-->>S: 新鲜计数
    Note over S: 按实时计数重排，返回前 N 条
options_en: Return the approximate indexed values directly to users for display.
Fetch 2N candidates, re-rank with fresh like counts, and return the top N.
Rebuild the index before every query.
Multiply the approximate value by a correction factor.
tradeoff: 多一次 Like Service 调用 vs 最终结果精确

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用便宜的近似层召回候选，再用昂贵的精确层重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage architecture retrieves cheaply then re-ranks precisely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护每个帖子实时、精确点赞数的上游服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Like Service holds the live, exact like count for each post.

optionExplanations: 直接展示近似值等于把陈旧数字和排序都暴露给用户。
多取一倍候选留冗余，再用实时计数重排，存储近似、结果精确。
查询前重建万亿级索引的成本完全不现实。
陈旧误差跟点赞数无关的固定倍数，乘系数修不了它。
optionExplanations_en: Returning the approximate value directly exposes both stale numbers and stale ordering to users.
Over-fetching twice as many candidates and re-ranking with live counts keeps storage approximate but the result exact.
Rebuilding a trillion-entry index before every query is completely unrealistic.
Staleness isn't a fixed multiple of the like count, so a correction factor can't fix it.

q: 「近似的便宜候选层 + 昂贵的精确重排层」这种两阶段架构，常见于哪些领域？
q_en: Where is the two-stage pattern of cheap approximate candidates plus expensive exact re-ranking commonly used?
options: 支付清算系统
DNS 域名解析
信息检索与推荐系统
数据库事务引擎
why: 检索/推荐系统普遍先用便宜的近似服务捞候选，再用昂贵的模型或新鲜数据精排；本题的近似 likes index + 实时重排正是这个模式的实例。
why_en: The two-stage pattern of a cheap approximate retrieval layer backed by an expensive precise re-ranker is ubiquitous in information retrieval and recommender systems.
options_en: A payment settlement system.
DNS name resolution.
Information retrieval and recommender systems.
A database transaction engine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用便宜的近似层召回候选，再用昂贵的精确层重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage architecture retrieves cheaply then re-ranks precisely.

optionExplanations: 支付清算追求强一致和精确金额，跟近似召回的模式不搭边。
DNS 解析是精确查找，不涉及近似候选和重排。
先便宜召回、再精确重排是检索和推荐系统的经典两阶段模式。
事务引擎讲究 ACID，跟这种近似优先的架构方向相反。
optionExplanations_en: Payment settlement demands strong consistency and exact amounts, nothing like approximate recall.
DNS resolution is an exact lookup, with no approximate candidates or re-ranking involved.
Cheap recall followed by precise re-ranking is the textbook two-stage pattern in retrieval and recommenders.
Transaction engines revolve around ACID guarantees, the opposite direction from an approximation-first design.
scenario: 本设计先用近似 likes index 捞候选、再用实时赞数精排，你要判断它属于哪种通用架构模式。
scenario_en: This design pulls candidates from an approximate likes index and then re-ranks them with fresh counts — name the general architecture pattern.

q: 采用里程碑近似计数后，把索引里的字段改名为 logLikes / approxLikes 的目的是？
q_en: After milestone approximate counting, why rename the index field to logLikes or approxLikes?
options: 改名昭示语义已变，别把近似值当精确数用
为了节省存储空间
为了兼容更旧版本的 API 接口协议
为了提升查询速度
why: 近似化改变了字段语义，最大的工程风险是后来者误信这个数字；用命名把「这是近似值」编码进接口，是廉价而有效的防误用手段。
why_en: Renaming the field to approxLikes signals its changed semantics so developers never mistake the stale approximate count for a precise one.
options_en: The rename signals the changed semantics so no one treats the approximate value as exact.
To save storage space.
To stay compatible with the old API version.
To speed up queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在计数跨过阈值（如 2 的幂）时才写索引，把写入降为对数级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Milestone updates only write when a count crosses thresholds like powers of two.

optionExplanations: 把「近似」两个字放进字段名本身，后来者一看命名就不会当成精确值使用。
改名字符数几乎不占空间，跟存储优化没有关系。
改名本身反而可能破坏旧接口兼容性，不是为了兼容。
字段名不影响查询执行路径，跟速度无关。
optionExplanations_en: The field name bakes 'this is approximate' into the API so no one later mistakes it for exact.
A field's character count barely touches storage; renaming isn't a storage optimization.
Renaming can actually break old-API compatibility rather than preserve it.
A field name doesn't touch the query execution path, so it has nothing to do with speed.
scenario: 索引里的 likes 字段改成里程碑近似值后，下游团队仍会直接读它做展示和统计。
scenario_en: Once the likes field in the index holds milestone approximations, downstream teams will still read it directly for display and analytics.

q: 把点赞写入优化的演进逻辑排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the evolution of like-write optimization in the correct order:
steps: 发现局限：多数帖子点赞稀疏均匀，batcher 无从合并、反添开销
问题：100k likes/秒，每个赞都要更新多个索引 key，写入压力最大
升级方案：只在跨越 2 的幂里程碑时写索引，写入量指数级下降
第一次尝试：batcher 按 30 秒窗口聚合同帖点赞
兜底：查询时取 2N 候选、用实时计数重排，最终结果依然精确
why: 这条演进链是本题最精彩的深挖：从批处理（只救爆款）到里程碑打点（普适、指数省写），再用两阶段精排把近似误差在查询时修复。
why_en: The like-write optimization evolves from windowed batching, which only helps viral posts, to milestone-based updates with a two-stage re-rank restoring precision at query time.
diagram:
graph TD
    Direct[Update every like] --> Hot[Hot posts overload index]
    Hot --> Batch[Batch like updates]
    Batch --> Milestone[Milestone score changes]
    Milestone --> Rerank[Precise rerank at query time]
tradeoff: 批处理只救爆款 vs 里程碑普适降写

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间窗口内聚合同一帖的点赞，再一次性写回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batcher aggregates the likes for one post over a time window into a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在计数跨过阈值（如 2 的幂）时才写索引，把写入降为对数级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Milestone updates only write when a count crosses thresholds like powers of two.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用便宜的近似层召回候选，再用昂贵的精确层重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage architecture retrieves cheaply then re-ranks precisely.

scenario: 关键词 Mark 的倒排列表有 1000 万个 postId，但用户几乎只看排序最前的一小撮结果。
scenario_en: The inverted list for keyword Mark has 10 million post IDs, but users almost always view only the top results.
q: 最直接的存储优化是？
q_en: What is the most direct storage optimization?
options: 压缩每个 postId 的二进制编码格式来省空间
采购更便宜的内存
直接删除这个关键词
给每个索引设上限(1k-10k)，砍掉长尾
why: 检索场景里用户只消费头部结果，每个索引留 1k-10k 条已覆盖真实需求；截断把索引存储压缩掉几个数量级，是性价比最高的一刀。
why_en: Capping each keyword's index at a few thousand entries discards the never-viewed tail and cuts storage by orders of magnitude.
whenOtherWins: 若「所有帖子可发现」必须严格兑现，被截断的长尾要有另一条可达路径（如冷存储或离线扫描），不能一删了之。
options_en: Compress each post ID's binary encoding to save space.
Buy cheaper memory.
Just delete this keyword.
Cap each index at 1k-10k entries, dropping the long tail.
tradeoff: 截断长尾省存储 vs 长尾可发现性

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

optionExplanations: 压缩编码只省几个字节，对千万级列表只是杯水车薪。
换便宜内存治标不治本，列表还是会持续膨胀。
删掉整个词连头部结果都没了，用户搜不到这个词。
用户只看头部结果，留 1k-10k 条就够，能把存储压掉几个数量级。
optionExplanations_en: Compressing the ID encoding saves a few bytes at best — a drop in the bucket for a ten-million-entry list.
Cheaper memory treats the symptom, not the cause; the list keeps growing regardless.
Deleting the whole term loses even the top results — users can no longer find that keyword at all.
Users only ever look at top results, so keeping 1k-10k entries covers demand while cutting storage by orders of magnitude.

scenario: 搜索分析显示大多数关键词一个月内很少甚至从未被搜索，但它们的索引仍占着昂贵的 Redis 内存。
scenario_en: Search analytics show most keywords are rarely or never searched monthly, yet their indexes occupy expensive Redis memory.
q: 合理的处理方式是？
q_en: What is the reasonable handling?
options: 直接删掉冷门关键词的整份索引
把全部关键词索引不分冷热都统一搬去 S3 对象存储
冷门词索引下沉 S3，查询 Redis 优先
给冷门关键词也保留一份内存副本
why: 按访问分析做冷热分层：冷词索引下沉到便宜的 blob 存储，Redis 只留热词；查询路径 Redis 优先、blob 兜底，冷查询慢一点——恰好被 NFR 允许。
why_en: A batch job demotes rarely searched keyword indexes from Redis to cheap blob storage, and queries fall back to the blob with a small latency penalty on a miss.
whenOtherWins: 若所有关键词都要求同样的低延迟（没有「冷查询可以慢」的豁免），就无法下沉，只能靠截断和压缩控制内存成本。
diagram:
flowchart TD
    Q["关键词查询"] --> R{"Redis 命中?"}
    R -- "是: 热词" --> F["毫秒级返回"]
    R -- "否: 冷词" --> B["S3/R2 冷索引"]
    B --> S["稍慢返回 (NFR 允许)"]
    J["月度批任务: 按搜索分析"] -. 冷词下沉 .-> B
options_en: Just delete cold keywords' whole index.
Move all keyword indexes to S3 uniformly, hot and cold alike.
Demote cold keyword indexes to S3; query Redis first, fall back to blob.
Keep an in-memory copy for cold keywords too.
tradeoff: 冷词下沉省内存 vs 命中 blob 的延迟惩罚

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

optionExplanations: 删掉整份索引违反「所有帖子可发现」的需求，代价太大。
热词也搬去 S3 会让高频查询集体变慢，得不偿失。
冷词按访问频次挪去便宜的对象存储，内存只留给真正的热词，读的时候先探 Redis、扑空再落到那边。
冷词也留内存副本等于没省下真正想省的内存开销。
optionExplanations_en: Deleting the whole index breaks the 'every post stays discoverable' requirement — too high a cost.
