Moving hot terms to S3 too would slow down every frequent query — a net loss.
Demote cold terms to blob storage based on access analytics, keep Redis for hot terms, and query Redis first with blob as fallback.
Keeping an in-memory copy for cold terms too defeats the whole point of saving memory.

q: 冷索引下沉 S3 之所以成立，靠的是哪条前面埋好的需求？
q_en: Which earlier requirement makes demoting cold indexes to S3 valid?
options: 「老帖冷帖可发现但允许更慢」这条 NFR
系统必须高可用
新帖 1 分钟内可搜
中位查询延迟低于 500ms 这条线
why: 需求阶段特意写下「冷数据可以慢」，深挖阶段它兑现为冷存储的设计许可——好的需求定义会为后面的权衡预留空间。
why_en: The requirement that old or unpopular posts may be served more slowly is exactly what licenses the blob-storage latency penalty for cold keywords.
options_en: The NFR that old/cold posts stay discoverable but may be slower.
The system must be highly available.
New posts searchable within one minute.
Median latency under 500ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟、吞吐、可用性这类衡量系统「好不好」的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover latency, throughput, and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外承诺的服务指标，如「新帖 1 分钟内可搜」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is a promised service level, e.g. new posts searchable within a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: 需求阶段特意留下「冷数据可以慢」的口子，才撑得起下沉 blob 的设计。
高可用要求系统不能挂，跟单次查询慢一点是两回事。
1 分钟可见约束的是新帖的可发现时限，不是冷数据的读延迟。
500ms 说的是中位延迟，冷查询本就被允许排除在这条线之外。
optionExplanations_en: The requirements phase deliberately left room for 'cold data can be slower,' which is what licenses demoting it to blob.
High availability means the system can't go down; that's separate from one query being a bit slower.
The one-minute constraint bounds when a new post becomes discoverable, not the read latency of cold data.
500ms is a median-latency target, and cold queries are exactly the ones allowed to fall outside it.
scenario: 把冷门关键词的索引从 Redis 下沉到 S3，单次 S3 读取要几百毫秒，远慢于内存。
scenario_en: Demoting cold keyword indexes from Redis to S3 costs hundreds of milliseconds per read, far slower than memory.

scenario: FB Post Search 估算：3.6 万亿帖 × 1KB ≈ 3.6PB；优化方向是把每个关键词索引截断到 1k-10k 条，并给冷结果留 blob 兜底。
scenario_en: FB Post Search estimates 3.6 trillion posts at 1 KB each, about 3.6 PB; the design caps keyword indexes at 1K-10K entries and uses blob fallback for cold results.
q: 这两个数字在存储优化链条里说明什么？
q_en: What do these two numbers say in the storage-optimization chain?
text: 3.6PB 说明{{全量内存索引不可持续}}；1k-10k 截断说明{{只把热结果留在快路径}}，冷门/长尾结果下沉到 blob。
why: 3.6PB 是粗估公式结果，1k-10k 是工程阈值/产品取舍，不是唯一真值。它们共同支持「热结果内存化、冷结果下沉」的设计。
why_en: The petabyte estimate shows a full in-memory index is impossible, while the one-to-ten-thousand cap keeps hot results fast and pushes cold results to blob storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: PB 是存储单位，1PB 约等于 1000TB，用来表达海量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A petabyte is a storage unit equal to roughly one thousand terabytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

q: 读路径最前端的 API 网关承担什么职责？
q_en: What does the API gateway do at the front of the read path?
options: 分词与构建索引
存储搜索结果
鉴权 + 限流，再转发给搜索服务
更新每个帖子的点赞计数字段并维护其排序
why: 网关是读路径的门卫：认证 + 限流之后转发给可水平扩展的无状态搜索服务；索引查询等重活在后面的服务层完成。
why_en: The API gateway handles authentication and rate limiting before passing requests to the horizontally scaled search service.
diagram:
graph LR
    Client --> Gateway[API Gateway]
    Gateway --> Cache[(Result cache)]
    Cache -->|hit| Client
    Cache -->|miss| Search[Search Service]
    Search --> Index[(Inverted index)]
options_en: Tokenizing and building the index.
Storing search results.
Authentication and rate limiting, then forwarding to the search service.
Updating each post's like-count field and its ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径最前端的入口，负责鉴权、限流后转发给后端服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway authenticates and rate-limits requests before forwarding them.

optionExplanations: 分词建索引发生在写路径的 ingestion，不是网关的职责。
网关不持久化任何数据，存储结果是后端服务的事。
网关是读路径的门卫：认证、限流之后转发给可扩展的搜索服务。
更新点赞计数属于写路径，跟读路径最前端的网关无关。
optionExplanations_en: Tokenizing and index building happen in write-path ingestion, not at the gateway.
The gateway persists nothing; storing results is a backend service's job.
The gateway is the read path's gatekeeper: authenticate and rate-limit, then forward to the scalable search service.
Updating like counts belongs to the write path, unrelated to the read path's front door.
scenario: 搜索读流量 10k/s 且可能突发 10 倍，读路径最前端要挡住滥用请求并保护后端搜索服务。
scenario_en: Search reads run at 10K per second and can burst tenfold, so the front of the read path has to fend off abuse and shield the search service.

q: creation index 用 Redis list 而 likes index 用 sorted set，本质区别在哪个维度？
q_en: What dimension explains why the creation index uses a Redis list while the likes index uses a sorted set?
options: list 的内存开销更大
排序键是否可变：时间到达即定序，赞数持续变要维序
sorted set 从结构上就不支持按区间做范围查询这类操作
list 不能存储字符串
why: 时间序是「天然到达顺序」，list 追加零成本维持；赞数是会变的分数，必须用 sorted set 在每次更新后仍保持有序。
why_en: Creation order is fixed at arrival so a list suffices, while like counts keep changing and need a sorted set to maintain order by score.
options_en: A list uses more memory.
Whether the sort key is mutable: arrival time is fixed on append, while like counts keep changing.
A sorted set structurally doesn't support range queries over an interval.
A list can't store strings.
tradeoff: 固定顺序(list 追加) vs 可变分数(sorted set 维序)

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

optionExplanations: 两种结构的内存开销差异不是这里的决定因素。
时间是到达即定的顺序，list 追加免费维持；赞数会变，必须靠 sorted set 按分数动态维序。
sorted set 恰恰擅长按分数做范围查询，这不是它的短板。
list 可以存字符串，这不是它跟 sorted set 的真实区别。
optionExplanations_en: Memory overhead between the two structures isn't what drives this choice.
It comes down to whether the sort key changes: arrival time is fixed so a list's append keeps order for free, while like counts keep changing and need a sorted set's score-based ordering.
A sorted set is actually great at score-range queries; that's not where it falls short.
A list can hold strings just fine — that's not the real difference from a sorted set.
scenario: creation index 按时间排序、likes index 按赞数排序；赞数每秒都在变，时间戳写入后不再变。
scenario_en: The creation index is ordered by time and the likes index by like count; like counts change every second while timestamps never change after the write.

q: 本题控制索引存储的手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which techniques control index storage in this design?
options: 每个关键词的索引截断到 1k-10k 条
按搜索分析把冷门关键词索引迁到 S3/R2 blob 存储
查询路径 Redis 优先、blob 兜底
把全部索引都换成 bigram 索引
why: 存储三板斧：截断长尾、冷词下沉 blob、读路径热冷两级兜底；bigram 恰恰是增加存储的功能性投资，不是省存储的手段。
why_en: Storage is tamed by capping each index, demoting cold keywords to blob storage, and querying Redis first with a blob fallback.
options_en: Cap each keyword's index at 1k-10k entries.
Demote cold keyword indexes to S3/R2 blob storage per search analytics.
Query Redis first with a blob fallback.
Convert all indexes to bigram indexes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相邻两个词组成的 token，Lucene 里叫 shingle，用于短语查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bigram (Lucene calls it a shingle) is a token made of two adjacent words.

optionExplanations: 截断长尾能把单个热词的索引存储压掉几个数量级。
冷词下沉 blob 把内存压力转移到便宜存储，只留热词占内存。
Redis 优先、blob 兜底让读路径在省内存的同时不牺牲热查询速度。
bigram 是为短语查询加的功能性投资，只会让索引更大，不是省存储的手段。
optionExplanations_en: Capping the long tail cuts one hot keyword's index storage by orders of magnitude.
Demoting cold terms to blob storage shifts memory pressure onto cheap storage, leaving only hot terms in RAM.
Redis-first with blob fallback saves memory on the read path without sacrificing hot-query speed.
Bigrams are a feature investment for phrase queries that grows the index — not a storage-saving technique.
scenario: 万亿帖 × 每帖 10-100 个关键词的倒排索引全放内存成本爆炸，热查询却仍要守住 500ms。
scenario_en: A trillion posts times 10 to 100 keywords each makes an all-in-memory inverted index unaffordable, yet hot queries must stay under 500ms.

q: 这对索引写入负载意味着什么？
q_en: What does this imply for index write load?
options: 一次发帖被放大成几十上百次索引写，双索引再翻倍
写入与发帖 1:1，没有放大
关键词在用户查询时才临时生成，发帖阶段根本不写索引
Redis 会自动展开，只写一次
why: 帖子按词拆解通常落在 10-1000 个关键词，一次发帖被放大成几十上百次索引写；双索引还要再乘 2，这是写压力的根源。
why_en: A post tokenizes into roughly 10 to 1000 keywords, so a single post fans out into dozens to hundreds of index writes, doubled again by the dual indexes.
scenario: 一个 100 词的帖子发布后，Ingestion 要为它拆出的每个关键词写索引。
scenario_en: After a 100-word post is published, ingestion must write index entries for each tokenized keyword.
options_en: One post fans out into tens-to-hundreds of index writes — doubled by dual indexes.
Writes match posts 1:1, with no amplification.
Keywords are generated only at query time, so posting writes nothing to the index.
Redis expands it automatically with a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把帖子内容拆解成一个个可匹配关键词的过程，中文叫分词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization breaks a post into individual searchable keywords.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写在底层被放大成多次物理写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification turns one logical write into many physical writes.

optionExplanations: 100 词的帖子拆成上百个关键词，每词一次写，双索引还要再乘 2。
拆词天然带来放大，写入次数远不止 1:1。
关键词是发帖时拆好写入索引的，查询时索引早已建好。
Redis 不会替你把一次写自动展开成多份，展开逻辑要 ingestion 自己做。
optionExplanations_en: A 100-word post tokenizes into around a hundred keywords, one write each, doubled again by the dual indexes.
Tokenization inherently amplifies writes; the count is nowhere close to 1:1.
Keywords are tokenized and written at post time; the index is already built before any query runs.
Redis doesn't auto-expand one write into many for you — ingestion has to do that fan-out itself.

q: 补全两阶段查询的推理：
q_en: Fill in the reasoning for two-stage querying:
text: 因为索引里的赞数是{{近似}}的，查询时先取 {{2N}} 个候选，再用 Like Service 的{{实时}}计数重排——存储是近似的，最终结果却是精确的。
why: 这条推理概括两阶段的精髓：近似候选 + 实时精排；多取一倍候选是为近似误差留出冗余。
why_en: Because indexed counts are approximate, we over-fetch twice the needed candidates and re-rank them with fresh counts from the like service.

rows: 近似 term 匹配(便宜)

tradeoff: 近似候选(便宜) vs 精确重排(新鲜)

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用便宜的近似层召回候选，再用昂贵的精确层重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage architecture retrieves cheaply then re-ranks precisely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护每个帖子实时、精确点赞数的上游服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Like Service holds the live, exact like count for each post.

q: Ingestion 服务在写路径上的完整职责是？
q_en: What is the ingestion service's complete responsibility on the write path?
options: 收事件 → 拆词 → postId 写两份索引
负责读路径的鉴权与限流
缓存最热门的搜索结果
为每条新发布的帖子生成一个全局唯一的帖子 ID
why: ingestion 是索引的唯一写入方：拆词、写双索引、处理点赞 score 更新；它的吞吐与可靠性决定「新帖 1 分钟可搜」能否兑现。
why_en: The ingestion service consumes post and like events, tokenizes content, and writes the post ID into both indexes for every keyword.
options_en: Consume events, tokenize, and write the post ID into both indexes for every keyword.
Handle authentication and rate limiting on the read path.
Cache the most popular search results.
Generate a globally unique post ID for every newly published post.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把帖子内容拆解成一个个可匹配关键词的过程，中文叫分词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization breaks a post into individual searchable keywords.

optionExplanations: ingestion 是索引唯一的写入方：拆词后把 postId 写进两份索引。
鉴权限流是网关的职责，发生在读路径最前端。
缓存热门结果属于读路径优化，不是 ingestion 该管的事。
生成唯一 ID 通常由上游 Post Service 负责，ingestion 只消费事件。
optionExplanations_en: Ingestion is the index's only writer: it tokenizes each post and writes the post ID into both indexes.
Auth and rate limiting are the gateway's job, at the very front of the read path.
Caching popular results is a read-path optimization, not something ingestion handles.
Generating a unique ID is normally the upstream Post Service's job; ingestion just consumes events.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索写路径要吃 10k 帖/秒 + 100k 赞/秒的事件，并保证新帖 1 分钟内可被搜到。
scenario_en: The FB Post Search write path consumes 10K posts and 100K likes per second and must make new posts searchable within a minute.

q: batcher 的数字对比：30 秒窗口内 500 赞的爆款帖 vs 均匀 1 赞/分钟（一天 1440 赞）的普通帖，批处理各省下多少写入？
q_en: In batching, how many writes are saved for a viral 500-like window versus an ordinary post with one like per minute?
options: 爆款 500→1 次；普通帖 1440 次照旧
两者的索引写入次数最终都能降到只剩 1 次
两者其实都得不到任何节省
普通帖反而能节省得更多
why: 批处理的收益完全取决于窗口内的事件密度：爆款 500→1，普通帖每个窗口只有 1 个事件、1440 次照旧——这就是为什么还需要里程碑方案。
why_en: Batching collapses a viral post's five hundred likes into one write but saves nothing for a post liked once per minute, which still needs all fourteen hundred forty writes.
scenario: batcher 用 30 秒窗口聚合同一帖的点赞后再写索引。
scenario_en: The batcher aggregates likes for the same post over a 30-second window before writing the index.
options_en: Viral: 500 to 1 write; ordinary post: still 1440 writes.
Both of them ultimately drop to just a single write.
Neither of them gets any savings at all.
The ordinary post actually saves more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间窗口内聚合同一帖的点赞，再一次性写回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batcher aggregates the likes for one post over a time window into a single write.

optionExplanations: 批处理收益取决于窗口内事件密度：爆款高密度合并多，普通帖每窗口只 1 个事件合并不了。
普通帖每个窗口只有 1 次点赞，天然没有可合并的对象。
爆款帖 500 次写合并成 1 次，节省是实打实存在的。
普通帖恰恰因为点赞稀疏均匀而合并不了，节省更少而非更多。
optionExplanations_en: Batching's payoff tracks event density in the window: viral posts merge a lot, ordinary posts have just one event per window to merge.
An ordinary post gets only one like per window, so there's nothing there to merge in the first place.
A viral post's 500 writes really do collapse into 1 — that saving is real.
Ordinary posts save less, not more, precisely because their likes are too sparse and even to merge.

q: 本题的核心非功能需求有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the core non-functional requirements for this problem?
options: 中位查询 <500ms，且支撑高请求量
新帖 <1 分钟内可被搜索
所有帖子（含老帖冷帖）可被发现、系统高可用
向用户展示强一致的精确点赞计数
why: 五条 NFR：快（500ms）、大流量、新帖 1 分钟可见、全量可发现（冷帖可慢）、高可用；「索引内精确点赞计数」从来不是承诺——后面才敢用近似索引。
why_en: The system must be fast, handle high volume, surface new posts within a minute, keep every post discoverable, and stay highly available.
options_en: Median query under 500ms while handling high volume.
New posts searchable within one minute.
Every post (including old/cold) discoverable; system highly available.
Show users a strongly consistent, exact like count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟、吞吐、可用性这类衡量系统「好不好」的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover latency, throughput, and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外承诺的服务指标，如「新帖 1 分钟内可搜」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is a promised service level, e.g. new posts searchable within a minute.

optionExplanations: 延迟和吞吐是明确给定的目标，直接约束索引和缓存设计。
新帖可见时限约束着索引流水线的延迟上限。
全量可发现+高可用是底线要求，撑起后面冷热分层的设计许可。
精确点赞计数从未被承诺，后面才敢用近似索引换写入性能。
optionExplanations_en: Latency and throughput are explicitly given targets that directly constrain the index and cache design.
The new-post visibility deadline bounds how much delay the indexing pipeline can tolerate.
Full discoverability plus high availability is the baseline that licenses the later hot-cold split.
An exact, strongly consistent like count was never promised — that's exactly what licenses the approximate index later.
scenario: 为 FB 帖子搜索定非功能需求：10 亿用户、万亿帖，后面还打算用近似点赞计数来省写入。
scenario_en: Setting non-functional requirements for FB Post Search across a billion users and a trillion posts, knowing you plan to approximate like counts later to cut writes.

q: 用纯内存 Redis 存放唯一一份倒排索引，宕机的直接风险与解决方向是？
q_en: If pure in-memory Redis stores the only inverted index copy, what is the direct crash risk and solution direction?
options: 查询会变慢但索引数据不会丢
索引可能丢失，需 MemoryDB 持久化兜底
宕机只影响新发布的那些帖子
CDN 会自动兜底并帮忙把丢失的索引数据恢复回来
why: 内存即易失：节点宕机索引就没了，重建万亿级索引代价巨大；文章的态度是「可解」——换 MemoryDB 等持久化兼容方案或作为专门深挖。
why_en: A crash can wipe the in-memory index, so you need a durable alternative like MemoryDB or a dedicated recovery story.
options_en: Queries slow down but the index data isn't lost.
The index can be lost; use MemoryDB for durability.
A crash only affects newly published posts.
The CDN automatically recovers the lost index data for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 兼容 Redis 接口但带持久化的内存数据库，可弥补纯内存的易失性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MemoryDB is a durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database.

optionExplanations: 内存本质易失，节点宕机时数据同样会丢，不只是变慢。
纯内存的唯一副本一旦宕机就可能整体丢失，得靠 MemoryDB 之类持久化方案兜底。
宕机丢的是整份索引，新旧帖子一样受影响。
CDN 只缓存 HTTP 响应，不负责恢复后端的索引数据。
optionExplanations_en: Memory is inherently volatile; a node crash loses data too, not just slows queries.
A single in-memory copy can vanish entirely on a crash, so a durable option like MemoryDB has to back it up.
A crash wipes the whole index, affecting old and new posts alike, not just new ones.
A CDN only caches HTTP responses; it has no role in restoring the backend index.
scenario: 唯一一份倒排索引放在纯内存 Redis 里，重建万亿帖索引要几天，而 NFR 要求高可用。
scenario_en: The only copy of the inverted index lives in pure in-memory Redis, rebuilding a trillion-post index takes days, and the SLA demands high availability.

q: 交集之后为什么还要「拉原文验证短语」这一步？
q_en: After intersection, why must you fetch the original text and verify the phrase?
options: 因为交集算法本身在求交过程中存在精度损失
为了顺便统计点赞数
两词都含≠短语连续，须回原文过滤假阳性
为了给缓存预热
why: 单词级索引只知道「词出现过」，不知道相邻关系；短语语义要求连续出现，必须回原文核验，否则会返回风马牛不相及的结果。
why_en: Posts containing both words separately, like Taylor made a swift exit, are false positives that only a phrase check against the original text can filter out.
options_en: Because the intersection algorithm itself loses precision while intersecting.
To count likes along the way.
Both words present does not mean a contiguous phrase, so re-check the text to filter false positives.
To warm up the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 看似匹配、实则不满足条件的结果，这里指含两词但非连续短语。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive looks like a match but is not one, e.g. both words present but not adjacent.

optionExplanations: 交集运算本身精确无误，问题出在「含两词」不等于「短语连续」。
验证短语跟统计点赞数是两套完全不相关的逻辑。
单词级索引只知道词出现过，不知道相邻关系，必须回原文核验连续性。
验证短语发生在查询路径，跟缓存预热不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: The intersection itself is exact; the gap is that containing both words isn't the same as a contiguous phrase.
Verifying a phrase and counting likes are two completely unrelated pieces of logic.
A word-level index only knows a term appeared, not adjacency, so you must re-check the original text for contiguity.
Phrase verification happens on the query path, unrelated to warming any cache.
scenario: 搜 "Taylor Swift" 时对两个单词索引求交，候选帖里这两个词可能相隔十几个字。
scenario_en: Searching "Taylor Swift" intersects two single-word indexes, and in the candidates those two words may sit a dozen words apart.

q: batcher 与里程碑更新在「对哪类帖子有效」这个维度上的区别是？
q_en: How do batcher and milestone updates differ on which posts they help?
options: 两者其实都只对少数几个高密度的爆款帖才有效
batcher 只救爆款；里程碑对所有帖普适
里程碑只对新帖有效
两者效果完全等价
why: batcher 的收益取决于窗口内事件密度（爆款专属）；里程碑与密度无关，任何帖子的写入次数都变成对数级，是更普适的一招。
why_en: Batching only helps posts with dense like bursts, whereas milestone updates cut every post's writes to a logarithmic count regardless of virality.
options_en: Both only help a handful of high-density viral posts.
Batching only helps viral posts; milestones help every post universally.
Milestones only help new posts.
They're exactly equivalent.
tradeoff: batcher 依赖点赞密度(爆款) vs 里程碑与密度无关(普适)

rows: 窗口内密集点赞的爆款

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间窗口内聚合同一帖的点赞，再一次性写回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batcher aggregates the likes for one post over a time window into a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在计数跨过阈值（如 2 的幂）时才写索引，把写入降为对数级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Milestone updates only write when a count crosses thresholds like powers of two.

optionExplanations: 里程碑不依赖点赞密度，对稀疏点赞的普通帖同样有效。
batcher 收益看窗口内事件密度，只帮爆款；里程碑跟密度无关，所有帖写入都降到对数级。
里程碑按点赞数打点，跟帖子新旧无关，老帖同样适用。
两者生效范围截然不同：一个挑爆款，一个覆盖全体。
optionExplanations_en: Milestones don't depend on like density, so they help sparsely-liked ordinary posts too.
Batching's payoff hinges on event density in the window, helping only viral posts; milestones are density-independent and cut every post's writes to logarithmic.
Milestones fire based on like count, unrelated to how new a post is — old posts benefit just the same.
Their reach is completely different: one targets viral posts, the other covers every post.
scenario: 点赞 100k/s 压垮 sorted set 更新，你要在 batcher 与里程碑更新之间选一个普适的减写手段。
scenario_en: Likes at 100K per second overwhelm sorted-set updates, so you pick between a batcher and milestone updates as your general write-reduction lever.

q: 交集法与 bigram 索引处理短语查询，核心权衡的维度是？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between intersection and bigram indexing for phrase queries?
options: 正确性 vs 可用性
查询计算成本 vs 索引存储成本
分布式系统的一致性 vs 分区容忍性
两者没有实质区别
why: 交集法零索引膨胀但每次查询付「传输 + 求交」的读成本；bigram 把成本预付在索引体积上，换取读时一击命中——读写成本搬运的经典权衡。
why_en: Intersection pays at query time with expensive transfers and set operations, while bigrams pay upfront with a much larger index for instant phrase lookups.
options_en: Correctness vs availability.
Query compute cost vs index storage cost.
Distributed-system consistency vs partition tolerance.
No real difference.
tradeoff: 交集法读时贵 vs bigram 存储贵

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相邻两个词组成的 token，Lucene 里叫 shingle，用于短语查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bigram (Lucene calls it a shingle) is a token made of two adjacent words.

optionExplanations: 两种方案给出的结果都正确，可用性也不是这里的分歧点。
交集法把成本留到查询时的传输和求交；bigram 把成本预付进索引体积，换查询一击命中。
这是单机数据结构的选型问题，跟分布式系统的 CAP 权衡不沾边。
两者在读时开销和索引体积上的差异非常真实，不是无差别的选择。
optionExplanations_en: Both approaches return correct results, and availability isn't the axis in play here either.
Intersection defers cost to query time — transfer and set operations; bigrams prepay that cost as a bigger index for an instant hit.
This is a single-node data-structure choice, unrelated to the CAP tradeoff in distributed systems.
The gap between read-time cost and index size is real and substantial, not an inconsequential choice.
scenario: 短语查询要么查询时求交、要么预先建 bigram 索引；存储预算和 500ms 延迟预算都很紧。
scenario_en: Phrase queries either intersect at query time or precompute a bigram index, and both the storage budget and the 500ms latency budget are tight.

q: 对这个你自己清楚的过度简化，正确的沟通动作是？
q_en: What's the right way to handle this over-simplification you know about?
options: 保持沉默，等面试官自己发现再解释
主动声明这是过度简化、稍后回来解决
当场停下，把摄取层拆成两个服务做完
只在图上标注，但口头不提及
why: 面试官会主动挑刺，未声明的缺陷会被默认为你没看见；主动认领并承诺回填，既保住推进速度又证明你看到了问题。代价是欠下一个必须兑现的 TODO。
why_en: Interviewers hunt for flaws, and an unacknowledged one is assumed to be one you missed; saying it out loud keeps your momentum while proving you saw it.
options_en: Stay silent and explain only if the interviewer notices.
Proactively flag it as over-simplified and promise to revisit.
Stop now and split ingestion into two services.
Annotate the diagram but never say it aloud.
optionExplanations: 沉默会被解读为你没看出这个规模失衡，越晚暴露越糟。
认领缺陷加承诺稍后解决，既不打断推进又展示了判断力。
当场展开会掉进兔子洞，牺牲了高层设计要求的推进速度。
面试官不一定读你的注释，口头不提等同于没声明。
optionExplanations_en: Silence reads as you missing the scale imbalance; the later it surfaces, the worse.
Owning the flaw and promising a fix keeps momentum and shows judgment.
Stopping to build it now rabbit-holes and sacrifices high-level-design pace.
The interviewer may not read your note; not saying it aloud is not flagging it.
scenario: 点赞每秒约 100k、发帖约 10k，规模差一个量级；你为快速推进先用单一摄取服务，而面试官正逐处审你的设计找缺陷。
scenario_en: Likes run ~100k/s versus ~10k/s posts, an order-of-magnitude gap, yet you use one ingestion service to move fast while the interviewer scans your design for flaws.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收发帖/点赞事件、拆词并写入倒排索引的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ingestion service receives post and like events, tokenizes them and writes to the inverted indexes.

q: 相比简单的批处理窗口，落地里程碑方案多付出的主要代价是？
q_en: Versus a simple batching window, what is milestone counting's main added cost?
options: 索引占用的存储直接翻倍
实现复杂度和工程投入明显更高
结果排序变得不可用
对普通(非爆款)帖子完全失效
why: 里程碑要维护「下一个触发阈值」、判断是否跨越、还要把计数语义改成 approxLikes，比「30 秒窗口累加」多不少代码；换来的是写入随赞数对数增长。
why_en: Milestone logic must track the next threshold and detect crossings, far more code than a 30-second window, buying writes that grow only logarithmically with likes.
options_en: Index storage doubles outright.
Higher implementation complexity and engineering effort.
Result ordering becomes unusable.
It stops working for ordinary (non-viral) posts.
optionExplanations: 存储翻倍是「创建+点赞双索引」的代价，不是里程碑计数带来的。
维护阈值、判断跨越、改计数语义，都比窗口累加复杂得多。
排序仍近似正确，量级差距还在，并没有不可用。
失效于普通帖的是批处理窗口，里程碑对各类帖都能压缩写入。
optionExplanations_en: Doubled storage is the cost of the dual creation+likes index, not of milestones.
Tracking thresholds, detecting crossings and changing semantics all beat a window in complexity.
Ordering stays approximately correct; the magnitude gap holds, so it's not unusable.
It is the batching window that fails on ordinary posts; milestones cut writes for all posts.
scenario: 点赞索引改用里程碑计数：只在赞数跨过 2 的幂(1,2,4,8…)时才写一次，把 1000 次写压到约 10 次。
scenario_en: The likes index switches to milestone counting: it writes only when a count crosses a power of two (1,2,4,8…), turning 1000 writes into about 10.

termDefinitions.meaning: 里程碑计数下索引里的近似赞数字段，明确告知开发者它并非精确实时值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: approxLikes is the milestone-based approximate like-count field, signalling to developers that it is not exact or live.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把某帖一段时间(如 30 秒)内的点赞聚合成一次写入的方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batching window aggregates a post's likes over a fixed period (e.g. 30s) into a single write.

q: 作为 Senior，剩余时间的重心应该放在？
q_en: As a senior candidate, where should the rest of your time go?
options: 继续补更多功能需求，追求最大广度
深入优化关键路径，把取舍讲透
主动走完多个深挖并给面试官带来新认知
反复打磨 API 和数据模型的细节
why: 面试官对 Senior 期望约 40% 深度：快速过完高层设计，把时间花在关键路径优化；底线是双路径、正确倒排、合理缓存都在。
why_en: For a senior, interviewers expect ~40% depth: speed through the high-level design and spend the time optimizing the critical paths.
options_en: Keep adding more functional requirements for maximum breadth.
Go deep on the critical paths and articulate the tradeoffs.
Proactively finish several deep dives and teach the interviewer something new.
Keep polishing the API and data-model details.
optionExplanations: 一味追求广度是 Mid 级打法，Senior 要拿出深度。
关键路径(写放大、缓存、点赞索引)讲透取舍，正好对上 40% 深度的期望。
主动走完多个深挖并带来新认知是 Staff+ 的 bar，Senior 不做到也行。
API 和数据模型是基础，反复打磨挤占了关键路径优化的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Chasing breadth is a mid-level move; a senior is expected to bring depth.
Nailing the critical-path tradeoffs (write amplification, cache, likes index) matches the ~40% depth bar.
Finishing several deep dives and teaching the interviewer is the staff+ bar, not required of a senior.
The API and data model are basics; polishing them eats the time meant for critical-path work.
scenario: 你是 Senior 候选人做 FB 帖子搜索，面试官期望约 40% 深度；你已快速画完含倒排索引的可用高层设计。
scenario_en: You are a senior candidate on FB post search; the interviewer expects ~40% depth, and you have quickly drawn a working high-level design with an inverted index.
whenOtherWins: 若你是 Staff+ 候选人，仅把关键路径讲透还不够——面试官期望约 60% 深度，要主动走完多个深挖并给面试官带来新认知。
tradeoff: Senior 讲透关键路径(40%深度) vs Staff+ 多个深挖+新认知(60%深度)

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定系统性能与正确性的主链路，本题指摄取写放大、缓存、点赞索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the chain that governs performance and correctness — here ingestion write amplification, caching and the likes index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把关键词映射到包含它的帖子 ID 列表的索引，是本题搜索的核心结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs containing it — the core search structure here.

q: 什么最能体现 Staff+ 的水准？
q_en: What best signals a staff+ level performance?
options: 把 API 和数据模型这些基础讲得格外细致
高层设计一带而过，主动多走几个深挖
严格覆盖全部功能需求的广度
画完高层设计后深入优化一条关键路径
why: 面试官已默认 Staff+ 懂 REST、数据规范化等基础，期望约 60% 深度：主动走完多个深挖，并让面试官带走新认知。
why_en: Interviewers already assume a staff+ knows the basics, so they expect ~60% depth: proactively work through several deep dives and leave them with new insight.
options_en: Explain the API and data-model basics in unusually fine detail.
Breeze through the high-level design and proactively take on several deep dives.
Rigorously cover the breadth of every functional requirement.
Draw the high-level design, then deeply optimize one critical path.
optionExplanations: 基础(REST、规范化)面试官已默认你会，细讲反而浪费宝贵的深度时间。
略过基础、主动多走深挖，正是 60% 深度并带来新认知的体现。
只顾广度是 Mid 打法，缺了 Staff+ 要的深度和主动性。
深入一条关键路径是 Senior 的 bar，Staff+ 要走完多个深挖。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer already assumes you know the basics (REST, normalization); detailing them wastes depth time.
Skipping basics and driving several deep dives is exactly the ~60% depth with new insight.
Breadth-only is a mid-level move, missing the depth and proactivity a staff+ needs.
Going deep on one critical path is the senior bar; a staff+ works through several deep dives.
scenario: 你是 Staff+ 候选人做同一道题，面试官期望约 60% 深度，且已知你懂 REST、数据规范化等基础。
scenario_en: You are a staff+ candidate on the same question; the interviewer expects ~60% depth and already assumes you know REST, data normalization and other basics.
whenOtherWins: 若你是 Senior 候选人，深入一条关键路径就够了——面试官只期望约 40% 深度，不要求走完多个深挖或带来新认知。
tradeoff: Staff+ 多个深挖+带来新认知 vs Senior 讲透一条关键路径

termDefinitions.meaning: REST(表述性状态转移)：一种基于 HTTP 动词和资源 URL 的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an API style built on HTTP verbs and resource URLs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个瓶颈或子系统的深入优化讨论，如写放大、缓存、冷存储分层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is an in-depth optimization discussion of one bottleneck or subsystem, such as write amplification, caching or cold-storage tiering.

scenario: 45 分钟面试要设计 Google Docs：只做纯文本协同编辑，权限与版本历史被面试官明确划出范围。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to design Google Docs, scoped to plain-text collaborative editing, with permissions and version history explicitly ruled out.
q: 设计 Google Docs 时，以下哪些属于核心功能需求（in scope）？（多选）
q_en: When designing Google Docs, which items are core in-scope functional requirements?
options: 多个用户并发编辑同一文档
实时看到其他协作者的修改
文档权限与协作级别管理
看到其他用户的光标位置与在场状态
why: 核心需求是：创建文档、多人并发编辑、实时看到彼此修改、光标/在场。权限、版本历史、复杂文档结构都被明确划到 out of scope。
why_en: The core requirements are creating documents, concurrent editing, seeing each other's changes in real time, and cursor presence, while permissions and versioning are out of scope.
options_en: Multiple users editing the same document concurrently
Seeing collaborators' changes in real time
Managing document permissions and collaboration levels
Seeing other users' cursor positions and presence
optionExplanations: 多人同时改同一份文档是协同编辑的定义，系统必须处理并发写入，这是范围内的核心能力。
光有并发编辑还不够，还要让每个人几乎实时看到别人的改动，这条决定了要上低延迟推送通道。
权限模型（谁能读/写/评论）没被列进这道题要做的功能，设计先只管协同编辑本身。
光标位置和在场状态让协作者知道谁在、在哪编辑，是 awareness 体验的数据基础。
optionExplanations_en: Multiple people editing the same document at once is the definition of collaborative editing, so the system has to handle concurrent writes as a core requirement.
Seeing each other's changes almost immediately is what makes editing feel collaborative, and it's why the design needs a low-latency push channel.
Access-control roles never made it onto this design's feature list, so it stays focused purely on the editing mechanics.
Cursor position and presence tell collaborators who's in the document and where, which is the data behind the awareness feature.

scenario: 面试官说：把文档当成一个纯文本框，先把多人同时编辑做对，其余能力一律后置。
scenario_en: The interviewer says to treat the document as a plain text box and get concurrent multi-user editing right first, deferring everything else.
q: 以下哪一项被明确划为 out of scope（不做）？
q_en: Which item is explicitly out of scope for this Google Docs design?
options: 多人同时编辑一份文档
文档历史与版本回退
实时同步彼此的修改
显示协作者光标
why: 版本历史、权限管理、富文本复杂结构都不在范围内——假设一个简单的纯文本编辑器，聚焦协同编辑本身。
why_en: Document history and versioning, permissions, and rich document structure are explicitly out of scope so the design can focus on collaboration itself.
options_en: Multiple people editing one document at once
Document history and version rollback
Real-time syncing of everyone's changes
Showing collaborators' cursors
optionExplanations: 并发编辑本身是核心功能，不是被排除的一项。
版本历史和回退需要额外存储和界面支持，这道题把它明确划出范围，先聚焦协同编辑本身。
实时同步彼此的修改正是这个产品的核心承诺，同样在范围内。
显示协作者光标是 awareness 体验的一部分，也在范围内。
optionExplanations_en: Concurrent editing is a core in-scope feature, not the excluded one.
Version history and rollback need extra storage and UI, and this design explicitly puts them out of scope to stay focused on collaboration itself.
Real-time syncing of edits is the product's core promise, so it stays in scope.
Showing collaborator cursors is part of the awareness experience, also in scope.

scenario: 设计一个 Google Docs 类协同编辑器：用户要实时看到编辑结果，单文档协作者有限，但全站用户和文档数量很大。
scenario_en: You are designing a Google Docs-style collaborative editor where edits must feel real time, one document has bounded collaborators, and the whole service has many users and documents.
q: 这些非功能数字各自约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Complete the non-functional constraints and the design consequence for Google Docs.
text: 更新延迟低于 {{100ms}}，所以编辑通道要用低延迟长连接；单文档最多 {{100}} 个编辑者，所以中心式 OT 可行；数{{百万}}并发用户要求 WebSocket 水平扩展；数十{{亿}}文档要求操作日志压实。
why: 这些是给定目标，不是推导结果；它们分别约束实时通道、并发编辑算法、连接层扩展和存储压实。数字的用途是把后面的架构选择收窄。
why_en: These are input constraints, not facts to memorize: they drive the real-time channel, the OT choice, WebSocket scaling, and log compaction.

scenario: 为一套全球办公套件设计协同编辑器：人人都能建文档，但同一份文档很少超过几十人同时编。
scenario_en: We're sizing a collaborative editor for a global office suite: everyone creates documents, but a single doc rarely has more than a few dozen simultaneous editors.
q: Google Docs 类协同文档编辑器的规模目标（非功能需求）是？
q_en: What scale target should this Google Docs-style collaborative editor support?
options: 数千用户、数百万文档
数百万并发用户、数百万文档
数百万并发用户、数十亿文档
数十亿并发用户、数十亿文档
why: 目标是数百万并发用户、数十亿文档。计数单位是连接：连接数 ≈ 并发用户 × 1 条 WebSocket；单文档编辑者 ≤100，所以单文档吞吐只是次要成本。
why_en: The target is millions of concurrent users and billions of documents, and the unit that actually scales is connections — roughly one WebSocket per concurrent user — while per-document throughput stays small because editors are capped at 100.
options_en: Thousands of users, millions of documents
Millions of concurrent users, millions of documents
Millions of concurrent users, billions of documents
Billions of concurrent users, billions of documents
optionExplanations: 数千用户、数百万文档低估了产品级流量，会让容量设计偏小。
并发用户量级对，但文档规模被低估——十亿级文档意味着存储和压实要另算一笔账。
百万级并发用户、十亿级文档是这道题给定的量级锚点，后续连接数和存储设计都围绕它展开。
十亿级并发用户超出了协同文档产品的现实规模，把目标定得过大。
optionExplanations_en: Thousands of users and millions of documents undershoots the real product scale and would size capacity too small.
The user count is right, but billions of documents is the harder number — it drives storage and compaction planning, not just connections.
Millions of concurrent users and billions of documents is the scale anchor this design works from for connection count and storage sizing.
Billions of concurrent users overshoots what a collaborative document product realistically needs to support.

scenario: 协同编辑打算用 OT：需要一台服务器独占一份文档来定全序，服务器容量就是扩展上限。
scenario_en: We plan to use OT, where one server exclusively owns a document to totally order edits, so that server's capacity is the scaling ceiling.
q: 「单文档最多 100 个并发编辑者」这条约束给设计带来什么好处？
q_en: What design benefit comes from capping one document at 100 concurrent editors?
options: 反正编辑者少，可以完全不做持久化处理
反正编辑者少，可以放弃低延迟实时性要求
反正编辑者少，可以放心选择最终一致以外的更强一致模型
单文档写吞吐有上限，让中心式 OT 服务器变得可行
why: 限制编辑者数量意味着单文档流量有上限，可以放心用「一台服务器独占一个文档」的 OT 架构。真实的 Google Docs 也这么做：超过上限后新用户只能以读者身份加入。
why_en: Capping concurrent editors bounds per-document throughput, which is exactly what makes a central OT server per document feasible, and real Google Docs does the same by demoting overflow users to readers.
options_en: Editors are few, so persistence can be skipped entirely
Editors are few, so the low-latency real-time requirement can be dropped
Editors are few, so a stronger-than-eventual consistency model can safely be used
Per-document write throughput stays bounded, making a central OT server feasible

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 编辑者数量不影响持久性要求，重启后文档仍要可恢复，这个好处不成立。
编辑者少不代表可以牺牲响应速度，实时手感是协同编辑的核心承诺，跟人数无关。
一致性模型的选择取决于「协同天然会短暂分歧」，跟编辑者数量没有因果关系。
把编辑者数量摁住，就等于把单文档写吞吐摁住，中心式 OT 服务器才扛得住这份责任。
optionExplanations_en: A smaller editor count doesn't relax durability — documents still need to survive a restart, so this benefit doesn't hold.
Fewer editors doesn't excuse dropping responsiveness; the real-time feel is core to collaborative editing regardless of headcount.
The consistency model follows from collaboration naturally diverging briefly, not from how many editors there are.
Pinning down the editor count pins down per-document write throughput, which is what makes a central OT server able to carry that load.

scenario: 两个协作者几乎同时输入，各自客户端先在本地应用再发服务器；产品只要求大家最终屏幕一致。
scenario_en: Two collaborators type at almost the same instant, each client applies locally first, and the product only requires everyone to end up seeing the same document.
q: Google Docs 类协同文档编辑器对文档内容选择的一致性模型是？
q_en: What consistency model should the document content use in a Google Docs-style editor?
options: 最终一致：所有用户最终看到相同的文档状态
强一致：每次编辑全员立即同步可见
读己之写一致：只保证自己看到自己刚写入的内容
因果一致且不允许任何乱序
why: 协同编辑天然会有短暂分歧（各自本地先应用），要求的是收敛：不管操作以什么顺序到达，所有副本最终一致。
why_en: The document is eventually consistent, meaning replicas may briefly diverge but every user converges on the same final state.
options_en: Eventual consistency: all users eventually see the same document state
Strong consistency: every edit is visible to everyone instantly
Read-your-writes: only guarantees you see your own just-written content
Causal consistency with no reordering allowed
optionExplanations: 协同编辑允许短暂分歧，只要最终所有副本收敛到同一文档，这正是这里要的一致性承诺。
强一致要求每次编辑立刻全员可见，代价是要阻塞写入，百万并发根本扛不住。
读己之写只保证自己看到自己的改动，不保证收敛到统一状态，不是协作要的收敛保证。
因果一致要求严格保序，对文本编辑来说保证过强也没必要，OT/CRDT 只需要收敛。
optionExplanations_en: Collaborative editing tolerates brief divergence as long as every replica converges on the same final document, which is exactly the guarantee needed here.
Strong consistency would make every edit visible everywhere instantly, which means blocking writes — not survivable at millions of concurrent users.
Read-your-writes only guarantees you see your own edit, not that everyone converges on one state, so it misses the point of collaboration.
Causal consistency demands strict ordering, which is stronger than text editing needs — OT and CRDT only require eventual convergence.

scenario: Document Service 把操作先收在内存里再广播，但运维每周滚动重启实例，用户的编辑不能丢。
scenario_en: Document Service buffers operations in memory before broadcasting, but ops restarts instances weekly and no user edit may be lost.
q: 「服务器重启后文档仍然可用」这条持久性需求，对写路径的直接约束是？
q_en: If documents must survive a server restart, what does that require on the write path?
options: 所有文档必须常驻内存，重启就会丢失编辑
编辑必须全部走客户端本地存储，服务器不落盘
编辑写入持久化存储成功后才向用户确认
必须使用强一致关系数据库才能持久化
why: 持久性意味着操作不能只留在服务器内存里：先落库（操作日志），成功后再 ack 给用户，重启后可从库中重放恢复。
why_en: Durability means an edit is acknowledged only after it is recorded in persistent storage, so a server restart can replay the log instead of losing work.
options_en: All documents must stay resident in memory — a restart loses every edit
Every edit must go through client-side local storage, with nothing written on the server
An edit is acknowledged to the user only after it is durably written to storage
A strongly consistent relational database is required for durability
optionExplanations: 把文档全放内存等于放弃持久化承诺，进程一重启编辑就没了。
只写客户端本地存储，别的协作者和服务器都看不到这份编辑，协作根本无从谈起。
落库成功再确认，是这条约束下唯一能保证重启后可恢复的做法。
持久性只要求「写下来能恢复」，不等于必须上强一致关系数据库，日志型存储也能满足。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping every document only in memory abandons durability outright — a restart wipes every edit.
Client-only local storage never reaches the server or other collaborators, so it can't support real collaboration at all.
Acknowledging only after a durable write is the one approach here that guarantees recovery after a restart.
Durability just means the write can be replayed on recovery; it doesn't force a strongly consistent relational database — an append-only log works too.

scenario: 为纯文本协同编辑器画数据模型：权限与版本历史不在范围，只需支撑并发编辑和光标在场。
scenario_en: We're modeling data for a plain-text collaborative editor where permissions and versioning are out of scope, so it only has to support concurrent editing and cursor presence.
q: 以下哪些是这个设计的核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which entities are core to this collaborative document design?
options: Document（文档）
Cursor（光标/在场）
Permission（权限）
Edit（编辑操作）
why: 四个核心实体：Editor（编辑者）、Document（文档）、Edit（一次修改）、Cursor（光标位置与在场）。权限被划出范围，不是实体。
why_en: The core entities are the editor, the document, the edit, and the cursor with presence, while permissions are out of scope.
options_en: Document
Cursor (position and presence)
Permission
Edit (a change operation)
optionExplanations: 文档承载内容、元数据和版本指针，是所有其他实体挂靠的中心对象。
光标把位置和在场状态绑在一起，是 awareness 功能追踪和广播的数据源。
权限被划出范围，管访问不属于这道题要建模的实体。
一次编辑操作是协同流的基本单位，OT/CRDT 都围绕它运转。
optionExplanations_en: The document carries content, metadata, and a version pointer — the central object every other entity attaches to.
The cursor bundles position and presence together, feeding the data that awareness tracking and broadcast rely on.
Permissions are out of scope here, so access control isn't one of the entities this design models.
A single edit operation is the basic unit of the collaboration stream, and both OT and CRDT operate on it.

scenario: 协作者要实时看到别人正在文档的哪个位置打字，而这份数据只在对方在线时才有意义。
scenario_en: Collaborators need to see in real time where others are typing, and that data only means anything while those people are still online.
q: Cursor 这个实体承载的是什么信息？
q_en: What information does the Cursor entity carry?
options: 文档内容的最新完整快照，跟光标无关
光标位置和在场状态（presence）
这次编辑操作生成时的时间戳记录
该用户在系统里的权限访问级别
why: Cursor 既是位置也是在场信号：它告诉其他协作者「谁在这份文档里、正在哪儿编辑」，是 awareness 功能的数据基础。
why_en: The cursor entity captures both where an editor's caret sits and that user's live presence in the document.
options_en: The latest full snapshot of the document content, unrelated to the cursor
Cursor position plus presence state
The timestamp recorded when this edit operation was generated
This user's permission and access level in the system
optionExplanations: 完整内容快照是文档实体的信息，不是 Cursor 要携带的东西。
Cursor 把「光标在哪」和「这个人还在不在线」绑在一起，正是 awareness 需要的两件事。
时间戳是操作日志的属性，用来定序，不属于 Cursor 实体。
权限级别归 Permission 管，这道题已经把权限划出范围。
optionExplanations_en: A full content snapshot belongs to the Document entity, not to Cursor.
Cursor ties together where the caret sits and whether that person is still online — exactly the two things awareness needs.
A timestamp belongs to the operation log for ordering, not to the Cursor entity.
Permission level is the Permission entity's job, and permissions are out of scope for this design anyway.

scenario: 编辑过程中客户端要高频发送小操作（插入/删除/移动光标），服务器也要随时把别人的操作推回来，往返延迟要求 < 100ms。
scenario_en: During editing, clients send frequent small operations like inserts, deletes, and cursor moves, while the server must push other users' operations back with under 100 ms round-trip latency.
q: 编辑通道最合适的通信方式是？
q_en: What communication method best fits the editing channel?
options: 客户端每秒轮询 REST 接口
WebSocket 双向长连接
每次编辑发一个独立 HTTP POST
SSE 单向推送
why: 协同编辑是典型的高频双向场景：客户端持续发操作，服务器持续推别人的操作，WebSocket 的双向长连接正好匹配。
why_en: Collaborative editing needs high-frequency bidirectional messages under one hundred milliseconds, which is exactly what a persistent WebSocket connection provides.
whenOtherWins: 低频的请求-响应操作（创建文档、改标题这类元数据管理）用普通 REST 更简单；只需服务器单向推送时 SSE 也够。
diagram:
graph LR
    Client[Editor client] <--> WS[WebSocket server]
    WS --> Collab[Collaboration service]
    Collab --> Log[(Operation log)]
    Collab --> Peers[Other editors]
tradeoff: WebSocket 双向长连接 vs REST 轮询/单向推送
options_en: Client polls a REST endpoint once a second
A bidirectional WebSocket connection
Send each edit as its own HTTP POST
One-way SSE push from server to client

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向长连接，适合高频双向通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server, well suited to high-frequency two-way messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器单向持续推送更新给客户端的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, or Server-Sent Events, lets a server continuously push updates to a client in one direction only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于标准 HTTP 方法的请求-响应风格接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is a request-response API style built on standard HTTP methods.

optionExplanations: REST 轮询每秒才问一次，延迟和无谓请求都撑不住 <100ms 的编辑体验，更适合创建文档这类低频操作。
WebSocket 只用一次握手就能维持一条双向管道，插入、删除、光标移动都能挤在同一条连接上来回跑，天然贴合编辑器的收发节奏。
每次编辑单开一个 HTTP POST，连接建立开销比编辑本身还贵，量一大就先被压垮。
SSE 只能服务器往客户端推，没有上行通道，客户端发操作还是得另开一条路，适合纯只读的更新流。
optionExplanations_en: Polling REST once a second adds real latency and wasted requests, so it fits low-frequency operations like creating a document, not sub-100ms editing.

WebSocket needs one handshake to hold open a two-way pipe, so inserts, deletes, and cursor moves can all ride the same connection in both directions — a natural fit for the editor's send-and-receive rhythm.
Opening a fresh HTTP POST per edit pays connection overhead bigger than the edit itself, and collapses under real typing volume.
SSE only pushes server to client with no upstream channel, so edits would still need a separate path — it fits a read-only update stream instead.

scenario: 客户端与 Document Service 之间只有一条 WebSocket 长连接，创建文档这类管理操作仍走 REST。
scenario_en: The client keeps a single long-lived WebSocket to Document Service, while admin calls like creating a document still go over REST.
q: 读这份 WebSocket 协议草案：客户端发送（SEND）和接收（RECV）的消息类型分别是？
q_en: In this WebSocket protocol draft, which message types does the client send and receive?
options: SEND: update；RECV: insert/delete/updateCursor
SEND 和 RECV 都是 update
SEND: insert/delete/updateCursor；RECV: update
全部通过 REST 端点完成
why: 客户端把自己的 insert/delete/updateCursor 发上去，服务器把别人已确认的操作打包成 update 推回来；文档创建这类管理操作仍走 REST。
why_en: Clients send insert, delete, and cursor updates over the socket while the server pushes back update messages, with document creation staying on a REST endpoint.
options_en: SEND carries update; RECV carries insert, delete, and updateCursor
Both SEND and RECV use a generic update message
SEND carries insert, delete, and updateCursor; RECV carries update
Everything happens through REST endpoints

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向长连接，适合高频双向通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server, well suited to high-frequency two-way messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于标准 HTTP 方法的请求-响应风格接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is a request-response API style built on standard HTTP methods.

optionExplanations: 方向反了：草案里是客户端 SEND 三类编辑消息，服务器 RECV 后再广播 update，不是反过来。
把 SEND/RECV 都写成通用 update 抹掉了协议里客户端发意图、服务器发结果这个区分。
SEND 走三类编辑意图，RECV 只回一种确认结果，这个不对称正是草案要表达的协议分工。
文档创建走 REST 没错，但编辑操作本身走的是这条 WebSocket，不是全部走 REST。
optionExplanations_en: The direction is backwards: the client SENDs the three edit types and the server RECVs then broadcasts update, not the other way around.
Collapsing both SEND and RECV into a generic update message erases the distinction between client intent and server-confirmed result.
SEND carries three kinds of edit intent while RECV only ever answers with one confirmation type — that asymmetry is exactly the protocol split the draft defines.
Document creation does use REST, but the edit messages themselves ride this WebSocket, not REST end to end.

scenario: 要在设计文档里写下协同编辑的 API，而编辑走的是一条长连接，不是一次一个 HTTP 请求。
scenario_en: We're writing down the collaborative-editing API, and edits flow over one long-lived connection rather than one HTTP request each.
q: API 设计里引入 WebSocket 后，表达方式上要注意什么？
q_en: When adding WebSocket to the API design, what should the API description focus on?
options: 把每条消息单独定义成一个 HTTP 端点
WebSocket 是一条长连接，本身不需要定义任何消息协议
描述连接上收发的消息 schema，而非 HTTP 端点
必须使用 protobuf 编码才算合格
why: WebSocket 是一条长连接，API 设计要描述连接上流动的消息类型和结构；具体记法随意，但要能讲清楚线上传的是什么。
why_en: With websockets you describe the messages flowing over the connection rather than HTTP endpoints, and any clear notation for the message schema works.
options_en: Define every message as its own HTTP endpoint
WebSocket is just a long-lived pipe, so no message protocol needs defining
Describe the message schema flowing over the connection, not HTTP endpoints
You must use protobuf encoding to be valid

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向长连接，适合高频双向通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server, well suited to high-frequency two-way messaging.

optionExplanations: 把每条消息拆成独立 HTTP 端点，等于用请求-响应的框架硬套一条持续连接，只会制造冗余定义。
完全不定义协议会让客户端和服务器各自猜消息格式，协作起来全靠运气。
描述连接上流动的消息 schema——每种消息长什么样、谁发谁收——才是 WebSocket 该写的 API 文档。
protobuf 只是众多编码之一，JSON 或其他清晰记法同样能把消息说明白，不是强制项。
optionExplanations_en: Treating every message as its own HTTP endpoint forces a request-response frame onto a persistent connection and just creates redundant definitions.
Leaving the protocol fully undefined leaves client and server guessing at message shapes, which breaks interoperability.
Describing the message schema flowing over the connection — what each message looks like and who sends and receives it — is what a WebSocket API doc should cover.
Protobuf is just one encoding option; JSON or any clear notation communicates the schema fine, so it isn't mandatory.

scenario: 存文档元数据（标题、docId，将来可能挂权限、标签），需要灵活查询，初期规模不大、以后可以再分区复制。
scenario_en: Document metadata such as title and docId needs flexible queries; the initial scale is modest, and partitioning or replication can be added later.
q: 元数据库的合理默认选型是？
q_en: What is the sensible default database for document metadata?
options: Cassandra
S3 对象存储
Postgres
本地文件系统
why: 元数据是典型的关系型小数据：Postgres 给灵活查询，规模上来再分区/复制即可，不必一开始过度设计。
why_en: Postgres is the sensible default for document metadata because it offers flexible querying and can be partitioned and replicated later if scale demands.
whenOtherWins: 如果是操作日志这种高频 append-only 写、按文档分区顺序读的负载，Cassandra 这类写优化的宽列存储更合适。
tradeoff: 灵活关系查询 vs 高频 append 写入扩展
options_en: Cassandra
S3 object storage
Postgres
Local filesystem

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化的宽列分布式数据库，常用于高频 append-only 的日志类负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a write-optimized wide-column distributed database, often used for high-frequency append-only log workloads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云对象存储服务，适合存放大文件而非高频小写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is a cloud object storage service suited to large files rather than frequent small writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库，支持灵活查询，适合结构化元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a relational database with flexible querying, well suited to structured metadata.

optionExplanations: Cassandra 为高频 append-only 写优化，元数据这种低频、需要灵活关系查询的负载，换成它反而没有索引和 JOIN 的方便。
S3 是对象存储，适合大文件整存整取，标题、docId 这类结构化小字段用它查询很别扭。
Postgres 给灵活的关系查询和索引，初期规模不大时单机就够，未来需要再加分区或复制。
本地文件系统没有网络访问、没有并发控制，扛不住多实例服务共享同一份元数据。
optionExplanations_en: Cassandra is optimized for high-frequency append-only writes; metadata's low-frequency, flexible relational queries lose the indexes and joins that make it comfortable.
S3 is object storage built for whole large files, and it's awkward for querying small structured fields like title or docId.
Postgres gives flexible relational queries and indexing; a single node handles the early scale fine, with partitioning or replication to add later.
A local filesystem has no network access or concurrency control, so it can't support multiple service instances sharing the same metadata.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 文档标题、所有者每天只读写几次；同一份文档的编辑操作每秒几十条，还要按序回放。
scenario_en: A document title and owner are read or written a few times a day, while its edit operations arrive dozens per second and must be replayed in order.
q: 为什么把「文档内容」和「文档元数据」分开存储是合理的？
q_en: Why does it make sense to store document content separately from document metadata?
options: 元数据低频结构化，内容是高频操作流，访问模式不同
元数据的数据量通常要远比文档内容的整个操作日志大得多
内容必须只能存在关系型数据库里
这样拆分可以省掉 API gateway
why: 元数据是低频读写、结构化、适合关系查询；内容是高频操作流。访问模式不同就该分开，各选各的存储。
why_en: Metadata like permissions, tags, and titles has a completely different access pattern from the high-frequency edit stream, so separating the two lets each use the right store.
options_en: Metadata is low-frequency and structured; content is a high-frequency operation stream — different access patterns
Metadata is usually far larger than the document's entire operation log
Content must live only in a relational database
Splitting them just saves an API gateway
optionExplanations: 元数据低频、结构化，适合关系查询；内容是高频操作流，两种访问模式根本不同，分开存才能各选各的引擎。
实际上文档内容的操作日志往往比元数据大得多，规模大小不是分开存储的理由。
把一切都塞进关系数据库是过强的假设，存储选型应该跟着访问模式走，不是跟着数据类型走。
分不分开存数据跟 API gateway 需不需要没有关系，两者是独立的设计决定。
optionExplanations_en: Metadata is low-frequency and structured, well suited to relational queries, while content is a high-frequency operation stream — the access patterns are different enough that each deserves its own store.
In practice the content operation log is often larger than metadata, so size isn't the reason to split them.
Forcing everything into a relational database is too strong an assumption; storage choice should follow the access pattern, not the data type.
Whether to separate the stores has nothing to do with needing an API gateway — they're independent design decisions.

scenario: 45 分钟面试，创建文档是普通的写元数据，真正的难点在并发编辑与实时同步。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute interview, creating a document is just writing metadata; the real difficulty is concurrent editing and real-time sync.
q: 「创建文档」这条路径的架构模式，以及面试里该怎么对待它？
q_en: How should you model the create-document path, and how much interview time should it get?
options: 单机服务架构，值得重点深挖
CRUD+API gateway 套路化，快速带过
必须使用 serverless 无服务器架构才能满足要求
让客户端直接写入数据库
why: API gateway 后面挂一排无状态 CRUD 服务是最常见的模式，面试里应该几句话画完，把时间留给协同编辑这些真正的难点。
why_en: Document creation is a standard horizontally scaled CRUD service behind an API gateway, a pattern you should sketch quickly to save time for the hard parts.
options_en: A single-server setup worth deep exploration
Horizontally scaled CRUD service behind an API gateway — standard, move fast
Serverless architecture is required to meet the requirements
Let clients write to the database directly
optionExplanations: 单机跑全部逻辑是单点故障，也没有任何值得深挖的权衡，面试里花时间讲它性价比很低。
这套路谁都见过，画完就该收手，别在这上面浪费面试官的耐心。
Serverless 有冷启动和连接管理的额外成本，对这个场景不是必须项，属于过度工程。
让客户端直接写数据库跳过了校验和一致性把关，安全和数据完整性都没法保证。
optionExplanations_en: A single server running everything is a single point of failure with no interesting tradeoff worth exploring, so it's a poor use of interview time.
Everyone has seen this pattern before — sketch it and move on, rather than spending the interviewer's patience here.
Serverless adds cold-start and connection overhead that this path doesn't need — over-engineering for a simple CRUD flow.
Letting the client write the database directly skips validation and consistency checks, so neither security nor data integrity is guaranteed.

q: 「每次编辑都把整份文档发给服务器」这个方案，带宽代价大约是什么量级？
q_en: If every edit sends the whole document to the server, what bandwidth cost are we talking about?
options: 每次键入大约传几个字节，量级明显偏小
每次键入大约传几 KB，量级依然偏小
打字快时每次键入要传几百 KB
编辑时不传，只有点保存才传输一次
why: 整篇快照意味着每敲一个键就传整份文档，对一篇普通文档就是几百 KB 一次键入——带宽被彻底浪费。
why_en: Sending the whole document per edit can mean hundreds of kilobytes for every single keystroke, which is wildly inefficient.
scenario: 协同编辑器最初的写路径设计：用户每按一次键，就把整份文档发送给服务器保存。
scenario_en: The first write-path idea is that every keystroke sends the entire document back to the server for saving.
options_en: Roughly a few bytes go out per keystroke, clearly too small a number
Roughly a few kilobytes go out per keystroke, still too small
A fast typist sends hundreds of kilobytes with every keystroke
Nothing is sent while typing — only one transfer happens on save
optionExplanations: 几个字节的量级只对应单字符编辑，远不是整篇 HTML/富文本快照的体积。
几 KB 顶多是一小段文字，一份正常长度的文档远超这个体积。
一份文档常有几百 KB，naive 快照方案下每敲一个键就整份重传，这正是带宽被浪费的量级。
只有保存时才传是另一套设计（本地缓冲、定期同步），不是这里在考的「每次键入都发」方案。
optionExplanations_en: A few bytes only fits a single character, nowhere near the size of a whole document snapshot.
A few kilobytes covers a short passage at most; a normal document is much bigger than that.
A typical document runs hundreds of kilobytes, so a naive full-snapshot design retransmits that much on every single keystroke — the actual scale of the waste.
Only transmitting on save describes a different design (local buffering, periodic sync), not the send-every-keystroke scheme this question is about.

scenario: 最朴素的协同方案：客户端每次改动都把整篇文档快照 PUT 上去覆盖服务器上的版本。
scenario_en: The naive approach: every change makes the client PUT a full document snapshot that overwrites whatever the server holds.
q: 文档为 "Hello!"，A 提交整篇快照 "Hello, world!"，B 同时提交整篇快照 "Hello"。快照覆盖方案的结局是？
q_en: With two concurrent full-document snapshots, what happens under a snapshot-overwrite design?
options: 最后到达的快照直接覆盖一切，另一个人的并发编辑完全丢失
服务器自动合并成 "Hello, world"
两个快照都被拒绝
系统检测到编辑冲突并抛出提示，让两位用户各自手动合并解决
why: 整篇覆盖是 last-writer-wins：最终文档完全取决于谁的请求后到，另一个人的修改被无声抹掉，协同体验彻底崩坏。
why_en: With whole-document snapshots the last write wins, so whichever snapshot arrives last silently erases the other user's concurrent edit.
options_en: The last snapshot to arrive silently overwrites everything, losing the other user's edit
The server automatically merges them into "Hello, world"
Both snapshots are rejected
The system detects the conflict and raises a prompt for both users to merge manually
optionExplanations: 整篇覆盖没有合并逻辑，谁的请求后到就整份生效，先到的人的修改被无声吞掉。
整篇快照本身不携带语义信息，服务器没有能力自动合并出 "Hello, world"，这需要单独的合并算法。
拒绝两个快照会让编辑完全卡住，用户体验上不可接受。
抛冲突给用户需要先侦测到冲突，而整篇覆盖方案根本不做检测，用户永远不知道发生了什么。
optionExplanations_en: Whole-document overwrite has no merge logic, so whichever snapshot lands last simply becomes the document, silently erasing the earlier concurrent edit.
A raw snapshot carries no semantic information, so the server has no way to auto-merge into "Hello, world" — that needs a separate merge algorithm.
Rejecting both snapshots blocks editing entirely, which is not an acceptable user experience.
Raising a conflict requires detecting one first, and whole-document overwrite never checks for conflicts, so the user never even finds out.

scenario: 为省带宽改成只发增量操作，服务器按到达顺序原样应用，不做任何位置变换。
scenario_en: To save bandwidth we send only incremental operations, and the server applies them in arrival order without transforming any positions.
q: 改为只传编辑操作（如 INSERT(5, ", world") 和 DELETE(6)）后，带宽解决了，但新问题是？
q_en: After switching to sending edit operations only, what new problem remains?
options: 操作数据包太小，网络协议头的固定开销反而占比过大
位置基于旧文档状态，INSERT 先到删错字符
服务器缺少持久化机制，无法存储操作
客户端缺少权限，无法生成编辑操作
why: 每个操作的位置隐含了「当时的文档状态」这个上下文；别人的操作先落地后，原始位置就指错了地方。这正是 OT/CRDT 要解决的问题。
why_en: Each edit's position assumes a specific document state, so if another insert lands first, a raw delete at position six removes the wrong character.
diagram:
graph TD
    OpA[Insert at position] --> Context[Depends on version]
    OpB[Delete at position] --> Context
    Context --> Conflict[Concurrent positions shift]
    Conflict --> Transform[OT or CRDT needed]
options_en: The operation packets are too tiny, so fixed protocol-header overhead dominates the payload
Positions assume the old state, so an earlier INSERT deletes the wrong character
The server lacks persistence and cannot store operations
The client lacks permission to generate operations

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 操作本身很小，协议头开销不是问题——真正的坑在位置语义，不在包大小。
位置是相对某个文档状态算出来的坐标，中间只要插了别人一手，这个坐标立刻作废——这正是接下来要引入 OT/CRDT 的理由。
持久化机制负责把操作存下来，跟位置语义对不对是两回事，操作照样能落库。
客户端本来就有权限生成编辑操作，限制不在这里。
optionExplanations_en: The operations themselves are small; protocol overhead isn't the real issue — the trap is in position semantics, not packet size.
A position is a coordinate computed against one particular document state, and the moment someone else's edit lands first, that coordinate goes stale — exactly why OT and CRDT enter the picture next.
Persistence just means storing the operation; whether its position is still correct is a separate question, and storage works regardless.
The client already has permission to generate edit operations, so that's not where the limitation is.

scenario: 增量操作的位置基于发送时的本地文档状态，但服务器上的文档可能已被别人改过。
scenario_en: Each operation carries positions based on the local document state when it was sent, yet the server-side document may already have changed.
q: 解决「编辑操作依赖文档状态上下文」这一根本问题，业界的两大方案家族是？
q_en: What are the two main industry families for handling edit operations that depend on document state?
options: 分布式锁 与 乐观并发控制两大路线
两阶段提交 与 Saga
OT 与 CRDT 两大方案家族
版本向量 与 Paxos
why: 两条路：OT 在应用前按先到的操作「变换」后到的操作；CRDT 让操作本身可交换，任意顺序应用都收敛。
why_en: The two families are operational transformation, which rewrites each edit against those before it, and CRDTs, which make every edit commutative.
options_en: Distributed locking and optimistic concurrency control as the two families
Two-phase commit and Saga
OT (operational transformation) and CRDT
Version vectors and Paxos

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 分布式锁和乐观并发控制是数据库隔离手段，不是给协同编辑设计的方案家族。
两阶段提交和 Saga 解决的是跨服务事务一致性，跟并发文本编辑不是一回事。
OT 靠中心定序变换操作，CRDT 靠操作可交换收敛，这正是业界解决「操作依赖文档状态」问题的两条路。
版本向量和 Paxos 是分布式系统里的定序/共识工具，不是专门解决文本并发编辑收敛的方案。
optionExplanations_en: Distributed locking and optimistic concurrency are database isolation techniques, not a family built for collaborative text editing.
Two-phase commit and Saga solve cross-service transactional consistency, which is a different problem from concurrent text editing.
OT reorders and transforms operations through a central server while CRDT makes operations commutative — these are the two real industry families for state-dependent edits.
Version vectors and Paxos are ordering and consensus tools for distributed systems in general, not solutions purpose-built for converging concurrent text edits.

scenario: OT 服务器已先应用 A 的 INSERT(5, ", world")，插入了 7 个字符，再来处理 B 的 DELETE(6)。
scenario_en: The OT server already applied A's INSERT(5, ", world"), which added 7 characters, and now has to handle B's DELETE(6).
q: 读这个 OT 例子：文档 "Hello!"，A 的插入先被应用。B 的 DELETE(6) 必须被变换成什么才能删对感叹号？
q_en: In this OT example, what must B's DELETE(6) transform into to delete the exclamation mark?
codeSample:
# 初始文档: "Hello!"（感叹号在位置 6）
op_a = INSERT(5, ", world")   # 先到并应用 -> "Hello, world!"
op_b = DELETE(6)              # B 基于旧文档生成，本想删 "!"

# transform(op_b, op_a) = ?
options: DELETE(6)，无需变换
DELETE(7)，顺移 1 位
DELETE(12)，顺移 6 位
DELETE(13)，顺移 7 位
why: ", world" 有 7 个字符，插入点在删除目标之前，所以删除位置要 6+7=13，才能删到已经被顺移的感叹号。
why_en: The seven-character insert lands before the delete target, so the delete position shifts from six to thirteen to still hit the exclamation mark.
options_en: DELETE(6), no transform needed
DELETE(7), a one-position shift
DELETE(12), a six-position shift
DELETE(13), a seven-position shift

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 位置完全不变会让删除还停在旧坐标 6，那里现在是插入内容里的逗号，删错了字符。
只顺移 1 位远远不够抵消 7 个字符的插入，还是会删到错误位置。
顺移 6 位比实际插入的 7 个字符少 1，还是差一位，删的仍不是感叹号。
插入发生在删除目标前面，插入了多少字符，删除坐标就要跟着往后挪多少——这里挪 7 位，6 变 13，刚好落在感叹号上。
optionExplanations_en: Leaving the position unchanged still deletes at the old coordinate six, which is now the comma inside the inserted text — the wrong character.
Shifting by only one is nowhere near enough to offset a seven-character insert, so it still deletes the wrong spot.
Shifting by six is one short of the actual seven-character insert, still landing one position off from the exclamation mark.
The insert lands before the delete target, so the delete coordinate has to shift by however many characters were inserted — seven here, taking six to thirteen, landing right on the exclamation mark.

scenario: 协同编辑要求所有副本收敛，而这套系统里每份文档都由一台服务器独占接收全部编辑。
scenario_en: Collaborative editing must converge, and in this system every document is exclusively owned by one server that receives all its edits.
q: OT（操作变换）的工作机制是？
q_en: How does OT, or operational transformation, work?
options: 各客户端各自决定顺序，最后由多数投票来裁定冲突
遇到冲突就把操作全部丢弃
给每个字符单独加分布式锁
中心服务器定最终顺序，按已到操作变换后续操作
why: OT 的核心是中心定序 + 变换：服务器收集所有编辑，按已应用的操作重写后到的操作，让它们在新状态下仍表达原意。
why_en: OT funnels all edits through one server that fixes a final order and transforms each incoming operation against those already applied before applying or rebroadcasting it.
options_en: Each client decides its own order, and a majority vote resolves conflicts at the end
Conflicting operations are simply discarded
Every character gets its own distributed lock
A central server fixes the final order and transforms each operation against those already applied

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 各客户端各自定序再投票，等结果出来编辑早就分岔了，收敛不了。
冲突就丢弃操作意味着用户的编辑说没就没，协作产品不能这样对待用户输入。
给每个字符单独加锁在高频编辑下是性能灾难，锁的粒度和数量都不现实。
全部操作先经过一台服务器排好队，再逐个变换成能接在已应用操作后面的形式，这就是 OT 定序加变换的两步走。
optionExplanations_en: Each client deciding its own order and voting afterward means edits have already diverged by the time a result exists — nothing converges.
Discarding conflicting operations means a user's edit can just vanish, which no collaborative product can do to real input.
Locking every individual character is a performance disaster at editing frequency — the lock count and granularity aren't realistic.
Every operation first queues through one server, then gets transformed to fit cleanly after whatever's already applied — ordering plus transformation, the two-step core of OT.

scenario: 本设计选了 OT 做并发控制，同时非功能需求把单文档并发编辑者限制在 100 人以内。
scenario_en: This design picks OT for concurrency control, and the non-functional requirements cap one document at 100 concurrent editors.
q: OT 最大的架构性代价是什么，本设计靠什么兜住它？
q_en: What is OT's biggest architectural cost, and what constraint contains it here?
options: 内存占用巨大，需要靠压缩机制解决
中心服务器定全序限制协作者规模；靠编辑者上限兜住
无法支持删除这类操作，需要额外引入墓碑机制才能解决
延迟太高，需要靠 CDN 加速解决
why: OT 需要一台服务器给出最终顺序，这限制了协作者数量、而且正确实现很精细；正好非功能需求把编辑者限制在 100 人以内，中心式方案完全够用。
why_en: OT's cost is a required central ordering server that caps collaborator scale and is tricky to implement correctly, which the hundred-editor limit conveniently absorbs.
options_en: Memory use is huge; compression solves it
A central server must fix total order, capping collaborators and inviting bugs; the hundred-editor limit absorbs it
Deletes of this kind are unsupported, needing an extra tombstone mechanism
Latency is too high; a CDN solves it

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 内存占用不是 OT 的架构性痛点，真正的代价在中心服务器和定序逻辑上。
中心定序器天生有并发上限，这本是 OT 的软肋；但这道题一开始就把编辑者摁在 100 人以内，软肋刚好被前提条件挡住了。
OT 完全支持删除，墓碑是 CRDT 的机制，不是 OT 缺失删除能力的补丁。
延迟主要来自网络距离，不是 OT 算法本身的开销，CDN 也解决不了定序问题。
optionExplanations_en: Memory footprint isn't OT's architectural pain point — the real cost sits in the central server and its ordering logic.
A central sequencer has a built-in concurrency ceiling — normally OT's soft spot — but this design caps editors at a hundred from the start, so the weakness never gets exercised.
OT handles deletes fine; tombstones are a CRDT mechanism, not a patch for something OT is missing.
Latency mostly comes from network distance, not from the OT algorithm itself, and a CDN can't fix an ordering problem.

scenario: 换个前提：没有中心服务器定序，客户端之间点对点、甚至离线也要能把编辑合并对。
scenario_en: Change the premise: there is no central sequencer, and clients must merge edits peer-to-peer or even fully offline.
q: CRDT 解决并发编辑的核心思路是？
q_en: What is CRDT's core idea for collaborative editing?
options: 让服务器变换每个操作
让每个操作可交换，任意顺序都收敛
禁止两个用户编辑同一段落
用时间戳做 last-writer-wins
why: CRDT 不重写操作，而是把操作设计成天然可交换：只要所有更新最终送达所有客户端，大家必然收敛一致，不需要中心定序。
why_en: CRDTs make every edit commutative so that clients converge on the same document no matter what order the operations arrive in.
options_en: Have the server transform every operation
Make every operation commutative so order doesn't matter
Forbid two users from editing the same paragraph
Use timestamps for last-writer-wins

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 让服务器改写每个操作是 OT 的做法，不是 CRDT 的思路。
把操作设计成天然可交换，不管什么顺序应用都能收敛到同一结果，这就是 CRDT 不需要中心定序的原因。
禁止同段编辑等于砍掉真正的并发能力，跟协同编辑的目标背道而驰。
用时间戳做 last-writer-wins 会悄悄丢弃别人的编辑，跟 CRDT 保证收敛不丢数据是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Having the server rewrite every operation is OT's approach, not CRDT's.
Designing operations to be naturally commutative so they converge to the same result regardless of arrival order is exactly why CRDT needs no central server.
Forbidding edits to the same paragraph strips away real concurrency, which defeats the point of collaborative editing.
Timestamp-based last-writer-wins silently drops someone's edit, which is the opposite of CRDT's no-data-loss convergence guarantee.

q: 补全文本 CRDT 的两个关键技巧：
q_en: Complete the two key techniques used by a text CRDT.
text: 技巧一：位置用可无限细分的{{唯一标识符}}表示（概念上像实数，实现常用变长 ID），插入永远不改变已有位置；技巧二：删除不真删，而是留下{{墓碑（tombstone）}}，展示时再过滤。
why: 位置标识不随插入漂移，删除只做标记——这两招让任何顺序应用操作都得到同一结果，代价是历史永久保留。
why_en: Text CRDTs use infinitely subdividable position identifiers that never move and tombstones that mark deletions instead of removing text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记已删除内容的占位符，数据仍保留但显示时被过滤掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a marker for deleted content that keeps the data but filters it out of the displayed text.

scenario: CRDT 里任意两个相邻字符之间随时可能有人并发插入，而已有字符的位置绝不允许改动。
scenario_en: In a CRDT, someone may concurrently insert between any two adjacent characters, and existing characters must never have their positions changed.
q: CRDT 的位置标识符如何保证「永远插得进去」？
q_en: How do CRDT position identifiers make sure there is always room to insert?
options: 位置用 32 位整数编号，用满了就得重排整篇文档
每次插入都把后面所有字符的位置 +1
由服务器统一分配递增序号
任意两个位置间都能生成新标识符（像实数细分）
why: 比如字符位置 4 和 5 之间可以造出 4.3、4.31……需要空间时随时细分；已有字符的位置永不改变，所以并发插入互不干扰。
why_en: Between any two existing positions you can always mint a new identifier, like picking a real number between four and five, so inserts never shift existing characters.
options_en: 32-bit integer position numbers; when they run out the whole document is recompacted
Shift every following character's position by one on each insert
The server assigns monotonically increasing sequence numbers
Any two positions can always yield a new identifier between them, like a real number

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 32 位整数位置一旦用满就要重排整篇，代价大、还打破了已有位置不变的前提。
每次插入都去改后面所有字符的位置，等于每次编辑都做一次全篇更新，开销随文档变长而变大。
服务器统一分配递增序号需要一个中心协调点，这是 OT 的思路，不是 CRDT 想要的去中心化。
任意两个已有位置之间都能造出新标识符，像在实数轴上无限细分，插入永远不用挪动别人的位置。
optionExplanations_en: 32-bit integer positions run out and force a full recompact, which is expensive and breaks the assumption that existing positions never move.
Shifting every following character's position on each insert means every edit touches the whole document, growing costlier as it gets longer.
Having the server hand out sequential numbers needs a central coordinator, which is OT's approach, not the decentralization CRDT is going for.
Any two existing positions can always mint a new identifier between them, like subdividing real numbers infinitely, so inserts never have to move anyone else's position.

scenario: CRDT 客户端要把整份文档结构常驻内存，而这份文档可能被同一批人编辑好几年。
scenario_en: A CRDT client keeps the whole document structure in memory, and that document may be edited by the same team for years.
q: CRDT 保留全部历史 + 墓碑的直接后果是？
q_en: What is the direct consequence of CRDT keeping full history plus tombstones?
options: 文档只增不减，内存和计算成本更高
文档会自动变小
无法支持插入操作
必须反过来依赖一台中心服务器来定序
why: 每个删除都留墓碑、每次编辑都被记住，文档永远只会变大；内存和计算成本都高于 OT，这是 CRDT 优雅性的代价。
why_en: Because CRDTs remember every edit and keep tombstones for deleted text, the document only ever grows and costs more memory and compute.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Client A
    participant S as Collab Server
    participant B as Client B
    A->>S: op at version 10
    B->>S: concurrent op at version 10
    S->>S: order and transform
    S-->>A: ack + remote op
    S-->>B: transformed remote op
options_en: The document only grows and costs more memory and compute
The document automatically shrinks
Inserts are unsupported
It must instead rely on a central server for ordering

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记已删除内容的占位符，数据仍保留但显示时被过滤掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a marker for deleted content that keeps the data but filters it out of the displayed text.

optionExplanations: 墓碑加历史记录只进不出，这份「什么都不忘」的账单最终体现在内存占用和计算量上。
CRDT 不做自动清理，历史和墓碑都永久保留，文档不会自己变小。
CRDT 完全支持插入，墓碑只是标记删除，不影响插入操作。
CRDT 恰恰是为了摆脱中心服务器而设计的，不需要它。
optionExplanations_en: Tombstones and history only ever accumulate — the bill for "never forgetting anything" shows up directly in memory and compute.
CRDT does no automatic cleanup — history and tombstones stick around permanently, so the document never shrinks on its own.
CRDT supports inserts just fine; tombstones only mark deletions and don't touch insert behavior.
CRDT is designed specifically to avoid needing a central server, not to require one.

scenario: 两个协作者在同一个位置并发插入不同文字，CRDT 里没有中心服务器裁决谁先谁后。
scenario_en: Two collaborators concurrently insert different text at the exact same position, and a CRDT has no central server to decide who goes first.
q: 两人同时在 "Hello" 后插入（一个插 ","、一个插 " there"），CRDT 得到 "Hello t,here!"。这个例子说明什么？
q_en: What does the "Hello t,here!" concurrent-insert example show about CRDTs?
options: CRDT 从根本上无法收敛到统一文档
CRDT 保证收敛，并发插入偶尔会交织成怪文本
遇到交织文本就必须放弃 CRDT 换回 OT
最终结果取决于哪个操作先到达服务器
why: CRDT 承诺的是「大家看到同一份文档」，不承诺「交织结果符合语义」；实时协作中看得见彼此光标，很少真的挤在同一位置写。
why_en: CRDTs guarantee that every client converges on the same text, but concurrent inserts at the same spot can interleave oddly, which cursor awareness usually prevents in practice.
options_en: CRDT fundamentally fails to converge on one document
CRDT still converges; concurrent inserts can occasionally interleave into odd text
Interleaved text means abandoning CRDT and falling back to OT
The final result depends on which operation reaches the server first

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: CRDT 的收敛承诺是数学保证，不会因为交织文本就失效，收敛和「好看」是两件事。
CRDT 保证所有客户端最终看到同一份文本，但没承诺交织顺序总是符合语义；实时协作里光标可见，这种巧合很少见。
交织文本不是 bug，是 CRDT 的正常行为之一，不需要为此换回 OT。
CRDT 的收敛结果和到达顺序无关，任意顺序应用都会得到相同的最终文档。
optionExplanations_en: CRDT's convergence guarantee is mathematical, not something that breaks just because the interleaved text looks odd.
CRDT guarantees every client eventually sees identical text, but not that interleaving always reads naturally — with cursor visibility in real collaboration, this coincidence is rare in practice.
Odd interleaving is normal CRDT behavior, not a bug that forces a fallback to OT.
CRDT's converged result doesn't depend on arrival order — applying the operations in any order yields the same final document.

scenario: 要做一个点对点（WebRTC）协作应用，没有中心服务器；客户端还要支持离线编辑，回线后把攒下的操作并入。
scenario_en: You are building a peer-to-peer WebRTC collaboration app with no central server, and clients must support offline edits that merge when they reconnect.
q: 更合适的并发编辑方案是？
q_en: Which collaborative editing approach better fits this peer-to-peer and offline-first scenario?
options: OT（操作变换）
CRDT
整篇快照覆盖
全局分布式锁
why: CRDT 不需要中心定序，只要更新最终送达就收敛，天然适配 P2P；离线时把操作攒在本地、回线后并入即可。Yjs 是推荐的开源实现。
why_en: CRDTs need no central server and merge offline edits naturally, which makes them the right fit for peer-to-peer or offline-first collaboration.
whenOtherWins: 有中心服务器、协作者数量有限（如 ≤100）、又在意内存和文本适配性时，OT 更合适——这正是 Google Docs 的选择。
tradeoff: 去中心化收敛 vs 中心定序效率

CRDT
Whole-document snapshot overwrite
A single global distributed lock

termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC lets browsers communicate directly peer-to-peer without routing data through a central server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点之间直接通信，不依赖中心服务器协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Peer-to-peer means nodes talk directly to each other without a central coordinating server.

optionExplanations: OT 靠中心服务器定序，P2P 架构里根本没有这台服务器，OT 直接失灵。
CRDT 不依赖任何中心节点，只要更新最终都送达就收敛，离线时把操作攒在本地、联网后合并即可，正贴合 P2P + 离线优先。Yjs 是常用的开源实现。
整篇覆盖是 last-writer-wins，离线合并时谁的版本后到就吃掉另一方，完全不满足收敛要求。
全网加分布式锁在没有中心协调者的 P2P 场景下无法维持，编辑也没法并发进行。
optionExplanations_en: OT depends on a central server for ordering, and a peer-to-peer architecture has no such server, so OT simply doesn't work here.

CRDT needs no central node — as long as updates eventually arrive everywhere they converge, so offline edits can queue locally and merge on reconnect, a direct fit for P2P and offline-first. Yjs is a commonly used open-source implementation.
Whole-document overwrite is last-writer-wins, so merging offline copies just lets whichever arrives later erase the other, failing the convergence requirement.
A single global distributed lock can't be maintained without a central coordinator in P2P, and it would also block concurrent editing entirely.

scenario: 要给一个轻量协作应用选开源方案，面试官追问业界大厂各自选了哪条路线。
scenario_en: We're picking an open-source library for a lightweight collaborative app, and the interviewer asks which route the big products actually took.
q: 关于业界实现，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about real-world OT and CRDT implementations is correct?
options: Yjs 是开源 CRDT，Figma 用裁剪版，Docs 用 OT
Google Docs 用 CRDT，Figma 和 Yjs 都用 OT
Yjs 是 OT 库
工业界只用 OT，CRDT 仍停留在论文
