q_en: If web scraping is your primary ingestion path, where does it break first?
options: 发布方改版页面，选择器失效，这个源静默断供
HTTP 协议本身不允许抓取网页内容
抓到的文章会被自动放进错误的地区 feed 里
对象存储无法保存抓取过程中下载的缩略图
options_en: The publisher redesigns the page, the selectors stop matching, and that source silently goes dry.
The HTTP protocol itself does not permit fetching web page content.
Scraped articles automatically land in the wrong regional feed.
Object storage cannot hold thumbnails downloaded during scraping.
why: 抓取把采集绑在别人的 HTML 结构上，一次改版就让解析器返回空且不报错；再加上慢、不可靠和法律风险，它只适合当没有 RSS 时的兜底。
why_en: Scraping couples ingestion to someone else's HTML, so one redesign makes the parser return nothing without erroring — that plus slowness and legal risk keeps it a fallback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网页样式语言，其选择器语法常被抓取程序用来定位页面元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascading Style Sheets is the web styling language whose selector syntax scrapers reuse to locate page elements.

optionExplanations: 对，静默是最难受的地方：没有异常、没有报错，只是这个源再没有新文章。
HTTP 只负责传输，能不能抓是站点条款和 robots 规则的问题，不是协议限制。
地区是我们在入库时按发布方属性打的标，跟内容从哪种方式采来无关。
缩略图走的是标准上传路径，抓取和 RSS 采集在这一步完全一样。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the silence is the painful part: no exception, no alert, just no new articles from that source ever again.
HTTP only moves bytes; whether you may scrape is a matter of site terms and robots rules, not the protocol.
Region is a label we attach at ingest time from publisher attributes, independent of how the content was collected.
Thumbnails follow the same upload path whether the article came from scraping or from RSS.

scenario: 我们开放 POST /webhooks/article-published 让发布方推送新文章，这个地址公网可达，任何人都能往里发。
scenario_en: We expose POST /webhooks/article-published so publishers can push new articles, and the endpoint is reachable by anyone on the internet.
q: webhook 端点该怎么挡住伪造和垃圾推送？
q_en: How should the webhook endpoint block spoofed and spam pushes?
options: 给每家发布方发密钥或 API key 并逐次校验
只要走 HTTPS 加密传输就能确认来源身份
不做校验就先入库，事后再靠人工抽查删掉垃圾内容
只看请求体里的发布方名字字段来判断是谁推的
options_en: Issue each publisher a shared secret or API key and verify it on every push.
Rely on HTTPS transport encryption alone to establish who the caller is.
Skip verification, ingest everything, and rely on manual spot-checks to delete spam.
Trust the publisher name field inside the request body to identify the caller.
codeSample:
POST /webhooks/article-published HTTP/1.1
X-API-Key: pub_cnn_9f3a...        # 每家发布方一把，可单独吊销
Content-Type: application/json

{"url":"...","title":"...","published_at":"2024-06-21T22:30:00Z"}
why: 加密只保证链路上没人偷看，认证才回答"这是谁推的"；每家一把密钥还能在泄漏时单独吊销。代价是要和上千家发布方分发并轮换密钥。
why_en: Encryption only stops eavesdropping — authentication is what answers who pushed this, and a per-publisher key can be revoked alone when it leaks.
whenOtherWins: 如果推送方全在内网且网络边界可信，IP 白名单比分发密钥更省运维。
tradeoff: 共享密钥的可吊销身份 vs 密钥分发轮换的运维负担

termDefinitions.meaning: 发给调用方的一串凭据，请求时带上用来证明身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a credential string issued to a caller and sent with each request to prove identity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加密传输的 HTTP，保证链路内容不被窃听或篡改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS is HTTP over an encrypted channel so traffic cannot be read or tampered with in transit.

optionExplanations: 对，凭据放在请求头里逐次校验，来路不明的推送在入队之前就被拒掉。
加密解决的是"有没有人偷看"，跟"对面是不是 CNN"完全是两个问题。
事后人工清理跟不上推送速率，垃圾内容会先出现在用户 feed 里。
请求体里的字段是调用方自己写的，任何人都能随便填一个发布方名字。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the credential rides in the header and is checked per call, so unknown senders are rejected before anything is queued.
Encryption answers whether anyone is eavesdropping, a different question from whether the caller really is CNN.
Manual cleanup cannot keep up with push rates, so spam reaches user feeds first.
Body fields are written by the caller, so anyone can type in any publisher name they like.

scenario: 个性化 feed 为每个用户预先算好，存在 feed:user:12345，后台 worker 在新文章到达时按相关性慢慢往里加。
scenario_en: Personalized feeds are precomputed for each individual reader in feed:user:12345, and background workers slowly add new articles by relevance score.
q: 除了内存开销，per-user 预计算 feed 还会在什么时候出错？
q_en: Beyond memory cost, when else does a per-user precomputed feed go wrong?
options: 兴趣变了 feed 仍是旧偏好，突发要闻也可能缺席
用户翻页时会拿到完全随机排序的历史文章列表
分类缓存会被个性化 worker 定期整块删除掉
文章的发布时间戳会被 worker 在写入时改写
options_en: Interests shift but the feed still reflects old preferences, and breaking news can be missing entirely.
Paging returns a completely randomly ordered list of historical articles.
Category caches get periodically wiped wholesale by the personalization worker.
Publish timestamps get rewritten by the worker as it writes entries.
why: 预计算把排序挪到写路径，feed 只反映上一次计算时的画像；全民该看到的突发新闻如果不在这个人的相关性列表里，就永远不会被塞进去。
why_en: Precomputing moves ranking to the write path, so the feed reflects only the profile at the last computation, and a globally important story never enters a feed whose score misses it.
optionExplanations: 对，画像变化和全局要闻这两件事都发生在预计算之后，缓存里没有就补不上。
排序恰恰是预计算时按相关性分数定好的，结果是固定顺序而不是随机。
分类缓存由采集侧的 feed worker 维护，个性化流程只读它，不负责清理。
时间戳来自采集时解析到的发布时间，个性化 worker 只拿它当排序输入。
optionExplanations_en: Right — both the profile shift and the global story happen after precomputation, and what is not in the cache cannot be filled in.
Ordering is exactly what precomputation fixes by relevance score, giving a stable order rather than a random one.
Category caches are maintained by ingest-side feed workers; personalization only reads them.
Timestamps come from the publish time parsed at ingest; the personalization worker only uses them as a ranking input.

scenario: 个性化改成用几 KB 的偏好向量在请求时混合分类 feed：60% technology、30% business、10% trending。
scenario_en: Personalization becomes a few-KB preference vector that mixes category feeds on demand: 60% technology, 30% business, 10% trending.
q: 这套按比例混合分类 feed 的方案要付什么代价？
q_en: What does this ratio-based category mixing approach cost?
options: 个性化只到分类粒度，窄兴趣漏要闻、宽兴趣显泛化
内存占用会比给每个用户存一份缓存还要大得多
所有分类 feed 都必须改回实时数据库查询才能混合
每个用户的偏好向量里必须完整存下 1000 篇文章
options_en: Personalization only reaches category granularity: narrow interests miss big stories, broad ones feel generic.
Memory usage ends up far larger than storing one cache per user.
Every category feed must revert to real-time database queries to be mixable.
Each user's preference vector must store a full 1,000 articles.
why: 混合只能在几百个分类 feed 之间调比例，换来内存降两个数量级；代价是深度不足，需要专门调多样性兜住窄兴趣和宽兴趣两头。
why_en: Mixing only tunes ratios across a few hundred category feeds, which cuts memory by two orders of magnitude but costs depth, so diversity has to be tuned deliberately.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户量小到给每人存一份缓存也扛得住，per-user 预计算能给出更细的个性化。
tradeoff: 分类混合的低内存成本 vs 逐用户排序的个性化深度
optionExplanations: 对，比例只落在分类上，同一分类内部谁排前面就没法再按个人偏好区分。
偏好向量只有几 KB，缓存数量从上亿降到几百，内存方向恰好相反。
这套方案正建立在分类 feed 已经预计算好之上，混合的是缓存不是查询。
向量存的是各分类的权重比例，文章本身留在共享的分类缓存里。
optionExplanations_en: Right — ratios only apply at the category level, so within one category personal taste can no longer reorder anything.
A preference vector is a few kilobytes and cache count drops from hundreds of millions to hundreds; memory moves the other way.
This design assumes category feeds are already precomputed — what gets mixed is caches, not queries.
The vector holds per-category weights; the articles themselves stay in the shared category caches.

scenario: cursor 从单一 published_at 换成 "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z_article123" 这种时间戳加文章 ID 的复合值。
scenario_en: The cursor changes from a bare published_at to a composite like "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z_article123" carrying timestamp plus article id.
q: 换成复合 cursor 之后要额外付出哪些代价？（多选）
q_en: What extra costs come with switching to a composite cursor? (Select all that apply.)
options: 应用要维护 cursor 的编码和解码逻辑
cursor 字符串变长，来回传输的体积增加
(published_at, article_id) 复合索引要额外存储
数据库从此无法再按 published_at 排序
options_en: The application must maintain encode and decode logic for the cursor.
The cursor string gets longer, so more bytes travel back and forth.
The composite index on (published_at, article_id) needs extra storage.
The database can no longer sort by published_at at all.
why: 复合 cursor 换来同时间戳也不漏文章的稳定全序，代价分摊在三处：多写的编解码代码、更长的游标字符串、以及复合索引占的磁盘。
why_en: A composite cursor buys a stable total order even under identical timestamps, and pays for it in encode/decode code, a longer cursor string, and index disk.
optionExplanations: 两个字段拼进一个字符串，客户端传回来时要拆开还原成元组比较的参数。
游标要在每次翻页请求里往返，长度增加是持续的小额带宽支出。
索引把两列一起排好存一份，这份额外结构是查询变快的实付成本。
排序能力没有丢失，恰恰相反，这个方案就是靠两列一起排序来定序的。
optionExplanations_en: Two fields packed into one string must be split apart again to rebuild the tuple comparison arguments.
The cursor travels on every page request, so extra length is a small but continuous bandwidth cost.
The index stores both columns pre-sorted as a separate structure, and that is the real price of the faster query.
Sorting is not lost — this design works precisely by ordering on both columns together.

scenario: 系统已经上线，文章主键用的是随机 UUID；现在想换成单调递增的 ULID，好让 cursor 只带一个 ID。
scenario_en: The system is live with random UUID article primary keys, and the team now wants monotonic ULIDs so the cursor can be a single id.
q: 已经用随机 UUID 之后再改单调 ID，代价主要在哪？
q_en: What is the main cost of moving to monotonic ids after random UUIDs are already in use?
options: 要做一次带外键引用的主键数据迁移
ULID 在关系型数据库里不能当主键使用
换完之后就再也无法按发布时间排序了
历史文章会在迁移过程中被自动清空掉
options_en: It forces a primary-key data migration that drags foreign-key references along.
ULIDs cannot be used as a primary key in a relational database.
After the switch you can no longer sort by publish time at all.
Historical articles get automatically wiped during the migration.
why: 单调 ID 是最简单的 cursor 方案，但它要求在设计期就定下来；事后迁移要动主键和所有引用它的地方，往往比直接上复合 cursor 更贵。
why_en: Monotonic ids give the simplest cursor but must be chosen up front, because retrofitting them rewrites the primary key and everything referencing it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一标识符，通常随机生成，因此不带时间顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Universally Unique Identifier is a typically random identifier that carries no chronological order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间戳放在前缀里的唯一标识符，字典序即大致时间序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ULID is a unique identifier whose timestamp prefix makes lexicographic order roughly chronological.

optionExplanations: 对，旧行要重新发号，指向它们的每一处引用都得跟着改，还不能中断写入。
ULID 就是一个定长字符串或 128 位值，当主键完全没有障碍。
published_at 列还在，按时间排序的能力跟主键换不换毫无关系。
迁移是改写标识符而不是删数据，会丢数据的方案本身就不该通过评审。
optionExplanations_en: Right — old rows need renumbering and every reference to them must follow, all without pausing live writes.
A ULID is just a fixed-length string or 128-bit value; nothing stops it from being a primary key.
The published_at column still exists, so sorting by time is unaffected by which primary key you use.
Migration rewrites identifiers rather than deleting rows; a plan that loses data should never pass review.

scenario: 文章由多个采集实例并发写入，而 cursor 分页依赖 article_id 大致按时间递增。
scenario_en: Articles are written concurrently by several ingestion instances, while cursor pagination depends on article_id increasing roughly with time.
q: 多实例并发写入时怎么生成有序 ID 又不卡吞吐？
q_en: How do you generate ordered ids across concurrent writers without capping throughput?
options: 各实例本地生成 ULID，用时间戳前缀保证大致有序
所有实例抢同一个数据库自增列，写入全部串行化
每个实例各自生成随机 UUID，反正保证了唯一性
实例之间每生成一个 ID 都先投票达成一次共识
options_en: Each instance generates ULIDs locally, with the timestamp prefix keeping them roughly ordered.
All instances contend on one database auto-increment column, serializing every write.
Each instance generates random UUIDs on its own, since uniqueness is guaranteed anyway.
Instances run a consensus vote among themselves before every single id they generate.
why: 把时间戳编进 ID 前缀，顺序信息就随 ID 一起本地产生，不需要任何跨实例协调；代价是同一毫秒内跨实例的先后并不严格。
why_en: Encoding the timestamp into the id prefix produces ordering locally with no cross-instance coordination, at the cost of loose ordering within the same millisecond.
whenOtherWins: 如果要求 ID 严格单调且不能有跨实例乱序，就得上中心化发号器，用吞吐上限换严格全序。
tradeoff: 本地生成 ULID 的吞吐 vs 中心化发号器的严格全序

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间戳放在前缀里的唯一标识符，字典序即大致时间序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ULID is a unique identifier whose timestamp prefix makes lexicographic order roughly chronological.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一标识符，通常随机生成，因此不带时间顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Universally Unique Identifier is a typically random identifier that carries no chronological order.

optionExplanations: 对，顺序来自 ID 自身的时间前缀，写入路径上没有需要排队的共享资源。
共享自增列会把所有采集实例挤到一个写点上，吞吐直接被单点限死。
随机值只解决唯一性，拿它当 cursor 翻页会得到毫无意义的顺序。
为每条数据跑一轮共识，延迟按网络往返计，高频采集写完全承受不起。
optionExplanations_en: Right — order comes from the id's own time prefix, so the write path shares no resource that needs queuing.
A shared auto-increment column funnels every ingestion instance through one write point, capping throughput there.
Random values only give uniqueness; using them as a paging cursor yields a meaningless order.
Running consensus per row costs a network round trip each time, which high-rate ingestion cannot absorb.

scenario: 区域 feed 存在 Redis sorted set feed:US 里，团队想让每篇文章各自在 30 分钟后消失，好控制这个 key 的大小。
scenario_en: The regional feed lives in a Redis sorted set feed:US, and the team wants each article to expire on its own after 30 minutes to bound the key size.
q: Redis sorted set 能给单个成员设过期时间吗？
q_en: Can a Redis sorted set expire an individual member?
options: 不能，TTL 只作用在整个 key，成员级要靠排名裁剪
能，用 EXPIRE 直接对 sorted set 的某个成员设置
能，把 score 换成过期时间戳，Redis 会自动清理
能，为每篇文章单独建 key 并挂进同一个 sorted set
options_en: No — TTL applies to the whole key, so member-level bounding needs rank trimming.
Yes — call EXPIRE directly on one member of the sorted set.
Yes — set the score to an expiry timestamp and Redis cleans up automatically.
Yes — give each article its own key and hang it inside the same sorted set.
codeSample:
ZADD feed:US 1719000000 article:123        # score = 发布时间戳
ZREMRANGEBYRANK feed:US 0 -2001            # 只保留最新 2000 篇
EXPIRE feed:US 1800                        # TTL 只能挂在整个 key 上
why: Redis 的过期机制注册在 key 上，sorted set 成员没有独立生命周期；所以 CDC 方案改用 ZADD 之后立刻裁掉最旧的，用固定条数代替过期时间控制大小。
why_en: Redis registers expiry on keys, not on sorted set members, so the CDC design bounds size by trimming right after each write to keep a fixed number of newest entries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长，到期后自动被清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is how long a cache entry survives before it is automatically evicted.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按 score 排序的集合结构，支持按排名或按分数范围读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure ordered by score that supports reads by rank or by score range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更数据捕获：把数据库的行级变更实时转成事件流供下游消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture turns row-level database changes into a real-time event stream for downstream consumers.

optionExplanations: 对，所以大小要靠"只保留最新 N 篇"这种按排名裁剪的方式来兜。
EXPIRE 的参数是 key 名，Redis 根本没有接受成员参数的过期命令。
score 只决定排序位置，Redis 不会去解读它的语义并据此删成员。
成员是字符串不是 key 引用，独立的 key 过期不会让它从集合里消失。
optionExplanations_en: Right — so size is bounded by rank trimming, keeping only the newest N entries.
EXPIRE takes a key name; Redis has no expiry command that accepts a member argument at all.
Score only decides ordering position; Redis never interprets its meaning to delete members.
Members are strings, not key references, so expiring a separate key does not remove them from the set.

q: 把区域 feed 的 cache-aside 读路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the cache-aside read path for a regional feed in order:
steps: Feed Service 先读 Redis 里的 feed:US
未命中时回落数据库，按发布时间查该地区最新文章
把查到的结果写回 Redis 并挂上 30 分钟 TTL
返回给客户端，同一地区的后续请求直接命中缓存
why: cache-aside 由应用自己负责回填：只有 miss 才查库，查完立刻写回。代价是每轮过期后的第一批请求要吃满数据库延迟，集中过期时还会形成惊群。
why_en: In cache-aside the application does the backfill itself: only a miss hits the database, so the first requests after each expiry pay full database latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存旁路模式：应用先查缓存，未命中时自己查库并把结果写回缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the application checks the cache first and, on a miss, queries the database and writes the result back itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长，到期后自动被清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is how long a cache entry survives before it is automatically evicted.

scenario: 第一页已经从 feed:US 这个 sorted set 读出，客户端带回最后一篇文章的时间戳 1719000000 当 cursor。
scenario_en: The first page has been read from the feed:US sorted set, and the client sends back the last article's timestamp 1719000000 as the cursor.
q: 在 Redis 缓存上继续翻下一页该怎么读？
q_en: How do you fetch the next page directly off the Redis cache?
options: 按 score 严格小于 cursor 做倒序范围读，限制 20 条
按固定排名区间 20 到 39 取出第二页的内容
绕开缓存回落数据库，用 OFFSET 20 LIMIT 20 查
把整个 sorted set 全量取回来后在应用内存里切页
options_en: Do a reverse range read by score strictly below the cursor, limited to 20 entries.
Take the fixed rank window from 20 to 39 as the second page.
Bypass the cache and query the database with OFFSET 20 LIMIT 20.
Pull the entire sorted set back and slice pages in application memory.
codeSample:
ZREVRANGEBYSCORE feed:US (1719000000 -inf LIMIT 0 20
# ( 表示开区间，排除掉 cursor 那一条本身
# score 就是发布时间戳，按 score 翻页 = 按时间翻页
why: score 就是发布时间戳，所以 cursor 分页在缓存层可以原样保留：按分数开区间倒序取下一批，新文章插到顶部也不会推动这个边界。
why_en: Because the score is the publish timestamp, cursor paging carries over to the cache unchanged: a reverse range below the cursor stays stable as new articles land on top.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要固定的首页而永远不翻页，直接按排名读 ZREVRANGE 0 19 更简单。
tradeoff: 按分数的稳定游标 vs 按排名读取的写法简单

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按 score 排序的集合结构，支持按排名或按分数范围读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure ordered by score that supports reads by rank or by score range.

optionExplanations: 对，分数边界固定在那一刻的时间戳上，顶部插入多少新文章都影响不到它。
排名会随着新成员插入整体后移，第 20 到 39 名指向的内容一直在变。
缓存里已有现成的有序数据，特意回落数据库等于放弃了这层的全部收益。
一次拉回上千个成员再切页，网络传输和序列化开销都花在没用的部分上。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the score boundary is pinned to that instant, so any number of new articles on top cannot move it.
Ranks shift as new members are inserted, so positions 20 through 39 keep pointing at different content.
The cache already holds ordered data; deliberately falling back to the database throws away this layer entirely.
Fetching a thousand members just to slice one page spends transfer and deserialization cost on data nobody reads.

scenario: 区域 feed 从 TTL 缓存换成事件驱动预计算：数据库变更 → CDC → 消息队列 → feed worker → Redis。
scenario_en: The regional feed moves from TTL caching to event-driven precomputation: database change to CDC to a message queue to feed workers to Redis.
q: 相比 TTL 缓存，这条流水线主要多出什么运维负担？
q_en: Compared with a TTL cache, what operational burden does this pipeline add?
options: CDC、队列、worker 三段都要各自监控和排障
数据库从此不能再接受新文章的写入操作
Redis 必须整个换成关系型存储才能被队列写入
客户端要自己订阅数据库变更来刷新 feed
options_en: CDC, the queue, and the workers each need their own monitoring and debugging.
The database can no longer accept new article writes at all.
Redis must be swapped for relational storage before the queue can write to it.
Clients must subscribe to database changes themselves to refresh the feed.
why: 新鲜度从 30 分钟提到秒级，代价是把一条读路径换成三段有状态链路；任何一段积压或崩掉，缓存都只会静默变旧而不会报错。
why_en: Freshness improves from thirty minutes to seconds by replacing one read path with three stateful stages, and if any stage stalls the cache goes quietly stale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更数据捕获：把数据库的行级变更实时转成事件流供下游消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture turns row-level database changes into a real-time event stream for downstream consumers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时长，到期后自动被清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is how long a cache entry survives before it is automatically evicted.

optionExplanations: 对，排查"文章为什么没进 feed"要沿着三处分别看延迟、积压和消费位点。
写入路径完全没变，恰恰是这些写入产生的变更事件驱动了整条流水线。
队列消费者是我们自己的 worker，它拿什么存储写 feed 由我们决定。
客户端只调 feed 接口，数据库变更是内部实现，不该暴露给外部。
optionExplanations_en: Right — diagnosing why an article never reached the feed means checking lag, backlog, and consumer offset in three separate places.
The write path is unchanged; those very writes are what emit the change events driving the pipeline.
The queue consumer is our own worker, so which store it writes the feed into is entirely our choice.
Clients only call the feed endpoint; database changes are an internal detail that should not be exposed.

scenario: 重大新闻发生时，几十家发布方会在同一分钟里向 /webhooks/article-published 集中推送。
scenario_en: When a big story breaks, dozens of publishers push to /webhooks/article-published within the same minute.
q: webhook 端点该怎么扛住这种同时到达的尖峰？
q_en: How should the webhook endpoint absorb this simultaneous spike?
options: 校验后立刻入队返回 200，处理放到队列后面异步做
在请求里同步跑完入库和缓存更新之后再返回 200
超出当前处理能力的推送一律返回 500 让对方重试
限制每家发布方每小时只允许推送固定的若干次
options_en: Validate, enqueue, and return 200 immediately, doing the work asynchronously behind the queue.
Run ingestion and cache updates synchronously inside the request before returning 200.
Reject anything beyond current capacity with a 500 and let the caller retry.
Cap each publisher at a fixed number of pushes per hour.
why: webhook 的调用时机由发布方决定，尖峰形状我们控制不了；端点只做认证和入队就返回，把处理速率交给队列后面的 worker 平滑。
why_en: Publishers decide when webhooks fire, so we cannot shape the spike — the endpoint only authenticates and enqueues, letting workers smooth the processing rate.
whenOtherWins: 如果发布方需要在响应里立刻知道文章是否被接受（比如格式不合法要当场报错），同步处理才合适。
tradeoff: 快速 ACK 加异步处理的抗尖峰能力 vs 同步处理的即时反馈

termDefinitions.meaning: 确认响应，表示请求已被接收，不一定已经处理完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acknowledgement is a response confirming a request was received, though not necessarily finished.

optionExplanations: 对，代价是发布方拿到 200 时文章还没进 feed，接收成功不等于已生效。
同步做完意味着响应时间跟下游最慢的一环绑死，尖峰一来连接池先被占满。
推送方看到 5xx 通常会立刻重试，等于在最忙的时刻把流量又放大一轮。
限流会直接丢掉重大新闻本身，而这恰恰是我们最想第一时间拿到的内容。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the cost is that a 200 means received, not live, so the article is not in the feed yet.
Doing it synchronously ties response time to the slowest downstream stage, and a spike exhausts the connection pool first.
Senders usually retry immediately on a 5xx, which amplifies traffic exactly at the busiest moment.
Throttling drops the breaking story itself, which is precisely the content we most want the instant it appears.

scenario: webhook 采集要求每家发布方在自己的发布流程里加一次对我们接口的调用，很多小站没有工程团队。
scenario_en: Webhook ingestion asks each publisher to add a call to our endpoint inside their own publishing flow, and many small sites have no engineering team.
q: 为什么 webhook 不能当作唯一的采集方式？
q_en: Why can webhooks not be the only ingestion path?
options: 它要发布方主动改造，小站没有技术资源做这件事
webhook 推送的内容一定缺少标题和发布时间
HTTP POST 请求体不能携带文章正文这类长文本
webhook 到达的文章会绕过我们的地区划分逻辑
options_en: It requires publishers to change their own systems, and small sites lack the engineering resources.
Webhook payloads are always missing the title and publish time.
An HTTP POST body cannot carry long text like article content.
Articles arriving via webhook bypass our regional partitioning logic.
why: 轮询和抓取我们可以单方面上线，webhook 必须对方配合，覆盖率注定不满；所以它只能是最快的那一档，RSS 轮询和抓取仍要留着兜底。
why_en: Polling and scraping we can deploy unilaterally, but webhooks need the other side to cooperate, so coverage is never complete and the fallbacks must stay.
optionExplanations: 对，能不能拿到内容取决于对方愿不愿意排期，这是谈判问题不是技术问题。
推送体里放什么由我们定的契约决定，标题和时间戳正是必填字段。
POST 请求体可以携带完整正文，很多发布方推送时就是这么做的。
地区是我们在处理时按发布方属性打的，跟内容通过哪条通道进来无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right — whether we get the content depends on whether they will schedule the work, a negotiation problem rather than a technical one.
What the payload contains is defined by our contract, and title plus timestamp are exactly the required fields.
A POST body can carry full article text, and many publishers do send it that way.
Region is assigned by us from publisher attributes during processing, regardless of which channel delivered the content.

scenario: 缩略图存在 S3 上并生成了移动端、桌面端、高密屏三种尺寸，前面挂 CloudFront 做全球分发。
scenario_en: Thumbnails sit in S3 in mobile, desktop, and retina sizes, with CloudFront in front for global distribution.
q: 补全加了 CDN 之后的成本与延迟变化：
q_en: Fill in how cost and latency change once the CDN is added:
text: 回源请求数 = 总请求数 × (1 − 边缘命中率)。CloudFront 在边缘缓存后能把回源 S3 的请求减少 {{90%}} 以上，因此多存几种尺寸带来的存储成本被整体{{抵消}}，全球缩略图加载也进入 {{200ms}} 以内。
why: S3 egress 按请求和流量计费，命中率高到九成以上时这部分只剩十分之一，足以盖过多存两三份缩略图的存储费。
why_en: S3 egress is billed per request and per byte, so once the edge absorbs over ninety percent of them the remaining tenth easily outweighs a couple of extra thumbnail sizes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络：把静态文件缓存在离用户近的边缘节点上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Content Delivery Network caches static files at edge locations close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据从云服务流出到互联网时按量收取的出网流量费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Egress is the metered cost of data flowing out of a cloud service to the internet.

q: 把突发新闻扩容时的逐组件评估法排好序：
q_en: Put the per-component scaling evaluation in order:
steps: 先算这个组件在峰值时的资源需求是多少
对照现有设计判断它能不能满足这个需求
不满足就选对应的扩展手段：水平扩、加读副本或让缓存挡在前面
换下一个组件，用同样三步重新走一遍
why: 扩容不是笼统地"加机器"：对 Feed Service、数据库、Redis 逐个算峰值再决定手段，才能看出数据库其实是被缓存挡掉的，真正要扩的是缓存读吞吐。
why_en: Scaling is not a blanket add-more-servers: sizing Feed Service, database, and Redis one at a time reveals the cache absorbs the database load, so the real target is cache read throughput.

scenario: 团队不打算引入 Redis，但同样要让区域 feed 承接突发新闻期间的千万级并发读。
scenario_en: The team will not adopt Redis, yet the regional feed still has to absorb tens of millions of concurrent reads during breaking news.
q: 不用 Redis 时，等价的读扩展结构是什么？
q_en: Without Redis, what is the equivalent read-scaling structure?
options: 一致性哈希分片，每个分片再带一两个副本
把全部地区的 feed 都塞进单台大内存机器里
让每个应用实例各自缓存一份完整的区域 feed
干脆取消缓存层，所有 feed 读直接打到数据库
options_en: Shard with consistent hashing and give each shard one or two replicas.
Cram every region's feed into a single large-memory machine.
Let every application instance keep its own full copy of the regional feed.
Drop the cache layer entirely and send all feed reads to the database.
why: 关键结构不是 Redis 这个产品，而是"分片摊数据量、副本摊读吞吐并做故障转移"这一组；换成任何内存存储都照搬。代价是要自己运维这套分片。
why_en: The structure that matters is not Redis itself but sharding to spread data and replicas to spread reads and fail over, which transfers to any in-memory store.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队已经有 Redis 运维经验，直接用主从加 Sentinel 比自建一套分片省事得多。
tradeoff: 自建一致性哈希分片的可控性 vs 现成主从方案的运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点映射到同一个环上的分片算法，增删节点时只搬动少量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto one ring so adding or removing a node moves only a small share of data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 自带的高可用组件，负责监控主节点并在故障时提升副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentinel is the Redis high-availability component that watches the primary and promotes a replica on failure.

optionExplanations: 对，分片解决容量和写入分布，副本解决读吞吐和主节点挂掉后的接管。
单机内存再大也只有一份网卡和 CPU，读吞吐会先于容量撞上天花板。
每个实例各存一份就没有统一写入点，同一地区不同实例会给出不同 feed。
这正是引入缓存要解决的问题，撤掉之后数据库会被千万级读直接压垮。
optionExplanations_en: Right — shards spread capacity and writes, while replicas spread reads and take over when a primary dies.
However large one machine's memory is, it still has one NIC and one CPU, so read throughput hits the ceiling first.
A private copy per instance leaves no single write point, so two instances would serve different feeds for one region.
This is exactly the problem the cache exists to solve; removing it puts tens of millions of reads onto the database.

scenario: feed 读被负载均衡到多个 Redis 读副本上，主从之间是异步复制，延迟通常在 200ms 以内。
scenario_en: Feed reads are load-balanced across Redis read replicas with asynchronous replication that typically lags under 200ms.
q: 对新闻 feed 来说，这个复制延迟该怎么判断？
q_en: How should you judge that replication lag for a news feed?
options: 可接受，一条新闻晚 200ms 出现用户根本察觉不到
不可接受，所有 feed 读都必须回到主节点上去
不可接受，必须改成等所有副本确认的同步复制
不用管，异步复制不会让副本读到旧数据
options_en: Acceptable — a story appearing 200ms later is imperceptible to users.
Unacceptable — every feed read must go back to the primary.
Unacceptable — replication must become synchronous, waiting for all replicas.
Irrelevant — asynchronous replication never serves stale data from replicas.
why: 非功能需求里明确可用性优先于一致性，200ms 的滞后远小于用户对新闻新鲜度的感知阈值；换来的是读吞吐可以按副本数扩。
why_en: The requirements put availability ahead of consistency, and a 200ms lag sits far below what a news reader can perceive, buying read throughput that scales with replicas.
whenOtherWins: 如果读的是余额、库存这类必须读到自己刚写入的数据，就得走主节点或同步复制。
tradeoff: 读副本的吞吐扩展 vs 异步复制带来的短暂陈旧读
optionExplanations: 对，这正是"可用性优先于一致性"这条需求在具体数字上的兑现方式。
把读全压回主节点等于放弃了副本存在的意义，主节点马上成为吞吐瓶颈。
同步复制要等最慢的那个副本确认，写延迟被拉长，可用性反而下降。
异步复制期间副本上确实是旧值，只是这里的旧得不够久，影响不到体验。
optionExplanations_en: Right — this is what availability over consistency looks like once it is cashed out in real numbers.
Forcing all reads back to the primary defeats the purpose of replicas and makes the primary the bottleneck.
Synchronous replication waits for the slowest replica, stretching write latency and lowering availability instead.
Replicas genuinely do hold older values during async replication — the point is that here it is not old enough to matter.

scenario: 要支持 Sports、Politics、Tech 等分类 feed，文章在入库时就得带上 category 字段。
scenario_en: To support Sports, Politics, and Tech feeds, each article needs a category assigned at ingest time.
q: 入库时可以从哪些来源提取文章的 category？（多选）
q_en: Which sources can supply an article's category at ingest time? (Select all that apply.)
options: RSS feed 里发布方自己打的 <category> 标签
分析网页结构，从栏目路径或版块位置判断
对标题和正文做关键词匹配来归类
按发布方所在的国家和地区直接推断
options_en: The <category> tag the publisher already puts in the RSS feed.
Web page structure analysis, reading the section path or placement.
Keyword matching against the article title and body.
Inferring it directly from the publisher's country and region.
why: 优先用发布方已经标好的分类，缺失时才退到页面结构分析和关键词匹配；准确度依次下降，但覆盖率依次上升。
why_en: Prefer the category the publisher declared, and fall back to page structure and keyword matching only when it is missing — accuracy drops down that list while coverage rises.
optionExplanations: 发布方自己标的最准，拿来即用，省掉我们全部的推断成本。
栏目路径反映的是站点自己的编辑分类，比猜内容语义可靠得多。
关键词是覆盖没有任何结构线索的来源的兜底，代价是会误判一部分。
地区和分类是两个正交维度，同一个地区的发布方什么题材都发。
optionExplanations_en: What the publisher declared is the most accurate and free to use, sparing us any inference cost.
A section path reflects the site's own editorial taxonomy, far more reliable than guessing semantics.
Keywords are the fallback for sources with no structural hints, at the price of some misclassification.
Region and category are orthogonal dimensions — publishers in one region cover every topic there is.

scenario: 区域缓存里存的是完整文章 JSON（含 category 字段），分类请求靠读回整段缓存再在应用里过滤。
scenario_en: The regional cache stores full article JSON including a category field, and category requests read the whole cache back and filter in the application.
q: 补全内存过滤路径的耗时构成和它支撑的判断：
q_en: Fill in the latency breakdown of in-memory filtering and the decision it supports:
text: 总耗时 = 缓存读取 + 应用内过滤：从 Redis 读回最近 1000 篇缓存文章约 {{10ms}} 以内，按 category 过滤再加 {{1-2ms}}，合起来远低于 {{200ms}} 这个给定的 feed 延迟目标。
why: 200ms 是产品给定的 SLO，不是算出来的；这里十几毫秒的实测说明余量充足，因此不必为 25 个分类乘 10 个地区维护 250 个缓存键。
why_en: The 200ms figure is a given service level objective rather than a derived result, and a dozen milliseconds of headroom justifies not maintaining 250 separate category cache keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队对外承诺的延迟或可用性指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is the latency or availability target a team commits to.

scenario: 个性化排序需要一份用户画像，排序函数本身是 ML 模型，这里只关心喂给它的信号。
scenario_en: Personalized ranking needs a user profile; the scoring function itself is an ML model, so only its input signals matter here.
q: 构建用户画像时会用到哪些信号？（多选）
q_en: Which signals go into building a user profile? (Select all that apply.)
options: 用户显式订阅的主题和偏好的发布方
点击、阅读时长、分享这类行为数据
协同过滤得出的相似用户的阅读偏好
用户设备当前的电池电量和存储余量
options_en: Topics the user explicitly subscribed to and publishers they prefer.
Behavioral data such as clicks, reading time, and shares.
Preferences of similar users derived from collaborative filtering.
The device's current battery level and remaining storage.
why: 画像由显式偏好和行为信号两类构成，再用协同过滤补上"读过 A 和 B 的人也读 C"；三者一起决定文章的相关性分数。
why_en: A profile combines explicit preferences with behavioral signals, then collaborative filtering adds the readers-of-A-and-B-also-read-C pattern to set relevance scores.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据"和你行为相似的人还喜欢什么"来推荐内容的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends content based on what users with similar behavior also engaged with.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习，这里指给文章打相关性分数的排序模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Machine Learning here refers to the ranking model that scores articles for relevance.

optionExplanations: 显式偏好是用户自己说出口的意图，最可靠也最不用猜。
行为信号补上用户没说但真实在读的部分，比自述更贴近实际兴趣。
协同过滤能推出新兴趣，帮新用户越过冷启动阶段。
电量和存储属于设备状态，跟这个人想读什么题材毫无关联。
optionExplanations_en: Explicit preferences are intent the user stated outright — the most reliable input, with no guessing.
Behavioral signals capture what they actually read but never said, closer to real interest than self-report.
Collaborative filtering surfaces new interests and helps new users past the cold-start stage.
Battery and storage are device state and say nothing about what topics this person wants to read.

scenario: 注册用户里只有一部分每天都来，但给全部用户都预计算个性化 feed 的内存扛不住。
scenario_en: Only some registered users show up daily, yet precomputing a personalized feed for all of them does not fit in memory.
q: 预计算和按需生成该怎么在用户之间分配？
q_en: How should precomputation and on-demand generation be split across users?
options: 活跃用户预计算，不活跃用户按需从分类缓存现拼
所有用户一律预计算，靠不断加内存来解决问题
所有用户一律按需生成，彻底放弃预计算这条路
按注册时间的先后来决定谁能享受预计算待遇
options_en: Precompute for active users and assemble on demand from category caches for inactive ones.
Precompute for everyone and keep adding memory to cope.
Generate everything on demand and abandon precomputation entirely.
Decide who gets precomputation by how early they registered.
why: 预计算的成本随用户数线性上涨，收益却只落在真会来的人身上；按活跃度分层把内存花在会被读到的 feed 上。代价是不活跃用户回归时首刷慢一点。
why_en: Precomputation costs scale with user count while the benefit only lands on users who return, so tiering by activity spends memory on feeds that actually get read.
whenOtherWins: 如果绝大多数注册用户每天都活跃，分层就没有意义，全量预计算反而更简单。
tradeoff: 预计算换来的读延迟 vs 随用户规模线性增长的内存成本
optionExplanations: 对，判断依据是这份 feed 被读到的概率，而不是这个用户是否存在。
内存随注册人数线性上涨而利用率很低，等于长期为不会被读的数据付费。
每次都现拼会让活跃用户的每一次刷新都承担组装开销，最热的路径最慢。
注册早晚跟他今天会不会来毫无关系，拿它分层等于随机分配内存。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the criterion is the probability this feed gets read, not whether the user exists.
Memory grows linearly with the user base at very low utilization, paying indefinitely for data nobody reads.
Assembling every time makes every refresh by an active user pay assembly cost, so the hottest path is slowest.
Registration date says nothing about whether they show up today, so tiering on it allocates memory at random.

scenario: 重大突发新闻发生，但很多用户的偏好向量里根本没有这个主题的权重。
scenario_en: A major story breaks, but many users' preference vectors carry no weight for that topic at all.
q: 混合组装的个性化 feed 怎么保证这条新闻能被看到？
q_en: How does a mix-assembled personalized feed make sure that story is seen?
options: 临时上调 trending 权重，压低个人偏好权重
把所有用户的偏好向量清空之后重新学习一遍
为这条突发新闻单独建一份覆盖全部用户的缓存
完全不做处理，等用户自己去分类页里慢慢翻到这条新闻
options_en: Temporarily raise the trending category weight and lower personal preference weights.
Wipe every user's preference vector and relearn from scratch.
Build a dedicated cache of this one story covering every single user.
Do nothing and let users find the story by browsing category pages.
why: 既然 feed 就是按比例混合几个分类缓存，突发期直接改这组比例是最省事的开关；代价是这段时间个性化被稀释，所有人的 feed 更接近通用 feed。
why_en: Since the feed is just a weighted mix of category caches, changing the weights is the cheapest switch during breaking news, at the cost of diluting personalization.
whenOtherWins: 平时没有全局要闻的时候，保持原比例才能让个性化真正发挥作用。
tradeoff: 突发期的全局重要性 vs 平时的个性化深度
optionExplanations: 对，调权重是全局配置改动，不用碰任何一个用户的数据就能立刻生效。
清空画像会把所有人打回冷启动，为了一条新闻毁掉长期积累的信号。
给上亿用户各写一份，正是这套方案当初为了省内存要避开的做法。
突发新闻的价值全在时效，等用户主动去找等于放弃了这份价值。
optionExplanations_en: Right — weights are a global config change that takes effect immediately without touching any user's data.
Wiping profiles resets everyone to cold start, destroying long-accumulated signal for the sake of one story.
Writing a copy for hundreds of millions of users is exactly the memory blowup this design was built to avoid.
A breaking story's value is entirely in timeliness, so waiting for users to hunt for it throws that value away.

scenario: feed 按 region 分区预计算缓存，但大量用户没登录，也从来没设置过自己的地区。
scenario_en: Feeds are precomputed per region, yet many users are anonymous and have never set a region.
q: 匿名用户的 region 字段该怎么确定？
q_en: How should the region field be determined for anonymous users?
options: 按请求来源 IP 推断一个默认值，允许用户显式覆盖
统一给所有匿名用户发全球混合 feed，不区分地区
强制要求先注册登录才能看到任何 feed 内容
随机分配一个地区缓存，反正后面会慢慢修正过来
options_en: Infer a default from the request IP and let the user override it explicitly.
Serve all anonymous users one global mixed feed with no regional split.
Require registration and login before showing any feed content at all.
Assign a random region cache and assume it gets corrected later.
why: region 是决定读哪个预计算缓存键的路由字段，每个请求都必须有值，所以匿名用户也要有轻量档案；代价是 VPN 和跨境用户会先拿到错的地区。
why_en: Region routes the request to a precomputed cache key, so every request needs one and even anonymous users get a lightweight profile.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户经常跨境或长期用 VPN，让他显式选择地区比 IP 推断可靠得多。
tradeoff: IP 推断的零摩擦 vs 显式设置的准确性

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络地址，可以粗略映射到访问者所在的国家或城市。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Internet Protocol address is a network address that maps roughly to the visitor's country or city.

termDefinitions.meaning: 虚拟专用网络，会让请求看起来来自另一个国家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Virtual Private Network makes requests appear to originate from another country.

optionExplanations: 对，推断给默认值、设置做覆盖，这样第一次访问就能命中某个区域缓存。
全球混合会让美国用户第一屏看到大量无关的外国本地新闻，相关性崩掉。
强制登录会挡掉聚合器最大的一部分流量，为一个可推断字段付出太多。
随机地区意味着首屏内容和用户毫无关系，而且没有任何机制去修正它。
optionExplanations_en: Right — inference supplies the default and settings override it, so even a first visit hits some regional cache.
A global mix fills a US reader's first screen with irrelevant foreign local news, collapsing relevance.
Forcing login blocks the largest slice of an aggregator's traffic, a steep price for a field we can infer.
A random region makes the first screen unrelated to the user, with no mechanism to ever correct it.

q: Gopuff 题目的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core functional requirements are in scope for the Gopuff design? (Select all)
options: 按用户位置查询 1 小时内可送达商品的有效库存
允许用户一次下单多个商品
首版实现支付、司机路径规划和退货
首版只关注 availability 和 ordering
why: 本题只保留附近 DC 库存聚合和下单不超卖：库存行数 = 10k DC × 100k item；支付、配送、搜索、退货划到线下范围。
why_en: The core scope is local availability aggregation and multi-item ordering without double booking, not payments, routing, or returns.
optionExplanations: 对。这是核心读需求：按位置聚合 1 小时可达的库存。
对。多商品下单是核心写需求，直接决定事务要覆盖多行库存。
错。这些明确写进「线下范围」，首版故意不做。
对。范围声明本身就是需求，划清边界避免过度设计。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - this is the core read requirement: aggregate one-hour-reachable stock by location.
Correct - multi-item ordering is a core write requirement that shapes the transaction.
Wrong - these are explicitly out of scope for the first version.
Correct - stating scope is itself a requirement that keeps the design focused.
options_en: Query the effective available stock, deliverable within one hour, by the user's location.
Let a user order multiple items in a single purchase.
Build payments, driver routing, and returns in the first version.
Scope the first version to availability and ordering only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放库存的微型配送仓，用户附近的实物库存来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distribution center (DC) is a micro-warehouse that stores physical inventory near users.

scenario: 面试只有 45 分钟设计 Gopuff 即时零售：10k 个 DC 分散存货，承诺 1 小时送达。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to design Gopuff instant retail: stock spread across 10,000 distribution centers with a one-hour delivery promise.

q: Gopuff 系统的关键非功能需求有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for this Gopuff system? (Select all)
options: availability 查询小于 100ms
下单强一致，不能两个用户买到同一件实物
支持约 10k 个 DC 和 100k 个 catalog item
允许库存扣减最终一致且可超卖
why: 读路径要快，写路径要强一致，规模锚点是 10k DC、100k item 和千万级订单/天。
why_en: The design must make availability reads fast, orders strongly consistent, and scale to thousands of distribution centers and catalog items.
optionExplanations: 对。读路径要快才能支撑类似搜索的体验。
对。防超卖是本题最硬的一致性要求。
对。这两个数字是分区和索引设计的规模锚点。
错。文章明确要求强一致防超卖，不能接受超卖。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - fast reads are needed to support search-like use cases.
Correct - preventing overselling is the hardest consistency requirement here.
Correct - these two numbers anchor the partitioning and indexing design.
Wrong - the article requires strong consistency precisely to prevent overselling.
options_en: Availability queries should respond in under 100 milliseconds.
Ordering must be strongly consistent so two customers can never buy the same physical item.
The system should support roughly 10,000 distribution centers and 100,000 catalog items.
Inventory decrements can be eventually consistent and allow overselling.
scenario: Gopuff 即时零售：浏览量远大于下单量，读要快；同一件实物只有一份，两人不能同时买走。
scenario_en: In Gopuff instant retail, browsing far outnumbers orders so reads must be fast, while one physical unit can never be sold to two people.

q: Item 和 Inventory 在这题里的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between Item and Inventory in this design?
options: 两者完全相同，只是数据库里的表命名不同
Item 是目录商品类型，Inventory 是 DC 实物
Item 只能被下单，Inventory 只能被搜索
Item 是 DC 的实物库存，Inventory 只是目录名称
why: 用户看到的是商品类型，比如 Cheetos；系统防超卖时关心的是具体 DC 里可扣减的实物库存。
why_en: Item is the catalog concept customers see, while Inventory is the physical stock at a specific distribution center.
optionExplanations: 错。两者语义完全不同，不是同义词。
对。用户看到的是商品类型；防超卖关心的是具体 DC 里的实物。
错。这里把下单和搜索的角色分反了，两个实体都不是这样限定的。
错。这里把角色整个说反了：Item 是目录商品类型，Inventory 才是某个 DC 的实物库存。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - the two concepts are not synonyms at all.
Correct - customers see the item type, while oversell prevention cares about physical stock at a DC.
Wrong - this swaps the roles; neither entity is restricted that way.
Wrong - this reverses the roles: Item is the catalog product type, and Inventory is the physical stock at a DC.
tradeoff: 目录概念 Item vs 物理库存 Inventory
options_en: The two are identical, just different table names in the database.
Item is the catalog product type; Inventory is physical stock at a DC.
Item can only be ordered, and Inventory can only be searched.
Item is physical stock at a DC, and Inventory is just the catalog name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 DC 中一件商品的实物库存记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inventory is the record of physical stock for one item at a specific distribution center.

scenario: Gopuff 目录里有 100k 种商品，同一种 Cheetos 分散在 10k 个 DC，下单必须扣到某个 DC 的实物。
scenario_en: Gopuff has 100k catalog products, the same Cheetos sits in 10,000 DCs, and an order must decrement real stock at one specific DC.

q: Gopuff 设计中的核心实体有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities belong in the Gopuff design? (Select all)
options: Inventory：某 DC 中的实物库存
Item：用户看到的商品类型
DistributionCenter：库存所在的物理仓点
Order：一次用户下单及其包含的库存项
why: 这四个实体分别支撑库存聚合、目录展示、地理可送达判断和下单记录；库存行数 = DC 数 × item 数。
why_en: Inventory, Item, DistributionCenter, and Order cover the physical stock, catalog view, geography, and purchase record.
optionExplanations: 对。这是防超卖判断真正依赖的实体。
对。这是客户端展示和下单请求引用的实体。
对。它承载地理位置，决定谁能在 1 小时内送达。
对。它把多件库存和一次购买绑定成一条记录。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - this is the entity oversell checks actually depend on.
Correct - clients reference this entity for display and ordering.
Correct - it carries the location that decides one-hour deliverability.
Correct - it binds multiple inventory rows to a single purchase.
options_en: Inventory: the physical stock of an item held at one distribution center.
Item: the catalog-level product type customers see.
DistributionCenter: the physical warehouse where inventory lives.
Order: one purchase and the inventory items it includes.
scenario: Gopuff 要按用户位置聚合附近 DC 的库存，并在一个事务里原子下单不超卖。
scenario_en: Gopuff aggregates stock across nearby DCs by user location and must place orders atomically without overselling.

scenario: 客户端要按经纬度查询当前位置 1 小时内可送达的商品库存，并避免一次返回过多数据。
scenario_en: The client queries stock deliverable within one hour by latitude and longitude, with pagination to keep responses bounded.
q: 最贴合 availability 查询的 API 是？
q_en: Which API best fits the availability query?
options: POST /drivers/{driverId}/route?refresh=true&window=1h
DELETE /inventory/{dcId}/items/{itemId}?confirm=true&reason=oversell
GET /availability?lat={lat}&lng={lng}&page={p}&limit={n}
GET /payments/{orderId}?include=receipt&expand=items
codeSample: GET /availability?lat=37.78&lng=-122.41&page=1&limit=50 -> ItemAvailability[]
why: availability API 的输入是用户位置和分页参数，输出是附近 DC 库存聚合后的商品可用量。
why_en: The availability API needs location and pagination because it returns the union of stock from nearby distribution centers.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目包含搜索排序，另加 catalog/search API 会更合适，但本文把搜索放在线下范围。
optionExplanations: 错。这是配送路径规划，不是查询可用库存。
错。这是危险的写操作，与只读查询需求无关。
对。位置定位附近 DC，分页避免一次吐出过多商品。
错。支付详情和 availability 查询完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - this plans driver routes, not availability.
Wrong - this is a destructive write, unrelated to a read-only query.
Correct - location finds nearby DCs, and pagination avoids returning too much data at once.
Wrong - payment detail lookup has nothing to do with checking availability.
tradeoff: 分页只读查询 vs 一次性返回全部库存
options_en: POST to refresh a driver route for a one-hour window.
DELETE to wipe out one item of a DC inventory, tagging an oversell reason.
GET /availability with lat, lng, page, and limit query parameters.
GET a payment receipt with its line items expanded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 page 和 limit 参数分批返回结果，避免一次响应过大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pagination returns results in pages using parameters like page and limit so a single response stays small.

scenario: 用户一次购买多个商品，后端需要再次确认这些商品在 1 小时可送达范围内且不会超卖。
scenario_en: A user buys multiple items at once, and the backend must recheck one-hour deliverability and prevent overselling.
q: 下单 API 应该包含什么关键信息？
q_en: What key information should the order API carry?
options: 客户端自己传来的库存锁 ID 和扣减数量
支付网关的内部私钥和商户密钥
商品发布方的 RSS 订阅地址
商品列表和用户位置，身份从会话取
why: Orders Service 必须用位置重新找可服务 DC 并在事务里扣库存，用户身份应来自认证上下文而不是客户端伪造字段。
why_en: The order API carries items and location while identity comes from the authenticated context, and the service rechecks local stock transactionally.
whenOtherWins: 如果已经有服务端购物车或 reservation，可只传 cart/reservation id，但仍要在后端校验库存。
optionExplanations: 错。客户端不该自己造锁 ID，库存检查必须在服务端重新做。
错。私钥不该出现在订单请求体里，这是安全事故。
错。RSS 地址和下单毫无关系，纯粹的干扰项。
对。位置用来重新核对可服务 DC，身份来自认证上下文而非客户端字段。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - clients should not invent lock IDs; the server must recheck stock itself.
Wrong - a private key has no place in an order request body; that is a security incident.
Wrong - an RSS URL is unrelated to placing an order.
Correct - location rechecks serviceable DCs, and identity comes from the session, not a client field.
tradeoff: 服务端重新校验位置和身份 vs 信任客户端传来的状态
options_en: An inventory lock ID and decrement count supplied by the client.
The payment gateway private key and merchant secret.
The product publisher RSS feed URL.
The item list and location, with identity taken from the session.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端保存的登录状态，用来确认请求方身份而不依赖客户端自报。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session is server-held login state used to confirm identity instead of trusting client-supplied fields.

q: 把 availability 查询路径按正确顺序排列：
q_en: Put the availability query path in the right order.
steps: 用这些 DC ID 查询库存并按 Item 聚合数量
Availability Service 接收用户位置和过滤条件
Nearby Service 返回 1 小时内可服务的 DC 列表
Availability Service 调用 Nearby Service
why: 先把地理问题缩小到附近 DC，再只在这些 DC 的库存上做聚合。
why_en: Availability first narrows geography to serviceable distribution centers, then aggregates inventory only from those centers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> Avail[Availability Service]
Avail --> Nearby[Nearby Service]
Nearby --> DCs[Nearby DCs]
Avail --> Inv[(Inventory DB)]
Inv --> Result[Available items]

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据用户经纬度返回 1 小时内可送达 DC 列表的内部服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Nearby Service returns the list of distribution centers that can deliver to a location within one hour.

scenario: Availability Service 和 Orders Service 都需要判断哪些 DC 能在 1 小时内送达用户位置。
scenario_en: Both Availability Service and Orders Service need to decide which DCs can deliver to a user within one hour.
q: 这段逻辑最好放在哪里？
q_en: Where should this serviceability logic live?
options: 共享 Nearby Service
各客户端自己算可送达 DC 集合
内嵌进 Orders Service 里各写一份
固定绑定用户最近的一个 DC
why: Nearby Service 复用地理和行车时间逻辑，让 availability 和 order 在同一可服务范围上做判断。
why_en: A shared Nearby Service centralizes serviceability logic so reads and orders use the same delivery-area decision.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是一个单体小系统，可以先做成内部模块，但抽象边界仍是附近 DC 查询。
optionExplanations: 对。两条读写路径共用同一次「谁能送达」的判断结果。
错。客户端各自算容易和后端结果不一致，也重复造轮子。
错。两个服务各实现一遍，半径和行车时间口径迟早漂移。
错。固定单个 DC 完全忽略了行车时间和多仓库存分布。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - both read and write paths share one serviceability decision.
Wrong - client-side computation risks disagreeing with the backend and duplicates logic.
Wrong - two separate copies will drift on radius and travel-time rules.
Wrong - a fixed single DC ignores travel time and the multi-warehouse layout entirely.
tradeoff: 共享服务复用地理逻辑 vs 各服务各自实现
options_en: Put it in a shared Nearby Service.
Let each client compute its own set of serviceable DCs.
Inline a separate copy of the logic inside each service.
Always bind the user to the single closest DC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断哪些 DC 能在 1 小时内送达用户位置的共享服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared service that determines which distribution centers can deliver to a location within one hour.

q: 只用欧氏距离或 Haversine 距离筛 DC，主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with using only Euclidean or Haversine distance to filter DCs?
options: 完全无法计算用户和 DC 之间的经纬度距离
忽略道路、河流和实时交通，1 小时送达可能落空
会自动把所有候选 DC 的库存全部锁定
查询结果只能返回一个商品，无法聚合多个
why: 直线距离只能粗筛，真实送达时间取决于道路网络和交通。
why_en: Straight-line distance is only a rough filter because real delivery time depends on roads, barriers, and traffic.
optionExplanations: 错。经纬度计算本身没问题，Haversine 公式算得出直线距离。
对。直线距离忽略路网和拥堵，可能把开车 90 分钟的 DC 误判成可达。
错。库存锁定属于下单路径，跟距离筛选完全无关。
错。这是聚合返回问题，和距离算法选择无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - lat/long math is fine; the Haversine formula correctly computes straight-line distance.
Correct - straight-line distance ignores roads and traffic, so a 90-minute drive can look reachable.
Wrong - inventory locking belongs to the order path, unrelated to distance filtering.
Wrong - this is an unrelated claim about result aggregation, not distance algorithms.
options_en: It cannot compute the lat/long distance between user and DC at all.
It ignores roads, rivers, and live traffic, so the one-hour promise can fail.
It automatically locks all inventory at every candidate DC.
The query can only return a single item and never an aggregate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 考虑地球曲率计算两经纬度间直线距离的公式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Haversine formula computes the straight-line distance between two latitude/longitude points accounting for Earth's curvature.

scenario: Gopuff 承诺 1 小时送达，要从 10k 个 DC 里筛出真正能按时开到用户手上的那几个。
scenario_en: Gopuff promises delivery within an hour, so it must pick from 10,000 DCs the few that can actually drive there in time.

scenario: 需求明确是 1 小时内送达，直线距离在城市、河流或交通拥堵场景下误差很大。
scenario_en: The requirement is one-hour delivery, and straight-line distance can be very wrong around cities, rivers, or traffic.
q: 更准确的 Nearby 判断应该引入什么？
q_en: What should Nearby use for a more accurate serviceability decision?
options: 库存表里那一行记录的自增主键 ID
Redis 里某个缓存条目的 TTL 过期设置
外部或内部 Travel Time Service
订单当前的支付状态字段和结果
why: 行车时间服务能用路网和交通估计 DC 到用户位置的真实耗时，更贴合 1 小时送达。
why_en: A travel-time service estimates actual driving duration using road and traffic data, matching the one-hour requirement.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是粗略展示附近门店，直线距离或 Haversine 可能足够便宜。
optionExplanations: 错。自增 ID 只是行号，和送达时间毫无关系。
错。TTL 控制缓存过期，不衡量行车时间。
对。行车时间服务能用路网和交通数据估计真实耗时。
错。支付状态发生在下单之后，和判断能否 1 小时送达无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - an auto-increment ID is just a row number, unrelated to delivery time.
Wrong - TTL controls cache expiry, not driving duration.
Correct - a travel-time service estimates real duration using road and traffic data.
Wrong - payment status happens after ordering, unrelated to one-hour reachability.
tradeoff: 真实行车时间估计 vs 便宜但粗糙的直线距离
options_en: The auto-increment primary key of an inventory row.
A Redis cache entry's TTL expiration setting.
An external or internal travel-time service.
The order's current payment-status field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用路网和交通信息估算从 DC 到用户位置实际行车时间的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A travel-time service estimates actual driving duration from a DC to a location using road and traffic data.

scenario: 系统有 10k 个 DC，不能每次用户查询都对每个 DC 调用一次外部行车时间服务。
scenario_en: The system has about 10,000 DCs, so each user query cannot call an external travel-time service for every DC.
q: 合理优化是什么？
q_en: What is the reasonable optimization?
options: 对全部 1 万个 DC 都串行调用行车时间服务
完全忽略用户位置，返回全国所有 DC 的库存
不筛候选，把每件商品的库存推给所有 DC
先用 60 英里半径粗筛，再对候选算行车时间
why: 半径粗筛先排除不可能 1 小时送达的 DC，再把昂贵的行车时间调用限制在小候选集内。
why_en: Radius pruning limits expensive travel-time calls to plausible nearby distribution centers.
whenOtherWins: 如果 DC 数量只有个位数，全量调用行车时间服务也能接受。
optionExplanations: 错。对 1 万个 DC 都调用外部服务，延迟和成本都不可接受。
错。忽略位置直接违反 1 小时可送达这条核心需求。
错。这是订单/库存分发问题，不是筛选候选 DC 的方法。
对。半径粗筛先排除明显送不到的 DC，把昂贵调用限制在小候选集。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - calling an external service for 10,000 DCs is far too slow and expensive.
Wrong - ignoring location breaks the core one-hour deliverability requirement.
Wrong - this is about distributing inventory, not narrowing candidate DCs.
Correct - radius pruning removes obviously unreachable DCs before the expensive call.
tradeoff: 先地理粗筛再精算 vs 对全部 DC 都调用精确服务
options_en: Serially call the travel-time service for all 10,000 DCs.
Ignore the user location and return stock from every DC nationwide.
Skip filtering and push every item stock record to all DCs.
Prune with a 60-mile radius first, then compute travel time for the survivors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用路网和交通信息估算行车时间的外部/内部服务，调用它有延迟和成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A travel-time service estimates driving duration using road and traffic data, and each call costs latency and money.

q: 按附近 DC 查询商品可用量时，为什么是取库存 union 而不是 intersection？
q_en: When querying nearby DC stock, why use a union rather than an intersection?
options: 用户只需要附近任一可服务 DC 能提供商品即可
每个商品必须所有附近 DC 同时有货才能展示
intersection 更容易防超卖
union 只能用于支付
why: 有效可用量是所有可服务 DC 库存的总和，用户不关心某个商品是否每个 DC 都有。
why_en: Effective availability is the sum across serviceable distribution centers because any one of them can fulfill the item.
optionExplanations: 对。只要附近任意一个可服务仓有货，用户就能下单。
错。这是把 union 和 intersection 的语义弄反了。
错。防超卖靠的是下单时的事务扣减，不是 union/intersection 的选择。
错。union 是聚合可用库存的方式，和支付流程无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - if any one nearby serviceable warehouse has stock, the user can order.
Wrong - this reverses what union versus intersection actually means here.
Wrong - oversell prevention comes from the order-time transaction, not this choice.
Wrong - union is how availability is aggregated, unrelated to payments.
tradeoff: 跨可服务 DC 求 union（任一有货即可） vs 求 intersection（每个 DC 都要有货）
options_en: The user only needs any one nearby serviceable DC to carry the item.
Every nearby DC must carry the item at the same time before it counts.
Intersection makes oversell prevention easier.
Union can only be used for payments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个可服务 DC 的库存加总，而不是要求每个 DC 都有货。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Union sums stock across multiple serviceable DCs instead of requiring every DC to have it.

scenario: 用户附近有 3 个可 1 小时送达的 DC，Cheetos 只在其中两个有货，要给用户展示可买数量。
scenario_en: Three DCs can reach the user within an hour, Cheetos is stocked at only two of them, and we must show a buyable quantity.

scenario: Availability Service 已拿到附近 DC 列表，需要返回商品名称、描述和可用数量。
scenario_en: Availability Service already has the nearby DC list and must return item names, descriptions, and available quantities.
q: 首版最直接的数据访问方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most direct first-version data access pattern?
options: 让客户端对每个候选 DC 分别单独发起库存请求
join 库存与商品两表后按 item 聚合
扫描对象存储桶里保存的商品图片文件名
把订单历史表直接当成当前可售库存来查询
why: 库存和商品目录都在同一个关系库时，join 后聚合是最简单的首版实现。
why_en: With inventory and catalog in one relational database, a join plus aggregation is the simplest first implementation.
whenOtherWins: 如果 catalog 搜索和展示复杂度提高，catalog 可拆到独立服务和搜索索引中。
optionExplanations: 错。客户端逐个 DC 请求既慢又把聚合逻辑错误地放到了前端。
对。库存和目录同库时，一次 join 加聚合就是最简单的首版实现。
错。图片文件名不是库存数量，这里混淆了媒体存储和数据查询。
错。订单表记录的是已购买的商品，不是当前可售库存。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - per-DC client requests are slow and wrongly push aggregation to the frontend.
Correct - with inventory and catalog in one DB, a join plus aggregation is the simplest first cut.
Wrong - image filenames are not stock counts; this confuses media storage with data queries.
Wrong - the orders table records what was already purchased, not current sellable stock.
tradeoff: 首版单库 join 聚合 vs 拆分 catalog/search 独立服务
options_en: Have the client fire a separate stock request per candidate DC.
Join the inventory and item tables, then aggregate by item.
Scan an object-storage bucket for saved product image filenames.
Treat the order-history table as if it were current sellable stock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按外键把 Inventory 和 Item 两张表的行关联起来，一次查询拿到商品名和数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from the Inventory and Item tables by a shared key so one query returns both name and quantity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的关系型数据库，支持事务和强一致写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a relational database that supports transactions and strongly consistent writes.

q: 真实电商为什么常把 Catalog 和 Inventory 拆成两套存储？
q_en: Why do real e-commerce systems usually split Catalog and Inventory into separate stores?
options: Catalog 只能存在 Redis，Inventory 只能存在 S3
Catalog 字段经常变动，Inventory 字段结构固定，所以要用不同 schema
Catalog 面向搜索展示，Inventory 面向实时数量和扣减，工作负载不同
拆分只是为了让两个团队各自维护一套代码库，和性能无关
why: 商品描述、搜索排序和库存扣减的访问模式不同，生产系统常按职责拆分；本题首版合并是为了简化。
why_en: Catalog and inventory often split because search/display workloads differ from stock-count and reservation workloads.
optionExplanations: 错。文中没有这种存储位置限制，这是编造的约束。
错。schema 差异确实存在，但本题强调的驱动因素是访问模式（读多展示 vs 强一致扣减），不是字段是否固定。
对。搜索排序是读多且可容忍旧数据，扣减库存要强一致，职责天然不同。
错。团队所有权是现实中常见的拆分理由，但不是本题给出的性能/一致性驱动因素。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - the article names no such storage restriction; this is a fabricated constraint.
Wrong - schema differences are real, but this design's driver is workload pattern (read-heavy display vs consistent decrement), not fixed vs flexible fields.
Correct - search/display tolerates staleness while stock decrement needs strong consistency.
Wrong - team ownership is a common real split reason, but not the performance/consistency driver this design cites.
tradeoff: 按访问模式拆分 catalog/inventory vs 首版合并简化
options_en: Catalog can only live in Redis, and Inventory can only live in S3.
Catalog fields change often and Inventory fields are fixed, so they need different schemas.
Catalog serves search and display, while Inventory serves real-time counts and decrements - the workloads differ.
The split only exists so two teams can each own a separate codebase, unrelated to performance.
scenario: 生产电商每天百万级搜索排序读，同时有高频库存扣减写，两类负载共用一张表会互相拖累。
scenario_en: Production e-commerce runs millions of search and ranking reads a day alongside high-frequency stock decrements, and one shared table makes them fight.

q: 把用户查询 A/B/C 商品 availability 的路径排好序：
q_en: Put the availability path for items A, B, and C in the right order.
steps: 把商品 A/B/C 在这些 DC 的库存按 item 求和
用户请求 Availability Service 并传位置
返回每个 item 的有效可用数量
Nearby Service 返回可服务 DC IDs
why: 位置先转成可服务 DC 集合，然后库存查询只在该集合内聚合。
why_en: The request converts location into serviceable centers, aggregates stock for requested items, and returns effective quantities.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Cart[Items A B C] --> Nearby[Find nearby DCs]
Nearby --> Query[Query inventory by DC]
Query --> Union[Union available stock]
Union --> Response[Availability response]

scenario: 两个用户几乎同时购买同一个 DC 里的最后一件商品，系统绝不能让两个订单都成功。
scenario_en: Two users almost simultaneously buy the last unit in the same DC, and the system must not let both orders succeed.
q: 下单路径最重要的设计目标是什么？
q_en: What is the most important design goal for the order path?
options: 读请求越旧越好
每次下单都异步延迟一天
只更新缓存不更新数据库
强一致的库存检查和扣减
why: 下单是防超卖路径，必须把检查库存、创建订单和扣减库存放进同一个一致性边界。
why_en: Ordering must strongly couple stock checking, order creation, and inventory decrement to prevent overselling.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是展示 availability，短暂旧数据可以接受，读路径可以走缓存或副本。
optionExplanations: 错。下单路径追求正确性，不是刻意用旧数据。
错。人为延迟一天不解决并发抢购的一致性问题。
错。只改缓存意味着数据库库存和事实脱节，最终必然超卖。
对。检查、创建订单、扣库存必须在同一致性边界内完成。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - the order path optimizes for correctness, not deliberately stale reads.
Wrong - an artificial one-day delay does not solve concurrent-purchase consistency.
Wrong - updating only the cache leaves the database out of sync, guaranteeing overselling.
Correct - checking, creating the order, and decrementing stock must happen in one boundary.
tradeoff: 强一致检查+扣减 vs 更快但可能超卖的宽松路径
options_en: The staler the read, the better.
Delay every order asynchronously by a day.
Only update the cache, never the database.
Strongly consistent inventory checking and decrementing.

q: 把订单和库存放在不同数据库，再用锁串起来，一个典型失败模式是什么？
q_en: If orders and inventory live in separate databases and are tied together with locks, what failure mode appears?
options: 订单已创建但库存未扣减时服务崩溃，后续可能超卖
库存数量会自动变成无限
用户位置无法传给 Nearby Service
所有读请求都会强一致
why: 跨数据存储事务需要处理部分成功、补偿和恢复，失败模式比单库事务复杂得多。
why_en: Splitting orders and inventory across stores introduces partial-commit failures that require compensation and recovery.
optionExplanations: 对。订单已创建但库存未扣，崩溃窗口里另一个用户可能买到同一件货。
错。库存数字不会因为崩溃而变多，这是无中生有的说法。
错。这个失败模式和地理查询服务没有因果关系。
错。崩溃通常让状态更不一致，而不是自动变强一致。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - the order exists but stock is not decremented yet, so another order can double-sell.
Wrong - quantity does not increase from a crash; that is a made-up outcome.
Wrong - this failure mode has no causal link to the geography service.
Wrong - a crash typically makes state less consistent, not automatically stronger.
options_en: The order is created but the service crashes before decrementing inventory, so a later order can oversell.
Inventory quantity automatically becomes infinite.
The user's location can no longer reach the Nearby Service.
All reads suddenly become strongly consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 订单和库存分别存在不同数据库时，很难保证两边同时成功或同时失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-store transaction cannot easily guarantee that writes to two separate databases both succeed or both fail together.

scenario: 订单放 DynamoDB、库存放 Postgres，两者靠分布式锁串起来，任何一个节点都可能随时崩。
scenario_en: Orders live in DynamoDB and inventory in Postgres, stitched together by a distributed lock, and any node can crash at any moment.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 两个订单都要买 A 和 B，但一个先锁 A、另一个先锁 B，可能出现什么问题？
q_en: If two orders both need A and B but lock them in opposite order, what can happen?
options: 两个订单都会成功，因为锁的是不同商品互不影响
死锁，双方都等对方释放另一个锁
先到的订单自动拿到两把锁，后到的直接失败重试
两个订单会被数据库自动排队，不需要额外处理
why: 多资源分布式锁如果没有统一加锁顺序和超时，很容易在重叠库存上死锁。
why_en: Overlapping multi-item orders can deadlock if distributed locks are acquired in inconsistent orders.
optionExplanations: 错。A、B 都涉及重叠库存，两个订单其实在竞争交叉资源，不是互不影响。
对。订单1占着 A 等 B，订单2占着 B 等 A，谁都不能前进。
错。分布式锁不会打包成一次性获取，是逐个申请的，后到的会阻塞等待而不是失败重试。
错。数据库本身不会自动解决跨锁顺序问题，仍要靠应用层统一加锁顺序。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - both orders actually contend for overlapping stock through A and B; they are not independent.
Correct - order 1 holds A and waits for B while order 2 holds B and waits for A.
Wrong - distributed locks aren't acquired atomically as a bundle; the second order blocks and waits instead of failing.
Wrong - the database doesn't auto-resolve cross-lock ordering; the app still needs a consistent lock order.
options_en: Both orders succeed because locking different items doesn't interact.
Deadlock - each order waits for the other to release its lock.
The first order atomically grabs both locks, and the second fails and retries immediately.
The database automatically queues both orders with no extra handling needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个及以上执行流互相等待对方持有的资源，永远无法继续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when two or more processes wait forever for resources held by each other.

scenario: 高峰期并发下单，两个多商品订单都要锁住 A、B 两件库存，锁没有统一顺序也没有超时。
scenario_en: At peak, two concurrent multi-item orders each need to lock stock A and B, with no global lock order and no timeout.

scenario: 面试中希望先给出简单可靠的防超卖方案，库存和订单都可以放进同一个 Postgres。
scenario_en: In the interview, you want a simple reliable oversell-prevention design, and inventory and orders can live in one Postgres database.
q: 最合适的方案是什么？
q_en: What is the best-fit solution?
options: 先写订单记录，几小时后再异步扣减库存
只修改 Redis 里的库存计数，不写关系库
一个 Postgres 事务里检查、下单、扣减
让客户端自己挑 DC 并直接扣减库存
why: 把强一致数据放在同一个 ACID 数据库里，可以让一个事务保证原子性和隔离性。
why_en: Colocating orders and inventory in one ACID database lets a single transaction enforce atomicity and isolation.
whenOtherWins: 如果订单和库存规模极大且强一致边界无法单库承载，才需要更复杂的分片事务或 reservation 流程。
diagram:
flowchart LR
OrderSvc[Order Service] --> Tx[Single DB transaction]
Tx --> Inv[(Inventory rows)]
Tx --> Order[(Order row)]
Tx --> Commit[Commit or rollback]
optionExplanations: 错。几小时的异步窗口足够让库存被超卖多次。
错。Redis 计数不是权威数据源，重启或过期都会丢一致性。
对。同一个 ACID 事务能保证原子性和隔离性，一次成功或一次失败。
错。客户端不可信，选 DC 和扣库存都必须在服务端完成。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - an hours-long async window is plenty of time for repeated overselling.
Wrong - a Redis counter is not the source of truth and loses consistency on restart.
Correct - one ACID transaction guarantees atomicity and isolation: it all commits or rolls back.
Wrong - clients cannot be trusted; picking a DC and decrementing stock must be server-side.
tradeoff: 单库单事务简单可靠 vs 拆库获得各自最优存储引擎
options_en: Write the order record first, then decrement stock asynchronously hours later.
Only change the stock counter in Redis and never touch the relational store.
Do the check, the order insert, and the decrement in one Postgres transaction.
Let the client itself pick a DC and decrement stock directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库事务的四个保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the set of transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: Orders Service 要在一个事务里检查多个 item 是否有货，成功才创建订单并扣减库存。
scenario_en: Orders Service must check multiple items in one transaction, then create the order and decrement stock only if all checks pass.
q: 哪段事务形态最符合防超卖需求？
q_en: Which transaction shape best prevents overselling?
options: 先给用户返回下单成功，再由后台异步扣减库存
只写入 Redis 缓存计数，不写数据库
SELECT 全部订单后在客户端排序过滤
SERIALIZABLE 事务内锁库存并插订单
why: SERIALIZABLE 或合适的行锁能让并发订单在提交时冲突检测，失败的一方重试或返回缺货。
why_en: A serializable transaction or row locks make conflicting orders serialize so only one can commit against the same stock.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是读 availability，走只读副本和缓存更便宜，不需要锁主库。
optionExplanations: 错。提前应答后台再扣减，窗口期内还是能被超卖。
错。只写缓存等于没有权威库存记录，崩溃就全丢。
错。这是读取和排序订单，不是检查库存或创建订单的手段。
对。这个隔离级别在提交时做冲突检测，两个抢同一件货只有一个能成功。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - answering first and decrementing later still leaves a window for overselling.
Wrong - cache-only writes mean no authoritative record; a crash loses everything.
Wrong - this reads and sorts orders; it does not check stock or create one.
Correct - this isolation level checks conflicts at commit, so only one of two competing orders wins.
tradeoff: 同事务锁定+检查 vs 先应答用户再异步扣减
options_en: Return success to the user first, then decrement stock in a background job.
Write only to the Redis cache counter, never to the database.
SELECT every order and sort and filter it on the client.
Lock stock and insert the order inside a SERIALIZABLE transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最严格的数据库隔离级别，保证并发事务的结果和某种串行执行顺序一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strictest database isolation level, guaranteeing concurrent transactions behave as if run one at a time.

q: 单个多商品订单里只要一个商品缺货就让整个订单失败，有什么产品层后果？
q_en: If one missing item fails the whole multi-item order, what product consequence follows?
options: 用户需要清楚知道哪些商品导致失败
系统会自动拆成多个支付订单
强一致性失效
Nearby Service 不再需要
why: 全有或全无能避免不完整订单，但必须给用户明确的缺货反馈。
why_en: All-or-nothing ordering prevents partial purchases but requires clear out-of-stock feedback to users.
optionExplanations: 对。全有或全无能防止半成品订单，但用户体验要求明确说明缺货商品。
错。全有或全无策略不会自动拆单，拆单是另一种设计选择。
错。一致性策略没有因为失败反馈而失效。
错。Nearby Service 仍然要判断可服务 DC，与失败反馈无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - all-or-nothing avoids partial orders, but must clearly report which items failed.
Wrong - all-or-nothing does not auto-split orders; splitting is a different design choice.
Wrong - consistency does not break just because a request fails.
Wrong - the Nearby Service is still needed for serviceable-DC checks.
options_en: Users need to clearly know which items caused the failure.
The system automatically splits it into multiple payment orders.
Strong consistency stops working.
The Nearby Service is no longer needed.
scenario: 用户一次买 8 件商品，其中一件刚被附近 DC 的别人买走，订单按全有或全无处理。
scenario_en: A user buys eight items at once, one of them was just taken by someone else at the nearby DC, and the order is all-or-nothing.

q: Availability Service 和 Orders Service 对 Postgres 的读写路径应如何区分？
q_en: How should Availability Service and Orders Service use different Postgres read/write paths?
options: 两者都只读从库，写入统一交给离线批处理任务
Availability 读副本，Orders 写主库
两者都只访问客户端本地缓存，完全不连数据库
Orders 把订单和库存都写进对象存储桶里，跳过数据库事务
why: availability 可容忍轻微旧数据以换取速度；下单扣库存不能旧读或乱写，必须走一致性主路径。
why_en: Availability can tolerate slightly stale replica reads, while orders must use the leader and transactions for strong consistency.
optionExplanations: 错。下单必须同步写 leader，攒到离线批处理挡不住超卖。
对。展示可以容忍轻微旧数据，扣库存必须走一致性主路径。
错。本地缓存不是权威数据源，两条路径都还是要落到数据库。
错。对象存储适合大二进制文件、也没有事务保证；跳过数据库防不住并发扣库存冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - orders must write to the leader synchronously; batching them cannot stop overselling.
Correct - display reads tolerate slight staleness, but stock decrement needs the primary path.
Wrong - a local cache is not authoritative; both paths still need the database.
Wrong - object storage suits large binaries and has no transaction guarantee; skipping the database can't stop concurrent oversell.
tradeoff: 读副本换低延迟 vs leader 写事务换强一致
options_en: Both read only from replicas, with all writes handed to an offline batch job.
Availability reads a replica; Orders writes to the leader.
Both reach only a client-side local cache and never the database.
Orders writes both the order and the stock into an object-storage bucket, skipping database transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接受写入的数据库主节点，副本从它同步数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The leader is the database node that accepts writes; replicas sync data from it.

scenario: Gopuff 读约 20k QPS、写约 100 单/秒；展示可以容忍一秒旧数据，扣库存一秒都不行。
scenario_en: Gopuff serves roughly 20k reads per second against about 100 orders per second; display tolerates a second of staleness, decrements do not.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: availability 查询只会访问用户附近的一组 DC，希望每次请求不要扫全量 10k DC x 100k item 库存。
scenario_en: Availability queries touch only nearby DCs, and each request should avoid scanning all 10k DCs times 100k items.
q: 库存表更适合如何分区？
q_en: How should the inventory table be partitioned?
options: 按商品名称的首字母做随机哈希分区排布
把全部库存塞进一张大表，不建索引，每次查询全表扫描
按地区/ZIP 前缀分区，查询只落 1-2 个分区
按用户注册时填写的生日字段做范围分区
why: 本地配送天然有地理局部性；按地区分区把扫描从 10k DC × 100k item 缩到 1-2 个分区内的局部库存。
why_en: Geographic partitioning matches local delivery because availability queries touch only nearby distribution centers.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询总是按 item 全局聚合而不是按位置，item-based 分区可能更合适。
optionExplanations: 错。商品名首字母和用户位置没有关联，查询还是要扫多个分区。
错。无索引单表在 10k DC x 100k item 规模下必然全表扫描。
对。本地配送天然有地理局部性，查询只需命中附近分区。
错。生日和「谁能 1 小时送达」完全无关，纯粹的干扰项。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - an item name's first letter has no relation to user location.
Wrong - one unindexed table at this scale forces full scans.
Correct - local delivery has natural geographic locality, so queries hit only nearby partitions.
Wrong - birthday has no relation to one-hour deliverability; a pure distractor.
tradeoff: 按地理局部性分区 vs 按商品名或用户属性随机分区
options_en: Partition randomly by hashing the first letter of the item name.
Keep all inventory in one big table with no index, scanning it fully every query.
Partition by region or ZIP prefix so queries hit one or two partitions.
Range-partition by the birthday field the user filled in at signup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 ZIP 前几位等生成的地理分桶标识，用来做缓存 key 和数据库分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A region_id is a geographic bucket, often derived from a ZIP prefix, used for cache keys and database partitioning.

q: 这个写入量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this write volume support?
options: 写路径需要立刻拆分为分布式写分片集群
读路径完全不需要任何形式的缓存层
这个写入量级说明系统应该放弃强一致性
写路径不需要极端扩展，单库事务够用
why: 日均 100 单/秒远低于单机 Postgres 事务写入能力，真正的扩展压力在读路径（约 20k QPS），不在写路径。
why_en: About one hundred orders per second on average is well within a single Postgres instance's transactional write capacity, so the real scaling pressure is on reads, not writes.
scenario: 系统日订单量约 O(10M)，一天约 10 万秒，平均写入量级约为每秒 100 单（高峰会更高）。
scenario_en: The system handles about O(10M) orders per day; with roughly 100k seconds per day, average write volume is about 100 orders per second, with higher peaks.
options_en: The write path needs to shard into a distributed write cluster right away.
The read path needs no caching layer of any kind.
This write scale means the system should give up strong consistency.
The write path needs no extreme scaling; one database transaction absorbs it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量读请求的吞吐量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS stands for queries per second, a measure of read request throughput.

optionExplanations: 错。日订单量级不足以逼近分片门槛，现在切分布式写集群是过度设计，还会平添运维复杂度。
错。这一条把写路径和读路径的扩展决策混在一起了——读要不要缓存要看读 QPS，不是写单量。
错。写入压力小恰恰让强一致更容易维持，不是放弃一致性的理由。
对。这个写入体量单机数据库轻松吃得下，高峰翻几倍也用不着现在就上分布式写路径。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - daily order volume is nowhere close to needing a distributed write cluster; sharding now just adds ops overhead for no benefit.
Wrong - this conflates the write path with the read path; whether reads need caching depends on read QPS, not write volume.
Wrong - a light write load makes strong consistency easier to hold, not a reason to abandon it.
Correct - this write volume is easily absorbed by one database instance, even at several times peak, so there's no need for a distributed write path yet.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 估算 availability QPS 时，假设每个购买用户买前看 10 页，只有 5% 浏览者最终购买。
scenario_en: To estimate availability QPS, assume each buyer views 10 pages before purchasing and only 5% of browsers convert.
q: 哪条估算最贴近文章中的读流量推导？
q_en: Which estimate best matches the availability read-traffic derivation?
codeSample:
availability_qps = 10_000_000 / 100_000 * 10 / 0.05
# ≈ 20_000 queries/second
why: 订单量反推浏览量能说明 availability 读远多于下单写，是需要缓存和副本的信号。
why_en: Backing into availability traffic from orders shows reads can reach about twenty thousand queries per second.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务转化率和浏览页数不同，估算公式仍可用，但参数要换成实际数据。
optionExplanations: 对。按每天 10 万秒折算订单量，再乘浏览页数、除转化率，约得 2 万 QPS。
错。没除以每天 10 万秒，转化率也乘反了，量级直接飞出去。
错。转化率要做除数：只有 5% 的人下单，浏览量得放大 20 倍。
错。每次购买看 10 页是放大因子，应该乘不是除。
optionExplanations_en: Correct - divide daily orders by seconds/day, multiply by page views, divide by conversion rate.
Wrong - it never divides by seconds per day and multiplies by conversion instead of dividing.
Wrong - conversion belongs in the denominator: only 5% buy, so browsing is 20x larger.
Wrong - the 10 pages per purchase is a multiplier, not a divisor.
tradeoff: 从订单量反推读流量 vs 凭感觉估计一个数字
options_en: 10M / 100k * 10 / 0.05 is about 20,000 requests per second.
10M * 10 * 0.05 is about 5 million requests per second.
10M / 100k * 10 * 0.05 is about 50 requests per second.
10M / 100k / 10 / 0.05 is about 20 requests per second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最终下单用户占浏览用户的比例，用来把浏览量折算回购买量或反过来估算浏览量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Conversion rate is the share of browsing users who actually purchase, used to translate between browsing volume and order volume.

scenario: availability 查询约 20k QPS，同一地区和附近 DC 组合会被大量重复查询，但结果允许短暂不新。
scenario_en: Availability receives about 20k QPS; the same region and nearby-DC combinations repeat often, and results may be briefly stale.
q: 最直接的读扩展方案是什么？
q_en: What is the most direct way to scale availability reads?
options: 把所有查询都直接打到 Postgres 主库 leader
给 Availability 加 Redis cache，miss 回填
把 availability 计算推迟到用户点下单那刻才现算，不预先缓存
把库存数量写进用户浏览器的 cookie 里保存
why: availability 是读多写少且可短暂旧的路径，cache-aside 可以显著降低数据库读压。
why_en: Availability is read-heavy and tolerates brief staleness, so a Redis cache-aside layer cuts database load.
whenOtherWins: 下单扣减库存不能依赖旧缓存，必须重新进入强一致事务。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> Cache[(Availability cache)]
Cache -->|miss| Replica[(Read replica)]
Replica --> Avail[Availability Service]
Order[Order commit] --> Invalidate[Invalidate cache]
optionExplanations: 错。20k QPS 全打 leader 会让主库过载，也没利用查询的重复性。
对。同一地区反复被查，缓存能大幅削减数据库读压。
错。用户需要在下单前先看到可用商品，不能等到下单才算。
错。cookie 存在用户设备上，无法被其他用户共享，也不是权威数据源。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - sending all 20k QPS to the leader overloads it and ignores repeated queries.
Correct - the same region is queried repeatedly, so caching sharply cuts database read load.
Wrong - users need to see availability before ordering, not only after.
Wrong - a cookie lives on one device, cannot be shared, and is not authoritative.
tradeoff: 缓存吸收重复读 vs 每次都打库
options_en: Send every query straight to the Postgres leader.
Add a Redis cache in front of Availability, filling on a miss.
Defer computing availability until the user clicks order, with no upfront caching at all.
Store inventory counts inside the user's browser cookie.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时查数据库并把结果写回缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside checks the cache first and, on a miss, reads the database and writes the result back into the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型缓存服务，用来吸收重复读请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory cache commonly used to absorb repeated read traffic.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: availability cache 设置 1 分钟 TTL 的主要意义和代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main benefit and cost of a one-minute TTL on the availability cache?
options: 保证下单路径的强一致性
让缓存里的库存条目永不过期
降低读压，但可能短暂展示已售罄商品
可以直接替代订单事务里的库存扣减和加锁逻辑
why: 短 TTL 让读结果大致新鲜，但缓存仍可能比主库慢一拍，所以只能用于展示 availability。
why_en: A short TTL reduces read load while allowing brief stale availability, so it cannot replace transactional ordering.
optionExplanations: 错。缓存 TTL 和下单一致性是两条不同路径，展示新鲜不等于事务安全。
错。TTL 恰恰是设置过期时间，说「永不过期」正好说反了。
对。短 TTL 减少数据库压力，但缓存这一分钟内可能还没反映最新扣减。
错。缓存只服务展示；真正的库存扣减和加锁仍必须靠订单事务完成。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - cache TTL and order consistency are separate paths.
Wrong - TTL is literally an expiration setting, the opposite of never expiring.
Correct - a short TTL cuts database load but the cache may lag the latest decrement.
Wrong - the cache only serves display; the order transaction does the real oversell prevention.
options_en: It guarantees strong consistency on the ordering path.
It makes cached inventory entries never expire.
It cuts read load but may briefly show a sold-out item as available.
It can fully replace both the stock decrement and locking inside the order transaction.
scenario: availability 读 20k QPS 打爆 Postgres，于是加 Redis 缓存，但库存每秒都在被扣减。
scenario_en: Availability reads at 20k QPS overwhelm Postgres so we add a Redis cache, but stock is being decremented every second.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: Order Service 扣减库存后，为什么要失效受影响的 availability cache？
q_en: Why invalidate affected availability cache entries after Orders Service decrements inventory?
options: 让订单事务更慢
阻止 Nearby Service 返回 DC
删除所有用户账户
避免继续把已售出的库存展示为可买
why: TTL 兜底不够，扣库存时主动失效相关地区/item cache 能减少过时展示窗口。
why_en: Invalidating affected availability keys after an order reduces the stale window for items that just sold.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Order[Order Service] --> Commit[Inventory decrement]
Commit --> Event[Inventory changed event]
Event --> Cache[Invalidate affected keys]
Cache --> Fresh[Next read reloads]
optionExplanations: 错。失效缓存是订单提交之后的一步，不影响事务本身的耗时。
错。缓存失效和 Nearby Service 判断可服务 DC 是两个不相关的模块。
错。这是无关的破坏性操作，和缓存失效毫无关系。
对。主动失效缩短了「库存已卖出但缓存还显示有货」的窗口。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong - cache invalidation happens after commit and does not add to transaction latency.
Wrong - cache invalidation and the Nearby Service's DC lookup are unrelated modules.
Wrong - this is an unrelated destructive action.
Correct - proactive invalidation shortens the window where sold stock still looks available.
