why_en: Lightweight transactions lack multi-partition atomicity, isolation levels, and rollbacks, and their consensus round trips carry real performance overhead.
q_en: Which limitations does Cassandra LWT have?
optionExplanations: 对——事务一旦要跨分区，LWT 就完全无能为力。
对——没有隔离级别，并发条件更新之间也没有额外的隔离保证，也不能回滚。
对——Paxos 共识需要多轮节点通信才能达成一致，往返开销是真实代价。
错——单分区条件更新恰恰是 LWT 存在的意义，它唯一擅长的正是这个。
optionExplanations_en: True — the moment a transaction needs to span partitions, an LWT simply can't do it.
True — there are no isolation levels between concurrent conditional updates, and no rollback either.
True — Paxos needs multiple rounds of node communication to agree, and that round-trip cost is real.
False — a single-partition conditional update is the one thing an LWT is actually built to do.
scenario: 面试官追问：每天 20 亿滑动的规模下，把互滑检测交给 Cassandra LWT，你会在哪些地方撞墙？
scenario_en: The interviewer pushes back: at two billion swipes a day, where exactly would Cassandra lightweight transactions break down?

q: 为什么不能直接用 LWT 解决互滑一致性？
options: 规模太大，事务必然跨分区而 LWT 不支持
LWT 完全不支持字符串这种数据类型
LWT 与推送通知服务互相冲突
LWT 只能在测试环境里使用，不能上线
options_en: At this scale, transactions must span partitions, which LWTs don't support.
LWTs don't support the string data type at all.
LWTs conflict directly with the push notification service.
LWTs can only be used in a test environment, never in production.
why: 规模是死穴：20 亿滑动/天塞不进单分区，一旦事务要跨分区，LWT 就无能为力——除非想办法让互滑的两条滑动永远同分区。
why_en: At two billion swipes a day the data cannot fit one partition, and lightweight transactions cannot span partitions.
q_en: Why can’t LWT directly solve mutual-swipe consistency?
optionExplanations: 对——20 亿滑动/天塞不进单一分区，事务一旦要跨分区，LWT 立刻失效。
这不是 Cassandra 数据类型层面的限制，与字符串无关。
推送服务和存储事务是两个独立组件，互不冲突。
LWT 完全可以在生产环境使用，限制不在运行环境上。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — two billion swipes a day can't fit one partition, and the moment a transaction spans partitions, LWTs stop working.
This has nothing to do with Cassandra data types or string support.
The push service and the storage transaction are separate components that don't conflict.
LWTs work fine in production; the limitation isn't about which environment they run in.
scenario: 滑动按 swiping_user_id 分区、每天 20 亿条；一次互滑判断要同时碰 A 的分区和 B 的分区。
scenario_en: Swipes are partitioned by the swiping user across two billion rows a day, so one mutual check touches both A's and B's partitions.

scenario: 想用 Cassandra 的单分区事务原子处理互滑，关键是让 A→B 和 B→A 两条滑动永远落在同一个分区。
q: 分区键应该怎么设计？
options: 给每一条滑动都用随机生成的 UUID 做分区键
按滑动发生的具体时间戳分区
user_pair = 排序后的两个 ID 拼接
按滑动的方向（yes 或 no）分区
options_en: Use a randomly generated UUID as each swipe's partition key.
Partition by the exact timestamp the swipe happened.
Use user_pair, the two ids sorted and concatenated.
Partition by the swipe's direction (yes or no).
why: 把两个用户 ID 排序后拼成 user_pair 做分区键，(A,B) 与 (B,A) 必然算出同一个键、落同一分区，单分区原子操作才有了立足点。
why_en: Sorting the two user ids into a single user-pair partition key guarantees both directions of the swipe land in the same partition.
whenOtherWins: 如果核心查询是“列出我滑过的所有人”，按 swiping_user_id 分区更合适——分区键永远要服务于访问模式。
tradeoff: user_pair 分区（互滑同分区，利于原子匹配） vs swiping_user_id 分区（利于查个人历史）
q_en: How should the partition key be designed for mutual swipes?
scenario_en: To use Cassandra single-partition transactions for mutual swipes, A-to-B and B-to-A must always land in the same partition.
optionExplanations: 随机键和滑动方向无关，A→B 与 B→A 会各自算出不同的键、落到不同分区。
按时间分区会把同一对用户的两条滑动散到不同的时间桶里。
对——两个用户 ID 排序后拼接，(A,B) 和 (B,A) 恒等，天然落同一分区。
按滑动方向分区会把同一对用户的 yes 和 no 分开存放，同样凑不齐。
optionExplanations_en: A random key has nothing to do with the pair; A-to-B and B-to-A hash to different keys and land on different partitions.
Partitioning by timestamp scatters the same pair's two swipes into different time buckets.
Correct — sorting the two user ids before concatenating makes (A,B) and (B,A) produce the identical key, landing on one partition.
Partitioning by direction splits the same pair's yes and no apart, so they still never meet.

scenario: 为滑动表写建表语句：要保证同一对用户的所有滑动同分区，且能按 from_user / to_user 区分每一行。
q: 正确的主键设计是？
options: PRIMARY KEY (from_user)，没有聚簇键区分行
PRIMARY KEY ((user_pair), from_user, to_user)
PRIMARY KEY ((from_user), to_user) 按单个发起用户分区
PRIMARY KEY ((created_at)) 按创建时间分区
options_en: PRIMARY KEY (from_user), with no clustering key to tell rows apart.
PRIMARY KEY ((user_pair), from_user, to_user)
PRIMARY KEY ((from_user), to_user), partitioned by a single swiper.
PRIMARY KEY ((created_at)), partitioned by creation time.
why: 外层括号里的 user_pair 是分区键，from_user、to_user 是聚簇键：一对用户的两条滑动同分区，行之间又能区分开。
why_en: The compound key makes user pair the partition key with the two user ids as clustering keys, so both swipes share a partition yet stay distinct rows.
whenOtherWins: 若按 (from_user) 分区，查单人滑动历史很快，但互滑检查就要跨分区——查询模式决定主键设计。
codeSample:
CREATE TABLE swipes (
    user_pair text,      -- 分区键: smaller_id:larger_id
    from_user uuid,      -- 聚簇键
    to_user uuid,        -- 聚簇键
    direction text,
    created_at timestamp,
    PRIMARY KEY ((user_pair), from_user, to_user)
);
tradeoff: user_pair 做分区键（互滑同分区） vs from_user 做分区键（查个人历史快）
q_en: What primary key design keeps a user pair in one partition?
scenario_en: You are writing the swipe table DDL; one user pair must share a partition while from_user and to_user still identify each row.
optionExplanations: 只用 from_user 做主键，没有聚簇键区分不了同一用户的多条滑动记录。
对——user_pair 做分区键、from_user/to_user 做聚簇键，两条滑动同分区又能分行。
以 from_user 分区会让 A→B 和 B→A 落到不同分区，凑不齐一对滑动。
按创建时间分区和“互滑同分区”这个目标完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Using only from_user as the key with no clustering key can't distinguish one user's multiple swipe rows.
Correct — user_pair as the partition key with from_user/to_user as clustering keys keeps both swipes on one partition as distinct rows.
Partitioning by from_user alone sends A-to-B and B-to-A to different partitions, so they never end up together.
Partitioning by creation time has nothing to do with keeping a pair's swipes together.

scenario: 实现 get_user_pair(user_a, user_b)，为一对用户生成分区键 / Redis key。
q: 代码里先执行 sorted([user_a, user_b]) 的目的是？
options: 只是为了让输出结果看起来更好看
单纯为了防止 SQL 注入攻击
单纯为了压缩生成的 key 字符串整体长度
保证 (A,B)(B,A) 生成同一个 key
options_en: Just to make the output results look nicer.
Purely to prevent SQL injection attacks.
Purely to shorten the overall length of the generated key string.
To make (A,B) and (B,A) produce the same key.
why: 不排序的话 A→B 和 B→A 会算出两个不同的键、落到不同位置；排序让键与滑动方向无关，这是整套原子方案的前提。
why_en: Sorting the ids makes the key direction-independent so both users' swipes always map to the same partition or shard.
whenOtherWins: 若两个方向的滑动不需要同处一地（例如只做单向历史记录），直接用 swiping_user_id 即可，不必合成键。
codeSample:
def get_user_pair(user_a, user_b):
    # 排序保证 (A->B) 与 (B->A) 同 key
    sorted_ids = sorted([user_a, user_b])
    return f"{sorted_ids[0]}:{sorted_ids[1]}"
tradeoff: 排序生成方向无关的 key（利于原子匹配） vs 保留方向（利于单向历史查询）
q_en: Why does get_user_pair sort the two user ids first?
scenario_en: Implement get_user_pair(user_a, user_b) to generate a stable partition key or Redis key for a pair of users.
optionExplanations: 排序不是为了展示效果，纯粹是为了正确性。
排序对注入攻击没有任何防护作用，这与安全无关。
排序后 key 长度和不排序基本一致，不是为了压缩。
对——排序消除了方向差异，A→B 和 B→A 映射到同一个 key。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting isn't for a nicer-looking output — it's purely about correctness.
Sorting offers zero protection against injection; that's unrelated to security.
Sorted or not, the key length is basically the same — this isn't about compression.
Correct — sorting removes the direction, so A-to-B and B-to-A map to the exact same key.

q: 在 user_pair 单分区方案里，怎样正确地「写入我的滑动 + 读取对方滑动」来判断是否互相匹配？
options: 先 INSERT 本次滑动，再 SELECT 反向滑动
把写和读拆到两个独立数据库连接上并发执行
先 SELECT 反向滑动再 INSERT，中间加 sleep 兜底
用 Cassandra 触发器在写入时自动检测互滑
options_en: INSERT your swipe first, then SELECT the reverse swipe.
Split the write and the read across two independent database connections running concurrently.
SELECT the reverse swipe first, then INSERT, with a sleep in between as a safety net.
Use a Cassandra trigger to detect the mutual swipe automatically on write.
why: Cassandra 的 BATCH 只能装 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE、放不了 SELECT。同分区下先写后读、靠读己写一致拿到对方滑动即可判匹配。
why_en: Cassandra BATCH takes INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE but not SELECT, so in one partition you write your swipe first and then read the reverse one, relying on read-your-writes to spot the match.
codeSample:
-- Cassandra BATCH 只能装 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE，不能放 SELECT
-- 同一 user_pair 分区内：先写入本次滑动
INSERT INTO swipes (user_pair, from_user, to_user, direction, created_at)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
-- 再读取反向滑动判断是否匹配（读己写一致）
SELECT direction FROM swipes
WHERE user_pair = ? AND from_user = ? AND to_user = ?;
diagram:
graph LR
    Req[Swipe request] --> Tx[Single pair partition]
    Tx --> Write[Write my direction]
    Tx --> Read[Read reverse direction]
    Read -->|right swipe exists| Match[Create match]
    Read -->|none| Done[No match yet]
q_en: In the single-partition user_pair design, how do you correctly write your swipe and read the reciprocal one to detect a match?
optionExplanations: 对——同分区写完立刻读，读己写一致保证读得到自己刚写那条，反向若是右滑就是匹配。
两个连接之间没有顺序或原子性保证，检查-写入的竞态原封不动地留着。
先读后写正是竞态的来源，sleep 只是把窗口挪个位置，并没有关掉它。
Cassandra 没有跨分区触发器，触发器也不参与协调，防不住并发双写。
optionExplanations_en: Right — write then read in the same partition; read-your-writes guarantees you see your own row, and a reverse right swipe means a match.
Two connections give no ordering or atomicity between them, so the check-then-write race survives untouched.
Reading before writing is exactly what creates the race; a sleep just moves the window instead of closing it.
Cassandra has no cross-partition triggers, and triggers take no part in coordination, so concurrent double writes still slip through.
scenario: 互滑的两条记录已用排序后的 user_pair 做分区键放进同一分区，你要在一次请求里判定匹配。
scenario_en: Both swipes already share one partition under a sorted user_pair key, and you must decide the match within a single request.
whenOtherWins: 要严格防住并发双写时，改用 LWT 的 IF 条件更新，或走后面卡片里的 Redis-Lua 原子脚本。

q: user_pair 单分区方案会带来哪些运营挑战？（多选）
options: 滑动历史随时间累积，分区可能无限增长、拖累性能
高度活跃的用户会制造流量不成比例的热分区
需要一套清理 / 归档旧滑动数据的策略，防止分区无界膨胀
user_pair 键会让互滑检查变慢
options_en: Swipe history accumulates, so partitions can grow unbounded and hurt performance.
Highly active users create disproportionately hot partitions.
A cleanup or archival strategy is needed to bound partition growth.
The user_pair key makes mutual-swipe checks slower.
why: 方案优雅但有代价：分区随历史增长、活跃用户造热分区，所以必须配归档清理策略；互滑检查恰恰是这个键最快的查询。
why_en: Partitions can grow unbounded and hot users create hot partitions, so the design needs a cleanup strategy that archives old swipe data.
q_en: What operational challenges come with the user_pair single-partition design?
optionExplanations: 对——每对用户的滑动历史都堆在同一个分区里，不清理就会持续变大、拖累性能。
对——活跃用户会和大量人互滑，对应的分区流量会陡增，形成热点。
对——需要归档策略把旧数据挪走，才能控制分区体积不失控。
错——user_pair 恰恰是互滑检查最快的路径，不是让它变慢的原因。
optionExplanations_en: True — one pair's entire swipe history piles into the same partition, and without cleanup it keeps growing and hurting performance.
True — a highly active user swipes with many people, so their partitions see disproportionate traffic and turn hot.
True — an archival strategy is needed to move old data out and keep partition size under control.
False — user_pair is exactly what makes the mutual-swipe check fast, not what slows it down.
scenario: user_pair 分区键跑了一年，头部用户每天滑上千次，而滑动记录目前只写不删。
scenario_en: The user_pair partition key has been live for a year, top users swipe a thousand times a day, and nothing is ever deleted.

scenario: Cassandra 擅长持久化海量滑动，但不擅长实时匹配所需的原子“写+查”。需要一个既强一致又低延迟的匹配检测方案。
q: 实时匹配检测与滑动持久化应该怎么组合？
options: 直接放弃原子性，接受偶尔漏匹配
Redis 做原子操作，Cassandra 做持久层
把全部滑动数据都搬进单机 Postgres 实例里
用消息队列把所有滑动强制串行化
options_en: Just give up atomicity and accept occasional missed matches.
Use Redis for atomic operations and Cassandra as the durable layer.
Move all swipe data into a single-node Postgres instance.
Force-serialize every swipe through a message queue.
why: 混合架构各取所长：Redis 原子操作做实时匹配检测，Cassandra 做持久化海量存储；既满足即时匹配又保持可扩展。
why_en: The recommended design uses Redis for atomic real-time match detection while keeping Cassandra as the durable storage layer.
whenOtherWins: 若能接受对账补通知的 AP 取舍，或愿意扛 Cassandra 单分区批处理的运维负担，可以不引入 Redis、少养一个组件。
tradeoff: Redis 原子内存操作（低延迟一致） vs Cassandra 持久存储（高吞吐可扩展）
q_en: How should real-time match detection and durable swipe storage be combined?
scenario_en: Cassandra is good for durable high-volume swipe storage, but not for the atomic write-and-check needed by real-time matching.
optionExplanations: 直接放弃一致性需求会违背这道题明确要求的即刻匹配通知。
对——Redis 做内存级原子操作保证即时匹配，Cassandra 做写优化持久层，各司其职。
单机关系库既扛不住写吞吐，也没解决原子检查-写入的问题。
全局串行化会把所有滑动排成一条队，延迟和吞吐都不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Giving up atomicity outright breaks the instant-match-notification requirement stated for this problem.
Correct — Redis gives instant, in-memory atomic operations for matching while Cassandra stays the write-optimized durable layer, each doing what it's best at.
A single relational database can't sustain this write volume and still doesn't solve the atomic check-then-write problem.
Serializing everything through one queue lines up every swipe behind every other, which kills both latency and throughput.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 用 Redis 实现滑动：HSET 记录我的滑动、HGET 读对方的滑动，两步之间绝不能被其他请求插入。
q: 为什么要把两条命令放进一个 Lua 脚本执行？
options: Lua 脚本比走 Redis 协议逐条传输更快
Lua 脚本能压缩内存
Redis 原子执行整个脚本，杜绝检查-写入竞态
Lua 支持更多数据类型
options_en: A Lua script is faster than sending each command over the Redis protocol.
The Lua script compresses memory usage.
Redis executes the whole script atomically, eliminating the check-write race.
Lua supports more data types.
why: Redis 以原子方式执行整个 Lua 脚本：写入与检查成为单一操作，别的请求插不进来；配合内存速度，一致性和低延迟同时到手。
why_en: Redis executes the whole Lua script atomically, so recording the swipe and checking the other user's swipe become one indivisible operation.
whenOtherWins: 如果两步允许分离——比如只记录滑动、不做即时匹配检测——就用普通命令即可，无需脚本。
codeSample:
script = """
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1], ARGV[2])
return redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], ARGV[3])
"""
other = redis.eval(script, keys=[key],
    args=[f"{from_user}_swipe", direction, f"{to_user}_swipe"])
if direction == 'right' and other == 'right':
    create_match(from_user, to_user)
tradeoff: Lua 脚本单次原子往返（无竞态，稍增脚本维护成本） vs 两条独立命令（简单但有竞态窗口）

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 支持的嵌入式脚本，整段在服务端原子执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script is an embedded script Redis executes atomically on the server.

q_en: Why put HSET and HGET inside one Redis Lua script?
scenario_en: In Redis, HSET writes my swipe and HGET reads the other user’s swipe; no other request can interleave between them.
optionExplanations: 传输速度不是把两条命令打包进脚本的原因。
Lua 脚本不会改变 hash 存储本身占用的内存。
对——Redis 把整段 Lua 脚本当一个不可分割的操作执行，检查和写入之间插不进别的请求。
数据类型支持和这里要解决的竞态问题没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Transmission speed isn't why the two commands get bundled into a script.
A Lua script doesn't change how much memory the underlying hash uses.
Correct — Redis runs the whole Lua script as one indivisible operation, so no other request can slip between the check and the write.
Data-type support has nothing to do with the race condition being solved here.

q: Redis 方案里滑动数据的存储结构是？
options: 给每次滑动都建一个独立的 string key
一个全局 list
按天分桶的 set
一对用户共用一个 hash，各占一个 field
options_en: Create one independent string key for every single swipe.
A single global list.
A set bucketed by day.
One hash shared by each user pair, with a field per user.
why: 一对用户共用一个 hash，两个 field 各放一人的滑动方向，天然支撑“写我的、读他的”。计数单位是用户对 × 2 field，不是滑动条数。
why_en: Each user pair shares one Redis hash with a field per user, which is exactly what an atomic write-mine-read-theirs script needs; what you count is user pairs times two fields, not raw swipes.
q_en: What data structure stores swipes in the Redis design?
optionExplanations: 独立 key 没法用一次 HSET/HGET 把两人的滑动原子地关联起来。
全局 list 没法按一对用户做 O(1) 查找，规模上也不现实。
按天分桶的 set 表达不出“谁对谁滑动”这层配对关系。
对——key 由排序后的两个 ID 拼成，谁先滑都命中同一个 key，HSET 加 HGET 一次往返即可判匹配。
optionExplanations_en: An independent key can't atomically tie both users' swipes together in one HSET/HGET round trip.
A global list has no O(1) lookup by user pair and doesn't scale to this volume.
A set bucketed by day can't express the pairing relationship of who swiped on whom.
Correct — the key is the two ids sorted and joined, so whoever swipes first lands on the same key and one HSET plus HGET round trip settles the match.
scenario: 匹配检测要在一次原子操作里写下我的滑动、读出对方的滑动，延迟预算只有几毫秒。
scenario_en: Match detection has to write my swipe and read the other user's in one atomic operation, on a budget of a few milliseconds.

q: Redis 集群横向扩容时，靠什么保证同一对用户的滑动仍落在同一节点？
options: 一致性哈希：同一 key 稳定映射同一分片
靠随机路由加上失败重试机制
让集群里每个节点都保存一份全量数据副本
靠客户端逐个轮询查所有节点
options_en: Consistent hashing keeps a given key on a stable shard.
Rely on random routing plus a failure-retry mechanism.
Have every node in the cluster keep a full copy of the dataset.
Have the client poll every node one by one.
why: key 已经把一对用户绑定在一起，一致性哈希再保证同一 key 稳定映射到同一分片——加节点扩容时相关滑动依然聚在一处。
why_en: Consistent hashing keeps the same user-pair key on the same shard, so related swipes stay together as the cluster scales horizontally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 将 key 映射到哈希环上分片，加减节点只影响相邻分片的分片算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys onto a hash ring so adding or removing a node only reshuffles its neighboring shard.

q_en: How does Redis cluster scaling keep a user pair on the same node?
optionExplanations: 对——一致性哈希让同一个 key 稳定映射到同一分片，加减节点只影响相邻分片。
随机路由没法保证同一个 key 每次都落在同一节点。
每节点存全量数据会违背横向扩容分摊数据这个目的本身。
轮询查找效率低，也解决不了路由一致性的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — consistent hashing keeps a given key mapped to a stable shard; adding or removing a node only reshuffles its neighbors.
Random routing with retries can't guarantee the same key always lands on the same node.
Replicating the full dataset onto every node defeats the whole point of horizontal scaling.
Polling every node is slow and still doesn't solve routing consistency.
scenario: Redis 集群从 6 个节点扩到 12 个，而一对用户的两条滑动必须仍落在同一节点才能原子判断。
scenario_en: The Redis cluster grows from six nodes to twelve, yet both swipes of a pair must still land on the same node to stay atomic.

q: Redis 内存有限，这套混合方案如何控制内存占用？
options: 无限加内存
激进过期：定期刷入 Cassandra
把 Redis 换成磁盘持久化模式
压缩所有 value
options_en: Just keep adding memory indefinitely.
Let entries lapse aggressively, flushing to Cassandra periodically.
Switch Redis to a disk-backed persistence mode.
Compress every value.
why: 因为 Cassandra 才是持久层，Redis 可以放心激进过期：定期刷数据下去、只留近期滑动在内存里做匹配检测。
why_en: Since Cassandra is the durable layer, Redis can aggressively let data lapse, periodically flushing swipes down and keeping only recent ones in memory.
q_en: How does the hybrid design control Redis memory usage?
optionExplanations: 无限加内存不是可持续的成本策略，规模化后成本失控。
对——既然 Cassandra 已经持久化了，Redis 可以放心让数据快速过时，定期把近期数据刷下去。
换成磁盘模式会牺牲 Redis 引以为傲的低延迟，违背引入它的初衷。
压缩带来额外 CPU 开销，也没回答数据该留多久这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Endlessly adding memory isn't a sustainable cost strategy at this scale.
Correct — since Cassandra already persists everything, Redis can let entries lapse quickly and periodically flush recent data down.
Switching to disk-backed mode gives up the low latency that was the whole reason to bring Redis in.
Compressing adds CPU overhead and still doesn't answer how long the data should be kept.
scenario: 每天 20 亿滑动全留在内存里放不下，而 Cassandra 已经承担了持久层的角色。
scenario_en: Two billion swipes a day will not fit in memory, and Cassandra is already carrying the durable layer.

q: 如果 Redis 节点故障丢了数据，实际损失是什么？
options: 全部滑动历史被永久丢失
所有已有匹配失效
只丢最近滑动的匹配检测能力
用户资料损坏
options_en: All swipe history is permanently lost.
Every existing match becomes invalid.
Only match detection for very recent swipes is lost.
User profiles get corrupted.
why: 丢的只是“非常近期”滑动的匹配检测窗口：历史都在 Cassandra，用户可以重新滑。这让系统敢于把 Redis 当易失层用。
why_en: Losing a Redis node only costs match detection for very recent swipes, because the historical record survives in Cassandra and users can simply swipe again.
q_en: What is actually lost if a Redis node fails and loses data?
optionExplanations: 历史滑动一直持久化在 Cassandra 里，不会因为 Redis 节点故障而丢失。
已经生成的匹配是历史事实，不依赖 Redis 是否还活着。
对——只有还没刷进 Cassandra 的近期滑动检测窗口受影响，用户重新滑一次就补上了。
Redis 只存滑动数据，压根不涉及用户资料。
optionExplanations_en: Swipe history is durably persisted in Cassandra the whole time, so a Redis node failure doesn't lose it.
Matches that already happened are historical facts that don't depend on Redis being alive.
Correct — only the detection window for very recent, not-yet-flushed swipes is affected, and the user can just swipe again.
Redis only holds swipe data; it never touches user profiles.
scenario: 一个 Redis 分片突然宕机，上面只有最近几天的滑动，更早的都已刷进 Cassandra。
scenario_en: A Redis shard dies holding only the last few days of swipes; everything older has already been flushed to Cassandra.

q: 把“滑动一致性”这条决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 选型：Redis Lua 原子操作做实时匹配 + Cassandra 做持久层
需求：互滑后必须立即向后滑者展示匹配 → 需要强一致
缓解：定期把滑动刷回 Cassandra，Redis 只留近期数据
推导：滑动写入与反向检查必须原子完成，否则并发互滑会漏匹配
代价：Redis 集群运维（节点故障、哈希环再均衡）与内存压力
排除：Cassandra LWT 只支持单分区，每天 20 亿滑动撑不住
why: 链条：强一致需求 → 原子写+查 → LWT 单分区限制被排除 → Redis 原子 + Cassandra 持久 → 代价是集群运维和内存 → 用刷回+只留近期缓解。
why_en: The chain runs from the strong-consistency requirement through atomic check-and-write, past the lightweight-transaction limits, to Redis plus Cassandra with its operational costs and mitigations.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求：互滑立即出匹配"] --> P["原子写+查"]
    P --> X["LWT 仅单分区 → 排除"]
    X --> C["Redis 原子 Lua + Cassandra 持久"]
    C --> K["代价：集群运维/内存"]
    K --> M["缓解：刷回 Cassandra，只留近期"]
tradeoff: Redis + Cassandra 混合架构（低延迟一致，多养一个组件） vs 纯 Cassandra 方案（组件少，但撑不住跨分区一致性）
q_en: Put the swipe-consistency decision chain in the right order.

scenario: 匹配检测方案最终由 Redis 和 Cassandra 共同承担：Redis 处理实时原子操作，Cassandra 处理持久化存储。
q: 这套设计里 Redis 与 Cassandra 的分工差异，本质在哪个维度？
options: 两者使用的编程语言不同
两者采用的开源许可协议不同
两者部署所在的机房与区域各不相同
内存原子操作 vs 写优化持久存储
options_en: They're written in different programming languages.
They use different open-source licenses.
They're deployed in different data centers and regions.
In-memory atomic operations versus write-optimized durable storage.
why: 各打各的强项：Redis 提供原子、低延迟的实时操作；Cassandra 提供持久、可无限堆量的写优化存储。混合后两全其美。
why_en: Redis wins on in-memory atomic operations for real-time matching while Cassandra wins on durable write-optimized bulk storage.
tradeoff: Redis：内存原子操作，低延迟但易失 vs Cassandra：持久海量存储，高吞吐但最终一致
q_en: What dimension separates Redis and Cassandra in this design?
scenario_en: The final matching design uses Redis for real-time atomic operations and Cassandra for durable storage.
optionExplanations: 编程语言实现和这道题的架构分工完全无关。
开源许可协议不是这里做技术选型的决定性维度。
部署区域是运维话题，不是分工设计要考虑的依据。
对——这正是两者分工的本质：一套管实时原子读写，另一套管海量持久存储。
optionExplanations_en: Which programming language each is written in has nothing to do with this architecture's division of labor.
Open-source licensing isn't the deciding dimension for this technology choice.
Deployment region is an operations topic, not the basis for this split.
Correct — that is exactly the split: one side handles real-time atomic reads and writes, the other durable high-volume persistence.

scenario: 朴素 SQL 过滤（偏好 + 经纬度范围）太慢，需要在 300ms 内实时生成符合地理位置与偏好的推荐。
q: 合适的基础设施是？
options: Elasticsearch + 地理空间索引
把用户全表加载进应用内存
给 lat / long 各加一个普通 B 树索引就够了
换一台更大的单机数据库
options_en: Elasticsearch with a geospatial index.
Load the entire users table into application memory.
Just add a plain B-tree index on lat and long.
Move to a bigger single-node database.
why: 搜索优化库为快速全文检索与复杂查询而生，配上地理空间索引就能高效取出某片区域内符合偏好的用户，实时生成 feed。
why_en: A search-optimized database like Elasticsearch with a geospatial index can retrieve nearby matching users fast enough for real-time feeds.
whenOtherWins: 数据量小、查询简单时，主库加常规索引即可，不必为引入搜索引擎付出数据同步的复杂度。
tradeoff: 搜索优化库+地理索引（查询快，需额外同步） vs 主库常规索引（简单，但地理范围查询慢）

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理坐标组织数据、支持高效范围查询的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index organizes data by coordinates to support fast range queries by location.

q_en: What infrastructure should serve low-latency geo/profile feed queries?
scenario_en: Naive SQL over preferences and lat/long is too slow; the feed must generate geo- and preference-matching profiles within 300ms.
optionExplanations: 对——搜索优化库配地理空间索引，能在这个延迟预算内取出区域内符合偏好的用户。
把全表塞进应用内存既不安全，规模上也撑不住全站用户量。
普通 B 树对经纬度这种多维范围查询效果很差，是这条朴素查询慢的根源。
单机纵向扩容只是加算力，没改变索引结构不匹配查询模式这个根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a search-optimized store with a geospatial index can pull matching nearby users inside this latency budget.
Loading the whole table into application memory is neither safe nor scalable to the full user base.
A plain B-tree is a poor fit for multi-dimensional lat/long range queries, which is exactly why the naive query is slow.
A bigger single-node database just adds compute; it doesn't fix the index structure mismatching the query pattern.

q: 地理空间索引（geospatial index）解决的核心问题是？
options: 主要用来压缩位置数据体积
主要用来加密用户坐标信息
高效检索地理范围内用户，替代区间扫描
主要用来预测用户接下来将去往哪里
options_en: Mainly used to compress location data size.
Mainly used to encrypt user coordinate information.
Efficiently retrieving users in a geographic area instead of scanning ranges.
Mainly used to predict where the user will go next.
why: 地理搜索是朴素查询里最慢的一环；地理空间索引让“取出该区域内的用户”变成高效操作，是 feed 提速的关键。
why_en: A geospatial index lets the system efficiently retrieve users within a geographic area instead of scanning latitude and longitude ranges.
q_en: What core problem does a geospatial index solve?
optionExplanations: 索引解决的是查询效率，不是存储空间占用。
加密和地理索引要解决的问题完全不是一回事。
对——把经纬度区间扫描换成高效范围检索，才能撑住这个延迟预算。
预测用户去向不是索引结构该解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: An index is about query efficiency, not storage footprint.
Encryption solves confidentiality, a different concern from speeding up location lookups.
Correct — it turns a lat/long range scan into an efficient range lookup, which is the key to a faster feed.
Predicting where a user will go isn't something an index structure solves.
scenario: 推荐要在几百毫秒内返回“我 50 公里内的候选用户”，而经纬度双区间扫描已被证明太慢。
scenario_en: The feed must return candidates within fifty kilometres in a few hundred milliseconds, and scanning lat/long ranges is already too slow.

q: 主事务库与 Elasticsearch 之间的数据同步风险及标准解法是？
options: 没有风险，ES 会自动感知变更并完成同步
同步延迟会致过期数据；用 CDC 保持同步
只能靠停机做一次全量重建
让客户端自己负责双写两边
options_en: There's no risk; Elasticsearch automatically detects changes and syncs.
Sync delay can serve stale data; use change data capture to stay in sync.
The only option is a one-time offline full rebuild.
Make the client responsible for dual writes.
why: 两库并存必有一致性难题：同步一旦延迟或失败，用户就会看到过期资料或错过新用户；CDC 是让搜索索引跟上主库的标准机制。
why_en: Keeping the search index in sync with the primary database is the hard part, and change data capture is the standard mechanism for it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获主库的数据变更并同步给下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change data capture, or CDC, captures changes in the primary database and streams them to downstream systems.

q_en: What is the sync risk between the primary database and Elasticsearch, and what is the standard fix?
optionExplanations: ES 不会自动感知主库的变更，没有同步机制就会立刻脱节。
对——同步延迟会让用户看到过期资料，CDC 持续捕获主库变更并流给索引，是标准做法。
全量重建成本很高，不是常规的持续同步手段。
客户端双写容易漏写，也难以保证两边顺序一致。
optionExplanations_en: Elasticsearch has no automatic awareness of primary database changes; without a sync mechanism it drifts immediately.
Correct — sync delay can serve stale profiles, and CDC continuously captures primary-database changes and streams them to the index, which is the standard fix.
A full rebuild is expensive and not a sustainable ongoing sync mechanism.
Client-side dual writes are easy to drop and hard to keep ordered consistently.
scenario: 用户资料写进主事务库，推荐查询却走 Elasticsearch；用户改完偏好会立刻下拉刷新 feed。
scenario_en: Profiles are written to the primary transactional database while the feed queries Elasticsearch, and users refresh right after editing preferences.

scenario: feed 生成用 Elasticsearch（搜索优化数据库）做实时查询，滑动数据用 Cassandra 持久化。
q: 在“读 / 写负载偏好”这个维度上，Elasticsearch 相对 Cassandra 的定位是？
options: 为写密集负载优化
读写完全均衡
与 Cassandra 一样偏写优化
读密集优化，高频写需批量合并
options_en: Optimized for write-heavy workloads.
Perfectly balanced for reads and writes.
Write-optimized, just like Cassandra.
Read-optimized; heavy writes should be batched.
why: ES 是读优化的搜索引擎：更新频率高时应批量合并写入，别把它当写密集库用——这正好和写优化的 Cassandra 形成对照。
why_en: Elasticsearch is optimized for read-heavy workloads, so high update rates call for batching writes into the index.
tradeoff: Elasticsearch（读优化，写需批量） vs Cassandra（写优化，可持续高频写）
q_en: How does Elasticsearch differ from Cassandra on read/write workload fit?
scenario_en: Feed generation uses Elasticsearch for real-time search, while swipe data is persisted in Cassandra.
optionExplanations: 这与 ES 的实际定位正好相反，它是为读设计的。
两者在读写优化上并不对称，谈不上均衡。
这混淆了 ES 与 Cassandra 的定位，两者优化方向相反。
对——ES 为搜索和读取优化，更新频率高时应该批量合并写入，而不是当写密集库用。
optionExplanations_en: That's the opposite of Elasticsearch's actual strength, which is reads, not writes.
The two aren't symmetric on read/write optimization; it isn't a balance.
This mixes up the two systems' orientation — they're optimized in opposite directions.
Correct — Elasticsearch is built for search and reads, so frequent updates should be batched rather than treated as a write-heavy workload.

scenario: 希望用户一打开 app 立刻就能开始滑，而不是等待系统现场计算推荐。
q: 预计算方案应该怎么做？
options: 用户打开 app 时才现场实时计算
让用户手动点刷新
后台周期性预生成 feed 存入缓存
把 feed 存到 CDN
options_en: Compute the feed live on the spot when the user opens the app.
Let the user manually tap refresh.
Pre-generate feeds periodically in the background and cache them.
Store the feed at the CDN edge.
why: 预计算 + 缓存让 feed 打开即达：后台作业周期性生成、低峰跑批降低资源冲击，用户体验是零等待。
why_en: Background jobs periodically pre-compute feeds from preferences and location and cache them, ideally scheduled off-peak, so the app opens instantly.
whenOtherWins: 查询条件频繁变化（位置漂移、改过滤器）时预计算容易失效，实时 ES 查询更合适——最终两者要结合。
tradeoff: 预计算+缓存（打开即达，但会陈旧） vs 现场实时计算（新鲜，但有等待延迟）
q_en: How should precomputation make the feed ready immediately?
scenario_en: The user should be able to open the app and start swiping immediately, instead of waiting for recommendations to be computed live.
optionExplanations: 现场计算没法满足打开即滑、零等待的体验目标。
手动刷新把等待成本转嫁给了用户，不是自动化方案。
对——后台批量生成 feed 存进缓存，用户打开时直接取现成结果，没有等待。
CDN 面向公开静态内容，不适合私有、每人不同的个性化 feed。
optionExplanations_en: Computing on the spot can't meet the zero-wait, open-and-swipe experience this needs.
Manual refresh just shifts the waiting cost onto the user; it isn't an automated fix.
Correct — background jobs pre-generate the feed into cache, so opening the app just reads the result with no wait.
CDNs suit public static content, not a private, per-user personalized feed.

q: 只靠“预计算 + 缓存 feed”会遇到哪些问题？（多选）
options: 高活跃用户很快把缓存的 feed 滑穿，然后就得等待新推荐
缓存的 feed 反映不了最新的资料变更和新注册用户，匹配相关性下降
滑穿之后又要重跑昂贵的查询，既低效又慢
缓存的 feed 无法存进 Redis
options_en: Highly active users quickly exhaust the cached feed and then have to wait.
The cached feed misses recent profile changes and new signups, hurting relevance.
Exhausting the cache forces a re-run of the expensive query, which is slow.
A cached feed cannot be stored in Redis.
why: 纯预计算的三宗罪：活跃用户滑穿缓存、内容跟不上最新变化、滑穿后还得重跑贵查询——所以要配上实时索引查询做兜底。
why_en: Highly active users can exhaust the cache, the content goes stale, and exhausting it forces the expensive query to run again.
q_en: What problems appear if the feed relies only on precompute and cache?
optionExplanations: 对——高活跃用户滑得比后台预计算的周期还快，很快就把缓存滑穿。
对——缓存是某个时刻的快照，之后的资料变化和新用户反映不进去。
对——缓存耗尽后，系统被迫退回最初那条低效查询，重新算一遍。
错——Redis 存字符串或哈希毫无问题，这不是真实存在的限制。
optionExplanations_en: True — highly active users swipe faster than the background cadence can refill, so they blow through the cache.
True — the cache is a snapshot; later profile edits and new signups aren't reflected in it.
True — once the cache runs dry, the system falls back to re-running the original expensive query.
False — Redis storing strings or hashes is fine; that isn't a real limitation.
scenario: 重度用户一晚滑掉几百张，同时每天都有新用户注册、老用户改资料和位置。
scenario_en: Heavy users burn hundreds of profiles a night while new users sign up and existing ones change profiles and locations every day.

scenario: 预计算缓存能秒开但会滑穿、会陈旧；实时 ES 查询新鲜但打开时要等。想要一个兼得的方案。
q: 混合方案是什么？
options: 只用缓存，滑穿之后就让用户干等着
缓存秒开，滑穿前切到 ES 实时补充
只用 ES，放弃缓存
每次请求随机二选一
options_en: Use only the cache, and make users wait once they swipe through it.
Cache opens instantly, and it switches to real-time Elasticsearch before running out.
Use only Elasticsearch and drop the cache entirely.
Randomly pick one of the two on every request.
why: 组合两者：缓存管“即开即滑”，索引库管“滑不完的新鲜补给”，剩几张时提前刷新——对用户来说 stack 仿佛无限。
why_en: The hybrid combines an instant cached open with a real-time Elasticsearch top-up before the cache runs dry.
whenOtherWins: 规模小或用户活跃度低时，单独一种方案（纯实时或纯预计算）就够，不必同时维护两套。
tradeoff: 混合方案（体验最好，维护两套组件） vs 单一方案（更简单，牺牲体验或新鲜度）
q_en: What hybrid feed-generation approach combines cache and real-time search?
scenario_en: A precomputed cache opens fast but can run out or go stale; real-time Elasticsearch is fresh but adds wait time.
optionExplanations: 纯缓存方案没解决滑穿后的等待问题，只是把问题往后推。
对——缓存负责秒开，剩几张时提前切到实时索引补充，用户感觉不到断层。
只用 ES 会失去缓存带来的打开即滑体验，每次都要等查询。
随机二选一没有稳定的体验保证，也不是有意设计的策略。
optionExplanations_en: Cache-only doesn't solve the wait once it runs out — it just postpones the problem.
Correct — the cache gives the instant open, and switching to the real-time index before it's exhausted keeps it feeling seamless.
Elasticsearch-only loses the instant-open experience the cache provides; every open would wait on a query.
Randomly picking between the two gives no consistent experience and isn't a deliberate strategy.

q: 什么时机触发 stack 刷新，能让用户觉得推荐是“无限”的？
options: 剩少量资料时提前后台刷新
用户滑完最后一张再刷新
每天凌晨统一刷新
用户手动下拉时
options_en: Trigger a background refresh while a few profiles remain.
Refresh only after the user swipes the last profile.
Refresh everyone uniformly at midnight.
Refresh only when the user pulls to refresh.
why: 在剩几张时就后台预取，新一叠在用户滑到底之前已就位——从用户视角 stack 永远滑不完。
why_en: Triggering the refresh while a few profiles remain lets the next batch be ready before the user reaches the end.
q_en: When should the app refresh the stack so it feels endless?
optionExplanations: 对——在存量还剩一小截时就悄悄触发后台预取，等用户滑到底新一批早就候着了。
等滑完最后一张再刷新，用户会明显感受到等待。
统一定时刷新没法适配每个用户各自的滑动速度。
手动下拉把等待和操作负担都转嫁给了用户。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — kick off the background prefetch quietly while a handful of profiles are left, so fresh recommendations are already queued well before the stack runs dry.
Waiting until the very last swipe to refresh gives the user a noticeable wait.
A uniform scheduled refresh can't adapt to each user's own swiping speed.
Pull-to-refresh just shifts the waiting and the extra tap onto the user.
scenario: 重新生成并拉取一叠 feed 要 1-2 秒，而用户滑掉一张只需要半秒左右。
scenario_en: Regenerating and fetching a new stack takes one to two seconds, but a user swipes through a profile in about half a second.

q: 缓存 feed 里的资料可能因哪些事件而变“陈旧”（不再符合过滤条件）？（多选）
options: 被推荐的用户改变了位置，不再在距离范围内
被推荐的用户修改了资料 / 兴趣，不再匹配过滤条件
看 feed 的用户改了自己的过滤条件
看 feed 的用户显著换了位置（去了另一个街区或城市）
options_en: A recommended user moved and is no longer within range.
A recommended user edited their profile or interests and no longer matches.
The viewer changed their own filter settings.
The viewer moved significantly, to a different neighborhood or city.
why: 陈旧的来源两头都有：被推荐者动了（位置、资料），或者观看者动了（过滤条件、位置）。后两类是用户触发的，可以顺势后台重建 feed。
why_en: Staleness comes from both sides: the recommended user changing, or the viewer changing their own filters or location.
q_en: Which events can make cached feed profiles stale?
optionExplanations: 推荐对象一旦移动出距离范围，缓存里这条推荐就不该再展示。
推荐对象改了资料或兴趣后，之前满足的过滤条件可能已经不成立。
查看者自己改了过滤条件，缓存里按旧条件生成的结果就该失效。
查看者位置发生大幅变化后，缓存结果的距离基准已经不适用。
optionExplanations_en: Once a recommended user moves out of range, that cached recommendation shouldn't still be shown.
Once a recommended user edits their profile or interests, the filter that once matched may no longer hold.
Once the viewer changes their own filters, results cached under the old filter should be invalidated.
Once the viewer's location shifts significantly, the distance basis behind the cached results no longer applies.
scenario: feed 在用户打开 app 时算好并缓存半小时，而这半小时里两边的用户都可能在动。
scenario_en: The feed is computed on app open and cached for half an hour, during which users on both sides keep moving and editing.

q: 对付缓存 feed 变陈旧的主要手段是？
options: 永不缓存
加密缓存
短 TTL + 定期重算
让用户容忍错误的推荐
options_en: Never cache at all.
Encrypt the cache.
Short TTL plus scheduled recompute.
Just let users tolerate wrong recommendations.
why: 短 TTL 限制陈旧上限，定时任务按计划重算；改过滤器、大幅移动这类用户动作也应触发后台刷新，让 feed 在用户开始滑之前就绪。
why_en: A short TTL bounds staleness, scheduled jobs recompute on a cadence, and user actions like changing filters also trigger a background refresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期即失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time-to-live after which a cached entry expires.

q_en: What are the main tools for handling stale cached feeds?
optionExplanations: 完全不缓存会直接牺牲掉打开即滑的低延迟体验。
加密和缓存内容是否陈旧完全是两回事。
对——给缓存设一个不长的存活期，配合按周期自动重算，加上过滤器变化这类事件触发的额外刷新。
放任错误推荐给用户看，会直接损害产品体验，不是技术方案。
optionExplanations_en: Not caching at all would give up the low-latency instant-open experience entirely.
Encryption has nothing to do with whether cached content is stale.
Correct — cap how long entries can live, pair it with scheduled recompute, and let events like filter changes trigger extra refreshes too.
Letting users just tolerate wrong recommendations hurts the product; it isn't a technical fix.
scenario: 缓存 feed 能把打开延迟从 1 秒降到 50ms，但业务只能容忍分钟级的陈旧。
scenario_en: Caching the feed cuts open latency from a second to fifty milliseconds, but the product only tolerates staleness measured in minutes.

scenario: 每天为全部 2000 万用户多次预计算 feed 成本极高，而其中很多人当天根本不会打开 app。
q: 怎么控制预计算成本？
options: 降低所有人的推荐质量
把每次缓存的数量减到 1 条
干脆放弃预计算
只为预计活跃的用户预热缓存
options_en: Lower recommendation quality for everyone.
Cut the cached batch size down to just one profile.
Abandon pre-computation altogether.
Only pre-warm the cache for users predicted to be active.
why: 规模化下不该为不来的人白算：只给预计会用到缓存的活跃用户预热 feed，把昂贵的前置计算花在刀刃上。
why_en: At scale you shouldn't compute for users who won't show up, so only pre-warming feeds for predicted active users targets the expensive work where it pays off.
whenOtherWins: 用户基数小或计算便宜时，全量预计算实现最简单，不值得先做活跃度筛选。
tradeoff: 只为活跃用户预热（省成本，需要活跃度预测） vs 全量预计算（简单，但浪费在不活跃用户上）
q_en: How should the system control feed precomputation cost?
scenario_en: Precomputing feed stacks many times per day for all 20M users is expensive, and many users will not open the app that day.
optionExplanations: 降低所有人的推荐质量是牺牲体验，不是针对无效计算做的精细化控制。
只缓存一条会让用户几乎立刻滑穿，反而更频繁触发重算。
放弃预计算会直接失去打开即滑的体验目标。
对——把这份计算只花在真的会打开 app 的人身上，别人不预热。
optionExplanations_en: Lowering quality for everyone sacrifices the experience instead of precisely cutting wasted computation.
Caching just one profile means users blow through it almost instantly, triggering recompute even more often.
Abandoning precomputation gives up the instant-open experience entirely.
Correct — spend that computation only on the users likely to actually open the app, and leave everyone else unwarmed.

scenario: 预计算 + 缓存 + 实时索引这套 feed 方案上线后，需要在不改代码逻辑的前提下按规模调优。
q: 这套 feed 方案里哪些参数是可调的？（多选）
options: 缓存资料的 TTL
每次缓存的资料数量
为哪批用户预计算 feed
Cassandra 的 gossip 端口
options_en: The TTL of cached profiles.
How many profiles are cached per batch.
Which set of users get feeds pre-computed.
Cassandra's gossip port.
why: TTL、缓存条数、预热人群都是旋钮：不改系统逻辑就能按规模与场景调优。gossip 端口是集群配置，与 feed 方案无关。
why_en: TTL, cache batch size, and the pre-warm audience are all knobs that can be tuned without changing the system's logic.
q_en: Which knobs can tune this precompute, cache, and search feed design?
scenario_en: After launching the precompute, cache, and real-time index feed design, operators need tuning knobs without changing code logic.
optionExplanations: 对——TTL 越短越新鲜，但重算成本越高，是控制陈旧度的旋钮。
对——每次缓存的资料数量越多滑穿越慢，但存储和计算成本也越高。
对——预热的人群越精准，浪费在不活跃用户身上的计算就越少。
错——gossip 端口是集群通信配置，与 feed 业务调优无关。
optionExplanations_en: True — a shorter TTL stays fresher but costs more recompute; it's the staleness knob.
True — a bigger cached batch delays exhaustion but costs more storage and compute.
True — a tighter pre-warm audience wastes less computation on users who won't show up.
False — the gossip port is cluster communication config, unrelated to feed business tuning.

q: “系统带可调参数”为什么被视为一个设计优点？
options: 能少写代码
不改逻辑就能调参适配规模
可以跳过测试
方便按不同配置向用户收费
options_en: It means writing less code.
It lets operators tune for scale without touching the logic.
It means tests can be skipped.
It makes it easy to charge users by their configuration.
why: 可调参数给了运营者强控制力：不重构系统就能找到适合当前规模的高效配置，并随演进不断微调。
why_en: Tunable parameters give operators strong control, letting them find an efficient configuration for the current scale without reworking the system.
q_en: Why is tunability a design advantage here?
optionExplanations: 参数化和代码量多少没有直接关系。
对——运营者靠调参而不是改代码就能适配当前规模，随演进持续微调。
可调参数和测试覆盖是完全不同的两件事。
计费模式不是这道题讨论的设计目标。
optionExplanations_en: Parameterization has nothing to do with how much code gets written.
Correct — operators can adapt to the current scale by tuning knobs instead of changing code, and keep adjusting as things evolve.
Tunable parameters and test coverage are two unrelated things.
Billing models aren't a design goal this problem is discussing.
scenario: 上线后日活从 200 万涨到 2000 万，预取张数、缓存 TTL、过滤器大小都得重新定。
scenario_en: Daily actives grow from two million to twenty million, so prefetch size, cache TTL and filter size all have to be re-picked.

q: 把“低延迟 feed 生成”这条决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 代价：缓存的 feed 会陈旧，活跃用户还会滑穿
改进：引入 Elasticsearch + 地理空间索引做实时查询
需求：打开 app 即刻能滑，stack 加载 < 300ms
缓解：TTL < 1h + 按需后台刷新，滑到剩几张时用 ES 实时补充
瓶颈：朴素 SQL 按偏好 + 经纬度过滤太慢，地理搜索尤甚
再改进：后台预计算并缓存 feed，实现秒开
why: 链条：低延迟需求 → 朴素查询是瓶颈 → 上 ES + 地理索引 → 再加预计算缓存实现秒开 → 代价是陈旧与滑穿 → 用短 TTL + 后台刷新 + ES 兜底缓解。
why_en: The chain runs from the low-latency requirement through the slow naive query, to Elasticsearch, to precomputed caching, and finally its staleness cost and mitigation.
tradeoff: 预计算缓存 + 实时索引兜底（秒开且较新鲜，架构更复杂） vs 纯实时查询（简单，但打开要等）
q_en: Put the low-latency feed-generation decision chain in order.

scenario: 生成 feed 时必须过滤掉用户已经滑过的资料，先考虑最直接的后端方案。
q: 应该怎么做？
options: 查滑动库做 contains 过滤，按分区路由
把全站所有用户的滑动记录都统统加载进网关内存
让客户端保存全量的滑动历史记录
完全不做过滤，让用户自己跳过
options_en: Query the swipe store for a contains check, routed by partition.
Load every user's swipe records across the whole site into the gateway's memory.
Have the client store the user's entire swipe history record.
Skip filtering entirely and let users scroll past duplicates themselves.
why: 最直接的做法：feed builder 查滑动库、把滑过的 ID 拿来做 contains 过滤；分区键保证这条查询只打一个分区。
why_en: The most direct approach queries the swipe store for the user's swiped ids and filters them out, routed to a single partition.
whenOtherWins: 滑动历史极大时 contains 检查越来越贵，就得升级为客户端近期缓存乃至布隆过滤器。
tradeoff: 查滑动库做 contains 过滤（简单直接，历史越大越贵） vs 客户端缓存/布隆过滤器（更省，但多一层组件）
q_en: What is the first backend approach for filtering already-swiped profiles?
scenario_en: When building a feed, the system must filter out profiles the user has already swiped on; start with the most direct backend design.
optionExplanations: 对——生成 feed 时拿滑过的 ID 集合去查滑动表做 contains 判断，分区键保证只打一个分区。
网关是无状态路由层，不该背负这类业务数据的缓存职责。
客户端保存全量历史是值得做的后续升级，但不是这里最省事的第一版做法。
不过滤会直接违反避免重复展示这条核心非功能需求。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — while building the feed, check the swiped id set against the swipe table with a contains lookup; the partition key keeps that query hitting just one shard.
The gateway is a stateless routing layer; it shouldn't carry this kind of business-data cache.
Storing the full history on the client is worth doing later, but it isn't the simplest first cut here.
Skipping the filter directly breaks the core non-functional requirement to avoid re-showing profiles.

q: “查滑动库做 contains 过滤”会遇到哪些问题？（多选）
options: 偏可用性的系统里，近期滑动可能尚未同步到所有副本，生成 feed 时漏检 → 有重复展示的风险
滑动历史庞大的用户会返回海量 ID，contains 检查越滑越贵
布隆过滤器会产生假阴性
分区路由会因此失效
options_en: In an availability-leaning system, recent swipes may not have replicated yet, risking a re-show.
Users with huge swipe histories return massive id sets, making the contains check ever more expensive.
Bloom filters produce false negatives.
Partition routing stops working because of this.
why: 两个软肋：最终一致让新滑动可能没同步齐、被漏掉；重度用户的 ID 集越查越大。分别由客户端缓存和布隆过滤器接棒解决。
why_en: The two weak spots are eventual-consistency gaps in very recent swipes and the ever-growing id set for heavy users.
q_en: What problems come with querying the swipe store for contains filtering?
optionExplanations: 对——偏可用性的系统里，刚写入的滑动可能还没同步到查询命中的副本，就会漏检。
对——滑动历史越长，contains 检查要扫描比对的 ID 集合就越大，越滑越贵。
错——布隆过滤器的设计目标恰恰是绝无假阴性，这与它的真实特性相反。
错——分区路由不受这个过滤方案影响，本身没有失效。
optionExplanations_en: True — in an availability-leaning system, a just-written swipe may not have replicated to the replica being queried, so it slips through.
True — the longer a user's swipe history, the bigger the id set the contains check has to scan, so it gets pricier over time.
False — a Bloom filter is designed to guarantee zero false negatives; that's the opposite of its real behavior.
False — partition routing is unaffected by this filtering approach; nothing about it breaks.
scenario: 滑动库是偏可用性的 Cassandra，而重度用户已经积累了几十万条滑动记录。
scenario_en: The swipe store is availability-leaning Cassandra, and heavy users have already accumulated hundreds of thousands of swipes.

scenario: 近期滑动可能还没同步到所有副本；但在服务端专门为“未落库数据”维护一层缓存又太贵。
q: 近期滑动未完全同步时，应该怎么过滤重复资料？
options: 再加一个后端专用 Redis 缓存层
客户端缓存最近 K 次滑动并自行过滤
把滑动改成同步强一致写
放弃过滤
options_en: Add yet another dedicated backend Redis cache layer.
Have the client cache the last K swipes and filter locally.
Make swipes a synchronous strongly-consistent write.
Give up on filtering.
why: 把客户端当作系统的一部分：设备端存最近 K 次滑动并自行过滤，比在后端为未同步数据养一层缓存便宜得多。
why_en: Treating the client as part of the system, the device stores the most recent K swipes and filters locally, far cheaper than a backend cache for unsynced data.
whenOtherWins: 若用户会在多台设备上同时使用，客户端缓存彼此不同步，就得回到服务端方案——本题假设单设备成立。
tradeoff: 客户端本地缓存（便宜，依赖单设备假设） vs 后端缓存层（对多设备友好，但运维成本高）
q_en: How should duplicate profiles be filtered when recent swipes are not fully replicated?
scenario_en: Recent swipes may not have replicated to every server yet, but maintaining a server-side cache just for unreplicated swipes is costly.
optionExplanations: 再加一层后端组件正是要避免的额外运维成本，没有绕开同步延迟的根本问题。
对——手机本地记住最近滑过的 K 条、自己过滤，不必在后端为这批还没同步的数据另起一层缓存。
把滑动改成同步强一致写会拖慢全站滑动延迟，代价过大。
放弃过滤会直接违反避免重复展示这条核心非功能需求。
optionExplanations_en: Adding yet another backend layer is exactly the extra operational cost this is trying to avoid, and doesn't fix the sync-delay problem underneath.
Correct — the phone remembers its own recent swipe history and screens locally, without needing a whole extra server-side cache just for this not-yet-synced sliver of data.
Making swipes a synchronous strongly-consistent write would slow down every swipe site-wide, too costly for this.
Giving up on filtering directly violates the core non-functional requirement to avoid re-showing profiles.

q: “让客户端参与过滤”依赖的关键假设是？
options: 客户端存储无限
客户端网络永远在线
假设用户只用一台设备
客户端能直连数据库
options_en: The client has unlimited storage.
The client is always online.
The user is assumed to use only one device.
The client can connect directly to the database.
why: 单设备假设成立，客户端才可靠：它看得到用户全部近期滑动，可以放心承担存储与过滤职责。
why_en: The single-device assumption is what makes the client reliable, since it sees all of the user's recent swipes.
q_en: What key assumption makes client-side filtering acceptable?
optionExplanations: 只需要存最近 K 次滑动，不要求无限容量。
离线时没法过滤是可以接受的边缘情况，不是这个方案依赖的关键假设。
对——只有假设用户只用一台设备，客户端才看得到全部近期滑动，方案才可靠。
客户端从不直连数据库，都经由 API 交互，这不是它依赖的假设。
optionExplanations_en: It only needs to hold the last K swipes, not unlimited capacity.
Being unable to filter while offline is an acceptable edge case, not the key assumption this relies on.
Correct — only if the user has a single device does the client actually see all of their recent swipes, making it reliable.
The client never talks to the database directly; it always goes through the API, so that isn't the assumption here.
scenario: 把最近上千条滑动放在手机本地做过滤，可以省掉生成 feed 时的一次服务端查询。
scenario_en: Keeping the last thousand-odd swipes on the phone for filtering saves one server-side lookup every time a feed is generated.

q: 用户在 200 张预取资料里滑到约第 150 张时，客户端应该做什么？
options: 直接弹窗强行要求用户先停下来休息一会儿再滑
立刻清空全部本地缓存里的数据
什么都不做，等滑穿了才处理
提前 ping 后端生成新 feed 并预取
options_en: Pop up a dialog forcing the user to stop and take a break before swiping more.
Immediately clear out all the data in the local cache.
Do nothing and only handle it once the stack is exhausted.
Ping the backend early to generate and prefetch the next feed.
why: 客户端缓存的第二重价值：接近滑穿时提前触发后端生成、稍后拉取，并用本地最近滑动继续过滤新 feed，保证无缝衔接。
why_en: The client should ping the backend early to generate the next feed and prefetch it, keeping the swiping experience seamless.
q_en: What should the client do around profile 150 of a 200-profile prefetched stack?
optionExplanations: 弹窗打断体验不是系统该做的事，这不是技术方案。
过早清空缓存会让最近滑动没法继续参与去重过滤。
等滑完再请求，用户会感受到明显的等待和卡顿。
对——提前 ping 后端生成新一叠并预取，保证滑到底之前就已经衔接上。
optionExplanations_en: Popping up a dialog interrupts the experience; that isn't a technical solution.
Clearing the cache too early breaks its ability to keep filtering out recently swiped profiles.
Waiting until the stack is exhausted to request more gives the user a noticeable stall.
Correct — pinging the backend early to generate and prefetch the next batch keeps things seamless before the user hits the bottom.
scenario: 客户端一次预取 200 张资料，而后端重新生成并返回新一叠需要 1-2 秒。
scenario_en: The client prefetches two hundred profiles at a time, and the backend needs one to two seconds to build and return the next stack.

scenario: 个别重度用户的滑动历史大到缓存放不下、contains 检查也太慢，需要专门手段支撑他们的 feed 过滤。
q: 针对这类用户的（略偏 over-engineered 但成立的）方案是？
options: 历史超阈值时为该用户建布隆过滤器
强制清空他们的滑动历史
限制他们每天最多滑 10 次
为他们单独部署一套数据库
options_en: Build and cache a Bloom filter for that user once history exceeds a threshold.
Force-clear their swipe history.
Cap them at ten swipes a day.
Deploy a dedicated database just for them.
why: 布隆过滤器以极小空间支撑超大集合的成员检查：历史超过阈值就为该用户建过滤器并缓存，feed 构建时快速过滤。
why_en: A Bloom filter supports membership checks over a huge set with very little space, built and cached once a user's history crosses a threshold.
whenOtherWins: 普通用户历史不大，客户端缓存 + contains 检查已足够；布隆过滤器只有在历史巨大时才值得上。
tradeoff: 布隆过滤器（省空间、查询快，但有假阳性） vs 完整 ID contains 检查（精确，但历史越大越慢）

termDefinitions.meaning: 用极小空间判断元素是否在集合中的概率型结构，可能假阳性但不会假阴性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic structure that may return false positives but never false negatives.

q_en: What specialized option helps heavy swipers with huge history sets?
scenario_en: Some heavy swipers have histories too large for cache and too slow for full contains checks, so feed filtering needs a specialized tool.
optionExplanations: 对——历史超过阈值就为该用户建一个布隆过滤器并缓存，用极小空间换来快速成员检查。
强制清空历史会让用户被重复推荐自己已经滑过的资料，违反核心 NFR。
限制滑动次数是产品层面的妥协，牺牲体验，不是工程解法。
为单个用户单独部署数据库的运维成本和收益完全不成比例。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — once a user's history crosses a threshold, build and cache a Bloom filter for them, trading a little space for fast membership checks.
Force-clearing history would cause the user to be re-shown profiles they already swiped on, breaking the core NFR.
Capping swipe counts is a product-level compromise that sacrifices experience, not an engineering fix.
Standing up a dedicated database for one user is wildly disproportionate to the operational cost.

q: 布隆过滤器用于滑动过滤时，正确性保证是什么？
options: 既有假阳性也有假阴性
可能假阳性，但绝无假阴性
可能假阴性但无假阳性
完全精确
options_en: It has both false positives and false negatives.
It may have false positives, but never false negatives.
It may have false negatives but never false positives.
It is perfectly precise.
why: 这正是它适合本场景的原因：假阴性为零意味着绝不重复展示（核心 NFR 保住），代价只是少量资料因假阳性永远不出现。
why_en: Zero false negatives means the system never re-shows a swiped profile, at the cost of a few profiles disappearing due to false positives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构判断某元素存在，但实际并不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive means the structure says an element exists when it actually does not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构判断某元素不存在，但实际存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative means the structure says an element is absent when it actually exists.

q_en: What correctness guarantee matters when using a Bloom filter for swipe filtering?
optionExplanations: 布隆过滤器的设计目标就是彻底消灭假阴性，这个说法方向不对。
对——假阴性绝不会发生，代价只是极少数资料因假阳性被误判为已滑过。
这与布隆过滤器的真实特性正好相反，假阴性才是它承诺消除的。
布隆过滤器天生是概率型结构，不是精确结构，这也是它省空间的原因。
optionExplanations_en: A Bloom filter is specifically designed to eliminate false negatives, so this direction is wrong.
Correct — false negatives never happen; the cost is that a small number of profiles get wrongly flagged as already-swiped.
That's backwards from how a Bloom filter actually behaves; eliminating false negatives is exactly its guarantee.
A Bloom filter is inherently probabilistic, not exact — that's precisely why it's space-efficient.
scenario: 候选池上千万人，而核心非功能需求是：绝不把用户已经滑过的人再推一次。
scenario_en: The candidate pool is tens of millions, and the core requirement is that a profile the user already swiped on is never shown again.

q: 布隆过滤器的错误率通常和什么直接挂钩、因此可以调？
options: 主要取决于 CPU 主频高低
主要取决于网络带宽大小
占用空间大小：空间换更低假阳性
主要取决于用户年龄大小
options_en: Mainly determined by CPU clock speed.
Mainly determined by network bandwidth.
The amount of space used: more space buys a lower false-positive rate.
Mainly determined by the user's age.
why: 错误率与空间占用是一对旋钮：调到假阳性够低、空间可接受、过滤够快的平衡点即可。
why_en: Error rate and space usage are a knob pair, tuned to a balance of low false positives, acceptable space, and fast filtering.
q_en: What does the Bloom filter error rate trade against?
optionExplanations: CPU 主频不是决定布隆过滤器假阳性率的因素。
网络带宽和这个本地数据结构的错误率无关。
对——位数组越大、哈希函数配置越好，假阳性率就越低，空间换精度。
用户属性和过滤器本身的数学特性没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: CPU clock speed isn't what determines a Bloom filter's false-positive rate.
Network bandwidth has nothing to do with the error rate of this local data structure.
Correct — a bigger bit array and better hash configuration lower the false-positive rate; it's space traded for accuracy.
User attributes have nothing to do with the filter's own mathematical properties.
scenario: 每个重度用户都要常驻一份过滤器在缓存节点内存里，这样的用户有上千万。
scenario_en: Every heavy user needs their own filter resident in cache memory, and there are tens of millions of such users.

q: 布隆过滤器方案的主要运维挑战是？
options: 无法用任何语言实现
过滤速度太慢
会拖垮底层 Cassandra
需持续更新，节点故障后重建开销很大
options_en: It cannot be implemented in any language.
Filtering is too slow.
It overloads the underlying Cassandra.
It needs constant updates, and rebuilding after a node failure is costly.
why: 布隆过滤器好建但要养：每次新滑动都要更新它，缓存节点挂掉后重建虽然可行，规模化下却很昂贵。
why_en: A Bloom filter is easy to build but costly to maintain, since every new swipe requires an update and rebuilding after a node failure is expensive at scale.
q_en: What is the main operational challenge of the Bloom filter design?
optionExplanations: 布隆过滤器是通用数据结构，主流语言都能实现，这不是真实限制。
过滤本身只是几次哈希计算，速度很快，问题不在这里。
过滤器读写发生在 Redis 或内存层，不会直接冲击 Cassandra。
对——每次新滑动都要更新过滤器，节点故障后重建虽然可行，规模化下开销很大。
optionExplanations_en: A Bloom filter is a generic data structure implementable in any mainstream language; that's not a real limitation.
The filtering itself is just a few hash computations and is fast; that's not where the problem lies.
The filter's reads and writes live in Redis or memory, not on Cassandra's write path.
Correct — every new swipe requires an update, and rebuilding after a node failure, while doable, gets expensive at scale.
scenario: 过滤器放在缓存层，每秒数万次新滑动都要写进去，而缓存节点会偶尔宕机重启。
scenario_en: The filter lives in the cache layer, tens of thousands of new swipes a second must be written into it, and cache nodes do restart.

q: 对重度滑动用户，“布隆过滤器”与“完整 ID contains 检查”的核心取舍维度是？
options: 空间/速度 vs 精确性
开源 vs 闭源
强一致 vs 最终一致
本地 vs 云端
options_en: Space and speed versus exact accuracy.
Open source versus closed source.
Strong consistency versus eventual consistency.
On-device versus cloud-hosted.
why: 一句话对比：布隆过滤器用可控的不精确换空间与速度；contains 检查零误差，但成本随历史线性膨胀。
why_en: The Bloom filter trades a controlled amount of inaccuracy for space and speed, while the exact contains check has zero error but scales linearly with history.
tradeoff: 布隆过滤器（省空间、快，有假阳性） vs 完整 contains 检查（精确，历史越大越慢）
q_en: For heavy swipers, what is the core tradeoff between a Bloom filter and full ID contains checks?
optionExplanations: 对——布隆过滤器用可控的不精确换空间和速度，contains 检查零误差但成本随历史线性增长。
开源许可协议和这里的工程取舍完全无关。
两种方案讨论的都是集合成员检查，不是复制一致性问题。
两者都能部署在同一层，不是本地和云端的区别。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a Bloom filter trades controlled inaccuracy for space and speed, while the exact contains check has zero error but grows linearly with history.
Open-source licensing has nothing to do with this engineering tradeoff.
Both approaches are about set-membership checks, not replication consistency.
Both can be deployed in the same layer; this isn't an on-device-versus-cloud distinction.
scenario: 重度用户的滑动历史有几十万条，而 feed 生成时的去重必须在几十毫秒内完成。
scenario_en: A heavy swiper has hundreds of thousands of past swipes, and dedup during feed generation must finish in tens of milliseconds.

scenario: 面试官只说'设计 Tinder'，没点明要深挖哪块；45 分钟有限，只能挑一条主线重点做。
q: 不确定该聚焦哪部分功能时，深挖主线应该怎么选？
options: 先和面试官简短来回确认，再选最能体现产品独特性或最复杂的那条主线
把有限时间平均摊到全部四条功能需求，让每一条都做到完全相同的深度
先挑实现起来最省事的那一条功能整段做完，剩下的时间再回头看要不要补别的
严格照功能需求的编号顺序，从第一条一路做到最后一条为止
options_en: Briefly align with the interviewer, then pick the line that best shows the product's uniqueness or complexity.
Split the limited time evenly across all four functional requirements so each gets identical depth.
Fully finish whichever feature is easiest to build first, then see if time is left for the rest.
Follow the functional-requirement numbering strictly, from the first item to the last.
why: 深挖时间有限，投给最能体现产品独特性或最复杂的主线信号最高；代价是其他功能只能高层带过。
why_en: Deep-dive time is scarce, so spend it on the line that best shows the product's uniqueness or complexity — the rest you cover at a high level.
q_en: When you're unsure which features to focus on, how should you pick the line to go deep on?
optionExplanations: 对——先对齐再挑最独特/最复杂的那条，把稀缺的深挖预算投在区分度最高处。
平均用力会让每块都停在浅层，最该展示能力的核心交互反而没讲透。
拣最省事的先做，等于把时间花在区分度最低、面试官最不在意的部分。
编号只是罗列顺序不代表价值顺序，容易在次要功能上耗光时间。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — align first, then invest scarce deep-dive budget in the most differentiating line.
Spreading effort evenly keeps everything shallow and leaves the core interaction under-explored.
Doing the easiest first spends time on the least differentiating, least-cared-about part.
Numbering is a listing order, not a value order; it burns time on secondary features.
scenario_en: The interviewer only says "design Tinder" without pinning down what to focus on, and with a fixed 45 minutes you can only take one main line deep.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计面试里对某个子问题做深入技术展开的环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the phase where you technically expand one sub-problem in depth.

scenario: Tinder 这类 product-design 题，功能与非功能需求都已定好，要开始搭系统，需要一个不跑偏的推进顺序。
q: product-design 风格题，推进设计的顺序策略应该是？
options: 先逐条满足功能需求搭出可用高层设计，再用非功能需求驱动 deep dive 的先后
一上来就针对预想中的瓶颈做优化和 deep dive，把高层骨架留到最后再回头补齐
先把数据库选型和分片方案敲定，再回过头搭 API 与高层数据流
按一致性、延迟、规模这些非功能需求逐条设计，功能需求穿插着补
options_en: Satisfy functional requirements into a working high-level design first, then let non-functional requirements order the deep dives.
Start by optimizing for the bottlenecks you expect and leave the high-level skeleton for last.
Lock in database choice and sharding first, then come back and build the API and data flow.
Design one non-functional requirement at a time and slot functional requirements in between.
why: 功能优先能快速搭出可用系统、定清组件边界；非功能需求再决定往哪些 deep dive 使劲。先优化会脱离尚未成形的设计。
why_en: Functional-first quickly yields a working system and clear component boundaries; non-functional requirements then decide which deep dives to push. Optimizing first floats free of a design that doesn't exist yet.
q_en: For a product-design style question, what ordering strategy should drive the design?
optionExplanations: 对——功能优先给出可用骨架，非功能需求再挑深挖点，节奏清晰不跑偏。
设计还没成形就调优，等于给不存在的瓶颈调参，容易空转。
选型和分片是深挖细节，过早定死会让接口与数据流被迫迁就存储决定。
非功能需求脱离功能骨架无处落地，容易讲得抽象、组件对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — functional-first gives a usable skeleton, then non-functional needs select the deep dives.
Tuning before a design exists means tuning a bottleneck that isn't there yet — spinning wheels.
Choice and sharding are deep-dive details; locking them early forces API and data flow to bend to storage.
Non-functional needs have nothing to attach to without the functional skeleton, so they stay abstract.
scenario_en: For a product-design question like Tinder, with functional and non-functional requirements already fixed, you need an ordering that keeps the design from wandering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计面试里对某个子问题做深入技术展开的环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the phase where you technically expand one sub-problem in depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 偏产品/用户功能的系统设计题型，按功能需求逐条搭建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A product-design question is a system-design prompt built feature-by-feature around user functionality.

scenario: 你以 mid-level(E4) 定位参加 Tinder 这轮，想搞清"通过"这条线到底要求交付什么。
q: 关于 E4 在 Tinder 这道题的达标线，下面哪项判断是对的？
options: 不必精通具体技术细节，但要给出支持传统过滤加地理过滤、且能防重复展示的可用设计
必须主动而且高精度地识别出自己设计中潜在的每一个性能瓶颈，并逐一给出对应的优化方案
必须说出 feed 该用哪种索引类型，并主动指出缓存 feed 会随时间变陈旧
必须能像 staff 那样脱离题目、把讨论引向自己最感兴趣的深水区
options_en: Deep tech mastery isn't required, but the design must support traditional plus geo filters and avoid re-showing swiped profiles.
You must proactively and precisely identify every potential performance bottleneck in your design and give an optimization for each.
You must state which index type the feed should use and proactively flag that cached feeds go stale.
You must, like a staff candidate, leave the prompt and steer the discussion toward your favorite deep waters.
why: E4 以广度为主(约80/20)：功能可用、覆盖传统过滤+地理过滤+去重即达标；不要求深挖具体技术或主动精准找瓶颈。
why_en: E4 is breadth-first (~80/20): a functional design covering traditional filters, geo filters and dedup clears the bar; deep tech mastery and precise self-driven bottleneck-finding are not required.
q_en: Which statement about the E4 (mid-level) bar for Tinder is correct?
optionExplanations: 对——E4 只需功能可用、覆盖两类过滤和去重，技术深度可以浅。
主动且精准地揪出每个瓶颈是 senior 及以上的信号，E4 不作硬性要求。
点名索引类型、预判 feed 陈旧属于 E5 的深度信号，超出 E4 的线。
脱题引向深水区是 staff 的表现，对 E4 是过度发挥而非达标项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — E4 only needs a functional design covering both filter types and dedup; depth can be shallow.
Precisely catching every bottleneck is a senior-and-above signal, not an E4 hard requirement.
Naming the index type and anticipating stale feeds is E5 depth, beyond the E4 line.
Leaving the prompt for deep waters is staff behavior, an over-reach for E4, not a bar item.
scenario_en: You're interviewing at mid-level (E4) for Tinder and want to know exactly what the "pass" line requires you to deliver.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工程职级，对应 mid-level 中级工程师。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E4 is an engineering level corresponding to a mid-level engineer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工程职级，对应 senior 高级工程师。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5 is an engineering level corresponding to a senior engineer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 比 senior 更高一档的职级(Staff Engineer)，要求更深的独立主导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff is a level above senior, expected to independently drive deep design.

scenario: 你以 senior(E5) 定位参加 Tinder 这轮，想知道相比 E4 还要多亮出哪些"深度"信号才算达标。
q: 相比 E4，把候选人抬到 E5 达标线的关键增量是哪一项？
options: 主动列出 feed 生成的多种 trade-off，并意识到缓存会随时间变陈旧
把功能需求与整体高层设计讲得比 E4 更细致，再把每一个组件都完整地重讲一遍
能像 staff 一样彻底脱离题目，把讨论引向任意自己擅长的分布式难题
把 API 与数据模型定义得比 E4 更规范、更完整，就足以到 E5
options_en: Proactively lay out the feed-generation trade-offs and recognize that cached feeds go stale over time.
Explain the functional requirements and overall high-level design in more detail than E4, re-covering every component.
Like a staff candidate, fully leave the prompt and steer toward any distributed problem you happen to be good at.
Just define the API and data model more cleanly and completely than E4, which is enough to reach E5.
why: E4 已交付功能可用设计；E5 的增量在深度：主动摊开 feed 生成取舍、说得出索引类型、预判缓存 feed 会陈旧。把广度做厚不算 E5。
why_en: E4 already delivers a functional design; the E5 increment is depth — proactively laying out feed trade-offs, naming an index type, and anticipating stale cached feeds. Thicker breadth alone is not E5.
q_en: Compared with E4, which is the key increment that lifts a candidate to the E5 bar?
optionExplanations: 对——主动摊开取舍并预判 feed 陈旧，正是 E5 要的深度而非更多广度。
把广度做得更厚仍停在 E4 的层次，深度信号没有增加。
彻底脱题任意发挥是 staff 级表现，不是 E5 的达标增量。
把接口和模型做规范仍属基础功，E5 要的是深挖而非更整齐的骨架。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — laying out trade-offs and anticipating stale feeds is the depth E5 wants, not more breadth.
Making breadth thicker still sits at the E4 level; no depth signal is added.
Fully leaving the prompt to freewheel is staff-level, not the E5 bar increment.
Cleaner interfaces and models are still basics; E5 wants depth, not a tidier skeleton.
scenario_en: You're interviewing at senior (E5) for Tinder and want to know which extra "depth" signals, beyond E4, are needed to clear the bar.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工程职级，对应 mid-level 中级工程师。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E4 is an engineering level corresponding to a mid-level engineer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工程职级，对应 senior 高级工程师。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5 is an engineering level corresponding to a senior engineer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 比 senior 更高一档的职级(Staff Engineer)，要求更深的独立主导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff is a level above senior, expected to independently drive deep design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在两个目标间做取舍，得到一个就要牺牲另一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trade-off is choosing between two goals where gaining one costs the other.

q: Top-K 类题目在面试中的一个显著特点是？
q_en: What is one distinctive trait of Top-K interview problems?
options: 每个面试官心里都装着同一套标准架构，背熟照搬就能过
变体很多，面试官常改需求来测试适应力，应跟随引导
它只考数据结构，不涉及系统设计
只要背下 YouTube 的真实架构就能过
why: Top-K 变体非常多，需求上的小改动会大幅改变设计；有的面试官心里有特定解法，此时应顺势调整而不是试图说服对方。
why_en: Top-K has many variants and interviewers often shift requirements to test adaptability, so ask targeted questions and follow their lead rather than arguing them out of a preferred solution.
options_en: Every interviewer carries the same standard architecture in mind, so memorizing and copying one passes.
There are many variants, and interviewers often shift requirements to test adaptability, so follow their lead.
It only tests data structures, not system design.
Memorizing YouTube's real architecture is enough to pass.
optionExplanations: 错。不同面试官关注点差异很大，没有统一标准架构可背，死记一套会翻车。
对。顺着面试官的引导调整，比硬守自己的方案更重要。
错。这题同样考数据流、扩展、一致性等系统设计判断。
错。真实架构会变，死记硬背扛不住追问和变体。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: different interviewers focus on very different things, so there is no single standard architecture to memorize.
Correct: adapting to the interviewer's lead matters more than defending one fixed design.
Wrong: this question tests data flow, scaling, and consistency judgment like any other system design.
Wrong: real architectures change over time, so memorizing one breaks under follow-up questions.
scenario: 面试给的是 YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K：45 分钟白板，窗口档位和精确度都可能被中途改口。
scenario_en: The prompt is Top-K views on YouTube Shorts, and in a 45-minute session the interviewer may change the window sizes or the exactness requirement midway.

q: 以下哪些属于本设计敲定的核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: Which items are core functional requirements for this design? (Select all that apply.)
options: 查询全时段（all-time）的 Top-K 视频，上限 1k 条
查询最近 1 小时/1 天/1 月的 tumbling 窗口 Top-K，上限 1k 条
查询任意历史时间段（如 2025 年查 2024 年 6 月）
支持任意起止时间点的查询
why: 核心需求只有全时段与三档 tumbling 窗口的精确 Top-K；任意时间段与任意起止点被明确划为 below the line，所有查询都默认从当下往回看。
why_en: The system serves precise top-K queries for all-time and tumbling one-hour, one-day, and one-month windows capped at a thousand results, with arbitrary ranges explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Query all-time top-K videos, capped at one thousand results.
Query tumbling one-hour, one-day, and one-month top-K windows, capped at one thousand results.
Query an arbitrary historical range, like June 2024 viewed from October 2025.
Support arbitrary start and end timestamps for any query.
optionExplanations: 对。全时段是两条核心读需求之一。
对。三档窗口同样在核心需求范围内。
错。任意历史区间不在两条核心需求之列。
错。任意起止点同样不在核心需求内。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: precise all-time top-K is one of the core requirements.
Correct: precise top-K for the three tumbling windows is also in scope.
Wrong: arbitrary historical ranges were explicitly scoped out as below the line.
Wrong: arbitrary start and end points are also out of scope.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间边界切分、互不重叠的窗口，比如整点到整点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tumbling window is a fixed, non-overlapping time bucket aligned to clock boundaries, such as one full hour at a time.

scenario: YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K：所有查询只允许从当下往回看，单次最多返回 1k 条。
scenario_en: For Top-K views on YouTube Shorts, every query looks backward from now, and one response is capped at a thousand entries.

q: 当前时间是 10:06，「最近 1 小时」在 sliding window 与 tumbling window 下分别指？
q_en: At 10:06, what does the last hour mean under sliding versus tumbling windows?
options: sliding 是 9:00–10:00，tumbling 是 9:06–10:06
sliding 是 9:06–10:06，tumbling 是 9:00–10:00
why: sliding = [T-1h, T]，随查询时刻连续滑动；tumbling = 对齐整点边界的上一个完整小时，即 [Floor(T-1h), Floor(T)]。
why_en: A sliding window covers the exact hour up to the current moment, while a tumbling window is the last full hour aligned to hour boundaries.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    subgraph S["Sliding（现在 10:06）"]
        A["9:06 → 10:06"]
    end
    subgraph T["Tumbling（现在 10:06）"]
        B["9:00 → 10:00"]
    end
options_en: Both are 9:06 to 10:06.
Sliding is 9:00 to 10:00, tumbling is 9:06 to 10:06.
Both are 9:00 to 10:00.
Sliding is 9:06 to 10:06, tumbling is 9:00 to 10:00.
optionExplanations: 错。这是把两者都当成了 sliding 的定义。
错。sliding/tumbling 的定义正好说反了。
错。这是把两者都当成了 tumbling 的定义。
对。sliding 随查询时刻连续滑动，tumbling 对齐整点边界。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: this treats both windows as sliding, which is incorrect.
Wrong: this swaps the definitions of sliding and tumbling.
Wrong: this treats both windows as tumbling, which is incorrect.
Correct: sliding moves continuously with the query time, while tumbling snaps to hour boundaries.
tradeoff: 紧贴查询时刻的直觉窗口 vs 对齐边界、易于预计算的窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 随查询时刻连续移动的时间窗口，比如永远是过去一小时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sliding window moves continuously with the query time, always covering, say, the last full hour up to now.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对齐固定边界、互不重叠的时间窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tumbling window is aligned to fixed clock boundaries and does not overlap with adjacent windows.

scenario: 现在是 10:06，用户请求「最近 1 小时」Top-K；系统按整点边界预聚合，不支持任意起止点。
scenario_en: It is 10:06 and a user asks for the last hour's Top-K; the system pre-aggregates on clock-hour boundaries and does not support arbitrary start and end points.

q: 补全两种流式窗口的语义：
q_en: Fill in the semantics of the two streaming window types:
text: sliding window 的「最近一小时」随{{查询时刻}}连续滑动；tumbling window 则对齐{{整点边界}}，取上一个完整的小时区间。
why: 这是流式系统里两种主要窗口类型：sliding 更贴近直觉但更难实现，tumbling 有固定边界、天然适合预计算。
why_en: Sliding windows move continuously with the query time, while tumbling windows snap to fixed boundaries and are much easier to precompute.

scenario: 需求澄清阶段，面试官没有说明「最近 1 小时」的窗口语义，你要主动提出一种定义把设计推进下去。
scenario_en: During requirements clarification, the interviewer has not defined what last one hour means, so you need to propose a window semantic that lets the design move forward.
q: 更聪明的开场提议是？
q_en: What is the smarter opening proposal?
options: 提议用 tumbling window，并给面试官反对的机会
先实现 sliding window，因为它更精确
两种窗口都实现再让面试官挑
跳过窗口语义的讨论，直接开画整体架构图，细节等面试官追问时再补
why: 主动提出 tumbling 展示了 foresight（预见了需求歧义），且 tumbling 远比 sliding 好实现，把难啃的 sliding 留到 deep dive 再谈。
why_en: Proposing tumbling windows up front shows foresight about ambiguous requirements and keeps the initial design simple, deferring sliding windows to a deep dive.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品明确要求「从此刻往前推」的实时体验（例如小时榜要求高新鲜度），就必须支持 sliding window，至少对最短的窗口支持。
options_en: Propose tumbling windows and give the interviewer a chance to object.
Implement sliding windows first because they are more precise.
Implement both kinds of windows and let the interviewer pick.
Skip the window-semantics discussion, start drawing the overall architecture, and fill in window definitions when the interviewer asks.
optionExplanations: 对。主动提出并留出反对空间，展示了对需求歧义的预判。
错。sliding 更难实现，一上来就啃硬骨头不划算。
错。同时实现两套窗口浪费面试时间，不该现在做。
错。跳过窗口语义会让后续聚合、预计算设计缺少定义基础，回头返工更贵。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: proposing it and leaving room to object shows foresight about ambiguous requirements.
Wrong: sliding windows are harder to build, so starting there wastes early interview time.
Wrong: building both windows now wastes limited interview time.
Wrong: skipping window semantics leaves later aggregation and precompute design without a definition to build on.
tradeoff: 先提议易实现的 tumbling vs 直接啃更精确但更难的 sliding

q: 如果系统必须支持「任意时间段」查询（例如 2025 年 10 月查 2024 年 6 月的 Top-K），对设计的直接影响是？
q_en: If arbitrary time ranges must be supported, what is the direct design impact?
options: 只需要多加一个时间索引
缓存命中率会更高
预计算基本失效
写入吞吐会下降
why: 任意时间段意味着无法预知要聚合哪些区间，预计算基本失效；这很少是面试官想要的，所以明确把它划为 below the line。
why_en: Supporting arbitrary time ranges kills precomputation and forces general time-series queries, which is why it is explicitly scoped out.
options_en: It only requires adding one more time index.
Cache hit rate would go up.
Precomputation would mostly stop working.
Write throughput would drop.
optionExplanations: 错。索引解决不了『任意区间无法预知』这个根本问题。
错。任意区间会打散命中模式，命中率只会更差。
对。任意区间无法预先聚合，只能退回通用时序查询。
错。这条要求影响的是查询形态，不是写入速度。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an index cannot fix the fact that arbitrary ranges are unpredictable ahead of time.
Wrong: arbitrary ranges scatter the access pattern, so hit rate would fall, not rise.
Correct: since the ranges can't be known ahead of time, precomputation mostly stops working.
Wrong: this requirement changes query shape, not write throughput.
scenario: YouTube Shorts Top-K 已按「窗口固定、只往回看」预聚合；现在要求支持查 2024 年 6 月。
scenario_en: Top-K on YouTube Shorts is pre-aggregated for fixed backward-looking windows, and now we are asked to support querying June 2024.

scenario: Top-K 的结果集理论上可以无限增长，有人问「能不能查前 100 万个视频」。
scenario_en: A Top-K result set can grow without bound in theory, and someone asks whether the system can return the top one million videos.
q: 合理的约束是？
q_en: What is a reasonable cap for Top-K result size?
options: 支持任意大的 K，用分页机制来解决
限制 K ≤ 100，多数榜单展示场景其实已经够用了
限制 K ≤ 1000，超出的部分交给别的系统
不设上限，靠请求限流机制兜底
why: 对几乎所有 top-K 应用，1k 是合理上限；给可能无限增长的结果集设实际约束是好习惯，全量排序导出属于另一个系统的职责。
why_en: Capping K at one thousand is reasonable because anyone asking for the top million really wants the full dataset from a different system.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品真的需要全量排序导出（离线分析、数据仓库场景），那是批处理系统的事，不该塞进在线 top-K API。
options_en: Support any size of K and lean on a pagination mechanism.
Cap K at one hundred; that already covers most leaderboard-display scenarios in practice.
Cap K at one thousand; anything beyond that belongs to a different system.
Impose no cap at all and rely on request rate limiting instead.
optionExplanations: 错。分页不解决结果集无限增长带来的存储与计算问题。
错。100 对不少真实榜单场景偏小，遇到要展示前几百名时就不够用了。
对。1k 覆盖绝大多数场景，超大导出该交给另一个系统。
错。限流管的是请求频率，管不住单次结果集大小。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: pagination doesn't solve the underlying storage and compute cost of an unbounded result set.
Wrong: one hundred is too small for many real leaderboard cases that show several hundred entries.
Correct: one thousand covers nearly every use case, and full exports belong to a different system.
Wrong: rate limiting controls request frequency, not the size of a single result set.
tradeoff: 给结果集设实际上限 vs 无限增长的通用查询能力

q: YouTube 视频观看 Top-K 系统敲定的非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which nonfunctional requirements are locked in for the YouTube views Top-K system?
options: 观看发生到被计入结果最多容忍 1 分钟延迟
结果必须精确，不做近似（先按此设计，近似留到 deep dive）
查询要在几十毫秒内返回
每秒观看量很小，单机即可处理
why: NFR = 1 分钟计入延迟 + 精确结果 + 几十毫秒读延迟 + 海量观看与视频规模（数值先标 TBD 留待估算）。规模恰恰是巨大的，绝非单机能扛。
why_en: The system tolerates at most a one-minute tabulation delay, must be precise, must answer within tens of milliseconds, and must handle massive view and video volumes.
options_en: Tolerate at most a one-minute delay between a view happening and being tabulated.
Results must be precise; no approximation for now (revisit approximation in a deep dive).
Queries must return within tens of milliseconds.
View volume per second is small enough for a single machine.
optionExplanations: 对。这是事件延迟与计入结果之间的宽限期。
对。先按精确设计，近似留到 deep dive 再谈。
对。几十毫秒的读延迟直接排除查询时现算的方案。
错。规模其实巨大（70B views/day），远超单机。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: this is the grace period between an event happening and it counting in results.
Correct: the design starts precise by default and revisits approximation later.
Correct: a tens-of-milliseconds budget rules out on-the-fly aggregation.
Wrong: the actual scale is massive, seventy billion views a day, far beyond one machine.
scenario: YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K：70B views/day、约 3.6B 视频，读写都要一条可裁决的量化线。
scenario_en: Top-K views on YouTube Shorts runs at seventy billion views a day over roughly three point six billion videos, so both reads and writes need a number we can design against.

q: 为什么要给「观看发生 → 计入 Top-K」设一个 1 分钟的缓冲？
q_en: Why add a one-minute grace period between a view event and its inclusion in Top-K?
options: 分布式系统里事件可能延迟晚到
为了配合缓存过期时间
数据库每分钟才能提交一次事务
用户每分钟才会刷新一次页面
why: 观看是真实时刻发生的事件，但 09:59:55 的事件可能 10:00:55 才到达系统；1 分钟缓冲回答了「等多久」。这个宽限期后来成了缓存与预计算的空间。
why_en: Events arrive late in distributed systems, so a one-minute buffer defines how long we wait before a view must be tabulated, and that grace period later enables caching and precomputation.
options_en: Distributed systems have delay, so events can arrive late.
To line up with the cache expiration time.
The database can only commit a transaction once per minute.
Users only refresh the page once per minute.
optionExplanations: 对。事件在真实时刻发生，但到达系统可能有延迟。
错。缓存 TTL 是后续优化手段，不是这条 NFR 的来由。
错。数据库提交频率不是设计约束的依据。
错。用户刷新行为不影响事件何时被计入。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the event happens at a real moment but may reach the system with delay.
Wrong: cache TTL is a later optimization, not the reason for this requirement.
Wrong: database commit frequency has nothing to do with this design constraint.
Wrong: how often users refresh doesn't affect when a view gets tabulated.
scenario: 70B views/day 的观看事件经 Kafka 到达，网络抖动下 09:59:55 的事件可能 10:00:55 才落地。
scenario_en: Seventy billion view events a day arrive over Kafka, and with network jitter an event at 09:59:55 may only land at 10:00:55.

q: 「几十毫秒内返回」这条非功能需求对解空间的直接影响是？
q_en: How does a tens-of-milliseconds read target constrain the solution space?
options: 几乎没影响，横向多加几台服务器就能扛住
必须放弃时间窗口功能
必须改用近似算法
排除现算方案，转向预计算加缓存读
why: 几十毫秒内不可能对数十亿行现场聚合，这条要求直接把「查询时现算」踢出解空间；给 NFR 配上数字，正是为了帮你做这类裁决。
why_en: A tens-of-milliseconds latency budget eliminates on-the-fly aggregation and forces precomputation with cache-served reads.
options_en: Almost no impact; just scale out with a few more servers and it holds.
Time window support must be dropped entirely.
The design must switch to approximation algorithms.
It rules out live aggregation, pushing toward precomputation plus cached reads.
optionExplanations: 错。多加服务器也绕不开对数十亿行现场聚合的耗时，延迟瓶颈仍在。
错。窗口功能仍是核心需求，不能因延迟要求放弃。
错。精确性是另一条独立的 NFR，这条不强制近似。
对。几十毫秒内不可能现场聚合，必须偏向预计算。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: adding machines doesn't fix the time cost of aggregating billions of rows live.
Wrong: window support is a core requirement and cannot be dropped for this reason.
Wrong: precision is a separate requirement; this one doesn't force approximation.
Correct: tens of milliseconds rules out live aggregation and pushes the design toward precomputed, cache-served reads.
tradeoff: 查询时现算 vs 预计算加缓存服务读请求
scenario: YouTube Shorts Top-K 的读 SLA 定在几十毫秒，而一个窗口的明细有数十亿行。
scenario_en: The read SLA for Top-K on YouTube Shorts is tens of milliseconds, while one window holds billions of raw rows.

q: 面试官给出的规模锚点：YouTube Shorts 的日观看量与内容上传速度约是？
q_en: What rough anchors did the interviewer give for YouTube Shorts daily views and upload rate?
options: 每天 7 亿次观看；每天上传 1 小时内容
每天 700 亿次观看；约每秒上传 1 小时的内容
每天 70 亿次观看；每分钟上传 1 小时内容
每天 7000 亿次观看；每秒上传 1 分钟内容
why: 两个锚点：Shorts 70B views/day、每秒约 1 小时内容上传——它们分别推出后面的 700k TPS 写入和 3.6B 视频总量。
why_en: The interviewer anchors the scale at seventy billion views per day and roughly one hour of content uploaded every second.
options_en: 700 million views a day; one hour of content uploaded per day.
70 billion views a day; roughly one hour of content uploaded per second.
7 billion views a day; one hour of content uploaded per minute.
